reviewText: Easy to install, and looks like they will be very useful in our truck this winter.  Hang your purse on it or bags of groceries or garbage bag.
easy to set up and help you hand more delicate items like eggs or bread to they wont sit around under the sode

Good product for the cost. I am happy with them. They are basically hooks that go under the head rest. If your head rest doesn't detach this might be a problem. Also they move around a lot so if you need something that doesn't move this wouldn't work for you.
I got them for my Camry and they are perfect fit for front or rear seat head rests.Convenient to carry shirts from laundry, hang umbrella, wife's purse and grocery bags.
No more fishing around the back floor board on those long trips !but do be careful if you fold the rear seats forward, they could catch the headrest.
summary: Great idea for hanging things right behind the seat !

reviewText: Looks cheap.  The hooks sit out too far, so I don't feel comfortable leaving them hanging in the car...I don't want someone to accidentally snag themselves or hit their face on this in the back seat...especially with a child in the back.

Let me say that for the price ($6.50) it's hard to complain.They are a heavy gauge steel and look like they will hold up to a reasonable amount of weight (that is, I doubt you'd have anything in a grocery bag that would create a problem for them.They came a little bent up...easily fixed.What I didn't like was that the protective end was not plastic or rubber, but wood - 2 of them were delivered unattached to the ends of the hooks  - and just like in the picture of one of the other reviewers, one of them split in half when I tried to put it back on.I need to find some new caps to replace the wood - as the ends are just a little jagged without the protective ends on - I suggest that the manufacturer switch to plastic or rubber - and something that stays on.------------------UPDATE: Downgraded my review...Soon all of the wooden caps had broken off. This created a hazard for little kids in the back seat as well as my flip up rear seat... They are only useful if they are in the car - and I had to take them out to save eyes and upholstery.

These hooks are really thin/skinny.  I had no problem hanging them to the headrest posts (2012 Toyota Tacoma).  However, they do not hang straight down.  I had to bend them so they would hang down instead of sticking out @ ~120 degrees.  The ride in my truck is pretty bumpy and anything hung on these do get tossed around a bit.
Does a fine job. Only had to do it once last season.  We'll see how it works on a full season

We own an Air-O-Swiss AOS 7135 ultrasonic humidifier.  For a few weeks now, the machine has indicated, through its warning light, that it required cleaning.  Our Air-O-Swiss 7135 is hyper-sensitive; its warning light goes on with the tiniest (invisible) speck.  So, initially we bought Air-O-Swiss EZ Cal Cleaner / Descaler.  Didn’t do the trick!  Thereafter we replaced the Demineralization Cartridge (and contents.)  Still no change.  Even after following the instructions to the letter and cleaning with specialized brushes, our humidifier wouldn’t extinguish its cleaning light.  So, last resort, this EZCal Pro. Again, applied the product as instructed; without success.  So, our humidifier is presently running with the irritating little light on, but operating as it should be nevertheless.  The EZ Cal Cleaner / Descaler and the EZCal Pro liquid didn’t do wonders in our case either.  So, can't say that we're thrilled with the Air-O-Swiss maintenance products.  In the future we'll stick to vinegar or some other generic decalcification agent.
summary: No longer sponsoring the Air-O-Swiss company!

reviewText: The instructions for our Air-O-Swiss humidifier say that every two weeks we need to drain the water, mix this stuff up in a quart of water, and let it sit in the base unit to remove mineral build-up. Hard to find locally, but much needed during the winter months.
summary: If you have an Air-O-Swiss humidifier, you need this stuff

reviewText: This is as simple as a product gets....it helps keep your expensive Air-O-Swiss investment running in tip top shape.  We have multiple humidifiers around our home by Air-O-Swiss and we have well water where we live.  Naturally the units can get mucked up pretty quickly...but using a pack of this stuff once every 2-3 months keeps them running perfectly fine...Highly recommended.
summary: If you use Air-O-Swiss - get this....

reviewText: Does the job for which it was intended. Added to HOT water and dissolved, pour it into the base of the Air-O-Swiss humidifier to clean any 'scaling' and other 'old water' contaminants. Then thoroughly rinse (without dunking the base under water) and do this about every 2 months.
summary: Does the job for which it was intended. Added ...

reviewText: 1-16-14.  I have used Air-O-Swiss AOS 7417 EZ Cal - Cleaner/Descaler for my Air-O-Swiss humidifiers for five years.  Following the directions it mostly dissolves the calcium buildup around the vent and atomizer unit of the machines.  Some mechanical scrapping is still required to remove all the calcium deposit scale buildup during normal operations.  Good product.
summary: Good product and does a satisfactory job

reviewText: I bought 2 of these and have needed to use one once. The car was parked head first in a single garage so jumping car-to-car would have been tough. I was able to jump the car in a couple of minutes using this gem without any trouble. They hold a charge for at least 6 months, which is how often I have been charging them.
summary: Works great, keeps charge for months

reviewText: I've owned Xantrex and Duracell jump starters in the past. Unlike those and similar products, the JNC does only one thing and does it really well -- starts engines like a champ. For the equivalent starting power in one of the multifunction Chinese-made products, you'd need to buy a bigger and heavier power pack for considerably more money.I've used the 300XL to start 4-, 6- and 8-cylinder engines. It had no problem with any of them. Starting a 4-cylinder engine is so effortless, I imagine I could start a whole parking lot row of them with one charge. The vehicle I actually carry the jump starter around in is a 2007 Lincoln Town Car with a big V8 engine. One night, my alternator died and the battery drained completely before the car finally went dead on the highway. Not only did I start the engine with the JNC 300XL, but I left it connected and used it to power the car while I drove it to my all-night mechanic (with the headlights off). This drained it flat, so I recharged it as soon as I could and it was fine.There's no AC inverter in this product, but the flashlight attachment pops out to reveal a 12V socket that you can use to power/recharge laptops, mobile phones and suchlike. I use to to power my air compressor to inflate tires. Speaking of which, I have a really good compressor that I bought using the money I saved by purchasing the JNC instead of a multifunction power pack, which would have included a really cheap air compressor made out of plastic parts.

I bought this for my daughter to keep in her suburban.  She always seems to need help starting her vehicle because something has been left on by one of the grandkids.  I plan on getting a couple more, one for me and one for my wife's vehicle.

My parent's SUV is five years old now and anything can go wrong with the battery.  Initially I never really wanted to buy a portable jumper because they were all too big and expensive and the small ones looked clumsy.  I stumbled upon this one and I knew just by looking at it that it would satisfy our needs.The JNC300XL is very sleek, it's small, and built like a tank.  It's heavy (about 10 pounds.)  I have the nice little trunk bag from [...] and this fits in there with their portable air compressor (very snug at that.)  One time we were at the airport and my dad left the lights on and we were stuck in the parking lot with a dead car in a creepy area.  Luckily for us, we were parked away from other cars and a nice person helped us out with a jump.  I don't think we might be as lucky next time.  When a situation like that arises, you wish you had something like this.  Again, I'm not for carrying a bulky jump starter because I don't like my trunk cluttered with stuff.  The JNC300XL is just the right size to carry in a medium-sized trunk bag. It just feels right when you hold it.I also like how it has a built in flashlight and you can use the 12 volt outlet to power a dead cell phone or some other 12 volt appliance.  The cables are nice and are 4AWG and the clamps are very sturdy.  Removing the clamps requires a little bit of force so keep that in mind if you are not as strong as you used to be or if you have arthritis.  Griot's Garage sells this same item for one hundred dollars under their name.  The only difference is they give you a lifetime warranty and their item is red in color.  I bought this from another online retailer for fifty-eight dollars plus shipping.  So do some shopping before you buy it.I'm glad I bought this item because even though you won't use it everyday, it is a lifesaver when you need it.  Also you can help your friends and neighbors out when they have battery problems as well.  It's a fair price and the quality is outstanding. It's hard to find quality items that last these days. I'm very satisfied with this purchase.
summary: A High Quality, Versatile, and Sleek Jumpstarter for the Inevitable

reviewText: Exactly what it does. Designed to be light weight, affordable, and reliable. Except that it should only be used in emergency situations. Situations where you walk out of a store to realize your car wont start. This will have enough power to jump start these kind of scenarios. It WILL NOT jump start a car thats been sitting for a month and the battery has been drained to nothing. Its not designed to do that. The light in the front is useless and isnt even LED, BUT it doubles as a cigarette lighter type 12v socket to charge up a phone or whatever. Dont lose the charger, it costs half the price of the actual jump box and is a very non standard voltage.Would give it 5 stars, if it had a more standard 2 prong or 3 prong standard wall outlet plug for charging. but overall. its good to have in the trunk for those just in case moments.
summary: Works decently as a nice emergency jump pack

reviewText: I used this little guy on a dead battery in a Corvette and it cranked it over with no problem and fired up in seconds. I will keep this in the car and it is smaller and weighs less than those bigger ones and has about the same power. This was a good investment  and a great price.

This item is made by Clore Automotive, stating it is a US manufacturer.This item is their "top of the line" with heavy duty cables and heavy duty battery.The cables do not stick very well in the clip-on mount (built into the carrying handle), twisting them a bit helped.The unit comes with a one-time lifetime repair voucher of $50. Impressive, considering the purchase price.Checking out the details before and after purchase revealed severe issues when checking for proper operating and maintaining the unit.The manual(s) for the unit, either the one that came with the item or the one online, call for a immediate charge upon receipt of either 12 hours or 24 hours. The times for charging after use or regular storage differ dramatically as well.Contacted the manufacturer. Answer was that "it does not matter if 12 or 24 hours". So why wasting a 12 hour charge if it does not matter and the unit still has full capacity? Does it have full capacity? Answer "Should not be critical". What???Contacted the manufacturer again regarding maintaining the charge after use or when in storage. Was told that "it does not really matter", just charge it every 90 days.This is in complete contradiction to the 2 different manuals for this unit. Lack of quality, an American issue, still present.So what is there to do now? Sure it will start a vehicle once, then how is it supposed to be charged? How is it supposed to be charged when not in use? How long will it last?Well, it is a small and supposedly powerful unit, so lets wait and see.Update:Ran the 1000 amp battery on a conversion van completely down (listening to weather radio when the tornado hit a few weeks ago at a Michigan campground). Turned everything off in the car and attached the unit to the battery, then waited about 3 minutes (should be common sense, to allow electricity to float and settle). The little unit turned the engine over with no effort at all. It certainly provided a satisfactory effect first (by not being stranded) and a "wow" effect right after. Quite a accomplishment for a small unit like that.The unit was recharged for some hours calculated from the different statements the manufacturer made, somehow in the middle. The unit got us going, and for this price it might be worth keeping it.
summary: Questionable Reliability in the long run

reviewText: I also use mine to power my NorthStar 16 gal. yard spayer. I can spray two tanks full before the JNC runs down.
summary: I also use mine to power my NorthStar 16 gal ...

reviewText: Purchased this to keep in my POS winter car which has a weak battery. So, I let the battery go dead to test this until and it worked like a charm. So later in the day I went to the post office and sure enough I left the lights on in the car and I was dead. So this unit has already paid for itself with time it saved me with a easy jump. Its very small and compact.

I bought this device and I hope that I don't have to use it anytime soon. It will be handy to have though. I would recommend this to young lady drivers too. This way they don't have to ask strangers for help on jumping their car off. I do however recommend carrying a set of jumper cables as a back up just in case. You just never know.
summary: A must have for safety for sure

reviewText: I've only used it to help someone else out, but it did what it was suppose to do. It nice to know that you have one of these just in case. I have 2 of them and both have held up so far with holding a charge while being left in a vehicle. Small and compact, so doesn't take up to much room.

reviewerName: Mr. Deeds "Opportunity is limited only by ima...
reviewText: I ordered this product to jump my second vehicle -- which due to the bad economy my wife and I are storing in the garage to save on insurance and also state license fees. However I want to keep the car in run-ready condition, so I try to start it every couple weeks or so. But I usually forget a time or two and the battery dies.That was the incentive behind my purchase of the Jump N Carry. And I can tell you it is a perfect little device. Not very big (and not terribly heavy), it's very easy to clamp onto your car battery. So far my car has started on the first attempt (been used twice now).When not jumping my stored car, we keep the Jump N Carry in the trunk of our main car -- just in case we need it or some other motorist needs a jump.I recommend this product.EDIT: March 16, 2011After one full year in the trunk, I just tested the battery and it's at 75 percent. Impressive! The only product feature I see now would be helpful would be to have the plug to charge this unit built-in. It's an extra charger -- and I've seem to have misplaced it. A retractable plug would be perfect.
summary: Small but mighty, my dead car started on the first try

reviewText: I recently rec'd this unit, charged for a full 20hrs.Just used it to jump start my 2005 G35 coupe, it worked perfectly as I used it twice, checked the status light, appeared to be be able to jump a few more V6 engines before I need to recharge unit.Also, my battery was totally dead, I mean when I turned the key...no lights on the dash, no clicking sounds from the engine...totally drained battery.I might consider buying another unit for my other carEdit: March 26 2013I tried to help my friend who had a 2008 Subaru Legacy 4 cylinder turbo, it failed to start it as he drained his battery when he forgot to turn off the interior map light. I was surprised it failed since it started my V6 G35 which also had a near dead battery. I hope my unit was not good for just one jump??Also, note that I recharge my jump starter after every single use.Reducing rating from 5 STARS to just 3 stars

We have tested a few chargers for fleet use - this being the best one I tested.I have a fleet of Ford E250 vans, mostly 2004, 2006-2008 models.  I have jumped at least 10 vans with this on a single charge.  The 10th van had zero juice in the battery (not enough to even dimmly power the cab light or even get a flicker on the dash), and it fired right up without any charge time.My ONLY complain is the charger leads do not grip well onto GM side post batteries (we have some '02 and '04 GMC 2500 vans as well).  It works but you have to work to make a connection.This jumps far better than some other brands we have tried and I am recommending that we purchase several more for our fleet.

Small package, well made, external 12V plug a plus.  I bought this unit to use remotely with a portable compressor I had purchased.  The 12V round plug worked great for this application.  The provided 12V plug in light was a little hokey (cheap) but I didn't buy this for the light.  Haven't used it to start a car yet.
Bought this for my father inlaw who loves this jump box.  Its small and light enough to carry around yet more than powerful enough to jump start any car.

I've had 2 of these now for almost 1 year and getting another now. I'm keeping one in each car now and a backup in my garage. I've used it to jump my Honda Pilot more than 20 times over the past year. Kids leave lights on mainly. I don't worry anymore.- It takes me <1min to pull this out, hook up and jump my car.- The battery lasts forever it seems. after 10 jumps still shows full power, but I charge it to full every few months just in case as I know with lead acid batteries if you get too low, it will create buildup and reduce effectiveness over time.- i've kept in my hot garage and inside my car without trouble (i keep it under some sheets in my car to prevent it from being exposed to direct sunlight). haven't noticed any problems or leakages over the year.I initially didn't believe it would work so well, but now I recommend it strongly to anyone as a backup. Never be stranded again.

We now have three of these units,one for each car. It is a real comfort having this item in your car especially during the pastwinter in New Jersey. I have also assisted other drivers during their time of need.
summary: A must-have product for your car !

reviewText: After reading all the positive reviews, I decided to pick one up as a Christmas present for my elderly parents so they had something on hand to jump start their Honda Accord if it was ever needed.  As of yet, of course, I have not had the opportunity to try it out.  However, I did do a bench test using the 12V adapter plug.I used a 120V converter outlet to plug into where the flashlight is. This enabled me to plug in a lamp.  I was amazed to find that it kept a 40 watt CFL bulb powered for 7 hours!  This unit is perfect for the unexpected power outage.  I wish I had found this unit much earlier on before I bought the Duracell 450 and 300 units.  It is so much lighter, less cumbersome and bulky.  It is also at the fraction of the price than the Duracell Powerpack units.Some side notes:  This unit does not have any indication as to when it is fully charged, other than to look and see that all 3 green lights are lit.  It states in the manual it should be fully charged within 3 hours, but should not be kept plugged in for more than 24 hours.  So, the owner must remain vigilant during the charging process or damage to the battery may occur.The final 3rd remaining green light WILL blink when the unit is low on power.  This is a nice feature so you can prevent depleting the battery to the point of damage.  I am unsure if it has an internal cut off to prevent this from happening, but I do not want to take that risk.There is another variation of this model at a lower price.  It is yellow and I believe it has thicker jumper cables.  I am going to buy one of them next for my own home purposes after Christmas.  If anyone has any feedback on that one, I welcome anyone to leave a comment.  It is appreciated.Be confident, buy this unit!

I purchased the JNC300XL for my wife, because she has a habit of leaving some load "on" and drain her battery.  I was attracted to this product because, (1) it was ranked well on amazon, (2) it does have lots a solid reviews, and (3) it was small and not too heavy for my wife.  Before purchasing this product, I was spectacle of the "900 Peak Amp" rating.  I researched all of the internet to try to find any battery specs that comes inside this so-called jump starter.  When it arrived I tried it on a friends sedan.  Connected it up, turned over the car, and nothing.  I took the JNC300XL back home and opened it up to check the battery.  It is an 8ah battery inside. To be frank, I am not a battery expert, but how can a 8ah battery delivery 800 peak amps? I reassembled the JNC300XL and connected it back up it my friends car, and left it connected for several hours (~2-3 hours), and it did eventually work. If you are purchasing this as a jumper starter for emergency situations, I think you will be disappointed.  If you just need something to boost your battery, and time is not an issue, it works just fine.  I just think the product description is misleading.  It should say battery booster, not jump starter.

reviewText: Star Brite Star Tron Gasoline Additive.  I have a 10 HP Tecumseh engine on a 5000 Watt Generator that for the past two years had become difficult to start and wouldn't run without surging, back firing,etc.,  unless choked two notches . I'VE ALWAYS PUT STA-BIL IN THE FUEL TOO.  Now it does set for long periods without running though. Well after cleaning the bowl jets and still having problems I stumbled on this stuff. So ordered some, (what to lose ?) not much. I had emptied the old gas so put 1 gallon in the generator tank with the dose recommended (doubled) and started the engine. Still needed the two clicks of choke to run without surge etc. when started. I let it run for about two minutes and could hear a smoother sound coming from the engine. But it still needed one click of choke to run without surging. After 15 minutes checked and it ran silk smooth without any choke. Have checked it since and starts on the first pull too. I put it in a Robins 11 HP engine that was getting hard to start and it cured that within 5 minutes of running (cold starts too). Put it in my wife's old car and it runs smoother. Have 4 more small engines I will use this in too. I sound like a commercial but believe me this is worth every penny and cheaper than mechanics too. I have no doubt if used regularly in gas I won't have those problems again. I would recommend this to anyone for small engines, cars, etc. It really does what they say and the proof is in the engine performance.ADDENDUM: There are two concentrated formulas one 143XX for small engines and 930XX for Marine/Standard engines=(AUTO), (XX equals Oz in a bottle). The 930XX is a higher concentrate formula.  I received the 93032 (32Oz bottle) formula but was able to use it in small engines by reducing the amount per gallon and not wasting product that way. 10 Ml of 930(standard formula) is about the same as 1 Oz of 143(small engine formula) for 6 gallons of fuel. The company also says you can't overdose with this stuff. In other words if you put to much you just waste product not harm the engine. By the way 10 bottle caps full equal one Oz of product. Go to the Company web site and read how much to use and that way you will understand better what I have tried to say here. Take it from a 70 year old guy, This stuff is great. Everything I have put this in has increased the idle speed some .  Means water and crude has been removed . I put this in my new 2013 Kia Optima and two things happened, 1. increased idle speed and 2. increased the MPG 1 mile to the gallon. If you don't believe that that's OK I wouldn't and didn't when reading others say that. That car also expelled black crude from the exhaust pipes which is water vapor combined with carbon deposits caused by fuel burning cleaner. Decided we don't know what we are pumping from station storage tanks besides gas but the engines do. I've used this in 5 small engines, an older car, a truck, and a 40HP diesel tractor with improved performance from all of them. Great stuff.

Hope to keep my new car running like new for a long time.I have read most of the reviews about sick engines getting better mileage and running much better after using this product.Most of us (including myself) wait until there is a problem then try to fix it and that can get very expensive. IF possible, I prefer to prevent the problem and save the extra expense and inconvenience.This additive should keep my fuel system clean and in new or near new condition maximizing mileage and performance while I own the car. Even if I get "bad gas", I probably won't notice it.My car is protected against the negative effects of methanol. Water, phase separation, varnish build-up. The injectors will STAY clean.I can't recommend this product because of personal experience because I have no engine problems nor an increase in mileage.COST: At the recommended 1oz per 15 gallons it is a inexpensive treatment. $25/32oz = $0.78 for 15gals. At 500gal per bottle X 25mpg, this 32oz bottle will last 12,500 miles.

Read through so many review on this product. It make me so curiously interest to try one of it. Is that really work.  I tried one of the similar product for 128 gal.8 oz. on my old Accord (1997) After number of day, the feeling of the engine run much smoother and much quiet than I tried other engine treatment. Until today, I haven't put additional in, the engine still running really well. According to other review. Now, I'm going to try this one for higher concentration to see what the different is. Theadditive star brite Startron enzyme was bought on the reccomendation of the service manager at the auto dealership where I bought my car. The additive is great and well worth the cost. However, Amazon packaging for this product leaves much to be desired!! clear instructions-easy to use and increased the miles per gallon on both of our vehicles by about 2mpg. Will buy again.

This is a big savings from amazon than buying retail.  It should come with a measuring cup.  Graduations on the bottle encourage waste. reviewText: This appears to be a very nice kit! I gave it 4 starts because I have not used it yet and would have been nice if the manufacturer included a tube of rubber cement to aide in and sealing any tire plugs. Also I see velcro material on the exterior of the kit case, but no velcro was included in the kit to apply to the interior of the vehicle or storage area.What I do like about this kit is that there is an adapter to run the compressor off the battery directly as some of these new car 12V sources can not handle the amperage load.I will report back after it`s first use, whenever that may be... otherwise it looks like a very good kit.

I bought this for my Mini Cooper since it does not have a spare tire. The compressor is the best portable unit that I have ever seen. The kit is nicely packaged and well worth the money. It's also 1/3 the price of the factory Mini/BWM unit. I highly recommend it.

I'll start off by saying that any issues people had with the air compressor can be fixed.  I tore it apart and sprayed Royal Purple MaxFilm on the crank and piston sleeve, put it back together and let it run 10min, it was barley warm to the touch. This kit is an outstanding deal, I think this is a must have for every vehicle, I will be buying more!

I bought this same kit from a hardware store when I had a flat and knew it was due to a faulty valve core on my tire and didn't feel like changing a perfectly good tire in a parking garage. At the hardware store this kit ran me $80 so this price on Amazon is a great deal. I'm a gearhead and at first thought it was just a cheap little gimmick but after using it, I am sold. The kit comes with spare valve cores and a key. It pumped up my tire from completely flat to 30psi in about 5 mins, way faster than changing the whole tire. Ignore the bad reviews, they obviously did not read the 1 page manual that comes with it! Save yourself some trouble and read it while you're waiting for your tire to inflate. The kit is for emergencies only, not your everyday use air compressor. If this is what you're planning on using it for then I doubt it will last very long. It says to not let it run longer than 10 mins or something or it shuts off automatically because it is too hot. Unplug it and let it cool down (like any air compressor), then you can use it again. It also clearly states not to rely on the built in pressure gauge (again, like all air compressors) and it comes with a manual tire gauge to check the pressure before you take off.The one thing I am slightly disappointed with is the bottle of slime is for ATV/Mower tires only, you shouldn't put it in your car tire. It worked for me cause I didn't need to use it and the only thing I use slime in is bike and mower tires anyway cause it is a pain to clean out of the tire and rim when you change a tire (I do mine myself so that's why I care). They do sell slime for highway use anywhere if you really want to add it to your kit.Long story short, I'm very happy with this kit so far and am buying one for my dad and grandpa for Christmas!
summary: Really great little kit! Ignore the bad reviews

reviewText: Ergonomically sound product.  It's compact design makes it efficient for use with my morotcycle.  It seems to work well.  I am hoping it last for several years.
I have used this a couple of times and it works great on checking the Motorcycle tire pressure. Love the angled head.
It works and is accurate.  It's a bit of a hassle trying to get a reading sometimes.  It doesn't fit as well as the manual (analog) gauge.

Need a 90 degree to make life easier on one of my bikes,  one has a 90 degree on the tires already but this fit the bill on my GL1200. only problem I can see is the pin in the center is  plastic so dont know the longevity on it.
The gauge is very, very accurate (to a half pound).  It does however need to be released VERY QUICKLY from the stem or the air escaping will re-set the gauge to zero.
the tire pressure gage is easy to read and  use, is small enough to carry in your pocket,  saddle bag, or glove box if using the gage for car or truck. Angled tip works well for motorcycle tires.

This gauge works perfectly, always giving a correct reading and fits on the back tire of my Yamaha XJ650 no problem which is hard there isn't much room between the valve stem and the break drum.  Its small size allows me to carry it in my riding jacket pocket so I can check the pressure of my tires anywhere!  You can't go wrong with this gauge.

This is a convenient tire gauge to carry along on motorcycle. Display easy to read. Maybe I just checked my pressure too often but the center stem in this wore down in a matter of a couple of months. (it's plastic)
summary: Accutire MS-4710B Motorcycle 5-99 PSI Digital Tire Gauge

reviewText: Works as advertised. Very easy to manipulate to get to the valve stem to check pressure on my motorcycle. It should since that is what is was made for.
Wouldn't allow accuracy to read numbers below 7lbs. My husband is lazy and i can't tell what the dog is saying...And i don't get an accurate reading from husband.
summary: Accutire MS -4710B Motorcycle 5-99 PSI Digital Tire Gauge

reviewText: very functional and easy to use.l  we keep ours in the harley bag for ease and safety. Recommeded to anyone
Handy to have on the road to check air pressure in suspension and tires.

I wish this had a swivel head and light. It is much lighter than the models that do, however, so this one rides in the saddlebag and the others are on the shop wall. I've compared accuracy with more expensive units and thus one reads the same every time.

I bought this for my motorcycle tires because they can be so hard to get at sometimes. This gauge works great. And very accurate.I've used the old style gauge forever and I am so glad I bought a digital gauge.Packaged great and arrived right on time.

I needed a replacement for my 10 year old digital tire gauge, so I thought I'd find something that would really meet my needs.  Since I ride a motorcycle most of the time, and on long distant rides, tire pressure is something that if not done right will ruin your trip.I was going to get a backlit version, but saw this one.  Accessing my R1200RT rear tire's valve is a bit difficult with the panniers and double brake discs.  This looked like a good buy.Highlights1.  Seems accurate.  I tried several analog and digital gauges on my car, and this was spot on.  I tried it on my bike, and apparently, I need some air!2.  Battery appears to be replaceable, which was the issue with my trusty old one.3.  Handle grip is nice.4.  Huge numerals for those who have poor near vision.The not so highlights1.  It's plastic.  Sure, that makes it light and probably cheap to make, but I suspect that 90 bend is going to be a problem.  You might torque it a bit getting it off the valve stem, which might break it.  But it hasn't broken yet, but I'm concerned.2.  It's hard to read in the dark.  Make that next to impossible.  OK, I could have purchased another version, but I'm just mentioning it.3.  There is no audible beep when it captures the pressure.  But, it's something I'll just have to accept.Overall, for the price, it appears to be a very well designed gauge for a motorcyclist.  Interestingly, I tried it on my car, and the angle precluded me from using it with the numbers facing me.This gauge isn't perfect, but it's pretty nice.  I wish it were all metal, but we'll see if I mess it up.  It's now in my tank bag, always available for use.
I use this on my motorcycle all the time. It makes it easier to get to those hard to reach spots and it holds the reading so you can see it when you pull it out. Works great. Well worth the money.

I have purchased other tire gauges from Accutire and have found them to be sturdy, long lasting and accurate. I purchased this gauge for use on my Honda Goldwing motorcycle. I needed a right angle low clearance gauge to clear the brake disks and check my suspension pressure. I also have found the gauge convenient for my wife's Honda 50, 2013 Honda CRV w/TPM valves and my ATV's. With this gauge I don't have to bend or place angle pressure on the sides of the tire valve stems.
Nice battery operated digital air guage. Nice enough to be 5 stars, and should pack away nice, look forward to using it. Thanks and 5 stars. AJL
summary: I like it but, have yet to use it 5 star review, for product and dealer.AJL

reviewText: OK, I purchased this for my bike, because I had a good experience with another accutire pressure gauge.But this one "sucks". It worked ok when I first got it, but after 2 years the battery went dead and I only used it maybe 20 times. My other accutire pressure gauge is 10 years old and I'm still on the original battery. So I purchased a new battery and found out you have to take this whole thing apart, to get to where the battery is buried. So I take it apart very carefully, not to lose these very small parts and replaced the battery. So happy with my battery install, I go out to my garage and try it out and all I get is 1 psi on the lcd, so I try a different car, same thing 1 psi. This is a disposable item, when the battery dies you just throw it away and buy a new one. No thanks, I will keep using my analog pressure gauge.

Don't believe the ad statement 'heavy duty cord' translates into 'heavy duty' anything, other than maybe rubber insulation. THIS IS FOR LOW-POWER ITEMS ONLY!!! It is 20-AWG wire inside, barely enough wire diameter to run a 5-watt speaker. If you think you are going to plug in a tire inflator, a 1,000,000 candle spotlight, etc., you are SADLY MISTAKEN. This is NOT, repeat NOT heavy duty. It is a crime that the wire AWG (American Wire Gauge) is not listed in the specs. Otherwise, you would know that plugging in a heavy amperage load is either going to burn this up in a split second, or turn it into a heater coil and set your car on fire when you try. If you want to charge a cell phone, an iPad, etc. on it, go ahead, no problem. But the problem is, most people buy an extension cord for a cigarette lighter to do something with a heavy amp load outside of the vehicle. This WILL NOT support a heavy amp load.
summary: WARNING - 20-AWG Wire will NOT support any serious amperage!!!

reviewText: I bought this as an extension cord from my pop up camper battery to the inside of my camper. I hooked up a 200watt inverter on the other side. Good, low guage wire.

I bought this as an extension for a tire-inflater and car vacuum where both plug into the 12V cigarette light socket.  With this, I can take the inflater and vacuum all around the vehicle with no worries.  I can even stretch it out and manage to use it for those items on another vehicle that's parked beside mine.  So, I'm please with it.

I bought this in May of 2013 and it's now September 1, 2013. I tried to use this cord for the first time over the Labor Day weekend holiday with no results. Michigan summers feels many times like your in Kentucky with the heat & humidity. With that said, I needed something to cool me down camping along the West Michigan shorelines. The Endless Breeze did a great job of that but I needed an extension cord to run it. I finally opened this extension cord up and tried to use it. NOTHING! I thought that maybe I needed to check the fuse? So I did and guess what. It didn't even have the capability of using a fuse. That's dangerous and could blow an electronic device up...I notified Amazon and as usual, they gave me an opportunity to send it back even though I'm out of the return date. Thanks Amazon, your the best.
summary: A 12 volt cord without a fuse

reviewText: I can't reach my travel trailer tires from the rear of my SUV with my air pump without this extension cord.  It's a good quality product and a smart investment.
If you know why you need one of these, you won't be disappointed. Quality construction and works well. Good buy.

I have a few of these, and I'm finding that they're very handy.  And, they seem to work well for me, although I don't think they're made with really overly heavy duty wire and wouldn't recommend them for anything other than relatively lightly powered items.  I've used mine mostly for powering laptop computers, and they've been good for that, and used that way they have held up to the usage okay.
summary: Not very heavy duty, but handy

reviewText: I leave a 30w solar panel on the roof of the rv as a trickle charger for the big battery bank,and use this to run out, and up to the panel.It is well made and will last me for years.
I really like this thing. It makes it so much easier to use the portable 12v tire inflator to add air to my tires.

It does look cheaply made however the price you cant go wrong I use with my air compressor for tire inflation and we camp a lot so it will be used a lot during the summer . if ya take care of it , it  should last awhile would recommend
It works, looks sturdy, long enough to extend thru out my car, came super fast and priced just rite. I would recommend.

I used this in conjunction with theVIAIR 85P Portable Air Compressor.  Worked perfectly, no issues.  While "by the book" it might seem that it's too small a diameter wire for the power requirements sometimes you just have to DO IT rather than worry about it so much.  They would be right on that if we all lived in books.  You obviously can't start your car with this thing but it is fine for the loads you can throw through a cigarette lighter.  I use it on occasion, not constantly, day in, day out.  It served its purpose and the insulation was quite a bit heavier than I would have expected from it.
summary: Can't beat it for the price

reviewText: I've already used this a few times, mostly for my 100W inverter, but for an air compressor as well. The extra 12' loses quite a bit of power efficiency when running my air compressor, but that's to be expected. It's better than not being able to air up my trailer tires. The end connectors are very nice.

I've seen the reviews questioning the capacity of this cord, so I'm wondering if maybe there are changes in the cord.  The one I received is marked on the back of the package:"18 gauge wire""15 Amp Capacity"Now, I'm not an electrician, nor do I pretend to be one.  I don't know that 18G wire is sufficient to carry 15A.  I'll be using this for a small GPS that I mounted up high and I don't want the cord in the windshield.
Love this product. I am wheelchair bound and use this to charge my chair when I'm in the van. Great product

No, I wouldn't use this to power a generator from 12' from my vehicle so my kids could play XBox...but it works perfectly well in my application. I run a 12V air compressor mounted in my truck with this from a standard 12V socket in my Mustang. It has never let me down, blown a fuse, or caused any weird power spikes/drops. It serves its purpose well!

The RP-203EC is just what is says it is - a 12' extension cable for 12VDC. I needed a cable to extend the length to the cigarette adapter in one of my cars.  It was just what I needed.  All in all, it is nothing fancy, but the price makes it hard to pass up.
This is a very heavy duty cord. Probably more than I need, as I only use it to power my porable Fantastic 12v fan, in my motor home, when I dry camp. But, bigger IS better, right ?
summary: An extension of a different type

reviewText: This item is great if you have multiple adapters and need to use the cigarette for charging items for those in the back seat. I have two ports and the extension is used for one of them.
Well mad and works as advertised. The rubber in the wire is a nice quality, feels like it will last.
We needed this for my children's portable dvd.player in our car. The stock cord didn't even come close and this one has many feet to spare.
summary: Needed for our children's portable DVD player

reviewText: THIS IS EVERYTHING YOU WANTED AND IT FITS IN THE TRUNK OR GLOVE BOX. i USED MINE TO RUN MY 12 VOLT IMPACT WRENCH TO REMOVE MY TIRES AND USED IT ON MY 12 AIR COMPRESSOR TO PUT MY AIR SHOCK UP..  ITS REALLY HANDY AND APPEARS SO FAR TO BE WELL MADE.  The WIRING MUST BE GOOD ENOUGH, AS IT DIDN'T GET HOT OR BLOW THE FUSE FOR A LIGHTER SOCKET.  SORRY FOR THE ALL CAPS, BUT I'M DOING THIS WITH ONE HAND,  SO DON T FLAME ME ..

I have a nice Slime brand tire inflator http://www.amazon.com/Slime-40022-12-Volt-Digital-Inflator/dp/B002ZBWKAU/ref=sr_1_1?s=automotive&ie=UTF8&qid=1402797569&sr=1-1&keywords=slime+inflator (which I did not buy from Amazon, but highly recommend), but I had to pass it through various doors and windows to get all the tires.  With this I can get all four tires much more easily.  I had tried a coiled extension, but there was too much resistance in the wires.  The inflator needs a full 10 amps plus from the power plug.  I could tell the inflator wasn't quite as exuberant with this extension cord, but the loss was not significant enough to impact the function of the inflator.
Extension cable for inverter. Can set up inverter a good ways away from car if I need to. Just handy to have.
ran this below the carpet to the rear of my jeep. i did not want to run a permanent additional, and having the ability to plug in to my cigarette or power outlet gives me the best of both worlds.

I needed something to reach longer than what the auto NORMAL items are and has been working daily for awhile now and is at a great price with no issues so far.  I have used it for about 100 hours and it works great.
Great extension cord and it's really long! Perfect and long enough to reach anywhere in my SUV. Would recommend it.
I bought this to go with my portable pump last year.  I have used it several times since because the pump does not have a long enough cord.  Highly recommend.
I use this as an extension cord for my 12v dc tire inflator. It seems heavy duty and I've used it a few times with no problems. It's exactly what i was looking for.
summary: It is what it's supposed to be

reviewText: I used this to release my wiper arm and it worked like magic.  Made it look easy.  Before this, I tried many tools but was afraid to pry because the underside is plastic.  This fits right under the arm so it is pushing on the metal and therefore the plastic never gets touched.

This made short work of pulling wiper arms off a 2003 Saturn Ion. Sturdy, heavy and well made. The only thing I'd change would be having a hex-head instead of a sliding handle on top, but not a big deal. A keeper.

These things have been around forever in one form or another.  The simplest ones work, but can sometimes be a real pain.  They slip, twist, and don't grip very well.  This OTC puller is very solid, and one of the best investments you can make for both your car, and your own temperament.  Having a frozen battery terminal is one of the most aggravating things that one can face when working on cars.  It's also one of those things that even people that hardly ever go under the hood can find themselves face to face with.  This puller is very well made and can easily free most frozen terminals in 30 seconds or less.  It pretty much works like a cork screw on a wine bottle and saves the user a whole lot of aggravation and naughty words spewed.  It's very reasonably priced, well made and designed, and one of those things that when you really need it, it's golden.  A very worthwhile investment for sure... : )

This is a well made battery terminal puller for the price. It's manufactured in Taiwan, but seems durable and operates smoothly. This tool will also come in handy for other things like pulling stuck windshield wiper arms and removing press-fit retainer caps and bearings found in small appliances and power tools.I'm happy with it and when considering the cost, I think it was probably the best overall value I could find for this type of terminal puller.
I've used this puller on wiper arms and battery terminals. It works great and is very well built. Everyone should have one of these.

OTC products have always been my go-to brand.  A little bulky, but these pullers also assist with windshield wipers and small applications, not just battery terminals.  That's the reason I rated it high because of the build quality.

I replaced my original filters with these FRAMs in my 2000 Chevy Silverado.  It only took me 11 years to figure out I had them.  So, now that I have declared myself as an Auto Incompetent, I can still say it was easy to replace them and the FRAMs fit perfectly.

Fits my 2002 Silverado LS 5.3L vortec RWD, extended cab. Very simple install, DON'T remove the third bolt closest to the driver side of the under dash shield, you can move it out of the way without taking it all the way off, saving you a headache trying to line the cover back up again. Doesn't have a "fresh breeze" smell and I can still smell the dirty air of city driving, but still a HUGE upgrade from what I had in there. Basically a pile of dirt and leaves with some filter in the middle. Air flow is superb.

I was embarrassed to see the dirt & dust fall out when I replaced these.  I have a 2002 Silverado & I'll bet it's never been done before!  What a difference it made in the air flow!  My AC really blasts now!  Good video on youtube on how to do it----pretty easy & well worth the effort.
summary: Not something on your radar screen, but wow!  Get this!

reviewText: In my 2001 Silverado installation was easy,fit perfect and pleats in filter were thicker than plain filter i took out. Airflow was not affected but noticed less dust buildup on dash and less odour with the FRAM FRESH BREEZE!!  You should change your cabin air  filter twice a year for fresh clean air and to protect your heat and air conditioning system! Great for people with allergies to dust and pollen. Will definitely buy again!!

Product was as described, and the instructions are actually pretty decent for this kind of product, which is kind of shocking. remove firewall, remove 1 screw, and pop open filter door. if you have the right tools, this takes less than 5 minutes. fresh air into the cabin and it has the noticeably cleaner smell. the screws to take out on the firewall are 9/32 and i think there were 3 of them. the 1 screw to take out on the cabin filter door was 7/32. make sure you find your tiny sockets! also the only thing you need to pay attention to when inserting this filter is the direction of air flow. there is an arrow on the filter - make sure it points toward the driver side.

Works fine as a filter. After the first week or so I did not really notice the fresh breeze smell any more. I would buy again if the price is good, but would not choose this over any other decent filter.

Saved $2.75 over wal-mart and better yet, I did not have to go in the dumpy store and deal with bitter & unattractive wal-mart associates that think wal-mart "owes" them something... oops, sorry, this is a review about the filter; it fits fine and works fine too. This only issue is removing the giant plastic cover and re-attaching it. GM stopped putting these in the Silverado trucks in 2003 or 04, probably cause no one ever changed them (and to make $1.00 more profit per truck). I suggest buying one now.

Bought a new 2010 Mitsubishi Evolution and straight from the factory whenever I used the hvac mainly with the AC I had a very odd and disgusting odor through the vents. Eventually I got around to replacing the cabin filter, came across this one. It seemed better then all the other filters available which were just paper. This one is treated with both carbon and baking soda. The day of installing it the difference in odors was night and day - i no longer have these weird chemical smells coming from the vents. Considering it's only a couple dollars more then the other filters out there and it's significantly better then OEM - I would strongly recommend this unit. I will purchase more of these and replace on a regular basis now (probably every 1-2 years).
summary: No more disgusting cabin air smell!

reviewText: For 10-20 dollars you can replace your cabin air filter with a carbon activated one!  It took me 15 minutes on my wifes acura mdx and 10 minutes on my nissan altima.  Most of that time is spent figuring out which end to insert first!
summary: Beats the 90 dollars a dealership wants!

reviewText: Perfect fit and replacement for my Lancer's dirty filter.  Just wish it were a tad bit cheaper, but happy nonetheless.

I prep for installation watching you tube videos and decided to give this a shot.  The in cabin filter is behind the glove box.  Once the glove box is removed, the filter is right in line of sight.  Removed 2 pull out pin under the glove box  and with in minutes pop the filter out.  Took less then 10 minutes to install.  The easiest installation done on a car to date.  If you own a Nissan Altima 2006 save yourself some money and do it yourself.
Works great in the car and fit perfect.  I would say it keeps the air fresh and it seems to be a better filter, than the factory filter.

Be careful when choosing your cabin air filters. I had ordered this Fram for my 2009 Nissan Murano and there was no way it was going to work in my application. Box had 3 different instruction sheets for 3 different vehicles. I sent back and reordered the TYC brand. I gave it 4 stars for quality.

Got it to replace the Air Filter on my Mitsubishi Evolution X. After a little research came across people saying this one would have the same same size.Well, it DOES. And is EXACTLY the same as the OEM Mitsubishi uses it but for 1/2 the price! Since FRAM is a very well-known brand for any kind of filters, this is the way to go! I wouldn't be suspect if someday people tell me that this IS the OEM, but without the Mitsubishi logo on it.Cleans well the air and since i'm a user of contact lens, any dust gets my eyes red. After changing, my eyes are much better.
I saved $100 over letting my dealer install this same item. Done in under 30 minutes! Couple of tools needed.
The air in the car smells so fresh with this thing!I waited too long to change out my last cabin filter (50k miles).I was so glad to put this brand spankin new cabin filter in my whip.

Don't even bother to buy the ones sold at the dealerships, you'll pay as much as 3 times the amount and get less protection. Comes with very easy instructions that by pass owners manual instructions to save a lot of time.

Got this for my dad and installed it last weekend. The 2005 Nissan Altima is an easy car to swap the cabin air filter in and out of and this filter fit perfectly in the air box. The Velcro ends were not necessary for my application as the filter itself fit snugly without them. My dad is a smoker so I chose this filter as it may help with the odor but I have not followed up to see if this is the case. None the less this filter is very affordable and built solid, a great product.

I basically purchased this filter simply because the OEM filter is way overpriced.  Not exactly sure if I can tell the difference in air quality when compared to the original paper filter.  But this is a bit heavier and a bit more dense than the OEM filter.  Good or bad? I don't know. Does it restrict airflow? Not that I can tell....My old filter was about 3 year old and it was a bit dirty when I removed it.  Installation was easy, and for this filter, the Arrow is suppose to point down for the G35 coupe. The filter was the perfect size and fit was perfect.Removing the old filter on this car was a pain.  I busted my knuckles removing the lower kidney shaped panel. Everything else popped out w/o issue.Installing everything back was a breeze.  This filter included 2 foam tape.  Not sure what exactly it is for so I didn't use it.After doing more research, I realized I could have purchase another charcoal filter elsewhere for $9 shipped.  Maybe I'll give that one a shot when I need to replace this one.
summary: It's a filter.  Hopefully it does what it's suppose to do

reviewText: I have not used this either but I am sure it will do the job its made for. I love ARB and the quality is there.

The ARB tree strap fills a void in the 10' length. I carrier a 4' tree strap along with this strap which feels a void for bigger trees. Plus this strap will also double as a tow strap when pulling other vehicles off the trail. The Capacity is plenty enough on this strap as well. One of the better tree straps I have used. The bright neon color sticks out as well which makes it that much easier to keep up with on the trails.
This tree saver is badazz to say the least, this thing is a beast. Very high quality easy to use I promise this will not let you down.
summary: This strap will not let you down

reviewText: ARB is known for having some of the best products on the market, this tree saver is no exception.  The quality material and crafmenship makes it almost a shame to get it dirty...  I expect to get a lot of years from this.
This strap is incredibly nicely made, I feel bad getting it all dirty putting it to use...a true quality showpiece!

Typical great ARB quality bright green so it won't get lost, I haven't had to use it yet and hopefully never will have to, but at least I can anchor to a tree and not tear it up if I have to. If it's 1/2 as good as their 30' snatch strap it should last a lifetime
After comparing this to other products in the same or similar capacity, I bought it.  I've now used it three times without any issue whatsoever.  Very well made and I would recommend.
Looks pretty well made.  I needed a very wide tree strap to avoid doing damage to trees when winching.  For the price, this was a good solution.
No headache replacement for the GenII Toyota Prius. This includes model years 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, and 2009. My 2006 was a 20 second job.

I'm a little overboard where filters and oil are concerned. Since I replace my own I save shop service costs and get "intimate" with my cars as well as know the conditions of my served components. I changed the Prius engine air and cabin filters at 14,000+ miles. Neither needed it but with the great Amazon prices and the ease of replacements I couldn't resist. I'll probably change them early again but it's a joy caring for my baby. The engine filter appeared identical to the original and I replaced the cabin with a carbon/baking soda model that was definitely a step up while price was less than OEM. Prius owners note that both filters took less than 10 minutes combined and required no tools!
My dealer wanted way too much money for a buying and installing a replacement air filter for my 2009 Prius. I saved big replacing my own filter which took all of one minute. The filter fit perfectly.

This filter is as good as you would ever require. The advantages of this deal is that anyone can change this air filter without the use of a mechanic or dealership and should.  Why bother with a fuel efficient vehicle if you don't get 100%.  Also sweet is the idea that in addition to saving money from a parts store or dealership you get this thing delivered to your door.  So...easy to replace, very good factory replacement, inexpensive, delivered to your door for free when you combine to spend $25.  It's a no-brainer.

This saves money if you have to replace them very often.  I need to 3 times a year.  It is the same as the original, it just costs less.This one is for a 2005 Prius but I order other ones for our other cars too.

It's hard to believe just how much the dealership charges for installing one of these filters. They're not super-easy to replace but the directions provided with this Fram walk you through the steps. I've used Fram filters for decades and have never encountered a problem.

Before I was able to track these down on Amazon, I was fashioning my own cabin air filters out of 3M home filters. Buying the Fram units is obviously much easier, and they are specifically designed for the environment of a vehicle. It really is amazing how much dirt and other crud flows through this vital A/C airway. The last filter I removed after 10,000 miles was almost black, and had anything from twigs to leaves to bugs stuck in it. It's well worth the $14 or so to know I'm not breathing that stuff in! This filter is also a quick and easy installation. For someone with basic skills, it should take no more than 10 minutes to complete the entire process; about 1/2 that time for those who are mechanically inclined.

Fits Perfectly into my 2006 Scion Xb. Easy installation better that toyota filters. Baking Soda really helps deodorizes the air coming out of the vents. I would buy this again and reccomend this to others.
summary: Fits Perfectly into my 2006 Scion Xb

reviewText: Here's a little hint: EVERY SCION xA & xB can use a cabin filter, and it is a great upgrade to make. It doesn't matter if it came with the option from the factory: every HVAC unit comes with the filter tray. All you have to do is install it.There is only one thing I require for a cabin air filter, and that's the absence of cow dung particulate when traveling along the Central California section of I-5 when it's 110 degrees and hasn't rained in four months.From personal experience, this filter delivers the goods at a great price. It fits the carrier tray perfectly, just make sure you lock the filter's lip into all the tray's plastic snaps. It'll click, so it doesn't require much brain power.
summary: Perfect fit for a 2006 Scion xA

reviewText: Toyota charges anywhere from 50-89 bucks to change the cabin air filters... it takes about 2 minutes time! if its time for you to change yours out, save yourself the coin and go with this set.

I used the OE cabin filter from when i bought my car brand new. It was an excellent filter, no complaints.However when looking for a replacement filter i noticed Fram fresh breeze. I was in love with the concept of baking soda and carbon lining in the filter medium. I couldn't be happier with the result. I get clean smelling air outside, even during traffic hour, and as far as i can tell it traps just as much dirt as the OEM filter media.considerations:The filter is significantly heavier than the OE filter which is to be expected from the carbon and the baking soda, and because of its rigidness, take care not to bend or force the filter inside the slot because there is a risk of breakage. your filter can burst at the seams, letting out its contents if not handled with care.I'm am not sure how long the fresh air effect will last because the capacity of the filter wont allow large amount of carbon and baking sodawith those considerations, I think its the best investment i made changing to fram fresh breeze.Car:2006 scion tcOwnership: about 1 month and still smells good
summary: BEST CABIN FILTER EVER USED PERIOD

reviewText: The filter in my car was getting smelly.  This Fram Fresh Breeze cabin air filter solved the problem very easily.  Will buy for other vehicles.
These filters are great for stopping debris and regular smells, but I don't think they would deal with a skunk !  They are easy to fit and certainly worth changing at least annually.

Wow, this wasn't what I thought I was buying. I was looking for a air filter, after I got my oil change and bought this. So I had to go online andd see where this product goes. And was I happy I bought it. The one I replaced was very dirty and clogged up. This one was very unique. Its brings in good clean air and also makes inside the car feel really airy. And I notice it right away. And good for the Air- Conditioners. And the price was really good.
summary: There is a Difference right away

reviewText: So, I bought this after the tool said this would fit my car. Well, after some further research and trying to install it I found that it doesn't go in my car nor does my model even take a cabin filter.

I have a 2003 Toyota 4Runner SR5 and it's recommended that I change the cabin filter every 15,000 miles or once a year. The dealership charges close to sixty bucks for this little bugger, so I decided to see about doing it myself and found theFRAM CF9846A Fresh Breeze Cabin Air Filteron Amazon. By doing a search on how to install it (video available on YouTube doing search 'Changing cabin auto filter, Toyotal 4Runner 2003') and buying this product from Amazon, I saved money and I believe I purchased a superior product to the stock filter.It is a bit of a bear to get the glove box back into place - at least for me, but generally speaking the replacement of this filter can be done in 15 minutes in most instances.  The tough part for me seems to be reseating the glove box so that it has smooth operation.  The directions in the air filter box are inadequate and the step-by-step ones on YouTube were a God send! Three basic steps to get to the filter: unscrewing screw on right side, unhooking arm and removing the glove box by pinching the sides to expose the filter behind the glove box.  Changing out the filter is simple and you want to have the flattest part of the filter down in the air filter rack when you slide it into position. Reversing the order of things is how you finish up.  I'm not a mechanic, but I am a girl who likes to save money, which is what I do when I change this filter myself.As for the 'fresh scent', I don't notice it too much, but I see that as a perk because when it's time to change the filter I really get some funky scents - especially in the summer with the AC going.  On this particular 4Runner, I sometimes get a sulfur smell in the cabin (a problem with this model year I'm told...) when I stomp on the accelerator, but this filter makes that much less noticeable.Overall, I'm pleased with this purchase and will by more of them in the future.  Local oil change places charge more than forty for the filter alone.  This is a great price, fairly easy to install and it works.
summary: Fresh Breeze Smells Sweet and on the Cheap

reviewText: Tired of being charged WAY to much pretty much everywhere for a 5 min filter change? I got this for my 2008 prius and you can do the install yourself in under 5 min for almost nothing. Never pay $120 again at the dealer.Your CAF is located behind the glovebox. To get to it, you need to open your glovebox and let it sit open all the way. Empty out your glovebox. If you don't, you'll be cleaning up the contents of your glovebox from the floor when you're done replacing your CAF. Next step is to look on the right side and unhook the dampener. Next, squeeze the rear of the glovebox sides inwards to be able to let the glovebox swing all the way down.Looking inside, you'll see a tray with latches on both sides. Press those latches inwards and start sliding the tray out.When you put your new CAF into the tray, make sure you follow the arrow on the filter as the air is meant to flow through in one direction. The air flow is down. If you forget, the tray has an arrow on it also that says "air flow".To finish the job, reverse the proceedures above. Slide the tray in, click into place, rotate the glovebox up and let it snap into place, replace the dampener bar, then close the glovebox.
summary: Great filter, easy self install... better than OEM

Considering these stands cost about four times as much as a lot of others, and considering the five star reviews, I was expecting perfection.  Unfortunately, they have design flaws.First, the packing sucks.  Two stands come packed together in one box with bits of cardboard that are supposed to prevent the two stands and the two separated stand arms from rubbing together.  I'm not sure if they scraped through the cardboard or if it just shifted, but all of my stands have scrapes on them and in one place the metal is rusting where the paint was scraped.  The manual says if you see rust to scrape it off and repaint it.  I shouldn't have to do that when they're new due to bad packing.  Also, the scrapes reveal just how imperceptibly thin the paint actually is.The description says "Formed base adds stability and helps reduce sinkage into pavement".  When I think "formed base" I think formed as one solid piece.  Instead, the base has tiny triangles of metal welded to the _inside_ of each foot.  Then they carefully take a picture of the stand so you can't see what they did till you get it.  That would still be acceptable except they made no effort to level either the feet or the triangles.  On many of the feet, the triangle sits too deep in the foot so it wouldn't even touch the pavement until the foot edge had dug into the pavement.  In other cases, an edge of a crooked triangle will form a divot in the pavement before the rest of the foot or triangle touches ground.  They could have splurged for a tiny bit more metal to make the triangles large enough to rest the edge of each foot on the triangle, then set the whole thing on a flat surface while the triangles were welded.  I've seen other stands with that design.One of the other reviewers mentioned that the arm that locks the stands at a particular height doesn't move very far and so it's hard to tell by looking if the lock is engaged.  I agree this is a problem and I wish the teeth were deeper so it was easier to tell when a locking arm was fully engaged.  However, it's probably not really an issue because the weight of the yellow bar and the shape of the teeth and locking bar will force the locking bar to fully engage.  Even if the locking bar is rusty enough to prevent the weight of the yellow bar from fully locking it, the weight of the car certainly will.  I could possibly imagine a case where the tip of the locking bar is barely touching a tooth of the yellow bar and putting weight on the yellow could cause a failure, but I couldn't get it to sit like that when trying, so it's pretty unlikely.  However, as the jacks get rusty and teeth possibly wear, or if you simply get one with a small manufacturing defect, such a situation could become more likely.  So I'm not a fan of this design where locking can't easily be confirmed visually.  Even if they had made it so the locking arm sits perfectly horizontal while locked and an inch off horizontal when unlocked it would have been better.While doing my tests with the locking bar I created quite a bit of shaved yellow paint particles just from moving the yellow bar up and down by hand.  This is probably typical of the paint used on jack stands and maybe there's no avoiding it, but it certainly doesn't seem that they used any sort of premium paint.  The coating of yellow paint does seem to be thicker than the coating of blue paint, at least.I don't think the description (or the 3-ton label on each stand) makes it very clear that the 3 ton rating is per PAIR, not per stand.  You have to read the manual to find that out.  They also have big warnings in two places in the manual not to put a car on four stands.  Since it's fairly common for people to put cars onto four jack stands, I don't know if that warning is just there to cover their butts in case someone lifts a car wrong onto four stands and it falls over during lifting or if there's something about these particular stands that makes them bad for using four at once.  Perhaps the bases are just too small.  Of course, using four stands in earthquake country is just asking for trouble so that could be another reason.In case anyone was wondering, these stands only lock at a particular position.  Just because the description says "ratchet" doesn't mean you can ratchet them up while the car's weight is on them.  If you manage to move the locking bar with the car's weight on the stand (which actually shouldn't be possible due to the shape of the teeth), the stand will collapse to its lowest level.
summary: Decent but have problems that shouldn't exist with such expensive stands

Not bad but the fabric moves too easy away from the shaft ......

I bought these at a well known camping store.  They work pretty good.  The plastic pins are not fastened in though, so I put a dab of superglue on each side of the pin (at the edge of the fabric) and now the pins are securely in place.I also was not a big fan of the hooks... so I used some small binder clips.  If you squeeze the metal tab on the binder clip you can pop it out of the clip - then feed it through the grommet and put the tab back into the clip.  Now you have a secure clip to hold your lights!This requires you to slide the tabs off the awning before rolling it back up.I downgraded this to 4 stars since they didn't have the plastic pins fixed into place.This is a much better way to hang lights than using clothespins to attach them to the flap of the awning.  We had some storms when we were camping and not a single string of lights came off.  (I had tie-downs on the awning)So buy these, get some binder clips, and get a tube of superglue and you will be all set.
These party light holders do the job but the eyelets will rust and leave a stain on your awning tube. I like the rubber holders better.
Pretty simple...not much to say here. They fit right into the axillary track in the awning, and then you hang party lights etc from there.

Think I might put some glue in the loop that holds the tubing.  Couple times now I've had the tubing come out and remaining in the awning channel with the holder in my hand.  I don't leave them sitting in the channel all the time as we have a sun screen to use in the day, so sliding them in and out creates problems with the tubing falling out - especially when it wasn't the last one to go in.

We put these on the awning on our 5th wheel, you need a ladder and it takes awhile to slide them all in the track. The other downside is you have to take the S hooks out every time you roll it up, if you get caught in a pop up storm good luck! But once they are up they work great.
These are much more durable than the original hooks we bought for our RV.  We used these to hand our flag and used biner's to keep the flags from flying off.  Really versatile holder.

First I want to say, the UPC tag marks this size as "small".If your wanting to store the Battery Tender Plus in this nice looking bag,I strongly suggest on ordering the Battery Tender Carrying Pouch - Large 500Large-0140.That case will hold all that comes with the Battery Tender Plusand additionally will hold the Battery Tender 25 ft extension cable with ease.The Battery Tender Plus and all the cables will fit inside this small size, 6" x 7 1/4" x 2" bag,but only a certain way, with ease and only before the cables are used.After you wrap the cables back-up, it's much harder to get everything in this bag.Lay the Tender to the right rear Conner of the bag,and it's two attached cords in front of the Tender.Lay both styles of battery clips on the left side to the rear, and the pouch can be easily closed.The inter pocket is perfect for the instruction/warranty papers.The package the Battery Tender Plus comes in is a pop-apart ~ re-usable packageand is just as good for storing the Battery Tender in, for a few yrs,and I often use pop-apart packaging on various items for permanent storage.But I know that after 4 to 5 yrs that this plastic disintegrates.Also, this Battery Tender plastic package takes up 2 ~3 times the space that the utility bag does.So this time I opted for an accessory, it's just plain fun !Footnote: After ordering and receiving this small size,I realized the difficulties to pack all the items that come with the Battery Tender Plus in this bag.I had also decided I wanted to order a Battery Tender 25 ft. extension cable.So I decided to also order the large size bag so I could hold all the original stuff, plus the extension.I've since received that order, and the large size is the one to get for ample room.

reviewText: No complaints,  works very well..
This works pretty well, I saw the lube come out the other sides of the cablesBUT it isnt the greatest rubber inside so you get some spray back (its not a complete seal)

Motion Pro Cable LuberThe latest version of this tool has TWO thumb screws.I purchased this tool because it was recommended as a basic tool for maintaining your motorcycle or any other vehicle/device that uses cables. Well, after talking to some experienced riders, they all exclaimed that lubricating the cable (clutch or throttle) is a good idea, but they generally have never done this in over 20-30 years. Looking at the latest motorcycles, the cables don't really allow you to lubricate them using this tool or any tool for that matter. On my Ducati, there are rubber boots that prevent you from injecting lube into the sheath assuming you can use the tool and reach the sheath. On my Ford, the throttle cable sheath isn't thick enough to form a tight seal with the Motion Pro tool. It almost seems like the OEMs don't want you to lubricate the cables. On top of it, modern cars and the latest motorcycles use drive-by-wire which is totally electronic where your throttle input (pedal or twist grip) is connected to a potentiometer that tells the computer your desired throttle angle/input, and it activates a stepper motor that opens/closes the throttle plates accordingly. So if you're interested in maintaining your new bike or car with this tool, you might want to reconsider buying the tool.If you have a vehicle that uses cables and has a sheath that is accessible and large enough to form a seal, this tool is very easy to use and well made. Just slide the cable through the slit, push the tool up against the sheath entrance, clamp down the screws, and insert your lubricant nozzle/tube into the open port. Then use rags to seal the tool and the exit of the cable sheath, and squirt away.Overall: 4/5 stars, the rubber seal could have been designed to accommodate really skinny cable sheaths. Newer bikes and cars don't need/can't use this tool.
summary: Works good if you have the right type of cable, newer bikes/cars - don't bother
