Although it is usually easy to spot a "bald" tire (i.e. one with virtually no tread), you cannot "eyeball" tire tread depth any more than you can "eyeball" the air pressure in your tires. Instead you need the right tool. Although this is one of the more expensive tire tread depth gages on the market, the quality of construction and ease of use justify the price, and definitely merit the five star ratings this product has received. Here is why I like it:1. This tool has a nice heft, is made out of nicely finished metal rather than cheap plastic, and comes with a hard shell foam padded case, which can easily fit into a glove compartment (the dimensions of the closed case in inches are 6 3/8 by 2 7/8 by 1 1/4). The quality construction is evident. This is a very well made tool, and looks better in person than in the picture.2. This is simple to use. Just loosen the lock screw, push the slide so the narrow point on the left is flush with the metal face, turn the unit on, press the zero button (or alternatively just adjust the slide until it reads zero on the digital display), choose whether you want mm, inches in decimals (tenths of an inch) or inches in fractions (64ths of an inch), put the metal face flush on the tire, push the slide from the "ruler" side until the narrow point reaches the bottom of the tread, and see the digital readout. The whole process takes just seconds.I like that you can simultaneously see the reading mechanically on the "ruler" part of the slide, which is marked in mm and 32nds of an inch. The new tires that I buy for my cars typically start at 10/32 of an inch (though this can vary depending on the kind of tire, so you need to check what the tread starts out as on whatever tires you are using). Therefore a reading of 5/32 for me means 50% of my tread is gone, at which point I usually replace the tire.3. Opening the battery compartment and installing the battery are simple. This product comes with the necessary battery (and in fact mine also came with a spare).4. The digital display is easy to read, and the digital reading remains on the screen until you either turn the unit off or "zero it out" to take another reading. Although I wear glasses, I can easily see the display even without them on. The digital display eliminates any guesswork as to the reading, though as noted above, you can also simultaneously look at a mechanical reading just to confirm the digital readout.5. I have my oil changed at a place that indicates the tread depth on each tire, but I bought this unit so that I could check myself between oil changes, and also verify the readings I am given. This tool easily and accurately lets me do that.Bottom line: If you like using quality tools that are easy to use and work effectively, then I recommend this product for checking your tire tread depth. This tool is handy for me to periodically check the wear on my tires, and is also useful for those who like to buy used tires, or are considering buying a used car and want to check the tire tread depth.
summary: Quality tool and easy to use

Every once in awhile you stumble upon a product that you know you'll be buying for as long as they make it - this is one of those products.Permatex Grez-Off is primarily a degreaser for tools and other equipment.  It has a notation on the bottle not to use it on glass or motorcycles - not sure why, but won't be testing it out on them either.  The directions say to spray on and leave it a few seconds before wiping and rinsing off.  'Do not allow to dry' is also on the directions.After a quick check of the bottle I set out to test-drive this product in my home for the Amazon Vine Reviewer Program, and this is what I found:Test #1: In my kitchen.  A greasy ledge that holds nic-nacks, but is rarely wiped down.  Other cleaners I've used have taken a lot of elbow grease to get it clean, and frankly it always seems to have a greasy film no matter what I've used. *Another bio-degradable product we've used (Simple Green) never worked this well and had a much stronger odor.*I sprayed Permatex Grez-Off on the ledge after removing the stuff and didn't even wait 2 seconds before wiping it off with a damp cloth.  AMAZING!  Worked great and I didn't have to really even rub, just wiped it off - rinsed the cloth and wiped it down again.  Done in seconds and done well.  GRADE: A+Test #2: In my bathroom.  The vinyl flooring in my bathroom is cream colored, but you'd never know it due to the sticky hairspray residue that gathers on it and collects dirt.  I've gotten down on my hands and knees to scrub it with Ajax powder and other assorted cleaners, but it's never come out looking like new - until now.The Permatex Grez-Off indicates 'do not put on plastic'.  I wasn't sure if this would qualify, so I sprayed a small test area, wiped it and then rinsed it.  It looked good with little effort, so I did the whole floor the same way. Virtually no scrubbing needed and the floor did come out looking darn near new!  I was thrilled. Again, I'd not left the spray on the surface for all but a second or two before wiping.  No need to let it sit to get things clean - at least not there.  GRADE: A+**NOTE: you will want to make sure you have proper ventilation while using this product.  It DOES have an odor and while not overpowering, some will find it strong.  You may also want to wear rubber gloves while using it as it does dry out your hands when you don't.Test #3: The sticky, greasy BBQ.  Left outside for three seasons uncovered, the gas BBQ needed a cleaning, but the few times I'd tried it too way too much effort and the products didn't clean it well.  I took the Permatex Grez-Off to it and within less than 5 minutes it looked shiny and clean.  Again, amazing stuff that does what it promises it will do. GRADE: A+The bottom line: if you need a good all-purpose degreaser/cleaner - BUY IT!  It's great and you'll use it to clean lots of things inside and outside; on boats, RV's, cars, in the garage and inside your home.
summary: Three home tests with A+ results

reviewText: Tested on several very greasy surfaces in a seasonally-commercial/heavy everyday residential kitchen. As it's a heavy-duty product, I only used it on those heavy-duty occasional jobs.First, tested it on was a wall that gets a lot of Pam overspray because it's behind the heavily-used waffle maker. I wasn't impressed until I tried some regular cleaner for comparison. I used Johnson commercial degreaser at recommended spray-and-wipe strength, then double and triple that. It was like water. The Grez-off needed elbow grease and 2 applications, but it cleaned the wall completely, whereas the regular cleaner even at 3x had no effect. Also did a great job on the exterior of waffle maker that I'd almost given up on.It was aces on the stainless commercial stove backsplash and work shelf, which had been neglected and were very sticky with baked-on grease. They get a regular once-over with standard (in other words, weak, but no-rinse) household cleaner, which has little effect on the baked-on grease caused by an always-hot commercial stove. This is an older model 6-burner Wolf with plenty of use/abuse, and it did a great job (I'm a little perplexed at those with household stoves who say this didn't work--maybe the wiped it so quickly it didn't have time to work? The instructions do recommend letting it soak in...). It does require rinsing (just a wet rag was fine) and I'd recommend drying as well on stainless surfaces, or you will get pronounced streaks and spots. It did a respectable job on the iron burner plates as well.There were a few spots on the commercial sink that I'd never gotten completely clean before (used, came from a hospital), even with steel wool, that this shined right up!Excellent on painted cabinet surfaces--but I'd highly recommend it only for spot cleaning (spray one spot, wipe immediately) or applied to the rag and wiped, as it is very strong and will leave streaks on your paint if you spray it across a vertical surface and wipe it all at once, as you would cleaning a window. It removed both kitchen grease and some old adhesive I'd previously failed to remove with cleaner and a razor. Again, rinse. It's not everyday cleaner, and should be rinsed full-strength.I'm not taking off a star for the heavy smell, since it's advertised more as a garage-y degreaser, and does have smell appropriate to heavy mechanical use (all super-concentrated degreasers are stinky; that's why you use the nice Mrs. Meyer's stuff for everyday), but I did take off one because it runs rapidly, making it less effective for vertical surfaces, where it drips off before it can really soak in and do its thing.The sprayer is excellent and strong, but must be turned completely to the desired setting or it's weak and resistant. I thought it was a problem with the sprayer before I realized I was between settings.Overall, great product that makes light work of those dreaded once-a-year kitchen jobs.
summary: Solid heavy-duty degreaser, a little runny for vertical surfaces

reviewText: I waited to write a review on this product, because I wanted to try it on several different things besides greasy tools. So let me start by saying it works great on my son's greasy tools (he works on cars), it has taken off grease stains on my driveway, I used it on our gas grill and it worked great. I also used it on my stove top to get off cooked on grease stains, and to my surprise it worked great without damaging the stove top. The fact that it is biodegradable puts my mind at ease. I really love this stuff, and plan on purchasing more when I run out.

After working on my cars, I have a compound I use to get the grease off my hands that works really well.  This product is as effective on degreasing parts that have been machined and have cutting oil on them, or used parts that are already encrusted in grease and need a good cleanup.For cleaning parts, this solution works exceptionally well withSCOTT- Shop Towels, 12 rollsa good shop towell like these.  Shop towells usually are much heavier than kitchen paper towells and help to wipe away grime from grease fittings, etc.Overall this is a good product to have on hand if you do not have an installed forced solvent parts cleaning system and only need occasional degreasing.  It does the job well!
summary: If you use hand degreasers, you'll love this

reviewText: !UPDATE! 8/22/2011After doing some yard work I wanted to give all of the equipment a good cleaning, this included the lawnmower, string trimmer, and a few other tools. After spending several minutes scrubbing on the string trimmer and getting nowhere with the caked on pulverized grass that NOTHING seems to be able to touch, I saw the Grez-Off bottle sitting there... so I gave it a shot. Sprayed it on, waited three minutes, hosed it off and wallah! It was clean! I've never found a single product that worked this well at removing the caked on grass/stains. Just for this use it is well worth the price!Time for me to bump this up from four stars to five stars!!UPDATE!When it comes to degreasers there are WAY too many choices. Some extremely chemically, others on the "green" side of things. Some work well, others not. Permatex's Grez-Off I am glad to report is both!On a scale of 1-10, here is how I would rank Grez-Off.Old grease 2 months and older: 4I have several old grease stains/areas in the garage and on the driveway. I applied it full strength and let it sit several minutes to do it's magic. The really old stains, it barely touched. The stains that were fairly new, around 2 months old, it removed it fairly easily. With the aid of a pressure washer the older stains came up even more so vs. just the pressure washer.New grease: 9For spot treating and cleaning tools it worked AWESOMELY! Very little work involved and left the tools and spots really clean.The smell is not unpleasant or harsh, just kind of run of the miss degreaser smelling.The pump bottle works well. I don't know how many times I've had pump bottles break or stop working before I've even used 1/3 of the bottle.Grez-Off has made such an impression I've added it to my arsenal of cleaning products. Well priced, fairly "green", and works! I'm happy.

I use this degreaser in the shop for small oil drip and spills. The spray works fast and allows clean up with paper towels. The lack of hazardous chemicals and odors makes it safe to use in the house as well. Good value for the money.

I tried this on two things.Webber Kettle Charcoal Grill - It worked pretty well on the cooking grate to take off a few layers of grime.  It was not perfect and not shiny, but it did look better.  I rinsed really well since I could not find anything online or on the bottle to indicate it is safe to use this on items that will come into contact with food.  It didn't seem to flare up or anything when I used the grill afterwards.Road Bike Rear Sprocket and Chain - I have a high end road bike and needed to change out the sprocket on my rear wheel and change the chain.  I figured I would try this on the old parts.  Nothing to lose.  It was a total fail.  This had little or no effect on the accumulated lube and grease.
summary: Worked great on the grill, but not on my bike sprockets or chain
Looking for a driveway degreaser?  Take a look.

reviewText: I'm in love with Grez Off!  Like another reviewer  here,  I use it for many tasks!  It does more than dissolve grease!I especially love it for removing grease spots from laundry.  We love to cook and I am forever in battle with stubborn grease spots on shirts.  It does not discolor clothes.My makeup bag seems to always turn into a mess with hard to remove eyeliner pencil gunk getting all over my tubes and bottles of makeup.  I use a dry terry cloth and spray a little Grez Off on each container such as mascara,  mineral makeup,..etc.  then wipe.  The Grez Off takes it right off and cleans the inside of the bag when nothing else will!  If you are a lady and use makeup,  you know how troublesome it can be to clean your makeup bag and wipe your makeup containers clean.  (unless you are a super neat nick and they never get grimy)I use it to clean out my bathtub also.  It's strong and I wear a face mask...but boy does it do the trick,  and does it fast!  Much easier than using scouring powder or spray bathroom cleaners such as Dow.  This product seems to just melt the scum off and leaves the tub really shiny with little effort from me.  So really it's more than just a degreaser!I haven't made it out to the garage yet to try it on oil spots,  but watching the video that a gentleman posted in his review,  it's plain to see that he did not leave the product on the concrete nearly long enough to reach the soaked in oil.When I get around to using it on concrete oil spots,  I will spray the spot,  cover it with plastic so it doesn't dry,  and let it sit overnight or so before I attempt to scrub and rinse.  I have faith that it will do just as great a job on those tuff garage floor spots if given time!  It cuts through grease like lightening but concrete grease soaks way down,  so my guess is it just needs more time and maybe that's why some people aren't seeing the results that they could have.The price of this product is also very economical compared to other products,  especially when purchased in the 12 pack that Amazon offers.

I tried out Grez-Off (yuck, what a name!) on several years of baked-on grease my gas grill had accumulated.  Grez-Off did a quite decent job of softening the grease and a lot was removed by letting it soak and then rinsing, but some parts needed many repetitions of spray, scrub and rinse.  Still, it did get the job done and I have not used any product that works better.I appreciate that Grez-Off isn't so caustic that one needs to wear rubber gloves and that it is water-based.

This degreaser is clearly the best choice when one considers that it is biodegradable and safe to use around the home.There might be more effective degreasers out there, but they are toxic in the extreme.This stuff is safe to work with and safe to dispose of.  For its intended purpose it works just great.Buy this stuff to use around your home and garage so you will never have to worry about what you just put your hand in again.

I have had the same old tread-depth gauge for 25 years. Purely mechanical, probably cost $2 back then and small enough to clip to your shirt pocket. But when I saw this on Amazon, I put it in my wish list and waited and waited before putting it in the cart. It was priced right but the shipping would push it above the "what the heck" level into the "will I really use it" category. In a moment of weakness one day, I decided to take the plunge. Click, click, click and pretty soon it was in my mail box.I have tested it on my aging BMW and low and behold, I am in trouble! It is time to "re-tire..." Forget about the shipping charges, now I know I have tires that are right at the limit of safety. For my money, this gadget has already paid for itself!It's easy to use. It's accurate and precise (i.e., the readings are reproducible) and it's seems made well enough to last a few years. I especially liked the spare battery that came with the kit.I own a lot of cars so having a tool like this really helps.
summary: Another cool gadget for car guy or gal with a tool Jones...

reviewText: Bought from Amazon back in April 2012, didn't try to use it until just recently. My Yokahama GeoLander tires when brand new had 13/32 of tread. Using this Fowler digital gauge, it told me I had 23/32 of tread???  How is that possible, these tires are magically growing more rubber!!  I checked on multiple spots on the tires and was always around 23/32, so at least that part is consistent. I went to the Fowler home page and emailed them last week, have yet to get a response.I ended up purchasing from amazon the Milton S448 Tire Tread Depth Gauge---Works like a charm and much much cheaper!!!  Not sure why the Fowler gives me the whacked out reading (took out battery and replaced it)but I guess there are always defective ones--especially when dealing with anything electronic---Another reason to go with the Milton tread gauge--very basic, yet it works.
This thing is very easy to use, sturdy and they give you an extra battery, excellent product for the price.

Hi, I got this after reading that it had great reviews, I was not disappointed. Usually I like to check my car's tire pressure usingAccutire MS-4350B Setpoint Tire Gaugewhen I fill the gas tank, so I thought I needed a device to check the tire's tread depth every once in a while just to be safe and to know exactly when to rotate the tires or replace them. I like this digital gauge, it's made of plastic, it comes with a soft protective sleeve and it includes a spare battery! what else can you ask for? Highly recommended.
Nice tool.  Seems accurate. Came with a nice case and extra battery.  I like being able to get fairly precise measurements to keep track of the tire wear.

I have a car that is not used regularly and am always concerned about the battery not having a charge when its needed. I've been using a float charger on it (a Battery Tender) which has been working out great. However, the charger doesn't give me any feedback as to the overall health of the battery.This device solves that problem. It is very easy to use even if you're not experienced using test gear. It gives you a clear status on the battery health ranging from "green" (good battery that can hold a charge) to "red" (battery can't hold a charge and should be replaced). You can also go further and run tests on voltage, charge system and starting system conditions.The only faults I found with the device is that the screen is very hard to read in the sun (best used indoors in a garage) and the manual is not very helpful for learning how (and why) to use the tester. That aside, it's a very handy device to have to assess 12v battery health without having to take it to a parts store for diagnostics.
summary: Handy tool for monitoring battery health

reviewText: I wanted to get this because I seem to be the only "car guy" in the household and amongst extended family (some 20+ people all in Dallas).I do all of my own car work, and could easily do simple battery voltage checks with a multimeter, but a device like this is important, because it measures amps correctly (and simply), something you don't want to do with most multimeters without calculating the proper size resistor to use inline or risk frying your multimeter.  Basically, this is a device designed to measure automotive voltage, plus check cold cranking amps, cranking amps, and load testing.The 3 stars is mainly for the usability.  First, the display (the most important thing!) is hard to read because it uses large LED bars to write out the words.  Let me explain - the first test is the battery test.  When you select the battery test, it reads "baFF" rather than "batt" only because the manufacturer chose to use a very simplistic display that doesn't have enough "bars" to create easy to read words.  It's like trying to make words with a calculator if that makes any sense.  (I will try to upload a picture later)Next, of all devices that truly need a carrying case, this one does, if only to hold the instruction manual.  It is not intuitive to use without the manual (primarily because the words are very hard to decipher or read).  There's a "glossary" on the back, but it doesn't include everything, nor the steps for each of the tests, if it DID, I would've added 1 more star.Then, on top of that, the manual somewhat confuses you a little in determining what type of battery you have.  For example, for battery types you must choose from the following:SLI - Starting/Lighting/Ignition Flooded batteryFLAT - Traditionally shaped AGM batteriesSPL - AGM-designated spiral wound batteriesGEL - Gel cell batteriesNow of the 4, what type of battery do you have???  I checked 3 cars and none have any of this written on the battery themselves.  I can only assume SLI makes the most sense.  Ideally, this would be explained a little better or use "Conventional, Marine/Deep-Cycle, Maintenance Free" wording instead.Overall, I feel 3 stars is fair for the usability - the item still works and seems to validate known good and known bad batteries and charging systems, but don't lose the instruction manual and good luck being able to read the too-simplistic screen.
summary: Display is hard to read, don't lose the manual!

reviewText: So the little LCD panel on this thing displays certain..."things" that make no sense to a normal human being.  Sure, you could click through them and select whatever it is they mean, but you'd really have no idea what you were testing.  So as far as the user interface and user experience goes, this thing is below the bar...as far as computing, but automotive items still have a ways to catch up.Luckily, the manual says what to press, which string of letters you'll see, what they mean, and what to do.  Without the manual, this thing is kind of useless.  As long as you keep the manual handy, however, you have yourself a pretty nice electric system tester.  Testing a variety of batteries - and charging systems (you know, the same kind of thing that automotive and repair shops have...connect to the battery, start the car, turn on all the power equipment...and they tell you that you need a new battery and/or alternator.)  Well, now you can do that on your own time and not have to trust somebody that's trying to sell you a battery and alternator!Overall, this thing was fairly easy to use with the manual by my side.  While I can't guarantee its accuracy, both cars I tested and a tractor battery all tested to be in good shape, which I believe since I've never had a problem with any of them.  The LCD readout is easy to read even in sunlight...though it is kind of an odd color.  If you mix orange and hot pink...that's the color.Good little tool to have...would recommend.  Just be very sure not to toss the instructions.

Oh, and the display can't be read in bright sunlight. That's the first thing I noticed when trying to use it, actually. I didn't know it was even on and working until I cupped my hands around the display to see that, indeed, my battery's voltage was in fact displayed. Very dimly. A better screen type would have been a great idea (in a garage, this likely wouldn't be an issue).This unit does two types of tests: one, with the car off, which tests the battery's voltage and (somehow) its cranking capacity. My van's 685CCA battery came in at 677, and got the green LED. All good there. It seems well built, and the clamps (permanently attached) are decent. Make sure you get a good connection to the battery posts, or the CCA reading will be inaccurately low (I had to adjust a few times to get it right).For part two, the charging system test, you kind of need a second person to do properly. One standing at the battery to watch the readout and control the test, and a 2nd person in the driver's seat to start the car, then keep it revved to 1200-1500 RPMs, and then turn on the vehicle's loads (hi-beam headlights + full-power fan + rear defroster recommended) for the load test. At each step, you press a button or two on the device to move it forward, and it doesn't store the voltage, so running back and forth from device to vehicle controls isn't ideal.The tester works well once you figure out how to navigate the device's menu and learn what the odd 4-letter contractions mean for various parts tests this thing can run (there's a cheat sheet on the back of the device). There had to be a more straightforward way to run through the steps though.Anyway, it's a handy device, and tells me more about the battery than just my multimeter did... but not that much more (just the current CCA cranking capability of the battery). If that extra bit of info is worth the cost of the device to you, then by all means get this tester. If you're okay just knowing voltage, and already have a multimeter, it tells you almost as much info as this device does, is far more "all purpose", and you can get one that will work fine for under ten bucks (harbor freight, etc).
summary: Small, portable, useful, and completely non-intuitive.

reviewText: I like this battery tester a lot so far.  I am not inclined to understand complex displays, I want something to tell me if my car battery is good, bad or so-so.  I connected the clamps to the battery terminals as directed in the instructions and 12.55 lit up on the LED screen and a green light came on saying my battery was good.  I don't really know what "type" of battery I have in my car.  I looked at it as best I could but I guess it didn't matter since the tester told me immediately the voltage it contained.  I was curious about it's voltage because I think my battery is around 3 years old and I wondered if it was still holding a full charge or not.This tester is very easy to operate, is extremely light weight, small and could easily fit into a car's glove compartment.  My car battery is the only battery I've tested so far.  I will take it over to my mom's house this weekend and test her car battery and any other batteries that fall within it's testing parameters. And it's great that this tester doesn't need any batteries of it's own to work.  It uses the charge off the battery it's testing to power itself.  Pretty cool!
summary: SOLAR BA7 100-1200 CCA Electronic Battery and System Tester

reviewText: Having gone away from home for long periods of time in the past, I've come home to dead batteries quite a few times.  I couldn't be more disgusted than having to drag a battery into Walmart or to some dumb kid in an autoparts store to try and receive my prorated warranty.  I am now fully confident in my ability to be sure if the problem is the battery or the charging system, but in my past, my absolute worst fear was that I went through the above process for nothing, that there was nothing wrong with the battery after all.And so for the average homeowner that maintains his own car, I think this is an excellent, simple and effective device.  Of course there are more sophisticated battery testing systems out there that put a heavy load on your battery and analyze each individual cell (this is what they're doing when they test your battery before giving you that prorated warranty), but this will tell you with high certainty what is wrong with your battery or charging system in under five minutes.  To me, a great device to have around.One thing that bothers me:  the name.  As this product is manufactured by a company called Clore Automotive, how did this thing get the name "Solar"?  I could be too cynical, but I swear they are trying to get the ignorant consumer to believe that this is some fancy solar powered device.  In fact, it gets its energy from the battery it is testing.  That part seems really cheesy and stupid, and if I was 100% sure of my suspicions, I'd probably drop my rating further.  But hey, it's a simple device, and I like what it does.Oh, by the way, it is smaller and better looking than I expected from the pics on Amazon.
summary: Nothing to do with the sun.

reviewText: If you don't want to drive out to the nearest auto center to have your battery and/or system tested for free then this is for you.  Or if you work with a lot of cars, then this is for you.  I frequent deal with 3-4 cars and this is easy for me to quickly check on the battery and system of each.  The price you pay for this is convenience.  The auto centers do basically the same for free but you have to drive there, and wait for help if they are busy or if they are closed or weather is bad, well, you get the picture.  Not a must have in my opinion but a good convenient product for the automotive do it yourself person.Please click YES if my review have been helpful to you, it will encourage me to continue writing and updating my reviews, and leave a comment if you have any questions, I will be more than happy to answer if I can be of help.

This was a very easy to use and understand battery tester and it worked very well I've paid more money and gotten a lesser tester in the past . I have two batteries in my truck one it said was totally cell dead and the 2nd one was about dead so I changed them both out .But its far better then the old resistor type battery testers .. Worked like a charm a deal at twice the price . I'd recommend this product to anyone , As for ease of use then I'd say if you can put gas in the tank then you will have no problems using this tool.

The SOLAR BA7 is an excellent addition to a solar energy system maintenance kit. The storm season just started and after having to endure a few bad storms last year, and the aftermath of many days without electricity; this year I'm ready. The first thing I did was to be sure the AGM batteries in my solar energy system are in good shape and for that I used the SOLAR BA7 to test them.The included user's manual indicates how to perform the test depending of the type of battery one is testing, and the SOLAR BA7 support testing for many types of battery and ratings. A good investment without a doubt, because one never knows when the unexpected necessity to test a battery might come.
summary: Great for testing AGM 12 Volt batteries in solar energy systems

reviewText: While this battery tester is quite toy like in appearance, it actually performs equally to ones that are 3 times more expensive. Sure, the LED display can be a bit difficult to read in direct sunlight, but you can cup your hand over it and it's not a big problem.This tester not only gives you the voltage and cold cranking amps (CCA) of your battery, but it can also test your starter and charging system as well These are features often only seen in the more expensive battery testers.So for this price, I really like this tool.
summary: Great battery tester for the price

reviewText: As the builder of a chopper motorcycles (with hefty 113ci S&S; and air rides with built in air compressors) I need to know exactly how much draw is done during a bike's start up. Especially since the compression tappets are vacuum controlled, the ride's suspension is computer aided and there's extensive LED lighting on the vehicle which kicks in on a button press.Using the the Solar BA7 I was able to diagnose exactly what goes on during the bike's fire up and adjust (and lessen!) the start up procedure accordingly. I made changes to the boot up of the bike including the 120+ LED lights based on the huge draw required to start it.Without the BA7 my only indicator of too much draw was a dimming headlight!If you're into any sort of vehicle construction or anything that uses 12V batteries you'll need accurate and informative feedback on what's going on with the battery status.The Solar BA7 seems to report consistently and it works. Worth every penny.

reviewerName: Alf "Let the cat out of the bag!"
reviewText: Given the tight space, it is hard to take off the filter housing without this tool.  Still, I hope someone will invent a better tool because it stuck to the housing when I took the housing off and when I put the housing back on.  I'll drill a couple of holes as suggested by some of the reviewers.  Still, I'll avoid buying Toyota next time becaue it is such a chore to change oil.

After reading that it's a very good idea to use a special tool to avoid serious damage to mounting parts I bought it and it's an great addition to my tool box. A must for do it yourselfers. Tool is well made too.
This tool worked great removing and re installing the oil filter canister on my 2011 Toyota Sienna. It can't get better than this

Needed for the 2010 Toyota Sienna.  I tried some others and they don't allow you to take off the canister.  This is necessary if you want to change your own oil.

Must have if you own one a Toyota that uses 64mm oil filters.This is the tool that will fit, many other socket wrenches on the market is either 64.5mm or 65mm, some may workBut more often then not, they slips and cant loosen nor tighten the filters enough.Cat in one piece aluminum, not assembled by spot welding pressed sheet metal. So it will do the job and wont break apart.Definite professional grade.

reviewText: Had to have this product to do the oil changes on my wife's 2009 Toyota Camry 3.5L V-6. Great quality!
Bought this for work... do a lot of Toyota, scion, lexus oil filters... works good. nice tight fit and hasent stripped anything yet...

Makes changing the filter element a breeze.  Made in the US.  If you have your oil changed by an independent shop, take this along for the shop to use.  Toyota and Lexus dealers have this tool or one very similar.
I ordered this to remove the filter housing on my 2011 Prius.  It is a solid and quality socket. You will not regret buying this Oil Filter Socket. I am very satisfied with it.

reviewText: This filter socket works.  It is much better than a 65mm generic oil filter socket.  However, I still had to break it free from the plastic with a pry tool.  If it fit a little better it would not bind like that.  I'm thinking a better tool must exist, but I have not yet found it.

reviewText: Oil changes should be simple, but Toyota and it's dealerships conspire to force you to take the car to the dealer for this simple maintenance.I tried to use one of the many oil filters I already owned to loosen the oil filter canister. reviewText: My Mechanic recommended I buy this tool to change my oil filter on my 2010 Toyota corolla, I bought other tools prior to this tool and all the other brand socket wrenches snapped.I recommend everyone get this tool. It makes it very easy to change your oil.  5 Stars
summary: this Tool is perfect for my 2012 Toyota Corolla

reviewText: Changed the oil on my own for the first time today.  Last person who changed my oil didn't have this wrench and couldn't remove it no matter how hard he turned it.  This is a must have if you're doing it yourself.  So simple to remove!  Nice snug fit but not tight, which is what you want.  After using it, you probably won't be able to remove by hand.  Wiggle it gently back and forth and it will come loose just fine.

I recently bought my 2010 Corolla 1.8 from a family member who was going out of country to work for 2 years and no longer needed the car.  They bought it brand new in Feb 2010 and it has had all of its oil changes from Toyota dealerships since new.It was time for an oil change last monnth, and I put the car on the small midrise sissor lift I have in my home shop. I attached the Assenmacher tool to a 1/2 drive ratchet with the correct socket and attempted to remove the filter housing.  It would not budge.  I decided to wait a while to let the housing area cool off since the housing is made of plastic and threads into metal, resulting in a mismatch of thermal expansion characterics (bad design IMHO).  I tried again after 3 hours, it still would not loosen.  I then got a 2.5 foot breaker bar and tried again; it would not loosen.About this time, I got a litte worried and decided to check the net for problems with removing this filter housing. I read one report where the housing was so tight, they had to cut the housing off and buy a new one. I finally decided to use my 1/2" air impact and attempt to remove it. I was initally concerned that the impact would break the stub end off the Assenmacher tool, but I had nothing to loose by trying.  I began using the impact and after 5 seconds of use, I noticed the plastic housing finally starting to loosen. A couple more seconds and it came off.I inspected the threaded area of the housing closely to see if it has somehow been cross threaded during installation at the toyota dealership; no problems found. I guess some oil lube flunky at the dealership has installed it with an air impact gun. I completed the oil drain and reinstalled the filter and new O ring and torqued to required specification of 18 foot lbs.Praise the Assenmacher tool, it withstood the hammering of my air impact and allowed me to remove this greatly overtightend filter housing on my 2010 Corolla 1.8.THIS TOOL IS WORTH ITS WEIGHT IN GOLD.  BUY NO OTHER.One final comment: Just because someone takes their car to dealerships does not need a job as simple as an oil change will be done correctly.  Do your own work and ensure it is done properly is you have the necessary tools and skills.
summary: This tool saved the day on overtightened filter housing: 2010 Corolla

reviewText: It's a bit different from the one pictured (smaller) but worked great. I can tell the previous owner did not have the proper tool because the filter cap on my truck was all busted up. Nonetheless this tool slipped right on and had no trouble biting on to pull the cap off. (Damn that thing was tight too!) It makes the messy and painful job of replacing the filter on a new tundra less messy and painful.

This product fit perfectly on the oil filter cover on my 2011 Lexus RCX350  . This one works great, and makes changing oil a breeze.  Make sure you use synthetic 0W20, get an OEM filter element, proper plastic drain plug, and your ready to change your oil in less than 20 minutes.  On a Lexus, you will save at least $150 (after buying the oil and needed parts/tools).

First I must say I hate purchasing tools that only do one thing...(uni-tasker).  I purchased this socket tool, becouse I had to.  Not becase I wanted to, but quickly found out I need another socket to turn it... and here's the kicker.  The socket is bigger then standard set 19mm or 3/4!  So you have go out and purchase a 15/16 or 24mm socket, which is a huge socket.  I will never use this socket unless I own a diesel truck.  Add that to the cost of the wrench. So about 8 dollars for the socket and the price of tool, just to get started.  The oil filter wasn't on too tight, so the cheaper plastic tool worked out just fine for me.  The 24mm socket stays on the aluminum tool and should ship like that.  Waste of time and money for a tool that only does one task....
summary: Need another tool to use this tool...LAME!

reviewText: We all have to deal with the seemingly non-sensical selection of bolts and nuts on our vehicles but usually changing an oil filter is straightforward and easy.Enter the Toyota Engineering Department.The engineers located the cap in a great spot but its a PITA to get off without the right tool.This is the answer.  Works great on my 2011 Tundra 5.7.

If your working on Toyota's with cartridge style oil filters this socket is a must.  Due to the odd size of the Toyota filter container nothing else seems to fit correctly, I even tried on that was a mm larger but that still didn't hold well.  Do yourself a favor if you do your own oil changes, you won't regret having this.The socket seems pretty durable, I've used it now about 10 times and I haven't noticed any wear on it and it still holds snug.I'm using this on a Toyota Highlander 08 V6.
summary: A must for Toyota's with cartidge style oil filters

reviewText: bought this to do the oil changes on my es350 myself. works great. i wish i had one of these for my other cars instead of the generic ones from wally.
great quality tool, must have for changing out oil filter. grips on firm and easy to use. no problems so far

Every person that changes their own oil needs one of these. It is a perfect fit.Simply attach a 15/16 socket to your torque wrench, attach this filter to the socket, and the rest is just as easy as can be. Perfect
summary: Perfect for the 2007+ 5.7L Tundra or 2009 Lexus RX350

reviewText: I have a Tundra with the 5.7L and the dealer took care of oil changes for the first two years, This is the first time EVER I let a dealer touch any of my cars unless it was a serious recall--- needless to say they didn't do a bad job and never had to go back to have them fix something they did wrong.So now I am out of free oil changes and am back to my typical routine of doing my own. The first time I did not have this tool... what a pain as my housing sits several inches above the sway bar and in the middle of everything. After finishing it the first time, I ordered this the next day. Now came my next oil change.... it made it a snap. With my truck I was easily able to take off the cap and in my case it was slightly stuck to it--- so I just left it on and once I tightened it back up--- it popped free without any trouble. I did notice some people mentioning that it does not have the cutout for a ratchet/ extension--- from an engineering standpoint, it should not. The reason is torque. In this case you have a cast piece of aluminum and if you used an extension you are exerting all of that force on a small area. When you use a socket--- it applies the force over a greater surface area and it also makes it much easier to get off. In my case, it was tight and with a standard length 1/2" ratchet it came off with a little bit of muscle.I would definitely recommend this tool as it works well and does exactly what it should.
summary: This is the first time EVER I let a dealer touch any of my cars unless it was a serious recall--- needless to say they didn't do

reviewText: fantastic tool fits true to its size hex on top is 24mm you need a socket to make life easy its heavy and well made
summary: Assenmacher Specialty Tools TOY 640 Oil Filter Socket Wrench for..

reviewText: The pin can be moved to either of two positions, giving it a pretty wide range of motion.  Using this to remove some pretty tight ball joints that a pickle fork and some serious persuasion with a sledge hammer would not budge, this did get the job done.  However, there's a steel ball in a recess on the end of the bolt to allow the bolt to turn while you crank it down.  I put a pretty good flat spot on that ball the first time I used it.  It still works, but not quite as smoothly as when new.  There was an incredible amount of force being applied to flatten about 1/4 of a ~quarter inch steel ball, and the tool didn't break, so I guess this is alright.  Either way, this worked on my '95 BMW 740i lower control arms, where a pickle fork couldn't get a good bite and where there was no room to directly hammer on the ball joint, so I'm happy with it.  I've used it on all of my subsequent jobs, and it hasn't broken yet.Probably the main thing I'd like to see improved upon would be the use of a flanged bolt head so a wrench (like a Gear Wrench) could be easily used without slipping up the head onto the threaded area.  But a socket on a ratchet handle (preferably a large ratchet) can be used just fine.

Very tough tool.Used on a hard to get at ball joint (2000 Eldo}that cannot be accessed from the top(thread end} using a standard puller.Cannot use a fork without destroying the boot.This tool slipped in easily and broke the ball joint loose without any struggle or flexing, very solid.It also worked well for removing a tie rod end.

Solidly built. Doesn't destroy the grease cup.  Adjusts to two heights.  Presses out the pin without damaging the threads (as long as the nut is only backed off so the top of the nut is the same level as the top of the threads) and is built to last. Works on the ball joints and tie rod ends. Mechanic quoted me $350 to replace tie rod ends and tie rod inners on 03 diamante.  That is a very good price for parts and labor.  Through Amazon I bought this tool and the $20 smooth inner tie rod remover (looks like a muffler clamp with a 3/8 inch square insert)  Two moog tie rods for $30 each and two ends for $20 each . (parts could have been cheaper but I like Moog)  With this tool and the inner tool the job took only 1 hour for both.  So I saved $200 and still have the tools.  Not bad.  What more can you ask for.  Next project is replacing the 9 ball joints on my 65 FJ40.

The correct tool for the job always makes things easier but sometimes the correct tool costs more than having a shop do the job and the affordable version makes things worse.I was skeptical that this $50 tool would be a time saver instead of an additional headache but I was surprised.It is well made and does exactly what it is supposed to do. What more can you ask for?I used this on an '87 BMW 325is and it fit well, popped the ball joints out and did not damage the rubber boots.Maybe I'm nit picking but the only reason I did not give it 5 stars is because what should be a hardened ball tip at the end of the bolt smashed flat after popping just two control arm joints.

I got this ball joint for doing the control arms on a 2005 Mercedes-Benz CLK500.  This did the job beautifully.  Remember to grease the bolt on this to make it last a good, long time.  It doesn't take a whole lot of force to push out a ball joint, but man does this thing get the job done.  With my trusty ratchet and 24 mm socket, I made a previously impossible job a smooth walk in the park.  I don't have any idea how I survived without this tool before.  One thing to keep in mind is that when using this, when the ball joint comes free, it does so quite loudly and violently.  I haven't had any problems with it, but though it sounds like you destroyed something expensive when you use this, everything is probably fine.

So this tool didn't work for me...I was removing my upper and lower control arms (ball joints) and I couldn't get this tool to work for me, I tried for hours to get this to work. It was as if it didn't open enough, just about a 1/4" more and I wouldn't have had any problem. Alas I had to cut my ball joint bolts by 1/4" before I could use the tool. FRUSTRATING

Highly recommended for anyone who does a lot of automotive steering/suspension work.  You will need something like this depending on what access you have to install a balljoint remover.I hate to use the pickle fork.  The pickle fork is the last resort for me, as it will damage the balljoint boot.I prefer to use the Snap On balljoint remover.  If that one cannot fit, then I will try this tool.  If this tool will not fit, then I will resort to a pickle fork.

Maybe you are old enough to remember the old forks you pounded into your suspension to remove ball joints.  This little gizmo saves the seal, and pops the joint out in just a few turns.  Leave the nut on so it doesn't go flying.  There is a bearing on the end of the screw on my version, so the end of the screw is not 'swirling' metal on metal.
summary: Subaru ball joints take about 2 minutes

reviewText: Special tool for a special task.  I tried to borrow one from others and no oone had one this size. This item was perfect for the job, priced right and shipped in record time.  I am pleased with the quality of the tool, and it will last a lifetime.

Mityvac makes this bleeder for every big manufacturer. MAC matco snapon etc. If it looks like this, mityvac is the designer. Strongest vacuum and the most reliable. Almost no maintenance required and ive never seen one fail. Comes with extra bleeder tips which is great.
summary: Gold Standard for anything that requires a vacuum

reviewText: No more up and down, up and down. No more wife leaving for the rest of the day because I wasn't sensitive enough, or I was yelling and commanding her.  I bled my clutch and brakes with this device and it worked very well when my compressor was on maximum pressure (6HP, 33 gallon, 220 V). With the compressor set on less than maximum, it hardly works. The 4 little bleed screw attachments are a joke.  They are too big and barely hold on the bleed screw.  I replaced it with a short piece of vacuum hose, so it stayed on the bleed screw and that worked perfect. The instructions indicate you will get bubbles because of the loose fit of the bleed screw attachments. When the fluid comes out while bleeding, it does not fill the clear tube like manual bleeding. It looks like foam is coming out. I just trusted it and the brakes bled hard in the end.I was impressed with the quality of the tool and would recommend it to anyone who bleeds brakes and can afford it.  Worked like a charm, but you will need a good compressor.

After installing a new rear end in my friend's Impala I attached this to the bleeder valve and it worked like a charm. After bleeding the brakes I put the hose in a bucket of water to flush the fluid from the hose line.Bleeding the brakes can be annoying but using this makes you want to bleed the brakes on all of your cars because it's so easy to do. I didn't use the auto refill attachment, instead I had my friend watch and refill the master cylinder reservoir. Worth every penny.

i purchased the mity vac 6835 a few months ago and have used it a couple of times it has certainly proved that it is up to the task.  I had my bleeder hooked up to an 80 gallon 5hp compressor.  this bleeder certainly made bleeding brakes quick and relatively painless. They're several attachments to fit various bleeder screws so that was really helpful.This product met my expectations and does a good job.  If i have a complaint, there's small valve like plug (spring loaded) on the cover of the reservoir.  when i was bleeding my brakes i noticed the seal of this valve plug coming off and i could feel air coming from it...logically speaking this should not be the case as it will certainly affect suction pressure.  There was also fluid leaking from the handle (near the throttle) after extended use (5-6 drops) so there may be a build quality issue there.  All-in-all, every time i used i was able to finish the job.anyways, it's good for the odd one-man brake bleeding, however it certainly is not what i consider to be a heavy duty unit...
This kit works as described. Plenty of Utube videos to show you how. Be aware that some lines are stubborn and you will still need to have someone in the car pumping the breaks.
great do it yourself brake flush or brake bleeder. no mess, clean job. 2 more cars to go.I will certainly recommend to friends.
summary: great 1 person brake bleeder, do it yourself brake flush

reviewText: This is by far one of the highest quality pnuematic vacuum brake bleeders i have seen and used for this price range. the quality is up there with the more expensive models, and it comes with a great set of accessories. i bought this for my shop use and upon the first usage i was very impressed with how well the Master cylinder refill attatchment worked to keep the fluid level perfect and just how well this vacuum bleeder works and makes my life so much easier cause i do not need to have someone sitting in the car pumping the brakes to manually bleed anymore. i would recomend this product to anyone in the market for a personal use bleeder or for your shop use so you can keep it at your box and not have to wait till "bobby" or "joe" is done with the shop supplied bleeder or track it down when someone broke it or misplaced it.
summary: GREAT VACUUM BRAKE BLEEDER FOR THE MONEY!

reviewText: This tool completely changed my opinion on bleeding brakes. I've always dreaded bleeding brakes because it's tedious and takes forever especially if I don't have a helper.This makes bleeding brakes a once person job and drastically reduces the time required to do it. I'm actually looking forward to bleeding the brakes on the rest of my vehicles.The Mityvac is also very well made. It's definitely designed and built to be used professionally. However since it's intended for shop work it is assumed that you have a decent air compressor. The manual doesn't list a minimum requirement beyond 60-150psi working pressure but it does state that their air consumption is 4.3 scfm @ 90 psi so it probably won't work well with a little 3 gallon pancake compressor.
Wanted covers for the trailer tires to extend their life due to sun damage. These were inexpensive but they fit fine and the adjustable straps hold them securely.
they do  there job

I purchased two sets of these for use in winterizing my RV.  Since I live in New England, I was a little skeptical on whether I truly needed them since I didn't have to worry about deterioration due to sun exposure, but I did want to protect my investment and the price was right to give them a try.  I use X-Chocks between the tires and wanted to make sure I had a little extra give in the cover allow them to stretch over it, so I purchased the 27-29" size for my tires that measured approximately 26".  They fit great, reaching down to but not quite touching the ground.  The straps with snaps are fairly easy to wrap around the tire and cinch tight.  They vinyl looks good, but I may want to consider conditioning it after year to make sure it doesn't dry out and crack.  And the beige color of the vinyl matches the beige of our RV cover as well.  I will try to update this review after the first winter of us is over.

fits nicely on trailer with 205/75-14 trailer tires.  Good quality/product.  It went on easily and the straps secured it behind the wheel so you'll have to get down on your knees to secure it tightly..but I think its very good product.
Easy to use and keeps dirt off when it rains and sunshine off the tires! Looks good while protecting the tires!

Better than I expected for the price! Nice grade thick materiel.  Looks like it will hold up nice for years I bet. Used to protect a seldom used utility trailer tires. Don't want the Sun to kill my tires before the miles do.
summary: Better quality than I expected! Nice!

reviewText: What can I say. They cover your tires.  I learned the hard way not having these on my tires, they dry rotted in (2) years.  After spending $800.00 on new tires it's worth protecting them.

Ordered 2 sets of these for my new camper ..put them on  day after I got them... great fit and look sharp next to the black camper  ...well made and seem sturdy but time will tell ..no problems buckling mine .. ordered the size recommended for my  tire size .. 15" they seem to be a little long and touch the ground by 2-3  inches ..the straps are long and easy to toss behind the tires to get to the other side to buckle them ..then I just lay the extra up on the frame to keep them off the ground ...works for me ..and I don't have to crawl on the ground ...I include the tire chocks when I snap them together and it helps keep the chocks in place as well .. Not sure I like the lining though ..it's nice and soft but if you put them on with dirty tires they will collect grass and dirt easily ... so I rinse the tires and let everything dry before putting them on ...
summary: Camco 45333 30-32" Colonial White RV Vinyl Tire Protector - Set of 2

reviewText: We haven't had these a long time, but they fit and the attachments seem sturdy. A friend has these same covers and hers weathered this winter just fine, which is why we also bought them.
Measured my tire and ordered the appropriate cover.... Fits and looks great!!! I'm very happy with this and the $10 is well worth keeping the spare in good shape.
Reasonably priced and very bright white. Easy to install and looks good. Will see how it holds up over time.
summary: Bright white and easy to install

reviewText: does the job...secures on 205/75-14 wheel/tire nicely The quality  decent..especially for the money.  Very WHITE!Get the Camco 45332 instead for a little more...its worth it.
You cant beat the price and it looks very very nice. It was wrinkled alot but a good rain and our humid Mn weather and those wrinkles went away in no time. Well worth the price.
Shipped fast and fits like a glove.  Looks good and protects the spare tire from the sun.  I will buy another for my camper.

Bought this to cover my travel trailer spare tire and was worried, based upon other reviews, about the fit but it fit my little trailer tire and rim perfectly!  In fact I can't imagine it being able to fit much else without a whole lot of tugging and pulling, it's a darn snug fit!
summary: Fits my 14" tire and rim perfectly!

reviewText: Great product, well made, looks great fits right and the descriptins and sizing charts are helpful. nI would buy again
summary: Camco products for the most part are great

reviewText: Yes; The back of my Travel Trailer looks so much better, I wouldn't mind following me. Fits well, Just a little sun shine took out the wrinkles.
Ordered the beginning of the year.  Cover has been on the spare tire and looks great.  I do clean it every chance I get.  Good for the price I paid.
This was a good deal . Its made a little cheap ,but it does the job. Buy it if you need it !

My last one, on my Coleman Sun Valley popup, came with it and already had some duck tape on it. One little accidental swipe of the bed supports tore it up. I did the same thing to this one and it didn't tear. Also love the black trim. Looks great!
Fits nice and snug. It's a bit thin, but we expected that. Cannot comment on durability as we just purchased it this year.

Very simple to install, I have a 27" spare and ordered the next size up. Quick and easy install (~1 minute) and seems well-made and durable; time will tell with critters, travel, and UV. I got the colonial white as I know in the back it will get dirty. Pure white would be hard to maintain, look odd, so an off white looks good. Highly recommend at first install. I recommend a lug lock set from Amazon to keep your spare and trailer tires; I bought the 5 pack McGard and ordered an extra key from them at registration.
Barely fits the 14" rim w/205 tire. It also collects a lot of raod dirt & difficult to wash off

I bought this cover to replace an old worn one that came with our used camper. It only survived a couple of years before it started cracking. Fortunately the price was not bad, but maybe there is something better.

I bought this cover to go over the spare tire on my travel trailer. I did not buy one larger than the measurement of my tire as suggested by some reviewers. I ordered one the same size as my tire diameter, and it fit perfectly. It has few wrinkles as a result.
Decent product.  Sizing is a bit of a guess.  I have a 26" spare and the cover is a bit large, but still very usable.  Delivery was quick, price was right.  Overall, I'm satisfied.

This is a good quality, well made product.  No cheesy seams to break like others I was warned about.  The size is generous and the vinyl is extremely water repellant and heavy weight.  Elastic at the bottom, and the color is not the typical dark colonial white and should work well with any shade of white.  A real bargain at this price.
Nice fit and well made.  Not the best I've ever had but for the price it's a winner.  The fir was just fine on my RV's spare tire.

I wanted to cover my spare. Received this the day before I went out of town. Right out of the box, one of the seams at the black cording was already frayed. Poor quality, but you get what you pay for.
Good.

Purchased these to protect my tires from the desert sun when I camp in the South West during the winter months.  They fit perfect and have an adjustable strap to snug them up on the tires.  I did find spiders living in one of them when I took it off of the tire getting ready to relocate!
summary: Must Have Item for Camping in the Desert

reviewText: I wanted some decent wheel protectors to put on my 29 1/2 to 30 inch diameter tires for UV protection during outside storage.  I ordered a set of 2 for a trial and they fit great, went on easy....although I did not use the strap yet.....might be a bit difficult for an old fat guy to get down on the ground and reach around to clip it....anyhow they do seem to be adequately held in place by the elastic sewed in to the top 1/2 of the covers.  I just ordered 2 more for all wheel coverage......the price is very good for the quality...Others said these covers hold up well...for now I am just gonna trust those other reviews since they do seem to be constructed well...especially for less than 10 dollars each delivered to my door
Nicely mad covers, but go to the next size larger than you think you need or you'll find as I did they do not cover the bottom side of your tires.  Kind of defeats the purpose.
summary: The Diameter Measurment Will Leave You Short

reviewText: I bought two pair of these cause dah if you have four tires obviously one set will not work. The quality is above normal. Yeah can be a pain in the but to clip the strap behind the tire, but holy crap we can't have everything we want. Quit complaining about BS like that and be thankful you can still bend down and do it. Highly recommended.

The 24-26 inch size fit my trailer's 26" tires perfectly , leaving about 1" of tire exposed on the bottom , which is just right IMO, since you wouldn't want these touching the ground (like the picture shows) for a couple reasons, one being ventilation of moisture from under the cover. These are nice, thick vinyl covers lined with a felt-like material on the inside, with an adjustable nylon strap and buckle on the back. I was a little leary of this purchase ,since these covers had a low price point, but they are good to go and I feel like I got a great value here on a high quality cover.  I'm tempted to order another set at this price and throw them in the garage as a replacement when this first set ultimately gives up the ghost...which I suspect will be after several seasons of year round use.I do wish they offered them in black , but whatever.
These covers are heavily built and price nice and I must say wayyyyy better than anco wheel covers which rotted out on me after a year so yes I would buy these again and recommend them to anyone!
summary: broncomania review on the camco wheel covers

reviewText: I like the feel and sturdiness of these and the buckles to hold them on to the tire give you more piece of mind that they will not be blown off and leave your tire un-protected. For the price they are Perfect!!!
summary: Nice fit and seem very sturdy

reviewText: I guess these things are alright but I won't know till I get them on and use them for awile

Vinyl is lined with fleece-like material; entire sleeve is very pliable (just warm it up before putting them on).  Straps are canvass cord with plastic buckles.  Highly recommended.*Update 10/27/2013: barely had these 2 & 1/2 months (purchased August 7, 2013) and one of the plastic buckle clips have broken.  I put them on once for about 1 & 1/2 months, removed them for a month to camp, and just went to put them back on.  The clip on one of them just fell apart in my hands.  Very cheap - DO NOT RECOMMEND!!!
summary: Affordable protection for your RV tires! (*update: broke after 2 & 1/2 months)!!!

reviewText: These appear to be better quality than what Walmart carries and have built-in straps (Walmart's doesn't).  I have 225/75/15 tires (about 29.5") and the size chart suggests size 27"-29". I chose the 30"-32" for easier removal and installation. They fit nice without being too snug and cover the bottom of the tire completely. Cheaper than the above alternative too.

These covers are much better than the more expensive ones that I have used and that I have found on the internet. They are wide enough to accommodate virtually any trailer tire. The elastic around the back is a definite plus and the built-in straps with buckles is an excellent addition. Others do not have these features. I've been using the tandem tire covers to cover the tires on both axles but these are much nicer. I measured the diameter of my tires and ordered the size that covered that dimension and they fit perfectly. I couldn't be happier.
I love these things! I've had them for almost a year. Well made and of quality appeal.  I bought mine slightly bigger and they fit perfectly.  They have clips that hold it securely, but I don't use.

Fits easily and excellent (bought 2 sets for tandam wheels), very simple to install (about 5 minutes for 4), look nice, but are snow white so bound to get dirty. I have 27" wheel's (pkg is for 27-29" and these fit easily with plenty of cover on the ground; just drape over (watch for wasp nests and critters/spiders in the wheel well and when you remove), toss the unbuckled strap around the back, clip and tighten (simply pull). One knee on the ground installation; very easy. The white is too white but it IS for winter (snow up here) storage anyway. Highly recommend so far, first impression, and easy placement. Durability is hard to determine but they feel adequate; with sun/uv and critters, time will tell and I will update as needed. I like them and highly recommend them at this point. Great Amazon price and fast Prime shipping.
I like the wheel and tire protection and good looks on my Travel Trailer. Easy to install and remove . . .
summary: Great Protection that looks good too!

reviewText: These are cheap and barely cover the tops of the tires.  It is also very difficult to maneuver the elastic strap around the back of the tire so it can latch to the other elastic strip.  I literally have to use a stick, wrap the long strap around it and push it so I can grab it at the other side.  I would think it would be a better design to put elastic all the way around so the tires would be completely covered without having to awkwardly strap it down.
summary: cheap enough, but don't cover the tire very well

reviewText: I bought these to keep the sun and my neighbors grass clippings off my tires, easy to install and they do the job!
I use braided straps to hold them even more securelyin high winds. I expect them to last about 3 years before Ineed to replace them.

works as expected, based on reviews I bought the next size up wheel size and am very happy I did so.  The next larger size fits well and has a little extra so I don't have to work hard to get it on and off.

The price was less than Camping World and free shipping..win  win! The product is as described and appears above average material..I expect it to hold up in the High desert sun. I liked the elastic snap strips also.Good product..good price....
summary: excellent price and good brand name

reviewText: Well if you didn't know the Southwestern US is terrible on rubber products.  So for RV storage these are a must.  Easy to put on and take off.  Should help my tires last a little longer while in storage.
summary: A must have for storage for the Southwest

reviewText: Camco RV Wheel Covers fit great, have a easy sizing chart to use for ordering. I would recommend them and buy again.
does a great job of covering the wheels and keeping dirt off of the tires and protects them from exposure to the sun.

The Camco wheel covers fit fine. My wheels are about 27" so they were a little big, but not a problem. I would expect that they would fit a 29" wheel perfectly since they are a couple of inches long for mine. Don't really need to connect the straps unless you are expecting a windstorm. The heavy-weight material is somewhat form-fitted to the wheel, so it is unlikely to blow off. They appear to be well made, and should last for years. No complaints.
These easy to install and remove tire and wheel sun protection are what my trailer needs when storing it.Good heavy vinyl should last a lot longer then my old ones.
These items seem to be very good quality and were easy to install.  I am going to buy another set.
These are lightweight and install easily.  They cover the wheels completely for sun protection to help preserve the rubber tires.  They fold up small so easy to carry in the RV too.
Just what I wanted it to do.  Easy to put on, protects tires from sun.  Can't say much more than that.  Only other question is how long it lasts in high sun area, but that remains to be seen.

I purchased these for our RV Trailer...Tire size: ST205/75R15. They fit perfectly! The quality of the fabric is great. Smooth on the outside, thick enough to fully protect the tires with a felt like inside. The covers completely cover the entire tire. The straps were very easy to use. I was able to secure them around all 4 tires in only 15 minutes. They clip together like the seat belt straps on shopping carts at the market. The straps were a little long after pulling them to the correct size, so I used a large paper clip to attach the extra part of the strap onto it's self, up off the ground.  Some people probably wouldn't mind the extra length of strap laying on the ground, but I just wanted it clipped up off the ground. I will be purchasing these again when they wear out, so I hope they stay in business.
Ordered and received in just a few days.  They were easy to install on my travel trailer.  I like the buckle and adjustable strap on the back side.  They are installed now for winter storage.
summary: Tire covers are better than what I had expected.

reviewText: These work very well on our horse trailer. Go on easily, have a strong build, soft insides and even in the heat of summer keep the tires cool. Best ones I have come accross.

Item was as advertised and good quality. These fit my Class C motorhome perfectly. Each cover comes with a strap and buckle to secure the installation. I tend to use that on the windy side only. Good product and worth the money.

These have been on our trailer tires for almost three months and the covers are turning brown. It's not from dirt, the cover material is discoloring. Must be a reaction with the rubber tires, but looks kind of gross. They are still serving the purpose but I wish they had stayed white :(

Would have given a 5 star if it was just a bit easier to get them hitched up. But this seems to be more a result of my wimping out in FL heat of summer. I get the unit unhooked and secure and if I have not passed out by that time I tend to forget the details. Other than that, the wheel covers are just fine and I'm sure will save me from lots of dry rot!
These went right on and snap on with an adjustable strap on the back. They will be a nice protection to my tires and wheels from the quite lethal sun in SE Georgia!
I recently grabbed 2 pair of the Camco 45322 RV Vinyl Wheel & Tire Protector - 2 pack. The help my yard have clean look as well as protect my tires.
Use these on my utility trailer to protect the tires from excessive sunlight deterioration.  Fit perfectly on the tires, and the strap to secure them prevents any loss due to wind.

These fit perfectly on my tires but the straps that go around to hold them in place were not easy to connect. I had to climb under the 5th wheel to connect the buckles. Normally this would not be a problem except I park the RV in a gravel lot. Just be aware of how they secure on the back side.

These are tire covers that go over your tires and protect from the sun (a good thing here in the sunny southwest).  They work.  They stay on despite the wind's best efforts to remove them.  They are impenetrable to light be it visible or UV.

This is an item that no RV should be without, I received these last week installed them in a few minutes now my new tire will be protected from the sun while it set up or in storage.Nice snug fit on the tires, just touched the ground no fold over like other brands. Good heavy material should get many seasons out of these.
i bought these to protect my custom wheels on my muscle car from my 2 male dogs peeing on them. good quality construction and materials. definitely worth the $

I Ordered three sets of Camco RV tire covers and did not know what to expect.  I was pleased with the fit and value/materials/construction.  Would recommend to protect your tires from UV damage, especially if you have G rated (expensive) tires.  They should pay for themselves in savings of replacing tires damaged by sun rot.

reviewText: I bought these to cover the wheels on our double axle RV.  They are quality made.  They are vinyl on the outside and have a soft blanket like liner on the inside!  They also have easy to tighten buckle straps on the bottom!  Don't waste your money on the cheap tire covers.  If you are looking for quality go ahead and buy theses and you will not regret it! I love them! I did buy the wrong size by accident but they fir like a glove!  I bought the size for a 14 inch wheel and we have 15 inch wheels.  The 15 inch cover would have been way to big!  Glad my mistake paid off!  I would Highly recommend the covers to anyone!
I ordered this for my parents RV and they use it when they park it and it is not in use. Easy to take on and off and keeps things cleaner and less damage from the sun.

Excellent and easy to use.  If you have difficulty getting the ball under the hitch use these. Set one just behind the ball and mount the other on the curved top of the hitch so it is vertical. Can't miss.  They seem durable to me and if a ball comes off glue it back on or use a tennis ball.  It prevents the back and forth and in and out of the cab hassle, as well as picking up the heavy tongue to move it to the hitch when you are fed up.  Also eliminates those hard to decifer hand signals from helpers; you can totally do it yourself. "No one yells"

I have a backup camera on my truck coupled to a double DIN DVD AV receiver and these two tennis balls work better.  The wide angle lens of the backup camera distorts distance and creates some confusion.  These don't.I stick the first one on my truck's trailer ball and elevate the ball to chin level, then do the same on the very tip of my boat's trailer hitch.  Then it's just a matter of backing up slowly using the rear view mirror until I see one of the balls start to tip.  I'm there!  I always hit it on either my first or second try.That being said, what others have said about the lack of sturdiness is absolutely true.  The most slender section of shaft is very easy to bend right at the joint if you manhandle it pushing the telescoping shaft back to its shortest position.  Once you've done that, you might as well just buy another.  You've got to be careful with these.I just broke one of mine yesterday after 2 years of use.  I went right back out to Lowes and bought another pair because I don't want to be without them, even if they are flimsy.  They work that well.

reviewText: If you are changing batteries or doing maintenance that requires you to disconnect  the battery this can be used with your ctech charger to prevent losing all your settings.

A must-have accessory if your cig plug is hot all the time.  It's much easier to leave the charger in the car plugged in this way.  I just unplug it and push it over to the passenger seat so it doesn't slow me down a bit.

Worked with the CTEK 3300 purchased for use with my 2014 Stingray.  The car has a receptacle in the rear that is always on and Chevy sells essentially the same (if not the same) charger brand labeled.  The charger does not come with an auxiliary receptacle.  This one comes with an adapter to fit the standard size auxiliary in the car.  Very well made.

Like all components of the CTEK system the cig socket charger is quality built with o-ring seals in the electrical portion to keep it dry and a firm grip on the socket.  That being said, there are some things to consider.Keep in mind not all cigarette lighter sockets on cars are live 24/7 - most imports tend to kill all outlets when the key is removed while american cars tend to leave the sockets live all the time.  This makes it difficult to use this with EVERY car without leaving the key in the ignition which can in many cases draw more power from the battery than the charger puts in, thus depleating the battery charge.  It's not a win-win scenario.One alternative is to install a second always on cigarette lighter jack for this plug.  If you are going that route I would suggest an alternative which works well with asian and german imports, again from ctek:CTEK 56-380 Comfort Indicator Panel- this is an alternative if your jack is not live without the key turned.  It occupies a blank spot on the dash and performs 2 functions - red/yellow/green blinking leds 24/7 to indicate the battery's state of charge and a ctek input jack to acccept any of their chargers where normally there would be a set of clips, rings, or the -263 cig socket.  Installed properly it looks like a factory install, provides an indication plainly visable, and a rubber covered location for inserting the ctek charger end.  If you can't use this 56-263 easy connect cig socket plug, then the 56-380 is the optimal solution which fits perfectly into a din switch array on imports.Both solutions get you the same result - you have an inside car convenient way to charge your battery from 117 VAC without opening the hood [or the trunk/rear seat/ all the oddball places some cars (ahem bimmer) put their batteries]Both methods are convenient, professional, well made, and part of a system that works well together to keep your car ready to start no matter what battery you use to start it.  The -380 version adds the battery state indicator wihch is a nice bonus at the end of the day to be able to glance at the dash with the key removed and determine the immediate charge status while the -263 (this item) can be used with most any vehicle even riding mowers!
summary: A fine addition to the CTEK charger system

reviewText: I ordered this adapter to make it easy to keep my car plugged in to the CTEK battery maintainer.  It couldn't be easier. reviewText: I try it out in my car with a voltage meter and it would not work. I check to see if I had fully mated to make sure I had power.
