reviewText: This product was exactly as described and works great. I charge two phones while on road trips and it works well!

This isn't a very complicated device so this review will be brief.It effectively splits a 12v connection into two functional ones, each with a nice handy cap on it.  Don't underestimate the usefulness of those two caps, as a stray bit of metal or anything conductive could blow the fuse on this.Having mentioned the fuse, let me point out that not all splitters are manufactured with a fuse built into them.  Without a fuse on the splitter itself a stray bit of metal or conductive material will cause the fuse in your car's electrical box to blow.  This adds a little extra security as likely the fuse on the splitter is of a lower rating than that in your electrical box: so it blows first.An earlier review mentioned electrical interference which made me wary about this product at first. However upon examination, I'm not exactly clear where such interference could be coming from.  The splitter is incredibly simple with no real electrical processing being done to the power going through it. It's a fuse gated adapter with two connectors on it.  As I have a zune controller and in line adapter running off one of the connectors on this, I was afraid that I would experience some hum or something similar to that mentioned in an earlier review. No issues here.The wiring doesn't seem to be of high quality, but since I paid so little for it and don't plan on using it for heavy duty applications, that isn't something I will deduct for. The wiring is adequate and likely will not break unless I pull hard on it or abuse it.
With more and more electronic devices available to use in the car, it's easy to run out of plug in space.With this, I can operate my GPS and recharge my phone at the same time.

I purchased this splitter because of it's safety fuse.  I dont want to mess with my car's fusebox incase i overload or short a socket so it's a simple product with a much better benefit than ordinary splitter.I just wish they had longer wires so i can hide it and not stay dangling on my SUV back socket.. But the product works well so far...

I use this one and a 3 outlet model by RoadPro  in my RV.  Neither have failed me, and I rely on them daily as I boondock most of the time and use solar power.  I like the fact they come with end caps and they are heavier than the regular ole cheap ones you can buy at your corner store. Use this with the 12 volt red extension cord they make and you'll be set to go.

This tool is unique due to its triangular shape and slightly con-caved form to follow the windshield slope. The triangular shape allows the tool to get into low sloping areas where the windshield is near the dashboard.  How well it cleans depends on the material used on the tool (microfiber is best for no streak clean).  It does require a couple of swipes to get the glass totally clean, but it does not require a lot of effort.I found this tool so convenient to use that expanded its use from the inside of the windshield to the outside of the windshield and the sunroof.  I am fairly shot and cannot reach the sunroof as well as some windshield portion of the outside glass of my SUV without the aid of a step stool.  I found using this everywhere really speeds up the cleaning.The tool comes with two covers: a mesh one (good for removing bugs) and a micro-fiber (no streak cleaning). Because I use it everywhere I added a couple additional microfiber sleeves of my own.I purchased high quality microfiber towels and using my sewing machine attached strings (I actually used shoe laces cut in half) to all four corners of the micro towel.  This allows me to tie the "sleeve" to the head of the tool (see attached photo under customer photos).This weekend I found yet another use for this tool. I purchased Griot's garage glass clayGriot's Garage 11049 Glass Cleaning Claywhich removes deposits from the glass.  I was able to use this tool to rub clay against the glass where I could not reach the glass by hand.  This tool worked well because it is not totally flat but con-caved to follow the slightly sloped glass of the windshield, so it worked very well to hold the clay ball.Thumbs up for this tool!Ali Julia review
summary: Excellent!  Tip on making additional sleeves

reviewText: Its a great time saver and so far it appears to work just fine. Now, if it would come with a robot arm

As stated before you don't need it but you will be thankful after you get and use it. I have a full size 4X4 pickup and there is just no easy way for this old man to get a good cleaning on the entire front windshield without making use of a heating pad on my back afterwards.This tool is sturdy and provides me the reach I need to get a good cleaning on the whole inside of my windshield. it works great because you can hit the windshield with one of the two "cleaning" pads and then finish it off with the microfiber pad and doing it twice that way is not so bad when it is so much easier to do. Don't forget that you can use it anywhere you want to in the car, house, boat and you get the same easy job. I definitely recommend this product.

I bought this tool based on the overwhelmingly positive reviews found here on Amazon.  Being an engineer, I am typically leery of buying "gimmick" products.  However, it didn't take 5 minutes to learn that this tool is excellent in all respects.  It is true that the bonnet is a bit tricky to install and must be placed exactly like the instructions (which are found on the bonnet itself) state or it won't fit.  But that is a small price to pay for such a useful tool.  The product is well-made and appears to be durable.  I really like the way the hinge lets the head conform to the curvature of my car windshield as it slides up, down, and across. Contrary to what some reviewers have noted, I didn't find that any extraordinary pressure is required to get a very clean windshield.  Like most cars today, my windshield is deep and slants back toward the driver on a very steep angle and naturally, the law of physics demands that a certain amount of pressure is required when reaching out at arms length to scrub the grime off.  As a finishing touch, I simply lay a clean terrycloth washcloth over the head and buff a little until the windshield is dry.  I also like the way the tip screws off the handle to allow an extension, such as a painters pole, to be used for hard-to-reach areas or to save your back when cleaning the windows of your home.The only minor reservation I have is, until now, I have not laundered the bonnet and it is showing a fair amount of grime.  My concern is how the bonnet will fare in the wash.  It would be nice to be able to buy a 3-pack or a 6-pack of bonnets at a reasonable price and just throw the old one away after several uses.  After all, they couldn't cost more than a quarter to make.If you are still using the old newspaper and/or rag technique (as I was until recently) I highly recommend this product for purchase.  It gets a solid 5 stars in my book.

Walmart sells it for $ 14.99. Amazon needs to drop the price to at least $ 14.99.Edit:Does what it says it does and does it well. 5 stars for the product itselfThanks to Amazon for adjusting the price to market conditions. 5 stars for the price also.
summary: Does what it says it does and does it well.

reviewText: I ordered this with the Stoner glass cleaning fluid to handle the inside windshield of my PU truck.  It worked fine.  Order was delivered on time and undamaged.

This windshield cleaner does the job.  It's great for getting into the corners and along all the hard to reach spots on windshields.  Especially on those sloped interior windshields most modern cars have.  On the inside, it's the way to go.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

With the exception of Invisible Glass, that is the ONLY Stoner product that deserves 5 stars.  I bought this for cleaning the inside glass of my car for the front and rear windshield.  It really provided no better results than if I had twisted and contorted my body and used a decent microfiber cloth.  Sure, it makes the cleaning task easier, but not streak free.The main problem is the bonnets that it comes with are not best suited for cleaning glass; the pack only comes with one true microfiber bonnet.  The rest are geared for other purposes and the others they allege for cleaning glass (not the right type of microfiber for the job).  They are also way too tight a fit around the triangular head which causes it to bow, so unless you apply enough pressure you will have an unevenly smeared, sloppy cleaned surface.This is a good concept, but marketed with too much hype.  Visit the Stoner website and view consumer reviews on ANY of their products and you will see only positive reviews.  They are one of those companies that filter out negativity and only post the positive consumer reviews.  I'll use it for only the purpose I mentioned above but for the most part it will sit in a closet with little use.

So by now all of us have seen the infomercial on a similar piece of hardware to clean our windshields.  However I do not tend to buy from TV and thus I came looking on AMAZON.  I found this item and it looked a bit better from the one on TV...simply because of the triangular shape in the front which actually does help you to reach the corners of the front windshield.We have all cleaned windshields and simply put, the front ones are a pain in the neck.  You can never reach all the way down without some sort of acrobatic movements.  This tool makes it easy...spray the windshield with your favorite glass cleaner and clean it...  Yes, it does take a few passes to make it 100% clean.  I mean...sit down and use this thing...your back will be thankful and cleaning the car will not be a chore anymore...The grip is nice and comfortable which makes this feel like a high quality item.  It comes with one microfiber and two mesh covers...which are washable and re-usable.  The mesh is for hard scrubbing.. :-) where as the microfiber gives it a great finish.I highly recommend this to anyone and everyone that cleans their own vehicle.
These headlight bulbs are better than stock, but they are marginally better. Cost/benefit analysis shows that one can find better bulbs, albeit more costly.
Easy to install and provides great brightness.  I am very happy with the product.  It makes seeing at night much better, easier and safer.
These bulbs are much brighter than stock and cast a clean white light evenly across the road. Compared to Silverstar zXe, I prefer these GE bulbs.
I ordered H7 bulbs and they sent me a wrong type.i still installed them on my father's car and the light they produce is ok though
Turned my yellow bulbs into bight white. Much nicer to see. I took a $1,000 mile round trip and both legs were after dark. Love these lights.

I was torn between the Nighthawk bulbs and theSylvania 9006SU SilverStar Ultra, Twin Pack. After reading some negative reviews about the lifespan of SilverStars, I opted to go with these.Initially, I was worried about how blue these would look, versus the regular Nighthawk bulbs, but I was happy to find that there's really not much of a blue tint in the light at all.The light is very bright and very white. I wouldn't put them against an HID system, but you can absolutely see a difference. Driving at night took a little getting used to, as the beam pattern doesn't seem to bleed the same way my stock headlights did.Another concern I had was that oncoming traffic would be blinded by the extra light output. However, this hasn't been a problem. And, again, from a distance these lights look pure white, rather than blue.December 2009 Update: Well, after just under a year and two months, a bulb died on me. Just outside of the 1-year warranty, no less. Since I'm just outside of the warranty, I decided to order the SilverStar Ultras.In the meantime, I had saved the OEM bulbs when I put the Nighthawks on, and am pretty surprised to see the side-by-side difference. The throw and clarity on the Nighthawks really is excellent. It's a shame they don't seem to last very long.February 2011 Update: Not so much an update as a tip: apparently, the SilverStar Ultras last just as long, and cost more. So, I'm going back to these bulbs.
summary: Nice, white light. A big upgrade from stock halogen lights.

reviewText: I ordered 2 sets of these one as back up.  I replaced the old halogen bulbs in a 02 Camry.  The difference in brightness is night and day.  My father always complained about the light being so dim and he has replaced the stock bulbs with replacements and they still were dim, so i got these and compared to normal halogen bulbs these are 5x brighter, i know they may not last as long but in the same aspect the regular halogens dim as time goes......Plus for the price you can't beat them.  These bulbs are slightly tinted blue and is not as yellow as other halogens but the light intensity is not sacrificed to provide you with WHITE ZENON LOOK that other brand claims .  Unless you get HID kits you'll never achieve a White light with Halogens....If you're just looking for brighter light and a little less yellowish tint then these are it.

My dealer wanted over $100 to replace the headlights in my car. I did it myself in a few minutes. The lamps are as good or better than the Toyota bulbs I replaced. They have a very slight blue tint but by no means are they the same true-white color as HID bulbs.
summary: Save money and do it yourself

reviewText: Probably the brightest lights that are street legal in my area for non-OEM replacement bulbs. Much brighter than the higher cost lights of the competitors.

....GE's Warranty department came through.  First off - the light bulb, as many other users comment it's brighter than stock light bulbs but not HID like headlights on a newer luxury vehicle.  They provide a bright, wide white light which illuminates the road and surroundings nicely.  I loved these but as I said before one of them burnt out 11 months in.  I thought GE's Warranty process would be quick and easy considering it's a major company....I was wrong.  They are pretty "out of date" when it comes to placing warranty replacements.  Through their website you can find an online form to submit a claim.  They don’t respond via email, instead you’ll get a letter in the mail saying they have received your complaint and will ship a replacement.  I received this letter almost month after submitting for a replacement(so keep your stock light bulbs handy to install them temporarily).  Next day the light bulbs came in.Just keep this in mind:  If you buy from GE, it may take a month for them to get back at you but it’s definitely worth the wait.

These fit the bill for license plate bulb in my 4Runner. They don't seem any brighter than my OEM bulbs. If you're not sure about fit (I wanted to be sure) you can check the GE Lighting website like I did to make sure you are ordering the correct model.

These lights work well, with a better than standard light performance. That being said, they are a little too expensive. I will however, get over it because I like the difference the new lights made. I know that because the older the bulb the dimmer they are, the new bulbs are going to be somewhat brighter. I still think it was a good buy.

I needed to replace a few interior lights and these did the trick.  I've tried the LED white ones but they didn't light up at all.  I can definately see an improvement in lighting with these and they are not too yellow which is what I was worried about.  Close to stock color and 30 percent more lighting.  Excellent buy for the price!
I have a 2004 Tacoma and needed to replace the bulbs in front on the side markers. These bulbs are much brighter. I was also looking at the LED type, but these are much brighter.
Needed some to replace the bulbs that went out on my car. They fit and work fine. Just like stock.

Was the cheapest price I could find and had free delivery.  The box they ship it in is far to little to be a shipping box for the weight of the this product.  By the time it arrived it had busted through the package and was damaged.  Amazon was quick to get it replaced with no hassle!!Second one showed up in similar condition but there did not appear to be any damage to the jack.  Hi-Lift its self can not be beat.  The company does a great job standing behind its product and the product just works (provided you do the very little proper maintenance).  I went with the X-Treme because I liked the finish and attachment point options at the top.
Great item! I have three of these One knock off and on my Great grandfather left me. This is smooth.
summary: Here again Amazon proves better pricing including Ebay

reviewerName: C. Beard "I have not gone where I intended to...
reviewText: This is an awesome tool for the trail with many uses other than changing flats.  Winching vehicles, pulling logs off the trail, rescue work, pulling fence posts, etc.The big downside?  This will rust instantly if you don't keep it away from water, add salt and forget about it.  The powder coat finish is not good enough.  I paint mine with Eastwood extreme chassis paint which works great.
VERY SOLID PRODUCT. THIS WILL WORK GREAT WHILE OUT FOUR-WHEELIN IN THE NORTH WOODS ALSO GREAT TO HAVE AROUND THE HOUSE.

I have no doubt this jack will perform well beyond the company's claims. I have owned several of these and have never had a complaint about failure or malfunction. I have only one suggestion for Hi-Lift and that is to make the handle more easily replaceable and add a soft hand grip that will help resist cold temps.
This is very nice lift jack I have installed it in my jeep and looks grate, price wise it's not too bad remember you got what you payd for it, so yes it's little bid $$ but you won't be disappointed

This is my favorite Hi-Lift jack yet.Super heavy and the gold anodizing is nice.Hi-Lift really needs to step up their powder coating/paint. It always wears off and rusts too easy. The jacks rust even in areas where there is no wear!None-the-less it is the best jack of its type and I do not leave home without it.

I highly recommend this to anyone who does any off roading, and for any truck.  the jack is the easiest to use and gives you the height that others will or can not.  I bought it for me 2011 Polaris Ranger Crew and have the Tire attachment, the bumber attachment, the off road base and the protective cover bag.  there is no better jack out there!
summary: The Best Jack on the market!

reviewText: this jack is great it might cost a little more but worth it. it comes with the clap already and and you dont need to purchase the jack mate either cause you dont need it

I have two of these jacks, they're both over 30 years old.  I've always known them as "wagon jacks," and I've used them both many many times for all kinds of jobs.  I read one review that recommends applying oil to the springs and pins, and that's fine.  Personally, I've always used an old tooth brush to apply grease to any portion of the jack that moves or operates in conjunction with any moving part.  Grease of course is messy so I recommend wearing gloves while operating the jack.  These jacks will last you a lifetime if properly maintained - and they'll always work.  Get an old car tire inner-tube, cut it in half and slip it over the full length of the jack, secure it with zip-ties and you're good to go.
summary: Have one on any off-road vehicle

reviewText: This thing is a TANK !  Seriously.  It's heavy, massive, and everything you could ever want from a hilift !  Minus a huge base, of course.  But that's easily fixed.  Anyway, this thing is meant to survive an apocalypse.  And I have no doubt it will obey my every command should my Jeep need rescuing, or I stumble upon a damsel in distress.

I have the 60" X-treme, but in a Tj there is no room, and mounting it outside exposes the jack to weather and thieves. I ordered the 48" X-treme and mounted it in the cargo area on the roll bar. I hope I never have to use it, but glad I have one in case I do. Insurance is another way to look at it. Great tool, great price and peace of mind. Very fast shipper too.
There's nothing like them so I usually keep them and stay wary of them moving when they shouldn't or opposite of were I thought they would .

Don't even bother with the generic knock off made in China crap. Buy one of these and be done. 48" works for Jeeps and smaller rigs, get the 60" for anything lifted or full size. The gunmetal gray on the X-Treme version even looks cool. Add some pipe insulation to the pipe and mount it somewhere. This could be used as a weapon if need be. Very heavy, durable and might save your life. Versatile tool that can be used to winch, pull, or clamp as well as lift. If you have an older vehicle get the bumper adapter too. This will minimize the scratches on your bumper if you should use it. Add a few pieces of wood, some gloves, tow strap and clevis and you are ready for off-roading. Just don't mount this thing to your bumper, you all look like fools for doing that. (You know who you are.)
summary: Just get one for your rig now!

reviewText: USED IT YESTERDAY AND IT PULLED MY JEEP OUT OF A HUGE MUD/ICE HOLE I FOUND MYSELF STUCK IN 4 WHEELIN IN NEW ENGLAND, WORKED LIKE A CHARM. ALREADY PAID FOR IT SELF.

great jack, every offroader should have one of these! so many different uses and very solid. the price is a little high but would not risk having a cheaper knock off fail me when i really need it. does need lubrication every few weeks or the action can jam a little

Simple, strong, brilliant design and what seems like an unstable base actually makes it easy on your equipment because the jack leans in to lift the load rather than pulling the load to it. It makes sense in action. It needs oiling right out of the box so don't forget to do that. I use it to lift a big ZTR mower deck that weighs 750-lbs., so I inserted a half-inch bolt and nut where I start lifting on that mower to keep the large runner from dropping the last 13 inches when lowering the load. If you ever need any work done on it, keep your receipt, as Hi-Lift requires proof-of-purchase within its 1-year warranty._______________________NOTE ON SHIPPING:SHAME ON YOU, HI-LIFT, AND YOU KNOW WHAT I'M TALKING ABOUT. You shipped this great jack in a big box without any packing material via UPS and they took up your challenge. Both UPS and FedEx are notorious anymore for destroying more goods than they deliver, and without any packaging protection, UPS not only tore off half the box, but managed to tear chunks off the powdercoat. The clevis was slightly rusted from where they must have left it in a puddle of water or fuel. I don't understand what so many companies are thinking these days that packaging should be nonexistent.
summary: Great jack, but shame on Hi-Lift for its shipping

reviewText: This looks great but, I have not used it yet.  All the parts came with it as stated and quality looks great.
summary: Looks nice but haven't tried it yet

reviewText: This is super helpful while storing my soft top windows. I simply roll them up, and put them in the back of my JK in case of a surprise storm. As others have stated - The rear window does peak out a bit between the soft inner lining, but the outer shell is long enough to contain it. It is a bit expensive, but I'm satisfied with the product.
summary: This is super helpful while storing my soft top windows

reviewText: Previous to getting this window storage duffle I never knew quite what to do with my windows.  But rolling them up works great.  Some minor design improvement could be done though.  Like others have stated the cloth dividers that goes between the windows is not long enough to cover the rear window.  I can overcome that though because I always keep several micro wipe cloths with me.  I put one on each side of the rear window and life is sweet.  I keep the micro wipe cloths with me anyway because I do not like to store dirty windows.The other improvement that should be made is the web straps that go over the windows to hold everything in place while rolling them.  They need to be shorter.  Neither of these items are significant and I would still purchase one again.

Previously, I had been taking my windows off and placing them on top of each other with towels (like: towel-rear window-towel-side window-towel-side window-towel) and then rolling them up and holding it all together with a couple of bungee cords.  It worked, but the resulting mass of stuff took up quite a bit of space and wasn't exactly pretty.  Or convenient. Or efficient.So I pulled the trigger on this window duffle, and I have mixed feelings about it.It's really lightweight, as a matter of fact when empty, it weighs nearly nothing. The outer layer looks and feels very durable, and I expect the material used is waterproof so at least if it gets dripped on the insides won't get wet.The inner layers (there are four inner sheets) are made of a material that reminds me of a lens cleaning cloth.  Not the super soft microfiber reusable kind, mind you, but the disposable kind.  Now, I'm not saying that these inner sheets are not durable.  I can't say that, because I'm unwilling to test their durability beyond normal use due to the price of the duffle.  But I can say that they don't FEEL durable, and that's a bit disconcerting.  However, the sheets remind me of the sheets I trust to clean my camera lenses that are worth thousands of dollars, so I feel like they will probably protect the windows pretty well.Finally, there's the price.  This may or may not be the best option for storing your windows safely, and keeping them unscratched for as long as possible.  I don't know.  But when you get it in the mail, it sure doesn't FEEL like something that costs what it does.  Bottom line, if it is successful in the long term in keeping these windows clean and scratch-free, then it's worth the price, as high as it may seem.  If it wears out, the inner fabric tears, or doesn't protect as well as it should, then it's obviously not.  Time will tell.

I wanted to keep my windows scratch free, and store them out of the way, and not exposed with the top down.  This just works.  I put the back window in first as it is the longest, drop a layer of cloth, which appears flimsy, but is not, just light weight nylon, and then repeat.  I roll it up, and hang it on the bar that goes across the back of the Jeep.  With the top down, you can't see it.  With the top up, and the windows out, it is out of the way, and doesn't get crushed under my kid's stuff.  Easy, reasonable price, does the job.
summary: Simple, and does exactly what I wanted it to do

reviewText: I ordered these to replace to tired pistons on the hatch of my truck topper.  I matched model numbers, and they were a perfect replacement.  These are much stiffer than the old ones.  The problem I was having was that the old pistons would let the hatch drop unexpectedly in cold weather.  It's summer now, but I don't expect to be hitting my head anymore this winter.INSTALLATION NOTE:These came with no instructions, so  had to figure it out.  Basically, its a ball and socket joint.  You don't have to remove the metal clips, which I did on the first set.  Just pull straight out on the old piston to remove them.  This will expose the ball on the mounting bracket.  Then, just push the new piston until it snaps in place.  It should take no tools and 5 minutes to replace a set.

Come with mounting clips in place ready to push onto the origianl ball mounts. (make sure balls are not worn out also)Easy to change and lower cost than I've seen in the past, found nothing to gripe about and now hope they last a good long time.
summary: Exact replacement of originals with same part number and brand on the strut....

reviewText: Back glass lift gate on the cap of my Dodge pickup wouldn't stay up, obviously one or both of the gas struts finally gave out after 18 or 19 years.  This was the exact part number printed on the original struts.  Worst part of installation was prying the old ones off the ball connection.  New ones went on with a tap from a dead blow hammer, and were on within 10 minutes of delivery from Amazon.  Lift gate now works like new.  Thanks, Amazon!
As expected, exact replacement and all worked well.  This is the third set in twelve years so the life is around six years. Not bad for something that is gas filled.
summary: SUSPA 28 LB Gas Spring/Prop/Strut/Shock (set of 2) C16-02622

reviewText: These are the OEM rods for certain models of "bed caps" on trucks.  They look identical to hood support rods, but they are usually not compatible.  I bought these for my friend's truck, whose rear window did not stay open because the original rods aged and once it hit in the head in the friend's wife.  My friend was using a 2x4 wood to support the window, but since these rods are not expensive, I bought them for my friend.Removal/installation is easy since they are held in place with a tension clip on each end.  Just pry it out with a flat blade screwdriver but make sure it does not fly away into the black hole or worse yet, in your eyes.  Installation: simply place the clip on top of the end and press hard on it; the same caution for removal procedure applies, however.
summary: A Necessity for Truck Add-on Cap

reviewText: Used it on my 2008sebring disc brake pads and pins..So far works great!! I put it in a little cup...and use a little brush..makes it easier. I also used it to lube my water pump bolts that like to rust and seize up in the pump. I highly recommend it ..it won't wash off..It is tuff to get off..i like it!!
summary: So far works great!! I put it in a little cup

reviewText: I used to use typical anti-seize in the past on my brakes on my motorcycles.  It'd work well, but just for a limited time before it would run and wash out.  This stuff...wow!  It sticks and stays!  I've had it on my pins for around 4 months now, and when I pulled out my pins to check, there was still some lube present.  The 8 ounce container will last a typical consumer a lifetime.
summary: Good Performing, Heavy Duty Brake Grease

reviewText: like i said in the title you only need to buy it once and never need to again you dont use much and if your just a home diy guy this will last forever and it works great
summary: buy it once and never need to again

reviewText: The bright purple color is good to see where it's been applied. Just be neat applying it as whatever is left beyond the contact areas is quite visible through the wheels. Instructions do say to remove excess. Had previously used OEM grade ATE compound (typically used by BMW); Permatex ceramic does appear to last a bit longer. It also does a reasonable job reducing the level of brake noise and squeal. This bottle will last years, but for the price, it's good value.

I used this to lubricate the caliper pins on my brakes. It seems like it will work well, it claims to be compatible with all rubber brake parts, so hopefully it will not degrade the rubber bushings on the pins. I'll check on them in 6 months and see how they are.I also used this as an anti-squeal lubricant on the between the back of the pads and the pad shims.

I used this product on my motorcycle while re-building the brake calipers on my dual, 4 piston calipers.  As expected, it went on easily and helped with re-assembly as clearances are tight.Hopefully, with the ceramic/higher temps, it will last longer than the lesser "Permatex 24110" (which lasted 3 years). A little goes a very long way....

Our shop uses this product with every brake job and it works great.  We use it to coat the backs of pads as well as lubricate the caliper slides and it never lets us down.  The only drawback is the brush and the container.  We tend to discard the included brush and use a higher quality acid brush.  We also cut the container open when getting towards the end of the bottle because it becomes very difficult to extract the last bit of lube out if you don't.
summary: Best brake lube on the market.

reviewText: I buy from Amazon with confidence of a perfect fit using the fitment chart. The rotors were priced right and with free shipping how can you go wrong. Once installed my car had no problems stopping smoothly with no unusual sounds.
I bought these because of the name brand and price.  I am very happy with the product and would purchase again.

I bought these brake rotors for my dads 2003 Toyo Corolla and he tried to install them himself but he had trouble.  He took them to a local tire shop and they installed them for him and they were great.  No screeching noise from the brakes, great stopping power and smooth tire turning. Great purchase for my dad.

Like so many I tended to think that brake rotors are pretty much all the same, but not so. The first thing I noticed is how well these were finished compared to the cheap auto-parts store ones they were replacing. These rotors are very well finished, no rough edges, and the ground finish is very even. I checked them for run out and they were spot on. They fitted our 2003 Corolla perfectly, and so far so noise or vibration.
summary: A Perfect fit...and a great finish...

reviewText: These discs were a great value on the subaru wrx I was replacing them on. I found the fitment to not have any issues and after 5,000 miles they are doing just fine.

These are installed on the outside of the vents using zip ties. The zip ties seem to leave spaced between the screen and the plastic cover that are bigger then the screen openings. I don't know if bugs might use these openings for access or not so time will tell. Assuming this isn't a problem, the screens seem to go on easily and, if they work, will be a good investment.

I bought this screen after a recommendation for or RV dealer.  The dealer had the screens in stock but at higher price.  I received these screens in a few days from Amazon and had to straighten out two of them that looked like they were bent before going in the box.  Anyway, installation was a breeze since you just use small zip ties to hold them on the the vent cover.  I'll have to pick up a few more zip ties to anchor down the bent areas that are creating small gaps but overall, this is a great product and a small price to pay to prevent bugs from clogging the gas orfice tube.
These fit perfect on my Norfolk fridge vents. I did like others and  added a few more ties. You can't den see they are in the vents.

The item description included Dometic.  The package stated that it was NOT for Dometic.  Despite some resizing modifications required to make it work, it is doing the job that the type of product was designed for.  Maybe the correct item would garner 5 stars?
These fit well, save for a few very small less than perfect fits...  No insects could get through.  I added an additional wire tie for each vent hole to be safe.

I was going to fabricate something similar but this is a way better solution. The cost is reasonable and the installation is easy.I was concerned that the three wire ties per screen would allow the wind while driving to rattle and over time damage the screens. Using more wire ties in the center and some hot glue, corrected my fears.
summary: This was exactly what was needed.

reviewText: These screen pieces are not going to give way and do not feel cheap - they are quite strong.  The drawback to these, and may be there isn't much else you can do, is that they are tie-wrapped to the cover on the inside. So they cover the openings pretty well as far as keeping out the insects of concern attracted to the propane.  But they don't cover as well as you might like and the possibility that a tie-wrap will break and you may not see it.  Still they do an adequate job for their purpose.
summary: Good quality screen material and solid

reviewText: A must have in order to stop the problems mud dabbers can cause and the mess to clean out after a nest is started. The only thing I did different was use three times more of the wire ties to avoid a little rattle you can get if the wind hits it just right , But no real problem and easy to do.

This works well to keep wasps in my area out of the vent. It is easy to put on and come winter, since I live in my RV full time, I will remove so it doesn't get too hot and cause damage (not sure it would, just a precaution).

Fits good on my 2011 Outback 298 re.  Hopefully will keep the bees from building a nest and causing lots of maintenance in the future.  Well worth the price to prevent future problems.  I would recommend it!
These are like the Mud Dauber screen - but the tool used to apply these is much better tool for setting the screen into place.
My brother-in-law recommended these for my RV vent to keep out the wasp.  I hate Wasp so I hope it does.
summary: Bought this for my RV Furnace Vent

reviewText: I ordered based on product name, not size. Next time I'll order by size. Well made, but the connection is a littke weird.

Camco is everything RV. I would say most Camco items are great and work well, this one including. Slap this baby right around the Furnace vents to prevent Wasps, bees, etc from entering and making nests. Installation is fairly simple and unit is built well. No problems and has not fallen off. Little springs keep it in place. Would recommend to any RV owner.
summary: But mommy, there is a hornet's nest in there..........

reviewText: Not the most elegant solution, but it does get the job done.  I'd prefer something with a more secure attachment, but that said, it's survived two cross-country drives and new england winters with nothing getting in, so it's doing the job.
summary: Not the most elegant solution, but it does get ...

reviewText: This fit perfectly on our '88 Fleetwood Avion and keeps the mud daubers out.  They already had gotten into the furnace and clogged up the orifice causing it to stop working.  They still try to get in and build nests attached to the outside of this which we just break off a couple times per year.
summary: Perfect to keep those little pesky buggers OUT!

reviewText: At first look these look hard to place on but they are simplier than you think. When removing screens from package becareful you dont loose the springs. When you go to put them on make sure they are hook to the screen and then gently take the spring tool and guide it thru the screen until it catches the spring. This allows the screen to be installed in a minute, just make sure the spring catches the cross piece of metal on the exhaust. You do this a second time for the other screen. When completed save the spring tool, it does come in handy when having to deal with other projects involving springs.
summary: Keeping insects out of the exhausts of appliances.

reviewText: It took me longer to unpack these things than it did to install them. Tool provided worked great. The screens were in excellent shape, no damage at all. No mud daubers in my furnace.
I only needed one for my Atwood furnace it is easy to put on and it stays put. And I have an extra for later!
Quality item at a fair price, what more could a person ask for. Hooking those little springs onto the RV does take a little effort if your eyes are dimming and your fingers are less then nimble.

Hi All.As most RV'ers know, bees and bugs like the smell of Propane, and they like to make thier nest in the worst possible places for making your RV Propane Items not working do to being plugged.  These Screens do a good job of keeping the bees and insects out of your Propane Burning items, so they don't get plugged and keep them working  when you need to use them.

I was a little weary about the rigidity of the screens, seeing as how I store my travel trailer in my driveway and there are a lot of little ones that play around my house (including my own 6 yo), but those fears were put to rest the moment I opened the package.  These screens are very solid and it will take a considerable amount of effort to push the domes in and actually deform them.  They install very easily, though the included tool is a tight fit between the screen holes.  Still, highly recommended - I am very happy with these!
summary: Very easy to install; very solid screens!!!!

reviewText: These  insect screens fit my Suburban furnace vents perfectly and were extremely easy to install with the supplied tool. I also put one on my water heater vent because the holes were large enough for bees to enter. We have a real wasp problem here in the Rocky Mountains and I'm sure these screens will solve the problem of them nesting in my trailer.
Works and secures to RV very tightly. Keeps your furnace vent free of flying and crawling insects. A must have for sure. Thankyou Amazon for carrying these RV products.

Excellent fit in the end but very difficult to install with the tool provided. The tool sent was defective, too hard to use to connect the spring. I ended up just placing the screen over the exhaust and closing the door and it works well. I think the connection spring attachment and tool need a re-design and better quality control but I highly recommend these screens for hole protection. They just need patience and creativity. Modify the tool as needed before application.Update 6-21-13:I used one of these on my Tankless Water Heater exhaust Vent as it had a large space around it and there was plenty of room for nesting in the exhaust and in the compartment. Since I need to access the heater switch to turn it on and off, the screen cover would come off the exhaust port. The exhaust pipe itself has a larger-holed screen within. I ended up screwing the supplied spring to the approximate center of the screen cover to shorten the spring and improved retention then hooking the spring to the built in internal screen (with a just-found previously provided screen-spring tool). The screen stays on now when I open the decorative unit side cover.The manufacturer legally has to tell you not to cover vents (to keep out wasps), but, as long as you periodically check and clean the screen it in no way restricts air flow. The decorative side cover keeps the screen centered in the exhaust hole, to screen it off from invaders and the spring retains the exhaust screen cover when the side panel is opened.There is also louvered intake venting. I ordered a large flat SS screen and cut it to size over the internal louvers with metal snips. There is plenty of air space but no place for wasps or mud daubbers. This solved my problem with the Tankless Water Heater unit. I bought the preformed screen for my RV air heater and it fit perfectly. If you are concerned about restricting air flow, just inspect it when you go through your set-up list and use a can of compressed air (Costco) to spray it clear of dust as you like. If you do not have a wasp problem don't use them. Hope this helps someone.
summary: Great item for RV's, defective and I had difficulties with my use

reviewText: Fast shipping.  Fit and works as expected.  A little difficult to attach the spring but it was possible.  The next time I have to install it I will use a stainless steel tie wire.
I got this because my dealer said we need to keep wasps mice and other critters  out it works as it says took a little to get on but look great

Purchased for my 2004 RV unit.  Easy to install and keeps the bugs out.  Come with its own installation tool. Just one thing to remember it to keep the installation tool with you at all time.  Cover do slid down and may need to be adjusted . No problemwith them................Would recommend

Quick, Free, Amazon Prime shipping to my door.  Product was a easy install, no tricks to it.  Take your time after reading the direction and it may take 45 seconds each to install.Downside if there is one is that they are sold in twin packs, where as I needed three (two for the furnace and one for the tankless water heater), but now I have an extra should I ever need it and can remember where I put it.These are an inexpensive investment when you consider the cost and frustration of wasp or other critters nesting in these exhaust vents.

These were so easy to install on our RV Trailer. The instructions were not quite clear, but there is a YouTube video on this product that shows how simple they are to install. It comes with the little tool that you need to stretch out the little spring that holds the screens in place.

These little screens really do work to keep the mud daubbers from moving in but...if you have a new RV, make sure you take them off prior to taking your rig in for any repairs. Most of the manufacturers say they void your warranty because they restrict air flow. Well, so do those pesky mud daubbers!
Works with the Heartland 2013 Cyclone. Keeping out the bugs and mice. Easy to install and came in unopened new condition.
Recommended by our RV mechanic.  It's not wasp season anymore, but I am ready for when it is.  Fairly easy to install after I stared at the instructions for 5 minutes.
These are very easy to install and keep the criters out of the sensitive RV systems.  I had a wasp issue that this solved.

I've got a Suburban furnace (model NT16S, if curious) and while these do fit the diameter of the openings, and the springs hold them on, with the suburban design, there is a big open gap at the bottom underneath the bottom screen.  It's the way the outside plate is molded.. it's raised most of the way around, except from about 5 o'clock to 7 o'clock.  There the screen bridges over the open gap and defeats the purpose.... any bug that wanted in could get in.  (Granted, it would stop a mouse.)You'd be better off, if you have this design, getting a rectangular one that covers the whole plate.  That's what I'll try next.Still giving it 2 stars because I'm sure they'd work fine on a different model, but they should say what models these fit.
We bought a used trailer that was missing just one of these screens. This screen matched the other one exactly. Fit perfectly.
If you have an RV this is a must have to keep out unwanted guest such as wasp, dirt dobbers, flies and all the other flying pest out there!  Easy installation and comes with the tool to install them!

Keeps those pesky dirt dobbers and wasps out of where I tell them endlessly not to go they listen as well as little kids it seems, Really the furnaces is not a nice place with the electric sparker and all that heat. I know in the winter warmth can be nice but not hundreds of degrees burning your wasp wings off. Oh well I like how it comes with a little notched tool to attach the springs and easy to attach keeps those little guys from blocking the exhaust and fumigating your trailer with Co2.

This screen fit fine but the mounting equipment leaves a great deal to be desired. It relies on very weak, loosely wound metal springs that are supposed to connect to the screen on one side and then hook around the vents of the unit to hold them in place. They provide a tool to help you complete this hooking maneuver - which doesn't really work well. Since you have to open the panel on the RV and access the back side of the vents to actually hook these springs, it would have been far better to provide a long thin screw and flat washer that you could just push through the screen and attach to the vent. The current mounting is rather loose so I'm a bit nervous about how well it will remain in place. I suspect I will find a long screw or use some caulk and mount it more securely. Overall, assuming the screen actually prevents bugs from entering, it will be a good investment.
summary: Not thrilled with the mounting hardware

reviewText: This was a little tricky to put on but with patience and a friend we got it on. So far it has stayed on my rV.

reviewText: Fits perfectly over the opening to protect and held on by a pretty good spring.  The edges are basically perfectly flat so there aren't little openings and it sits flat on the cover as expected.

reviewText: Easy and fast to install . If you don't have one installed on your RV you will have problems and at the most inconvenient time. Made from stainless steel so it will last you a lifetime.

Works wish it was a little flatter sticks out pretty far but it really keeps all the dirt dobbers and wasps out from where they just know they shouldn't be but like little kids don't listen. Attaches with springs and even comes with tool to attach the springs.

Even so, she normally has a tear in the gloves when we're through.  I'm the one wrestling to attach and detach the coupling at the rv tank's outlet, so that effort just shreds these things.I picked up some nitrile gloves on sale at Harbor Freight for 77 cents for 10; they're much stronger and puncture-resistant and are what Camco should be making these Dump Gloves out of, in my opinion.

reviewText: I travel all summer. I am dumping tanks a few times a week. I need a disposable glove to keep my hands from getting dirty with waste so I can toss them and get in the truck to drive off to my next stop.These I would not consider nothing more than cheap thin plastic gloves. Baggie sandwich bags would work as good and fit as good. Maybe even work better as baggies dont rip as easy as these. Save your money and the frustration.They dont fit, they rip so easy and usually fall of half way through and are ripped. So I end up having to wash up in the end like I never used any gloves at all.  I would buy good latex gloves that fit snug and wont rip so easily.
they work great and well needed. I have this carton of 50 gloves placed inside one of my outside compartment. the container has stick on tabs. price was good and quick shipping.

Purchased these glove to use when dumping my tank on my RV.  I was not very satifiedy with this product.  The problem that I had was that before you could get them on you hands the glove would come apart and either they would rip at the finger holes or just come apart putting them on.  They are very thin to use and I believe one size fits all. When I did use them I ended up using several gloves just to get the tanks emptied.I ended up buying a box of rubber gloves to use.  That were 100% better then these very thin gloves. Sorry, I would not recommend this product for dumping your tanks..
These are simply a plastic bag with fingers.  They are worth maybe $1.00/pkg.  If you are careful they work great.

Too light.  Flimsy and just about useless.  Great for new RV/Camper owners that are afraid they'll get their hands dirty while dumping their RV/Camper tanks.  They don't fit well, slide around on your hands.
To thin. Ripped before the job was done. I tossed them and got a heavier glove. Don't waste your money.

I only wish I had purchased this in the beginning.  I am pulling an 18 foot box trailer with a Dodge 3500 (much larger tow vehicle than required) and didn't think I needed a weight distributing hitch.  After buying an expensive heavy duty receiver and ball, I found that although the trailer towed fine, it also caused a lot of ride issues in the truck, especially when the road surface had dips or was rough.  I looked at a used Eaz Lift hitch, but found it was missing parts.  Then I checked on Amazon and found that I could buy a new hitch for little more than was being asked for the used one.  This hitch seems like a great value.  It is relatively easy to set up and the ride when towing is much improved.  The instructions make the initial installation sound a little more difficult than it really is.  The only real problem for most owners is that they won't have the tools required to adequately tighten the large bolts that hold the hitch together.

The dealer wanted to charge me $800 to purchase and install this from them.  Hopped onto amazon and with a video or two from youtube I became a pro in about 2 minutes.  Very glad I read through the entire post.  I almost bought the version without the shank but I definitely needed it so I'm glad I bought the right one.  What a difference this makes in towing a trailer.  I pull a 5200 lb trailer with an 06 Nissan Armada and can almost not even tell it's there.  Great price.  Great innovation.
Used on 2007 Nissan Xterra and works great. Quick to install. Easy to remove. Great to used with sway control.

We got a new to us Travel Trailer.  It was easy to set up once you have the right size tools.  The guys at the RV shop helped me out because you will need some large sockets (1 1/8 in).  It's very heavy and well made.  The instructions are a bit hard to read but I watched a few videos on you tube and that helped me get it all figured out.  Does a nice job.  I think, however I'll be buying the sway control bar to add on to it.

Oh well, I never would of expected that.Works well and with the addition of Air Bags to my truck it rides like a dream with the trailer behind me... Very smooth ride.

reviewText: as it states it was stolen right out of the receiver. my stupidy for leaving it on the truck. the new one is an exact replacment. and the price was a lot cheaper than camping world or any one else.it even came with the torsion arm lift pipe which is longer than the origional, which is a big help gices you more leverage.. thanks much///

reviewText: very heavy duty and very well made. easy to install and makes a real big difference towing. also a fantastic price.

This is a MUST HAVE for any camper.  There is nothing like being able to see what is flowing out of your holding tanks when using the black water flush to be sure the tanks are rinsed clean.  Well made and no leaks ever!!
it can be very useful to see what is flowing and how much.  solid lockup, no leaks, is build sturdy enough for the task at hand.
Needed a little more clearance for my new Valterra F02-4350 Black 'Flush King' Reverse RV Flush Valve. Attached to trailer dump outlet and I just leave it on there.
No problems, just don't love (five stars) anything associated with black tank. I deem it nesessary to have clear fittings at both ends of sewer hose for obvious reasons.

The Camco 55343 RV 30 Amp female replacement receptacle seems to be very well made . . . with one exception.  The instuctions indicate you should strip the wire insulation exposing the copper strands for 1".  It is my believe what it does not explain is you should fold this exposed copper end in half prior to placing under the wire clamp in the housing.Failure to do this leaves two serious issues:The single row of copper strands of a 10 guage wire will be loose under the terminal clamps even when tightened all the way down.  This can result in electrical arcing, loss of power, or damage to your electrical equipment.  This is of course assuming the stress clamp was securely tightened so all the wires would not all together pull out and possibly and cause bodily injury.If you follow the instructions exposing 1" and placing it under the clamp, it will also leave a significant amount of uninsulated wiring exposed within the housing for no purpose other than to possibly short out against one another.Thus, the way around this concern and to have a great connection under each terminal clamp is to fold the 1" exposed copper strands in half, leaving 1/2" of copper.  You will find it securely fastens under the clamp as well as has a significant amount of surface area for the electric current to pass through.I would purchase again, but am disappointed in the poor instructions/loose design of the terminal clamps.  I hope this helps.

Keeping the mp3 player, a GPS, cell phone and a AA battery charger all going on a trip, this is a lifesaver.  The LEDs tell you how healthy your (car) battery is to keep charging everything, and this unit has a heft to it to keep it in place.On a more personal note:  Since Volkswagen didn't learn where to appropriately place cupholders until circa 2007 (my car is older, with cupholders inches from the Cig Lighter - and smack dab in front of the radio), this adapter feels perfectly at home, despite the somewhat short cord.Highly recommended.

This is a nice device for people who need a lot of power/charging functionality.  The main issue? The USB ports installed in the unit do not provide rated current.  My issue? Generally for whatever reason the blackberry will charge first and then only after completely full only then will the iPhone charge. Plug in just one and either works perfect.My bet is that to maximize profit the manufacturer installs a 1000mA converter and labels one port 1000 and the other 500... ASSEMBLY: First you have to attach the high pressure grease hose to the head of the gun, making sure you use the supplied copper gasket before tightening down. Then, you have to attach your inlet coupler to the bottom of the handle, making sure that you use teflon plumbers tape on the coupler threads.INSTALLING GREASE CARTRIDGES: First, remove the pump head from the grease cylinder. Second, pull the grease loader (Also called follower) all the way back and then lock it into place. The side which has the simple pull off cap, that end goes into the grease cylinder. Then you pull off the sardine like lid, and then screw down the pump head onto the grease cylinder. Then you release the grease loader.PRIMING: Every time you install a new grease cartridge, you have to prime the gun. The quick way to prime, is to operate the gun slowly, until grease flows out of the coupler. If that does not work, you may have air pockets in the system. The manual recommends that you open the filler valve on the pump head by two turns out, holding the gun with the discharge hose pointing up. Then you close the filler valve once the air has been removed.OPERATING: To operate, attach the coupler at the end of the high pressure hose, to a zerk fitting. As you depress the trigger, air enters the chamber, which pushes the piston with the plunger. The grease that is under pressure from the plunger, opens the check valve and delivers one shot of lubricant. The more you depress the trigger, the faster this process operates, thus increasing grease flow. The gun is designed to have a full speed limit, as to limit damage to bearing seals and dust boots.EXPERIENCE: I think this gun weighs a bit much, but it has to be constructed of durable metals, in order for it to be commercial built. The body of the gun is constructed of a durable metal. The handle has a really nice rubber grip that I like, while the trigger is made of plastic. On both ends of the high pressure hose, heavy duty springs can be found. These springs are used to make sure the hose doesn't kink, I find they kind of get in the way, but I can get used to them, just have to have a good grip on the hose is all.I find its best to just let the bottom of the gun rest against the ground, this way you don't have to hold the weight for long periods of time. I like the 30" HP hose on this gun a lot more then the 17" hose on my old gun, as it allows me to get deeper into a place that has a grease zerk. Using this gun is so easy! All I have to do is press on the trigger a little bit, and grease will automatically be pumped into the grease fittings. No more hand fatigue, and no more useless time wasted, trying to fill the fitting with grease.One of the things I like that Lincoln Industrial did, is they incorporated their cover cap, into this gun as well! This is a great option, because when you are done using the gun, you can slide the cap onto the end of the coupler, keeping the grease from getting contaminated by dirt.CONCLUSION: This is the best grease gun I have ever bought! Not only is it made by a awesome brand like Lincoln Industrial, but its extremely durable. Despite a few of the negatives, I really like this gun. I can tell I am going to get a lot more use out of this gun, then my old one. This gun is not necessary for the home-owner per say, but is absolutely necessary for any small engine or automotive shop. 5 out of 5

reviewText: Excellent construction and as the saying goes you get what you pay for.  I struggled with manual grease guns bought at big box stores that just were not quality products.  Decided to take the plunge with a quality product.  Paying for quality is painful...until the first time you need it.  This gun really delivers and the hose is long enough you don't struggle to much.  The only thing I struggled with is that the nozzle has to be screwed on and off the zerk fitting which is great in that you don't have to push the nozzle on the fitting so grease does not ooze out.  The tough part is turning the nozzle so it locks onto the zerk when there is any grease on the nozzle body.  This product could be improved with more pronounced knurling on the nozzle for better grip.  This would add pennies to the cost of the unit if anything and earn it that fifth star. reviewText: This inexpensive replacement air filter fits my 2006 Honda Civic EX just as well as the OEM product, and costs a lot less.  Engine power qualitatively feels the same as with a new OEM air filter.The engine air filter is one of the easiest things to replace under the hood, and makes a big, immediate difference in performance versus an old clogged filter.  Replacing this filter is simple auto maintenance that the average consumer can and should do themselves.  No tools required, it takes me about 3-5 minutes to install in my Civic.My only qualm is that the box states a filter lifespan shorter than the Honda replacement recommendation (11,500 miles vs 15,000 miles, if memory serves correctly).  However, actual filter lifespan is largely based on environmental conditions, and even on that accelerated replacement schedule, DIY filters from amazon will cost less than having an auto shop do it for you.Recommended.

Preparation is the key to any succssful mechanical projects & coolant change is no exception. Try to make sure the following are in order:  (1) Buy a new drain cock valve, as most drain cock valves are plastic & can become brittle under long term exposure to heat, you don't want to be stuck with a broken or cracked drain cock once your coolant has been drained, (2) Check the condition of your radiator cap, if the rubber gasket show signs of cracking it is time for a new one, (3) Most importantly, locate the air release valve on your engine block, without opening the air release valve you will not be able to drain the coolant from the engine block. Air release valve's location varies depending on the manfuacture, but I found the easiest way to locate it is trace the upper radiator hose back to the engine block. (4) Turn temperature control to full hot, need to drain coolant out of the heater core as well. (5) Buy the manufacture specified coolant, do not use after market universal coolant to save a few bucks.Once the old coolant is completely drained & you have replaced the radiator cap & drain cock valve as needed, fill the system up with the air release valve in the "open" position.  This way you allow the coolant to push the air out of the engine block to minimize air bubbles getting trapped in it.  Once the coolant starts to seeping out, close the valve (12mm wrench on Acura/Honda). Mount the funnel full of coolant to the top radiator with the correct adaptor, then run the engine at approximately 2000 rpm until the cooling fan kicks in, then just stand back & observe if there's any air bubbles burping thru the funnel.Tip: After turning the car off, leave the funnel attached until the car completely cools down because coolant will contract & consequently will suck more fluid out of the funnel.  I squeezed the radiator hose really hard & fast for a dozen times & that seemed to purge even more air bubbles out of the system.In summary, I replaced coolant for all 3 of my vehicles within the last 2 days: Dodge RAM, Acura RL & Toyota Prius. And thanks to this funnel there're no air bubble trapped in any one of them, which we all know can cause erratic idling as well as over heating.

Oil, filter and tire changes are taken for granted as periodic maintenance necessities. Others, as wiper blade replacement, are more often neglected until their declining function forces attention. But your dimming headlights are such a gradual process that it's easy to go completely unaddressed though degraded lighting poses a real safety threat. The clear plastic covering the headlights is exposed to chemicals splashed up from the road surface and acid rain which is constantly baked on by the intense heat of modern bulbs. Oxidation happens until it looks like it's wrapped in wax paper and your headlight beams are severely compromised. This kit and 20 to 30 minutes of your time can render those lenses crystal clear and looking like new.  The instructions note that you will need to have access to an electric or battery powered drill.  The kit comes with a disc pad holder that fits into the drill. Small circular sandpaper discs are attached to the pad via a velcro-like backing. There are supplied several discs of 500 grit, 800 grit, a "trizak" disc for further polishing, a foam pad and and a small amount of polish/rubbing compound cream.  Before beginning work, the area around the headlight needs to be protected with recommended masking tape. 3M Kits I'd purchased in the past included this tape, but this particular kit does not.  (Kit #39014 also sold on Amazon includes 25' of tape but costs about $7 more. If you already have suitable masking tape from a painting project you can save a few dollars with this kit though.)  I used blue masking tape found in big box home supply stores in the painting section.  Two layers are recommended to assure no damage happens to the adjacent car body paint surrounding your headlights.  Once taped, the lens should be washed with soap and water to remove any dirt. Attach the first disc and with light to medium pressure go over the entire lens, making certain not to stay in one spot too long which would heat and damage the plastic. You might feel some uncertainty and wonder if you're destroying your lenses because they become a milky white. Be certain to periodically pat the disc to remove any residue dust buildup. When you have a consistent surface, move on to the next finer grit, the white 800 disc. This refines the surface though still an opaque white. The lens should be wet with a spray bottle or damp cloth and kept wet while using the Trizak disc. Finally use the foam pad attachment with dime sized amounts of the polishing cream. It's best to put the cream at the center of the disc and then slide it around the lens before you turn on the drill to have an even distribution and less spatter.  If you don't rush through the process and do each step completely, you should now have headlights that look completely new. I've used perhaps 5 of these kits over time and the results are consistently amazing. There are kits that are easier to use with only fluids you apply by hand and elbow grease. They work ok, depending on the degree of residue and oxidation you have to remove. But if you want a professional looking restoration and you have a little patience, this kit provides outstanding results. Just be certain to purchase the necessary masking tape and try not to rush through the process.
summary: The most effective kit I've used to clarify cloudy headlights

reviewText: Now that I've finished using the kit on my car, I can't say I'm entirely blown away with the results, though I will concede that my case was a particularly difficult one.  For more common situations, the kit would have worked better.What made my case difficult was the following:- My headlights didn't match.  Due to an accident I recently had one headlight replaced. This new headlight was crystal clear and beautiful.  The other headlight was 10 years old, had faded and yellowed.  I managed to improve the look of the old headlight, but the fundamental problem is when many lamps age, they also yellow and harden as well.  So even though you polish the outside of the lamp, the discoloration which has occurred over time affects the material below the surface as well.  Try as I might, there was just NO matching the old headlight to the new one.  It just wasn't going to happen.  I wound up with a slightly yellow, highly polished 10 year old headlight to go with my crystal clear highly polished brand new lamp.  Less bad than before, but no where near the look of the new lamp.- My headlights were an odd contour.  I drive a 2000 Toyota Celica and these headlights are very elongated with a big "bump" right in the center.  This made it very difficult to get a thorough, uniform polishing of the headlight.  The polishing pad supplied with this kit is about 3" in diameter and flat.  This works great for flat surfaces.  However if your headlight has odd contours, it's going to give you trouble.I takes a LONG time to get a good polish on even an ideally shaped headlight.  The task is generally manageable if your headlight is a convenient shape (like the Taurus in the picture - small and round).  However if the lamp is larger and/or oddly shaped, you have quite a task ahead of you.  After about 30-40 minutes of work on a SINGLE headlight, I called it quits.  The headlight is now better, though nowhere near matching the other lamp.If I had two identical headlights of the same age (as most people will), the situation would have been better.  Still though, for the price, this is a good kit and a solid value.
summary: A valiant effort, beware of these caveats

reviewText: After using this product, my headlights looked brand new! I've used several "restoration systems" before but this is the only one that worked and it worked great!Not only did my car look great after this, but headlamps performed much better at night too!Follow the directions closely and you will not be disappointed.

"Holy frickin' moly!" comes close.  "Miracle"?  Perhaps a little too powerful.I plugged a pair of Sylvania Silverstar Ultra headlights into my 1996 Subaru Legacy sedan and . . . bleah.  Where's that intense white near-HID light I paid for?!A non-abrasive headlight restoration kit yielded negligible results.  The Manny-Moe-Jack chain wanted at least half a C-note as did my trusted shadetree mechanic.  When I asked him about the 3M kit, he admitted, "It's what we use."  Next stop: Amazon.com.I read the reviews, watched the video and gambled the price at the local O'Reilly (I was impatient) where the counter guy continued the litany of praise.  Armed with my Ryobi 18 volt drill and the rest of the required tools, I plunged right in and restored the headlight with the worst corrosion, including a snowy white oxidized silhouette of a mountain range along the bottom.  I was skeptical, believing nothing would remove the oxidation.  Amazingly, it sanded right out.  Upon completion, I stepped back and reveled for a few moments in the difference.  After a battery recharge (yes, it takes the power of 2 battery packs per headlight), I finished the task and topped it off with a quick trip to an automated car wash to remove the restoration residue.  A bottle of 3M's lens cleaner and protectant is on its way from Amazon.comAnd, yes, I've posted a before-and-after photo.

This has got to be one of the best if not the best headlight restoration systems you can buy. I have used them on dozens of headlights and vehicles over the years and without fail, they produce excellent results that look good as new from about a foot or more every time and substantially increase headlamp output.The key with this system is using a corded drill (I seriously doubt any battery operated drill could even handle one headlight with the amount of time this takes) and being very, very patient. The instructions repeatedly remind the user that time spent on each individual step will reduce time needed at the next step. What they mean to say is, "When you think you might be done, keep sanding. Then when you really think you're done, keep sanding more."Make sure you tape off (two layers at least) the painted parts of your vehicle that you do not want damaged by rotating sandpaper.There are usually enough supplies in the kit to do 2-6 headlights.
summary: This is probably my 10th one. Never get tired of using these

reviewText: Great product.  Super-easy to use, with detailed instructions.  The correct and ONLY way to restore headlights is to sand and wetsand them, and then use a rubbing and polishing compound.  All the gimmicks with using toothpaste and that is rubbish.Definitely buy this.  3M always delivers.

I first used a cheap non-power-tool refinishing kit,Turtle Wax T-240KT Headlight Lens Restorer Kit, and came to the conclusion that I needed to sand more off (than you can by hand) to get the clouding and oxidation off my headlights.  So I turned to this 3M kit.  Take your time buffing each step, making sure to evenly and completely sand each stage because it makes all the difference when moving to the next stage.  If the sandpaper gets gummed up make sure to switch out sanding pads or you'll leave lines.  Works great.  Note: the Turtle Wax kit may work for you if all you have is light clouding not deeper oxidation like I had.
summary: Makes a Big Difference, Take your Time on Each Step

reviewText: This is the second headlight restorer I have tried.  The other one by Turtle Wax did a fine job, but its not as good as this one designed to be used with a drill.  This really does do the best job you are probably ever going to get out of a home kit.  It's a little more work than the kind that promise a wipe on wipe off deal, but it is well worth it.  And don't be fooled by the look of the headlight after the first round where it looks even worse than before.  You start off dry sanding it with the roughest sandpaper included and it really messes it up.  But it's necessary, and it sets it up for the final wet buffing that loosens up everything and removes it.  The directions are clear and straight forward, and it really does take from 45 min to an hour to do one headlight.  Don't be in any rush, it will pay off in the end.  My headlights look better than they have in years and has made in a big difference in the beams on them... Highly recommended.. : )
summary: A Little More Work...But The Best

reviewText: Believe the reviewers, the 3M kit does work. The sanding attachment is great.I used it on a 17-year-old Volvo station wagon with severely yellowed headlight lenses. It removed the yellowing completely, and most (but not all) of the cloudiness. The lenses are much improved. I consider the kit highly worthwhile, and the project a success.Be sure to watch the YouTube video before using, and they are not kidding about taping around the lights. Do it.I give the 3M kit a 4-star for one reason only: The kit is a bit stingy with the final stage "lens clarifying solution." The complete amount is contained in a single wet-wipe-style packet. I really could have used more for the Volvo.I was able to use the final-stage sander (the "Pryzbitel" disk or something like that) and sponge buffer on a second vehicle, an 8-year-old truck with visible but less severe clouding. Using skills gained in the first job (and chemicals from another kit) it does look new.So overall, yes, the kit does what it says it will.

It took about an hour to do both headlights. They look like brand new. It is a miracle product. You can't go wrong buying this kit. It even removed the surface scratches that I had on the headlights. Must have product.

It worked great to remove the hazy and dull lights.  I think this model only works for plastic not glass. Check it out for your self
