reviewText: Well worth the time and money
This is a very nice kit that was easy to use with straight forward instructions. Made a huge difference on my headlights. To me about 45 minutes per headlight.

This kit is easy to use and it doesn't a fantastic job but the results are temporary lasting about 10 months before they start looking cloudy again.They need to add a lens treatment to the kit that preserves and protects the lens.

Great kit. It took me about 90 minutes per headlight. I took mine out of the car to make it easier. It was very easy on my e39 BMW. They look like new now. You just have to be patient and use light pressure only. And I did it all wet sanding. I don't think the directions stated that you should use wet sanding. That's very important. Otherwise you'll melt the plastic if you're not careful. It also sands much much faster and you use fewer sanding discs.Afterwards, I used the Blue Magic 730-6 Headlight Lens Sealer to hopefully protect the lens a little bit. It did seem to help. Water beads up very nicely on the lens now and ice doesn't stick to it so solidly. I'm happy with my purchase.Also, note that not all headlight lenses are made the same. My BMW has a very hard polycarbonate lens. After 14 years, it was only slightly aged. It took a LOT more sanding than on my parents 10 and 8 year old VW Jettas. My BMW had some kind of really hard coating on the lens that needed to be sanded through. Then it polished up much quicker.I used a 12v Milwaukee cordless mini drill on my lenses. The small size was very convenient and my two batteries worked fine for my headlights. In the case of polishing, more power is not always better.
summary: Nice kit. Worked well on my BMW.

reviewText: My headlight lenses had finally gotten bad enough that something had to be done.  There are two choices - replace the parts for a huge cost (parts) or restore them with an over-the-counter product.There are lots of automotive products that promise the world and deliver nothing.  I researched this product and learned that it basically polishes the plastic back to a high gloss.  Just like preparing a surface for painting, progressively finer sand-paper is used to remove the scratches from the previous paper and gradually get the surface shiny again.The 3M Headlight Lens Restoration System kit has the following components:- P500 Discs (6)- P800 Discs (4)- P3000 Pad (1)- Compound (small packet)- Sponge- Drill PadThe approach to restoring the headlight covers is simple.  Use a drill to carefully rough up and gradually polish the surface.  Following the instructions, I masked off the surrounding area with a few layers of tape to prevent the sand paper from taking paint off.Then I set aside half of each grade paper for each lens.  I retrieved some extra paper of the same grades from my personal supply to start each round, because my lenses seemed really bad and I wanted to stretch the kit as best I could.I knew the process described in the instructions and the supplies provided to do the job would work, but I was still very pleased when I finished - they end result is amazing.  The key is not to run the drill too fast and to follow the instructions to the letter.  If you do, the results are worth the $15 (give or take) and the hour's time you will spend!I provided pictures and the before and after really tells the story!

Before you buy this, don't.  Get the 3M 39045, which has the top coat included in the kit!First, the before and after pictures are not an exaggeration.  The system will indeed produce a clear lens by following the directions.  That part of the process I would give 5 stars to.  The directions are very clear, but I would add a few items of my own, having made some mistakes.1) If possible, remove the covers from the vehicle and secure to a stable work surface!!  If not, put a triple layer of masking tape around the edges of the lens to protect everything within 1.5 inches of the cover. (Use the green 3M tape or blue if you have to, NOT the tan kind!!)  If you are inexperienced with using a pad mounted in a drill, you will have trouble holding the pad on the surface at first and you'll end up with nicks and edge marks around it.2) Use very, very light pressure on the first stage.  Let the sandpaper do the work.  This will help you keep more of the pad in contact while you control the pad's movement. Plus, it will help you avoid digging in the edges of the pad and causing very difficult-to-remove marks or burns.3) Use a slow speed at first.  The instructions give a min/max RPM recommendation, but I found the pad difficult to control when it was spinning that fast, plus it was very easy to cause burn marks.  Once I dropped the speed to slow, it became very easy.4) The first pass is what does all the yellow removal, so take your time, use up all the sanding disks (3 per lens), and wipe the lens often to see where you've missed.  If you dig into the lens a little, then concentrate on that spot more.  The second pass will not correct deep scratches, so work them out on the first round.5) The remaining steps are simply to remove the previous step's sanding marks.  Use light to medium pressure.  Wipe often.6) With the final tri-zact pad, it takes light pressure.  Be careful not to damage this pad, since there's only one in the kit.  It had no problem going the distance, but be cautious around the little nibs that stick up from the lens, etc.  Keep the pad wet, and also keep the lens wet.  The instructions say "damp", but you'll have better results with more moisture (to a point.)  Rinse the slurry off and wipe with a terry cloth often.  If you have a light handy, shine it at an angle to help see any sanding marks you've missed.7) With the sanding complete, you'll need to polish.  The sponge pad is very absorbent, but a little compound goes a long way. The first time you add compound, use the recommended dime size and work it lightly around and into the pad with your finger (drill turned off.)  Then put another dime sized drop on and place the drill on the lens lightly before turning it on.  Same as sanding, but now you're using medium to firm pressure for the first 4-5 passes.  Cover the lens in repeating passes left/right and up/down until you've been over it 4-6 times (per directions.)  Use reduced pressure for the last couple passes.  You will probably have to add compound a couple of times, but after that there will be plenty in the pad.  I only had to add it once on the second lens.  If it slings off or builds up, you've got too much on the pad (just squeeze a little out on a rag.)8) Finally, use a microfiber cloth to remove the hazy compound.You are NOT done, however, because this kit only cleans off the lens.  It does NOTHING to protect the lens! It's going to yellow again within a year if you don't protect it somehow.3M makes a protectant product, which is included in another kit - 3M 39045, which is an overall better choice than this one (the protectant and green tape are included in that kit.)You can also clear coat it with a clear gloss spray-can finish (as long as it's an exterior grade finish.)  You've already got it taped up, so mask off the area and go for it.  That will last much longer than the 3M protectant.  Don't forget to do an extra prep cleaning before spraying.That's it.  My total time was about 1 hour for two lenses on a Toyota Corolla.  Overall, I'm satisfied, but I wish I'd known about the more complete kit for just $4 more...
summary: Great results - Still needs a top coat to be completely restored

reviewText: There's enough information in these reviews, coupled together with online video demonstrations, to do the job yourself and get good results with this kit (plus Meguiar's PlastX Clear Plastic Cleaner and Polish as a final step).  I just did it with my 1500 rpm cordless drill and two charged batteries and I'm very pleased.  I saved a bunch of money compared to having a pro do it for me too.I did, unfortunately, slightly burn the lens once from a bit too much friction when I held the rotary disc in a spot too long.  The fix was to put the previous, tougher grit disc back on and rebuff that spot and then go back to work more carefully.The job itself took about an hour for each lamp from start to finish and they look new again.  Highly recommended...

If you use this right, it'll give you whole new headlights.  I love it.  Used it on an older gm truck with the rectangular headlights and the difference was amazing.  Just follow the instructions and spend a little time.  don't try to rush it or it isn't going to work as well.  I've tried the knockoff brands and this is hands down better.  worth the $
I am already a big fan of 3M. This product holds up. Get a good drill and follow the directions. You will be happy.

If your goal is to remove the top yellowing layer of the lens inexpensively, this product may be your most cost effective bet. The project took quite a bit long than I estimated because I had to deplete and switch multiple batteries on my cordless drill. To get the sanding and polish with a cordless drill, expect to have a higher quality model with multiple batteries -- not an entry level model.The before and after difference on an 11 year old Mercedes ML320 is quite striking. The yellow is gone and driver visibility improved. There are the fine and somewhat deeper crazing in the plastic that may be be removed by this kit.  In fact, the crazing could be too deep to remove in any manner without structurally weakening the lens.In the past, I have used a variety of tools from Dremel along with conventional drills to sand, shape, cut and bore holes in plastic.  Most this work took place at room temperature.  These actions often lead to melting plastic that gums up the tool at hand. For this restoration project, I did it in a windy environment with 34 degree ambient temperature.  It worked very despite that discomfort in the cold. There was no evidence of thermal warping. With the most coarse sandpaper, I could apply significant downward force while sliding across the surface, removing large amounts of yellow plastic shavings in the process.One downside is that the circular design of the wheel makes it difficult to get into corners.  Something with a triangular sanding surface like the Dremel MultiMax would be better.
summary: Works well, especially in cold weather - doesn't address deeper crazing in plastic

reviewText: The included instructions are very clear, and this product did a decent job of clearing up the faded/hazed headlights on my 2002 Volkswagen Passat. The system uses progressively finer grit sandpaper disks to buff out the lenses. The disks attach to any power drill/screwdriver. It took me 30-45 minutes from start to finish. My lenses have rehazed after about 18 months of driving, so it's probably about time to give them another polish.

My Lexus had very "foggy" headlamps due to being parked outside almost every day.  I was going to get another car, so I bought this kit to "refurbish" my headlights so I could get top dollar for the trade in.  The headlights looked like new after I used this and the process was not as hard as I though it was after reading the long and detailed instructions that comes with this.  Only some scratches were visible after I did this.  The dealer gave me top dollar for my trade in so it worked very well for me.  I should have done this years ago.
summary: Fixed my Lexus IS-350 before I traded it in

reviewText: This is way more work than a wipe on polish, BUT, the results are amazing. This is one of those cases where you get what you pay for.
summary: I can see clearly now, the haze is gone..........

reviewText: this thing works great ! well that's if you put lots of elbow grease in action.  headlights are crystal clear !!i should have bought two of these since my 7 series BMW had extremely damaged headlights but i managed to keep sanding and cleaning the discs.  maybe four 500 grit discs per headlight would have been perfect (in my case anyways).A tip: use a layer of automotive tape on the paint and instead of keep adding layers of the automotive tape, use instead the gray threaded heavy duty cheap tape, i forget what its called but it leaves residue glue everywhere which is why you need the first layer of automotive tape.  this makes a nice protection for the paint.also don't forget to use a UV protectant after your done.  otherwise they'll turn yellow again.i used dupli color headlight restoration UV clearcoat spraywe'll see how long that lasts

This took me a little longer than just an hour to get my headlights perfect again. When I was done they were crystal clear and without any visible scratches. This just finishes a restoration job brilliantly.

I used this in hopes of getting my Miata's old passenger headlight to look as good as the new driver side one. It wasn't very cloudy in the first place but you can definitely notice the difference between the two.I followed the instructions down to the letter and after wet sanding with the 3000 grit disc for an eternity, the lens came out better than before. However, it also had a new feature that it didn't have before which are hundreds of minute and very fine scratches. It annoys me but I will just learn to live with it versus paying a pro $100ish for a slightly better job, or paying $250 for a replacement headlight.I should've started with the 3000 grit from the beginning instead of going the whole nine yards. But for a extremely clouded/hazed lenses, this will definitely remedy the headlight and bring it back to about 90% of the original condition. I had some extra material left and knocked out my roommate's corolla which had some clouding. Worked very well but as mentioned earlier, it left many fine scratches.Overall, would recommend and buy again
I got this item. It gets them back to new. And you don't pay alot of money for new head lights. It took me less than one hour to use it.  SW

Overall: Highly recommend the product. Quality of result is dependent on amount of sandingTips: The whole packet is designed to be used on one car. Take your time during each step and replace pads as needed. Be sure to tape the edges (I found blue painters tape worked fine) to prevent damage and don't allow the sanding disc to remain in one location for more than a few seconds (to prevent heat build up and discoloration).

There's a product being pushed on TV right now that claims to fix your old dingy headlights. Looked too good to be true so I checked it's reviews on Amazon and found the overall consensus was that it did not work. This 3M product showed up under suggested items and the reviews were good so I purchased it. To my amazement it took my cloudy yellowed 1997 Subaru headlights and made them look brand new! It was easy to do and the instruction video was all I needed to accomplish the task.(The print on the paper instructions was too small to read). My drill is a variable speed drill but it is not the kind that has a limiter on it. A bit tricky trying to keep it between 1200 and 1600 rpm.I could not be more impressed with the outcome of my lenses. Now I can see at night and I don't have to drive with my brights on.
I had a yellow glaze and now it's not so yellow. It didn't hold for very long. might of been me not using it properly

The headlights on my Caravan and F-350 were hazy so I purchased Meguiar's headlight restorer because a friend had recommended it. That didn't work at all. Then I purchased the Turtle Wax restorer based on reviews. It worked a little bit better than Meguiar's, but still not good enough. Then I purchased the 3M kit and it worked the best. Unfortunately, the drill I used was too powerful and caused some burn in on the Caravan headlights and I ended up just using various grits of wet automotive sandpaper. The sandpaper worked very well and produced excellent results. I would never spend another dime on the kits. All you really need is some wet automotive sandpaper and a spray bottle with water.
summary: Works the best out of all the ones I've tried

reviewText: Works as advertised, my lights were not bad but I wanted better night visibility so I used this to polish my lenses. Worked like a champ and took less than an hour.My lights didn't need much tape as when I opened the hood I missed most of the metal surrounding the lights, make sure to take your time and tape off, and use nice even pressure. I went over my lights a few more times than what was said to do and they sparkle like brand new.I added a set of new SilverStar bulbs and seeing at night is no longer an issue

Used this on my 2001 Honda Civic EX Coupe. Headlights were pretty glazed ("white looking"). This took me about half an hour to do properly, but the headlights look significantly clearer now. The difference is dramatic. Even using a drill, prepare for some physical exertion - holding the drill steady as you move it back and forth across the lens, and exerting pressure on it. It's worth it though - I am ordering a second one for my s/o. Highly recommended!

This does what it says: But there are a few things to keep in mind.1) Expect to spend 30 mins on each headlight if you want to do a good job.  Have extra batteries ready for your drill!  The quality of your finished work will be directly proportional to HOW MUCH time you spend on each grit of sandpaper.2) When you use the first sandpaper disk, you are literally removing the top layer of plastic on your headlight.  You will think you are ruining the lens.  And you are!  Intentionally!  But don't worry ... if you take time, it'll finish up looking like new.3) The reason your lenses haze over is due to UV damage from the sun.  While this product will remove the damaged upper layer of plastic on your lenses, bear in mind that the next layer down has, over the same time, suffered *some* damage, too.  It looks good now, but sooner than you think, it will haze over as well.  The deterioration has already begun!  So you should either be prepared to do this work every other year or so, OR get some anti-UV protectant for your lenses and METICULOUSLY apply it every time you wash your car.UPDATE -- TWO YEARS LATER --A little oxidation returned to my headlights, so I bought another 3M kit.  This time, it only took about 10 mins on each headlight to return them to "factory" condition.  (Still loving the product.)
Made my old headlight covers shine like new ones. However it requires patients to make it happen, thus you need to be detail when you grind.

I own a 2009 Tacoma and bought a 21' travel trailer.  I looked around for mirrors for the Taco but found that no one makes them, so had to go with "universal".  Bought these thinking that I needed something fast to bring the trailer home and I could always return them.  They work fine.  Once adjusted for your mirror(s) they can be clamped on and removed easily.  No scratching of my mirror backs and very little vibration at highway speed.  I was pleasantly surprised and will be keeping them (sold as singles, so be aware when ordering).
I tried 4 different mirrors and this is the best on our 2012 Honda Pilot. Its got a rubber strap and ratchet mechanism to get a nice firm fit. And the OEM mirror can still be used!

Great fit and very secure. No vibration on 700 mile trip...... I liked the price very much and will recommend to friends..... The straps slipped a bit with Armor-all on plastic so I secured with a small bungie cord on each mirror..... No movement at all.....

OMG what a difference these have made in manuevering our 36ft 5th wheel. They are super easy to attach and work beautifully. Very well made and sturdy. Excellent purchase. We have a 1995 Ford F350 with the standard stock mirrors...and these fit perfectly.

I'm a new travel trailer owner and I have to say once I strapped these big ol' mirrors on my confidence was greatly improved.  Easy to take on and off and stay put!  Had a friend with those "sleeve" kind and watched both of them come off and fly by me as he towed up ahead. Enhances your field of vision a LOT and that's what you need when you've added 24' to your vehicle!

these mirrors are extremely helpful. i pull a forty foot goose neck, that's 102" wide, so they greatly increase your rear visibility. as stated by another reviewer, it would have been nice for the mirrors to be flat glass instead of convex. distortion is a bit annoying, but not a throw-a-way detail. fit snug and very little vibration as earlier stated. good expenditure for the job at hand.

I am honestly shocked at how well these things work.  They're sold, easily adjusted, and strap on very securely.The convex mirror is large, clear, and not absurdly fish-eye as some towing mirrors are.One extremely minor caveat -- if you strap them down tight (as you should) & you have plastic mirrors (as many mirrors are), they will get quite warped/distorted while these are clamped on.  It isn't permanent with mine [so far], but who knows.
Hooked them up to my 01 F-150 mirrors and they strapped on easy and stayed right were on putt them .
I got two of these on amazon for les than the price of one at an RV dealer.  They work great and were very easy to install.  They are also very easy to remove and put back on as needed.

I tow a 33 ft. Travel Trailer with a 3500 Chevy Express van.  We drove in excess of 25,000 miles with these mirrors (and still going!).  I have intended to come back to Amazon and review many of the products we purchased in preparation for our trip around the country and today I had time while I was listening in to a conference call!  :)  These mirrors look a little clunky to me and I was unsure of how they would work.  I researched strap-on mirrors extensively before I purchased them and I have been VERY happy with their performance.  They have never wobbled or been unstable while I drove.  They provide a great additional mirror to be able to see into my towing blind spot.  Really the only reason I rated them 4 stars instead of 5 is that I think they look clunky.  They don't mesh well with the shape of my van's mirrors, but they fit, and they fit sturdily (is that a word?).  But they have the look that they are kind of jammed onto something they weren't designed for.  No big deal in the big picture, since they quite literally give you a "big picture" of what's behind you.  We have been very satisfied with these.
be sure you know that only one mirror is included in this price. bolts on good, gonna give it a try this weekend
just got this today, and put it on my truck.  works great, will never go blind again towing stuff.  very sturdy.  good price.

got these for the new rv so I could see around the trialer.  They work good and stay put, I didn't take them off the whole week we drove around without the trailer.  The only thing that would be better is a set of real tow mirrors but those were a few hundred bucks and I didn't want to shell out the cash for those at tht time.

We purchased this mirror after returning the clamp on mirror.  It is very easy to install (about 2 minutes per mirror once you get it adjusted for your vehicle) and very secure (we normally drive ~60mph and faced 40mph headwinds with no problems).  I do wish the mirror extended out a little farther to see around our trailer bettter, but that is pretty difficult to find.  The convex mirror one sit he one to get (imo better field of fiew than the flat).
summary: Great mirror, easy to install, very secure

reviewText: My work truck is a 2001 Dodge Ram 2500. On occasion, I have to tow a 26 foot long converted toy hauler. This mirror gives me the extra distance I need on either side of the truck to be able to have a view of the side and back of the trailer when making turns and backing. If you put them on without hooking up your trailer, you won't be able to tell that there's a difference. Once that trailer gets hooked up though, you'll notice you can actually see. It's quite nice.Easy on, easy off. Built in little ratchet helps get the mirrors extra snug. Mirrors seem to be SLIGHTLY convex, which gives you a bit of a better view.Looking over at two mirrors is disconcerting at first, until you get your brain used to looking at the OUTSIDE mirror. This isn't the mirror's fault... it is the brain's fault. =PFew things: If you have plastic backed mirrors... like the trim molding that you often see on the tops of truck bumpers... the stuff that gets faded after too much exposure to the sun... yeah, that stuff. If you have that, the rubber gripper things from the straps will leave stains. I don't know if it's the agent they use to release the rubber from the molds or what, but it definitely leeches into the plastic. Some armor all on the rest of your mirror should blend it in.If your truck mirrors already have a vibration, these things will vibrate quite a bit. I don't know how comfortable I'd be relying on them for vision on a bumpy freeway at 55 mph.That being said, I'd highly recommend these things any day of the week.
I have a 2011 f150 and they fit great very easy to tighten with the ratchet system, I will let you know if they fall off but so far everything works great

Driving a Toyota Highlander and purchasing a 22 foot camper last summer- I have tried 4 different mirrors before finally trying these.  Hands down these are the best yet and I have finally found the right mirrors.  We just completed a 2000 mile trip on busy highways and navigating in big cities and I do love these mirrors.  You can try different mirrors or just read the reviews and try these.  You will be please with these- I know I am! Its so nice to find and get to use a great product!
summary: After trying multiple different mirrors - these are the ones to get

reviewText: Mine mounted firmly, but having a convex mirror limits what I can see from the outside edge. A flat mirror would show me farther down the side of my trailer.

I installed these mirrors (2 qty, as they are sold in single units) on a 2012 Toyota Highlander to help tow a 21' travel trailer. I use this to monitor the instant and daily energy production of my solar panel with storage battery. It's exactly I need and works perfectly.Pros:- Works great- Simple to use, and excellent instructions (with more on their website)- Seems well made, robust, good thick wires- Great features - I especially like the cumulative and min/max readings. Also easy to reset, and so get daily energy production.Cons:- Smallish screen with no backlight. No reading this thing from a distance- No way of getting data out. Strongly recommend that manufacturer adds pin-outs or USB plug to enable external data. Bluetooth would make this device magic.I saw some questions about how to get this to work with a solar panel/battery system. According to the instructions and my experience: Connect the black wire of the "source" side (the side with the pins) to the negative terminal of the charge controller. Connect the black wire on the non-"source" side to the negative terminal of the battery. Connect the positive terminal of the charge controller to the positive terminal of the battery (like normal). Connect the red wire of the "source" side to the positive terminal of either the charge controller or the battery - this wire can be thin since it is only measuring voltage, not conducting power, and if you add an in-line switch to it then you can easily reset the Watts Up measurements by briefly turning the switch off. The red wire of the non-"source" side is not connected to anything.
This item is working just fine and is really usfull in finding out what is going on with the battery and solar panel.  Great service also.

I like the information this item/meter provides, including, or especially the historical "peak" and "total".  And, it seems to work well, at low enough amperage.  But, buyers should be aware that it comes with 14 gauge wire (that cannot be changed) which seriously limits how much amperage can go through it (before it starts to heat up, or I assume eventually melt).
This is so handy for testing high power LEDs and other various electronics. Such a nice concept and simple to use.
Have several of these now, and I love them all.  They are well priced and do exactly as described.  Perfect little meter.

the reason it lost a star is because there is no way to conviniently mount it.  id love a flush mount version that had terminals, rather than leads.  this thing makes our electrical "closet" quite untidy looking with our rigged up mount job.we use it to monitor our energy usage at our off grid cabin.  we mainly use AH, and know that our battery has x AH before it gets drained to where it isnt usable for our water pump.  it has also allowed us to get accurate #s on what item uses how much juice.  the only thing i wish is that it was possible to change the display.  there are 3 main displays...  current amp draw, volts, and wats.  then the 4th display flipps between all the other #s.  it would be nice if you could customize it so what you want to display is displayed...  but thats just nitpicking.finally, the screen is not backlit.  it would be nice, sure, but no biggie.  i knew it going into it, but the pic can be deceiving, i suppose.  figured id throw it out there.

The meter supplies the information on whatever you are testing but the lower left data cycles very fast and needs to be slower. If wired in to your solar power cable before the controller every day you will have to unhook a wire on the source side to get it back working again. When the sun goes down, the meter loses power and when it comes back up for some reason it will not automatically power back on. For the reason and the cycle data area being so fast, I gave it a three star rating. I had ordered three and sent back two of them just keeping the one. Plan to make some testing cables and use it more like a test meter than something always wired in to stay. If it were hooked on the load side of the meter, it would do the same thing when the meter shuts power off to your DC powered items if your MPPT controller is set dusk to dawn.

reviewText: I bought some of this at my local harbor freight anddid not have good results.  I wanted to remove some rust from and repaint my skid plates for the SUV.  After reading the directions I sanded down the worst spots, covered the parts in paper towels, soaked in the evapo-rust and covered the paper towels with saran wrap to prevent evaporation.  After leaving it sit for 12 hours (the maximum recommended period of time) there was no difference.  The parts were still as rusty as ever.If you have large parts that need rust removal I recommend naval jelly first and foremost.  It is a thick gel that you paint on and it eats away the rust within 15-20 minutes.  Handle with extreme care because it is highly corrosive, but you will get the results you're after.  In a pinch the napa brand is almost as good and readily available.
summary: Slow and ineffective compared to other products I've used

reviewText: I picked up a bunch of old tools that had been laying around forever and had a bunch of rust on them. I set them in an aluminum turkey pan and poured Evapo-Rust in with them and let them sit for a few hours. I pulled them out and scraped them with a wire brush in the sink and was amazed how well they cleaned up! Rubbed them down with some WD40 after I was done and they look great!

In the process of restoring an old mower deck, I got this to hopefully clean up some parts that were going to cost $$$$ to replace.It did the job overnight. Rust was gone, needed a little spot sanding, but overall, I'm amazed.Also managed to splash some in my face when a part fell, and some water was all it took to wash it off. Good stuff.
Soaked a rust filled multi tool over night...it was completely rusted and I couldn't even move all the little screwdrivers etc. embedded within the unit.  The next morning it worked like new!

I had to take my hella horns apart to repaint the grilles bright red for my Suby.  The screws and nuts were completely rusted.  I had to spray a little oil pentrator on them and let them sit but was able to get them off the grilles... Once looking at them I would have ususally started by taking a small wire dremel wheel and getting the rust off them like that.  Keep in mind these have been through 5 winters and lots of SALT...  Read all the reviews on this product and I do think it's expensive for what it is and HOW much you get...  However I poured about 2oz into a small container and put the screws and nuts in just so they were covered..  Waited about an hour and it didn't do anything... was thinking this isn't going to do anything.  Waited about 3 hours and still nothing.  Decided to shake the container left and right for about 20 seconds and then started seeing the fluid changing colors.  Then started seeing the screws turn to a normal metal color.  Success it's working!  So I left it sit for another 12 hrs.  Still going now but as I would shake the container and swish the liquid around I could see the rust coming off... It's great.Given I think this is best for SMALLER parts... If you have large parts and need to keep it submerged you are going to be buying a LOT of this stuff and in my opinion it's going to get quite expensive... White  distilled vinagar will do the same thing and much much cheaper.  This is however very good and in the need that I have the smaller parts that need the rust off this is going to be my go to item... Just wish the gallon containers of it were around $10 as I think that would be a good buy on it.  10 bucks for 32oz is not a good buy in my opinion...Stuff works though.-Nigel
summary: This stuff is great so far!

reviewText: I've tried this on a couple of items and will update my review accordingly.1. 10 Year Old Camshafts (found in the Back of my garage) - rusted and oilyResults: Submerged for 24 hours and most of the rust and all of oil was gone. I took a Scotch Brite pad to the remaining rust and it came right off.2. Battery Corrosion in Flashlight (three AAA batteries were in a flashlight in my car for two years)Results: I soaked the corroded battery holder (the plastic piece that held the three AAA batteries inside the battery case) for two days and most of the corrosion was gone. This was after I tried using baking soda. A quick hit with a tooth brush sealed the deal. The metal contacts are not perfect, but clean enough that I can use the mini-flashlight after it went unused for at least years! The corrosion inside the aluminum flashlight was fixed with baking soda, but if it was any worse I would have soaked the corroded portion in the solution.Overall, this is a good non-toxic product. The are faster alternatives, but it's safe, reusable and can last for years if you keep it sealed.Next on the testing block will be an old rusted pressure plate from my Nissan Silvia clutch and a bunch of rusted bolts.To be continued....4/14 Update:I filled two Quart containers with oily, rusted bolts that I found around the garage and added Evapo-Rust. After one day, the bolts looked a little better, but nothing amazing. Day two looked better. On day three, you could see a layer of crud building up at the bottom of the containers. I decided this was long enough, so I dumped them in the sink and grabbed a clean rag.The remains of the rust wiped right off most bolts. The rust that was REALLY invasive, didn't come completely off, but I have no doubt another few days would have done it.While you can recycle Evapo-Rust, it was so dirty from the oil and rust remains, I decided to get rid of the used portion. Overall, 98% of the bolts look like new (in addition to a few rusted nut driver bits that I threw in for good measure) so I can't complain. If you are in a rush, you may want to try something else, but I like what I've seen so far.In terms of the chemicals, there was little to no skin irritation on my hands, so that's a big plus!

This was a straight bolt-on for my 2012 Sahara. It is completely flush with the bumper, which is great because you won't hit your shin on it when loading the trunk. Fit and finish is excellent and it is of excellent quality, and made in the USA. It is a bit more than the Smittybilt and Rugged Ridge hitches, but it is worth the price difference for the quality of this unit.You do not need to remove the bumper or lower the exhaust to install the hitch. Fit the washers onto the bolts, fit them through the holes from the front of the car to the rear, then grab a 19mm open end wrench and hold the nut in place while tightening. Make sure the hitch is positioned in the center of the cut out in the bumper, then get your torque wrench and tighten the bolts to 75 ft-lbs. You'll see the washers start to bend when torqued, and I checked with Curt, and they said it is to be expected when torqued to spec. To me it seems like the washers aren't quite strong enough, but no worries.Only drawback is no wiring holder if you plan on attaching a trailer, but since I don't have a trailer and will only use this as a recovery point, it didn't matter to me.

I just installed this on my future son in law's '12 Wrangler. I also found 2 holes that were a little tight but I just screwed the mounting bolts into them to clean them out before mounting the hitch. No drilling or bumper removal necessary. Neither was the muffler needed to be removed either: just wiggle the bolts through the hitch and frame holes. I do suggest using 2 flat wrenches or ratchet wrenches to snug down the bolts as space is tight for a socket. Took about 25 minutes and it looks like a factory hitch. The mounting holes are slotted to allow centering the receiver in the factory bumper cut out (use a rubber mallet to avoid chipping the paint). I've used and installed Curt hitches in the past with no issues.

2013 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited Sahara fits perfectly! Well made and ready for the abuse I'm going to put this through.Hint: Wait until the muffler is cool and you can push it far enough to slip the bolts in the proper hole to bolt this bad boy down. I used red thread locker and cranked her down tight. Better than factory in my opinion. Great addition and price value increase to my Jeep.

Not sure if it was a Jeep issue or a Curt issue but I ended up having to buy a couple of smaller length bolts to get this to work (I didn't want to mess with taking the muffler down).  Otherwise, a five star product.

it looks great and feels very well built. I had to drill the holes out better on my jeep to make it fit right but that was not the because of the hitch. The holes in my jeep frame were welded crooked and it took a great titanium bit to drill them out but went on in about a 1/2 hour.

Practice on a tire with a torque wrench to get the feel of how much pressure to put.  The cable that goes with this is super easy too.  There is also a video on youtube for you JK people.  That's where i went for my "instructions."

I wish it had a mounting tab on the side to snap in the wiring plug to keep it from dangling.  No big deal, but it would have been nice.  I'll rig up something with a zip tie or two.

reviewText: Wow, for 10 bucks, it worked really good.  Only used it once so far and I feel like I have definately already got my money out of it. reviewText: I like this cargo net.  It's great for securing the load in the back of my pickup.  It stretches out to fit around a big load.  I like the visibility of the large yellow hooks.  I've gone through a bunch of cargo nets in the past, and this one is much more durable.  This one should last longer.I like the size of the weave in the net (is that what you call the distance between the chords in the net?):  The grid is small enough to keep the load secure, but not so small that it turns into a tangled mess.  That's been one of my big complaints about cargo nets I've owned in the past, that they are so stringy and the grid is so small that the whole thing turns into a tangled mess every time you try to work with it.If the cargo in my truck is complicated enough that I need a cargo net to secure it, then I'm already a little cranky.  The last thing I need is to fight with the net too.

Product clips are very flimsy. I would not trust this net on my car during highway driving. As soon as I put it on my roof-top carrier the two opposing corners came apart. On close inspection I realized the corners were simply tied together just as you would tie your shoes. Very dangerous and sloppy workmanship. I was very fortunate the item came apart during installation and not on the road. If you zoom in closely on the product pix you'll notice the two corners tied together, those are the 2 failure points. NOTE: the net was not stressed nor overstretched during installation in order to cause this type of failure. Be safe on the road, stay away from this item.

The hooks on this are perfect for the 5 x 2 foot hitch mounted tray I bought.  The other nice part of this is that it doesn't get super tangled, they all do to some degree, just found this one was less than most.  I use it after I tie down coole, firewood, and gear bags.  Keeps everything from shifting around while getting from the blacktop to the campsite.
It works ok when you need to secure a large load.  It is not the best I have ever used nor is it the worse.  On a 1-10 scale I give this a resounding 5.
Used it to hold down some firewood and a cooler in a hitch tray for a 5 hour drive. No issues during trip. Do wish it came with some type of cheap sack for storage.
that net will be useful, fits good, not expensive and will do the job when carrrying light stuff in truc box.
We use this for the back of our pickup truck when pulling our fifth wheel. It works very well and keeps things from blowing out the back of the truck. It works very well.

I think it's good for the price. I think I paid ~$10. The only cons are the cooks don't stay attached to the webbing, unless under tension. And it also requires some setup, attaching the hooks where you want them on the webbing.But I think after you set it up it works as expected. I've only used it once so I'm not sure how durable it is.
This fits as a large would and was good quality.  Seems to have good construction and durable material.  Its a keeper.
What can I say. My second one for use on a cargo hauler. My fleet of two vehicles now has a cargo hauler. Much easier to load and unload than a roof top carrier. Also no noise and no drag.
It's a nice, bright bulb.  The orange glow that enhances visibility is purely imaginary on my K1300s.  I'll wager the effect is highly dependent on headlight design.
Heavy duty made for motorcycle applications.  The orange hue is a little over hyped, but it does stand out a little more than a regular bulb.  Seems a little brighter than a car bulb.

So because of the title Amazon seems to think this won't fit H4 models, but it will.  In fact if you look at the picture it says H4.Anyway, the orange glow is pretty cool.  I am not sure how well it actually does to make other drivers aware of you, but I'm up for any type of change that might help.  I certainly don't think it can hurt.As others have stated, the output is still white, and very bright.  I did notice some difference in my light output, but I was also comparing bulb to an older bulb so it's hard to make judgments.  I can say that I have no problems seeing at night.I like the fact that these are designed specifically for motorcycles so I'm hoping they will last a while.  Be careful when taking the bulb out because it's not wrapped in any plastic so you have to take care not to touch the bulb.Other than that, it's a cool conversation piece with other bikers.

reviewText: Orange glow certainly looks cool -- the headlights look like bloodied eyes. The orange glow is way more pronounced for the low beams; high beams are appropriately bright and nicely focused. Other than the orange tint, the bulbs are ordinary halogen lights, they are not noticeably brighter than most of the bulbs that I'd put in my headlights.The bulbs are not advertised as exceptionally vibration resistant; some other motorcycle bulbs are. I don't know what it means in practice.

I LOVE this bulb. it is NOT the brightest bulb I have used but having the "Unique orange reflection" in the headlight REALLY DOES HELP YOU STAND OUT IN TRAFFIC. This bulb combined with my headlight modulator really does get peoples attention and if you ride you KNOW how important this is for your safety, plus it helps to be unique and have people wonder how you got your headlight to do that LOL . Especially if you like Harley ORANGE which this bulb kind of looks like.LOUD PIPES SAVE LIVES - SO DOES ACTUALLY BEING SEEN IN TRAFFIC !ANYTHING TO HELP YOU BE SEEN IS A REQUIREMENT THESE DAYS - it seems people no longer DRIVE - they are to busy talking on the phone, texting, in too big of a hurry to even look OR just plain don't CARE ANYMORE ABOUT ANYONE ELSE ON THE ROAD.UPDATE- over a year later and still happy with this bulb - and loving the Harley orange tint LOL

reviewText: I purchased these Smittybilt brackets for my 2011 because it positions the lights down & outboard & don't block my view out of the windshield. They're also a great bargain compared to the Mopar brand which are essentially the same thing. The antenna is the real problem though and I did not like the provided bracket that bends it away from the light (even though it works), so I angled the antenna back to follow the slope of the windshield pillar which eliminates the interference. Here's how I did that. Remove antenna & pop off the black plastic cover (there's a small access notch on the bottom that should help to get it started off). Then remove the three bolts that secure the antenna fitting to the body (the nuts are welded to the inside of the body & won't fall off). Hand file the index slot wider on the body panel a little at a time until you have the angle you want. I drilled (3) new holes in the body (avoid the nuts), touched up with primer & secured the antenna fitting with stainless steel #8 hex head metal screws. Radio reception was not affected. The KC SlimLites & Smittybilt brackets look great!
summary: Puts the lights right where I wanted them!

reviewText: Perfect mounts for my KC Daylighters.  Created gasket to protect metal with bathtub liner.  Solid mount that I would buy again without question.

Bought rubber gasket material and made a real non metal to metal mounting application.Please note these Do Fit a 2014 Jeep Sahara Unlimited. So I suspect it fits all JKU's even though the fitment guide say it does not fit the 2014 JK Jeep.The stainless hardware is great. But you do have to Hack-Saw the carriage bolt down to about 5/8" in total length. I also cut out a rubber square to place between light bracket & light mount.Kit should come with a Ny-Lok stainless nut to deter thieves from using a 1/2" end wrench & spinning it off & taking your $325.00 pair of 40w Spot LED Lamps!Overall this is a better product than the rest because your lights are not mounted as to hinder your view thru the W/S.

reviewText: Well, I am a fan of Smittybilt stuff.  I have found they make some cool "stuff" to customize your Jeep.  These mounts are no exception.  They are made of thick guage steel, painted semi-gloss black, and fit perfectly using existing screws at the lower corners of your windshield.  There was other review(s) concerning protecting paint under the brackets in case you want to remove them later.  I found two solutions.  Either lay the mounts on some old pieces cut from an inner tube, or I used the rubber backing from an electrical wall cover box that I had in my workshop.  Just traced around the mount, cut the material to match and punched a couple of holes (with a paper punch) for the screws-problem solved.  I like how low and out of your way these mounts put your lights.  I mounted two Rupse 2x2 27W Square LED Work Lights (from Amazon) 1600lms and installed a lighted rocker switch in my dash.  One flip of the switch and 'HELLO DAYLIGHT"!  The location of the lights do not block your vision or cause glare on your windshield.  The mounts are cool.  I didn't use the antenna bracket as I replaced my wire antenna with a "AntnnaX Shorty" (also from Amazon) which I really like.  You'll like these simple mounts!
summary: Nice mount for windshield level aux lighting
