I added these D rings to my Smittybilt Black Box.  They now give me four points to tow from with the two already on my truck. They are rated high enough to haul my four door 4x4 F250 out of the mud.
The threads were buggered on one of these I bought. I had to use a wire brush to remove the powder coating and then a file to fix the thread. After that it is fine.
these are nice almost like a rubber coating on them.. problem was the rubber coating was not covering the whole thing it was splotchy simplie fixed i sprayed them with rhino liner
Not used this yet..... but there is no doubt about it strength and ability. Smitty is not Sh$^%#. Gotta get more.
I have been known to get my JEEP stuck in the mud.  :-)I keep 4 of these in the back.  There are 3 already on the car.  Extra D rings can come in super handy when you need hand.
summary: You off road? You MUST have many of these with you

reviewText: Shipped and received in short order as advertised. Has a thick casting and a durable powder coated finish. Haven't actually had to use it yet, so can't really comment on how the finish and material will hold up under load.
It's a shackle what else is there to it, quality was excellent very stout, heavy duty, and you'll need several of these in your goody bag for when you need them. They were exactly as the photo shows.

I decided to save a few bucks and get the used or "blemished" d-rings. They look almost brand new and since they are going to get dinged and scratched anyways why not. I'm very happy with the quality.

this great product from this great brand serves its purpose well. its pin fit fine, the paint is still there and great looking even after some jostling around the back of my truck. haven't used it yet, but the 4 3/4 ton weight rating will no doubt hold up.
Very good price D-Ring quality very high as well as the paint. Would buy again. Holds up to any torture test you give it with a winch.
Arrived promptly as promised. Seems OK. Just getting tired of everything coming from CHINA. I think country of origin should be required in description.
Does the job you expect it to.

I own two of these d-rings (yes, technically they are a shackle, but in the off road community they are commonly referred to as a d-ring).  Please note that they are 3/4" and that is an INSIDE diameter, not outside.  They are more like 7/8" outside.  I read several reviews where people had a problem with the size and said they weren't 3/4".  If you have recovery points on your ORV that take 3/4" d-rings, these should work.  They are 3/4" d-rings.Please also note that these are rated to 9500lbs.  The d-ring does not say this on the ring, which is a minus to me.  I had to look up the specs on Smittybilt's website.To sum up: if you are going to use these as an occasional recovery item, they will work fine.  I have used mine to recovery buddies on the trail without any issues.
summary: Very Good Shackle/D-Ring for its price

reviewText: They work like they are suppose to. They are mounted on a smitybilt  stinger front bumper. Package was great. No paint chips.
VERY heavy duty d-ring. i have used this twice with my winch and it works just like it should. Very happy with this.
These D-Rings fill the bill!  They're made of heavy metal, and should handle any winching job I'll be involved with.  They're perfect for use with a recovery strap.
I have a black rig and wanted black shackles to hang from my bumper recovery points.  They don't look out of place and handle the stress of recovery operations just fine.

Man, I thought these were going to be smaller.  But they're huge.  The size of your fist.  Couldn't be happier !  Hung them from my SRC bumper (which installed without any problems and is flawless to the human eye.  Suck on that all you smitty haters !)
so it is big. i could play horse shoes with this thing. it would be ok for fitting to a bumper. the frame or as it seems designed to stick out of a stinger and give yourself a place to tie to.
summary: a lot bigger than i realized

reviewText: Does exactly what it says it will. Towed several mutliple-ton vehicles using this and the smittybuilt 30,000lb strap. Works great.
Good and strong. I like the look of the black. The finish is solid and hasn't knicked or scratched. Solid point for towing or winching.
This product works great and I love it. Im using it on my 2011 Yamaha grizzly 700. durable and great finish
This product is very well built.  It is great for the pulling I need to do and I am not worried of any problems.  I would highly recommend this product.

Yes----it was aesthetic reasons i purchased, but i hate chrome.  My bumper came with chrome drings, and these black ones are perfect for my black jeep bumper.  Solid, and I'm sure will not fail when the time comes to be needed for recovery.  FAST shipping as well!!

It is a D Ring. It is in the shape of a "D". I need a few more words to meet the minimum number of words for this review. Just kidding. It's high quality. The coating has only chipped a little from moderate use. I would buy it again. A must have.
Very tough and durable product. I sent mine back and downgraded to the 1/2 because the 3/4 would not fit like I expected.
Straightforward product at a great price, I see no need to buy a more expensive D-ring. Comes with a gloss black finish that seems durable
came quick, looks great, will come in handy for my winch when I get stuck next time i'm out four wheeling.

Bought this as part of my "emergency kit" for my F-250.  I used to do recovery (Tanks) in the Army and this is of better quality than what we were issued as part of our "kit" for the tank retrievers.  The coating should keep it rust free until I (hopefully never) need it.
work smoothly and have a nice finish. the only problem I have is they are MADE IN CHINA!!! REALLY WE CANT MUSTER A COULPE OF D RINGS IN THE U.S ANYMORE.PEOPLE WERE IN A WHOLE HEAP A TROUBLE.

I use "D" rings on my Jeep for recovery points and to connect tow straps together. these 3/4" are so heavy duty, they would be the last thing to fail in a tough recovery and are big enough to handle several strap ends at one time. They are stainless too so no worries about rusting

So, I bought this as a part of my emergency recovery tool kit for my rig.  It's solid and well constructed.  As mentioned elsewhere, I'm continually surprised by the quality of Smittybilt products.  I'm giving it 4 stars for current fit and finish, withholding that fifth star for performance under fire...I haven't gotten stuck yet, so have not yet had a chance to see it in the line of fire.  Once I'm able to use it, I fully expect being able to give it the fifth star.  Great stuff!

High quality.  Perfect capacity for recovering passenger cars and trucks.  Bought two and keep them in my toolbox with my smittybilt recovery strap.  30' strap and 2 of these fit nicely in a .50 cal ammo can.
great product, heavy duty construction.  easy to install and look great. the powder coating looks like it will last a while

Rock solid as expected.  Coupled with my Smittybilt 2 x 20 Recovery Strap I should be just fine, after getting my Wrangler stuck in some big mud holes.  Delivered quick and rock solid.....nothing more to ask for....

These are heavy D rings.  I got them for the Jeep.  The new front bumper has welded brackets for these and I measured the hole and thought it was 3/4"... but when these parts arrived, they would not fit,  the pin is too big.  So I enlarged the hole in the brackets by 1/16" and now they will fit.  Royal PITA.  Nonetheless, they will probably be great if they are ever needed... hope I never find out, LOL.
Bought 2 of these to go with my new bumper and winch.  Decent finish on them and the finish on the threads is decent.  Will buy more when I need them.
Got these in case of emergency ( hope not for myself ) they seem sturdy and well made they are just the right size for my truck and straps. great to have when you need them

They came in little boxes stamped with "Made in China" as well as little stickers saying the same.  There is a place where the coating had chipped off-- maybe during shipping, but that is likely where they will start to rust.  Should work as I expect.  If they don't, I will make another post to let you know.
summary: Not the quality I had expected

reviewText: Was disappointed that it wasn't made in the U.S.A.  Other that that it looks like it will work out fine.
I picked up a few of these d-rings to go with my atv's recovery equipment. Never had to use them other than practicing winching out but even then they work flawlessly.

I have bike racks, step hitches and trailer hitch attachments and none of them fit as poorly as this.  I'm using a Curt hitch receiver, btw.  It is a good 1/4" off on the sides.  I would never drive around with this thing clanging away at the hitch and possibly bending the pin and damaging the hitch receiver.  This is strictly a vehicle toolbox attachment to only be installed when you get stuck.  It's a shame because the quality otherwise seems top notch.
summary: Keep it in your vehicle, not on it.

reviewText: The hitch fit into my 2" receiver hitch perfectly without issues.  The hitch insert and D-Ring have a sleek black finish that blends in well to the undercarriage of my Jeep.  It feels sturdy and well built and I would trust it to recover my vehicle if needed.1 star was removed only because it was manufactured in China and it seems that Smittybilt could certainly manufacture casted metal products within the United States without significant additional expense.  Doesn't effect the product review, but maters to me and many others as well.
Well made and heavy. Nice and solid.

Item was not packaged correctly. Item has come out of manafactures box and the amazon box had come apart. Item was first lost. Item must have been dropped. its banged up and scratched. Does not even look like the nice finish on the item in the picture.

Pros:  Very sturdy, strong hitchFantastically mobile and usefulThe D-Ring is solid and the removable shackle unscrews nicelyCons:  NoneSometimes Smittybilt gets a bad rap from true, hard-core offroaders, but I must say I'm very impressed with the materials quality and the quality of the design of this Smittybilt hitch.  I wanted a removable hitch and liked the price of the Smittybilt.  In this case, I must say that I came from the price....but left impressed with the quality.  Well done Smitty!

I had a bunch of nasty thorny bushes that I could not even get close to that I lassoed with a slip not then yanked the crap out of them with the Smittybilt 29312b attached to my Toyota FJ. I then pulled out some old stumps and some huge fence and fence posts on the side of a hill that were buried in concrete by some crazy person who had the property before me. No other method I could think of would have the possibility of working and the pro guys with bobcats estimate was over a thousand dollars. I even had all four wheels of the FJ spinning on a concrete drive yanking and that is some kind of force.All in all I am impressed with this Hitch, and recommend it.
summary: Pretty Darn Good.  Yanked A Bunch Of Stumps And Posts In Concrete And It Survived

reviewText: this is really a cool looking addition to any tow hitch assembly.the good thing about this is that it is functional as well.

Reading through some of the reviews leads me to think there may have been a change in manfacturing processes.  The unit I received is perfect. Fits perfect, and ,measures out perfectly. I had no problem installing it. It weighs a lot, and had no problem holding up when in use.  I wish it came with a pin, but other than that I can only say very positive things about this receiver.
Item was back ordered and took a while to receive. Fits the 2" receiver and should be a good pull point if needed. Its to bad they don't include a receiver pin with this product.

Mine fit with no issues at all no seems like some of the reviewers noted, what I received is exact to what is pictured, this hitch & shackle are heavy duty, probably more than what I will need, but when you need it you want it to work I don't foresee any issues with this on my Jeep Wrangler at all.
Keep this tow point on my Rubicon all the time. Easy to put recovery strap on the shackle and don't have to worry about it coming unhooked.
i purchased this for my 2011 Polaris Ranger Crew so I can get pulled out and pull othr people without damaging my vehicle.  The things is extremely well built and is well worth the money!

I was skeptical of purchasing this particular item due to the negative reviews.  However, I was pleasantly surprise with quality of the item...I had no issues with he fit and finish of the item.  As with most Smittybilt products, I found the this item to be of good, sound quality for a very fair price...a very good overall value.

I almost didn't purchase this receiver shackle due to some of the poor reviews.  I ordered it regardless, because I've had no complaints with previous Smittybilt products.  It fits my 2000 Tundra receiver just fine, a little loose but it's stored in a toolbox anyway.  I purchased a Curt 21510 hitch pin and clip with the receiver shackle, the combination works great and I'm satisfied with both.

This product is strong like bull! It fit my Rough Country receiver with a bit of play but I'll take it up with 2 or 3 turns of duct tape to eliminate the rattle. It's usually an advantage to have a centered tow point in the back rather than having to rely on an offset factory hook. Perhaps not the best looking product but it's functional & not likely to fail and that's what's important.
This is a heavy duty product.  This thing is solid steel, very heavy.  The D-Ring looks to be up to the task.

This is a heavy, sturdy product easily capable of the job as described.  The only problem I had was that it just barely didn't fit in my receiver.  The finish on the product felt like it had a ton of paint on it and even through the paint the surface was rough in most places.  The item didn't fit in my 2 inch receiver hitch (2012 Toyota Tundra). It actually got stuck in the hitch and I used a hammer to knock it loose. The hammer nicked off the paint and I could see it was very thick.  I used a bench grinder to remove the paint and smooth out some of the rough spots (took maybe 5 minutes).  I then re-painted it and it fits like a glove.
make sure not to buy the d ring as i did the receiver come with the d ring so now i have two d ring
This is both the 2 inch hitch and the D-ring. Hitch is built solid and is painted a sleek black. Great product that feels very solid.

This thing is solid! It is not a bent piece of steel like some other ones, it is a solid cast piece and is very heavy. I've towed lifted 3/4 ton trucks out of mud pits and through trails with it with no signs of wear. The powdercoat finish hasn't chipped after over a year and there's been no rust (even living in New England) and the pin turns easily.The only complaint I have is that the semi gloss finish has lost it's luster on the top where the sun hits it. It is still perfectly functional but doesn't look as nice.It does run small but I haven't experienced any rattling, My hitch was a little rusted so this was the best option for me.

Love the price, quality, and appearance but be aware that it has very thick paint that may interfere with fit inside some 2" receivers which could be a disappointment/surprise. We used it on another vehicle than the intended one, with a more forgiving receiver rather than grind off the beautiful black finish.
summary: Well made, nicely finished but caution: the thickness of the paint may not allow a fit/insertion in tight 2" receivers

reviewText: Ok, this is a very nice piece.  Slides into the receiver hitch very well and I've got it locked into place with a locking hitch pin.  Very secure. No noise or rattling noted, and I have it on the truck at all times for recovery purposes (helping me or others get out).  I continue to be impressed by the quality of Smittybilt products.  I only give it a 4 because this is an essential piece of recovery gear, and have not yet had an opportunity to really test it in extreme conditions
summary: Only a 4 because I haven't had a chance to break it

reviewText: Great piece of towing hardware.  Very solid and dependable, BUT.....it rattles in my receiver hitch.  I solved that by wrapping duct tape around the body before inserting it into the receiver hitch.  I love it...!Make sure you lock it in....these babies get stolen around where I live.I'm very happy with it.  In fact, I ordered another....

Works great to pull someone out of the sand at Pismo (Oceano Dunes) Beach makes it quick and simple to get people unstuck from the sand or even yourself if the need be. So far it has worked every time and the tow driver out on the beach doesn't like me pulling people out for free. another item got here fast and is great thing to have in your truck for emergency
summary: Tows people out of sand great

reviewText: Very heavy and solid product.  I have not tested it yet but there is nothing about it so far that leads me to believe that I will have any issues with it.  Only thing is that it is a little bit lose when I originally inserted it into the receiver but some back duct tape fixed that and now I have a very snug fit.

I picked this up last month as part of a lightening deal and I couldn't be happier. I didn't see any reason to buy a more expensive strap, as for my light uses this will work fine. Always good to have one of these under the trunk in the Jeep. Never know when you will need it, or when you have to pull out a friend.

I got the 30,000lb strap for extra strength and capability.WOW - it's huge.  With all packaging removed, the strap weighs 5lbs, 4oz.I also ordered two of the Smittybilt 13047B 3/4" Black D-Ring from Amazon to go with this strap.I would recommend spending a little extra money and getting this high quality strap.  It's much better to have more strength than you need than to be nervous about the integrity of the strap when you're in a jam.
Good quality, definitely notice a difference in texture over cheaper brands. Does what it's suppose to do. Have not tested it to the max limit yet, but recovered a 4 ton vehicle with ease.

I'm so happy with the purchase of this strap.  My first use was actually to pull a fallen tree out of my driveway at my remote cabin.  It felt great being able to use a product intended for things like this as opposed to trying to get some type of crazy rope to make this work.I strapped this recovery strap to my tow hook - wrapped it around the trunk of the tree - securing it behind a strong tree limb and then just pulled that tree out of the way like it was nothing.  The strap looked like it stretched just a bit - a little is okay (even good) - but the strap is in great shape and now I won't look like the goofy guy with the brand new strap when I go to use it in the future!  Good quality - would highly recommmend!

This is another quality Smittybilt product.  This tow rope has made my hunting buddies braver because they know I can get them out of most sticky situations.  This rope is very sturdy and an excellent addition for my Smittybilt equipped truck.
summary: Helpful for pulling my buddies out of the mud.

reviewText: I've been hauling around another type of strap  and hoping I'd never have to  use it.  So far, so good.  This  Smithybilt strap showed up on the Cyber Monday deals and I jumped on it.  I'd rather had the 3"x30' strap but they sold out fast.  This one will do - maybe I'll never have to use it but if I need it - I should have it.

reviewerName: Esteban A. Valle "--Don't ask what Windows ca...
reviewText: I recieved this recovery strap and it was the same brand as advertised, however the loops on the end came with black durable nyon protection sewn in liike some of the others I've seen. This was good as I was going to purchase a more expensive strap because it had the reinforcements, but this one ended up having them too.
summary: Good, came with protectors on loops

reviewText: Nice solid strap, well built. Should do its job when called on. Like all of this  type of product, it rolls up tight and compact, but when you need to get un-stuck, it will softly yank just about anything free.

I used this strap to get a little better pull angle with my snatch block. The pull was a very hard one and my Smittybilt winch busted into pieces. The mounts on the winch actually split and then ripped the entire winch apart. The strap along with my winch line and D-rings held well.
summary: Winch busted before this product gave up

reviewText: heavy duty and excellent price.  I purchased this for a gift for the brother in law and he was very happy.

Although i haven't yet used this for its built purpose, it feels sturdy, strong, is definitly 30 feet, and the loops are sewn around with high strength worksmanship. the strap feels heavy, and i have no doubt it will pull when i need it.

This looks heavy duty and I can't wait to use it, but I must say that it might be awhile before I actually "have to" use it. I could take it outside and try it out just for fun to make sure it works. If I do that, I will update this review and let you know how well it works, although from the looks of it, it should hold up to normal/proper uses.

They say a picture is worth a thousand words.Check out the image.  The Smittybilt CC330 3" X 30' Recovery Strap -30,000 lb capacity - is being used to guide a 90-foot hickory tree, leaning drastically over a house, so it will fall exactly as planned away from the structure.  The orange rope, threaded through a Smittybuilt 13047B 3/4" Black D-Ring, is arborist bull rope with a tensile strength of 23,000 pounds.  At the other end of the rope are two 5-ton Come-A-Longs, side by side attached to separate anchor ropes, tightened to about 80% which is a total of 16,000 pounds.Unless you are an emergency responder called on to pull Big-Foot out of a swamp, this recovery strap is all most folks will ever need.

I have owned a 4-wheel drive vehicle for over 35 years and I always carry a tow strap in the back.  What I've learned in that time is that you have to have a good strap, 30 feet is the right length and you need good shackles.  The shackles help you safely attach the strap to a vehicle and help to prevent the strap from being sliced by sharp parts of the car.The length lets you get far enough away from the person you are pulling to not have them hit you and in one case I actually pulled a car on the shoulder of the road several miles to a service station as it was 25 below zero and I didn't want to leave them there.I used to only carry this strap in the winter and when I went 4-wheeling but now it is always in the back of my SUV all the time. I wouldn't leave home without it.  I even used it to pull out some shrubs around my home that I wanted to replace.  I have a huge logging chain but it weighs 10 times what this strap does and the strap is just easier to use and store.It is very handy and good quality.  Every car owner should have one in the trunk or in their truck.
summary: Great strap for those emergency situations!

reviewText: A must have for off road recovery kits.  solid and strong, Smittybilt gives you simple form and function at a reasonable cost.  you don't feel guilty using this strap.
This strap is heavy duty and well made.  I have yet to use it, hopefully will never have to but I'm sure it will be up to the task.

Day two of having this in my truck, I came across a broken down Honda blocking a lane of traffic up a hill.  I pulled in front, got out my shiny new strap (I was eager to try it out and "dirty it up").  It's pretty sturdy, and although I was just towing a little Accord, it was nice knowing I had something more than capable of handling it.At one point, when negotiating a corner, the driver in the Accord managed to run over the tow strap when it got a little slack (it was unavoidable).  I goosed the gas to make sure it didn't wrap around his axle and it yanked out from under the tire just in time, gave the strap a nice skid mark, but aside from some rubber on it, it's barely scratched.  I call that a pretty good test.  And I got to do a good deed, so that's another good part of having something like this on hand "just in case".To be honest, the reason I got this was because I didn't have a recovery strap in that truck, and I managed to get myself stuck in some deep sand on a beach a few months earlier.  I had to get towed out by someone in a Jeep to haul me out, and all they had was some pretty flimsy rope that fortunately held just long enough.  Never again!  Next time I do something stupid like drive into soft sand, at least I'll have my own strap so someone can get me outta there easier. :)

Since I purchased this item, I've pulled several vehicles out of snow, sand, and even a ditch. My Toyota FJ had no trouble pulling a 35,000LB motorhome that was stuck in some sand and just needed a little OOMPH to get it going.Five or six tows of varying sizes, sand, snow, rain - and the strap is still good as new!Highly recommended, can't beat the quality for the price.

I ended up having to use this strap a couple days after buying it to pull a truck out of a mud pit and it worked perfectly.  The strap I received has a better apparence than the one in the picture, however it didn't matter once it was caked in mud.Definitely a good buy.

Only used once and didn't test the strength much (lighter load than 20k advertized capacity) and the towed item was wheeled.Quality appeared to be great (no rough patches in the weave or snags) and stretch was less than expected. I was pleased.Can't comment yet on wear and durability.
Excellent quality, very strong and sturdy.  The looped ends are extra beefy and reinforced which is a nice plus.  I have used this a few times on the farm already and it has performed great.
I have not had to use the tow strap yet but I am happy that I am ready to tow my friends vehicles out. I also bought the tow strap bag and fit grate in the bag.
I USED IT TODAY TO PULL MY JEEP OUT OF A HUGE ICE/MUD HOLE I STUMBLED INTO(AND I WAS SUNK) FELT VERY STURDY, DIDNT STRETCH. PULLED MY RIGHT OUT, ALONG WITH THE HILIFT JACK.
Pulled my Jeep out of a puddle with a moderate tug and it has begun to fray after one use.  Looks like it will be around for a little longer, but I didn't expect that to happen.
I haven't used it yet but it appears very solid and should be very adequate for any kind of use.

I have used this strap to recover other full-size pickups at the lake (Elephant Butte, NM) as well as having to use it to have myself recovered (wait, no one admits to getting stuck, right?).Held up great in all cases from Tundra's and F150's to Superduties.  Stitching is still good.  No tears or other damage.Buy one.
what can i say, it helped get my hummer H1 out of the mud when i was up to the frame. no issues here, very well made product

Just got my Smittybilt 2x20 recovery strap in the mail.  I haven't used it yet but I can tell you it seems very well made.  Solid, and the stitching is perfect.  I have no doubt it'll pull my Wrangler out of any hole I end up in.
Good strap that has worked well.  I've used it once and it did very well.  Nicely constructed and build to last.
I have never had to use it for myself, but helped a stranded motorist get out of the snow.  It wraps up nicely and the loops at both end seem securely attached. I will keep you posted.

Lots of mixed reviews on this one but I thought I would give it a try.This product WILL NOT fit ANY "D" cell Mag Lite. The strap that loops over the head of the flashlight is way too short and can not be modified. I didn't want to go buy a "C" cell maglite so  back it goes.
Pretty simple concept. It holds a flashlight with straps and velcro. easy to put in, just choose the bar you like.
Fits my maglite great.  Used it the other day to direct traffic away from a broken down car in the middle of the night until police showed up.  Just a great way to easily store a good tool.
I have the two d cell battery mag light led and it fit just right. The only thing is the straps are just a little long and I had to cut the strap
summary: Keeps my flash light right where i want

reviewText: Materials seem to be of high quality and the design is clever, but this should be a little bigger overall if they're going to say fits "most" Mag Lites. It barely holds mine and it's just a double C battery Mag. Not nearly the biggest they make. As of now the velcro enclosure is hanging on by maybe 1/4". Confidence is not high. I wish the retainer strap was an inch longer.
summary: OK, but could use from improvement.

reviewText: Good gauge. Easy to read, easy to use and seems to be accurate.  Particularly like that you can have the pressure reading in between the air source and your tire.  I pumped a tire up to 65psi and the gauge worked flawlessly.  I gave it for stars because I was expecting it to be a little heavier/hardier.  Out of the package I was surprised how "cheap it felt -- the rubber around the gauge is thin and comes off easily (but is also easy to put back on). I guess I was expecting thicker and heavier all around.  BUT, although it feels a little cheaper, the big picture is it works very well.  I've had no issue(s) with it and realized that my initial out of the box concerns are trivial in comparison.  If I could give it 4.5 stars I would.  If you own a professional garage, you might want to get something beefier.  If you will use this in you home garage or vehicle., it is definitely worth the money.

I have purchased this gauge from another catalog company several years ago and was very pleased with the quality and performance and features of this type of gauge.  UNFORTUNATELY, this gauge purchased on Amazon is terrible.  I don't know if this is a knockoff or if this company is allowing other manufacturers to manufacture under license but the one I got is terrible. The locking chuck on my previous purchases would clip on and stay locked on tight to my tire valve.  The ones here do not stay locked on.  The second I let go of pushing it on the valve, the pressure drops to zero.  I contacted the manufacturef on the package - GH Meiser - and they were so kind as to send me replacement chucks but these were only marginally better.  But when I tried inflating my tire thru this gauge, the gauge reading would swing all the way past 100 as the compressor was pumping air.  This is not the way my previous years' purchases behaved.  If the recommended pressure was 35, my old Accugauges would read around 40-ish as the compressor was running....not swing wildly to 100 as this one does.  I won't buy this gauge thru Amazon anymore, as a previous Accugage I bought a couple of weeks earlier was also returned for non-locking chuck.
This is only fair. The clip mechanism does not hold well to a valve stem and must be frequently readjusted.
summary: This is only fair. The clip mechanism does not ...

reviewText: Got this to extend the hose on our back-up tire pump for our Cessna. Works best on that hard to reach nose wheel. The lever fits in narrow spaces unlike the typical "L" shaped models. Also provides about a foot of extra reach when used with a bicycle type pump. The gauge seems to be accurate and it appears to be well made.
summary: Works well for hard to reach tire valves - like aviation.

reviewText: I had this gauge for about a year and was very pleased with the accuracy and handiness, but the first time I dropped it, it was finished. I took it apart and found the little ball had broken off the stem that provides the seal in the gauge. It looked like it had been glued on.Before I dropped it, it worked great. So much for the rubber armor on the gauge.

I bought this EZ Air because of the reviews on Amazon.  Its a unique design, their web site says its patented. It has a Schrader valve on the gauge so you can fill a tire through it, so you can measure and fill at the same time, as an adjunct to any dedicated gauge on the air pump.Meiser can manufacture custom gauges with different logos or company names, so many look alike models sold under different names are very likely theirs.  The original one is cheapest, the custom named versions go as high as $30.Pros1. Check and fill tires simultaneously.  For typical consumer gauges, you'd have to fill tires then measure pressure as 2 separate steps, this is often because the gauges built into air compressors are not as accurate as stand alone gauges.  If you do this often, on say 4 car tires, it can be cumbersome.  If this EZ Air works as designed, it saves a step that adds up over time.2. Quick Connect Clip On Air Chuck.  Like pencil gauges, you press and get quick pressure read, but with the clip on, you can add air, check pressure, bleed pressure, and repeat as often, with less motion because the gauge remains connected to the tire.3. Flexible hose.  Allows you to position the chuck or yourself, to a more comfortable working position, and the hose swivels on this axis.4. Brass construction.  While the machining is a bit rough, its rare to see gauges of this type this cheap.  The chuck, hose, bleed valve assembly, and gauge assembly are screwed in, and the hoses have crimped connectors on them.  This means should the assembly get dirty by grease, dust or dirt, as is often in garages, it possible to do some DIY servicing to clean it out.  The bleeder valve assembly is hot glued shut, but it can be scraped out if needed.  Brass is good low cost material to make pressure gauges out off as its light weight, easy to clean, and doesn't rust.5. Rubber gauge guard, makes it easy to grasp the gauge.6. Accuracy. I compared EZ Air's readings with a digital gauge and 3 pencil gauges read on the tire by itself alone then on using EZ Air simultaneously through the air inlet port.  It was within <1.5 psi compared to them.7. Numbers are easy to read compared to a smaller pencil gauge.Cons1. Clip on Air Chuck takes some skill to connect properly.  Many reviews complain it leaks or won't seat properly.  I found it will work ~100% of the time if you push it in to the tire valve firmly, before locking it in place; this is what the instructions say anyway.  If not connected well and you are filling the tire with air, it will hiss and leak, and confirms the problem.2. Air chuck is big.  The air chuck works well on tires without wheel covers, because the large air chuck may not fit the limited space where the valves stick out of the tire covers.3. If the air chuck doesn't sit completely, it will read low.  Make sure you push the chuck in firmly before engaging the lock.4. The air chuck has a floating brass valve that seals against a thick rubber gasket.  Since it floats, there is a tiny enough space that can pick up dust and dirt, causing it to leak, regardless of what you do.  Its easy enough to unscrew, blow out or wipe clean.I'd deduct a star because of the air chuck could make an error prone reading.  However it works so well once the technique is learned, and almost never leaks air when attaching to a tire compared to most gauges I've used, that's its pros overweight its con.A pencil gauge is far simpler and error free since if you hear the pencil gauge leak or hiss, you're not measuring the tire properly, with EZ Air, you can still connect it improperly without a leak.EZ Air is better when you think you'll fill the tire, rather than just reading its pressure.  Pencil gauges are smaller, have few parts that can go wrong, compact and dirt cheap, so its more practical as the go-to gauge for just checking pressure, rather than filling tires.  I buy them at Walmart for $2-3 each, check they are accurate for the pressure I need then leave 2 each in all my cars.
summary: Great gauge for a technical person

reviewText: Loses accuracy after riding in the saddle bag for a while. I filled up tires with a portable compressor with digital gauge, that shuts off at designated PSI. Double check with this EZ Air Gauge and had to let like 10 pounds out.I think to myself, this isn't right so double check pressure with a pen gauge from the car, and sure enough tire is 10 pounds light. Either my portable compressor and pen gauge are lying identically, or this gauge has lost it's accuracy.I will know for sure how much it's off once I get the chance to swing it by a tire shop.All of this may seem minor but on a motorcycle 10 pounds can become a huge safety concern. A gauge that is more than 3-4 pounds off will go in the trash. My safety is worth more than the 5-10 bucks I save on a bargain gauge.

the guage works well enough. I would just say that on my bike motorcycle (I have a Harley with spoke wheels) it is a bit tough to get it on the valve. I am not sure if there is an adapter which would be a little more accessible but I would certainly get it.

After messing with a cheap digital pressure guage that was always hard to use and eventually broke, the EZ - Air Tire Gauge by G.H. Meiser is a relief. I wish I would have bought it sooner. I use it to check the pressure on my Avalanche and it's fast, simple, solid and accurate. It attaches easily to the tire and you get a quick reading. You don't have to adjust the gauge or make it just so on the tire like you do with other gauges. The only conceivable negative is that it is somewhat large but that doesn't matter to me. Don't waste your time on anything else. Spend a little extra money and get this one.

I can't believe how hard it is to find a mechanical gauge that actually works.  This one seems to be pretty good.  I've bought expensive and cheaper ones, but price doesn't seem to guarantee quality or accuracy.  I guess you just have to keep trying until you get one that works.  So far, this one is doing well for me.
summary: Been through a variety of these.

reviewText: was nice enough to be stolen.  ohh well.  it is very accurate to gauge tire pressure, but dont expect to try and use it while filling the tire.  nothing but a normal gauge.  check pressure, fill, check pressure again.

reviewText: It works pretty well for light use after I cut off the cigarette lighter power plug and replaced it with a10 GAUGE 2 PIN QUICK DISCONNECT HARNESS, into which I can plug a set ofBattery Tender 081-0069-4 Alligator Clips with Black 2-Pin Quick Disconnect Plugor plug directly into aBattery Tender 081-0069-6 Ring Terminal Harness with Black Fused 2-Pin Quick Disconnect Plugattached to my motorcycle battery. It works pretty well now with a direct connection to the battery, especially if the car/motorcycle engine is running.With that modification, this little pump is fine for bicycle and motorcycle tires and for topping off a slightly low car tire, but I wouldn't want to use it to fully inflate a full-sized car or truck tire from beginning to end. The little pump gets pretty hot after a couple of minutes.The gauge on mine is fairly accurate, close enough to be considered reliable.Before I modified the power connector, it continually blew fuses, and, after putting in a stronger fuse, the connection got exceedingly hot after only a few minutes of use. My new connections don't get hot at all.
summary: It works OK, but only if you modify it

reviewText: We race Professional level Go-Karts. We have a rolling stand that the kart is transported on from the pits to the starting grid. We have installed this tire inflator on the kart stand and have a 12v battery mounted on the stand to operate it. Since we have been using this inflator, we have not rolled up to the starting grid and found our portable air tank didn't have enough air to change the tire pressure. Great product very reliable and used by most of our competitors when their air tank is empty.

I wanted to buy a good quality inflator to mainly put my car tires to proper PSI but to also inflate other inflatables around the house like bike tires, balls, etc. I bought this one due to its ratings and name brand.Overall I am very happy with it. I like the nice case it comes with and all the different types of inflation devices you can put on it to inflate other things like balls. One of my biggest complaints with other inflators I've had in the past was lack of power/ taking TOO long to inflate serious items like car tires. With this one, it's no problem! I keep it in my trunk and it has never given me any problems.UPDATE: Nov. 14, 2012: The fuse on the inflator went out and I tried to find one of the same amperage/ voltage at Radio Shack with no luck. I bought a 10-Amp, 250 Volt fuse which was the closest one they had to the one that was originally inside the inflator. Using this fuse, the inflator works for about 2-3 minutes then shuts down because the fuse blows. I am in the process of trying to find a correct replacement now.

I like the fact it is small,heavy duty, and fits easily in the trunk of my car. It doesn't take up much space. If I need to use it I just plug it in to the power outlet in my car. Comes in a bag and ready to go.

I can honestly say that this is one of the best inflaters I have owned and I love it!!  It comes with several adapters to allow you to use it for inflating several different things (like air mattresses).  If you use it as a tire inflater, it actually screws onto the valve instead of just clamping onto it . . . so, you don't run the risk of it popping off if you walk away while it's running.  It has a fairly accurate built-in pressure gauge and a light.  But, what impressed me the most is that this thing is REALLY quiet.  I don't mean "you don't need earplugs" quiet, I mean "you can carry on a conversation beside it" quiet.  This really surprised me considering its small size and the fact that it's actually lighter than some others I've owned.  It seems to be of good quality and has handled every inflating job that I've thrown at it, so far.  So, I'm anxious to see if it holds up over time.  I hope so.  :-)
summary: One of the best inflaters I've owned...

reviewText: I wish I had bought it several years ago.  I've used it twice in the past month.  One time I had a completely flat SUV tire.  The i7000 inflated it in ten minutes.  It does get a little warm when it runs that long...the device itself and the 12 volt plug.  The 12 volt cord is long enough for any normal passenger vehicle and the hose adds several more feet.  I haven't used the flashlight but it seems bright enough to help out in the dark.  I love the way the hose attaches to the tire...it screws on.  Nice tight fit but turns easily.  It has a nice case in case you want to carry it in the vehicle.

Needed a small trash can in the bathroom of my old travel trailer (I have been using just one that sits on the floor but of course it just bounces around when its being hauled) and this was a perfect small size to mount right next to the toilet paper roll holder. Its not big enough to use as an actual trash can for say the kitchen but in a bathroom it is perfect. I give it 5 stars cause the purpose was for it to be smaller for my bathroom and it was exactly that. Mounting bracket is great to for easy removal to empty then re-attach. Camco makes some ok RV products and this fit the bill for me and my oldey but goodie travel trailer.

reviewText: It is small and convienent and can be placed out of the way to utilize all those small areas in trailer.

Our travel trailer is small.  Two adults and 2 children or 3 adults...tightly!  Anyway, the bathroom is small. It suits our needs fine.  But I needed a small trash can just for dry paper, wrappers, kleenex etc since you must not put Kleenex (facial tissue) down those toilets....This will be perfect for our needs.  Small enough to not get in the way, stylish with a self closing flap.  I could spray paint it, and might.  Not sure yet.  Kinda like it the way it is.  It seemed pricey for being so small, but now that I've received it and it will fit perfectly in our small bathroom and fit our needs perfectly, the price seems right now as well.  I crafted a liner for it..UPDATEI installed in the bathroom. Easy to do. I thought originally it was a little pricey for it's size. But it works so perfectly for me, I now think it is PRICELESS!

I agree with the former reviewer that these seem a bit pricey but I purchased two via warehouse deals and managed to save a bit. One went under the sink and fits absolutely perfectly on the cabinet door in front of the sliding trays. The other went in the bathroom. Both are easy to install and provide a nice closing action. Use small kitche bags for ease of emptying. Tiny spring is simple to fit back in if it falls out or easy to replace. Perfect for tissues, kitchen scraps and other small misc needs.

reviewText: 8 x 4 x 11!!! Dont make my mistake, this thing is tiny, check the dimensions. At nearly $13 you would think it would be of some size? Wrong, again, my fault for not reading. Should be advertised and a bathroom trash can. There is no way this is worth $13 bucks!

reviewText: I have not had the problem with this falling off that others have but even if I did, this would still be a good buy.  It did what I wanted it to do which was to block the light from the window on the door.
summary: this would still be a good buy. It did what I wanted it to ...

reviewText: Really my screen door pushes up against this thing and holds it in place and I hardly ever open the door when camping so I can't comment on the one negative thing about this and that's the sticking and holding of the Velcro ... love how it blocks out the light from the morning sun and totally worth it for me really.It's kinda on the cheap side though ... really it's a tiny version of a cheap $5 walmart car front window shade .... for what it is and the material it's in my opinion a few bucks overpriced ... BUT it does fit a need and size that no other company makes so I guess that justifies the increased price.I would buy again though if I ever needed a new one.

This sunshield does exactly as advertised!  I have to agree with a few of my fellow campers, that the Velcro fasteners come off as they heat up.  A person might have to secure them with a screw in to the door, and some hot melt glue or similar on the shade itself. I recommend this as it works and definitely keeps the hot sun rays outside.

These seemed like a nice, cheap way to darken up our RV for sleeping in, and keep out unwanted solar heating.  However, we really want and need them most when it's hottest outside.  We've had 100 degree weather this week.  I installed these on the door and ceiling skylight, by simply peeling the backing off some Velcro tabs and sticking it between the mat and the window box.Unfortunately after the sun had been beating on ours for about an hour, the Velcro glue let go, and the covers fell off.  The Velcro stuck to the window and skylight, but it pulled off the shiny chrome window covers.  It sticks fine when it's cool, but that defeats the purpose of being a "sunshield".  Now I'm concerned that the glue will take the finish off the windowframe if I pull the Velcro tabs back off.I wanted these to be easily removable. Good idea, but I don't know how you fix that without screwing them down or something else that will leave permanent, unsightly residue or hardware.  ???Buy some custom-fit window shades instead.  Your local home-improvement store can help, give you options, and cut them to size.
summary: Velcro glue lets go when it gets hot.

reviewText: Maybe it is the plastic on my travel trailer's window, but even after making sure the surfaces were clean and applying the Velcro tape, the window cover did fall off.  I'd normally take a star off for this, but I'm not sure if it is the velcro tape's fault or the plastic on the window, so I'm giving this the benefit of the doubt.Normally, I'd say something like this is a must have, especially if one has a rig with two doors, one door going directly to the bedroom, so blocking light out is something needed for some rest.
The velcro that is sent with it is not very good...on hot days in the RV they fall off and they tear easy.
It is too small for my standard sized RV door which makes me wonder what sort of very thin door it is made for.

reviewText: have not in stalled this yet, looks like it will also take care of the issue i had with the light.

reviewText: Once camping season starts again, I will know how well it works, love the concept and cheaper than sewing one myself.
These are great for privacy and for a thermal barrier. I mainly use this to block out the sun.  I never even used the hook and loop stickies.  3M RED double sided tape worked for me.

These vent protectors are a must on a car in the Southwest. It lets air in and if it ever rained, it would keep the rain out with window down to edge of vent. I have them on both my pickup and Toyota Camry Hybrid. You may have yo work a little, but Amazon.com will get you you the right ones.
summary: Lets air in keeps sun-rain out.

reviewText: I tried the premade sunshields, as with everyone the tape failed and here I went chasing the cover under my rv. What I have found is basically the same however it requires a little work on your part.Reflectix BP48050 48-Inch-by-50-Feet Square Edge Bubble-Pack Insulation. We have a bay window in the front and a full length window in our RV and its a sun magnet during the summer months. What we did was cut to fit slip it behind the sunshade / privacy shade and Sun-be-gone. Same with the doors I cut a full length piece for each door, placed it between the screen door and outside door cutting out for the locks and handles it fits snuggly and add extra insulation to the door. When they are not in use roll them up place under the bed until needed.Reflectix BP48050 48-Inch-by-50-Feet Square Edge Bubble-Pack Insulation

This item is very cheaply made and the Velcro that it come with does not stay stuck.  As soon as the Velcro heats up is falls off of the RV window.  I had to go but industrial strength Velcro to attach it with and it seems to work pretty good.  Just be careful when removing them from your window because they will tear very easily.  Also, if you are looking for something to keep the light out this is NOT the product!  It will filter some of the light out but if I had to guess I would say that it only filters about fifty percent of it out.  Oh well, lesson learned.  I would not recommend this product unless you are willing to go buy some industrial strength Velcro.  Disappointed in this product.  You get what you pay for and it is Not made in the USA therefore you judge the quality of it!Update:  I gave in and bought some industrial strength Velcro, it is black Velcro, and took the Velcro off that came with them and applied the industrial strength Velcro.  They stay in place now and the Do help to keep the sun out.  They do not darken the room to a blackout but they do help.  Happy now that I solved the problem of them staying put in place!

reviewText: i read the comments from other buyers before ordering these window covers and they really helped. everybody said the velcro that came with the covers was bogus so i just used some i got at the hardware store and the covers work as they said. i am very happy with covers.
I had a problem adjusting this to fit the small drawer in my camper. I had to take part off, but that is why it's called adjustable. Very good quality and shipped nicely wrapped and on time.

I purchased this thinking that it would fit our camper drawers, but upon installation found that it was too large for our silverware drawer and too small for the others.  There was just no way to make it work efficiently.  I suggest that you measure each potential drawer in your camper and note if it pulls out 'all of the way' for complete access. reviewText: This works well for a camper.  My camper's drawers are small and this fit right in.  I would recommend this!

This drawer insert is way better quality than I was expecting!  Too bad my RV drawer is not wider.  I barely get to expand the drawer at all.  However, I wanted to open it up for a tight fit in the drawer and it works just fine.  I didn't expect the plastic to be as thick as it is.  Nice product.
Worked great for us, nothing super special but nothing to complain about either. If you need one this will likely work just fine.
I could not use it in one piece because it was to big for the drawer. Took the expander off and it is OK.

reviewText: Love this because it is expandable and just tall enough to hold your flatware in your camper or home!  Just as described!
It's a little hard sizing the wipers on a 4x4 suv
Work nicely.  Glad to have refills without having to replace the whole metal wiper brackets.

I was a little apprehensive about using a Break to Fit windshield wiper refill. However the process was easy and it fits fine. They seem to work well and we've had 8" of rain recently to test them out.

reviewText: My Wife drives an Audi A8 and new Wiper Blades cost a fortune so I took a chance on these Trico 47-700 7mm Break to Fit Narrow Refills and they work fantastic at a fraction of the price of complete Audi Wiper Blades.

Have a big F150.  Needed this to get the roof, bed cover, windshield, and hood.  Makes reaching these parts easily with a stepstool.  Will be interesting to see how the mop wears over time.  So far helped speed up the wash though.
I bought this to wash the roof of my car without needing to get out my step ladder and it does the trick. I also use it to get rid of the spider webs on the ceiling of my room.

It does work. It is a bit flimsy, but one shouldn't be scrubbing hardwhile washing your vehicle. If care is taken, it should last. Microfiberhead is not very plush like my Griot's mitt, but I use it to do the hard to reach areas of my SUVonly, then switch to mitts.
this product is very useful in my car detailing business.very easy to clean with the removable mop head,also doesn't scratch your paint!

Wow- for a very inexpensive telescoping microfiber brush this is awesome. I bought it to detail my F-150. I am 5'1" so I have a hard time reaching the entire hood and roof. This worked perfectly. And the added feature where you can remove the top and use it like a mitt is convenient.I also washed the microfiber already (just untie it and it comes off). Washed up great and was easy to reinstall on the brush.

The problem with this wash mop is that the head falls off the handle quite easily. If you try to shake it off to get some rinse water out the whole head pops right off. Obviously this is very annoying. And this problem occurred from day 1 it is not that the thing was abused over time.

Has great reach, even for SUVs. Also keeps your hands out of the water on chilly days.You have to push a good amount for it to scrub well though. It leaves some streaks that requires another pass or use of a hand sponge.  Still good and I still use it often.
summary: Good for reach and cold days

reviewText: I bought it for washing my car. I have used it for a year now and it works great.Pros:-The microfiber part is thick and soft. Much better then simple microfiber cloths and has no wear and tear after a year of frequent use (but make sure you cleaned it well, tiny gravels may get trapped inside the cloth and may scratch your paint). It absorbs the shampoo water great and diffuses it to the car.- The removable cloth gives the advantage of easy cleaning.- 48" extension pole (fixed length) is adequate for reaching every spot on a sedan size car. (I am not a tall person).-The head and pole parts are articulated with a hinge so can move freely adjusting the shape of your car.Cons:-Although not very often, every now and then the removable cap falls off during operation. You need to secure it tightly using the adjuster string and it is not the simplest thing in the world.My conclusion:So far it looks as a durable and well performing item. I am happy about this purchase. $ 14 is a bit on the higher side but due to its quality microfiber, it may still be considered as a fair price

I bought this item to wash my car during the winter months. I don't like to dip my hands into freezin cold water so I figure this would do the trick.It was ok, ... you really can't get into the nooks & crannies of the car, I found I had to use my wash mitt to get under the rear spoiler, the recessed fog lights on the bumpers...etc. I also figure it could use a few more strands of microfiber...not enough.If youre hoping to NOT touch the soapy water with your hands, you will be dissapointed. I like to wash my cars in great detail...this wash mop was just OK.
I have a large SUV and large boat. I use one for each. It helps in reaching certain areas a normal person can't reach.
This thing will break within 5 minutes of your first use.  The plastic which holds the head on is incredible thin and unable to move without the wash head flying off.

Bought this 2 yrs ago and as a man with a bad back I can assure you it saves me from alot of pain. Bending and reaching down into a bucket was a real drag. I love this thing but the other day as I was washing the wifes car the head of it cought between the wheel well and tire and I yanked it just a little {not hard at all} and the head broke off. Its not very tuff I can tell you. As others mentioned it does break easy.Even though it breaks easy and it would be nice if it was tuffer built,it still saves me alot of pain so here I am looking for another one. I feel I got lucky getting two yrs out of it as easy as it broke. I'll give it another shot and I'll be more careful using it. If your looking into buying one of these this review shouldnt stop you from purchasing one. These are not junk by any means. The head will not break under normal use. Just dont force it out if it gets stuck like mine did.As far as the head coming loose as some state here mine stayed tight after screwed in. If you encounter one that wont stay tight you can wrap duct tape around the threads and then screw it back on, thats an easy thread fix I learned from Red Green.....If the women don't find you handsome, they should at least find you handy!
The small end works great through thick ice and the bigger (wider) end is nice for clearing frost and remaining ice chunks.
summary: Nice grip and quality ice scraper

reviewText: i like how it has a nice foamy grip which works well with gloves.  Both ends of it work well to scrape ice and snow.  I used the toothed end many times to clean the underside of the car/fender to fit chains in after driving in the snow/ice for a while.

We do not usually get freezing snowy weather in south Texas. But a few weeks ago was an eye opener for sure. I came out to my car and there was 1/4" of solid ice on all my windows. All I had in the car was a credit card and a wooden paint stir stick. I spent almost an hour TRYING to get the ice off, and I barely did the windshield.So now, a week later, all 3 of my cars have one of these Hopkins scrapers in them (I even bought an extra one if one breaks).I have not had to use these scrapers yet, but the plastic is thick and looks strong enough for hard ice. The handle is foam lined to help with fatigue. The overall length is about 12", and it fits nicely in the driver side door compartment.Don't be that guy (like me), and get caught in a ice storm with out a ice scraper! Do yourself a favor and go buy a few of these, give them away as gifts. Someone will love you for it!

I know, I know, my "whiney" is showing in this review. I wanted a normal sized but strong ice scraper to go in my truck for the small areas and windows I can reach on my own and this absolutely fits the bill. Great handle shape, nice non-slip neoprene like cover for the "hand" area of the handle. The only reason it gets 4 stars instead of five is for the individual that was asleep when they loaded the product image and/or the person that placed my ice scraper in the box for shipment. That is because I'm one of those "Type-A" guys that gets a little too far down in the weeds when I research and then select an item for purchase. If I see something in a picture with a blue handle that adds to my liking it and the product description in no way says anything about "colors may vary" then I expect to open the box  upon arrival and see a blue handle. Well, it does the job and it's dark more often than not when I leave for work so I'm keeping it.

This ice scraper works well for light duty and has a comfortable padded handle.  Also, due to its small size, it is easy to store in the glovebox or car door pocket.  I imagine if you live someplace that gets a lot of ice/snow, you'll want to look for a much bigger scraper possibly with a brush on it.

These scrapers are awesome.  They flex to follow the curve of the window and take out frost easily.  The crusher end of it effectively breaks up ice when it is thicker.  I used to have one of these a few years back and loved it until I lost it.  Now I've found the same one on Amazon, so I ordered two of them.
Very basic unit that works perfectly.  One thing to note, it attached to a standard size oil bottle and pumps fluid OUT of the bottle.

These pumps will get the job done but not very well.  The straw provided is not long enough to reach the bottom of a bottle of Valvoline gear oil (1 quart).  They only provide one length of straw.  You leave about 20% of the oil in the bottom of the bottle.  It also takes a very large number of pumps to move one quart of fluid.  I lost count at over 200.The second pump that I used with transmission fluid began leaking on its first use. Screws right into a quart sized bottle and I used this to pump 2 quarts into my transmission. It doesn't move much fluid with each pump BUT for the price it;s worth it.
summary: Works well, takes a long time to empty 2 quarts

reviewText: This pumps 4cc per stroke. That is 237 pumps per quart. It takes a while to get 4 quarts pumped.I wasn't over hard on this thing. I was changing oil in both diffs and the transfer case, on the last quart bottle the cap cracked.

I replaced the manual transmission fluid and differential oil in my 1998 BMW 323is, both of which hadn't been changed in at least 100,000 miles.  This fluid in the transmission and RP Max Gear 75W-90 in the differential.  I expected some improvement, but it runs much quieter and smoother than I thought it could.  Sometimes it is like I nudge the shift and it sucks it into the gear I want.  Really surprising how smooth it is.  And my car is quieter even though I never thought it was noisy before.  Now the main sound is the engine when accelerating and if I'm at cruising speed I just notice the quiet.Having said that, I should note that the existing transmission fluid was black and only about 1/4 to 1/3 full.  There was some form of slow leak since the transmission was caked with dirt and oil yet I never had stains where I park my car.  So I'm comparing to what was an obviously under-filled transmission with old fluid.  The first 50 miles or so after replacing the oil the shifting was notchy and terrible and I was thinking I'd have to put something else in.  I was also worried I'd fried it due to low fluid.  But then one day it shifted smoother, and the next even smoother, until it was noticeably better than before.  Now a week later I'm really impressed.Forgot to mention my transmission is one of the manual ones that take automatic transmission fluid (Getrag) and this is rated for that usage.  Also I've noticed I have to go to 2nd gear much sooner now because the car gets to speed much quicker.  So it seems to be responding better to the throttle as well.  That seemed to have happened right after the change but I was babying the car due to the rough shifting so I only really accelerated normally a few days ago.Update 06/2012 - Several tanks of gas later and my MPG is higher.  Really improved the highway MPG, and it just did 32.09 MPG, doing the relatively flat round trip Los Angeles to Palm Springs plus some other mainly highway driving. My car has been getting 23 to 24 for the last two years and maybe 25 to 26 before that.  I've only hit 32 mpg once before in August 2009, and have had only 6 tanks of gas get over 30 mpg in the almost 12 years I've owned the car.  Stop and go driving is just slightly higher than before though as the prior three tanks of gas were 23.03 mpg, 27.38 mpg, 24.99 mpg.Update 10/2012 - The mpg the last 3 tanks of start and stop local driving were all over 27 mpg. The EPA estimated mpg for my car was 17 city/ 25 highway. So it seems to be doing well given it has the original engine and transmission.
summary: Car running smoother than I thought it could

reviewText: The best manual transmission shifter so far that I have use to change out my BMW fluid.  This is a must have for your transmission need.
summary: Royal Purple 01512 Synchromax High Performance Synthetic Manual...

reviewText: I like RP and they make quality fluids. I use them throughout my car and have never had anything bad to say about it. I have had their trans fluid in my car for the past 30,000 miles and it has worked well. Towards the end of the service life (30,000 miles) I was having some minor grinding when going into reverse but only when the car was cold and the air was cold (under 45 F). I just bought more to change out the old fluid.

You should be looking more towards the heat reduction and less parasitic loss more than smoother shifting. If your transmission already has the proper clean fluid, don't expect this to change much. It can smooth your shifting, but on my car with 200k miles, I didn't notice anything different.

I used this product in my E30 1991 BMW 318is (Getrag 5-speed). The housing has a red label/orange label. I flushed out the old fluid and put in 1.3 bottles of RP. I only drove the car for a few miles and I can tell there was a positive difference in shifting. Overall shifting became easier. I'll update this review after some more break-in.

A must for the 6MT connoisseur. Thought your tranny was silky factory smooth before??? Try this in your box and get ready for happy smile. Really can't top this folks. Allows for noticeably faster throws of the lever.

Not sure what was in my transmission before, but after driving for a bit at highway speeds, it would be difficult to shift into lower gears.  Noticeable difference after I put this in.  It's highly recommended on wrangler and jeep forums, since we have bronze synchro sleeves in the transmission, have to be careful what we put in there (otherwise it'll eat up your synchro sleeves and you'll end up with little gold flakes in your fluid when you drain it)TL;DR: great for Jeeps

Put this in my 04 Jeep TJ (NV3550) and like other reviews on here, it seems to work great in there. Not sure what fluid was in it before and I didn't notice a massive improvement or anything, but shifts smooth and no issues so far. Good price too. Recommended. The NV3550 takes exactly two bottlesUpdate: It has been cold the past few days (-10C) and my Jeep is extremely hard to get into gear for the first 5km or so. Wasn't doing this before the fluid change. It seems to work fine above 0 though. Just an FYI for anyone living in colder climates

I switched to this product for my new 6 speed vehicle because of its reputation.I used both the transmission fluid and the gearoil and time will tell if I notice a significant difference. I do feel that I have used a premium product based on so many positive customer reviews.
Well priced and a good investment.

Got it for my 330i 2006 perfect fit and also helped eliminating the moldy smell. Easy install in less than 10 min.
Fitment was about right and quality just as good as OEM. Good replacement part for your BMW without paying a premium price

Purchased this to replace what appears to be the original, manufacturer installed cabin filter in my BMW 3 series. Looks like the real thing (I do believe Mann is actually purchased and used by BMW as original equipment) and performs just as well! Excellent product!

Well done to fit my 2007 BMW335i sedan.  Quality built and really activated charcoal.  use just 5 minutes to install.
Fits my BMW 335i 2008. Easy replacement. Works fine. Everything good. You will need to remove some plastic covering, but that's it. 10 minutes job.
Mann filters are always great, i don't buy anything else. This filter is currently working well on my 2007 Z4.

reviewText: I do support my Mercedes dealership and resent anyone arrogant and stupid enough to refer to them as "stealerships".  My dealership has always been a great source of support and information, and as I like to repair my 2002 ML320 and 2004 E500 myself whenever I can, this is priceless at times.  I do like a good deal though.  I can buy 3 of these for the price of 2 at the dealer.  That math works for me.  I wouldn't buy an inferior, replacement product ever.  But this is the same thing.  And I like saving saving money too.  I just don't do it with attitude.  Besides, Mann makes excellent filtering products: fuel filters, air filters, and oil filters.  I've been using them in my BMWs and Mercedes' for over 30 years, and wouldn't use anything else.  I do still buy from the dealer at times, in fact quite often, but they sell Mann filters with dealer part numbers.  If they are original equipment for Mercedes Benz, BMW, and Porsche, then they are simply the best.  Buy them, regardless of the packaging. And support your dealer whenever it is practical.  You'll be amazed how much free assistance they'll provide to their customers.
summary: Exact original: Identical to Mercedes Benz factory part

reviewText: There is no doubt that I like to take care of my vehicle.  Therefore, with a car that calls for oil changes only every 10,000-13,000 miles, I want to be sure to use the approved oil filter that can survive that long.First, let me put this early in the review.  I had had the Mercedes Branded and Box part side by side with this one.  They are identical besides the labeling (and part of the labeling is the same as the Mercedes branded one still has the Mann logo and part number too).  They are identical because Mann makes this filter, their own brand, and the filter for Mercedes. They are truly one in the same.These Mann HU 718/5 have a beautiful, strong construction, and indeed they are actually the OEM part.  The OEM Mercedes-Genuine part has the Mann HU 718/5 part number right next to the Mercedes part number.  The only thing missing on this filter is the Mercedes-Benz star logo, Mercedes part number, and the Mercedes-Benz box.  Indeed, the filter is made in Germany as well for anyone wondering.  Several of the other aftermarket brands actually use the OEM filter rebranded too, as of this writing, K&N; oil, and Purolator oil.  However, those products tend to be much more costly since those companies must buy the filters from Mann and resell them.The Mann branded filter is the best value and easiest to procure since it is right here on Amazon!  How could it be any easier?  I will only say that the OEM dealer Mercedes labeled filter is not too much more money than this one.  Therefore, if you ever happen to be at the dealer or know of a dealer that has good parts pricing, you shouldn't necessary run from the genuine filter.  It's the same as this and depending on the dealer, might just be a couple dollars more, if you're in a pinch and can't wait.Overall, extremely recommended filter.  You can't argue with the original product!  This OEM filter is designed to hold up for the extremely long oil change intervals recommended by Mercedes.  Just be sure to use this filter along with an approved oil such as Mobil 1 0w40.
summary: It's the Genuine Part - Fits Large Selection of Mercedes Cars

reviewText: The other reviewers aren't wrong: this works as good as OEM, and its easy to install in most cars.  In fact, the owners manual mention this and the cabin filter as among the few things they recommend you install, so you can do it often.In a Toyota its fairly easy, open the hood, find the filter housing.  Unsnap 2 retaining springs, wipe clean the lining of the filter housing so it won't leak, pull out the old filter, insert the new.  Return the cover, set the clips, and you are done.  I did mine in restaurant parking lot waiting for my guests to come.I will change these more often, because the next gas fill, I got 3+ mpg more than I expected.  Many months later, my overall average mpg has increased, so clearly, I needed one changed sooner.  Mea culpa.  These filters cost as much as 2 gallons of gas, at current prices and easily pay for itself when changed.
summary: Just as good as OEM, cheaper and easy to install

reviewText: Item was for a 2004 Toyota Corolla. Got the filter in a timely fashion. Looks and feels like a quality item. It is replacing a Fram and it appears to be of equal or greater quality. Pricing is also good. I also replaced my cabin filter with aMann-Filter MC 1013 Cabin Filter for select  Toyota models

I hate paying $20 plus to the local oil change place for a dang drop in air filter, these fit the bill and work just fine. I'll be coming back to Amazon for all my air filter needs in the future.

This filter is made in China, however it appears to be reasonable quality. Has a thin foam gasket around the perimeter to enhance sealing with the airbox. Purchased to fit the Australian Toyota Corolla 2004 with 1ZZFE engine.

Can't compare to other compressors, but I needed one because a hose from my bike pump is short and won't reach one of the wheels on my car because its nose is always in upper position while three others are down, I probably need to lift that side of the car and roll the wheel so that the nose goes down and becomes reachable for pump's hose. All my friends and neighbors were surprised that simple bike pump from ToysRUS can easily pump my Honda Accord's wheels. But, for that small inconvenience and just in case to have an instant protection from flat tire I bought this compressor on a deal. It works as a pump when you don't use a sealant, PSI gauge is off but I have my own anyways. For this small compressor it does the job, not that fast - very loud when you're right next to it - but I guess all of them like that in this price range. Having a sealant feature in this compressor is just a peace of mind I guess. The only thing I wish it could do is to deflate - nice feature for pool toys that I carry when travel to pool with kids.

I bought this Slime 70005 Safety Spair Tire Repair system to replace my Continental Tire Repair system which had a 2 year expiration date. This system is so much nicer and does not have a use by date so I am guessing it will last longer than the Continental system. In addition the Continental system will damage the Tire Pressure Monitors in your wheel where the Slime system says it will not. It has a nice light and is easy to use. I am hoping I never need it but it is comforting to know I have it in my Corvette which does not have a spare tire. It came fairly quicky and has a nice carry case with a reflective triangle on the back of the case to place while you are fixing the tire.
What a deal this thing is everyone needs one of these in their car, the compressor on this thing rocks! If anything get one for your wife or girlfriend just don't tell your wife....

I've used Slime Spair Repair in a can before, that worked great so I bought this kit because it included an air compressor that runs off the 12V plug in the car.  I didn't expect much from a small compressor, but this surprised me.  I was able to add 10 PSI to my mini-van's large tire in about 1 minute.  That is much quicker than other portable air compressors that I've used.I would definitely recommend (and have already done so) product to friends and family.Nice compact unit that comes in a case with velcro to attach to the carpet of the car so it does not slide around.  Love it!Was going to buy a 2nd unit for my other car, but now the price went up to $50 :(NOTE: I am unable to find the refill Slime cartridge for this unit, except for the Slime website for $13 plus $11 to ship, which is way expensive!  Amazon, why don't you carry the replacement cartridge?
summary: EXCELLENT - compact and quick air compressor

reviewText: Two reasons for 4 stars instead of 5.  One, I've not yet used the product, so I have no first hand experience with its performance.  That said, I hope I never have to use it. :-)  Two, I also subtracted 1 star because of the clear crappy plastic/vinyl storage case.  The pump/device itself appears to be of very high quality, and it really deserves a much nicer case made of a more durable quality material.  The plastic/vinyl case looks and feels very cheap.
