Because of the limited area this item works in, it's best suited for small containers. I put this in the tackle box and it works great. When it's not fishing season, hooks and leaders sit for months at a time going unused and this little thing is the perfect thing to help prevent rust. It's not powerful enough to put in a gun safe or anything like that. Just suitable for smaller containers like small tool boxes or tackle boxes. However, the cost of buying these and keeping them in a tackle box year round to prevent rust on hooks and leaders may not be cost effective, since hooks and leaders are cheap. However, if you have fishing lures your looking to keep in good condition, then this would be the right item for you.
summary: Good for use in tackle boxes. Keeps rust off your lures!

reviewText: Why not just keep your tools and other rust-prone items in a dry place?  This is a great idea if you've got things you absolutely can't keep out of rust-prone locations, but at the same time you have to replace these little units every three months and the area they cover is minimal.  These little inhibitors start to add up...fast.  Great concept, but it should really last longer, especially for the price.
This is a great idea because rust is a fact of life.  This seems like a great idea, but, as others have said, 90 days is not long enough to test.  I will have to report back to see how this works.
summary: Great idea; let's see how it pans out

reviewText: I have used this for only a month so it's rather too early to tell if the product holds up to its claims, but so far so good.  Rust is a major problem for tools and other items I keep outdoors so having a rust proofing mechanism will really help me out a lot.

I tossed one of these in one of those many boxes of miscellaneous mystery parts that people who always have a lot of projects tend to accumulate. After several months in a modestly humid, partial basement workshop (no mildew problems, but it does tend to feel damp down there), there was some light rust, but nothing horrific. For comparison, I've had some more substantial rust in open several boxes (so full exposure without corrosion inhibitor), but nothing that looks like a flood hit it. While this was by no means a scientific experiment, I'd say if you have expensive parts or gear you want to protect--particularly if they're well sealed--it may be worthwhile (certainly wouldn't hurt), but for odds and ends, probably not worth it.

This product does exactly what it's supposed to do, so long as there is no rust present beforehand.  My only issues with it are needing one of these for every drawer in my toolbox and having to replace them every 3 months.  I believe I'll stick with my combination of using camelia oil and a desiccant like silica gel, (I get the kind that comes in tins which can be resurrected in the oven).

This product was just okay. I don't think it would be something I would recommend that highly because of the 90 day replacement factor. We used it on the tools that we store in a toolbox in the basement and it worked well, but knowing that I will need to replace it every 90 days sounds like more of a hassle then a help. There isn't a lot of humidity in our basement, so I can honestly say that I don't think it was the best environment to test it in. So far so good, but I'm not looking forward to having to replace this every 90 days.

First ... the product description on Amazon Vine said "(package of 12)", and there was only one piece.  I had thought this might be ideal for my tool chest which has several drawers to store different tools.  One package will do little to help or to decide whether it would pay to purchase several of these to protect the entire chest.I suppose it will depend on the pricing as well as how effective it is.  If it is inexpensive it may be worthwhile.  But my initial thoughts are similar to others expressed here.  I always wipe my tools down after use, and while those that go unused for a long time do show rust, it's hard to say that I would want to buy 16 shields (the number of drawers in my chest) and replace them every 3 months.  I have a hard time remembering to put chlorine in my pool every other day!  Remembering to change rust inhibitors every 3 months would be a miracle for me.Until I learn the cost and see the effects in 3 months, I will simply continuing using a light coat of oil on each tool after use.
He loved it. Hope it works as well as it says. Will update review in future.
summary: Idea is great. Gave to my husband for his tool box.

reviewText: I put one of these with my garden tools, which seem to become rusty even though I live in Arizona; there is little to no moisture in the air here.  Time will tell if these work!  I'll come back and edit my review in a month or two and detail how they are working out.
summary: Seems like a great idea, time will tell

reviewText: This unique product does for metal items stored in confined locations what automatic air fresheners do for living spaces.  The 3-in-One No Rust Shield emits a vapor that provides an invisible barrier against rust and corrosion of metal products.  It doesn't release a mist and there's no oily residue deposited on items left in its vicinity, but it does provide a barrier between moisture and all metal surfaces.  It only works in a confined space, such as cabinets, small closets and tool cases.  I use mine in a gun cabinet and it works as advertised.  I have one particular shotgun that is almost 50 years old.  Light surface rust will often form on it when stored for several weeks.  Since I've begun using the 3-in-One No Rust Shield, however, no rust whatsoever!  I just attached the device, about the size of a small cell phone, to the back of my gun cabinet and it silently protects everything in the cabinet.  It even has an indicator which displays when it needs to be replaced.  It really works!

Living in Florida means rusty tools and since we invest a lot in various tools, blades, japanese wood saws/knives and much more...this looked like a very useful product. Plain and simple, the oil just doesn't do the job given the ultra high humidity of Florida especially during summer. We literally can get 90 to 99 percent humidity on hot summer afternoons right before the rain.In any case, I suspect that nothing short of total climate control will totally eradicate the problem but for those living in places with normal levels of humidity this should perform fairly well and is much more convenient than using oil after every use.Bottom line - given the cost versus convenience, I'd be inclined to use this product for higher priced tools, coin collections and other valuables but wish it provided an extended coverage period and/or larger size for big items.

30 Day Update!It's been thirty days since I put all of that items in my box and stuck it in my shed. We've had less then a quarter of an inch of precipitation this entire time, however rust HAS developed on several of the items. Just after 30 days... so in my eye this product DOES NOT WORK. The box sitting IN a shed and with very little precipitation has fallen, rust has developed... this isn't cool.Pros:Easy to use.90 day timer seems to work flawlessly.Cons:Did not work for me.Price.It's really hard to say if this product works as advertised UNLESS you actually test it for a period of time, so that is exactly what I am doing.The best way I can come up with testing this item is to put some items that seem to rust easily and put them in a small enclosure with this 3-in-one No Rust Shield and see how they fair after 90 days of sitting in my leaky shed that seems to be a breeding ground for rust.The test container consists of nothing more then a cheap cardboard box, not the best container in the world, I know, but I'm going with the worst case scenario sort of test.Within the box is a pair of pruning sheers, some nails and staples, a small file, a screw driver, and a piece of plumber's tape/strapping, all of which I have had rust sitting in my shed and even garage.I will be checking on the items at the 30, 60, and 90 day mark as well as updating this review with comments and pictures of the items.Installation was easy, just take it out of the package and stick in the container... can't get much easier then that.I also like the fact that it comes with a 3M command adhesive on the back.I am actually afraid that this product is nothing more then a 90 day silica gel container... after the 90 days I'll take the product apart and see if it contains silica gel or not.So we'll see how it performs and I hope some of you come back and see how the test is going and leave me some comments, I always appreciate it!
summary: On going test in progress... UPDATED 9/28/2009!

reviewText: I put the rust shield in a sealed plastic box of woodworking machine parts stored in my basement.  It is August in the Midwest, so humidity can be a problem.  The unit has "command" self adhesive strip to make it more use friendly & easy to remove but I didn't need or use this feature.The unit has an indicator that tells you its approximate status into its 90-day life.  They call it a "timestrip gauge".  Directions say to press a button to start the indicator, and "within 5 minutes...a black line will appear".  A line did appear after a few minutes.  So far, so good.Update:  So, it's been a month now....the RS seems to be working.  There is no rust on any of the parts.But I'm not sure these work any better than a piece of charcoal wrapped in a sock or nylon.  And that old tried & true method is a lot cheaper!
summary: It works..but at a high $ cost.

reviewerName: Lisa Shea "be the change you wish to see in t...
reviewText: I received one of these through the VINE program and tried to perform a controlled test with it. Really, the only way to say that the item works would be for me to have a pair of sealed containers full of a rustable item and watch the unprotected container rust while the protected one remains pristine. Fortunately for all of us, unprotected items don't rust that quickly in most climates. Unfortunately, it makes it impossible to provide a definitive review in a timely fashion. Since the product only claims to function for 90 days, any observation beyond that time would be unfair. I have to give it a star rating, so I'll set it at three since I can not say how well it works.On the other hand, I have a bunch of items that aren't using these and aren't rusted. I certainly have some that are, but if I need to "care" about them every 90 days to replace a cartridge, then I can care about them to give them a spray of WD-40 or wipe them down to prevent rust as well. I have to wonder if this is an item that most people would find useful with this short of a lifecycle. I would be a lot more interested if it had a 12-24 month functional life.

3-IN-ONE  No-Rust ShieldHonestly, this is a difficult product to review without doing a controlled experiment to determine if it is working:  if there is rust, it isn't working but if there is no rust, it may or may not be working.3-IN-ONE has a large stake in maintaining their excellent reputation--the same company also sells trusted products such as WD-40 and Lava soap.  So this is the rare situation where I would be willing to trust the manufacturer that the product works.I can say that after about a month in my toolbox, there does not appear to be new rust forming on the tools that have rusted in the past.  Average humidity here for that month is in the 60%-70% range and the storage area was not air conditioned.The product is basically a piece of sponge that holds the chemicals encased in a plastic shell that may be attached to a surface with the strip of 3M Command tape on the back.I did a great deal of research on what to me was a novel and interesting product.  Vapor Phase Corrosion Inhibitors are a tried-and-true method of preventing rust.  An excellent overview paper may be found on the website of the professional organization of corrosion engineers:  [...]The exact formulation of this product is not given by the manufacturer.  When I called their customer service number, I was referred to the MSDS which lists only polyurethane foam and "proprietary ingredients".The manufacturer recommends one unit for every two cubic feet of space.  On the manufacturer's website, the diagram in the demo slideshow showed dimensions of 2' x 2' x 2' which is eight cubic feet.  I explained this error to the very pleasant customer service representative and said that I would be checking back to see if it was corrected.  I am very pleased to report that it has since been corrected and my conclusion is that the company is responsive to consumers and is diligent about the integrity of their products and marketing.  Yes, that is impressive and all-too-rare these days.The product is activated when it is removed from the packaging so you should not open it until you are ready to use it.  (The button on front you push activates the timer only, not the product.)It is stated to last up to 90 days.  On the company's website you can sign up for an emailed replacement reminder when it is time to replace the product.  This is a clever marketing ploy but it is also very useful to the consumer.  The website is very informative and worth taking a look at if you are considering purchasing the product.  I would also not hesitate to call customer service with questions.  [...]I would recommend this product as useful for protecting valuable items prone to rust that are stored for moderate to long periods of time in small enclosed containers.  Other reviewers have pointed out that there are other methods of rust prevention that are more appropriate in other situations but it is a good product for the intended use.
summary: Great for rust prevention in small spaces

reviewText: First off, I could not see any benefit using this product in my toolbox. It's a 30-day product so what's the point? I suggest priming and painting any metal items to prevent rust.

I immediately put this into my safe and expect it to protect my valuables.  Keep in mind that each Rust Shield covers an area of 2 cubic feet.  I need about 12 to cover my safe according to the manufacturer's instructions.One Rust Shield is probably enough for a toolbox but there's no way it will protect a safe.

reviewText: While I don't begin to understand the chemistry of how these work, I'm a long-term fan of 3-in-one oil so I'm inclined to believe that they'll perform as promised. However, at nearly $6 each and with a life-span of only 90 days I'm not quite prepared to give up my conventional methods of protecting my tools, instruments, guns, etc. just yet. I've put them in the molded plastic cases of my least-used power tools and the drawers of my tool chest where I keep my infrequently-used handguns and knives and will wait to see how they perform. If each module cost a couple of bucks or lasted for a year I'd be inclined to rate them much higher but, so far, their price/performance ratio when compared to how long a less than $5 can of 3-in-one oil lasts just doesn't measure up.
summary: Seem great, but are they worth the money?

reviewText: I have been spending my summer fixing up a house that has a damp basement.  I have liked this product because I can stick it to the bottom of the tool tray in my toolbox.If you are `temporarily' having to store tools in a damp area this is a great application.  If my tools were regularly stored in a damp area I would want a longer term solution than having to remember every 3 months to put in a new thing.  However  this is a great short term solution.

3-IN-ONE No-Rust Shield Rust & Corrosion Inhibitor works by emiting Vapor Phase Corrosion Inhibitors (VpCI) that form a layer just a few molecules thick over metal surfaces. This layer acts as an invisible shield to protect metals from rust. It looks like a fancy device with a "gauge" for indicating when you should replace the "cartridge." In actuality, it's just a piece of specially treated foam encased in a plastic shell. The gauge is simply a chemically-driven indicator that changes color from one end to the other over time.Pros----+ No messy greasing and degreasing, for example, of fire arms.+ Vapor penetrates cracks and crevices to protect out-of-reach or hard-to-reach surfaces.+ Accurate gauge that tells you when to replace the cartridge. I started using the 3-IN-ONE sometime in the beginning of September (just over 30 days ago). The gauge is now correctly showing it has just under 60 days left of use before it needs to be replaced.+ Easy removal of 3M Command' adhesive strip.+ No-hassle protection (other than the need to replace the cartridge very 90 days).Cons----- Needs to be replaced every 90 days.- Cost of replacing cartridges over a lifetime of protection can really add up.- Works only in confined or enclosed spaces.---Whether the pros outweigh the cons or vice versa will depend largely on what you use the 3-in-one Oil Rust Inhibitor for. Personally, I wouldn't recommend it for protecting the stuff you plan on putting away in storage for long periods since you will need to remind yourself to replace the cartridge every 90 days. As it is, I'm sure we all have enough to worry about in our busy lives, and we really don't need to be tacking on yet another task on our to-do list. So, for long-term storage, a light coat of oil might be the way to go. For everything else that you need to use fairly frequently, the indicator will serve as a convenient reminder to replace the cartridge when necessary. In this case, the 3-in-one Oil No Rust Shield Rust & Corrosion Inhibitor definitely merits some consideration. Ultimately, you have to decide whether the 3-in-one Oil Rust Inhibitor is practical and economically feasible for you.

Not being a gun toting person, I'm testing this in my jewelery box.  It is a small enclosed area with items that tend to tarnish quickly as the jewelery box is kept in close proximity to the shower. reviewText: I expected to be able to just put this product in a toolbox, gun case, boat, etc and forget about it. But to my surprise, it only lasts 90 days! I'm not sure I fully understand this, if the product vapors a corrosion protection on the contents of the toolbox then why does it have to be replaced? The only reason I can think of is that if the tools are used then the protection is lost. There are tool box drawer liners that do not have time limitations that would be significantly cheaper in the long run. And it is only good for 2 cubic feet of space, it says that this is the size of an average tool box, most of mine are quite a bit bigger than that. Wiping tools down with an oily rag would also be a lot cheaper. If this product lasted for a year, it might be worthwhile but there are so many other cheaper ways to protect tools and equipment from rust and corrosion. But if you have an enclosure or equipment that cannot be protected any other way, then this product might be worthwhile (if you can remember to replace it and have access to it).

reviewText: I was curious as to what chemicals are actually used in a No-Rust product.  I dug around on their website  [...]  but could not find exactly what is used (they list it as proprietary on the safety sheet).  I was able to determine that it is a low risk substance and that the only harm that should come to you would be if you were to remove the chemical impregnated sponge and eat it.  In that case you probably have larger difficulties in life anyway.After reading through the information I decided to do a little experiment. I polished up my good silverware (it is annoying to polish as it has many small crevices and engravings that collect tarnish).  I took a third of the silverware and put this product in with it.  I usually keep a piece of regular chalkboard chalk in with the silverware (this is supposed to absorb moisture and slow down the rate of tarnishing) so I kept a third of it with the chalk.  The other third I did nothing to at all.  Put each in a plastic box.  Three weeks later the silverware with nothing is showing some tarnish.  The chalk and No/Rust are not showing any black.  I tried to take photos, but the detail does not show up.I will try to remember to check the difference at the end of the 90 days (that should put me around Thanksgiving when I will use the silverware again) and report back.  I wanted to get this review up, because I am not sure when the product will be released.I do feel like I will need to rinse off the silverware with the No Rust, as I do not know what chemicals are used.  The website says it is approved for use with food containers, but unless I actually know what that chemical is, I will have to rinse them off.I am giving it 3 stars for now, because it does work better than nothing I do not know the cost and I have some concerns about not know what chemicals are used.  Once I see if it works better than chalk I will revise my rating.**UPDATETook them out at Thanksgiving,  I notice a little less tarnish than the chalk but not a lot. We live in a dry area, so I am not sure if there would be a difference in someplace with more humidity.**UPDATESome difference at Easter, but not enough to make me continue using them.
summary: Running an ongoing test, so far better than nothing, but not different from using chalk. Wish I knew what chemical is used...

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Vapor phase corrosion inhibitors are not new (Common in military or industrial applications.  What is different here is that the technology has been repacked into a neat little plastic case with a self actuated timer and adhesive back and marketed to the general public.  I put mine in a box with several hand planes which have high carbon blades.These work by emitting a vapor which deposits on the metal surfaces forming a film only a few molecules thick.  Close inspection of the 3-in-One product shows some open cell foam peeking through the slot.  Foam is a common carrier for VPCI's  There are other common carriers - kraft paper, plastic film etc.  Do a search on "VCI anti rust paper" or "Armor Wrap Paper" or "VCI Emitter"Who really needs this?  Fishermen perhaps, where you are exposing expensive things to a salt water vapor.  Because it works by depositing a film on metal, I wouldn't use it on cameras or other optical instruments.  Musical instruments, jewelry, and silverware should be fine.  If you're just trying to keep your sockets from rusting, there are less expensive options.  Oh yeah, you need to keep it in a closed space or the vapor won't protect very well.It's a good idea but here are the following issues:1) This product is only "good" for 90 days.  Similar products are good for TWO YEARS - they lack the nice packaging that the 3-in-One product has, but are also less expensive - about a dollar or two apiece in quantity. (search for VCI foam emitter)2) Each time you use one you will be throwing a way the plastic case - it would have been nicer if they had designed it with a plastic holder, but the internal foam emitter was replaceable.3) This last one isn't an issue - 3-in-One missed the opportunity to tell you that these also protect electronics - these would be ideal in a computer you had on a boat or if you lived near the coast.  We had a problem at work with computers being exposed to sulfur (common in clay) some years ago and these would have come in handy had we thought of it (we ended up changing clay)Here's a cheap substitute - I put desiccant bags into my tool boxes.  These work differently (by absorbing moisture) and are not as effective, but you get them for free in many things you buy.  Just look for the little pouches that say "Do not eat" or "Dessicant - do not eat" and save them.Full disclosure: I received this item through the Amazon "Vine" programIf you've found this review helpful, please let me know.
summary: Existing technology repackaged for mass market - Interesting but expensive

NOT A SIMPLE DIY INSTALLATIONBe prepared to take the collar off your ignition and cut into your ignition wiring.As other reviewers suggested, throw away the directions and go to their website for instructions (although they still aren't very good).Aside from my beef with the installation though, the product works great and gives me the steering controls that I enjoyed with my factory stereo. Not complains, this product it's a good fit for my f150 truck with the pioneer AVIC d2 radio. I set it once, I had removed the battery of the truck several times in this 3 years and this device don't lose the configuration, so, it's a set it and forget it.

reviewText: We had this professionally installed 2 years ago, so we can't comment on that.  But we can say that it works really well in our Toyota van and has never given us any trouble these past 2 years.  Controls are responsive, never lags, and it really is cool having the controls on our steering wheel.  Very convenient to use while driving without ever taking your eyes off the road.  No complaints at all.  Wasn't expensive to install; included for $200 with GPS/Stereo install.  Price for the unit was good too.  Perfect!

This product is well worth the expense. The product is very small. Easily tucked into the dash. Programming the unit was easy. reviewText: After struggling to get old ones off these Timkin wheel bearing hubs couldn't fit any better. The ABS wires already had exact duplicates of the clips installed in the right place so they fit exactly in line to the holes for them to snap right in. After completion the wheels were so quiet as the bearing worked so smoothly. Would buy this brand again for sure.
These are great replacements to the stock Chevy truck units that both slowly failed on me.  worked great for my need.

Top grade steel and perfect fit.Timken makes wheel bearings for new GM vehicles and if you need a OE replacement don't cheep out and get a a less expensive one.I have know people that bought other brands and they are changing them within the first year.Another plus is that it comes with the ABS sensor that would cost $70.00 alone at the dealer.

reviewText: I always use Timken bearings in my vehicles. This unit has been in for about 16 months and 40,000 miles and it's still turning like it's brand new.

I purchased two of these for my 2003 Chevy Tahoe 4x4. These are the real Timken deal and made in the USA. I always try to go with Timken when it comes to bearings and now that everything comes with these bearing assemblies, I'm glad i can still do that. These come with the ABS sensors and all the clip bushings were in the right spots. Make sure you get a 36mm socket to get the axle nut off though!!
Fits Curt 13534 great.  Looks good.  Has a built in holder to avoid loosing it.  Easy installation.  I am very satisfied.

It works and it fits perfect. It fits tight and won't come off unless you want it off. It is also tight fitting enough to prevent water from getting inside the receiver preventing any rust. Looks clean and pretty much non-noticeable.

The product looks real nice. Larger than expected as it not only has a flange but a lip that covers the perimeter of the receiver opening.I have two issues.1) The slip on part that keeps it on the receiver (stretches around opening) does not fit my Curt 13130 receiver. It catches on the safety chain rings on the receiver. I tried to install it with the 4 pin wiring harness holder down. That extra rubber gave me trouble. I could rotate it but did not like how it looked.2) In the same orientation, "hinge" at the top, the extra rubber at the top (the hinge) was a real tight fit on my RDX. It actually pushed up the rear trim when in place.I really wanted this for a clean look. The texture is real close to car trim and has no logo. I ended up cutting the hinge off and installed it. Looks great just wish I did not have to cut it (or if I could buy a plain rubber cap without the extra retainer).

Had to install this "upside-down," but that's okay. My hitch is so close the bumper cover that the hinge "bump" on this cover was wedged between the hitch and the cover. Since I just had the car painted, and was concerned that it would rub a hole in the paint. I just turned the cover over and put the connector socket on the top of the hitch.Well, maybe this is how it's supposed to be? My light connector is in the trunk, not hanging outside the car, although this would work good for lighting kits that plug in outside the trunk to keep the connector up out of the way, hidden, and dry.Actually looks a LOT better than the bare hitch starting back at me. No logos or words on the thing either.This is only a couple of bucks more than the CURT "plug" that has the logo, etcetera. Well worth the investment, I think.

Very easy to install, fits like a glove and at a very good price. While I use the auto very little (as a back-up if the other needs to be used at the same time and towing) it has not come off or loosen.

This cover fit my new Curt hitch perfectly. I tried using an old cover I had for a 2" Reese hitch on my new receiver before buying this and the old one fit way too loose.  This is a nice design with thick rubber and fits perfect.

My girlfriend has a black 2002 S10 Blazer that is in fantastic shape and really looks good (for what it is) but she never liked the open trailer hitch receiver hole. I agreed that it looked "unfinished" and we began looking for a cheap, plastic plug with no logo. This was what she decided on and it looks great.We tow a small, 2 bike trailer from time to time and having the retaining ring mounted to the receiver allows you to just lift the cover and insert the hitch without having to remember where you put the cover later. It fits a 2" receiver perfectly and has no issues that I can see. It is pretty well made and is cheap enough that if you get 3 good years out of it, then you just get another one. She is on year 3 and it still looks perfect. Having said that, she is a fastidious car washer and keeps her vehicle in very good working condition. YMMV.
Fits on my Class III/IV hitch! Gives the back of the vehicle a nice clean look and should keep the hitch clean and free from debris.

OK, so no one likes a trailer hitch mounted on their vehicle unless of course it's a pick-up truck where it is the nature of the beast. But on SUV's and sedans, that receiver hitch just looks like unfinished business. Of course there are those options of placing caps with team emblems, and other affiliations in attempts to put lipstick on a pig, but then the whole point is defeated by drawing attention to the unappealing hulk of functional metal drooping from the rear of your vehicle. No logos, no lettering, just a thick black cap to give the hitch that finished look. The rubber is very thick so it should hold up well for many years. There is a little tab added to neatly tuck and protect your flat four plug. The whole cap is one casted piece of rubber, so when you do have it unhinged while towing, there is no hard plastic that will bang around while on the road.

This not only protects the receiver from dirt and water it also protects the trailer harness from dirt and water.  I'm very satisfied with this product. I highly recommend this for anyone wanting a quality and useful item for their trailer hitch.

stays in place. looks good especially since the hitch is curt brand also!

reviewText: Total fit - square peg inserts into square tube - insert pin with carter key and your done, ball nut is already inplace and tighten for you - from box to finish - 3 minutes.
Fits my trailer hitch just fine, only thing I changed was I spray painted it black to match my blacked out Jeep.

This works great on our trailer with the reese sway bar attachment!! We turned it upside down and mounted it the other way for a 2" lift on our 25' trailer and it really helped out!! Highly recommended!
Good News1) mates up well2) fair priceBad News1) none so farLooks good and solid. What more do you want?
summary: Great match for Curt towing mount

reviewText: I've had this hitch on my truck for a couple of months now and it's done what it was supposed to. The ball hasn't loosened, it fits fine in the hitch, and there's not much more to it. The ball does rust quickly but cleans up quickly with some chrome polish. In the end, it's meant to work, not be a fashion statement.

This ball mount has the same thick paint as the CURT receiver hitch that I bought for our GMC truck. It promised to provide more protection against rust, but Amazon failed to pack it properly.  This item, which is rather heavy, was bouncing around inside a box with some other items on the way here, and the paint is damaged (a few nicks). I'll dress that up, but make sure you inspect yours before it's exposed to the elements, and do the same.  The ball is already mounted to the metal structure. The quality of the metal looks good, based on the surface that looks more smooth (no imperfections) than the Reese I replaced.
summary: This one is better than the Reese

reviewText: Arrived as described and very fast. Love my Prime membership. Unit is perfect for my truck and I replaced an older on with it.
summary: Great hitch for my truck - good price

reviewText: looks good and fits perfect. I would reccomend to anyone who wants it to go with the Curt receiver. nice
Does the job intended for, no problem with it, good stuff, good price, I do recommend. I also recommend that you buy the locking pin instead of that one coming with it.

This tow ball is a great step up from the stock u-haul one i had. This adds +1500lb towing capacity and is a lot sturdier. Rock solid and nothing can get through this. Surprised at the price, should be more for how much of a tank it is. Great buy!
This looks like a good, high quality hitch.  I have installed it but have not used it for any towing so I cannot comment on it's actual performance.
It is a hitch ball.  It does the trick.  What more needs to be said. Five more required word s.
I had a reese before i got this and man can you tell the difference in the quality this looks and feels much better made and even the pin is better quality than others. great buy!
I needed a hitch for my Titan pickup and this one is heavy-duty and works perfectly.  It's easily stowed away when not needed.
summary: CURT Manufacturing 45036 Class III 2" Loaded Ball Mount with 2" Ball

reviewText: What can I say; it's a piece of steel with a hardened steel ball that does what it's supposed to do. The best thing is that the made in china sticker is missing, cause it's made in the USA; a rare treat. Buy two & give one for a Christmas gift.
I've only used this hitch once since I bought it, but it did its job. I used it to pull a utility trailer about a total of 200 miles.
Gets the job done. Needed to tow a car transporter in a pinch and this little jobbie did the trick.

My husband installed the Rugged Ridge Black Receiver Hitch Kit on my 2012 Jeep Wrangler Sport, in less than an hour all by himself and attached the CURT Manufacturing 45036 Class III 2" Loaded Ball Mount with 2" Ball.  Not only was it easy to install, but we towed a full 8'x6' trailer from Ohio to Florida and back and it did great!!

PERFECT size for my 2012 Jeep Grand Cherokee Laredo.It makes a ton of noise with an empty trailer attached, but with the trailer loaded, it's smooth and quiet. I have no need to change the ball size right now so I like that it's securely installed into the ball mount already.Used it to tow a Uhaul 5x8 trailer (1200 lbs) over 3,500 miles and gave me no problems!
summary: Great Ball Mount for the Price!

reviewText: I bought this to go withValley 74080 Class III Receiver Hitch. I use the hitch to pull a boat and to pull a trailer. The hitch is well made and so far it has held up to a lot of abuse. The chrome on the ball mount has also held up pretty well; it hasn't started cracking or rusting. Great value product gets 5 stars.

My hitch receiver sits fairly low and I require different height ball mounts depending on the application in use at a given time. I use small trailers, cargo carrier and bike racks depending on my need.  This mount allows me to tow a trailer and carry bikes when used in conjunction with the double receiver accessory. Well made. Great delivery service. A happy Amazon customer
Works as described. Brake controller doesn't recognize it but the plug brake light will illuminate if you use the manual slide on the brake controller.

Seems I am slow, as I tried the 1st one and could not see it working...the 2nd one "snap" in place working as it should.  I then got the 1st one it too now works...guess there was some pin off or something.  Thanks to Amazon's great return policy I am sending back one of them...
Not much to say but when you need one of these things you need it NOW.  Comes in handy tracing down wiring issues especially those found in older vehicles.
This is such an easy way to check the wiring.  I used to use a voltmeter and this is so much simpler.  Highly recommended.
I used this to test my truck power source and my extension cable after my grandson pulled the truck away form the RV without disconnecting it. Fortunately, I didn't have a problem.

This 7 way tester is a must to have for any one who tows anything behind thier vechile. It makes it so easy to test any  vechicle'S tow recepticle.  I purchased it and used it to test the wiring at my motorhome's 7 way plug and then plug it in the 7 way plug on the front of my towed vechicle to find the problem, It's Great ! The lights tell you exactly which wiring to test.
This tool provides a simple way to diagnose wiring problems, more specifically it lets you isolate the problem to either the tow vehicle or trailer.
summary: Must have if you tow a lot!

reviewText: Now I can look quickly at the problem and find the problem quickly.

I have placed one of these on our 2002 Honda CR-V, and one on my 2012 Ford Fiesta. Both hitches went on very easy and instructions are great!  The only thing is the original muffler hangers allow the muffler to swing against the hitch (on both vehicles), causing a very annoying vibration and clunking sound. Easy fix was to go to automotive store and buy longer muffler hanger. Perhaps they should include them!!!!
summary: Better get a longer muffler hanger!

reviewText: This hitch was probably one of my best purchases ever for my 2003 Honda crv.  It's of exceptional quality and finish.  Installation was a breeze if you read the paperwork/instructions prior to the installation.  Fishwiring can be a little tricky at first.  I am purchasing a second one (different model #) for my new/used 2010 crv soon.  Just remember that this is a class III receiver which naturally can support significantly more weight than a class I receiver.  Make sure your vehicle can handle the weight being towed.  Great product and looks sharp under the bumper.  Highly recommend.

Put this on my 2002 Honda CRV. Everything lined up perfectly. It is very well built and easy to install. Watch the installation video on the curt website. I sprayed the muffler brackets with silicone a day before install. I put the back of the car on jack stands to have more room to work. removed muffler hangers lifted in place by myself laying on my back and using my arms and legs and got the nuts started, it would have been easier with two people. Total install time was about 30 minutes. It is solid and pulls my small boat and flatbed trailer just fine. Hope this review helps.
This receiver went in just as described and planned for. I wanted a heavy duty receiver for attachment of a winch or for pulling logs. Nice and heavy.

Pros - Bolted right up.  Fits perfect, well made, easy instructions.Cons - noneI do not know why but I did not have the problems some stated.  The muffler hanger hooked right back up.It is tough getting it up by yourself.  I would recommend 2 people.  I used some wood and a floor jack.  Jacked the jack up before I started and put the one side on the wood and then pushed up the other side and pumped it up tight.  It did take some gentle moving so that it did not fall off the wood.  The wire guide worked well and it only took about 30 mins.  The one thing I did was to get all the bolts in and the nuts started before I tightened them down.  Before I tightened them all the way down, while just a little loose, I knocked it around to make sure it was straight and as far back as I could get it.Fit perfect, sets nice and high tight up against the bumper.Way less than buying one local.  Cheapest I found was still over $50 more than this delivered.Well worth the money.
Fits and looks great on my 2007 Sequoia. I installed a metallic (Masonic) car emblem on it and it looks awesome.
Nice look on my 2013 all black F150 fx2.  Fits loose so I wrapped some electrical tape around it so it fit snug.  Looks great though.

It is being used with a Curt hitch.  This seems to be a great deal compared with others and I like the fact that it is steel and not plastic.  It is of high quality construction and the padding behind the head prevents the cover from making any noise when touching the receiver.
Mine has never been used and paint chipped off.  Can be a real tight fit too (can make it work still but the foam gasket has to compress way too far).

I wanted a decent black hitch cover to use as a base to mount a skull head to something sturdier than what it originally came on. This is a nice well made plain hitch cover so whether you want something plain in itself or something plain to work from, this is a great hitch cover. I highly recommend this product.
summary: The right tool for the job

reviewText: A perfect fit to finish off a 2" receiver hitch. It looks great and does not rattle when you drive.

I ordered this before measuring (a big mistake) the distance from the plate to the hole and this wont fit many applications correctly. With the pin in the hole, the plate sticks out way too far from the receiver, over an inch and then rattles. I just threw it away as its too costly to send back. Drilling new holes would be difficult and then rust problems. BOTTOM line, measure your receiver application and then ask them if this unit will fit correctly before buying. Their specs should indicate the distance from the plate backing to the center of the hole.

This replaced a broken plastic cover that was hit by a car 11 month ago in January on a expedition then to a trailblazer could not find one for 8 months till now this has a water tight gasket that will help keep water out
Fits the Class III Receiver by Curt.  I like the durability of this cover much better than plastic ones.  It does have a small amount of play but not enough to make noise.

has a little rust  ( I have the kids paint it for me )the metal mesh floor  is really lightweight ( cost cutting by MFR. )I added an attachment by MasterBilt.. a bike carrier that piggybacks to the Curt Basketgood product but would doit  again with an aluminum basket from Harbourfreight 99 dollarsand add the Masterbilt carrierstill 4 stars though
I have used this a few times and it is easy to put on and take off of my Jeep. So glad I purchased this Carrier.

Thia says 500lb capacity, maybe right over the main support, but otherwise you should balance your load well and I will use straps to help support the outboard corners.  I kept it because it is a usefull thing, but not for a heavy items.

Used for one trip so far... worked well. Sturdy construction. I added $5 worth of reflectors to it just for safety's sake.Like others have said - it sits a little loose in the hitch. But not because of the hitch or anything, it's because of the bolt-together design where the rack pivots to be raised/lowered.F.Y.I. to any FJ Cruiser owners - no, it won't clear the spare tire to flip up into the stow position. But it does extend far enough out to where your gear in the rack will clear the spare.

I've only used it once, and it works. It's sitting in my shed till I need it again, so I'll have to report back if it starts to rust or something.Assembly wasn't to difficult, I put it together by myself, but might be slightly easier with an extra set of hands. The railing didn't line up perfectly so it didn't slide together easily.

Amazon shipped this carrier's OEM box in a larger Amazon box so I don't have the issue other's have expressed.  Mine arrived in great shape.  Bought it used on Amazon for about ninety dollars shipped to my door.  Not sure what "used" indicates, but this thing was shipped in as new condition...very pleased...Assemble and install were a breeze...about 30 minutes with proper tools. I also bought the anti-rattle pin for nineteen bucks and a Rola waterproof case for eighty which works out great.  All-in-all, very pleased with my set-up.  You won't be disappointed...this is the one...You won't find a person who does more research and price comparisons than I do...believe me, if you find this under ninty bucks shipped to your door, buy it!

Pros:* Sturdy construction* Looks decent* Was a good buy at the Lightning Deal priceCons:* Instructions suck - but it's fairly easy to figure out. Put together in a half hour. WIth instructions that didn't suck, it could have been 15 minutes.* As others said, box arrived in TERRIBLE condition. It's amazing all the pieces were still there* Too pricey at the non-special price* Mine arrived with a few scrapes and a badly dented mesh floor panel. I pounded it back in shape, but it's a bit tacky if you look closelyCould Go Either Way:* Heavier than I expected. My wife will never be able to hook this up to her care by herself* Would have preferred it to be a few inches less wide. It looks a bit funny on the Focus as it's almost as wide as the car, and definitely wider than the back end... and that's an awful lot of torque/leverage to put on the 1.25" connection point. (much better on a standard 2" hitch)* The bar that goes into the receiver can rotate 90 degrees to store the platform on the back of the vehicle in an upright position, or flat, up against a garage wall, whichever you prefer, but when extended horizontally, it adds an extra foot to how far behind your vehicle the platform sits.Other Notes:I stuck this thing on a 2012 Ford Focus and on a Dodge Ram and instantly hated it. As you can see in one of the customer photos, it sticks WAY out, and on a small car it just looks ridiculous. There's around 20 inches between the bumper and the backside of this platform.The good news is, and I don't think the instructions mentioned this, if you don't care about being able to fold it up at a 90 degree angle, you can remove the entire pivoting piece  and the platform will still plug right into the receiver, matching pin holes and all. By leaving off this piece (which I don't care about anyway since I'm not going to leave this thing on my car full-time) you save a good 10+ pounds, lessen the torque load, and bring the platform to a respectable 9 or 10 inches (even closer if you don't have to use an adapter) from the bumper where it doesn't look so dang stupid.However - as feared - if you want to use this on a small car, you will likely have a class I or II hitch with a 1.25 inch receiver, and by using an adapter, you introduce two points of sloppiness to the mechanism, meaning the platform can move and tilt. I don't think it's bad enough to cause you any problems as long as whatever you are carrying is securely fastened down, but you might feel it jumping around a bit as you drive. I'm wondering if I can shim it a bit to get rid of the excess play. The sloppiness if much less on a 2 inch receiver with no adapter.Minor other note: my car came with proximity sensors to warn you if there are kids or obstacles near your car. With the platform attached, the alarm stays on solid when you are in reverse gear. It thinks you're about to run over a tricycle or something. No problem in drive.4 stars at lightning deal price3 stars at regular Amazon price2 stars if dumb enough to pay list price1 star if it arrives with pieces missing!0 stars if you use it with the pivoting piece and drive around like a dork with it hanging 3-4 feet behind your car... especially on a small car.
summary: Pros and Cons - things to be aware of if used on small car

reviewText: 5 starts if it were not for them being a bit light on durability.they fit my hand like a golve, go fiture... but the velcro strap is a real weak point.The hook side of the velcro is a ridgid adequate, but the loop side is weak.Not only the loops themselves, i can see them wearing out after a long while, but the entire patch...The threading that holds the loop part gets torn up from the hooks... the glove area around the strap gets torn up by the hooks, the delicate yet fashionable mesh part REALLY gets torn up by the hooks...i took some ice hockey skate protector liquid and just slopped it all around the area for some protection, but still those hooks are tearing up everything they touch... and i am very careful with their use.otherwise 5 starts i love the feel fit and look of these...I almost reduced to 3 stars because of this, its that bad.And if you dont do something to take care of it, they may only last you a seasongood warm weather glove though

reviewText: The gloves looks great.  Looks like a quality built.  But after using 5 times, foam paddings from the inside started to come out.  Let's see how long it will last.UPDATE (9/17/2013)Developed a hole on one of the fingers with only about a month and a half of use.  Maybe about 10-15 rides.  I still like the fit and feel.

reviewText: i bought theres for my daily comute back and forth to work theres not as much padding in them as my more expensive alpinestars but they were much less
summary: i like these gloves for there price they work well

reviewText: These seemed to run a little bit on the tight side for me, but I didn't send them back because they're so close that I feel like going one size larger might end up being too loose. They seem like they'll be pretty comfortable after breaking them in. My first impression when I put them on was, of course, the snug fit, and also that the seam in the fingers of the left-hand glove were a little uncomfortable. The right-hand glove was very comfortable. After a few minutes the left hand glove almost started to feel like the seam was pushing into my index finger in such a way to separate my nail from the finger; this left my finger tip pretty sore as you can imagine. I also noticed that the seams on the left-hand glove were fraying a bit and that glove's wrist opening doesn't fit me snugly like the other glove does. Anyhow, I reported the problem and if I can get the left-hand glove replaced with one that fits as well as the right-hand, I'll love these.All-in-all, assuming most sets don't come with a defective glove, I'd recommend them.

I have ridden my 2011 Hayabusa in 100+ weather for 539 miles with these gloves and can say they are fairly decent so far.  They are true to size and keep my big hands really cool with no sweating.  The seams and velcro are holding up well. The palm material seems a little thin.  I think the padding should be a little thicker for injury prevention in case of a fall.  Overall, they are good gloves.
Nice gloves. Good grip, hands don't sweat, good fit and comfortable. Nice look and easy to put on and take off. Would recommend.

Just what I needed for my 2012 voyager motorcycle . Under the seat on right side is a wire connector, you want to use the blue wire to make the connection for the brake. This device gives you two options on how your lights for the brakes can be set , i chose the blink blink blink and steady light than a recycle again. Works great.

Just installed the Back Off XP on my 2013 Ninja 300 and it works without any problems.  Took about an hour or so to install since I wanted to make sure the wiring was cleanly done.  I do wish however that it had a switch to change the different modes rather than having to connect a specific wire since this makes it more of a permanent install, but it is just a small gripe.This unit also has a yellow wire which can be used for hazard lights using an on/off switch.  I personally didn't use it, but it may come in handy for others.  Overall the unit is compact and nicely sealed.  It also comes with a mounting sticker so that it doesn't rattle around.  I'll have to see how it lasts over time.
Lets just say I havn't been rear ended yet. Thinking of putting one on my dualsport as well. Works well and is easy to install.
Arrived promptly. Quick, simple installation. Module has two available configurations. Nice to have an attention getter to help drivers see you on your motorcycle.

This module attaches to the wiring of your brake light. The instructions are reasonably clear. It helps if you have had some experience in 12v wiring but is not absolutely necessary. You will need some small connectors and you will have to know which wires to connect to, so a wiring diagram would be helpful. It has 2 modes of operation, one which flashes continually on application of the brake, and one that flashes and then remains steady. Before you tap into the wiring, make sure you have enough space for the module when you put everything back together.

I had another grille add-on that involved a lot of zipties and adhesive behind the grille.This grille is SOOO much better.HIgher quality, better looks, etc.It's worth the better price.Yah, it's technically NOT billet, but that doesn't matter for this application. It's aluminum slats on a plastic mounting portion that snaps into the grill with no adhesive, no zip ties, etc. It stays secure.

Not exactly custom fit for the grill (there's a little play for them to move up and down) but they look good and do an admiral job keeping rocks, sticks and bugs out of your radiator. Super easy install, they just snap right in.

I wanted to something to both protect the delicate cooling fins on the condensor and tranny cooler, plus make the grill look better by hiding all that stuff.  These were super-easy to install and they look great.  You can even ignore the instructions to remove the grill (which only takes about 90 seconds) and just snap them in from the front.

I put these in myself (55 yr old woman) took like 5 min. Just snaps in, they look great! There is a top and bottom to them so make sure if it does not snap in easy to turn it around. I get so many compliments on these, love them!

The first batch came cracked or with broken tabs. Exchanged for replacement and all pieces arrived in new condition. Installation was a breeze and I like the look it gives. If the replacement order would have also come with broken pieces, I might have likely look for a homemade solution.

I took the grill off and these snapped in quickly and easily.I really like the look, and it will protect from crap from flying into the grill.

These fit perfect. I changed the screws out since the stock torx screws are a nightmare, but these mount any lights away from the body. Rather than putting the bolt of the light near metal/paint, these mount it high, but as far out as possible on the windshield.

Very easy to install takes about five minutes I pre drilled mine with a very small bit and installed it.

Installed it yesterday. Looks great! Much needed improvement for a low price. We will see how the paint holds up as per other users have complained
Looks great and clean.  Easy to instal and it appears to holdup to everyday use.  I would recommend this to everyone.
