If you want protection for your lights, go elsewhere.

I would stay away from the rugged ridge light guards all to together they are poorly made for the price you pay you not going to be happy with the welds or if they even can get the bars lined up right

Nice product. Very easy to install. Looks great. I have already ordered the grilles for the turn signal and marker lights to match these. You need to take off the front grill and use a star drive bit to remove the factory silver retainer ring around the headlight. Took me five minutes to do both of them. I've seen reviews about the screw tabs being flimsy or poorly welded. Truthfully, they are identical to the tabs on the factory retainer ring so don't think they are going to snap off the moment you take them out of the box and screw them in. They are well made and they serve their purpose. These are however, just for looks. Do not expect them to protect your lights from rocks, heavy branches, or collisions. They are simply for aesthetics only. A must buy for anyone looking to add a rugged sporty look to their Jeep.

This item that I ordered twice in two different sizes. Always said it would fit my 2013 jeep wrangler sport unlimited. Never fits!! Says easy to install, but it does not go over the light cover. Really wanted this to work the second time. Chance the description and say doesn't fit 2013 jeeps.
The light guards look great and were pretty easy to install, even on a cold winter day.  Works well with the matching tail lights.

Be prepared to remove the front grill to get these things installed.  A Torx screwdriver with a magnetic bit or head will help a lot since the screws are so tiny.  The arcs are made cheaply and bend easy, so you have to be careful not to bend them while installing.  They look good once installed but probably not worth the money.
You do have to take your plastic grill to install these. It is easy to install just follow the instructions and remove your old trim rings. Fit on a 2011 jeep jk sport with ease.
summary: Buy these it makes your jeep cooler

reviewText: This product arrived quickly and was very easy to install.  I have a new 2012 Jeep, and they add a nice visual touch.  I don't expect to be bumping through a field of brush, but I don't know how much this would help anyway.  But they look great.
This is a big cargo carrier! I installed mine on the back of my rv,to carry 300 lbs.worth of gear( presently).It is made well!
Cargo carrier was surprisingly easy to put together. It is very solid and well made. I would recommend it to anyone who wants or needs such a thing.

Use this on our 2012 Tahoe.  We have 3 kids and it is a must have when going out of town to have the extra room for an extended trip.  Strong and durable.  One of my best purchases.  Much better than the cheapo ones.

I was looking for a carrier to put on the back of my travel trailer.  something to put my generator and cooler on.  this met my dimensions and assembly was simple.  11 nuts and bolts and less than 10 minutes and its ready to go

easily assembles and good dimensions well worth the money . if you are going to place a fitted cover to it then lay a thin sheet of plywood to protect cover from getting holes worn in it, I used a sheet of floor vinyl to do it there are some models that are just a few inches smaller but this is so far the largest size. the weld joints are 1 St. rate I am confident that its going to be a sturdy carrier

We bought this for a beach vacation for some extra room in our vehicle.  We hauled all of out beach chairs, umbrellas and ice chests without any problem.  There are plenty of tie off points to strap everything down.PROS:  This carrier is sturdy overall.  The expanded metal at the bottom is not super thick, but good enough.  All of the rails have held up well without any problems.  Assembly was as simple as it could get for something this big and bulky.  Build quality seems good.  I never worried about our stuff back there after the first pit stop.CONS:  After a week at the beach some of the bolts rusted a little.  Not a huge deal, but not good either.  I just painted them with primer and a matching black paint.  Also, and this may seem silly to some, but the sticker on the back plate is crooked.  That's just irritating to me.  If you are going to put a sticker on something, make it straight.OVERALL:  So far I haven't had any issues with this carrier.  It's worked well on a long trip and also hauling gas cans to the local store.  Painting over the bolts wasn't a big deal to me, but it may be for some.  That stupid crooked sticker is the only thing I don't like about this.
The Pro Series 63153 60" x 24" Hitch Mounted Cargo Carrier is a great cargo carrier.  Very solid and sturdy.  Well manufactured and designed.

Easy to put together and works great. I'm glad I bought a better one like this vs the others in its class.I really like the extra deep basket (24in) compared to the std 20in ones.Very good quality and great price!

I bought this carrier to allow me to pick up more mulch and top soil from Home Depot than would fit in the back of my Jeep Grand Cherokee, take brush to the dumps, and transport items that I would not like to put in my truck (such as yard waste).  I've been using this hitch carrier every weekend for nearly two months and it has performed well.  The heaviest load I've used it for was 8 bags of mulch which were 2 cubic feet each so a total of 3/4 of a cubic yard.  I'm guessing around 450 pounds.  The cargo carrier was very stable and the top rails gave plenty of locations to strap the bags down to.The only bad thing about these carriers is since they extend past the frame of the car/truck it puts the weight outside the foot print of the vehicle which make it feel like you are carrying a heavier load.  Don't expect to put this on a standard car and carry significant weight around town.
summary: Great carrier for hauling extra gear

reviewText: I purchased this to haul extra cargo behind a Toyota Highlander and I'm glad I purchased it.  We just used it for a 1500 mile round trip and it performed wonderfully.  I used it in conjunction with a hitch tightener to guard against bounce and sway.  I also purchased the Rolo LED tail light assembly that fits this carrier.  It held a cooler and several suitcases in a cargo bag very well.I used a torque wrench for assembly as directed, and things went smoothly.  I think that mine assembled a little crooked - either that or the hitch is a little askew, which is totally possible.  Regardless, I'm very pleased with the quality and build of this carrier.It is light enough for one person to carry and install.  Probably easiest to set the bottom on the ground and lean the tongue up onto the hitch before lifting into place, but feel free to install it however you like.  If you're feeling sporty you could try a sideways javelin toss if you have good aim and a steady arm.I'd recommend this to you if you want to carry extra cargo without climbing up on a step stool or ladder to load a rooftop carrier.  This is easy to access and it doesn't wreck gas mileage either.UPDATE 3/12/14:  Still a five star review from me.  I've used this a few times in two months and it remains easy and solid on the back of our suv.  After putting it in and out of the hitch a few times, the paint has chipped off the edge of the hitch attachment, which is to be expected.  Otherwise, no rust, and this has been through several rain storms.  We are very glad we have this for extra cargo.  We are getting a hitch extender that will allow us to mount a bike rack above it so we can use it when we go on vacation and take our four bikes with us.

The receiver on my Dodge caravan sits fairly low and my other carrier tended to drag entering and leaving driveways. I did three things. I added a roller on the bottom, put a hitch on the wires Subaru and transferred that carrier to her. This new Pro series carrier has shaped mounting bar that raises the entire carrier. No more dragging problem plus this is 60" wide where the other is only 48". Now I would like to find plastic tubs of optimum size to fit this carrier. Any suggestions?

I bought this bulb as a replacement for a burned out clock backlight in my '00 Accord. The installation was easy enough (pry the clock section up and out with a screwdriver, disconnect the cables, and unscrew the old bulb), and it lights up my digital dash clock just fine. If you can find it cheaper somewhere else, definitely go for it, I would rate 5 stars if this bulb wasn't $6 (it definitely isn't worth that much!).
The light for the clock went out, and I used this to replace it; and it works great. The replacement procedure is super easy, and this part was super cheap.If your clock light is out, get this.
My clock light was out in my 2001 Honda Accord, and this was a perfect replacement.  Easy to replace and looks like OEM.
summary: Works great in a 2001 Honda Accord

reviewText: just what i need it for my dashboard clock light.just like the factory one. i wend to Radio shack no luckamazon is the right now to get it thank you.
My 2000 Honda Accord, has the clock light go out. So, I ordered this to fix the issue. Works great and has been working fine for the past three months.
summary: Hey, it fixed an issue I had.

reviewText: Performed a test out in a nearby parking lot with my camper. Once placed under the tire, the item never slipped when the camper was pulled up onto the item. They are wide enough not to be concerned about the tire slipping off the side of the item.
Very easy to use.  Great for not only leveling, but tire changing as well. A must have I your RV tool box

These are rugged, very solid and made in the USA. These are also lightweight and will pack/travel easily. A snap to use, you'll find this product much easier to work with than other traditional leveling methods. I recommend going to their website to see a video demonstration.
Excellent results. Used to level our 38' motorhome. Definitely would purchase again. Their not cheap price wise but then they are well made and very sturdy.
summary: Excellent results. Used to level our 38' motorhome

reviewText: This could not have been easier. Put it under the wheel, drive up until the trailer is level, put on the parking brake, push in the chock and you're done. Two people make it much easier to use but you could do it on your own.

When I first came across these my thoughts were......I need those.  To date I haven't have the need to use these, however there build quality is amazing and should handle the job they are intended to handle.  These will make quick work of the task of leveling a trailer with ease.  They could also be used to raise one axle on a tandem axel trailer high enough to allow for elevating the other axle in the event of the need to change a flat tire.It is very easy to justify the purchase if for no other reason then the need in an emergency to change a tire.  They can also be used a tire chalks to prevent the trailer from rolling.

Got these to use in mt 05+ Tacoma. They do fit in the blank panels on the left, however you do need to file down the lip on the edges. The switch itself works good and looks good. Has a OEM look to it. The color of the light is okay, but I wasn't expecting much. Easy to wire up, the switches are kinda deep ( compared to others ) so keep that in mind.

purchased a couple of these for my accessories on my wrangler. Light is bright so at night you know exactly if its on or off. also takes some effort to switch so its hard to accidentally switch it on.
the switch is very nicely constructed and the light inside the switch is very bright.although it is more green than blue so buyer beware.

Needed to add another 12 volt device in my motorhome dash.  Wanted an exact match with other switches already installed.  Works great.  My only complaint is that they do not give either the dimensions or pattern for the rectangular hole size needed.  Would be an easy and very helpful fix.

I installed this in the stock Fog light switch location on the dash of a YJ Jeep. It works great and should last for years. It does get a little warm, and it's on a relay so not many amps running through it Overall, very happy with this switch.
summary: Fit my Jeep YJ dash perfectly

reviewText: The Rugged Ridge side A-pillar switch pod will work with this switch.  Rugged Ridge makes similar switches but I like the shape of these better.  The directions that come with the switch are clear and so they are easy to connect.  The power for the lamp light comes from the wire going to the relay.  There is also one terminal on the back that needs to go to a ground connection. So there are three terminals on the back; Power In, Power Out, Lamp ground.  The terminals are standard size and easy to connect terminals to.  You will have to get your own terminals and wire; there is no wiring harness for the switches.The plastic for these switches seems a little light weight but other reviewers have indicated no long-term problems.
summary: I Paired Four of these Switches with the Rugged Ridge Black Left Side A-Pillar 4-Switch Pod.

reviewText: Required some minor trimming as this is slightly bigger than your typical switch holes. Probably only by 1-2 mm.The blue light is not really blue. It's really light blue and almost feels like it has a hint of green. I got this to replace a green colored switch since most of my lights are blue. This did not help that much.Don't expect the blue to be a true blue. I wanted it to match my blue colored dash lights, but it doesn't.In the end, it works fine and is of acceptable quality. I'll try a different manufacturer next time though.
summary: It works... but it's not really blue and needs minor trimming.

reviewText: I bought this for my light bar/fog light setup, it fit perfectly in the switch blank on my Nissan Titan without modification. The only complaint I have is that the light is not blue, it's more of an aqua/blue-green color. Next time I think I'll use red.
I bought this to hook up some electronics in my jeep and I needed switches and these worked great I am glad i bought these.Make sure to look at the other daystar stuff also
summary: I installed this in my jeep

reviewText: Son installed it in his boat and works as it should.
I've purchased quite a few of these but have started switching to another brand that isn't so bright.  Once you have more than 2 near each other, they get VERY distracting at night.

I got these for my drive lights I mounted on my grille guard. They work great and are very well built and look sharp as well so I gave them 5 stars.However, for the Ridgeline they do not fit very well in the utility spots underneath the A/C controls as that they are not wide enough to fill in the extremely wide gap Honda has. Eventually I will possibly try to get OEM switches to replace these so I have a more finished look.

I love these rocker switches, nice quality.  Added a custom instal to my truck to control the off road lights, these switches look great, have solid a solid feel when being used and the illumination can be seen during the day and is not overwhelming at night.  Will be buying mor for future projects
Bought these for my FJ Cruiser, and they fit...ok. Not great but they fit. You have to trim a LOT. So keep trimming and trimming and eventually it will fit. They looks great, and work well!

Great switchs , I have a JK and bought  the Daystar KJ71034BK Lower Switch Panel - Black and they are a well made switch and if wired correctly you will have years of use with no problems will recommend.
This is a good switch for all needs. I have used several and never had a problem. Daystar switches are good quality,

I have a RZR and had a switch plug in the dash, I tried other more expensive switches and had more problems with that. This fits just perfect, it wires up easy and stays dry in rainy condition. I would recommend this switch over any others that I've tried any ways, and the price is great... Michael

BOUGHT A FEW DIFFERENT COLORS OF THESE SWITCHES TO PLACE IN THE FACTORY KNOCK OUTS IN THE DASH OF MY 2012 POLARIS RANGER 800HD. THEY FIT PERFECT AND MAKE THE DASH LOOK LIKE IT CAME THAT WAY. USED FOR POWERING UP OFF ROAD LIGHTS AND SOME INTERIOR LIGHTS THAT I ADDED. THEY HAVE BEEN SPRAYED DOWN AT THE CARWASH AFTER EVERY RIDE AND HAVE NOT STOPPED WORKING YET (1 YEAR OLD).
summary: PERFECT SWITCH FOR A POLARIS RANGER

reviewText: Awesome, 3-pronged switch! I have the Daystar 4-switch panel in my Jeep JKU and these little buggers are awesome! Paired with the light harness from Tuffledsdotcom (also here on amazon), and the daystar switch panel, the result is a completely clean, stock looking switch setup  for anyone who owns a Jeep JK. Using this setup, I run an array of led light bars and led flood lights all over my Jeep and I could not be happier with their function.

I installed this in a 2005 4-Runner with a set of Hella fogs. The switch that came with the Hellas was a total joke. This switch fit the factory slots next to the steering column with minor filing needed. It functions well with a good, clean look on the dash. The light is bright but not too much so. Awesome switch for the price - cost me half as much as any of the others that would fit the factory slots. Very satisfied.
Works great and fits in my oem spare switch spot. Have it controlling the fog lights installed. Definitely would recommend  this switch

I bought two of these.One of them provides power to my ARB switches and the Dakota Digital air pressure gauge that monitors my ARB system pressure and the other provides power to another Dakota Digital air pressure gauge that monitors my airbag pressure.The switches closely match my ARB switches...which is nice because it just doesn't look nice when the switches on the dashboard don't match.Clearly labeled for ground, power in/out, etc.The light comes on only when you turn the switch on and is not very bright so the light does not present a night-driving distraction problem.Durable.

The LED blue is a little faded kinda light blue color, but otherwise it has a nice click action for the rocking mechanism, fit very well into my car's switch bezel, so im real happy with this switch.If they can make the blue LED a deeper blue color, would definitely be a 5 star rating.  but anyway, I am happy with the switch.
summary: Fits well into factory switch bezel

reviewText: Daystar makes nice switches and amazon's price is hard to beat anywhere else. Fit and finish is hard to beat too.

I have this sitting in the Rugged Ridge A-Pillar of my 2012 Wrangler JKU. It's switched to my KC Hilites. Switch works great. Nice solid feel to it. When you turn it on there is no extra play. Very well built. I'm getting ready to get another to act as a power switch for my HAM radio in the jeep.
much better quality and appearance than the ones you buy at the auto parts store.These look OEM and look great
Very neat design, it fited perfectly on my Wrangler 2000' light does not bother my eyes at at all, good material.
It took me a lot of research to find this rocker switch.  I have some like it in my motorhome and needed another installed nearby. Works great.....and matches!

I have use these for KC Hilites, as I do not like the factory switches that KC sends with the lights. I have had them in two diffrent Jeeps and never had any issues. Will buy again as needed in the future.

The light might be a bit bright for nighttime driving, but at least you know it's on.  It almost fits in a stock TJ Wrangler auxillary switch location, but not quite.  A little bit of filing was needed.

These switches are very bright, and constructed well.  The only reason I gave it 4 instead of 5 is because I mounted them on the dash where my knee can hit them entering the truck.  The first time this happened... One of the 4 broke.  Granted... My knee did it... But it still happened.  It's a good enough item that I replaced it with the same exact switch.

I like these daystar switches. I have 6 of them in my Jeep currently and have yet to have on fail. The light is bright but not too bright. They are well built and sealed from dust. Water resistant to a degree, I just wouldn't submerge them.

This switch works fine, and looks great in the dashpiller for a JK from rugged ridge. But the lights are BRIGHT whether the switch is on or off. In the day, there is nothing wrong with this. At night, if you have your panel full - there are 4 bright lights putting light into the cabin. If you like the cabin to be as dark as possible it is annoying.The hot issue has seemed somewhat silly as these could/should have been LED bulbs. They are incandescent, and if it is warm and the car has been on for a while I would guess the light part gets to around 130-140 degrees. Hot enough you don't want to keep your finger on it. I cannot imagine this is going to be detrimental to the long term (5-10 years) function of the switch, or at least its appearance. When you have gone to the effort to install and wire everything up - you don't want to do it again ever.Edit - solution given to me by fellow customer.
summary: The light is always on and it gets HOT! - Can be fixed

reviewText: Daystar makes a great switch and locally they're twice the amazon price and sometimes more. Quality construction puts these above the rest for the price point.
these work as advertisedwill eliminate the un easy highway hood flapping.these are much sturdier than the factory ones. easy to install

I didn't notice that much hood bounce after buying my 2009 JK 2 door, but after installing a bug shield I thought I'd have to move the spare tire onto the hood like a '60's Land Rover. The hood would lift at anything over 60. I'd already seen a set of these on a friend's JK, so I knew they were tight.Install took just minutes. I decided against unbolting the lower as the instructions suggest, and just went all in and cut the stock elastic away from the pin. (1st pic) Once the pin is exposed you can just snap the plastic sleeve over the steel pin inside and slip it out. I cut the sleeve with nippers.Do this on a warm day - Daystar's elastic doesn't even give you enough length to drop the latch into the top pocket the first time, so you'll have to muscle it up. Can't even imagine how this'd work out on a cold day.A required mod for freeway rides, certainly with the bug shield.
summary: Serious Hood Tension - No More Bounce!

reviewText: Like everyone. I had the dreaded hood flutter on our 2010 JKU. These solved my problem. They are much stronger than the factory rubber pieces. I have my doubts about the hardware though, time will tell if it rusts, but I would have liked some other kind of fasteners. I'll update if I spot rust on them.EASY way to install?  Throw away the instructions. I used a small chisel to split the factory rubber off the plastic retention pins then a pair of side cutters to cut through the plastic cover on the factory pins once the rubber piece was removed. Then it is as simple as putting the new pieces in place and tightening the hardware down. You should be done with this install in 5 minutes.I highly recommend this product.
summary: Awesome product. Throw away the instructions.

reviewText: Great product from Daystar.  No more hood flutter.
easy install and great replacement for the factory hood latch. It takes away any and all hood flutter especially at highway speeds.
summary: great product, secures hood very well

reviewText: This helped to keep  the jeeps hood from flopping up and down while driving down the highway. I sold the jeep because they are crap.
summary: A good fix for a crummy vehicle

reviewText: 2013 jeep....hood flutter at higher speeds....drilled the old latches out and put these on....no more flutter...i even notified jeep that this was a flaw in the factory latch.
Easy to install and looks good. Have not really used it much, I guess it was more a want than a need. I've seen some guys attach a GPS to it.

I used a interior panel tool and had this installed in under 5 minutes.  The Compass module screws right into the pre-drilled holes that came already built into this panel.  Great spot for sun glasses, change or other small items.  Absolutely matches previous panel and looks like it was always meant to be there other than the Daystar logo on the front.  Worth five stars but it does not come with clips to latch on to mounting slots so you have to them off the OEM piece you just removed.  They should have come on the panel or I would have given 5 stars.  Also agree with advertising but wish the Daystar logo was a little smaller.  Not sure fitment issues with other viewers, but fit with not problems on 2007 Jeep Wrangler Sahara.Would buy again and definitely recommend.

This is exactly what Jeep should have done with the dash from the very beginning, but I guess this is why we have aftermarket parts...to improve upon an already great canvas. It fits well and looks very factory besides the Daystar logo but I don't mind it.
This panel installed in under ten minutes.Super easy to install and looks and works great. Now I have a place to toss item on my dash where they will not fall off.
Bought for my 2009 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited. It was very easy to install and good quality. I would highly recommend this to others.

Would be nice without Daystar on it. Not a major complaint just a comment.Be really careful not to lose the clips from the stock panel, i dropped one into the dash and found they are not listed as a separate part from the dealer (gotta buy the whole panel). They hang on good but a couple seconds to make sure they did not stretch when removed from the stock part can save some grief if you have to take it off later. I dropped mine after pulling the panel back off to change the radio. I will be sure it is on good this time.
summary: nice to have somewhere to put things

reviewText: Installation was easy and only took 15 minutes to complete.  I didn't have a problem taking off the clips - just be sure to take your time and dont rush it.  The finished product doesn't exactly look factory, however no one other than a die-hard Jeep fan would notice anyway.My GPS unit is too small for the lips so I'm still going to use the window mount for it.  I'm also considering getting rubber matting for the insets to ensure things dont move while in motion.  Overall I'd recommend it as it does add more space to put things like a phone.
Can be made more useful with a strap that can hold in rear tray goods, as well as anti slip materials for both trays.  Other than that, great product!

I purchased this to hard-mount my Garmin GPS unit to, as I refuse to suction-cup it to my windshield.I didn't want to screw through my factory dash panel, so I purchased this one, and put my stock one away in the garage.This thing fits perfectly into the place where the stock panel sit, and honestly it looks better too. If you're wondering howthis panel installs, it's literally just a pop out and pop in design. I used a large flat-head screwdriver to pry the end closestto the window up (that's the end with the tabs), and it came out easily. The change over from stock panel to this onecould not have taken longer than a minute to complete.One thing though, you will need to remove the metal snaps from the stock panel and attach pop them onto this one.For some reason this item doesn't come with any, which almost made me knock off a star... but it's awesome so I didn't~Rusty

It took me a lot of research to find this rocker switch.  I have some like it in my motorhome and needed another installed nearby. Works great.....and matches!  The only thing missing is a template for hole needed for installation, but I was able to measure and get it done.

This switch is HUGE! so unless you are planning to cut the whole in the dash or put it in other location - it will not work.It doesn't fit in the dash opening for fog lights.Also, wiring the light is very complicated in my case. If I wired the way it is deigned, my fog lights would have been always on.I sent the switch back
summary: Looks good, hard to wire, VERY big - doesn't fit the opening

reviewText: I bought this for my jeep I had to hook up two more switches for some electronics I put in my jeep and it works great and takes up no extra room at all
summary: I bought two of these and they both work great,

reviewText: Great lighted switch that fits tightly into factory blanks on my 05 Tacoma.  The lights on these are VERY bright, so beware of where you install it, it could be an issue at night!
I have purchase several of these Daystars and all are still going strong. Precise fit in the precuts in my dash. The switches look as good as they function. AAA+++

We have purchased several of these in different colors for use in car.  One nice thing is the mounting is via a  hole which allows the switch fit an opening in our Toyota dash.  Hole needed a little trimming with a Dremel grinder..  Good price; good quality.
Fits directly into the blanks on a Nissan Titan. Knocked off one star because the price is a little steep. Other than that, they're great.
Switch is water proof and lit to show on or off, easy installed and just plug in and go. If you have lights and don't have a switch to turn it on, this would be a great one to have... Michael
Rocker switch fit perfectly in Polaris Ranger. easy installation. I've used it multiple times since installing and it appears to be well made and will last a good while. Time will tell.

This is a great switch they really care about compatibility with different mounting.  The plastic "holders" on the back have shim grooves on them so it grabs like a hook yet it is still easy to remove from the panel.  The wiring instructions are simple and easy to read.  The light is bright but not so bright that it is distracting.  They work great with Rugged Ridge A-Pillar for JKs.  They are heavy built and look great.
Hard to beat the daystar switches, they're quality made and the price here is nearly impossible to match elsewhere, you won't be disappointed.

Overall, this is a very good wheel brush. The bristles are long and soft, so no worries about scratching or overly harsh treatment of the wheels it cleans.The brush area is very large, so those who have wheels or rims with intricate openings may need an additional cleaning aid. My wheels are like this, and so I go behind this brush with a washcloth for the deep detailed parts of the wheel.I also wish the handle of this brush was slightly longer; another 4 to 8 inches would provide better leverage.
summary: Good wheel brush, but not quite perfect...

reviewText: Okay, so it's great, but it's too big to get between the gaps on my mags and clean behind the spokes. If Mothers could just make a set of 3 wheel brushes ... so I can clean the front, then the sides of the spokes, and then reach around to get the flat part of the rim too ... the part you can see.

What's not to like about a wheel brush?  :)  This brush actually does beat other brushes out there. The bristles are just right for my chrome/clad rims. I have noticed any scratching at all and have been using for a year.  Water and soap only.

I bought the Mother's Wheel Brush to help keep the spoke wheels on my Harley clean. They look great, but are a pain to keep clean. This brush helps clean them in one swipe. The softness of the brush keeps from putting any marks on your wheels or tires.
Medium bristled brush is just right for my truck wheels, to get into the tight spots. Soft enough not to scratch the finish.

The bristles are much softer than I thought.  I use this for washing my convertible top.  If you're looking for a brush to really scrub something, you might want to find a brush with stiffer bristles.

I already had a wheel brush however it was beginning to reach its useful life so I looked around and found what I think is one if not the best wheel brush on the market. This one is 10 times better than the one I am tossing. I especially like the handle as the soapy water tended to make the all plastic handle on the  other brush slip in my hands. This is a very good product that should last for years.

Does a good job on your "tires".  Has a threaded hole for an extension stick so you don't need to reach down as far.You should use a microfiber towel and detail spray on your wheels.  Treat the "painted" finish on your wheels just like you do your cars body.  They have a clear coat and finish just like your cars body.

I'm pretty happy with this brush as it can get in to a lot of nooks and crannies of the wheels. The bristles are soft, so I feel confident that it isn't damaging my painted wheels while cleaning them. My only suggestion which prompts me to give it four stars instead of 5, is a change to the design. While trying to get in to all of those nooks and crannies, it would be helpful to have the bristles going in multiple directions, not just straight out the brush facing one way. The edges of the flat part where the bristles come out, came in to contact with my wheels over and over. If there were bristles coming out of the top, I wouldn't be banging that rubbery part on my wheels but instead cleaning the wheels that much faster. Just my opinion
Another quality product from Mothers. I am not sure that you necessary need a brush dedicated to wheels, but considering how dirty they get, it's probably a good idea.
Well, it's a brush but I've never bought them before but it worked amazing and wasn't too rough but perfect to scrub :D

This works awesome for cleaning wheels and rims! The brush is very soft so it wont scratch the rims and it gets into a lot of the nooks in crannies! I really like this wheel brush and would highly recommend it!

reviewText: I purchased this brush to work in carpet cleaner into my vehicle's carpet.  For that purpose, this brush worked perfectly.  It also worked well on my car's heavy-duty cloth upholstery, but I had to take care not to scrub too vigorously, as the brush's bristles are very stiff.When I used the same brush on my high/low 70's carpet, it did the job, but I had some concerns again about how hard I should scrub.  Then came the Berber carpet, where with very little scrubbing with the Mothers Carpet and Upholstery Brush I snagged it.What did I learn?  This brush, while very well made and easy to grip, should be tested out on an area of the fabric or carpet you plan to clean prior to committing to use it on a large area.  It's tough! Too tough for some jobs that require a gentler touch.This brush could easily be used to scrub tile floors or similar jobs on hard surfaces, so if it doesn't work for you on carpets and upholstery, it's definitely not a throwaway item.  Just know that it may take some time to find a brush or brushes that are 'just right' and not too hard or too soft for your cleaning job.Other brushes to consider:Fuller Original Garment & Upholstery Brush,Chemical Guys ACC_202 Professional Interior Induro Brush, and if you have a drill,Chemical Guys (ACC_201_BRUSH_MD) Yellow Medium Duty All Surface/Purpose Carpet Brush with Drill AttachmentorDrill Powered Upholstery Scrub Brush.
summary: Not for every carpet and upholstery job

The soft bristles will not scratch, however, they retain dirt or staining and are difficult to clean after use.
summary: Not so good for small multiple spokes

reviewText: It's a bit flimsy, the wires that loop around are thin and will bend easy.  The fuzzy part is also a thin low-count bristle, and doesn't really seem to dig in and clean.  Good handle though.
summary: Ok, but you'd do better finding a similar brush locally

reviewText: Great product, it does a great job of removing contaminants from barrels of rims. Be careful with how much pressure you use. If you use too much pressure the wires that hold the brush together can scratch the rims. I would purchase this product again.
Does the job but I'd like it to be a little softer on the brush and of a sturdy construction as it bends very easily.
Not everything promised, easily bends and losses bristles, not long enough.  Not overly happy with the product and would get a longer or bigger brush.

great to clean these new rims on most cars especially the ones that get filthy from brake dust that just doesn't want to come off in a car wash -- a few quick strokes with the handy dandy double loop brush and voila clean as a whistle - sometimes no amount of chemicals and technology can replace some good ole' elbow grease in using a brush - thanks Mothers for staying true to the roots of what makes sense for car enthusiasts

It did the job but its bristles are a bit soft and fold easily under pressure.  I guess the softness is based upon using it on classic cars and it will prevent scratching?  makes sense but for use on your driver, it seemed a bit lacking.
summary: This brake dust brush was very good.

reviewText: I bought this along with the wheel brush to make cleaning my wheels easier.  I get tired of all the cracks and crevices in the wheels where brake dust and road grime like to hid.  This brush does a great job with just car wash.  I did not use and wheel cleaner and it did a great job.I took one star off because on the first use, as I used the brush to reach the inside of the wheel - the part accessible through the holes in the wheel itself, the black wire brush was getting bent out of place as it made contact with the rotors.  Because it's wire, my fear is that it will move back and forth too much and eventually break off.  I would have like a more rigid connection to the handle.All in all, I'm happy with the brush, and it's a good addition to the car wash kit.  I may add the lug nut cleaner eventually.  If I have three different brushes, just for wheels, is there something wrong with me?

I finally got tired of having dirty wheels - with caked on road grime and brake dust.  These Mothers Detail Brushes work great.  I use `em along withMeguiar's G14324 Hot Rims Aluminum Wheel Wash - 24 oz..  The brushes reach into every nook and cranny, even around valve stems and recessed lug nuts.  They even clean the metal logo on the center of my wheels.  Very cool.The bristles are strong and they don't fall out.  They do, however, take a real beating.  Hey, better them . . than my nails.  As a suggestion, I found it's easier to clean my wheels if I ask my hubby to remove them from my car and put `em up on a work bench.  He'll do this for me - if he's in the right mood.  That way I don't have to stoop.I also discovered that these brushes are great for cleaning behind my faucets, which is always hard to reach.  As a size comparison, the bristles are about twice as long as a regular toothbrush's and much firmer.  They're the perfect tool for the job.  I'm sure these Mothers Detail Brushes probably have many other uses, as well.  I just haven't discovered them yet.  This is a product I highly recommend.  Enjoy.
summary: Works Great.  Saves My Nails.  Good for Behind Faucets, Too

reviewText: Nice small brushes that are useful on the car and also bicycle. They're good value at this price, but I'd not buy if they cost much more.
What can I say other than they do what is advertised but if I had to do it again I would just get the large brush and skip these smaller ones.

I'm a fan of Mothers car care products, so when this item popped up on a search, I had to try it!For more years than I can remember, I've saved old toothbrushes for cleaning in tight places.  There have been many times I wished the toothbrush bristles were longer to get into deeper crevices.  The Mothers detail brush has longer bristles, plus its crushed bristle ends won't scratch as a toothbrush bristle could.  The nonslip handle is a nice touch.  I haven't used that rubber piece on the end of the handle, so no feedback on that.One of the reviews I read said the bristles were too hard & could scratch.  In my opinion, they're soft, almost too soft.  I'd prefer them to be a bit more aggressive.Another review I read said they didn't last... wore out too quickly.  I cleaned 3 vehicles with one of the 2 brushes & there was little to no wear that I could see, comparing the used brush to the unused brush.I'm giving 4 out of 5 stars.  I like this detailing brush, but I'd prefer a stiffer & longer bristle.► Update - May 5, 2014The last couple packs of these that I purchased have stiffer bristles!  Not sure these are as safe to use on a painted surfaces, as the first batch that I purchased with the softer bristles?I decided to drop my product rating to reflect my dissatisfaction with the stiffer bristles.
summary: Much better than using an old toothbrush!

reviewText: I bought these to use on cleaning my rims.  They're the perfect size and have a comfortable grip.  It's like having a toothbrush for my car.  :)

Getting to the cracks and crevices on any car is always an issue when you are detailing a vehicle. These are really heavy duty brushes that do a great job in getting to the hard to reach places on a vehicle. There are sturdy and I believe they will last  a long time. Especially like the along and strong handles.

These are very soft indeed, which make them more useful for some things, less for others.For getting into hard-to-reach areas for regular cleaning, these are perfect. Will clean but will not scratch or damage the surface.For cleaning embedded or attached grime or similar, these do not quite get the job done.In that case you will want a different tool and/or cleaner.

reviewText: I love these brushes for cleaning in and around emblems, they are soft enough not to scratch the paint, however I would press too hard on the paint with them.  I use the other one for cleaning corners of wheels, where brake dust collects, makes it so much easier.  They also clean up easily with some degreaser.  They are larger then I thought they would be too, but thats not a bad thing.

This inst really a piece of finally tuned machinery, it is a brush. It does what it was meant to and doesn't have any defects or flaws so far. I like Mothers car products and this one is no exception. I would recommend for tires and scrubbing the wheel spokes. Could also be useful inside the car
Not really worth having as the brush is smaller than the head making it hard to get it in the hard to reach spots.The brush is not very sturdy so doesn't last very long.
Very handy to use, good ergonomic design, comfortable to hold and rubber handle  grips well , even when wet.A bit expensive for what it is, but works much better than you used tooth brushes.
These brushes came in handy for me when cleaning up a new/used truck, and also when cleaning between the fins of a motorcycle engine prior to painting.

reviewText: If you have show cars, these detail brushes are a must.For those that want a nice clean detailed ride the same applies.They get down in the hard to get to places.Good deal for the price.I love them and would highly recommend these detailbrushes for anyone that takes pride in their ride.Complete Microfiber Towels Car Kit - 2 All Purpose Microfiber Towels - 1 Microfiber Towel For Streak Free Glass- For Home Or Auto - 2 Ultra Plush 16 by 24 Microfiber Auto Detailing Towels - 1 Auto Dust Pad For Home Or Auto

These are nice and soft brushes. The help me clean the crevices in my car's wheel. Before I would have the squish a sponge in the areas to get it cleaned. Now with the brush it, it goes much quicker and cheap to boot.

reviewText: well i bought this set of cleaning brush.s so the i could get inbetween the crack.s and areas you wouldnt normally be able to get to and this set of brush.s delivers the kind of cleaning only a brush like these can deliver and is highly recomended

The 3 brushes work well both inside and outside the car.  They dust hard to get areas and they help get ride of old wax on the outside.
These work well for detailing and cleaning the small hard to get areas when cleaning my truck and cars.  Very pleased with these from Mothers.

reviewText: Great for small crevices and the price is right for such a well made brush. Can  be used for other small cleaning around the house.
The brush is okay. It does what it's suppose to but the hairs on it are very weak and brittle. After a few uses or hard use, it seems like it will come right off.

I use these brushes on my car to clean the spaces between the door, fenders, hood and every place wax might not be reachable with a cloth. The brush is sturdy and the bristles are long enough to get to those hard to get places.

These are great brushes for tight areas like little corners where the spokes meet the hoop of the wheel.  They are actually a little larger than I was expecting, probably about twice the size of a toothbrush.  The bristles are stiff enough to actually clean without being too stiff so you have to worry about damaging the finish you are cleaning. a must have for a auto detailer gets into all the nooks and crannys of any car with ease 5 star rating

reviewText: I have been using one for the wheels and one for the carpet in my Genesis Coupe. My wheels are plasti dipped and the brush doesn't harm the dip or remove parts of it which I love. I like the size of the brush because it fits into my little detailing bag perfectly.

reviewText: These little brushes have allowed me to clean some hard to reach areas on the exterior and the interior of my vehicles. I can wrap a cloth around the end and it allows me to clean small crevices that I would not have ordinarily have reached.  On the exterior, I can remove wax that sometimes gets into small linear crevices with the tip of the brush.

reviewText: The bristles are not as stiff as I had expected for a detailing brush.
I bought these for cleaning the nooks and crannies of my rims and also around the emblems.  Perfect for the job at hand!

These work pretty good , really. I wanted them for my wheels and they do the job. The only thing I could ask for is that ...they could be a little longer so I don't have to bend so much. But I have a bum knee and if it were not for that, they would be a four star.
These are great detailing brushes. Good firm bristles yet soft so as not to damage anything. They do a great job of getting into cracks and cleaning out dirt or wax. A must for good detailing.

I don't understand why but the two brushes I got were terrible. I used them to wash the small crevasse's on my motorcycle. Bought these along with wheel brush for my car.  These handle the difficult spots and those where the brake dust is more difficult to remove.
it is small n helps to clean my wheels and also engine bay. not giving it full 5 stars as already brush bristles are worn out with 6 month use.
These are great little QUALITY brushes.  Perfect size for small areas and clean up very nicely with the hose for next use. We love them.  Seller as fast and efficient.

I love these guys for detailing our cars.  They're small (not too small) and can get in just about everywhere and don't force me to try to use my big brushes and towels on fine work.  Especially for doing grills and around windows and what not.  Buy them, you wont be sorry.
If you are looking to get all the dust in the blower vents and around the buttons on your radio this soft brush will do the job! The best thing is it comes in a pack of two for both of my cars.
Good brushes sturdy will last a long time very good quality product.  I will buy more of these types of products again in the future.

I cannot believe I did not buy these sooner. They are great for cleaning my brake calipers. My calipers are painted yellow on my CTS-V, and always get dirty. It's very difficult to clean with a sponge. But with these brushes, they make them look brand new and I'm quite happy with that.

Primarily intended to be used on automobiles, with bristles which are of medium softness, Mothers Detail brush is not supposed to do any damage to painted surfaces, providing it is not used dry.  This far, that claim seems to be true, as the brush has not done any damage to the finishes on my car.The handle is well designed, providing a nice solid grip, even when your hands are wet, while also allowing for applying leverage.  The brush is a little on the thin side, so you're generally not able to attack a large area, but the bristles, which are about 0.9" long, do provide a little extended reach.The soft bristles however, are kind of a double-edged sword.  The brush doesn't tend to scratch surfaces, but the bristles do seem to get deformed rather easily.  When tackling a tough job, like wheel rims, you can apply a lot of muscle, and the brush still does only an average job of cleaning.  Because the bristles tend to get bent out of shape rather easily, you can expect to replace them rather frequently, so it's good that these brushes come in a pack of two, and are not that expensive.These bright red brushes by Mothers, do a fairly good job, and can be used for detailing, but they don't stand up to heavy use very well, so you may need to be prepared to replace them on a regular basis.
summary: Mothers detail brushes work well enough, but will probably require frequent replacement...

reviewText: I have an 11 year old yamaha in my riding stable and after having some paint repair work done on the back end of it, I found I had an opportunity to clean areas that would otherwise be inaccessible when the bike is assembled. I purchased the Mothers Detail Brush Set to clean out gunk, old dried oil, bugs, debris and eleven years' worth of dirt from the underside and within cracks of the engine, frame and back end.And these brushes worked perfectly. I used soapy hot water in a bucket and basically brushed these parts as you would your teeth, occasionally rinsing out the brush in the water. The temperature of the water made the bristles super-soft and despite vigorous brushing I did not damage the paint on the frame or any chrome areas on the engine. With that said, these ARE brushes and I wouldn't use them on open areas of paint such as the bodywork/bike tins for fear of scratching the clear coat. If you have such dirt and gunk on your vehicle on very visible areas whether chrome or paint you probably should be looking at an alternative more delicate cleaning system.The handle was comfortable and firm and didn't bend or break despite applying quite a lot of pressure to it at times and by the end of the cleaning - probably two to three hours - I was still using brush number one and it still has a good bit of life left in it. I was honestly expecting to go through both brushes on this project and then I was intending on throwing them away. So I felt I have received excellent value in terms of longevity by still having one quite usable brush and one brand new too.Do take into account that these aren't replacements for microfiber cloths to save time nor are they stiff wire bristles. They're over-sized toothbrushes and when used for the appropriate purpose are perfect.
On my cars I prefer microfiber over anything else. They just seem to glide easier, clean better, and hold up longer. I've tried sheep ,sea, and other types of sponges. This one is  a good deal.

I just tried out this microfiber wash sponge on my car this past weekend. It was great to use a sponge that held the soap and was strong enough to hold up when I rubbed hard into the very dirty areas around the wheel wells and down under the bumpers. But, what I really liked best was that I could just toss it in the washer and dryer, and it came out looking brand new again!
I feel so much better washing my car with this . it cleans so much Better than a regular sponge . the one I got was Yellow.

I'm pretty OCD about my cars and scratching up the paint - these sponges are super soft! Nothing like a "normal" sponge, and almost feels like it's not doing much cleaning-wise. Anyway, if you want a sponge you can use when washing the car and don't want to worry about scratching the paint, this is the one!
This is a great tool for washing the car. The color varies. I just happened to get my favorite color by chance. I got the color green. I was overly happy. I would recommend this to others.

I bought this because I wanted something to wash my rims. I used to use rags but it was hard to get in to the crevasses.This is great because the foam conforms to whatever I'm scrubbing/wiping so I don't miss spots and things get cleaned better and faster.

This is designed to get the bugs and other stubborn material off the front of your car, and itworks wonders. Everyone knows hhow hard it would is to get bugs off. Using this product makes things much easier. You can also scrub pretty briskly and not damage your paint.Great product.
it works, its a sponge to remove bugs.....ya, its that simple....not sure a review is really necessary but why not, people like to be reassured when buying online
SEEMS TO DO A DECENT JOB ON MY CAR WITHOUT SCRATCHES...RECEIVED IN GOOD TIME, PRICE IS FAIR, WILL PROBABLY PURCHASE A SECOND ONE..PRODUCT IS AS SHOWN....NO SURPRISES

The mesh on the outside of this sponge makes it easy to gentle remove bugs and most other foreign objects from your car in a gentle fashion without damaging the finish.  I have found that you do need an additional liquid product to help with the removal of sap.

Works great, just remember to clean it during the process, some of the things you remove may scratch your car. Works great with turtle was or armor all bug and tar remover.

reviewText: Armor All Ultra Shine Wash & Wax would be a great car soap if it didn't leave behind a white film. I thought it was just because my truck was black but I just purchased a new car in red and have the same results. I mix the proper amount of soap (1 oz per gallon), the surface of my car is always cool to the touch and in the shade but nothing seems to solve the problem.
So I'm giving this 5 stars because it does what it does, and is decently priced. It's supposed to be a wax and wash in one.

Cleans very nicely, I can use it in direct sunlight with no spotting or streaking (white paint job).  Car pretty much dries off by itself like that, not a whole lot of towel drying necessary, but every finish might be different.  I consider this mostly a car wash soap; I don't know how the wax aspect is, altho I think the finish looks a bit better since I've been using this.  I would recommend a regular waxing every so often anyway.  But I'll keep using this about once a month.Like to add something.  The directions say to use it in a bucket of water.  I do it differently, by dripping some lines of it on the car, then hosing it down a little, then sponging it, then hosing it off completely, then drying it.  Like I said, you might not have to dry it too much, depending on the temperature, today it was a bit cool out (S. FL), and almost dried itself.  I used it in direct sunlight.  I checked the finish carefully afterward, no spots, and the paint felt very smooth.  So I think the wax aspect of this is pretty good, but will still wax every 3-4 months anyway.

This car wash works pretty well on the painted surface.I dont like the wax residue it leaves on the windshield.It makes the wipers streak very badly,even after cleaning with glass cleaner.If it rains within a few days after washing the car you will notice the wipers streaking.
This armor all car wash ultra shine worked great on any vehicle. I would highly recommend this to anybody that wants to give their car and very good showing.

This is the best car wash and wax out there. My car shines bright for about a week after a wash.Removes all the dirt and grime with no problem. This is the only product i will use on my baby.I get about 6 washes out of the bottle, well worth the money. I would however reconnmend that you useMeguiar's Supreme Shine Microfiber Cloths (Pack of 3)to dry your car. Those are seriously a must to make sure your car looks its best.

very good purchase. i added it to a purchase and got three for a little over 6 added bucks. can't go wrong if you need one for that price.

I wish this came with a tether, since I just ordered this from Amazon after losing my first one due to having to head out suddenly.Other than that, I give it five stars because it works quite well, easy to remove, but yet fits in tightly enough to prevent the CEL from coming on if the door seal isn't working right.I always use a gas cap lock on all vehicles I own... it not just prevents gas from being removed or unwanted substances from being introduced, it also has kept a vehicle from being stolen in the past, since the car was so low on gas, the thieves couldn't fill it up, so it was abandoned at a gas station.I do wish Ford could offer a locking fuel door, or like in the older Japanese cars, a fuel door that would pop open if one pulled a lever near the driver's door. bought and fits perfectly my 2013 F150 Supercrew FX4.  Overall, it's pretty cheaply made, despite being OEM, and I don't doubt if someone really wanted to pry it off to get to your gas, they could do so easily.  But, it's better than nothing, and it'll hopefully be the deterrent I need.

reviewText: For some reason, Ford seems to think that cap-less fuel filling is a major selling point for their new vehicles.  I bought a 2011 Fiesta in January 2011 and, with the price of gasoline rising since then, worried about my gasoline being stolen.  Add to that a slight inconvenience I experienced when my "Check Engine" light came on shortly after refueling.  When the Ford dealership checked the car out, the verdict came back that the fault code probably was caused by the flapper not sealing completely.  This Ford locking gas plug comes with two keys, fits well in the USA-spec Fiesta (although another reviewer's comments suggest a possible incompatibility between this plug and vehicles built for Ford's Asian market), and seems to be just the ticket to calm my fears and hopefully keep the "Check Engine" light off.  The only reason that the plug didn't rate a 5-star rating for me was that it is a little inconvenient not to have a tethered plug/cap.  It seems sturdy, the lock works just fine, and it is not a lot to pay for additional peace of mind.  Highly recommended!
It fits my 2010 Mustang V6.  And with gas approaching $4.00 a gallon again -- a way to protect that very expensive gasoline from theft.
Works as advertised and comes with two keys.Bought it for a '13 mustang, which to my surprise had no gas cap and locked gas door!

Needed a cap for the truck 2011 Ford F-150 XLT and didn't want to go to dealers and waste time when this could be delivered to my door in a few days. It arrived in 3 days. Fit perfectly and even the keys have "fuel" imprinted to avoid any confusion if attached with numerous other keys.

This is a much cheaper alternative to dynamat and works even better than it.  It's thick, but easy to handle in terms of cutting (use a utility blade) and very sticky so it adheres well.  One thing to beware of is to ensure you do not use bare hands when pressing down on the surface as the aluminum layer you cut through is sharp and will easily slice through your fingers.How much will you need?  This has 36 squares to it.  Most small to midsize cars will need about 60 squares for comprehensive coverage of all doors, trunk, quarter panels,and wheelwells - you'll need more if you want to do the floors. So you'll need to order 2 boxes.  Luxury vehicles with extensive soundproofing will probably be able to get away with just 1 box though.  For those with performance vehicles, realize this does add considerable weight if you start throwing in too many so use caution with the right amount of weight penalty to coverage.  For those who haven't already done so, you probably want to do a speaker upgrade on your doors when you do the door panels as you'll have to take them off, it's easier to do them both at the same time.Once installed you'll notice it right away. Vibrations will be more damped and while it wont turn your tin can vehicle into a luxury vehicle, it will be much quieter - you'll keep staring at the speedo and wondering if its reading wrong when it says 75 when your ears think its 40.

Great product. Easy to cut to needed shapes & easily malleable. ORDER the roller; it provides pressure needed for best adhesion. Aluminum tape (separate purchase) closes tiny gaps which are bound to occur. Cut, trim with box-cutter. Except for the underside of the trunk lid, this pack covered the entire trunk, spare tire well, rear wheel wells, rear doors - all the areas which produced the majority of intrusive white noise. Roadkill provides excellent cabin-sound damping. The woofers are in the rear deck above the trunk. Lining the trunk brought them to life, making them produce studio-like sound, i.e., instruments and voices are brilliant. Easy to apply, however, be sure to set aside enough time to do a neat job. Worth the cost and effort.

this stuff is great. LESS than half the price of the dyna brand. and better quazlity. yes i have used both. lots of it. and this is hands down a better deal. works flawlessly, thicker, easier to use, and price is unbeatable. applied well even at 55 degrees.
Very easy to work with.  I did both front doors on my car.  I have never used any type of sound deadening and this stuff did not cause me any issues during installation.

There are so many of these products on the market these days.I spent a few weeks reading reviews and trying to decide if I really wanted to bother with using this stuff or not.After a lot of online reviews, youtube videos, car audio forums I finally decided to buy the Stinger brand.I'm very happy that I did.It's a very high quality product, the price fair and it's easy to work with. I made sure to buy a nice quality roller and a heat gun to get the best results.I used this kit on a 2001 F150 Supercrew and there was plenty for all 4 doors and I had a lot left over that I'm going to use on other areas of the cab.It worked very well in eliminating rattles and reducing road noise.

I have in the past used dynamat due to that was all i knew. then someone turned me onto the stinger overkill which is in everyway identical to the dynamat as far as i can tell. I love dynamat dont get me wrong and th stinger is actually a little less flexible due to it seems thicker aluminum which i hear is a good thing. However it performs just as well and its 40.00 cheaper on amazon! Fat mat may be decent for horizontal surfaces but is not good for vertical and smells to high heaven unless you air it out. Stick with stiinger!

reviewText: I purchased this item and at first, thought of those goofy Sham Wow! commercials and their unfounded claims.  When this arrived I put it away until a good day to wash my car came around.  I wet the Absorber XL before using, and squeezed out the excess water, and discovered that it was amazing at removing the pooled water (from a waxed surface) with ease.  I followed with a quick micro fiber towel to remove any excess water and to completely dry my car.  I highly recommend this product.

Despite the great reviews this product has garnered before I bought it, I was half expecting to be disappointed by it.I've been using very sweet real chamois cloths for years, and expected anything else to pale in comparison.I liked the fact that it ships damp, in a sealed bag inside this plastic case, so that when you get it, it's flexible.  As with any good chamois, once it's dry it's pretty stiff, and will need to be moistened again to get used.The size was good, large enough to be useful without being unwieldy.  It lets you get a good section of a car dried before getting water out of it to go back for the next section.And for someone like me with a tiny little smart car, that's a large part of a car to dry in one shot. ;)So for anyone who's been using something like this for a while, you know what to expect, and you won't be disappointed.  Only thing better is to have kids old enough to do the work for you as a chore. ;)
The water absorbency properties are not as good as the old chamois from these guys... but still better than some other brands out there. In my opinion is much better that Turtle Wax or Maguires
summary: Not like the Old "The Absorber" Chamois

reviewText: I just recently purchased both the XL and the original, the XL being about $3 more. The size is virtually the same, it's maybe an inch wider and an inch longer, that's it. It is a waffle weave like texture, which I'm assuming is supposed to replicate the waffle weave texture of automotive microfiber drying towels. However, my biggest complaint is that the XL version is THINNER! They made it only slightly larger in length and width, but since it is noticeably thinner, it weighs less and has less material overall. On top of that, they used gimmick marketing by putting it in a larger plastic container that is completely unnecessary, it fits in the normal plastic container just fine.The original is better and cheaper. I assumed it would just be a larger version of the original, but it is not and it is not worth they extra money. I'm disappointed in the company considering the original Absorber is my absolute favorite drying cloth and have been using it for years.
summary: Not as good as the original

reviewText: I own 3 different absorbers, and have used 5 in my lifetime, but this one is different. reviewText: First of all, I must state that the scan tool worked well for my cars. Once connected it will:- display diagnostic codes- erase ALL codes- retrieve I/M readiness status- display the VIN number on 2002 or newer vehicles- rescanThe MS300 supports the OBD II or OBD2 (On-Board-Diagnostics II) system and it understands all OBD2 protocols that a car may use: PWM, VPW, KWP2000, ISO9041, EKWP2000 or CAN. Once the proper protocol is detected, the MS300 is ready to display whatever Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) the car computer's memory may be holding.It should be noted that:# it only retrieves codes already stored in the computer# it does NOT provide any 'real-time' monitoring# it is completely stand-alone and no Web-updates are possible# it does not have printing capabilities# it is powered through the car's own DLC (Data Link Connector)The manual while not completely accurate does offer sufficient information to successfully connect and operate the device. It also includes a printed list of over 1000 generic Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) definitions. 8000 more manufacturer specific DTCs can be found on the CD with more information at the company's own Web site.In my case, I was able to diagnose within minutes the source for the 'Service Engine Soon' warning on my dashboard:P0442 - EVAP Emission Control System Leak (Small)I erased the codes and, if the warning reappears, I will know EXACTLY what to tell the technicians.Given that I purchased this during one of Amazon's lightning deals, the price was right and I feel that I am getting a lot of value out of this little tool. The manual's small shortcomings do not compel me to subtract a star so, it's a 5-star device for me. I am happy I ordered it._________________________________________Note: Sep. 1, 2009It does NOT work on a Honda Insight 2010. No matter how many times I try, all I get is a 'LINK ERROR'.
summary: Excellent tool, manual needs some editing (see note below)

reviewText: I have an Silverado pickup with 200,000 miles on it. Never any trouble until one $30 sensor went bad. That was a $400 dealership repair. I bought this code reader, and now I fix my truck myself. The truck's computer signals the driver if there is a problem saying "service engine soon". You plug code this into the connector under the dash. The connector goes to the truck's computer. The code reader gives you one or more numbers called DTC or Data Trouble Code numbers. The code reader comes with an instruction booklet, and you look up the numbers in the booklet. It tells you what is wrong. Typically, you clean or replace whatever sensor or small part that sent the trouble code, and that corrects the problem. In addition to the booklet, you can go to Google and enter the DTC code, and read user forums all day long about what problems might be causing the code. This code reader has saved me thousands of dollars repairing my car myself. At the very least, it gives you information to keep your repairman honest!

This CAN diagnostic scan tool works with most modern automobiles, and comes with a manual and computer software mini-disc to help you identify what the codes mean. You can also search online for more information about the codes for your specific vehicle. This is powered automatically when you connect it to the port in your vehicle (usually located near the steering wheel under the dashboard). Just follow the instructions to have it scan and retrieve the codes. It worked as described when I used it on my vehicle that had its service engine indicator lit up. This will help you know if you need to see a mechanic right away (and if your mechanic is doing the proper repair). Until car manufacturers decide to have car computers show the code info on a built-in screen, it is helpful to have one of these scanners for when your engine warning light comes on.
summary: Simple, inexpensive device to read automobile codes

reviewText: Needs nothing.Works great.Easy to understand.Highly recommend buying one for reading and clearing codes.I used mine on my Toyota pickup under the dash.

The manual provided all information as to operation and meaning of the code. For the price, it did a wonderful job. I did look up additional information regarding my code on the internet, but that's to be expected.

When the check engine light came on for my 1996 Ford F150, I checked the gas caps and reset it by removing the positive battery connection for a few minutes.  When it came on again a few days later, I broke down and bought this code reader.  It instantly linked up and gave me codes for "system too lean" on bank one and two.  A quick Internet search pointed to a likely cause of a vacuum leak and, upon inspection I discovered the hose to the PCV valve was cracked.The quote for the local tune-up shop was $95 just to look at the truck.  The meter and hose cost me under $40 and a small amount of my time.  Now that is a good deal.

Got tired of bringing a Nissan I have to Autozone every few weeks to see if a code has changed. Keep getting a misfire in cylinder 2 but haven't yet ran a compression check. Seems like it was the spark plugs but replaced them all and still misfire. Swapped the coil on plugs between 1 and 2 hoping the error would come back as 1 so I would know that's the issue. Anyway. Works great, shows codes, clears them. Really don't need much more than that.
its seems to be ok but the construction of it seems to be cheap but I don't work on cars for a living (Backyard Mechanic )

cheap scan tool, I got this one so I could loan it out instead of my much more expensive one. not bad for such a low price.

Great inexpensive product that will pay for itself after fixing two items. I was estimated $800-$1100 to repair the problems with my car. After getting this device I found the codes and spent around $350 (including repair manual,parts, and this product) on the repairs doing it myself. Mechanic "diagnostics" told me that I needed 2 or 3 things that were actually part of replacing the part they were saying was broken (I was told I needed a new upper and lower gas manifold gasket and fuel injector when they are typically changed or evaluated for change at the same time as they are in the same place in the engine.) No fault with the unit itself, just that there is better value to be had elsewhere.

reviewText: i can't believe how simplistic this device is compared to the high end scanners and it just works. i mean what else could you ask for. its so simple. plug in, turn key, it auto detects the car's programming and if there is an active code will automatically scan. is very fast and effective. i used on 2 cars, my friends Pontiac grand am and my Pontiac g6. my g6 had no codes on it just wanted to see the difference. if there are no codes active it will not auto scan. however you can still manually make it scan, and it also can see certain things from your emissions systems. not everything but some things, but it really just tells you if they are working or not. if the programming is compatible, it can also pull the VIN off the car and as i found out, i can't on every car. my g6 it could see the VIN, while my friends grand am, it could not. still for the small affordable price of 20$ has already saved me 110$ in diagnostics fees. im sure will save me much more in the future. The other nice thing being, even if this thing broke after 1 use..... it cost 20$ and electrical diagnostic fees at a shop where i live are 110$..... even ONE use would pay for this product. and yes it doesn't give you a description of the code but who cares.... most the software in high end scanners has to be constantly updated to be accurate. it reads code, you type code in Google and presto..... you saved yourself a ton of cash. i like cash. if you like cash you can order too!

This little device is a gem in the rough.  It is limited in its' spec, but it can speak to any 1996+ (or fully ODBII compliant systems) vehicles, read pending and set codes, reset them, show pending faults, read the VIN on 2002+ cars, and even comes with some PC software which helps you decode the results.  Its powered by the ODB port in your car, and is small enough to keep in your vehicle.  It's a great piece of mind for about the price of a pizza.
summary: Just what you need for a price that is affordable.

reviewText: Works on my 2001 Honda Civic.Does not work with 2010 Honda CRV.  Link error.  It's so incompatible that when the scanner start to scan, that the Slip Warning light would come on.  (freaked me out, but after I turn the ignition key off and back on, the light would go away).I might keep it around just for the civic and as a loaner.I know this thing is cheap, but if I was to do it all over, I would save the money and buy a better unit.I wish there would be a spreadsheet where people can enter type of cars would work or wouldn't work on this unit.====update 08/13/13Well, I finally called the tech support and see if anything could be done to the "Link Error" issue that I'm having with my CRV (tricks or updates).Apparently ,  this model MS300 has been discontinued since 2007.  The support person can't even find the support document on his side. Since the support person was a nice guy, I didn't want to give him too much hard time, so I asked his opinion on a better model from Autel.

I've used this several times to read codes, perform repairs and then clear the codes on a 2000 Subaru and a 2004 Saturn.  From what I've read though it will not read airbag codes or ABS codes.  For the price it seems hard to find any better.

The unit is great for what it is, and for how much it costs. I am yet to face the "link error" thing mentioned by others; so far, every vehicle I've checked connected well and gave out information. It is important to remember that the unit only retrieves codes and erases everything (permanent and pending codes, the state of the monitors and some adjustments made by the PCM over the time, like the long term fuel trim.)There are no code descriptions. There is no access to data streams. There is no access to freeze frame data. There is no built-in database of vehicles. There is no reading of proprietary non-OBD-II codes from systems like ABS, SRS or power steering. There is no need for updating the firmware. This is a very barebone OBD-II code reader, but in that capacity it works well. There is no internal battery that may leak. There is a bright LED inside that lights up the screen. Symbols on the screen are big and bold and the contrast is just right, and it is not hard to read at all. The body is all wrapped up in plastic and it looks reasonably water resistant. The cable is neither too long, nor too short; it also doesn't feel flimsy, but only the time will tell about that.Quality control at Autel may be inappropriate, because many people report reading errors that seem to be related to the cable, or the connector, or both, or to the internal soldering.The booklet that comes with the unit is a throwaway. The instructions seem to be outdated, but the unit only has two buttons and it is extremely easy to figure out what they do.

I know I can probably run down to the local Autozone and have them pull a code for free, but most of the time they want you to purchase their part and won't reset the code. Before I buy an emmission controls part (sensor), I want to make damn sure it's the problem. With this tool, I can reset my check engine light and wait and see if it comes back on with the same code. I'm aware you can reset your check engine light by disconnecting you battery for 10 minute, but again, what a pain. Just means I'd have to reset all the controls on my vehicle because of the loss of power. You ask yourself, how may times will I use this? Who knows? I own a 2002 and my daughter has a 1996. The wife's car is still under warranty. I've used this 3 times in the first 6 months since I have purchased it, so I consider the amount of time it has saved me, it has paid for itself.......
