reviewText: This scan tool couldn't be easier to use. Plug it in (in my 2012 Jeep Wrangler that's just under and to the left of the steering wheel), turn the ignition forward (but don't start the vehicle) and press enter on the scan tool. It will scan your vehicle in seconds and let you know how many error codes there are and what they are. It also gives you the ability to have the tool delete the codes from your vehicle's on board computer. Simple press of a button.It comes with a little book that tells you what all of the generic engine codes mean.I highly recommend the product.

I am reviewing the Autel MaxiScan MS509. I had done a considerable amount of research on ODB-II scan tools.  The big consideration was do I look simply for a code reader and reset device OR do I look for a real-time diagnostic tool.  I had no less than six different models from various manufacturers on my "short" list.  Previously in the automotive repair industry I was familiar with the protocols with OBD scan tool devices.  I spent time reading Amazon reviews, OBD forum sites, youtube etc.  [I went through a lot of Visine from staring at the PC monitor for extended periods!]. I went with this model largely on credible reviews, features and price. Amazon's price is respectable but if you dig into the issue you will be able to find one thru an importer.  I got mine direct from where they are made overseas [$60].I just received it and these are my initial impressions: Good heft and build quality, feels like a real "professional" grade tool, came with all the accessories you should need except 9V battery.  I hooked it up to my wife's '99 Jeep GC which is supported by SAE J1850 protocol and was able to quickly navigate the tool set up and DTC scan/test options.  The live data stream mapping is a great feature.  I will be trying it out on my '09 Dodge Ram which is CAN supported and should get even more information from that protocol.  This spring/summer I plan on scanning as many of my friends and neighbors cars that I can to get proficient with it.  I will make occasional updates as I work with this tool.  I know some folks have had issue with specific scan tools, the only bad thing about reading too many reviews is that after awhile one goes into "information overload" and you have a hard time making a decision.  So far I think this is a solid choice, I'm not saying there are not better choices so don't get all wound up if you disagree with me.  Tech. has come a long way from 10 years ago which was the last time I used a shop-owned scanner that my employeer paid $4500. for!  It was a Snap-Off brand and at the time thats what they were all going for, all the updates were with plug in modules [$100 plus each!] that you had to buy from the traveling tool rep.  Now updates are via the internet and usually free or low cost.  That eliminates the middle-man and his mark up but it reduces good customer service since you are dealing with a corporation five states away that does not give a rat's A@@ about you [usually].  I can't speak to Autel's customer service yet, but I did send them an email yesterday requesting information on the latest firmware updates available....we will see what the outcome is.  If anyone wants any other [specific] information I will do my best to answer.

I bought the Autel MS509 because I wanted a scanner I could use at home to run diagnostics on my three, soon to be four, family cars.I researched several brands, liked the reviews and price of the Autel line, and narrowed my search to the MS309 and MS509.  For the majority of my needs, I could have used the MS309, which cost about half of the price of the MS509.  I went for the MS509 because it includes 3 additional scans the MS309 does not.  These are Mode 5, 6, and 8, which are Oxygen Sensor  tests, Non-Continuously Monitors Systems, and Special Control Modules tests.I was interested only because some of those apply to vehicles I have owned.So, what's in the box?* The MS509 scanner* Serial to DLC cable* Serial to USB cable* Nylon carrying case* Maxi-Link software on CD* User ManualI had no issues using the MS509.  I followed the basic instructions,  Locate the car's DLC connector, connect the MS509, then turn on the ignition.  You usually do not need to start the engine, just set your ignition to the `On' position.The device powers on as soon as you connect it to the DLC.  The DLC is the Data Link Connector, typically under your dash.  The device enters Set Up mode, which is very simple to navigator.The device keyboard is pretty intuitive, and simple.  It has Power, Enter, Esc(ape), up/down/left/right,  and Help (?)The scanner is lightweight but feels durable.  It has a black bumper all around its edges to help prevent damage.  The display is large and bright and you can adjust the contrast.  The back holds a 9 volt battery, not included, for power when you are not connected to a car or PC.I tested by scanning three cars, two which I knew had no errors and one which had a Check Engine light on.  The scanner worked on all three without issue, and found the code on the car with the error light and diagnosed it and also reset the Check Engine light when I wanted.The cars I tested were a 2001 Volvo S60, 2002 Dodge Durango, and 1998 Plymouth Grand Voyager.I think the scanner is very easy to use, and I didn't really need the manual for most functions.I also installed the Maxi-Link software.  I installed it on a Windows 7 32 bit PC, but did have a small issue.  Initially the install failed, reporting it could not find and install the driver.  I did not download any drivers.  I just ran the installation software again and it worked fine.  This is not uncommon in some hardware devices you connect to a PC via USB.  Sometimes if you launch an installation before you connect the device to the laptop, you get a false `can't install driver' message.  I've had it happen on TV remotes, other small wired devices such as a label printer, and now the scanner.  But in the end, the software did load.  The software is minimal, but does have a list of codes and the ability to update software, etc.I would absolutely recommend this product.  It is reasonably priced, easy to use, and has  a lot of features.
summary: Full Featued, Simple To Use, And Reasonably Priced!!!!

The 2 chips end to end need power to work and talk.before condemning it, try 2 cars, 96+  (it fill work )1996 and newer....it only reads EPA codes, P0xxx and never, factory codes P1,(unless lucky)mine reads P17xx factory tranny codes. (nicely but not on all cars)P0xx DTC codes and PIDS, are federal codes,  (basic to all cars here) 96+it's a federal rules scanner ONLY, you will never see a tool that gets all carsand all factory codes, no P1xxx  or p2xxxx. for cheap. $5000 yes.with a box full of plugin for $300 each.  but not for $50ever,, go to  [i cant post other linkings so search OBD2 tools....]it does not do ABS either. sorry.  (it does have lots of bang for the buck)you do not need windows 7 for it to work, in fact,the tool works all by itself.it has a nice graphic mode.  unlike! any other tool! for this price.!for that, i give it 100 points. reviewText: Bought this for my 325Ci BMW. Read codes and resets them while also doing many other features. Real time monitoring and can tell u exactly whats wrong with your car. Would def reccomned this product

I have used these on my last two bikes they really work as advertised and sace a lot of cramping in you throttle hand.  One of inexpensive simple ideas that work just as good or better than anything more expensive or fancier.

I was pleasantly surprised by how well this cruise assist works. No more hand cramps. Install is simple and the cramp buster works very well. I'm very satisfied with the performance, easy of use, and low cost. Great purchase.
summary: Very nice product to reduce hand cramps for long or short rides.

reviewText: Helps a bit on the long stretches of road.  Gives your hand a break from gripping the throttle but you still have to have your hand or wrist on the grip or the bike decelerates.  I ended up getting a throttle lock so I could free up my hand when I need to.
summary: Decent product, it does what it is meant to

reviewText: Easy to adjust, this little tool , takes the arm and hand cramps out of highway driving. For mainly city driving, however, you need to turn it down a bit to avoid sudden acceleration upon bumping it. I love it and use it constantly. Works well with or without gloves and with heavy or light gloves.

This is a great item to uses on long trips. It does help with numbness in your hand. Need to watch how you set it on your throttle as your speed can creep up on you if you don't check it once in a while.

I ride to work and to school on a vstar 650.  I wanted something to reduce the cramping when wearing winter gloves.  This does the job.  I ordered the standard based on the other review from a vstar rider and it fit perfect.  Be sure to place where it does not overlap either end of the grip to prevent throttle sticking.  I have found that it allows for ease of keeping throttle just barely up when at the first couple of stoplights on cold mornings.  I know I should let it warm up but often run behind and the small increase in throttle to keep engine from dying would cramp my hands along with the cold weather gloves
summary: Works great for this newb rider

reviewText: this works okay...  i commute about 30 min every day and this is okay for that period of time however, any longer it starts to slip and I  readjust on the fly.  it works but could possibly use some better r&d

I added Grip Puppies to my V-Strom for the same reason many others do, which was because the stock handle bars feel too small. If you too have larger grips due to heating elements or Grip Puppies get this one! It went on in seconds, easy to adjust, yet tight enough where it doesn't budge at all. I've only got about 100 miles of experience with them yet during my rush hour commutes but am already starting to get used to it.Why did I get the cramp buster in the first place?1. Safety. With the CrampBuster installed I can naturally keep 2-3 fingers hovering over my front brake lever. Since I commute year-around in rush hour traffic on my bike I take every advantage I can get!2. Hand cramps on longer rides. On rides longer than 3-4 hours my hand would start killing me. Since the CrampBuster takes the "twisting of the handle bar" out of the equation I should be able to ride much longer without worrying about my hand cramping up.

reviewText: My hand falls asleep really fast while riding.  I use a breakaway throttle lock for open roads.  But around town I don't want to use it.  The crampbuster was exactly what I needed.  Since the throttle is not locked on, there isn't any danger of the throttle sticking when you move to grab the brakes.  A lot of folks (on other sites) keep referring to using the palm of their hands to hold the throttle in place.  Technically, that's not correct, at least for me.  It lines up with the heel of your hand under the thumb.  I tried using it with my palm, and it felt very awkward.  With the heel, you can increase/decrease your throttle using this device, or just hold it steady.  It only takes a few miles to start feeling comfortable with it.I bought the standard size, and it fit over the throttle on my Honda with a 1 inch handle bar (1300 VTX).  To adjust it, I just twisted the throttle to where my memory said was where it would work best.  I got it right the first shot.  Try it, if it's too high or low, pull over and move it, then try again.  It won't take much to nail it.  No tools are needed.  Once it's slipped over the throttle grip, you rotate it forward to adjust it.I have read reviews on other sites that said this device got tangled up in gloves and caused problems.  Looking it, and my gloves, all I can figure is the problem must be with the style of glove.  My gloves clasp in the back, and have no openings on the palm side.  I had no problem.  Before I set out, I even played with it trying to duplicate what I'd read, but could not.  I would think if your gloves clasp on the palm side of your hand, or if you have some kind of opening in the glove around the area where the crampbuster touches your hand, perhaps that could be a problem.All in all, it has to be the best 9 bucks I ever spent on the bike.  I bought the plastic one just to try.  Will probably get the chrome one later.
I use them for drying my car after I wash it. They're absorbent and very thick, I'm very happy with them. I have many general microfiber towels, but nothing else like this. Great towels!
Really does absorb well,good construction.It is really not that big but works well.I even brought one to the gym to use after a show and was impressed

Never really had a microfiber cloth before to wash my vehicles, I always used just regular towels.  Not any more, these things are amazing and wring out almost completely dry, just be careful you don't pick up any rocks in the rag.

Very nice towel I purchased based on reviews that claim it will not mar the surface of your cars paint. This has held up to be true.  The thickness of the towel is good and I use it for everything from removing wax, applying spray wax, and as a finishing towel to dry the car.  I wash them in warm water with a natural detergent and add distilled white vinegar during the rinse cycle to remove and remaining soaps.  Machine dry but do not use a dryer sheet.

I bought the Cobra Gold Plush Jr. Microfiber towels before I bought these and I must say that I never thought microfiber towels could get this soft. These towels worked great for removing wax and hand buffing. I've demoted my Gold Plush Jr. towels to dirtier jobs now that I have these towels but these are more expensive then the gold plush. Worth every penny!!!

reviewText: These are some really nice microfiber towels.  Thick and soft.  I use them after applying Turtle Wax Ice.  Reviews of other towels always said something about being thin.  These are not!

These are good towels for auto detailing. I have used these for drying and also for buffing purposes. The soaking capacity of the towel is excellent and does not leave streaks on the car. While buffing the towel catches nicely initially and is very effective in buffing off the wax / sealant. The other good thing about the towels is that they are very easy to clean just soak them in warm water with a very gentle detergent and they get clean.
These are soft, thick enough without being too big to fit in tight areas.  They show no signs of wear, and clean up easily.

I need new applicators about every year so these will do the job.What I like is that these applicators put your chemicals on smooth and take dirt off as well.Cheap enough to throw away after dirty and I don't have to buy dozens at a time..

reviewText: Love mothers the only products I will use on my jeep. used for applying wax no scratches from product. like I said mothers are great products.
It is what it says it is, microfiber applicator.  Works great for waxing and detailing the car.  I Would recommend.

These microfiber pads are the best I have found to apply wax to my cars.  They are very soft, will not scratch, and are easily washed for future use.  At the price ($3.77 as of this writing) they can't be beat.

I used this product about an hour ago. The foam is much to soft and will not reach the areas it should. It does not polish well at all. Grab your rags, polish, tin foil, and a can of elbow grease, do it by hand and you will be a lot happier.

I bought this cone on the recommendation of a friend however I find that after just a few uses the cone losses its conical shape and is rendered useless eventually. Even after cleaning it the foam simply crushes down into a narrow strip that does little to clean your hard to reach areas. Because of its conical shape I like it better than the BALL but it doesn't last very long and it is rather expensive.
This product really takes care of chrome rims. It came out so shiney I could actually use it as a mirror!!! I recommend this product to anyone interested in keeping their chrome rims shiney and new.

I use this and some semi-chrome polish to clean my wheels and it gets in the tight places where the larger ball won't go.Washable, see internet instructions. Problem here: Too high priced to just throw away. I get about 3 washes to one of these and that makes it affordable. Is not use and toss for me.

Tried wheel polishers before (Mother Powerball, cotton buffer wheels, Mequire's Wheel Restoration kit) and was left all but appalled with this product. Went to apply pressure to buff some oxidation out only to find out that a plastic rod is what holds the cone together. I was only able to complete one wheel before the product was in three piece on the asphalt. I do not recommend this product.

This cone is VERY fragile, BUT, it goes where my poor old fangers can't ! You can't use this one like the mini power ball, you just have to take your time, but it does what it's supposed to do, w/o killing yer fangers.
I have a four cars in my family and I like them to look nice. This product allows you to spray it on the paint and the glass and gives the vehicle a very nice clean look.
I love this stuff, I put it on my Brand new 2013 KIA Rio, Wow The shine and water run off is amazing. This wax goes on smooth and lasts for a long time.

this is the best wax I never used....I have a silver explorer and after waxing it looked showroom new....goes on easy and wipes off easyer....and the shine is outstanding....I think any body looking to buy wax needs to try it ...

I bought this cause it was cheap and had good reviews.  But its ok at best.  I am OCD about washing my cars.  The best spray wax is NXT however couldn't find so gave this a shot.NXT is actually milky in color and texture leaves a slippery surface behind.  This stuff is clear and just scented water, doesn't not leave a slippery surface behind, no real shine.If you want a good wax or spray wax look at Meguiar's NXT Generation
summary: I fail to see all the rave

reviewText: I've been waxing my cars for forty plus years trying many different waxes over that time. I know there are many top end products out there but I'm not interested in spending a fortune for a car wax. My main goal is to clean the surface and protect it leaving a decent shine with minimal effort that will last for a few months... I'm not overly fussy about the results. I used this for the first time about two months ago and was very impressed with it. It applied with ease and little effort to buff out using a microfiber pad to apply and a microfiber cloth to remove. So far it's still beading and shining nicely but I do wipe my car after drying it with Meguiars Ultimate Detailer which may contribute to that. Another big plus for me is that a wax doesn't leave white residue on plastic surfaces and I had no problems with that using this wax. I can't say how it will perform on an older finish as so far I've only used it on a 2014 Outback.

I have been waxing my cars for many years. This is one of the easiest wax products I have ever used. The product went on very easy with a pad by hand, it  dried quickly and wiped right off.  The shine is incredible.  There is no need to spend big money on fancy sealants or waxs Mothers products are all you need.  I maintain my shine by using the spray wax after every wash. It keeps the car shiney and smooth. I highly recommend Mother's California Gold  Synthetic wax it really stands up to northern Indiana winters.
summary: Great price great wax very easy on and off

reviewText: I actually called Mothers one day to ask them which product to use for my truck since they have so many to choose from and this is what they recommended and I am on my third bottle and have not been at all disappointed.  Thanks to the free two day shipping, I dont stock up and keep numerous bottles in my garage where the liquid wax could freeze in the winter.  Not sure if that affects it, but why worry.
This wax easily lasts six weeks and it adds a high level of shine to your paint that is sure to last.

Mothers California Gold Synthetic Wax applies very easily, and polishes clean just as easily. Even on sun heated surfaces, this wax polishes with ease. The shine it produces is among the best I've seen, easily matching Meguiar's Gold Class for outright high shine, but lasts longer and holds up to the extreme elements Florida throws at it for two to three times as long. Mothers also has a pleasant scent to it during application. This product doesn't come with an applicator though, so I'd recommend picking up a decent microfiber applicator if you don't already have one.

I've switched to this wax from the Mother's Instant Detailer, and I use it every time I wash the car. It doesn't provide as lasting a shine as traditional waxes that are rubbed on and left to dry, but it only takes about 10 minutes to do the whole car, and the results are impressive.I use one microfiber cloth to spread the product after lightly spraying a section, followed immediately by a second dry microfiber cloth to buff the wax. I use very little product, just a light spray does the trick, so this 24-oz bottle goes a long way. Like all waxes, it should only be applied to a clean car, and it won't remove surface dirt or finish imperfections - that's what Mother's Clay Bar is for!Also, this wax does not leave any white residue on black plastic trim, so any overspray on trim is no problem, just wipe it off.Highly recommended!

Dont expect it to last forever! Its a great touch-up product for streaks, Little hand marks etc. However it works wonders on my Black Stove Top in the kitchen, The stove did not look this good new and i could never get rid of the streaks! Use with a good quality microfiber cloth and you ca not go wrong. I even use it on windows around the house, on electronics, Appliances, Window Tracks (Makes them nice and Slippery) You can find many uses for it!
i had used jet seal 109 before and found it very hard to apply as well as expensive.  mother's california gold liquid wax was a breeze to apply and easy to wipe off.  thanks for such a good product!!

I tried to get this thing to work but could not. The LED light would never come on. I followed the directions exactly as stated for my specific vehicle from the xpresskit web site but no go. It just did not work so I sent it back to Amazon.

Installed with my Avital remote starter in my 2008 civic. Worked right away after being programmed. Programming was very simple as was wiring. The unit is much smaller than I imagined which is great as hiding these things away under the dash can be tricky.

I don't know what I was thinking. I bought this and it is not used for what I thought it was. I think this has something to do with a remote start. Didn't do what I wanted it to but it's not their fault.
generally more reliable than the new FL Cans but has its problems too. sometime programming fails when updating or changing the firmware. otherwise once installed seems bulletproof

Had to return it and wait for a FLCAN to arrive in the mail.  My recommendation is to simply plan ahead and buy the FLCAN.  A bit more money but a lot less hassle.

reviewText: As someone who has used many car cleaning products and has hunted for distributors of my favorite one for my husband, this is a real find. We have several vehicles that we take to car shows and so we are constantly using a California duster and waterless cleaning products to instant shine our vehicles. My husband will spotclean his truck if there is any mark on it. I have a big old Dodge diesel that is a work truck and after washing the mud off I cleaned half of it using this product and was amazed at how good it looked. I had to finish the other side and my husband was also amazed. He actually used it on his precious truck and was satisfied with the results. He is very particular about his vehicle so the fact that he used the product and was satisfied with the result speaks volumes. Follow the directions and use it sparingly for the best results.

We have been having severe weather problems here on the East Coast and today was the first time I have had a chance to use the Eco Touch Waterless Car Wash.It worked well on my SUV.  Because we have had such bad weather and I live in a Coastal Community, our cars get very dirty, sandy and salty.  I followed the instructions and sprayed the solution on a Microfiber towel and cleaned the back tailgate.  I could see the dirt come off on the yellow towel.  It took a little bit of effort to completely remove the product with a fresh towel.  I am not sure if I want to do an entire vehicle with a waterless cleaner.  I think it might take very long time, but for a quick clean up and wipe down, the product is pretty good.  I will use it between car washes.

I used Eco Touch on my 92 Camry that had been outside under a tree and was pretty dirty. Following the directions, the dirt came off and left a nice shine. It looked pretty good. It took a lot of elbow grease I think because the car was so dirty to begin with. When I do it again, I would go ahead and wash with water to knock off all the heavy dirt then wash with Eco Touch.  I will use this more in the future.

The Concept: Cleaning a vehicle by simply spraying on the Eco Touch WCW24 Waterless Car Wash, wipe off with a microfiber towel, then polishing with a clean microfiber towel, without using ANY water sounds too good to be true.  Wow, nothing wrong with saving water in eco-concerned and drought stricken CA, plus no chemicals flowing down the sewers into the ocean.  But wait, there's more: this product is also biodegradable and non-toxic.The Reality:  Anyone with any common sense knows that washing or cleaning a vehicle without any water is going to scratch the finish.  I followed the instructions exactly and was able to clean off recent bird droppings, tree saps, and other small spots on the hood with no noticeable scratches on my anthracite gray metallic vehicle (Note: 3 days before using WCW24, my vehicle was washed normally and polymer coated (NXT Wash and Wax Kit) so there was minimal dust/dirt buildup).  HOWEVER, I wouldn't take a chance with cleaning off entire body panels because when dirt is wiped across larger areas; more chances for scratching the finish; especially noticeable for darker colored vehicles.  I could understand people using this spray when there's no access to water and hose or as a small spot/stain remover prior to the next wash.  Even the instructions advise to rinse off excess sand and mud with water to prevent scratches prior to spraying/wiping/cleaning.  Use it to clean an entire vehicle covered with dirt/dust at your own risk.
summary: Good for cleaning small spots and stains but not entire vehicle.

reviewText: This is an idea whose time has not arrived. Perhaps if one has a teeny tiny vehicle then this may work out. First of all, you have to purchase micro-fiber towels per the instructions. Be sure to get lots of them. You are instructed to do one panel at a time - spray, wipe and buff. Supposedly you will save 80 - 120 gallons of water and eliminate toxic runoff (apparently referring to the soapy water). I HAVE NEVER USED ANYWHERE NEAR THAT MUCH WATER TO WASH MY CAR. With eco touch I am left with a whole slew of micro-fiber towels that would end up in a landfill because I don't know how to recycle dirty towels.I believe that eco touch has a problem with "truth in advertising". I can see using this for minor cleaning such a a deposit left by a bird or an insect meeting its demise on my vehicle. But, to wash the entire car is best done with a bucket, hose, sponge and chamois cloth. Or, take it to a car wash.

reviewerName: Hummingbirder "Don't ask for a man's soul whe...
reviewText: Water and polishing agents are emulsified with detergent in this pump spray car cleaner.  Simply spray it on aZwipeor other microfiber cloth, wipe on a small section of exterior, and buff with a dry microfiber cloth.  Imagine your car is a large coffee table and you get the idea.The polish component is a blessing and a curse.  It shines up great, but if there is more than a thin film of dirt, it inhibits cleaning because the polish ingredients will not dissolve dirt.This is a great spit shine product, and there is nothing wrong with that.  Use it before your car is grimy and use it often.  Not only do you not have to use up water, you do not have to drag out buckets and hoses.  This is very convenient!TIPS:  If your car is filthy, you need to wash it with conventional methods.  If it is starting to get grimy, you can clean it very well with microfiber cloths and plain water or water and white vinegar.  You will not get the high shine, but this works better for heavier dirt.  Just put water in a plastic spray bottle, fire at will, wait a few seconds for it to dissolve the grime and wipe off.Do not use any product that contains polish and/or wax to clean mirrors or windows because they distort visibility.  Use a mister with water/vinegar (you can add a drop of dish detergent) and your microfiber orSqueegee.

Like most people, I was skeptical about the waterless car wash when I received this bottle. But it proved to be an effective product.It took me about 30 minutes to wash my Honda Odyssey Van. Hasn't washed the car for a month. And I didn't do pre-wash rinse. I used about 1/4 of the bottle. I think 4 washes out of a bottle should be no problem. The Eco Touch did remove surface dirt, but it has hard time to remove some that had formed a film...even if I did some scrubbing with Eco Touch. It leaves a slight protective coating and a decent shine that seems shinier than a basic wax.It makes the car wash task easier without dealing with bucket and hose. All I need is just a bottle and couple of microfiber towels. Excellent ideal and great product that I will definitely recommend to my friends.
summary: Great product to make car wash task easier

reviewText: If someone told me last year that I could wash my SUV with a 24 oz bottle of stuff and not have to do anything else I would have probably broken a rib laughing.  To make it even funnier I would have had great difficulty in thinking that any would be left over.  Alas, I waited for a rainy, bleak day with few good reasons to do anything outside.  Out came a bottle of Eco Touch and a few micro rags (I sure wish they had been included in the package).  I was having a hard time thinking that Eco would work.  A spray and a wipe and in about an hour I had a sparkling Tahoe that looked as if it had just come out of the professional car wash joint.  I had enough left over to do it all again.  The package said I could expect at least 3 or 4 washes; however, a Tahoe has a few more square inches than a normal car.  (Is there such a thing now as a "normal car?")  The best part is not having to worry about all the water that I normally waste.  Living on a well and trying to wash vehicles is not a good pairing.  Then I did not have to rewind the hose and on and on.  You know the routine.  That's over.  It is now pull our the bottle and the rags and in a reasonable time you have a clean vehicle.  Wow!
summary: Too Good to be True but it Is

reviewText: I used this product on my car and by and large it is good for getting rid of droppings or other stains and for a quick area clean for bugs on the grill area or dust/pollen elsewhere.  But I definitely prefer Meguir's (or Mother's) products to the Eco Touch line.  The idea of a waterless car wash is somewhat misleading.  Basically, its a spray on cleaning solution.  But it's still ideal to use water whenever you clean your car.  Without the water as lubrication and the hose as a method to remove dirt, you wind up tracking/grinding dirt across your paint- which obviously is not good.  As a cleaning agent, it's adequate, but as a true wash that eliminates the need for water, it's not.  Hence 3 stars.
summary: Decent product but not a must have

reviewText: I have to admit to a fair amount of skepticism when I thought about this product. It claims a water-free car wash and that you can get 4-6 washes from each bottle. Well, I live in the city, and that city is Minneapolis so the water hose is already put away (October) due to the cold. I did a couple of spot cleanings with the product, and they worked well, so I went ahead and did a full car cleaning. Yep, this stuff seems to work pretty well. It still takes some elbow grease (as my parents would put it) to clean off really stuck on stuff (pitch from trees and berry-filled bird droppings) but the Eco Touch stuff does work.It's not cheap though, and if I had a garden hose out, I'm not sure that I wouldn't use some cheap Turtle Wax car wash. But for the winter season in Minnesota this looks to be a good product. And if you're committed to using less water, then this is a car wash that works well without water.

I normally wash my car with a bucket and lots of water, but I know there are many people who either can't or don't want to do that.  Eco Touch Waterless Car Wash is a relatively new kind of product that lets you clean your car without separate water. If car washing with water is prohibited due to water restrictions, or you don't have a hose available, or you just want to keep your car clean in between regular washes, this is an attractive product.I tried it on my wife's car which was, I admit, pretty dirty.  You squirt the solution onto a microfiber cloth (which I had), wipe down a small section, and then buff dry with a clean cloth.  I found that the Eco Touch wash did remove a lot of surface dirt, though it didn't get some that had formed a film - I probably would have had to scrub it some with detergent and water.  I did try "scrubbing" with the Eco Touch but it didn't touch it.  Buffing the area did bring out a nice shine.Even if you're not going to use the waterless car wash to wash the whole car, you may find this product handy for in-between cleaning, such as the trunklid or other surfaces that tend to collect dirt faster.  I like it and will keep using it.
summary: Good for a touchup or if you can't use a hose

reviewText: I really looked forward to using Eco Touch Waterless Car Wash.  I have used Quick Detailers for years.  These are the products by a different name, same purpose, to remove light dust, other light contaminants, etc. from your paint, rather than wash the entire car.  I literally use such products almost every day.I quickly found that Eco Touch was not at the level of the products I regularly use from Meguiar's and other speciality car care companies.  The reason being, even on a light color car, the Eco Touch would want to streak terribly.  It took a lot more effort to get the finish consistent looking.  Even then, the product did not add the gloss and finish I have grown to love from competing products.The price is also a negative. Meguiar's top consumer detailer, Ultimate Quick Detailer, sells for less on Amazon and is a far superior product.  Why not pay less for a much better product?  I really can't even begin to describe how superior every Meguiar detailer is to this product, plus for this price, you can buy the very top product from Meguiar's and still keep the hose/water away from your car to save water, when your car only needs a quick cleaning.Another tip, make sure to use at least two high quality, large, Microfibers when using such products.  If using smaller towels, I'd use three or four.  Dampen the towel and spray a small area of the paint, wipe clean, and dry with a clean, dry microfiber.Overall, while the idea for the product is great, it's not new.  Meguiar's had Trigger Wash in the early 1980s.  Furthermore, Meguiar's and other car care companies products are superior in how they clean and leave the finish of your paint.  I'm going to use the remaining Eco Wash I have, to clean small bugs off the front bumper, which I do every time I drive the car (unless there are too many).  In a small controlled area like that, it's a bit less frustrating product.
summary: Ok for Front End Touch Up, Otherwise, Better Products Available

reviewText: This product seems to perform no differently than the host of "quick spray detailers" out on the market.  Spray on, wipe off, buff off the residue haze . . . surface is clean and lightly protected.  I like such handy products.For gritty type dirt, or dirt requiring heavy scrubbing pressure, you'll likely get into trouble scratching your painted surface. The Eco Touch Waterless does leave behind a haze, so that buff off step is manadatory.  It's likely that this product will take more time and labor than a conventional wash.Being a detailer type spray product (in my opinion), it is useful for spot cleaning, loosening up bugs/tar, or a quick wipe down to remove water spotting from an almost clean car.  Obviously, it is of use when water is just not available, such as for apartment dwellers, or water restricted communities. By the way, you can wash your car in the same way with a bottle of Windex, although it lacks the residual protection ingredient.Is the "ecology friendly green" aspect, so much hype?  I was skeptical and stated so in my original version of this review. The ingredients are touted as "plant-derived" . . . You might want to click on the "Comments" button at the bottom of this review to read a good explanatory comment from the product manufacturer.  Maybe this Eco Touch is indeed more earth friendly than the heavily perfumed spray detailer alternatives.  The manufacturer also provides an explanation for the health warning printed on the bottle.  Still, the required micro-fiber towels will have to be laundered WITH WATER, or transported by a fuel consuming truck to help fill up a landfill -- get my point?  (Sorry for soapbox, but the "green" issue is not important to me.  It may be to you, and if so, this product seems to be what you are looking for).Some green hype and not a miracle in a bottle, but a satisfactory spray on detailer that has it's place.  Used as directed, it leaves a perfect clean surface with a slick wax feel.  And if it's important to you, the Eco Touch probably also does its eco part.  Does what it claims and for that, 5 stars.  I'll use it as a quick detailer.
summary: Over-hyped?, but good for what it is

reviewText: I wanted to quickly review this product to tell you about my experience with it.I used teflon/plumbers tape to make sure my connections were sealed tightly so I would not lose air. At first the separator functioned great for about a year. Kept all of the moisture out of my air tools!However, a year later the separator formed a crack in the acrylic housing and began leaking so much air out that it caused my compressor to turn on every 5 minutes! I understand why they used acrylic so the person could tell if it was full of water and needed to be drained.The point is however, acrylic, no matter how thick, is not designed to hold pressure above 50 PSI (Pressure Per Square Inch). And since most air tools require 90 PSI or more, the separator will not stand up to that pressure for very long.I think it would make a better solution to make the separator out of metal, since it can hold up to great pressures more, and the person just needs to remember to drain their separator same time they drain their compressor.In conclusion, I like these things when they work, however I don't recommend this product and I highly recommend the buyer to spend more money on a metal unit. That is all...
oh ya this is a nice one, it looks great on my gun.  I highly recommend this seperator to anyone,

Seems to be fine and seems to be built well no problems so far and it does not restrict air or I would have not 5 stared this product. As far as Im concerned tekton products are good products for the price and also lifetime warranty. I own other tekton tools and have had no problems with them.
summary: Broncomania review on Tekton 4755 Oil/Water Separator

reviewText: Great little air/water separator. Does the job well and was a lot less than what the competitors wanted!  Great buy!

No drips, no leaks, no errors, works as advertised.  I am not a daily pneumatic tool user, but when I do use mine, I like to take care of my tools and other equipment.  These things are perfect for guys like me.  Simply push the button and drain any water that may have accumulated.  Protects your tools from moisture damage, and adding an in-line oiler is the final step to not only protecting your tools, but also conditioning them for future use.If you are painting ANYTHING, invest in this item, you won't be sorry....

Sturdy little unit.  Wish it had an extender so I could mount it directly to the tank, but it's too fat at the end.  Also, watch out for the air flow direction arrow.  It would be nice if the ends were interchangeable since this is directional.
summary: Small, rugged but ends are not interchangble

reviewText: I have two of these at the end of 50 foot air lines, just before the tools. They do a good job of collecting moisture.The couplers (the black piece illustrated) is actually plastic. I initially worried this would break during assembly. My worries were unfounded, the separator attached just fine.The quality is not that of an Ingersoll Rand separator I already own, but it works just as well.

I paid about 6 bucks for this from Amazon and it was worth it. I had a small HVLP sprayer to paint the hood and roof of my 1990 Chevy K2500 truck and didn’t want any water in the spray. We don’t have much moisture here in the high desert summers but the compressor does condensate on the inside. This worked fine, was easy to attach and well worth the few bucks I paid for it… at a much higher price I would likely have shopped around a little more.
summary: It did the job… and was pretty inexpensive.

reviewText: It does work as advertised.  Just a little bit in a tank of washer fluid and it does smooth out the blades, and less grime.

Those who go on long road trips in particular know all too well the difficulty of cleaning your windshield due to bugs and road grime.  Regular water in your reservoir never does the trick but is quite cheap and easy to refill so many use this by default.  Some go as far to buy chugs of windshield wiper fluid at discount stores and this works better but still not that great.  None of these solutions ever worked so what I would do in areas with a lot of bugs was bring along paper towels and windshield cleaner, pull over to the side of the road every so often, and manually clean.  Obviously this wasted a lot of time as I had to find a safe place to pull over, and wasted gas for needless deceleration/acceleration back to speed.Fear not, this product actually does what it needs to do - it clears off your windshield by using a unique formula that attacks bugs and grime so you don't need to apply a lot of wiper fluid to get the window clean.  Yes, I am a believer now.  No longer do I need to bring along my paper towels with cleaner to manually do the windshield.Some hints - use a gallon chug of bottled water to do the mixing.  I would ensure you use bottled water rather than tap because tap water has high mineral contents that can end up clogging your windshield fluid nozzles over time.
summary: I'm now a believer in clean windshields from this product

reviewText: For years I have used peak and rain-x washer fluid, but this concentrated mix beats them all. Does a great job cleaning my windshield, dries without spots, and is not greasy or oily.
If you are a do it your self-er, this product is the way to go. Mixes easy and works even better on your windshield.

Good stuff, it will clean your windows but be careful not too add too much and not enough water or it will foam or leave somewhat of a smear first, but eventually dries out. Overall good quality washer fluid, can't believe it comes from Germany.

This was an easy Plug'n'Play part. You can find a video online about where to plug it into the connector block. TIP: WHen you removed the block cover, Take note of it's orientation so you can put it back more easily. I didn't and had to figure it out by turning it at 90's to see what fit.

Awesome fit, no big ball of left over wire to tie up like the last harness that was under there.  I highly recommend this if you are installing the Tekonsha brake controller. I had the new unit installed and dialed in under 30 minutes.  Controller works awesome too! great buy.
Fast & easy to install and worked perfect when connected to my Tekonsha P3!! So glad I went ahead and purchased this!!
This allowed me to install the brake controller in 20 minutes...no joke. No splicing, no fuse manipulation, no electrical tape. Power is included in the harness so it really is just plug in and go.
Plug and play for 2003 GMC. I'm happy with all the Tekonsha trailer brake products I've used. I already have a Tekonsha controller, so for less than $12 I'm good to go.
summary: Great insight by Tekonsha to provide this product.

reviewText: This wiring adapter made for a much quicker install.  No splicing, etc.  Just plug and go.  Worked great withTekonsha 90195 P3 Electronic Brake Controlin my 2000 F-450 pulling a 14k pound 5th wheel trailer.
summary: Quick way to wire up a Tekonsha brake controller

reviewText: great product.  makes wiring easy.  wire up yourself for your girl in no time and give her a jolt she never had.

There is really no question about the value of this item.  I just finished installing my Tekonsha P3 brake controller in my 2011 Ford Flex using this wiring adapter.  The wiring portion of the installation took about 30 seconds using the adapter.  It too me longer to figure out where to mount the P3 than it did to actually install it.  At first I was a little concerned that the length of the adapter would be too short, but it turned out to be just right.  If it were any longer I would have had to coil the excess up.As I mentioned, I used this adapter for a 2011 Ford Flex - which is not listed on Amazon's description as a matching vehicle.  If your vehicle is not listed here I suggest going to Tekonsha's website, click on "Products" and then on "Plug Adapters."  That has a fairly comprehensive list of vehicles and the correct adapter for each one.
summary: Soooo worth it!  It makes installation is a breeze!

reviewText: Ordered this after I had already ordered and received my brake controller.  Wish I would have ordered at the same time.  This made the installation a breeze.

plugged it in to the harness and clipped in the prodigy brake controller and everything worked perfectly.  I did some research and was worried that i would have to add some fuses and a relay to the car's fuse box (i guess ford wired everything up but didn't add all the fuses and relays for a brake controller), but everything worked perfectly!
summary: Worked Perfectly with 99' Ford Expedition (with factory tow package)

reviewText: Plug and play...  If you have an 09 Ford Expedition with the trailer towing package this is a simple plugin installation.  One end plugs into the Expedition's trailer package harness (under the drivers dash) and the other plugged into my Tekonsha Engineering 90885 Prodigy Brake Controler.  No fuss...no muss.  Just make sure your Expedition comes with the trailer towing package and you're set.
This made wiring the brake controller in my 2000 F150 take less than 5 minutes.  It was so easy, an idiot could do it.
Beware, you may not need one if you order with Prodigy P2 brake controller. Fast shipping, but was not needed as one came with the Prodigy P2 brake controller. Now I have two cables.
summary: Buyer beware! These cables typically come with the Prodigy P2 brake controller

reviewText: Installed a brake controller in my daughters Expedition with this cable.  The entire brake controller installation process from start, cabling,mounting of controller, and testing was done in 30 minutes.

I have not hooked up a brake controller since the 80's when I had to tap into the hydralic lines of the tow vehicle.  Tekonsha has made this ridiculously easy.  Choose your brake controller, find the correct adapter, 5 minutes later it is hooked up and ready to go.  This is one impressive company to make this so easy!!

I installed a set of 8 ACCEL coils into my 2005 Ford F-150 with 5.4L V-8 motor and 72,000 miles.  I did the coils at the same time as renewing the spark plugs, mainly because of the labor savings.  The ACCEL coils fit as good as the OEM ones.  Between the new spark plugs and the coils, the engine does feel smoother at idle, and seems to be more responsive at acceleration.  ACCEL uses high quality materials that should stay within spec longer, and has experience in developing high performance products.  And, more importantly, ACCEL has quality controls to match the electrical characteristics requirements with precision and consistency -- which is the key to a good coil.  Since any gain in horsepower is the same as a gain in mileage, and with the high price of gasoline, then it makes sense to invest in this small upgrade.  It is also good to look at those yellow coil packs on the engine.
The set was cheaper than the motorcraft brand and way cheaper than the stores in my area,so whats not to love about more power and a better price!

I had replaced my spark plugs in my Explorer with the 3V 4.6L V8 after I started to notice a slight misfire (as others have said, really feels like a transmission issue but it's not). It seemed to run great after that until last week, when it had an obvious misfire again and I was afraid it wasn't going to make it home. I decided to replace the coil packs as I couldn't figure out what else it'd be.Man, I wish I had done these at the same time as the spark plug. I didn't realize how much power my engine had been loosing until I popped these in. Also my gas mileage immediately jumped up 2 MPG. I had written off my slowly decreasing MPG to the number of miles I have on my car, the ever increasing amount of ethanol in fuel and the all terrain tires I had put on it. Now my mileage is back to what it was when it was new if not higher and has a very noticeable extra spring to it's step. I would recommend replacing them even if you don't notice an issue, because these are notorious for going out in Fords (and will sooner than later) and you may be surprised it solves problems you didn't know you have.

I replaced the stock coils on my 2008 F150 with these and, so far, these seem to work great.  There are a fairly straightforward changeover - provided you can get access to all of them (which proved to be quite a challenge with my truck).  However, these combined with a cold air intake upgrade feels like it's given my truck a horsepower boost and, while I haven't checked it yet, I seem to be getting slightly better gas mileage.  Not sure if the coils contributed to that or not but, hey - the yellow color looks cool.  ;-D

I purchased these to replace the stock coils on my triton 5.4. Have yet to install them (its pretty cold outside up here), but my past experience with Accel SuperCoils has been very positive. The quality seems to be top-notch and results are immediate. Have always had faster starts, smoother idles, better throttle response, a little more power, and better gas mileage. While I find the "Lethal Voltage" markings to be pretty neat, they quickly remind you of the care and responsibility that needs to be taken when working with these items. Furthermore, i'm ecstatic to support this company (Accel), as it is one of the few remaining automotive performance entities that still remains headquartered in the Cleveland area. Great product

These lugs are the real deal.  Don't spend unnecessary dollars on other lug kits.  These are high quality...much higher than I expected.  With one installation I see NO visible scratches from the hex key!  They stayed flawless.  The finish is ultra durable.  Time will tell to see if they keep their gloss luster.I have aftermarket rims for my snow tires and they required skinnier lug nuts to fit the bore of the rims. These were a perfect match.
Works fine , if the fitment is correct.Quality material and workmanship.Nothing special and nothing fancy,  simply great value

I've had these lug nuts on my car for about a year now, and I have to say that I'm really impressed with the way they're holding up. I Haven't had any issues with the black finish chipping or peeling, and the 4 times I've rotated my tires, the threads always go on nice and smooth. Before these, I had a blue set of Muteki lugs, which are very similar to these Gorilla lugs, but at twice the cost. Do yourself a favor and go with these instead!
summary: Just As Good, If Not Better Than Muteki Lug Nuts, At Half The Cost

reviewText: I had to take my car to a dealership for some work.  When I got it back the back wheels had bad scratches around the lug nut holes.  The dealership tried to argue and say they weren't the first one to have the rims off but in fact they were and I made them refinish my rims.  I was able to get the regular Gorilla black lugs on and off without hurting my rims but apparently mechanics using air tools and not caring as much as me would scratch my rims.That is when I discovered these.  The key for these actually fits inside of my old key for my "Gorilla Automotive 71633NBC "The System" Acorn Black Chrome Wheel Locks".  They are much smaller but even after doing multiple high speed/torque launches and high speed runs in a modified Camaro SS they are still solid.I don't have to worry about a mechanic hurting my rims now unless they're a complete idiot.  I highly recommend these over the standard Gorilla locks or anything else I've run across.
After searching for a an hour or so, I finally stumbled onto these lug nuts.  My Jeep wrangler rims, required an acorn style type lug nut.  Great kit, enough for 4 tires.  No issues.

I bought these for a set of Work Meister S1 wheels and so far like them.  The lugs are impressively small and have a snug fitting key adapter.  I have used a number of lugs before and these are probably the smallest I have seen.  The diameter of the the outside of the lug (with the key on) is no bigger than the diameter of the 60 degree lug seat.  This means it should theoretically fit in even the tightest tolerance wheels.These are spline drive lugs, so a standard lug wrench won't get them off.  This likely provides a small degree of security by itself, though for expensive wheels I would recommend a good set of locks.  I picked up theGorilla Automotive 71631NBC Acorn Black Chrome Wheel Locks (12mm x 1.50" Thread Size), Pack of 4.  The finish will likely hold up well over time.  This is due to the nature of the finish itself and the fact that the key fits very precisely and will not slip across the splines.  I find that one of the main reasons regular hex lugs get scratched is ill-fitting wrenches which slip and slide across the surface of the lug.  You will get none of that with these lugs.The key for the lugs has a section for a 3/4" wrench and one for a 13/16" wrench.  I would suggest using the 13/16" since it is closer to the middle of the key, and is a larger diameter.  This will put less stress on the key itself, reducing wear over time.Overall a very well designed set of lugs for tuner wheels.

I wanted a smaller diameter nut than what I have now but these are really small. I did not install these on my rims I just didn't feel confident that these would keep my wheels on my car. They probably weigh about 1/2 of what I have on my rims now. Too much trouble to send them back, I'll keep them and show them to my mechanic and get his input on them, for now I feel safer with what Ive had on them for a couple years now.

The finish is durable.  However, a few came skuffed.  The socket key is oily and seems to fit just a bit looser than I wanted.  This was not an issue.  Plenty of clearance with my wheels.Can NOT beat the price.I would by again.

I have these on my Speed 3. They look great with my gunmetal rims. They're very strong and fit perfect. They were very easy to install and have a very solid key that doesn't slip or damage the finish of the lugs. I torqued these down to 100 ft/lbs and they're holding strong so far.

I bought these to replace the huge stock silver/chrome lug nuts on my 2013 Focus ST.  These black lug nuts fit great and look great.  Although they are shipped all in one bag, there were no visible scratches, before or after installation.  UPDATE: Please note that I am NOT using these lug nuts with the stock wheels...I have Team Dynamics Pro Race 1.2 wheels and these lug nuts fit perfectly with them.

20 Lugs, 16 needed, leaving 4 spare for my 18" American Racing Chrome Casinos. I was worried they wouldn't fit as I've never purchased lugs online, but these acorn lugs were the same length and width as my originals. Comes with a standard wheel lock key to be used with a 3/4" torque wrench. Would definitely buy again, let's see if they rust and break after 8 years like my original set did.
summary: Direct fit for my 18" American Racing Casinos

reviewText: Bought these for my 1983 Pontiac firebird. they went on nicely. look good and feel pretty high quality. good buy.

These were perfect for my vehicle and fit exactly right. They look nice and no noticeable scratches on the chrome as some other reviewers have stated they are just in a plastic bag, which is correct. I will buy again from this manufacturer

See Update Below original 4 star review.(Original:) Unless you are taking your vehicle to the track, and have a need to spend $60-100 for a set of fancy locking lug nuts, these will suffice! I have used these on several vehicles without a hitch, and they are a great buy for the money. Only reason for rating 4 stars is that there is always a little play in using the lug adapter, which makes torquing the lugs a little bit more a pain.(Update:) The last set of these I received had a "Dud" lugnut in the batch... That is, that the threading was either of a different pitch, or not threaded properly. Fortunately I caught it before attempting to forcefully thread the nut on, possibly ruining the stud as well... When one lug would not rotate by hand onto the stud I tried it on several others without avail. Instead of risking the stripping of a stud, I attempted to thread it on my spare wheel carrier (suspecting that the threading may have just had a bur on it,) where it required I would estimate in excess of 30lbft to rotate any bit past 1/3 turn. I am unsure if the quality control has just gone down hill, or whether this was an anomaly, but this could mean bad news for someone who is less experienced with vehicle maintenance, or uses improper procedures such as installing with an impact wrench.
these were a perfect fit for my new wheels. these are smaller diameter than the originals and fit perfectly on my 05 tacomas new rims
You'd be shocked at how handy this little is.  It really is a must.  Not sure on how accurate it is, but it is great piece of mind.
summary: great price for a handy tool

reviewText: It performs very nicely, and can beat more expensive ones. I recommend it to all automobile enthusiasts who needs to test their batteries and circuit boards.

These unit works fine for me, although I have not used all the functions yet. I bought it as a second/back-up multimeter to read circuit voltage at a second location without the hassle of having to move my primary (higher quality) meter. In other words I would recommend it as a secondary meter, but maybe invest a bit more in your first/primary meter. I can't believe we live in a world where you can design, manufacture, ship and make a profit on this product for 11 bucks.
The hands-free strap & clips set this one apart.

This is a good choice if you're looking for a decent performing multimeter for a low price. No, you won't get the accuracy and durability of a Fluke, but it is much better than the other low-priced multimeters I've tried. Voltage and resistance readings are very accurate when checked using a high-end meter, and the probes are of better than usual quality for this price point. It also has a clear, easy to read display, probe holders, and an elastic band on the back for ease of use.I debated getting this or the next model up (3310) but found, after reading the specs on the Equus site, that the accuracy is the same for both. The 3310 does add some features, such as a continuity tone, but since I didn't need those, I went with the lower-priced 3300.The only significant complaint is the tough to open clamshell packaging. Hate that!It's a good choice for general homeowner usage, and better than the typical cheap multimeters out there. Highly recommend.
summary: Better performance and design than the typical cheap multimeter

reviewText: I have purchased many Multimeters over the years..some great..some not so.  This meter was inexpensive and works flawlessly.. my wife would recommend this also for household toolbox

This is really a good meter to test for hot stuff. I have used it in my line of work to test for STDs and STIs. You just put one in in the mouth and the other in the yoohoo and if the screen shows 666 then you are in trouble!
Another Meguiar's product lover here. Supreme shine protectant does just that...shines. The fragrance isn't bad either. Makes a scent that gives a sense of being inside a new car.

Detailed my 2005 G35 interior with this protectant.Made my 8 year old interior look nice and new.The shiney-ness was not very "greasy" though it did look almost wet.Non greasy to the touch, and has a nice tropical scent, love it.For best results, make sure surfaces are very clean before applying
cleans and shines very well ....you will need to apply 2nd coat to get even shine..it well look fantasic when done...
Produces a higher gloss about like the Armor All high gloss product, don't use on Dash. Meguiars products usually perform as advertised
It not just make the Dash shine a lot it also cleans it, and the result stay for many days.
this stuff worked like a charm. i had a few light scratches on my hood from sand paper. 1 pass with this on a mothers power ball and scratches were gone. highly recommend.

I got this for my new black 2013 charger and I was not very impressed. To be honest all the videos I've seen show this being so good a removing the light scratches but I didn't feel it did that at all. I honestly feel there is probably something better out there. I was very disappointed because I have been buying a few meguiars products lately and this one just missed the mark.

I did not see any difference even after applying for long time. It may work better on older paints (but I doubt it). Does not even remove swirls, I was very attentive and applied for long time - no difference at all. Does nothing.I Do not recommend this one.
summary: Waste of time applying ('08 Silver BMW)

reviewText: I bought this product in removing fine surface scratches from my black 2007 Chevy Cobalt.  The paint is still in great condition and only has some minor surface scratches from automatic carwashes.The first time I used Meguiar's Ultimate Compound I used an orbital buffer.  The instructions are quite vague and more or less state that all you have to do is rub the compound in a circular motion in a small area then buff away.  So I figured if that was all you really had to do, an orbital buffer would be more than enough.Wrong.While Ultimate Compound is excellent at removing water spots (and even dead bugs and tar) it is horrible at removing swirl marks and fine scratches.  I can use a simple wax and get the same results as with this "Ultimate" compound.The second time around I decided to try the product on my victory red 2001 Chevy Blazer.  Years of automatic car washes have really taken their toll on the paint, but not so much that it had lost all of its shine.  Instead of the buffer, I used a 100% cotton terrycloth and some good ol' elbow grease.  Unfortunately I got the same results as before.I can get the same result that this product offers by using Turtle Wax Ice and in a fraction of the time.Do I recommend this product? NoWill I buy this product again? Probably not
summary: Not worthy of the Meguiar's name...

reviewText: I bought Meguiars Ultimate Compound because I had neglected my paint job for too long. I had swirls, oxidation and it made my black paint job look dull. After using this, those deformities were gone (or at least very well hidden.) I love this product, and have recommended it to everyone I know. It goes on easy and wipes off easy as well. There was no real wait time, but I would suggest following the directions cause it will be harder to remove if you let it set long on the paint. Other than that, this is a very good product.

I used Meguiar's Ultra Cut and Ultra Finishing products to remove swirl marks from my black car. Those products worked very well. A month later, I tried Meguiar's Ultimate Compound to remove any remaining swirls, but, in my opinion, the two "Ultra" compounds work faster/better and produce more substantial results. I do not think I'd be able to remove as many swirls with just the Ultimate Compound as I did with the Ultra Cutting and Ultra Finishing. However, after I used the Ultimate Compound the paint is very smooth and mirror like.I applied the Ultimate Compound with Meguair's DA polisher and Meguiar's 9006 pad, followed by Meguiar's Mirror Glaze and Meguiar's NXT wax, the car looks very well and shiny.I think this product would be good for removing light, possibly moderate swirls, but for heavy swirls, I'd recommend Ultra Cutting and Ultra Finishing with a DA polisher.
summary: Good product, but not for heavy swirls.

reviewText: I just purchased and tried this compound for the first time, last weekend. I have tried other compounds, but found that they either, didn't rub out scratches and tough dirt was advertised, or was too harsh, leaving me concerned it would ruin my paint.  This stuff is just right! It did the job very well, even removing some rather large scratches on the bumper that wouldn't rub out in the past. I would definitely recommend.

The Ultimate Compound is a very good product. I do have some suggestions that took me almost a full bottle of use to figure out. Make sure the car is cool to the touch (if the car has been running, open the hood and let it cool off. The product will dry too quickly if the car is hot. Use a Clay Bar on the car first. A clay bar is one of the easiest items to use on your car and it makes it very smooth. The smoother the surface, the easier it is to apply and remove the "Compound". I cannot emphasize this enough. If you have not tried it, you really should. Meguiars and Mothers sell it. Some reviewer stated that they have seen "zebra stripes" after using the product. The Zebra stripes are caused by their fingers. Most applicators are about  -  " thick and your fingers compressing makes an uneven application, unless you truly are using the palm of your hand. The best applicator that I have found is an inexpensive car wash sponge. Not a sponge with loops, but a smooth foam surface. I placed a bead around the edge and a couple of lines in the center and used my fingers to rub it into the sponge. I then placed a line around the edge and a line in the center and applied even pressure to the car. The sponge is about 3 - 4 inches thick, it produced an even pressure and I could go over the hood very quickly. This is non-abrasive so you will not be getting swirls after using the product. Just the same use a forward backward motion instead of a swirl pattern. The more you rub back and forth, the more water spots will come off. You may want to repeat the application. I had heavy duty water spots and I found that each time I used it, it got better and better after every use. The more you use this product the better it will be. Meguiars also has some excellent "Cut Cleaners" sold in the auto paint aisle. You can use those as well, but be careful as most are abrasive. If you do use a "cut cleaner" you will have to use the "Compound" afterwards to smooth it out. Always remember that when you use the Compound, it removes everything old wax, spots, etc..  This is really a "polish" not a wax. Should you use a wax or a sealant ? Paste or liquid ? If you hate to wax your car and only want to wax it once or twice a year, then you will want to use "Nu Finish". It stinks though' smells like chemicals, but it produces a good shine and lasts a long time. If you do not mind waxing your car every 90 days and want a very good shine, then a synthetic polymer sealant, such as Meguiars NXT 2.0 is what you want to use. If you want the absolute shine and do not mind waxing every 30 days or 2 weeks, then a high quality liquid carnuba is for you. Paste waxes last longer, but are a real pain to use as they require more work to remove. Liquid waxes and sealants are very easy to use. If you are new to waxing I would go to the Meguiars NXT 2.0. Do not forget to use microfiber towels to remove; they work very well. You may want to use Meguairs Ultimate Black product to use on all black rubber trim surfaces. It works very well with a single application. Pick up a little chrome polish and finish the trim as well. Last but not least get a detail brush to remove the extra wax that goes into the crevices. It is very very easy to use. Good Luck

If you follow the directions and use the proper applicator this compound will take out light scratching. I didn't expect miracles on my old 1999 Toyota Corolla, but the Meguiar's did a better job than anything I've used in the past. I'm even thinking with continued use I'll be able to take out some of the deeper mars.

I was a little dissapointed with this product I spend a lot of money on meguiars products and and it was hard to remove this one just didn't seem to cooperate. Followed directions but would not remove the lightest of scratches. I don't recommend this compound
I really like this compound, It works great on plastic headlight lenses also. I used only the polishing foam attachment from my 3M headlight restoration kit and it made the lenses look like new.
The product works and does what it says. If you are missing paint or hoping on a miracle the product will not replace paint just fix certain flaws with the paint.

Works as described, I've a long time user of Meguiar's products, I use this compound by hand for removing water spots and other paint imperfections as well as maintaining the appearance of my auto. Easy to use by hand or with machine.

Compare to 3M and turtle wax, it is easy to take off the dirt and stink spot on the car.  I think it is the great product to start when you need to do the detail for the car.  I used it with the Meguiar yellow wax all the time
summary: much better than turtle wax compound

reviewText: Someone left a nice big scratch on my new car when I was parked and didn't leave a note. I used this polish and it got rid of most of the marks left.
Great product but this must be used with the correct combo of cleaners and such to get the right results.

Best compound ever, long working times, good cut with yellow pads, and has great finish sometimes it looks as good as the Ultimate polish.  Best of all there is little or no dusting like some other compounds. Very user friendly, especially for new detailers.

I bought this product to remove oxidation and small scratches from my son's 1997 Honda Accord. I didn't expect miracles since the car is nearly 15 years old, although the product packaging does suggest it is miracles you will get. The truth is the following: you won't remove all the small scratches and have the car look like new, but you will remove the oxidation and renew the car's finish quite a bit.Be prepared to sweat. First, I suggest you get a soft cloth or sponge to wipe the compound on. Small circles as the product directions recommend. I did half the hood and half the roof first just the see the difference and it was quite apparent. The car is black and the surfaces I compounded looked much darker and richer. I removed the compound with a terry towel. Please keep this in mind, because if you try to remove the compound with a microfiber cloth, it will be nearly impossible, as you need the texture of the cloth or towel to help remove the compound.I complete the rest of the car in sections just as I detailed above. I was able to remove many slight scratches and nearly all of the oxidation. Afterwards, I polished the car, since I had just essentially removed the old finish. After a few years of washing and waxing (3 times a year for the wax) a car, and you'll likely have built up finish in some areas, though not all. That's one reason it's a good idea to use this product every year or 2 to bring it down to a base you can evenly polish again.End result: A nice shine on an old car and many, though not all, imperfections removed. It took about 2.5 hours to wash, compound and wax the car. But I feel it was worth it and makes my son's car--my old car--look well maintained, which is what I wanted.
summary: Works quite well, as you work up a sweat

reviewText: This is definitely on the cutting edge (sorry for the pun) of technology.  Instead of using three different cutting compounds in bringing out the paint, this stuff starts out a little more abrasive and breaks down to a finer compound as you keep buffing.  I don't have any idea how they figured that out, or how it accomplishes the process, but it does work just like Meguiar's says it does.  Very easy product to use with my Porter Cable buffer.

very much a great product to have in the garage or car care products for removing oxidation.  it will not remove heavy water spots but it will take care of oxidation very well. it is a great beginners compound to step up to.

reviewText: It was only effect with super fine scratches. With normal fine scratches , the product won't make them disappear. I tried to scrub fine scratches for hour but they were still there. reviewText: I used this to buff the paint on a vehicle that had been fairly neglected over the years. I washed and clay bared the car first. I used this compound with a rotary buffer and a wool pad. It did a good job, but was difficult to remove. No, I did not allow it to dry like I would a wax. Perhaps I applied too much and or didn't buff long enough, but I had to do a considerable amount of hand buffing with a microfiber cloth to remove the residue. I consider this a good product for non professionals.

On my car, on my sideview mirror, I noticed that the paint was quite faded the last time I washed my car, which was last week. I already had Meguiar's Ultimate Compound on hand so I grabbed a microfiber towel, poured some of the product on the towel, and rubbed in a fast, circular motion.Maybe like 20 seconds of rubbing, the finish was restored! I was happy to see that it indeed did work and wasn't a gimmick. I will upload photos to show the end result.So a week later, the finish is still as good as it was when I first applied the product.  Next up is my rear bumper!Great product and I do recommend it for restoring faded portions

Since Meguiar's is known for high quality stuff, this is no exception.  This is pretty amazing stuff.  I have 3m marine grade rubbing compound and turtle wax polishing compound.  I used the rubbing compound is great for getting really deep oxidation spots off and polishing compound was used for shining it up.  It did a decent job but this stuff would probably eliminate all those runs in just a few simple applications.  I used this stuff first on my headlights because they were a little oxidized and had little speckles of dirt or something on them.  I just rubbed like a dime sized on a microfiber cloth onto the headlight and wow.  After putting it on like wax, and kept going over and over it until it disappeared, this stuff is pretty amazing.  I used my polishing compound on them before, and it cleaned it up a little, but nothing how clear and spotless that this Ultimate compound works.  I then buffed it with the other side of the microfiber cloth and my headlights now look pretty brand new.  They are crystal clear as they could possibly get.  I used them on my dad's headlights and he said the same thing.  They just really make the glass on the headlights perfect so you can see right through them.  You know how when you clean your windows sometimes and people can't tell if they are up or down, this is what it looks like on the headlights.  You can hardly tell there is a piece of plastic protecting them.  Same thing with your tail lights as well.  But anyways, since all it needed was one run to get everything off, I can't imagine what this stuff will do for the paint.  I think my review is long enough to bore you, and I think you get the point that this is the stuff to get.  Don't waste your money on other polishing compounds, trust me.  You might want to get a good rubbing compound though.  Even though this stuff is like rubbing compound and polishing compound, it goes on pretty thin and feels almost like polishing compound.  Also, this stuff is very easy to work with, unlike my polishing and rubbing compounds.  Those things took forever to rub in and had barely any shine.  This stuff goes away and shines like crazy.  Get this stuff, you won't be disappointed.

This product is fantastic and very easy to use. I applied it with a twenty buck random orbital polisher, no fancy equipment needed. I did three coats/passes on the hood and trunk and one pass on the rest of the car. The results are amazing. This works far better than a cleaner wax.The only thing better would be a Meguiars professional grade compound with a Porter Cable buffer, which would cost much more and require skill to make sure you don't mess up. This product is basically fool proof and very easy to use.If your paint has general issues with micro-scratches all over the car, this is your fix. For specific scratches, try Swirl-X.
I used this with a random orbital polisher and just did the hood of my car - it looks great.  Easy to compound, nice finish, and no swirl marks or issues in the finish.

I had fine scratches and swirls on my pearl paint, not oxidized or faded. I would recommend Meguiar's Scratch X 2.0 for minor blemishes as this Ultimate Compound cuts deeper. Used Meguir's 6.5 inch pads on Home Depot's Ridgid Random Orbital Sander. The pads will stick to the sander's hook and loop pad perfectly. The sander is like 60 bucks as compared to a so called "car" random orbital polisher that costs $140+. They're the SAME THING!
Went on well and came off easy. Did what I intended it to do. Works very well overall and doesn't take much

I just used the set of Meguiars Ultimate Compound, Polish and Liquid Wax.  The set together was great.  I used a Griot's Garage Dual Action Polisher with Orange, White and Red 5.5" pads. On bottle is probably enough to do 4-5 cars.

now this compound i bought to go over my repair work, however i left it unfinished on purpose because i seen where i could do more improvement to my truck, so i'm leaving this till next time.will post review later
