reviewText: these are fun goggles and look good. I have been seeing more and more people wearing these. I cant say they work to well with helmets.
summary: they are what they look like

reviewText: These work great and look cool.

I use this pad more than anything else. They last long (Stay away from emblems)Loads up nice and the 7" allows for fast coverageI use these with #21 and #26 wax from Meguiar'sI've always had success with this and the other 7" 2.0 buff pads from Meguiar's.This pad when paired with the proper WAX does wonders.I would recommend this with Meguiar's DA also.
summary: Ah how I love you my black finishing pad

reviewText: I bought the Meguiar;s polisher for Christmas! Couldn't wait to use it! Been using their products for years, keeps my cars looking like new! couldn't be happier! :)
This products does what is says it will. I use this for my DA Meguiars polisher. Best use for waxing, finishing buff.
This finishing pad was easy to put on the polisher and did a good job in applying the wax to the the boat.  Performed as expected.

I love these and other Meguiars products.  Their claim is true that you can use these, and wash them with your microfiber towels in the washing machine and have a clean pad for future use.  The skill of using these is to know exactly how much material on the pad.  It seems to come with time and experience.  Too little no good.  Too much no good.
summary: I like what you've done with your pad

reviewText: Bought this to go along with theDEWALT DWP849X 7-Inch/9-Inch Variable Speed Polisher with Soft Start. Fits perfectly with the hook and loop backing. Great to learn buffing with. I do prefer the hex-logic pads because they seem to produce less splatter. I went with Meguiar's pad because most their products are high quality with a good reputation. Used with a few different waxes and finishing polishes.
summary: Great beginner's finishing pad to learn with

reviewText: Very soft pad, easily attaches to Meguiars DA Polisher wheel. Machine washes well but it does seem to collect lint and fabric debris from the wash. You might want to wash the pad separately by hand. I was worried that the velcro style attachment would collect bits of fabric and lint and affect attachment to polisher wheel but it was not a problem.
summary: Meguiar's W 9207 7" Soft Buff 2.0 Foam Finishing Pad

reviewText: Meguiars is my product of choice, and I personally like this finishing pad better than the diamond finishing pad, the diamond one seems to wear faster, and I think the pattern is simply asthetic
I use this for polish and sealer.It serves the paint on my truck and corvette with a great shine.I would suggest a more agressive pad if your needs a compound.
I use this pad as a final finish pad, and it works great, nice and soft, washed it several times by hand, and the velcro still sticks great.
They work well. But too over priced. All profit! But they work well. An I can't find these any cheaper? So there you go.  SW
I use as last stage of polishing my car using Porter Cable 7424XP. It works great after 2-3 usages. I don't now how long it will last. I will update the review later.
CheaP cloth seat cover. Works for what I needed and it fit pretty well. A little small and my seats aren't huge.
I put it on the first night and the bands ripped out of place. I had to rig it up to get it to stay in place. It bunched in the corners because there was too much material. But it does its job.

I didn't expect much from this cover considering the price, but I was surprised at how cheaply made this cover is.  I broke two of the four straps that are used to secure the covers - they just pulled apart from the cover.  I do not recommend these covers since the fastening mechanisms are faulty.

We take our puppies with us and they both shed some. One is a red and white Corgi the other is a little black mutt. We have light gray seats in our 2012 Subaru Forester and we use the cover for the back seat. It does cover the seat well enough to protect from the puppy hair but isn't a perfect fit. But for the price we aren't complaining - it does what we needed.
summary: Not a great fit but good to protect the seat from dog hair

reviewText: Works well on the old farm truck.

This is a perfect light for the back yard when the dog goes out at night time, the light comes on and I can see him...  This is exactly what I wanted and it has a solar pannel that I moved around the corner of the house to pick up the most sun light, all in all a perfect light for me...
These motion activated solar powered lights provide adequate lighting for sidewalks, driveways and decks in two directions for as much as 30 feet.

We installed it over a step on the path leading to the house, and it works great. The solar panel is up on the roof, the sensor turns the light on when approaching the place at over 10 feet in both directions, and stays on way after you passed the tricky spot.

Not as bright as I would have liked but it could be because I have it installed very high, probably 12' or so.  The sensor isn't super sensitive, ie., you have to come pretty close to activate the light but that may be because of the height as well. All in all though I'm happy with it.  Not having to do any wiring was key!

My mother in law needed more light in the walkway leading to her garage.  With the interior walls already insulated & finished out, it would have been a major undertaking to wire in a 110 volt security light.  This Maxsa light was just the ticket.  While not bright enough to light up the whole yard, it is perfectly adequate for its intended use.  During daylight & even dusk hours, it doesn't seem all that bright, but at night, it lights up her walkway up to about 30 feet from the door enough to see well enough you don't stumble.  The two lamp heads are a plus, as her walk has a corner in it, and you can angle each one to shine where you want it to.  Being LEDs, the bulbs should never need replacing.Installation was simple, just 4 screws & it was up.  It is light & easy to install, and the solar panel can be about 8 feet from the main unit and still have the cord reach, a plus if you want the lights under a door overhang, as you can put the solar panel up where the sunlight will reach it.  Setting takes a little time, but is straightforward.  Adjustments include:  Time 'on' after motion stops, sensitivity, or distance from sensor before the light turns on, and how dark/light you want conditions before the light comes on.  I found it easiest to set the first two settings during the day, with the light adjustment set to full daylight, and then waited in the evening to about the conditions I wanted the light to come on, and set the dark/light dial so it would just turn on.  The instructions warn you only have so much light between charges, so you don't wanting it to turn on during the day if the neighbor's dog wanders by and use up the batteries.What swayed me to this light over others was the fact is uses standard rechargable AA batteries, instead of a special purpose built battery.  When the time comes, I know I'll be able to replace them easily & cheaply.
This is a nice portable motion light that can follow you any were, nice and bright for the size. The LED should last a very long time ( I hope so anyway )

Installation was simple and fast I used ss screws ins. instead of the zinc ones that came with it. After the light was fully charged ( 3 days), I set it up and used it at night, The lights are dim and don't light the area brightly.  I will not recommend of buy this one again.

Buy two of these, watch a youtube video on "2 bucket wash", and you will be on your way to stardom as this will help keep your car looking like brand new! Seriously, if you are washing your car yourself and not using this method you are going to slowly destroy the finish of your car. I searched all the sites and you can't find a better deal than this, especially if you have prime since shipping is free!

This bucket is just the right size good value for the money, like the lid that comes with it helps you store your wash mitten. I haven't used the car wash yet but soon will, would recommend anyone that likes to wash a car to purchase this bucket!

I find this to be just the right size for washing a mid-sized car, and the bucket has held up to repeated abuse in the driveway. It gets dragged around a lot when washing my car (I should really consider one with wheels), but the bottom of the bucket has nice extra lip to offset such heavy use.I haven't had any issues with the fitment of the grit guard, as I've seen here on other reviews. The washing mitt that came with my set was also quite plentiful, and I still have yet to use it, but it's nice to know I've got a high quality backup.
summary: Perfect Size For Home Use & Love The Soap That Comes With It

reviewText: The bottle of soap was leaking yellow goo all over everything ever since I got this. I tossed it in a ziploc bag for the moment, because hey, it's still good soap. I wasn't so sure about the wool wash mitt so I tossed that aside, as I have many microfiber wash mitts at my disposal. The grit guard is a must have for washing your vehicles properly.
summary: Bucket works as it should, the soap however....

reviewText: Love the bucket and grit guard. The Chemical guys soap is awesome, love the bright color. The wash mitt, not really a fan, I stick to my MF mitt or my CarPro mini.  This is a great value for sure.
I needed a no spill bucket and all the rest of the stuff was a bonus. I find myself using this every weekend! The wash and glass it comes with works very very well!!
Great starter kit my only issue is the grate that sets at the bottom spinns and moves around so I wonder if its doing its job?
I use mostly chemical guys products and this package is awesome. The bucket and grit guard are heavy duty and will last a long time.

Love the grit guard feature. Use 2 of these for a 2-bucket car wash system. Very sturdy and reliable. I've tried a couple of cheaper buckets from home depot and wal-mart. Both broke and cracked after a few weeks of light use. The wash mitt is great for getting rid of stubborn stains on the vehicle, although I use it as a secondary mitt and a microfiber mitt for my main washing. Soap is great and has a nice citrus scent. Very concentrated. Top is a nice feature as well.
summary: Great Product and Car Washing Kit

reviewText: I bought this kit after watching what seemed like 100+ videos from the Chemical Guys on Youtube. It seals perfectly, so you can fill it with water and take it to the coin op car wash if you want (they recommend this in a video). The soap is nice, great scent. I would recommend this to a friend, if I had a friend that was as anal about washing his/her vehicles as I am.

The best quality home car washing I have done in all my years. The bucket keeps the dirt at the bottom. The citrus based wash fluid leaves one heckuva shine. Very pleased. The bucket and wash fluid should last a very long time.
summary: Makes washing the car more enjoyable

reviewText: The bucket/grit guard works exactly like it said it would. The dirt stays at the bottom of the bucket and does not mix around. That prevents you from transferring dirt back on your car. I was skeptical about the car wash solution that it came with. Once I used it, I was surprised at how effecting it is. I think it works better than the Meguiars gold wash, which I've been using for forever.

Bought for a Jeep compass and worked as promised and alot cheaper than OEM. This one is 314mhz (i think, or around that) Check what yours is when you have it off and make sure it matches. Highly recommend.
Had new wheels and tires put on and decided might as well get new TPMS sensors, and these activated perfectly, no issues.
summary: Exactly replacement for my Jeep JK 08

reviewText: I installed an aftermarket lift, wheels, and tires on our 2010 JKU. I wanted to be able to rotate the full size spare to keep tread wear even. The dealer wanted $80 for the OEM part plus labor for each tire. I ordered this here, and had the local tire shop install it for $5. It paired instantly with my vehicle and the tire warning light turned off.So 5 of these here cost me less than one would at the dealership. I can't see why you wouldn't order this if you had the need.

Got new wheels without TPMS and was sick of TPMS sensor going off.  Had the local tire shop put these in for 20 dollars a tire.  TPMS monitor has not gone off and U have put on at least 1K miles with them
summary: Dorman OE Solutions 974-001 2008 Jeep JKU Sahara

reviewText: Bought this for my 07 Jeep Grand Cherokee for some reason only one of my tires keeps going flatI have used rebuild kits on the original sensor still leaks very frustrating when I was looking one of the previous purchasers said it fitted straight into his Jeep and connected with the car immediately well you cant argue with that can youJust a word of Warning this is not for Export vehicles my Australian 07 Jeep GC has a different type that needs the sensor to be 433MHZ this unit is not suitable product is still high quality just not suited to Australian models
summary: Dorman OE Solutions 974-001 Chrysler Pacifica/Caliber/Compass Tire Pressure...

reviewText: I bought this for my 2008 JK jeep wrangler after the valve stem on the stock sensor corroded and developed a leak.  Discount tire tried to sell me a deal to replace the old TPMS and stem for $60.. Now I wish I would of done it.This sensor after installed shut off the TPMS light before I left the tire dealers parking lot...  "Awesome" I thought, problem solved.Well in the week that has followed the light comes on and off intermitenly with out any real rime or reason.  Hot or Cold, Night or Day.  I've had my preasure checked numerous times and it's alway spot on.  Usually it comes on after I just start the car and will go out after a few minutes but yesterday it came on and stayed on all the way to work.  When I left the office for lunch it was off.I too live in Minnesota like another reviewer and had concerns about the sensor working correctly in cold winters.  If it wont work right in 70+ degree summer / fall it's not going to get any better.  Worst part is I'm out the installation fees and what do I do... Buy another one?  I'm going to the dealer which I should of done the first time.  -Lesson learned.
We have two black vehicles. Hard to describe. It's almost like the towels pick up swirl marks and those ever so small dust particles right from the finish of the car.

I saw all the rave reviews and the photo made these towels look exceptionally plush, just what I had been looking for.  I saw one review that reported surprise at all the rave reviews and found the towels disappointing.  I guess it depends on how particular you are but I agree with the latter reviewer.  These towels are better than the bulk Walmart type (they should be for the cost!) but they are not the luxurious high end towel you might be expecting.  The "silk" binding is really cheap looking and the stitching looks like the mass produced product that this is.  They are not as plush as the photo suggests.  If you are just looking for a thicker towel that is better than most you'll be happy with them.  However, I am extremely particular about my detailing supplies and if that describes you then pass on these towels and find something else.  I have a large towel from Griot (with pockets) that is a bit of a pain to use but the quality is absolutely there (the towel cost about $25).  I find that the reviewers at Amazon often provide great info and I'll be looking at other reviews to find leads on the high end towels I'm looking for.  I've ordered some standard sized towels from Griot and will report on those after the arrive.  Hope this helps.Update July 9 2013.  I received Griot towels the other day (blue, about the same price as these) and they are MUCH better.  There is some lint but it shakes off easily and prewashing is not required.  The Griot towels are what you are looking for if you want the Porsche of detailing towels.
summary: Midrange, not what I had hoped for

reviewText: I would recommend these towels.They are plush and do a great job of waxing our vehicles.When you're done just throw then in the washer, and they're ready for the next time.Sometimes after I wash a car I use them to wipe it down.Works great.4 - Pack of Ultra Plush Premium Microfiber Towels 16" X 16 "- At 360 Gsm, This Is One of the Best Microfiber Cleaning Cloths- Ultra Plush Micro Fiber Material on One Side, and the Other Side Consists of Medium Terry Microfiber Material.
very well finished and seems to work very well. will have to wash a few times to see what happens. Just don't use fabric softeners on any of your detail stuff. it makes it not absorb water as well.
These are the best microfiber towels I have ever used.  They are super soft, plush and work great.  I love these towels.
Work great. Buff, polish and dry.

In my opinion and from what I've tried (Which is a lot) I consider Dura Gloss brand microfiber towels to be the absolute best. They seem thirstier than these, probably because they have two layers sewn together which makes them thicker also. The silk edging is nice as is the color on these. Not a bad product by any means.
summary: Good but nothing like Dura Gloss ones

reviewText: I prefer to use these for washing the exterior or wiping dust from the interior. I find that they do not dry as well as they should leaving many streaks.
These microfiber towels are nice and plush.  I use them solely on my paint for compounds/polish and sealant/waxes.  Easy to wash too.

Well, I ordered a few of these to replace some from oddly enough, Meguiars.... They're made in China... OF COURSE. WELL, LONG STORY SHORT, great towels!!!!! But the edge material came apart at the first use. We hadn't even laundered these yet.... Just be ready to return em for replacement. They're glad to help... As they want you to co e back!

These are a really good towel for quick detail sprays or buffing and/or taking off wax. They are decently priced when buying the 3 pack. Comparable towels are a couple more dollars a piece per towel. I bought a package to try and have since bought 2 more 3-packs of them.

Arrived earlier than I expected. Installation was easy and made a big difference walking in the camper. I felt no sway at all. Glad to get this. May get another one for total stability alto this one seems to do the trick

Use - Gooseneck living quarter horse trailer - with single jack.  Trailer was not stable.  Tried regular screw up RV jack stands but they were not tall enough half the time without using lots of blocks.  Saw this and ordered.  Used it last weekend.  Works perfectly.  Works on uneven ground.  Adjusts to varying heights.  Several persons who saw this stopped and ask where I got it.  This is much easier to use that the typical screw up stands.  One modification you might need.  The "rachet" strap that is shown is only a certain length.  Should you need to "spread" the legs of the stand out to make the height "lower" you might need to use a longer strap.  However, most people have these laying around or you can get them for next to nothing at Wal-Mart.  If you have a trailer - this is a great item.

Bought the Valterra 020106 RV Stabilizer because the theory behind it seems ok.  Took the travle trailer out camping and tried it out, I installed it under the rear sewer hose bumper.  As far as the product working "yes it does keep the trailer sturdy"  I'm  63 and Installing this product I had to lay on the ground to spread out the legs, and keep them steady as I ratcheted it tight. Maybe securing the product in place would help, but then you all ways have to deal with the ratchet on the ground.  The locking rods off of the seissor jack seems the way to go.

I just installed it yesterday on my 38' fifth wheel under the back bumper. It did help with the overall shaking in the trailer. I intend to buy two more. One for the front and one for the side by the door. Although I like the product the first one I received had a cut in the strapping and when I went to tighten it down the strapping started to come apart. I sent it back. I do find that the strapping and ratchet is very light duty and not the best quality otherwise I would have rated it 5 stars. I recommend this to anyone because of it's simple design and super easy installation, no holes to drill.
summary: It certainly helped and super easy to insatll

reviewText: Great product and works as described. I use this with our travel trailer and the floors feel almost like we are at home. Very solid and well made product

Now my trailer sits like a rock.  No more rocking when we move around.  Feels like a "real" house when these are installed.  I can't imagine being without them.  The only problem is I have to get on the ground to put them on.
each to work and seem to take the rock and roll out the MC when moving about. MC is 32 ft and using it under the back bummer. Just don't over do it. It's not a lift.
summary: Will see how it stands up

reviewText: One of the best stabilizers we have tried for our toy hauler.  You do have to sit next to your rig to install but it's fairly easy and the results are astounding.  One on each side toward the center of your trailer and you have ended the rock and roll blues!
summary: Rock and roll ender for RV's

reviewText: Would have given it a 5 star but the feet are a bit small when the lot is small rocks.  It tends to sink in and need tightening more often.  Worked great when lot was concrete or hard ground.  We placed it under the step area for more support at that point so there was a LOT less bounce when someone went in or out of the trailer.
summary: helped a LOT on our lightweight travel trailer

reviewText: We own a 35 foot travel trailer by Forrest River, a Rockwood Signature Elite. We bought a set of these RV Stabilizer to cut down on the swaying when you walk across the trailer. We had no idea if they would reduce the swaying on our trailer, so we took a chance on them and they worked. We have two slides in the rear of our trailer so we installed one under each slide under each frame of the trailer. This has reduce 90% of the sway we had when we walked across the trailer. We are thinking about getting another set for our front, we have one slide in the front. These stabilizers won't reduce it a 100% of the swaying but they come close. I would recommend these to anyone.
I used these to steady my 32 foot Class C RV.  They do a great job.  I placed one under the rear bumper and one at the side entrance.  They made an immediate and noticeable difference.

EZ Creme smells great and works even better. I really do not like doing IPA wipedowns after polishing my car so this does just what I want. After I finish polishing I apply this with my Flex and it adds a nice deep gloss. Comes off super easy with a microfiber towel and without a doubt the best glaze I have found. This creates a great bond for a sealant also.
This in combination with a clay bar treatment made our beater 07 Toyota look like a show piece. The car has literally not been washed in over 2 weeks and still looks clean.
summary: Just ordered my 4th bottle of this. Definitely a fan!

reviewText: I think EZ Creme Glaze is a great product. Used after claying or polishing, and before a sealant or a wax job, EZ creme will make the final result very wet and glossy looking, to say nothing of super smooth. It hides small scratches and swirl marks. It is very easy to apply. No effort at all, applying or removing. And yes, the grape scent is wonderful.This product brings a lot of bang for the buck, and I encourage anyone interested in having a beautiful looking, stand out gorgeous car to try this product. You will be delighted with the results of this simple extra step. A good carnauba wax, like P21s, Chemical Guys 5050, or their Hardcore XXX Carnauba Paste wax on top of the EZ Creme should yield outstanding results. I used original Chemical Guys Butter Wet Wax and the results were jaw dropping.Try it. You 'll like it!
summary: Excellent, easy to use glaze will add depth, gloss and reflectivity while hiding swirl marks

reviewText: Goes on smooth and comes off easy.  Shines my car to a mirror-like finish.  Highly recommended for dark cars, especially layered with a good synthetic wax.  My car has never looked so good!  Pleasant grape smell.

Used this stuff on a black Subaru Forester, and it made the flakes in the paint really shine. Didn't take much either, considering the size of the vehicle I only used maybe an ounce or two of product.
summary: Makes the metallic flakes in black just pop out at you.

reviewText: I was very hopeful given all the great reviews, but other than the nice smell, I was not overly impressed. I did not notice the filling properties other mentioned and I found it quite hard to work with by hand. Maybe this is better machine applied, by hand it takes quite a lot of work to get it completely buffed out and the shine does not look much different than other products I have used.

This is my second Chemical Guys product, and I'm sure there will be more to come. I applied this glaze with my Porter Cable 7424XP paired with a Lake Country black finishing pad. EZ Creme went on easily and buffed off very easily and left the paint feeling silky smooth. If your car already has wax or sealant on it, you'll want to strip it all off, do some claying if necessary and then apply this glaze and then follow it with whatever wax or sealant you prefer.This glaze also has minor filling capabilities and I saw this first-hand. There's one isolated scratch on my hood that just doesn't seem to want to come out, but it's only noticeable at a very particular angle in the right lighting. The CG glaze filled it in pretty nicely, making it harder to spot. I then applied Menzerna Power Lock sealant once the car was completely glazed and it was buffed off. Very nice depth, shine and clarity to the paint. I must say I'm pleased with this product.
summary: Awesome glaze, left paint feeling smooth, smells great...

reviewText: Relatives and Friends are always asking how I get it to look so shine because I have a Audi Black 2014 but it is different to others contemporary Audi cars, more shine, more depth in the paint. Long lasting even after rain or washing, no need to remove previous wax because preserves and acts like sealant as well. Chemical Guys seem to understand how important it is to satisfy customers. You won't be disappointed. It’s crazy, but I apply shining even the structure of the windows from my house and the fridge in the kitchen, everything it touch... beautifies and gives a mirror shine.
I really enjoy using this product.  I apply after cleaning and claying.  Honestly, I don't know if this product is any better then my 3M products, but the 3M doesn't smell as good as this one!
summary: Another great product from Chemical Guys

reviewText: This stuff is awesome. While it might not have the same amount of filling capability as Chemical Guys Glossworkz, it has a more-than-acceptable shine and a brilliant wet look that I just love. If I'm glazing, I'll use this first unless I need to fill in marring and swirls and don't have the time (or they don't have the budget) to do a paint correction the 'right' way. This stuff is a great in between. Always follow up with a sealant and/or wax for extra protection, and to increase the durability of a glaze!This stuff smells like grapes, so like other Chemical Guys products, they all smell great.
summary: Light filling capability, and an extremely bright shine

reviewText: This product is great (as most Chemical Guys products are!).  I apply this either after the paint has been clayed or after a full paint correction, before I apply my sealant or wax.  This leaves the paint feeling amazingly slick and smooth.  It also adds depth and gloss to the finish that is then further enhanced by your sealant or wax of choice.  EZ Creme Glaze also helps to protect your vehicles finish.  I would highly recommend this to anyone looking to enhance the look and feel of their vehicles paint.  It is a great product that truly works.-Zach[...]
summary: From a Professional Detailer - This is a MUST HAVE!

reviewText: Yes, it smells like bubble gum with a hint of cinnamon. It smells amazing!! I was tempted to drink it :)Anyway, I used this to clay my car and aside from smelling so dang good, it also seemed to work well. There were only a few occasions in which the clay really dug in but that may have been because I wasn't keeping enough of the lube on the car. It was simple to use, just thoroughly spray the area you are working on (keep it limited to 2 feet by 2 feet at a time for best results IMO) and then continue to spray the lube as you work to keep the surface well coated.As an FYI, I would wear gloves, like Nitrile for example, because this stuff will turn your hands blue and you'll look like Violet from Willy Wonka's in no time! Also, if you get any on your trim, I wouldn't wait too long to wash it off once you're done with that section. I made the mistake of doing the entire car before finally washing the car and it bleached out some of the trim on my car. I wasn't happy but I spent about 8 hours claying my car, so it was on there for a very long time.Otherwise, very happy with this product
Great product Much cheaper then using ANY spray wax for claying and it does what it says it does and does a great job doing it I would def recommend this product to anyone who claybars cars

I use this stuff as a lube for clay baring and the Nanoskin As-006 Autoscrub fine grade and it works good.It also works well as a quick detailer.The price was right $15.00 on the gallon size.If you have a black car you will notice streaking more than lighter color cars.Thats why only 4 stars.

This works just like they say that it does. I had great results and it does smell good. Clay baring my car was a breeze. I bought the gallon size so I don't run out in the middle of dodging my car or someone else's
I use this with 3M detailing clay and it works perfectly. Great smell and leaves little residue. You still have to wash afterward but you should be doing that prior to polish anyway.

This stuff is surely meant for what it says - to be used with a clay bar when detailing cars!Goes on super easy and comes off just as simple without having to scrub like crazy too!This is a great bottle to have around if you have several cars and go thru the stuff fast-refill containers are good to have around!
I bought this thinking you could dilute it, but learned that you don't.  It's a good price for lube, but I'd rather have a product that you can dilute and make gallons of instead.

It does the job. Smells like bubblegum. Wipes off very cleanly and easily with no residue. First time doing clay bar and on brand new car. This product made it easy. I note that the product was packed in a plastic bag, and the bottle leaked a bit. The bag leaked, and the box was noticeably soaked through in places. Not much product was lost.

This product works really well. I diluted it down 1:2 (1 part water:2 parts chemical) to make it last a little longer.Clay lube tends to go pretty fast, especially if you're liberal with it (which you should be). It maintains a great amount of lubrication even diluted down. You can use it full strength, but honestly I couldn't really tell the difference. @ 2:1, it was a little thin and didn't have a good 'feel' to it.I tested on old paint, and glass and was pleasantly surprised. It has a semi-strong bubblegum scent, doesn't dry quickly (it's not hot out, so I can't really test the heat part).When I run out I will definitely buy another gallon. For the price, you can't beat it.

I Clay Barred my car. I used one half gallon of this for the whole car and 1/2 of a clay bar. Do NOT skimp on the lubricant. Spray it ON the car and ON the clay bar for each area of the car that you do.

I have to agree with another reviewer that this cloth is almost identical to those you find in Walmart.  It is THIN THIN THIN and not at all worth the price.  This is a surprise from Mothers as I use a lot of their products and typically their quality is excellent.
summary: Cheap, thin, not worth the price

reviewText: These are soft, sturdy, and do a good job, but they are small.  They are great for a quick polish, or touch up a few small areas.  I had planned to use one of them to remove the polish or wax, but felt I would be rubbing too much old into the new, due to their small size.  I also bought the Mothers Quick Detail Towel, and they are larger and thicker, and could do my entire full-size car.

I know some people wouldn't want to spend this much money on polishing cloths, but if you're a bit on the OCD side like me, you know these things work like a charm and polish everything to a lustrous finish. I even use them on my guitar collection and my plasma TVs!
summary: Easily The Best Polishing Cloths Out There

reviewText: I would recommend these towels.They work extremely well polishing our cars.There's just so many microfiber towels on the market.Some are heavier than others, but most all work well.Polishing cloths are usually a bit thinner than others, but leave a great streak free shine.Show Car Guys All Purpose Microfiber Towels 16" X 16"- One Of The Best Microfiber Cleaning Cloths There Is. summary: Get the Detail ones by Mothers and use these for petty jobs and the Detail ones for real waxing.

reviewText: I thought my cheap microfiber clothes were just fine. They did not produce lint and moderate streak. I started using other Mothers product and found them to be the best so I decided to give this a try. I must say that... WOW this one polishes like no others.Zero lint, almost zero streak, and much superior polishing power. Great for both paint and glass.It also works great to polish right after waxing, to remove the excess wax and give the paint a great shine. I have used it with both a spray (foam) type of wax and with a thick paste.I would absolutely recommend it. The price is not bad and you won't be disappointed.I am right now placing an order for a second one of this... Great stuff!!
summary: Superior to any other microfiber cloth I have ever used

reviewText: I've detailed cars for years and most of the microfiber towels are nice enough, but this product is clearly superior.  Thick, plush, no nasty labels, can't recommend them highly enough.  You won't be sorry.

I like these because they are thick, soft, have a long nap and short nap side, and are bigger than the Polishing Cloths.  I could remove the wax haze from the exterior of my full-size car with one towel without feeling I was driving the old wax into the new finish.
summary: Thick, soft, sturdy, and bigger than the Mothers Polishing Cloths

reviewText: Perfectly sized and quality material. I purchased several of these at once. I use these to wash and wax my car. Eliminates streaks and does a great job. Lasts a long time.

Here you are talking! These are the very best for waxing and having your auto pico bello as they say in Germany. They last and they won't ever scratch your car paint even if you use the for dusting afterwards...
summary: The very best for experts and my car collection

reviewText: I love this towel. It is very thick and much larger than most microfiber towels. Absorbs perfectly, leaving no streaks or lint.
Works great to shine your car. No lint residue....I use it to buff streaks in my black car after washing it.

I read reviews about this thing falling apart and I have not seen that with my mitt (or the lint problem). I love it, it really soaks up the suds and water and lays it on your car real thick. I never throw it in the dryer of washer and maybe that is why other people were having problems with it falling apart. I have never been let down my Mothers products and this is no different
The wash mitt does an A-1 job  but, it is a bit small for my hand. I use it much like a cloth and, it works out very well.

i thought it was a little high on the price until i used it. I also bought a cheaper wash mitt and realized that this mitt has an inner liner that helps keep your hands dry, as long as you don't dump your hole hand in the wash bucket. A big factor if you are washing out in the cold.good wash mitt, will buy another.
Great while it lasted, but doesn't last long at all. Falling apart after a couple months of weekly use. Guess I will try a Microfiber mitt.
Lambswool mitts are great for washing your car.  I prefer to use them over anything else.  I have also been a fan of Mothers products. Win, Win

I've been using this mitt for the last year or so and finally decided it was time to move on to a microfiber offering. It's not that this doesn't do the job - it does, but it gets lint everywhere! For the most part it washes off in the rinse but you will notice them sticking out of places where two pieces of the car come together i.e. bumper to body or spoiler to trunk, etc. Again, its super soft, does a great job cleaning and does not leave any marks/swirls... but it does leave lint. Been using the microfiber mitt for a few weeks now and I LOVE IT.
summary: Good, not great - Better alternatives out there

reviewText: This lambswool mitt is so much better than my old one. It fits my hand better and gets in corners and tight places better. What I really like is that it doesn't seem to grab trash and keep it. My old one would cling to leaf pieces and tiny stuff and I would have to hand pick it out. This one it washes off easily. It even has a small loop so that you can hang the mitt to allow it to dry inside better. Good mitt!
summary: Best wash mitt I have ever had!

reviewText: I own a black car, and this is a must to keep debris from scratching across the surface of my paint. This product is built well, and very soft, and I will surely buy another when the one I own gets worn out.
This is an excellent wash mit.  It holds a lot of soapy water allowing user to wash a large area before having to go back for more soapy water.

I bought this to use on my son's 1997 black Honda Accord. Although I've maintained the car well and it has no rust, there are enough small scratches on the hood from rocks over the years to mar the color.This product requires some work. You have to wash the card first, naturally. Then you apply the pre-finish, which you remove with the detailing spray. After this step alone the car looks 100% better.After the pre-finish, apply the wax. Be careful, it's a thin consistency and will spill and leave black stains on a light surface, such as a garage floor. Try and keep the car in the shade or work on it (carefully) in the garage. It's much easier to work on a cool surface. Also, just a word of caution, wear latex or vinyl gloves if you can to prevent the black wax and pre-finish from getting on your skin and under your nails.When the car was done it shined very nicely with a beautiful black sheen that masked a multitude of scratches. The 15-year old car looked just great.I can speak to durability yet and I'm tempted to put a coat of conventional clear wax on top of the black wax.I would highly recommend this to anyone looking to enhance the look of their black car. Just know that it's a reasonable amount of work--but worth it!
summary: Made an old car look like new

reviewText: I will agree with posters that say this is a bit difficult to remove, it took some work by hand and you need to change towels frequently.  However the end result was stunning.  It isn't going to be a miracle cure for chips and scratches, but it will definitely blend and cover a lot of surface deep imperfections and add an incredible polish and shine.  It's a Carnauba based wax so like any it does last six weeks.  I recommend following up with a polymer based wax with gives you six months protection.  For under 20$ it's well worth the results.

So i bought this for my car because i havent really ever found somthing that really brings out the shine of my black car. I gotta say that this make my car pop and creates depth that i havent really ever found. The only reasoits not 5 stars is because in order to it right it takes 4 step of polish and buff out. It take 2-4 hours. So i hope you got time.

I have to admit this is a lot of work but the results are totally worth it.  Make sure you wear gloves.... make REALLY sure you wear gloves... but once you get done with this system you'll be thrilled with the way your car looks.
summary: THE system to use for black cars

reviewText: This is a wonderful product for black painted vehicles.  I use it on my Suzuki GSX1250FA black sparkle motorcycle.  It is very messy, so wear gloves.  Also, you might want to pre-make two plastic bags labeled Step 1 and Step 2 to store the applicators so they don't get mixed up.  You can see my video on youtube, search under RedonKiLaus.

I just finished waxing my 1999 Isuzu Rodeo. It's never been waxed before.. I know, I know. This stuff makes the vehicle shine, looks great. But it did take me about 5 hours to get the entire SUV done.. there's a 4 part process basically. Apply cleaner, apply detailer, apply wax, apply detailer.. then use the detailer again. All the products are black based, not white - which is a good thing. It did bring back a luster to the vehicle which was starting to become dark grey/bluish. I will have to apply a second coat at some point, as the hood has been replaced about 2 years ago, and has a different level of shine. I will more than likely buy this product again, but I'll also know to set a whole day to the process.
summary: Good stuff, takes a while though..

reviewText: Whether you want protection for your hands if you dump or something to keep them warmer these gloves do a great job for very little money. Strong durable and look great
summary: great leather riding gloves for little cash

reviewText: Well before it turned cold enough that I had to wear winter gloves, these came in so handy riding my bike
they fit very good and recommend to anyone

I am a med-large and saw these run small so I bought the large, these are too big. They fit but kinda swim on my fingers. If you are a in between like me then get the med. Worst case they will be tight but they do stretch out after wearing them.

I couldn't even get my fingers in. I normally wear Large so I ordered XL and can't even get my fingers half way in. I have the Raider full motorcycle gloves and they as well as these are a good deal when they fit.I JUST WISH THEY WERE HONEST ABOUT THE SIZING AND QUIT WASTING BUYERS TIME. IT'S A CRAP SHOOT GETTING A PAIR TO FIT.

reviewText: I saw the gloves were nice & thick leather so I thought this would last! right? I had these gloves less than a month they already have a tear from stress @ the thumb base.Luckily that was the only problem, so I still use them after a year.
awesome gloves ,real leather , can't beat the price.came fast with great shipping. good quality gloves. was very impressed with them. hands dont get so tired when riding.
They are ok. Nothing special and pretty thin. If you want some cheap low cost fingerless gloves, they are just that.

I ordered an XL pair of these gloves. However, they barely fit my wife's hands and she is all of 5'2" and has small hands.The package and the gloves were clearly labeled XL. Poor quality control at the manufacturing plant somewhere. The quality of the product itself seemed to be adequate but unfortunately I could not even try them on.

The first pair I ordered XL were to big so I ordered a second pair Large. The second pair I got didnt even match, the sewing was junk and the inside of the gloves were two different types of leather. I guess you get what you pay for, cheep price, cheep gloves !!
This item does seem to be a bit low quality but of course I did not pay out the wazo for it. It does well and I use it as summer riding gloves
They are OK for the price but when ridding in 105 degree weather they quickly grow in one size, but for the money will work for now.

These gloves are made off the same design blueprint as the First Classic Half Glove. However these gloves are much more comfortable for approx the same price. The First Classic Half Glove is stiff, not comfortable, can't move the fingers. This glove is comfortable, the slightly thinner leather making it less stiff and enabling finger movement. Both are made in Pakistan. This Raider version is actually very dark brown (at least mine is). Both are XXX-Large. Both very tight for a triple X. I guess this Raider being a thinner leather, but still plenty thick, should more easily stretch out. I have some mink oil that should do the trick. Both are well made. I'd return the First Classic glove but the return cost would be more than the value of the glove.
But they were too small for my hands, gave them to a friend who had smaller hands and he loves them...
Now that cold weather is here I need to wear Jersey gloves inside my leather gloves and these gloves let me do just that.
I expected them to be larger.  Tight getting on but fine once I am wearing them.  They are nice and warm
I only got to use these a very few times, however, they were very warm and fit very nice on me

I ordered these gloves because it seemed like a good deal for the price.  Problem is I can't even get them on my hands!  They are too small and I can't even return them for a larger pair (say XL or XXL) because apparently they only come in large.  So I end up keeping them and I still don't have a warm pair of gloves to use when I want to ride my bike and it is cold.  They did seem like a decent glove but I can't rate them on use or performance since I can't get my hands in them.

Warm well made gloves and they look great. They fit my hands perfectly. I used them at 48 degrees on my bike and for me that was the limit on how cold I could use these, any colder and I had to use my other gloves.
Leather tear and stitches coming out on both gloves in the inner-finger areas.Sending them back for refund. Would not recommend you purchasing them.
I live in NY and the season is turning cold. These gloves are keeping my hands real warm. I am honestly surprised.Very comfortable too. Go for it!
summary: Great gloves for the price. can't be beat

reviewText: The gloves appear to be very well made from quality leather and are nice and warm. I ordered extra large and they're tight on me but I can wear them. Order the next size up and you should be okay. I don't think they come in 2XL, so if you wear XL, expect them to be tight. I applied Lexol leather conditioner and Neatsfoot oil and that softened the leather and allowed the gloves to stretch a little. The price was definitely a bargain.

I ordered the large size and they fit snugly. I don't have very big hands. They feel good and should be even better after using them a few times. The quality is very good for the price. I took that flimsy clip off immediately and put 2 small split rings and a small D-ring on to clip them together. That was the worst feature on them but a small thing. I like to set up all my gloves so they are easy to clip. The little plastic clamp it a nice added touch to clip them together when storing.Good timing, it dipped to 36 deg in San Diego this morning. They are a GOOD BUY.
summary: They "fit like a glove" Very Good for the Price

reviewText: These gloves are very comfortable & warm. I've worn them in temperatures as low as 38 & keep my hands from going numb.
summary: Raider Black Large Leather Motorcycle Riding Gloves

reviewText: i froze my hands off before i got theese gloves.i had fleece gloves. didn't work in 20 degree motorcycle trips. the leather blocks the cold wind and the linning keeps your hands so warm i drive 70 to 75 mph in 20 degrees and  hands never get cold 1 bit.even blosk the cold wing going up your sleeves and into your jacket. what a great investment it has been to get theese gloves. the price was awesome. try going to a motorcycle shop and buy theese. high dollar.shipping was fast. i ride my motorcyle 365 days a year ,so i have to have the best gear .
These gloves were much better than I was anticipating, at this price point. They are great for those cold mornings! Love the fit.

I didn't expect the type of glove that I got for the money. These gloves could keep you warm in Montana!! Thick leather, well made, great fit. I don't need them in Florida and probably will not very often. But at the great price, I'm hanging on to these until the day I ride when it is really cold and they will save my hands from freezing. You would expect to pay $75 - $100 for these.I paid more for half finger thin gloves. Great deal.
Very nice product and excellent value!  The leather is very durable.  I was surprised at the dextarity with such a snug fit.  These were worth every penny!
They are a little stiff when you get them but a little leather softner and some time in the saddle and I think they will work well in cold weather. When ever that may happen I live in Arizona !!
I ordered these for my ride to work in the mountains, the protect well but are not even close to water proof. there are a lot cheaper the HD gloves but sometimes you get what you pay for.

I purchased these gloves to be able to ride in Georgia over the winter season.PROSGreat fitGauntlet not too longGood feel of control while riding motorcycle wearing my gloves.Worked pretty well down to a 40 degree start out so farCONS:None at this time.  We'll see how they handle 30 degree weather when that gets down here.Safe Riding all.
The leather is thin as a sheet of paper.  The quality of the leather is not very good.  However, for the price, I would consider them to be Fair.  Always remember, you get what you pay for.
the fit is perfect and as far as keeping your hands from that numb,burning feeling these gloves keep your hands nice and warm.i'm able to grip and use all controls without any problems.
summary: for the price they can't be beat

reviewText: I own four pairs of motorcycle gloves and the Raider Black X - Large  are my most recent and best purchase yet!  I was not completely satisfied with Naked Black Leather from Jaffrum (they are nice be not as neat as these), so I ordered the Raider's.  Wow, if you buy a pair you will recognize several features right away:  1) these are long and fit way up your sleeve to prevent air from getting into your jacket; 2) these gloves are heavy duty and the fill inside is second to none for keeping your hands warm; 3) you will want to order a second pair when you try these gloves!
summary: BEST PAIR OF GLOVES THAT I OWN FOR RIDING IN THE COLD WEATHER!

reviewText: I wear between L and XL sizes in gloves, ordered the XL and they fit "snug", not too tight, but a good snug fit like they should.  The right glove is a bit tighter, but loosened up after liberal application of saddle-soap to both gloves.  Gloves arrived in very stiff condition, but saddle-soap loosened them right up... they fit and feel great!Gauntlet slides over my jacket sleeves and makes a good seal.  I would love to see the gauntlet with a zipper to make it easier to get over my jacket, but they are what they are and do their job.Also, the description does not indicate "insulated", but they do have a fleece lining, not Thinsulate, but a generous volume of heavy fleece insulation to make them very usable down to 40 or 50-deg F.  I wore them today in 80-deg weather, and they were a bit "warm" (my hands started to sweat), but they will be perfect for cool evenings and cooler days (as Autumn approaches... which is what I really wanted them for!).UPDATE:After using these gloves for several weeks, they are not getting any better.  The leather is still too stiff, even after liberal applications of saddle-soap and Meguire's Leather Conditioner.  They hold my hands in a rigid position, and it's very easy to give too much throttle because of it.  Reaching the clutch and brake levers is an "effort" to say the least.  Furthermore, the gauntlet slides easily over my textile jacket sleeve, but is too tight for my leather jacket... I have to really work to cram the sleeve into the glove, and the feeling of tightness at my wrist is just TOO MUCH... very uncomfortable.  I feel like the Michelin Man when wearing them... unable to freely move my hands and wrists like I should be able to.  It's not a "dangerous" feeling, but it makes me uncomfortable.I've dropped to 3 stars because they are still good leather, fit my hands, and decent, mid-weight insulation... but I'll be looking for a different style/brand to wear in the cooler weather.  I'll hang on to these for my passengers to wear so their hands will be able to stay warm... won't give them much grip, but at least they'll have warmth and protection from the elements.
summary: Decent quality, and worth the price - Bulky and Clumsy feel

reviewText: I ordered these for my husband however they will not fit his hands, they are too small, and you don't make them any bigger than these.
summary: Raider Black X-Large Leather Motorcycle Riding Gloves

reviewText: Great gloves for the money. Fit perfect.
I use these gloves for the colder weather riding.  They are well worth the money and fit well. I may buy another pair.

I have worn these for several rides now. They are well constructed and as warm as I expected, for non-heated gloves. The gauntlet fits over my jacket sleeves, keeping wind out. And the hook-and-loop wrist straps do an excellent job keeping the gloves tight and in place.The gloves have good flexibility for clutch, brake and throttle control. Sizing for me XL was spot on.
summary: Best value in gloves I have found

reviewText: These gloves are stiff and tight and warm (ok for longer rides in 50-ish temperatures). I initially thought that I would not be able to operate a motorcycle with them.After riding a few hundred miles, I changed my opinion. They worked out ok, and for the money there is not much wrong with them. Get them larger if possible.
Constructed well, a little too long and you need to order two sizes larger than you would normally wear if you wear a large order a 2 X large.
summary: My Review of the Raider Black Leather Gloves

reviewText: These gloves are ultra-sexy and felt warm, and fit good.  I was all ready to fall in love with them.  The moment I pull on the wrist strap on one of them to tighten it so I could fasten the Velcro fastener, the whole band that is sewn to the leather ripped off.  A real heart-breaker, because these are some fine looking gloves.  I may even buy another pair and just be ultra-careful with the bands or re-enforce the sewing myself... dunno yet.Update: re-ordered and just left velcro strap alone (although I'll probably just go ahead and re-enforce it (sewing) myself in case it get's so cold I need to tighten it around the wrist).  Nice and warm and cozy fit; go well with my rainsuit that I got.  The straps are not tough, but the gloves are badazz for this price, cozy, comfy, cool as hayall, and fun.  They were a bit stiff at first so I rolled each one into a "ball" of sorts and put them between two heavy books for 12 hours instead of using any balms or anything; softened them right up.  Pleased.
The X chock is a quality product that does the job of keeping the wheels in place.  I would recommend this product.
This works GREAT!! Easy to use, great stablization!! Could tell the difference right away!! Highly reccomend!! Great for my camper!!

absolutely fantastic item - cannot believe I ever messed with blocks and or regular chocks - super easy to use - on any surface (pavement, dirt, sand, etc...), very solid and well constructed - should last a lifetime - if you own an RV trailer - you NEED a set of these chocks!! Highly recommended!

This chock is much easier to install and especially easier to remove than normal chocks; holds the tires still which makes the trailer more steady. It also has a place where you can lock it so it won't "walk" away while you are away from your campsite.

Safety, safety, safety...a must on those less than level sites.  Advise...place a reminder in your truck to remove chock.  It fits so seamless into your RV wheel wells it is easy to over look.  Trust me...axle won't turn with these in place! Just sayin!

We initially bought this for security however, the lock I have on it isn't really big enough to be serious for that however, what we have found is that it makes the trailer a LOT more stable to work in! It also eliminates the possibility of our chocks being stolen (don't need to use them once this is on).  Easy to use as well, even going between two different trailer wheel spacings.
The instructions preclude using this as a chock when hitching or unhitching so what is the point? What a waste of money.

I like this chock a lot.  The Amazon image shows it almost fully extended, but it can compress to fit easily between the two tires on your RV/trailer.  Simply use the enclosed rachet, and screw it open.  Presto - you're chocked!I use a socket and a cordless drill to extend my stabilizer jacks, and the same socket fits this chock.  Talk about convenience!The screw-head has holes which can accomodate a padlock.  BAL sells one for this chock, but I found that a normal padlock (skinny u-clasp, slightly longer than a 'normal' padlock) can work just fine.My wife accidentally tried moving our trailer with the chock still in place, and after a foot or so the chock was ejected from between the tires.  A small cotter-pin broke, and BAL sent me a new one for free.  What service!Consider buying the 2-pack, and use one on each side.  I've tested it, and two chocks DOES provide more stability inside the trailer than a single chock.  Although, if you don't care about the extra stability, ONE chock WILL keep your trailer from rolling away.Sure, the traditional wedge-shaped block of plastic will work just fine.  But I've seen those blow away if they weren't kicked in hard enough, and nothing would keep someone from stealing them.  This chock works better and it can be locked.I would definately buy this again.
This thing is a must have. So easy to use, I am thinking about a second one!And of course Amazon has the best deals around! Free shipping, whoa...what a deal!

I bought these to help stabilize my 38' 5th wheel, they are probably an over kill vs the plastic ones. These are very well made and extremely sturdy and keep the trailer form moving front and back but....... they are very pricey.
I've only used it one time so far.  Seems to work as designed.  To keep track of the wrench, I tied a piece of string around it, and attached the wrench to the chock to keep from loosing the wrench.
very light will work in applications with smaller vehicles
These work very well and the rope handle makes it a little easier to pick them up. Fits nicely with a dual axle setup between the 2 tires.

This single chock without the rope sells for half as much.  The chock without the rope also has a hole in the side for the rope, if you want to add your own.I like these chocks, because they re Made in USA.  It makes a difference.
summary: This is a "single" chock.............with a rope....

reviewText: They are plastic but will work.  I just hope they hold up over time and can hold back a 5000 lbs trailer on a small incline.
Order the ones w/o rope. They are the same chocks add your own rope and save money. The others have the hole for rope already drilled.

Placed my order from Amazon Prime free 2-day delivery, which was received.  However, I had to refuse shipment because they shipped the jack in it's factory retail packaging and no outer box, which caused the box to be destroyed while in transit, and the jack had apparently been thrown around by UPS until it was dropped straight on the plastic cover, cracking and breaking it in several pieces.  When I contacted Amazon, they were apologetic, but offered no other solution than a refund because they didn't expect any more for 1-2 months.  I ended up having to order it from another seller in MN.  I will leave a review on it upon receipt.  What is funny is that last week I ordered a $15 nylon belt, and it showed up in a box that could have housed a small refrigerator, and it had so many of the air-pac bubbles in the box, that it took a few minutes to actually locate the item that was in the box.  Literally like shipping a golf ball in a refrigerator box.  Absurd.  This item had NO protection whatsoever.EDIT 4/26/12:  I raised my review by two stars, and I will say Rec-Direct (whom I bought another one from after Amazon failed) came through like champs.  Fantastic service, and correspondence to my concern it would not arrive intact again.  A+ to them.Now, the big turd of this edited review.  The jack does not fit my TT tongue.  The top flange is 2 3/8" hole and the bottom flange has a 2 1/8" hole.  Don't ask me why my TT is different from everyone else's.  The post will go through the top hole, but will not seat into the bottom hole so that it can be mounted properly.  I am going to have to take my TT to a welder to have a new bottom mounting plate fabricated, and a 2 3/8" hole drilled in it and welded back to the tongue of the TT.  I have a R-Vision Trail-Lite 27QBSS TT.  Nothing out of the ordinary to any of the other TT that are out there, except my tongue is different.I am keeping the jack, and will post another update after I finally get my tongue ready so I can install it.EDIT 12/20/12:  I was able to get the jack installed, but not after using a plasma cutter to correct the hole size on the trailer tongue.  We had to cut the hole out larger because the jack pole was bigger than that the crank pole that came from the tongue.  The jack has worked flawlessly afterwards however.
summary: SHAME ON AMAZON - The jack was destroyed upon delivery

reviewText: The history of Airstream is one of legend. Long known for their iconic design and now classic Art Deco style, they have chosen to use Baker jacks on their units. I bought a previously owned 22' 2008 Safari Sport with the standard manual jack. At 4,500 Lbs, she is easy to lift with her current equipment, however, it gets fairly tiring if you are using weight distribution hitches (you should) and sway controls (you REALLY should!). Unfortunately, Amazon only stocks the VIP 3500 w/24" Stroke with a white head unit. Many have spoken about excellent customer service from Baker -- BELIEVE IT! I called them to ask where I could locate this item with a black head unit and learned that the majority of distributers only stock the other color. HOWEVER, they said one could be made for me on the next day's production and be shipped to my home in time for a planned trip in six days from my call to Baker. IMPRESSIVE! Since I live in Michigan (they are in Battle Creek, MI), I offered to come to their location to pick it up -- a two-hour trip each way -- that's how serious I was to NOT use the manual jack anymore! I was told, essentially, to save my fuel because the shipping costs to my Airstream's location was less than $28.00. They calculated it right then, without me asking! A REAL person answered the phone and handled the transaction; I was never on hold AND I didn't have someone that was CLUELESS as to what they were selling -- OMG!! Also, I was not sure if I needed a 3000 or 3500; the woman I spoke with stated either would work, however, the 3500 would lift faster since my Safari was about 4500 Lbs. if at maximum cargo. Drum Roll.... I still payed less than $300.00 -- complete. For any of you that may need advise on towing and safety, please visit: [...] (I met Andy Thomson of CanAm RV and he is indeed a Guru on the subject!).
Haven't used it a lot yet, but I'm really impressed.  Moves pretty quick and has a long reach.  Should have done this a whole lot sooner.

Just completed a 6,000 mile, 2+ month trailer trip. We have a 28foot Pilgrim Lite trailer…..about 5500 lbs gross weight. This is the first power jack we've had in 6 years of trailering.  It was a pleasure to use, since we have to go up/down/up/down with our weight distributing hitch.  This made it very tolerable.  Easy to install.  Arrived in rough shape, but Barker made it right ASAP.  Great product, great customer support!  You won't regret buying this one.

I've had two Barker jacks. One on each of the two travel trailers I've owned. The first never had any failures/problems what-so-ever. The second had an internal micro switch die. Barker immediately (got them in 4 days) sent me a free package of all the switches the jack uses. This is customer service Plus.The second time I contacted them was to request the price of a new "light lens" as mine had yellowed from sitting in the Sacramento sun for a few years. They just sent two lenses free of charge. Again, GREAT customer service.My highest recommendation goes to these folks for a great product and customer service!Update:  November 21, 2012 - Have had a Barker on a new Cougar 30 Travel trailer for over a year now and it's working flawlessly.  Still 5 stars for a great product.

I got this set for my outdoor rug with my RV. I actually haven't had a need to use them yet since the rug pretty much stays in place anyway. I can't see how you can go wrong though since this is basically just a long nail and a washer set - you can also put a kit together from Home Depot.
summary: Long nails with washers - not much to say

reviewText: Good product holds down my outdoor patio rug.  Be sure to have something on hand to pull them back up as they lay very flat and the disks are recessed to prevent the nail heads from being trip hazards. Through trail and error I've found it best to not drive the nails tightly flat against the disks, leaving just a small gap that allows me to grip the heads with pliers when I'm ready to pull them back out. I'm very happy with this product.
Bought these to use at our camper for in the fake grass mat, they were being put into kind of soft dirt, they still bent. Used them and they are in the ground so I won't be able to reuse them.

These are made for outdoor carpeting on grass or soil and work great.  They will work loose in loose soil or sand but anything will.  They look nice, can't trip on them, install and remove easily, are treated to not rust, and work well for me.  5 Stars, great service, fast and green shipping. Highly recommend!

These will do just the trick for keeping the out door mat from blowing or just heaving up from traffic.  Nice safety item.  The item was received before promised and cheaper then in the stores.  Thanks
While they are what they claim to be, you can go to your nearest hardware store and buy mch longer nails and a few washers for a lot less money.
This product works as advertised.  I am fully pleased with the purchase.  I recommend it to anyone seeking the same type item.
summary: The stakes keep the ropes tied down.

reviewText: Needed for our Camco Outdoor mats for when several are put together and there aren't any other gourmets on the one.
Yes, you could do almost the same thing with some spikes and fender washers but that would cost about the same.  I did have to scrounge out an old tent stake bag to keep them in.
These work great.  Not so great if you're on asphalt or concrete, but then I didn't get them for that.  Keep the entry piece of indoor/outdoor carpet in place.
Hold my rug down and pulls up easy . the washers on it give it a good snug fit ...
Kept our camp rug in place for 10 days with a ton of traffic and 20-30 mph wind. It sure beats the rocks and things we have used over the years!

I use these for putting down my outdoor rug when camping. I also use these for tie-downs for the sun screen on my awning with bungie cords and my football tent. The "washer" on the top makes a big difference - easy to pull the stake out and it holds a lot better. These are easy to hammer into the ground. The only down point is that after a few uses the tip gets blunt BUT they are cheap enough to replace as needed.

seems to work fine - we needed only 4 of the 6 to secure the 9x12 rug.  i am concerned about them rusting - but time will tell. otherwise they are nice and flat on the ground and its nice not to trip over tent pegs or worry the dogs will roll over / step on a sharp tent peg.

Yeah, they look like, and are, just a half-dozen large nails with recessed-head washers.  But sunk into either dirt or sand, they really do hold an outdoor rug down tight - against even a strong wind.  I was surprised (and even a bit worried) when I tried to pull these things out, because they were far more resistant to removal than I anticipated.  They'd get another star in my rating if they came with a storage bag.
summary: Not Much to Look At, But They Do the Job

reviewText: I use these for eveything I need locked to the ground at an RV park. Outdoor rugs, my HD sat dish tripod, the long mesh screen that attaches to my awning etc. The only problem I have w/them, is the nails are a little to thin for some hard ground, but other wise the work good.
i suppose the only possible down side is loosing them?!  what can i say--they work great at the campsite. word
summary: they do what you need them to

reviewText: These are a must-have for those of us using large mats in front of an RV.  Keeps the edges from curling up and creating a trip hazard and keeps everything in place during the windy times.
They work ok unless you are camping where the ground is hard. The nails bend easily if put in hard dirt.  Otherwise, they do the job ok.

Work as advertised.  we needed them at almost every campsite to hold our patio rug down.  These go in the ground relatively easy where the ground is not solid rocks.I gave it four stars only because two of the stakes bent on our last stop.  The ground was a bit hard due to lack of rain, but I did not think we forced them enough to bend as they did.All in all a good product that we need and at a great price.  I will use them again when I need more.
Bend too easy. Went to Walmart and bought heavy duty tent stakes.
I use this socket in a cordless drill in order to operate some scissor jacks that I have. It's a lot better than using a handheld ratchet to jack something up with.
This works great and doesn't risk loosing the shaft or the socket in my tool bag. I recommend it for any bumper pull trailer.
summary: A must have for trailers with crank down stabilizer jacks

reviewText: great idea for the guy who has everything, a drill bit ti raise and lower the jacks on the trailer

I really didn't expect to like this gadget as much as I do.  It sure makes lowering and raising the stabilizers a breeze.  I bought it for my wife, but I'll be using it too.  It just makes the job much quicker.

I was wanting something to use with my portable drill to crank the stabilizing jacks on our travel trailer. Being somewhat of a cheapskate, I first was going to try to use some of my existing tools to be able to use a regular socket. I saw this listed and decided to buy it because it was a one-piece solution to what I wanted to do. I think it was well worth the money--it is a specialized tool that does what it is supposed to do very handily.

This is a great product, dealing with the stab jacks is no longer a sweaty affair.  But it takes a lot of juice out of the cordless drill to it.  This is because my drill batteries are old and no longer hold their charge well.  But I absolutely recommend getting this unit and packing along your cordless drill to make setting up camp that much easier.  My FIL was jealous of this thing when we camped this summer!
I bought two of these so I would know where one was for our camper. They work great. I have no problem using them.
I needed this for the stabilizer on my camper. This works great and makes the process much easier. Made of heavy material and should last forever. Good price also.
My back is 65% happier now. Slap onto cordless drill, pull trigger four times, go sit some place out of the sun and contemplate the meaning of life.

I found this item around the time I bought my trailer, but didn't get around to actually buying this until almost a year later.  I have no idea why I waited so long.  Instead of spending a minuted or two on each jack, it is now 15 seconds.  Very nice if the weather isn't nice.  Also nice to not be crouching uncomfortably while using the manual tools.
summary: Don't wait, buy this thing now!!!

reviewText: I have been RV'ing for five years or so, all of which I have hand cranked my jacks. This makes setup so much faster. I can literally back in, unhook, and have the stabilizers down in under 5 minutes now. This is a back saver. I highly recommend this, but be sure you use it with a high quality and high speed drill.
summary: Wow why did I just buy this?!?!?!

reviewText: I use this all the time. I attach it to my cordless drill, but mine has a clutch feature so that if you set it right, it won't overtighten the stabilizer jacks. Quick up, quick down.
Being able to use my high speed cordless drill to lower and raise my camper jacks is a back saver and a huge time saver. I highly recommend this socket.
Cheap gizmo to make RV'ing much easier.  Use this and a drill (cordless or plug-in) and the scissor jack stabilizers go right up and down.  Lot less work at the camp site!
i have a big time bad back and this little socket saves me everytime i bought a cheap drill and attached this to it and leave it in the trailer awsome i wish i got one sooner.
Makes putting the stablizer jacks up and down easy, since you can attach socket to a drill. Only thing is to snug the jacks with the hand crank, so you dont damage them.
This tool, combined with a cordless drill, beats the heck out of the crank that came with the stabilizer jacks.
I had the adapter/socket setup and the socket was always falling off the adapter, so I finally ordered this and did it right..  Much much better.
Use this with your cordless and your jacks will go up and down with ease. Such a simple tool but so worth the price.
Bought this for my father in law for his travel trailer.  He says so far it has worked very well.

We always bring a small lithium battery powered drill and use this socket to raise and lower our RV stabilizer jacks.  It has saved my back and makes the job quick and painless.  Excellent little product - another must-have for RVers.
summary: Way better than hand-cranking your leveling jacks

reviewText: I have not used this yet since I have not bought the new scissor lifts for my travel trailer yet ... but it seems solid and seems like it will work perfect! (I will come back after first use to either give a 5 star or a lesser score ... 4 for know to keep it fair since I have yet to use it)
Awsome gadget to speed the set up of your camper.  Lazy mans dream.  If I could only get the wife to use the drill!
I decided I didn't need mine because my leveler came with a great ratchit. It's more of a pain to carry a drill than to use the ratchit!
summary: Good and sturdy if you need it

reviewText: Wow, put this socket on a good battery hand drill and use it to lower or raise your scissor jacks quickly. It works great and highly recommend this socket.
This is a must have if you own an RV with manual stab jacks. This makes it fast and easy.  Seems very durable and will last forever.
summary: If you own a travel trailer with manual stab jacks then this is a must have

reviewText: Oh, where would I be without you, little socket?  My jacks take an AGE to crank with the manual handle, and this makes it SO easy.  Truly a MUST in the toolkit.

I've been camping for more than 10 years and just purchased this a month or so ago... Had the pleasure of using this about four or five times now, and can't beleive I didn't buy this sooner.. With my Ryobi cordless it takes abot 15 sec, a side on my rear stabilizers... Amazing.... I know you can use the manual crank and it works fine... You can also dig your own septic sys. but you'd gladly pay a backhoe 3K to do it for you... Buy this and buy a cordless drill if you don't already have one... you'll be so glad you did.
summary: the best 6 bucks you'll ever spend!!!

reviewText: Use this and a cheap drill to set my trailer stabilizers.  Thanks to this cool little gadget, I can have all four set in less than three minutes.  Considering that I want to spend less time setting up the trailer and more time enjoying it, this tool is a great addition to my trailer tool box.
summary: Makes Short Work of Setting Stabilizers

reviewText: This product is designed for one use, and does it well.  The convenience of a shank and socket combination make it very useful.
I use this with a 12 volt ion drill/driver to extend and retract the leveling jacks on my travel trailer. Save a lot of time and hassle.

This makes putting your RV jacks up/down so much easier. Hand screwing is so much more work than doing it with a power implement!Simple product but works ok, however kinda looks like cheap metal so I  am concerned if it will rust over time (time will tell as it is most probably NOt made in the good 'ole USA). Need a good battery drill (preferably ar least 18 V0 to get the jacks down or up, depending onhow high off the ground that your trailer is).

No more do I have to bend down and crank the trailer up...  I connect it to an electric drill, (decent sized one), and the drill will lift the entire trailer...  I have no idea why anyone would not want one of these...  Takes about 30 seconds to extend teh jacks to teh ground.  Best 5 bucks I have spent.

I'll be honest and admit I didn't research this all that much.  I just made the assumption that the stem was a 1/4" hex insert bit.  WRONG!  This is more similar to the drive design of a drill bit.  Makes sense since it's intended to be chucked in a drill.  However what if your jacks are a little recessed or your just feeling your age and you want more reach?  Guess your just outta luck...As for me, I'll be shopping for a 1/4" insert to socket adaptor and a 3/4" socket instead.
If you have to hand crank your sizzor jacks you need one of these. It is easy to work with and makes leveling a trailer quick and easy.

If one is RV-ing and has stabilizer jacks that use the long handle, get this and a drill (a high torque cordless is best) and save yourself a headache, unless you are doing it for an exercise regimen.  You and your back will be glad you did.

If you have the type of scissor jacks that use a hex-type wrench to raise/lower and you have a battery operated drill/screwdriver, then you have to get one of these. I was using a socket out of my socket set but then that socket was always missing from the set when I wanted to use it. This is cheaper than buying another individual socket and comes with the shank to fit your drill so you don't need to have one of those to attach your socket. reviewText: Since becoming active in the trailer transport of my cars several years ago, I had used a wood ramp to raise the wheel needing to be changed.
