reviewText: BACKGROUND:I purchased the basic version of this tire pressure gauge (Accutire MS-4021B Standard Digital Tire Gauge) several years ago and have been using it up until about a month ago (at which time it failed to give me any pressure readings). The problem with the 4021B is that the part of the pressure gauge that mates with the tire (shrader) valve is made of plastic and fails after repeated uses. I had considered purchasing another 4021B gauge as it did perform for several years and is certainly cheaper but ultimately decided to pay for the improved version (4355GB) and see if it was worth the difference.MY EXPERIENCE:There is an immediately apparent build quality difference between these gauges. The 4355GB has more heft, feels more solid and, more importantly, has a metal "coupler". That is, the part of the gauge that mates with the tire valve has a metal housing with brass internals instead of plastic. This alone is enough to justify the price difference and, in my opinion, makes the 4355GB the better purchase. There is one other minor but significant difference between these gauges. That is, the 4355GB has a "pin" on the back of the "coupler" that allows you to release air pressure from the tire if it is overfilled. This was one extremely annoying aspect of the 4021B - anytime I overfilled a tire I was looking for a rock or a screw driver or something to release the air as the gauge had no way to do this. There are some other bells and whistles that don't matter that much but are nice to have (I guess); the coupler rotates independently of the display so you can always have the display facing you, you can program your tire setpoints into the gauge in case you can't be bother to check your door label, it comes in a nice case.The only downside that comes to mind is that it is still ony accurate to 0.5 psi increments (like the 4021B). This isn't an issue for me but if you are really fussy about dialing your tire pressures in then you should probably look at getting something different.FINAL THOUGHTS:Having used both the 4355GB and the 4021B pressure gauges from Accutire. I would recommend purchasing the 4355GB if you intend to use it for many years as the build quality and features provided are a significant improvement over the 4021B.
summary: A Definite Improvement on the Basic Version (4021B)

The feature "records factory recommended pressure of both front and rear tire" is superfluous but I suppose some people who either don't remember or cannot find the factory settings might benefit.

Since Black Friday of 3 years ago, I've been trying to find the old red Craftsman air gauge that looks exactly like this.  The "new" model is a stick model, this one has a pivoting head.  Using it on a motorcycle where I have saddle bags in the way I need to get at the stem from all kinds of crazy angles.  As a memory jogger I can input the pressure for front and rear (on the bike it varies front and rear).The old Sears model just disappeared only to be replaced later in January with a "new" model -- I bought one, but wanted one for all of the vehicles I own...so finally I will get my wish!  This is IDENTICAL to that one, other than the color and the embossing.
summary: Just like the CRAFTSMAN gauge I've been wanting

reviewText: Digital gauges are the most accurate. I've never used the programable features. When you have more than 3 cars what's the point? I like the display and the rotating head.

This is a really nice quality unit and it works very well and is extremely accurate.  Also nice shape and feel and great nozzle attachement built to last.  I gave it 4 stars only because I'd have liked it to store a few cars worth of tire pressures not only one car.  It wouldn't be hard to add that into it's memory.  Many of today's cars have two different pressures front and rear - which it does remember for a single car, but many of us have two+ cars and that would make it easier to use.  So additional memory would be sweet.  That would make it perfect.
I bought two of these for each of our cars.  It works as described, is simple, legible, and easy to use.

I bought the digital tire pressure gauge for a truck that takes 80 PSI for its tires. I found on a recent trip that the tire pressure monitors in the tires were providing a very different reading from the Accutire pressure gauge - a difference of 8 PSI. I found a Love's truck stop where they sold a high quality tire pressure gauge and it confirmed that the tire monitors were accurate and that the Accutire pressure gauge was way off with its readings.Had I continued to rely on the Accutire pressure gauge I would have risked a blowout and certainly would have had uneven tire wear and in either case the end result would have been expensive. I recommend that before trusting an Accutire pressure gauge that you compare it to another quality gauge (not the ones at the gas stations) and see if they agree. The truck stop tire gauge is now in the truck and the Accutire pressure gauge is at the local dump.
Works good, I like it..

Upon opening the box and viewing it's contents I was very pleased with the quality of this product. The quality of materials used to make the PZ-1900 exceeded my expectations. After parking my car exactly where I wanted it I mounted the sender and receiver units on the wall in front of the car and connected all the necessary cables and plugged it into the wall. All that was needed after that was to push the on/off button to turn the unit on and watch it calibrate itself. A few seconds later the calibration was finished so I backed the car out of the garage then drove it into the garage to test the Park Zone unit for the first time. The Park Zone light was green at first but as I slowly got closer to the wall the light changed to yellow so I slowed down a little bit. A moment later the light turned red and I parked the car. The car was sitting exactly the same distance from the wall as it was when it was calibrated. Excellent quality product!
Gotta have for the wife coming into the garage. Sure has saved the walls, and I have become dependent on it also. Works really great.

I purchased this item 3 years ago. This item still works with no problems and I have not had any issues. I use batteries to operate it and my batteries last at least a few months before I need to recharge them.
This works really well but one thing that i would change is the length of the power cord.  My garage doesnt have a lot of outlets and the power cord that comes with the unit is too short.
Wife parks in the same spot every time now.  She loves it!  And it couldn't be easier to set up!

this will keep you from having to patch up walls in the garage because you backed up too far and bumped something, and it will keep you from messing up your car hood by having the door close on it. just set it once and it's very consistent (unless the power goes out and you don't have a battery in there) I have a small ups in the garage to keep all the timers and stuff going when power goes out so that keeps it from resetting without using batteries

I've had several tire pressure gauges over the years, the last two of which being digital.  The Michelin Gauge is a good, reasonably well built model that should last for years.Pros:-Well built-Long battery life-Easy to read-Relatively easy to mount on tireCons:-non-AA/AAA battery-Easy to lose too much air when fumbling around for a tire pressure indication

I like the build quality and the look of the gauge.  The pouch is a nice addition.  My car has 245/40/18 tires, and I did not have any problems with how the gauge attaches to the valve (see pic).  I like that the goal tire pressure can be programmed into the gauge while allowing separate settings for front and rear tires.  I also like the little flashlight feature.  It is bright enough for finding the valve in the dark.  My only concern is that batteries might be dead on the day when you really need to use it.  This is why I am not ready to throw away my low-tech stick pressure gauge.Overall, I think this gauge works and would make a nice present.

.A good tire gauge is easy to line up at the correct angle to the valve stem. You can line it up visually before you press it on. You lose very little air while checking the pressure. If the pressure was already correct, you do not have to add back 1-2 PSI that you lost with the gauge.The nose of a good tire gauge is offset at about 45 degrees, so you can use it without difficulty on bicycle tires, or in other special situations.This Michelin MN-4357B is none of the above. The offset is 10 degrees and hard to visualize on this curvy objet d'art. The seal is quite sensitive to mis-alignment. Most people will have a hard time with this. You'll get a tight seal through trial and error while air leaks out of the tire for a few seconds. It's quite a hassle with bike tires...spokes interfere with your grip of the gauge (see pics).The beautiful form-fitting zipper case should be immediately thrown away. Why? Because it sometimes holds the flashlight button down, draining the batteries while it's being stored.You can enter your car's target tire pressure (front and back), and it displays below the pressure reading. Useful if you only have one car. Otherwise, ill conceived.One thing this gauge would be really good for: A design school case study. Beauty and clever features count for nothing when real-world basics are ignored.- - - Alternatives - - --Accutire MS-4021B Digital Tire Gauge-Viair 90052 Digital Tire Pressure Gauge~~~ Comments & questions welcome ~~~
summary: Nice Frills, They Neglected the Basics

reviewText: Having only used standard, dial-type, mechanical tire pressure gauges for my cars, motorcycles, and bicycles over the years, I was curious to try out this Michelin Digital Tire Pressure Gauge.Likes:>Includes two CR2032 batteries and carrying case.>Built in LED light next to the Schrader (automotive type) nozzle.>Programmable front and rear tire pressures.  Could be useful for relatives/friends borrowing one's vehicle.Dislikes:>If the battery is low or drained, tire pressure can't be measured.>Cumbersome, barely angled nozzle is difficult to line up perfectly with the tire valve stem.  Even more problematic with valves that are close to the wheels/spokes.  That means lots of air leakage prior to getting a reading.>Is it really necessary to have the programmable tire pressure feature for our personal vehicles, motorcycles, and bicycles?  How hard is it to memorize a few PSIs?  What if we use the digital gauge on more than one vehicle?>Doesn't have a relief valve to lower tire PSI when pressure is slightly high.>When placed in a moving vehicle's glove/storage compartment, the hard nylon carrying case may inadvertently press the power button on the side of the gauge and drain the battery.Overall:Tire gauges are critical for maintaining proper pressures, safety, and optimizing MPG for vehicles.  Even more so for lower volume, high pressure tires on motorcycles and bicycles.  I will continue to use time tested and reliable mechanical tire gauges such asAccugage Dial Tire Gauge With Hose RRA60Xrather than rely on digital tire pressure gauges.
summary: Gimmicky digital tire pressure gauge not simple to use.

reviewText: I obtained this product from Vine.  As other reviewers have pointed out, the main functionality on this Michelin product leaves a lot to be desired.  It is difficult to seat onto the tire valve stem, lacking in this key point of ease of use.  The case is also a pain to open since it needs to be unzipped nearly all the way around in order to remove the tire gauge for use.  Otherwise, it is decent quality overall make and digital readout.For another vehicle in our household, we have the Accutire MS-4355GB Programmable Tire Gauge, which is a better choice (although more expensive).  The Accutire is very easy to seat onto the valve stem, has given consistent performance and held up for the last 9 months.
summary: Not the best option for a digital tire gauge

reviewText: This is a well made pressure checker with an easy to read display.  The example I received is spot on in terms of accuracy, as well.  I compared its readings to a very precise professional dial gauge.The gauge is easy to hold and is coated in a soft non-slip finish which is pleasing to the touch.  The display, as mentioned, is large and easy to read.  While the gauge is programmable for the desired pressure, I find myself just using it as a direct reading gauge.  It comes with a nice zippered soft case which will help keep it clean when not in use.My only criticism, and the reason for only four stars, is that the pressure probe is not angled.  In order to use this gauge, you must have the full length of the gauge in which to maneuver.  It will work fine for most car tires, but some motorcycle tires don't have angled valve stems (pointed outboard) and therefore it will be difficult, or impossible, to maneuver this gauge for a tight fit to the valve stem and achieve a solid reading.Notwithstanding the criticism above, I like this gauge very much and use it often, despite that one limitation.

This is a very nice gauge. First off it is easy to read. Next you can set the PSI for both the front and the back most cars today have a differant psi for the front and the back so u just set it and when you check it you just hit the set button and it tells you where you need to be and it is very accurate I checked it with our gauges at work and it was right on the money!! The best part is u can change the batteries which is very handy as with most other gauges you just through them away!! This is a cool tire gauge.

the Michelin MN-4357B is very easy to read, and quite accurate, but is very difficult to seed to the stem and requires a lot of pressure to keep the thing tight, so you can get a good reading.It is not at all useful if you don't have a straight shot to your valve stem.  Trucks or something with angled valve stems or are in tight quarters, this would not be useful at all.The backlight feature and the PSI vs. millibar readout is useful.  The case is really nice.But, if you have quick and easy access, and don't mind the seeding issues, it's very accurate.

This tire gauge worked for me about as good as most others I have tried.  Some air leaks out when I first push it onto the valve stem but I quickly learned the correct angle.  This can be an annoyance so I deducted a star for that, the gauge should have a steeper angle to fit valve stems better.  Overall, the gauge was accurate, has a clear display and is easily stored in a glove compartment. The small light is a nice touch but I don't usually check my tire pressure at night. The quality seems to be good, it has a one year warranty.

This looks really great, but looks can be deceiving.The part that actually connects to the tire air valve is flat--which made it unpredictable for me as to whether I would get it right the first time. And, of course, if it isn't just right, it  lets air out of the tire. Half the time, I would hit it just right and it would work great. However, I don't want to spend a lot of time messing with my tires, so having to mess with just getting the connection to the pressure gauge is annoying at best.Actually, someone who uses it a lot might like it a lot more, since they could figure out how to dependably use it. (I use a pressure gauge once a month to check my tires.)This gauge has a really nice shape, good surface feel, and very clear screen. The light would be useful in some dim lighting situations. The case is handy, but not really that impressive or useful. I checked it against a couple of other gauges (not as cool looking, but dependable). All three agreed with each other, so apparently accuracy is not a problem.The programming lets you input the pressure you want for the front and back tires, so you don't have to keep opening the driver's door to check. However, since it only does it for one car, it isn't a lot of help if you have more than one car and they have different air pressure requirements.BTW, whether you use this or another gauge, it is well worth the cost. Your tires last longer and are safer to use when they are inflated properly.
summary: Not as good as what I have

reviewText: This gauge is about as simple to use as a manual gauge: Press set, and when the display appears, press the gauge against the tire valve. The display will hold the setting until you press set again. Simple. I tested it against my expensive mechanical gauge, and they agreed to within a pound. Simple. It uses lithium button cells, rather than AAA cells, which means the batteries will last for a long time. It comes in a nice storage case that should protect it from getting banged around in the glove compartment.There's an interesting, though somewhat complicated, memory function that allows you to store two reference pressures, one for your front wheels and one for the rear. I played around with it for a bit, but it's really unnecessary as (1) my main car has the same tire pressure at all four wheels and (2) you can find the tire pressure on a sticker inside the door jamb on just about every car made. Too dark to see the sticker? The gauge has a built in flashlight, too.  With a price less than a lot of mechanical gauges, I think this gauge is a very good value.
This item works excellent.  The pull tab for the battery broke when pulled leaving the insulator on the battery.  Had to open to remove it.  Other than that the item preforms great!
summary: Accurate compared to a commercial type gauge

reviewText: I think C. MacPhail already said it all. I'll try not to be too redundant.This gauge has a nice large read-out, a back-lit screen, and a light built in to help align things in the dark, all of which are great. A downgrade comes in because of simple problems, like the light switch activating inside the case and subsequently discharging the batteries, rendering the gauge useless when you need it. If you plan to have one in each vehicle, then the single car memory isn't an issue, but I prefer to leave the gauge in the garage for all to share so a single memory function is of little value to me. I gave it 3 stars simply because if one is willing to be extra careful with the light switch when storing, is happy with only one memory function, and is willing to take the time to learn how to correctly align the gauge and put up with the sensitive seal, then it is at least nice to have such an easy-to-read display. There are better designs out there, though, and C. MacPhail's review provided a couple. My favorite Topeak D2 SmartGauge is a bit pricey but it works very well for Presta valves (many bikes) as well as the more common Schrader valve found on cars and other bikes. It's accurate up to 250 psi, has a swivel head, and it's very small (about half the size of this gauge.
summary: Works well but screen is not scratch resistant enough

reviewText: I have these and will be buying more. I have 30 of UB 12350 35 ah batteries that are almost 8 years old now. They run 2-1500 watt tru-sine inverters and are filled by 21 harbor freight 15 w panels, also 8 years old and 8- 90 watt kyocera. With a﻿ 6+ year old HY energy HY400 12 volt wind turbine, known now as a Windmax HY400 5 blade. The Universal Battery brand is tough and easy to find. The Amorphous panels from H F are not the best but charge a hour before and hour after the Mono panels do and they do charge ( 1.09 amps) in a full moon a few times for a brief moment,  In full sun they still work well, 19 amps when they were new, 14.8 amps now after 8 years. New style HF (topray) panel seem better than the old ones I have.UPDATE: All the HARBOR freight panels are now on a shed/RV parking building 1000 feet from my home, making power still and they have been replaced with 22 of the UL SOLAR branded 85 watt panels and new charge controllers. We replaced the batteries finally with East Penn Manufacturing Deep Cycle 6 volts, and bought 8 more of these for our shed on the other end of our property plus added 3 more cheapy harbor freight 15 watt panels and a cheap 30 amp controller and all is good still. The Kyocera panels are still up and kicking on the back of my shop going into the new system I designed. [See pictures of the panels and controller system I built]Wanna save ? Use soft copper plumbing - refrigeration tubing, type L to link your batteries. I have 3/8 OD inserted into 1/2 ID ( 5/8" OD) typle L soft copper pipe. Cut to length, bent to shape, hammered flat 2" of the ends, bent to dual 90 Degrees ( like little handles )  and drilled 5/16 holes used stainless bolts and brass washers to bolt up all the batteries. Slip 1 1/8" heater hose (black and red hose) over it to insulate "before" flattening ends cut hose 4 inches less than length you made in the copper or split it and slip over the tubes. This set up handles a 1500 amp hit easy, clean and saved me $400 bucks on cables for 30 batteries. Also made my 9'3" run to big 5000 watt HF inverter with it adding a 1/4" soft copper tube in the 3/8ths OD. I use it for 4 to 6 hrs a week of welding and cutting.Suggestion? Shop Amazon suppliers for these. They will warranty them better than a local dealer, lesson learned on that one in my case.****Helpful LEARNED facts: Never allow the voltage to drop to 10.7 volts, ever. That level is 80% D.O.D. (Depth of Discharge). When it drops to 11.4 you are at a safe but taxing 55% of D.O.D. and to make yours last as I have never let voltage get below 11.6 and you too may get 8 plus years out of your battery. I also hit mine with a 40 amp plug in battery charger 2 times a year till they get warm to stir them. I've owned Trojans, suretttes and Walmart (johnson controls) and NONE have the balls that 30 of these have (1050 hair frying amps) for my solar/wind home. Exide 6 volt- real good, Odyssey Deep cycle - High $ but really good. The UB 35 amp - So far, still kickin a$$. Your choice, I even have 6 of these grouped in 2 packs of 3 that for 4+ years have started my 1997 Ford diesel truck, cheaper than the batteries they told me I needed by $60.I am shopping now for 30 more because I doubt they will make it through the winter in Idaho. But, I thought that last year too!
summary: Out lived every other so far

reviewText: A while back I hooked a UPS to my sump pump to provide some protection in case of power outage.  The UPS uses two 12V sealed lead acid batteries in series, so I purchased two of these to replace the batteries that came with the UPS to give it extra capacity.  They worked like a charm.FYI - while the batteries work great, I'm not recommending anyone else put them to the same use.  To power motors, a UPS should produce a continuous sine wave output, rather than a square wave (or PWM approximation of one), which requires a specific type of UPS.  While the wiring involved isn't tricky, care should still be taken, and you need sufficiently thick wire (if powering an AC device through an inverter, the amperage at 12V or 24V is going to be much higher than the amperage drawn by the device at 120V).
summary: Two of them power my sump pump

reviewText: I had aftermarket tires (33), and this helped me adjust my speedo. As well as try different tunes. The JK 3.8 is a dog, so I can't REALLY a difference, but anything helps. I was also able to lower the temperauture that my E fan comes on, and disable my TPMS for when I air down to go offroad. It's a good buy. Especially if you can get a deal of $250 or less.

i bought this because i currently dont have the funds to do a regear on my JK wrangler.  im running 35'' tires and when i installed them the power at the wheels went to crap.ive had big issues with the jeep not being able to hold 65 mph with a headwind, nevermind with the a/c on and going up a freeway overpass.  the jeep wont stay in overdrive and constantly shifted to third and even second gear now and again.when i got the flashpaq i had a full tank of 93 octane and was ready to run the 93 performance tune.  the flashpaq actually walks you through the entire process, not making you guess "well should i have the key in now?  should i have it in the on position?  when do i turn it off?"  it tells you everything which i really like.  takes the guess work out.  the entire flash process took maybe five minutes, which isnt bad.  the results?VERY notable power gain.  i think the advertised power gain for the 93 tune is something like 18 hp / 24 lbs torque which isnt anything to thumb your nose at for a vehicle that feels likes that how much it puts out without a tune to begin with.  mind you this will not make you feel like you just installed a supercharger or did a hemi swap, its a little boost of power to help you get some power lost from bigger tires.i havnt tinkered around with much else on the unit other than putting in my proper tire size.  i have an aev procal and had already had the ecu calibrated for the proper tire size.  if you have oversized tires and have not adjusted for it its a necessity.  lastly, if you already have an aev procal like i do and want to continue to use it, before you run the flashpaq flash take your ecu back to factory settings with the procal, run the flash with the flashpaq, then you can use the aev procal to make whatever adjustments you want.i give this unit 5 stars.  excellent product and excellent tune.
Greatly improved my throttle response. Have not used the other functions yet, but am happy with my purchase using the performance tune alone.
Calibrated speedo, shift points are now excellent. Gas milage not really affected which is my only complaint. Would buy again.

I was looking at this and the FlashCal, this has tuning features along with the Tire size adjustment but the FlashCal has some options this does not.  If you do not need the tuning, save the money and get the FlashCal.

I purchased a different brand, but it appears to be identical.The valve tool is smaller than I expected, only 1" tall, by 1" wide. It consists of 4 tools: 1) valve removal/installation tool, 2) a die for repairing the outside threads, and 3) a tapering tap and a 4) non-tapering tap for cleaning or cutting the inside threads.The die and taps are of fairly good quality, probably not suitable for cutting new threads in hardened steel, but adequate for repairing threads in a brass valve.Because the thread pitch (18/inch) is rather fine, great care should be taken not to cross-thread the die or taps, which is difficult because the tool is so small. I suggest using an adjustable pin-vise to hold the tool when cutting threads--the length of the handle makes it easier to be sure that the tool is perfectly aligned (and remains aligned) as you cut. It may be hard to find a pin-vise large enough, but they do exist. I made up my own pin-vise with a Dremel adjustable chuck and a hex extension which I just happened to have lying around.If the threads are badly damaged (or in my case, never properly cut in the first place), you should be cautious in recutting them, cut at most a half-turn at a time, then back off 1 turn, repeat, repeat, repeat as necessary. Oil the tool and the valve before cutting (ideally using 3-in-1 oil). After cutting several full turns, it is a good idea to remove the tool completely and clean off any metal shavings, add more oil, repeat as necessary. If cutting the inside threads, you may wish to swab out the interior with an oil-soaked Q-tip--you don't want metal shavings to jam up your new valve.If you are cutting the inside threads, don't over-cut the threads it with the untapered tap--you need a tight fit, and you don't want the valve to be too deep when you re-install it. The tapered tap would probably be useful for expanding a crushed valve, but it is too steep for cutting threads, too easy to cross-thread.Even though the tool is small, it can get in its own way in tight spaces. Fortunately it is easy to disassemble it with a hammer. Soak it in penetrating oil (or WD-40) for several hours in advance. Place the tapered tap in a hole (ideally in hard wood or plastic) at least 1" deep. Then tap on the other end, with a hammer, protecting the untapered tap with perhaps a penny.

reviewText: Even though the Dowco website recommends a Large for my bike, I found it too tight to go over a tall windshield and BMW 49L tail case. Others on the BMW RT forums agree that the Large is too small.So I returned the Large and got the XL. It fit perfect. It's a thick beefy material that is protected against UV light, so it seems like it will last forever. And with Dowco's customer service with regards to their products, I feel confident that it will have a long life.On my bike, it covers everything, but the lower ⅓ of the wheel. Perfect.The only issue, and it's just the consequence of having a big beefy cover, is that it takes up a boatload of space when put into it's carrying bag. On a long tour, I'm not sure I'd bring this with me. But when I have parked in my carport, it does what it's supposed to.I heartily endorse this cover.Follow up after a couple of months of use:1. I've used this cover in bright sunshine much of the time, and it seems to take a pounding from the sun. According to Dowco the cover is UV stabilized, unlike other motorcycle covers at this price point.2. My neighbor had a broken sprinkler and soaked my bike. The cover didn't let a drop in. Not a single drop. And the water seemed to bead up on the cover and just roll off.3. I put it on in about 30 seconds. Takes a bit longer to remove, fold, and stuff in carry bag, but it's simple.4. Heat resistant panels work. I usually let the bike cool down, but I need to get it covered and nothing happened to the heat resistant panels.5. This cover is a beast. The material is so thick that I don't think a knife could cut through it (not going to try however).The WeatherAll Plus is definitely high quality and high functioning protection for your bike. I can't find any faults with it, other than not being able to fold up into a small size, so I wish I could give this item a 5-star. I've had a bunch of different covers for my bike and this is the best.And for those of you who still look for American Made products, this one is. Made right in Wisconsin, probably near Harley Davidson itself!
summary: Great, high quality cover for a decent price

reviewText: I have been using these filters since 1987.  I use them both in a slid in  Bigfoot camper and 30' 5th wheel.  They work well and should be used with reliable sources.  They are not intended to take pathogens out of the water.  They are to take particulates and are a charcoal (for taste) type filter.There are a few things to keep in mind. Make sure to look at the water source that you are hooking up to, if you are not familiar with that source.  If it is really dirty, it can clog your filter - don't use it.  If it looks clear you should be ok. Make sure you flush your filter out each time you use it before you hook it up to your camper, This is most critical with the first use.  You will get a good amount of the charcoal dust, make sure it clears up then attach to your camper.  Again remember that even clear looking water can have pathogens in it and this filter will not take them out.  This filter is to remove particulates and improve the taste.Replace this type of filter every 6 month with heavy use and at a minimum once a year.  Do not let the filter freeze (with water or moisture in it), if it does replace it.  If you do not you could end up with water that is not being filtered.  Meaning that if you hare hooked up to a source with rust, you will be filling your tank and camper with rusty colored water...  This seems to be the case when people have told me that the filters do not work.  They will of you take care of them.  If you do not change them out, let them get clogged, frozen or do not purge them out, you will have less than ideal results.
summary: Good filter, just make sure you use them correctly

It is easy to adjust and does not slip when you place your weight on the center of the step.  It will give slightly if you place your weight on either side of the step.  If that bothers you then buy two and place one on either side.  I have seen campers in the 'Big Boy' catagory that have snapped the brace supports on their steps and it isn't a pretty picture.  I'm in a lighter weight catagory and don't want to take any chances.  The product is very sturdy.  Be sure to measure the normal distance from the bottom of your step to the ground and decide which length brace will suit you best.

Note: the photo shows two of these under RV steps, but these are priced individually.Our RV has three steps and it feels like a lot of strain is being placed on the bottom step when entering trailer carrying heavy loads.  Having these give the needed support.  The trailer doesnt creak or flex when entering or exiting once these are setup.  There are two small holes in one end of the brace plates, so I mounted to a small piece of fence board left over to keep them together.
One of these under my bottom step ain't getting it, I am going to buy another one and put them on each end, one only keeps moving around. Well made, good quality unit.

I bought two of these to help support the step on my travel trailer.  I installed them securely at the rear of the bottom of the step.  My wife stepped off on the step from the camper, and the steps collapsed into themselves, and the braces flipped up causing injury to her shins and legs.  It could have been much worse had her leg(s) fallen between the two steps and the steps collapsing on her, possibly causing her leg to be severed.  I am very disappointed in the size of the tops and bottoms.  They are only about 4 inches square.  These are very flimsily constructed.
summary: BEWARE:  INJURY CAUSED BY THIS PRODUCT

reviewText: I love it.  I have a new 2014 Jayco and the manual steps will certainly last longer than most with the support stand.  I definitely love that it easly extends over 1 foot.
summary: a must have for travel trailers

reviewText: these are great for there size. wish the plates were a little larger . but they support the step better then blocks of wood//

Bought these somewhere else, had a friend in the camper business, but they look really similar.  Not only do they really stabilize the steps and reduce the "rocking" when someone comes and goes, but they reduce the stress on the step supports.  After many years of coming and going fatigue of the supports is only going to happen.Buy 2, you won't be disappointed.
they work fine under the step to our rv.It keep the rv from moving when you step up to go in.
Will have to order another they do not work very well single centered. The one I purchased "scoots" after a few steps on it, annoying have to keep adjusting it back to sturdy.
summary: You really need two for effectiveness

reviewText: Very sturdy under the step I am thinking, well built but haven't used yet. No problems I can see. Will be using soon this summer.
summary: No reason this won't do well.

reviewText: I originally bought one for my brother who's steps broke (partially).  I thought this would  hold the steps in place for him instead of paying to replace entire step unit.  Well, I decided to purchase one for our camper that we keep in an RV park on the lake we frequent in the warm months (just to protect the steps from future abuse).  WOW, this little thing is easy to tighten up (on any surface) and it makes the step totally stable (almost like you had solid stairs).  I think this will certainly save the life of our steps long term.  Very pleased.

Talk about a let-down and a rip off!!!  I paid almost $15, for what I thought would be two units (as the product picture shows), only to take delivery of the component and find that you only get ONE OF THEM.Seriously. I could have bought a $17 pair of black jack-stands at big-box-car-parts, and done the same thing. I most assuredly would not have spent the equivalent of $30 for what would be a pair of screw jack stands!Save your money, and consider another solution.  They are solid, they are ok, they are nothing but screw-head jack stands...and there's no 'THEY' to it, you are buying one unit.*** ADDED DETAIL ***After trying to use this a couple of times, I also have to mention that the lower footer is about 3 x 3-inches, and the upper head of the jack also has a head of about 3 x 3 inches...this doesn't work really well with some steps...like mine. My steps are steel with a reinforcing ridge in the middle, running laterally across the bottom of the step. As a result, you can't 'nest' the head beneath your step treadplate, it only precariously sits on the edge of the step. As a result, there's not a lot of 'bracing' from using this at all. Yes, I could put a piece of pine shelving beneath the step and screw the jack into it (not good, if you don't want your steps to rust apart)...but you can't take that upper plate off, and the screw head is not removable...so in the end, this is the oddest white-elephant I've ever bought...can't get it to work whatsoever.I've got a pair of aluminium spinner jacks for loads up to 1000 pounds that work MUCH better than this thing...unfortunately, I can't even use it to stabilize the rear of the rv...there is only one of them...and it isn't rated anywhere near high enough to do something like that with...
summary: PICTURE IS MISLEADING - YOU ONLY GET ONE

reviewText: Was worried thought I might need two because of sand and size of steps. But it works perfect no problems no complaints.

We bought this our camper because it has three steps down with some play on them.  It works well if the grounds below is not rocky or bumpy.  The plates could be more rectangled to help with the support.  I would still recommend.

The idea is good, but this is not stable under my step. Each time up or down the step, it moves and there's no way to hold it in place. I went back to my nailed together stack of 2X8s. It might work in sand though.  ~Pegleg~
Makes the steps stable and stops the little shake when you climb in.  We use it all the time both at home and on trips.
summary: Easy to use and works well

reviewText: It is a waste of money for the intended purpose!  Got ripped purchasing this!  It might be a great product for some other purpose but not a Save-A-Step brace!  It is made ok, if I could find another purpose for it.

I'm sure you've had those times when, after traveling all day, you open the refrigerator and out tumbles half of your food. These Fridge Braces are just the trick to prevent that. I purchased two sets and put two on each of the upper and middle shelves. They work just like advertised. No more trying to catch falling food items when you open the fridge.
Keeps things snug in fridge......Camco 44033 RV FridgeBrace - Pack of 2....they are easy to install and were are glad we bought them!~
Well so far this item is a deceived. It works. I have had no items move around on me much even during pothole moments
I bought these on a whim for our new 5th wheel. Turns out they were able to keep stuff from falling out when we traveled. Simple, but efficient.
summary: More helpful that you might think

reviewText: work great. keep items from moving around. a little a pesky to remove when things are taken out of  the hold downs. but you wont cry over non spiled milk//
I've experienced what happens when items move around in your refrigerator and I highly recommend getting a couple of these.
This helped me keep things from moving around in my RV fridge as we motored down the road. This will not work on smooth surfaces---only the wire style.
These little braces work great to keep even heavy items in place. They work great, and will stay hooked to the wire shelf.
summary: Keep your milk etc., where it belongs.

reviewText: It does what it is supposed to do!  It keeps the milk from tipping, and keeps stuff from sliding around.
These work well and come in very handy to help keep stuff from falling out of the fridge. I would buy again.

I bought a bunch of these braces for my RV fridge, but I don't find them very useful and most are in a box outside the fridge.  They are hard to fit up securely against an item, they come loose easily, and I can't recommend them.  I'd say, with the right sort of refrigerator shelves they might work better than my ancient one, so they are probably ok in a newer RV.
Attaches easily to the shelf and holds the container in place, even a heavier Pyrex dish. More secure than the tension bars.
I was actually able to screw this rod into my rv water heater.  Never was ableto get the plastic one in correctly that it did not leak!
Perfect fit and protection for my rv tank water heater.  Make sure to check yours to prevent premature tank failure due to corrosion.

This anode rod should work fine once installed.  The threads are 1/2" and my water heater has a 3/4" threaded fitting so the application of a simple brass 3/4" outside threaded/1/2" inside threaded adapter was required.  That adapter was about $2.00 at the local hardware store.

All water heaters in motorhomes and trailers should come with these instead of a plastic plug to drain the units.  This installs easy and all of the water doesn't need to be drained if your fast enough.
summary: Help save the life of your hot water heater

reviewText: These anodes are shorted than some brands, but they work just as good. I got it so I could open it after I get home and drain the hot water heater. This has eliminated the foul odor that has built up in my water heater from time to time.
I like the orange citrus smell. It's easy to use and you don't have to wait for it to dissolve like others on the market.
We have used one time and there was no bad smells from black water... #1 only, no #2...

If you have ever gone in a camper and wonder what that smell is... well it's the stuff they tell us to put down our toilet.. wow had my camper for less than 2 hours put the green stuff in and then almost found myself left on the side of the road my family was so upset. So I did some research and learned that most of this stuff has formaldehyde which cause the camper to have a sour dead smell.. YUCK! and unless you don't intend to empty your holding tank daily like we need to it's a necessary evil.. however since we are only weekend warriors we don't need to use the gross stuff and I was VERY PLEASED to find this product. It doesn't have the strong yucky odor but keeps the pipes from gumming up.

Very, very convenient and easy to use. Even my wife will use it, as there is no mess to opening and pouring it in, unlike using a larger bottle. I guess if you men wanted to keep your wives happy....you could refill these little bottles from the larger bottle...just a thought!  :-)
Camco seems to make a good middle range product that does the job.  No need to spend more to get the job done.
Mix it up in an empty gallon jug and pour it down the toilet, its easy as that! It seems to help control odors very well and the single use containers are very convenient. No complaints!

The Camco 41191 TST Orange Power RV 4 oz Toilet Treatment - 8 pack was delevered on time and the package was well done, right size. The product itself, it works very well. I think it's the top of the line.I found out that the "extra" large tank that I have I need to put two to three bottles in the tank.
Easy to use with just one bottle for one tank load, smells nice before it goes in, works as advertised.
First trip in our new RV was uneventful. Put the recommended amount in our black water tank. Doesn't seem to work any better or worse than other products we've used.

Tell me what Rv'er likes to mess with the black water tank. Unfortunately it a chore that has to be dealt with. This does make the chore a little more bearable.While we are on the subject there is another product that I would highly recommend, Is the Valterra F02-4350 Black 'Flush King' Reverse RV Flush Valve I have one and depending on the usage I will back flush the tank about 4 or 5 times it works amazing it is the best $40.00 you will spend on your RV.
Three week trip to and in Yellowstone park. Not once did the wife complain of odors and trust me she has the nose of blood hound so if there were any she would've let me know...

I tried installing this but found that the stairs on my trailer have a support bar through the middle and there is not a good place to install it. (I should have read the reviews and would not have even ordered it!)  I will wait until I get home to my shop and make some modifications so I can use it.
It keeps my stair more stable for sure. I wish I can adjust the length as in some case I can not extend fully.

The only reason I wouldn't give it five stars is that you have to work with the holding clamp (bend it a bit) or the support will fall down during transit.  Advice for dummies like me: I kept trying to adjust the leg while the step was down.  Pull the step partially out and screw down the support.  Test it until the support barely rests on the ground.  Lift the step back up and give it a couple of turns.  That makes for a very secure step.

i've just put this on ....it makes the step pretty stable...I had to modify it to fit my step by saws alling about 1/2 inch  off the brace's foot so it could fold up properly...I also had to cut 2 stove bolts  to length and redrill the holes to fit bolts but all in all it has solidified the step....I like it

As others have noted, you need to buy the nuts and bolts to install this.  It also wants a nice flat area to install - about 1-1/2' x 8'.  My steps aren't flat - but have some built in ridges for water drainage.  My step also has a cross member for strength (or lifting), but certainly limited my choices of locations.  One screw location conflicts with the support itself  in the "up" position (near the retainer clip) - so you either need an exactly correct length bolt so the leg can swing back into the storage spot, or drill two holes (one to either side that will stay clear of the leg).  I had it, so I found a way to install it with some shims and it seems to be stable.  As others have mentioned, it might be better to overdrill the factory 3/16" holes and use larger bolts.  The leg doesn't lock in the down position, so it seem that it may slowly swing out of position over time when in use.  I purchased just one and mounted it to one side of the stair - when my door is open you are sort of pushed to use just one side of the stairs anyhow.  Hopefully should work OK - if it's a failure I come back and modify this review.
summary: Needs modificaiton to install, and doesn't fit super nice

reviewText: can't use this because the step on my camper is close to the ground and the adjustment isn't short enough to work on level ground. maybe it would be great on uneven ground, but what camp ground is that uneven? how about a shorter one?
Works somewhat but the clips that hold the brace up broke off.  A little quality control would go a long way.
I really like these. They were easy to mount and easy to put away as well as added extra stability to the step wheather entering or exiting the trailer.

I have all ways wanted one, but use caution look at the picture the step is flat, plus this step does not have a pull down bar.  Anyway a 2013 keystone cougar with curved steps and the step pull down bar, this product will not fit properly. Other than not fitting a curved step,  I like the idea.
Only takes a couple of holes to drill and you have a nice stable step when adjusted to the correct terrain.  It makes the steps much more sturdy.  Very happy with the purchase and shipping was quick.

My camper needs this step support extended pretty far and it seems to be kind of wobbly as a result.  Also when it is stored, it snaps between 2 claws. They dont seem to hold too tightly.  Afraid i may find a nub ground down from scraping on the highway while towing if this thing pops loose.  On the plus side, it does help to reduce the bounce in our camper step.  I think 3 stars is fair for this product. Installation requires drilling two holes into your camper step.
summary: i like it but it's a bit wobbly when extended

reviewText: No problem installing. Just drilled two holes in the bottom step and attached with the screws provided. I'm a big guy so I feel much safer with this product installed. It easily adjusts to different heights.

I'm not sure if the supplier is reading the reviews or not but I read that the hardware to mount this was not included. That issue must have been heard, because my steps (I ordered 2) came with screws, lock washers, and nuts to mount them to the step. I had it installed in about 5 minutes after I found a fresh battery for my drill.A few notes:The good:- Once installed, they are really sturdy and made a big difference in the feel of the step and reduced the motion in the camper when we were climbing in and out.-Like I noted above, the hardware is included to mount and install.-The legs are adjustable and do in fact store out of the way once you adjust the retention springs.The bad:-The retention spring on both of my steps needed adjustment out of the box. It isn't a big deal, but is a nuisance. I used a set of locking pliers and reshaped the spring to provide a secure hold on the legs for travel. Having said that, I'm still worried that it will come loose on the road and cause some damage. I think I may throw a zip tie on it before I move the camper. I always have a pack on hand so it isn't a big deal.-The material looks like it will rust very fast. I will update my review at the end of this season and report back on this, but I did put some grease on the threads of the legs to prevent issues down the road.All in all I still recommend them. It is a good value for the price and did the job it says it will do.
summary: A minor tweak and it works great.

reviewText: It's wonderful to be able to go in and out of the trailer when my husband's sleeping and not have it rocking and bouncing from just going up and down the steps.  Great product.

Have yet to get these installed on my step. They seem pretty sturdy and 2 are required for a proper installation. The only issue I'm going to have is that the bottom of my step is not flat so it makes the mounted options limited but I think these will do the trick and make the step more stable.

I bought this to mount to our Odyssey camper steps because, well, I'm getting up there in age and let's just say I'm now built for comfort and not speed. I didn't want there to be continued stress on the step (okay, it's not really THAT much stress. I'm only 250 pounds!) like on our previous camper. You know, that K-Z Sportsman I bought and had to refurb the whole front end because some farmer DOESN'T KNOW HOW TO SEAL A FREAKIN' RV WINDOW! yeah, so... there's that.

This installed very easily and works great to keep the edge of the step stiff when stepping on it. On our old travel trailer we had a problem with the step mounting bracket bending/breaking from people going in and out putting all of their weight on a corner of the step. With this installed it is much less of a problem. Very happy.

Once I received the SSS (Self-Stor Step) I reviewed the contents and set about installing.  The SSS comes with very little guidance and I understand why.  Too many variables with multiple step manufactures and RV models.  Also absent is any hardware.  So I went to my local hardware and purchased 4 stainless steel button head 1/4-20 by 5/8" bolts, self locking nuts and 6 flat washers. I pre-drilled the existing mounting holes in the SSS to accommodate a 1/4 inch bolt.  I flipped my lower step up, located the SSS, c-clamped it down and drilled the SSS hinge side.  I installed the bolts and tightened them in place.  That held the SSS while I drilled the clip side holes.  I installed the remaining bolts and I was finished.  I used one flat washer at each inside nut location.  I used the remaining two under the bolt head at the clip location.  And I feel the SSS is a very nice addition which makes my RV steps stable and SAFE.  I prefer using Stainless Steel hardware as the powder coat will cause enough rust on its own someday.
summary: Easy Install of the Self-Stor Step

reviewText: I purchased a size small.  I've been wearing Arai Corsair Helmets most of my riding life and I wear a small there as well as for KBC and HJC helmets.  This fit more like an x-small to me.  It did fit, but on the sides you can feel some rivits dig into your head a bit.For 2x bucks it's okay as a spare helmet or for someone going to use it on a scooter.Bonuses would be it comes with a nice storage bag (which it will be in a lot).  Tempted to return to amazon.com but the cost of shipping etc..might as well just keep it or give it to a kid that rides a scooter up and down the street.
summary: 3 stars for someone riding a scooter...fit is iffy at best

reviewText: fits perfectly, can't wait to wear it this summer when it is too hot for either my full face or modular helmets.
The helmet is a large, however, the unit is running small sizes. It sets too high on my head. I could use a extra-large size

I bought this helmet because the cops in Irvine, CA care too much about me riding a little motorized scooter with a proper helmet.The helmet is great! It functions as it should, it looks appealing, and protects. The only problems with it are that it is a bit heavy, big, and doesn't have a buckle to unlatch for short trips around town. I have figured a way to slide the helmet on and keep the strap in a fixed position without adjusting it every time. It fits tight, so I'm sure it's fine.This is a good helmet, and paired with a good set of glasses or goggles, it would work for motorcycles or faster bikes. I just ride around town going 25 mph max, so no need for anything else.
summary: Great Helmet, a bit big and heavy

reviewText: Got it yesterday and set it up for my wife. Medium is a bit bigger than anticipated but seems fine. After putting a quick clip on the chin strap tried it on and was really comfortable...

Though I am sending this product back, I still want to be fair in my rating.  It's a very nice looking helmet and seemed to be quite comfortable.I just couldn't get over how HUGE it was. I mean, I just need to come to grips with my 24" head.  That's right, 24"...Insane.  I'm only 5'11" 167lbs.This helmet really humbled me. Think spaceballs....Will have to go with a closed face, so at least nobody will recognize me.
Well made helmet at a great price. I just use with a scooter, so it is comfortable for just very simple trips.  .

I looked at helmets at the local bike stores and was sticker shocked. Yea I know it's for protection but they all seemed the same to me as long as they were comfortable. This was a great buy and a great fit. My friend has a $200 Harley helmet and mine is just as nice for a lot less. It's very light on your head all day too.

I mean for the price its not a bad buy, but don't expect to pick up any style points. this helmet is huge on the head. it tries to mimic the higher end helmets with similar design concept, but it does not quite achieve. it is very immense.
Ordered this from the Warehouse and it is a very high quality helmet for a really good  price. It is exactly as described, very high gloss finish.

vcan make reasonably priced ones. I've bought a few over the years, I like to be able to change helmets, like women and their shoes. comfortable fit. good price and very quick service. worth a looking into.
Great helmet and love the fit. Very well made and I ordered a second for my woman. She loves her's too...

UPDATE - Try not to let the mat or your roof become wet prior to loading. The Sherpak becomes icy slick on your roof once it becomes wet!The Sherpak SuperMat Roof Mat serves several purposes1- It acts as a barrier to keep your roof from being scratched2- It provides an *Anti-Slide* surface for your cargo bag/carrier - PLEASE NOTE - this mat becomes very slick if it becomes wet!3- It helps to reduce (or eliminate) the possibility of wind getting underneath your cargo bag. This helps increase the safety and provide a modest improvement in gas mileage.I am happy to report that the "SuperMat" preforms well in all of these categories. It is easy to put down... easy to store (Although it does have a strong odor when it is first purchased) and works as advertised.Is it a bit expensive at the listed price. Well maybe... but it is not prohibitively expensive and it works. For me that makes it well worth the money!5 Stars

I bought this roof mat along with my roof bag order. This is a good product to protect the paint of your cars roof. only $20 you can save yourself a lots of money if you damage your roof. Buy it! if you transport anything on your cars roof!
These work very well if using a roof bag to keep it from sliding and keep the roof from getting marred up.

You could find something suitable at many retailers.  I thought it would be a heavier.  It's like that stuff you use to keep things from sliding in your droors!  Oh yeah, and it drives me nuts in the wind slapping the roof!
Well the product arrived quickly, it did protect my roof, a little pricey. Hey worked well. Just what i needed and on time!

this filter looks the same, acts the same, and provides the same filtration as the OEM z filter, just a lot less expensive. One would be a fool to buy from VW. Just wish I could get a discount for buying them 3 or 4 at a time. Don't hesitate get some NOW!Mann-Filter HU 719/7 X Metal-Free Oil Filter

Used this recently in a 2012 Jetta Sportwagen with the CJAA TDI engine. Used in conjuction with the Pennzoil Ultra Euro L 5w30 oil, also purchased on Amazon. The filter in the car was a Purflux that the VW dealer supplied. This Mann fit fine and I expect it to work fine as well since I've been using Mann filters for several years in my VW diesels with no problems. This filter was made in Mexico.
I use these in my VW Golf TDI.  Does the job as good as any other for less cost.
Bought this for a 2011 VW Jetta Sportwagon TDI (don't forget the filter wrench unless you want to wrestle with a crescent wrench).  Fit right in, comes with both gaskets/o-rings.  No problems.
This filter is a touch shorter than the OEM filter. The pleats are also horizontal verses the zig-zag of the OEM filter. I'm comparing this to the OEM filters from my 2010 and 2011 TDI sedans.
I use this in my 2006 Volkswagen Jetta TDI. It works well, and I would recommend Mann filters for both oil and fuel filters.
summary: Works well for 2006 VW Jetta TDI

reviewText: This filter comes with both O-Rings (Small and Large) and make sure you lube both of them with new engine oil before you install the new filter. Overall it's well worth the money, its a Mann Filter after all.
Although the filters I've bought at the dealer come in VW packaging, I believe this is the exact same filter. Save over 25% vs buying this filter at the dealer.
Great filter lets just hope it can filter all the bull you had to go through to get it. Verified purchase you betcha

The HID bulbs are said to save fuel over the long run as they require ~ 40% less current to operate.  This is faint consolation when the time comes to replace them.  These bulbs work just fine.  Regular bulbs, however, are all the consumer needs.
summary: A lower cost version of an overpriced product

reviewText: Although it says Sylvania on the box, the actual bulb is made by OSRAM in Germany and the label on the bulb itself shows OSRAM 66144. I replaced this bulb on my 06' BMW and it is really bright. This is one of the brightest 4200K D1S except now it is surpassed by the newly released OSRAM Cool Intense Blue which is 5000K. The CIB is hard to get in the US as of this writing and some vendors are selling it around $180 a bulb.The 4200K rating on this bulb will look a bit yellowish but easy on the eye. Some people will prefer whiter color but you will definitely lose some light output as you go up the Kelvin rating except the CIB I mentioned above which boost light output by 20% compare to regular D1S. New technology does wonder.On this bulb, for the first 50 hours or so, the light output looks really yellowish. After that, it turns whiter. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this bulb.
summary: This is OEM quality by OSRAM

reviewText: Picked these up for my VW Touareg.  These are actually German made OSRAM bulbs in a Sylvania box.  The VW stealer will charge almost $300 for these.HID bulbs do slowly degrade over time.  You will be pleased with how new ones restore the wow factor to your lights. Stick with these over the whiter aftermarket bulbs,you will get much better bad weather performance.
summary: German made osrams in the box at 1/3 the price

reviewText: The original bulb in my wife's Enclave started "blinking," which seems to be one of the problems that can happen with HID bulbs. The local shops wanted $100 for the replacement; dealers want even more. FOr a very reasonable price, I obtained this bulb. It looked slightly different than the original (the plastic at the base of the bulb was slightly different) but it appears the original is only available from the dealer and this is the aftermarket replacement (original was 66146; this is a 66144). Same brand as original. Same color, same wattage, same type (D1S).Fit perfectly and works perfectly. Exactly matches the color of the original on the other side.

These aren't 5000k, more like 4000k. The color will shift from yellow to white/blue, but it takes a very long time. These are great. DON'T BUY CHEAP BULBS! I bought some off eBay, about 30$ a pair, and they stopped working within a week. They also smelled terrible too, the plastic was burning off because the bulbs were so hot. I wish these were 5000k, as described! I guess some other dealer wrote that.Save your time and money and buy these!

I used the kit to bleed the brakes on a motorcycle, worked good. I gave the kit only four stars because the tubing in the package was rolled up in such a way that when unrolled it was kinked and would not draw a vacuum on the fitting. A quick trip to the hardware store for new tubing fixed the problem. Two bucks for new tube.

I tried the old manual method of pumping the brake and loosening/unloosening the nipples, but this system makes it so much quicker.  I only wish the drain bottle magnet was much stronger, it does not hold its own weight much less when its almost full.
summary: Makes DIY brake jobs MUCH easier

reviewText: If this kit was of better quality it would be a nice way for one person to bleed brakes. However, this kit is sorely lacking in the quality dept. First, the plastic hose is packed in the box with kinks in it. So even after trying to relax the kinks, they collapse with suction is applied. The adapters are a 'one time' application. Once I seated the adapter to the first brake bleeder valve (which worked well), it was all over... The following bleeder valves wouldn't seat, as the adapter was not pliable enough to re-seat. Do yourself a favor and buy a set of speed bleeders...and leave this kit alone!

I just completed my first hydraulic fluid change using the Mityvac MV8000. It was an intuitive process although a thorough and detailed instruction book came with the product. Bleeding and replacing old, discolored hydraulic fluid on my motorcycle brake and clutch lines was a snap. Now I'm riding much safer and the Mityvac MV8000 was a big part of my success. My next brake job will be much easier and I can do it single handed. Great product.

reviewerName: GOB PROGRAM Y/N "Example of a Real Name"
reviewText: First off, the picture looks like metal-but it's plastic. This wouldn't be too bad if the rest of the kit wasn't so poor. The suction pump is okay-though tiresome- but the jar is too small, the hosing is chintzy and the fittings leak like crazy. Regardless of how much you pump, you will always see air-even if there isn't any in your brake lines. This can make it very difficult to tell if you've actually bled the lines or not.Perhaps this would work better for a motorcycle.
summary: Sloppy mess. Have fun with this thing...

reviewText: There aren't a lot of positive reviews on this item but I didn't have a problem. I was able to bleed my brakes as fast as I would have been with a shop pneumatic unit. As long as a good vacuum is created on whatever your bleeding or testing, this unit will work. The only thing that is a drawback is the size of the bottle, but that was more of an annoyance and I got over it because it worked great and wasn't expensive. I would recommend this to any professional mechanic or Sunday DIYer.
summary: Great if you know how to use it.

reviewText: It is rather flimsy. The gauge is not always working. Thin tubes have hard time keeping vacuum when breaks are bled. But if tight connection is achieved, it holds vacuum well.Since it is a very small pump it can not achieve air flow required for many applications. I needed to bleed accidentally emptied ABS and had to pump so many times, before fluid showed, my hand got tired. but for initial caliper break, or simple vacuum check - this is a great tool.

The standard for automotive vacuum pumps.  Made of plastic, but this makes it nice and light.  A bit less industrial looking than my old Pittsburgh tools pump, but then that one didn't last more than a couple of years.  TONS of adapters for every type of application you can imagine.  Capture container is a bit small, but I made a larger one from an old glass jar using the included adapters.
summary: The Standard of Auto Vacuum Pumps

reviewText: with so many attachments and tube sizes I could attach this thing to about anything. The reservoir could be a little bigger but no big deal. It was tough to do everything one handed but I have seen others do it and I would chalk that up to my in-experience. Getting the tube to stay on my bleeding valve on my motorcycle was tough too so I had to use one hand to hold that on and the other to pump. Luckily everything was close to the floor so I could use that as an extra hand. I was able to flush my brakes at 1/8 the cost the dealer was asking.

I did not want to pay a lot of $$$ to have someone bleed my brakes given how simple that process is. I used it to bleed all 4 brakes and it improved my "mushy brakes" and I saved a lot of $$$. Product works. It is plastic so I do not know if it will work in 2/3 years but it did the job for me now. Buy more brake fluid than you think what you need. My brakes had much more air than I thought and it took me more time and fluid to bleed them. Also, you can use a turkey baster to suck some fluid out of the master cylinder before you start the bleeding - it makes things a bit simpler. When you bleed, check that the master cinder is full with fluid as it will drain quickly. If you it goes below the level, you will introduce air into the system and you will need to start all over.

I used this on my motorcycle. Works perfect.4 star because there are 4 kinks in the line that will eventually tear a hole and leak vac. Packing of the product should be done better.Run some hot water over it, it'll un-kink before use. That and if you ever drop this, it'll fall apart. Cheap thin plastic gauge housing.Overall, it works. Instruction sucks though. It's trying to do too much. It should just stick with it being a brake bleeder with better instruction.Something about ABS break on the manual, didn't read it.

I had the same problem as others with a poor seal at the jar.  A thin o-ring on the lid would fix that.  I resorted to gobbing silicone dialectric grease on the seal each jar full.  The hose that came with it was kinked, which got in the way.  Strange that an otherwise good item could be far better with a couple of simple changes.  Otherwise a good device.

Nice package for the price...can do vac readings, bleed brakes, bleed clutch etc.  The canister which fits inline does take a little bit of force to fit snugly without leaks.  For those doing brake bleeding be sure to READ THE DIRECTIONS where they recommend taking the bleeder out completely and using TEFLON tape to seal the threads.  If you don't do this, you will suck in air around the bleeder threads...seems pretty basic but I think a lot of unhappy customers don't get this and omit this step.Also, Mityvac has a "Mason Jar Adapter" which will work better than then included small jar for larger jobs.  It also should form a better seal and is more suited to keeping (and capping the fluid) from spilling.
summary: Good basic tester, some fitment required

reviewText: I don't know why this has received bad reviews, unless people just don't know how to use it properly...Out of the package, I was bleeding brakes on my motorcycle within 5 minutes.  The whole process was painless and took all of 15-min total to bleed both front brakes AND my clutch!  Simply an awesome tool!My only complaint about the entire thing is this... I wish there were TWO collection cups included (small and larger).  The smaller one is perfect for motorcycle, or bleeding each brake in a small car, but when bleeding the brakes in my F250, I had to stop half-way and empty the cup before I could finish each rear wheel... not a huge issue, but it would have been nice to be able to do each wheel without stopping in the middle.The vacuum gauge is also handy for testing and adjusting the vacuum advance on my truck's distributor... properly adjusted, I gained a couple MPG, which is great for our current gas prices!
summary: Works perfectly for bleeding brakes and testing vacuum

reviewText: I bought this kit as a gift for my brother, who was about to undergo a complete brake system rebuild on an '87 Heritage Softail. Perfect for this type of task and built with long lasting quality in mind, he was extremely happy with it.
summary: Mityvac MV8000 Automotive Test and Bleeding Kit

reviewText: It didn't worked so well, a gasket was leeking, They send me a complete rebuilt parts parts fast and free. But still I had to have the purge done at the garage at the end.
summary: It didn't worked so well, a gasket was leeking ...

reviewText: The pump seems to work fine. The flaws arise in the leaky reservoir and fittings. The only way for a vacuum pump to really work is to be able to create a seal. This thing leaks not only from the poorly designed reservoir, but from every tube connection point.I ended up going with the Motive pump for my Audi A4 instead. It costs more but its actually usable.
summary: Too many flaws to be good...

reviewText: This is a must have for changing to spark plugs on the 04-08 ford f150s. I own a 2006 ford f150 with 75k mikes. 5 out of 8 spark plugs broke upon removal even though I soaked them with aerokroil. This tool took all 5 out with no issues.

This is by far the best broken spark plug end extractor I have used. It is easy to use and the chance of breaking this tool off in thehead is about zero. Other styles I have used do not work as good and are scary. If you break the tool in the head you have to remove the cylinder head and step one for head removal is remove the cab from the frame!!
summary: A MUST FOR 3 VALVE FORD PLUGS.

reviewText: I only had one plug break but with this it came out without a hitch and I didn't need to pay tow prices to get it to the garage!

I just finished replacing the OEM motorcraft spark plugs in my F150 2005. 4 broken when removing, the other 4 left the engine in one piece (as they are suppose to be).Longer time with pb blaster soaking around the spark plugs and turn 1/16 by 1/16 seems to help a bit, but if you end breaking one, you will need to have this tool handy.The tool helped in all the different cases and removed the stuck parts of the spark plugs, without leaving shaves of ceramic inside. netherless, i vacuum the cylinders before to insert the new ones (Champion one piece design now)In addition the tool, you will need a 15/16 deep socket to use this tool and a long plier in case the ceramic stay in one piece to help remove it. I started the job really very worry after learning from others experience on this, but ended with a lot of confidence after seen how this tool can really deliver what it offered. it did a really great job. and saved a lot of money as the dealer was asking for several hundred of dollars to do the job.
summary: Excellent to remove the broken spark plugs in triton engines

reviewText: Out of a lot of makers, this is the best. I removed a broken plug from my friend car. He was so happy and will buy one kit.
summary: The best tool and maker you can count on.

reviewText: This tool works perfectly to remove Ford's ridiculously designed broken spark plugs. The first one probably took 10 minutes to do due to reading the instructions and learning as you go. At first I wasn't screwing the center piece in far enough. I threaded it down to where it got tight but realized I had to turn it hard to push the center electrode down. Once you get the first plug out and examine it then it makes total sense what exactly the tool has to do. The next plug probably took 3 minutes, but too, I was working on a Mustang which has more accessible plugs than some of the SUV's.If you're even considering doing plugs on one of these Triton 3 Valve motors I would make the small investment in this tool first so you have it on hand. No matter how hard you try and no matter how many precautionary steps you take it seems at least one, and probably several plugs break off.Remember too, when you install the new plugs use high heat anti-seize to the part of the plug you just extracted. This may help the next guy remove plugs.
summary: Buy this BEFORE attempting plug removal!

reviewText: After researching the '05 F-150 5.4L spark plug replacement issues, I was ready to do the job -- my goal was to beat the odds, and have zero broken spark plugs.  Unfortunately, one spark plug did break, the one nearest the driver.  Normally, that is the moment  when one begins the mental preparation to fork out $3 to $5 large to the stealership, and prepare to receive their advice to let the grown ups handle it.  But not today though, because I had purchased the Lisle tool as insurance, so one hour later I had removed the broken spark plug!  Wow!  Lisle has earned great respect from me.
My friend used my tool on his 2004 F-150 which broke 6 of the 8 plugs but the kit worked flawlessly!!

If you are going to change plugs in a 5.4L ford with the long plug that has the ground electrode around it you will need this tool to remove the broken electrode when changing plugs. I was lucky had only two that broke. Don't wait for the hundred thousand mile. Do it sooner.

Don't get caught changing plugs on a 3V Ford modular engine without this tool in your tool box.  The plugs tend to break off in the head during removal and this tool makes it a breeze to remove them.  In the past the cylinder head would've needed to come off to remove the plugs but with this tool you can remove the broken plug in under 10 minutes.  As far as the quality of the tool, my friend has the Matco version which is twice the price as this Lisle version.  The funny thing is that I think Lisle actually makes the Matco stamped tool.

If you own a Ford vehicle with a triton motor and plan on doing a spark plug change, save yourself the migraine/nervous breakdown and get this tool kit. Chances are, you will break spark plugs in an otherwise simple procedure. Having this tool on hand will save you the money of having your vehicle towed to a repair shop and stave off the risk of damaging the motor from debris falling into the cylinder. Costs a FRACTION of what it will cost you to have someone professionally remove the broken spark plug.
summary: Lisle Ford Triton Broken Plug Removal Tool

reviewText: Would have gone 5 stars for this tool but for the 'grab' threads, not being done like a 'tap', have suffered.  I'm afraid that one or more blades on the thread broke off on the second (my last) spark plug extraction and I wouldn't trust it to be doing the same task one more time.  Anyway... All this because 'attention-to-detail' wasn't 'Job 1', obviously, at the Ford plant (ie anti-seize compound NOT having been applied at the time of installation on these 4.6L and 5.4L 3-valve engines when new.
summary: Lisle 65600 Broken Spark Plug Remover Tool - Job 2 recovery (fix) for Job 1 (FORD)

reviewText: I love this jack b/c it does exactly what I need it for.  I've had no issues whatsoever.  Buy with confidence.

I bought this back in 2010, so I figured it was time for a review.  I'm not a gear head...  But I've changed enough flats in my time to know that the cheap and DANGEROUS scissor jacks that ship with nearly all vehicles today aren't worth a crap.  I wanted something I could stow in my trunk for emerengcies.  I've used it three times in that period and it's made an otherwise pain in the rear-end job a snap.Torin is a chinese brand, but unfortunately unless your spending hundreds or even thousands, American made racing jacks are hard to find.  Their quality control from what I've been reading seems to be hit and miss.  But mine has been fine.  Materials and machine work don't feel cheap to me.  Everything is tight fitting and works as it should.  The weight is perfect for my use at under 30lbs.  If your using a racing jack on a garage floor I don't see why you sould care if it's 100lbs as long as it rolls.  But lifting it out of a truck...YOU CARE!  It's compact size leaves me plenty of space in my Lancer's trunk.  The two section lift and release handle is perfect for this too.  Make sure you bleed this thing as the included instructions state when you unbox it!I've lifted my Mitubishi Lancer, my friend's Toyota Camery, and my father's F150.  It never complained even once.  The lift speed was fine with me.  I don't remember how many pumps it took, it wasn't 3 but it wasn't rediculous either.  People make too much of a fuss over that (unless they really are a race crew, in which case SPEND the money and buy American!)  Most recently I did lift the F150 however I really would recommend a bigger jack.  The capacity was okay more or less.  But the height was a challenge.  An unloaded half ton is right around 5500lbs, one corner should be within rate spec, but your pushing it.  Do yourself a favor and invest in a 2.5 to 3.5 ton rated model with better reach and a bigger piston.One final word...  And this really should be common sense...  NEVER and I mean NEVER craw under your vehicle when up on a jack.  Buy some jack stands with nice large base pads and a few wheel chalks!  And make sure it's solild before you get underneath.  I've personally been there when a vehicle comes down unexpectedly.  No one was hurt but that was pure luck!
summary: Great jack for cars of all sizes and small/medium pickups

reviewText: Somewhat of a low rating in tonnage, but it does the job.  It lifts the car very quick and is very easy to maneuver due to it's light weight.  The only downside is when you're in tight spaces.  You can remove half of the handle, but then it becomes very difficult to pump the handle.

The air purge procedure was easy. A sticker on the jacks says to do it before use, so I didFits under my lowered Miata and raises the car with only few pumps. Handle is two piece which is great for transporting the jack to track days. For $100 this is a good buy. You'll feel like a racing pit crew when rolling it around the garage==Update==It's still working fine a year later but after reading more recent reviews I am thinking about changing it for something safer
summary: Great value for $100, beware reports of sudden failure
