reviewText: First...... follow the directions and bleed the pump.  Very simple.  Open the bleed valve on the top of the pump and open the pump valve by turning the handle to the open position(in other words the pump wont lift). Now,hand pump the jack several times very fast and then tighten the screw back down on the top of the pump housing.  DONE.  Easy enough.  Now attempt to jack up one corner of the car.  No, not a thirty ton tank.  It's only a 1.5 ton lifting jack.  Jack should lift the car or item very easily.  Use jack stands after you have finished lifting the car into position.  Better safe than sorry.  Never rely on just a pump jack, always put stand(s) under what your working under!! That's just common senseAs for the pump leaking.  well i've found that most guys try to lift something too heavy and blow out the gaskets and that's why they find the pump broken down the road a week later or after a few uses.  Get a bigger lift if you need to lift more weight!  A few bucks spent now saves more in the end!I live in a cold climate i even used the jack in a freezer where the temperature was 26 degrees.  No problems there either.  So, why so many complaints? Hmmmmm, my guess faulty or just trying to lift the heavy stuff and figure it's the pumps fault.  Amazon has an excellent return policy and Torin is helpful. I now own three of these jacks and couldn't be happier.Works well under a Camaro SS 2011 650 hp....  Even under a 25hp John Deere riding Mower..... happy lifting my friends!!!Update............  Still going strong and using daily! February 9,2013
seemed of good quality. read it was better lasting than oem. shipped quickly. also, the egr valve is included. wish i knew this sooner.

Wow gaskets have come a long way.  Pulled the intake off (watch the vids on other sites for help), cleaned it off with a wire brushed, vacuumed it out, changed the knock sensors, put it all back together with zero issues.  Runs perfectly!  Strong easy to install gaskets, no guess work anymore!

Purchased these after looking up needed parts for a Tahoe Z71 I recently bought. There was a check engine light showing so after checking the codes and doing my research on not only the caused but also what the best parts were, this is what I found. The came in a nice box from Fel-Pro, very durable metal and rubber gaskets, and fit perfectly. Tip: make sure to clean the surfaces of the heads very well for best adhesion as well as the grime behind the bolts where the metal lip will go (over the bolt!) before installing these. Very easy to install. The original gaskets were badly worn and compressed creating air and oil to escape being inefficient. I highly recommend these!
summary: Can't ask for a better gasket!

reviewText: I wanted to replace the intake gaskets because I had to take the intake off to replace the knock sensors. The gaskets fit perfectly and was a complete set for an intake job. Amazon says it does not fit my 2002 Chevrolet 2500HD crew cab 6.0L gas but it does.

I had to replace a knock sensor and figured I would replace the gaskets while I was at it. For what they do and how hard they are to get to, getting a good quality product just makes sense. Thus I choose this set.However, most other gaskets snap on the bottom of the intake manifold. These do not. They must be placed on the engine head. While the ring around the head was nice and clean, the bolts were covered in dirt and this product requires those bolts to be clean to put the gasket on. Since the cylinders are open at this point, taking a wire brush and risking dirt getting into the pistons is a real danger. The only way is to have a good vacuum and an assistant to make sure the dirt can come off safely to install these gaskets.
summary: Great product, but have a good vacuum ready.

reviewText: this is probably the best torque wrench i ever had. Quality to the touch. I do alot of shock work with my cars, so the wheels has to come off all the time. Once its off, it has to come on again, but it could be dangerous if you dont torque on your lugs at the proper torque. Thats when this baby comes in and saves the day. Not to mention it looks cool, and gorilla has a tool industry reputation. When people that knows tools see you with a gorilla torque wrench, there should be no doubt, respect is given!Awesome Awesome wrench!!!

This is an excellent, easy to use torque wrench. The instruction sheet included in the protective heavy duty plastic box is simple to follow. With alloy wheels and light weight disc brake hubs, getting the torque correct when changing tires is critical. Too much force on those lug nuts and the studs can break off, too little force and the wheel can wobble, uneven force and the brake rotor can warp. It is an important job to do right.The wrench has a reversible ratchet with a half inch drive. The box includes a half inch to three eights drive adapter, and a half inch extension. While tightening a bolt, when the proper torque is reached the wrench gives off a reasonably loud click and definite feedback in the handle (sound and feel that the torque setting was reached). Presetting the torque is fairly easy by loosing the lock nut and twisting the handle until the desired torque lines up with the center line. The only tricky part is a half turn is 10 foot pounds. Odd number tens are on the left and even numbers are on the right. Increments of 2 are marked on the handle for really precise torque. Once the torque is set, turn the nut on the end to lock the setting.This wrench looks to be really rugged. I expect it will last a long time. Like any other precision instrument (I know it sounds weird that a wrench is a precision instrument) dropping it isn't a good idea. Store it in the plastic case and it will give years of service.How long do I keep my tools? A very long time. I finally decided to replace my ancient antique Craftsman torque wrench. You know the incredibly accurate, easy to use flexible bar with the fixed pointer you read on an analog scale near the handle. Yes that old.

This tool works great, much better than my older style pin torque wrench;1 click and it is torqued. No straining to see the pin position on the scale. Very easy to set-up and use and comes in a nice protective case.  I only use a torque wrench 2 x yr on 3 vehicles so I can't write about durability and ease with frequent use, or calibration, which I understand needs to be done periodically with regular use.  5 stars from this weekend DIY'er. Great price through Amazon with free Prime shipping.

Great torque wrench.  I have used it a few times to change brake pads.  My only complaint is the markings on the torque wrench are difficult to tell what torque the wrench is set to in terms of the 10s.  90 ftlbs vs 100 ftlbs takes me a second to determine.  I have 20/20 vision without corrective lenses.

This is a very good torque wrench. It's perfect to get the lug nuts on your car up to proper levels as described in your car's manual (in my case 94 foot pounds). However, for things like an oil drain plug the wrench is too unweildy to get up in there. Even with the extensions. It may just be my particular vehicle's clearance. Great torque wrench. I just wish it was a big smaller. And I understand it's large because when you get up high in foot pounds you need the extra leverage. Just a nitpicky thing of mine. I really wish it were smaller to get into those tight places. If it could start small and telescope for extra leverage then it would be perfect. Anyway, the wrench works perfectly. When you hit the proper poundage it makes a loud popping noise to alert you that you've reached the level you set on the wrench. Really, a great torque wrench.

Anyone who works on cars knows, the difference between a properly torqued bolt and one that that is just short of proper torque specs can cause anything from odd noises during daily driving, to broken brackets and supports.  If you do any kind of work on your car, even if it is something as simple as changing/rotating wheels, you NEED to have a good torque wrench.  This one has more than enough adjustment to torque down wheels, motor mounts, sway bars, etc.  I gave it one less star because it is a bit expensive for a non-digital TW, but it is very well built.  Just remember these few simple rules when working with a torque wrench:1. NEVER use a torque wrench to loosen bolts.  It takes more torque to loosen most bolts than it does to tighten, and you risk damaging the tool2. ALWAYS bring the torque adjustment back to zero before putting the tool away.  This is a spring loaded wrench, and to prevent any damage to the calibration, always reset the torque before storage.3. NEVER torque more than your torque setting.  If you hear a "click" stop!  Remember a spring loaded wrench's click noise is when the internal spring slips off the shaft thus indicating that you reached the torque spec.  Proceeding to torque after a click could cause damage to the spring.
summary: Work On Cars? Then You Need This

reviewText: for the price, the gorilla automotive torque wrench is a great buy.  It is simple and easy to use.  No complaints.
This is my 2nd torque wrench and find it to be extremely effective and accurate. It's made of high quality material and comes with a durable plastic case.Highly recommended.

I've purchased this torque wrench before for a family member and had the pleasure of using it a few times. Initially, I purchased from TireRack.com and the wrench itself is the same price, but at TireRack you have to pay nearly $10 for shipping.When it was time for me to purchase one for myself, I searched the internet and amazingly found it on Amazon.com with free shipping.It shipped almost immediately after the order was placed and arrived at my door in 3 business days.I like this torque wrench because it functions very well, comes in a carrying case and has a 1/2" extension and 3/8" adapter.

The one I received broke on the first torque adjustment.  Went from base to 20 ft. lbs. and it made a grinding sound then locked up.  Got it to move backwards, tried again... no luck.  Immediately sent back as defective.
It seems to be accurate and it works just fine. However, it looks kind of cheap and odes not measure up to the old ones that were built in the good old US of A!

reviewerName: Ethosian "You never have to wait for anything...
reviewText: Reviews like this are hard because there isn't much to say - the item is exactly what I was expecting at a price that seemed reasonable.  I needed a gauge for a new vehicle (I carry one in each of my vehicles, just in case).
summary: Fine item - good price - no complaints

reviewText: I have several of these and they all work well, some for many years.  I purchased a dial pressure tester for my wife and it lasted for about 2 months so I went back to old reliable.  They seem pretty accurate as one of my vehicles has a digital tire pressure monitoring system and it matches this gauge within one PSI.They are easy to carry and I just put one in every car and one by the air compressor.  I like the air bleed nipple on the end of the gauge to lower pressure if you have to.  These are inexpensive, accurate and reliable gauges and mine have been a life saver.  Just remember the safety of your car on the road (and family), protecting your expensive tires and improving your gas mileage depends on having the right tire pressure. I recommend this to you as a good buy.
summary: Works well and lasts for years!

reviewText: its a old style tire gauge it works good and its what you need to check your tires easy ti use
Have this kept in my car at all times.  Has saved me a lot from riding on tires that were woefully under pressurized.  If I get a new car in the future this will be coming with me.

This product works great! Seems to be of good quality and not ready to come apart like my other tire pressure gauges. It would be nice if it went up to about 70 psi or so but then again I'm asking for too much. Well worth the purchase.

I picked this up based on the excellent reviews here an on a consumer site. It's a good price, but I'm not happy with the way it sits on the valve stem. For some reason, I can never get a good seal right away and almost always end up with a pound of air out of the tire.Quality is okay. It feels cheap and don't suggest drop testing it.Accuracy is very good, but I noticed over the course of several months that one of the two that I purchased became less accurate. I'm not sure why, but it could be a quality control issue.I had an old NAPA pencil model that was highly rated by CR and worked great for a decade, but I can't seem to find it's replacement. I'll keep trying until I find a good one...
I am pleased with this simple, inexpensive, and accurate tire pressure gauge.  You don't need any of those other electronic, programmable gauges.  This one works fine.
summary: An inexpensive yet accurate tire pressure gauge

reviewText: i like it. it is very easy to use. i would definitely recommend. i was doubtful with this product at first, when i've read all these negative comments.i didn't regret a thing when i tried this jack.

I constantly do thing to my car and do weekly checks underneath it. This is a good way to just get my jack stands underneath the car. Only downside to this is that it doesn't lift very far(I suggest using a block between the car and jack) and struggles to lift my 1.5 ton car, despite the 2 ton rating. It has lifted my car at least 8 times in the last 2 days. Will update this after I've used it quite a lot more.

I recently purchased my first home and didn't have many supplies to stock my garage for DIY projects. A  car jack was one of the first things on my list as I am always completing my own oil changes and rotating my tires. This jack worked just as advertised and held my 2006 Chevy Cobalt while I changed the oil a few weeks ago. A couple weeks later I was able to get under my wife's 2003 Toyota Corolla and her oil was changed in a flash. The jack did its job!

It deserves five stars as for $37 shipped with a case this is a stealIt's not really low enough to be used on my Miata MX-5 and had be used on the sub-frame of our Honda CR-V as it would not jack the regular jacking point high enough but that's where I put Jack Stands anyway. With the Miata I'll probably drive one wheel onto a 4x8 piece of wood first, then this jack should fit under okIf you have a regular car or small SUV you should be fine. The jack works great.
summary: Not for low cars or tall SUVs

reviewText: My garage has quite a selection of vehicles and I was hoping to find something that would work for all of them. There probably isn't such a thing. This one is too tall to fit under my daughter's mini cooper, and too short to raise my other daughter's jeep.
summary: Not for very short or tall vehicles

reviewText: This is a great tool for getting under the car for the occasional oil change. The only grip I have is that there is no place for tools to be held but other than that it is quite useful. The padding is thick and comfortable and the headrest keeps the strain off the neck for the longer processes.
Very nice product. I use it under mt 5th wheel and it sure makes maintenance a lot more easy. Rolls easy and the headrest provides comfort while doing your work. Highly recommended.

This has made so many things so much easier. I have a lifted truck, so I by no means needed it to get under it, but I can't exactly sit up under it, so this helps to rest my head up on when working under it.
Sturdy wheels and heavy duty frame; rolls great and turns well on uneven floors.  I would recommend this to anyone who needs a great creeper for a great price!!

This creeper works exactly as it should.  You will not have any problems getting around under the car and it is very easy to maneuver around.  The wheels are not large, so you can even use it without the car on jack stands, depending upon the ride height of the vehicle.  The headrest, however, is not the greatest, as it is difficult to manipulate while you are on the creeper.  You have to lift up and use the handle to move the headrest, but you should be able to move it more easily while under the car.  The pad is adequate without being too thick and it is comfortable enough to use for decent jobs.
summary: Good creeper with a questionable headrest

reviewText: Today I used the creeper for the first time to change an O2 sensor.  The creeper works well, is solid, and moderately comfortable.  This is not a creeper for everyday or shop use, but for occasional home use it is very good.
I have a 2" lift on my Wrangler JK and the extension on this is perfect to ensure that I can either jack from the axle or the frame and still get plenty of lift.

Lifts my Honda Ridgeline just fine. I especially like the removable extension piece. Gives me the capability to use it under my regular vehicles as well as the truck. I did not have any problems with damage during shipping like other reviewers. My only complaint is that it's not rapid pump but you really can't expect that at this price.

This has been a really decent jack for the $. I used it on a 2.5 ton Discovery 2. It's a heavy truck and this jack worked great. I love the additional piece to make it an SUV/truck jack. Very helpful. Also great because you can remove the piece, and still use the jack on a car as well.Mine arrived completely ready to go out of the box. The day after I got it, I used it to change the rotors and pads on all 4 wheels of my Disco. Worked great. Made the job a lot easier and quicker.Two out of probably 100 pumps I would get a weird sound and the jack wouldn't go up on that pump. Would immediately go up again on the next pump, and it would not the jack did not go down at all. Not sure if this is common, or if it means it could fail. This is my first floor jack so if anyone wants to comment below that would be great.The release is a little touchy, but after the first time I was able to control the descent to the exact amount I wanted.It feels like a pretty good quality product. And most importantly, it works.Only would want to change two things. 1. Add a handle or something to carry it with. Not a huge deal because you don't really carry them very often, but would be nice when you need to. 2. I would have liked a mount for the removable pump bar. Again, not a huge deal, but I would have liked a mount to keep the pump bar when not in use.Lastly, be safe and use wheel chalks and jack stands when working on your car.

I will start out by saying that this jack has no problem lifting my Chevrolet Trailblazer high enough to put jack stands under it at their tallest setting.  The mechanism is smooth and the release/lowering is easy to control.  There isn't a lot to say about the performance of the jack, other than that it works exactly as it should.The problem I have with this jack is the wheels.  One of the bolts holding the turning wheels bent over when lowering the car, so it appears that the bolts they use are not rated for the load that they will experience.  I am going to grind the top off of the bolt and replace it with a new one, but I shouldn't have this problem.
summary: Good jack, but not the sturdiest ever

reviewText: Bought this for occasional jobs like changing oil and brakes.  I've used it twice now with a Toyota Camry and a Toyota Sienna and it performed well with both.  I did discover that to use the riser I first drove the car onto my steel ramps and then put the jack under to lift it up farther.  The clearance on my cars did not allow the riser to fit under the car without that initial life.  Without the riser it did raise up the cars, but not enough for what I was looking for.My jack worked right out of the box, and although there was some wear on the box, everything arrived in good order.  It raises and lowers as I expected, and it does lower slowly if you gently release the pressure.  I haven't given 5 stars because it does not scream high quality just from handling it a few times and seeing other jacks.  If this holds up over time I will update my review with another star.  All in all, a solid jack that does exactly what I wanted at a price I was willing to pay.

It is only good under the tire. If you use this for the 5th wheel front jack it is too weak to handle the weight and it will bend. If I buy the flat top it would still bend and it is also very slippery.. I'm still searching for a perfect leveler.
summary: Not very useful in all cases.

reviewText: The leveler works great for our 5th wheel. We went camping and we used these. Better then using blocks. The camper didn't move. We put them under the legs. For winter we will put them under the tires.
No more boards.  I love being able to throw a couple of these under the tires and drive right up onto them.  They store nicely and are very lightweight.  Thanks for a great product.

recommend these for any type camper ours is a class c m.home weight 12.000lbs  easy to use and store...have two sets...works great and will hold up...follow instructions and use common sense...stores easily in it's own nylon bag
We bought these for our camper.  They are lightweight, easy to use, and the carrying case is a plus.  They will fade in the sun, but expect to be using them for years.

These are great levelers made of hard plastic (not the cheaper yellow brand from EZ).  They can be used with the other products from Tri Lynx like the caps (Tri Lynx 00019 Lynx Cap Leveler) and the chalks (Tri Lynx 00018-2PK Lynx Stop'n Chock Leveler). You get a bag of 10 orange levelers that can be used with the above mentioned caps under stabilizer jacks, or under the tongue jack (if you have a lighter trailer).  Of course, you could also use them under the tires as levelers.  Bottom line: great product, but should consider getting the caps.

I used to bring boards with us everywhere we went when camping.  This product is a wonderful replacement.  They are very light, and connect like legos.  We have a dual axle trailer, and ended up needing two sets.  Most of the time one set was sufficient, but occasionally our site was bad enough that we had to build up both tires on one side.  We've used them on stone, dirt, in mud, and blacktop.  The design works well, and keeps them from sinking into the ground.  The storage bag is convenient as well, and allows them to be neatly stored away when not in use.  It's a must-have for RVers.

These Tri Lynx Levelers are an absolutely wonderful accessory for leveling your camper or trailer. We were given a set of these when we bought our pop-up camper and they have mad leveling our camper so easy to do.We have it down to a science now and generally get the number of needed squares right on the first guess. We find that it is best to build a wide base and make a gentle slope, but on at least once had to only use a two square base with two more placed on top (see picture in "Customer Images") and it worked just fine.These are surprisingly well made and very easy to use!Highly Recommended!CFH
summary: So Easy To Use - Highly Recommended

reviewText: This is definitely a lot lighter & easier than stacking up wood 2 x 8 boards, and driving up on them to level our RV as I have done in the past.  One thing keeping me from giving this a a 5 star rating is the lack of UV stabilization.  We are disappointed they were orange and are fading to a lighter yellowish orange color after only 3 weeks of use, obviously from exposure to the sun on the outside edges.  I hope they wont be continuing to degrade, as usually the "chaulking" or dusty look follows fading, which leads to cracks and eventual disintegration. If this is the case, then it is far too expensive for blocks that provide less than a year of service.
summary: Great product but fading in less than a month?...

reviewText: These work fine....  Nest together fine.  Be sure to only try and drive your trailer up one at a time.  If you try and drive up two stacked, then they slide on pavement.  When they slide the do abrade, but not badly.  I would buy more, in fact I did!  They are great for leveling.

The Tri Lynx company has given RVer's many options to level and stabilze most every part or nearly any RV.  The only limit is your creativity.  This is a 10 pack of 9"x9"x1" (thick) levelers. If that sounds like alot, it's not.  I have 4 of these...for a total of 40 levelers.  And I've come close to using them all.  I would recommend buying at least 2 of these to start.Having camped for years I've seen some really aweful and frankly dangerous leveling inovations.  Everything from 2x8s to concrete and even bumper jacks.  These are needless to say MUCH safer.  Because of their modular nature they conture to the slope or even a curve in slope of the pad.  For safety's sake I'll say the following even though I don't think I need to.  These should never be over the edge of a pad, never bridging a hole, and no tire (particularly in dual wheel axels should be unsupported.  I say this only because I've seen it.There are 3 basice things these can be used for.  Trailer leveling (via) tires, stabilzer jack (extension), and a base pad for tongue jacks.  All have caveats and added equipment...  First- axel leveling.  For this you should also have in your arsinal the Tri-Lynx Stop n' Chock.  The levelers will be stacked in an alternating and interlocking "brick wall" form (like the stock photo) then the Stop n' Chock will lock into the rear to prevent your rig from rolling of the rear.  With a little planning, you can level both the front and rear axels of a tandem trailer.  As well as have different heights on either side of the trailer.  For Class A and Class C users, these can be stacked side by side for dual real wheel con figurations.  No matter your rig nor your pad, with enough of these, you should be able to level any or all of it's tires without issue.  Next- using with stabilizer jacks.  I think a must have is the caps for the tri-lynx levelers.  I've read reviews where the tops of the levelers were damaged from the pad of a jack.  The leveling caps will prevent this by giving a smooth top surface to set a jack pad on.  The instructions say never go higher than 5 levels but under jacks I feel perfectly safe with 10...assuming the trailer is chocked securly.  Finally- tongue jacks or landing gears on fifth wheels.  Again an absolute must is the lynx caps.  Furthermore, your tongue jack should have it's own pad or foot on it.  Just the shaft (that many people use) is too small a footprint to dispurse the weight and could easily crack the cap of the lynx levelers themselves.  With these I would not go more than 5 inchs high.  There's a lot of weight and torque pulling in the direction of the slope of the trailer.  It could destablize the stack in the worst case scenario if stacked too high.I've reviewed other "leveling chalks" that are by far cheaper and work well.  However, you can't beat the versatility of these.  The PROS to these are assuming you have enough and the required accessories, you can level just about any rig in any situation.  The CONS are cost.  As I said I have 4 of these "10 packs".  If you intend to use them for jack stabilzing and wheel/axel leveling you should that many as well.  For all of that plus the "Stop n' Chocks" and the 4 pack of leveler caps you looking at somewhere in the $200 range.  Still if your only going to get one type of leveler, this is the one I would recommend.  And if your still on the fence...remember how much you spend in gas getting your rig to and from is destinations.  Getting there then finding out you don't have what you need would be roughly the same cost in wasted gas as investing in this now.

What can I say. Quality product. Better than carrying block of wood. Love them and use them for 2 years now and use them everytime we go caping. Stack them out and simply drive up over them.  Have 3 sets now.
summary: Very sturdy and ease to stack

reviewText: I've had these for a year and bought 2 sets of them.  I use them to support the tongue, tires and, jacks.  Getting ready to order another set because of leveling tires at times I'm short a few.  The only wear of these are from the sun.  I have not experienced any of them chipping or breaking.
Very sturdy and well built.  Buy the chocks that work with these to chock the side of the trailer that is raised with the levelers.  Works great.
summary: Easy and effective with the companion chocks

reviewText: you are paying a lot for plastic bricks but they really come in handy. started by buying 1 pack and figured out quickly i needed another. use them on the stabilizers, tongue jack and under the wheels.
These are convenient light weight and makes leveling the travel trailer easier by driving up on to them when needed.  Pleased with the purchase so far.

I used them for landing gear support and at the back supports for my 38' 5th wheel trailer along with the cap pieces by the same company. Some of the ones under the landing gear cracked immediately when weight was applied. I was shocked. As for the ones in the rear of the trailer, I used four of these with a cap piece. There is simply to much give in them. Not stable at all. I took them out and used concrete blocks. I give them two stars because of the handy bag they come in. I would not recommend this product.
Better than wood blocks. Lighter, stackable, and comes in handy carrying case. easy to stack to get the right height needed for leveling.
These levelers work great, especially if you're camped on unlevel surfaces. Coupled with the chocks, they make leveling a snap.
This was my 2nd set of levelers.  They work well and when not used for leveling they make great leveling jack stands.
These work as intended. I have only had to use them a few times but have been pretty happy overall. Much better and more reliable than the wooden blocks I used to use.
Could've saved the money, cut 2x6's work just as well. They are nice and none have broken yet. Big boy legos.
these square orange blocks work great and are very light.  We use these orange lynx every trip to level the camper, just wish the earth was flat.

I have a 32' Ford Triton egnine (heavy) Class A. Used the blocks under both front wheels on gravel and they worked very well. No damage to the blocks at all and quite easy to set up and use - I ordered more (one package as has been stated won't be enough).6/13 The longer I have these the happier I am with them!Larry

These appear to be as well-made as other brands of plastic RV leveling blocks. Amazon's price was slightly higher than Walmart's when I bought mine. They work under the tires to compensate for uneven campsites and under my hydraulic leveling jacks to extend their range and/or prevent them from sinking into soft ground or damaging soft asphalt in summer heat. Kept clean, they won't mildew or hold dirt and moisture like blocks of wood, weigh less and they come in a handy zippered bag for neat storage. I haven't yet broken any of them.Unfortunately the splashy advertising on the box touting a 3 year comprehensive warranty is a joke. Once you unpack your purchase you discover that in order to file a warranty claim, you must ship the broken or cracked block prepaid to Irving, Texas along with a check for $5.00 for "shipping and handling." Considering that Amazon's price per block is about $3.70, paying to ship a broken block plus sending a $5.00 payment means that a warranty claim costs more than twice the original purchase.
summary: Good Value But the Warranty is a Bad Joke

reviewText: We use these for leveling (role tires up onto stack) and also for pads under leveling legs, steps and front tripod.
I love the lynx leveler Blocks and the storage case, they are light and so easy to use.  You do need several sets to have enoughfor sufficient leveling.

Tri-Lynx 00015 Lynx Levelers, (Pack of 10) This is my second set ...guess I could of updated my other purchase ..but I didn't ...They work for me .. light weight but strong ..I ordered the caps with the first set and been happy with them ..They do fade pretty quick ..but I didn't buy them to look at ..they just work and not had any problems breaking or bending ..I needed another set for uneven ground ... I had to use wooden boards I carry  in a pinch but would rather use these they are so easy and light ... if I find I need more ..I'll buy another set ...looking forward to a day when I don't have to drag out the boards ..lol

Better in every way than 2x6 wood ! We traveled the entire US for our first RV trip. From friend's advice, bought these and took a bunch of 2x6 and 4x4's as well. After 4 months we came home, and I bought another one of these sets and got rid of the wood. They are lighter, plenty strong enough, and interlock unlike wood. They don't soak up water and you can easily knock mud off of them. I feel sorry for all the people I see in RV parks using crazy pieces of wood and rocks to level. I'm sure they think I wasted my money since I could just use scrap junk like them, but these are just much more solid when stacked and really light.
summary: Better in every way than 2x6 wood !

reviewText: I bought these to supplement my existing leveling blocks for my 31' Class C motor home. They work as advertised and are one of those essential products that you hate to buy, but always need. For me, the bag is pointless but others may like it.
Used these for a 2 month cross country trip, very handy, very easy to use.  Bright orange so you don't forget them as well.  Stores easily in a nice stackable fashion.
summary: Easy to use, easy to store

reviewText: I bought two as I have tandem axles on my travel trailer and they have worked out great. I have a solar panel on top and it needs to pointed toward the sun or at least straight up, but absolutely not away from the sun. The design of the leveling blocks allows me to fine tune the height of the leveling blocks to ensure that the solar panel is not pointed away from the sun and that the sinks and shower drain properly as well.

I have been using these for a year with my double axle toy hauler. In the past i used good old wood planks cut from 2x8's but they took up a lot of space, so decided to give these a try. i feel that they must have the design all wrapped up and patented so its hard for another company to provide competition. I looked into the Camco's but i decided against them due to some people reporting them failing(crushing).ProsLight weightFully adjustableEasy stackingConsPrice1 set of 10 isn't enough for a double axle trailerThe carrying bag sucks. The stitching has unraveled in a couple areas, and the zippers teeth wont stay locked together. I gave up on the bag and tossed it in the garbage.
summary: Works much better and more versatile than wood planks, but costly.

reviewText: These work as described, seem sturdy, and come with a decent bag to store them in.  The Lynx Leveler Caps really should be standard equipment however, especially if you intend to use these as contact points for your stabilizers.  The ridges and gullys of this product do not make for a clean surface area for stabilizer pads without the caps.
summary: Excellent product - leveler camps should be standard with these however

reviewText: We travel in a 36' fiver and we use these exclusively now.  We have thrown away every piece of wood we used to level and stabilize our camper with.  You can build them in any shape height or size you need,  they take up very little space inside our trailer.  I haven't broken any yet and use them every time we camp.  I have 3 sets in the camper.I only have 2 complaints.  The storage bag is very light weight and can develope a hole very easily.  Also I think they should come with the caps to make the blocks flat, but you have to order them seperatly.  That is the reason I gave them 4 stars.

Any travel trailer, pop-up, or 5er should carry one or two sets of these.  You can also buy chocks that work with these.  They are strong and much lighter than blocks of wood for leveling your camper.  I recommend these for ease of use.
I use this mainly for my stabilizers, I use this for every camping trip.  Nice color so you don't leave them behind.
Bought these to replace a set of the yellow colored brand levelers. These are less brittle and stack better than the others
These levelers are ok they work and they are good for solid ground. you can level rv a little bit at a time. they do sink if the ground isn't solid
I have not used the as of yet, but they Iook like they will do the job they were made for. Package and deleivery was spot on.

I have two bags of these now, a must for every rv'r 10 of them come in a reusable bag. They fit together to prevent slipping apart with the load on them, and you can get other wheel chock fittings that will snap in these too. It beats carrying blocks of wood around..

We already have one pack of 10 of these levelers but found that we might need more so I ordered another set so we can have them on hand for our RV trips in case of a severely un-level parking pad!  We used them on our last RV trip and loved them.  No wood to have to carry everywhere you go!  Great product and would recommend!
summary: We love these Levelers for our RV...

reviewText: These blocks are great because they can be adapted to most any situation.  The bag is very convenient.  The only drawback is that they fade pretty quick.  Not a big deal, but something that may bother some.  As a bonus, the kids enjoy building with the blocks that are not being used.
These are great leveling blocks that work perfectly with the Tri-Lynx 00018 Lynx Stop 'N Chock Interlocking Wheel Chocks.  These can also be used as pads for the stabilizers on my trailer!
Makes wiring the horn so much simpler!. Highly recommended!

If you're gonna install an air horn on your bike, then I highly recommend this product.  It was simple to install with the instructions.  It comes with everything you need.  Don't buy the other imitations on Amazon, because this one is the best.
summary: Must have for air horn install!

reviewText: This is a high quality harness.  I ended up modifying it a bit so I could retain the use of the stock horn.  However, the time it saved me was worth what they charge.  I am happy I bought it.

Had this horn still in package for nearly a year as didn't think i could fashion a workable wiring harness for it.  Now when i saw this product i flipped and ordered it.  Looks kinda intimidating but it isn't. Its really fairly simple. Take your time, step by step (only 3 or 4 steps) and it installs with few hitches. Place it right the first time and thats it. Fit on my bike wth one inch to go. Perfect fitment...
summary: Have exact horn as in picture.

reviewText: I have continued to purchase these harnesses simply because they come with a full compliment of hardware that may be needed for your wiring project. I have used these harnesses to connect Stebel Horns to various motorcycle applications.  The kit comes with a relay, fuse, connectors, wiring.  A little wiring know how is also helpful, but this kit helps remove quite a bit of guesswork.  Good product.

I wondered about the value of this wiring harness, but I purchased it anyway.  I was glad I did. It saved at least two hours on the installation. The length was perfect for my Honda VT750. All I did was plug it in and connect it to the battery. Great product. Recommend it highly.
Buy it and make your life a whole lot easier. A little pricey can create your own and save a few dollars but really this is the safe and easy way to go. Worth the money.
Works just like its supposed to. Good product. I have used this to clear off surfaces I want to paint and windows I wanted to put decals on.
summary: Works just like its supposed to

reviewText: I got this along with some of the Dupli-Color prep wipes to clean the surfaces for painting. I've already commented on the wipes and it's pretty much the same thing here. Dupli-Color paints are great but the wipes and this prep spray are no different from any paint prep solvent out there so you're simply paying for the name here. It works great but so does a lot of others that cost less. So there is nothing wrong with this product, I just can't see paying for 2, 3 or 10 cans of this to get the prep job done when you can go with a much cheaper quart or gallon of acetone and some cheese cloth to do the same job. Save some money and get the prep cleaner you need elsewhere for cheaper.
This product really cleans but you need to be careful with it. If you try to clean fresh paint ( enamel couple of days old) with it, it will start to remove the fresh paint.
summary: Good prep product but be careful

reviewText: I guess it is a good remover because it did remove the wax from my paint before painting it.  A good choice.

I spray paint a lot of things, cars, bikes, jetskis, plastics, fabrics and stuff around the house. This Prep Spray might work if there is only light grease and certain types of waxes but does not work all the time on all surfaces. I would say it works about 30% of the time, the rest of the time requires more intense cleaning, scrubbing, sanding or even sandblasting. If the surface you are painting has been waxed or contaminated with oil, this Prep Spray will probably not do the job. I really expected more from a Duplic-Color product meant to clean surfaces before painting.
Works OK but no better than Dawn dish soap or many other spray cleaners that are less expensive. Save your money.

The towels are very nice and soft only problem is that these are more for washing than wiping things. Highly recommend washing them before use. The "feathers" of the towel will come off and it gets kinda of annoying to see feathers on my car or flying around me. These do soak up a lot of water and gets the job done but not the towels I was looking for.2 stars because it's a great buy but if your looking for microfiber towels that dries+washes like I was, stay away from these.
I purchased several different brands of microfiber towels and these were the least expensive but are the softest and most durable of the bunch.

These are very soft towels that are great for washing/drying cars. I used mine right out of the package so I also had a few pieces of lint on the car after using it to dry it, but this is not a big deal. I am confident that washing the towels first would eliminate this problem. I highly recommend them.
summary: Very soft and high quality towels.

reviewText: I originally used these to buff off wax on my cars, but felt they did an ok job of it.I then tried them out using ONR (Optimum No Rinse) and really like it for that purpose.I would use 3-4 of these in a bucket of ONR solution and get my car washed and cleaned.Once I was done I just toss em into the washer til next time.I also originally bought these to use with a spray wax but felt it absorbed too much product therefore wasted my wax.I thought these would help me dry my cars after a traditional hose and bucket wash...but it did not seem to suck up water too good.

Really thick, really soft towels.I would use these for waterless washes, wax removal, or even was a wash media.However, these towels do lint a lot. Perhaps it is due to their long fibers, but I noticed lots of lint on my car after I use these. They do not lint as bad when I use them when wet or damp such as when I perform a waterless wash on my car.I use Blackfire Microfiber cleaner and dry on low heat so I am sure it is not "me" who may cause the linting.

This is the worst piece of crap ever. I was always warned about buying the gimmicks on tv. It didn't do what it stated it would do, I did better cleaning my windows with window cleaner and a regular microfiber cloth. This was a waste of my money and time buying this piece of crap.

My wife bought the Windshield Wonder Car Glass Cleaner on a whim, and much to our surprise they work very well. We had been using using paper towels and Windex, but that ever really worked too well. Using these leaves the windows clean and streak free.I also like the long reach provided by the handle also makes cleaning the window of our mini-van much easier as it is very deep and hard to reach by hand.This works! Recommended!CFH

An amazing little tool to clean windows. I used it to clean my auto windshield interior. It turned a laborious, awkward task into a simple 5 minute chore. The result was nothing short of perfect! Worth the price!

I don't know what it is about the inside of a car windshield, but until I tried this product nothing worked to clean it. I would use paper towels and Windex. That didn't work. I would try using a different glass cleaner with paper towels and with new white cloths. That didn't work either. No matter what I did; my windshield would always end up having streaks on it. When the sun was at a low angle; the streaks were so distracting that it was hard to get a good view of the road. That's when I purchased this item at Walmart. My 2009 Camry has a very angled windshield, making it especially difficult to clean. With this device; you simple snap the arm piece together, put the cloth pad on, spray it with water, than run in down the length of your windshield. You then repeat the process until the whole window is clean. It takes just a few minutes and it really works. All the streaks are gone. The only reason why I rate this 4 stars, instead of 5, is because it's cheaply made and mine broke after a few uses. Maybe I was pressing too hard, but if I didn't; it probably wouldn't have worked very well. I've since replaced this with Windshield Master Microfiber Reach & Clean, which is basically the same thing. I don't know whether or not it will last any longer, as it too is made of inexpensive plastic, but for now it does the job. If you're sick and tired of trying to get the inside of your windshield clean, either one of these products will work and will also save you a lot of aggravation. Just be prepared to replace them when the plastic breaks.
summary: Absolutely awesome, but don't expect it to last long.

reviewText: This product is a wonderful Idea, and works like a charm.  One problem I noticed early was that the head did not attach firmly to the extension handle (I do not know why the handle is removable, the whole point of this product is to reach hard to get to areas on windshields without straining).  As a result, the head would make a loud snapping sound from time to time while in use, and would sometimes even fall off.  Finally one day while using it, the plastic handle split in two and broke.  The results of this product are wonderful, the windows in my car had never been cleaner, but the product is of horrible quality.  There are other, more quality, options out there.

Finally I have a product that allows me to reach all areas of the inside of our windshields, all the way down to the bottom where I could hardly reach, and even under the rear view mirror. I do enjoy clean windows.For some reason all new cars seem to produce a film inside the windshield and it doesn't take long to form. This product provides a quick and easy way to get rid of that film. I will use on the inside of the windows only to keep the micro fiber cloths as clean as possible. I've used water and so far it seems to work fine.I think the product would be better if the handle were a single piece. The design isn't the best and the two parts don't fit together as well as they might. I feel as if I have to be careful and can't apply as much pressure as I'd like for fear of breaking the handle.Good idea, good price, but the replacement covers are expensive.Given the questionable design and expensive covers I might look at the Glass Master Pro here [...] It doesn't have many reviews, is more expensive, but the covers are cheaper and you get six with the product. I couldn't tell if the handle was a single piece or if it too was plastic or metal. Just an alternative.
summary: Could be improved but not bad

reviewText: I use this to clean of the inside of the windshield of my A class RV.  Makes it easy to reach all the glass without stretching.
Works great ,gets smoke or fog off windshield  so I can really see now.Product Is made very good, two pads, wash one ,use one.

I was complaining about how it is impossible to clean my rear window to a friend.  She bought me a silly looking microfiber cleaner thing that you just use a spray of water (the Windshield Wonder)."As seen on TV"...eeek.  I was extremely skeptical.But I used it yesterday for the first time... AND IT WORKS.  I can't believe it!  Somehow it is able to remove that plastic residue haze that forms on glass from all the plastics.  And it did it easily and I only used water.I really don't understand how it is possible for it to work; one would think it would just push the contaminates around and/or not even dissolve them with just water.  I would love to know if it works this well for other people too.

I bought Windshield Wonder because I always struggle to clean that front slanting windshield and the side passenger windows of my minivan.  Windshield Wonder does the job.  It comes with two pads, one to wash and one to use.  It also comes with a little bottle to fill with water.  This is so much better than using window cleaner and paper towels.The wand is long enough for me to reach every nook and cranny.  The head swivels as I wipe.  I use a scrubbing motion.  The water works amazingly well and my windows have never looked better.  After cleaning, I just take the pad off and toss it in the washer.Some of those made for TV products are iffy, but this one really works.
summary: Finally, something I've been searching for!

reviewText: Works well. Available for as little as $7.95.  My second one.  The first one broke at the junction on the handle but was easily fixed with electrical tape. I taped the second one, for my wife, before use.  I would buy a stronger one but have not seen any.
While this product does make it easier to get to some of the hard to reach places of the inside of a windshield, the cloth is too thin and overall to small to effectively clean.

This is like the Swiss Army of snow brushes. It's got an ice scraper, brush that sweeps or converts to a broom that pushes snow, and it's even got a squeegee! Wiper fluid frozen? Put some in a spray bottle and squirt it on your windshield then squeegee it off with this bad boy. The cherry on top of the already mind blowing sundae? This thing is telescopic which makes it great for storing in my car (I have a Juke so space is limited). I watch my coworkers struggle to get snow off their car while I switch this into a broom and just push all the snow off in a minute. Cannot say how much I love this thing.
summary: Why are there even other brushes?

reviewText: A very good size for a compact or hitch back car, the handle extension locking handle is fine.. for sure it will be short for a mini van.

I wanted a compact snow brush that could be put in my trunk or under a seat. This worked great because it telescopes in and the brush head swivels. I had no problem with the locking/extending mechanism, it may not be horribly intuitive, but it's very easy to use once you figure it out. You just have to hold the shaft and turn the center black part. The head also swivels easily, and holds strong in either position. I've pushed show off my cars a couple dozen times with this, the bristles are soft and it works well. The ice scraper is pretty much standard, you'll have to give it some force and use your defroster, but it works as well as any other ice scraper I've ever had.
summary: Held up a very harsh northern winter

reviewText: I purchased one of these because every time I buy something related to snow removal, such as a snowblower, we end having a mild winter with little snow. It's less expensive than moving to Florida. Seriously, although it hasn't snowed yet, I can tell by the sturdiness of this product, that it will definitely hold up under any type of snow. It's extremely well made and easy to use. It even comes with a button, so that you can retract the brush when not in use. A 5 star product for sure.
summary: Very well made and useful snow removal brush/scraper

reviewText: Nice size, but I found the center black locking collar for the telescoping handle does loosen very easily, meaning I have to keep tightening it when using. Also, the end with the ice scraper does not do a great job on the ice. I had to grab my old ice scraper only from the garage to clear the ice on my windshield.

Was expecting something a little more substantial.  The tool is rather small, and difficult to hold and use with any force to break a windshield.  The cutter is useful, but is basically a straight blade held in the plastic two part handle.The entire tool is about the size of a utility knife, and basically constructed like one, only out of thin plastic instead of metal.It is compact, and therefor somewhat useful in an extreme emergency, but I wouldn't rely on it as my first choice if a larger, sturdier version made by a competitor was handy.Spend the extra money and buy the better one if you are a corner worker or need this for other than a once in a million chance need.
summary: Too small, cheaply made, but still useful

reviewText: I just hope I never need to use it.  Just in case I purchased one for every car.  All three of them.

For a tool I hope to never have to use, this thing seems great. Small enough to fit in my center console so both myself and front seat passenger have easy access. It's weighty enough to seemingly break windows without too much force needed (note: I haven't actually tested this, nor do I plan to).For under ten bucks, this seems like a no brainer to have in your car, "just in case".
summary: Compact, weighty, a no-brainer to have in car.

reviewText: Can't go wrong with this product.  It's affordable and high quality.  I bought 3 of these [One for me, my mom, and dad].  If your car ever goes into the water try to immediately open your windows and doors; If you wait 5 seconds it could be too late; The water pressure makes it so you cannot open the doors and makes it so the windows can't go down; That's when you need this tool.  I also bought the reqme The Original Keychain Car Escape Tool, Made In USA (Black) to put on my keychain (in case I am in a friends car and go into the water).

You do hope you never need one of these, but planning ahead could mean the difference between life and death.  This is a small price to pay for peace of mind.  Just make sure you keep it between the seats and not in the glove compartment so you can reach it if you need it.  And keep one in each car.
summary: You hope you never need one

reviewText: Razor is sharp and can cut thru the seatbelt, however after watching some videos on youtube that showed this fail to break, i decided to head out to the junkyard and find an old window that wouldn't be missed.  Glass may eventually break if struck hard enough in the right spot but i wasn't able to break the window and believe me it wasn't for lack of trying.Def consider purchashing a more reputable item like the ResQ Me or a knife will a HARDENED carbide tip as this just doesn't seem to do the job.

After a famous News Anchor died in her car from drowning in a small NJ pond, I purchased the window breaker for both our cars.They really are a life saver in many emergency situations. I keep mine in the back pocket of the front passenger seat for easyaccess.
summary: It is a necessity for your car or truck

reviewText: While on a trans-Atlantic ferry trip I accelerated accidentally which launched me and my car into the Atlantic Ocean. I sank to a depth of approximately 12,000 feet before hitting the bottom of the ocean with a thud. I thought I was a goner!.Just as I was saying my final prayers and begging that I would receive my eternal reward from Christ a glimmer of glorious orange light caught my eye. Mine escape device. Hallelujah, no prayer for entry into heaven required. I went this mother out, reared my arm back and let go with a haymaker which instantly shattered the window and set me free. If I had known how cold the water was going to be I would have just stayed in the car and expired. That no longer being an option I waited for water to fill the car and swam out of the window. While I wanted to stop and admire some of the deep sea creatures which I had never seen I decided to be prudent and head to the surface.About five minutes later I reached the surface and breathed a sigh of relief. Not needing the device anymore I chunked it into the ocean. Looking back I wish that I had not done that because it will probably rust in the salt water.Unfortunately by the time I reached the surface the ship was long gone. I had to tread water in the South Atlantic for four more days until a passing airliner spotted me and radioed for help. I think that this device would be even more useful if it included an inflatable raft and a radio transmitter.I am so happy that I had one of these. It saved my life!
works great fast shipping

Griots has numerous products for which they really ought to be lauded and recommended.As a professional Auto Detailer (who has spent, and therefore blown, THOUSANDS of dollars testing products), I simply cannot do withoutGriot's Garage 11104 Interior Cleaner - 35 oz.,Griot's Garage 11040SP Leather Care Spray - 8 oz.; or (and especially!) theirGriot's Garage 11173SP Vinyl and Rubber Dressing - 8 oz., which is -- hands down -- the most superior product on the market for dressing and protecting one's interior vinyl, rubber and plastic components. (I have purposefully linked the smallest, lowest cost product offerings for you to test for yourself).That being said, Griot's Undercarriage Spray is... well, it's garbage, really. And "garbage" is not a word I use lightly as a pro detailer.1.) It will, in fact, re-color one's under-carriage and wheel wells... for about as long as it takes to drive through a hard rain and all the water left on the road from such a soaking.2.) It smells AWFUL of petrochemicals: DO NOT use this product in your garage or any sort of confined space: you WILL get the mother of all headaches.3.) Holy Moses, is this stuff EXPENSIVE for what it is and what it does: which is true of a lot of Griot's stuff. I need not say this to most people, but just in case: buy the PRODUCT, not the hype behind it. Further, trust the reviews of those that are probable to know better.The truth is this: ANY spray tire dressing will work as well (and likely better) as Griot's Under Carriage Spray for reconditioning one's wheel wells (which is what most people buy this product for).Here's a free tip: most tire dressings are silicone-based and are therefore very heavy. When squeezing the trigger, give your wrist a fairly quick flick in the direction you are spraying to minimize running of the product.AJBest-Auto-Detail.com
summary: Review From A Professional Auto Detailer

reviewText: I purchased Griot's garage Speed shine / glass clay / paint clay on a recommendation of a auto enthusiasts forum I follow. I have been using paint clay on my car for a number of years (using Mother's products), but this was my first experience with glass clay. I used Griots Speed shine in combination with clay and the combination worked very well. The deposits on the glass were removed without cleaving streaks and without too much work on my part.Speed shine has almost no scent, provides good cleaning and and a good surface for the clay to glide on. I enjoyed working with it.I am attaching a collage of 2 photos under customers photos on the main page, and will be referencing the photos by the unique numbers that each photo was labeled with.The 35 oz bottle is fairly large, photo #1 has it next to a ruler for relative size. The sprayer worked well - a nice generous even spray. Photo #2 shows how much I used during one cleaning during which I only used it for claying the windows, I did not use it on the body of the car. I was a bit surprised how much I used in one application.Thumbs up overall!Ali Julia review
summary: Excellent cleaning, works great with clay

reviewText: There was this glue/gum/tree sap looking spot on my hood. I tried washing my car twice and wasn't able to remove it. I even tried to scrape it off with my nails but was unsuccessful and turned into a white smudge instead.  Not very pretty on a black car. I thought there was nothing left I can do but was lucky enough to have Griot's Bug and Smudge removal product. I washed my car for a 3rd time and after I dried it, I sprayed a little bit onto the spot. The directions tell you to not use on a hot surface but unfortunately, the weather was warm and I was eager to see if Griot's Bug and Smudge would work. After about 10-15 seconds of soaking, I used my micro fiber towel to rub it gently. Needless to say, after spraying it a few more times and with gently rubbing, the gum was removed leaving my paint finish just fine. I've only heard good thing about Griot's car care but never got the chance to use it. I am very impressed.Car specsBlack - Coupe - 2002

Like all Griot's Garage products, Griot's Garage Bug and Smudge spray is an excellent product that works well and is safe on surfaces.  Bug and Smudge spray is used as a pre-treatment to remove bug residue, rubber marks and general road grime.  It is sprayed on and it softens the substance for easier removal by washing.  Equally important as being effective, it is safe.  Griot's Garage products are among the few brands that I trust completely when it comes to cleaners.  Some over the counter brands sold in auto part stores can be too harsh or even caustic in some cases (e.g. some brands of wheel cleaners).  I always trust Griot's Garage products and use nearly every form of cleaner and dressing that they sell.  The only downside is that they are on the expensive side.
summary: Great Like All Griot's Garage Products

reviewText: Griot's Garage Bug and Smudge remover works great on dried on bugs and bird poop on your car's finish, but it does not remove tar from the roads.  I have two convertibles which I baby from the outdoor elements constantly.  This Bug and Smudge remover worked great for removing dried bugs and bird dropping without leaving a residue or stain prior to washing the cars.  All you do is spray, let it fit a few minutes then wipe off.  I avoid hitting non flying items, so I can't comment how it works on smudge marks.However, tar was not as easy to remove.  Maybe Griot's is not made to remove tar since it states it removes "bug and smudges".  This was a bit of a disappointment since my BMW Roadster Convertible sits really low to the ground and the front end picks up everything from the road, especially the new tar being laid in the early Spring.  It would of been nice to use one spray to remove all the contaminants, but I still have to use a tar remover separately.
summary: Works great on bugs and bird droppings

reviewText: Does what it should do. It is not sticky, it is not slippery but seems to improve the appearance of vinyl and rubber in the car.  I use it both inside and out.

To the extent I used it, this wax produced results that are no better than you can get from many other products. I never did do my whole car with it because, applied according to instructions using the Griot's random orbital machine, this wax was ridiculously difficult to remove. After some experiments with application technique, I decided there was no point in hassling with it and went back to my Meguiars. To add injury to insult, Best In Show Wax is a non-returnable product. Now I've got most of a $20 bottle sitting uselessly in my basement. This may be my first 1-star review, but at such a price it's got to be the worst value in car wax I've ever encountered.
summary: Way overpriced and difficult to use

reviewText: Good stuff as always from Griots, you can adjust the amount of shine you want on your tire, by varying how many coats.  Lasts pretty well, but on the expensive side.

For year I've used Turtle Wax "Zip Wax" wash & wax.  My local store was out of this, so I thought I'd give Griot's Garage Wash & Wax a try.  I use many of their products & have been happy with the product performance.The Pros:+ $11.97 here, compared to $9.99 on the Griot's Garage website, but the shipping is free here!+ Nice scent, a plus if you have to have your hands in it!+ Leaves behind a layer of protection (wax) as it cleans.+ Gentle soap with high lubricity.+ 1 ounce per 1 gallon of water.The cons:- $11.97 for 16 ounces seems a bit high to me.- We use two 3 gallon buckets when we wash a vehicle, so that means less than 3 washes per bottle! :(Closing thoughts...If I continue to use Griot's Garage wash & wax, I'm going to buy the gallon (128 oz) size, which costs $44.99 + free shipping!

reviewText: I had purchased those bug and tar remover by the Turtle company before and that didn't work good, so I had my doubts with this one.WOW! Amazing product, I tried this without water just spray and wipe and it cleaned well, it removed the bigger bugs and dirt seamlessly.  I didn't want to rub too hard on the paint so I did it right before washing the car, there was still some bugs but the bird poop wiped right off!As for washing the car, the Griot's Bug and Smudge made my job easier, I sprayed the bumper with the hose and most of the bugs just washed away, I just had to lightly scrub the rest off.Overall, super happy, highly recommended.

I really couldn't be much happier with the results. It is a great product. I have used it on 2 cars and still have a bunch of it left. The polish works very well, takes out the minor imperfections very well. The sealant seems to work well. Feels smooth as glass and seems to hold up over time as well. Wouldn't quite say a year as they say but I wouldn't trust any product that long.I used it on a friends car that was severely neglected... used dish soap for car washing.... so we properly washed it and clayed it then broke out the Griot's Garage polishing machine and used the one-step on it (mostly because I was lazy and didn't want to use a polish, wax, etc.). He was amazed at how quickly it all went and the smooth and shiny finish it left. I was a little surprised as well, considering the car is 7 years old and had never seen a real car wash outside of rain.....Not my primary sealant but for lazy days or when I just want it done quick this is GREAT stuff. Well worth the price. Goes on easy and comes off pretty easy. Not sure how it would do by hand though.

reviewText: It's a decent wax, there's just much better out there in terms of application, removal, and appearance. By the time I had waxed my entire car I did the "finger-swipe" test and it showed the wax was ready to come off. Using a quality Cobra polishing microfiber I went to remove the product. It was MUCH more difficult than the other waxes I have used (Pinnacle, Collinite, etc). I used some Griot Speed Shine to help with removal and that helped.  After all that elbow grease, I was hoping for a little more of a shine. The scent isn't pleasant either. On the hot days following the waxing I could still smell it.
summary: It's OK, better are out there.

reviewText: I'm not a fan of quick detailers as a rule, but I need them when I use a claybar.  If you like using quick detailer in between car washings I think you like this as well. This is a good deal.  You get a lot of product for the money.
summary: A lot of detailer for the money.

reviewText: Spray on wash is used after you wash the car and before you dry it. Just a little spray on wax makes drying so much easier and gives the car a nice smooth, just waxed feeling. Then the next time you go to wash you can see the results. Water beads up on the car like it has just been waxed. If you have never used Griot's products and you like taking care of your car, there are no better waxes and car care products on the market. Big believer in their products. I have a 2003 Jeep Grand Cherokee with original paint and we get compliments on it's shinny paint all the time. People want to buy it. Same with a 2001 Toyota pickup with original paint. The pickup shines uncontrollably.Griot's makes some great products.

On the plus side, this comes in nice packaging (doesn't include the sprayer) and smells nice.Unfortunately, it is carnauba-based and doesn't last at all. Think maybe one or two car washes or a month max. Of course, there are some paste/liquid carnauba waxes that only last a month, but there are some that will last several months. My point is that there are better polymer-based spray-on or quick-detailer products out there.This cannot take the place of a proper wax, but it is convenient in that you can spray it on while drying your car and add a little bit of protection until you can use a proper wax.As far as spray on products, there are better products out there if time is what you're trying to save. These include a range of products from Ultima Paint Guard Plus (a wipe-on walk-away paint sealant) to Finish Kare #425 (a spray-on/quick-detailer).In the end, it is OK, but then I knock off a star because it has a pretty bad tendency to streak which takes extra effort and towels to buff off.

I've never used any Griot's Garage products before and never even heard of them before discovering their product line on Amazon.While most automotive vinyl and rubber dressings are expensive it's my opinion that they are not all the same.I took a chance thinking that this product's value based pricing indicates high quality - 10 bucks for 8 oz.The product description,"Leaves surface with a matte or satin finish and non-slick" is what lured me.Greasy, slick dashboards and kick panels don't appeal to me.The spray nozzle has a misting-type action that creates a bit more over-spray than I would like. I like to use a wedge of foam sponge to apply these types of dressings, that way the solution goes precisely where needed. You conserve the dressing this way, which helps make the high price more acceptable to me.This purchase was an introduction to Griot's Garage products. Their product description was true enough.I'm somewhat satisfied - there's an excellent chance I may explore their other products.

The pad I used last year held up for three polishes, but this year's pad broke down after only one polish.  I wonder if it had to do with the fact I used the one-step sealant this year as opposed to separate polish and wax?  I use these with griot's random orbital.
summary: Not as good as last year

reviewText: Not sure this works so great.  I just tried using it to remove scads of bugs on the very low grille on the front of my Scion FR-S.  I read the simple instructions multiple times just to get it right.  But, I have to say that very little junk was removed - some was, but not much.  I even tried a rough-surfaced pot scrubber in spots, but that didn't get much off either.  I was able to clean up a few very small smudge spots here and there around the vehicle; that was nice.  Overall, I won't use it again.

reviewText: This made the car look great! Wax lives up to it's name best of show, easy to apply and wipe off will buy again

I like these pads.  I use them along with a 3" backing plate on my 6"Griot's dual action polisher.  I prefer to use Griot's polishing and waxing pads due to their consistent quality.  Applying wax or polishing with cheap pads makes little sense to me, so I don't mind paying a bit more for the Griot's pads.  They also clean up very will and will last through numerous uses.

I think this was one of the first products I bought from Griot's back in 2003 when I started using their products exclusively.  Before this product, I was using Armor All, Black Magic, whatever Meguiar's had at the time, and a few other auto store brands.All the other products suffered from one problem...they were too shiny and greasy.  The Black Magic actually was the messiest of all of them as it had "plasticizers" in it.Now I want to make one point very clear and that is I believe certain car interiors actually look good with the "Shiny" look that you get from products like Armor All.  There are certain interiors however that should never look "Shiny."  For example, I think cars from the 80's and 90's actually look properly detailed with the shiny look just because of the design and materials from that time.  Picture the interior of a 96 Ford Mustang or a 96 Trans Am. Picture that rubber and plastic and then picture Armor All on it...I think that actually looks pretty good. Modern cars look good with a natural appearance or only a subtle sheen. The Griot's Vinyl and Rubber Dressing is for these cars. Imagine trying to put Armor All on the interior of a brand new BMW or Mercedes; it would make the interior look cheap and unsightly.The Griot's product can be applied with either their blue pad or you can use almost any other foam pad. What I like to do is actually take their blue pad and cut it in half and use just one piece to apply the product so that the sponge does not absorb too much product (As of 2012, Griot's has introduced a mini blue applicator pad which I think is perfect for application of this product.)  If you apply it with a cloth, I think the cloth will absorb most of the product. Griot's offers, or used to offer, these in wipes but I found those to dry out very fast.The Griot's dressing gives your interior a nice subtle sheen without any oily residue and it doesn't attract dust. This is due to the fact that the Griot's product is non-silicone based.  I find that certain interiors show more sheen than others and this is due to the texture of the vinyl or plastic.  For example, this product takes several coats to become visible when I apply it to my BMW dash but when I detail my dad's Toyota, one application is enough to bring that nice sheen.Regarding Tires:I would not use this product on any tires without a smooth sidewall.  If you have a family car, a truck, a minivan, or a vehicle that is equipped with standard all-season tires, skip this product and use Stoner's "More Shine Less Time." IMO, that is the best product to detail "Daily driver" tires.  The Stoner's is easy to apply via aerosol and has the correct amount of shine for these types of tires.  I stopped using Armor All on tires several years ago because it makes the tires look unrealistically wet and I think it looks sloppy; not to mention that it slings all over the place. Also most tires dressings that "Foam" up usually run down your tire and will stain your driveway.  The Stoner's is more controlled and the staining, if any, is minimal.Griot's Vinyl and Rubber Dressing is an amazing product for tires with a smooth-sidewall typically found on performance rubber with thinner side walls; it is also great for vintage tires found on collectible cars. I wouldn't use any other product on a car that I wanted to display or for a competition.  Just remember to properly clean the rubber before you apply this or any other dressing.  With the Griot's product, you don't just spray it onto your tire and leave it.  You spray the product onto your sponge pad and you buff it into the tire.  I would actually make at least two passes.  In the end, the tire should look clean, black, and have a sheen to it.  It took me a while to accept that good tires should never be shiny.  The effect is more understood when your vehicle is properly detailed --including the wheel well area.I want to share the following tip with you...It was brought to my attention that Lexol Vinylex performs similarly to the Griot's product for a fraction of the price.  I haven't tried it out myself but I have this feeling that the Vinylex might recreate the same look of the Griot's based on the fact that some of the dashboards that I have seen with Vinylex don't look shiny and look similar to dashboards treated with the Griot's product. Vinylex is also silicone-free.As far as the Griot's pricing of this product, I have never purchased the 35oz bottle as I think it is too much money.  The 8oz should easily detail the interiors of several cars and their tires.  Personally I just use this product for interiors and I use the Stoner's for all my tires.  I only apply the Griot's to my tires on special occasions as I don't find it cost effective or durable enough for daily drivers.It's a great product, it's unique to Griot's and I find it superior to any other rubber and vinyl dressing currently on the market.  Once you try it, I think you will like the results too.I highly recommend it if you are serious about detailing your car.
summary: How rubber and vinyl should look...Pricey though.

reviewText: I've use this product on our RAV and TACOMA and just love it. It applies and wipes easily and lasts a long time compared to others similar products. Unavailable locally and works great on all painted surfaces.  Groit's seems to have good, quality products no matter which on you buy and use. Excellent offering Amazon...
summary: Easiy to apply and wipe, provides great, lasting shine.

reviewText: Very fast acting cleaner. Gets out stains that have been in my floor mats for a long time. Griot's garage knows their stuff.

The product is intended to use as a spot cleaner or a problem area pre-prep during regular washing. I keep it in the garage to clean up bugs, tar and bird droppings right away before they have a chance bake on and damage the paint. It feels like it has a bit of silicone in it and leaves a slight gloss on the finish. It does a quick job of cleaning up brake dust from wheels too. Does not work well on tar.I also like that it has a light odor and the packaging is a spray pump rather than aerosol.

1.  make sure your surface is as clean as possible.2.  clean these pads as often as possible while using them (i use compressed air and a pad brush).these pads do NOT like to get dirty and they do not like to overheat. The center just disintegrates and foam goes everywhere.I've since switched to lake country pads and have found they are much more durable and more versatile.These are a good beginners pad, but once you figure out how the whole DA polishing thing works, upgrade to better pads.

reviewText: Got for use in my Camaro for the dirty stained carpets and seats. A must have for anyone who likes keeping everything in their car clean!

It does what it says it will and rather quickly. The product says to let it soak for at least 30 seconds before wiping off with a rag or microfiber cloth. reviewText: Does a good job, however, I probably will not buy aging. Smell is nauseating. Does not last too long. Did bring back the black and looked ok. Dirt stuck to well after 1 light application and let dry.

reviewText: Splat! How many times have you smashed a bug on your windshield? Bug juice must be one of the complex biological compositions around because it doesn't just stick to your windows and paint, it attaches like a barnacle. Usually, I rub with a good terry cloth towel and lots of window cleaner to get their sad remains off my car. Works OK but window cleaner also removes wax from the paint so you have to re wax or at least spritz with a quick detailer. Not so with this stuff. Yes, it works well on the glass but it also does the same for the painted surfaces and, if you don't rub too hard, it leaves the wax.As with all Griot's products I have tried, this is quality stuff. The sprayer too is a keeper.Recommended if you drive in bug country!
