reviewText: I love griots products. Use as directed and you will get great results. So far everything I have used has worked out great. I tried this product on some vinyl on my truck that was faded and it has brought back the black color and kept it through a few washes so far. Going to try a larger area soon. Like the results so far.

Have only used to a limited on with polishing compound on 13 year old truck. Seemed to help with prepping the surface for the subsequent waxing. Cleaned up well with Dawn dish detergent. No complaints so far.

These are great I recently purchased the 3 inch griots polisher and man it does all types of cool stuff from waxing/polishing a car to polishing granite counters and windows thiese are great for windows too

Have you ever driven through the state of Louisiana at night?  If you have you know all about thousands of bug splats on the front of your vehicle.  They can be really hard to remove......enter Griot's Garage 10982 Bug and Smudge!  This stuff really works, not perfectly, but good.  Spray it on and let it sit at least 30 seconds and then wipe!  Most of the bugs will be removed after wiping.  It works better than another bug remover product we have used before.  We have never used Griot's Garage products before but will now give them a look.

This is an excellent product.You can use it after you wash the car (for the best results) while its wet or dry.Also if you keep your car clean you can spray it on wet or dry and use as a quick clean in a pinch.

This has been around for a really, really long time so you'd think that someone would've improved on it by then.I've tried a lot of other detail sprays but none work as well as Griot's.I've used this for so many years that the nice smell now makes me nostalgic.
Way better than the other types of draw string pads. Fits nice and does what it was intended to do.
summary: Way better than the other types of draw string pads

reviewText: I have used Griot's Paint Sealant for years, on many vehicles.  Keeps everything protected, from the BMWs I baby to the truck that I take off-road.  Just a little of this product is all you need to achieve a good layer of protection, a deep shine, and an important seal to keep the harsh chemical elements out of your finish. The product buffs off easily with a microfiber cloth and does not require too much elbow grease. It is rare for it to "cake on" or be hard to remove.I have found that with normal (frequent) washing and detailing, this sealant will still provide almost a full year of protection.  I try to apply at least twice per year, and double-coat for winter.
summary: Provides a nice layer of protection

reviewText: Love this product!!! Does a great job of removing break dust and other crud from by bare aluminum wheels. Will be ordering more fore the winter months here in NE PA

My car has painted alloy wheels and I had some serious adhesion when I had to drive the car through some soil that was high in clay content. Nothing would remove it, even with intensive scrubbing. This stuff worked better than anything else I tried.It's not magic - you still need to scrub/agitate the surface, but it works faster than anything out there.

There's really only so much a paint and clear-coat safe liquid can do against baked-in, smushed-in, dried-in bug parts and guts. If you can get to said nastiness before its' had a chance to really settle-in, this stuff does a wonderful job of clearing it out. Even the stuff that's been there awhile has a chance to be obliterated with this good stuff.But you can only expect so much, if the offending critter got really dug in enough that this cleaner can't get it out, then it's likely time to step up to a polish like Meguiar's M205 with some "cut" to it to dig it out...And if that doesn't get it out, then Megs M105 with even stronger "cut".Excellent product, especially if you take very good care of your vehicles' paint protection this stuff works great in conjunction. I'd give it a 5-star but the cost is, in my opinion, excessive. Otherwise, well recommended.

Stumbled on this product by accident. It was on clearance for $5.99 at an auto parts store, clearly marked down in error.Let me start by saying I keep my SUV immaculate, so I know if a product truly works or not, and this does!!!After washing I leaving it wet and go to town with a QUALITY damp microfiber, spraying a panel at a time and wiping. No more big clumsy towels or absorber nonsense, simple 16x16 towel works well. This spray wax gives that just waxed POP we all love. I follow up my drying with a dry mircofiber to buff..Cons:You vehicle MUST be cool, after washing get it put of the sun. It doesn't do well on a hot surface, it will flash very quickly and streak, especially on dark colors.I purchased a gallon only bc it was cost effective. Basically for the cost of 3 24oz bottles, you get 4! Works for me!!
I'm new to the in depth car care world. Always took care of my cars but with this pad and the Griots Polisher, I found a new hobby. This pad stayed together and I have plans on buying the 3 pack.

One of my car cleaning rituals when I got into a detailing mood was to wipe down the entire vehicle withTurtle Wax T-520A Bug and Tar Remover, Trigger - 16 oz.after a preliminary wash, then to apply a paste wax.  Lately, I haven't been as motivated or as satisfied with the results of the Turtle Wax stage as I am convinced the formula was modified to accommodate less durable car finishes and resulted in less effectiveness of the product.With the substitution of this product, I just might find the energy to enact the full process more often.  The Griot Bug and Smudge made removal of a winter's worth of dirt and grime much less of an aggravation and left the car with a sheen that I felt didn't require an application of paste wax thereafter...except on those plastic bumpers which * nothing* seems to get clean entirely, anyway.It might cost three times as much as the Turtle Wax product but it works.
summary: Griot's story of the turtle and despair.

reviewText: I'm not one of those car-care nuts who spends hours polishing their vehicle. Sure, I'd like mine to LOOK like that, but I don't have the time. Besides, keeping a showroom sheen on a mini-van is kind of pointless. That said, we DO spend a lot of time on the road... driving to practices, events, visiting relatives, vacation, etc. You know, living life. A life that does not have much time for car maintenance, but also does not want its car to look like crud.Here's where Griot's Garage Bug and Smudge Remover comes in. Simply spray it on, do something else for a few minutes, then come back and clean it off. The bottle says 30 seconds, but more than that won't really hurt (ok, don't wait 3 days. Be reasonable). But seriously, once you come back and clean it off with a gentle sponge or microfiber cloth and a hose. Just like that, most of the bug guts, road tar, bubble gum, dried-up bird poo, etc., will be gone. It's not a miracle worker, so don't expect bird guts to disintegrate or pine tree sap to melt away. It's not hydrochloric acid. But it does seem to work better than most other products I've tried, and seems gentle enough on the paint job.Once you're done, load in the kids and go get some ice cream, knowing you save some $$ not having to get that stuff detailed off.
I love these products as I stated before really easy to use no scrubbing and you can use it quickly.  But try not to use it when it's to cool you may or may not have problems.
I bought this thinking it was the wash product. Was going to return it but did not. I use it but it does not seem to shine any better than a duster or clean towel.

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I've already used the entire bottle and am hunting for another! I live in Central Florida and twice a year we have love bug season. If you live here year round, you know what that means. These bugs bodies are so acidic that they eat right through your paint. Our cars get covered with them while driving. Since I drive over 100k miles annually, this is quite a problem trying to keep them off because they really stick to the paint. Of all the things I've tried, this is the BEST product. It's very gentle, and after letting it sit on the paint for three minutes (if it's not too hot outside) I use a washcloth and bucket of water with car wash soap. They wipe right off. It takes me only a few minutes to safely remove these. I plan to buy this in it's biggest size, and I've already requested my local parts supplier carry this as well.

Yes. This product works, and it's just as effective as most of the other products out there claiming to do the same thing. For a large swath of the population, this is probably ideal. Spray something on, let it sit, and wipe off the offending contaminant. Those people will probably then wash their car and be done for that week.What those people don't realize is that it's also removed your wax in the area you just used the product. This is fine if you're cleaning your car for a full detail job. However if you're an enthusiast, you're going to clay your car, which is far more effective at removing contaminants down to the paint level. And you now start with the detailing process.Skip the spray, buy some clay and do it right.
summary: There's no magic bullet for bug, oil, or other fallout removal

reviewText: Not just for the car! I use it inside the house too. It is not harsh on things and the smell is neutral. I always use a clean WHITE rag and you can really tell how much you are cleaning up. Sometimes I have to clean a spot a second time after it dries but it doesn't leaving any type of cleaning mark, even on white/off white furniture. I have used it on suede they use on furniture, good results.

I used these pads with my Griot's 3 DA polisher.These pads are soft and small enough to fit an average can of paste wax so i can wax and load up the pads as I go.I can get into all the tighter areas of my vehicles with these smaller pads, highly recommended 3 pk.

Simple, quick review.This works well if your wheels are not very old and very dirty.I had my 94 Camry Wheels ACID cleaned (be careful have a PROFESSIONAL do it).After the wheels are cleaned of the years of brake dust, this will keep them clean.

I usually use this spray-on wax when washing my car between paste waxes.  It helps to keep the hand buffed look last a little longer than washing alone.  The wax can be sprayed on the car after rinsing while still wet.  It adds very little time to the rinsing and drying process and gives a great look.  When I purchased it, it was cheaper to get through Amazon than from Griot's direct.  This is not intended to be the primary wax product - some reviews have said the spray-on wax does not last long, only "one or two car washes."  The spray-on wax is intended as an enhancement and not a substitute for a proper waxing.  I have never had it streak, requiring extra effort to buff off.  I always use this while the car is still wet from rinsing, this seems to work the best and does not result in any streaking in my experience.It's worth noting that this is a gallon size refill.  In order to use this you will need a suitable container.  You can get the 35oz size of spray waxGriot's Garage 11098 Spray-On Wax - 35 oz.and a sprayer such asGriot's Garage 11022 Finest Sprayer.  When the 35oz spray bottle runs empty it's much cheaper to use the gallon refill.

I love my Griot's Garage Random Orbital polisher, and this pad is a great "backup" for when my main one gets dirty.  Easily run under warm water and wring out & let air dry.  During a big project, that's when the spare one comes out to help finish the job!
summary: Always good to have a spare one of these!!

reviewText: Speed Shine is a very good product. I've purchased a lot of products from Griot's Garage and they have good product throughout.
These work great use them on my Griots garage DA with a 3 inch backing plate. Great when applying wax

I applied this product on a black car. I used a Griot's orange pad on a Griot's 6" polisher. I found the product easy to apply and easy to remove. It gave a good finish.  For the price and easy of use I recommend it.  I would also recommend that before you apply it you wash your car and use a good quality clay bar on the paint. This give the best results. The only negative I found is the product did not last as long as Griot's suggests. I got about two months before I felt I needed to reapply.
summary: Easy to use all in one product

reviewText: Works great to buff your vehicle with wax, polishing compound or rubbing compound. Perfect size to get in those hard places a 6 or 8 inch buffer just can't do. Very durable and you can clean them and get many uses out of them.
Griot's products are awesome--including these Red Waxing Pad.  They lasted a lot longer than I thought they would.  I waxed an entire 35foot RV with ONE pad!!
summary: Griot's products are awesome--including these Red Waxing Pad

reviewText: I've found all the Griot's products to be pricey, but absolutely worth that price. They're formulated in a way that doesn't cause damage to your paint job or finish, which is a big thing. This bug-and-smudge formula works really well and I'd absolutely recommend this.

Works great for applying waxes, glazes, or sealants. These don't mar or dull the finish at all. My only complaint is that on a Griots DA polisher the Velcro sticks almost too well and I can tell that after two uses the backing on the foam pad is eventually going to separate from the foam.
summary: Great for waxes, glazes, and sealants

reviewText: I can't believe how well this works and how clean it is. It has literally saved me money on not having to replace rubber parts. Just another Griot's product that is worth the money and does what it says. FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS. They have some of the greatest car products out there.

I have used this a couple times and it seems to work good so far. I really don't have any other pads to compare them to as I just got the machine last summer and I bought the same brand pads. I wouldn't hesitate to buy more when this one wears out.

Like pretty much all of the Griot's Garage products I have used, and that's a lot of them, the Bug and Smudge Remover does what it claims and works well. I tried it on both mashed bugs and on muddy scuffs on my car, and both wiped away after a spritz of the remover. I saw no detrimental effect on the paint or wax.
summary: Works very well, gentle on paint

reviewText: It started off as a joke.  A 1990's era Cherokee chicken coop find.  And they left the windows open!  Well, long story short the interior soon looked like NEW and that isn't an exaggeration.  This product cleans and shines very well.
summary: I'll Buy THis Again.  And Again.  And Again.

reviewText: As someone who does a lot of interstate driving, I can attest to the annoyance of bug accumulation on the windshield and elsewhere. I also live in an apartment, so washing my car involves going to a car wash, which may or may not do a satisfactory job of getting the bug guts off of my car. Griot's Bug and Smudge remover is a great solution. I use it on the tough spots before going to the car wash, and the car always comes out looking great. It's not cheap, but it definitely works.

Griot's Garage is a well known car care & maintenance products manufaturer and sourcer. Their mantra is quality and to this end they produce and/or source very high quality products. They also have some very innovative products like their 'Multi-Fluid Extractor' which makes oil changes a breeze for anyone - even with limited experience.The Griot's Bug and Smudge spray works as advertised - just spray onto bugs or bird-poop on any external surface (it is paint-safe) wait for 30 seconds and wipe off with a lint-free paper or cloth towel. Alternately you can spot-treat the surface just prior to a car-wash for the same results. The Griot's was not successful at removing dried bird-poop that got into my clear coat which was as expected! I have not come across any product that cleans stained clearcoat.The only complaint I have is the cost. It is a great product but at almost 4x the cost of my regular bug and grime cleaner - the Armor All Auto Glass Cleaner, I find it difficult to justify the cost. The Griot's is definitely better than the Armor All but not by that much.Recommended.Pros:* Works well - probably the best in the market* OdorlessCons:* Pricey
summary: Probably The Best Multi-surface Bug Cleaner In The Market

reviewText: Griot sells a buffer that these fit and they are perfectly matched.  I use the orange ones for various levels of polish on my paint and I love how I can get into places on the nose and tail of the car that the 6" pads don't do well with - or do at all.  They also work nicely around wheel arches and my rocker panels that stick out from the body.  Hand polishing is not my thing.  These work great and hold up well - and I'm not easy on them.  Be careful removing them from the hook and loop plate.  If you don't grab the back of the pad down by the connection you'll rip them in half.  I've been using them for about 8 years and they really make it easy to polish out "areas and spots" where I don't want to sit with a bigger 6" Porter Cable or my heavier Flex buffers.I also use the red pads for applying wax in the same spots but like a white pad for less aggressive polishing.Oh yeah, I wore out my old buffer bought at Griot's and they REPLACED IT AT NO CHARGE AND SHIPPED IT FOR FREE!
summary: Perfect polish applicator for the 3" Buffer

reviewText: Bought the GG sealant after spending 30 hours doing a full paint correction on my black car and wanted to protect my paint.After I was done polishing for hours on end I thought, wow,what a shine , then I layed a coat the the Griot's sealant and it took it to another level of shine.It was very easy to put on and wiped off as easy as a wax.It's been a few weeks and still looks amazing , I can tell it will last for many months.You can beat the product are the price.Oh, a bottle goes a long way, I did two trucks and an SUV and still can do about two more.

Here in the humid South bug splatters on cars is a fact of life in spring and summer.  And they can be difficult to remove after they have been dried on for days.  Griot's Garage Bug and Smudge can make it easier to remove those pesky smashed bodies.  For best results you have to let it soak for a minute of two, which is difficult to do when most of the bugs are smashed on angular surfaces of the car.  Aside from holding a rag underneath to keep the spray from running off I haven't found a good solution for that problem yet.  But the product does work, especially if used prior to a good car wash.  My main criticism would be cost.  This is some expensive bug remover.  But if you are having trouble removing smashed bug bodies from your car's finish it will make the job much easier.
I have been a big fan of Sonax, but this works just as well without the strong odor and at  1/3 of the cost.

Been using SpeedShine for 10+ yrs with much success.It is easy to use, and leaves behind a nice natural wax protection and shine.  I use this product so often that my car does not require any more wax since it is my garage queen.

My result using this was not very good. It tends to leave light dried wax residue streaks that you cannot set while drying the car and only notice later. This will promote you to wipe them off, which subsequently can leave more swirls on your car.I think you are better off not using this and just waxing your car normally a little more often.

I'm always trying out new high end cleaning products for my cars. This is the best wheel cleaner I've used yet. The product foams up nice and when it turns red you can start cleaning. As with most Griot's products, it's a little pricey, but it's worth it.
Spray this on your wheels and let it set for 1 minute and it will work its magic and convert your old wheels to new wheels.

This cleaner does fairly well at getting brake dust.  It will not remove hardened brake dust.  One negative is that this product puts purple stains on rotors.  The stains come off once you drive the car.  I will be trying Sonax next.

Makes your car slick and shiny. I use it between waxes. Just spray on and wipe off, nothing special. Also it uses less wipes to become dry. Use it on glass and plastic surfaces. And also your interior.

I have used this on two vehicles.  It worked very well on the curves and dips of each vehicle.  The handle is flexible, and I found that how you hold the handle affects the performance of the blade on curved vs. flat surfaces.  If you want to know how flexible it is, your wife or girlfriend may be able to provide you some good comparison information...:)  I bought this one to replace a very stiff blade.  I can clear a lot more water with this flex blade. I am very happy with this purchase.  This blade will get a lot of use! Like many others, I do miss the purple one from Costco!!

Someone else here also had the same comments:  It's noisy, very annoyingly so, and skips and bounces, leaving trails of water. A real time waster.  Glad to hear it works for some, but didn't for me.  Problem might be too much flexibility, too soft, and the "T" part of the blade itself.  My comparision, Detailer's Choice:  no noise, straight blade, no water trails, a very fast blade.

I have an original California Jelly Blade that I bought from Amazon. I was surprised I couldn't reorder, so looked around and started reading the reviews. I bought a Pilot Automotive CC-2010 and really didn't like it. The handle was too hard and the blade felt short. Frustrated, I tracked down the website that seemed to be for the manufacturer and wrote the following email:"Hi Don,I'm one of many who came to greatly appreciate the original California Jelly Blade, and am looking for a replacement. Every review comparing "Superflex" with the original says it is too flexible. The Pilot ultraflex is no longer available if it ever was. The "Soft-N-Dry" doesn't work well and the handle is too hard for the shower. (I bought one.) The California Car Duster Jelly blade is clearly avoiding the original patents and isn't a "t-bar" blade. Your website has a "gel" version that doesn't appear to be for sale anywhere.My questions:1) Which one is closest to the original original?2) Where can I buy it?3) Why not make one to those specs again?Thanks!Larry"I was pleasantly surprised to find out that Don is the inventor. Here is his reply:"Larry, I quite frankly can't understand people not liking the Superflex that is what i prefer and I designed them all, I have all of them in my garage and I'll grab the Superflex every time. The Gel blade was turned down because of cost, I designed that model as well, however I still prefer the Superflex. Feel free to call if you have questions!!  Don"So I bought a Superflex and it is good, but not quite as good as the original. The handle is right. The length is right. Whew. However, it really is, as some suggested, too flexible. Not a lot too flexible, but just enough that it takes a little more concentration, a little more feedback to use it. Hence the four stars. However, it works very, very well, and is better than the original on curved surfaces such as my car.I believe this is, as Don suggests, the right one to buy. However, I wish it would be just a little stiffer, say halfway between where it is now and the original. Then we're moving forward with this product and I'm not longing for a past product I can no longer buy.
summary: Best replacement for the original Jelly blade but not perfect

reviewText: I found this to work beautifully on the larger areas, not so good on tight places but that is a given. It is soft and supple and really removes the water great. The handle is soft yet firm, good grip. Before I was going through a lot of towels or wringing the chamois a lot. This has prevented that to a very large degree. It also is quick and easy so spots don't have a chance to form. I love it and wish I had bought one earlier.

I tried this out on my minivan a couple days ago.  Now, I wonder why I ever used towels.  One swipe is all it takes.  I went from end to end, back and forth.  My car was dry in no time.  The blade is soft and doesn't scratch.  It flexes around the curves so nothing gets missed.  Perfectionists may want a towel for the nooks and crannies, but I was fine the way it turned out.  I only wish there was a removable handle so I could reach the top of the car.  For anyone who washes their own cars, I highly recommend it.
Product works as claimed.  It does a great job of removing the major part of water after washing cars.  Very soft and unlikely to scratch paint.

I'm sure it works great compared to similar objects. I just don't find this drying method as useful as I thought. You have to swipe it right after you rinse the car while there is still a ton of water or it just streaks. If I wait a few seconds, most the of the water runs off my car anyways so this adds an unnecessary step.*Update*After owning this for a few month I find myself using it more and more. It works really well on straight surfaces that are still mostly wet. I find it the best way to quickly dry the roof, hood, windows, and side panels if I can get to them in time. I still need to do most of the drying with a towel but using this does speed things up and I have changed my mind about the product.
summary: Not a miracle solution but it has it's uses

reviewText: I use this as the first step in drying my car and I must say it makes it WAY easier because by the time I'm done with the water blade there is hardly any water left for my drying towel to dry.

This does a good job of removing a lot of the water from the surface of my car after I rinse. The soft blade is very flexible and doesn't scratch the paint. I still have to use a towel to get what little water is left over, but it is minimal.

This water blade speeds up the drying process on my automobile. It saves a lot of towel drying which can streak and leave water spots on the car. I would recommend this to anyone who handles their own car care,.

I use this only after my car is completely clean.If you do a lousy job cleaning your car don't expect this to be a good purchase.One day I just rinsed off my car without properly washing. The water blade caught some dirt on the back bumper and very tiny, minuscule scratches on the top coat.  Next time I washed and waxed properly and they went away but I learned my lesson because my laziness could have caused a less desirable situation.This is a great product if used correctly!  I use aMeguiar's Water Magnet Drying Towelafter I lift off all the heavy beads of water with the water blade.
I use this everyday in my glass shower. Streak free and the silicone is lasting perfectly. High Quality and built to last.

This is the only water blade I've ever tried so I don't have anything to compare it to.It's a little clumsy - especially on non-flat surfaces.  However, it still speeds up the manual drying process quite a bit.Remember to rinse it before every use so that you don't get dirt on your freshly washed car.

I really like this drying blade. I have used others before they work awesome for quickly drying large parts of your car. The only reason I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 is because the design is not as nice as the original California blade I used. Overall though this is a great product!

This works great at whisking water off a car.  I have a 2012 sonata and this easily whisks water off all the glass and horizontal surfaces of the car.  This works even better on the minivan.  This is really going to help my drying towel last a lot longer.
summary: Wish I had found this sooner

reviewText: This thing is awesome! Allows for drying a car so much faster than using a towel and it doens't leave swirl marks behind. Just make sure you use the waterblade from the top of the car/truck down to the bottom so the water doesn't drip or run over the areas that you've already used the waterblade on.This thing is a must buy for those that love to keep their vehicles clean and clear of swirl marks left behind by drying towels.TIP: When giving your car a final rinse after washing it take the sprayer nozzle off of the hose and run a soft stream of water over the entire car. this causes the water to bead and quickens your drying process even with using the waterblade.
summary: Makes drying so much quicker and easier!

reviewText: .I've used these for years.The blade on this model extends 1-5/16" from the handle.The car and blade need to be clean. If there is micro-dirt present it could create micro-scratches.On an older car, I sometimes use it after a hard rain...almost as good as a car wash.It eliminates about 90% of the water, greatly reducing the wipe-up time, effort, and number of wiping cloths to launder.This model is currently at Wal-Mart for under $9.~~~ Comments & questions welcome ~~~
summary: Works great. Saves time and energy.

reviewText: For anyone who washes their own car this item is a must. You will save 10-15 minutes just drying your car. (You'll save even more time for larger cars) You will be less tired, less sore, and the car will come out looking just as good. The only negative is you wont get it completely dry, you will need to go over it with a chamois or towel, however this amount is minimal compared to drying the whole car with just that towel.

I really enjoy using this blade to remove large slabs of water from the car's windows, roof, hood and even sides. By doing so, drying is a lot faster and easier and water spots are reduced. The blade itself is made of very soft rubber or similar material and I don't think it could cause a scratch the paint if you paid it to. Makes car washing a simpler chore.
summary: Makes car drying quicker and easier

reviewText: Watched the video using this, ordered one.  Haven't used it yet.  But for all those reviews on  absorbers and chamois, and complaining about having to wring it out and then it's not absorbent or leaves streaks or doesn't dry...here's your answer!

This waterblade is very handy if you want to wash your car. It really only takes one swipe to dry the surface, and it makes car drying a lot easier and faster especially over large, flatter areas of the car, such as the hood, roof and trunk. However, this product does NOT replace towels, it is only an aid. If you dry your car using this, bring a towel to dry more detailed parts of the car, such as the grille, lights, etc. The good thing is that you don't have to constantly wring out your towel.I would definitely recommend this to a friend.
summary: A Very Good Product. Worth Every Cent

reviewText: I tried a few other methods for drying my car after my last water blade fell victim to my neighbors dog, and I ended up going back to this same model. The newer one seems a bit stiffer, but that could just be because my last water blade was almost 10 years old. This one seems to work just as well.

works great on the cars body, but every time i try to clean the windows it drags and snags every bit of the way, i have yet to find an angle that works when cleaning the windows on my car with this thing. However when cleaning the body of my car this thing works like magic, it doesnt snag at all and makes drying a breeze
summary: works great on car body...not so much on windows

reviewText: This blade easily removes most of the water from my vehicle. I still need to use a towel for those hard to get spots, but overall it is a good tool
I use this many mornings to quickly remove the dew off of all of my windows and it makes drying my car with my waffle weave towel a cinch after using this first.
This seriously is a incredible wiper. Wipes the water off my windows and car body easily and without a trace of water residue.

So I purchased this not too long ago to use on my old 97 Jeep Grand Cherokee.  I am skeptical about using it on my new car after a professional detailer I know told me it can scratch the paint if there is even he smallest amount of debris left on the car.  He told me not to use this until after I clay bar my car. Anyway, I don't mind about using it on my old Jeep and let me tell you, it works great.  It really helps me to the car dry in just a few minutes, preventing water spots.  I did find a different use for it this product though.  When I wash my car mats, I lay them on the ground, spray with water, pour the correct Meguiar's soap on there, brush and work in the soap, then rinse.  I used to leave the mats out for hours to dry, but then I decided to try this product to simply wipe the water off. Using enough force, swiping side to side, this works AMAZING. Dries my mats 100x's faster.PRO'S:DurableWorks greatNice grip handleCON'S:Can possibly scratch paint (read review for details)
This is a good tool to help dry the vehicle. In the sunny south, anything that can get the water off the vehicle before it dries is a big help - this does the job.

As you can see, the end of the blade is shaped like a "T".  I found on flat surfaces, it works pretty great.  It has trouble on curves.  Too much curve, and the "T" doesn't bend as I'd like.  Overall, it works well.

Sorry, if you can't get an original old-stock super-deep California Water blade for ~$30 from someone selling old stock merchandise - just give up and go back to old-fashioned chamois or towels. The blade on this new-style (not-so) "original" one is way too stiff and just does NOT work that well.The current style California blades are not as good as the older ones. We have also tried numerous knock-off style silicon wipers but none or them (either)  have the deep highly flexible blades of the old-style original California water balds.Why California Water blades changed their great original design is beyond our comprehension.
summary: Not as good as an genuine old-style original (wide blade) California Water Blade

reviewText: Excellent flexibility and the size is perfect.  I've owned the larger water blades in the past and although they remove more water in less strokes on the hood and roof, this is great for smaller areas.  Works very well and the material is soft and won't scratch at all.
summary: Def a cheap, must have for the car lover.

reviewerName: P. Repage "FT Dad, Doctor & PT photographer"
reviewText: Other reviews here are from car restorers, enthusiasts, and those who might spend 2-3 hours detailing one of their cars over an afternoon. I am not that guy. As a doctor and a dad, time is at a premium, but I do like to do this myself rather than paying $25 for each vehicle at a car wash.That being said, this unit is a MAJOR time & money saver.Bought this and aCarrand 93089 Flow-Thru 10" Wash Brush with 68" Extension Poleto wash our 5 series BMW, Volvo S80, and a Honda Civic in a single 1.5 hour period.The drying blade is a fabulous complement to the brush. It turns a 6 towel drying job into 1 towel for ALL 3 CARS and cuts the time by at least 75%..Quick tip - I spray large amounts of Simple Green on my tires & rims FULL STRENGTH before I even start this process - it cuts through just about anything, and 80% of the brake dust and road dirt just hoses off. The rest I leave for the brush at the END of the car wash cycle.
summary: this unit is a MAJOR time & money saver...

reviewText: I have had other wipe blades and I have to tell you this one works great. You won't be sorry with this item. If it ever wears out I would buy another.

This product will take a lot of water off but you will still need to thoroughly dry your car afterwards. I still use it as it makes drying after easier, do not expect this to do all the work for you though.

I have used these water blades for over 10 years now.  They are a fantastic time saver once you learn how to use them properly.  You can't dry your ENTIRE car with the water blade but you can get atleast 75% of the vehicle completely dry.  I use the blade starting on the roof then working down the front and rear windshield. I have found that the blade works best on glass as it has the desing of a regular windshield wiper just softer.  I then move to the trunk lid and hood.  Lastly, I will do the sides of my doors, fenders, and quarter panels.  To get the hard to get places, like front bumper, grille, and other crevices I use a chamois.  The trick is to hold the water blade at about a 45 degree angle and do one long movement along the panel of which you are drying. This Pilot 11" soft dry water blade is a bit smaller than I am used to.  My favorite brand is the California Water blade which is a bit longer.  They both work great though.
summary: Saves time drying your car and wont cause damage to your paint.

reviewText: If it took you 20-25 mins to dry your car then after you buy this product you can cut that in half! it barely took me any time to dry the hood and all the big panels, the rest I dried with a chamois. This blade is so soft it wont scratch your car and also bends for those panels with curves.. Highly recommend this to someone who washes their car regularly, I wash it every week or 1 and a half week at the most so I needed something to make drying a little less hectic.

I was a little skeptical on how well this would work and I am glad i bought it.  I am not sure about the other blades that the other reviewers mention but I would recommend this one if you have never tried this type of product.
I wanted to like this but all it did was squeak and bounce across the glass and the car surface, leaving the water behind. It was useless.
summary: Didn't work for me at all

reviewText: The right tool for the right job, as they say.  I used it to straighten the radiator fins on my Dodge Ram 2500.  I'm not a vehicle or HVAC mechanic so this is a luxury a tool, but the cost was reasonable (Check) and it did the job (Check.  Couldn't ask for more.
summary: It fit the bill or at least the fins

reviewText: Our outdoor AC units got hit hard by hail. Insurance adjuster quoted about $170 a unit to fix the fins. It took me about an 1-1/2 hours per unit and fixed over 90% of the bent fins. Worth the money.
summary: Our outdoor AC units got hit hard by hail. ...

reviewText: It's a fin comb that has almost all the sizes. It works, what more is there to say?Amazon was once again super fast with the shipping.
summary: Does what it is supposed to do.

reviewText: I bought this product much because of the reviews and am glad I did.  You get 12 different combs all in two pieces with an easily attachable handle.  The handle is just a nut and washer that can be tightened by hand.  You don't even really need to put the handle on if you don't want to.  It's simple and easy.  I like it.

It does help train slightly bent fins but if they are too far messed up, it really cant help much. That may not be the fault of the tool but due to the my fins being to badly bent. It also makes it easy to clean into the fins.

Yes, it will work but it is really difficult to get it on the fins because it is wide and the other straighteners on the wheel interfere with your ability to get close to the edges.  I've seen some that are straight with one size per rod.  A friend purchased that one and it is much more useable.  I also found that the cheap plastic is so flimsy that some of the blades are not evenly spaced and this will cause it to press the fins apart unevenly.Will it work?  Yes.  Is there a better choice?  Definitely.

i can see how this might work good on big pitch window ac units and the like.... but I tried to use it on a 22 pitch 5 ton 14 seer modern unit and it is basically useless....  that tight of a pitch caused real problems with the plastic material successfully mating with the fins and the plastic got damaged right away....  then on top of that, even when using soapy water or lube to try to ease movement it wouldn't effectively spread the fins....  it might be a good product for some uses, but for tight pitch modern large systems... it's a waste of money
summary: doesnt work well for small pitches

reviewText: Great way to straiten fins.Much more effective that sitting there with a ruler or scraper to sort out any dings.This set is nice as it has the common sizes (pitches) for both AC and automotive work.
It works and there are a lot of sizes but the handle is awkward to use; difficult to get any leverage if the fins are badly damaged

Definitely an addition to the stock installed 1141 bulbs.  They are spendy, but if you want a white light, and not a yellow hue, these are the ticket. They use much less power and virtually zero heat.  I have an 08 Damon, and I am replacing all the overhead bulbs (1141's) with these.  Plenty of room and easy to install.  Highly recommend!
summary: Whiter and brighter than the stock 1141's

reviewText: Ordered the for our RV and they are fantastic!  They give off a bright white light with no blue tint to them.  They do not get hot so that saves the light covers.  I would recommend this light!  I love it!

I used a pair of these in my gaslight conversion project (see my posted picture up top).  I gutted the gas fixture of my lamp post and then installed a Charmlite copper dual bulb stem which takes automotive 1156 bulbs.  I have bought from LEDwholesalers before and find their products to be excellent.  This one is no different.  Love that it has a range of operating voltage and is AC/DC--you can't get any more foolproof than that.  These bulbs are "warm white" but not that warm.  I would say they are white with a hint of warm coloration.  In any case, they worked well and I am very pleased with the purchase.Update:  So after about 6 months of running these 10 hours a day at night as part of my 12V landscape lighting, I noticed some of the LEDs were burnt out.  With most of the ones left, they are still pretty bright, but I think I will have to be replacing these with less than a year on the clock.  All things considered, I still think these are a good buy since they still last longer than regular bulbs and save quite a bit of money in electricity.

The actual lamp I received had orange LED's and not the yellow ones shown in the picture. The light was very "warm" or at the yellow end of the spectrum and like an old tungsten lamp.I bought one to compare to a couple others sold on Amazon and this was the one I liked the least.The one I thought produced the best white/neutral light is the HQRP BA15S.
summary: Very warm light more like tungsten bulb

reviewText: I just installed a number of these in my RV to replace 1156 incandescent bulbs in the overhead pancake light fixtures. They are working really well and provide nearly as much light as what they replaced. I feel a lot more comfortable using all the lights when dry camping now, as they use a fraction of the energy. I also tried BrightChoice LED BA15s Bayonet Base 36LEDs SMD Bulb - 2nd Generation with 36 LEDs - Warm White bulbs, and actually preferred those, as they were a little bit brighter.I definitely recommend the Warm White over the regular White (or Cool White, depending on the manufacturer.)
summary: Fairly close replacement for 1156 incandescent bulbs.

reviewText: Recently (on a Sunday) our 2006 Volvo V50 displayed the check engine warning light.  With all regular garages closed, we asked a Napa representative to briefly decode the error message.  It showed a (yet) unknown issue with the catalytic converter.  After checking with the Volvo garage, as well as a local emission control center on Monday morning, it became clear that a major catalytic converter issue was unlikely.  If in fact the catalytic converter of our 2006 Volvo would have been defective, the replacement would result in costly repairs.  The emission control center representative suggested that we try Mr. Gasket Cataclean.  At best, it would help.  At worst, it would do no harm.  Well, in our case, the check engine light was reset and didn’t reappear.  And thus, we are believers!

I have a Check Engine light on, Code P0420 I believe on my Chevy Truck.  I tried it but it didn't work.  What has happened is my Converter has broken up into Pieces.  So nothing you dump into the fuel is going to fix that issue!  Now my problem is that I can't buy a Replacement Cat for my 2003 Chevy Silverado with a 5.3L Engine that's California Legal other then the whole Pipe and both converters from the Dealer.  Even though if I was in any other state I could buy a converter for like $90.  So I guess I'll just Pollute for another Year+ until either one gets Certified, or I have to fork out $800+.So this stuff won't work if your converter is broken up.  Your just wasting your money.
summary: Still don't know if it works!

reviewText: I don't have any scientific readings or measurements to offer but, I saw black clouds of smoke coming out under acceleration and the van runs better.........I'd use it again and frankly probably will.

I'm going to call as I see it and it did not work for me at all. I did not think it could really do what it claims to do and I was optimistic hoping it could make a difference but it did not help at all.I used as directed and had no check engine light on, but when I filled up after using this product my check engine light came on on the way home from the station. I was hoping it needed more time to work but it keeps coming back on -  this did not help at all -  $30 wasted
My 10 year old cars would not pass the ridgid polution tests in my State but the prescribed usage of Catcleal causes a positive result.

My car's two catalytic converters & O2 sensors were fouled by engine coolant leaking into the combustion chambers & passing through the exhaust. Result: the check engine light came on & my car would not pass PA emissions testing. Estimate to repair: $900.I read about Cataclean & decided it was worth a try even though it's pricey at $25/bottle. Followed the instructions, reset my CE light & was able to pass the emissions test. I suspect the the CE light may come back on at some point. If so, I'll put tape over the light to keep it from bothering me & use Cataclean again next year to get me through the PA vehicle inspection.
comes with mounting hardware and east to install and many different configurations that it can be used for, recommend highly
I wish I would have measure my trunk first to see what size I actually needed. I was able to tie up the stretch cords to make it work. It seems to have done the trick and works as expected.
Using it in  the  cargo area of a Nissan 370Z.  High quality matches the look of the Z and works well.
we ordered this net by mistake and ended up returning it.. the quality was fone.. we needed one that has stretch not flat straps

This is a great net that I used in my Mazda CX-5. After 1 day of not even using it the adhesive fell of the sides of my trunk. I have strong binding tape so I just reapplied with my own tape and so far it is working. I suggest buying this and either using the screws they provided or buying strong binding tape.
summary: Net works but adhesive is weak

reviewText: I love the netting and I have a trunk net and a side net to hold all my personal items and groceries
summary: It nets my packages and items very well.

reviewText: its ok. seems solid. pretty stretchy. the corners are loops. it works for what i needed it for. not super strong, wouldn’t recommend for holding down a load, but it’ll keep light stuff from blowing out if you can pull it tight over it. hooks on the corners would be nice.

This net fits pretty well in the back of my suv. The dimension of the suv space is 31" x 42" The net itself is not particularly expandable, but the edges are stretchable. When it is in place, it just lays on the floor. However, when I put a couple of grocery bags under the net, they stay in place really well.The corners have loops and the attachments in my suv are loops, so I had to get connectors. I found Cable Cuffs (small) to work really well. I bought them locally and they are pretty cheap. Another possibility is those fake caribiner clips (cheaper than the real ones, but still work well for this).The net comes with some "hooks" that you can install, but I don't think they would work in my car. On a shelf or something like that, they might work well.
This cargo net has an acceptable price and holds up well. I would not want to miss it and I gladly recommend it!

There is not any product much better than these Battery Tenders....I have about 12 of them for my toys and machines with batteries. I have not had any problems what so ever. Try to stay away from the Tender Jr. Doesn't seem to have the staying power as the rest of them...

I like this charger.  Not happy that it didn't come with alligator clamps (4 stars instead of 5) but overall it does the job.  I first bought the 1.25A Battery Tender but soon found that I didn't have the luxury to keep it on a large car battery for a couple days.  This one charges four times faster and I use it on all my batteries except the one for the Moped which I use the 1.25A version.

This charger is water proof and designed to be mounted. I have not mounted it, I just use it as a portable. It has maintained my battery for two years so far without over charging or drying it out. It has a micro processor that will automatically choose the best charging rate. It has a bulk charge, an absorption charge and then a float/maintenance charge. It can also let you know if your battery is sulfated. This charger is pricey, but buying batteries can also add up.

The battery tender provides an easy way to keep your batteries happy in the off season. Just check the water levels every couple weeks (to be safe) and you should be good. I have found that this charger does not boil the water off your batteries like the low quality WFCO converter that came in my RV. The two lights provide easy to follow feedback on what the charger is doing.
summary: Must have for the RV off season

reviewText: I rarely use my truck and have come across a weak battery from time to time.  Now that I have this Battery Tender (mounted to the outside wall of my house where the truck is parked), my battery is always fully charged when I decide to use it.This unit is weatherproof, which is extremely nice since I do receive a lot of Hilo rain throughout the year!  Installation in my truck was a breeze.  Quick connect cable is easy to use as well.  I did need to purchase the Battery Tender Extension cable, which is also found here on Amazon with Super Saver Shipping too!
summary: I use this to trickle charge my barely used truck

reviewText: I used it combined with the 5 way connector to reach a second vehicle from my battery charger, and it works just great. I am now maintaining two batteries with one charger and both are easily disconnected or connected with these simple plugs.  I love it.
I use this to extend the distance so I can reach the batt. charger. This is a must if you need to charge something that is across the room.
summary: Must have for charging things a way from Batt. charger.

reviewText: These extension cables by Battery Tender are perfect for hooking up solar chargers to Controllers with these connectors. Got to love em.
Not much to say other than it did the job to extend the cable to the location needed to charge the battery.

I used this cable together, along with two other battery tender cable to connect a car battery to a solar panel I put on the dashboard top to keep the battery topped up. The connector plug is bulky, and it was difficult to find a way to get it through the firewall. But, these are standard connectors, and I didn't want to cut the cable and then butt-splice the cut ends back together. I've been pleased with the whole battery tender system.
I use this everyday along with the solar panel from battery tender and with great success. Stay away from the knock offs or you will just end up coming back to battery tender products.
Not much to say here. Its an extension cable that gave me the additional length needed to use the Battery Tender in my garage...
i like this cord because its cheaper than the ones that batteryminder people sale. just the rite size to get to my harley

I have a couple of these for the battery tenders on my car and motorcycle.The gauge and length of the wire works well and the wire never gets warm due to the length of the wire.The conections at each end fit securely as well.

Not sure what to say here, it's an extension cord.  I do like that the cord came with end plugs for when it is not in use at either end.  I use this cord to run from the short hardwire battery connection that came with my Battery Tender, down through the chasis of a 2001 corvette and out of the front brake cooling duct in the front of the car.  This makes for very easy connecting/disconnecting from my batter tender very easy.  I have this on 2 of my cars that I use in good weather only and can go long periods of time without being started.  I've yet to have a battery fail!  Though I guess that says more about the Battery Tender than the cord. :-)

I have a motorcycle I keep a Battery Tender Jr. on constantly, and this is perfect so that I can keep the wall-wart hidden away, and neatly route the cable to exactly where it needs to be. Great product!

Great item.  Works just like it's supposed to.  Arrived in mint condition.  Would order another or recommend to a friend who was looking for one.Battery tender is mounted on a wall.  This allows me to charge my bike anywhere in the garage with ease.

I bought this thinking that it would be better than using an AC extension cord.  I think it is OK for the smaller 1.25A charger but I'm not so sure about using it with the larger 5A charger.  At 5 amps, there might be too much of a voltage drop when using this cable which will cause the charger not to deliver the proper voltage at the battery terminals.  Went back to using just an AC extension cord.
summary: I don't think this is good to use with a 5A charger

reviewText: The extension cable plugs easily into the Battery tender devices adding a little more distance between your item to be charged and the electrical receptacle.  Nothing more can be said other than the product works just as it should.

We use 3 different battery tenders on our ATV's and mobility chair.  Not are in the same place, and we need the option of different length cords so we can park them where we want, and not right next to an electrical outlet.  The cords are heavy duty and can only be attached one way (the right way).  Two of them (on the ATV's) remain outside year around in Michigan's weather, and show no signs or wear because of the weather.  They have been soaked by rain, frozen in ice, and exposed to the sun, and they continue to perform flawlessly.I might add that I do use dielectric grease on the "outdoors" connections to keep the weather from getting in and causing corrosion.
Purchase to use with a Battery Tender.  Needed extra to reach boat battery and keep the charger out of the boat.  No issues.

Not much to say about this that's subjective - it's an extension cord. That said, getting aBattery Tender 022-0165-DL-WH 12-Volt 2-Bank Battery Management Systemand using this extension cord works great. I use this setup to charge my two ATV's in one garage, and a jetski/car in the other garage. Can't go wrong.
summary: Makes reaching multiple or far away vehicles a snap!

reviewText: It's just an ex-cord for your battery tender charger or a ex-cord to help out a buddy with a dead battery while out of the road.
not much to say I needed a extension for my battery tender and the 12.5 ft extension was the right length and works perfectly. No problems it does what it's suppose to do.
These are perfect for attaching ez pass transponders.  Same as what comes from the turnpike folks in MA.  Just clean your windshield before applying them.
this was what I was looking for.  I needed this to add mounting locations in our other vehicle for our ez-pass.
These are great little mounting strips. I have used several pairs not just for the E-Z pass. They are so strong that they can hold an RD to the window llss
This is exactly what I needed to hang my EZ Pass transponder in my new vehicle. Works great. Would recommend.
summary: Why didn't think of looking here earlier?

reviewText: Did exactly what I wanted. Allowed me to affix an MP3 player in my glove yet allow for removal when servicing cabin filter. I know it will last as I have used these strips for years.
Actually a little longer than I need for my ez pass.  You could probably cut them in half again and they would still work fine.
Changed cars and needed to transfer EZPass tag.Was kind of surprised Amazon had these!I was going to purchase a roll and cut it myself, this was just more convenient.

I use a lot of Griot's garage products and like them.  So when I found myself running low on Meguiar's Gold Class Car Wash I decided to buy this Griots's Garage Car Wash.  I am attaching a photo of the bottle I received in this order next to the ruler - the 16 oz bottle is 6 inches tall.Griot's Garage Car Wash generated good suds and worked well.  However, it did not work any better than Meguiar's Gold Class Car Wash or several other car wash concentrates I used in the past.  I did not spend any less time on washing, I still needed to clayGriot's Garage Cleaning Claymy car to remove small imperfections. The main difference which may matter to someone that Griot's Garage is totally orderless, where as other car washes I used have a scent.On the negative side Griot's Garage Car Wash is rather pricey.  At the price of $8.99 this works out to 56 cents per oz. Meguiar's Gold Class Car Wash that I bought at a local retailer was $4.43 for 72 oz., 10 cents per oz.  Overall, I satisfied my curiosity and will not be buying it again.Ali Julia review
summary: Good but not better than the old brand I used with 5 times smaller price tag

reviewText: It's true that it's concentrated. It's true that it works well. You're still better off buying one of the many quality products out there that cost less. When it comes down to it, it's just detergent, not rocket science. Many reputable car care brands have a good car wash. With this product, you're paying for the Griot's Garage mystique. It's not that they don't have products worth buying -- they definitely do -- but you have to pick and choose. They aren't all the best, and they aren't all a good value. Stars deducted for value in this case.
summary: Double the bottle size and it'll be worth it

reviewText: Big fan of Griot's products and the car wash is not exception. Works well with the other Griot's products. Doesn't strip wax and builds a nice bucket of suds to help pull dirt away from you paint while you wash. I buy it by the gallon. I have four vehicles to wash and Griot's is used on all of them. All of Griot's products have a great fragrance. Very pleasant to the nose and my wife will come outside and comment on the pleasant smell. Great product.

I've used this product since 2003. It's a premium car wash but I think it is overpriced considering you can get a lot more for a lot less with some other brands.The suds that this car wash produces are really good. The product is very slippery, it smells great, and I think the cleaning power is very effective.  You can even use it full strength to remove stubborn dirt. I like the fact that it is a little thicker than most car washes and I think this is why it produces such rich suds. This car wash is tough on dirt but it won't strip wax.16 oz for eight bucks is a little too much for a car wash considering you can get 64 oz from Mothers for a few more bucks.  I also think that the Mothers is the better product simply because it does everything this product does for less money.I personally switched over to Mothers California Gold and I haven't looked back.  It does everything a car wash should do and at a great price. These day's you have so many different car washes on the market and most of them are pretty good.  Meguiars Gold Class is also an excellent choice.  I really don't think one car wash can perform any better than another as far as cleaning goes; they will all get your car clean.  The only differences would be suds, smell, if it is gentle on existing wax, and of course price.If price is not a concern and you insist on the Griot's Car Wash, then this is a great product.
I love this car wax, it really dosen't leave spots! Unavailable locally.  Groit's seems to have good, quality products no matter which on you buy and use. Excellent offering Amazon...

It cleaned as good as any other soap out there, but $10 for 16 ounces is a bit drastic and I just did not see anything about this soap that justifies the extra expense. Don't get me wrong, I am a fan of the Griots line, but this is one product that falls short of my expectations. I am happier using the half-gallon jug of Meguairs car wash that I bought for $5.

I've tried all brands and my search has stopped for a great car wash liquid.  It has a cherry sent which is different then any other brand I've ever used, so it was kind of weird.  That aside, it just sudz'ed up really nicely.  The foam lasted the entire time while washing the car.  Since it's a strong concentrate, you don't need much per car.The bottle itself is well thought out as well.  In lieu of removing the cap and pouring out the product you just pop the top that doesn't come off and just squeeze out what you need.  No cap to lose.  There is also an indicator that tells you approx how many cars it will do.Great product and you can buy one gallon refills.
summary: Love it.... Finally found a car wash that maintains the suds.

reviewText: This car wash is definitely worth the price.Streak free shine, pleasant smell and a little goes a long way.Cleans very well.
The car wash smells like cherry's and is high quality for the cheap price. Griot's Garage products are really good products and recommend for a detailer and enthusiasts.

I have used many different brands of car wash soap, and this is among my favorites. I still like the Meguire's products a lot and use them too. But Griot's Car Wash is well engineered for washing cars. It is highly concentrated, so a little bit goes a long way. A gallon of this stuff should last you all year. It is also very very slick and slippery - which is good!! I don't want to scratch my car while I'm washing it carefully by hand (that would defeat the purpose). This formula provides great lubrication to glide the dirt and grime away without scratching.I also use this for my wheels and tires, though sometimes a stronger detergent is needed there, depending on the level of grime and brake dust.Griot's also sells a pump dispenser for their gallon containers that I find very useful for the car wash. It pumps it easily into a smaller bottle for daily use, with no mess and no waste. I recommend looking for that.Overall, this is an excellent car wash soap - from a company solely dedicated to the care of your baby. I trust Griot's products to keep my cars top notch, and use them all the time!

Product works well using my 2-bucket wash system.  I wish that the price would be quite a bit cheaper as Chemical Guy's car wash products appear to do the same tough work on dirt and grime for less $$$.  Overall, though, am satisfied with this product.

I'm a big big fan of all these products if you love your car and you want something non harsh to use on new paint or older cars this car wash stuff is what you need it soaps well and  along with the other products will give your car a high gloss and shine.

These jack stands are ok.  If I had seen them in a store, I wouldn't have purchased them.  The welds are not very good, and the stands are only welded on one side of each seam.  I haven't had any problems with them though.  They just make me a little nervous.  Inspect them carefully before each use!
Jack stands appear well made and sturdy.  They held up front and rear axles just fine during recent brake change.

I ordred these for my 1999 ford explorer sport. To get underneath for oil changes, replacing fuel filter. These are taller/bigger than our stock 3 ton hack stands. So if you are planning to use them on multiple vehicles (especially ones with lower ground clearance), you may want to get jack stands that can fit the needs of ALL your vehicles.  My other vehicle is a nissan quest, and these jack stands even at the lowest setting are too high for the pinch welds on the side and you may crush the thin metal piece on the pinchwelds. IT's okay to jack up the car higher to get it on these. but sometiems its just too hgh for my comfort level. If you have a family of SUV's and higher ground clearance vehicles. These Torin Jack stands are perfect!
summary: Heavy Duty well built jack stands!

reviewText: Good value, easy to place and adjust; they did a great job holding my Tahoe off the ground while I rotated my tires.  Took a week or two to ship even with a prime membership.  Looking for more to say... okay how about when considering the cost of these items on Amazon, it saved me $50-$70 on a shop doing the rotation for me.  What more can I add?  Nothing.

Had defective one on first set, but thanks to Amazon's A to Z had new set in know time. I don't expect heavy steel stands for this kind of money, but do expect a good weld, good castings, fit, finish, and this set did improve on that. my craftsman are just a tad better than these and their made in china to. Instructions:To replace, turn on the accessories, flick the wipers to the on position, and then turn off the the accessories. The wiper blades should come up and stay up for an easy change. If they don't, redo the steps and they should come up. Taking the old ones out is easy, but getting these in are a challenge if you haven't changed the wipers in a long time. If you compare with the old OEMs, these Bosch wipers have an extra ledge / groove that will guide the metal clip in so it requires more force and the old one. If you are consistent with your motions and just go in for the "click" everything will work out alright.Performance:They work great! I didn't even know my wipers needed replacing until I went in for a complimentary checkup at VW. They charged $45 also for a lesser quality product. These were less than $30 and took less than 3 minutes to install. When I tested them I was shocked at how good they were. All streaks were gone and the glass was so transparent that I thought there wasn't a windshield. I haven't seen my windshield looking this clean in a long time.Note:Replacing wipers is good for your windshield as sharp debris and exposure the sun will make the wipers hard and scratch the windshield. For best results, use the wipers when the windshield is wet and clean under the wipers monthly to make sure no debris was lodged under the blade which will cause damage to your $300-$500 windshield.Thoughts:Bosch is a quality product and brand. They are OEM for many German makes so rest assured, these will do the job and are probably the best replacements you can get. Bosch was chosen by the manufacturers who know their cars best. It's best not to second guess their expertise of 1000s of engineers. Most decisions about your car should not be trusted to the average person and their neighborhood guy at Autozone. I've heard of a lot of people using aftermarket parts which affect other parts. Even though a windshield wiper isn't the most critical part, the same concept is true in terms of the longevity of the wiper and quality of performance. I have kept my car stock to the nuts and bolts and it has never broken down on me. Treat it like a lady and it will treat you and your wallet well.

These snap in directly, need no modification to the wiperarms, and look /identical/ to the more expensive OEM blades for a MKV (Mark V) Golf chassis VW.  At the time of this review they were two thirds of the price as the OEM blades at the dealership.Since the OEM blades are produced by Bosch as well, I am inclined to think that these are literally the same.This set contains the 24 inch driver side blade, and the shorter passenger side blade. Not two 24" blades.  The set does not include the short rear hatchback wiperblade.(Edited to fix a spelling mistake.)
summary: Direct replacement that equals or surpasses OEM quality at a far lower price.

reviewText: This product will help quiet down cheaper cars that don't have much sound insulation in the wheel wells - you know this when you can tap on the plastic underneath and hear how thin it is.  One can was able to do a thin coat on two front wheel wells - I will need another can to apply a second solid coat to thicken it out.  So basically, consider 1 can per wheel well.  It dries fast and is easy to apply - just shoot it out.  No need to remove your wheels unless you have a sports car where there's no space in between the tire and fender.  Just use a plastic trash bag to wrap your tires around.  No worry on some overspray - this isn't paint.  However, it does emit strong smell like spray paint so ensure you apply it somewhere well ventilated.Overall, this product used alone will not turn your vehicle into a silent road machine but it works in combination with other sound deadening methods.  Simple fact is that the tires rolling generate a ton of noise so helping dampen that out from the get-go will go a long way.
Sprays on easy, goes quick so I always buy an extra can.  I would recommend at least 2 coats.  It holds up well and will protect your metal from salt and water.  Highly recommended!

Coats well, however that comes at the expense of a can not lasting very long.  Took 9 cans to thoroughly cover just the bed area of my 2013 F-250 (estimating 20 cans for full coverage of the entire undercarrage), but I'm a bit picky about my vehicle....  We'll see how it holds up to the Michigan winter...UPDATE: 15 Oct 13 Took a total of 18 cans to do the entire truck (includes touch-ups the insides of the step bars, back sides of the bumpers, inside the doorwells, you get the picture...). Still cheaper that taking it to a shop! It seriously reduced the engine and road noise!
