Over the years I have tried less expensive buffers, everything from a "grinder" style that worked well for it's era, the 70's and 80's (but you had to be careful of burning through the paint on corners and edges) to newer orbital buffers that also did an OK job of applying waxes and buffing out very minor imperfections. I had read reviews and watched online videos of this buffer and after a lot of debate I finally loosened the purse strings and bought it along with several Meguiars pads. I washed my car and wiped it down and let it dry overnight. I had recently clay barred my car so next day I applied Meguiars NXT wax using their black pad and this buffer. The results exceeded my expectations. No swirl marks, no wax marks. The wax went on easy and wiped off easily. Between the wax, pad and buffer it did a great job of hiding minor imperfections and scratches and the shine is amazing. I will never go back to waxing by hand. This buffer is so easy to use I could reach over the roof and apply wax using just one hand! My black car never looked so good.
It is easy to Use. It makes my car look really nice and fun. I love it and recommend it

This is an absolute must for an auto enthusiast, do it yourself detailer, or a professional detailer.  For the price on amazon it's practically a steal.  These things sell for as high as 200+ shipping elsewhere.  I will admit, I'm not the best with a rotary buffer... I did a full paint job on my 94 bronco after replacing both rotted out fenders and my rotary left bad marring, swirls and hologramming behind despite how fast/slow and what combination of pads and polishes I used.  This dual action literally erased all of that in a matter of a few minutes as opposed to the countless time I applied with my rotary.  Obviously, a good rotary is an essential tool to have, but this dual action is a must!  Lightweight an very manageable.  Half the time I used it I only used one hand!  Nothin like my other polisher made by ATD that weighs a ton compared to this.  Combine it with Meguiars soft buff pads and you're good to go.  One downside of this polisher is, and the only one at that, it comes with the smaller hook and loop pad backing plate which is good but it doesn't have the raised center piece for the easy centering.  Some say they have issues with the pad sticking without that plate but I didnt experience a single problem.  It didn't come with a side grip but it isn't really needed due to the lack of weight.  Really like the speed settings and label on the machine informing speeds 1-3 for wax and polishing and 3-5 for scratch and swirl removal.  Never put mine past 3&1/2 and it did just fine!  Just be sure to start with the least aggressive pad & polish combo as possible and work your way up only if you have to and just follow it up with a less aggressive combo for final polishing.

This dual action polisher is good, and will do a good job on large areas but the smaller Meguire's G3500 drill mounted polisher is far easier to manage and get better precise results in hard to reach area's. Also the G3500's pads stay on much better! In fact working on a large SUV I abandoned using the larger polisher and used the G3500 instead. Using the smaller polisher I could work faster with more control and did not need to redo the same spot over and over.
summary: Good but smaller DA Polisher from Meguire's is better and easier to manage.

reviewText: This polisher is a bit heavy in the hands for my tastes but I really liked the way it works and the ability to adjust the speeds. For being Chinese made, it seems to be a good quality item. I particularly like the pad attachment system when used with Meguiar's W 9207 7" Soft Buff 2.0 Foam Finishing Pad  and W 8207 7" Soft Buff 2.0 Foam Polishing Pad.

This polisher is a well-built and excellently presented package with all the accessories to make sure you can use it for years to come! It comes with all the hardware (allen key & wrench) plus extra bushings if they wear out & additional spacers to keep the polishing pad far from the polisher itself! The speed settings are easy to and the pulsation of the speed makes for quick & easy application of any wax, compound, polish you need to apply! Make sure you buy all the extra pads you need now rather then cutting corners later! I highly reccomend the Diamond finishing pad it makes spectacular results! Also, cleaning the pad's is super easy, just flip, turn on, and rub gently with a clean white towel.
summary: Hands down best polisher I've ever used

reviewText: Amazon's "Frequently Bought Together" shows 6.5" polishing and finishing pads as being appropriate for this wonderful polisher.  I fell into that trap and ordered those with my new polisher on Amazon's suggestion.  Then I found out from Meguiars that they recently upgraded the backing pad to a 7" backing pad and that now 7" pads are the order of the day.Not only that I just found out from Meguiars that the 6.5" pads are NOT washable without risk of the Velcro backing coming off.  Do NOT waste your money on the 6.5" pads!So be sure to order the W8207 and W9207 7" pads to go with your new polisher's 7" backing plate.  Fortunately for me Amazon's wonderful customer service fully took care of my exchange and is changing the Website as I type this.Here are the links to the correct pads:SOFTBUFF 2.0 FOAM POLISHING PAD 7 inchMeguiar's W 9207 7" Soft Buff 2.0 Foam Finishing PadAlso, Meguiars highly recommends their 4" backing plate and pads for doing small areas of the car like bumpers and "A" pillars.  I plan on ordering those but unfortunately Amazon does not yet carry them.Finally, I will be writing a proper review once I have had a chance to fully experience this product.  So far it seems awesome.
summary: Warning!  Buy The Right Pads!!! Amazon "Frequently Bought Together" is Incorrect

reviewText: Excellent Dual Action Buffer and polisher.  Easy to use, excellent velcro pad, nice storage bag.  I loved polishing and waxing my car with this machine.

This is a very good polisher. Its a bit heavy and the pads don't last long but it gets the job done well. Keep in mind the handle is very thick so if you have small hands, it will be harder to handle.

These are okay.  I love the spray but I get a little crazy with the spray so thought this an alternative.  Very thin wipes that fold and compact up easily leaving big drips coming out your hand.  I am going back to the spray.

I use this product on any black auto trim, our ATV's, the camper, and mowers.  Bottom line it does exactly what it says it will.  I had the 32oz. bottle before this and it's nice, but sometimes clumsy to use for detailing.  I tried these wipes to see if I liked them better, and I do...for what I use them for.  If you use this for your boat or water craft, it will work for small jobs, but the spray bottle would be better when treating the seating areas due to the amount of coverage needed.
summary: Just as good as the 32oz. bottle.

reviewText: its way better than the stuff you get in any auto zone or advanced auto everyone needs to use thus on there UV beaten stuff

This protectant really works well. My Chevy Astro Van' s dash was looking really dry in a few areas. I figured I'd give this product a try. It made a remarkable difference. My dash looks restored to its original condition but with a slight sheen that looks better than when it was new.  I highly recommended it!

More expensive than Armor All. Only time will tell if  this really works or if it's just a good advertisement gimmick. I don't really understand the apply and wipe completely dry instructions but followed them with every application. Now we wait!!

Very happy with the performance so far, but I have not been using it very long so cannot speak to the long term protection capabilities, but compared to other protectants it yields a nicer less oily and less glossy surface (I consider this to be a good thing). Just be warned that it should be wiped off immediately, this is clearly stated on the packaging, but I failed to read it on first use. I think the spray bottle is much more cost effective, but the convenience of the wipes is nice. If you do not use it for a long time however, the top wipe gets a bit dried out and pulling out these wipes at the very beginning is not so easy. These use factors are the only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5.
303 is a great product, I used it for years and have always been very happy with it. Thank you very much.

Ive got a 2003 jeep rubicon that is over ten years old and the black bumpers, fenders, and black hard top look as good as the day I bought them because someone suggested 303 the day I got it. I use nothing else and its payed off. The wipes leave no lint and stay moist with 303 solution and they dont just shine they actually provide protection from the sun and elements. Highly recommend.
summary: Best product on the market to clean and protect your vehicle

reviewText: I have been using a small spray bottle of this product for about 30 (!) years. I love it. I use it on the rubber liners / gaskets / insulators around car doors;  wiper arms; plastic trim around hatch push buttons, etc. It preserves the rubber / plastic and gives it years of life.I love this product . . . . and the new Wipes are a GREAT idea.

First things first, the bad.  The towelettes are a bit small and we had trouble tearing them.  That's the reason for subtracting a star.We used only four towelettes to do the full interior so although the towelettes are small, they go a long way and do an excellent job cleaning up dirt, dust and when dry, leave a nice finish to the surface.  For comparison purposes, the car interior is that of a 2000, Dodge, Durango, SLT.Using the towelettes is nice because there are no issues of over spray on the windshield or side/back windows.  And there wasn't any oily residue left on the fingers or a noticeable chemical smell/odor/scent to be picked up by our noses.For ease of use with no over spray, the towelettes were top of the line and coupled with the 32oz spray bottle, one can easily extend the life of the towelette should they find in the summertime heat, the towelette drying out.We purchased both this product and the 32oz spray bottle.  One can also use the spray bottle to spray product on a microfiber cloth for larger cleanup jobs.This is a product I feel comfortable recommending and as needed, we will be purchasing more in the future.
Easy to use and perfect for my 09 Ford Expedition.  No need to wright a lengthy review.  What is there to say?  It works great.  It's simple to use.  It's fairly cheap when compared to other models.

I have been using inertia brake controllers for several years and already have 2 of the earlier Prodigy controllers I was well satisfied with.  When My Uncle asked me to get him a controller and help instal it, the decision was very easy.  These units are not the cheapest on the market, but their function is excellent, and do not require the leveling procedure that many controllers do.  The mounting options are fairly flexible, including a kit that allows it to easily be moved from vehicle to vehicle, a display that shows the voltage applied to the trailer brakes, and will also tell you if the brakes are not connected, the wiring has a short, etc.  Tekonsha has good technical support, and the Prodigy has a lifetime warranty, so the deal is hard to beat.
summary: One of the best brake controllers I have seen

reviewText: I purchased this item a couple of years ago when we bought our old 24' trailer. We are towing it with a 2011 GMC Sierra. I have had no problems with the brake control itself. Last year I did find out a couple of things. If for some reason the automatic braking does not work, the manual braking may still function using the lever. The fuse for the cruise control is connected to the automatic braking circuit. My fuse blew because the cable that plugs into the truck dragged on the ground for part of our trip and wore the insulation off some of the wires. I repaired the wires, but did not realize that the fuse had blown. It was like a game trying to find out which fuse protected the automatic braking circuit. I would suggest that you ask whoever installs it to tell you which fuses to check if you have an issue. Other than that, it is simple to adjust, reasonably priced and does what it supposed to do.

I can't believe how great this unit works. It was extremely easy to set up. I replaced an older Tekonsha, a non digital unit. This is so much nicer. Very much worth the money. I just returned from a trip and one feature that I realized is... Braking power starts arounf 2.0 when the brakes are hit. If the unit does not sense slowiing down much or angle change, it actually releases to .8 to 1.2 or so. This keeps you from dragging with the trailer than you really want to. I set my unit up so when the brake pedal is pressed, the trailer starts to slow the vehicle down slightly. If I do not brake much, it will lighten up. If I begin to brake harder, the braking power to the trailer increase proportionally as needed. It will go to 6 if it needs to. This is a very smart unit. I really like the feature to hold the button down when brake is engaged to go into reverse mode. This disables the brake controller for a set time for manuvering without brakeing at the trailer. Very nice.I highly recommend to anyone wanting electronic brake control.

My brother inlaw has this same unit and he loves it also. Very easy to install and works well. You will have to tweak with the adjustments in order to get it set just right for your setup but that's pretty easy to do, just follow the included instructions.

I bought the Toyota version of this funnel and it worked great.  It is sturdy stiff plastic and does not deform.  Also it has a gasket on the bottom so it won't leak oil.  The thing is great and if you use 1 qt containers of oil can save you not only time, but also fiddling around with the containers.  It was pricier than I thought it should hence 4 stars.
summary: Makes changing your oil a 10 minute job

reviewText: both of our lexuses has a piece of metal flange inside, so it block the common funnel from fit in all the way.  some oil always spilled out in the past, when i was in the hurry.  this new funnel screw in and seal tight, also it help support the quart container to drain.  this is a must have tool  for a shade tree mechanic like me.
summary: 2013 lexus rx350 fit perfect, no more spill.

reviewText: You may think it is just a funnel, not much to get excited about until you actually use it. You will then understand all the other reviewer's excellent reviews. If you have a Toyota and do your own oil changes, I would highly recommend this funnel, as another reviewer states, it is almost spill proof.

I love this funnel.  The fact that it threads right onto my oil filler opening saves me from inevitable spills when refilling the engine.  The funnel is pretty sturdy and well made.  It has a gasket on it for a better seal.  I've never had my leak and it hold a fair amount of oil.  If you do your own oil changes you need this in your arsenal of tools.
summary: A must have for Toyota DIYers

reviewText: Talk about a great funnel. You cant mess up an oil change with this funnel. Fits my 2013 Highlander perfectly.  Without this type of funnel  you would need at least three hands, because the valve cover baffle wont allow any other filter down inside the oil fill hole.

This is a nice tool to have.  Not only can you check the gap on the plug, but you can also use the end to open the gap up if need be.  I just used it to verify the new plugs were gapped properly at factory.  I also checked it to see if my old plugs had lost their gap.  There is not much else to really say about it.  It was a good buy and much easier to use than some of the other type of gap tools out there.

If I pay for a  "A & E Hand Tools 4450A E-Z Grip Spark Plug Gap Gauge" I expect to see the red gauge...instead of a orange, cheaper grade LANG gauge, no pocket clip. Having the pleasure of owning a real "A & E Hand Tools 4450A E-Z Grip Spark Plug Gap Gauge" this is nowhere the same item. No where in this listing does it say or substitute, not even a email or nothing saying it would be substituted.  I mean if I wanted the cheap LANG I could have stopped by SEARS for five bucks.
summary: Bait and switch, offer A & E, send cheap LANG.

reviewText: The ramp seems easier to use and identify markings. While feeler gauges may be the most exact method I find myself using this tool most of the time with complete trust.
summary: Much better than the round/keychain gauges

reviewText: This tool seemed very cheap for $5. The chrome didn't seem to be of good quality and I could see it peeling after limited use. I'll just go back to the 'coin' gap tool that you can get at any major auto parts store for $1-$2. I ended up returning it because the item I received wasn't the same brand as the one in the description (I think I would have kept it if it was what it was supposed to be).

If you need to figure out and set spark plug gap, this little tool works great. For the money, you can't go wrong with this in your tool box. Run the plug along the metal bar to the correct gap and you are all set to go. Not much else to say on this. Perfect size and perfect price.
summary: GAP set is important. This makes it easy!

reviewText: Awesome cheap little spark plug gapper. You don't realize how handy something like this is until you have one and don't need it. It gaps plugs by bracing the top flat part of the prong against the back straight part of the prong, NOT the electrode like coin style gappers, etc. This is an absolute must for more expensive "platinum" style plugs that don't have the traditional fat sturdy copper electrode, but rather the tiny "pin" style electrode. You will break the electrode on the "pin" style plugs without a gapper like this.Suck it up, pay less than the cost of one of your fancy spark plugs for this tool, and never need one again. This tool lives permanently on top of my tool box now.There are slight variations in what you will get when buying this, but there are all made by the same company, but just branded a little different. I ordered one and got one with an orange handle branded 'Lang' my friend ordered one and got one with a red handle branded differently, but they are all exactly the same.
summary: AWESOME gapper, why don't parts stores carry these?

reviewText: I purchased another gauge from an auto store and it was expensive, cheap quality. I decided to purchase this and it was 100% better for the job. Solid, polished and very easy to read. Great tool to have to verify or change your spark plug gap.

This leather care spray works alot better than I thought it would after using it, but it's essentially designed for leather maintenance and isn't going to add life to old leather that's truly worn and dirty.  I ended up trying this on three different surfaces, the first being our ten year old vehicle upholstery, our 6 year old sofa that supports five large dogs, and a new leather chair.The solution sprays on lightly, almost like water, and helps to losen surface dirt, but even with a good rub down with a terry cloth, it's not up to the challenge of dissolving ground in dirt.  I was expecting something a little more creamy to help condition and smooth leather, but the watery treatment does appear to work, although not as well as thicker solutions I've used.  The conditioners took a while to absorb, but after about 10 minutes or so, it's does, and the leather feels softer and looks shinier, but is completely dry to sit on.Last but not least, I've seen reviews that the smell is a little off and I have to admit, I can't identify what the smell actually is, but it's definitely not unpleasant.  It's a very light clean smell, inspired by new car leather, but doesn't quite capture the essence. Overall, it's a good all purpose leather cleaner, but best for new leather or general leather maintenance and not reviving or conditioning older leathers.
summary: Cleans and moisturizes with a light unidentifiable scent

reviewText: On dark, matte-finish leather, the application of this product is rather fussy.  It's best used in very small areas at a time.  After spraying and rubbing and drying with another dry cloth, you'd best be prepared to take a new, dry cloth and rub the leather a little more, otherwise, you'll be able to see every stroke you made with the first two cloths when the light hits the leather just right, and that's almost worse than just having dirty, unconditioned leather.  This is one or two more steps than I have patience for, at this point in my life, especially when there are products out there that are just spray, wipe and go.However, I like this product for dark leather with a shiny finish.  It is spray, wipe, and go ease on this kind of leather.  It makes quick work of cleaning and conditioning my living room furniture, and makes it just gleam.

I've been using Lexol leather care products for at least a couple of decades, and I remenber my Dad using them on leather goods when I was a kid some 50 years ago. This is the first time I have tried a one-step, all in one Lexol product, having always used the separate Lexol cleaner and Lexol conditioner. I tried the "3-in-1" spray on the leather seats of my Bimmer, using a slightly damp wax applicator sponge and a terry cloth towel to remove the excess and buff, per the product instructions.  It's very easy to use, does not leave a greasy residue, and seems to clean and feed the leather nicely, buffing to a nice satin sheen.Don't expect the same rich, creamy conditioner, or the same deep cleaning you will get using the two step Lexol products - or the great, fresh-tanned leather aroma that the traditional Lexol conditioner gives to leather. Unlike another reviewer, I did not find the aroma of the 3-in-1 offensive - more like inoffensively non-descript.  This spray on, combination product doesn't strike me as a substitute for periodic cleaning and conditioning with the traditional Lexol two step method. However, it does seem to provide an easy way to keep leather supple and looking good between regular Lexol cleaner and conditioner treatments. It's a nice addition to the old standbys in the Lexol line of leather treatments.You will pay a price for convenience, however: this 16 oz spray bottle costs about as much as a full liter of Lexol conditioner.  Still strikes me as a worthwhile product.
summary: Lexol quality, easy to use one step leather care

reviewText: Lexol is a great product for cleaning and conditioning leather. I clean my office chair weekly and this did a good job. Only minor complaint is the spray splatters a little bit when you try to spray it onto a rag. I would recommend this easy to use product for anything leather: car seats, saddles, leather clothing, etc.
I'm always apprehensive that these sprays will leave a greasy residue on the surface.  Not so here.  It cleans and protects without any residue at all.  Overall, seems to be worth the money.

This is a premium product for those who have a strong desire to car for their leather seats.  Similar to when armor-all first hit the market, this product applies very well.  Although it is pricey, it is designed for true leather seats.  I applied some on my Audi and the shine was brilliant.  It is a bit concentrated so you don't need as much as you probably use with similar products.  Instead of have several care products....Leather, Rubber Trim, Dash Board, etc., this product is designed for many finishes.  So far, so good.

Lexol 3-in-1 Leather Care Spray - 16 oz.I've used Lexol cleaner and Lexol conditioner in the past on all of my genuine leather articles. These included leather steering wheel wraps, leather shoes, leather boots, motorcycle racing leathers, and anything with leather. The Lexol conditioner always made the leather feel soft and supple, and I never have any complaints.The Lexol 3-in-1 is supposed to make things easier by combining their separate products into 1, so you can spray and wipe. I found the 3-in-1 to be easier to use because the liquid is thinner and less viscous so it seeps into stitching and porous material more readily. Unfortunately, it also leaves a sheen on some leather surfaces and makes it feel slick to the touch. I also noticed that it turned some leather "stiffer" or "harder" than when I used Lexol conditioner. The odor is also very unruly, it no longer made my leather articles smell like leather, but instead it smelled unnaturally.The cleaning power is about on-par with the Lexol cleaner, but I did not like how the 3-in-1 left a sheen on the leather surfaces and made some of the leather surfaces feel slicker and stiffer. The smell was not very good either. I would be hesitant to use the 3-in-1 on steering wheel wraps and seats because of the slick feel. I wouldn't mind using the 3-in-1 on leather dashboard surfaces or boots/shoes , although I still prefer the separate Lexol products.Overall: 3/5 stars
summary: Odd smell, leaves some leather slick and shiny, still prefer the original Lexol products

reviewText: The office chair I use at home is leather. I admit I've been remiss in cleaning it properly for quite a while, and have been very lucky so far. But I realized that I really needed to start caring for the leather properly if I want it to last a long time.I researched leather cleaners, and the Lexol brand seemed to be the best available. When Amazon presented it to the Vine Voices for review, I didn't hesitate to choose it since I was already planning on buying it.The Lexol 3-in-1 Leather Care Spray was easy to use. You just spray it on, massage it into the leather, then wipe it off after a bit. Voila! The leather on my chair looked shiny and luxurious and felt great. I was afraid it might be greasy or slippery but it is not.I am very pleased with the way Lexol cleaned my chair and will definitely buy more when this bottle runs out.
summary: Easy to use cleaner leave leather looking rich and shiny, feels great

reviewText: This is fantastic leather cleaner.  I've used leather cleaners before and not one has come close to matching the quality of this one.  It actually makes the leather look cleaner and softer.  I used it on the 3 rows of leather seats in the SUV and on the two leather recliners before emptying it.  Each SUV seat (all leather, no plastic) was so much cleaner and the rags proved it.  The second row is the dogs area and they really appreciated a new surface to dirty up.  The recliners had some surface dirt on the bottoms thanks to dogs wiping their faces on it but with Lexol the dirt was eliminated with almost no effort.  This is a really great product and it will become a staple in the car care box along with the other items.
summary: A Whole Lot of Clean Leather

reviewText: Frankly, Lexol's tire treatment is a disappointment; therefore, I was anticipating the worst when I obtained their leather-care product.  Oh, boy, what a pleasant surprise!  I've tried many of the commonly available leather treatments on a couple of classic cars (as well as on shoes, for which they generally are not recommended).  The Lexol 3-in-1 cleans and, because of its oil base, penetrates leather.  You're left with a nice shine and suppleness.  Because of the change of season, it's difficult to tell how well it will hold up to full sun and high temperatures, but it seems promising...

It has taken me some time to write a review for the Lexol 3-in-1 Leather Care Spray, because I wanted to be sure and put it through its paces and give the product a good real-life evaluation before doing so. For years, I have used a competitive product with which I was always generally satisfied. I compared the Lexol side-by-side with the other product I've used previously, not so much to pit one against the other (though that is inevitible), but to compare Lexol to what was my baseline expectation for a leather cleaner/conditioner.The first thing that one might notice with Lexol is the odor of the product. I would be less than forthcoming if I didn't say it is borderline offensive. Though the smell did put me off, I persisted using the product both on automotive leather and household leather. My observations are listed below, but my overall opinion after some good evaluation is very favorable. I may just switch and buy Lexol from now on.CLEANING -  The first important thing we need this product to do is to CLEAN the leather, right? While I will often pre-clean badly soiled leather with a mild soap and water and dry before using a leather care product, I tested the Lexol without any pre-clean to see what it has to offer. I was pleasantly surprised at the general effectiveness of cleaning ground-in dirty leather. I found that for heavily soiled areas, if you spray the Lexol on and let it soak in for a minute or so, then agitate gently with a microfiber cloth, it does a very good job of lifting the dirt out of the grain. I have ivory colored leather furniture that I allow my German Shepherd to lie on, and believe me - it gets dirty! It cleans as well as any spray-on product I have used.ODOR -  As mentioned above, this really bothered me at first. It does not have what I consider a pleasant smell. Okay... I think it stinks (there, I said it). This is subjective, and others may mind it more or less than I do - but I would prefer a nicer smell.CONDITIONING -  The conditioning properties seem to be good. Lexol leaves the leather soft and suple and it retains that quality for quite some time. One thing I like a lot about Lexol compared to some other brands, is that it leaves the leather with "grippy" natural feel - not slippery like many others do. Particularly when it comes to the leather seats in my cars, I don't want to slide around on them. I want them to grip me like leather is supposed to - and Lexol provides this feel very well. During evaluation, I used the Lexol on one leather sofa cushion and another spray-on leather cleaner/conditioner on the adjacent cushion. The results of the way the surface is left was remarkable. The "other product side" was quite slippery, while the Lexol side was nice and "grippy" (but not tacky).
summary: Good cleaning & conditioning without the slippery feel

reviewText: The leather that we have is the rougher, what I call 'unpolished' but is really full grain leather. It doesn't have the high shine of top grain leather so this product definitely worked differently.I tried this on an ottoman that had a few stains (pen, a glass mark) and lots of general use wear. I did test it in a discreet area first and knew going into it that it would leave it slightly darker. With that in mind, I used it on the entire top of the ottoman. It sank in really quickly and was much darker. I really had nothing to wipe off since the leather soaked it all up. But my rag had some discoloration with may have come from the leather dye - although it was very minimal. The end result is that the ottoman has dried to a slightly darker version and evened out some of the stains but has not removed them. I would have been amazed if they did come out since they had really penetrated. Overall, the leather looks in better condition, like it's been given a good drink after being thirsty. Which is probably what has happened!I believe it will work better on a top leather surface and in using it on smaller leather products, it has done a good job.
summary: Pretty Good, Gives Nice Conditioning to Leather

reviewText: This is a no brainer for car leather seats.Use this one.  It cleans (though maybe not as clean as those dedicated for the job), but I have some stains that I got rid off by using this one.It conditions my leather seat but I don't know about softening.Honestly, I've ran through a couple of bottles of these leather care sprays on my leather seats (all of my cars have leather seats, I like them because they are easier to clean than fabric.)  And I really don't see any short term benefits.  I can see long term benefits because by using them, you keep the leather conditions to be shiny and soft.  But for the driver seat which takes the most abuse, it can't get rid of the wrinkles from daily abuse.It's a good bottle.  It handles easy and sprays well, maybe a bit too much per squirt, but you need to wipe it down with a cloth.I usually leave it in without wiping for like 20 min and come back and wipe it off evenly.I recommend this product but I think it's a bit expensive.  I think something like this should be in the $5-7.99 price range.

I had been using a separate cleaner and conditioner/protector on my car interior. When I saw a product that was all three of these in one I jumped at the chance to lose a few steps and save some time. Plus, I would be more likely to clean the car seats if it was an easier job.The product was easy to use, just spray it on, rub it in and wipe it off. The leather retained a soft, shiny look to it and didn't feel greasy. The smell was mild. My seats were not grimy, only dirty with normal wear, so I can't comment on whether or not this would work on really ground in dirt but it worked fine on everyday dirt.I only used a small amount of the bottle to clean the car so I had plenty left over to test other items. I asked my husband to try it on the leather saddle bags on his Harley motorcycle. He was pleased with the results but wondered whether the protector would offer any resistance to rain. The bottle didn't say so I'll report back if he gets caught in a storm. Then I tried it on an old, dull looking pair of leather shoes and it made them look shiny and new. Even if I need to clean them every few weeks to keep the shine it will be worth it as this cleaner is so easy to use it only took a minute per shoe.For the price, results and ease of use I would recommend giving this cleaner a try.
summary: Easy to use, great results and reasonable price.

reviewText: I tested this product on my office chair, leather car seats and our leather sofa.  It very quickly removes surface dirt & grime.  I'm not crazy about the sprayer on this bottle, simply because you really can't spray this and control where it goes this is very thin & liquid-y, so I sprayed this onto my cloth to apply.  I'm not crazy about the smell, but its not a deal-breaker.  Its just an oddly unpleasant scent, fortunately its not overpowering.  After a few minutes be sure to go back over each surface with a clean dry cloth, as the instructions state, it really made a difference in the final condition.

Lexol is one of those products that has been in my clean-up bucket for the past 20 years.  Ever since I purchased a car with leather seats, I have had Lexol products to care for the leather.If you are like me, you have chemicals for washing the car, treating the paint finish, treating the rubber, the tires, the chrome, and glass.  Each product has a specific purpose and each is suited for the part of the car being treated.Lexol also comes in a two-step configuration - one bottle for cleaning and conditioning, and another for preserving.  This product makes it a one-step job to clean and preserve your leather.If you don't have time to do the two-step process, this is a good way to maintain your leather and save some time!

I think this product is great for most vehicles and lots of other uses. It does a great job of both cleaning and conditioning leather at the same time. If you need a quick clean and condition then I would recommend this product. But for a longer term solution, I would use a dedicated leather preservative/conditioner instead. While I do like this Lexol 3-in-1, I don't use it on my treasured vehicles that I only drive occasionally. For those vehicles I use a more expensive top grade leather preservative.I do use this for quick cleanup and conditioning on my regular vehicle that I drive mostly every day. I do not use it on the steering wheel rim as I don't want to take the chance of it getting too slippery. You definitely need to go back over the leather with a dry cloth to remove some of the slipperiness.It does work really great on boots! Cleans them, conditions and gives the boots a nice shine. You don't have to use this Lexol 3-in-1 just for vehicles.This Lexol 3-in-1 is an excellent value and one bottle will last quite awhile.
summary: Works great and leaves leather in nice condition.

reviewText: I needed to have a Leather cleaner for my GTO's seats and looked around searching for best products. The Lexol 3-in- 1 Leather Care spray looked inviting so I gave it a try. It has worked better than I expected and my seats are clean, soft, and smell great. Very good product and I'd buy it again when needed.

Seemed to work about as well as other products, but based on minimal use, no better. I had one dark smudge on my tan leather and it did not help remove it, but perhaps this was an exceptional case? Freshened up the rest. First thing I noticed the next day was that I no longer "slid" into my seat as it left the leather just slightly tacky instead of slick. You may perceive this as a good thing or a bad thing. By the second day, it was "buffed out" (presumably with my jeans) and felt neutral.
summary: If it's supposed to be something special, not sure what it is

reviewText: Usually I use saddle soap to care for my leather products. I applied this to the leather seating areas in an older car. It improves the appearance, smells nice, and does not make things too slippery. It would be nice if it created that "new car smell" and also would be nice if it could take out some of the more ingrained markings. Overall, though, I was very pleased with Lexol 3 in 1 leather care. It did very well given the age and condition of the leather. As far as cleaning, though, saddle soap does a better job. Since Lexol is specifically formulated for car upholstery it may do better in the long run. I also used it during the colder months around here and it may work better in the summer. 4 1/2 stars for this. I would have given 5 stars if it beat saddle soap in the cleaning category.

I would highly recommend this product to anyone and everyone I know.  I'd never heard of this before I purchased a Saab and everyone raved about it.  Well, now I'm a believer too.  If you have leather seats this is THE best in my humble opinion.  This is all I will buy from now on.....period.

One of the best leather cleaners and conditioners available.  I use the leather cleaner and rub it in with the square applicator pad.  Then I wipe it clean with a micro fiber towel.  Then I apply the leather conditioned with the round pad.  I've used it on my seats, steering wheel, and shifter.  The items are not greasy or slippery afterwards.

Been the standard of the industry for years.  I used primarily on my car's seats. Once or twice a year, depending on the amount of use.So far, all the leather surface are just fine, not a hasty praise, one car is almost 20 years old !Great for leather sofas and furniture  too.I may be wrong, but I  believe Lexol was the recommended brand by Rolls Royce, when they were still British owned.
i use many brands of car care products and this is one of the nicer ones.  i would recommend it to a serious car enthusiast.

Overall the products are good but not great. Be careful using the vinyl cleaner conditioner around your leather as it will take all of the color out of the leather. The leather cleaner conditioner is only fair and does not clean the fabric very well. Only marginal
summary: As a leather cleaner- just so so

reviewText: This is a good set of cleaners to take care of vinyl and leather. I didn't find the vinyl cleaner as effective as Armor All, but I prefered the vinyl protector--it's less shiny and greasy than Armor All.The leather cleaner is moderately effective; I have a dog who manages to miss the seat protector and barf UNDER it (how does she do that!) when I take her for a ride. So I keep this in the car for quick clean ups and my seats are kept clean and free of stains. For the price, a good value and useful set for detailing the car.
summary: Maintain the leather and vinyl of your ride

reviewText: I was skeptical on buying a leather cleaner for my new 2013 toyota venza which is all leather on the inside, my leather is a grey leather, it's my first time ever having a leather interior in a car, I tested the lexis on a small HIDDEN area on the leather to make sure it won't discolor, I did the cleaner all over the leather in the car, and then did the conditioner and the leather, And then I used the Vinylex on the dash and the door panel and it made them soo clean and look like I just bought the car brand new again. I highly recommend this product, 5 stars, does not have any akward scent either.
summary: Excellent!! It makes my leather real clean!!

reviewText: For anyone serious about using quality products to protect leather and give a great look to vinyl and tires this is the kit.  Much less than buying the individual bottles with the added benefit of the pads.  The leather cleaner and conditioner also work well on my leather recliner in the house.  I have also used it to clean and condition a leather jacket.

Although only available via 'scratch and dent' used items via Amazon warehouse - there was nothing wrong with this product.  I immediately used the cleaner on the leather on my 14 years neglected seats.  I saw an immediate difference (and an ugly pad to boot from all of the dirt).  I then followed up with the conditioner, and I could see the difference within the first application.  As suggested by an associate who details for pleasure, I applied it three times over a day (in the shade, mostly), and let it dry.  I then sprayed a fourth time, and wiped it down - and the haze cleared right up, with no "Armour All" finish.  This is truly an awesome product.
summary: A decent pack for the introduction to Lexol.

reviewText: I read about Vinylex on a car-detailing site, and it's the best vinyl cleaner I've used.  Lasts a long time, keeps the white film from forming on the inside of the windshield, and, most important of all, doesn't just make it shiny, while drying it out.The cleaner works great, and is especially nice for lighter colored leather, since the dark-spots are very noticable.Conditioner works very well also, and doesn't smell like some weird chemical.  Also seems to last a good long time.  By the time I re-do the seats, the last cleaning still is good.If you've never bought Lexol projects, pick up this kit, you get all 3, and a couple application pads.  Even if you are a Lexol person, you really can't beat the price for this kit.

I've used lots of different oils and protectants for various leather goods over the years.  Nothing has impressed me as immediately and consistently as Lexol.  I've starting using it on my car seats, steering wheel, office chair, jackets, belts, and boots.  It's completely replaced almost every other product I've ever used.This kit includes basically everything you need to clean and protect your entire car interior, minus the glass.  You don't have to use it that way, though.  Here's what I do: after I've cleaned my car, I'm left with a rag covered in Lexol.  I take that rag and wipe down any other leather goods I have handy.  The rag winds up soaking up more than is necessary but at least this way I put it to use.Vinylex works great on the various plastics inside my car.  Not as much to say about that but it does the job and well.The sponges work well as applicators and to wipe excess away.  They aren't really any better than a good microfiber rag or any other brand of microfiber sponge.
summary: Lexol rocks for protecting leather products.  Simple as that.

reviewText: I ordered these products to condition the inside of my car.  They were easy to apply with the sponges included.  (I ordered two more.)  The leather cleaner and conditioner cleaned and put a protectant on the leather which will prevent it from developing cuts.  I haven't tried the vinyl cleaner and conditioner, but feel it will work just as well.  The kit was fairly priced and arrived promptly.
summary: Great products made for a specific purpose

reviewText: I have used this on my B7 S4. Made the steering wheel feel great. Also used it on my 2002 Saturn SC2 steering wheel, cleaned a bunch of crap off I didn't even realize was there. Wish I had this sooner! The vinyl cleaner is good but I prefer 1Z Cockpit cleaner for the dash.

Lexol's premium tire shine provides a nice (not too glossy) finish on the sidewalls of your tires. It is easy to apply; simply spray onto the sidewall. Getting it on the bottm side wall is a bit tricky, but thankfully application doesn't have to be perfectly smooth. Drips disappear.In the past I had my car washed at a car wash (the kind where your car is towed through a tunnel with various activities performed by machines). One of the services is tire shine. My car wash's shine was extremely glossy, almost enough to see your refelction. The Lexol product does not produce that type of shine. Theirs is more subdued. There is a definite gloss, but it is muted compared with the car wash product.One thing that is very important to me is that the product does not damage my tires. Bridgestone and Michelin warned that tire shine products can damage the tire. Lexol claims that their product is safe for all tires. I have only been using the product for a few weeks, so there is no way to determine if there are any adverse effects from using the product. However, Lexol has an excellent reputation and I have been very happy with other products they make.
summary: Good shine that is fairly long lasting

reviewText: I think it's a little hard to review a product like this accurately until you've used it for a really long time.  And, you can pick up the comments from other reviewers regarding the shining properties and texture, etc.  To me, the shine is not overwhelming and it's not extremely easy to spread on tires.  But, I'm counting on Lexol to give me the same kind of quality formulation here that I believe they deliver in their leather protection products.  Those seem to me to be outstanding and I'm going on faith here that this product will be similarly good in terms of protecting tires from UV, etc.  I've read that some of the leading competitors in this product field are not good at all in terms of protection, so I'd rather have great protection and fair shine than great shine and poor protection.If you drive a lot of miles and wear out tires well before UV damage or sidewall rot would ever be a concern, you may weight shine over function.  I'm not in that category, so I'll select this product for its brand goodwill from leather products and hope for carryover here.  I think it's a decent bet.

Not an expert in tire products, but I do like my wheels to shine without too much fuss. The Lexol kit sent to me by Amazon Vine is quite good, shines up real nice and hopefully will last for a few days in our AZ heat.  Plus, it goes on easily and is not too messy.

I review for Amazon Vine and they were supposed to send me the Tire Spray, but I receive the 3 in 1 Care Care Leather  Cleaner--so I will review what I received.  The Leather Cleaner does a very nice job. It is easy to use, leaves no residue and has a very pleasant smell--or maybe that is the smell of clean leather.  I recommend this product to care for the leather interior in your car.  It works well.

I ordered this product and received the Lexol 3 in 1 leather careas well.  No worry, I picked one up locally and now with both products, my car has some nice shiny tires and a fresh look to the interior leather.  The tire shine is still standing up, even after a light rain for about 7 days and I imagine in decent weather it would hold its luster longer.  For a product to use at every wash the tire protectant works well.  Keep it off of the rims or it will collect dirt on your rims.

This product doesn't seem to outlast any other tire shine product I've used in the past.  I sprayed it on Wednesday and by today, there is noticeable fading of the overall "black" look.  My tires are larger than most, for a 2000 Dodge Durango RT, so I do like them to have that deep black wet look, which this provided, for about a day and a half.

I am one who pampers my cars.  I am very familiar with Lexol products, having seen them at various car shows.  I was looking for something to compare against my regular brand, which is Maguire.  The product is pretty sraight-forward and easy to apply.  My only critique is the application nozzle, prevents a full stream, but on the other hand I could be using it incorrectly.The product presents a high quality finish and doesn't run like so many shines.  In other words, when you drive a good portion of the product finds it way on the exterior of your car (near the tires) because it doesn't dry evenly.The product is a good option for those looking for an alternative or those who are loyal to branding, since Lexol is known for premium exterior car care.
Tried this for the first timt this past weekend on three vehicles. It works well, as advertised.  Easy to use, and makes the tires look like new. Really dresses up the looks of the cars!
I would say this is pretty good stuff. I tried them all and this is in the middle, maybe a bit better than average. Gives a nice look and lasts fairly long.

I do enjoy using this product line. Their leather conditioners have down wonders for my leather chairs, upholstery and jackets. I expected nothing less from the Tire Shine Spray and was not disappointed. This provides the perfect finishing touch to the car after washing and waxing. The dull blackwalls that usually stand out after the rest of my car is detailed were a source of annoyance. Now that I have the perfect finishing touch for the last detail, I am truly proud of the way my car looks after spending a Saturday afternoon working on it.

At least I obtained Lexol's Premium Tire Shine Spray through Amazon's Vine program, because I would have been greatly disappointed had I paid the going price. The main issue is that Stoner, Meguiar, and Mother's all make superior products, and all of them are readily available at auto supply stores.  The spray nozzle on the Lexol product produces an awfully wide spray, which tends to lead to waste and having to clean the overspray off your wheels when used in the wide setting.  On the narrow setting, there's still a fair amount of run-off waste.  The biggest problem is that this product is not nearly as shiny as its competitors, nor does it seem to last appreciably longer.  If you're in a pinch, Lexol's Premium Tire Shine Spray is ok, but if you can find one of the three competitors listed above at a comparable price, then think twice about this product.

My car has leather interior and I have tried all kinds of products to clean the leather.  I recently tried this Lexol 3-in-1 Leather Care product because it states that it is an easy 1-step solution - exactly what I wanted!  I was pleasantly surprised with this product, it worked really well and cleaned my interior, removing black spots from grease and dirty hands, leaving the leather soft and shiny.  The best feature about this product was that it didn't stink.  So many of these products that I have tried really smell and have a strong lingering scent, not this one. I really liked that I wasn't being suffocated by the fumes when I was using this, and I tried it on a day that it was raining so I didn't have all the windows open.  This product is 3 steps in one bottle, the smell won't give you a headache and your leather will look great. I would recommend this leather care.
summary: Cleans, conditions and protects without being stinky!

reviewText: I wasn't looking for a shine that looks like I slicked oil on my tires, just something to make them look "new". This product did that.  My car is garage kept so I can't attest to the protection that it gives but it did clean the tires and make them look really nice.
This product works exactly as described and it is easy to use.  It keeps our Jag's tires looking good between washings too.  Well worth the money and effort.

This product has silicone which has been proven to degrade tires and dry them out. So while this product will make your tires look shiny, the tires will not last as long if you use this.The manufacturer claim that this product protects your tires is completely false.

I am not a professional automobile detailer. However, I ordered this product to see if it could shape up the looks of 4-5 year old tires. My answer is yes it does. I compared the effects to my local dealer and what they do to make their pre owned inventory look good since I was there having my car inspected. The results are comparable. Any early "dry rot" magically disappears. I do not know what this does to improve tire life. All I can say is it certainly makes them look good. And good looking tires increase resale or trade in value. It may even help to prevent dry rot the same way waxing protects the finish of a car. I give Lexol Premium Tire Shine 5 stars. It is easy to apply with minimal mess or fuss. I highly recommend this product.

I did not buy mine from Amazon, but I love this thing.  A great product at a great price.  You just set the pressure and just let it run.  It will inflate the tire and shut off when it reaches the set pressure.  I've been using mine for well over a year now with no issues.  I did however recently buy one of these http://www.amazon.com/RoadPro-RP-203EC-Extension-Cigarette-Lighter/dp/B000Z0HVHA/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1402797883&sr=8-1&keywords=RoadPro+RP-203EC+12V+12%27+Extension+Cord+with+Cigarette+Lighter+Plug, which makes it easier to reach all four tires.  The inflator has enough cord to hit all four tires, but it means passing the device around through the various doors and windows.  With the extension cord, I can hit all four tires more easily.

Okay, I didn't expect a lot, but I did expect it to inflate an automobile tire. Compressor would come on, but tire would totally deflate while running--same thing with trying to inflate a bicycle tire! I learned my final lesson with Slime. This was not my first faulty product from this manufacturer.
summary: Slime is an appropriate name for this piece of trash

reviewText: The power cord quite long you should be able to get to every tire even on a large truck.. You can preset the pressure you want hit on and it wait until it fills to where you want it. I'd say its pretty quick compared to some others ive used in the past. the screw on hose is something I kinda like because you dont have to hold it in place. Its also much better than the level style it you have rims with poor clearance. The light thats built in I find kind of useless. It has an illuminated display which is nice at nighttime. It was a great price and appears to be well made. You can also adjust between psi, kpa and bar. That feature might be usefulll to someone. the cord and and fill hose fit all neatly inside the unit.
summary: Automatic psi setting and oretty quick

reviewText: Works really well and fairly fast for bringing tires to recommended pressure.  I did not try it myself,  but would probably not work well to fill a completely empty tire,  but then who would want to do that?The pressure gauge and automatic shutoff works  really well.  ( if you set it properly).  It is a little loud,  but then so is a regular compressor.  The only issue I have is that it does  loose about a  half to one pound of pressure when unscrewing the pump from the valve stem no matter how fast you are. That is why I did not give it 5 stars. To resolve this issue,  just set it to half pound higher than desired pressure. Or do what I did and order the “Topeak Pressure-Rite Anti-Air Loss Connector “ .If you read some of the bad reviews,  many are non-founded and many are operator inadequacy, not the pump.I would definitely buy it again!
summary: Really four and a half stars or even four and three quaters stars

reviewText: Every car should have this one. Portable and reliable with reasonable price. Works well with my mid-size car. Highly recommended.
summary: I've should have got this since I had my 1st car.

reviewText: First use, set the pressure to 37 psi & started inflating the tire. After 5 minutes, I unplugged it & found the tire pressure to be 53 psi. Not sure if it's me or the unit. At least it works.

I bought this 2 years ago and it is still working great. It is easy to use and the auto psi is amazing. I can hook it up to each tire and let it run as I am doing other things in the garage. The light is very handy in situation such as your tire gets low while you are traveling at night. The compressor is small enough to fit under the passenger seat. The only complaint I have is it is really loud. In a little garage it can really get to you after 5 minutes.
summary: Great quality 2 years later, just really loud

reviewText: no problems so far. I used it to inflate my whater pressure tank for my water pump, and it worked very good. Accurate too, at least at the first 2 times i used it so far
Piece of junk. Took forever to inflate a normal car tire and broke after about 2 months. Total waste of money.

I got a small construction staple stuck in my tire. Right on the tread, a few very small holes. Exactly what this product is designed for. I followed the directions to a 'T', the Slime "clotted" in the hole and stopped the leak, and then I drove a few miles slowly to get the stuff well distributed in the tire. I measured the pressure over a few hours and it held. The next day, however, I drove to work and when I came back to my car that evening, the tire was flat. Lost pressure faster than when I had the staple in! It's been extremely cold here (Boston in February) and we've got a lot of snow, so my guess is that this stuff doesn't work too well in those conditions.I know a lot of people seem to have good luck with this, but I figured it would be useful to temper things a bit with the perspective of somebody for whom this product didn't work at all. Most importantly, watch out when using this in very cold weather.One more thing: if you look at the reviews you'll see that's it's pretty much either 5 stars (worked for people) or 1 star (didn't at all) with not much in between. It appears to work for about 3 out of 4 people, resulting in a pretty high average review (hence the four star overall rating). And that's assuming the Slime people are uncommonly honest and don't post false positive reviews.Put another way, THERE IS AT LEAST a 25% CHANCE THIS PRODUCT WILL BE A DISASTER FOR YOU! A 25% chance this will cause you far more trouble than if you'd just had the tire patched or used a more conventional tire sealnt, and that will make you deeply regret buying this. I'd actually say that for a product like this a 25% chance of failure is WAY too high. So, consider the 4/5 star review in that context. 4/5 might be a good rating for a TV, but for a product that is fixing something as important to your safety as a car tire, having a 3:1 ratio of five to one star reviews actually isn't that great.
summary: Works great... Until it completely stops working at all!

reviewText: I bought Slime Spair for my car's emergency kit.  I used it yesterday for a nail in my Honda Odyssey tire and it held up overnight until I could get to the tire shop.  It's very easy to use.  I just connect the hose and press a button and it inflated my tire.  I put some more air into the tire with my portable air compressor and didn't have any problems.The guy at the tire shop says this stuff ruins the rims when people drive around with it in their tires for months.  Since I only had it in overnight and I don't do it often, it was okay.  They were able to clean it out and fix my tire so it's good as new.  I'd rather do Slime than change a tire, so I am back on Amazon to buy another can.

reviewerName: P. Repage "FT Dad, Doctor & PT photographer"
reviewText: fix-a-flat generics are NOT a dime a dozen, as everyone claims - your local auto store or gas station make a fortune selling these to you when you need them at $9 / can or better. Buy them NOW for less, put 'em in your cars, and forget about 'em. You'll remember this review if that time ever comes...

I have a whole bunch of hobbies. One is off-roading in dune buggies, quads and motorcycles. Out in the middle of nowhere, flats are a super drag...I have tried all the liquid patches, and this stuff works by far the best. One trip out on a quad I grazed a very sharp rock, and it sliced a 2 inch long cut in the sidewall. I thought I was screwed, but I tried the Slime anyway. To my surprise, the tire held pressure for the 10 mile ride back to camp! Of course the tire was toast, but Slime got me back home.Another great use is rim sealing on big tires. I have 24" rims on my truck, and over time was having problems with the tubeless tires leaking air around the aluminum rims. I tried the fix a flat from the convenience store, and it worked only for about 10 miles, then started leaking again. Had to take it into the tire shop, where they remove the tire from the rim and applied a tar like sealant to the rim. Took 1 & 1/2  hours and $45 from my life...When my next tire started the same problem, I tried 1/3 a can of Slime. Problem solved, no leaks in 20,000+ miles. Even worked on the small tires on my commercial hand truck that needed air ever time I used it, and on the bicycles.Slime comes in two application types. One is just slime in a bottle so you can inject it into a tire before there is a leak. It just stays in there waiting for an air leak to plug up. The other application type is their "Quick Spare", which includes Slime and compressed air in a can to seal AND inflate a flat or low tire when your out and about.One of the things that worried me was if the Slime would damage my tire pressure sensors. No problems so far after 60,000 plus miles and 2 sets of tires.Over time I have put a can of Quick Spare in all my vehicles. It has saved me (and my friends I have had to rescue) a lot of time and money...
I keep it in my car, my Family's cars, and on my motorcycle. Ive seen another biker use it on a flat on his Harley and he got home OK.

The Slime is ideal if you want to avoid changing a tire or the hassle and expense of being towed to a service center.This is one of those things (like air?) that you don't know it's there until you miss it. We had a can for I don't know how long in the trunk, just in case and... the 'just in case' happened a couple of weeks ago. My wife was driving alone and it was night when one tire lost pressure while on an local road. With the Slime she was able to quickly fix the problem and drive the car home. The following day we drove to a place to have the tire replaced - no need for changing the tire on a road with no shoulder or calling for a tow. We're happy we had the Slime and I just ordered a replacement.Operation is as easy as attaching the nose to the valve and pushing a button. Once the rim gets off the ground you drive the car slowly for a couple of miles for the goo inside your tire to distribute properly and seal the puncture and then it's better than driving with a spare tire.As for limitations, it says on the can that it's not going to work on sidewall cuts, real large one or on valve leaks.
summary: We forgot it was there until we needed it

reviewText: I wanted to remove the full size spare tire from my trunk to reduce weight. I decided to get one of these instead and throw it in my emergency trunk bag. This weighs 1.5lbs, whereas my spare, tools, and floor weigh 46lbs. I also have AAA so besides when I travel across the country there's really no need to keep that dead weight in my trunk. I've only used slime once on a Saturn about 8 years ago, and it worked great. It reinflated the tire and filled the hole no problem. I drove on it for about 1k miles before getting it plugged. Note: This slime is TPMS safe, so it states. However it DOES make a huge mess inside the wheel. My rims and tires are rather expensive so I'd be apprehensive of using this, I really only keep it for emergencies when a tow (or phone call) home or anything else isn't an option.
I've used this stuff 3 times. Worked once for a day. Second time it failed, and the third time it seems to still be hanging tough. So kind of inconsistent has been my experience.
This stuff works for a little while but is not a permanent fix. On the other hand, it will get you going an is simple enough to use.

I have not had to use this. I am glad. It is in the RV side compartment and it is still liquid and would work just fine. It's been almost a year since we set out for the western deserts. We got two of them because Slime is good stuff and this does not have explosive propellant. I am going to buy two more to take on out Hurricane surf chasing trip this fall along the East Coast. I'll keep the old ones to hand out to folks with flats along the road as always.Robs report: This is something you should always carry and this is a good brand. Don't screw around. Get one and replace it yearly.
summary: Get it, you might need it.

reviewText: This is a great product. I live in ''Goat Head'' country here around the Four Corners area of NM. I use it in all my tires. Yard tractors, Wheel barrow and the neighbor kids come by for a squirt in their bicycle tires on occasion. I recommend it for all. I also carry a can in all my vehicles for emergency use, I'm to old to be changing a tire on the side of the road.
It works, but doesn't last

I use Slime in my farm equipment (tractor, tiller, dump cart) so I believe in the stuff.  I carry a can in each car and I showed my wife how to use it in case of a flat.  It's a hell of a lot easier than changing a tire (safer too).  It will get you anywhere you need to go and you can have the tire repaired whenever it's convenient.
summary: Carry one in your car for emergencies.

reviewText: Had some old may pops on a old truck I work on off and on, the rear tires always go flat and they are too expensive to replace now.  They are 20 year old tires.  Split a can of this in both of them, they hold air now.  Didn't even drive it around, just jacked it up and spun them some.
summary: Had old leaky tires, this fixed them

reviewText: Great hose for a small engine in need of new hose. This is durable and inexpensive hose sure to bring longevity when dealing with todays gasolines.
This hose worked well, though it does not stretch well, and gets hard if heated at all. Tough fit over nipples.

I put this fuel line on all of my outdoor equipment that I could.  It seems like it is holding up 200% longer than the cheap fuel line that you find in a store.  Well worth the purpose, no problems yet!
Product was exactly as described!  No defects or problems, recieved when promised, what you want when you order a product online.did not fit my 2000 yamaha golf cart. They seem good quality.
I paid 4 bucks a foot for this hose in a small engine shop ! I use it to connect my 2 Honda 2000i  generators to a 6 gallon external boat gas tank.Just wish it came in 10' pieces also.
This hose works great for getting fuel from the tank to the engine on the equipment it is installed on. I would recommend this to even my neighbor, it is that great.
These type of rubber might not last long. My last one rotted in just 2 years. I guess you suppose to cover your RV to protect these part from breaking.
summary: It works and I hope it last longer

reviewText: I certainly can not complain about this product.  It works great.  They only last about a season of camping due to the weather and sun damage.  I'll continue to buy them again.
It replaced my broken plug and strap perfectly. I think it could have been built out of a different hardness of material, but it should work as advertised.​
This simple, inexpensive, and important device will keep the fresh water inlet on your RV clean and sanitary.Good quality.
