reviewText: One of the large members only clubs sell a version of these towels that are thicker.  They also smell like they were dipped in a vat of WD-40 before they were shipped to me.  At least they don't leave a film on my vehicle.  I probably won't reorder.

These towels were a much higher quality than I thought they were going to be.The price was right to buy and try without costing a lot.I will buy more of these towels as they work well on cars and work well in the house for cleaning.I would suggest these towels to anyone that does not like iint.
Cheapest microfiber towels on all amazonI used it for 3 months with no problemsWashed in washing machine with no problems
I guess I only bought these to use for doing a rinseless type wash for the car and for doing general purpose cleaning on the car. Good value for the money.
summary: Not a bad cloth for the money.

reviewText: Bought these towels to use for rinseless washes but after a while, I felt they weren't the best towels to use for my paint.The towels themselves are quite grabby but they do make good window towels and for other general purpose ones.I'd recommend something else if you want to use this on your car's paint.

as most locking gas caps go, it's a pain to use the things and this cap makes it just a bit more of a pain... about a month ago, I unlocked the thing to put gas in, since you need the key to even put the thing back on the car I poked the key back into the hole and turned it and began putting it on as usual. It kept locking, causing it to spin freely even though the key was in and turned... and then it unlocked and stayed that way and I used it for about a week until I got another gas cap. I was afraid it was going to lock and I'd have to pry the stupid thing off and nothing would ever work on it again! meh, I'll find a way to make the door lockable...

Ordered this to fit my 2008 Dodge Ram 1500 Quad Cab. Did not fit at all...so I sent it back. It was well-made but not as well-made as the OEM that came on the truck. The keys are sturdy. BUT...after putting on my truck and locking it, I simply rotated it off. Either they sent the wrong one (I ordered the one they noted for my type of truck) or it simply doesn't work. Heard my truck has a system that doesn't allow anyone to put a syphon hose in the filler neck anyway.
summary: DID NOT FIT MY 2008 DODGE RAM

reviewText: This is a nice locking gas cap for my Jeep JK. it fits well, they may have updated it, you do not need to keep the key in it. Plastic is a little cheaper than I would like.

Used this to replace the gas cap going bad on my JK Wrangler. It fixed the problem completely. Looks like a good cap, the locking function is of much higher quality than most I have seen. The key is solid, and the cylinder is more substantial. The only complaint I would have is that the cylinder cover seems to be a little bit fragile - and will probably break off at some point. Otherwise one of the better locking replacement gas caps that you can get.

I've owned a few locking gas caps. Some have been junk and others were a pain to use. This one fits tight and the key/locking/unlocking action, by comparison to other locking gas caps I've purchased, is smooth and easy. A pleasure to use. What I consider to be a quality product.Price wise, considering the cost of today's gas, stopping a would be gas thief from jacking your car for five gallons, what price peace of mind? So it's money well spent.
summary: It's a quality locking gas cap.

reviewText: Fits my 04 r1 really snug and just about right without the rear fender. I mostly leave my bike in the garage with the cover on and keeps dust out. Would recommend

In short - at the price paid there's no reason not to have this cover.I measured my bike carefully and added this to a recent order, and I'm glad I did. I was a little hesitant to order a medium but it fits every dimension like it was made for my bike (Yamaha 250). While the material is light it's by no means flimsy, and the stitching and seams are spot on.  There's even an elastic clip and grommet to close it up under the pegs.If my bike was fully exposed to the weather I'd consider a heavier cover, but at the price point there's really no reason not to have one of these even for a bike that's stored in the garage.
My wife uses this cover for her scooter and it works pretty good. It does not cover the whole thing, but it gets the important stuff.
kinda cheezy. but it will get ths job done till it disentigrates from the sun and general exposure. cheap price.

Not a bad cover at all! I use it to cover my Yamaha XS1100, which is stored outside at all times, so this cover sees  everything that the weather can throw at it. I'm in Alabama, so this doesn't mean much snow, but lots of sun, humidity, and rain. I've been using it for about 8 months now, and have been very satisfied.Pros:* Waterproof. Keeps my bike completely dry even in some torrential rain. It has elastic at the front and rear that holds it to the tires, and there are grommets at the midpoints of the cover to run rope and cinch it in the middle.* Lightweight. I can easily ball it up and throw it in my backpack when I go on a longer trip, and don't notice its bulk or weight.* Fairly durable. It survives brief touches to the exhaust and hot engine. Brief. Very brief. It's not melt-proof by any means.Cons: (very minor, but I don't believe in a flawless product!)* Sort of hard to orient on the bike until you're used to it. I may just be slow (hey, it is what it is), but for the first few months I put this thing on in reverse every time. Look for the "ears" that accommodate your mirrors!* After 8 months, it is showing some weather damage. It has torn slightly near right mirror, so I'm going to replace it. This looks like it's due to sun damage. Again, it stays outside 100% of the time, and survived an Alabama summer with temps regularly in the mid-high 90s.Realistically, I'm more than happy to replace it every 8-10 months. Great product!Edit - 12/14/2011 - I finally bought another after 8 months of ownership. The old one is still okay, so I compressed it well, and it's now an emergency rain cover with my gear. Still happy!
summary: Best cover I have found for the price!

reviewText: I have a ninja 250 and this is the right size.  I think that is a small bike so beware the size but it is a good cover.

I bought this for my husbands yamaha yzf R6 and it covers it completely with room to spare. I bought this from amazon because they are more expensive in wally world and doesn't last long at all. His bike sits outside not in a garage and this is a must have. I will update again once we had it for a year to let you know how it holds up.

This is basically a dust cover. If it were advertised as a dust cover, I would give it 5 stars as it's great and cheap. However, they say it is water-proof which is definitely not the case.If you need a water-proof cover, look elsewhere. If you want a simple cover, you can't beat this price.
summary: Good cover for the price - Not waterproof

reviewText: Its listed at water resistant but it is not water resistant.Its raining right now and I can see my motorcycle is covered in water. No protection. Nada.Great fit great looking cover for maybe dust and wind but not for rain.Plan to return and get something with real water resistant cover.
summary: Good cover for price BUT NOT WATER PROOF

reviewText: works perfectly as described.  keeps my bike nice when I have to store it out side for a little while.
Cover fits my Daytona 650 sports bike just right with a little extra room. Perfect for keeping the dest away while stored in the garage.
heavier than expected, no rain storm yet so i wont know how it holds up, the other tore so easily, will repost if dosn't hold up well

This is a good product and the price is very good, esp for stainless steel. Does not look cheap and am confident that it will hold up in  the weather of the NW! Installs easily and scews were included (also S/S). Replaces the cheap plastic ones that come on so many RV's and generally fit existing holes (at least on my Arctic Fox trailer).
This was easy to install and works great!  Make sure you match up both sides or you will have issues when trying to latch it.

reviewerName: Hobbyist "Chemistry for fun, Computers for mo...
reviewText: Lots of plastic door stops fail.  Once you see this one you'll know it is the last one you'll ever install on that door.  Great fit and finish.  Bonus bumper stop which is not normally included.
this is really nice. its stainless steel so it wont rust an the bumper stops the bang and noise. plus it keeps the door open.
have not in stalled this unit yet, but, looks like it will take care of the issue just fine thanks
this adds so much more room to any shower with a curtain.  especially in campers.  best part is you can fold it out of the way for more room when not in the shower

As most of you know trailer shower tubs are ok, but tight.  This Extend -A- Shower worked great it gives you that extra shoulder room.  The only thing I changed was I bought a more aggressive screw rather than the ones that are given. Works great love it.

This is a great product.  As you know, the tub/shower is pretty small in a travel trailer and one is always 'up against' the shower curtain when taking a shower.  This extend-a-shower curtain holder provides additional space when showering and allows the shower curtain to keep the water inside the tub.  Great product and easy to install too.
summary: Best change ever made in my RV

reviewText: We have a 25 foot travel trailer and I really like having on board bathroom facilities but the shower is not very roomy. This thing makes a huge difference in available elbow room while showering. We added a shower curtain that has several mesh pockets and our shower space problems are solved. When turned back into the shower space it's also handy to hang wet items, like raincoats, to drip dry .I had some interference with the medicine cabinet but that was solved by installing it just above the top of the cabinet. At this height we could still use a standard 72 inch curtain and still keep the bottom within the shower enclosure. In fact about six inches of the curtain lays on the bottom of the shower floor which assures water does not run onto the floor. After showering I draw the curtain to the back left corner of the shower and hold it there with a nylon cord and a Scotch brand removable hook to which I fasten the cord. This keeps the curtain off the shower floor and allows it to drip dry.  Showering is much more convenient now.

We had those accordian shower door on our RV shower which seriously limited your elbow room.This gives us more room in the shower when it's in use and folds up out of the way when it's not.What more could you ask for?It is a little on the beefy side weight wise though.

We own two Specialized and two Raleigh bicycles that we mount on the Thule 4-Bike Parkway Hitch Bike Carrier. We use the carrier on a 1.25" receiver tow hitch. We always secure the bicycles to the carrier with a long corded bike lock. The only problem is that we used only a drawbar hook with a pin to secure it to the hitch. Anyone can just remove the drawbar and walk away with the bikes still attached to the carrier. The Heininger Hitch Lock is a great solution in protecting our investments. It is easy to use, solidly constructed and it is made in the USA.

I think this is is a dumb design. You have to put the key in and turn and turn and turn and turn. What it does is unthread on a small diameter bolt, maybe 1\4"? I get the impression that I need to put some silicone on it before using it to keep it from corroding and rusting. It will probably work fine to keep the hitch in the receiver, but not convenient and I doubt these small threads would survive a good pry bar. JMHO

The Heininger 6012 Advantage SportsRack 1.25" Receiver Trailer Hitch Lock appears to be well made and heavy duty. The lock operates smoothly and the threads are deeply cut and easy to thread. The lock cap and rubber knobs appear to be made with UV stable materials and should last a long time.I highly recommend this lock for your hitch, I will leave it on mine 100% of the time.My only concerns about the design is that the key rotates around several times when you unlock/remove the pin as the key must stay in the lock during the entire process. The problem with this is that any keyring the key is attached to will be spinning around and perhaps be a hindrance to unlocking the device as it could bind up in the confined area around the hitch pin lock.The solution is to use the key without a ring, but that can make the key easy to loose.I keep mine in a key box with with the spare tire tools.

We have always had trucks and trailers. My husband even used to build trailers. But for some reason we have never had a hitch lock. We used to always remove the receiver hitch if a trailer wasn't attached to the truck. An empty hitch can be real shin buster anyway. But now with this hitch lock we don't have to worry about someone stealing our hitch if we haven't removed it from the truck.The hitch lock is a Deadbolt brand and it's top notch. The ends are rubber coated so it's easy to grip. When using, you are actually screwing a pin in and out so turn the key 2 or 3 revolutions. Comes with a set of 2 keys. Love it, easy to insert, easy to use and protects our hitches.Highly recommend.
summary: Now I Can Leave The Hitch On

reviewText: This Heininger 6011 Advantage SportRack 2" receiver trailer hitch lock is a good solid deadbolt that will keep someone from removing your bike carrier and walking away with your bike(s).  If you have a Huffy, it's no great loss, but if you put a lot of money into purchasing high-end bike you really aren't into losing it.  The lock is quite solid with rubber-like grips on either end.  It has a weather-type seal to protect the key hole from being exposed to the elements.  Two keys are included and because they are so "generic" looking, I'd recommend labeling them with a daub of paint and etching in something that will enable you to recognize what they are for.I wanted this for a Thule hitch mount rack and it works perfectly.  I checked around and it does fit most Thule racks.  Most of the racks I looked at from the Allen to the Yakima are set up for the 2" hitch lock.  According to the manufacturer,  it fits" 2" x 2" trailer hitches (Class III and Class IV.)"  It's an easy process to check out what your rack needs before purchasing. The only thing I didn't like about it was that the flap to the weather seal is only " wide and might not hold up to a lot of use.  All things considered, I'd highly recommend it.
summary: This is a good solid trailer hitch lock for the money ...

reviewText: I like this a lot.  It does exactly what it says it will.  I havent tried to shoot it off or anything, but it seems strong and heavy duty.  I'm sure someone with a plasma cutter could take care of this in no time flat.  Of course, they could also just as easily take a hack saw to cut off the tongue of your trailer.My only gripe - the one star deduction (would really be a half star if possible) - is that the rain cap is tough to work.  It fits on nicely to keep the key hole dry and free from debris.  However, after a few muddy wet exposures, it becomes very difficult to open and even more difficult to close.Overall, great product.  I am not aware of any that is better.
summary: Works great so far - rain cap is a bit tough to work

reviewText: If you're traveling and need to keep your hitch on for some reason, and you're worried about people stealing it, then this is for you.There's only one key, so don't lose it.I locked my hitch on my truck and it worked great...BUT I forgot it was there and banged my shin on the hitch LOL...so watch your shins :)It seems sturdy enough, but I worry about having only one key.
summary: Nice if you want to leave your hitch on...but watch your shins.

reviewText: This lock is advertised and labeled as fitting class III and IV hitch receivers.  It is also recommended by Amazon to be purchased with the Allen 2 Bike Hitch Carrier.  Although this lock is solidly constructed, the 5/8" diameter pin is too large to fit either the Allen 2 Bike Hitch Carrier or any class III hitch receiver that I've ever seen.  Amazon was gracious about allowing me to return it for a full refund.  I've replaced it with a lock with a smaller pin that actually does fit a class III hitch receiver.  This large, heavy lock was apparently designed for a class IV hitch receiver, not a class III.
I liked this Hitch pin lock enough to purchase another for a different vehicle. easy to use and well built.

Purchased this to secure my tow hitch ball mount in the receiver. Felt a little more at ease that I had a lock on this, but the lock is cheap and looks like it can easily be broken into. The key has to be inserted and turned all the way multiple times to unlock it so its best if you don't have a bunch of crap on your keychain.Still have it on my tow hitch so that the ball mount does not get stolen.
summary: but the lock is cheap and looks like it can easily be broken into

reviewText: This is a bit larger than I originally anticipated and has a bit of a bulky appearance but unless you are really concerned about your hitch being the fashion envy of the neghborhood...this is terrific to help reduce those bruises when knocking knees. Very flexible, this installs easily just by slipping it into place. Helps reduce rusting - a nice extra - but the major benefit is in the additional layer or protection afforded.Simple yet effective idea!

My husband snorted when the HitchMate arrived.  "We already have a hitch cover," he said.  Then why, I thought but didn't say, is it rusting?  And how come your shins look like the shower scene in Psycho every time we haul brush.Today, he sheepishly admitted that the HitchMate was a good idea.  "It's nice," he said.  "It fits, and makes everything look neater."  Aha!  High praise indeed! I suspect that "nice" describes the flexibility of the HitchMate rather than its appearance, since the HitchMate actually lives up to its claim of being soft. I'm hoping for less gore during brush hauling.  Life is difficult enough and if a relatively inexpensive product can eliminate even one petty annoyance, why not go for it?The HitchMate snaps over the trailer hitch.  It takes about half a second to install, protects the hitch from the elements and one's limbs from the hitch.  It's elegant and intelligent in its simplicity of design and fits virtually all sizes of trailer hitches.Five stars and why did no one think of this before?

If you have ever really knocked your leg or knee on your hitch, or smeared grease on your pants, you will love this hitch guard!!This is a simple guards/pad that you just slip over your hitch ball to protect yourself and your hitch.  It is fairly thick but soft and claims to help keep your hitch ball from rusting and getting damaged-time will tell.This is a nice product that is reasonably priced but I wonder how long it will stay put and if it will deteriorate in the sun.
This is my second one. First one lasted 3 years before it split and still used it another 2.  Was updating some things and just replaced it. Other was still usable.

I don't know if the Heininger 6028 Hitchmate Soft Hitch Guard will stand up to the weather, but that's not an issue for me because I do not keep a tow bar in my receiver unless I'm towing every day (like when we're down at the beach).  I have front and rear receivers on my Jeep Liberty so I keep the Hitch Guard on my front tow bar when I'm towing one of my trailers and on the rear tow bar when I'm positioning trailers with the front hitch.  It has saved my shins a ton of times already and for $7 it has been well worth it.  Also, I've seen complaints about the fit but I solved that problem by putting the Soft Hitch Guard over a simple hitch ball cover.  I highly recommend the Heininger Soft Hitch Guard if you frequently have a tow bar in your receiver just waiting for a shin.  Hey, for $7 it's a great deal even if the weather eats it up in a couple of years!

Anyone who ever hit their shins on an unprotected hitch will appreciate this soft covering for the ball. Slips on and off easily yet is snug enough that it won't fall off.  That said, it could be pilfered by a lech.

The Thule Transport was designed to hang on the back of the passenger front seat to allow easy access to immediate necessities AND to be easily removable and taken away and carried as a shoulder bag or by the handle. It's a practical solution, properly sized to hold essentials, including a water bottle.It is organized as follows:- Main partition, zippered, about 16" by 11.5"- 8" by 11.5" zippered pocket- 8" by 11.5" semi-open pocket held closed with a Velcro patch- Water bottle pocket with an adjustable strap, able to hold any reasonable sizeThe black bag has grey, 2" wide adjustable shoulder/car seat strap and a grey handle.Well made of quality materials, the design stresses functionality, convenience and durability. It took us a few minutes to figure how to hang the bag to the back of the car seat but, once we learned the right ways and adjusted the strap to the proper length, taking the bag on and off the back seat was easy. Taking it off and wearing it as a shoulder bag was also quite comfortable for as long as the bag wasn't overloaded. However, carrying the bag by the ONE handle did not seem to be a good idea as the lack of a second handle makes it feel a little unbalanced.The Thule Transport can be a good storage solution, especially if the car lacks pockets on the back of its seats and, even if such pockets are present, this has the advantage of easy portability. A well built, well designed product, it deserves its 4 stars meaning "I like it".
summary: Quality build, well-thought design - can't get much better if you actually need one

reviewText: Update: my partner has since employed this as a macbook sleeve. Not its intended use, but effective, so I'm bumping it up a star.The idea here is that this organizer/bag's shoulder strap (which is attached at the top of the bag on one end and the side of the bag on the other, to better wrap around a car seat) slips over your passenger seat, so that that your bag can be conveniently accessed while you drive. The problem is that the bag is just too small to be useful outside of the car. . The bag itself is essentially flat and padded like a laptop sleeve--and not much larger--a mere 11" tall x 15" wide, and less than an inch deep inside at the bottom.The exterior pockets do have deep gussets--but not on the bottom--so what they hold has to be either small or flat as well, unless you never intend to remove it from the car (and that's the whole point, right?), because if you put much inside it won't close. The bottle pocket alone is gusseted on two sides, so it will hold a large bottle, and it does have a nice strap near the top, so you can cinch your bottle in when you're on the go or loosen it for when you're in the car.The other exterior pockets--two essentially flat pockets layered atop one another--have a gusset only on one side, which means they can't hold much, but that it is easy to access what's inside--this is a great feature when you're rummaging around in a pocket while you're driving. The layer between the pockets is stabilized with the same padding of the main bag, which also means the pockets stay upright and distinct, another nice feature. The exterior pockets are the best part of the bag, and why it gets 2 stars instead of 1.If it were advertised solely as a 3-pocket auto caddy--and the price were correspondingly lower--I would give this bag higher marks. Like all Thule products (I own 4 other Thule organizers between our two cars), it is very well made and will stand up to much abuse. But unless all you need to hold is a laptop or a few magazines or papers, it's virtually useless as bag (much less as a diaper/toy bag, as suggested--you could maybe fit 3 small diapers, laying flat and side by side, or a few children's books or happy meal toys; forget anything else).Thule typically makes very sturdy, clever car organizers, but this bag has an identity crisis. It should either be simply a caddy that stays in the car, and have an extra strap to secure the bottom as well (the laptop sleeve portion would be okay for mail or maps, etc.--although who uses maps anymore?)--or it should be deeper with a boxed bottom on both the main bag section and pockets, like a messenger bag, so it's roomy and useful outside of the car, as well. As it is, it's missing the mark both ways.[For the record, I received this bag from Vine for review. Both the Vine description and the product packaging pitch it more as a bag--the box even shows it slung over the shoulder, messenger-bag style. However, the regular Amazon listing makes it sound more like a simple car organizer. Based on the packaging and the price--$10-15 more than the typical small Thule car organizer--I'm assuming the intention really is a dual-purpose bag designed for easy car access/organization, not simply a car organizer, and I'm reviewing it based on that assumption.]
summary: decent organizer; but too small and flat to be useful out of the car

reviewText: This organizer is very well-made.  The zippered, main partition, as well as each pocket, is padded, and lined with nylon fabric. The padding reminds me of a laptop sleeve. I expect the organizer to last a long time.I had a little room to spare when I put my daughter's laptop in the zippered, main partition. Her laptop measures approximately 13.5" x 10.25" x 1". A pad of paper and a pocket folder will fit in the pocket, but you won't be able to fasten the velcro. There is a zippered pocket in front of the velcro pocket, and a third pocket which is designed for a bottle which has a strap so the pocket can be cinched tightly around the bottle.This organizer would also be handy to carry a few diapers, some wipes a couple bottles, some small toys, & your wallet for those quick trips to the store, rest area stops, or anytime you don't need to bring a huge diaper bag with you. It's designed to slide over the back of the front passenger seat so the driver can reach into it...but the bottle holder is on the far side making it difficult for the driver to reach...if there's no front seat passenger, the organizer can be faced forward making everything easy to reach. It's nice and sturdy, not flimsy;  items are easy to grab. As stated in the product description, it comes with a lifetime warranty.Handy for passengers in the back seat, too, it's not very wide & won't take up too much leg room. It's always nice to have some place to put your drink, pull out a book or magazine to read, an activity book, some tissues, pen & paper, & hand sanitizer...maybe even your dog's leash & brush for those long car trips.Thule designed this organizer to be portable, to slide over the front passenger seat so the driver can have access to it...and if need be, it can then be taken with you...carry it over your shoulder or use the grab-and-go carry handle.I can think of lots of ways to use this...just be aware that it isn't overly big.

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: Thule.  It sounds like some monster you'd find Conan battling with. The way this thing is constructed, Conan could probably carry it around.  That's Conan as in the Barbarian, not the red haired one. All the hardware is heavy-duty and has a quality finish. The shoulder/seat strap is a generous 2" wide and is soft and pliable, yet strong and does not stretch.The organizer has two large zippered pockets and one sleeve - this has an accordion fold at one end with a separate water bottle pocket. I wish they would have put a drain hole in this area. A sweating / leaking bottle can get the neighboring section of the accordion fold wet. The zippered pockets will remain dry.Each of the zippered pockets has a minor amount of padding - it feels like 1/8" high-density foam. These zippered pockets are also pretty darn water resistant.  I dumped an ounce of water in one - at first no leaks - added more water and it started to leak.  Tried it again in the other pocket - same result.  Although the zippers are not waterproof (few zippers are) the zippered pockets are pretty close.There's really nothing that delineates this shoulder bag. It's not specifically for a vehicle - more like dual purpose.
summary: Well made, quality components and construction

reviewText: This is a very well made bag.  It has one very large zippered and plastic lined section, another smaller and plastic lined front pocket,  as well as a small water bottle sized section.  Between the front section and back section is a full length pocket, unlined, secured by a tab of Velcro.  The bag has carrying handles as well as an adjustable strap to fasten it to the car seat.I found that having it behind the car seat as shown made it more difficult for the driver to reach back and get the drink, as it is then at the other side of the car.  For a back seat passenger this would be fine.Instead I use the bag so that it hangs on the front passenger seat (when there is no passenger of course!). This leaves the water bottle pocket close to the driver and I am able to store all the stuff that accumulates in the car in the pockets (wipes, tissues, pens, cord for the mp3, magazines etc).  Then, if I have a passenger I simply flip it to the back part of the seat. I no longer have to clean all that stuff off of the seat before someone can get in.I would give it  4.5 stars if possible because I would have liked to see smaller pockets along the front for really tiny items (like gum, sunglasses and so on) as well as a way to unclip one side, to make it easier to remove from the car as needed.A really well made item, strong stitching, quality metal parts and clean design which makes me round it up to the 5 stars.
summary: Well made bag, helps with organization, although I use it facing forward, not along the back of the seat.

reviewText: Pros:Storage that fits nicely in our CRVStrong zipper and handlesFabric weight goodCons:Overpriced at even the discount cost of approx. $35No compartment storageMetal V side braces difficult to posiitonReality:Holds stuff!Will not be subjected to much stress as it will stay in our CRV and items will be taken in and out as needed; and will most likely hold up for quite some time.Any good duffle bag might serve the same needs.Suggest Thule:Lower priceAdd compartments

This product does not deliver value.  It is labeled as 'large' and having a capacity of 64 liters.  I had hoped this tote would live up to its advertising but it did not even come close.  I am still wondering what the purpose is for the "clear" top panel since a) it has a dense white grid pattern  and b) it cannot be seen through.  The carry handles are inconvenient and require one to use two hands as they are placed vertically at the midway point of each side.  Very awkward to carry anything, let alone a full load.  The frame is not sturdy and you would not be able to put anything on top of this.  The non-skid base does not keep the tote in place as claimed.  The final nail in the coffin is the price; I find the $50 price tag almost laughable since the item falls so short of its claims.  Depending upon your need I would recommend using duffel bags or those plastic molded totes with lids if you need more support.  In both cases you will save yourself some hard-earned cash.

I had high hopes for this product since keeping things organized in my trunk is challenging. I have a hatchback and always keep the back seats folded down. I am also not able to fully grasp the concept of "traveling light" so there's always a lot of stuff knocking about.I have an organizer that I really like - it's made by Rola (their M.O.V.E. model which comes in various sizes and is sold by Amazon). It has moveable dividers, collapsible, and is perfect for keeping grocery bags and the like secure in the trunk. But, it's low, so tall things can topple out. I had been using an old plastic bin to carry taller items, and thought the Thule bag would be much better.Well, it looks nice, but in terms of actual use, doesn't offer any more value than my $1.99 plastic bin. The Thule bin has the capability to collapse, but it's somewhat ackward to do - the metal rods are tough to wedge into place. It's a two-handed operation. The Rola design is much better/easier.There's no dividers within the bin, nor are there any pockets on the outside. It's basically a nylon representation of a box, with a zipper on the top and handles on the side. The base is non-skid, but is not all that grippy. Stopping short caused the bin to slide quite a bit.I wish I could be more positive about this since Thule does make some good products. While this is well-built (good zipper, nice stiching, and quality nylon material) it needs to go back to the drawing board -- either add more value to it by adding features such as dividers, pouches, etc. or drop the price by way more than half. As it stands, if you buy this you're paying an awful lot for something that is functionally equivalent to a plain box.
summary: Nicely made, but not a good value

reviewText: At first glance the high quality of the materials and construction makes this seem like a very nice bag.The design however is a bit baffling.  As shipped, the side handles come inside the side straps. (making it difficult to use the handles until you take it apart and reassemble it "correctly") What purpose do the side straps serve?There is no handle on the top, so if you are going to carry this somewhere it is a "two hand" job using the side handles.  This is not your typical luggage bag.The basic idea is that this bag is normally collapsed and thus takes up almost no space.  However the metal supports, which are used to prop the bag in the open position, have nothing to secure them in the open position and thus the bag tends to collapse frequently.  Certainly this results in an exercise in frustration as you attempt to store items inside the bag.It's a nice bag, but I would prefer if they didn't bother putting in the metal frame which deludes you into thinking this is intended to be propped open.

This is a trapizodial box with a zipper top.  There is a wire frame you must push down to get it to stand up.  (Hint: place it on a hard flat surface to get the wire sides to stay in place.)  There is a zipper across the top, handles on the sides and cynch straps on each side to tighten ____ (?) (I have no idea.)Mine arrived incorrectly assembled.  The cynch straps ran outside the handles and made the handles unusable.  I looked at the picture on the box and realized the cynch straps were supposed to go inside the handles.  You can't unthread the cynch straps, but you can unhook them from the bottom attachment and re-run them.The "clear" panel on top is not clear at all.  Translucent maybe.  No chance you can see what is inside.The "non-skid" base is really not very effective at all - especially because the smooth fabric from the sides wraps around the bottom edges.I really don't understand the purpose of this.  A cardbox would do the same thing.  In fact, it might do it better.  This has a trapizodial shape which is smaller on the bottom than the top. This greatly reduces your ability to put things in the bottom.  It also only has a central zipper, so you can't even open the whole thing up to put in tall items.There are no internal dividers, and not even any tie down points around the outside to afix it to the floor of your trunk.Essentially, you are buying a fairly ineffective box with a THULE logo on the outside.  I, for one, am not at all impressed with this product and do not recommend it.  Two stars - not one - because the fabric, zipper and overall assembly are pretty high end.
summary: A cardboard box would do the same thing

reviewText: I thought this would be the perfect organizer of sorts for my husband's SUV. The size and description seemed perfect. However, unless you plan on loading the organizer/tote inside of the vehicle, it is not very easy to carry or transport. The handles are awkward and the quality of construction just did not seem worth the price. I agree with the other reviewer who mentioned that Amazon went overboard with non-Eco friendly packaging for mailing the item -- unnecessary! The box could have been shipped in it's original packaging as the item it is not breakable, and the cardboard box it was packed in at the factory was sturdy. Disappointing.

This is a nice product that is larger than I thought it would be yet it fits nicely in my trunk against one of the sides.It collapses nearly flat for storage when you aren't using it and yet it is quite sturdy when set up correctly. It's way more attractive and durable than a cardboard box.It can be a bit tricky to set up at first; the trick is the side metal supports need to slip UNDER the bottom surface. Pressing the arrow labels on the bottom surface helps with this. If you read the instructions, it will tell you this. Once you do this, the organizer is all setup and very rigid. I do not miss the lack of a top handle on this since it's mainly designed to remain in your trunk all the time.The bottom line is this is a useful, utilitarian and attractive item that I recommend to anyone who typically has a lot of loose items floating around in their trunk. Get organized!
summary: A Large trunk organizer that is well made!

reviewText: The mount is very solid, and is about as good as you can get w/out getting an aftermarket bumper. The only reason I took off a star is because the instructions are absolute garbage! I had to search for write ups/explanations online because the pictures in the instructions are just a black blurr.. Can't see anything. Also, I managed to install with the hinge covers. I trimmed the ends of the black plastic covers off, but was unaware that they would eventually tighten down and clear the hinge. Oh well. Still a good mount. Doesn't make any noise and I didn't have to make any fabrications.

This is a good, solid mount.  It's very sturdy and pretty nicely made.  Why didn't I rate it five stars?  A couple of things weren't quite perfect.  First off, the bolt holes for the top swing-away holder weren't lined up.  Not a big deal, it was fixed pretty readily with some pliers to bend it into place.  But not perfect.  Also the included locking washers are flimsy and got all mangled, so I replaced them with some I had on hand.  And finally, the instructions are pretty useless so look through the installation first before getting started.Overall, I'd certainly buy it again, but it's not worthy of a perfect rating because of these little things.Install tip:  You will want to mark and drill the stock hinge covers.  The product includes spacers to allow enough separation so you can install those, but you have to drill two holes in each one.  Mark them carefully, then drill with a 1/2" bit.  The fit doesn't have to be perfect as this mount will cover the holes on the right and the spare covers the holes on the left.
NICE MOUNTING BRACKET. FITS WELL PRETTY EASY TO PUT ON. NO PROBLEMS WITH NOISE. ITS A JEEP AND JUST TURN UP THE MUSIC. LOOKS VERY NICE TOO. ALSO LIKE THAT IT LOCKS.

reviewerName: Esteban A. Valle "--Don't ask what Windows ca...
reviewText: This mount is bombproof. It is very solid and looks great. I didn't have any trouble installing it, and I installed it first without the plastic covers, and then reinstalled it with the covers. It is very strong, alot stronger than you would think. I would almost not hesitate to stand on this mount, at least one foot. I really like how it locks the jack, and the rubber pads keeps it from vibrating too much. One thing I did do is line the jack stand platform (where the base of the jack sits) with a shop towel, although I am changing to a thin rubber mat. This keeps everything from scratching and lowers vibrations.I really like the way that this mount looks on my Jeep, especially with the hinge covers installed. It feels very solid with the jack in place, and the jack fits perfectly. The only gripe I have is that you have to totally remove both knobs, the bottom washer, and plate to remove the jack from the mount. This isn't a huge deal but it makes them prone to getting lost.Other reviewers are right about the instructions, they are not very clear. You can find some tutorials online though, which are great. Personally I just followed the instructions as they are not horrible and it is pretty much self explanatory.Biggest thing is make sure to measure the gap when drilling your plastic hinge cover, as some claim the template provided is not accurate. In my case, it was, but I still did it by hand. It's easy if you have one half (top or bottom) installed, you can place the cover underneath the uninstalled half and use a center punch through the bolt holes to mark where to center your drill bit. Use a 1/2" drill bit, but wiggle it around a bit. You can use a larger (9/16") bit, but I do like how tightly the spacers fit into the hinge covers using a 1/2". It makes it look nice and feel more "watertight" even though that doesn't matter at all. Having them tight also makes it alot easier to fit everything together when installing all of the pieces (I think some of the bolts need like 6 pieces to line up for the installation). I actually used a little tiny strip of duct tape to tape some of the washers to the inside of the spacer which made my life alot easier. I also tried taping the washer to the end of a firm wire rod and "fishing" it into place. Both methods were pretty good actually, and with the "fishing" method I didn't have to leave the tape on the washer.I don't particularly like adding this much weight to the tailgate of my Jeep, especially with a bike mount on my spare tire. So when I get the money to replace my bumpers I'm going to move my high-lift onto a bumper with a rear tire carrier built in. That will push the weight off the frame and onto the chassis.
My Hi-Lift with the cast base (v. the stamped) doesn't fit very well in this.  Not sure if I will end up using it.
summary: Doesn't fit my jack very well.

reviewText: The 48" hi-Lift hangs over the soft top roof by 3.5" (with the top clamp down or off). I may cut my 48" jack down to 44".  It has tons of leverage against the gate bolts if it snags a good sized limb. Having the extra weight on the gate isn't ideal, but at least it's over the hinges. The manual says only to put 50lbs on the back including the spares weight. The rubicon tire is 75lbs (guess they are not great at math) so really adding any weight isn't great.The base of my cast steel doesn't slide under a lip it was made to slide under. It still will work. I'm going to try to pry it up a 1/16" to make it work better. Maybe it would fit with the cheaper black model base better.NEEDS BOLTS AND ANOTHER SPACEROn the 2012+ there is an extra three 1/2" spacers included to clear the larger hard top window. It's on the last page of the instructions included. It hasn't been added to the online PDF instructions yet. Take a look at that last page before installing. They forgot to add 2 bolts and a spacer to properly take care of the issue. At very least it is missing one 8mm x 70mm metric hex cap bolt. It should say 8.8 or 10.9 on the end. 2 of those bolts is better with a 3/8" x 1" nylon spacer. I found the hardware at menards. Home Depot doesn't carry it.The finish is a wrinkle powdercoat. It looks alright, but will likely hold dirt.The instructions pictures are easier made out off the web. They are on the RR website.After installed it is pretty stout.If you have a 4dr just stick your 48" jack under the rear seat. It's a better option. There are also some good roll bar mounts.INSTALL NOTES AND TIPSI had to remove my rubicon tire before installing. I tried with it on, but the top left bolt was an issue.TRIMTo remove the gate trim pull/push toward the handle side. Then pull back on that side. Then after that angled retainer pops out just give a good tug straight out to get the other side. Label the bottom and top on the inside trim. The top is slightly deeper. It will be very noticeable if they are swapped (1/8" gap on the top. Bottom will look nice).  The instructions template was not printed to scale in the directions. I printed out another true to size template off the RR site. There was an 1/8" difference. It turns out the supplied template was a better fit for me. Line it up with the bolts before drilling. I drilled the hole with a 3/4" wood bit (1/2' will not work for sure).  That will give you some wiggle room. You can also use a hole saw. It will get covered by the plate so no reason to cut it too close. There are a couple places were duck taping the washers to the mounting plates can come in handy if using the factory trim.. It will show if you look directly down at it, but will not be noticeable. If you extend it off the edge maybe you could pull it out after the install.BOLTSThe bolt sizes are mostly 13mm and a couple 15mm at the end. You will want touch-up paint after removing the factory bolts. You can take both the bottom off at the same time with the gate closed. Same thing with the top, just don't take all the bolts out at once. Leave 2 in.  If your installing with the factory trim you'll need to tape the washers before installing the trim. With no tire carrier you will install the big mount also with the right side bolt.On step 2 It's really confusing they say if you have a RR tire carrier do this. Well here is what your going to end up doing with just the factory set-up. Your going to install all the washers and spacers on the bottom right. On the bottom left you will also add the main mount before bolting it on. 2012's that are using the white spacers can bolt both sides with the included bolts and skip adding the main mount part. A better method IMO is to use a longer 70mm bolt and also put a store bought 3/8" spacer (between the main mount and the mounting plate) in on that step.2012+ hardtop owners will add a spacer to the top right bolt. If you use the supplied bolt you will be lucky to get 2 threads screwed in. It really needs a 70mm length bolt.Hope that helps someone. The install took way longer than I expected. Mostly hunting down the bolts. Overall I don't love it on the back. I like it there just a bit better than adding it to the hood because of the jacks weight.
summary: It may be the best 2 dr option but it's got issues

reviewText: Price: a bit over priced for what you get.Design: A great place for your jack and a good start at the design.  Metal plates could of been better sized and shaped to fit the stock Jeep hinges.Quality:  Although this seems like it will hold up in the weather and is nice thick powdercoated steel, the mounting holes on mine did not merry up with the hinge holes in my jeep.Directions: poorly written photocopied directions with images that are too dark to see.Overall:  A decent mount, but poor implementation.
So far, so good!  Meets my BMW needs or requirement.  I would definitely get it again in the future and use it for my other cars.

As owners of only BMWs and Volvos, this product works for both. Free shipping makes it affordable. Price is still less than BMW's own antifreeze. One Volvo is 30+ years old without any cooling system issues. Changed every two years, car(s) will last forever.

I bought it for my 2001 Dodge Intrepid. I used exactly one bottle, 1 gallaon, of it and mixed it with 1 gallon of distilled water. I did a complete flush using the Zerex flush it works perfect also if anyone was wondering it's a redish orange colour.

I called several Auto Zone, Advance Auto Parts, and O'Reilly stores in my area and none of them carried this coolant that is required for my Mercedes C230. Great price and quick shipping with Prime here from Amazon.
summary: Great price on coolant for my Mercedes

reviewText: Used after a full-flush of my 2005 Chrysler Crossfire Limited Roadster.  Seems to work fine, will know more when winter hits.  Only odd thing - the back of the container seems to indicate that this isn't the product to be used in Mercedes engines of my year, even though almost every website around indicates that this is indeed the required product.

Works as expected.expensive, but a good product.i recommend it.i looked and couldn't find it at any of the part storesSo amazon was as convenient as I could get.engine doesn't overheat,that's all I need

I read my owners manual and for my 2007 Jeep Commander Overland with 5.7L HEMI, it was clear that only an antifreeze/coolant that has HOAT composition would be appropriate for topping off the radiator - at least if I didn't want to ruin the anti-corrosion protection of the MOPAR original fluid, and have to completely flush the system later....Be careful because in the stores the antifreeze/coolant bottles all claim that you can pour their stuff into "any" car, "any" color antifreeze/coolant.  But the fine print says "only for short term topping up" and "must completely flush system and top up with fresh coolant" to preserve the anti-corrosion properties of the original fluid.  So basically I read these and concluded that it was misleading.This fluid is a correct replacement for the MOPAR fluid in my vehicle (2007 Jeep Commander Overland with 5.7L HEMI) and will not react with the existing fluid in the vehicle or compromise the long-term protection provided (100K miles between services).I purchased a gallon of distilled water from a large retailer, and mixed up two gallons from this full strength gallon here.  It was a slightly cheaper alternative to purchasing the pre-mixed 50/50 solution that is also offered.  I made sure to tightly cap the two bottles and label them so they're not confused with windshield washer fluid or orange juice....
summary: Hard to find at brick and mortar stores...

reviewText: Purchased sand paper  used 400 grit first, then 1000,2000, then 3000 grit and then buffed with polish and then used a lens sealer purchased separately...most important use sealer or it will oxidize again.  love the buffing ball....follow directions, use at a low speed to avoid heat...melting the lens.  If your lens is lightly yellowed you wont need to sand, just buff and seal!
It works to the extent that it clears up your lenses.  It would of been nice to have another set of abrasion pads included because they wear out on the drill quickly.

I've watched the demonstrations on how to restore your headlights and I couldn't believe it until I actually tried it out myself. I give this product 5 stars because it actually works! Now I don't have to worry about driving at night because my lights are CLEAR. It beats buying new headlights for sure.
This really does appear to work.  Admittedly, I didn't have much to clean up, but once done they look brand new.  Now I want to find some unsuspecting neighbor car and do one side; take photos.

My wife's car had headlights that were so cloudy, you couldn't even see through them. Her headlights were very dim, so much so that her high beams were only about as bright as most people's low beams.My dad purchased this kit to use on his vehicle, but we tried it out on my wife's car first. It took about 30-45 minutes per headlight, but we were able to restore them to like new condition. They are now crystal clear, and there is no yellowing at all. We can't even see any scratches left from the wet sanding process. It worked better then we could have ever expected. Her lights look like they could have come right off the assembly line.The key to this kit is the wet sanding pads. It is the specific reason we bought this kit over the others. There are 2 pads, and 4 grit levels that you work your way through before using the power ball. You start with #1 and work your way up to #4. In all, it took about 30-40 minutes or so of wet sanding per headlight to get through all the 4 levels. Once finished with sanding, the lights should have be white and cloudy. Then you take the polishing compound and the power ball in a drill to the lights. The polishing compound will completely get rid of the cloudiness left from the sanding, and your lights will be crystal clear once again.I would recommend this kit to anyone. It worked wonders for us and will definitely use it over again.
summary: Restored severely cloudy headlights to new condition.

reviewText: Simple, quick review.This is a headlight polisher, not a restoration kit despite what the box says.Will improve your headlights dramatically.Has to be used about once a month to keep the head lights in good condition.Not bad for the price.

Following the directions years of cloudiness and yellowing disappeared completely.Our two, ten & 14 year old, Toyotas cleaned up like new.  The one car was so bad weHad to use the four sanding disks included in the kit.  This is not back breaking work, but merely keeping the sanding disk wet and rinsed makes this job a breeze.The kit is complete with everything you need except a 3/8 corded drill for the enclosed buffing ball.For the faint of heart checkout the numerous U-Tube instructions for this product, it really works!
I couldn't see any improvement at all. I sanded, I polished, over and over again. I got nothing. This was a total waste of money.

I have tried other headlight restoration kits and some of them work OK.  Mothers PowerBall 4Lights works great.  I did one headlight and just started laughing because I could not believe the dramatic difference between the headlight I had done and the other one.  It was fairly amazing.  The headlight I had done looked practically brand new while the other one was still so cloudy I started wondering how I was ever able to drive the car at night.  I did the second headlight and it came out just as well.  Tonight we drove the car to the DQ along our dark country Ranch Road.  I started laughing again because I could not believe how much further down the road I could see.  Again, it was fairly amazing.  This product works and the entire job took about 20 minutes.  I will definitely recommend this product to my friends.

These wiper blades are extremely sturdy and do a great job of clearing the windshield in rainy conditions. Not sure yet about snow as it's still summer here,  but I'm pretty certain they'll do a great job at that too.  The fit the windshield very snugly and have a very strong arc in them. If your wiper arm is not extremely strong, however, they may not fit the curvature of your windshield and thus leave a gap in the clearing action.All the necessary installation "how to" is in the package. Along with the blade comes various parts to fit a variety of wiper arms with the instructions for all of the types.  I don't mind the pink ribbon on the blade and it's really not noticeable unless you fixate on it. As another reviewer wrote, if you want to get rid of it just cover it with a sharpie marker swipe.I'd recommend these with a caveat, that I have not tried them out in winter just yet.

This is the strangest offering yet by Amazon Vine.The wipers are offered in packs of 1, and I was not aware you could not order two of the same size.  I have a GMC Savana that requires two 22" blades.  I place the Vine order for one, and then found I could not order another.  Obviously, replacing one wiper blade is not going to help.  What use is receiving just one?I can buy another from Amazon for approximately $17, but my Anco wiper refills cost $6 and work fine.  We are not allowed to return or give away Vine merchandise, so what was this offer good for?

On receiving this wiper blade in the post I cleaned off the tree sap from my windshield.  It took five minutes to figure out how to change the old wiper for the new one.  The diagrams on the packaging were a bit confusing and the box says see installation instructions enclosed are but there were no instructions. Thankfully you can work it out and once you do, it's a piece of cake to install.The blade is constructed quite simply, is well made and far lighter than the blade I removed. The wipers I have are the 18 inch ones to fit a Mazda Miata.  I sprayed the windscreen with water and turned on the wipers and it worked perfectly so now I'm ready for the rain this autumn.The Autotez wiper seems to have a more even pressure along the length and followed the windscreen evenly. It's a bit too early to judge overall performance but everything seems to work as it should, it's a nicer more elegant -looking wiper with fewer parts to go wrong.  I like it.

Don't get me wrong, I am rating the performance of this item.It does a really nice job cleaning the window without streaking, smearing or having any drop outs.  It was super easy to put on and it looks good on my sons vehicle.The only down side is the little pink bow decal on the top side of the blade.  I am all for fighting breast cancer (men or women) but I don't want to look at a little pink bow and neither does my son.  Fortunately, a dab from a sharpie pen corrected the situation.Nice blade, good cause, but don't force me to look at your logo; regardless of color.

I did a little research on Wexco Industries while I was awaiting the very swift delivery of my AutoTex "PINK" - Black Bracketless Premium Wiper Blade - 18" and learned that the company is woman owned, and began in 1991 as Wipers Express.  According to their website, "Today we are a global supplier of quality windshield wipers and engineered systems to the heavy duty bus, RV and other specialty markets."  I trusted the newfangled design to work and I've not been disappointed.  The label, "PINK" can imply that the blades are pink, but they are definitely black like most other windshield wiper blades.  The "PINK" represents the company's  partnering with the NBCF.  Another plus for the product.  Men, do not be turned off by the notion of blades with the pink ribbon insignia, it's very small and unobtrusive.  It does not affect the functionality of this blade.  Since I've replaced many wiper blades, this was very intuitive for me.  If you are inexperienced, you can watch the video which I think designed to show how easy the process can be if you're not replacing rusted blades.  The instructions are inside the box with an assortment of connectors for a majority of arm types, and there are additional diagrams and information on the box.  They are written in English, Spanish and French.  I expect that the blades will work as well in inclement weather as they do in a slight rain.  It's easy to remove debris by lifting the blade from the windshield and I've seen no unusual streaking or skipping on this smaller blade of my pair for a Honda Accord.  The longer blade does have problems not fully touching the windshield, hence a three star review for these blades.

I bought this for my wife's Miata because the typical windshield wiper does not have enough curvature to meet the curve of the Miata's windshield. It does a better job than most but still does not curve enough at the very end.Since we get little rain in Reno, I haven't been able to test how effective it is in wiping off the rain but I will update this review when I find out.12/29/12 Update: With little rain here I can say that it seems to work as well as any other wiper blade. Because of our hot dry climat, blades don't last very long in Reno before becoming stiff and unable to flip over, thus squeaking. This blade is still doing O.K.

The AutoTex wiper blades are easy to install and compatible with most vehicles (use the "Make Sure It Fits" compatibility tool to check compatibility - more on that below).- Compatibility CheckFirst things first - Make sure to check whether your wiper arm is compatible with these wipers by using the compatibility tool ("Make Sure It Fits") on top of the product page. Select the Year, Make, Model of your vehicle and click "Go" to determine whether your wiper arm is compatible. To see other AutoTex PINK blades that fit this vehicle, click on "See similar products that fit this vehicle", click on "Blades" in the breadcrumb trail "Replacement Parts > Windshield Wipers & Washers > Wipers > Blades," and click on "AutoTex PINK" on the left.- Compatible With Different Wiper Arm ModelsThe blade comes with G, B, D, and H adapters for fitting the different types of wiper arms. Right out of the box, it comes pre-fitted with a G adapter for the Hook, Pin, or Bayonet type wiper arms. The other adapters - the B, D, and H adapters are for Side Lock System, Top Lock System, and Top Button System wiper arms, respectively. The blades comes with clearly illustrated instructions on which adapter to use.- Easy To InstallMy wiper arm is the Hook type, so the blade is ready to install right out of the box. The installation went without a hitch. A lever has to be pulled up before the wiper arm can be inserted into and hooked onto the new blade. The blade needs to be pushed in all the way into the hook before the lever can be pushed down to secure the attachment. The whole installation took me seconds to complete.- Good PerformanceI had the wiper blades for both the driver and passenger sides replaced. The blades effectively squeegee water from the windshield. However, the blade on the driver side skips a little and squeaks on the return stroke. It's rather annoying, really. Actually, my old blade had the same problem, so I won't fault the AutoTex blade for the malfunction. If your blade has the same problem, it might be well worth looking into a couple of remedies:1) Thoroughly clean your windshield with Windex. Stuck on deposits can sometimes cause skipping.2) Lubricate the wiper-windshield contact surfaces with Rain-X or WD-40.(i) Rain-X - Rain-X not only helps water droplets bead off the windshield, it helps to lubricate the windshield to allow the blade to glide on it smoothly.(ii) WD-40 - Spray some WD-40 onto a cloth/paper towel and rub the lubricant on the rubber contact points on the blade. Make sure to use the WD-40 *SPARINGLY*; excessive WD-40 can cause streaking!- Pleasing AestheticsFrameless wiper blades are still somewhat of a novelty. The simplicity of the design is a refreshing departure from conventioanl windshield wiper designs. Its smaller profile helps it blend in unobtrusively with any windshield. The obverse side of the blade features the pink Susan G. Komen Breast Cancer Foundationand. The smidgen of pink the logo imparts to the wiper blade is a nice touch. The logo is visible from the cabin and its eye-catching color helps you declare your support for the Breast Cancer Foundation to find a cure for breast cancer.- A Word on PackagingThe corrugated cardboard box (not the AutoTex box) the AutoTex blade was shipped in was almost twice the length of the AutoTex box. It arrived snapped in two a third of the way from one end. The contents had also been tampered with. The AutoTex box was opened and the adapters and instructions were missing! That's disconcerting. Luckily, I didn't need any of the adapters. Just thought I'd mentioned the problem with the packaging.---The AutoTex wiper blades are easy to install and delivers very satisfactory performance. If you're not satisfied with your AutoTex wiper blades, AutoTex offers a 30-Day Money Back Guarantee. Simply return them for an exchange or refund. These AutoTex wiper blades are definitely worth consideration if you're looking to replace your wiper blades.

Since I had just noticed my wiper blades needed replacing, I was pleased to see this item on the Vine newsletter and promptly ordered. The compatibility check is very convenient and tells you instantly which size to order for your car. Delivery was prompt, but the cardboard box was huge. Twice the length of the blade. Then the real surprise - there was only one blade! When you order one - you get one blade, not one set.I looked at the blade carefully, trying to decide if I wanted to order another one since the price per blade is more than most. The rubber blade is certainly much thicker and seems more sturdy that any I've ever had before, so I ordered another one and waited for it to be delivered.It arrived promptly, too, and installation turned out to be very, very easy, since my car has the bayonet type fitting, which the blade arrives with. The frameless style is quite nice. BUT, if you have a different type of fitting, the back of the package instructs you to refer to the instructions and additional adapters inside the box. Well, neither of mine came with any instructions or adapters in the box. Lucky for me that my car uses the the adapter that comes installed in the blade and I have installed wipers before. Other reviewers seem to have had the same experience.The blades fit well and seem to work well. I would actually say they are of exceptional quality. But selling them individually at a premium price and neglecting to include instructions or adapters as advertised is an issue for me. Even though the blades are very nice, I'm not sure I would buy these again because of these issues. Hopefully the manufacturer will read these reviews and take action to make sure the instructions and adapters end up in the box.As a side note, because it isn't specified on the packaging, I Googled for the Autotex PINK website and found that 10% of every purchase, year round, is donated to the National Breast Cancer Foundation. I'm impressed.
summary: Good replacement blade but be warned...

summary: Excellent wiper - better than other frameless ones I've tried

reviewText: I'm comparing this to a "premium" Michelin wiper blade I had installed previously on my Civic, which I had purchased at the local Wal*Mart, and I think it holds up quite nicely. First of all, they both have a bracketless construction which prevents chunks of ice from getting stuck between the arms which would otherwise cause the wiper to become ineffective. Come blizzard time here in New England, that will be much appreciated.  This wiper installed more easily than the Michelin; the default mounting bracket worked perfectly and there was only one way--the correct way--to snap the blade onto my wiper arm. In addition, the mounting bracket is somewhat closed to the elements, and should prevent ice and other foreign objects from getting lodged there.So, I would characterize this wiper as well and thoughtfully constructed.[Update: wiper failed when the blade shredded after 2,5 years of service, pretty good as these things go.]As for the breast cancer awareness ribbon logo, it is clearly visible to the driver. I don't know what to think about that. My dear sister is a breast cancer survivor, and the disease has cost me in emotional pain; maybe I don't want to be reminded of that pain every day on the way to work.

Update 5/4/2013: I finally needed to replace these -- in October 2012!  That's more than two years after I installed the original blades!  Not bad for blades that "should" be replaced every six months.Updated 12/31/2011:  I still have the same blades on my car, and they still wipe as good as the day I installed them!  I can't believe they're lasting this long!I ordered this wiper, along with the 24" wiper blade, for my 2008 Hyundai Sonata.These blades come with three different connectors, making it more likely to fit a wider variety of cars.  For my car, I didn't need any of the extra connectors, as the default connector was the proper type.  It was very easy to replace my old wipers with these, with one exception (which isn't the fault of this blade, but my old blade assembly and my arthritic fingers). With age, the old connector was difficult to pry open.  I don't expect this problem when my blades need to be replaced again (because I plan on replacing these every 6 months).The instructions claim these wiper blades take five minutes to replace.  That's much more than I needed.  I figure it took me a couple minutes to replace BOTH blades.The best praise I can give for these blades?  When I took my car into my mechanic for an oil change, he told me that these are high quality wipers.  It takes a lot to impress my mechanic, but these blades did it!  When my wipers need replacing again (about every six months is recommended), I'll use these AutoTex "PINK" Premium Wiper Blades again.

I have the hook style wiper, so installation was less than 5 minutes for both blades. The blade is 100% plastic/rubber which means no rust. The blades are pricey, yet they conform to windshield more effectively than the metal kinds. This company is owned by women, and part of the proceeds goes to Cancer research. Overall, a great product worth checking out. I haven't used in snow/ice winter conditions (which is why only 4 stars) and will edit review accordingly at a later date. Hopefully, they won't stick to the windshield.I feel for the person who was disappointed they could not get two of the same size. Personally, all my vehicles have had two separates sizes. Overall, worth a try.

Excellent wiper blades. Very well made qulaity and easy to install. Comes with several adapters; however, the vehicle I was installing these on did not require the use of any of the adapters. Excellent quality material that will hold up in both the Summer and Winter months. Was very impressed with the quality of these after running them. No streaks, just clean windows and no noise like some other type of wipers.

For something you do once a year or two, it always takes a little longer to install than expected.  One of the plastic pieces fell out due to my bumbling, and after returning it the the compartment, it took a few tries to get the plastic lid to shut again.  Now that it's on my windshield, it's working great.  I have a standard J hook, so thankfully, there was no drama with the half dozen included adapters.I came out of a auto car wash without the blow dryers and it was able to wipe off almost all of the water in one pass.  There was no squeaking sound while wiping at high wind speeds, which indicates a good fit with the glass.  It is definitely not your seven dollar discount wiper.The little pink ribbon logo, while highly obvious during handling, was barely noticable once installed.  So no, I do not feel emasculated with the wiper and was able to enjoy some brownie points with the significant other.Now on to the bully pulpit- these pink ribbon fund raisers have gone on for decades and have raised billions of dollars.  It makes everyone feel good to give, but does it really do anything?  None of the leading foundations have voiced concern about the thousands of unregulated chemicals in personal care products, no doubt because the big cosmetics manufacturers are their biggest donors.  Without tackling the potential causes at their source, we're really just cleaning up after the oil spill, so to speak.  Search the Skin Deep database to check your favorite products' ingredients, and perhaps you'll be able to contribute even more the cause.

The installation of this wiper blade was fairly easy.  It is a frame-less blade and supposedly does not leave streak marks on the windshield as there are no uneven pressure points on the blade.  I actually installed this blade on rear of my car and has been very effective at clearing out the morning fog and condensation.  No long term review on this blade as I've only had it on for 2-3 weeks and it's still "Indian summer" in California.  I will update this review as I encounter winter/fall weather as needed but so far so good!
summary: Fits and works on the Acura RSX 2002

reviewText: Auto Tex Black Bracketless Premium Wiper Blade is an excellent product that clears away the rain from your windshield in a most satisfying fashion. It gets right down to business and looks good doing it, too. It fit snugly in place with ease, and is a first class wiper blade.Recommended.Brian W. Fairbanks

I've been using Bosch bracketless blades for some time and decided to check out autotex "pink" to see how they compare.  Thankfully they aren't PINK!..  they are normal looking black blades.  They do have a pink ribbon symbol that is visible from inside of the car, but not so much outside.As for wiping.. in the summer and rain they work well and haven't shown any wear.  I'm hopefull that they will last throught Ohio winter.

I always invest in a premium wiper blade when it's time for a change. I figure that it's worth a few extra bucks since I only change my wiper blades about once a year.  I have used Rain-X Latitude blades and Bosch Micro Edge which both work fine during the summer but both of them have the typical metal frame with can easily be frozen solid during the winter months.These blades are all black except for a small pink ribbon that is visible on each blade. They clean my windows as well or better than any other blade that I have tried so far.These blades are more like the Bosch Icon because they are frameless so they should work much better during the winter. This design seems to be a little bit quieter as well. The current price of these wiper blades is several dollars cheaper than the Bosch Icon wiper blades so I would give these a try.I installed my blades on a Ford F150 and it was a breeze, I think it only took about a minute. If your vehicle has the hooks on the wiper arms then installation should be very easy, otherwise it might take you a couple extra minutes to figure out which mounting brackets to use. Each wiper blade does come with a mixture of mounting brackets to allow installation on most all vehicles.Plus it is nice that a donation is made to the National Breast Cancer Foundation with the sale of every AutoTex wiper blade.
summary: Similar to Bosch Icon wiper blades but they are less expensive, I like them a lot

reviewText: These seem to be decent, standard-issue windshield wipers.  The feature of being frameless is perhaps somewhat novel, but I've never had a problem with windshield wiper frames (I always snap them against the windshield when scraping off frost or ice, anyway), so I can't really regard that as a significant benefit.  The wipers do work, and they work well.  In my currently mild weather conditions, both blades cleared a silent, streak-free path when using washer fluid.  But any brand-new blade should be able to do that.The box proudly states that Autotex supports the National Breast Cancer Foundation, but nowhere on the box (or on the scanty instructions) does it say if a portion of the purchase price (or how much) is donated, so I'm not terribly impressed by that point.The instructions were virtually non-existent.  Considering that this product is clearly aimed towards women, I would have expected (and appreciated) a "Windshield Wiper Changing for Dummies" type of instruction sheet (not because women are innately inept at this but just because many women will have had less experience with it; and any mechanically disinclined man would also appreciate such assistance!).  No, changing wipers isn't rocket science, but I personally struggle with it every time I attempt it.  Once I get it figured out, I always have an "Ohhhhhh" moment, and it seems like it should have been so obvious, but it never is, and I don't change my wipers often enough to remember from one time to another.  I took these "Pink" wipers out of the box, looked at the few sentences of instructions (which were clearly written by a non-English speaker), and decided to just hand them off to my husband, who completed each side in probably under 10 seconds.  But he says all windshield wipers are this easy and quick to change (clearly I lack the windshield-wiper-changing gene), so the design of these blades can't take the credit for that.On the other hand, the box is a beautiful lavender, black, and pink.  It doesn't enhance the product itself, but if you have to change your wipers, you might as well have a pretty box to handle in the process.  The small pink ribbon on the hinge of the blades is kind of nice, and very discreet, but I wouldn't have minded a more-pronounced display of pink.Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to buy these again (especially considering the premium price), but I wouldn't avoid buying them, either.  They work as they are supposed to, and time may prove the price to be justified.  I am only giving them three stars because the instructions really are especially bad (worst I've seen for windshield wipers) and because I feel it's slightly unethical for AutoTex to sell a "pink ribbon" product without prominently disclosing just how much support they are actually giving to breast cancer research.

Hopefully, they won't stick to the windshield.I feel for the person who was disappointed they could not get two of the same size. Personally, all my vehicles have had two separates sizes.

I made the switch to frameless wipers a couple years ago.  I found they work much better than the factory wipers.  And the ones I have used in the past work very well (Michelin).I had a chance to try these and what an improvement.  This wiper at least one feature missing from the ones I have used.  Where the wiper attaches to the wiper arm, there's a little cover that snaps open.  The wiper blade simply snaps onto the wiper arm, and the little door closes, giving a nice clean appearance and one additional assurance that the wiper blade will stay on the car!These wipers also feature the pink ribbon symbol, tastefully placed on the wiper arm showing your support for the National Breast Cancer Foundation.The wiper blade and all other parts are the normal black plastic and rubber that one expects.  There is a large assortment of parts intended to adapt the wiper to various makes and models of cars (these fit my 2004 Chrysler Crossfire without any of the adapters).  They look great and wipe the glass super-clean.I am very happy!
summary: Time to Refresh the Wiper blades!

reviewText: The AutoTex Pink Bracketless wiper blade 20" reviewed here is a "OKAY" purchase but longevity may be an issue down the line as mine came with one edge slightly sheared off. I was thinking to myself as I was attempting to put this on the car - If it can be damaged in the box how long will it really last?By the way, It came with multiple attachment choices and it was a perfect fit to my car. IMHO you cannot really review a Wipe blade, you need a pair to evaluate fully and as these usually comes in two different sizes, you need to carefully pick the one which fits your car and then do a complete review for feedback.In my honest opinion, With the one I received and what I feel is that these will not last long. I will update my review after couple of rainy days and usage and let the amazon community know about my findings.Stay tuned!

Installation on my Camry was very simple, pop'd-off the old ones and attached the new, could not be more than 30 seconds per blade.  The blade is similar to Bosch Icon, it's one piece construction, with pressure on whole width of the blade for smoother wiping.  Works really well, no complains for about 3 weeks now.  I also applied RainX (original) recently to my windshield, so the combination is working superbly.  This review covers 20" and 22" inch sizes.
summary: Simple to install & good looking blade!
