reviewText: I had a difficult time figuring out how to get the right connector on here for my VW Passat, and was afraid of breaking something when I tried to remove the default connector to swap in the one I needed. I eventually figured it out, but the instructions could have been way better.After installation, it's a wiper blade. I don't notice anything special about it, and it works fine.
summary: a little bit tricky to connect, but works fine

reviewText: This blade makes a very effective use of the windshield surface area - every millimeter of the blade touches the glass, so all water is wicked away on one swipe. I found this effective with small mud splashes as well. I live out in the country and the county has been doing road work the past year. We're frequently traveling at 55 mph on gravel and dirt - and if you're behind a truck, your windshield is going to get pelted with mud splashes as they work crew has water trucks to constantly keep the roads moist so they don't cause a dust storm. I was finding myself having to manually scrub accumulated mud off at the gas station using the squeegees - but this wiper blade removes most normal levels of dirt on just a swipe - bird droppings as well.
summary: very effective, high quality wiper blade

reviewText: These wipers worked great and I liked them, but winter came and the performance has gone down. The wipers are not clearing evenly even on days when it's not super cold.

I bought a set of these a few years ago and really liked them as they seem to hold up well thru Kansas City winters.  I bought a second set for my 08 Silverado that takes a 22" blade and Amazon shipped them promptly but the blades in the boxes measured 20 1/2" inches.  I contacted Auto Tex and they told me the all blades should measure about 1/2" shorter than the size on the box, but not 1.5" shorter.  I didn't want to go thru the hassle of returning the blades to I kept them on my truck.  Auto Tex makes a great blade and I'd buy them again despite me recent problem.

I, for one, don't spend a lot of time thinking about windshield wipers. But I sure notice when they don't do the job. We decided to give the AutoTex "PINK" bracketless wiper a try. We got one for the driver's side of my wife's Toyota Tacoma truck. The driver's wiper is the pink and the other is the factory wiper.In the high wind simulator (the car wash's dryer blower), the factory wiper blade lifted up off the windshield. The pink stayed put. One point for the pink. On rainy days (we get a lot here), the pink left no streaks. The factory wiper did leave some "rain tracks". Another point for pink.We have only had the wiper on for a few weeks, so I can't report on how long these blades will continue to perform. I can say that the difference is easily seen, and I will be getting a blade for the passenger side too. There is one other thing I really like about the pinks: the way they look on the truck. Very sleek. I also expect that these blades won't freeze in winter since there is no visible frame for ice to form.This product is better than traditional wipers and the price is comparable to high-quality conventional wiper blades.
summary: They not only look cool, they also do a superior job

reviewText: I got this for my brother who badly needed a new wiper for his car. It took him half a minute or so to attach it, and it works perfectly. This is a high quality product, much better than the average wiper blade, and its design not only makes it more effective at doing its job, but it's also more attractive than the standard wiper blade. Some of the proceeds from sales of this blade are being donated to the National Breast Cancer Foundation, so in addition to getting a quality wiper blade, you're contributing to a worthy cause. Naturally, I recommend it.Brian W. Fairbanks
They where very easy to install and worked great right out of the box would recommend to anyone! Snap and click an you are done... Didn't need ANY directions to install but I guess some might.

these work as well as any other brand but sure cost a lot. I did notice a little better cleaning than the WalMart cheapies but they do seem much heavier so I'm sure they will last a lot longer as well. We had an absolute down pour the day after I put it on, the kind you can barely see the road, this keep the window crystal clear & did seem to clean it closer to the glass from the wind & rain than my Walmart one I had on the other side. I'll be anxious to see if they work better in the heavy,wet, icy snows we get in the bitter Iowa winters. I'll update in December or so after it goes through a big storm.
summary: AutoTex "PINK" - Black Bracketless Premium Wiper Blade

reviewText: A review of this wiper blade was entered in the AutoTex 18" by mistake.However, the same thing applies to this offering.  You can get one blade, but not two that are needed.  Vine should consider this before offering items like this.To purchase a second AutoTex wiper blade via Amazon would cost 3 times as much as I spend on wiper blades, and I truly don't believe the AutoTex blades can wipe rain off my windshields three times faster.Not a good offer for Amazon Vine

AutoTex Frameless WipersWINTER USAGE WARNING:Like any other rubber wiper blade, the blade can/will freeze at really cold temperatures rendering it less effective.These are 22" frameless wiper blades, similar to the frameless design found on most foreign luxury cars within the past 2-3 model years. The main feature of the frameless design is a reduction in the number of moving parts, joints, and components. Instead of a frame with several joints, you end up with a single rubber squeegee integrated with a flat metal spring and a composite aero "wing" surface.In my experience with other frameless wipers from Trico (NeoForm), Rain-X Latitude, Pylon/Michelin Radius, and Bosch, they are not worse or better than quality framed wiper blades but they do cost 2-3 times more. They still suffer from the same problems in the winter, namely with the rubber squeegee getting hard or freezing up. TripleEdge is one manufacturer that uses silicone for the squeegee and I had used a set of TripleEdge blades for nearly a decade without any problems. I only changed them because the silicone had started to fall apart.The AutoTex "Pink" has a pink ribbon logo that shows how Autotex is dedicated to wiping out breast cancer. This logo is visible to the occupants of the car when the wipers are at rest. The Autotex blades install just like any other traditional wiper blade. The standard J-hook adapter that comes with the blade is easy to use, but does not have a retention tab. It simply slides and clicks into place, and has an external latch that keeps it from walking. Rain-X Latitudes will have a retention tab inside of the clip that fits into the "hole" at the end of the J-hook.I used the AutoTex blade through a heavy rain storm and didn't detect any performance deficiencies, they work just as good as any other frameless blade at the beginning. I did not hear any chattering at high speeds (70+ MPH), and there was no streaking. The true test of performance comes with age (6-12 months of use) and snow/ice. I installed the Autotex on my winter daily driver and it sees a lot of winter precipitation here in Michigan, so I will keep updating this review as I find stuff to write about!Pros: Contribute to the global war on breast cancer, and help wipe out this atrocity that has claimed the lives of millions of loved ones.Cons: None.Overall: 3/5, could use a better retention adapter, still need to see how well it handles colder temperatures.UPDATE: After 16 months, these blades have bought the farm and are chattering even in warm temperatures. They performed on-par with other frameless blades in winter conditions, but I re-installed the Rain-X frameless blade that I removed to test this AutoTex blade.I would recommend you just buy name-brand framed wiper blades and replace them every year to be on the safe side. It takes 5 minutes to do, just wear gloves to avoid cutting yourself when changing the blades.

...When you install it on your car. The packaging says PINK is very large letters, but the frameless blade is the traditional flat black color.No brackets (frames) means there is no place for water to collect and freeze in winter. That is a big improvement over stock wiper assemblies. I haven't tried them in cold weather yet, but I am certain the frozen frame problem can't occur with these innovative blades.Each package contains adapters for older style slide lock, top lock and button release type wiper arms. For newer cars like mine, the "G" adapter that comes already fitted to the blade allows for installation in a matter of seconds.
summary: When is a pink wiper not pink?

reviewText: rain season is coming so I was thinking of replacing the wiper blades on my cars--Honda Odyssey and Honda Civic.The locking mechanism is so easy to replace it's incredible.Basically the Honda cars come with the same wiper locking adapters where you use your nail to clip open the top locking lid.Then pull the blade portion down (to unhook the main wiper arm from it's U-shape hook).Then it basically just slides out very easily.I didn't see a 26" version even though that's what's on my cars (both) (22" and 26").I took the 28" version and to my amaze, it fit as well.  It's an inch longer on both ends and it doesn't extrude over the windshield glass section or hitting the border.The wiper makes a very clean sweep and very low noise level.It's aerodynamic enough where it doesn't create extra wind noise (compared to your stock ones).The wipers are light weight and curves just perfectly to cover the entire sweeping path/area.Highly recommended.

I orderedAutoTex "PINK" - Black Bracketless Premium Wiper Blade - 22" , Pack of 1, for our 2006 Honda Civic 4-door sedan. Even though my hubby is very handy, he was concerned he wouldn't be able to replace the windshield wiper blade on his own. I assured him there was a video posted, so I figured it would be 'a piece of cake.' Well, it wasn't quite as easy as the video depicts...at least for my hubby because Tess's wiper 'arm type' wasn't at all like ours. He went out to the car armed with the instructions; ready to get the blade changed in 5 minutes. It took him approx. 25 minutes because neither of us could figure out which adapter/connector we needed to use. He brought the instructions back in the house for me to look at. My goodness, the print was so small, I had to put on my extra strong reading glasses to magnify it.Neither of us thought the instructions were very clear; we weren't sure what to do next. Then I looked at the back of the box which has nice large pictures of the four adapter/connector pieces (G, B, D, & H) and large pictures of the 'Arm Types.' So, I thought, "I know he/we can do this." I began searching online...maybe, I'd find more information about our Honda's arm type, but there hasn't been much posted yet. Twenty minutes later, my husband pulled out the car's manual. Don't you know, there's information right in the manual that tells how to remove the wiper blade. (He squeezed the sides together to push off the tab; the tab wouldn't push off so he used a screwdriver to pry it off). He came inside holding the old wiper blade to show me...*victory! I finally removed the old one.* Still not sure which adapter/connector to use, my hubby goes back outside; less than five minutes later he comes in and says...I didn't need to change the adapter, the G adapter (which is on the blade when you receive it) worked fine!I was driving through a foggy area late last night & used the wipers to clear off the windshield. (I'd totally forgotten about the new blade) When I got home, I mentioned how foggy some areas were & that I had to use the wipers. Hubby asked, "Did they work? I wondered because I didn't test them." Oh my gosh! I was out in the country, no street lights, very foggy evening, & no white lines on the sides of the road...thankfully the new wiper worked perfectly. I will post more updates when we use the wiper during inclement weather.4 stars - I think the instructions could be a bit clearer.  Be sure to check the back of the box for much larger pictures. Also, having your car's manual available might help with removing the old blade; it helped us.AutoTex PINK donates a portion of every windshield wiper sale to the National Breast Cancer Foundation. AutoTex PINK wipers are continually tested to assure performance in all weather conditions (for better winter performance, use AutoTex PINK Frameless wipers). These wipers have a 30 day money-back guarantee.

I have the hook style wiper, so installation was less than 5 minutes for both blades. The blade is 100 % plastic/rubber which means no rust. The blades are pricey, yet they conform to windshield more effectively than the metal kinds. This company is owned by women, and part of the proceeds goes to Cancer research. Overall, a great product worth checking out.  I haven't used in snow/ice winter conditions (which is why only 4 stars) and will edit review accordingly at a later date. Hopefully, they won't stick to the windshield.I feel for the person who was disappointed they could not get two of the same size. Personally, all my vehicles have had two separates sizes.

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I drive a lot of miles every year, especially in rain and bug season here in Florida, so I frequently replace my wiper blades. The passenger side blade was streaking, so I was looking to replace that anyway so this came in handy. I've put it to the test, and it works well to clear my windshield of rain or of bugs while using wiper fluid. The installation was the easiest ever! The quality/construction is very good, and the price is reasonable. I would definitely consider this brand again.

I put a pair of these (22" & 24") on my 2007 Honda Ridgeline this morning before taking it to the car wash. Like most of the newer blades they go on extremely easily (maybe five minutes for both, including opening the packaging) and the appear to be really well made. They're noticeably heavier than the premium Valeo "Ultimate" blades they replaced with most of the added heft in the blade material itself. They effortlessly wipe the windshield sparkling clean and should be ideal of all of the snow we usually encounter each winter here the Northeast. We spend a lot of time in snow-bound Vermont so they'll really get a good workout up there.Since my wife is a 10-year+ breast cancer survivor I'm really pleased that AutoTex has brought out this "PINK" series of blades and will be donating some of their profits to support the Breast Cancer Foundation and help put an end to this disease that will strike 1 out of every 8 women here in the U.S.!
summary: Great wiper blades, now I'm ready for winter.

reviewText: I made the switch to frameless wipers a couple years ago.  I found they work much better than the factory wipers.  And the ones I have used in the past work very well (Michelin).I had a chance to try these and what an improvement.  This wiper has at least one feature missing from the ones I have used.  Where the wiper attaches to the wiper arm, there's a little cover that snaps open.  The wiper blade simply snaps onto the wiper arm, and the little door closes, giving a nice clean appearance and one additional assurance that the wiper blade will stay on the car!These wipers also feature the pink ribbon symbol, tastefully placed on the wiper arm showing your support for the National Breast Cancer Foundation.The wiper blade and all other parts are the normal black plastic and rubber that one expects.  There is a large assortment of parts intended to adapt the wiper to various makes and models of cars (these fit my 2004 Chrysler Crossfire without any of the adapters).  They look great and wipe the glass super-clean.I am very happy!

Let me first get the "Pink" issue out of the way. I guess I am finally becoming so overloaded with "correct thinking" bombardment that I now am irritated that I have to be reminded on the package that this is a "woman owned" company. Does it make any difference? Does this company owner need any extra help because she is a woman? We have been so conditioned to believe otherwise. I'm confused. I can hardly wait until we get past all that. I'm OK with the contribution to fight breast cancer, but I really would prefer to donate outright rather than pay more for an auto part than it is worth in order to make my contribution to the cause. Now about the wiper . . . .Around town and at low speed, great wiping performance. Period. I kind of like the "bracketless"concept. Actually, the "bracket" is built into the rather thick blade backing structure.Also built into that structure is a neat little air spoiler designed to hold the blade down against the windshield at speed. Strangley, that is the source of a problem with this wiper.  The spoiler works great for a blade mounted on the left (driver side) and extending to the right.  But . . . for those cars (such as my GM mini-van) with the passenger side wiper mounted right annd extending in toward the left . . . THE SPOILER IS EDGED IN THE WRONG DIRECTION.  It serves to lift the wiper from the windshield at speed and is not removeable.  Bad.Sorry I can't be totally positive with this review, but this is my thorough and complete take on this premium priced wiper.
summary: Great wiping performance, but has a built in problem -

reviewText: Installation on my Camry was very simple, pop'd-off the old ones and attached the new, could not be more than 30 seconds per blade. The blade is similar to Bosch Icon, it's one piece construction, with pressure on whole width of the blade for smoother wiping. Works really well, no complains for about 3 weeks now. I also applied RainX (original) recently to my windshield, so the combination is working superbly. This review covers 20" and 22" inch sizes.
summary: Great smooth wiping, quick install & good looking too!

reviewText: As other's have stated before me... these are not PINK but rather "PINK" branded; AutoTex PINK in conjunction with the National Breast Cancer Foundation.  I will very quickly gloss over the fact that the packaging informs us that the company is indeed women owned and cleverly promotes "Wipe Out Breast Cancer - Change your blades... change a life!"  Considering all the advertising these days with no positive effect whatsoever; these were a welcome change.Directly from their website/packaging:Wipe Out Breast CancerEvery three minutes a woman is diagnosed with breast cancer and 1 in 8 women will develop breast cancer in their lifetime. Because of these startling statistics, AutoTex PINK is doing its part by giving 10 percent of its proceeds to support the National Breast Cancer Foundation.Many have stated they were weren't really positive what sort of proceeds were being donated; for anyone still wondering it is 10%.Now onto the actual product!  I offered to help my husband change the wiper blades for the new "PINK" ones so that I could see the difficulty level.  The directions were printed on a tiny sheet and showed all the parts that were in the packaging.  We were set off track for about 3.5 minutes (lol) because we were trying to figure out what to do with the extra little parts.  My husband then realized that they were "ready" out of the box to be installed, where he proceeded to just snap them into place.  VOILA! done.  I was still reading the directions holding the little black pieces... beginners learning curve (and I am sticking to that).  Hubby decided that he loves the way these rubber wipers hug the windshield and cleanly wipe the window.  There is no sound and they stay nicely in place at windy/high speeds thanks to the frameless design .  We were not able to test the no snow/ice build up claims, but we will update later in the Winter.  If they do not hold true to the snow/ice claims we will still be "repeat" buyers of this frameless design just because of the difference in performance.The bad:  If cleanly wipes without leaving any streaking, but he has found that when water accumulates on the top of the driver's side wiper it can at times splash it over to the passenger's side.  Not a biggie at all though.Highly recommend for all to try the High Performance Frameless design; even better knowing that 10 percent will go to a wonderful cause to help so many women that have suffered/will suffer through this disease.FYI: You need to order two for your vehicle (one in each box)!  Amazon makes it easy to figure out which wipers and sizes go for every vehicle type right on the order page.  For our '07 Nissan Armada it was a 24 & 22 inch.
summary: Great product.... with a pretty "PINK" ribbon

reviewText: I never thought I would get excited over wiper blades... these have a great weight and feel to them, and the curvature looks like it will work better than those with less of a 'bent.' One pet peeve I have with wiper blades is when they loose their 'contact' with the windshield.I cannot determine their snow and ice efficiency because it's almost 100 degrees F outside now.  But the design looks like it will be better than my standard ANCO blades.

I used this wiper blade to replace a wiper on my 2003 Toyota Corolla. This model has 1 24" blade and one 18". This blade fit perfectly and works great. It has a smooth, quiet stroke and doesn't leave any streaks. The only quality that remains to be evaluated is how long the blade lasts until it requires replacement but so far, so good.

Update 5/4/2013: I finally needed to replace these -- in October 2012!  That's more than two years after I installed the original blades!  Not bad for blades that "should" be replaced every six months.Updated 12/31/2011:  I still have the same blades on my car, and they still wipe as good as the day I installed them!  I can't believe they're lasting this long!I ordered this wiper, along with theAutoTex "PINK" - Black Metal Wiper Blade - 19" , Pack of 1, for my 2008 Hyundai Sonata.It was very easy to replace my old wipers with these, except for one exception (which isn't the fault of this blade, but my old blade assembly and my arthritic fingers). With age, the old connector was difficult to pry open.  I don't expect this problem when my blades need to be replaced again (because I plan on replacing these every 6 months).The instructions claim these wiper blades take five minutes to replace.  That's way more than I needed.  I think it took me a couple minutes to replace BOTH blades.The best praise I can give for these blades?  When I took my car into the shop for an oil change, the mechanic told me that these were really high quality wipers.  It takes a lot to impress my mechanic, but these blades did it!  When my wipers need replacing again (about every six months is recommended), I'll use these AutoTex "PINK" Premium Wiper Blades again.

Let me first get the "Pink" issue out of the way.  I guess I am finally becoming so overloaded with "correct thinking" bombardment that I now am irritated that I have to be reminded on the package that this is a "woman owned" company.  Does it make any difference?  Does this company owner need any extra help because she is a woman?  We have been so conditioned to believe otherwise.  I'm confused.  I can hardly wait until we get past all that.  I'm OK with the contribution to fight breast cancer, but I really would prefer to donate outright rather than pay more for an auto part than it is worth in order to make my contribution to the cause.  Now about the wiper . . . .Great wiping performance.  Period.  I kind of like the "bracketless"concept.  Actually, the "bracket" is built into the rather thick blade backing structure.  Also built into that structure is a neat little air spoiler designed to hold the blade down against the windshield at speed.  I really like it.My only negative is the mounting bracket device.  My car uses the ubiquitous hook/loop system.  When installing the wiper, I could not obtain a distinctive locking click.  The wiper seems to be firmly in place, but it definitely is not locked, and in fact I can force it off without depressing the locking tab.  I've been changing wipers for decades and this is the first time I have ever experienced this lack of locking.  At this price, that is not really acceptable. The wiper has not fallen off, however.  If it does, I will edit my review and share that problem.Sorry I can't be totally positive with this review, but this is my thorough and complete take on this premium priced wiper.
summary: Great wiping performance, questionable mounting device

reviewText: I've purchased the AutoTex wipers 3 previous times for my wife's van and my truck.  The wipers do an excellent job at clearing the windshield during the warmer months but don't seem to last long (haven't found a brand that does) especially in colder weather.  I typically get about 6-8 months use out of them but the last set I got didn't last that long.  One of the blades had and end cap fall off and the plastic latch that secures the blade to the arm kept popping up.  The issues I had were just with one blade and may have been caused by ice after a winter storm but the verdict is still out on these for use in the winter.
summary: Nice wiper, may have received a bad one

reviewText: "Pink" here, leaves streak free wipes, even when dirt and grime such as pollen, sap and bird droppings have built up on the windshield.  I'm very pleased with its performance thus far, and installation was a snap.  It took me literally less than a minute to pull the old blade off and snap this much cooler profile blade on top.  The breast cancer ribbon is a subtle but powerful reminder of the efforts this company goes to to be socially conscious.  Very cool.  The only reason this product doesn't get 5 stars is because the durability is something I haven't been able to vouch for yet as the rainy season approaches.

I installed this on my wife's 2009 Civic 4 Door Sedan, replacing the original Honda wiper. I'm not sure if it is better to fully replace the wiper, or just buy a replacement blade from the local Honda dealership. After nearly 2 years of use, the original blade was showing signs of deterioration, but the rest of the OEM wiper assembly looked fine; I'll keep it around for when this wiper wears out.This AutoTex blade is a good looking wiper blade. It easily installed, taking perhaps 30 seconds to snap into place using the default mounting hardware. Alternative mounting adaptors are provided, but the standard one works with the Civic. It uses a bracketless design that is a bit floppy in appearance, but should keep snow and ice from getting in disrupted cleaning when it is needed most, in snowy conditions.There is a small pink breast cancer logo where the wiper arm meets the wiper. It's clearly visible when driving, which may or may not be something you want to deal with emotionally.

Autotex did a good job of thinking "out of the box" when they designed this frameless wiper arm and blade. There are no hinges to collect water and freeze in the winter. So, these would qulify as "snow blades".Autotex did a horrible job with the package labelling and graphics. 95% of wiper blade shoppers are guys who avoid the color pink. These guys are going to walk by the purple and pink package that says PINK in letters 6 times the size of the words "Wiper Blade". While it is true that the product itself is black, the package implies otherwise. I think it's admirable that the manufacturer donates money to breast cancer research that will potentially benefit my mother, my sisters, my wife and my daughter. Too bad the package will cut sales drastically.One more thing, I was careful to order the right blade for MY application. Why does the package include adapters for several OTHER applications?
summary: Nicely designed wiper blade, stupid packaging.

reviewText: My Honda Accord needs one 26" wiper and one 18" blade. I see the only difference is the longer blades cost more money. Their look is the same, and they work the same. The longer blade also hugs the windshield. If your car requires two different sizes, I'd recommend that you check to be sure both sized blades are in stock or you may end up with only a single blade in this style. My review for this blade follows, but it's the same as I wrote for the 18" blade:I did a little research on Wexco Industries while I was awaiting the very swift delivery of my AutoTex "PINK" - Black Bracketless Premium Wiper Blade - 26" and learned that the company is woman owned, and began in 1991 as Wipers Express. According to their website, "Today we are a global supplier of quality windshield wipers and engineered systems to the heavy duty bus, RV and other specialty markets." I trusted the newfangled design to work and it's been only average.  The longer blade does not hug the windshield and there's a section where the blade attaches to the arm that simply doesn't make contact, even after time. The label, "PINK" can imply that the blades are pink, but they are definitely black like most other windshield wiper blades. The "PINK" represents the company's partnering with the NBCF. Another plus for the product. Men, do not be turned off by the notion of blades with the pink ribbon insignia, it's very small and unobtrusive. It does not affect the functionality of this blade. Since I've replaced many wiper blades, this was very intuitive for me. If you are inexperienced, you can watch the video which I think designed to show how easy the process can be if you're not replacing rusted blades. The instructions are inside the box with an assortment of connectors for a majority of arm types, and there are additional diagrams and information on the box. They are written in English, Spanish and French. I like the blades and hope that they will work as well in inclement weather as they do in a slight rain.
summary: Sizes vary in price, it's an okay blade

I originally bought this product on a whim, thinking that it would do just as good a job as my Turtle Wax Wash and Wax. As soon as I poured it into the bucket and started getting ready, I can tell the product was already better quality than my previous washing liquid. It created a lot of suds, and only 4 capfuls was needed to wash my entire car! Plus the smell was an added bonus! It smelled like citrus fruit and did not bother me the whole time I was washing. It made washing my car pretty enjoyable.

I have been addicted to Meguiars Gold Class car wash for years and have never used anything else. It is fantastic and gives a nice shine afterwards as well. The water beads up and it is very easy to dry. It seems as if it is a shampoo and conditioner. I went to the auto parts store and found Meguiar's "Ultimate car wash" on sale for $7.99 and thought I would give it a try. I was a bit disappointed. It is a strange yellow color and it is thick and I personally did not care for the smell. It cleaned very well, but it was almost as if the wax was gone after I used it. The car was not slippery anymore, it had am actual layer of water and not beads, so it was harder to dry as well, even with an absorber. I have only used it a couple of times on two different cars and I think that ... I am going to pass it up and go back to the Gold Class ! I may try it once more, but if it produces the same result I am going to toss it out in the trash. No wonder it is on sale. "Ultimate" ? I don't think so.

The first time I used waaaaay too much. After a couple washes I found an ounce is all you need for a mid sized car that isn't truely a mess. Even worked great on my snowblower and rider. Made them shine too!!! What a bonus.

I know what the label states, that this is a wash and wax. Friends ---if there is any great lasting wax shine after you wash your car then I have done something wrong. This is avery good car wash and if your vehicle needs waxing then don't expect miracles coming out of this product. I used a paste wax after washing and got good results. That was I believe entirely from the paste wax and not anything left from the washing. The price is very reasonable for this product and it is a five star product.

This is a pretty good soap used in between waxes. I usually use Gold Class, which I think suds better in my pressure washer bottle, and I think the gold class might do a bit better as a cleaner for caked on dirt. However this gets a much better shine in between waxes. I believe this preserves the wax layer longer and keeps your car looking great. This is much thicker then the Gold Class soap, and has a very pleasant smell to it. The instructions recommend drying with a towel immediately after washing a section with it, however when I use my CRSpotless to rinse it off (spot free dry/clean), then I think it shines/brings the wax finish out more so then towel dry.I think this has it's place in my cleaner assortment. Usually I'll pull this out if I have to do light washes shortly after a wax. This doesn't seem to bring any significant shine or wax to a car that has no wax layer (comparable to what you'll see from any decent cleaner like Gold Class).

I've been using Meguiar's Wash and Wax on my Corvette for years, and it's a good wash for cars. It produces a lot of suds without using a whole lot. In fact, I find that less is better than more. If you use too much, it can leave a slight film on your car from the wax which is especially noticeable on dark vehicles. If it happens though, it is easily removed by wiping with a good polishing cloth. Meguiar's Wash and Wax is also not really a good substitute for an occasional real waxing. It is good to extend the period of time in between waxings."Meguiar's Wash and Wax" cleans well, and its hybrid blend of waxes offers a little bit of extra protection. As long as you don't use too much, and don't substitute it for an occasional real wax job, I recommend it.
summary: Good, but not a replacement for real waxing.

reviewText: Just like any other car high quality car wash but has lots of bubbles which I like. Cleans your car very well. Shines it up good!

its ok just wanted to try something new.  This product cost a little bit more then the Meguiars Gold Car Wash. and the bottle is 48oz compared to 64 oz for the  Gold Car Wash.  personally if you can get the Gold was for $6.97, that is a good deal.so in the End both products wash about the same.  If you want to see a different in your car.  Invest the time to WAX IT.update Wow How things change. Don't think its worth 13.87$

Super easy to use, just pour some into water and you're done!This will help maintain your car waxed, and will not remove old wax as most car wash liquids do.The smell of this is absolutely stunning, makes you want to wish the the smell was inside the car and not outside!Cons: A bit pricey, but quality matters, and this product absolutely has it.Worth every cent for sure! In my personal use, this is enough to last at least 3-4 months. (just washing one car)
summary: Awesome way to wash your car!

reviewText: Best wash and wax soap money can buy! Meguiar's is one of the top products out there for car detailing. This stuff is great. Leaves my black car shinning bright! 10 out 10!!!

My car lives outside in the sun so unfortunately it collects a lot of baked on environmental contaminates (dirt, pollen, water spots, etc).  I've used this soap for a few washes so far and it has worked great.  This is a highly concentrated yellow soap that goes in the bucket with a "plop".  Since it's so thick, only a small amount is necessary to create a large amount of lubricating sud to wash your car with.I tend do add more than is necessary to the bucket for a little more protection as I'm washing.  Adding too little soap will increase the tendency of your wash mitt to damage the clear coat on your car by grinding contaminants into the surface.  This thick, high quality soap helps prevent against that.As for the "wax" part, I haven't noticed any appreciable increase in shine after washing.  I suspect that whatever effect there is, it is mild and probably acts as more of a restorative "freshning" for a wax coating that is already on your car.  If you're washing an old car, don't expect any difference in shine after your done.

I'm a Meguiar's product lover and this here is another prime example as to why I use their products. Lasting shine that keeps car looking showroom finish. Makes water bead up preventing water spots when drying.
Cleans all the dirt, smells great and keep your car shinnyi love Meguiar's products and for me this is the best shampoo for my car
summary: The best Shampoo for your car

reviewText: This is an update to my original review in June 2010, which was very positive.This IS a nice product, producing copious suds that last, good at cleaning the vehicle.  So, nothing new there.However, I always wondered about the claims of the wash containing carnauba and polymers. Since one normally has to buff waxes off the car, just HOW did this product leave these wax type finishes on a car? Why wouldn't you have to buff this after using it?Then it occurred to me. My black car always has a good wax finish - do I NEED to be putting something from a wash in addition to that? When I wash a car, I hose it down, mix up the sudsy shampoo, wash all areas, squeegie off the water with a silicon blade and finish up by wiping up any remaining droplets/moisture with one of those damp, ChamWow type, high absorbancy felt towels. This worked fine, BUT, with the Meguiar's, I always had to follow up on the glass with an additional buffing from a bath type towel. If I didn't buff the windows, even though they had been wiped clean of droplets by the ChamWow, they would be very streaked/spotted in the direct sunlight. So, although I didn't see direct streaking of the paint, I have to assume that it had the same issue as the unbuffed windows, given I wasn't buffing the car paint itself.I actually had gone to buy a new bottle of the Meguiar's. Hadn't paid much attention to prices, in that I always want a good shampoo. But then I noticed that this product is twice the price of other name brand shampoos such as Black Magic and Rain-X. PLUS, this product calls for 1 oz per GALLON, whereas those others call for 1 oz per BUCKET. So, it's actually FOUR times the price of the others.So, came back with the Black Magic, which is just a cleaning shampoo. At 1 oz per bucket (vs. the Maquiar's 2) it foamed very well, but didn't last quite as long. But, long enough to get the job done with foamy soap. I DID notice that the windows weren't streaked and car actually DOES seem to have a better shine - but have to admit, that could be wishful thinking.So, in conclusion, think this product leaves some sort of film on the car, and not a glassy one. There are plenty of options out there at 1/4 the cost, that leave NO film.  If you are willing to pay four times the price, suspect you already keep your vehicle waxed, so the dubious benefit of this product containing waxes as protectants, is a waste of money as well as leaving a less that sparkling clean finish on the car.
summary: Nice suds, not so nice finish

reviewText: Despite already knowing that washing and waxing go together about as good as trying to stick equal ends of a magnet together, I decided to purchase this to give it a shot.  1st, am a huge Meguiars loyalist and I tend to use their professional line up of products due to experience and owning my own automotive detailing business.  2nd:  being in the business of detailing vehicles I've grown accustomed to utilizing the appropriate steps thorought the detail process.  I purchased this for my own vehicle for a trial and error run.  One thing that I will say about the product that is positive is if you are tight on time and waxing is not a choice, I would recommend this product for you as something is better than nothing.  However, keep in mind that it will not produce the quality of protection or shine that a hand or machine applied proper wax would.  This is due to 2 reasons:  1: you are waxing while washing, the coverage is not as thorough, it's essentially as if you'd wax before washing.  It's going up break down because it's diluted.  Secondly, a major advantage of a paste or liquid wax is the application of the product itself.  You will find much better coverage and masking of paint defects when the right steps are taken.  Meaning more shine.  I'm not tryin to deter anyone away from trying this product nor disagreeing with the positive votes.  Just giving some useful feedback about the truth behind the product other than basing my rating off of the fact that it smells good.
summary: Not the best option by any means..

reviewText: I've been using this car wash soap for some time now. What really drew my attention to it is that you pay 10 bucks for 48 oz., whereas most other car wash soaps are 5, 6 bucks or a little more for 64 oz. It made me think maybe it's a better product, so I gave it a try. I don't depend on the soap to wax my car in any way at all, but I do notice that the suds are really nice and last all the way to the end of the whole car washing process, but it does seem to leave a very nice shine to the car and leaves the paint looking really clean, especially when it's been waxed. I use 2 tablespoons, pretty much a standard medicine cup that you get when you buy cough syrup. I think it amounts to 4 cap-fulls, but I prefer using the medicine cup. I take my Home Depot "Homer" bucket and put the spray nozzle in the bottom and fill it until the nozzle becomes covered in water and the water stops churning. Then I take the soap in the medicine cup, pour it in, and then continue spraying the water pretty much directly into the soap so that it foams up really nicely. By the time I'm washing the wheels and tires, always with a separate mitt, the suds are still there. So far I've had 2 bottles of the Meguiars Ultimate Wash & Wax and I'm already thinking of getting another even though my current bottle is only half used. It lasts quite a while.
summary: Nice suds, nice shine, rinses clean...

reviewText: No real complaints.  You won't get a great shine from jsut this wash.  A paste wax is recommended after washing.  I used Meguiars ultimate polish and gold class paste wax afterward and had my car looking great.

I wash my cars often so when I use a "regular" wash soap, I usually dry the car then apply a quik spray wax(wipe on wipe off)When I don't have much time, but want to wash my cars, I use Meguiars Wash & Wax.I'm not sure how much wax protection is actually left on the car versus regular waxing or the various quik spray waxes out there.I do know that using this soap does make drying of the car a tad quicker....other then that, I don't think it's better than the other Megs soaps avail.It creates nice suds, cleans good, has a nice scent to it as well.For me, this soap is kind of reduntant as i like to use a quik wax after washing.I bought 2 bottles and will not be buying more as I prefer a "regular" wash soap like Meguiars Gold Class or Meguiars Hyper wash.
I use this on my wifes Mercedes Benz CLK 350 and my Nissan Quest Van. I have been using Meguiars products for quite some time and have never been dissappointed by them

I have tried many car shampoos including Meguiar's Gold Class Car Wash, NXT Car Wash, and some from the professional Mirror Glaze Line of Meguiar's washes such as Hi Tech Wash.Among those products, Gold Class was always my favorite for its solid cleaning ability, but also its ability to leave a final shine and maintain the previous layer of wax on the car.I purchased Ultimate Wash and Wax and got my two wash buckets with Grit Guards ready!I used a fair amount of the product to ensure I had plenty of suds and so that I would be sure to receive any of the wax/protection benefits if indeed they existed.The smell of Ultimate Wash and Wax is lovely.  Furthermore, it looks unlike any wash product I have ever used.  It is rather opaque and thick, so there must be something special and different about the product as Meguiar's suggests.The cleaning ability was solid, if only the slightest bit weaker than Gold Class.  The suds were great, and it was a pleasure working with the pleasant smelling product.I dried the car thoroughly.  The result?  The car was clean and had a subdued sparkle to it.  However, the paint was not very slick and there was not much shine.  Certainly, even using a Quick Detailer leaves more shine afterwards than Ultimate Wash and Wax.  Therefore, I felt the need to follow up Ultimate Wash and Wax with Ultimate Quick Wax.  This restored the shine and slickness to my vehicle, but also questions the legitimacy of using a wash with theoretical protection benefits, if you still need to follow with a wax product.In conclusion, Ultimate Wash & Wax is another fine product from Meguiar's.  It's a pleasure to use and wash your vehicle with, and there are no significant negatives to using the product.  Perhaps others will find the product leaves more protection/wax than I found in my trial.However, like many wash and wax products, the protection provided by any car shampoo/wash seems to be almost non existent.  The wash and wax products usually have a higher price tag, so many will find it more price effective to simply get Meguiar's Gold Class wash and follow it with a Quick Wax for touch up maintenance, or a regular wax for full protection, if you have not waxed in a while.However, for those wanting to try something new or hold onto the hope that there might be some small protection left by a car wash after all, Ultimate Wash and Wax is another solid product from the folks at Meguiar's!
summary: Great Wash, Please Understand Limited Wax Capabilities

reviewText: It suds up good, i used this in an attached sprayer bottle on my hose and it foamed up good spraying it out. Noticed after rinsing it immediately started beading water off which is a good sign. Only time will tell on how long it will last. As far as cleaning power it does fairly good, but i've seen better. Then again it is trying to do two jobs in one. The best cleaning of a car is in steps, but for an all in one cleaner and wax i think this outperforms most.
summary: Meguiar's G17748 Ultimate Wash and Wax - 48 oz.

reviewText: Price was attractive but very poor quality construction material. I have not use because I am afraid it collapsed under high presion.

For the money this is a nice block but not a heavy duty block I would say medium duty. I use the block to lift V6 & V8 engines on my hauling trailer and it does fine. Another thing I want to add for people looking at this block is the load limid which is 4000K to 8000K because when I was looking this was not listed and I was not sure if I wanted it or even if the block would have enough load limid for what I wanted to use it for. The block weighs about 4 to 5 pounds more on the 4 pound range and can take up to 5/16 steel cable other than that the block has held up to everything I have thrown at it.
summary: Broncomania review for the champion power equipment C18003 Winch Snatch Block

reviewText: Simple to install, smooth running, and very heavily constructed, I used four of these on some small, hand cranked cranes. Only negative is that they must be exactly lined up or the cable will jump off and pop loudly back onto the sheave, which can become startling. BUT they do function just fine.
Just right size for packing in the Jeep and for use with synthetic cable winch. Haven't used it yet and hope I don't have to but nice to know I've got it just in case.
I bought this snatch block to go along with my atv's recovery gear. It handles the atv's weight with ease.

These are high quality lights, and installing them was a breeze.  The sit nicely in the corner of the tailgate and are easy enough to remove for cleaning or to get dirt and grime out.  The lights all function as I hoped and it truly was "plug and play".  I haven't taken them through a real rainy season yet, but the extra brightness (read:SAFETY) is a must have especially since we lug our kids around all the time.I deducted a star because of the shipping waste/hassle.  I had to pick this up from my local post office because they could not fit the package in a regular truck.  The shipment packaging was exceedingly oversized given the length of the actual product's packaging.

When this arrived, it was in a long, tall box that, once opened, seemed to contain a roll of wrapping paper. "What the heck is this?" I wondered. Then I remembered that I ordered the Putco 90009-60 Tailgate Light Bar with Turn Signal Function from Amazon.This is long - very long -designed for a 60 inch tailgate. Frankly, it's too big to have any use for me, so I passed it on to a nephew who owns a truck for his business that keeps him on the road a lot. He installed it and had no complaints. This is very bright and serves its purpose exceptionally well. The price tag is understandable since this is a quality product, much better than most of what's out there.

This Putco 90009-60 LED Tailgate Light Bar with Turn Signal is easy to install if you have a tow package & a place to plug it in.  If you don't have a plug in and no automotive knowledge, the light bar may be a little more difficult to install.I installed the light bar using the enclosed 2-sided tape (did not want to drill holes into my tailgate). So far, after approximately 200 miles, the light bar is still securely fastened to the tailgate.The LED light is bright, and is bright enough so that you can see it in the daylight.  The turn signal function is nice and works well with no additional installation requirements.  With the plug in, the turn signal, brake lights & running lights work automatically,  I will have splice the reverse lights in, and I have yet to do that.Overall, I am happy with the light bar and believe that it really helps others see my truck (especially when fully loaded & the cab light is covered).
summary: Bright LED Light. Full Rear Coverage on a Ram 1500. Easy to Install (if you have tow package & a place to plug in).

reviewText: My husband loved this new tailgate light bar. He installed it on our sons red truck and it looks awesome. My husband said the key to secure installation is to wash area with soap and water and dry, then clean with plain rubbing alcohol. This prepares the area clean for the secure application of the sticky tape.It looks like it came on the truck. The light is really bright and and can easily be seen in daylight.Great for drawing attention to the back of the truck and hopefully will prevent another rear end collision.
summary: Awesome tailgate light bar with turn signal function all trucks need this.

reviewText: This is a very good LED Light Bar that works very well. I installed it on my 2007 Dodge Ram 1500, just above my bumper so it isn't very visible in day light until it come on. The lights are bright even in the day, and very bright at night, adding more safety to my truck. My only complaint is with the instruction sheet, which indicates to install the light with the wires on the right side as in the picture. I installed it like indicated and plugged it into my trailer wiring plug. When I tested the lights the turn signal activated the wrong side, so I had to remove the light bar and reinstall it in the opposite direction. The good thing was I had installed it using the included brackets instead of the double sided tape. I highly recommend you plug it in to test it BEFORE you install it to your vehicle, especially if you plan to use the double sided tape. Other than the poor instruction sheet, this would have rated 5 stars. I also like the lifetime warranty on this item.
summary: Putco LED Tailgate Light Bar with turn signal, and backup light feature.

reviewText: I'm not too fond of the mounting options -- either double sided tape or drilling screws through the body of my car.  Tape will just fall off after a car wash or two. And screws would cause the body to rust at the puncture points.  I'd prefer some sort of clip-on option. Aside from that, this works quite well. Setup is very easy, so long as you have the proper wiring. If not, it'll take a little more work, but still pretty easy. The LEDs are bright, but not blinding. Like how each side flashes with each respective turn signal.  A bit long for my purposes, but workable. But I'm tweaking my own mounting solution.  A little overpriced, but good overall.

I got this for my husband's truck, a '98 Ford F-150.  Because his truck didn't have a factory-wired 4-pin connector, we needed to buyHopkins 48205 48" Vehicle and 12" Trailer End 4-Wire Flat Set, before he could successfully install the light bar.If you use the 4-pin connector to hook up a trailer, the left and right turn signals will be reversed.  On a factory installed 4-pin connector, you should have the lead wire on the left side, instead of the right side (which is opposite the directions given by the manufacturer).Whether you have a factory-installed connector on your vehicle (or you have to buy a wire set, as we did), hook it up BEFORE you permanently attach it.  That way, if you have to flip the light bar, it won't be a big deal.The lights are bright, and they look cool attached to the rear of my husband's F-150.  We especially appreciate the back-up lights, as the truck's existing reverse lights are not very bright.  The lights on this bar are bright enough to make up for that.
summary: A bit tricky to install, but works well.

reviewText: Simple plug in hookup  for most modern vehicles with a trailer hitch set up.  Color coded instructions if you must wire directly.  Bright and  very cool looking on your vehicle.  Recommend doing a preview  test before permanent attaching, to make sure you have it turned the correct way etc.  Comes with double sided tape or brackets for permanent attachment, you will also need a drill for the bracket attachment method.  Works with Brakes, Running Lights, Reverse Lights & Signals.

Installed easily, looks great.  Product quality is rather high.  Instructions and the double sided tape that was provided were on the weak side though (-1 star).  I trusted the provided instructions but once the bar was on the truck I discovered the left and right functions were actually the reverse of what appears to be written.  It also appears they've done a good job with the silicone to seal up the hole(s) where the wires come through the body of the light bar.  Here's some tips and other info...1) forget the tape provided and get some3M Double sided tape.  You will want to verify the turn signal directions prior to mounting with this tape.  Pretty difficult to remove after using this tape.***UPDATE*** Forget tape at all and use the plastic mounts.  Yeah you have to drill but way more reliable.2) Use dielectric grease on the 4 pin connectors3) Some people frown onScotchlok tapsbut I like them.  It made tapping the reverse wire very easy.  Then some liquid electrical tape and it's all set.4) On my 2005 Dodge Ram 2500 Diesel the reverse wire was the white with green stripe in the wire loom connecting to the 7 pin trailer plug.  This will of course vary by model.

I got this installed at my local workshop when I went for the inspection and liking it so far.When I compare the price on amazon for other products, this seems pretty expensive, but looking at the quality of the weather sealing, connectors and the brightness of the light - it does deserve the premium.
summary: Good and worth the additional premium

reviewText: Bead buddy seems sturdy and well made.  It held the bead on my GS1200 front tire but it didn't come close to fitting on the back.  I purchased this preparing for my first foray into manual tire changing.  Although the item seems well made and it's definitely sturdy, I couldn't use it on my back tire and really didn't need it on my front.  I'm sure some will find it very useful, but I suspect many end up discovering that a couple of spoons and tire irons are sufficient.
Very good quality toolKeep your tire bead in place when you install bike tire (good helper)This tool should last forever, i saw professional use it tooNice to have one at home for your bike tire

It works.  It is well made.  You need this tool.  What else is there to say?If you are doing any tire replacement at all, you need one of these tools.  It is worth the price even if you change just one tire.  It keeps the bead down in the dish during install so that you can spoon on the bead on the opposite side.  You use it for exactly 1 minute, but it does exactly what you need it to do and it saves you a bunch of time from 'bead hell'.Another quality Motion Pro product.  Solid one-piece aluminum construction, anodized, should last a lifetime of regular use.  Note: this is for motocross/motorcycle spoked rims.

reviewText: This product is the answer to changing small motorcycle tires.  I wish these had been around years ago when I was racing.
I installed my first dirtbike style tire the other day and used this bead buddy 2.  Using it is natural and effortless so you can focus on getting the rest of the bead mounted!

reviewText: Works as designed. Kept the bead in place while working the tire around the rim. Locks in place on spokes perfectly.
garbage product, i spraied it well until the can became empty, i have stuck brake dust just after 3 days of driving, so the commercial is???????.

Keep those wheel clean after a wash. The film this spray provides helps with brake dust and grim. It makes a wheel cleaning last that much longer. And it makes cleaning the next time around that much easier too. Win win

This product is very easy to use make sure that you are not going to drive for at least a hour. The wheels look good and no more brake dust I don't apply after every cleaning. Just when I think it needs it.

Armor all wheel protectant is the best way to go to keep your wheels nice and clean for up to four weeks. I have had the wheel protectant applied to my wheels more than four weeks now and it still repels brake dust like the day that i have applied it. I rate this product 10/10. There are no cons, Only PROS!!

A neighbor recommended the Armor All Tire Protectant to me a year or so ago... he uses it religiously on his Corvette wheels. I picked up a can to try and was very impressed. I've used it many times since, and as I have gotten more skilled at applying it, I am even more impressed. It takes a little practice to become good at application, just like it does for spray painting, but once you master it you will spend very little time cleaning your wheels (or putting up with dirty wheels).I use it on BMW wheels. If you know anything about BMW brakes, you know that all you have to do is think about touching the brake pedal and your wheels are filthy! Very depressing after spending an hour cleaning them... but no more. Make sure the wheels are squeaky clean and dry - apply Armor All Wheel Protectant to them, using an even coating (nooks and crannies too) - and you will go more than a month without needing to clean them again. This is especially great if you live in an area where winter can be harsh, and grimey, and too cold to wash wheels.Here is another tip - use Armor All Wheel Protectant on the tips of your exhaust pipes - especially if they are chrome or satin. Be sure to coat the very end of them... and it will keep soot from building up on your exhaust!The product will slightly dull the wheels when you apply it, but very little. This is much more desirable to me than what they look like after just one driving...Can't recommend this enough - great stuff!!!
summary: Incredible protection for your wheels - and more!

reviewText: This product really does work very well at repelling brake dust. It will keep a wheel clean substantially longer. In fact, if you miss a spot, you will quickly see brake dust build up in that spot and not on the rest of the wheel.The downside? It only appears to work on silver alloy wheels. It basically leaves behind a white film which resists the brake dust. If you wipe off the white film, you lose the protection. I tried applying it to black wheels, and it looked terrible. I imagine on chrome wheels, polished wheels, or any other colored wheels, it will also look terrible. On stock silver wheels, however, you can't really tell. This is what this product is meant to protect. If you have stock silver painted alloy wheels, this product works great. If you don't, it will look terrible.
summary: Does it work? Yes, but only on certain wheels

reviewText: I own a BMW and the front wheel get caked with brake dust very quickly. I have tried various products including wheel wax and was not satisfied with the results. With Wheel Wax, it is a hassle to rub it on and wipe off. Also, it does nothing to repel dust except make it easier to clean. With this armor all wheel protectant, it saves me time and hassle. It is so easy to just spray it on and let it dried by itself. It doesn't cloud the finish of my silver painted wheel either. I did a test by just spray it on one of the wheels and drove the car for a month without washing. The other 3 wheels were caked with brake dust. The wheel with this protectant look a lot cleaner and was very easy to clean off. Highly recommended product!!I usually don't like Armor All product but this is an exception.

I like how simple this product is to apply, but noticed that on my machined, and partially painted wheels it dries visible, and requires a lot of elbow grease to rub out completely to a perfect finish. I don't like to have to overwork any product on my car - not just out of laziness, but the more aggressively you have to rub anything in, risks scratches. I didn't even finish using this product, I just threw what was left away.NB: once it was completely worked in, it does leave the wheels beading - so it works, but there are other products out there that finish "right" first time, without the extra labor required.

I have done both of my vehicles and very pleased with the results. The product states the coating will last 4-6 weeks and that is the only part I have not verified yet. I'm working on 3rd week and still very happy with the protection. I have washed once and it made cleaning the wheels almost not necessary. Just hitting the wheels with the water hose blasted almost all the dirt. I've driven in the rain once and the dirt and water just runs off. It's like the wheels now have a teflon coating. I will order more for my wheels are difficult to clean all the ins and outs.

A lot of people are saying that this unit blows the fuse on their car. Yes, it will do this unless you have the engine running if you are going to use the cigarette adapter. If you don't want to run your engine (say you are in an enclosed garage), then get a RoadPro cigarette adapter to battery terminal clamps and plug directly to the battery in the engine bay.With that said, this unit is quite powerful and inflates tires quickly and with ease. It also doesn't sound horribly loud and rough like most other air pumps that I've used. It's a bit on the expensive side, but I expect that it should last for a while, and not fall apart after a few uses like my previous Slime air pump.
summary: Powerful and Quiet - You MUST have your engine running while using this pump!

reviewText: I just bought this and tired it out for the first time with my Jeep Wrangler for airing up the tires after a trial ride. It works great and it's fast!I did take recommendations and I included the battery clip-on and cigarette lighter adapter. Awesome!Hopefully it will last a long time, as it seems well built and much better then the less expensive Black and Decker, large plastic compressor that gave out after a couple of years. I'll update this review should a failure occur, but so far five stars. One thing, the manufacturer should include a nice bag for storage as I'll keep it in my Jeep. reviewText: The reviews said that this was the best of the air pumps.I ordered it and returned the pump without actually using it.My Black and Decker did not have as good of  reviews as this unit had,but I didn't like not having the option of a 120 volt plug.Since I was going to give it as a gift, I wanted to make it as easy to use as possible.The idea of not being able to plug it in to a garage outlet,since you can't run the vehicle in a garage, in the time to fill the tires.

The Viair 85P operates relatively quietly, with hardly any vibration, and it moves a lot of air. I use it routinely to top off car tires, which it does in a snap, and have used it to fill tires from flat in just a few minutes. Its price is pretty reasonable considering what a sturdy, high-quality product it is.You should choose carefully between the Viair 85P and its cousin, the 70P. With the 85P, you might think you're getting a more powerful compressor for just a few dollars more. Actually, BOTH compressors are designed to be the most powerful you can run from a 12V car accessory socket. With a limit of 15 amps, the two products just use the available power differently. The 85P has a larger stroke to move air faster, but the motor only has enough torque to operate up to about 60 psi before it blows its own fuse or that of your car. The 70P has a shorter stroke and is a little slower, but will work up to 100 psi. The way you can think of it, if you're familiar with a manual car transmission, is that the 70P runs in a lower gear and can climb a steeper hill.If you know that you'll only need the compressor for automotive or higher-volume applications where the pressures are relatively low, you might prefer the 85P. It's really terrific for car tires and comparable uses. I imagine it's the one you'd want to use for something like an air mattress, though I haven't tried that. However, with the 70P you can trade off some speed for a little more versatility.I think the 85P is a solid product and I've rated it highly, but personally I made the wrong choice. I always imagined that I could use my great air compressor not only with the car, but also to pump up my tires when I got around to riding my bicycle again. Since my bike tires require 75 to 80 psi, that wasn't going to happen. I actually did manage to inflate them, but it was impossible to top them off. You have to turn off the compressor to get a pressure reading, and then the motor stalls when you turn it back on, blowing the fuse.By the way, if you do manage to overload the compressor and blow the fuse, it's located inside the 12V plug. Unscrew the metal tip of the plug to replace it. You need a fast-acting 15A 250V glass tube fuse. The 6x30mm AGC-type fuses are easy to obtain. You can even get them from or through Amazon.Of course, if it comes to that, it's possible that the fuse in your car will blow before the one protecting the Viair does. Personally I don't have that problem because I always run the compressor from the battery power pack I keep in the trunk for emergency engine starting. That way I never worry about blowing a fuse in the car or needing to run the engine to use the compressor. I recommend theJump-N-Carry JNC300XL 900 Peak Amp Ultraportable 12-Volt Jump Starter with Light. It's smaller, lighter, more powerful and cheaper than the power packs with built-in tire inflators, and of course it has an accessory socket. For the price of a bells-and-whistles Chinese-made power pack, you can get the better JNC product plus a Viair air compressor!
summary: Limited PSI, but great quality and performance

reviewText: High quality portable compressor for emergencies.  Sure wish that it had come with its own carry case.  As it is I just leave it in the box in back of the Jeep.  Something that everyone should have, and is much better than those cheap plastic compressors that I wouldn't trust for anything.  VIAIR makes high quality compressors and this is one of them.

I purchased this for my truck, however it keeps tripping my 15amp fuse. I had to replace the fuse 3x, even with following the instructions on the site to the dot, I could not get it working. I was able to power it up on my other car successfully, however the pressure gauge is off by 5lbs, I would need to pump up to 40lbs (built in gauge) for my tire gauge to show 35-36lbs.Other items that I wasn't happy with:1. The connector is hard to turn, at one point, it got stuck and it leaked out alot of air. (I am very familiar with threaded connectors as I use it on my bikes)2. No bag included.The Goods:1. Its fast, I went from 30lbs to 40lbs in around a minute.2. Smallish, but not as compact as the 70P.

This compressor is small, light weight and very quite. It draws too much current for me to use my lighter outlet without possibly blowing a fuse so I bought a battery clip-on to lighter adapter to run it and it works perfectly. The air gauge doesn't report accurately while running, but is close. When you turn off the compressor it reports pressure accurately. The compressor has a screw-on hose tip and I loose almost no air when disconnecting it.

I have enjoyed this item it was cheaper then the 43p  and puts out more volume . It doesn't go to as high of pressures though I believe 70 or 80 pounds is the top limit .  To  properly use it since few cars have 15 amp ports you need a longer cord and to connect direct to the car battery while it is running . So buy a road pro extension port with battery clips . Then your set as long as you don't need to air a trailer on the road . Just make sure the cord doesn't get near the fan , belts or manifold . This will inflate a 15 inch car tire in just over a minute and a half .  The cheapo models take much longer and often burn up trying  . You can plug a tire and inflate on the side of the road with this as long as you don't pop the bead when it goes flat  in 15 minutes and be on your way if you have a full kit , know what your doing and find the leak . I carry a bottle of windex that I can spray the tread with to find the leak after putting air in it with the pump  and keep one that's atleast half full so I can do it at all times in a map pocket in my car where it won't spill . I am disabled and its hard to impossible to change a flat so I have fixed them with a plug kit and been done with it every few years this way . I just buy a good plug kit with a reamer and pliers to clear the puncture hole  , and have windex and a yellow crayon to mark the it in my car emergency kit .
summary: This puts out decent volume the next best thing to a lithium battery portable  pump .

reviewText: Using it in my f150 truck, with a long extension even reaching my trailer tires. I always ran my truck while using it, never had a problem. Great product. It's fast, doesn't complain about the size of the tires.

Very reliable air compressor.  I've used it a few times now, feels very solid and well built.  The light is a nice touch, the pressure gauge seems pretty accurate.  I wish this had a carrying case, otherwise it's great.  Much quieter than less expensive compressors that I've used in the past

reviewText: You pay for what quality you getThis is one of the best names in compressors and deservedly so. Their products are long-life functional and reflect the SPECS in their Ads.

reviewText: i had the Viair 70pm for my wife's Subaru that has 17" tires. When i got an Audi S4 and put 19" wheels on it, i figured i needed a more powerfully rated compressor, so i got the 85p.  Seeing some of the reviews warn of blowing fuses, i got a pair of those $5 alligator clips to connect the compressor to the battery terminals just in case i needed to.Well, i haven't needed them, this sucker works great via my cigarette lighter without blowing a fuse.  I've pumped my 255/35/19 tires a couple times (once from 30 to 40 psi, the other times just topping off a few PSI) and the 85p has worked well.  It'd be great if it had a little carry case like the 70p does, but no big deal. i keep this along with my jack and other little items in a tray in the trunk.

I'm sure it would have been a great product, could I have used it.  15A rating?  A sedan or minivan would need some fuses replaced if you tried.

reviewText: I've used moderately expensive Black and Decker and Sears air compressors in the past.... this one is top flight and way better than those...- substantial construction- rubber feet contain vibration and noise well... also it doesn't walk at all while running- chrome compressor finish is nice- gauge is very accurate, obviously you turn the unit off to measure... it has about a 4lb drop from on to off.- performance is very good.... reviewText: This may be a little over-kill for some, but personally I like the extra room.Five of the Battery Tender small bags will fit inside this one.Note that none of the measurements stated in the product descriptionfor this large bag are correct, as of Oct 10, 2012.Actual measurements of bag ~ 7" x  9" wide, and 6 1/2" tall, and has two carrying straps.(For comparison the battery in my car is 6 1/2" x 10" and 6 3/4 " tall)I suggest this Battery Tender Carrying Pouch - Large 500Large-0140.This case will hold all that comes with the Battery Tender Plus ~also the Battery Tender 25 ft extension cable ~AND have an inside empty space of approximately 4" x 5" x 9" for other stuff ~an electric ex cord ~ flashlight etc.I had first ordered the Battery Tender 500-0017 utility bag pouch.The UPC tag marks the size as 'Small". reviewText: I looked at different similar products and decided to pay extra to buy this because I wanted something that would last. Unfortunately this did not.I used it when I first got it and it worked fine. I liked the fact the hose clips on to the inflation valve and the gauge seems accurate.I stored it on my compressor over the winter and went to use it yesterday but couldn't. The pressure release button on the side had somehow fallen out of the body, leaving a gaping hole that lets all the compressed air escape. There does not seem to be any way to repair or replace that part so now the whole thing is useless and a total waste of money.
Works great for both inflating and deflating.  Makes it easy to ensure all tires are at the same pressure with out needing additional pressure guage.
This is a great inflator.  It was more expensive than most out there but the quality is awsome.  ARB is a very reputable company and will recommend this to everyone.

Amazon sent me a previously-returned ARB inflator and, not surprisingly, its hose leaked.  It was leaking from where the silver hose connected to the silver body.  I returned the ARB and bought a Milton Dual Chuck Tire Inflator With Gauge which uses higher-quality materials and higher-quality construction, though the ARB has a few advantages in design.The ARB has a gauge that's easier to read than Milton's.  The only problem is that the chuck on the ARB's air hose doesn't rotate like on the Milton, so you may need to clip the ARB's hose onto the air connector at an angle that makes the ARB's gauge hard to read.The Milton's chuck is open on both sides of the tilted silver end which I've read means you can push the Milton's hose into a tight space and pull the chuck back onto an air connection.  Apparently this is necessary on certain vehicles and equipment.  If you don't need that feature, then the ARB's clip-on connector is probably more convenient.  The clip itself feels a little weak and might break over time, though if it did you could hold it against the air connector.The ARB comes with a type D quick disconnect already screwed in but on the Milton you have to supply your own sealing tape and screw in your own quick disconnect.The ARB has a button you can use to release pressure from what you're inflating but the Milton has no such feature.  I don't think it's at all difficult to release some pressure on the chuck and just let air escape from the tire and that's probably easier than using a pressure-release button anyway.  Plus having a button creates another point that can fail during manufacture or after you've owned the tool for awhile.
Just what I expected after looking for the best options air gauge options for car, bike and accessory inflating needs.  Gauge measures well and clamp holds valve stem securely.

As others have noted, this is good design but it leaked from very cheap o-ring where the shielded hose meets the blue body that was already disintegrating.  I replaced that with a new o-ring.  There was also leaking from the poorly applied teflon on the end that connects to your air hose.  The rubber guard that goes around the guage is extremely cheap material and fits poorly.  It's unfortunate that this nicely designed item is so cheaply finished and poorly assembled.  With the replacement part and re-wrapping of the teflon, it works better now.  Someone ought to send a QC team into that factory to straighten things out.
summary: good design but leaked like a sieve

reviewText: I'm very happy with this inflator. It attaches to the valve stem with no leaks and allows fast inflation. The bleed valve allows me to bleed off 5 pounds of air before I set my tires.

This is a great product. It would be 5 stars except the pressure release pin is a weak link. Otherwise very sturdy and looks great. Very accurate and looks great. I keep this gauge in my Jeep to air down and to fill tires. Works great with any compressor.
This should take a lot of abuse getting banged around in my recovery tool box on offroad adventures.  Makes filling tires back to street presure a snap.  easy to read.
Nicely built, love the steel-braided hose and rubber shock mounting of the gauge. This makes tire air check and inflation to proper pressure a simple one-step process. Quite a time saver.

Finally got to use it on my and grandkids cars.  What a great tool, nice design, light and clamps easily on valve stems with no leaking.  Threw away my old useless pop-up stem indicator inflator.  This is the tool for my home garage...

Pros - Accurate, air line, bleed valve, gauge size, valve lock, large fill lever, swivel hose, air hose fittingCons - Psi and Kpa marksDead on accurate.  I tested this against my 2 other pressure gauges and they all were dead on, or they were all off the exact same amount.  LOLOLThe valve lock is great and makes filling anything so much more comfortable than trying to press on a traditional air chuck and hear the hissing when you do not get it just right and end up dumping more air than you put in.The steel braided fill hose that swivels makes it so nice just turn the hose and the pressure gauge is always towards you.The large fill lever is easily operated with just one finger.The bleeder is excellent for dumping over filled air in small amounts instead of pushing the valve stem and then having to go back and forth with pressure gauge and something to bleed the air thru the valve stem and back again.Pressure gauge size makes for easy reading of pressure, and being clipped onto the valve stem, and the one handed design is exceptional.With the air hose fitting already installed you just plug it into your air line and start pumping.  No running to the store to buy a fitting.The PSI and Kpa marks, to me are backwards, should be PSI on the outside of the gauge and KPA inside, but no biggie.PSI is not well marked but easy enough to read.  It is marked in 2 PSI increments instead of one.Over all this is a great Gauge that cut my monthly, tire pressure inspection on my vehicles in half.

I just purchased this and only time will tell how long it will last, but I am impressed so far.  It seems to have quality construction.  And it comes with the lock-on air chuck, which I use on all of my tire filling equipment.
