very nice inflator.  got a chance a few weeks ago to compare it to my friends calibrated one and this thing was dead on.  and much cheaper than the $80 something he paid.  wish the scale was a little more precise, but for that the cost will go up.  perfectly happy with this one.

reviewText: Bought the buffer for Christmas! Couldn't wait to use it!  Been using Meguiar's products for years! Keeps all my cars looking like new!

Got the Meguiar's Professional Dual Action Polisher and a bunch of the different 7" pads. Unfortunately, they would NOT stick to the backing plate that came with the DA over 3,000 rpm like they are supposed to for the cutting compound to be used. Meguiar's sent me the 6" backing plate for the DA and they stuck to that like glue. I put all these pads I used right in the washing machine and they came out like new. Just remember to tape off the hard corners and where the body parts meet so you don't grind the paint off! And, yes, I am talking from experience!!! summary: Multiple Uses for a Handy Funnel

reviewText: The flex part and the funnel are separate pieces.  The flex part screws on to the funnel.  Very good.The plastic is not heavy duty.  The funnel may crack if stepped on.  The flex part will not stay in position by itself.  The funnel opening is about 6 inches diameter.

This is a pretty decent little tire gauge. For the price, it's a great little tire gauge.The Good:- I think mine is pretty accurate. I've compared it to 3 other gauges and it's within 2 PSI of them. It's also pretty consistent with readings, which is a good thing.- There is only one button, which makes it easy to use with gloves on. This is very nice in the wintertime!- The little light throws just enough illumination to find the valve stem in the dark, which is nice.- It can measure in PSI, KPa, Bar, and Kgf/cm2. Which must be nice if you're .... Swedish?The Bad:- It's not the easiest to seal onto the valve stem to get a good reading. You sort of have to press and wiggle.- Batteries are difficult or impossible to replace. There is no little battery door - you'll have to take the thing apart to see about new batteries.- My clumsy hands frequently bump the button. This changes the unit of measurement to KPa, which I don't know how to read.I like this thing, and I'm sure it'll give me years of usage, as long as I can figure out how to take the thing apart and change the batteries. It would be a five star product if changing the batteries was easier.
summary: Good Gauge, Difficult or Impossible to Change the Batteries

reviewText: I'm crazy about the MPG, so I love to use this and make sure my tires are at their optimal PSI for >55mpg at all times.  It's a simple device, but it works great!
I don't check my tire pressure often and so I don't know how this may hold up over time but it seems to be pretty accurate and convenient. Great price and nice looking.
The tire gauge works really well. The readings are consistent. It's come in really handy especially now during the winter.

Broke quickly after first usage and when it did work for a little while the readings were off compared to two other guages I own- a Slime and a craftsman digital so it was definitely defective then it just quit reading after a month of VERY light usage. Unhappy is an understatement and hopefully these folks read these reviews and re-design this product. Quite unhappy.
summary: Terrible, inaccurate, broke within one month.

reviewText: This is he first tire gauge that I've owned that doesn't allow air to leak out of my tires while checking the pressure.  Surprisingly, all of the other ones that I've purchased were more expensive than this one, yet they all give inaccurate readings. In addition, the prior ones end up leaking out more air than I put in. I use my own air compressor, which is only capable of slowly adding air to tires. When I use my old tire gauges they let out more air than I can add back in. It's a pleasure to finally find such a simple gauge that actually works.

Yes it does the job, nice size, easily latches on, but what i find truly annoying is how long it takes to reset back to zero!!  It takes like 10 seconds!  Is that a long time, in the grand scheme of things no.  But once you get that initial figure, lets say 33.5, and ur goal is 32 psi.  It can take awhile to get down to that 32.  I bought this for my father in law....I have a craftsman tire gauge that zeroes almost instantly and it has a bleeder valve, that lets the air out, and can see the psi!  love it!!  Guess I was spoiled, as this Tekton gauge annoys me.  Luckily I don't have to use it often.  Don't get me wrong, it isn't junk, but just do not like it.

These work okay for the price. They don't compare to my craftsman ones that I use for personal use, but they work just fine for work since I could care less if they break or if someone borrows them. Did sorta break one where I have to take the battery out from time to time to reset it, other than that, works as advertised.
This gauge works easily and quite well. It remembers the pressure until you turn it off. Very enjoyable irreverent Opera book.

The tire gauge works great and is very fast.  It shows your pressure in 4 different measurements in case you're super nerdy like that.  It has an illuminated LED front, so you can find the valve stem at night with ease.  The back-light LCD is easy to read.  I had zero issue with air leaks and no difficulty seating it firmly on the valve stem to get a reading without wasting a bunch of air.  Measures in half PSI increments and displays the previous reading for 30 seconds before the tool auto-offs.It seems very accurate and is super easy to use.  Has an internal battery from the factory, so is ready to work out of the box.
This works well. It is simple one button use and the light is bright enough to check tires in low light areas.
Accurate, easy to use, and well-lit tire gauge.  It has a non-slip surface and comes with batteries.  I like the look and feel of this quality item.  Highly recommend.

I like it!  Seems to work fine and numbers are consistent.  I like that it displays different measurements of pressure (psi, bar, etc).  I live in Europe so all the gas stations don't measure in PSI.  This device has all the different measurements at the press of a button.  Light is useful to in low visibility!  Its also the coolest looking air pressure gauge I've ever owned!
summary: Works for what it is intended for

reviewText: I'm one of those that check tire pressure once a week so having a good tire gauge is imperative.  For the past year I have used several different digital and mechanical gauges.  I had issues with all of them.  Few of the mechanical one's did not work well in extreme cold weather, also hard to use with gloves on and too cold to use with bare hands.  Few others had issues with sealing the valve so it would not read accurately.  Some of the other digital brands did not seal the valve, or the battery would die quickly (like every week), or it was reading inaccurately.  I've been researching for the past few weeks on Amazon and this was the only one with great praise so i decided to try it out.  As soon as i got it i ran out and compared it to a mechanical one which I have been using with frustration and also a friend of mines gauge (Commercial grade digital gauge) and low and behold this one read accurately to 35 lbs, w/o issues and the mechanical one I had took me about a minute to get a correct seal to get a reading and then it read 3lbs too high, 5 lbs too low, etc. Compared to the commercial grade gauge.  This gauge is simple to read, easy to get a seal w/o much pressure to the valve and comfortable to hold glove or not.  So clean out your gauge drawer like i did and replace it with this one.
This is a must have tool to have. I would recommend having this tool in your car at all times.
summary: A must have tool to have

reviewText: I was looking for digital gauges for some time. There are definitely many choices and price points. This is an economy priced gauge that works perfectly for me. While a pencil type gauge is simple and reliable, it is difficult to see and not as convenient, especially in poor lighting conditions.Updated 3/25/14After using it for some time I can only confirm that this gauge is perfect for its intended purpose. No reason to look for a more expensive alternative

It is very light and feels cheap. I wish there was a way to turn the light off to save battery life, and I wish it took a standard battery instead of button cells. Having a little more weight to it would make it feel more durable. Not sure yet how long the batteries will last. I hope a while, because you have to use a screwdriver and take it apart to change them. Not bad for the price, though.

This tire gauge seems to be very accurate and is nice to use when you don't have light and you need to check your tire pressure.  I love the feel of it how to can switch what measurement type to what you need.  I would definitely recommend this product to anyone.

This is my first digital tire gauge. So far so good the light on the head of the nozzle is very useful when it is dark and you need to get a reading.  The non-slip makes it real easy to hold and it is an awesome price!
I use this gauge on our three cars every two weeks. It is east to use and sure beats the old pencil type gauge. The gauge is smalland can fit almost anywhere in your car and it is very precise!

I use this gauge for checking pressure in my car's tires to insure the pressure is balanced. The gauge is easy to use. The reason for four stars is that the accuracy is only 0.5 psi due to the decimal digit only displaying the number 0 or 5. I could estimate the pressure more accurately on my analog tire gauge that had a pointer like the second hand on a clock. But after many years of use the analog gauge broke and I decided to try a digital gauge. For ease of use I prefer this digital gauge with the light. For accuracy I prefer the analog gauge.
summary: Easy to use tire pressure gauge

reviewText: I purchased this digital gauge because the new tires on my Jeep are 80 PSI, and my old mechanical gauge only went up to 50. I am very pleased with this unit. It's fast and accurate. The fact that it displays tenths of a pound is actually more useful than I initially thought it would be.~Rusty Spoons

The only thing I do not like is it is easy to turn on when something else skims across the button while i storage, such as in a glove box.  I think the on/off button needs some kind of recess or covering so one must intentionally press the button to turn it on.  At least it turns itself off also after a short period of time.Its accuracy compares well to my high quality, air pressure measuring devices in the 35 - 45 PSI pound range.
Easy to use. The light makes it much easier to read than other digital gauges.  The pressure readings agree exactly with my other digital gauge.  I bought a second one for my Wife.
This inexpensive air gauge is the best one I have used. I get a consistently tight seal and quick/accurate reading.

I have been buying small items to put on a key chain set up.  This has a hole in the handle so it looked like it might work but it is about 5 inches long and much bigger than reasonable for a key chain tire gauge. However it is a great tire gauge.  The features I like best are that both the display is backlit and there is a blue led light that is not particularly bright but bright enough to do it's job that shines on the tire valve so it is easy to use at night time.  It is also digital of course and takes readings not just in PSI but also BAR, KPA, Kg/cm so that adds some versatility to the unit as well.  It also can read up to 100 PSI which will cover a wide range of vehicles beyond just passenger car tires should you need that. It is very lightweight being made of plastic but appears like it will be pretty sturdy. I think it is a good value, a reasonable price for what you get and will keep it in my main cars glove box. I might get more after I have had it longer.  Tire pressure gauges at gas stations can be very inaccurate if working at all so having this with you will cover you tire pressure readings day and night, would be good for a motorcycle too.  So far no complaints at all.
summary: Nice features. Bigger than I thought but still keeping it.

reviewText: I've compared the Tekton's readings to a standard gauge and they were the same. The light has been nice to have when checking tires without having the best ambient light.
summary: This thing is cool and accurate.

reviewText: Works as intended displays accurately and is backlit
Simple to operate. Easy to read display. Seems to be reasonably accurate. Easy to hold and operate. Overall, a really nice pressure gage.

I bought this product to use on my dashboard, center console and exterior trim. I had completely neglected these areas, except for minor cleaning and protection. Once I applied it, the difference was night and day! Literally, the product brought out a shine I had not seen on my dash at all, not even when I drove my car home off the lot. There is a spray, but I tried to liquid and it went on smoothly with no greasy feel. I applied using a generic microfiber applicator and rubbed it into the surface. Within a second I can see it covering up wear and producing a shine, which you would see with any protectant you use. It has now been a month and the shine is still there and still as bring and clean as the day I applied. I've tried Armor All, Turtle Wax, Mothers, but this is by far the best and I don't see me trying a different product anytime in the future.

After reading some poor reviews I think that it may just be the type of dash that you have. It worked very well for my dashboard in my Lexus. It is not a smooth surfaced dashboard, but somewhat of a matted finish. It shined up real well. My only beef with the product is that I do not like the top. It is the same as the black product and it has the same problem. When you squeeze some out it makes a big mess. You have to be careful or it will be messy. It is hard to describe but you will find out when you use it.
Greesy, messy, doesn't spread evenly and attracts dirt. Using it to shine my tires until its gone because its worthless for anything else.

Does Darken Black Plastic but it does not last like the Meguiar's Trim Spray they used to have. If you use this, use some F-21 protectant spay on the surface first (made by Turtle Wax Company). The shine and darkening of black plastic will be a lot better and last's a lot longer.

This product makes all the black exterior trim on my cars looks brand new again, currently it is protecting my new Impreza's black trim, refreshed my 2005 G35's trim and made my 2003 MPVs trim go from old and dull to a rich dark black again.You do not need a lot product to cover unpainted plastic bumpers or unpainted sideskirts. Trick is to use a foam applicator pad, not a microfiber or cotton pad as they absorb too much of the product, therefore you need to use more.
works great for jacks so u don't starch or slide off the frame or where ever u put it plus it matches all my prothane parts on my truck
This item works well. My only complaint is the price. It's just a peice of plastic. And the black is more expensive than a the red...???
my old urethane disc finally wore out after over 10 yrs of service.it fit perfect, been using it awhile now lifting truck to do work/protects under body parts from direct metal to metal contact.
If your jack didn't come with a jack pad this is the one to buy. The pad keeps metal off metal and if you are like be that's important.

This pad was obtained to replace a 2x4 block of wood which had been used on the saddle of my floor jack to protect the chassis parts where contact was made.  Because the saddle is quite large, in excess of six inches diameter, I had hoped this would fit the cast-in recess with a six inch diameter.  Being 5 inches diameter, it does fit, but another  inch would make it perfect !

They are actually a 4.5 and I use them on my jack stands but they fall off until I have the weight of the car touching them. Other than that these things do not cut, tear, and or smash and loose their shape.

The tool is very sturdy and more than adequate to remove original pre-cat sensors after 10+ years, circa 100k miles. Has a quality feel that belies its low cost.On these cars, a spanner wrench _almost_ works, but is extremely awkward. Using this tool makes the job simple.Do use a quality penetrating oil first, on a cold exhaust system, and let it sit a while first. But you knew that.PS: on super tough O2 sensors that won't come out, many mechanics suggest cutting the sensor's cable and using a box wrench or six point socket, which in theory will be stronger and give maximum torque. With this tool I cannot imagine that coming into play very often.
summary: Works well on both my VWs (Jetta IV 1.8T, Passat B5 1.8T)

reviewText: I bought this because my o2 sensor in my car was extremely deep and others did not work. This removed the old one perfectly and tightened the new one right up. This got into the tight spot where the sensor was at and made it very easy to work with! It seems to be made with high quality material for the price.
This tool worked like a charm. Not much more to say really... It did its job. Seems fairly well made.

I used this to remove/install AC Delco O2 sensors AFS109 and AFS123 on a 97 Pontiac Bonneville and it worked like a charm. It did not the strip the sensors and it had a solid grip onto them. It made the job so much faster than trying to use a wrench. To replace both sensors it took me 30 for removal/installation of both together. I think this is a better design then a socket because depending on your type sensor, the sensor maybe to long to fit into a socket type puller and you may damage the wires. This offset works great because it alleviates that problem. I would recommend this product

I bought this with a straight oxygen sensor puller and I thank Amazon for suggesting it.  I would have never been able to take one of my sensors off if this was not available.  A bargain price for a much needed quality tool.
Works great!  Very solid and easily removed two oxy sensors that were in a hard location to reach.  You can really put some torque on this and it handles it no problem.  Great tool.
A faulty O2 sensor was keeping my check-engine-light on and hurting my gas-mileage. However, it was very seized, and I was only able to change it because if this tool and an appropriate breaker bar.
summary: Very useful for O2 Sensor Replacement

reviewText: This oxygen sensor remover worked great but only the break the sensor loose.  The socket verion is better for many reasons including the use of air tools and ease of use. I would recomend a long sensor socket before buying this model

Used for all 4 sensors on 03 diamante.  3 were good but I figured after replacing the first one, I'd crack and re-tighten the others just to prevent them from being frozen when they go bad.  It worked so well I did it on my other cars as well.  The only issue is retorquing to the 30lbs.  With the offset you have to recalculate the torque wrench as a percent of the total length of the torque wrench with this device to the calibrated length of the wrench without the device.  I found it was pretty easy to loosen the sensor when the engine was hot.  I also found that it was easier if the ratchet handle and the tool flange were aligned and the ratchet handle didn't cross over the tool.  Anyhow this works OK.
Works like a charm, just as expected.  First time using a tool like this, and very valuable to have in your toolbox.  Buy buy buy.
Does what it needs to Do! fits into those tight places on my Ridgeline. This is more versatile and easier to use than my Socket style o2 sensor tool.
summary: Does the job! cheaper than other places and better than my socket style o2 sensor.

reviewText: While Oxygen sensors have improved gas mileage, hesitation, smog, etc, it is also true that the engineers in their great wisdom and made sure they are placed in the hardest-to-get-to locations. This tool is extremely well made and it will help you get to many of those locations.

This offset sensor socket works very well for what it's made for; installing an oxygen sensor. To remove my old one, I cut the wire off (the sensor was dead so it felt no pain), slipped on an impact socket, and a half-second later my trusty air impact wrench had it out. No sweat whatsoever! A minute later, this offset socket had tightened the new one into position.

The right tool makes a job simpler. I'd guess there are workarounds to using a specialized tool, but I'm glad I got this. It has a cutout to slide over the wires so I didn't have to cut the wires on the old part. It was deep enough to fit snugly on the recessed O2 sensor on a 2003 Honda CRV. It had no give and wasn't flimsy. It made the job easy.
summary: This made installing Denso 234-9005 Oxygen Sensor very easy

reviewText: Very well made and works like expected you can not go wrong with this tool if you are handy specially in tight areas

Item came nicely packaged, item is built rugged, with a great fit,wont make you nervous applying good torque to it. very handy tool to have being that most cars now a day have atleast 2 or 4 oxygen sensors.

A could not imagine that factory manufactured item can be so much off. Sizing of the socket too loose even for 7/8" and completely unaceptable for 22 mm.As mentioned in other reviews oversized sockets will round the nut surface since the full force will be applied to a very small area of the edges.
Using this tool will make the job go so much easier.  Makes the hard part unplugging your sensor and feeding the new one correctly to reconnect it.
summary: You'll want this to make changing your oxygen sensors easy

reviewText: Ive used this tool several times with no issues. It holds very firmly and feels very solid. So far, so good!

Just the right tool for hard to reach sensors, you may have to try with and without extensions to achieve working room but this does give the extra leverage for harder to remove sensors. Always start removal after car has reached operating temp and begins to cool for easier removal.
Having to change O2 sensors can be a real pain where the manufactures mount them nowadays, this makes a tedious job usually pretty easy, nice heavy duty construction
I needed this tool to remove my Oxygen sensors on my BMW. Could not have done it without this tool. So easy to use!!!

This tool works fine if your a/f or o2 sensor isn't recessed into something.  On my 2012 Accord the a/f sensor is recessed into a 1/2 inch deep heatshield and this socket is too chunky to reach it.  One of the straight sockets might work, but I'm skeptical those have a slot that's long enough to fit the wires without mashing them.  Ended up going with a Snap-On S6176 oxygen sensor socket that the service manual calls for.  It's expensive ($40), but I'll pay the money to have the proper tool for the job.3 stars because this worked fine for my O2 sensor that doesn't have a heatshield.

I used this to remove the O2 sensors on my 2005 Silverado and it worked exactly as advertised. They were stuck a bit, so I had to use PB Blaster to get help loosen them up. I wish this had a 1/2" drive so I could use my pry-bar and get some more leverage, but it ended up working fine with my 3/8" ratchet and a couple taps with a rubber mallet. It also would have been nice if it actually attached to the ratchet and wouldn't fall off, but it still worked fine. Just don't move it around much.
summary: Worked great; Just wish it was 1/2" drive instead of 3/8"

reviewText: will make swapping out sensors allot easier. Much more heavy duty than I expected, a great addition to my tool box
Good heavy piece. Would work just fine but for me an open wrench socket head did the trick better. Don't forget to run the engine for a bit before wrenching on the O2 sensor!
summary: Well built but I had better luck with another tool

reviewText: This looks really cool on, I put this on my self (55yr old woman) used blue painters tape to mark placement then push on and I pressed down around it to make  sure tape had good hold. Can't really tell it does anything but looks great!

Installed it as shown. Gives a cool "cowl" look, and I noticed a major improvement in my heat last night. It was so hot it was burning my face off. Will also be nice to keep mud and debris out of the vent.
This I believe is for looks only, I can not tell any difference in air flow. I did turn my opening facing the windshield, look factor A+
Got it, easy install, jiust not sure how effective it actually is.  guess it's more of an esthetic than function, but you get what you pay for

fits well. good 3m brand auto adhesive. easy install. wouldn’t recommend installing with opening facing rear bc leaves get in there and it makes it hard to clean out, plus the way that its shaped it would fit right on the base. it would hang over slightly, so be sure to test fit it before you pull the covers off the adhesive strips. air flow to my heat/ac was slightly improved, but not drastically. it does look cool and keeps leaves and mud etc out of the air intake. its a kind of glossy black. i would’ve preferred a flat black as an option. didn’t bother painting mine. the sun may do that over time anyway. I’ve had mine on for thousands of miles now and its still looking good and sticking well.

I bought to just for looks and mounted it on a 2011 jeep sport. It fits perfect and looks awesome and actually does pull in more air. Just mount it the way it is on the box, because it looks cooler and because the way the jeep is designed it functions better that way. The wind hit the windshield and bounces off and gets pulled into the vent. Check out the forums and they confirm it works better mounting the scoop towards the window. Its made of quality plastic and matches the black trim on the jeep.
Very easy to install, but the only issue will be cleaning it out.  Tough angle to reach, and I've scooped up several bugs in it already.
Great to add a little flare to your Jeep and protect that scooped out section from women's rings, etc.I like that it is just a small detail that only Jeepers really notice.
summary: not earth shattering, but relatively cool

reviewText: The plastic and finish is cheap.  I got adhesive remover on them and it ruins the finish.  I do not have high hopes that they will not fade in the sun light.With that said, I love the look and since they are already on, I would just repaint and reinstall if they do fade.
Easy to install and they add a nice touch to the Jeep.  I would buy them again without any hesitation.

If you own a Jeep Wrangler, these are a must have item.  I could not be happier with the ones that I purchased.  They go on fairly quickly once you peel off all the 3m tape!  But I am pleased to protect my door handle areas!

I really love these!  I highly recommend them to keep scratches, etc. from behind the door handle of your Jeep.  Being female with rings and such, I know I will not be scratching the surface behind the handle.  Be sure and use the alcohol wipes provided and clean really well behind the handle, check the placement well before completely securing and press and you are done!  Great look and functionality!!

It covers paint scratches that seem to show up even on the doors where no one uses a key.  I was a little disappointed in the design. The outer edge should be thinner.  When combined with the thick 3M backing tape the outer edge does not sit completely flush with the outer edge of the recessed hole.If there was a manufacturer that produced one that was more flush with the side of the door I would get it.  But otherwise it is adequate.
summary: Covers scratches well, but could be designed better

reviewText: I got these strait to my dour very fast and I'm very satisfied with them, it was very easy installation and very urged material that protect my doors from scratches
I installed it on my 2009 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited. Very easy to install. Just take the tape off. Make sure you have it aligned well before you take off the tape first.

While ordering these, I was wondering if I was going to like the look...I really do, it looks stock - as a matter of fact it looks like these should have been part of the design of the Jeep to begin with.A little harrowing to put on - since once they are on - they are on, and I fear that I did not align them all absolutely perfectly...BTW I bought the 5 piece kit for my 2 door jeep - it was only $1 or so more, and it is probably a good idea to have some spares.
They look great, very functional for clumsy people like myself, and very easy to install. Yet another great, cheap mod!
Looks great and keeps the fingernails from scratching the paint behind the handle . Glad I bought it. Superbuy.
I screwed up and got the 5 piece set and only needed 2 but it was still worth it.Easy double sided sticky tape and had both installed in about 10 minutes. They just add a nice touch.
summary: Rugged Ridge Black Door Handle Recess Guard

reviewText: Easy install, great addition to looks of the vehicle, bright red looks great with all the black matte fendors and bumper and door handles so this piece behind the handles not only protects the door divets, but accents the red even more.My only concern with them will be this winter, there was a tiney gap behind them yet and if water gets in there and freezes it might try to pop them off, this would be solved by using thinner doubled sided tape like they use on the rugged ridge window visors (the visors tape is a very thin 1/16th or so of an inch) and covering more of the rear surface then this thicker tape did (about 60% of the surface are is taped, and its about 1/8th of an inch thick)
summary: A must have for black trimmed non black wranglers.

reviewText: I bought this for my2 door jeep sport because it was a few dollars cheaper. I also have 2 more extra door guards.in case anything happens to the others but I doubt it.

SPLAT - the "Cleaning Putty that removes debris from nooks and crannies" -- does what it claims to do -- it DOES pick up (very nicely) that dust and dirt and debris that collects in those hard-to-reach corners, nooks and crannies of the car body.Using it takes a bit of adjustment -- it is super "viscous". You need to hold it firmly in your hand, and then press down just as firmly to make total contact. Lift it up - there's the dirt. Don't leave it on too long, or you will have to tug at it to get it off, and there might be some "droplets" left on the finish, MOST of which can be picked up by pressing SPLAT back onto the droplets. There was a "Shadow" left on my car's surface for a brief instant after lift-off, but upon inspection, it was not any kind of oil and it actually dissipated/evaporated in a few seconds.This would, IMHO, be great to use as a "before" wax prep, after you have washed the car and dried it off -- so all the dirt is actually GONE before you wax. I would think it would also be great to use at a rod run or local car show, to get off any bits of dust that may have migrated to that otherwise-spotless finish.Word of caution -- try not to drop it on the ground. Sadly, there was a newly mulched lawn right next to my car and while I was using this product, I dropped it... on the mulch. True to form, after I picked out what mulch pieces I could, SPLAT just prety much surrounded the rest of the mulch with its gooey body (after being placed back in its jar for a while) and kept on performing its job flawlessly.June 2012: UPDATE. SPLAT is Dead. Long Live SPLAT... Would I buy this again? well... I would consider it. It has now turned into a container of SPLAT soup. Yes, I left it in the car over the winter but we had a mild winter....

It is orange and kind of "icky"- seems like something a 5 year old would think is cool. If you stepped on it in the dark, you'd scream.But the purpose of the stuff is to get dust and dirt out of small places. It seems to do that well. I tried it on a couple spots on my car that always seem to gather dirt but resist cleaning- such as radio buttons, the lips around buttons and controls, crevices in the trim panels, etc. In every case it seemed to get most of the dust out, although it seemed to have trouble with larger pieces of dirt. It does not work very well on anything that is "stuck", since it doesn't seem to have a whole lot of sticky attraction.It never seemed to leave any residue on any of the surfaces in the car-although I never tried it on glass or clear plastic where a residue might be more visible.I also tried it on my cell phone-which seems to have all sorts of places to collect dust. It did a reasonable job on the dust, but I did notice small pieces of the goo breaking off, especially around the buttons. These came off pretty easy, but you would hope this wouldn't happen. Based on that, I was afraid to try it on my laptop keyboard-something I was hoping it would be suited for.Is it the cure-all solution to all your tight-space cleaning needs? No, I don't think so. But in 5 minutes it did make a noticeable improvement on my "just cleaned" dashboard. It works great on dust, not quite as good on larger particles. It did "refresh" my cell phone and got rid of some dust that has been there for quite a while.It does come in a jar with a tight seal, so it should last between uses...unless your 5-year-old finds it. I do hope it is as non-toxic as advertised, because it certainly will be attractive to kids.While I don't see a residue, I would certainly not trust it on photo lenses or sensors.

Splat is an orange colored glop. It feels like something a kid would like on Halloween. It's kind of fun actually. More importantly, this product solves a problem that has bugged us all at one time or another: it gets those crumbs and bits of stuff out of hard-to-reach cracks and crevices. You know, like the space on the center console of the car where crud accumulates next to the automatic transmission lever. I have tried everything from cotton swabs to pencil points. That stuff just refused to leave.Another problem place is the small spaces on a computer keyboard or a laptop. You can't use liquid cleaners unless you want to short out the computer. Another one of those petty daty-to-day problems.Enter Splat (what a great name!). Just take some of the stuff and jam it into those hard-to-reach spots and Viola! the dirt comes up with the goop when you remove it. Even better, the stuff is reusable. Just stuff it back into its jar, tighten the lid and save it for the next time you want to get some crud out of a small place.Bottom line: this stuff is great. It works as advertised, gets the job done, and doesn't appear to leave any residue. It's also non-toxic and reusable. This stuff is truly a bargain. It works, it's fun, and you can use it to scare your friends. Cool!

This Splat stuff is really interesting.  When I first got the jar, it was filled to the top with gooey shivery bright orange goo that is the same type of thing we used to get at the toy store and throw against the wall and watch it roll down.This glob of goo, however, is supposed to be used to clean crevices in your car- speakers, dials, switches, vents, etc, that you can not easily clean otherwise.  I did not use this goo right away, and almost a month later, I was surprised to see that the volume of the Splat goo went down by half.  It had shrunk- and no one had taken any out either.It is a bit weird to get used to using at first too, but it quickly becomes easy to manipulate into little places you want to clean.When using it, it really does work.  Little switches and indented areas that gather a lot of dirt and dust were cleaned well with no residue.  The only problems I had were two:---Don't drop it on the floor or it will grab every single stone, piece of dirt, or garbage it touches.---Don't let it touch the windows or it will leave a smudge that you can only see at night when lights are coming at you and it can be very distracting.  It does wash off relatively easily- but it takes a bit of work to get it back to the way it was.All in all, however, I like Splat.  As long as I don't drop it or let it touch any windows in the car, it does a good job.  It is only useable for 50 uses and that is not a whole lot- but it is biodegradable.  I have not used it up yet so I can not comment on the biodegradability of Splat.
summary: This stuff is weird, but it works- just be careful not to drop it

reviewText: Ok, so it looks strange, feels strange, and makes you think of 50's movies...but it works. I've cleaned out the vents of three cars and all their other nooks. Used in the house for heating vents, air intakesanything small and difficult to get to. It's simple, easy to use, shows no sign of reduced effectiveness after some hard use.Leaves no residue I could detect it's a simple smart fix for a niche problem almost everyone has. Good stuff.

I wasn't 100% sure what to expect when I got this, but I tried it out as soon as it arrived, and WOW!My car was professionally detailed about three weeks ago, and I was blown away by how much crud Splat picked up. Splat works so well in vents and crevices like around the shifter, gaps in the dash molding, and other places that you'll fall in love instantly if you like keeping your interior looking as new as you can.Cleaning my vents used to take 15 minutes or more with a detailing brush to get them dust free, and Splat knocked the job out in a couple minutes, with results better than I've ever got on my own.Now, looking at the pictures, you might be thinking "Oh, it's slime. My kid's got that.", but the consistency is much different. Splat stays a cohesive blob, and is much more tacky than toy slime. It isn't unbreakable by any means, but for grabbing dust and debris, you're not going to lose pieces of it when you take it off.Based on my experience with it, I'd expect it to cost twice as much as it does, and to be honest, I'd still consider it to be a fair value. For how well it works, how much time it saves, and what the cost is here, it's a tremendous value. You really owe it to yourself to give Splat a shot.

If you were a kid in the 1970s, you will remember the useless toy called "Slime" - a bright green concoction that while cool-to-the-touch, felt like holding the world's largest ball of snot. It was packaged in a plastic trash can and lid that kept the product moist and fresh. While the color has changed, the smell has not. I had an immediate flashback to the 1970s when opening the container, and a tactile flashback when handling the bright orange goo.Like the green slime of the 70s, it doesn't keep its looks for long. Back when your slime went bad, you threw it out and hoped mom would buy you more. The genius of Splat is that you take that gunk-acquiring goo to pick up stuff you can't.It will pick up gunk on its own, but it shouldn't be the only thing you use to clean your car, or you will do a mediocre job and exhaust all uses of the Splat. The description of "50 uses" is a bit vague, but it does underscore that its useful lifespan is not 'forever.'I live out in the country and my car gets dusty - fast. I've got two dogs that shed and I've been known to eat in my car on more than one occasion. Yesterday, I did a long-overdue detailing on the inside of my car. I took out the floor mats, vacuumed the entire car and cleaned the dash with an all-purpose cleaner and paper towels. Once everything was all spic-n-span, the nooks and crannies still gave my car the 'yuck' look with the stray dog hairs, road grit and crumbs sticking in places that were visible, but inaccessible to mere mortals. I grabbed the ball of splat and pushed it into the crannies and rolled it out and voila! All the debris was gone! In short order, the bright orange splat was mostly grey after I ran the ball of goo through the louvres of the air conditioner vents, all the buttons around the radio and the slot-loading area of the CD player. Now I understand how dealerships get a used car looking showroom fresh... because my 4 year old car looks brand new inside... and smells fresh, too. All the gunk in those nooks & crannies holds bacteria and hence, odor. Getting rid of all that junk makes my car look as good as it did when I drove it off the lot years ago.I discovered that pushing and pulling and/or rolling is the best way to go. You don't want to use a 'scrubbing' motion or grind the Splat, or pieces will break off instead of grabbing the gunk - the gunk will grab the splat. After I got the knack of it - cleaning when by in short order. If you like a well detailed car and are eager to get to the crumbs and dust particles in your floor shift area, around your hand brake, around your window controls, etc., this is the stuff for you. I highly recommend Splat.
summary: Finally - a real use for "slime" in a can!

reviewText: When I first opened the jar of SPLAT, it looked sort of like orange Jell-O. I worried that it would be sticky to deal with, but I simply upended the jar and the putty slid out easily onto my hand.  It is not at all sticky, it is a wet gel that holds together much better than I expected.  I rolled it around on various surfaces in my car, and it did a great job of picking up dust and lint without leaving any kind of residue.  The only issue I had was that there was a narrow crack between two dash panels where there was a piece of some white lint - the SPLAT did not manage to work its way enough into the crack to pick up the lint, but a swipe with a brush took care of that.  No matter how I manipulated the SPLAT, it stayed as one "blob" and did not separate.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Summary: Ingenious cleaning product for anywhere dust gets into nooks and crannies.  A decent add to your detailing tool kit, but with definite limitationsUpon opening the container I was greeted by a bright orange lump of goo.  I was expecting something more like silly putty, this is exactly like a thicker version of "slime" with an orange color and slight citrus / chemical smell.I immediately started to clean the center console of my car.  There's dust, crumbs, spilled coffee, etc here and all sorts of nooks and crannies.  I was immediately disappointed by what it didn't pick up and it did nothing to the drops of dried coffee.  I was thinking that I'd much rather have a damp microfiber washcloth.After a few more days and lots of experimentation on lots of other things I have a higher opinion.  After watching the video I realized they were pressing the goo and holding it for a few seconds.  This really helps SPLAT pick up more stuff, though it's still so-so on larger crumbs and debris (I'm talking about stuff the size of a fingernail clipping.)There are definitely situations that SPLAT works is better - they all involve dust instead of crumbs, and very intricate detail.  For example, on my office seat there are narrow creases in the fabric that trap dust.  This stuff is a champ for pulling it out.  I immediately used it on my nylon briefcase and TV remotes and cordless phones.  It also did a nice job removing the dust on my keyboard.On the other hand it's not so good on cleaning screens and chrome.  It leaves a filmy residue that you have to wipe off.  Also, the consistency has changed just in a couple of days - there's condensation on the lid of the container which suggests that what I am seeing is drying out during use.  I added a few drops of water to the container and it re-hydrated so the consistency is back to original.  At the same time, I noticed that the slime re-hydrated some bread crumbs from the console.  Yuck.  I picked them out - I hope this has some antibacterial properties or I could see this getting moldy before too long.  Finally, seven bucks for 3 ounces seems pricey. I'd give it 4 stars if it was a couple of bucks cheaper.TIP - knead the putty as you use it, otherwise the dust anc crumbs you just picked up will probably end up somewhere else in the interior.There are recipes on the web for making slime.  It's just borax, water, and white glue.  Cut the water and add a few drops of citrus cleaner and you might have a reasonable substitute!>>PlusGreat for dust in hard to reach crevices.Great for getting dust, etc out of fabrics.>>MinusDoes not pick up crumbsLeaves filmy residue -Seems quite pricey for the amount they provideIf you have questions, comments, or if you found this review helpful, please let me know!
summary: Great for dust, for crumbs, not so much

reviewText: Simple product?  Yes... but it sure does impress when in use.You'd think it was a magnet the way it holds on to items placed on it, really sticky but with no residue on items or fingers, just sticky rubber mat.It works, and that is saying something these days.Note that any item placed on the mat that is round or cylindrical COULD still roll if it's heavy enough and you go around a corner hard enough.  Flat items with smooth surfaces..... can't see them moving until you pick them up.It will also stick dirt, lint etc but easy to wash off and after it's dry, back to sticky again.Make sure you clean/dust the area you want to place the pad or it might not stick as well for you.  Not sure you want to place it on a dash that has had "shiner" spray put on it, might make it slip and slide.I've already found uses for it outside the car dash/center console.  If you work with small tools or parts on a table top or smooth workbench, it will keep tools and small parts from moving around and are right where you put them.I'm sure there are many other uses as well.  Nice product.
summary: What's not to love about this pad?

reviewText: Think fly paper when you buy this item. It is very sticky which means it attracts everything. It also sticks a little too well to a dash and gets worst when it is a hot dash. Pulling it up leaves a mark on your dash for a few days. I thought it would be a friction mat, not a highly sticky mat.

There are some reviews on here that give this product a bad review because it is too sticky (which is ridiculous). It does it's job REALLY well and it should not be rated low because of it.This dash grip is VERY sticky; I have never had anything fall off of it, which is what you are looking for. I have had other grips before and they are all worthless. We put this one in my wife's car because she has a Hello-Kitty bobble head, and we just did not know how to put it on the dash without it falling off or being too strong and damaging the dash. This is the key. We can put our phones on it while the bobble head still sits on the dash, and nothing has ever fallen off.I would say though, that this is very sticky. The bobble head has been on the grip pad for several months and it has gotten more and more stuck to the pad. In the hot sun the pad gets more sticky, almost gummy feeling, and this has caused the bobble head to become firmly placed. The only way to get it off the pad is by removing the pad completely from the dash.So, to conclude, this product does it's job very, very well. If you leave something on if for a long time, it will probably get somewhat stuck, but if you remove the pad, it everything will come off just fine.I would buy again.
summary: It does it's job, and it does it well.

reviewText: This product is not touted as being a marvel of engineering. It is plainly and simply a mat that will cling to your dashboard and upon which you can place a few items that will cling to the mat. For example, if you travel on a toll road you can put coins on the mat where they can be easily seen and retrieved. You would not leave any coins in an unattended vehicle, of course. There are those who will break into a vehicle to steal a nickel.If you happen to be a handyman (or handywoman)you will find many other uses for this mat.The mat is exacty as advertised and that is saying a lot these days.
Thought it was a big sticker it was so sticky, but its not. Just peel and replace multiple times, still stays put. Use it on my dash to keep items in place.
This is one amazing dashgrip. Holds my phone in place without it falling off or moving a inch, even during sharp turns.Highly recommended.
Purchased the first one for myself, re-ordered more for my Wife and children.  Amazing product, exceptionally useful, leaves zero sticky residue.  Do yourself a favor and get this.

Several issues to consider after using it.1. a small rubberish smell in the car after you use it.2. starts to collect dust too, so I don't know how long would it last if it continues to get dusts on it.3. having sun shining on it (on the dash board), don't know if it will have "hardening" effect on the rubber or the stickiness.4. the "mat" is toooooooo small.  I thought it was bigger.  But it's really small for my needs (I wish it were double in size or at lease 50% larger).Due to so many questions and small size in particular , I gave it a 3 star review.
Nice and sticky.  Holds everything perfectly and easy to wash and renew.  It was exactly what I was looking for.

This seems to work exactly as promised.  Lay it on your dash, lay a pen and some sunglasses on it and there they stay until you want them.  Not being one accustomed to leaving things on my dash, I'm not sure that will be my primary use though.  Change, pens, sunglasses all have their place in my console or existing dash cubbies.  I don't see using it for a cell phone, GPS etc unless you take all that with you when you're parked.  Do you really want to leave that exposed to the elements and visible to thieves?  Instead, I am intrigued by other applications for this product.  I can see it on the side of the little TV in my kitchen to hold the remotes in place.  The possibilities are endless.  Bet it could even fill in as a lint roller in a pinch!

I don't care what the other folks said about this being too sticky; it couldn't be too sticky for me.  I also read that the items stick to it better than it does the dash.  I can tell you that if you have Armor-all on your dash, it doesn't stick to the dash as well as if you take an alcohol rub and clean the area it is to sit.  It sticks so well that I can lay my sunglasses in any position and they will stay.  I even placed the glasses lens down to see if it would leave a residue and it didn't.  I think it actually pulled the fingerprint off the lens.  I've got an old flip phone that isn't in the best shape and it actually stuck so good that it almost pulled the batter cover off.  It doesn't hurt my iPhone at all.  The only regret is I don't have more to put on the dash for everything I use often and road trips.  I know, I know, it'd look goofy but I'm telling you, no more cd cases or thumb drive or sunglasses sliding our the window or landing in the door pocket of the passenger door.  I'm going to buy more.
summary: Where have you been all my life?

reviewText: We put this on the dash of my wifes mini van, it holds phones and sunglasses with out any movement at all. I turned around and bought one for my truck.

Many people complain that it leaves residue on their dash board but I did not have any problems with it. I had it during the hot summer months with no issues. If your dash board is affected by the sun and discolors like some reviewers says, then this is not the product's fault. Anything you put on your dashboard will keep that spot dark while the other surface is exposed to the sun. So overall the product itself is great, its at a good price and it's worth a try.
If you ride a trail this is a must. Very easy to use and install. This is one of the best that I have used. Very little if any vibration while riding. Well worth the money.

These mirrors work well when mounted on a front rack of my ATV.  I like the mounting bracket better than the u-bolt on the ATV Tek ATVMIR2.  I like the fact that they are a quick disconnect (without tools) as well.BUT........I'm not a fan of the round mirror--it just does not give the field of view that the rectangular ATVMIR2 gives (at $10 more in cost). The disconnect mechanism on this mirror is PLASTIC, and if not handled with tender loving care, IT WILL BREAK (and it is prone to weathering, especially from sunlight). This brand has a good rep to protect and the relatively inexpensive product here is no exception to what I think is a well reputed line.  It has the hardware to mount it and does as good a job as not looking over your shoulder can do.  Use it to be legal in some states, and to keep track of who is gaining on you.  The image is clean and the construction nice for the price.

Good quality, but I cant get it to stay firmly in place... yes I've tightened all the screws on the mount and on the bottom of the mirror and the swivel thing... I'll keep trying because it is a good thing to have on an ATV when riding with others.

you gotta protect your rv from high water pressure as the pipes are made to handle typical city water pressure of 90 psi, this will help and make sure while you are hooked up your rv is protected.  doesn't get any easire than this just screw it into the water connection at the park and let it go from there.

First off, I use one of these on my RV. It works great, and rare to find actual good-quality metal ANYTHING now days.  It gets pressure below 50-psi...depends on several variables as to how much lower...their ad info is right though, always between 40-50 psi.As for every one of the reviews I've read here on the 'negatives'...I'd like to point out that this is NOT an anti-hammer reservoir, nor is it a filter.  Nasty water at any RV park will most assuredly clog it up to where it won't work...pre-filter between your camp connector and your regulator. That will fix the issue (or, replace your filter element then).As for 'hammering' due to pressure...this is also a simple fix. Get an anti-hammer reservoir. You can 'rig up' your own, buy a 'house-type' anti-hammer at most any hardware store, or you can buy one like the SHURFLO Pre-Pressurized Tank (available on Amazon). It helps to buffer 'hammer' out of your water system. I find it to work best on RV's, because RV's use vaned-pumps for 'off-system' water, and you get a natural 'stutter' as a result. If you put a small pressurized tank in your system, the tank buffers that vaned-pump stutter, as well as acts like a anti-hammer to on-system water sources.This is a really good product.
summary: It's a good Regulator - not an anti-hammer or filter

reviewText: I have not yet used the regulator but as I see it and the construction I am very pleased and quite sure that this product will serve me well and long. The brass construction should hold up to years of service.

When I first tried it the coupling leaked just a tad and I stored it away as lesson learned. Since then I was having a problem with my water hose getting torqued and unscrewing itself and leaking. I decided to revisit this pressure regulator again as the coupling allowed it to turn freely and it solved my problem with the hose unwinding and loosening the cap. The coupling that leaked before on the regulator also leaked again, but this time I could tighten it better as it was more out in the open and was able to stop the coupling from leaking. I still haven't figured out how tightening it helped, but it's not leaking now. Problem resolved!
This can save your internal water system on your camper or motorhome from damage.  Some water supplies at rv parks have very high pressure and this little reducer will do the trick.

Well made and priced right. A real necessity if you are going to hook up to water systems with unknown presures.

I do note some other users complaining about sticking and will be on the watch for that, but I don't expect backpressure issues in my installation. Serves its purpose.

I often have a need for simple two wire connectors when doing automotive wiring. I generally like to use Delphi and other modern weather proof connectors but sometimes those are overkill in both price and complexity. These connectors are very simple in nature and pretty small in size.These admittedly are a pretty tight connection and fairly tough to fully seat. I would imagine that if you were to plug and unplug these often they would loosen up in time making them easier to fully seat and unplug. For my application I just need them to be able to be disconnected in the even I need to replace an electrical part. For that a tight connection isn't an issue at all.
These are good to use when a little more room is needed. I use on my ATV to extend the rear pig tail for my Batt. charger as I have a basket on it and now you don't have to craw under the basket.
summary: Great connector when you need a little more room.

reviewText: This product from Allstar Performance is Number ALL76232 and is a Universal Two wire connector with a 12" loop of wire so you can cut it at the proper length you need for a power feed connection or an other use with low voltage.

reviewText: It is well made,connects well,and doesn't kink.I will by more,as my needs for this connector increase.Theyr'e cheap,andthey work well.

Use as it is or do as I have, cut it in the middle and use each segment as the joiner between power/ground and whatever you're powering.  I bought a 'hydra' connector for my motorcycle that goes to the battery and these cut connectors will be attached to the LED lighting and other light-medium current accessories with the addition of ATC inline fuse holders for protection.  It eliminates a mess of 'bullet' connectors.  Makes the airbox 'busy,' but it works and is safe, and the connections are all resistant to weather and can be disconnected easily for service.

If you use a battery tender this is useful.  I use a splitter, also found on Amazon, and maintaing multiple batteries with one battery tender.  Rather then buy multiple ends and pieces I bought these inexpensive connectors.  Ofter if I just need one end I cut it in halve so I have what I need and can splice to extend if necessary with old lamp cord or pretty much any wire you have laying around.

However I mainly got it for the winter here in ND. The trickle charge helps keep the battery warm and topped offed. It is really hard on the car and the starter to not have ample amperage to turn your car over in the cold winter months. Not to mention having it be cold outside and having to jump your car. Well since I use the charger almost daily the plug to my battery simply wore out. I cut off the old plug and soldered this one in and now I'm good for another few years before this one will need to be replaced. Oh and my car starts first try every time even with it being -30. Use the right motor oil and have a topped off car battery and your car shouldn't hesitate to start.

fits perfectly.  i used it to connect a 12v socket(lighter socket) on my fourwheeler to the battery via a "Battery Tender 081-0069-6 Ring Terminal Harness with Black Fused 2-Pin Quick Disconnect Plug" to allow me to put the charger inside of my front box, and disconnect it if i ever remove the box..  regardless, it fits the battery tender jr sockets perfectly.  good quality.  good wire gauge.  i recommend it.

I tought I'm buying A brand new idem but I gues I was wrong this was priviusly used and it has marks of wearing all over it, it make me sad I fall for such a scam

Great snatch block! I would not use it with synthetic rope though. It has plenty of reserve capacity for what I am using it for.

Arrived promptly as promised. Seems to be OK. Just getting tired of everything coming from CHINA. I think that country of origin should be required in the description.

bigger than I expected. quality built block. I have used twice and it works perfectly. will be buying a second soon.

This is a large and heavy snatch block, and seems to be well built.  I especially like the grease fitting, which makes sense. reviewText: This is the second Smittybilt Snatch block I bought, the other came with Winch accessory kit (Smittybilt), well built and should last for years. Works great and seems well built. I will buy again if needed be. I'm using it with my 2011 Yamaha grizzly 700

So far, works great but I have not yet gotten close to weight limitations for this item. This is rated "up to 17,600 lbs." and the largest item I've used it with was around 5,000 lbs. That amount may have been increased due to resistance from being pulled from a ditch, items inside the vehicle (unknown) and foliage being pulled through. Even if that added another 2,000 lbs (number tossed in for good measure), it still isn't a good test of the item.That being said, I would buy the item again, without hesitation. The pulley spooled freely and did not get hot from friction during usage. Fact is, my winch is rated for 12,000 lbs., so I'll never have a "full test" of capability. I'm left with plenty of margin for safety.

Excellent snatch block for self recovery or having to pull another truck from an angle. Appears to be extremely heavy duty, fortunately I haven't had to use it yet, very happy to have it on board, just in case.

It truly is well made, with a nice finish.  The cost had me worried about quality. After comparing this to other products in the same or similar capacity, I bought it.  I've now used it three times without any issue whatsoever.  Very well made and I would recommend.

I have 2 of these. It's GREAT it comes with a grease zerk, however, neither of the 2 I purchased has a drop of grease in them. GREASE IT BEFORE YOU USE IT! To check this just plug something into you outlet, and take the key out of the ignition.  If it continues to draw power you're good to go and you can plug this in and not worry about it.  If the outlet shuts off you need to leave the key in the on position for this to work and that may not be preferable depending on where your vehicle is and if it is secured in a garage or sitting in a drive way where someone could jump in, turn the key, and drive off.If your car doesn't have powered outlets when the key is removed it is not the fault of this product that it isn't working when you take your keys out.We use this to charge my car while I'm away and it is very easy.  Unfortunately they battery terminals aren't compatible with the type that connects there but this lets my wife plug this in and not have to worry about anything. reviewText: Amazon supplied an exact fit replacement, for my RV water heater. The anode rod that is part of the water heater plug had broken [by intended corrosion] before it had been entirely consumed. this new one fit perfectly.

For a maintenance task that is fairly simple but important in extending the life of a water heater, this is an item that does what it is supposed to.  Even though water heaters in RVs are not that expensive compared to most appliances, it can be expensive and time consuming to replace them.An anode rod is designed to be eaten up over time (keeping the steel tank from getting corroded), so replacing this on a yearly basis is a wise idea.Don't forget -- it is crucial to use Teflon tape (wrapped at least twice around the threads), (or a pipe dope that is suitable for potable water applications) on the threads before screwing it in.  If this isn't done, there is a good chance it will electrically weld itself to the tank, requiring a complete water heater replacement later on.Recommended stuff to have on hand for the replacement:  Teflon tape, a 1 and 1/16" socket, a fairly long ratchet arm (because the threads can corrode making it hard to get it loosened), and a six inch socket wrench extender.Why choose this over the competition?  Two reasons.  First, it is US made, and the second, it is made by the same people who made the water heater.  This doesn't mean other brands are deficient in any way (The Camco model has a built in drain which helps a lot with winterizing.)  It is more of peace of mind that one knows this will do the job.
summary: Does what it supposed to, and made in USA.

reviewText: I install a new anode rod in the water heater every spring.  It lasts for the year.  Easy to remove and install.  A must to keep your water heater protected from harmful elements in water.

For RV owners with aluminum water heaters it is essential to make sure that they always have sufficient reserve on the anode, and replace when it has corroded about 75% of its original size, otherwise the body of the water heater will corrode from the hot water. Certainly this is the cheapest and easiest way to prevent that from happening. Replacement is dependent upon usage. When not camping, remove the anode and drain the tank, and it'll last longer. Keep an extra on hand always.

reviewText: OK why do I need an ice scraper in Texas? Truth is I don't need it very often but when I do it's great to have this OXO Extendable Ice Scraper. That brush will rotate by pushing a button on the scraper and just rotating with your hand. This is an very good  ice scraper and brush that should last a long time.

reviewText: This snow brush is great for versatility and when you have light to medium snow.  The brush changes from vertical to horizontal.  When it is vertical, you can quickly brush off light snow from the car and windows.  Then when you change it to horizontal, you can brush off larger amounts of snow, but not too much, otherwise this is not overly efficient compared to our other brushes.The button that allows you to change the direction of the brush locks well into place so there is not a problem of it changing around as you use it.  The trick to the button is that you have to press the top of it in- if I press in the center of the button, it does not always work and I get frustrated until I remember the key to using this.The ice scraper is quite narrow.  This makes it take quite some time to clear off an ice covered windshield.  Again, if there is just a light coating here and there, it is not a big deal, but if there is significant ice built up, it takes quite a bit longer than our other ice scrapers.The bristles are indeed very soft and do not cause any damage to glass or the car, so that is a great feature.  Handy to have on hand in the car, but if you are in an area that has consistently periods of heavy snow and/or ice, I would suggest having a larger capacity snow brush and scraper handy in case you need them.  This might frustrate you now and then otherwise.

reviewText: I would not buy this scraper/brush to replace my gas station cheapie.  The scraper is not so sturdy, and while the brush head can be rotated, it's actually shorter than my cheapie.Also, it does not extend.  Wrong item?  I thought perhaps there was another on my newsletter, and I accidentally ordered it instead of the extendable brush.  But there was no other OXO snowbrush, and the item I'm to review is an extendable brush.  But mine isn't.  How I struggled trying to extend the grip from the handle, until I realized the way the handle is made it couldn't possibly extend!  And sure enough, that white button toward the end of the handle that you can see in the product picture is missing from my snowbrush.A mistake can be forgiven, and I've given favorable reviews when I've bought one item and received another - so long as form, fit, and function comply with the product description.  This does not.It's a good thing it has that nice, comfy OXO grip.  I need it for the extra time it takes to brush the snow off my car, and it earned this item two stars, rather than one.

Like most OXO products, this is very well made.  Yes, it is a bit heavier than a plastic brush but I don't think that limits it's usability.  The bristles are soft so you don't have to worry about scratching your paint and the extension feature is nice.  It would be nice if it got longer though.  It is barely long enough to span a small SUV and not long enough to clear the roof of a small SUV, especially for a woman or person of smaller stature.  The handle did not telescope easily out of the box but a squirt of silicone fixed that and it slides in and out easily now.  The button for twisting the head is difficult to press.  My wife has arthritis and she can't press it to swivel the head as there is too much spring tension.  This won't be a problem for most people but I wanted to make you all aware.  Overall, it is a very nice brush but if you have an SUV, it may not be long enough for you.

Alright, enough Star Wars allusions...I live in Wisconsin, snow brushes are a part of life.  Right now I have four different ones in my car, because each has a use and none did it all.  That gets annoying because they're always on the floor of the rear seating area rattling around.  But sometimes I'm brushing snow side to side, sometimes I need to pull it off the top of the car towards me so it falls off the side.  I don't often need to scrape ice since I have a garage and when I'm at work it usually isn't in place long enough for ice to build up, but I have a special ice dozer unit I got here from Amazon that I keep in there for bad ice days.  That's a nice small unit though, little larger than a grown person's hand, so that stays no matter what.  But I think this little beauty is going to replace the rest of them.The extendable handle is great, but other ones I've seen at local brick and mortars had that.  What I HAVEN'T seen locally or online was the rotating brush head that this one has - so I can rotate it to brush to the side, or rotate it again to pull or push directly away from me.  The button works very well, is large enough that, as I found today with our winter storm happening, it's easy to push when you have big gloves on your hands.  The rotation brush allows it to drop down and spin then set back into place.  The button for the handle releases a detent that goes into a series of holes, so when you extend the handle, you can pick how far to extend it and release the button and the detent will slip into the next hole.  I can't see if they have metal over the end of it or if it's just plastic that extends into the holes to lock it into place, so if it's plastic that could be a weak point depending on how rough you are with it.  For my use, plastic will still last.  There's a catch inside so you can't pull the handle all the way out.It's solidly made, the longer part of the handle that goes up to the brush being a hard plastic, while the black end of the handle that you grip is a rubberish coat so it's easy to grip even in gloves when you're wet from snow.Whichever way you have the brush locked, there is NO play in it at all - no wiggling.  It's very solidly made.I absolutely love this thing, since now I can just have two winter car cleaning devices in the back, which won't rattle around and touch each other.  One of the few Amazon Vine items I've gotten recently that I was able to give a very positive review for.
summary: This IS the snowbrush you are looking for...

reviewText: The OXO Good Grips Snowbrush is built like a tank, extends so far that even the largest windshield is likely to be entirely reachable from one side of the vehicle, and has a brush that can be twisted so the you can easily use it back and forth or up and down.  The only negative, and it is only a slight one, is that this snowbrush is one of the largest I've ever seen, even when the handle is fully retracted.  Although I have owned this only for a short time, it seems to be genuinely well constructed and sturdy enough to hold up heavy use.  Highly recommended (and let it snow)!

I have tried a number of different brushes and scrapers this past winter, and hands down, this one is my favorite.As you no doubt already know, the brush part rotates, so it can work like the brush/scraper combos you're used to, or you can use it more to push (or pull) the snow, at a 90-degree angle to the handle.Pros:1. Like probably every OXO product I own, this is well designed and sturdy.2. The rotating brush thing works well and seems like it will continue to work well for some time (e.g., it doesn't flop around, but stays in place).3. The handle telescopes for a better reach -- also a win!4. Very reasonable price.I have no cons. I just really like this thing. It is also the sort of thing that would make a good gift for a young driver or really just anyone in a snowy climate with a car. I have collected many automotive snow and ice removal implements over the years, but this is absolutely my favorite.

I don't know what everyone else is complaining about...this is the best snow brush I've ever used.  I love the fact that the brush can swivel and locks securely into place.  I prefer the perpendicular setting which effectively plows the snow from my Jeep Grand Cherokee's roof, windshield and hood.  The feathered bristles don't damage your car's surfaces but still penetrate heavy snow.  I didn't find the brush too heavy at all.  Actually I enjoyed it's slight heft, as it helped the brush penetrate deep, heavy snow.  Use it's weight, people, don't fight it.  The extendable feature really came in handy for reaching every part of my Jeep's roof.  I finally took it out of my SUV now that I'm enjoying a southern California winter.

I have a Toyota FJ Cruiser, which is a good bit taller than I am, so I need an extendable brush for the winter.  I had a different one that extended with a little rotatable lock but that was awkward and it ended up being too tall to get under the standard FJ roof rack.This one extends more obviously with a button that lets you pull the handle out and it's just short enough that I can push it under the roof rack which is a big help for getting the snow off.  It's plastic whereas the last one I had was metal but so-far-so-good.  We only had a few light snows this winter so I've only used it a few times but I had no trouble with it.  This one replaced my old extendable scraper/brush.

Don't have much to add except to echo comments already made by others.  It is perfect for removing light fluffy snow.  Yes, the extendable handle could be longer, but I also have another type of SUV brush that can handle that task.  This brush is perfect if you drive a small to intermediate size vehicle like a Corolla, Civic, Sentra or Elantra.I bought mine off of Amazon without realizing they sold these at my local Bed, Bath and Beyond and could have gotten it cheaper with the use of a 20% coupon.  Then again, I have an aversion to shopping in malls and stores so the price was fair and worth it.  I imagine it will hold up just fine, but I imagine it might be a challenge to remove heavier, wet snow.  An alternative brush with stiffer bristles like the other one I have may work better.  Construction appears to be solid and built well.EDIT 2/4/14:  Tried using it on more wet, heavier snow today after a snow storm dumped 4 inches.  As anticipated, the wetter snow caused the bristles to become heavy and clogged a bit.  If you are going to store it in your car after removing this type of snow, it will cause quite a wet mess.  Bang off or brush against your car tire to minimize the melt off.  The brush still did its job, but once the bristles are heavy and wet it starts to get a bit more challenging.  I still give it 4 stars, just be aware that this will happen.
summary: Perfect if you want to save your car's finish

reviewText: If I can get them on by myself, YOU can get them on by yourself.The instruction that come with it are Shittybuilt.Here's what you need:5\8th Deep socket and medium or larger ratchet. A power wrench or pwr driver would be beneficial, just don't cross thread.These things will help:Friendsmall to medium auto jacks standsfloor jack (i used my HF 3 ton and could move, twist handle etc with one hand)patiencecommon senseCaptain MorganThe Instructions say small end, they mean the ends that STICK OUT where the rails bolt on, one end is longer and goes at the back.There are two nuts at each end of the vehicle mentioned in the instructions, remove all of them and stage beneath closest tire tread.Place the rails on the correct side of vehicle with short at front, longer at rear.Prop the rails on to the jack stand as close to the height required to move in to place, and as close to the vehicle as possible.Place the 5\8th socket on to a 4" or more extension and place 1 nut on to the socket.Move the back end in to place first, and look up in to the rail hole to see if aligned with bolts.LIFT AND HOLD whilst putting the socket up in to the hole on the rail and hand thread until nut is secured. Do this for the second nut.Move to the front of the vehicle and repeat by inspecting the hole\bolt alignment and placing nut in to socket - LIFT AND HOLD, hand thread. If there is an alignment issue, use the floor jack to push the rail UP in to place, do not block the mount holes you need with the floor jack.Tighten the nuts at the front all the way since you will be at the front anyway, then tighten the back all the way. I found no torque specifications but common sense and "pretty danged tight" should be fine. If still in doubt consult Captain Morgan.I'll say this, the packaging for these rails is great, and even though the box mine came in looked gouged it wasn't a problem, there is more cardboard protection underneath.The date on mine was 9-2013 and I had no issues, just used the floor jack to push up where tight and was pretty easy.The powder coating is decent, the welds look good and the only stickers that were on there was a QA and a tiny gold "MADE IN CHINA". There are additional SMITTYBUILT yellow stickers in a bag you can use or not.The step areas are decent size, smoother than the rest of the powder coat. I bought some rubber tread at HF to put on there.Although the product quality seems good, I knocked off a point for the sheer LAMENESS of those instructions and terrible pics.

Bought this oil for an oil change in a VW TDI. It meets or exceeds VW 507.00 specification and does it for less money than many imported brands shipped to your door. I bought this in conjunction with a Mann filter and a set of drain plugs and comes in $10.00 cheaper than anywhere else.Mobil 1 105856-CASE M 5W-40 ESP Formula Motor Oil - 1 Quart, (Pack of 6)

Since the first SAE number refers to cold viscosity ("W"inter), it meets the VW spec on cold viscosity same as the ESP 5W-30 (VW certified oil).  The second number refers to hot viscosity tested at 210F/100C degrees.  Unfortunately, the SAE standard itself is not precise due to the variance range it allows.  While other brands may have significant variance from 30 to 40, these two products do not.  Mobile 1 data says the 30 has a low sheer viscosity of 12.1 cSt, while the 40 has 13.4 cSt (11% difference).  In my opinion, the 30 is actually worse for the engine and this is why: The newer HTHS (High Temperature High Sheer) test is performed at 302F/150C degrees.  Turbocharged engines in their high stress/pressure areas can approach these temperatures.  The 30 tested at 3.58 mPa*s and the 40 at 3.8 mPa*s (a higher number equals better engine wear protection).  The trade off is that it slightly lowers fuel efficiency and this is why most manufacturers are lowering their viscosity recommendations.  They have government agencies pressuring them to increase fuel efficiency but we the owners are losing engine longevity similar to what ethanol is doing.  If this oil was harmful to common rail diesels, Mercedes would not be recommending it.  Instead, Mercedes is putting its customer's engine longevity before minor mpg gains (basically telling the EPA to take a hike).
summary: Ok For 2009~2013 Expired Warranty VW TDIs
