reviewText: I had to use the ADP adapter to install it on my MDX.  Getting it all the way on was quite a trick because there was not quite enough room to rotate easily.  I did eventually manage to get it fully seated.  Now that it is on I love it.  Very easy to use and the tube makes the clean up a snap without any mess.I would certainly buy it again.

I put a full skid plate on the Wrangler and couldn't see dealing with a drain plug and oil dripping and running all over the thing, so this seemed like a good investment. I got the valve with the nipple, intending to attach a hose to direct the drainage. Should be squeaky clean!Can't imagine getting by without it.

It's a good quality valve, and the other reviewer is correct that it takes longer to drain. But oh so much better than handling that hot drain plug, dropping it in the oil pan, getting the drain oil running down your arm - - well, you know the drill....BUT WATCH OUT!! the valve is actually too easy to open.... running over some brush or twigs could easily slap the lever to the open position and it will stay there and not spring back --  then you'd better be watching your pressure gage and carrying 4 quarts of spare oil (yeah, right).  I got a small steel hose clamp and put it on the boss of the valve just above the lever (upper part of the valve in the photo). With the hose clamp snugged down and tightened up, it is absolutely impossible to open this valve. Yes, it's one more (small) step to loosen the hose clamp in order to drain the oil, but I think it's well worth the safety precaution.Would have been 5 stars except for this frailty.

I just picked this up for the second car I've installed one on. Sure, oil changes aren't the most difficult thing to do, by any means - but these seriously help. I don't end up getting oil on half of my hand, and dropping my drain plug into the oil tray anymore, which is nice. Just watch your arms, keep them out of the way, and turn the valve. Drain away. No more needing to replace crush washers, etc, as it never gets removed from the car.The valve itself is all solid brass - so I highly doubt these will wear out very quickly. I can imagine that, over 10+ years, perhaps these will leak, but they've done some pretty solid testing, and I doubt that will happen while I own the vehicle.To recap - Solid, clean, saves me 5 minutes when I do an oil change. (not to mention, it's MUCH easier to collect samples for an oil analysis!)If your vehicle is compatible, definitely get one, you won't regret it.

Installed on a 2012 Ram 1500. Very solid valve.  Tired of grabbing a hot oil plug. Last time I changed my oil I dropped the plug in the pan and it rolled into the drain hole of the pan and it almost overflowed. I was convinced I didn't need this valve until that happened. I used a zip strip for a safety latch that may or may not be needed. I also used a 3/8" rubber vacuum plug to keep the tip clean. Some 3/8" plastic tubing from HD and a gas can and I'm set for my next oil change. This valve will make oil samples and changes a snap. The valve does not protrude below the frame. I'm not an offroad guy but a simple spring hose clip or zip strip on the lever for a little added security is nice. I read the few negatives on this valve and don't believe them. If you are hitting enough stuff on the bottom of a truck to worry about this valve you may want to consider a thicker walled oil pan. Slow draining is not a problem for hot oil. I never change cold oil. I'm happy with this so far.
summary: Makes for a much cleaner oil change.

reviewText: First off note that this will not fit the truck model equipped with the plastic oil pan, that has the large yellow quarter turn release oil drain plug.  This fits the trucks with the redesigned metal oil pan and removable bolt for draining the oil.When you remove the OEM oil pan bolt you will experience a rush of oil as 13 quarts of oil pours out.  With the Fumoto you have a more controllable flow as it is choked down into a smaller stream of oil.  It can also be flipped back to the closed position if you need to stop the flow of oil.  This model comes with a extended nipple, which allows for a hose to be attached for directing the flow of oil where you want it to go such as into an empty oil jug for the ease of recycling with no mess clean up.
summary: Oil drain valve for the 2013 Ford 6.7 PSD

reviewText: Wow, I need this for all my vehicles.  I have it on my Dodge Durango and it went on easy and draining oil is now mess free.  Has been on for 15Kmiles and not leaks.  I would recomend this to anyone.

this piece is VERY easy to install, just like re-installing a regular oil drain plug (make sure you don't over-torque & strip the threads) then simply buy a few feet of 3/8 ID tubing and drain straight into an empty bottle. The valve has a lock on it so you'll never have to worry about the valve opening up on its own, and is extremely durable.

this is a very well made product, aircraft quality.... spring detent with notch then 1/4 turnthe notch is not deep, so I suppose it's possible for a well placed piece of debris to get kicked up perfectly and depress and turn it slightly to open it....  but honestly I think it would be lotto odds.... I've never seen someone report a failure, and anyone on the internet who did, I would be sceptical of....I've seen the hoseclamp thing to prevent the valve from turning, and while inventive, it seems to take the time savings of this product and throw it out the window...  so I did without.after a couple of months, it has not dripped a single drop (I park indoors with a mat under the car)the adapter is required without a doubt for all indented plugs and with it's washers, it gives you more flexibility as to direction to place the valve with varying tightness...it does drain much slower... think about 10 minutes for a complete drain as opposed to 2 by pulling the plug outright.... but no big deal as you are changing the filter and looking around checking stuff anyway.great product, enjoy!

This is exactly what I thought/hoped it would be... a beautifully engineered ball valve drain plug to make changing the oil in my car easy. I got the valve with the nipple because I wanted to be able to direct the draining oil right into the plastic gallon milk jug or washer fluid bottle so I can take it to be recycled. This way I don't even have to drain the oil into a drain pan first, then transfer to another container. I can just attach a short piece of 3/8" ID tubing to the valve and drain it directly into the container. If the container is getting full, I can just shut-off the valve, switch containers, and continue. No mess, not even a drop.

I learned about this from work, we are a meguires dealer and found out how much dirt there is after washing your car and how much of the junk can come out with your wash mit and damage your finish. This devise pretty much gets rid of that problem and nothing gets to the bottom of the bucket besides the grit. If your a DIY kinda person this is a hands down must have item !!
summary: must have for real car buffs

reviewText: This item is well made and works as advertised.  It sits in the bottom of your bucket so dirt stays in that area and doesn't get on your brush or sponges.  I use a large handled brush so the brush sits higher now in the bucket and tends to be less balanced.  Not a deal breaker since the item keeps dirt off my car from scratching the finish so that is more important.

I was never really concerned with how I washed my cars until I bought a modern musclecar with a sensitive black finish. This grit guard does the same job as others that cost more, it keeps that dirt out of your wash water when using the two bucket method.

reviewerName: Lust4STi "Stuff sold by the gram is always mo...
reviewText: This is a great product and works as it should. I can't stand swirls in my paint and this is another ingenious product to help prevent them. I should have bought one of these years ago!
summary: Great product for car wash lovers

reviewText: This baby fits right in your 5-gallon bucket and keeps the soapy water separate from the dirt and loose sediments that would scratch your car should you reach in with your towel and bring out grit and spread it all over your paint job.  Great item to have, wish I would have know this existed a long time ago.

Every time I wash the truck, there's the grit at the bottom under the guard. Works good, just need to have the correct size bucket as indicated.  Also, consider using the two bucket method - one bucket for clean soapy water, one for rinsing the mitt/sponge after working an area of the car.  the grit/grime can be rinsed off in the second bucket, then redunk in the clean water and repeat.
Well made and a good value.  We bought several of these, one for each bucket, and they keep the wash mitts and rags MUCH cleaner than before.  I'd buy them again.
summary: Well made and a good value

reviewText: says it fits the 12" buckets but I got a 3.5 gallon and it barely makes it halfway... so if you're getting this make sure to measure at the bottom of your bucket for the diameter of this which is 10 point something? to be sure it fits.  it does it's job though to get rid of grit on my car wash pad

If you want a high foam car wash, look no place else.  This is a great price, and if you're just washing the one or two cars you own this should last a while.  I pair this with a foam blaster, you can buy the g-clean foam blaster here on Amazon for about $20, you can see my review on that there.  You can hardly see the car if you do it right, I normally mix 4oz soap and 4oz water and that's enough to wash the entire car.  So at only 4oz a wash, this should last a while.
I've tried many car wash soaps over the years. This stuff rocks!! The wax on my car is over 4 months old now and the wash still gives it that nice luster.
summary: Great product to keep the luster of your paint.

reviewText: it clenas very well using the gilmoure foam gun, nice suds, better then other shampoos, but it leaves still soap spotes on paint, but much less than other products, and leaves the car with a nice shine, may be what i need is a pressure washer , maybe then the results will be even better with zero water or soap spots, but at the end its an excellent product, compared to other car shampoos, and i will keep using it in the future.
This car wash is the best I have ever used, really suds up and cleans very well you will like the smell of the wash.recommend this product.

I use this with a foam gun attachment to my garden hose.  Lots of suds.  i recently switched to using a foam gun with Chemical Guys Maxi Suds II and have had really good results washing my car.  The thick foam lifts dirt off the surface of your paint, minimizing risk of little particles making swirl marks on your paint.Make sure you rinse REALLY well however. I've noticed this soap leaves a little more residue than other soaps I've used in the past.
summary: Thick foam.  Leaves a bit more residue but shouldn't be an issue.

reviewText: Not only this soap cleans better than other name brands such as Gold Class Wash Soap, when paired with foam lance and a gas pressure washer, will wow your neighbors with all the suds you leave on your vehicle.  You need to get the correct ratio of water and soap for thick suds.  Besides the visual effect, Chemical Guys soap cleans better than competitors.

Yeah! we'r in business now, you see how a small amount of this shampoo in a foam gun can actually clean my T-Rex Ford expedition, my car is big and this Shampoo does the job nicely, no more car wash shops, I have everything handy.I have ordered the Mr. Pink, I want to try it, can't wait to see the results!
summary: Oooh man this is my baby

reviewText: I purchased this to try something new, and I wasnt disappointed. Has a wonderful aroma, soapy, and foams great with my foam gun. I will continue to use Chemical Guys Maxi Suds, My wife even enjoys when I use it on her car, doesnt just run like other products. Great buy..
summary: Foams nice, and soapy.. SMELLS great.

reviewText: This stuff works great on my car.  It smells good and my car is Clean after using it. Road grime and bird poop are no match for this product

This is AWESOME STUFF!!!  This was MUCH cheaper than buying brand G***t and the job it does is phenomenal!!  Used with the Gilmour 75QGFMR Foamaster Adjustable Multi Ratio Cleaning Gun, this makes a great combo and smells great!

Bought this in conjunction with the Chemical Guys foam blaster 6 foam gun. I don't know how some people say this can would last them a year- It ain't going to last me 6 months. This stuff suds well in the bucket but not so well in the foam gun which surprised me. The smell is OK and the red does stain my car wash brush so I have to hose it down a bit more to get the red out.
summary: Just OK. Doesn't foam too good in a foam gun.

reviewText: This is my first Chemical Guys product and I bought it to use with my Gilmour Foam Gun (the original Foamaster) and it works pretty well. The foam was really nice and thick for the foam gun and likewise while using it in my wash bucket. The cherry scent also adds to the experience. And you can't beat the price for the amount you get... 128 oz. (1 gallon). This will last me for quite some time.

Excellent product, ridiculous amounts of foam.  Highly concentrated.  Great value.I've used this on two car washes and I love it!  I use a small splash in a 5-gallon wash bucket, and an even smaller splash in my hose-connected foam sprayer.  Lather is thick, smell is good, and at my current use rates, I think this gallon size will last about a year.I plan to use in a pressure-washer connected foam cannon soon, which I hear is great.Can't really think of any negatives.Side note - I have no idea why Chemical Guys have so many different soaps.  This one is one of the cheapest, and I don't really know why Mr. Pink or Honeydew snowfoam would be any different/better, but who care, just use this one.
summary: Hope you are ready for bubbles

reviewText: A gallon of this should last a long time.  I use one of those foamer guns and it makes a lot of suds.  As I said a gallon will last a long time.

I detailed for 12 years and have used and loved Meguiars, Griotts garage, Mothers and all the cheap brands and professional brands i have heard of. And while this stuff doesnt necessarily shatter expectations i would say it performed as good if not better in some categories than anything else ive used.#1- It sud'sed(?) up very nicely on par with griots garage at half the price.#2- it smelled great... i know i know not a big deal but hey it does#3-The suds lasted longer without refreshing in the bucket than anything else i have used#4- i did not have to go over some spots on my white car like i did with meguiars gold class soap#5- the price is great and not much product was needed.
summary: One of the best i have used

reviewText: I use this with the Gilmore 75QGFMR (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000XTH1GY/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_5) Foamaster Adjustable cleaning gun.  The two together make fast work of washing our RV without the need for a bucket, and without risk of dipping a sponge or brush into dirty bucket water.  If you own an RV, you need to consider these two items!!  Foam on the soap top to bottom, use a soft bristle brush or sponge on a stick to wash top to bottom, rinse, and squidgy or dry with your choice of implement/towel.  I can get the whole coach done in about an hour if I want a quicky wash.. 2 hours if I do windows and wheels and touch-ups..
Makes nice bubbles, but not bad ones, and it washes the grime off fine.  I think it's a good product.
summary: Just washed both of our cars with this.

reviewText: This is the best car soap I've ever use, it gently removes the dirt from the paint without causing swirls.I'm sold on this product.I had suds all the way down my driveway after I was done washing.Amazing product.

I have nothing bad to say about this product.  It mixes really well with water and does not leave any residue on your car when used properly.  I use this detergent along with a foam master and it produces a ton of soapy foam!!!

I don't let my car get in bad shape and usually wash it every week or two and coat it every wash with Optimum Instant Detailer (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0015DIJ4A/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_img_sol_14), so I cannot speak to the cleaning ability of this shampoo.  It is pH-balanced, produces lots of foam in my Gilmour foam gun, and provides plenty of lubricity to allow my cleaning mitt to easily flow over the paint without swirls or scratches.  As I am starting to get low on the Maxi-Suds II, I ordered some samples of Chemical Guys Mr Pink and Chemical Guys Glossworkz Auto Wash for comparison.

This is a super plush wash mitt that is my current best pick for microfiber wash mitts. Highly recommended over cheaper micro fiber wash mitts as this will help reduce time spent washing and correcting paint vs saving a buck or two on price with others. Trust me when I say this, don't buy the other microfiber wash mitts on Amazon that are .50-2.00 cheaper because they are not the same! I have spent a lot of time detailing my cars and motorcycles along with lots of research regarding methods to improve my technique and have used lots of different kinds of wash mitts, but this is the best bang for your buck! There are currently 14 wash mitts/sponges in my garage ranging from this brand new chenille microfiber wash mitt to old nappy lambswool mitts, a wash sponge to everything in between. Some came from Autozone, K-Mart, and even some from other online retailers, but this is definitely the best you can get for scratch free washing of your clear coat finishes (with proper 2 bucket technique of course!). Buy this one for keeping your clear coat clean and use your old wash mitt for cleaning your wheels, exhaust, and other areas where light scratches are less of a concern!
summary: Hands down the best wash mitt for the money!

reviewText: Makes washing your car easy.  It is also easy to keep clean.  Just rinse and dry.  I wouldn't use with your hand in the mitt, I would just use it like a regular wash sponge.

I bought two of these and they are as good as there is available. However, there are other mitts just as good (maybe even the same mitt) for close to half price of this one. Not complaining, just trying to be helpful. I have no regrets on purchasing the Chemical Guys mitt, but, if you search around at your brick and mortar stores, you can find the same for less.\However, don't think for a second that the ones you buy on eBay from China are the same....... they're not worth the time of day IMHO. They're tiny, hold very little suds, and just don't have much of a purpose unless you have a little one who just "has" to help wash the car...... :)

Good job catching dirt and glide thru paint surface quicker than an average dollar store sponge. Problem is it keep slipping of my arm wrist so I ended up using it like a sponge, held it on my and and rubbed.to all small arm wirsts, BEWARE!
summary: Good but not Good for small arm wrist

reviewText: Can't believe how easy my job just became in washing my Dinosaur (Ford expedition) after I got this product.I am going to order a big amount of stuff from chemical guys,.Hey Chemical guys, keep up the great work. I like your products
summary: This is absolutely the best product - Look no Further !!!

reviewText: This is a better quality mitt than you find at the auto parts store.  Very soft and seems pretty durable.  I've used it for about eight washes so far and then washed it in the washing machine inside out after each wash, and it still looks new.  I haven't noticed any scratches or swirls, but you do have to keep an eye on the mitt as you wash to make sure you don't get debris trapped in the fabric.

This thing holds TONS of suds! It's much thicker than I had originally expected (obviously, being that it'd dual sided). This gives it the great advantage of being able to hold onto more water and soap, giving it greater ability to dislodge gunk on your finish and gently whisk it away. I'm OCD about how my car is washed (I won't let the dealership touch it) and I love this thing! I've had nothing but great results, time after time. Follow the two-bucket wash method and you'll be amazed as well!
summary: For the OCD Car Freak in Everyone

reviewText: I like the idea, but when it is saturated with water and soap, it gets heavy to a point where the insides pop out.  Hard to explain, but I won't be buying this one again as a wash mit....maybe a buffer or something on glass.

Holds suds like crazy and easily picked up stains that I thought might be too stubborn for it.  Easy to clean as well; wrung out what I could,  flooded it from the inside with clean water, wrung it out again and now it's air drying over a broom handle.

This mitt is so fluffy and soft it will not scratch your paint! It has a lining inside which doesnt make it easy to flip while its on your hand so I used it as sponge more than a mitt.It came with a few loose threads (that would keep pulling) and that was annoying so I docked it 1 star.

This thing holds GOBS of suds and water. It's actually *heavy*, so if you don't have a good washing arm, you'll have to ring this thing out a bit when you take it out the bucket. But that means this thing is going to keep you from going back and forth to the wash bucket a dozen times while doing a wash.It's soft and glides over surfaces smoothely. I used this on a black car and it left no swirls.Always use a quality soap. I use Chemical Guys products exclusively - all of their soaps are wonderful.This is microfiber. So treat it like you would a microfiber towel - always rinse it out, and only use a good dedicated microfiber detergent. Once again, Chemical Guys microfiber detergent comes to mind. I love that stuff.

I bought this as a substitute for a lambswool mitt, but this wash mitt is too large, and it's very heavy and clumsy when wet. There's an inner lining that prevents spinning the mitt on your hand to expose the unused side, because this inner lining clings to your hand.Also, the microfiber "fingers" can easilty catch on car trim.I won't be using this again to wash my car.
summary: Too Big and Heavy, Hard To Use For Washing Car

reviewText: I've tried a dozen different mits, and have always come back to these. They just flat out work great. If you rinse them properly, you never get the "OMG - I just scrathed the H out of my paint!!!!" Feeling, which is always dreaded.

After much debate, I ordered this, as I like to leave my tires/undercarriage until last.None of the stuff I have used in the past has been able to dwell on the rim until the end.This clings to it without compromising clear coated rim. My Murano dumps brake dust badly. I do recommend to agitiate with a proper wheel brush.The smell, while pleasant, can be a bit overwhelming.Will probably try their Signature series wheel cleaner next at this link:Chemical Guys (CLD_203) Signature Series Blue Wheel Cleaner - 1 Gallon

Spray, let it sit about 10 minutes and hit the wheels with your cloth/brush/pad of choice. I used a well-worn Scotch-Brite sponge and worked great for removing the years' worth of brake dust on a Saturn Ion (previous owner was detail-challenged).Still needed the elbow grease, but not much. Using 1 part cleaner to 3 parts water it still sprays as a semi-gel; this should last awhile (I only used 1/3 of a spray bottle diluted). Good stuff.

A lot of wheel cleaners I have used in the past always seem to have a strong chemical smell that can get nauseating. I love using diablo, my rims are 15 years old and this product brings them back to new. If your serious about your wheels first buy this but then invest into some great wheel brushes and even a lug nut brush to keep them like new. It really works well at repelling brake dust but if you have some beautiful rims and recommend to follow up with the Chemical Guys wheel guard. it does wonders at keeping wheels clean and shiny and when your next wash come around the particles just come right off and nothing really sticks like it would on an untreated wheel. KEEP IT UP CG!
summary: Works GREAT and like all other CG products it smells awesome

reviewText: I purchased these for my new rims and did not like it at first.Apparently I don't understand dilution ratings for the gel and didn't use enough with water.Highly recommend getting the Chemical Guys spray bottles that have the ratios and are very durable.This stuff really works and requires very little work especially with the Daytona speed master
I bought this stuff and it didn't clean anything off my chrome rims.  Worthless crap.  wouldn't mind getting my money back for this red bottle of goop.
summary: cheap rim cleaner from walmart works better than this crap

reviewText: This is a very good product. I've used Meguiars and Mothers wheel cleaners, and this one works the best by far. Previous product have a lot of trouble getting the dirt and grime from around the nuts. The Diablo gel works really well and takes the most dirt out compared to any other product I've used.I put this in a spray bottle, and it works great. It cleans well and leaves a really nice shine.

I have a closet full of detailing products and I'm always willing to try something new. After having some very positive results with other Chemical guys products I ordered the Diablo Gel. It's good if you don't want to spend a lot of money. This makes about a gallon of product at a quarter of the price of Griot's Heavy Duty Wheel cleaner. That being said, I think Griot's is that much better. The diablo is fine for my weekend car which doesn't produce a lot of brake dust. My daily driver is a Carrera S4 which makes a lot of brake dust, so I need the Griot's. If your wheels don't need a harsher wheel cleaner and a lot of elbow grease, buy the Diablo Gel and save some money.
I used scrubbing bubble and baking soda and an eighteen volt drill. It took me fifteen minutes to remove grime that I was not able to remove manually even after hours of scrubbing.

Bought based on the great reviews.  After having a Meguiar's pad denigrate on the drill, I was skeptical.This saved a pair of 12 year old heavily used floormats, had amazing results on my plastic weathertech liners, Made the trunk floor look like new, and along with SpotShot worked magic on white residential berber carpet.  All in a day's work.The bristles are just rigid enough to hold up well, but still soft enough to not damage most surfaces.I used myMakita LXT211 18-Volt LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless 2-Piece Combo Kitand it just went to work.  You could see instant results, especially on the floor mats where the dirt was visibly ejected as the brush spun the carpet back to life.This fits in a standard chuck and holds tight even with tough use.  After a couple weeks of heavy use, it looks a little worn but still plenty of life left in it.Would definitely recommend.
summary: Indispensible for tons of Cleaning Projects

reviewText: I only paid $12 for my item and it was the best deal I've ever gotten. When attached to a high power drill this thing is awesome and takes all the effort out of cleaning carpets.

If you detail your own car all the time this is a must have i only use it on carpets but imagine it would clean up anything well for carpets this is the coolest thing invented I swear i can't tell you how many times i've cut my hands scrubbing by hand on seatrails and such this thing makes the job go quick and easy
Very solid.  Looks like it will last a long time.  Bristles are tough and scrub well, without too much risk of scratching surfaces as you would with a wire brush.

Had really bad stains in my trucks carpet.  It did a great job of making the job easier and lifting out the dirt.  Probably need to be sure you have a shop-vac.  I do and can't imagine not having one as part of this cleaning process.
summary: Did a number of those spots

reviewText: Great drill attachment. I used this on the bathtub and tile surround and it does a great job of cleaning. I put some water and soft scrub on it and go to town. Would recommend to anyone looking to a tile scrubber. Keep in mind that it is quite big. Took me by surprise.

Great little tool, wish I had one sooner!  So far I've used to clean tires and tried it on the bathtub and worked great.  I could say many uses for this tool!  Make sure you get the correct bristle stiffness for the job you are doing.  This one is medium duty, and probably better suited for carpets, bathroom, and other surfaces that won't tear it up too much.  While it did work for tires, the bristles on the yellow one a tad too soft for that.  High quality construction and the part that fits in the chuck is hexagonal so it allows to apply as much torque as your drill can put out without slipping in the chuck.

Not good for cleaning tubs. I believe the description said it would work on tubs/bathrooms. This took a lot of elbow grease to do anything. I ended up using theDico 541-786-21/2 Nyalox Cup Brush 21/2-Inch Blue 240 Grit which worked great.

Mounted on a hand drill, Chemical Guys ACC-201 medium duty brush, with medium stiff, yellow, 0.9" high bristles, is very good tool for general cleaning.  The bristles are firmly seated into the hard plastic circular base, and won't easily be dislodged by pressure being applied to the brush.  The medium stiff polypropylene bristles will bend, rather than break, so it should work reasonably well on most carpets.  If you have a reversible drill, you might want to change directions periodically, to avoid having the bristles bent over too far to one side.The shaft is hexagonal, to provide a secure grip in the drill chuck, and provide a good amount of torque.  You can apply a good amount of pressure to this brush, which makes it very good for harder surfaces like sink, tile, granite, wood panels, and concrete.  Scratching shouldn't be an issue on these harder surfaces, but you should exercise care on softer materials.  The bristles aren't metal, so they will wear down, but under normal use, this brush should have a decent usable life.There are some more expensive drill mounted brushes, which makes the Chemical Guys brush a good value buy.  The price fluctuates, so if you do a lot of cleaning, you might want stock up when the price dips.
summary: great circular brush for general cleaning...

reviewText: This is excellent for car interiors! Great for scrubbing carpets.First wet the carpet with water/cleaner/GP, let it soak then come in with this bad boy and it will clean anything.Awesome for seats too! Just make sure you have the soft or medium one if you use it on your seats.This is also excellent in the bathroom, getting soap scum off the shower, cleaning floors in bathroom and more.Lot's of uses! A+ stuff!
summary: Hands down best brush scrubber available!

reviewText: It cuts up surprisingly easy, and you can stick it about anywhere.  But just remember this stuff works through it's density - and it's dense.  Very heavy.  On my big Mercedes, it doesn't really matter as the suspension is hydraulic and adjusts itself anyway.  But for lighter cars you may notice it if you use 5-6 rolls of it.As far as efficiency - boy does this stuff work!  It makes those long trips as easy as sitting in your living room easy chair - literally.  Noise/vib takes a very heavy toll on your energy, and will affect your mood, exhaustion etc.  Get the most dense you think you can get away with.  It can be a pain to put in, but you'll be glad you did.Everything you've heard about the bass from your speakers is true.  This stuff absorbs so much hi pitch sound that the bass just blasts through.  Most people are amazed by this when they hear it.  Frankly I could care less but it is a nice little side affect

If you are anticipating  whether or not to buy this you better think again! Amazing product for any vehicle! Put it in a single cab 4x4 ranger and it was plenty enough to do the floors, rear wall, all of the doors. This product made it so quiet I couldn't even hear the engine running. Even driving I could barely hear the little v6 humming. That alone did it for me! The tar smell is the only reason its not getting 5 stars. Yes it goes away but lingers for the first week or so. Great Product!!!!!

My wife's 06 Kia Sportage has a very growly engine.  I never considered it that bad, but it bothered her.  I lined under the hood and some areas around the engine.  It quieted the bit of engine "growl" just enough that it no longer bothers her.Here is why I say another star would be possible for this product.  These cheap auto's have a lot of cheap plastics for wind control under the front bumper.  Ours had a lot of cracked pieces but no way to bond them back together.  This stuff is SO adhesive that I was able to get everything back together by lining the insides of all of these pieces and then mount back on the car.  I've never found a product that has more uses than noise control in my life.  If the adhesive holds up well to the elements, all the better.  Brilliant product for people who don't want to pay out the leg to a dealership, or wish to fix subtle sound issues on their own.
summary: It deserves 6 stars and I'll tell you why.

reviewText: I put this FatMat sound deadener under the front half of our 30-foot RV. I would have kept going but that's as far as one roll went. I cut it in short strips, raised the RV as high as I could, crawled under it and spent the morning pealing the backing off and sticking this stuff on the floor and engine housing. It's easy to stick on. The hard part was reaching around things like mufflers, drive shaft, etc. The dirt has to be wiped off so the FatMat will stick.I took the RV for a short spin after installing it. It's amazing how quiet it is inside now. And I mean amazing. No road noise at all. I was hoping for a little bit of improvement but all I can say is WOW! Money well spent. I'm now thinking where else I can put this stuff.

This comes with a roller and a cutting blade. The roller is low-quality so I recommend getting something more durable if you're going to install a lot of this, but the knife will serve you very well.  The cost per square foot of this product is absolutely fantastic and it works every bit as well as more expensive products.While I installed in mid-70 degree (F) weather, I advocate the use of a heat gun with a roller to ensure the most uniform adhesion -- especially if doing the roof of a vehicle.  Expect a bit of a synthetic, 'new car' type smell for 2-3 weeks after the installation, simply due to the composition of the product.I gave it 4 stars.  It'd get 5 stars from me if it were completely odorless.
summary: Works great at a fantastic price...

reviewText: I thought Liquimoly was sold as Lubromoly in north America. reviewText: Good for "start-stop" engines like the Prius.When the engine is stopped, the oil pump is not running.  Eventually the oil drains off of the piston rings and other mechanical parts.Molybdenum disulfide or MoS2 has been well known for its lubrication abilities.  It is retained on the metal parts even when the oil drains down from the engine parts.Here is where this product prevents engine wear.  I'm not worried or expect mileage gain.
summary: Great protection for "start-stop" technology engines like on the Prius, BMW, Mercedes and others.

reviewText: There are only two proven friction modifiers on the market, with a third (ceramic) on the horizon.  The first one is ZDDP which might be the best but you should NOT use it on modern vehicles that use a catalytic convertor as it will harm it!  The other proven friction modifier is molybdenum, and this product is full of Moly.  The difference between Moly and ZDDP is that Moly HAS NO DOWNSIDE!  Except for idiots who get it on their shirt.  It is a product that is already in most oils.Now there are many other products out there, solvents, PTFE (Teflon) slick 50, detergents like Prolong, but all of these products have risk that is unnecessary to take. My first advice is too just run a high quality synthetic oil and nothing else is needed.  However, if you are someone who feels better adding something to your oil this is the only product I recommend with the exception of MMO.  Marvel Mystery Oil also has some lubricating qualities and a naphthenic solvent that is harmless.  I use Lubro Moly on my new cars for breaking in, and in my Toyotas as they have sludge issues and this stuff really smooths out those rough engines.To give this product a bad review is to not understand engine dynamics and oil products in general.  It would be like saying the slick stuff in oil itself is bad for your engine.  Listen people that is just not the case.  There are no miracle products out there but this one is beneficial to all engines!!!  Run it in your lawn mower and you will be amazed at the lack of smoke at start up!Have a Good Day

I've used this LM Mos2 in numerous vehicles; including an '07 F150, '03 Corolla, '70 F100, '07 Mustang, '97 Civic, '98 Escort and many more. It still always surprises me that all cars i've added it to run smoother and quieter.The stuff isn't snake oil either, it's just Molybdenum Disulphide. Most oils that use Moly, utilize an organic form of Moly. These types reduce friction but don't seem to make the engines run smoother/quieter as does the Mos2.Well worth the money.
summary: Best oil additive I've used, great value

reviewText: I used this in my ford crown vicroria 97, and the difference is most definitely noticeable. The engine runs so smooth, sometimes I forget the engine is running. This stuff simply makes the engine a tank.

I added the entire can to my BMW M50 engine along with my scheduled oil change. I am currently a little over 100 miles on my new oil and there is already a considerable difference in my engine's response and feel.Just to clarify, my engine was performing quiet well before adding this product. This additive will not turn a neglected engine into a factory fresh engine. If you are expecting this, save your money for a rebuild instead.So far I've noticed my engine is quieter, smoother, has less vibrations at idle, and has a slight increase in MPG, according to my car's on board computer. On top of those perks the additive also reduces wear and tear on crucial engine components.I'm looking forward to the next thousand miles as the product sets in and will be including it in my scheduled oil changes from now on. To clarify, the additive needs to be added during each oil change for continued results. I will likely had half a can next time for my particular engine. You need to add 50ml for every quart of oil in your engine according to the instructions on the can. However, some are claiming to add half the amount after the first treatment.I would strongly recommend giving this additive a chance if you want to thoroughly protect and get the most performance from your engine. I also plan on using the Liqui Moly line of products as this particular product has exceeded my expectations.

reviewText: It is nice that it meters out 1oz of product per pump, this makes it easy to use soaps and such that have a fairly specific dilution ratio. Citrus Wash & Gloss or Mr. Pink, either/or - doesn't matter.My only complaints on these pumps are that if you tilt the gallon jug over, product will leak. Also when you are done pumping, a little more will dribble out. The way to combat this is to tilt the container over to drain the top portion of the pump, and voila - no more drips. Either way, you'll be best to hit the end with a rag and probably not let it drip down on expensive stuff. Like your buffer/polisher.Unfortunately, trying to find gallon pumps anywhere is like a needle in a haystack and the options are limited here. Small variety and this is probably the only worthwhile pump on Amazon. At over $8 a piece they are also kind of expensive.But hey - would you rather fight a funnel and a heavy jug when you want some chemical?So a cool thing about these is that they screw down into place. So make sure you have that rag ready... but it's nice because my garage shelving is *JUST* a tad too short to accommodate the Chemical Guys gallon containers and this pump extended. About me:  I run my own automotive detailing business and have cleaned and detailed vehicles for over 10 years.  For the record, I am a big time Meguiars loyalist and use their products almost exclusively.  However, I was getting tired of spending $20+ dollars for the 200gram clay bar in their professional detailing line up and furthermore, I was tired of spending $17+ on the consumer lineup bars for either the Meguiars or the Mothers that come with the detailing spray to use as lubrication.  I don't need the detailing spray bottles about 90% of the time as I rarely use them since I favor buying the professional lineup bottles in bulk as they are more economical.About the clay:  This is by far my favorite clay of choice.  Not even because it's cheaper, if it was more I would still probably buy it.  Maybe I shouldn't have said that in case the manufacturer is reading their amazon reviews.  Here's why:  The clay is always more firm.  The mothers and meguiars brand clay (aside from Meguiars professional) is always smushy, soft and very flexible.  So flexible that it becomes a pain to use seeing as paint contamination removal works in large part by friction and that friction relies on pressure.  The consumer line up of Meguiars and Mothers literally squeezes out of the sides of your hands with minimal pressure applied.  This brand stays rigid and allows you to apply more uniform pressure to the surface thus taking down the contamination quicker.This clay will NOT harm the surface of your vehicle much like the other brands that I have used UNLESS, used improperly with too little lubricant.  Make sure you give your vehicle a complete and thorough wash prior to using any clay bar on your vehicle.  If you drop the clay, THROW IT OUT.  Do NOT think you can salvage some of it.  I always start with the body panels that have the least amount of contamination on them FIRST and the heaviest contaminated surfaces I save for LAST, just like you should during a wash.  If you are not sure run your hand over the entire surface with a plastic bag on your hand and you will be able to feel what's what.  Try this test again when you think you are finished.  When finished, your vehicle will most likely be free of harmful contaminants and as smooth as silk.  I always clay vehicles prior to buffing and always follow up buffing with a good machine applied/hand removed waxing.Packaging:  Could be better as it arrives in a plastic bag that tends to stick to the clay and is taped shut making opening a pain.  Should package it in a container.  (I know this part doesn't fit into the review portion to some, but I figured it'd be worth mentioning). It doesn't effect my review by any means, obviously, as I rated this product it's deserving rating of 5 stars.Final notes:  If you are only claying a vehicle every so often it might be worth your time to pick up the Meguiars or Mothers kit.  They even sell them at wally world, usually cheaper than your auto parts stores.  Reason being is, it comes with the detailing spray/lubricant and a microfiber towel.  But, if you clay often and want IMO the best clay bar for the buck then I highly recommend going this route instead.Make sure to use plenty of lubricant.  I beg to differ with some of the reviewers comments about usage such as "wash one panel with soapy water at a time"... Why one panel at a time? Why not wash the entire vehicle at once first, from top to bottom?  Why "soapy water"?  We should be using automotive car shampoo.  "You can use one bar on a grimy vehicle several times over"... Personally I wouldn't encourage this process. If someone has a severely contaminated vehicle and they use this bar it should go in the trash after usage, in my opinion.  +1 to the make sure you fold/turn/flatten comments often during usage.  Spray a little detail spray on your windshield or rear window and press the bar flat into it with moderate pressure. Manipulate/stretch the bar a little when necessary.

reviewText: I used a bucket of distilled water instead of the clay lube. As long as the clay is kept wet it works great, but don't run out of water it will stick to your paint. It takes a lot of elbow grease to get the rail dust (rusty looking spots) off of a white car.

But after reading the negative reviews about this product saying it scuffs paint and leaves residue and then feeling the difference in my hands, I'm really inclined not to use this product at all. My car has been pretty much repainted because of past accidents and road debris hitting my car. I think the only original paint on my car is what's on the roof. I keep my car in immaculate condition as much as I can, so I can't say I'll take the risk with this clay bar. It may be better to use the package deal clay bars that you can find in Mothers and Meguiars. Those are both great clay bar kits.I sent the clay back and got a full refund including shipping. It definitely wasn't worth risking damaging the paint. I had a new clay bar left over from the Mothers kit and I must say, BIG difference. A lot of people think it's all a gimmick, but I could really tell the difference. Plus the Mothers clay bar kit is not that much at all considering what you get. At least I can say I tried this product and can have an opinion to share. I'll stick with what I know works.

reviewText: So, for $30, I wasn't expecting the jack to end all jacks.  This one is actually pretty good.  It goes up quick, has a nice little rotatable thing on the jack point that lets you encapsulate those little jack points on your car perfectly, and it definitely gets the car off the ground for several hours just fine.One of the problems is the release mechanism is too touchy - I've accidentally turned it too fast at least 3 times now, and the car has basically fallen to the ground.  You have to be extremely slow and methodical when releasing this jack.  Another issue that's not too big of a deal is the noise it makes when you get a bunch of weight on it - right before I get a wheel off the ground on my car, the handle gets hard to pump and eventually the jack makes a chirping sound and continues as it was.  This is weird, and makes it feel a little unsafe, but it's probably fine.  The third con is that it doesn't go high enough.  Definitely take a look at the listed height before buying and make sure 13 inches is high enough for you.

The spring makes noise and there are some interesting sounds as it loads up but it was smooth in both directions when handled smoothly and slowly as well. Go slow, on level concrete and you won't have a problem. Once raised I place a stand under it and left it just below. This made my first brake job a dream. If you plan to use this weekly or 20+ times a year then get a real jack and pop the appropriate money but for a once a month use then this is a great find!

reviewText: Thankfully I had this jack when my RV had a blowout in the rear on the highway. I was able to get my tire changed and kept on going. This is a great little jack for a heavy truck. I really do love it.

It lifts much faster and lowers way smoother. It seems like a decent quality piece of equipment and so far I'm very happy with it. It was packaged well and shipping was fast. I got this jack for my 2004 Toyota Prius.  I thought it would be fine since other reviewers said it worked under low vehicles, but it actually won't reach far enough under to touch the manufacturer's recommended jacking point in the front.  I had to use a point farther forward as recommended by someone online.  The actual height of the back of the jack is about 6.5 inches, so measure your car before you buy this one.  Why the heck no jack maker seems to list the jack body height is beyond me.This jack is about 60 lbs and is very heavy to carry around (at least to for me).  If you don't have a garage where you can roll this jack around and not have to lift it anywhere, I recommend getting a lighter one if you don't need the 3 ton capacity.  My car really only needs a 1.5 ton jack so I wish I'd gone with an aluminum model with a lower profile and a weight of around 27 lbs.  Then again, I couldn't find any 1.5 ton jacks with good reviews from lots of users, which is part of why I went with this one.With my car's low clearance I have to move the handle up and down in very short strokes so it probably takes about 40 or more up and down pumps to reach full height when jacking in the front.  The pumps aren't very difficult so the jack seems to have good leverage.  Quality seems pretty good, but I've never owned a floor jack before so it's hard to know what to look for.  I did find that after jacking it up once, the rubber pad was fairly crushed where the car's weight rested on it.  It looks like the rubber may rip through or tear after a few jackings.The manual says to put grease in between the handle and the handle socket.  I did so, but there was still a lot of paint scraped off the handle from simply turning it a few times.  Apparently the finish is low quality.  The handle itself is a little tricky to get on as you have to turn it till it matches a tab inside which allows it to slide in deeper.  It's easy to think it's deep enough and even turn it and move the jack around when it hasn't actually engaged the tab inside that closes and opens the hydraulic fluid valve when you twist the handle.One thing the manual doesn't mention is this wire partly coated in plastic that holds the back of the jack down during shipping.  The wire hooks into where the handle slides in but it can't be pulled out from that end.  On the other end it slides into a small hole under the jack.  I used a screwdriver to pry the wire out of that small hole and it almost hit me in the face as it sprang out of the jack and landed ten feet in front of me.  They really need to put instructions and a warning label about that wire, or come up with a safer method of holding the back of the jack down during shipping.

reviewText: I've used this jack several times now to raise and lower a Jeep.  It works great and holds pressure to keep the vehicle up.  Be sure to use jack stands before you get underneath the vehicle!

Great jack for the money.  Fits nicely under my sport package equipped BMWs (E46, E90) and works well with the factory jack points.  Great range and easy to lift/lower vehicle.  This is my first "nice" jack and I am happy with the purchase.

The Powerzone 3 Ton Jack is one massive hunk of jack. This thing is massive and heavy. But darn is it a nice tool.I finally decided to replace the 20 year old 2 ton Craftsman floor jack. You know the kind that was a commodity so many years ago, a short jack handle, you have to remove the handle to turn the bleed valve, it took 50 pumps to get it even a few inches off the ground, a single piston model, and, the worst of all, you had to stand on it to get it to retract. Yes, that jack, the one I struggled with the day I bought it. From my research, this jack looked like overkill, maybe not really necessary.Oh was I wrong. Oh am I sad I didn't buy this jack sooner. Yes it weighs a million pounds - 58 to be exact. Yes there are aluminum parts. No I can't imagine what this would weigh if it was all steel. Oh yes this thing is a beast. But does it lift up cars effortlessly.In the box, the handle is in two parts and removed from the jack. There is a 10mm bolt to attach the two halves of the handle. The lower end of the handle has a big thick foam rubber pad on it to protect the car finish if you get to crazy pumping the handle. The foam also makes it nice for pulling the jack around. For shipping there is a metal coat hanger that holds the jack socket down. Just pry at the bottom end of it and the handle will release. The handle socket is also full of grease.Assembly is pretty simple, and well documented in the instructions. Overall, assemble the handle, and attach it to the jack socket. It seems important to follow the initial bleeding instructions. That takes about a minute or two and simply involved pumping the handle - there is no spilled hydraulic or pump fluid.Wow does this jack lift stuff up high. The jack starts out really low to the ground, about 4 inches to the rubber saddle. The front wheels are heavy duty fixed steel that take all the weight of lifting. The rear wheels are steel casters for guiding the jack where needed. I think this jack will lift around 18 inches high. That should be more than enough lift for most car work.A twist of the handle releases the jack. It is spring loaded so it lowers slowly and all the way down.This is one amazing jack. Sure wish I'd bought it a long time ago.

Edit: I had the jack for about 3 weeks, used it to lift my friends Honda CRV, not a heavy car by any means. I was left with my jack bleeding oil all across the pavement. The jack still worked as I describe below, held the car up for lengthy amounts of time along with jack stands, and didn't fail otherwise. Amazon sent UPS the next day to pick up the jack and the new one is on its way. I'm sure it was just a manufacturer defect. I will post more later, but the 5 star rating is staying unless this happens again. 5/9/13This jack is pretty amazing. I'm just a home mechanic that does his own auto work instead of feeding money to the local shops that tend to overcharge and provide sub par work. By this, I mean some shops that do oil changes have been lazy and forgotten to tighten the drain plug, so I got home and nearly blew my engine since it was out of oil. Last time I do that for the special $20 rate.I had previously bought a Harbor Freight jack, a 2.5 ton low profile, high lift jack for around $75 with coupon, along with a set of 3 ton jack stands for $16. I used this for about a month, working on my civic and family's odyssey with little problems. It was a good jack and didn't disappoint me. It was an all steel, nearly 80 pound beast that had pretty incredible reach for a jack, along with low ground clearance at 2.75'' and lift range of 21''. The only concern I had was reliability, as seeing reviews were mixed. I decided to spend a bit more money and buy this jack.This jack is simply amazing. Even though the box says "Made in China", it seems like a good ol' USA jack at heart. It is primarily aluminum on the construction, with steel on the lift arm mechanism for strength. The weight was modest, at 58 pounds (I checked), and the two handles are good for lugging around, since jacks are otherwise awkward to carry. I checked the statistics that were presented on amazon and was pleasantly surprised. My measurements were as follows:Minimum height: 3 7/8'', less than the claimed 4'' height.Max Height: 18 1/2'', greater than the claimed 18'' height# full pumps to max: 5 1/3, just a tad over the claimed 5 pumpsAlso has a safety mechanism to prevent overloading, and a non-complicated air purge system. The jack came with an abundance of lesser quality grease applied liberally, which I cleaned up to leave the nice finish in tact. The harbor freight jack worked as quoted on their website, except the rapid pump 3 1/2 pumps to max. I never got anywhere near that number, even after purging the air, though it didn't really matter when I was jacking up various cars.The jack pad works great, has a 360 degree rotation (though not sure what good it does), free rolling wheels that don't bind, and a removable handle that is good for breaking loose bolts as a breaker bar/extension. Materials look quality, the bolts were all tight out of the box, and I feel good to own this jack (I was always given concerning looks from family with the Harbor Freight jack, guess people have had bad instances with them, though all the tools I've bought have been on par with the competition at a discounted price. One note is that I do replace any grease within a Harbor Freight product with high quality lithium grease.I also pair this jack with 2 sets of Craftsman 3 ton/pair jack hi-lift stand. They are tall, at 13 7/8'' at their lowest, but 21'' at max. For most work, it is nice having tall jack stands to limit the amount of jack stand arm that is out of the stand. Hope people get what I'm trying to say here.I tested this jack on our family scion xb. It lifts the front end to the max 18 1/2'', enough for the jack stands to slide under the jack points on the side with a couple of inches to spare. I then jacked under each suspension piece the full 18 1/2'' and raise the jack stands to 3/4 their full height. Done on each corner, the car can be up in the air by 16-17'' easy, plenty of space for anyone reasonably sized to work under. Just the front half jacked up on stands, the front of the car was 27'' off the ground. Plenty for any kind of front end work. The tires were off the ground by a good 5-6 inches, overkill for most people.I've stated this at least 4 times, but this jack is awesome and performs like a jack should. It instills confidence in the user, and has such good control for lowering a car super slow onto jack stands or back to the ground. By no means is this a racing jack, with 58 pounds, it is light enough to lug around if need be with handles that are awesome, but compared to aluminum counterparts, it is hefty.This jack is what I like to call cheap insurance. It will raise up your car with confidence and not drop it part way through, and if you like, will hold up your car (along with jack stands of course) without any worries. Your life is worth more than the premium for this jack.Many of you may say that Harbor Freight sells a comparable jack (the one I bought probably) for half the price. Yes, the jack from HF was good, but it was heavy and bulky. The lower saddle height was nice, though i don't know very many people with under 4'' of ground clearance (even so, a scissor jack can lift the side of the car enough to get this jack under if need be). If extra height is needed, a small block of wood on the saddle will do, though 18'' is plenty for most applications. I did my exhaust on my car with under 12'' of clearance before I had either of these jacks or high lift jack stands, so anything is an upgrade.All in all, I probably spent a tad over $210 for a great jack and 2 sets of quality jack stands. Guys, its well worth it and this is a great jack for the price (figure in tax into the price too). If you have any doubts, I will stand behind this jack until it decides to  quit on me, which will be after countless years of oil changes and maintenance. Harbor Freight is good and cheap, but if you want quality you can trust, buy this jack over the cheaper alternatives. The number of positive reviews for this jack (and the few negative reviews complaining about defects and such) sold me on this jack.I will try to post a follow up later on this jack to show long term progress.
summary: Best Jack I've Owned, Hands Down

reviewText: Pretty low. Pumps quickly. Good combination of aluminum and steel. All the necessary parts are steel and supporting parts are aluminum to reduce weight. Slightly. It's still heavy though because it has a lot of steel. But I feel more comfortable having a heavy steel jack anyway. Best jack I've owned.

Written January 2013:  For as big and heavy duty as it is, it's not very heavy since it has some aluminum parts.  Very easy to use, straight out of the box.  Great jack.  Nice handles on the sides that I use.  Most others don't have them.  Update September 19, 2013.  It started to leak a little oil the first month, but then stopped before I even looked for the problem, so maybe it just had too much.  No dripping since.  Important measurements:  It starts at 4" and goes up to 18 3/4".  It is 25" long and 12" wide.  I like how it goes up quickly when there is no load on it, then slows down when there is weight on it.  I still recommend it.

I wanted made in the USA floor jack, but at the moment I only found one mfg; Hein-Werner and their products come at a price (over $400 for a 3-ton jack). Knowing this is made in China, I wanted to have 1-ton margin (my car weighs 2-ton) as many Chinese-made jacks have poor reputation (I would not lift a 3-ton vehicle with this jack).Overall quality seems good for a Chinese product, but after several use the front wheel shaft seems to have bent by 2-3mm (one wheel touches the ground but the other idles unless loaded) but does not affect use. All 4 wheels are made of steel and seem robust; they probably would not explode as would on some resin-made wheels.  The rubber on the lifting pad is a nice addition.  Lifting is easy; long bar allows less force to exert, and the bar is detachable so make it in 1/2 length. Even after contacting the vehicle, it lifts reasonably quick.I've debated this against Arcan's 3.5-ton all-steel jack, but Arcan did not include shipping so I went for this.  However, expect this to be as heavy as all-steel jack, but I value durability over light weight on a floor jack for safety. Be careful when you lift this off the ground/floor so as not to break your back.One last note; the black paint on the wheels will come off after use.  I don't know why these jacks/jack stands are painted, knowing that the paint will come off easily.

I bought this because of the supported weight and the price. Additional positive reviews also helped with my purchase. I use it on both a Tesla Model S and a Subaru Outback. It works very nicely on both vehicles. Works very well within Jackpoint Jackstands as well!

I ordered this late at night & thought I was buying an all aluminum floor jack because I have a bad back.  My steel floor jack weighs a ton.  Well when it arrived,  UPS needed two people to carry it to my front door.  Yikes!  Amazon made it right, so in this case, Amazon gets 5 stars as they understood and sent UPS out to return it.After numerous replies to my poor review, I have decided to change it as my review was not on the jack operation itself which in retrospect was not fair.  I based my review simply on the weight of the jack that was delivered.A good floor jack is worth its weight in gold.  I've read many of the other reviews from very happy users.  In the case of this floor jack, I never even lifted it.  Two UPS delivery people brought it to my porch as this one weighed over 70 lbs (UPS or the shipper had affixed a heavy package warning sticker).  I purposefully rated the jack one star to bring to people's attention that the jack is heavy and it was not clear.  Some people were also  surprised that the jack weighs as much as it does when I read their reviews.The shipping weight of the jack is only 62 lbs according to the specs for this jack.  I have no idea why UPS put a heavy item (required for items over 70 pounds) warning label on the box.  This happened quite a while ago & I simply remember the two UPS guys it took to carry it along with the UPS warning sticker which stated: heavy package over 70 pounds.  UPS also sent out two people when it was returned.I never opened the box or used the jack.  It is very possible the wrong jack was delivered to me.  As for the operation of this jack I will defer to the many others who have used it.  I encourage everyone to read all the reviews.  The bottom line is if I had to do it all over again & had a need for a good 3 ton jack, I'd probably purchase an all aluminum.  I noticed one on Amazon that weights 56 lbs has a shipping weight of 59 lbs.Arcan ALJ3T Aluminum Floor JackThe more I think about this incident, the more I wonder if I was shipped the wrong item.
I could not lift the car!Oil changes were not to par.Aluminum and steel gave me air.The clearance underneath was fair.And now I can look like a star.

I have two now and both have performed flawlessly.  They have been a real life saver.  light weight and half the price of the ones from the big box stores that charge 350.00 for theirs.  These work with no problems. Follow the directions to bleed them before use and I have had no problems with them in the cold weather of winter or in the heat of the summer.  They don't slow leak either.  But do use safety Jacks under them.  Never trust a floor jack EVER!!  It's your life.

I don't know how I ever lived replacing junk jacks yearly from the hardware store. The lifting arm ALONE is as thick as the other jacks. This could not be a more solid feeling jack. The lifting plate is HUGE, you'll be able to find a jacking point easily. Would recommend this to anyone, do not waste your time with any other jack.
great great stuff

For years, I have been using sprays and foams to clean my tires only to lose the shine in about a day.  Sonax gel goes on easily (I recommend Chemical Guy foam wheel applicators) and the gel looks great and stay on several days.  Minimal splatter on the sides of the cars.  I always apply after washing the car\wheels and putting down a layer of quality matte spray.  I wipe the matte spray off and apply the Sonax gel and let it sit for a couple hours.  Turns out perfect!
summary: Much easier to use than spray

reviewText: I used Meguiar's hot shine, Eagle One and 3m in the past. I was impressed with the last one, but it is a spray and it does not last long. This Sonax gel works wonders and it's the best value -seems pricey, but I've done my car 2 times and my wife's 2 times and still have 90% of the bottle. It shines for weeks and does not attract dirt.One last thing, if you don't like your tires too shiny, you can simply apply it sparingly with a cloth and remove any excess. The rubber will look like new but without the gloss.

I really love the wet gloss show finish and goes well with my glossy glass black car. If applied when tires are dry you won’t get it splashed on the side of your vehicle.  If not wet lasts for 3-4 days before it gets dull. If rained on it will strip some gloss but you still have a nice matte black.Only complain it’s pricey and don’t like how the tube applicator slides out this leaves some to drip at base of cap when flipping on its side when applying. I normally wear latex gloves so not a big deal but has left a little mess on shelve.

This stuff works great.  I used it on yesterday for the first time and I must say it is fantastic on my tires it leaves a nice sheen on the tires not overly shiny but nice and neat (no sling off ).  The product is thicker than most tire dressings and it stays where you apply it .I will be using these SONAX products a lot more in the future.
Great lasting results. Have only used this product once so far. Applied after a regular hand wash and still have great results 500+ miles later and multiple days of rain.

Sonax gel will not leave a very high gloss, if that's what you want. I've tried putting two coats on which makes the tires a little glossier, however the dressing just ends up slinging all over the fenders. A light coat, buffed out with a microfiber towel will leave the tires looking good, with no sling I you don't want a high gloss.
I cannot wait ti use this cleaner for my tires and my rims on my car very highly recommended
summary: ... tires and my rims on my car very highly recommended

reviewText: I need to hit the wheels again on my F150. Bad bad bad brake dust, never seen another vehicle this bad.This stuff works way better than store bought. No one here carries this in the store and the other stuff is just a big waste of money.Now it the dust is bad, you'll need to scrub anyways. Just this makes the job doable, yeah that's the word I'm looking for. If not, then the baked on brake dust would be staying. I'm sure there is better or professional stuff out there. This one doesn't seem to hurt anything as long as you follow the directions. Spray, let it soak in, scrub and rinse really well. Don't get in on painted surfaces or yourself. If you do, rinse really well....LOL

Other than the price, I'm very happy with this product.  It melted the gunk off my wheels like magic.Tip: Use a small brush right about two minutes after spraying.  It doesn't take much brushing but I've found that it helps to spread the solution evenly.Tip: Don't let it dry like I did the first time (due to my apartment complex not having the water on at the car wash bay.  If you do, just spray on more, rub with a brush, and it all comes off just fine.

This product is the best product made, I love it. This thing literally cleans the dirt off and literally takes just a rinse to clean off if done correctly, the key is to wait a few minutes to get in there and break up the brake dust.

So I am looking forward to cleaning my car this spring. One part of the car that most people don't think about is the wheels. It really does make a difference when looking at your car. This product worked ok, but there are so many different kinds, I am not sure this one is any better than another. I basically will just buy the cheapest when this runs out.

I use this to help clean the brake dust from my car's wheels. I find that if I use it regularly, I don't need to do anything more than spray it on, let it work, and rinse it off. However, if my wheels get really dirty (or I go too long between washings), then I need to bring out the brush and do some scrubbing.In addition to the wheels, my car has stainless exhaust tips and a DFI (Direct Fuel Injection) engine...a recipe for lots of soot at the tailpipe. I find that a small amount of Sonax helps keep the exhaust tips looking pristine, so long as you're careful not to get any on your car's paint.Definitely recommended!

Simple spray application. Wait a few minutes then rinse. No scrubbing required. I think I did wipe off a few drips or something. My wheels looked very polished after using this product so highly recommend.Please note there will be a pungent, chemical odor.PLEASE NOTE: My rating system is fairly simple; "Does the product perform equal to or better than advertised?". I never seek perfection. If the manufacturer is telling me the truth about the product that is all that I ask. I also factor in bang-for-buck and labor required.Thus my ratings typically are a little higher on average because I research and read a lot before pruchase.During my research I try to adjust my expectations accordingly. This product does not tie my shoes for me but it really cleans my wheelsextremely well in a virtually effortless way which is all I expected, hence the five stars. It smells bad but so what. Realistic expectations is how I try to rate so please factor this in with my rating. Thx.

This is by far the best wheel cleaner I've ever used. I've used both Meguiar's, Mother's and Chemical Guys. They all worked decently, I tend to prefer the Meguiar's Hot Rims over the rest; however it doesn't come close to how well this works. With 4 piston brembo calipers and hawk hps pads, my Evo's brakes spew out a TON of dust onto my wheels. It's a constant battle to keep them somewhat clean. If I let it sit on there too long and gather more road gunk, it was impossible to get off with Meguiar's (or anything else) alone, and would require scrubbing (sometimes with a harsh/dangerously hard bristled) brush. Not anymore! This cuts through caked on rims even after a couple months of horrible neglect.You might need to use two passes with it, depending how hard caked the gunk is. My advise is:-First spray the wheels with my meguiars soap and pressure wash them to get off as much as possible before applying this.-If you have a light cleaning (usually less then a couple weeks for my car), then you can get by with spraying two rims at a time. If you're going to have to scrub some of the gunked on mess it's probably best to do one rim at a time. Spray your rim(s) generously getting in your inner rim if possible, your lug nuts, etc.-The liquid will come out kind of greenish and then turn an orangish/redish as it breaks down brake dust. It has a very strong (like cat urine) odor that you just have to get used to.-Let it sit on there for a couple of minutes (usually don't want more then 5). You don't want it to dry on the rim, although having accidentally done this - it washed off no problem.-If it's a light cleaning you can probably get by with just pressure washing it clean at this point, although to make sure you get all parts of the rims I usually go over it withGriot's Garage 15704 Micro Fiber Wheel Wand, (Pack of 2). If the caked on mess requires harder scrubbing I'd recommend something like autogeek's "speed master wheel brush".This bottle usually last about 16 individual wheel cleanings. It makes it the most expensive option out there, but by far the best and safest! It is acid free and ph balanced, and is specifically designed to be safe on all rims. I use this on BBS, Enkei, and WedsSports rims that cost over 1000-1500/per, all the time. I have no worry that this can in any way danger them. A lot of other products out there can be a hit or miss, and especially if you have refinished rims it can be very risky. My BBS are refinished and so far this has not worn it off or damaged them whatsoever. If you're looking for a bit cheaper solution, there'sSonax 230500 Yellow Wheel Cleanerto use as a refill. You can also checkout autogeek, depending on their sales, coupon codes, and shipping situation - you can usually find a better deal there.

Wow, just wow!I drove to the local coin operated pressure washer car wash place, sprayed on the wheel cleaner and gave it the required bit of time.  Product changed color as it reacted with brake dust.  Then I used the moderate pressure washer wand to rinse off the wheels.THEY HAVE NEVER BEEN SO CLEAN.  Only way to get the last 4% of brake dust off would be to roll the car forward so the wheels have half a revolution, then repeat to cleaning process.What was more surprising is the wheels stayed clean for a month after, and a couple months later are still cleaner than they were after normal pressure washing of the wheels without cleaner.  Could not be a better product!I run stoptech (very dusty) pads on an old Lexus LS400, 23 year-old original wheels with 70k miles.  The dust sticks like glue.
summary: I did not think it was possible for a product to work this well, the way I used it.

reviewText: LOVE THIS PRODUCT.  IT WORKS BETTER THAN ANY OTHER PRODUCT OUT ON THE MARKET THAT I HAVE TRIED. BEATS THEM ALL HANDS DOWN. YES THERE IS NOT MUCH IN THIS BOTTLE BUT STILL WELL WORTH THE PRODUCT THAT IS IN THERE. I WAS ABLE TO CLEAN APPROX 5 VEHICLES WHEELS WITH THE AMOUNT IN THE BOTTLE.  THANKS FOR AN AMAZING PRODUCT.
This stuff works. I tried a dozen other wheel cleaners and nothing even comes close.This is the best and you don't need to use much of it.
Used on neglected wheels and made a real difference but not magical as some say. Saved me some rubbing and would recommend to others.
Spray and let it sit, be sure to agitate with a soft brush or mitt, then rinse off after it turns red.
Does a great job removing stubborn break dust. Is a little pricey but it does work. Probably would buy again

Sonax wheel cleaner is by far the most effective product on the market. Ya its $15 a bottle, but there is nothing else i have ever seen that just melts caked on brake dust off this well. Make your wheels bleed brake dust.

Ordered this after reading reviews. I was very surprised and happy with the results. I have a 2012 Passat. One thing that attracted me to the car was the spoke wheels. I paid for the upgrade and immediately forgot they were on the car. It's an age thing, I take care of my cars but my condition dictates a limited time for work that requires being bent over. I've been washing the spokes and outer rim all along but forgot the polished deep dish part of the wheel. I just finished using product with a soft wheel brush for the first time and was shocked to rediscover the effect of clean highly polished deep dish spoke wheels. I sprayed it on, let it sit a minute, brushed the surfaces, hosed it off, wiped it down, done. No mussel required. Works wonderfully. P.S.  I bought the cheap Griot's Garage  15704 well wand (brush) purchased here along with this Sonax. Perfect combo for me but no two wheels are alike. Choose the right brush.

Used this on my 10 year old wheels that have probably never been cleaned beyond the car wash.  They had years of baked on brake crud that I once tried removing with the pressure washer to no avail.Sprayed this on, brushed it around a bit, and wheels look like new.  Smells bad, works great.Way above expectations.

I've cleaned everything on wheels from Harley's to hot rods,so when people ask me what I use to keep my wheels looking new Sonax is what I recommend. The only quality spray and rinse I have found that works and repels.

With that said, it makes the stuff you buy in the auto parts store look like water.Some people have complained about the smell, I really don't find it that offensive, maybe it's because I was working outside on a cool windy day.Sprays on well, with good coverage, and my guess is that each bottle will be good for about 3 wheel cleanings on my 18"s. The subsequent cleanings should be easier though now that the wheels have been sealed.My one gripe is that it still does need scrubbing for complete cleansing. You will not get perfectly clean wheels unless you remove them from the car (OK maybe if you have tiny brakes). Most calipers have a relatively tight tolerance to the wheels, which prevents you from scrubbing the area immediately adjacent to the calipers. Removing the wheels from the car is the ideal method for a baseline cleaning.
summary: Not quite the full effect as advertised...

reviewText: I find it hard to describe the odor produced by this stuff.  I feel like it itself doesn't smell as much as whatever is in it makes the inside of your own sinus cavity smell like it's rotting.  If you're sensitive to chemical odors I would recommend you skip this and use a wheel brush and a bucket of soapy car wash,  which by the way is what I ended up having to do anyway.  I was hoping this product would make easy work of cleaning the many nooks & crannies of my BMW's M-Sport wheels,  and the areas did turn red to indicate it was doing something, but it didn't "remove" much so I had to go back over them again to clean more thoroughly.But again, the odor...  maybe wear a respirator? Absolutely requires being outside anyway. I couldn't comfortably get within 25 feet of my car as this stuff was doing its thing.
summary: oh my god, the smell.  Also not terribly effective by itself.

reviewText: I have committed myself to using two wheel cleaners, the first being IronX, and the second is the product shown here, Sonax Wheel Cleaner.  This stuff does a fantastic job of getting out one of the worst parts of wheel cleaning, and that's getting off grime and brake dust.  The first time I used this I was hooked as road dirt and grime just started to run off without issue.  Because I had some significant brake dusting as my pads were new (new car), I had to agitate a bit with a wheel brush.  After a few swirls with a wheel brush, the dusk started to run right off.  From then on maintenance is a breeze as all I have to do is spray this on my wheel when I am washing my car, wait for the colors to start changing to a dark purpleish color, and wash right off to a beautiful shine.I didn't buy from here as I like to buy this product in cases, but the price here for a single bottle is as good as any other place.The only negative that I will give this product is that it has a tendency to smell really bad depending on what it is reacting with on your wheel.
