Also, (this didn't affect the rating) do not spray this stuff in a windy environment!  I was washing my car one day and this liquid is so light that just a small little brush of wind came by and i got some spray that was in the air in my mouth and boy does it taste bad.
summary: One of my favorite wheel cleaners

reviewText: Any Audi, BMW, or Mercedes-Benz owner with OEM brake pads will tell you that brake dust is a constant problem. The unsightly brake residue builds up quickly and can be hard to remove. I've tried lots of products, but Sonax Full Effect Wheel Cleaner is the first product that really works on brake dust. Spray it on a cool, dry wheel, let it sit for 3 - 5 minutes, hit it with a brush and spray and the brake dust is gone. This product is a permanent part of my car cleaning kit.

This is great for cleaning wheels.  Best thing I have ever used.  Just spray it on, let it sit and then a quick brush and then wash it off.  Great stuff.  It also seems to keep the brake dust from building up as fast.
Best Wheel Cleaner I have used Yes, you have to scrub the wheels but the outcome after it all, is just awesome the wheels look brand new.
Sonax Wheel cleaner is the best wheel cleaner ever. Sonax products are simple the best. I have used so many products before this none worked like this.

As others have noticed, the smell is bad, but after a few uses, it doesn't bother me. I will argue with others here and say that this is nowhere near worth the money they get for this. I know there are individuals that swear by certain brands, but come on... really? This product is worth the cost if you enjoy science experiments and watching the changing of colors (and you are 9 years old), but it gives you no additional benefit over the $6 bottle from a parts store, except maybe that it doesn't dry as fast, but using it one wheel at a time, that's a null point. If no scrubbing was necessary, I would have given this 5 stars, but like ANY OTHER wheel cleaner, you need to brush. In addition, the bottle lasted through a total of 8 wheels. Not worth the cost to me at all. Still, 4 stars because it's not terrible.

After the winter, my rims were filled with black iron spots that no other cleaner could remove.  I purchased the Sonax in hopes it would make quick work of cleaning the rims - and that it did.  It smells horrible but works great.

Chrome wheels are nice looking, but they are open to collect black brake dust.  The cleaner which is made in Germany is just sprayed on the wheels.  It turns from green to red indicating it is time to wash the liquid off.  I give the cleaner help with a wheel brush and then spray the cleaner off with a hose.  The chrome wheels look very good when finished.
summary: A Really Effective Cleaner for Chrome Wheels

reviewText: This stuff is great, You need to rinse with really strong water stream or a pressure washer. If your wheels are really bad, if Sonax does not get them clean they need refinished. Try a little wheel brush action if they are really bad to spare product. I get about 8 wheels out of a bottle. By no means is this product cheap, Use sparingly with a nice wheel brush.
summary: All I can say is wow

reviewText: I am curious about why people rate this product based on how it smells?It does a better job on my wheels than any other product I have used in the past. The bottle is about half the size of the competition's (500ml vs 1 quart), but the results make up for the difference in cost per wash. I use the Sonax brush, dip it into a bucket, then brush over the rims that have sat for a few minutes with the Wheel Cleaner on. It loosens the brake disk gunk nicely.I have to deduct a point because the spray nozzle does not produce much of a mist and it is difficult to get good coverage without wasting any of the cleaner.

Used this on several wheels and it works great.I found this best to use on neglected wheels. My car gets washed at least once a week so my wheels never get that dirty. So when I used this product for the first time, there was not much color change.However, when I used this on another car that went several weeks without a proper wash, the product started to turn purple very quickly.My only gripe is the smell. Its pretty harsh but hey, this cleaner does work quite well compared to simply using car shampoo in a bucket.
This is a awsome wheel cleaner. I love how it changes colors. I have 20" poweder coated black wheels and this cleans it with ease and gives it a nice shine. It is a little pricy but works great.

Goes on easy, am using it for my tires,very nice shine, but even after letting it sit on my tires for 10 minutes and wiping the excess off, when the tires get wet the shine goes away, will keep on looking for a tire shine that does what it says

Made the interior dash board and doors plus leather seats look awesome! Used it on black trim on the outside of car looked really nice so glad I bought this product I signed for subscribe and will be getting it every three months glad I did!
very easy to use and is a nice quality item  very mice scent  I would use it again and recommend it

I was skeptical at buying this item before since the brand Chemical Guys is new to me.  I ordered a few items before this for my detailing business and Im amazed by their products.  New Car High Shine is so concentrated that you would need to dilute it before using.  Basically I got more bang for my buck..
Like the product this is a keeper wil order a gallon. Size next time make it shine but not oily

I like this because it's just a step down from the Silk Shine, and depending on what you're applying it to, will give a better finish.This stuff is good on center consoles, etc - that are smooth and not so porous. The glossier stuff will be super glossy on something smooth, where this is that happy medium.A little goes a long way.Also keep in mind that this dressing isn't sprayable unless you add water (don't...) and comes with a flip top cap, and has the consistency of hair conditioner. Spreads easily, and less is more. Use a microfiber applicator pad to apply with, as it'll help you get a smooth even surface. Let it dwell for a minute or two to reveal any 'soak up' spots, and then buff it all smooth with a microfiber towel to get a smooth, even sheen.Smells like cherries, and the scent lingers for a small while - and isn't overpowering. The scent goes away after a day or two, but the protection doesn't.5/5

I've installed these on all the vehicles I've owned over the last 10 years or so since I am the one doing all the oil changes. They have always worked just as advertised and are very convenient. I will continue to buy them in the future

I've had fumoto oil drain valves for all my vehicles and they've always worked and been reliable. The make doing an oil change easier, saves time, and the valve always functions as it should. Definitely worth the money if you are a do-it-yourselfer.

If you are going to keep your vehicle for awhile and you change your own oil, this is a real time saver and installs very easly. I have them on both my cars and love it. No worrys about leaks and like I said saves time and is less messy.
All is good except the outlet hole is too small.It would be perfect if they made the hole bigger.
summary: The outlet hole is too small

reviewText: I like how easy and clean this product makes doing an OC, but it takes forever to drain the oil.First try, cold engine - oil cap off - dipstick out, took 25 minutes to drain.Second try, engine at operating temp - oil cap off - dipstick out, took 15 minutes to drain.I leave it on, but have not had success in it being quicker. Fact of the matter is, it's a smaller drain hold that the pan, slow flow rate WILL be lower. Can't defy the laws of physics here. Had dripping from the valve, but it was very minimal and required no addition of oil between 5k OCI's. If you want cleaner OC's, this product is convenient, however if time is crucial, stick with the standard drain plug.

I wanted to wait a while (1 year) before I reviewed this Fumoto valve so that I would have several oil changes and many miles of experience with it. I had a few concerns prior to purchasing this valve, and all concerns have been eliminated. I installed this valve on my 2012 Nissan Frontier 4x4 a year ago. Since I do a fair share of off road driving, I was concerned about debris hitting the little lever and losing all of my oil, but the valve is made in such a way that it is virtually impossible for that to happen. The lever has to be pulled forward (towards the front of the vehicle) and then turned downward to open the valve, so unless you are operating it, the valve will not open.Oil changes are a breeze. No tools required to drain your oil. I have put my truck through some pretty compromising situations off of the road, and this valve has no issues. It really is a "must-have" for anyone who does their own oil changes.
summary: A Must-Have for the DIY Oil Changers

reviewText: It now takes me longer to swap the oil filter than it does to drain the oil and refill. I have had fumoto valves on many of my vehicles over the years and a strong believer.
perfect, have one on my truck and one on my wife's car, if you do your own changes this is a must. NO MORE HOT OIL ON MY ARMS!!!!!
Bought this and thought I would give it a shot on our new Van.  It works very well and oil changes are now much faster and I don't need a wrench.

I have these on both of my cars, a Nissan Sentra and a Subaru Forester.  All you need is a short length of vinyl tubing- put one end on the nipple, the other end in an empty oil container, and turn the valve.  A few minutes later it's done.  It's virtually impossible for the lever to get moved on it's own, but if you ever bottom out (or worry about it), a simple hose clamp will hold it in place.
summary: The only way to change oil

reviewText: Have this drain valve on both of our vehicles and love it.Installation was super easy, obviously. Have not had a single leak on either vehicle since using these (over a year).Highly recommended as it is much cleaner method to changing your oil.Got clear tube to attach to the nipple from a local hardware store.
summary: This is a must for anyone that changes their own oil.

reviewText: the F-103N is awesome because it has a short nipple to it. I put a 1/4" ID tube on the tip and train directly into an empty winshield washer jug. Then I'll punch a hole in the oil filter to drain it directly in as well and I dont need a drain pan!

Very well constructed and does just as advertised. I do my own oil changes and have them on both my vehicles. I love the ease of draining my oil now if they would just come up with a eaiser way to change oil filters.

My experience with this wax is confined to using it on 1 black, and 2 dark grey metallic vehicles.  Your vehicle needs to be properly prepped to get the best out of any wax.  1 to 2 year old vehicles should be clay barred.  Any older and you might need to paint cleanse or polish as necessary. This wax should be applied thin and allowed to haze, 20 minutes per Chemical Guys instructions.  Time will vary per temperature and humidity.  Use the swipe test.  Even applied a little bit thick this wax is forgiving, just needs a little bit longer to cure.  Comes off easily.  I would say longevity is average to good.  This wax really makes your properly prepped paint look wet and shiny.  For the price you pay for it on Amazon this wax is a very very good purchase.  You'll get a lot of bang for your buck!

I layered this on top of Colinite Insulator Wax (which is the easiest wax to use ever), and it beads like crazy. Preferred method is to apply a second coat a day later (garaged) but since I don't have a garage, I applied two coats right after each other. Like any other wax, if you don't prepare the paint properly (correction and clay) you won't get the benefits. I recommend getting the red round foam applicator from chemical guys, my applicator (typical kind) had an edged seam around it and it kept getting chunks of wax stuck to it.  The biggest issue I see is that when applying it sets very quickly and you cannot distribute it any longer as soon as it starts to dry. You have to work in 1' by 1' areas, any larger and it doesn't spread out like it should. What I did enjoy, is that once you apply it, you don't have to keep "working" it into the paint. Overall, it's foolproof, but I felt like a little doesn't go a long way. As for the depth of shine and the "glow" afterwards, I've seen a wetter shine from using Meguiars paint sealant, but this will last longer than Meguiars which is interesting. Perhaps using this on its own or over JetSeal would yield better results. I loved a streak-free shine on my 2 stage black SUV.
summary: Great paste wax, for the price

reviewText: I use this wax on my Ducati 1199 and works awesome, now although its just a shine enhancer I put this on the top of Jet Seal 109!
And I wasn't disappointed.  This stuff leave  the paint feeling smooth as butter and makes the water bead up something awesome.  Definitely worth the price.
summary: bought this because the rest of their stuff is great.

reviewText: Side by side. This product performed as goods as gold class wax.  Not as caky or thick as gold class.I will continue to use this wax, but for a 90% white wax, seems very yellow to me.Goes on smooth and wipes off nice with micro fiber towels.
I would order again I like it very much the way it cleans and foams up real nice product to wash your car

Great at loosening up grime. None of us want to admit it but there are times our cars go almost a month without a bath. Even dried on 80mph bug splatter came off with ease. Once again awesome product.
Great maintenance soap.I like the lower suds level this gives, instead on mostly suds, this has, in my option water with soap in it!Will not remove waxes/sealants.
summary: Great maint. soap for those that want a clean finish with NO shine additive. No wax.

reviewText: You really can't smell the scent. I hate artificial fruit scents, especially cherry and grape, which is why I didn't get the soaps I REALLY wanted from them. Thankfully, after trying this stuff, I can tell you that you don't really notice it. You might catch a slight whiff every once in a while, but it's NOT strong when you're actually using it.I've been using this in my foaming gun. It definitely is not a very strong foam, but it is a great soap. I spray the whole car with foam, then rinse, then go one section at a time, refoaming, washing with a mitt, then rinsing. I've read that's the best way to go about it, and it got my car pretty darn clean.Oh - FYI, this stuff works great on bugs and tar, too.
summary: Don't worry, you don't smell it.

reviewText: If there are any areas that you miss and do not rinse before it dries, this soap leaves major water spots. And no, it's not my water since my water measures just 40-70 PPM on the TDS scale for mineral deposits.These water spots can happen if you are soaping the car in the sun and it is allowed to dry on the car, or if you simply do not wipe down the inside of your door jams well, etc.I've definitely had better luck with other car wash soaps.

I use this only when I want to strip the wax or at least, help strip the wax, off my car.I use one once per gallon of water and it does a good job of cleaning the car. I always follow up with a pre-wax cleaner then a wax when I use this product so I can't really comment on its wax removal ability but it certain helps with my piece of mind.I also put this shampoo in a foam gun and the foam that comes out is nice and frothy. Eventually I will upgrade myself to a foam cannon but in a foam gun, it does a good job of clinging to the car's surface to help breakdown dirt and grime.The fact that the price is pretty low, I do not mind using more than I should. I have another shampoo for my maintenance wash so this is perfect to start from a clean surface.
This sponge works great on both trim and low profile tires. The handle is easy to grip and helps keep your hands clean.
The handle is easy to grip and the applicator foam glides over the sidewall effortlessly. I expected these applicators to be cheap and cheesy, but they are lasting.
I bought these, but won't buy again. I own a detail shop and after just one use on a 33" off road tire the foam separated from the plastic handle. They work pretty good on street tires.
Work very well. One of the foam pads did come off the plastic handle. Other than that they are great!
summary: Other than that they are great!

reviewText: I'm a big fan of Chemical Guys' products, but I'd have to say these applicators are just a waste of money and waste of time to use. The most noticeable problem with this poarticular product are the blue plastic sleeves which hold the foam applicators (as seen in the product's picture).Almost immediately upon contact with the tire/rubber surface, the foam comes out of the plastic sleeve, and does so repeatedly. I tried applications with several different pieces and it happened over and over with each of them.Color me un-impressed with this product. Don't waste your money.They look "nifty" and "fancy", but they are hardly that. If you want quality Chemical Guys applicators, get the green and black contoured applicators which are also in this section. They are superb.These? I'll just mark them down as an abherration.
This applicator evenly spreads the tire dressing without dripping. Easy to clean as well and appear to be well made.

I used this clay with some hesitation, after reading that some do not like to handle it.  If you do not like cooking with your hands, just use a disposable glove.  The clay does nothing of itself.  It is merely the most effective way to work the surfactant on your paint.  The spray is rather generous because it lifts out all the deep crud into suspension.  The trick here is to use fluid solution rather than the surface abrasion.  You are left with the cleanest surface to use a fine polish and a nice hard wax.The success on my 1989 Mercedes got me thinking about some antique furniture.  I generally use hot water, turpentine (which I dislike) and a bit of linseed oil to clean old furniture. You need to clean these valuable objects without removing the original finish, or you destroy a significant amount of its value.  I was able to clay away a hundred years of smoke and grime from the furniture and see the finish as it was.  Old paint came true again.  The bare patches of wood gave up dirt without abrasion.  I put a new coat of wax and all is well.

I have been usingMothers 07240 California Gold Clay Bar Systemon my car for a number of years, but only recently tried Griot's Garage Clay kit for the first time.  Overall, Griot's Garage did the job, but I liked working with it less than I like working with Mother's clay.  I will explain the differences below.I am attaching a collage of two photos under customer photos.1) The stock photo is somewhat deceiving as it makes you think the clay fills the nice container it is shipped in. Photo #1 shows the clay in the plastic wrap is it arrived. The amount of clay is sufficient to work with, I am not complaining about that, just the photo makes you think you get a lot more. The container itself is very nice for storage. Mother's clay does not come with a container and I had to come up with a plastic container of my own. A tip on storage: before storing the clay ball in the container wet the outside of the clay ball with Griot's Speed Shine or any other detailing spray. This makes the clay easier to take out the next time as it sticks less to the container.2) Photos #2 shows the 35 oz of Speed Shine which came in this kit. Speed shine has almost no scent, provides good cleaning and is easy to work with. Its spray trigger (included  in this kit) delivers a generous even spray of liquid. Because it is a generous spray the solution is used fairly fast. On the first application of clay I used 1/4 of the bottle. I think I will be able to get 4-5 washes out of this bottle.The clay worked well to remove debris. It took more swipes to remove debris with Griot's clay than with Mother's Clay, but the results were very good. The clay itself is softer and fairly sticky and my hands were slightly yellow when I finished, and there was clay under my nails.  This does not happen when I work with Mother's Clay system.  I was able to remove the residue from my hands using Griot's Speed Shine followed by a vigorous washing with soap.  This made working with the clay less enjoyable.  For example, when the phone rang while I was cleaning my car I could not pick it up because I had clay all over my hands.A tip for short people: I am fairly short so reaching the middle of the roof of my Honda CRV to clay it is difficult. I found that that I can do it if put the clay ball under a triangle-shaped Windshield Reach and Clean ToolStoner 95161 Glass Reach and Clean Tooland use it to rub the clay ball on the parts of the roof I can not reach.  The reason why it works better than other tools is because its surface is concave to follow the windshield shape and that curve holds the clay ball without the ball sliding out.Ali Julia review
summary: Did a nice job cleaning but sticks to your hands

reviewText: I am a great fan of Griot's Garage products. They make a range of car cleaning and finish-maintenance products which work well and which, of equal importance, I feel are safe to use on my car. Based on my experience with their products over years, I use them with confidence that they do not contain harsh chemicals which will damage the finish of the paint, leather or plastic surfaces of my car. They are expensive, but I think worth it for the additional peace of mind in knowing that they are effective and safe for the finish.I am just as pleased with the Paint Cleaning Clay Kit which consists of the Speed Shine Cleaner/Lubricant and the Paint Cleaning Clay.  Even if you think that your car's surface is clean, you will often find out that it is not when you start cleaning the surface further with clay.  The clay lifts off tiny particles of contaminants that have sealed to the paint (tree way, etc.) and which can't be seen, but which can often be felt.  In some cases they can't even be perceived as much while they are there, but you definitely notice the slicker surface once you use the clay.  It is like having your teeth cleaned at the dentist's - you had forgotten they could feel so smooth.  The clay lifts these particles off leaving a much smoother, cleaner surface.  Just like a cleaning at the dentist's, I clay a car once a year or so, not every time I wash the car.The Griot's clay will get under you finger nails, so you may wish to use gloves.  Griot's also makes an applicator pad which can be useful as it holds the clay in the center of a foam ring which, when sprayed with Speed Shine, applies a layer of the Speed Shine as you move across the car's paint.  I have used the version of that product which fits on a random orbital polisher, but I prefer to use the clay by hand as I often found the clay losing grip in the sponge applicator and flying out if I made the mistake of lifting the orbital polisher off the car while it before it had completely stopped spinning.  As well, I have experienced it falling out as well from time to time if the speed shine had coated the clay surface that you are trying to stick into the pad applicator surface.  The clay becomes too slick to grip.One word of warning in this regard which should be obvious - if you drop the clay onto your driveway, you should throw it away as it will have picked up rocks and other items which will scratch your paint.  I recommend that you don't try to salvage it as it may contains grit and sand that you can't see to pick out.In addition to making good car care products, it also may be useful to some to note that Griot's is also good at sourcing and selling hard to find or extremely useful tools. I have purchased many over the years (e.g. solid, machined aluminum, lifetime water hose sprayer, no-drip caulk gun, a cam-locking separator gate for truck beds, etc.).

I used this clay to clean my wife's black SUV before applying Collinite 476 paste wax.  Prior to this clay I used Mother's clay and I didn't notices any significant difference in the results.  However,  the spray bottle that came with this kit was very handy.The paint cleaning process itself was easy, although time consuming.  I think I can do it once a year at the most.

reviewerName: B. McCarthy "Engineer, CERT, Amateur Radio Op...
reviewText: I've used many Griot's Garage products over the years.  This is a fantastic kit which lives up to the Griot name.  I can't wait to use it on my wife's car too...

I am a car and car care nut.  I have shelves of products.  No, make that a whole closet full.  The best features of this kit are the excellent packaging.  The products, themselves, are just OK.  My overall rating is 3 stars.First, I'll say something about the packaging.  That is one of the best features of Griot's products. For example, the Speed Shine comes in a nice wide-base round bottle with a quality sprayer. When you are detailing a car, I can't stand cheap bottles with junky sprayers that are thin and fall over easily. Often, you are carrying multiple things in your hands and need to rest the bottle down on something and having it fall over all the time and dribble out or pick up dirt is just irritating!  The bottle is very high quality and clear so you can see how much is left and where the end of the pickup tube is.  Similarly, the clay come in a nice, screw top jar with ample space.  Every other clay I've used comes in some cheap cellophane wrapper or some tiny box and getting it back into, well, anything to protect it is nearly impossible.  Hats off to Griot's on the packaging/containers.First up, this contains a generous lump of paint clay.  You can read about claying a car elsewhere but the basic idea is it's a very good part of the prep process for polishing/waxing a car.  The clay in this kit is of a fairly mild type.  It's kind of hard to explain, but there are aggressive clays that are for really poor condition paint that will also start to remove sealants and such, and there are mild clays which remove less contaminants but are more gentle on the paint.  And, there are some in between.  This follows the tradition of most Griot's products that I have used in that it is mild and relatively fool-proof for the beginner but better suited towards well-maintained cars.  The generous lump can be kneaded and used on many cars depending on the level of dirt/contamination.  High rating for a mild clay that can be used frequently and comes in a best-in-class jar.This kit also contains 35oz of Speed Shine which can be used as a clay lubricant.  Speed Shine is technically a quick detailer for used on a slightly dusty car with microfiber towels, but in this kit, it is used as a clay lube.  There are a lot of products that can be used as a clay lube.  In this case, this product works fine.  I also used Speed Shine as a quick detailer (its original use).  For that, I was less impressed.  It seemed to leave a lot more streaks and the lubricity was not as good as competing products that I've used.  The bottle and sprayer are excellent, though.In sum, this is a good, but not impressive kit.  I would be tempted to just buy the clay separately.  There are other better quick detailers out there (Finish Kare #425 is one of my favorites), but if you are new to detailing, this kit will serve you well, and you will appreciate the quality containers which you can reuse.
summary: Decent enough, but I am not wowed

reviewText: Over the years, I've taken great pains to preserve the finish on my now nearly two decades old, one owner M3. But never before had I taken the plunge and tried "paint cleaning clay." The very idea - you tellin' me to rub play-doh all over my car to clean it? - struck me as somewhat ludicrous. A colleague and fellow BMW addict insisted that it works and that I try it.OK then.  I've tried it and I'm sold. Cleaning with Griot's clay will be step one in my exterior car care routine from here on out. Unlike another amazon reviewer, I had no problems with 'sticky clay' on the car or my hands.  (And by the way, if you feel the need to wear gloves to deal with this seemingly non-existent problem, Griot's Garage offers an enhanced and slightly pricier version of this kit - also sold on amazon - that includes disposable gloves and three microfiber polishing cloths).  Start with a good wash, of course - P21S "shampoo" or one of the Meguiars wash preparations are my usual choice. Dry your car well. Then generously spray the Spray Shine on an area about 12 inches square. Pull off about half of the clay provided, spray it well and knead it vigorously in your hands. Spray it again, then start to rub, refreshing the clay and the surface of the car with the Spray Shine once or twice.  Then wipe down and buff the area with a good quality microfiber polishing cloth.  Wow. The surface of your paint will feel as smooth as silk. Those tiny bits of bug, sap, and grime will be gone. And the process itself is a very pleasant, tactile experience - like giving your beloved auto a thorough exfoliating massage. The clay provided with this kit seems to be very mildly abrasive.  As a result, the clay massage is effective at removing surface contaminants as well as fine swirls, but still very gentle on your paint.I follow with a very fine grit hand polish - 3M Imperial Hand Glaze is my preference.  Then wax - P21S carnauba or Zymol (the real stuff, not the dumbed down turtle wax version) for me, although there are lots of other choices out there. With that regimen, my "Hellrot" '95 M3 looks pretty darned good, considering it's now an 18 year-old daily driver and not a garage queen. The minor dings - the evidence of the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune that beset any car that is driven and victimized, over the course of many years by those who parallel park by braille, and others who feel their car door is not open wide enough until it bangs the car beside it -- will not be gone. Ain't no such miracles in this kit.  But your car will look its best - with a few blemishes to give it character.Overcome your skepticism and try this stuff.  I swear to you, it really works, and your car will gleam.

While it is not a requirement to clay your car after each wash, you are missing out if you skip this step and go straight to wax.  This kit comes with everything you need.  After washing and drying your car, break off a small piece (smaller than a ping pong ball), and flatten it in your palm.  Spray a 2' x 2' area of your car with the spray detailer, then begin claying, side to side, no circles.  You will have to continue spraying as you move to maintain lubricity, and after you have completed a few sections, fold the clay in on itself to expose a fresh surface.  If you drop your clay, or it becomes too soiled, throw it out.  If you find the clay thinning out too quickly, ease up on the pressure and/or use your palm instead of your fingers to move the clay around.  If you did a thorough wash, are not using super-hard pressure, and are using clean clay, it would be hard to mess up.  Happy detailing.

I had to wait to use this product as it was a pretty cold winter (so far) and when it finally got to be above 50 I went for it.  After a basic wash to get rid of the dirt, salt etc, I used the clay and shine as directed.  I was amazed at how nice it made the black and our red car look!  The clay definitely got "dirty" and made the paint smooth as glass to the touch.I think I will definitely keep using this product.
summary: Used it after a cold snap and warm up.

reviewText: I have been a Griot's Garage customer for several years and have always been happy with their product quality, prices and, more important, the value of their products. However, I never tried their clay cleaning kit because it sounded counter intuitive - rubbing clay on my Porsche's paint - forget that! As they said in Ghostbusters, "It would be bad!"But one day, I was in my Ferrari friend's "ta die for" garage and he said he was about to "clay" the paint on his $300,000 Italian beauty - getting it ready for a car show. I think I said, "Are you SURE you want to do that?" about 10 times. But he just laughed and said, "pull your Audi in here and let me show you why you want to clay your paint." Skeptical but trusting, I wheeled the A3 into the shade of his workshop and watched in awe as he washed off a big section of my car's hood. Then, after drying, he sprayed Griot's Speed Shine on my paint, grabbed a wad of this silly putty looking stuff, soaked it generously with Speed Shine and began to carefully massage my paint. He gently rubbed, re-sprayed and worked the clay until, testing the finish from time to time with his left hand, stopped, wiped off the paint and said - "Touch your paint and you tell me what you think..." I was AMAZED! The finish was as smooth, scratch that, SMOOTHER than new. The clay, as if by magic, had removed whatever was stuck to the paint and it did it without scratching and without removing paint! It was the best finish I had ever felt on any car I have ever owner and I have won more than a few car shows with my Porsches.If you have a car that you really care about and want to have the absolute best finish possible, give the Griot's Clay Kit a try. The Speed Shine product (something I have used for years) comes in their high quality, reusable sprayer and by itself, it does a great job touching up your wax job. In this kit, it's the lubricant that helps the clay glide off the impurities stuck to your paint. A match made in heaven. Claying is a labor of love but there is labor involved so if you are into instant coffee and microwave TV dinners, this may not be for you. But if you are a little nutty about your car, this kit is for you.  Without being too redundant, the end result is simply amazing. I especially like using it on glass because the wipers seem to work better and I think I see better too.Good product, good company - highly recommended.
summary: Another great product from Griot's Garage

reviewText: I used this product for the first time the other day. I hadn't been able to wash my car for over two months. It was filthy, to say the least. Even after a thorough wash there was still gunk on the paint. The clay itself is a very generous size, and the container is a nice addition. The spray detailer is also of a generous size, and while this doesn't really matter, it smells good too. In my opinion, this clay was a bit more aggressive than Mother's or Meguiar's. Although a microfiber cloth would have been a welcomed addition to this kit, the spray and clay are excellent in and of themselves. ALL the stuck on crud was removed after I clay bared my car with this product. All around great product. One tip, even with the container, the clay is rather sticky and will stick in there so I wrap it in parchment paper so it won't stick to anything (wax paper doesn't work nearly as well).

For those of you not familiar with paint cleaning clay, the clay bar is used to remove both seen and unseen grit and grime from the surface of the paint.  Gently rubbing the clay bar over the paint causes dirt to release from the paint and adhere to the clay.  The clay is then kneaded and used over and over again.  In order to prevent the clay from damaging the surface of the paint as it's rubbed across, a lubricant is required.  This kit contains not only the clay bar but also a spray bottle of Griot's Speed Shine, which is an ideal lubricant.  The only item missing is a soft cloth to dry and buff the treated area.Three suggestions when using this or any clay bar, (1) wash the car first then use the clay bar, (2) work slowly and (3) treat small areas at a time.  I've been using this product on my Porsches and my Ferrari for several years and I'm very pleased both with how gentle it is and how effective it is.  I think you'll be amazed at how smooth your paint surface becomes after it's been "clayed".  It then makes it easier to wax and water just runs off.This is an excellent product pairing by Griots.

Two years ago I had a problem waxing my 2008 Civic. The polish I was using was not leaving a smooth finish. After polishing, the paint looked good, but it was rough to the touch. There were contaminants embeded into the paint that my name brand cleaner/wax was not removing.I had read about clay bars, so I purchased a clay bar cleaning kit and followed the instructions. It worked! The clay bar and detailing spray that came in the kit left the paint smooth and glossy. So the concept was proven!Clay does a great job cleaning paint.When I saw this Griot's Garage kit, I had to ask, Is it as good as the more recognizable brand I used before?.I just tried it, and I am impressed. It works as well as the high prioed kit I used before.The Griot's kit comes with a clay bar that is 4 times as big as the bar I had in the previous kit. And this bar comes in a resealable container that was absent in the other kit.The bottle of detailing spray that comes in this kit holds 35 oounces of high quality detailing spray, compared to the 16 oz. bottle in the name brand kit.What missing in the Griot's Garage kit? The fancy box, and a microfiber cleaning cloth. The fancy box I don't need. The microfiber towel you can get in any auto care store for less than a buck.
summary: Yes, clay does a remarkable job cleaning your car's paint!

reviewText: The clay works well to remove overspray and other deposits without damaging the finish. Needs a lot of elbow grease but far less damaging than rubbing compound. The container to keep the clay brick in is a nice addition that the competition doesn't offer. The only thing bad about this is that the size of the little clay brick is very small for the price. It resembles a hotel bar of soap. It should be a larger bar and cheaper, how much can the clay cost to make?Don't leave it where your dog can get at it....

This works fine and the speed shine is great for touching up your car in the winter after a laser wash.  Spend the extra $10 and get the kit that includes the towels.  You get 3 microfiber towels and 5 pairs of gloves for $10.  The towels are much more dense and soft than any other microfiber towels I've used so they are well worth $3.00 each.  The clay is good not great.  Some complained that it is too fine but if you are trying to remove material, use a buffing compound.  Clay is supposed to remove contaminants not paint.
summary: Spend $10 more and get the kit with the gloves and towels

reviewText: The ultimate car cleaning is the use of a clay bar, or paint clay to remove contaminants and dirt that you can't even see. If you are someone who uses clay to deep clean your paint, you know what I'm talking about, and you may proceed to the third paragraph. ;-)Why clean your car with clay?? If you've never tried it - don't worry, that's a legitimate question. Here's why - micro-dirt, oxidation, atmospheric contaminants, etc. can all become deposited onto and embedded into the surface of your car's paint finish. After you have just washed and dried your car, run your clean hand over the surface (even better to use the back of your hand). Feel that grit? You can actually hear it... catching on the skin of your hand - yet you cannot see it. This is where clay cleaning comes in.  If you are new to using clay, I strongly recommend looking at some videos on YouTube on how to do it. You can't really `harm' anything, but you can certainly make a mess and frustrate yourself if you're not familiar with the process.  I will summarize the key points and steps for reference:- Starting with a CLEAN car, freshly washed and toweled dry (even better if you have stripped off your wax.. tip: Dawn dishwashing liquid will remove all the wax):- Tear off a manageable sized chuck of clay.  Something that will be about 3" diameter when fairly flat is good.- Saturate the clay with Speed Shine - both sides. Don't worry about getting your hand wet, you'll be glad you did (or the clay will stick to your skin). Some people wear gloves - I do not. I like to feel the clay, and I know if it starts to stick to my hand it needs more lubrication. Lubrication is critical - the clay should always be WET with Speed Shine.- Working with small sections of the car (like a fender, or  of the hood, etc.) apply a mist of Speed Shine to the area to be treated.- Flatten the clay from a ball so that it forms a fairly thin disk. About 3" diameter and " thick is a good place to start.- Making sure the clay is wet with Speed Shine, lay it flat against the paint, and gently move it around the area you're working on. There is no need to follow any specific technique such as "back and forth" or "up and down" or "circular" - other than to ensure you don't miss any spots. DO NOT apply any pressure. Just enough pressure to control the clay is all you need, no pressing down. Re-we the clay and surface as needed. You will feel the clay "grab" or "stick" when it becomes too dry - spray it with Speed Shine and continue.- Occasionally lift the clay and inspect it. You will want to fold it over as it thins itself out with use - and/or as it picks up the dirt and becomes soiled. You don't want to drag the dirt back over the finish - so fold frequently to keep fresh clean clay in contact with the paint.- When finished with a section, use a mist of Speed Shine and a soft microfiber towel to wipe clean and lightly buff dry.- When done - some recommend re-washing the car. To me that is optional (you decide). But bear in mind that there is now NO WAX on your paint. You'll need to re-wax the entire vehicle now.As far as clay cleaning goes, there are two main parts - the clay itself, and the lubricant. I think most clay is about the same. Some are more or less pliable than others, some seem more porous - some smoother, etc.  I like the Griot's clay really well and find it easy to use. The amount supplied is very generous. I can get more than a year's worth of use from each container - often longer, depending how frequently I use it and how much stuff it picks up. The clay is nice and pliable, and I find it to be a good consistency - smooth enough to glide well on the surface and still porous enough to grab the dirt.  The most important component is the lubricant used. This is where the contest ends, in my opinion. I have used Griot's Speed Shine for many years. Not just for clay cleaning, but for nearly daily use to do a quick detail on the car, remove some light bird dropping or bug juice, etc. I even clean the glass (windshield too) with it. The stuff is just amazing. It will not harm anything - paint, chrome, glass, rubber, plastic - you name it, it is safe to clean with Speed Shine.If I could have only one product in my garage for car care, it would be Griot's Speed Shine. And for deep cleaning before waxing - the use of Griot's Clay is the best way to deep detail your finish.  Ten stars!
summary: Ultimate deep cleaning for your car's paint finish!

reviewText: A friend who collects Porsches turned me onto this product, and it is terrific.  It is easy to spray on the liquid and rub the brick over the paint.  It completely removes old wax and residue, and gives the paint a terrific shine and your car will feel as smooth as glass.  Simply apply your favorite wax afterwards.  It makes the finish look and feel like new.
summary: Your Car Will Look Like New

reviewText: My car is about 10 years old so there is some oxidation on my paint.  After cleaning the paint with clay, the paint was smooth and clear again.  I didn't realize how not white my white car had become.  Keep in mind that you have to put on a coating of wax after the clay treatment.  I used Astro Shield (wax) and my car now shines like new.The clay also took out some light surface scratches but it's much less abrasive than rubbing compound.  All things considered, This is a unique and useful product.
I've said this before about this stuff I like most of there products there easy to use and they work well.

I've been a big fan ofAdam's Detailing Clay Bar & Detail Spray Comboproducts. I'd say these two products are pretty equivalent, but I prefer Adams detailing spray over the Griots. Items like this, I buy the gallon size refills, so the sprayer bottle itself should be of high quality and the Griots bottle does rank up there in terms of quality. There's nothing worse than a leaky spray bottle or one that fails to pump and the Griots bottle carries the namesake proudly.This was taken from Adams site: Current US patents prohibit the sale of certain types of clay within the United States. These patents expire at the end of 2012 at which time Adam's will again have control over the choice of clay included with our kits. Until then all kits will include clay marked 'Made in Japan'. We apologize, but this matter is out of our control at this time and we look forward to bringing you domestically made clay options after 2012.This really makes me believe that the higher quality clays are probably all pretty much the same, and in reality your purchasing choice in these kits comes down to what detailing spray/carrier you prefer to use.
summary: On par with other quality clay bar products

reviewText: I've heard that you ought to "clay" the paint on your car to remove minute particles of dirt and what-not.  So I bought this kit and tried doing my 2010 Altima sedan (white).First off, there's a lot of clay in the kit.  As you rub it over the paint, the warmth of your hand causes the clay to flatten out and spread, so a small amount of clay goes a long way.  I did my entire car using about 1/2 of the supplied clay.  When I finished, the clay looked almost as clean as when I started, so perhaps my car didn't have as much embedded dirt as other cars.Second, the lubricating fluid, Speed Shine, smells nice. Again, a little seems to go a long way, as it evaporates slowly from the car's surface as you use it to lubricate the clay.  I used a little less than half a bottle for my car.  It also works well alone to remove bug dirt and other small bits of crap that land on your car, leaving a nice shiny spot where the crap was."Claying" an entire car is time-consuming but not hard work.  I took it slow and did small sections at a time in my garage over three days -- YMMV.  This stuff is easy to use and you'll feel better about your pride and joy when you're done, regardless of how much dirt you remove.

I thought my car was pretty clean.  Until I used this product.You really MUST try this. It made my cars paint as smooth as a baby's butt!The detailed spray smelled okay too.  It made the car feel nice and smooth. I love this thing.The amount of clay is plentiful--about three bars worth of individual clay bars found in other products.  You can use half of it but I recommend using all of it.  Speeds things up quite a bit.  Overall this is a must have product in any detailer's arsenal.  It took me about an hour to do the entire Jeep with that big bar.  Otherwise I would normally take over two hours with a regular size clay bar.The bright yellow color helps you see the dirt much better. I've done three cars now and the bar still looks new when kneaded.  This thing will probably be good for 20 or more clay jobs.HIGHLY recommended!
summary: Amazing how much crap this thing picked up out of my paint!!!!

reviewerName: Sean P. Logue "If you can't win, change the r...
reviewText: Even after a car is washed, it really isn't very clean.  If you run your hand across the finish, you'll find it isn't as slippery as it used to be due to it picking up small particles in the paint.  Paint cleaning clay is the answer for that.The large sprayer made spraying each panel (I did about a half-panel at a time) easy.  I made sure it was all wet, then moved the clay over the panel.  Every so often I folded the clay so that I was working with a clean side.  I also used about half of the bar, both because it is a little large, and also because then if I accidentally drop it I have a backup bar to finish the job with.  Once dropped, the clay is ruined.I also like the fact that it comes in a screw-top plastic container for storage.  That helps keep the clay from drying out when it isn't being used.Griot's claims the clay won't strip wax.  I'm skeptical about that, and recommended cleaning and waxing your car when finished claying it.Overall, this is a good kit for the money.Sean P. Logue, 2013

I have used Mother's clay but like the Griots system better.  The clay is a little more malleable so that when the surface of the clay has picked up a good amount of particulates, I like to fold it in and start with new material.  The jar of clay has a good amount of material and I use about 1/3 of it to do two cars at a time.  I do throw away the used clay.  That makes for about 6 car cleanings, which I do once a year.  Definitely worth the price of the product.Personally, Griot's Garage products are fantastic.  I use their interior cleaner and also use the buffer pads with hook&loop; backing with my Porter Cable buffer.  All excellent stuff.

4 stars with cost as a factor, 5 stars without.This product is not for everyone.If your car is just transportation and gets a quickie car wash a couple of times a year, don't bother.If you like a clean car, but think the clay barring is too much extra work, think again. This may be for you after all.If you're obsessive over making your pride-and-joy look its best, this is definitely for you.The first time someone introduced me to clay bar cleaning, they made it sound like you had to press the clay onto the surface, a few square inches at a time, and lift out the contaminants like you were waxing your legs. Not so. It's just one fairly easy extra step to a basic cleaning.Give the car a light wash to get any large, abrasive particles off the surface, then spray with the Speed Shine and wipe the clay bar over it, just as you would a cleaning cloth. Depending on the condition of your finish, you will feel a tiny bit of resistance as the clay slides over the slippery surface picking up the particulates that normal washing doesn't get. Then spray and wipe with a microfiber cloth. Additionally, if you're getting ready for a car show, or just want to look great, follow this fairly easy cleaning with a polish.I've used other products a few times with good results. It's hard to say one is clearly better than the other, but Griot's certainly seems to be at the top of the pack. The amount of fluid provided is much more than the off-the-shelf competition, and while the amount of clay provided may seem small the first time you buy it, it's actually more than the other brands I've used as well. Griot's only costs a couple of bucks more (for more product) and produces great results.I used this on a dark metallic blue Mustang (Kona blue) - a finish that's enormously difficult to keep shiny and accumulates countless micro scratches. Results were a shiny, deeply reflective gloss, and even though I do not believe clay bars claim to fix micro-abrasions, they definitely appeared reduced. I lightly rubbed my fingers over the surface afterwards - silky smooth.
summary: When you want your baby to shine...

reviewText: I purchased Griot's Garage Speed shine on a recommendation of an auto enthusiasts forum I follow. I used it withGriot's Garage 11153 Paint Cleaning ClayandGriot's Garage Glass Cleaning Clayand the combination works very well. The deposits on both paint and glass were removed without leaving streaks and without too much work on my part.Speed shine has almost no scent, provides good cleaning and is a good surface for the clay to glide on. I enjoyed working with it.The 35 oz bottle is fairly large. I am attaching a collage of two photos under customers photos. Photo #1 has the bottle next to a ruler for relative size. The sprayer worked well - a nice generous even spray. Photo #2 shows how much I used during one cleaning during which I only used it for claying the windows before I used it to clay the body paint. I was a bit surprised how much I used in one application.  Based on the amount I used I would guess the entire bottle will last me through 4-5 cleaning jobs.This kit comes with 3 micro fiber towels.  I find micro fiber towels an important part of getting great streak free results.  I use more than 3 towels in one car wash, so  I bought a large bag of micro fiber towel at CostCo.  However, I like these towels as a supplement because they are a different color.  This way I can use them for a specific job, such as applyingMothers 06108 Back-to-Black Trim Careon the plastic parts of the car and don't mix them up with my yellow washing/drying towels from CostCo.Thumbs up overall!Ali Julia review
summary: Excellent cleaning results, works great with paint and glass clay

reviewText: Like i said in the comment. Its awesome for maintaing that look. Combined with the Quick Detailer i keep my Mustang looking black and shinny in between detailing times.
summary: Great for maintaing that "just washed look"

reviewText: I have used this twice now and have to say that I love it!. I have two kits, and use four of the microfibers to clean my 2010 Wolfsburg Jetta. It can probably be done with only the three included towels, but I wait until my car is pretty soiled to use it and the towels get really dirty fast. I follow up with Chemical Guys Speed Wipe QD afterwards and the cars finish is left looking shiny and slick!

I bought a new car this fall. I want to keep it showroom clean. Unfortunately, we get a lot of rain here and the temperatures are in the uncomfortable 40's. I took my car to the local car wash (manual kind, the "brushless" ones put swirls in my paint). I gave it a through wash. I didn't use the foam brush they provide. Dirt trapped in the public brush scratched my last car. When I got home, I found areas of the car that were still dirty. The pressure washing removed much of the dirt, but not all. The fenders and doors still had dirt on them.After getting my Girot's Spray-On Car Wash Kit, I used it to remove the residual crud. I did a great job. I also did a quick once-over on the rest of the car. The result was amazing! The key to a good wash with this product is to not allow any cloth to get too dirty. You may need additional microfiber cloths, but they are inexpensive. Ok, thirty bucks isn't cheap for a "car wash" product. Detailing costs a lot more! Try this product. It's worth the money.
summary: A spray commercial carwash followed by this product produces a showroom shine

reviewText: I live in a Condo and so a hose and water are not always conveniently available for a weekend wash job (there is a hose and water, but not within easy access of where I park).  So my poor car often goes a bit too long between washes.  Here's the perfect solution (no pun intended)!  Now I can spot clean and touch up between washes easily because this kit really does work.  Yea, a product that delivers what it promises.The towels that come with the kit are above average in quality.  Most micro fiber cleaning towels I've seen are thinner.  Also, they have a very nice softness, no chemical odors (a sign of quality manufacture), and a decent size.  I'd prefer a little larger, but they are plenty good for the job.  The sprayer also is good and works well.Be sure to watch the video here to see how this is meant to be used.  You do *not* want to apply a lot of pressure!!!  Let the solution/solvent and the microfiber cloth do their job and so avoid scratching your car's finish.  You just wipe and lift off the dirt.  You can buff a little, if needed, afterwards using a clean cloth.  Again, the video shows you exactly how to do this.I will probably use this more for touch up and spot cleaning, but you really can do your whole car with it.  It does work pretty well.  You can buy extra solution and towels here on Amazon.  I recommend cleaning the towels by hand with just a bucket of soapy (dish detergent) warm water.  Agitate and let them soak, then wring, rinse very well, and hang to dry.  They dry quickly.You don't really save much getting the kit, but maybe it will go on sale from time to time.  It seems a fair value to me, given the high quality of the towels and the cost of other comparable products.  And it's so easy to use, you can keep the kit in your trunk and grab it and clean anytime you find yourself waiting around somewhere with nothing to do.
summary: Excellent - great for spot and "in between washes" cleaning

reviewText: The car wash product is amazing, thats all. It is great to have around to do a quick touch up, especially if a bird targets your car with it's poo, or spend a good fifteen minutes to give attention and detail to fully wash your car. This stuff washes your car well. The only way it will not work well is if you don't use enough, don't know how to spray and wipe, or use it on an extremely hot summer day in the blazing sun.If I could do it over again, instead of buying this kit, I would personally buy microfiber cloths and a good spray bottle separately and get the gallon refill; this is probably more expensive up front, but it will save you more in the long run.
summary: I don't know why you would vote this product any less than 5 stars.

reviewText: This product works great on lightly dirty vehicles.  The liquid cleans to a super smooth and glossy finish (excellent water beading), the sprayer works well, it even smells good.  The microfiber cloths are very soft and are good for lifting dirt from the vehicle's surface so the paint does not get scratched.  The system is fast and easy to use - cleaned a full size truck in ~20 minutes.  If your vehicle is very dirty, this product does not replace the car wash but is great for quick touch ups to keep your vehicle show-room clean.  This is convenient in the northern winter when bucket washing in the driveway is not possible.  A surprisingly good product.

I have used theMeguiar's Ultimate Wash and Wax Anywhere Spray. The results with that are spectacular and I am a Meguiar's fan. If the Griot's hadn't become available on the Vine program I doubt I'd have gotten it. Meguiar's products are very good.If you have never used this type of product then watch the video Griot's provided for a short overview. The video even has a wise crack when the voice over says "Is it green? Even the towels are green!" hahaThe included MF towels are small. They have a good plush feeling. If you need some high quality MF towels the -3 Pack Cobra Miracle Towels, 16 x 24 inches- are just excellent. Sturdy too. I've had mine for at least 4 years and they are still going strong. Wow.If your vehicle is only lightly dirty then the 3 towels should be enough. Dirtier means more fresh towels are required. A bigger vehicle means more towels. Have plenty on hand the first time you do it to get a feel for what you need.It is supposed to be safe on grim as heavy as shown in the video. I doubt it but I'll never find out because I wouldn't do that even to my daily driver. If I had a dinged up vehicle with messed up paint I'd consider it.Starting from the top and working down is good advice. It gives you a chance to moisten and remove overspray that will get on lower parts of the vehicle as you do the upper parts.The video shows about 21 minutes for a small car. He was taking his time because you could do a car that size in 10 or 15 minutes I think. I think it only took me about 25 minutes to do my full size extended cab truck that was lightly dirty (coating of stuck on dust type thing).It smells really good too. Is it pina coloda? Whatever, it is a pleasure to inhale.Although I think these products are expensive I am a big fan of them. You can get to work 20 minutes early and give your car a quick cleaning. Or after work you can chill out for 20 minutes while giving the vehicle a once over before a tedious drive home.Perfect for a daily driver that you do not try to keep meticulously micromarred-free.

We have not yet had a chance to use the spray cleaner, since we have always been able to use the normal soap and bucket to wash our cars. But we have used the towels. They are very nice, absorbing much more water than the cloths we normally use to wash cars. For washing, rinsing, and drying, these towels work well.

Really dirty? Use the Spray-on Car Wash Kit. The wash cloths are so great and works perfectly with the product they are intended to work with. They are so soft, good absorbents, and smooths the car the way they should. Not a single scratch from these towels.The cleaner itself just works. Light spray for upper part of the car, and moderate for the lower part. Heavy spray for the parts that really get dirty, like the exhaust, and even the wheels! Smells great too!Verdict: I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT.
summary: Must-have car product for car lovers.

reviewText: This is a novel idea but not the most practical, unless you are unable to use water due to local laws or droughts. My car was really dirty when I tried this product. It worked pretty well for the most part, but for the really bad areas behind the tires where crud is flung up and sticks, it didn't work as well. Also, I used nearly the whole bottle on my compact car, so it can get expensive. One thing that I really liked were the microfiber towels. They are very plush and soft, which allows them to pick up and hold the dirt without just smearing it around. I ended up washing my car the old fashioned way after using this, and then claying and waxing it since it had been over two months since a wash. Overall, I'd say it's good to have one of these around for the time(s) you will need something like this, but unless you can't used water and sponge, this isn't the most practical thing. I still think it works pretty well for what it is, however.

Spray-On Car Wash KitWhile the idea of a waterless spray-on car wash is a great one, especially for situations where you can't use water, it isn't an ideal solution. It is below freezing in the winter here in Michigan, and I just cleaned the outside of my car with the Griot's solution and wiped it off. I found that I needed to use a lot more than 3 towels to cover the car and avoid smearing grit over the clearcoat. In addition, the Griot's car wash was starting to freeze before it dried. Even indoors, I noticed that the car wash did not dry very quickly.After wiping down the car exterior, it left the surface somewhat slick to the touch and with a coconut-like scent. However, it left smears and smudges all over the place. I had to buff it off with more clean microfiber towels. Honestly, if I had to go through all this trouble in the freezing temperatures, I'd rather just go through a car wash. That said, the Griot's car wash did cut through road salt quite well but it had a hard time on other grime like bugs, bird poop, and dried leaves.The saving graces in this kit include the microfiber towels, which feel a lot softer and finer than the typical microfiber towels I'd find in stores, and the wonderful sprayer and bottle. What I used to do in the past was pour in some car wash detergent in a spray bottle and mix with water. I'd use that for cleaning certain parts of a car in the summer. For instance, bird poop struck a part of the car. I'd use the sprayer and some paper towels to remove the acidic poop. I could see the Griot's Spray-on Car wash excelling in this department, but it would be far less expensive and just as effective to use a mix of water and car wash/wax detergent.As much as I like this kit and the Griot's brand, I honestly don't see the benefit to using this type of car wash kit. I'd recommend at least 5-6 towels at hand, and pray that none of them trap any grit that could scratch the clearcoat. My normal method of washing cars is using a bucket with a grit guard, chenille wash pad, and a hose of running water. The chenille cotton doesn't trap dirt at the surface of the nap and does a much better job of cleaning, while the grit guard ensures grit sinks to the bottom.Overall: 4/5 stars, not an ideal solution for washing cars. The sprayer and bottle are fantastic, and it is a great way to spot clean certain parts of the car. It is easy to use, but still freezes very easily in cold weather. Lots of towels are required for an entire car. I used half the bottle for just 4 door panels on my full-sized sedan.
summary: Not the best solution, but good quality product

reviewText: I used this kit over the winter when I couldn't get the car outside to wash it properly.  As you might imagine, it's best used for spot cleaning, washing the entire car this way takes a long time; however, it can be done.  When washing the entire car, it's best if you utilize two people -- unless you've got a lot of patience.  It's best to work slow.  This is not a matter of spraying the entire car down and then wiping it clean in 5 minutes or less.I found it best to work on moderate size areas at a time; a fender, half the hood, the roof, etc.  Spray the area liberally with the washing agent and then gently wipe the area with the include towels.  Don't rub too hard because the grit's still there.  Let the microfiber towels lift the grit off the surface and don't re-use portions of the towel that are visibly dirty.  The towels can be washed many times, but don't use fabric softeners, they interfere with the functionality of the microfibers.The washing agent works fine in loosening most dirt and grime (we're not talking mud, here!), the spray bottle is a quality product and the towels are perfect for their intended purpose.  Good kit.

I already have this in my garage, I use it quite often on my black car and it is great for those times when I do not want to drag everything out for a full-on wash. I am especially a fan of Griots premium micro fifer towels that come with this kit.

WOW I sure had my doubts about this stuff beacuse here in Nevada right now it ius very very cold! So I rode my bike the other day in the rain and it was real dirty so I used this spray on was and it worked just fine and did not even hurt the wax job unbelievable I really like this stuff it goes a long way I did just like it says to on bottle and my bike was clean and still looked GREAT!!!

works well, not sure that it works any better than similiar items. it does streak a lot but that may be because its winter time and it does not evaporate well. the microfiber clothes are top quality and thick.

First I'm not a big fan of washing cars without water, if you can't first rinse off the heavy loose dirt with water you'll end up grinding the dirt into the paint leaving marks that don't go away. The only time I'll use this produce is when I'm looking to clean minor dirt and water spots that form after rain. Cars get dusty sitting parked, when my car is dusty I use Griot's spray on wash and wipe off using the included soft micro fiber towel. I lightly spray one panel at a time then towel off, this product doesn't leave streaks or film, it does a good job lifting the dirt into the towel leaving a decent shine! This is great for car shows because it allows you to clean up anywhere fast doing a good job. Like I said I would only use this product for minor cleaning or touching up to make your car look good anytime any place.
summary: Easy waterless way to wash your car.

reviewText: First, let me qualify my review by saying that I didn't expect this product to clean a really dirty car and I would never clean a really dirty car by spraying any type of cleaner and wiping it off.  I can't imagine you would have good results and I'd be concerned about scratching the finish.  That said, I live in New England and it is not possible to wash the car in the driveway when it is 20 degrees out.  I won't go to the cloth or brush type car wash because they always scratch the paint, so I go to the touchless laser car wash.  The problem with the touchless type car wash is they don't clean the car very well.  They don't scratch but they do leave a cloudy film.  You just can't clean everything off the finish without some rubbing.So my purpose for this product was that I wanted something that I could use after going to the laser wash to make the car look like it was actually washed.  For that purpose, this product works fantastic.My car was heavily covered with salt and road grime after a recent storm.  We use a lot of salt on the roads up here.  I took it to the touchless laser wash to get the major grime off.  It came out like it usually does; cleaner but dull and cloudy.  You can see the outline of the wipers on the windshield and the mirrors and paint look dull.  I followed the instructions on the box and sprayed on the Car Wash, let it sit and gently wiped it off with the included towels.  The towels are very soft and thick and they worked very, very well.  It only took about 20 minutes to clean the whole car (a large SUV) and when I was finished, it looked perfect.  Even the windshield came out great.  No streaks when the sun hits it.  This product leaves the finish looking like you used a spray detailer so it looks better than when it is just washed with soap and water.So for my intended purpose, this product gets 5 stars.

This stuff works much better than other waterless cleaners I have tried for sure.  Here in New England we get harsh winters with lots of snow most of the time.  And good car wash places are not just getting expensive, but are also very crowded on nice days as well.  Cars around these parts get mighty dirty with all the road salt, and washing a car outside with water is out of the question for me when its really cold. This Griot cleaner is not just expertly formulated for waterless washing, but also does a great job of really deep cleaning your car. Not just a passable cleaning job, but a darn good one. I have a 12 year old truck that this stuff did an excellent job on cleaning thoroughly. No rinsing off first or scrubbing required.  It does a fine job by just spraying it on, and with very little running.  I used about half a bottle doing the truck, and that was with no sparing it. (The truck was really dirty, but not truly filthy.  I go along with the other reviewer here that suggests if your car is really a mess, go to a car wash first and then use this going forward as an in between). And I believe that over time when used regularly, one would get even better at using it more efficiently. The towels that came with it lasted throughout the job, but were extremely dirty at the end.  I very much advise anyone using this stuff to rinse out the towels in a sink when done before machine washing.  And if your car is not that dirty to begin with, a rinse and dry will be all you need for another job later on.  I really am amazed at how good this stuff worked in the cold.  It was 28o the day I used it and the truck came out looking great.  It may be a little pricey if used regularly, but as far as how good it works, it's the best I've used and well worth it in my opinion. Highly Recommended... : )
summary: Ideal For Cold Weather Cleaning...Works Great

reviewText: I have been using Griot's Car Wash (started out with this very kit) for years. In fact, I first purchased this product from Griot's when it was announced as a new product several years ago. I was already a user of some other Griot's products (Speed Shine, etc.) and trusted the brand.I have not yet purchased this product from Amazon (they must have just started selling it) but I have purchased it many times directly from Griot's Garage. I also purchase the 1 gallon refill size and ensure that I am never out of it. I really mean that - I have to have this on hand in the garage because I use it on an almost daily basis! Here's why:1. BUGS: For most of the year we have little (and sometimes not so little) flying insects that seem to be happy to sacrifice their lives in order to make the front of my cars a filthy mess. These tiny winged terrorists aim themselves at the front of my highway-speed vehicle and splatter themselves all over it. Yuck.2. POLLEN: Ah, spring... when love - but mostly pollen is in the air. This yellowish/greenish dust covers your car every day. One of our cars is black... and really shows up bad.3. LIGHT RAIN: Don't you hate it when you car looks pretty good, only a couple of days since you washed it - and then there is a light drizzle or a passing thundershower - and suddenly your car looks like it hasn't been washed in months! The light rain gets the car just wet enough to puddle up all that dust that was invisible into ugly dirt clumps, but doesn't rinse them away.4. BIRD POOP: Yeah. This is the worst. I don't know what some of these birds are eating... but what they leave behind on the hood, roof, and fenders of my cars is like a nuclear biohazard. The truth is, that bird droppings will etch the paint and even eat right through it if you don't remove it timely enough. And when it has "hardened" it can scratch the finish as you try to clean it off.For all these problems and more - enter GRIOT'S SPRAY-ON CAR WASH KIT to save the day. I keep this in arm's reach of both cars in the garage, and when I travel I take a small 8oz. bottle with me!HOW TO USE: The best way to use Spray-On Car Wash is just the way it comes in this kit. The finest sprayer does a very nice job of putting the product where you need it, and easily regulates the volume applied. For this wash, I recommend a mist application, but a liberal amount applied. This will coat the area to be cleaned well and minimize it running down the surface too quickly. If you are accustomed to babying your cars, then you know that it is a mortal sin to ever rub a dry dirty surface! Using the green terry towels (part of this kit) wipe the area that you've saturated, in a one-direction scooping type motion. What you want to achieve is lifting the dirt from the finish without dragging it across. It may take several wipes in a very dirty area to get it clean. Then, using a dry clean part of the towel (or another clean towel at hand) lightly buff the area you just cleaned. Don't put any weight or elbow into it... just let the towel buff it lightly. Now feel that - and look at the shine... AMAZING!I started with this kit years ago, and continue to reorder as needed to keep all the components on hand. The Finest Sprayer does a nice job of regulating the application of the product and is very easy and ergonomic to use. The towels that Griot's provides for his products are really good. These towels are so much thicker and softer than any microfiber towels I've ever found elsewhere. They last a very long time too, if you keep them washed after use.Even if your car gets dirty a lot - this 32 oz. size will last you awhile. I use mine very liberally and I can go months on a full 32 oz. bottle. I recommend this product very highly!! I have been using it for years, and I will continue to use it for many years to come!
summary: Unless you love a dirty car - this should be in your garage!

reviewText: First a couple advantages for waterless car washes.1) No water dripping from trunk, mirrors front grill etc causing spotting.2) You can lower your windows immediately without water streaking the outside of the window.3) You can do half your car take a break and finish it later or another day.4) Save a lot of money on brush-less car washes and no waiting in line. ($20 to $30 in my area)The towels are amazing. They are thick and plush and 15" square. I only needed 2 to do my mid size 4 door car including wheels and tires.My 1st use: My car was dirty from driving in the rain and wet roads for a week. The dirt and grime effortlessly wiped right off and then buffed up shiny (with 2nd towel). This cleaner seems to have a light wax in it. My paint finish was glossy and slippery when dry. It took me an hour to do a filthy mid sized car. I used less than 1/8 of the 35oz bottle. I'm sure I'll need lot less next time when my car is not so filthy...I even detailed the engine compartment with the damp cleaning towel without needing more spray. Looked really good after 20 minutes work.One WARNING: Hand wash the dirty application towel(s) before putting them in the washing machine. You'll be shocked how much dirt is in the towel(s). Even if you wash them by themselves in the washer, they'll surely leave a dirty ring in the wash tube and then you'll have to clean the inside of the washing machine. Not to mention your wife will be upset if you're married. :)Be sure to read the simple instructions on the bottle label......1st time using it was easy. No tricks needed or learning curve to get it right. Leaves a shiny lightly waxed shine. Don't worry about using this on an expensive car. Mine is a 2011 Infinity that looks like new. You will notice some light hazing in a few places that looks like wax not completely buffed. Just buff it with the towel. It comes off easily.Thank you to all the other reviewers who's reviews convinced me this product was worth a try
summary: WOW, does a great job even on filthy cars. I'm amazed!!

reviewText: I am totally UNimpressed.I ride a motorcycle, and as most people who ride, use waterless car/cycle wash products all the time.  I have tried many, many different varieties, and most are along the lines of this product, Griot's Garage 11285 Spray-On Car Wash Kit.  They leave much to be desired, leave bugs and road grime, and leaves a less-than shiny end result.That said, the towels are GREAT.The price is 29.99 for one bottle and three towels.  This is FAR overpriced.My recommendation--get the EZ Detailer!  It's awesome!  It applies evenly, cleans bugs and road grime, and leaves a SHINY bike.  You can see it here, but you can get it directly from their website by the case (that's what I do).EZ WAX 579221 DETAILER Waterless Cleaning Wax 4 PACKI think that if you buy them from the home  site, they sometimes send free towels with the order (cyclical special offer).I hope this saves you 30 bucks.  LOL

I should have read the product description more thoroughly.  This is great for cars that already look clean.  However, I live 3 miles up a dirt road, so this didn't work out well for me.  However, my son lives in a real city, and he doesn't need to drive much, so I tried it on his car.  It did a fair job of keeping his car clean, but then it wasn't that dirty to begin with.
Love love love this stuff great and very easy to use and it works without using a lot of it just a little goes a long way

This item is expensive but it works great. It really got my car clean without having to put too much effort into it. You spray it on your vehicle and wipe it off. I did it in sections so that the cleaning liquid wouldn't dry before I could wipe it. Obviously, to use this stuff is more time consuming than a normal car wash but it's serving a specialty need. You're going to use this product when you don't have access to the things you need to do a regular car wash (water, hose, sponge, soap, etc). I would buy it and then use it sparingly.

reviewerName: Raquel S. "Avid Amazon Fan and Kindle User"
reviewText: Griot's Spray-On Car Wash Kit is handy to have. It's pleasantly scented of coconuts that I really like a lot.For spot cleaning having this onhand is priceless. The cloths are nicely thick and take in a lot of dirt and moisture before its unusable and needs to be washed. Get rid of the offending dirt quick and easy.If you're doing a full-on clean, it will take a lot longer depending how dirty your car is, but you will have a nice smooth, glassy-shine clean when you're done.
