It did a pretty darn good job getting a my rather weather-filthy pick up truck clean without feeling like I'm scratching or otherwise destroying the paint. (I will post before/after pics to show.) There were stubborn leaf/sap stains that Griot's had trouble removing easily, but with persistance and time, they worked off too.Water is a definite no-no when it comes to cleaning my Trek bike. I now use the Griot's to clean my bike. Much better results than just a wipe down.I am very pleased with Griot's Car Wash Kit and would gladly buy again to keep onhand for both my cars and my bike.
summary: Does a surprisingly good job. Like using it on my Trek mountain bike too.

reviewText: I've used Griot's products for many years, but had not tried the Spray-On Car Wash before. I recently bought a station wagon that, as most do, collects dirt on the tailgate almost instantly. I sprayed the product on the tailgate and wiped gently with the cloths - the dust and dirt came off very easily.  The cloths are super-soft, though they left some lint behind. I expect this would go away after they are washed.I have tested similar product from other companies, and I like the Griot's best. It didn't drip and released the dirt from the paint very well, leaving a fairly clean surface behind. It's not a replacement for a regular wash, but as a touchup or when you can't do a regular wash, it works very well.
summary: Gets the dirt off - extra soft cloths

reviewText: I have been using Quick Detailers and Waterless Car Wash sprays to clean my vehicles for years.  Indeed, my two cars have had a minimal number of traditional car washings with water and bucket because I use these products so often.Therefore, I was extremely excited to try a waterless wash product that I had not yet tried, Griot's Garage Spray On Car Wash Kit.  A 32-ounce bottle of the waterless wash and and three microfiber clothes are included in a beautifully printed box.First reaction, it was fun to receive an entire kit with everything you need to get started.  If you have caked on dirt, mud, tar, etc. you probably want to stick with a traditional wash.  However, if you're like me, most of the time, it's simply dust on the car, so a product like this can work great.I immediately went to remove the tags that came on the towels.  Tags can potentially scratch the paint's finish.  While the towels seemed of high quality, the tags did not cleanly rip from the towel.  Therefore, I had to constantly make sure I was not using the portion of the towel where the tag was torn off.  The towels also seemed to become concentrated with the spray on wash quickly, but if it had not been for the tag issue, I would have liked them more or less.  They are approximately 12 inches by 12 inches.  I quite like Meguiar's Supreme Shine towels as the tags remove cleanly and they are a great 16 by 12 inch size.Second, the wash product itself was great.  It cleaned the dust on my vehicles nicely.  The spray nozzle was another slight weakness though.  There isn't a fine enough setting, so you get a lot of overspray.  This is not a problem when you're washing the entire vehicle with the product, but say you wanted to just "touch up" the front bumper or hood, you might find you get overspray on nearby panels and have to clean them too.However, the product left a great slick, smooth, and glossy shine.  It not only cleans, but adds a bit of slickness and shine too.Overall, Griot's Spray on Car Wash is up there with other quality quick detailers and spray on car washes that I have tried.  However, considering its price and slight flaws, I will be sticking with my Meguiar's products most of the time.  Meguiar's Ultimate Wash & Wax Anywhere is a superb product combined with Meguiar's Supreme Shine Microfiber towels.  I find the Meguiar's offering is overall probably a better experience at a lower cost.  Griot's offering is a good product, but for the price, it should be refined.
summary: Competent Product, Small Flaws, Potentially Cheaper Alternatives

reviewText: I use this on my car and it works. It was able to remove dirt, grim and dried bird crap without scratching up my paint. I use it on my windows and mirrors. The product does not leave a haze it leaves a nice shine. be warned if the clear coat on your car is not in good shape then this product may not give you good results. For example, I used it on my work van and although it was able to remove surface dirt it was not able to remove the oil marks that were on the paint/embedded in the paint(the clear coat on the van has uv damage) for those marks I had to use soap and water.

This kit comes with several microfiber cloths, a large jug of interior cleaner, and a pretty sizable bottle of leather care spray which was impressive, but overall, I'm going to ere on the side of caution with this particular leather kit.  It says it won't harm factory dyed leather, but after market leather is up for grabs.  It doesn't state what the ingredients are anywhere on the bottles or packaging, but it clearly has a very strong alcohol and chemical smell to the likes of hospital cleaner.  The smell dissipates after about 10 minutes, but I wouldn't say you have a brand new leather smell afterwards.  I have no doubts it will clean leather to within an inch of its lfe, but conditioning leather to a supple softness with moisturiing, not so much.I have not had the horror stories some may have had with it stripping the leather but I believe it's possible based on the smell.  If you choose to try it, definitely make sure you spot test an inconspicuous area first and make sure your area is well ventilated.  I think this would work wonders if you're dealing with a musty or mildewy smell, either way, I would recommend conditioning lotions and not the leather care spray after cleaning.  I've tried several leather cleaners and conditioners from coat and shoes accessories, to Blue Magic, to other name brands, with decent results and nothing that potent in smell.  I have to believe something that smells that industrial/alcohol laden can't be good for your leather long term.
summary: Not sure what's in it, and not sure it's worth the risk

reviewText: The inside of my Jeep Grand Cherokee is black leather.  As much as I love the black leather and the interior of my Jeep, dust might as well be neon and flashing with as well as it shows up on the surfaces.  I try to keep ahead of it, but over the winter, it was cold, and I got lazy.  By rights, before taking Griot's Garage 11259 Leather Care Spray Kit for a spin, I should have vacuumed the seats, dash, cupholders, inside panels of the doors- you know.  But it's still kind of nippy outside, and I was just lazy.Because it's been a little while since I cared for my car interior, and a little bit of grubbiness was also showing, along with the dust (I'd blame this on my toddler, but I'm messier than she is), I used the cleaner first, like the instructions say for especially soiled areas.  The bottle of cleaner in this kit is good-sized.  I used it liberally and also used the included microfiber cloths.  I have lots of microfiber cloths at home, and these are on par with the rest of my microfiber cloth collection, but I think you can't have too many of these cloths, since they get "borrowed" for other household chores, or wind up up at the garage.  The microfiber cloths clean well.  I was able to get into the crevices with just the cloth and my hand.  This cleaner works well on leather, plastic, and fabric.  It even isn't a tragedy if you accidentally get some on your windows.  It buffs right off windows, no streaks.  I probably could have gotten really particular and used a cotton swab to get into the really tight spaces, but I didn't take the time to do so today, and the Jeep still looks practically new inside!Like I said, it's been a little while since I've taken care of the inside of my car- pre-winter, we're talking.  So of COURSE I used the leather care spray in the smaller spritz bottle.  It looks really milky and viscous in the bottle, and the instructions say to spray it onto a microfiber first, and then apply it to the perfed leather, which I do have on my seats, so that's what I did.  On the areas that aren't perforated, though, I spritzed directly on the leather, and that was fine, too.  I wanted to make sure the dash area was really conditioned, so I gave the entire interior a once-over with the conditioner, and went back to give the dash a second helping.  The interior gleams now!As for the smell, the cleaner doesn't really have much of a smell, and that's fine.  The leather conditioner has a good smell- there used to be a store at the mall I frequented as a kid called Wilson's Leather.  When I'd walk by that store, it smelled like rich leather.  This leather conditioner smells just like that.I'm really happy with the way this kit performed on the interior of my car.Now, I also have a leather motorcycle jacket I've worn all winter.  I wipe the outside with a damp-dry cloth when I need to, but I figured the leather on it seems similar to the leather in my Jeep, and that jacket's been out in the elements all winter long, so I used the cleaner and conditioner on my leather jacket, and it worked great on it, too.  I know I could get a product made just for leather jackets, but the Griot's worked just fine on it, and I had the Griot's out, anyway.  And I think it's fun to find a two-fer use out of a product.I still have a lot of this product left, too.  As it gets warmer, there'll be no excuses for not keeping my Jeep's leather interior well-conditioned and well-taken-care of!
summary: A Little TLC For the Leathuh

reviewText: If you have been around vintage cars, you know that they are the best advertisement for taking care of leather. As someone who not only has a vintage car but vintage saddles, I pooh poohed most leather products for cars. I have used my saddle conditioner on the leather and found it superior. The important thing with leather is cleaning without drying it out and losing the flexibility. This is a car product that gets it. We have used it on an old Lincoln with leather seats and they feel like new. My skepticism went away quickly. Follow the simple directions and the results are great. Somehow they have incorporated a new car smell without a perfume sensation. My husband was thrilled with this package and now we each have our own leather products.

I am a car fanatic, and I have used practically every leather care product on the market as well as a host of Griot's products.  I will review each of the components individually.  Overall, my score is 4 stars.First, I'll say that one of the best features of Griot's products, in general, is the packaging.  For example, the Interior Cleaner comes in a nice wide-base round bottle with a good sprayer (more later).  When you are detailing a car, I can't stand cheap bottles with junky sprayers that are thin and fall over easily.  Often, you are carrying multiple things in your hands and need to rest the bottle down on something and having it fall over all the time and dribble out is annoying.  All the bottles are very high quality and clear so you can see how much is left and where the end of the pickup tube is.This kit contains 8oz of the Leather Care Spray and a separate pump spray nozzle. I was quite surprised by the Leather Care Spray.  It is an excellent regular-use cleaner and conditioner.  It leaves a very nice leather smell as well.  I would recommend it for leather that has been well maintained and in good condition.  What I REALLY like about this is that it does NOT leave a greasy, sticky mess behind like most other leather products.  A little goes a long way.  If your leather is in bad condition, look for something more like Leatherique.  The pump spray delivers a well-controlled fine mist, although sometimes it felt like it got stuck and I had to press extra firm.This kit contains 35oz of the Interior Cleaner and separate trigger spray nozzle.  Like the Leather Care Spray, both bottle and spray are packaged separately and sealed so that there are no leaks.  The sprayer is a very high quality and delivers a large volume per pump, but I found the spray pattern to be a bit large and often this led to overspray which I had to wipe over previous areas.  Like the Leather Care Spray, the Interior Cleaner is a mild, regular use product.  I used it on everything from leather, vinyl, to plastics, to even touch screens.  It was fairly all purpose and cleaned mild dirt well.  It did not remove heavy duty stains like some sunscreen on black leather, but that was to be expected.  This is not a miracle product, but an everyday maintenance product.  I felt this cleaner is a bit on the expensive side, but you can also buy a gallon refill bottle.  If you are really cheap, you can make your own refill and just use the excellent bottle.  It has a good amount of surfactants and did not leave streaking.Lastly, this kit contains four 16" x 16" green microfiber towels.  I would rate these towels as a "basic grade".  I have a LOT of much higher quality ones that I use for paint waxing, etc., but a good basic towel like this is better suited to the task at hand.  Can't fault them for that as it would just make the kit more expensive.  I also have much cheaper MF towels.In sum, this is a good kit for routine maintenance on well-cared-for interiors, and the bottles are nice and Griot's makes larger refills for the leather and cleaner sprays.  If you are expecting some super heavy duty miracle worker products, then I think you will be disappointed.
summary: Very good leather care kit for regular use

reviewText: A word about Griot's products. While never cheap, the overall quality and ease with which these products can be utilized makes them stand out. The instructions are carefully written and the behavior and tactile feel of the products is rarely less than exemplary. They just work well, as advertised.So, as expected.. the cleaner dissolved some fairly nasty, well-baked-in material from my "leatherette" dash cover and door panels - working better than the interior cleaners I've sampled in the past. While some stains in the carpets would not release, I was surprised by how many spots *did*.On the leather, the cleaner removed dirt while leaving the surface uniform in color and texture.The leather conditioner resulted in a more more supple feel and a nice smell. Unfortunately, it's not going to fix scratches - which I begrudgingly admit is normal patina for a leather seat. Careful use, and regular maintenance of your leather - over many years - is the only way to avoid the typical rips and tears of a dryed-out leather seat.
summary: Encourages You to Keep Your Car's Interior Clean

reviewText: I've got a 2008 prius with leather seats, and I'm pretty sure the last time it got a good going-over was a car wash in 2009. While I typically keep the windows up, I also live in a rural area in drought, so with all the dirt roads, there is always a ton of dust. So I had a pretty dirty job ahead of me.I used the cleaner and the cushy microfiber cloths on the textured dash, doors, console, and leather seats, and the combination of cleaner and cloths did an excellent job cleaning and conditioning every surface. It was quick, easy work. I was really impressed at how little effort and how little product I had to use.After cleaning the leather (and frankly, I was surprised at how beatifully the same leaner for the grimy dash worked on the leather--it even removed some kind of residue I was sure was a stain on the leather armrest), I used the conditioner on the leather, spraying directly on the solid leather and with a cloth on the perforated leather, as directed.It all looks awesome. The only thing not covered is the glass, which of course got streaky and needs a shot of windex.The cloths are really nice, not the cheap, thin microfiber you usually see. And the scent is very light, not at all bothersome even though I was using it in a closed car.
summary: Made my filthy car look great!

reviewText: ThisGriot's Garage 11259 Leather Care Spray Kitis just an outstanding product.The interior cleaner is simply the best I have ever used.  It was able to remove grime from the leather seats of my nine-year old car that I would not believe was there had I not cleaned the seats myself.  In fact, it removed "cooked" grime from a vinyl dashboard after just using another brand's cleaner.  The sprayer is top quality too and reusable, so the next time just get the refillGriot's Garage 11104 Interior Cleaner - 35 oz..The leather care spray is just another milder cleaner and conditioner that leaves (what my nose believes is) the original fresh leather smell of the seats.  I could just sit in the car for hours smelling away :-).  This stuff can make a common man (or woman) a leather fetish!This is it. I finally found the holly grail of leather cleaners.

This is a quality product and designed for the person who takes pride of ownership in their car.  Or, for the person who wants to improve the look of their leather or leather-type part of the car.I have several Audi's and the product applies very good.  It comes with 4 quality cloths, which are nice size and perfect to apply the product.  The "new car" spray is excellent as it does freshen things up and is a better alternative to products such  as ammoral.Prior to using this product I used Meaguire's, however this brand and the experience I have received might justify making a permanent switch.  Plus, I noticed Griot's has a full line of car detail products, which is great for DIY'ers like myself.

I've been using Griot's Garage products pretty much exclusively for the past 4-5 years for a couple of hobby cars I own, as well as for my daily driver.  Like everything else in the company's cleaning, waxing, and protecting lines the Leather Care Spray Kit is excellent.  The cleaner and the leather treatment spray do exactly what Griot's Garage claim they do, and the microfibre cloths that come with the kit are also suitable for using with the company's waterless car wash, the spray on wax, and any type of glass cleaner you'd care to use.  I'm not entirely convinced that the ratio of interior cleaner to leather care spray is going to be perfect for everyone, especially since the leather care spray also cleans to a certain extent.  Even if there's still quite a bit of interior cleaner left, though, it is a product that can be used on a wide range of surfaces, so there will always be a need for it.  Highly recommended products and a useful packaging idea for three products that can work in conjunction with each other.

I have used Griot's Garage products for years - almost exclusively for my cars of course. But for some reason I had never used the Griot's Leather Care. I have several other leather cleaners/conditioners in my cabinets, so I suppose I just figured I'd wait until I was low before giving it a try.Well, I finally did give it a try - as part of the Leather Care Spray Kit. First, here's what the kit contains:- 32 oz. of Griot's Interior Cleaner- Griot's "Finest Sprayer" for the above (a very nice adjustable sprayer by the way)- 8 oz. Leather Care spray bottle (sprayer is included)- 4 microfiber towels (appoximately 12" square)I have had the Interior Cleaner in my inventory of Griot's products for some time, so I am familiar with using it - and it works very well. But I had never really used it much on leather (mostly on the plastic and vinyl interior parts). Seeing that it was part of this kit - and obviously intended to be used on leather - I gave it a try. Works great!!Using the Interior Cleaner, and the green microfiber towel, I chose a formidable test area: a ivory leather couch... that my dog lays on. It gets filthy! I mean right down into the grain of the leather filthy. I usually clean with gentle soap and water and lots of elbow grease... and even then it never seems quite as clean as I'd hoped. The Griot's Interior Cleaner made much shorter work of the dirt than my usual method. Between the Interior Cleaner and the micro fiber towel, it realy gets into the deep grain of the leather and pulls out the embedded dirt. I was fairly astonished. I got the couch cleaner than I am usually able to - in about 1/4 of the time!Next step - apply the Griot's Leather Care, to condition and treat the leather (and clean whatever dirt still remains). Also using the microfiber towel (either a clean towel, or clean section of same towel), applying the leather care and using a gentle but deep wiping motion - back and forth - until the 'wetness' is gone. Then a light buff with a dry section of towel, and you're done! The leather is left with a very clean fresh look, and the surface is well mosturized but not slick or greasy. Running your fingers over it gives no "icky" feel of excess cleaner or the greasy film that some leather conditioners leave behind.Another noteworthy comment about the Griot's Leather Care is that it is (to my nose anyway) almost odorless. Some leather care products have a very strong and unpleasant odor. Some are almost perfumey... but the Griot's Leather Care is a very neutral smell. I actually stuck my nose into the towel after cleaning with it, trying to get a better idea of the smell - and it was still difficult to do.All in all, this is a great kit for cleaning and conditioning leather of all types. In the car, or in the house. I would even be willing to try it on leather clothing, like a jacket. I have not done that yet, but if I do I will update with comments. I will tell you first hand that you can trust it with the "white shades" of leather. I have various shades of "white" in one of my cars, and on family room furniture. Both cleaned up great with the Griot's kit with no side effects at all.
summary: Perfect kit for cleaning and conditioning all your leather

reviewText: I own a large number of Griot's Garage car care products and have always been a big fan.  This kit is no exception, it gets the job done, albeit at a high price.  The kit includes an interior cleaner, a leather cleaner/conditioner, high quality spray bottles for both, and a set of four micro-fiber towels.PROs------------------------------------+ Kit works well, as advertised+ Griot's spray bottles are the best+ Leather conditioner leaves no residue so you can sit on it right away+ Generous-sized towelsCONs------------------------------------- Minor linting from towels (very very minor, but there is some)- To do two cars, I think you'd need 8 towels (not 4)INTERIOR CLEANER------------------------------------The Griot's Garage interior cleaner has a bubbliness to it that hints at its cleansing properties.  I sprayed the cleaner directly onto the black rubber and leather surfaces of my two cars and then wiped with the towels.  My cars are always  fairly clean and, I think distilled water would have worked just as well.  I'm pleased that the cleaner air dries and leaves no streaks, even on glossy surfaces.  The end result was a spectacularly clean car interior that my wife commented on the next time she drove the car ("wow, clean!").  This kit includes the typically excellent Griot's Garage sprayer.  The pump is well built and will last a long time, even allowing for refills.LEATHER CLEANER/CONDITIONER------------------------------------------------------I later applied the leather cleaner/conditioner to the leather surfaces of two cars.  Both cars have smooth black leather and in each case I couldn't tell any difference after applying.  My assumption is that enough conditioner is soaking in to keep the leather fresh and supple over the long haul.  That is hard to judge after just one use so I'll keep my eye on this over time.The leather cleaner/conditioner leaves behind no residue; this is great because it means you don't have to worry about ruining your clothes after using it.TOWELS------------------------------------While the box that this comes in proudly claims "made in America", the four towels are clearly tagged "made in China".  That said, my experience with Griot's Garage microfiber has always been positive and these were quite good for what essentially amounts to rags.  The towels are generously sized and I used one towel per front seat for cleaning, and one towel per front seat for the leather conditioner. Unfortunately, since the kit only includes 4 towels, that means I can only do one car at a time.  I'd prefer to have 8 towels so I can do both of my cars.I was doing some hard scrubbing and the towels coughed up a couple of small lint balls.  This was so minor that I was hesitant to mention it.  But the guys that I know that buy products from Griot's Garage have high standards and they would have been angry to see green lint on their black carpet after doing the cleaning.  I'm washing the towels and will report back if the linting improves or worsens.SUMMARY------------------------------------This is another very good product from Griot's.  I only gave it 4 stars because there was just enough lint from the towels that some true car care fanatics would be upset.  At this price, you have to be perfect to get 5 stars.  But this is still a really nice kit and makes a very good gift for someone that likes to take great care of their cars.
summary: makes a great gift for car guys

reviewText: If you've got leather seats in your car, you know one of two things:1) Leather seats are a bear to maintain --or--2) Leather seats deteriorate fast if you don't maintain themI've been fairly partial toMeguiar's Gold Class Rich Leather Cleaner and Conditioner, I thought I'd give this a shot, and I'm glad I did. As a whole kit, it's a brilliant present to give someone, but even as something for yourself, the products work really well.While I can't say it restored the texture of my Charger's leather seats to like-new condition, it did a nice job working out some discolored spots, and the rest of the kit helped bring my interior back to the day I picked it up from the dealership.At this price, it's a pretty great value, especially if you visit an AutoZone or O'Reilly store and see how far this much money gets you in their car care aisles.
summary: Great gift, and the products really work.

reviewText: In includes:-Micro Fiber cloth wipes-Sprayers for both bottles-Interior Cleaner-Leather Care SprayUse Interior Cleaner first to get off the heavily soiled leather.  The Interior cleaner contains no dyes or chemincals that will alter the surface of the original OEM finish.  The leather treatment contains a mild cleaner which removes contaminants while maintain a supple finish.  It contains vital nutrients to help leather and wipes off.  It won't alter factory dyed leather.

reviewerName: Sean P. Logue "If you can't win, change the r...
reviewText: I love these Griot kits.  They take a few of their products, and package them together for a single purpose.  In this case, it is their interior cleaner, leather cleaner, and some microfiber cloths.My car has an off-white (actually ecru) leather interior.  I also have an eight year old daughter who rides in it and tends to get footprints in seemly impossible places.  Consequently, the passenger seats really needed a through cleaning.Using only the items in the kit, I first sprayed the seats down with the interior cleaner.  The large sprayer head made this easy.  Perhaps a little too easy - the seats were a bit wet!  I then wiped them down with one of the cloths.  Most of the dirt came off at that point, but there were some nooks and crannies that needed some rubbing.  I also cleaned the interior door handles with the cloth, which was now wet enough that I didn't need to spray.  The oil and grease came right off.Then I used the leather spray.  While the interior spray really didn't smell like anything, the leather spray is scented to smell like fine leather.  This was great, because after wiping down the seats my whole car smelled great!  The spray dried to a nice matte finish after wiping with a fresh cloth from the kit.This kit really works, and is easy and quick to use. So easy, in fact, that it would make a great gift to anyone with a car that has a leather interior.  Particularly if it is ecru.Highly recommended.Sean P. Logue, 2013

I have been a user of Griot's products for many years. Their Interior Cleaner I have used before and it is one of the best products of its kind I have tried. It cleans well, has no dyes or perfumes, and doesn't leave a residue behind. It's safe on many surfaces, including leather and vinyl.The Leather Cleaner was new to me and I tried it on my car seats. Unlike many similar products, it doesn't have a strong odor and isn't greasy. It cleans surface dirt well and soaks into the leather quickly, not altering the color at all.Griot's offers many different varieties of their microfiber cloths, color-coded for each use. These are thick and nicely textured, good for cleaning purposes.  I did not find they left any lint behind.I have taken to using the Interior Cleaner in the home as well.
summary: A great combination of products, for more than cars!

reviewText: I have no idea why Griot's Garage products are so expensive. They certainly get the job done, but so do other products from Armor All, Pledge, Windex, etc. The interior cleaning spray is fine, although it's better at light cleaning than intensive tasks like stain removal, which to be fair, it doesn't claim to do. Some people have indicated problems with the leather cleaner, but I haven't had the same issues. I recommend trying it on a small, out of the way spot to see how it reacts with your leather.The best part about this bundle is the microfiber towels that come with it. They're washable and high quality. I'll still be using them long after the Griot's cleaning solution runs out and gets replaced with some equally good, but cheaper substitute.

Griot products are dealer quality. I always wondered how dealers were able to impart that new car feel and smell to leather upholstery. Now I know. This is for any car enthusiast who wants the best quality leather care. I strongly recommend it.

I bought this to give my car a quick shine when i dont detail my car. Give you a shine just like you are using was and a buffer. Used with the quick detailer from Griot's Garage it makes your car look like you just detailed your car.

I received this on Friday and have already used 1/3 of a bottle shining my car and my fully faired motorcycle with bags.  I have not seen the car or the motorcycle shine so good since I purchased them from the dealers.  The included soft shining cloths are great and work extremely well to buff up the shine.  I highly recommend this to those who are car "buffs".

I needed some more of the Speed Shine, but saw this and decided that I also needed some microfiber rags to go along with it. These rags are awesome feeling. Works really well with the speed shine to deliver a smooth, even finish.

Dusty or dirty? Use the Speed Shine Kit. The wash cloths are so great and works perfectly with the product they are intended to work with. They are so soft, good absorbents, and smooths the car the way they should. Not a single scratch from these towels.The cleaner itself just works. Removes dusts with light spray, and light dirt with moderate spray. Smells good too!Verdict: I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT.
summary: Must-have car product for car lovers.

reviewText: Was not sure what to expect, but this stuff certainly delivers a great shine with little effort. I will definitely be buying the gallon-sized refill in the future.

I have been using Griot's Speed Shine for about a decade. If I could only have one car care product - this would be the one, without hesitation. Speed Shine is not only in my garage within easy reach, but I carry a small 8oz. bottle in each car, along with a blue towel, for on the road needs.Speed Shine has many useful purposes, and excels at each:1. Quick detailer. Use Speed Shine to do a quick dusting of your car, remove a small bird or bug mess, or just shine it up!2. Lubricant for clay bar. Speed Shine makes a perfect (and recommended) lubricant for clay bars. Keeping a mist of Speed Shine on the clay and paint is crucial to proper lubrication and effectivness of the clay.3. In-between-wash touch-up. I often use Speed Shine to clean up an area of the car that has gotten dirty, such as puddle-splash on the rocker panels or some light bugs on the front, etc. I have even used Speed Shine to clean my windshield! Yep. Works great too (the secret is to buff it well with a dry towel).This kit contains a 32 oz. bottle of Speed Shine, which will last you a long time (even if you use it often like I do). Three very nice microfiber towels (these towels are soooooo soft and fluffy), and the Finest Sprayer. The sprayer is good because you can dial up just the right amount for your application. The squeeze trigger is ergonomic and easy to operate.I can't say enough about Griot's Speed Shine. It is the best quick detailer I have ever used. I also use it for exterior glass, and of course as lubricant for clay bar. It is the single most used car care product I have in the garage!!
summary: An absolute MUST HAVE in the garage!

reviewText: I love love love this company. I'm a new customer and just tried this for the first time. It works like magic easy to get off and help me keep that awesome shine on my car in between washes. I've purchased other stuff and it works great as well.

I will start by declaring that I am a great fan of Griot's Garage products.  They make a range of car cleaning and finish-maintenance products which work and which, of equal importance, I feel are SAFE to use on my car.  Based on my experience in using their products for years, I use them with confidence that they do not contain harsh chemicals which will damage the finish of the paint, leather or plastic surfaces of my car.  They are expensive, but I find that I am more comfortable using Griot's products that many off-the-shelf, less expensive products sold at Auto Parts stores or large chain/discount retailers.I am equally pleased with the Interior Kit, consisting of Cleaner and Vinyl and Rubber Dressing with applicator pads and cloths.  The Interior Cleaner works.  A stubborn stain may require multiple applications of the product, but I would rather apply a milder cleaner several times than risk damaging a surface with a stronger cleaner.  That said, my personal preference is to use the Griot's dedicated leather cleanerGriot's Garage 11142 Leather Care - 16 oz.for my leather surfaces rather than a more all-purpose cleaner such as the Interior Cleaner even though it says it is safe for leather surfaces.The rubber and vinyl dressing works well.  I have applied it to the rubber door and trunk seals on several cars and the dash on one car.  I like the fact that there is no pronounced smell or excessively glossy surface when applied to plastics (unlike Armor All).  Before applying the dressing to the rubber door and trunk seals on cars that are a few years old, it is wise to clean the rubber thoroughly using the Interior Cleaner or Griot's rubber cleanerGriot's Garage 11136 Rubber Cleaner - 35 oz..The microfiber towels work well and although the sponge applicators perhaps do soak up some of the product, they are often the most convenient method of applying the product.  In any event, I would not soak the sponge applicators to the point of saturation, however, as this could lead to drips and waste of the product.  Further, any of the product that migrates deep into the sponge can always be released by merely pressing a little harder on the surface to which you are applying it.In addition to making good car care products, it also may be useful to some to note that Griot's is also good at sourcing and selling hard to find or extremely useful tools.  I have purchased many over the years (e.g. solid, machined aluminum, lifetime water hose sprayer, no-drip caulk gun, a cam-locking bed separator gate for pickup trucks, etc.).
summary: Great Cleaner and Dressing  - Work Well and Are SAFE

reviewText: Griots is always good quality cleaning supplies, but their products do not like temperature fluctuations. If you leave it in an area where is will freeze most of their products will separate. You can still use them after you vigorously shake them up and let them sit for awhile, but you will not get great results. This is particularly true of the speed shine product. Keep them stored indoors / not in a non heated garage and you will be satisfied. I have tossed quite a bit of Griots over the years because my garage is not heated and just not enough in house storage room for everything.The interior cleaner here is nice and does not have that funky smell of a lot of interior products. The biggest advantage or plus is that griots won't deteriorate your vinyl, leather, and plastic parts like armor all does when its hit by the sun. If you can get used to the price Griots will be your friend.

Griots has a good reputation for quality detailing products, and this kit is a good example of that.  The Interior cleaner works well without a strong smell, and lacks dyes and perfumes that would gunk up your interior (nothing worst than a chemical smell that lingers after detailing- too many cheaper cleaners have that).  The vinyl and rubber dressing is easy to apply, has UV protectant (a plus in my book) and dries to a nice finish.  Even the consumables like the pump head, sponge and the nice microfiber cloth (which you never can have too many of, trust me) are nice quality items.  And once you buy the kit Griots also sells larger refill sizes here on Amazon which will save you some money.  All in all, a great start for those looking to detail the interior of their cars with a proper set of tools with an all in one bundle.

This is a nice little detailing kit that I keep on a shelf in the garage next to my car - it's very easy to pull in, get out, and grab the leather/vinyl cleaner for a quick wipe down!  The cloths are high quality and look the same after a few washes.  Recommended!

The dashboard spray included is OK stuff and leaves a clean finish on your dash. The microfiber cloths are good for application. Use one for the spray and one to clean up the over spray. Unfortunately you will have over spray with this applicator but it comes off the windshield pretty easily. I just would prefer an applicator that can be better focused on the nozzle to minimize the amount of liquid on the glass. The rubber dressing works alright and applying it with the sponges is easy although they have a tendency to soak up the liquid when you first start using them. Once they get a little saturated they work fine but that ends up wasting some of your dressing. All in all a decent kit but you can buy the same or better products from different manufacturers at a cheaper price.
works nice and has a good scent. seems to be a notch better than the average product. the microfiber cloths are are really nice as well...worth the money.

My leather seats were a lot dirtier than I thought.  This product picked up a lot of dirt.  The micro-fiber cloths are good but once they become dirty, your just spreading the dirt around.  I used paper towels and Q-Tips for most of the job.Everything was clean when I was done and my interior looks like new in my 10 year old car.I didn't try cleaning my rugs but I did clean a stain off of a floor mat.  It worked well and didn't discolor the carpet.  All things considered, this is a good product but you need to be willing to put in some time to really clean the car's interior.After everything was clean, I applied a leather conditioner to my seats.  This helps keep the leather supple and prevents it from cracking.
summary: Picked up a lot of dirt - Nice!

reviewText: This is all you need to complete your interior car cleaning needs. The products do not leave and oily residue and have a fresh scent. The cleaner does a teriffic job and the cleaning towels, sponges accent the job.

This product came with everything needed to clean out the inside of a car.It came with:-Sprayer for both bottles.-Interior Cleaner-Sponge-Vinyl and Rubber Dressing-Soft wipes made of clothIt has no dyes, perfumes or other comtaminants to discolor the surface your cleaning. For use on vinyl, carpet, cloth, headliner, and leather.The Vinyl and Rubber Dressing contains no oils, petroleum distillates, waxes or other dangerous solvents that can harm or dull vinyl and rubber over time.  Cleans and protects in one step.This product works very well and leaves the inside of a car very clean.

Griot's has a reputation for excellence in car care accessories and cleaning solutions. Although some of their products are excellent, I found their cleaning solutions to be no different than virtually anything else. For example, they make some cool little brushes that help you clean in the tiny spaces in your dash board and instrument panel. I can see paying good money for a quality, specialized cleaning tool. What I can't understand is why their cleaning solution costs so much.I might pay extra if the solution is particularly powerful, or if it's non-toxic, or something like that. Considering that the cleaning power (in my experience) is equivalent to other options (e.g., Armor All, 409, Windex Interior spray), I don't see any reason to pay for "high end" cleaners. Each of those cleaners has a special power: Armor All makes your car shiny and kind of sticky, 409 seems to break down tough stains and disinfects, and Windex works well on glass as well as any mildly dusty surface. Griot's interior cleaner seems to be a general formula that isn't especially good at anything other than the general cleaning of dust and light dirt off your interior.The microfiber cloths and sponges are actually pretty decent. They don't justify the price, but at least I'll have something to use in the future when I buy another bottle of Armor All.

The Griot's Garage product cleans well but you probably could just as well use windex (like I used to) to clean the interior of your car.  The difference is that the vinyl and dash protectant is much better than the Armor All and other products that leave a greasy slippery finish.  I will say that Griot's is a little on the pricey side, but you do get some nice foam pads to apply the protectant and some nice microfiber cloths to clean.

These are excellent windshield wipers packaged with multiple adapters to allow mounting on a wide range of arms (including mine, which are the "post and hook" or "P&H;) variety.I simply removed the originally installed adapter (a twist with needle-nose pliers took it right out), replaced it with the P&H; adapter and slipped it on the arm.It wasn't raining when I installed them, but I've been using this model for about three years, and find them superior to the OEM blades that came with my car. They make firm contact with the windshield, and wipe without streaking, squeaking or chattering.Although I do treat the windshield with the included activation fluid (which is supposed to create a beading effect: wipe on, wipe off and run the wipers for three minutes), I think the wipers are the key to this equation, and they work very well.This wiper was for the driver's side. The passenger side of the my car takes the19" modelwhich performs similarly.Winter months in the mid-Atlantic are marked by the infamous "wintery mix" (snow, sleet, ice, freezing rain..sometimes all at once, or in a matter of minutes). These wipers stand up well to all of these.
summary: Excellent wipers (even if the value of the "activiation fluid" is debatable)...

reviewText: These wipers work well on my 2500HD Pickup although a bit pricey I think they are worth the extra money.

Great wipers. They came with a sponge which I guess is a rain-x application for the windshield and combined they work way better than the cheaper ones I got at the auto store by my house. Just be sure to follow the instructions when applying the sponge. As for the wipers, no streaks and no dragging across the glass. Smooth and easy.
I have been using rain-x products since the mid 70's and have never been disappointed with anything they make.  Price was right and I received it fast.
summary: Best wiper I have ever used

reviewText: Good price fast delivery.  Have been using rain X for both my cars for several years.  Very good product.

for this price and quality and the buzz, i expected more.  The wiper is really like any other out there, so nothing special about that (especially if you treat the windows with the Rain-x yourself).BUT given its large length, it looses friction toward the tips. you can see that it leaves some water behind.Updated: the wiper is loosing traction and even after cleaning the blade it still doesn't "wipe" as well as it did the first days.  This is bad since i've only used it a couple of times in the past 3 months of purchase.
summary: the far edges are the issue

reviewText: These new wipers are excellent. They do a good job and are very quiet. They come with blue protectors that slip over the wiper blade. It really helps to remove these. At first I thought they were supposed to be left on! Stupid me....Here it is months later and I still love these wipers! They are excellent performers. I'll never use anything else!

These wiperblades installed easily and quickly on my 2004 Ford Excursion Limited, and upon use are the best wipers I've had on any vehicle. No streaking, squeal, or chatter. Smooth motion and vivid visual clarity in heavy rain. I'll continue to use this brand and model blades on all my vehicles. They are high quality and worth the price.
summary: Super slick wiping without squeaking or streaking, no chattering

reviewText: Once winter hit and the road salt got on the blades they began causing a LOT of smearing. I would highly recommend Rain-X Latitude but not this.
summary: The repel formula seems to leave smears

reviewText: These wipers are noisy and leave streaks. I could tell they weren't well made right when I took them out of the package. You get what you pay for.

I bought a set for my car about 4 years ago.  I recently bought a replacement set for the same car, but I'm switching the old ones to my weekend car since they are still functional.  I loved them so much I want my dad to experience the goodness of the product.  It was simple to remove and to install the new ones.  Each blade comes with a Rain-X wipe.  USE IT!!! Read the direction and treat your window(s).  You won't regret the effort you'll get from the treatment.
summary: Loved it for myself.  Buying this as gift.

reviewText: These are on my 1995 honda accord, they work good. Four months later they are still working good. These work in all weather conditions. A great buy for any car.
This product works well, not sure yet of the lasting affect..time will tell...good purchase
Yea I am not impressed with the oily way it goes on and how long it lasts. When I finish this bottle I will for sure try a different product.
If you want it really, really black and shinny, this is the stuff.  Much better than a tire shine and it works on tires also but as an interior product, none is better.

I have never seen a product that turns vinyl and rubber pitch black with a high gloss finish, I detailed my engine compartment with this stuff and it looks brand new. My car is 13 years old and the wiper arms and windshield cowl also came out looking brand new. It seems to last a long time and after 1 month it is still working.

I use this on my 99 Isuzu Rodeo on the few black plastic trim pieces. This makes the color go from dark grey to a rich black. It's very easy to apply and I would purchase again. I do have to reapply after a few washes, but I find that acceptable.

I've seen advertisements of this type of product on infomercials on TV and always thought it was full of crap. Despite by skeptics on this product I decided to give it a try and I am glad I did! This product is a clear solution so it isn't dying your trims, it physically embeds into your weather damaged trims to make it look brand new. The product is UV activated which helps your damaged trims absorb the solution into it's surface. It is also rubber safe, I also wiped down my rubber window linings with this product and it works like a charm without leaving residue or grime. Would recommend this product to anyone who is a car fanatic.
summary: Thought it was a gimic but actually works!

reviewText: not much to add that hasn't been said, but this did work well to find coolant leaks on my '01 Regal (was the plastic coolant elbows by alternator) and on my '93 Ford work van (just a loose hose clamp)  So it easily paid for itself in saved mechanic costs already.  Recommend having one on hand for the shade tree mechanics like me.Also used it to test the radiator caps on both these vehicles, since I now could.  :)

Not a commercial tool but for the backyard mech. it is perfect.  Solved my leak problem within 15 minuets of receiving the shipment.Most likely the plastic caps would not hold up for everyday shop use but perfect for my needs.

Mityvac MV4560I needed an inexpensive pressure testing kit, and I've been using Mityvac's plastic brake bleeder kit for years without any problems. So the MV4560 looked like a great deal for a DIY mechanic like me.I used this on a late model Ford, which uses the designed yellow cap for the system (MVA353). However, in order to test the radiator degas bottle cap, I could not use MVA410 as identified in the instructions. Instead, I have to use MVA350 in conjunction with MVA411 - which are not identified correctly for my application!The plastic nuts that hold down the clear tubing could possibly break if tightened too much, so be careful!Overall: 5/5 stars, inexpensive kit for a DIY mechanic. For something that you will use on a daily basis, consider upgrading to a more durable test kit.
summary: Easy to use, but directions are wrong for some applications

reviewText: I purchased this tool because I was trying to track down a coolant leak on an 04 gto. The item came with the correct adapter. The tool worked like it should and I found the leak. Handy tool, I'm very satisfied!

Just tested mine today on two new radiator caps (1.1 / 16lbs). Guess what ? the cheap cap only could hold 10.4 lbs of pressure and the quality cap holds a solid 15.7 lbs.  Talk about accurate. Most pressure gauges I come into contact with are way off (like 5 - 15 lbs off) and its surprising to find one in a value kit thats very accurate. The kit comes with caps that fit virtually all common vehicles and some uncommon ones. The overall built quality is VERY good for the price. Very, very sturdy caps and sturdy,rugged adapter neck. Solid, thick, no nonsense rubber seals on the caps. The only flaw is, might be the pump itself, as this is made mostly of plastic, and anything thats made of plastic that gets repeatedly flexed gets worn down very quickly. But again the price is a major factor in selling point. After all, its not meant for commercial purposes, its for home use. As such, we should not go out and test 100 cars with it.The manual is a bit on the o.k. side. But more work needs to be done in that area. The manufacturer places too much emphasis on repeated safety rather thanwhy the diagnosis is accurate in (that user) instance. Meaning, in some instances the diagnosis is a bit ambigious. To say that the problem MIGHT BE the head or block, you should change the gasket - is not really comprehensive enough.Its definitely a must buy for home mechanics. Definitely a 5 star product. Absolutely glad I bought it. Its possibly the cheapest quality tester on the market right now.
summary: Best-value cooling system tester on the market

reviewText: I am trying to diagnose an overheating issue on my delorean but one of the Mityvac caps is leaking and unable to test cap pressure.  I am trying to get a replacement or warranty service  but it is so hard to get a hold of company. I discovered a leaky cap issue after 30 days so cannot return to Amazon. Based on other reviews, leaky cap seems to be a common problem.Other than a leaky cap, price was good and it measured coolant pressure well.  I wish it had more adapters so that I can use it on other cars. For example, It won't work on my lotus.  Lack of available adapters make this less useful in long run.I am going to keep try to get a replacement part.  If successful, I will change my 1 star rating.Update: Mityvac company refused to honor their 1 year warranty since Amazon is not their authorize dealer.  However, when I contacted Amazon about this, Amazon mailed me a new one with next day shipping.  I am giving 5 star to Amazon for standing behind products that they sell and their impressive customer service.  Zero star for Mityvac company.
summary: Zero star for Mityvac but 5 star for Amazon

reviewText: Works great, but make sure you have a spray bottle of soapy water to check for air leaks on fittings when you pump it up, if the hose is not cut straight & pushed on all the way will leak. you can buy more hose at the hardware if you need it. found a bad cap on Kawasaki teryx with it also. great tool for the money if you can't find a leak or test a cap.

Nice and simple, put the adaptor on, connect up and pump pump check !Simple way to pressurize your cooling system to find leaks while the system is cold and the engine not running.Whilst the kit is all plastic (except for the internals of the caps) it seems heavy duty and well made.Only down side is no case. I normally hate blow moulded cases for tools but for speciality tools you need one.

I work on my own cars and motorcycles  I had a leak in one bike I couldnt find,, the adapter worked fine,, dont think I would want this if I did pressure test every day, but if you are not a gorilla I think it will last forever
As described. Really works so far. I've used it as a regular stabilizer and it works great. Very sturdy and well made
They work surprisingly well. I honestly had no idea just how much these would stabilize our RV and I'm very glad I was talked into getting them

Purchased these to stabilize the slide out on our trailer and its a night and day difference. It never really felt like we had a lot of sway before but after installing these the change was very evident. Nice and compact for storage and very smooth and easy height adjustments.
summary: A must have for slide outs..

reviewText: I have intended to get something like this for a long time.  I've been concerned that our superslide would start to sag over time.  It is 12 feet long and slides out 3 feet.  We have never had a problem with the slide, but I don't want to create one either!  We are now planning on a long term trip around the US and felt I should finally get these.  I'm not disappointed.  Others have stated that it stopped, or at least cut down, on the RV shaking.  We have a large family, so I doubt I'll cut down on the movement much.  My primary concern is that we don't cause the slide's functionality to deteriorate.  We have used these jacks now in our driveway, our side yard, and in a state park for a long weekend.  I am very satisfied with how well they work.  They are simple and straightforward.  I don't really know what the long term affect of using vs. not using them would be, but I am convinced that they will help as they are very sturdy and easy to use.  Also, I like that they are fairly small (narrow) for what they are.  They don't have a flared out tripod base which would take up more room when stored for travel.
summary: Exactly What I Had Hoped For

reviewText: After buying a new trailer with a slideout, I started reading reviews on stabilizers. This one seemed to be the best bang for the buck. Not much to go wrong here, screw threads and a hefty nut with a welded handle. Powder coated steel tube should resist corrosion and rust for many years. The only negative in my opinion is the base, it could be a little larger diameter but I use jack pads anyway. So far so good...

I bought two sets for my 38' 5th wheel with 3 slides they mount nicely under the two rear slides and stabilize them very well. The only flaw I have found if you don't have to extend them very far( around 6" until it clears) the adjustment bar hits the slide rail and you can't take full turns to tighten it so you have to kind of play with them a little longer than you should.

We had a hailstorm which dropped some baseball sized hail here, and there was a lot of golfball sized hail also. My brand new, two week old, camper took a pounding which broke a couple of these lights and punched a hole through the vent cover. The orange/yellow plastic part snapped right on and even looked to be sturdier than what had been installed on the camper. I'm please with the replacement.
And got a bulb out of the deal. Couldn't find these lenses locally so this option worked good. Needed the lenses to replace missing ones on my Skyline camper trailer.
summary: Cheaper to buy this assembly than just the lense

reviewText: The quality of the light fixture is good.  There is no base gasket provided with the fixture.  I used silicone to seal it to the camper.  Would  have been better with a foam gasket.
summary: Bargman 34-59-002 #59 Series Amber Clearance/Side Marker Light

reviewText: I bought this to replace a missing lens on my camper.  My lights look like this one, and this full light assembly was about a buck cheaper than buying just the replacement lens.(plus if it is not the same size I could just put the new light on... and have a spare bulb...)Turns out it was not quite the same size.  But it was extremely close.With a little squeezing and pushing I got this lens to snap onto my old light.  It fits very tight so it should not blow off.Even though I didn't use the entire light, I can still say that it looks nice.All the parts of this light look well made.The lens is a nice clear color that really catches the light better than my old ones.If you don't want to drop the big bucks on LED marker lights then this one is a good way to go.
summary: Good for use as replacement lens

reviewText: The two upper clearance lights on my 5th wheel had seen their better days so I purchased these lights as a replacement.  They were very easy to install and luckily I was able to use the same holes as the factory lights.  I put clear silicone around the bottom of the lights before installation which made it waterproof.  Would highly recommend these clearance lights for an RV application.

What can one say about an anode rod? It either fits the tank or it doesn't.  This one went into a Suburban SW6DE and fit fine.  I'm assuming its chemistry will behave accordingly in my tank and do its job.  Price seems good - recommended!
summary: Fit my SW6DE like a glove!

reviewText: pure magnesium anode is the best choice for my application.  Will buy again in 2 summers to keep the heater from rusting
Fits my 6 gallon water heater in my 35ft Keystone Laredo. Looks just like the one that came with it.
Very happy with this Anode Rod. I hadn't replaced mine in my 5th wheel trailer water heater for 5 years didn't even know it was there. This one worked fine.
This was a direct replacement for my aging anode rod in my RVs hot water heater.  Installation was very easy and straight forward.
Perfect match for a Suburban RV water..  My experience is that it will last a year.  Put a deep well socket on it to assist in getting it started when threading it in.

I replace the anode in my water heater each year when we put the mh away for the winter. These rods last longer and work better than the oem anode. We use our mh a lot except during January through April and so I think these are well worth the price.
summary: Lasts the full year and still works

reviewText: A perfect solution to the uncontrolled oil drainage on the Ford F150 with EcoBoost motor. The first oil change (without the Fumoto installed) was an oily mess. This valve makes it much more manageable.  The valve appears to be of good quality. I didn't need the adapter and if installed it would cause interference with the transmission to cooler lines.I would recommend this product to anyone who does their own oil changes.

If you have one of the newer "sealed" automatic transmissions...YOU NEED THIS IN THE PAN!!!Sealed for life means your burned fluid, which likely happened before 50K miles, will end your transmission's life before 115K miles, if you even get that far.Put one of these in the pan, though, measure how much drains out, then, using a small hand pump, like $8 from Hazard Fraught, put back the exact amount which drained out.  Repeat every-other-oil change, and your transmission, and wallet, will thank you.

Fits and works will on my 2012 F-150 EcoBoost.I installed it to avoid the mess of changing oil (the drain points sideways and oil sprays everywhere).Now I can just put on a rubber tube and drain it right to the pan.
summary: Fits and works well on my 2012 F-150 EcoBoost

reviewText: Been using Fumoto Valves for over 30 years.  They work, have never leaked a drop and make oil changes a breeze.

now i can do my oil changes without any wrenches.im worried about clearance issues a little bit, since the valve and hose nipple sit ~1.5" lower than the drain plug.i also placed a vacuum cap over the nipple for added dirt protection
Installed this drain on my avalanche. It makes quick work and clean work for an oil change. I have lots of trust in FUMOTO because they are quality parts. Thank you~!

This ladder is nice to have making it a lot easier to get in the bed of my 2004 Ranger Step side. Easy to install, the only problem is with the Velcro strap as it is too short. I made sure to install it as in the video with the D-ring flush to the ladder frame and the screw directly underneath the ladder frame but it was still too short.Video ---> ( http://youtu.be/Zmqy-TmXUZU ) ... Look @ 4:30 min.I emailed the company from their "contact" tab on their web site and received a response within 1 hour, they are sending a new strap. They probably had a quality control problem and corrected it since some are getting short straps at 4&1/2 in. and others are getting the correct straps at 5&1/2 in.Edit: 10-20-13.I received the new holding strap and installed it, works as it should.But I noticed that the weld joints are now starting to rust. The Ladder is mounted under a Tonneau cover and has not gotten wet.I ended up re-painting it with gloss black Rustoleum.

Easy as pie to install.But I did have to remove the tailgate support on my old 86 F250,no problem.Used the ladder,seems good & sturdy.If I experience the rust problems as others,ill have to use some spray paint I guess.The d-ring & strap worked fine,but needs another one which I guess ill make my own.Time will tell if this will last very long.

I should have bought one years ago, what a treat. No more climbing up onto bumper, then tailgate, no more slipping off either. works as advertised. Easy install too, attach a magnet to your drill bit to keep some of the fillings from falling into the drilled holes.

I have a new 2014 Ram 2500 diesel, and this was the only one I could find that was tall enough. However, I had to modify it for my truck since I added heavy duty bumpers. The material could be heavier, and the welds could be stronger, but I'm 100 lbs over the rated capacity, so adding a few more welds ensured that it held. The hardware kit was also a bit flimsy for my needs, so I replaced the bolts and used insert rivet nuts. These mods will probably not be necessary if you are within the rated 250 lbs stated for this product.

The options for assistive devices to access your truck bed and everything but this is horribly expensive. This product arrived with a damaged box, so it could have been the reason why one velcro strap was missing. in any case the company corrected the problem immediately when I called.Easy installation with good instructions. This IS NOT the $500 steel step that slides under your truck. It is a very inexpensive, useful alternative. I am an old fellow and I needed to be able to access my truck bed and tool box, and I couldn't afford the alternatives. The tailgate ladder is a great alternative. It folds up out of the way and when I put my tailgate down, I can fold it out and have easy access. My little grandson really likes it--he can climb right up and help grandpa.You won't get a better bang-for-your-buck or better support than with this product.
summary: Great product for this price range

reviewText: This net will work out real good..The quality is very good..well worth the price...this arrived nearly 2 weeks ahead of schedule. I givethe seller a big "thumbs up. " excellant...

reviewText: This product stretch's and stretch's and holds its shape after many uses in both hot and cold weather. I highly recommend this product.
first time i bought a cargo net but i am happy i did.this thing can stretch and attach to anything.
I got these in delivery and found they work very well and I did sell my scooter so never did get my moneys worth

Not sure why some are grumbling, I am loving this thing. Mine came with metal hooks with plastic no scratch caps, they seem quite strong. I am using the net on my BMW F650 stretched from pannier to pannier, for that it works great and holds my book bag quite well. I would say this would be much too large to be of much use on a bike without panniers, it is more the size of a quad rack.So if you have a need for a large stretching net, this one is the one, if you need a small one, look for another.

I haven't used it yet but it looks good and stretches across the back of my bike.  The hooks have little plastic caps which may not last long but they seem fine now.  This thing was long in coming as China is a long trip.  I would recommend this $3.50 net

This is a good strong net. It's bigger than i expected, but the clips can easily move around the net, so you can essentially make it smaller for whatever you are trying to carry. I use it to keep a backpack or other bags on my bike when needed. Could fit a helmet under it if needed. I recommend.

I purchased a Kent Bayside Adult Trike and wanted a two-wheel cargo hauler; price efficient with folding/removable side bars and 110lb capability. I ride it to Walmart and have received numerous comments about it and the trike. I purchased this cargo net and it fits the cargo hauler perfectly.

Here's one:B003M694T2
Not bad for a Buck Fifteen and free shipping , buying extras.....cheaply made but should last a couple of years anyway! I'm happy!

Worried about the plastic hooks a little with age I know they get brittle but for the price seems can not go wrong.

keeps the helmet on the back pad very tight, able to carry other items as well with out having to stop and check to see if it's still there. i highly recommend this product.
I keep it in the saddle bags in case I need it.Hope it will do what I need when put to use.Stored in the unopened package for future needs.

I decided on the larger size of net to make sure it could handle any item i needed to secure. i was glad i did!, this is the best size for me and is easy to use. its strong and when you secure stuff with it it stays there.

I used this fluid to flush the brakes on my 06 Beetle TDI, and it worked fantastically well.  The old fluid was so dirty that there was really no need to use a product like Super Blue, because the fluid turned from brown and dirty to a clear amber, like a delicious hefeweizen.  You'll know when you've bled enough.  I also used the Motive brake bleeder to apply pressure to the brake fluid reservoir so I could bleed the brakes myself.  Worked great, and the stopping power is fantastic in my Beetle.  I'd stick with this high quality stuff over Autozone or Napa stuff, to make sure your vehicle performs as well as it possibly can.

THIS IS NOT YELLOW .IT IS CLEAR < NO USE FOR EXCHANGING BRAKE FLUID IN SYSTEM.I wanted yellow or blue to see exchanged fluid .Not possible with this item.Beware you wil be unable to return this can through  Amazon.

I'll keep it short and simple since there are thousands of praises for ATE fluid. If you own a BMW that requires DOT 4, don't look further.  Yes it costs more than Oreillys brand brake fluid but you are paying for quality.  Too bad US banned the colored fluid, made bleeding brakes much more accurate
I like the specs on this fluid. Not sure I can add anymore than I did my research and a lot of guys who know cars suggested this fluid.

Good stuff, but thanks and no-thanks. Due to the DOT requirements, the "Super blue" is no longer available. I used to alternate the "blue" and the "amber" between brake fluid flushes. The different contrasting colors were especially helpful when you flush out the old fluid replacing with the new ones and knowingly there is no guess work because when the color changes while you a bleeding the line, you know the old fluid were purged, replaced with the new ones. Well, thanks to the DOT requirements, with no valid reason, they banned such a distinctive useful feature just because they specify that the color for brake fluids from now on should either be amber or clear. I thought DOT's function is to ensure safety issues, surely their interests in cosmetic preference is running amok and goes over and beyond their purpose. Thanks to all the Ralph Nadar wannabees...running that department into a typical government dumb failure.
summary: Good stuff, but thanks and no-thanks

reviewText: This is as close to OEM as you can get for Euro cars. Did a brake/clutch flush on my Saab with 2 liters of this stuff and it worked just fine. Brakes and strong and clutch is taking up just fine.Don't cheap out on brake fluid, go pick this stuff up and don't look back. Why skimp out on something as important as brakes?!

The US is crazy and doesn't allow "colored" brake fluid.  So you now have to settle for this.  It's still the same great product, but now it's just hard to tell when it makes it through the system.  Overall, a great improvement over the DOT 3 that was in the system.
summary: It isn't the blue, but it works

reviewText: It's fluid, it works.. If you're buying this then you already know you wanted something better than OEM. Switch between Amber and Blue this way you know exactly when your system is flushed.
summary: Upgraded to this from OEM for light track and autocross duty.

reviewText: Used this in my 97 Miata.First of all;Brake fluid is one of the worst substances you will even encounter. It melts paint, and skin, and everything else it touches. You have been warned.The Good;Easy to see if clean fluid is coming out due to color.Actually quite a stable containerThe Bad;Melts EVERYTHING. Seriously.I would buy DOT 5.1 in future, which is less hazardous.

reviewText: This fluid stays true its reviews and it works awesomely. I do wish that the would legalize the color additive that they previously used  (Blue) so you could easily tell when your old fluid is flushed out.
Just as good as the super blue fluid, just not blue and thus, legal. Container is easy to store and easy to pack.

I have two vehicles, both of which have headlight covers which were getting cloudy and yellow. The first is a 11 year old Jeep Grand Cherokee and the other is a 7 year old Subaru Outback.The Jeep's headlights were by far the worst. I honestly though my night vision was starting to go, because I couldn't seem to see the road when I was driving at night. Then I noticed that my headlight covers were quite cloudy, so most of the light was either being blocked or scattered.I tried the headlight restoration procedure, and tried it again. I spent about a half hour rubbing each lens, and the net result was only a very slight improvement. It is hard to tell, but looking at the lenses, it almost appears that there is as much cloudiness and yellowing on the inside as on the outside.So the Jeep effort was a failure. I ended up replacing both the lenses. It cost a few bucks, but at least my night blindness seems to be cured.The Subaru lenses weren't nearly as clouded, and it was more of a light haze over the front of the lens. There was no yellowing or discoloring. The product worked great on this vehicle. I spent about 10 minutes on each headlight, and they now look very close to new. If you look very close, there is still a slight amount of haze, but nothing like when I started. And I am not sure if I just gave up too soon, or if that haze is on the inside of the lens.=== Summary ===So I am happy with the results on the Subaru, and would recommend it based on that vehicle. The Jeep was a disappointment, but to be fair, I don't think that anything was going to work on those headlight covers.The stuff takes a bit of effort to use, but nothing too bad. The abrasive pads could have been just a bit bigger, but they were OK to use. Too much bigger and they would have been too large to work around the contours of the headlight.I have treated two vehicles from the contents of the kit, and there are at least two more treatments left before any of the contents start running out. Upon opening the kit, my first thought was that I had just paid for three pieces of emery cloth and some car wax, but the two spray bottles seem to have some positive effect on the polishing. The yellow tube seems to contain something very similar to a car wax, with a little bit of polishing compound mixed it.In short, for the price, I was happy with the performance. If you own a vehicle with basket case headlights like my Jeep, forget it...just replace them.

My headlights were only slightly hazed at the top of the plastic cover.  All of these products really do the same thing, remove the top layer of plastic and recondition it.  This works with hand pads and you get decent results, but if your haze and discoloration runs deeper into to the plastic, you will probably need a 3M or McGuire kit and a drill. For anything light this stuff works great and I can see a big difference before and after.  I'd guess with one treatment and a lot of elbow grease 90% restored.  Not bad for 15 bucks.The real problem for me and part where this product didn't totally fix it was the swirl marks from an idiot that detailed my car and did slop work with his wheel.  This did help a little with that but if you look real close you can still see the swirl marks. Oh well.. maybe after some more sanding and the next treatment...
summary: Decent for price, works well but not quite as good as a buffer with 3M

reviewText: I had cloudy, not yellow, headlights on an RX330.  Bought the kit hoping to get good results.  Cloudiness of the lenses was partially removed to about 50% better than it was.  I followed steps closely.  At the end the plastic lens had more noticeable fine scratches than before (basically this is a fine sandpaper system). It seems the final coat is just an oil based gel that makes the plastic look wet and shiny but I doubt it will last more than a week.  Not fully happy with the result, on a whim I got out my Novus kit (1,2,3) that I bought on Amazon for plastic on my boat and around the home. I gave the lens a good Novus 3 rubbing, then 2, then the final polish coat Novus 1.  Honestly I think my results were much better than with the rain X kit.  Less scratching and seemed more effective.  I think the Novus 1,2,3 kit cost around $12 but I cannot remember as it was a few years ago.
summary: Partial restoration only of Lexus Headlight - Novus a better option?

reviewText: either buy new light covers or deal with having dim lights. This should have a traveling carnival with it. Not worth it, wouldn't use product even if it was free!
this saved my yellow headlamps!Really recommended. has been 2 months now and they're still going strong!(2003 Ford Sport Trac)

I was able to get 3 vehicles headlights restored with this product.  All 3 were starting to frost over or go yellow(ish).  With about 20 minutes on each car, I was able to make the headlights look brand new.  You gotta put a little back into it, but it's well worth it.  Considering the cost of new headlights this product is worth every dollar!  In a few years when the headlights look dull, I will buy this kit again!

I waited awhile before doing this review to see the long term results.This kit worked very good when used on a 2008 model vehicle with hazy light covers.The covers ended up looking better than they were when new, but the effect doesn't last.I have had to redo those light covers about every three months in order to keep them looking good.The procedure is not very involved and just takes a little time and effort to bring the look back.I guess once that showroom shine is gone you just have to keep at it in order to keep things looking good.Thanks to Amazon.com for this offering.
summary: I did the review reading and settled on this kit.

reviewText: Works exactly as described. A note to the wise: take extra time on the first (#1) sandpaper step. Go over the entire surface of the headlight (and in my experience the direction of sanding didn't make a difference at all, so don't sweat it) multiple times, washing the dusting of plastic off between each sanding. This was not in the instructions but helped me immensely. If you do not wash the plastic film off after each sanding the sanding becomes less and less effective. Also useful was rinsing off the sandpaper after each sanding to get the grittiness back. Overall, I am thoroughly impressed with this product. This will take some elbow grease, but WELL worth the time and money. Makes the headlights looks brand new. I did this for my mother-in-law and the thought I had replaced the headlight covers altogether because it turned out so well! Take your time, follow the steps, this will work great for you.

The Schumacher XM1-5 1.5 Amp charger/maintainer I bought came with this connection included in the box. The pig tail stays hooked up to the battery and all you have to do is plug it in to the charger cord when you want to put it back on the charger.
Another fine product from this company,that will last me for a long time.I prefer sae connectors for my solar setup.
I have these charger pig tails on all of my toys (ATV, Rzrs and motorcycles).  They plug right in to the Battery Tenders.

reviewText: This cable worked great for my 4 wheeler ,I hooked it to my battery , and don.t have to rase the seat to charge the battery
Just what I needed. I need one more for my scooter. Batteries need maintenance during winter here. Long winters in PA

Not much to say about this unit other than it works and a lot of convenience for the price. Put one on each of my implements that had a hard to get to battery and the easy plug connection really simplifies maintaining a battery in our Michigan winters.

Got this for a lawn tractor, so I could quickly hook up to a charger I use for everything with small batteries (U1 and under). I was stunned when it arrived with a captive plug cover (the illustration doesn't show one), maybe they forgot to mark the present production as "new and improved" or something of the sort. Still, it's a welcome addition to an already extremely useful battery-charging accessory.

reviewText: I installed these onto an SLA battery used in a portable device.  Very handy to make a quick connection to my battery tender.  I like not using the usual clips that were hard to find a place that I felt comfortable leaving clipped to on the battery.  Also allowed me to move the device around while it was charging and don't have to worry about the battery clips falling off.
