reviewText: Fits and functions as intended, good price and very good quality.
summary: Fits and functions as intended, good price and very good quality.

reviewText: Great extension to get from one A.T.V. to another and back to the charger that has a number of plug in's. Great price, best around. You should have one of these around if you use Battery Tenders.
summary: Nice heavy duty plug in extension.

reviewText: I use this to connect my mini wind turbine.It keeps my battery bank charged up,and works fine.Will last for years.

My plan was to install one of these cables from the battery to the grill of my "toy", a 2000 Honda S2000, so I wouldn't have to raise the hood to disconnect the battery maintainer every time I wanted to use the car.  Just take off the cover, unplug the wire and tuck the connector back behind the grill.  The ring adapters that come with any of the maintainers, from Deltran or Schumacher, are only in the 1 to 1.5 ft range, much too short to make it to the grill given the battery is back by the firewall.  The short cables I could find, of 5 to 6 ft in length, either didn't have the caps, which I wanted to keep any road dirt or rain out of the connector, or were ridiculously pricy.  I reckoned I could bunch up the extra length and tie wrap it someplace.  Which I did, but a much cleaner solution would have been a shorter wire.  Its a pity some place like Radio Shack doesn't carry this type of connector.  I suppose I can cut and splice, but that at present would rather leave it as is.  So the question is, why can't Schumacher or Deltran make the same wire, with caps, and different lengths, let's say 3, 5, 10 and this 25 ft?  With pricing to match length?
summary: Overly long, but with caps for both ends

reviewText: I bought this one to have a long extension for my SAE connector which is near my speedometer.Going out for a ride I attach the "SAE to USB Adapter - Motorcycle Cell Phone Charger" to my bike:B007VFFQREBut what can I do when my battery dies? So I bought this adapter and stored it under my seat.I also bought the "Black & Decker BM3B 6V and 12V Battery Charger / Maintainer" to charge mymotorcycle - the SAE-to-cigaret-adapter and the battery clips are also stored under my seat.B0051D3MP6So if my motorcycle battery dies I can take out the extension cable and charge it using any car.

reviewText: For anyone that hasn't tried them yet, Battery Maintainers can easily double the life of seasonal or occasionally used equipment such a lawn tractors, power generators, cars that are fair weather use only etc.  Having an extension will make your life easier, particularly if you use a splitter to maintain multiple batteries with one maintainer.
summary: Very handy if you use battery maintainers

reviewText: Very nice extension cable.  Heavy duty work really good.

I have multiple chargers and this extension was prurchased to reach a vehicle on the other side of my garage from the power plug.The cable works well and I was able to tack it along the wall with no issues placing it out of the way and then directly to the vehicle.Great pricing as well thry Amazon as it was higher priced at my local auto parts store.

These are real handy to have in order to reach the battery without having to relocate the charger itself. I have three chargers that are in a fixed position in a certain area, so I can just plug these extensions in and be able to reach the battery I want to keep charged.
Very good quality cable. It will more than suffice for extending my solar charger connections. I would say that amperage handling is pretty decent also.

The cords also fit Battery Tender brand chargers and may fit other competing brands of chargers, though I'm only guessing about this.All things considered, the flexibility these cords offer, the quality of construction and the value pricing combine to make these an easy five review.

reviewText: works with the battery tender.  way longer than i needed.  i just used it for the end connectors.  cut about 6" from the connector on each side.  now i have a bunch of extra wire to use.it does have covers to seal it when not plugged in.
I need this 25 foot extension cord in the garage to reach about 15 feet from the battery tender to my riding mower. The tender is doing its job and the mower should be ready to go in the spring.

reviewText: Thats what I use these for mainly.I tend to have so much wax on my car that I just pressure rinse,then use these to dry my car so as to avoid those nasty spots.These absorb very well,wring out,& go again.Had the yellow ones last time.Got red this time,,doesnt matter what the color,,same towel,I will continue to buy as long as they produce them.

These towels are awesome. I bought the red ones and they don't bleed or run at all. They are super absorbent and last for a very long time. reviewText: I have an old police bike with a very small gas tank and not very good mileage.  I had a previous gallon gas can that I carried in one saddlebag.  It was made of thin plastic, and I had to add an outside vent hose to keep it from expanding in the saddlebag.  This REDA gas container not only has a better shape, but it is much heavier plastic.  I haven't used it in hot weather yet, but I doubt it is going to require a vent.  Seems like a very good product for this application.

This little fuel can fits in my saddlebags perfectly and will give me 40 miles or so if I guess wrong about how far the next gas station is. Priced right at Amazon, appears well made, and I hope I never need it.
summary: 40 miles in a little leakproof can. I love it.

reviewText: The C.A.R.B spout is difficult to use and nearly worthless.  It only is leakproof, in the extended outside position.  The spout is not leakproof when stored inside the can and when removed, gas drips everywhere.  The V.O.C.'s or volitile organic compounds "permeate" through the plastic over time.I tried the camper fuel Primus and MSR bottles.  But, they are awfully expensive.Now, I use the empty cans from the Fuel South TruFuel premixed 50:1 product that I use for my 2 cycle string trimmer and lawn blower.TruFuel 50Fuel Pre-Mixed 50:1 - 2 Cycle Fuel - 6 Quart CansThe cans are under $6 each after sales tax at either Lowes or Home Depot.They are DOT approved for transporting gasoline.  They are tin lined steel, so there is no VOC permeation through their walls.They come with a "locking" "child resistant" safety cap.  Remove the cap, and it pours easily into the motorcycle gas tank.  No funnel or C.A.R.B. spout is needed.You do need a funnel to fill them, however.They are one quart each.  Carry as many as you need.Best thing is that they are FREE and saves me having to recycle them or to put them in the trash to be placed in a landfill.
summary: SAVE YOUR MONEY and get "FREE" or nearly "FREE" metal spare gas cans...

reviewText: Awesome idea. This can barely fits in my aftermarket bags on my VTX1300R. It does not leak, no fumes and I would trust putting other things in this bag now. The only change I would make to this design is making it a little shorter to fit most Medium sized bags. I would buy this again and have recommended it to a friend who also ordered one.

I just got this and have to say it seems slimmer and taller in the pics. When I took it out of the box I was really worried that it was to fat to fit my bags. I ride a 07' Victory Kingpin Tour which has fairly small side bags. The gas can would not fit pipe side but fit like a glove in the other. The can itself seems really well made. It is very hard plastic and the nozzle has a valve in it to keep your gas in the can and not in the bag. Overall I think it was a great buy.

This unit works well and is compact.The coiled air line opens up to a nice length.....giving plenty of reach.I am still getting used to the "screw on" tire fitting vs a clamp on fitting.Be quick on attaching that fitting......air will leak out until it's seated.

It's a decent inflator. It's not too loud and the cord does stretch far. I'm not too sure the gauge is always accurate. The gauge gives a different reading that other handheld gauges I have that are in agreement.

this compressor is nice and high powered it will pump up car tires with extreme speed would recommend buying a high quality tire gauge to see what pressure your really at the gauge on this thing isnt accurate by any means

I was hauling out my 45 pound air compressor to fill up the tires, and this makes it 1,000 times easier.  It's a small unit, the size of a football, and it weighs probably only about 8 to 10 pounds.  The blue cord stretches out surprisingly long, and the main adapter screws down tight over tire valves.  You screw it on, flip the switch, and wait for the reading you want.  Easy.It does inflate a car tire rather slowly.  To take a car tire from 26 psi to 35 psi took me about 45 seconds to a minute.  That's not terrible, but it's noticeably slower than the pump at the gas station.  Still, you can do the whole car, even with moving the unit, in under 6 or 7 minutes, and that's not bad at all.  The gauge seems to be dead-on, and the unit feels heavy and well built.  With gas at $4.10 a gallon it's very nice to make sure the tires are rock hard and giving you every last mile you can squeeze out.I thought about getting one of those cigarette lighter jobs, but then I kept reading about blown fuses and so forth.  I got this for the garage and stuck an old bike pump in the trunk.  The bike pump is for roadside emergencies, and no blown fuses and some good exercise with that.
Needed a good little air pump that would last. So far, it works on my RV big tires, and all the pool toys. Easy to use and the gauge is accurate.
this has been a great addition to my garage. I use it on everything ... car, motorcycle, bike, balls etc.
inflates everything quick - easy to use and easy to store - must have tool for all your inflatables plenty of adapters and plugs in for consistent power

It works well and as described.  We use it to ensure proper inflation of our cars every month.  The guage is roughly accurate but you should always use a digital or something else for more accurate readings.  The one complaint I have is that I do not like the screw on valve connector for tires.  It is a pain and you do get some air loss, so you have to over inflate slightly.
summary: works well but valve connection could be better

reviewText: I had hoped for the heavy gauge cotton towels we used to get for surgery but these are light/medium weight.  They are not as bad as the disposable grade you see all over Ebay but if you're looking for a heavy quality towel this is not it.  Shrinkage, as in most of these types of towels is severe but to be expected.
Ok towels .. But not as absorbent as everyone is saying... I'm not really wowed with them ehhh. Whatever. Win some lose some.

I don't do much in the way of surgery, so I'm not sure that I'm 100% qualified to have an opinion on "surgical huck towels", but I do wash my cars & motorcycles and spill stuff and change oil and fwap my kids when they walk by.  So apart from the surgical use, I guess I'm not completely unqualified.This is a good pack of shop towels.  These are much better than the shop rags that I buy at auto stores for garage cleanups.  My typical shop rags are only good for oil changes: I would never touch something valuable with a shop rag--they're just for cleaning messes.These huck towels are pretty nice though.  They're bigger than a shop rag (16" x 25") and the quality is much nicer.  Not that I'd want to use them on my body, but they're perfectly suitable for drying our cars & motorcycles.  They stay together pretty well and don't generate any lint that I can detect.You get a pack of twelve and the bundle is actually pretty big.  They all have nice square corners, unlike my shop rags that were puckered at the corners even when they were brand new.  You can also pick from an assortment of colors.  I haven't tested these for color-fastness yet, but I'd be nervous about the brighter colors (fuchsia or orange).  I've accidentally had one of my red shop rags sneak into a load of laundry with other clothes, and it wasn't pretty.  The color is already faded enough on these blue towels that I wouldn't panic if one went through the wash.EDIT (1/3/11):  We just returned from a four day camping trip and I forgot to pack enough dish towels.  I discovered that these towels work great in the kitchen as dish towels or tea towels.  I don't think I'd want to mix their use though:  either use them as shop towels or kitchen towels, but not both.  The garage grease stains don't come completely out in the wash, so I wouldn't want to use those greasy towels to dry dishes.EDIT II (4/24/12):  I just bought another pack of these to use as bar towels at my office parties.  We have a lot of social functions at work and nobody seems to have any towels to tidy things up.  These are perfect for wiping up all the drippy water that comes off cans and bottles when they come out of the cooler.  So what's it been now, almost 18 months since I got the first pack of these?  They've held up well and I like them well enough to want more.  Two thumbs up.EDIT III (December '12):  I bought another pack of these for a Christmas party.  I bought them in green this time.  The green color is nice, kind of an emerald green.  The quality of the towels isn't as good as the first set of blue ones though.  These definitely look and feel like shop rags.  I tied a few of these to the hot handles of chafing dishes and they were OK.  I also used some as bar towels.  My wife wouldn't let me use these in the kitchen though; she said they looked too cheap and rough for kitchen towels.

'These Doctor Joe Blue surgical huck towels are a great way to clean mirrors and glass without leaving the annoying lint behind.  They work great for cleaning the windshield of your car in addition to drying the exterior of your car.  These towels can also be used throughout the house such as for drying dishes or cleaning mirrors in the bathroom without leaving lint behind.*** Positive Points: ***- Lint Free and excellent for drying and cleaning- Large size allows you to work quickly*** Negative Points: ***- Not sure how durable they will be after several washings but these are nearly disposable for this price.'Overall: An automotive and household necessity!!
summary: Very Handy For the Car and Home

reviewText: I just bought these towels from Amazon last night and so I have not used them but my review is based on having used this type of towel for years.  As other reviewers have noted, they are great for a lot of work, especially jobs where the towel will have to be sacrificed to get the job done.  You don't want to have to do that with microfiber because those towels are many times the price of one of theseOne of the most difficult parts of a car to clean properly is the glass.  These towels are perfect for the job.  They have enough "bite" to dislodge most garbage from the outside glass and they absorb most of the glass cleaner.  These towels do the dirty work protecting the more expensive microfiber so it can do its job of buffing the glass to remove the final moisture and streaks.  It's an excellent combination.  After a proper cleaning, both inside and out with this combination, using Stoners, it's almost like there's no windshield at all.The price:peformance ratio is excellent and I wouldn't be without them.UPDATE: I have just received the towels I bought at Amazon.  It should be pointed out that these towels will require some break-in.  Right out of the package, they are not very absorbent so pop them into the wash (no fabric softener, please) and they will be much better.  It will probably take 2-4 washings before they reach full efficiency.  I bought the light green towels and I noticed that the colors did NOT run.

These towels work great without leaving any fibers behind. I relied on white terry cloth before so I was a little concerned when I first felt them.  At first they feel a little coarse.  However, after I washed them they became soft and felt much better.  And so felt safe enough to try cleaning the car with them and I wasn't sorry.  They turned out to be great for cleaning my glass table, car windows, rubbing off polish, bathroom mirror and so much more.The bottom line is that these cloths are great for any surface.  They don't leave those annoying fibers behind and don't scratch.  And the price is reasonable. I recommend them.

These towels are OK for the price and for basic function. But - they are not regular surgical towels. They are like surgical towels.The good news is that yes, they are very handy.In the time of "greener" alternatives, these make a decent replacement for paper towels and can even serve as regular napkins. The white "terry cloth" towels don't work as well as napkins - but these could work if you are not worried about impressing a date.get these if you are looking for a cheap and more versatile towel than the regular white terry cloth towels, just don't expect these to work as surgical towels or to have the same thickness or durability.

I don't know what a "huck" is, but I like these towels to keep in the house and garage to clean up spills and messes. They are machine washable and hold up pretty well even after many washes. They do lint in the dryer so be careful what you wash/dry them with. The price could be a little cheaper since they are just basic towels,hence the four star rating. Overall, I'm happy with the purchase and will buy more in the future if the price doesn't go up.

These towels are hyped as great for cleaning windows. I fully agree with this assessment. I previously spent much more on a package of two, similar towels to clean our house windows, so I was pleasantly surprised when I saw the similarities between these and those, and the marked difference in price (these being a much better bargain). I used these cleaning the windows in a solution of vinegar and hot water, and the results were a clean, fresh smell, as well as windows without streaks. But these towels can be used for much, much more, including everyday household cleaning or washing the car. The best part is that they are reusable, and that means less use of paper towels. Highly recommended.

These are wonderful, heavyweight, 16 by 27 inch towels, sold specifically for car wash and detailing. My husband is thrilled, since they do a much better job than the "rags" he normally keeps for this purpose.But I'm thrilled with these as well. We still do our dishes by hand, and these are the perfect size (and absorbency) for drying our dishes. :-)  I have the sky blue, and they do NOT look like garage towels, rather they look like a pleasant bathroom blue ... and they are much better than the towels normally sold for kitchens.So if you are looking for house and kitchen towels, do not overlook these as an option.The key to making towels absorbent is indicated on the wash instructions with these - wash them first for proper fluffiness and do NOT add fabric softener.Get the full dozen - and split them between the kitchen and garage. You won't be disappointed.Edit ...After several months of regular household use, the edges of these are very frayed. So, while they are nice at first, they definitely are not top of the line towels in any sense of the word.

These towels are decent and after one washing/drying (recommended by manufacturer) they are "broken in" and ready for use.  They are a bit stiff prior to the first wash, so I would suggest following the manufacturer's instruction.They are a decent size (approximately 16" x 27").  I would consider them average in weight, pile, and thickness.  Although they do feel thin, they also seem strong when you tug on them.As far as mixed reviews on absorbency, this is how I see them.  I would not say they are super absorbent compared to a heavyweight, plush bath towel.  However, they ARE NOT a heavyweight, plush bath towel.  They are average weight and more thin than thick.  For their weight they are quite absorbent, which makes them great for wiping off our car after a wash, and also easy to store as they take up a bit less room.Plus, not being overly thick, they can be easily run around car details such as grilles, spoilers, etc. without getting wedged or snagging.They leave no towel lint or other residue while/after being used.I found the towels a bit easier to use than a chamois, as I did not have to wring them out as much, and being towels they moved more freely over the car's surface than would a wet chamois.In the end they are nothing special, but I would rank them preferable to using your old, discarded house towels since those typically are worn down and may streak the car's finish.

These are nice, thick, absorbent towels. I have always looked for car drying towels that can absorb quickly without leaving a trail of fibers. These do that job better than most other towels I have tried, like the bag full of terry towels you find at Home Depot. They are also good for other jobs, as well. One that they are ideal for is as sweat towels used when on the treadmill. Against the skin they are soft and seem to absorb even better than off a car. You may also be tempted to use them as everyday hand towels in the bathroom. The body of the towel looks the part, but the edging and stitching is pretty basic and unadorned, so even though they work well, I wouldn't want guests to see them.

Now I know why using cheap towels at the discount stores and older towels from your home suck for car washing.  These are great.  As others have stated, wash them first before using.  Do not use frabric softener either.Anyway, enjoy your cleaner car!

These are thick, absorbent towels - more thick and plush than some of the hand towels you'd get at a big box typical retailer. But there are a few drawbacks, mainly with regard to the quality of the hem stitching and shedding.I normally use microfiber towels for utility chores (I get them cheap at the warehouse stores). For some applications these Dr. Joe cotton towels are clearly better. They absorb more water, and do so quicker. Great for drying the car. The size is a good match for car work as well - not too big so that it gets in the way; not too small that you have to go through a bunch before the job is done.They are not as good as microfiber towels when it came to applying and buffing wax. Microfiber distributed the wax more evenly, and picked it up faster. The cotton towels did well, however, when used for a final buff. The thickness really helps bring out the best shine.The Dr. Joe towels are also handy in the kitchen - much better for drying dishes and sopping up spills than microfiber. Granted, they are not targeted for kitchen use, but they certainly are up to the task.The downside is lint. These towels shed like mad in the first wash. There was less shedding in the second and third wash, but it still filled up the lint trap in the dryer. This shedding is also seen when using the towels for cleaning glass - lint stuck to the windshield and side windows, and there was some streaking. Microfiber towels are clearly better for glass cleaning.My biggest problem was with the hem quality. After only one wash, two of the towels had frayed hems. After a second wash, the number increased to three. I re-stitched the hems on the frayed ones, and will probably do some preventative mending on the rest to (hopefully) stop that from happening.Overall, a generally decent product but not outstanding.
summary: Nice and thick, but so-so on hem quality

reviewText: These towels are perfect for drying your car / truck after washing it. They are soft and very absorbent. I own a Ford F150 and I can easily dry the entire truck with one towel. In the past I would use old bath towels to dry it with but they would often leave fibers behind. These towels will not leave any fibers or water droplets behind on the surface. Each towel measures 16 x 27 which seems to be a good size. It's large enough to dry your entire vehicle but not as large as a bath towel.They also work really well for detailing rims but I wouldn't suggest cleaning your tires with them because the black from the tires is a little difficult to wash out. Apply some Windex and they work very well to clean your windows as well.You get a dozen towels when you order from Amazon and the price is very reasonable in my opinion. Purchasing similar towels locally might very well cost you three or four times as much.
summary: Very good quality car wash and detailing towels at an excellent price

reviewText: Doctor Joe car wash towels are a 12 pack of thick, soft, super absorbent towels. The size is a nice, large size. They are great for drying the car after washing because of the absorbency and good for window cleaning. They are also good for dusting and detailing inside of car, doesn't seem to produce much lint.We kept a few out for car washing but the rest we are just using for shop towels. They are great for anything. Wiping up spills, drying hands, anything that needs a towel. Does great in the wash too, gets even softer washing. Not that crazy about the blue color but I guess blue shows less stains than a white towel would.

The Doctor Joe Think Thick Super Absorbent Car Wash and Detailing Towels are OK for washing/detailing your car, but I find them nothing special. They feel and perform like any cheap terry towels. I just don't see the claims that they "absorb like a mop" being true. I also don't find them thick at all. They are thin, small, and lightweight. Don't confuse these with microfiber because they're not. They're 100% cotton terrycloth. If you need a towel to wash and clean your car, you might be better off just using one of you old bath towels, or buying cheap new ones at a department store. They will probably work equally as well as these small 16x27" cotton towels.

I am pretty picky about how clean my car looks. You might even say I get OCD about it. These towels did a great job in drying off the water spots, and even hours after the car is clean, there are no streaks. I highly recomend these towels, they are even great after you wash and dry them. Highly recomend!
summary: I really liked these towels for cleaning my car

reviewText: These towels work great on cleaning autos.Good quality at a very reasonable price.You get what you pay for.After all these towels will last for several years.What else do you buy these days that last this long, and always ready to clean for you?Show Car Guys All Purpose Microfiber Towels 16" X 16"- One Of The Best Microfiber Cleaning Cloths There Is. This 6-pack Of High Quality All Purpose Microfiber Terry Towels Can Be Used To Clean And Detail Cars, Clean Glass, and Kitchen Appliances Using N...

I've used these towels for just about everything so far, and they are everything they claim to be.  Very strong, absorbent, and thick...just what's needed for a multitude of cleaning/detailing jobs.These work equally well for drying/detailing/waxing the exterior of a car as they do for the interior.  Squeezing and twisting them, even when wet, doesn't make you feet like you're about to rip them in half like some other detailing towels I've used.They also work quite well for applying RainX, and for cleaning the grunge out of wheels.  And for cleaning up various household messes.Would highly recommend.  Keep most of them for car detailing, and a couple extra for rags and minor cleanups.  Great towels!

Just like many other reviewers have said, wash these first before using them. Just to see the difference I washed all but one and sure enough the ones that were washed not only absorbed more, but didn't leave fuzz behind.How well do these work? Very well actually. They are almost on par with the quality of mid to top end terry cloth bath towels (you could use these as wash cloths or hand towels because they are actually that good).The only complaint and reason for 4 stars is that these are still not on par with my Big & Little Blue Microfiber Drying Towels that I normally use as Doctor Joe's Think Thick still don't absorb as much as them and these still leave fuzz (not much, but some).With all of the different sizes available, Doctor Joe has the right prescription for car detailing!
Terrible quality. These towels leave behind tons of lint and immediately began to become threadbare. After only a few months and limited use most of these towels are destroyed.
summary: Terrible quality, you get what you pay for

reviewText: Finally we have weather that permits using these towels for their stated purpose and I only wish I had these the last time I cranked up the hose and water contraptions.  The size of each towel (12 altogether) at first blush was too big but once I started I could not have been pleased more.  More soapy water meets the metal faster and therefore making for a speedy application.  I used another towel for the rinse cycle (sounds like a washing machine to me) and that was the right combination so far.  Then to finish the job I used a barely damp third towel to wipe off the water spots.  That sound in the background is the drum roll for the finished job and it's a beauty.  I firmly support not using any cleaning product but those that are professionally suggested and by no means would I ever use fabric softener with the towels.  Upon completion of the job I put the three of them in the dog sink for a through hand washing and they are air drying and look fantastic.  I had never thought of it before using a fairly large towel especially since I normally used a towel or rag about the size of a large wash cloth but the larger towel like these is so much better because the weight of the water in the towel makes removing dirt so much easier.  Great product with many more uses than cleaning a vehicle.  Watch out garage doors and all that other flat surface.  You dirt is short lived thanks to Doctor Joe.
summary: Perfect for Vehicle Washing and more!

reviewText: These are high quality towels that do not deserve to be compared to the big box store bulk towels.  As the label states "think thick" - and they are guaranteed to be broken in after one wash.  Absolutely true for these 100% cotton towels.  And they maintain their size.  I have had bath towels that cost many times more and also took several washings to break in.  These are absorbent right away and even better after one wash.  In addition, the stitching is more than adequate for a work towel and polishing cloth.All in all, if you are NOT looking for potentially disposable towels, these are the best I have come across.
summary: Not your big box shop towel.  A true tool for the shop.

reviewText: I didn't follow manufacturer recommendations and used these towels without machine washing and drying them first. You know what, they still worked well, and with only a little lint and streaking on my cars' finish. The second time I used them "the proper way", there was no residue at all. I prefer them over microfiber cloths because they have that strange "sticky" feel. These little towels are the perfect size for car washing -- larger than a dish towel but less bulky than a bath towel. Drying my mid-sized sedan used only one towel while my wife's mini-van took two. I find it amazing since these Doctor Joe's Towels seem quite thin, though much plusher than your standard shop towel. They just absorb and absorb and absorb, and still soak up more after that, leaving a streak free finish.They aren't bulky so you can more easily use them to clean and dry hard to reach places like the spokes on rims or in small crevices. I use one to buff thewaxoff my paint's finish and it worked great for that as well. A dry towel easily clears of the hazy film from inside my car windows, and they work well applyingRain-Xtoo. I keep one in my glove compartment in case my windows fog in the humid Florida weather.I really like the idea of the twelve pack since these towels are so useful. I find them a good value since they appear to be holding up well to heavy use. If you don't mind their plain appearance, I think they work even better in the kitchen than regular dish towels due to their larger size. They soak up spills quickly as well. Drying your hair with one of these is a snap as they wick away moisture faster than you would imagine. Their soft terry cloth texture feels good on the skin and small children can use them as bath towels or adults as hand-towels. Doctor Joe's Towels are now dispersed throughout my home and garage -- ready for whatever challenge comes next.~ Kort

These towels are quite good for the purpose intended - washing/drying a car.  However, I like to use towels for all sort of other purposes and these fit the bill nicely.  They are slightly larger than bathroom hand towels.  My husband said they absorbed the water off the car just fine.  I like to use them laid out on my counter top two layers thick, and set my hot canning jars on them to cool.  Just use your imagination and whenever you need something soft and absorbent, think of using one of these towels before using a fancy bathroom towel.The only thing negative I have to say about them is that the hems seem to unravel a bit, and the lint in my dryer filter was very thick.  I only washed them once but it seemed to suffice.  They aren't super-thick but average thick. I like the smokey blue color too, very lovely.UPDATE 6/23/11I took several of these towels with us on a week-long camping trip and they came in extremely handy from drying dishes to sopping up tent leaks when it rained.  Also are the perfect size for towel drying a chihuahua who just had a bath.

reviewerName: Raquel S. "Avid Amazon Fan and Kindle User"
reviewText: "Only need to wash and machine dry one time in order to perfectly break-in this towel."When I got my towels and that is what I did. Machine washed and dried like usual using no softeners. When I pulled them from the dryer, four of the twelve towels started to rag at the edges. Badly. It's a little disheartening as I can see these will be short-lived towels.They function well as towels to do what towels do. I use mine for all sorts of misc. housework as well as for the car. I have no complaints there. My only concern is how quickly these towels have started to shred. As I re-washed the used ones, some of those started to rag at the edges too.Otherwise good towels for those wet, messy jobs.

These towels work fine to buff and dry surfaces. I would question the statement that they are thick and super absorbent. They are about the thickness of the towels I was issued back in my army days, although they are softer. They do say to wash first, but I did not notice any difference between the washed and the unwashed with one exception.There were some loose snags/threads/loops on the towels before, but after they were washed, I had to sit down with scissors and trim the very long loose loops on especially the sides or they would have caught on everything.They are a nice size to work with and with a different color than your bath towels they won't get mixed up...if you use thin bath towels.
I liked using this kit.  After using it I have noticed a gain in acceleration.  I am glad I found this product, would recommend it to anyone looking for the same type of product. 3M is very good.

I used this with my 1999 Nissan Pathfinder.  It was simple to use and the instructional video was easy to follow.  I don't really feel more power than what it had before, but I don't think it hurts to use it.  The dealer would charge you an arm and a leg to complete the same task.  I would invest in this first and see how it goes.

Was already using Techron additives regularly, so not sure after I did the 3M treatment, if there is any perceptible improvement, but one sure thing is, the idling revs seems to have lowered by about 200 RPM and seems to reaching idling revs quicker after the first morning start, not sure if this was also an effect of transition from Winter to Spring temperatures. So will accept it with some lingering doubts. No bad side effects though.
summary: Snake Oil or real - Seems to do the job

reviewText: I have a 2000 Toyota Celica GTS with 193k miles on it.  I have used a couple in-tank fuel injector cleaners in the past, but have never cleaned the throttle body or intake manifold.So after 12 years I figured it was about time to get on that.  Well, the kit was fairly easy to use.  The most difficult part was getting the hose for the intake manifold cleaner to stay put while it ran.  Also, depending on the packaging underneath the hood, it may be difficult to reach this.With the car running you'll need to disconnect the intake tube, start the cleaner spraying into the manifold, then walk back to your car and increase the idle to 2000 rpms.  What I've found is that the car will idle erratically with the cleaner spraying and the intake tube off.  There is a slight tendency for stalling between the time you start the cleaner and you walk back to your car.  I managed to do it fine by myself though.You will need a second person to jog the throttle body while you spray the cleaner on it.  This takes about 5 minutes and is the only part you can't do by yourself.So this is a fairly complete, easy to use kit I would recommend for older, dirtier engines.  If your car is running fine and making good power, this kit will make little difference for you.
summary: A very thorough kit for dirty engines

reviewText: My 1996 F150 started to stall - especially when running the AC.  I picked up this kit on a gold box special to see if it would help.  Best few bucks I have spent in a while.  First, I took the suggestion of a previous reviewer and parked the truck with the nose down in my driveway.  Big help with clean up.  Followed the directions and everything is running much smoother.  Of note, the F150 has two throttle bodies so I split the first can between the two.  With the gold box deal and the rebate I am one happy camper.

My 2005 Terazza has 100k on the odometer.  For a while it had not been starting as it should and would sometimes stall after start.  Dealer said they could not find any problem.Picked this up thinking it might help.  It exceeded expectations in every way.  Throttle body was caked in carbon.  After cleaning, she starts up instantly.  There is a remarkably noticeable improvement in smotothness and responsiveness.  I am sure that mpg will also be better.Kit has everything you need with easy to follow instructions.  Worth every penny.
If you want to do professional cleaning of your modern car's intake system then this product is for you at great price and instructions.
summary: Clean your Engine intake system completely at fraction of price and an hour of your time.

reviewText: which is more than you can say for the cheapest models sold here on Amazon (read the reviews ) .Spend an extra five bucks on this regulator....it's much better value than the $8 one.
my hose does not vibrate when in use and i have much better flow to all faucets in the RV.
summary: Way better than the camco version

reviewText: I replaced my old, leaking "WaterMate" regulator with this new, lead-free Valterra -- and it works great !!The Orange plastic grip allows easy, screw-on installation and removal. It comes complete with an internal screen/washer, too.NOTE: The included screen/washer is NOT stainless steel, so it WILL rust through in a couple of months -- I use ONLY stainless-steel screen/washers to avoid bits of rotted screens from clogging the Regulator, the Timer, or the Sprinklers.The lead-free "brass" regulator body is designed primarily for RV hookups -- to keep dangerous LEAD from leaching into your drinking water, but mine is mounted on the garden hose faucet to prevent blow-outs of soaker hoses and drip systems. Another feature of the  Valterra shows up in the monthly Water Bill -- it's MUCH lower than before the installation of the Valterra regulator !!The Valterra Regulator runs at 52-55 psi., tested at the faucet with a Rainbird P-2 Pressure Gauge.I use the Valterra regulator ahead of an Orbit Digital Timer for precise lawn watering and accurate water distribution through GILMOR Gear-Drive Sprinklers, also available at Amazon.My order arrived promptly and in perfect condition. Thanks, Amazon !!UPDATE: 14 June, '14 -- Regulator is still working perfectly -- with no leaks and/or drips -- and the Water Bills are still lower than before the Valterra was installed.
I like Valeria products. They are well made and stand up to heavy use. I full time RV and find them very useful.

I've always used the higher flow regulators.  Just that extra 5 or 10 lbs of pressure is nice in the shower.  Highly recommend.  My first one that I purchased was in 2010 and I use them all season long.  Just purchased the second one so will have a backup if this one goes.  I also use a gauge to verify pressures wherever I am at that you can purchase here.

I used it for the first time this last weekend.  I love the fact it's lead free.  My friend was next to me and had a pressure gauge on his regulator and the water pressure at this camp was over 100psi.  My regulator worked fine and we had no issues.

reviewText: Soon after I bought my first RV (recently) I think I came close to burning it to the ground because of a water leak. What had happened on my first outing was I hooked up to a place where the water pressure was VERY high. But, I'm a camping newbie so I was oblivious. The only initial clue was the jarring noise as the air was forced out of the lines. A couple hours after hooking up at the camp site the bulbs started dimming on their own. Definitely had me puzzled. Then there was the smell of something electrical getting way too hot. Puzzled turned into concern. Thank god we hadn't left for dinner before the problems started. What had happened was water was dripping into the convertor from running down the water line from a small leak.I haven't had any problems with this pressure regulator. Well made and I have decent pressure in the camper with zero leaks. I can also adjust the pressure one way or the other. Very happy.
summary: Keeps me from burning to death in my sleep.

reviewText: Great for the RV. I like the fact that all you have to do the adjust it is with a screwdriver. I have a 90 degree elbow which I attached this valve to. Highly recommend the 90 degree elbow. Relieves stress on the valve and hose connection. I use an inline wateKer filter along with the valve and I have had no leaks. I have adjusted mine to 50 psi. Most water lines in RV are rated at 65 psi so this is just right when you park at an RV site were the pressure is to high. Maintains pressure all the time. If you have an RV you need an adjustable regulator. Those so called preset are a gamble if it is was it says it is set at at the factory.

Must have!! Don't waste your money on those cheap pre-set regulators ( most are NOT lead free - how do they get away w/ that?????) This is easy to attach and use and the water pressure makes for a wonderful shower and cleaning your toilet (just sayin) while protecting your RV pipes.

First of all, you must have a pressure reducer in your RV's fresh water line. The fixtures in all RV's are rated at a maximum pressure of 50 to 60 psi. Campground water pressure can be over 100psi. The surest way to burst a fitting or fixture is to let this high pressure water go into your city water inlet. This device is a cheap way to avoid that problem.There are pressure regulators that sell for a lot less than this one. They are fixed pressure reducers, mostly 45psi. They can be problematic. Check your RV's specs. My fixtures are rated at 60psi, so with this unit I can accurately set the city water pressure to what I like. I normally have it at 50 to 55 psi. This pressure vastly improves showers and dish washing. The pressure meter gives you an instant view of the water pressure...so if there is a problem, you can easily rule out the city water first.Some tips on using this device:1. This should be the first thing connecting to the campsite's city water connector. I follow this with a water filter and then my supply hose. By putting this regulator first, you protect your filter and hose as well.2. If you want to adjust pressure, do it ONLY with all water turned off inside the RV. Make sure that no water is running or filling anywhere. Once done, gradually move the adjusting screw a bit. Wait 10 to 20 seconds and look at the pressure. Once set, you can begin using water. When water is running, don't expect the reading to always be at the set pressure.3. Replace this unit after a year or two. All pressure reducers wear out. For safety, I replace mine every year. $50 isn't a bad investment in protecting my water system.4. Use a water filter! There are lots of inline filters available. Most screen out particles bigger than 30 microns or so. this is enough to protect your fixtures. These inline filters do not purify the water. They just remove sediment in the water line. We never drink campground water. We do carry a good quality purifying filter and bottled water.5. Avoid banging up the regulator. This unit is not indestructible. We keep it in a plastic container in our "garage" when we travel.SummaryYou will be surprised how much better a shower in the RV can be when you can control the city water pressure. This unit does the job at a good price.
summary: Much better than fixed pressure units!

reviewText: Plastic material is light weight and has been used to raise a minivan. Rated for 1500 lbs each ramp but have not tested to capacity. Low ramp angle does not force small engine cars to rev engine to drive up ramp. Owning standard metal ramps before with much steeper ramp angle, I was always concern that I need to rev up the engine to get car up the ramp. I may not stop in time and wheels overshoot stops and then have damage under body. That was my main reason for buying this ramp because of the much lower ramp angle. To accomplish the low ramp angle, the ramp has be to much longer in length. The two piece ramp make storage easy. High price but in the long run worth it. Note of caution. The first time I use it, the ramp was on a slight raised lump area and it left an indentation in the ramp bottom. Just make sure you are working on a flat surface since the ramp material is soft.

I love these ramps.  They're solid, so I don't worry about them collapsing like most other ramp designs; there's nothing to collapse.  They're lightweight, so they're super easy to move around and handle.  The removable front part gives way more room to work on things.  They're foam encased in basically a bedliner-type material, so weather doesn't bother them (I left a car sitting on them outside all winter once).  They're long and smoothly sloped so I can finally pull my low-ground-clearance cars up on them.  They're also really handy for things like my '95 Caprice and '04 Grand Marquis, where the front overhang and lower air dam make it a pain to get a regular floor jack underneath to the front crossmember; I can drive up on these and then use a floor jack to get the car farther up in the air for something like removing a transmission.  The relatively long length of these does make it more important to get out a tape measure and make sure they're parallel before pulling up on them, but that's a small price to pay for the incredible convenience.  The stops on the end are adequate to keep you from driving off unless you get too wild.I did buy the Race Ramps branded wheel chocks (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003ZAGPGU), which are not the chepaest chocks around, but are also of good quality.  It's important to chock the wheels when using ramps like these where there isn't really an indent for the tires - but the flat part is honestly wide enough that it shouldn't be a problem if you want to live dangerously.
Purchased to change my oil and am very impressed with these ramps. Amazingly light, strong and easy to store away thanks to the two piece design.

These are very light weight (much lighter than the cheap steel ramps) and they have nice carrying straps on the ends. I bought them for my sports car because of how low it sits to the ground, and it ends up these ramps are too steep still, I will be ordering the extenders. If you have a low profile car, I would recommend that you do the math to figure out the maximum angle (remember geometry?) you can have to get your car up on ramps, this way you will know beforehand if you will need the extenders or not.
summary: Nice ramps, like the 2 piece design

reviewText: These are ok - they've held my 24' trailer on the steep hill in front of my house.It doesn't really show in the photo, but they are hollow - the rubber is maybe 3/4" or so thick, which allowed me to drill a hole and attach an eye-bolt and chain them together in sets of two, which makes them a lot more convenient to carry around when you are chocking and un-chocking your RV.  I think the price is a bit high, but not outrageous, and they certainly do the job.

These are good chocks.  I was disaaapinted, however, to find that one of the set I received had errant cut on the base, where the rubber was trimmed at the factory.  I had to return them.Unlike other Race Ramp products these are NOT made in USA.  They are NOT marked with the country of origin. They are nearly identical to the ones selling at $8.99 each at my local Northern Tools store. Those are marked made somewhere in Asia.  I don't recall which country.  That means I can get a set of 4 for under $36.  The mold numbers inside the bottom cavity are the same, and the dimensions and weight are the same.  Yes, as another reviewer stated, they are hollow but heavy rubber.The only difference between these and the Buyers' were shallow slits cut into the bottom running parallel to the car axles in their installed position.  I'm not sure that they help very much and are worth the extra dollars.  I gave a set of four of the Buyers to a friend for his boat trailer a couple of Christmases, ago.  They are quite heavy work very well.If you likee to see these, just go to either Northern or Tractor Supply.  They are heavu and work well, but I'd wouldn't pay over $20 more for the Race Ramps label or the slits on the bottom.For my Race Ramps to check the tires on the ramps, I'll get the $3.24 each yellow Camcos lightweight plastic ones that, to my surprise, ARE Made in USA.  Since the Race Ramps material is a little flexible, I see no problems with the cheapies working just as well.On concrete, however, the Buyers are a better deal.
summary: The Buyers Model# WC1467A  Chocks are nearly the same for $23 less..

Ideally, it should be much less than what Race Ramps charges for the chocks.Please click YES if my review have been helpful to you, it will encourage me to continue writing and updating my reviews, and leave a comment if you have any questions, I will be more than happy to answer if I can be of help.

reviewText: Joes Racing tire gauge is the gauge I should have bought long ago. It is simple to use, rugged, and incredibly precise.My son took one of our cars back to college with him. I needed to give him a tire gauge, so I dropped the rubber surrounded Brookstone gauge I've used for years into his glove compartment. Fortunately, he understands how important it is to keep the correct tire pressure (he even gets it to measure the tires cold). So that left me with no tire gauge. Wow, am I ever happy I gave away the Brookstone.This is such a cool precise gauge. The hose is roughly a foot long. The valve connector has a pivot point at the hose. The angle is just about perfect to tap onto a valve, and I really like the metal push part on the back of that connector. Up top at the gauge, the fluted rubber surround is easy to hold in my hand. It is just the right size, not too big to hold, and just the right size to easily read the PSI. Just at the gauge there is a bleeder valve. How in the world did I ever get tires to the correct pressure without a bleeder valve? The gauge is marked off in 1 PSI increments and major numbers every 5 PSI. The background of the dial is glow in the dark phosphorus green (very nice touch in a garage). This is one of the easiest to read analog gauges I've ever seen.To use this gauge, hold the round gauge in one hand, rotate the valve adapter to line up comfortably with the valve stem on the tire, push down onto the valve stem, hold the adapter there making certain there is no air leaking noises, and read the gauge. If the air pressure is too high in the tire, press the bleeder valve to release some air. If the pressure is too low, remove the gauge and add air with a compressor. Then retest the pressure. It takes way longer to describe than to perform.The gauge comes with an air chuck style replacement head. If the angled adapter is not a preference, it can be changed to a chuck. I can't figure out exactly why anybody would do that, but the option is there.The instructions are very clear to not over pressure this gauge. This model works from 0 to 60 PSI, and they recommend measuring pressures more in the 30 PSI range. This is good scientific advice for really precise measurements. The odd spare tire that needs 60 PSI is probably OK. But there is a strong warning to never over pressure this gauge, as it will reduce the precision and possibly ruin the gauge. So this gauge won't really work for bicycle tires.What a great gauge. Thank you son for going away to college with one of our cars, I got to buy a fantastic new tire pressure gauge.

I take full responsibility in not researching this enough but, this model just has a vent down button to allow you to drop the air pressure down to the pressure that you want. I wanted the "hold" function and purchased the wrong one. If you want the hold function then you want JOES PN# 32310.Overall, I am very happy with the product. I have measured it against other tire pressure gauges that I trust and is always comes out right where it should be. The gauge is easy to read and the rubber surround helps minimize drop impacts and marring a wheel if you happen to drop it on the wheel somehow. It is well made and looks very nice. I can use it on cars and motorcycles that have odd angles to get to the valve stem.
summary: This is not the "pressure hold" version

This is an excellent, very affordable tire gauge. Actually, it's very inexpensive for what it does. The biggest problem is that those buying this style of gauge for the first time do not know how to use it properly. Perhaps the following will help.The proper use of any gauge with a hose and dial requires two hands. Period. One to hold the chuck on tight, and one to bleed off excess air. Always overfill by a few psi and gently bleed out the excess. It works every time. You don't use this type of gauge like a pencil gauge. The gauge goes on two times max per tire. First time, check pressure. If ok, you are done. If you need to add air, add air then place gauge on tire and hold in place. Do not remove it until final adjustment is made. No on off, on off. It's that simple.Incidentally, no one needs a hold feature on a gauge that is visible while in use. It is a waste of money and pointless. The whole idea is to keep this style of gauge firmly in place and bleed off excess air. Once you learn to use it, it will make perfect sense.

I could not find a body shop that was willing to blend in a repair on a series of 4" x 4"  scrapes-they wanted to paint the whole fender.I used this as a final coat to a repair using the Perfect Match primer and color coat as a base. All three products are totally compatible with each other so you won't get any crinkled surprises.I let the base coat dry one week before hitting it with this clear. Just wanted to make sure that everything stuck.Please make sure you do at least an alcohol wipe between the primer, color, and clear steps (NOT between coats however), especially if you drive around in between painting, as any wax or oils that find their way onto your repair will ruin paint adhesion. Avoid painting outdoors or on humid days at all costs. You will be rewarded with a fish eye and orange peel free finish.It took 6 coats of clear to get an acceptable "gloss" over the color coat. You must take your time and allow each coat to set up (10 min)before spraying the follow up coats. The first few coats will look frosted-don't panic- just keep adding coats until you can see a gloss set up.You must mask off any areas you don't want overspray on. I covered most of my 'front clip' for my repair. This stuff is designed to stick, and any over spray will have to be buffed off with a fairly aggressive compound.  If you mask with tape, be prepared to sand and buff out the tape line-especially if you don't feather in the last few coats.Like every paint repair, you will have to slightly expand the repair area by overlapping your spray target with each step. Shoot for 1/2" expansion and settle for 1" for each step. Resist the temptation to overlap too much or you'll end up painting the whole panel-just like many body shops want to do. I lightly wet sanded the color coat and expanded that slightly to the good factory finish with 2000 grit paper, just to give the clear something to grab onto when I feathered in the last few coats.And speaking of buffing, in order to complete the blending process, you will need to buff with a power buffer and the appropriate compound (or series of compounds if you are fussy). To avoid any lifting, I waited another week after applying the clear to make sure it was reasonably hard.  It was able to withstand some pretty heavy buffing at that point, and I was able to blend and match the PM clear to the factory gloss.
summary: The final part of a spray touch-up system

reviewText: I used this to finish the coat on my '98 F150.  It is an excellent clear coat match.  The only problem is that you will probably need more than one can.  8 oz. is just not enough.

Brought our Jeep Wrangler's floor pan back to looking like new and is affordableWe have a 1998 Jeep Wrangler TJ that has been passed down the family to our son.  It is in overall excellent condition, but there was one thing that went unnoticed over the last couple years... the drain under the fresh air intake does not flow well, causing rain water to pool on the HVAC system and eventually overflow. When parked on a nose-up grade, that pool overflows onto the passenger side's front floor pan.Since we have Husky Liners (Husky Liners Classic Style Custom Fit Molded Front Floor Liner for Select Jeep Wrangler TJ Models (Black)) over the carpet in the front (and in the rear too, actually), we did not notice the damp carpet underneath the liners until a few months ago... when I saw a little pool of water sitting inside the liner and investigated.We caught the problem in time; no serious rust, but a decent amount (maybe 40% of the pan) was covered in surface rust and here is what we did to bring it back to looking like new:1. Cleaned the pan with some Simple Green and dried it2. Brushed the heck out of it with a good wire brush until as much of the rust was removed as possible3. Vacuumed the rust dust away, then cleaned & dried it again4. Sprayed the pan with Dupli-Color Rust Fix (Dupli-Color RF129 Rust Fix Rust Treatment - 10.25 oz.) and let it dry, then repeated twice more -- lightly sanding between each coat and also after the final coat.5. Sprayed the pan with four light coats of Dupli-Color Emerald Green Pearl (Dupli-Color BCC0421 Emerald Green Pearl Chrysler Exact-Match Automotive Paint - 8 oz. Aerosol), an exact match for our Jeep, with a light sanding between coats but not after the final one.6. Sprayed the pan with three coats of this Dupli-Color Clear Coat, which made the floor pan look like it is brand new, factory issued.  The spray went on evenly and coated well, and looked great after the first coat and even better after the next two.Am very happy with the results of this combination of Dupli-Color products, especially the matching of the color and the factory-like shine that the clear coat brought back to life. I checked on the floor pan again earlier this week and it still looks like new.If you have a similar need, we recommend this product and product line. Like anything worth doing, the end result is only as good as the intellect and elbow-grease that you put into it. My only recommendation, given the tight confines of working in the front floor pan area, is that you wear a good mask when using any of these spray-delivered products.Go for it.
summary: Dupli-Color Clear Top Coat - Used on our Jeep Wrangler's floor pan with excellent results - Affordable

Excellent coverage, and great looking final coat.  Only time will tell if it ever yellows or not, but for now, the old car looks pretty darn good!

We have a 1998 Jeep Wrangler TJ that has been passed down the family to our son.  It is in overall excellent condition, but there was one thing that went unnoticed over the last couple years... the drain under the fresh air intake does not flow well, causing rain water to pool on the HVAC system and eventually overflow. When parked on a nose-up grade, that pool overflows onto the passenger side's front floor pan.Since we have Husky Liners (Husky Liners Classic Style Custom Fit Molded Front Floor Liner for Select Jeep Wrangler TJ Models (Black)) over the carpet in the front (and in the rear too, actually), we did not notice the damp carpet underneath the liners until a few months ago... when I saw a little pool of water sitting inside the liner and investigated.We caught the problem in time; no serious rust, but a decent amount (maybe 40% of the pan) was covered in surface rust and here is what we did to bring it back to looking like new:1. Cleaned the pan with some Simple Green and dried it2. Brushed the heck out of it with a good wire brush until as much of the rust was removed as possible3. Vacuumed the rust dust away, then cleaned & dried it again4. Sprayed the pan with Dupli-Color Rust Fix (Dupli-Color RF129 Rust Fix Rust Treatment - 10.25 oz.) and let it dry, then repeated twice more -- lightly sanding between each coat and also after the final coat.5. Sprayed the pan with four light coats of this Dupli-Color Emerald Green Pearl paint, which really is an exact match for our Jeep. We did a light sanding between coats but not after the final one. The spray went on evenly and coated well, and looked great after the first coat and even better after the next two.6. Sprayed the pan with three coats of Dupli-Color Clear Coat (Dupli-Color BCL0125 Clear Exact-Match Automotive Top Coat - 8 oz. Aerosol), and this made the floor pan look like it is brand new, factory issued.Am very happy with the results of this combination of Dupli-Color products, especially the matching of the color. I checked on the floor pan again earlier this week and it still looks like new.If you have a similar need, we totally recommend this product and product line. Like anything worth doing, the end result is only as good as the intellect and elbow-grease that you put into it. My only recommendation, given the tight confines of working in the front floor pan area, is that you wear a good mask when using any of these spray-delivered products.Go for it.
summary: Exact color match for our Jeep Wrangler's floor pan and is affordable

I received the cover and it took only 10 minutes to install.  It looks great and is functional.  I had really gotten tired of the open gas filler area.  The chrome screws that can be seen from the outside are just for looks it seems, since the filler assembly is held to the quarter panel with plastic snaps.The directions that came with it had no words, only drawings.  However, overall the drawings were good.  One of the drawings had you remove the wiring connector going to the rear taillight.  This is not really necessary, just slide the connector off of the clip that is holding it to the taillight.  The second drawing that is not quite clear is drawing #7.  It shows the rubber gasket that goes around the filler tube.  Basically, the rubber gasket is attached to the filler assembly.  When you remove the assembly from the quarter panel the rubber gasket comes off with it.  You can then remove it and then reattach it to the filler tube opening of the new assembly.  When you reattach the filler assembly to the quarter panel it goes around the filler tube.I researched all of the different after market covers and decided on this one.  I really did not like the idea of those filler doors that were simply a cover over the existing assembly.  This OEM assembly looks original and enhances the appearance of the vehicle.  I contemplated getting a locking cover but decided against it.  Simply too many keys already with the under seat lock boxes, etc.

reviewText: These look great overall, so no complaints about the product.  The only issue, as you may read in other reviews, is the installation on the small fender lamps is a nightmare. The problem is you have to remove the light, which very difficult to work out of the plastic housing in front of it (behind the fender).  The project is do-able, but be prepared to spend some time and make sure you have plenty of patience before you start.

Everything about the design is a positive.  The metal is well finished and the paint looks good.  The included instructions have text in addition to just pictures.To elaborate on the included directions I have included the comments below:The larger guards (for turn signal) have three tabs that line up with the light holder. These were slightly too tight to place over the corresponding area on the light assembly. Bending them out slightly allows the guard to be attached easier.  The longest tab needs to be attached first and then the others.  If you have bent out the tabs some be sure to press them back in after the guard is attached.For the smaller guard (side lights) the directions have you completely removing the assembly.  I found it difficult to press the tab holding the lens to the fender assembly to perform this action.  However, I found this removal unnecessary and was able to separate the two assemblies (fender flare and fender) enough to slide the guard into place.Overall time to install was less than 20 minutes.

reviewText: Good quality and shipped fast. Fits my 2009 Jeep Wrangler. Took a minute to figure out how to install it but once I read and understood the questions, it was okay.

Looks great, pretty easy to install if you know your way around the front end of a jeep. Install took about 20 minutes for all four. Installed to the parking lights and fender lights. Directions didn't match my vehicle. Seems like the directions were for an older model jeep wrangler. I managed to get the parking light covers on but not the fender signal covers. Need to update your information rugged ridge.

I guess I just changed my mind about installing this product.why would I want to limit my light beams for false security. After taking so much stuff off the jeep,didn't make spence to put these on. Think about what your buying for your jeep or your gonna have a parts department in your garage.

reviewText: I was skeptical about using these 100 lb shocks in my RV when I first got them since I couldn't compress them no matter what I did. reviewText: Replaced 80 lb. struts with these 100 lb. struts to keep a large door (75" x60") on the back of a motorhome open.  The 80 lb. were week and almost cracked my head many times, and now they stay fully extended and taunt.

I like getting these here for my Honda 2009 Fit, empty your glove box push in on the sides, glove box swings down. reviewText: This is the 2nd TYC air filter I've purchased.  The 1st one was for my Honda CRV, which fit great, so I purchased this one for my Honda Fit.  Easier to replace than my old CRV.As others have noted, the TYC filter has three strips of glue and require an easy snipping of the adhesive on the opposite ends.  What you want is to be able to have the end walls separate from the rest of the pleats so you can seat the filter properly into the frame.  It is a very easy step, a scissor or a knife will work, you may even be able to tear and separate the adhesive with your hands if you are careful enough.  It's so simple, I wouldn't even dock it any stars.  So, on the Fit, open your glove compartment, take out all the junk you have in there, just squeeze in the sides of the glovebox walls, drop the glovebox lower (it's hinged so it won't fall off) and you have access to the cabin filter frame in the back.  Release the left and right clips and slide out the frame with the air filter.  Replace with new filter and put everything back together.Remember to note the direction of the air flow (I believe it's downward) and remember to seat the filter properly.  You should see a little "lip" like protruding plastic part on the frame (opposite ends).  Slide your filter into this part (both ends), you want to do so or there will be air that can possibly get bypass the filter.  It is because of this part on the frame and the full coverage of adhesive on the TYC filter that causes a conflict.Please let me know if my review have been helpful to you, it will encourage me to continue writing and updating my reviews, and leave a comment if you have any questions, I will be more than happy to answer if I can be of help.
summary: Perfect fit with a little snipping necessary

reviewText: This cabin filter was easy to install and fit perfectly. Replacing the filter myself was much cheaper than having the dealer do it.
I had to trim one row of the glue on both ends of the filter to make room for the factory filter frame.  It is very easy and nothing to worry about.  Other then that it is a perfect fit.

I followed all the steps carefully, and these turned out pretty nice.  My only complaint is that perhaps starting with 400 grit wet sanding was a bit rough.  You basically start with 400 grit, then move to 1,000 grit, then 2,000 grit, and then a clay type rubbing compound.  When finished, this kit included the critical final step and liquid UV sealant to finish the job.  The finished lights look pretty good, but there were still some apparent deep scratches that I suspect were caused by the initial 400 grit sanding.  I think that was still a little harsh for the initial rough sanding of plastic material.

I used this on my 1999 Isuzu Rodeo. The headlights weren't super awful, but visibility was low. Well, I decided on this restoration kit versus the rest and I'm glad I did. Took me about 30 minutes, no tools needed. It's a easy process and just takes a little time and elbow grease. Word of advice, if you are like me and don't have a water faucet outside, get a spray bottle and fill it up with water. I had to fill my water bottle 4 times throughout the process. I would buy this again (and probably will for my Ford Ranger). Great buy.

The result of the restoration kit is better than expected. My headlights were nowhere near the "before" examples shown in advertisements but the improvement was nonetheless fantastic. However, the process is pretty long (1.5hrs) and not very enjoyable even though I'm a 'car guy.'

reviewText: This product will not make a headlight look brand new.  It cleaned up the headlight about as well as I had expected, but they over doing it on the commercials.  I also didn't really even notice a difference in headlight brightness at night.  The turn signals are much easier to see at night though.  I have only had it applied for a couple weeks now so we will see if it lasts.The main reason I lowered the rating is because this kit should have the ability to be reused on multiple cars.  Stage 1 and stage 3 solutions are reusable(and they give you way more than you need).  The stage 2 compound, sand paper, and cloths are not reusable which will require you to buy the package all over again.  With the exception of the stage 2 compound you could easily replace the rest with the product from any store, but without being able to reseal/reuse the stage 2 compound it would make reusing the kit a hassle.  Overpriced for only being able to be used once, in my opinion.  Make stage 2 resealable and increase the volume and I would be happy.

This product worked amazing well. I put in new headlights and I wasn't really impressed with the results. I used this restoration kit and the nine years of cloudy sun damage on my headlights disappeared. My lights are ridiculously bright now. Some people even flash their lights at me while driving at night, assuming I have my brights on when I don't. I definitely recommend the Sylvania Headlight Restoration Kit to anyone who has dull headlights.
summary: Nine years of sun damaged gone in less then an hour

reviewText: Works amazingly well.  You will think that you have totally screwed up until the last couple of steps, then it will look as it did when new.Great product.
This was the first product I used on my 2000 and 2003 car. It does take at least an hour to do on the car but it comes out well. It was 6 months ago and so far they do look as if brand new.

I followed the video instructions exactly and I'm very impressed with the results. I have tried other methods in the past to restore headlights on older vehicles and this has provided the best result for me. The 30-minute claim is a bit optimistic and there is a little bit of effort needed (mostly the hand sanding can start to get tiring after a while) but I can't find too much to complain about here. I do recommend not using the written directions and following the video on Amazon or YouTube instead.

I was working on a 2000 Honda Accord in 2012, and the lenses were extremely yellowed and cloudy.  I got failed on inspection and the shop offered a $100 job to clean the lenses.  I went with this kit after reading the good review it got in Consumer Reports.It does take a long time, about an hour or maybe an hour and a half of total work.  I spread mine out over an evening and a morning to let things fully dry.  I followed the directions to the letter.  The one thing that had me worried a bit is my lenses were cloudy even after the clarifying rub, right up to the very end.  Much clearer, but still cloudly.  Then I hit them with the UV stuff and WOW! just like new.  Well, that's not really fair.  Not just like new.  I'd say 90% to 95% of just like new, but enough of an improvement that for $22 I'm well satisfied.  It's been a month and a half now and the lenses still look good.  I'm pleased.Watch the video, read all the literature, and get ready for some elbow grease.  You do have to put some work into this, but it's not terrible.  Bring a chair out into the garage so you can get comfy as you sand away.

The video for this kit is very useful. I watched it several times, finally pausing the video, taking notes to refer to while actually using the kit. Be sure to read the kit instructions too. I used the kit on a 1998 Mercury Grand Marquis.I followed the instructions exactly to maximize success, sanding for the full 5 minutes for each sanding/polishing operation. For the three grits of sandpaper plus the compound, times two headlights, it took a full 40 minutes of sanding/polishing. The headlight surface should be kept wet while sanding/polishing. Altogether it took me about 1  hour and 45 minutes to complete the job. One thing:  be careful not to use too much pressure when using the #400 (coarsest) grit sandpaper to avoid too-deep scratches. For the finer two grits and compound use firmer pressure. The video mentions this.There's a lot of rinsing and drying to be done and I used nearly a half roll of paper towels. Rather than a bucket or hose, water in a spray bottle works very well for rinsing; much better control.Not mentioned in the video, but in the kit instructions, is this VALUABLE tip: Complete the sanding/polishing/rinsing/drying steps first on BOTH headlights before applying the final step, the UV clearcoat. This avoids inadvertently wetting the  clearcoat (with drifting spray) on the completed headlight. Lay the coating on rather heavily, but not so much as to cause running or dripping. The coating must set for an hour in order to cure to the touch, and accidentally wetting it could be a problem. Also, it's MUCH easier to clearcoat both lenses at the same time. Otherwise the already-used blue applicator cloth will dry out in a short time and you'll have to refold and fiddle with it trying to create a neatly folded, usable application edge.Another tip: I cut the sandpaper sheets in half so I could use a fresh piece of each grit per headlight.I chose the Sylvania kit because it was the only one I found that has the protective clearcoat that  affords UV protection and long-lasting results. Although many kits make use of a drill or other power tool, hand sanding and polishing avoids possible wandering of the power tool and allows getting into corners as well as providing control and "feel."Bottom line: VERY pleased by the results. The lights don't look brand new (probably because the internal reflectors are not pristine), but pretty darn close and MUCH improved. For me it was well worth the money and effort. I gave it 4 stars because (for me) there are so many steps. But the very good results might well deserve 5 stars.
summary: Well Worth the Money and Effort

reviewText: much better that the Maguire's product we sell at work, great cord, heavy duty motor, will review later after some use.

reviewText: I used the Griot's Garage 10765LNGCRD 6-inch random orbital polisher (with the Griot's red pad) this weekend to apply liquid marine wax to my 35' motorhome. This tool made fast work of a nice, even wax application.  The 6" size is PERFECT even for an RV. A friend used his (cheaper) 10" orbital of a different brand and complained that it couldn't handle the curves well.  This Griot's machine nicely handled all straight and curvy parts, and honestly, the 6" size is none too small even for an RV.  The hard part, as you'd expect, was removing the wax after it dried.
