reviewText: I FINALLY used this polisher that I had purchased a while ago, waxing my truck before the cold weather sets in. It is very well balanced and with the speed selections that are available,it does a great job and you won't burn the paint. The large handle provides very good control. Another great feature is the Velcro backing which provides a quick and secure placement of the pads. If you buy additional pads or for example, a lambswool polishing pad, just be sure it has a hook and loop backing to stick to the Velcro.

while it's true that you can get polishers like this for less money, and likely also true that you can work magic with them, I have to say that I am consistently pleased with Griot's. When I got this latest toy, I thought it looked a bit too much like an "in-house" creation and not so much what I would expect from a "professional tool" as it's advertised. That feeling lasted about 15 minutes, the time it took to unpackage it and start my play time. I have this, and the 3" inch and I've done more amazing work on two cars in the last week than I think I've done in years.Pros:Works as advertised, EASY to control!!! EASY to maintain, change pads, etc. OH, and definitely use their polish, it washes out with water and no mess. I had black rubber mess all over my pads in addition to the polish and it came out with running water.Balanced and naturalComes with instructions that really deliver what they promise to. So many times you buy stuff that comes with a "perfect world" scenario in the instructions that you just can't seem to replicate, well, not Griot's. What they did on the videos is exactly what I did in real life.Complete so far: (using #3 polish, yellow pads, orange pads, and rubber restore1999 Camaro Z28 HEAVY hood and door sill oxidation and clear coat breakdown- Solved with like new appearanceSame car, fully oxidized headlights, full restored to the point that I don't need to buy new ones.....clear and clean.Same car, window and door exterior rubber welt/weather stripping, oxidized, partially pasty white and appearance of deteoration: fully restored with light sheen and factory appearanceSame car, window quarter panel: discolored and faded: fully restored and shiny. T-top roof bands, swirled and discolored: fully restored and glossy1999 Jeep Grand CherokeeFactory orange peel: straight as an arrowBumper fascia front and rear: faded/discolored: cleaned with yellow pads and restored with #3 polish.2008 350z:Mild surface swirls: goneBottom line:I've spent a bunch of money on their products, and each time I get one, I end up going back and buying more to "try" and have thus far not been disappointed. I put wax on by hand for years and decided it was time to outfit the garage with a power tool for polishing and waxing. I can't believe I waited so long to buy one. I have only had this item for 3-4 months but already find it more useful than my 6 inch DA polisher.  So far it has worked flawlessly, holds onto the pads firmly, and gets into the tight spots. First this is not like a full size DA in power. Setting 1 is essentially vibrate as the pad with not spin unless making near 0 contact. Setting 2-3 are basically the same. Setting 4 you get some spinning but not really a useful amount for much other than light object finishing. 5&6 the tool becomes useful. To give you an idea I was applying wax with a microfiber pad at like 5 effectively. Even at setting 6 this tool is like level 2 on a normal DA. But this tool has some advantages in size and intensity. It fits everywhere which is great and it buffs chrome and grills very well without destroying the pad. I like how they advertise all of it's other uses as it would be very good for household things as well. This tool can definitely outdo the hand approach at higher settings but don't expect anything like a full size DA's power. I personally love it for what I use it for but am glad I own a full size DA also.

reviewText: This was the first small polisher I ever owned, and it was ok for light jobs. I have added the Rupes Big Foot Mini to my polisher arsenal and it is a much more capable machine.  Admittedly, it also costs 2.5 times as much so I can hardly compare them. Received as part of the Amazon Vine reviewer program, the Carrand AutoSpa Bagless Auto-Vac turned out to be a pretty good portable vacuum for small jobs.Carrand is a brand that I was unfamiliar with, so I looked them up.  Around since 1983, they specialize in a niche market - quality auto detailing and car care on a budget. This product definitely fits that bill.  It's not a heavy-duty shop vac, but for light, small, dry jobs for cars, boats and RV's it would be a good choice. Having lived aboard a sailboat for three years and having used a similar product, I can say that I would have loved having this one instead for its lightweight build and suction power.The vac comes with three attachments and essentially a fourth built in to the hose; this slides inside each attachment and is angled to be used along narrow spaces.  The hose is about 3' long and about 1.5" in diameter.  You're not going to want to suck up marbles with this one, although suction-wise, I'm sure it has the power to do so.The exhaust (opposite end of the canister from the intake hose) forcefully blows air when running.  You could use it to blow off things... it's that powerful!  I can't see myself using that feature, but good to have I guess.The bag that catches the debris that is sucked into the vac - yes, there is a receptical that I would consider to be a 'bag', thus this is truly not a bagless vac but rather a re-usable bag vac - is very small, but so is the unit.  You are not going to be able to vacuum up a ton of dirt and dog hair out of a 4x4 pick-up owned by a logger in one run through the cab, but two swipes should get it pretty clean!  Perfect for detailing most vehicles except for the vac capacity and the short cord.The only real negative I found when using this powerful little auto-vac was the short cord.  The containment system for the cord (wrapping around the base with a notch for the plug to be protected underneath) is great, but oh how I wish there was more length to the cord itself.  For most jobs, you will need an extension cord handy when using this item.If you want a lightweight vac with powerful suction for small jobs around the house and/or cleaning out your vehicles, this is a good choice.  Just be aware that it won't vacuum up wet things (that would gum up the bag in the 'bagless' vac) or a lot of debris at one time.  You will also need an extension cord for most jobs.UPDATE: 5/10/11I used this vac to detail two of my vehicles.  As stated above the suction is great and yes, extension cord needed.  On the negative side, I discovered that durability of the rubber coating on the end of the attachments that would be placed against the carpet is an issue.  After one vehicle - the rubber was tearing off.  I'm not particularly hard on tools of this type, and the carpets were not in need of lots of rubbing, so this bothered me a bit. I was also not thrilled with the 'bag' that needs to be frequently emptied, which for me meant dumping the large debris and then folding it inside out and tapping it several times to get the fine dust out of it it.  The bag is made of a fiber cloth and there's no real way to clean it, thus the fine dust may (over time) affect the vac's suction ability as it would block airflow through the vac.This vac is still one of the most powerful of its type I've ever used, but durability of the attachments and the unit itself may be an issue.  I'm going to treat mine very gently and hope it lasts.
summary: Inexpensive unit with great suction, but durability may be an issue

reviewText: This vacuum works really well and it's very powerful.  Because of it's small size, it is easy to handle and the accessories should handle the vast majority of situations one will probably face.  The hose is long enough for most cars and trucks and can reach each side of the floor if you place the vacuum on the passenger's seat.This unit also functions as a blower by attaching the hose to the blower side (What a surprise!) .  The attachment is quite secure.Negatives include the doors on each end of the vacuum.  They open too easily so some care is required when moving the vacuum from place to place.  The vacuum's tools fall out too easily as well.  I solved this problem with a couple of wraps of tape (painter's tape in my case).  I had to experiment to find out how much tape was necessary but that only took a few minutes.The cord wraps very neatly around the base and there are slots to hold the end of the power cord in place.I fits very easily in my service cars as I detail my ride.I think this is a very well thought-out product and I expect to be using for quite some time.

As other reviews have said, this thing is very powerful!  It is lightweight, so it is very easy to move around the car.  The only reason I give it 4 stars is that the rubber around the attachments has started to come off after one use.  I am assuming this happened because the vacuum is too powerful and the suction wears away at it as you are vacuuming. Either way, this is still the best vac I have owned, and it is perfect for the car as it gets in all the crevices and easily pulls up crumbs and animal fur out of cloth upholstery. It would be nice if it were cordless, but that may sacrifice some of the power, so I am fine with this and and an extension cord.I am not sure why another reviewer commented that the vac caused an odor.  I have not noticed this at all.
Wow this little vac is no joke sucks up everything.really powerful suction is very strong.. i love it it's worth all the money. i purchased it usedwith this vacuum you can't go wrong.

Remarkable power for it's small size. It's a mere 560 watts, but this little bag-less sweepercan accomplish an excellent cleaning for all but the toughest jobs.The vacuum is handy for a large variety of uses ~ in house ~ garage & auto.I've used this many times and I've found it's done a great job.(125 watt = one amp, this sweeper is approx 4 1/2 amp, even though it's stamped 5 amp on side of sweeper)HOUSE ~ the console brush pulls the dust off our PC keyboard ~ lamp shades ~ grate of the furnace vent ~edge of bookcase (in-front of the books) ~ statues ~ and lots more.GARAGE ~ The blower exhaust is great for blowing off a workbench.AUTO ~ Three attachments, carpet tool ~ console brush ~ crevice brush, are designed to clean hard to reach places.> Carpet tool ~ goes under a seat with ease> Console brush ~ has bristles just over 1" which reach in vents.> Crevice brush ~ great for cleaning the 'bend' of seats.Has a nice length 12 ft cord which wraps around base for storage.MOTOR ~ has a thermal safeguard, the sweeper will shut off if it overheats, if this happens -1. Turn sweeper off2. Unplug3. Wait for it to cool4. Remove, empty & clean dirt bag. ( if needed, wash & air dry)When cool ~ reverse these steps & use.Features I wish worked easier ~1. (360 degree) Swivel elbow is quite stiff and requires turned by hand,trying to turn it by directing the hose simply flips the sweeper around.2. The hose reaches 40" then starts to pull the sweeper along also.3. The plastic edges of the base are a bit rough from molding.I sanded the edges smoother before sitting the sweeper on auto seats.4. I've learned to remove the attachments while in use, since sweeper easily tips over.Having said that ~ I still feel this is a five star product for the money.Bought at Costco, Nov 2013 after $4 coupon $29.99 + tax

This little vacuum is super handy to have.  My vehicle has a lot of nooks and crannies and when I am detailing it is handy to have this little vacuum that has a blower function to get the water out of those spots that you can't get to with a towel.  The suction is awesome for such a small unit.  My only complaints are that the attachment storage is not very good and the door to the filter can easily open if you don't use caution.  Oh... and the crevice tool has nice soft plastic around the tip that comes off pretty much the first time you use it.  All in all, it's a handy tool to have and you can easily keep it in your vehicle because of it's size.

This vacuum is small enough and light enough to move around my car with ease but powerful enough to pick up the dirt that has collected in my car this past year. It comes with three attachments to make the job easier.  My only concern is that uses a 12 foot power cord that worked fine for me but will be a problem for someone who can't park his or her car near an electrical outlet.The vacuum cleaner is light and easy to carry. It comes with a carpet tool, console brush and crevice brush in addition an attached blower grip handle.  All these brushes and tools have storage spaces on the vacuum so and are easy to attach and detach from the vacuum.The suction of the vacuum is strong and it picked up dirt that was under my car seats as well as between an arm rest/storage console that is between the two front seats in my car (I used the Crevice Brush for this). This is a good feature since I have used hand held vacuums that charged in my house and these had much less suction.All three attachments work well. The bristles on the crevice brush and console brush are soft enough so that they won't damage anything. The carpet tool is long enough to get under my car's front seats. There is an exhaust blower feature that works but I have yet to use it on anything.It is easy to change to dirt collection basket.My only concern as mentioned above is that this vacuum only works plugged into an electrical outlet and cannot be charged at an electrical outlet.  I have a garage with an electrical outlet so this is no problem for me especially with a 12 foot cord.  In addition, I have found that vacuums that can be charged at electrical outlets don't seem to have great suction and this vacuum is powerful. Still, if you can't park near an electrical outlet this will be a problem.Overall this is a small, lightweight vacuum that has a powerful motor and some good attachments.
summary: Light Powerful Vacuum With Usefull Attachments

reviewText: Used it today for the first time.  I was able to get all the areas I never could get to in my cars with other vacs.  As opposed to some other reviews, I prefer to use the cord rather that some "plug into the lighter vacs" that drain your batteries or a battery operated one that loses power after a few minutes.  This is one is much more powerful and gets the stuff that is caught in the car carpet, under the seats, the sides, etc...............  My wife also loves it to vacuum the furniture with it.  She doesn't have to pull out the big vacs with all the hassle to do upholstery and break out into a sweat having to drag the home vac all around the house.  She just carries an extension cord that is easy to do.  All we do is take a extension cord, keep it hooked up to the 12' cord that comes with the vac and just then wrap the extension cord around the vac,  Never a hassle.  One of the best things we have bought.  Makes life easier and who doesn't want that......?
Best drying towel I've used so far.  Only gripe is that because it is a large towel it is difficult to wring out.  Other than that it works as advertised.

Maybe it;s just me, but paying this much for a drying towel seems a bit silly.  But, I did.  The towel does work fairly well, but is not all that much better than the old terrycloth towel I was using to dry my car.  The only thing that MIGHT make this towel worthwhile is that it is micro fiber and will scratch the paint less than a regular terry towel.
summary: A pretty good product but overpirced

reviewText: This is one of those products that stands alone.  I bought this item back in 2003 and I haven't come across a product that performs better.  Keep in mind that some other companies sell a similar towel and I'm sure it performs just as well.  I just stick to Griot's because they have the lifetime warranty.Before I purchased this towel, I used to use cotton towels which tend to absorb very little and instead push more water around.  They also leave behind lint no matter how many times you try to "season" the towel. Then I used a product called the "Absorber." I think it is a synthetic chamois but I just grew tired of it. This drying towel is superior to any other drying product for a few reasons.1. The waffle-weave design is perfect for absorbing water and not introducing new swirl marks.2. It has hand pockets sewn in so moving it around your paint is easy.3. It's big enough that one towel will dry a medium sized car in no time.4. It's very efficient; it cuts your drying time down considerably.My advice regarding using this towel is to make sure that you do a final rinse of your car with a flat stream of water so that most of the water sheets off.  Don't try to dry a car that has too much water already on the surface as the towel can only absorb so much.  Just remember to do that final rinse and this towel will work 10x better. Also, you might be tempted to dry off some dirty parts of your car like the windshield cowel but don't do it. Don't stain this towel.  Use this towel only on the painted surfaces and then use the Griot's door jamb towel for dirty spots.  Do your best to keep this towel clean.  I have never washed this towel since 2003 because it never got dirty and I just air dry it after every use.I liked this towel so much that I bought two.  If they ever discontinue it, I don't know what else I would use.Five stars.
summary: A little pricey but I haven't found anything better, A very efficient product.

reviewText: I have to admit that I am a bit of a Griot's fanboy. I have been using the products for years, and my garage looks like a Griot's commercial. Somehow, I had avoided trying this towel for a long time, although I stared at it in the catalogs regularly. Like many others I probably thought it was too expensive for just a towel to dry the car with.I finally bought one, figuring "I'll give it a try". That was two or three years ago - and I've bought more since then and use them every time I wash the cars. I have two SUVs... one full sized and one medium sized. I can dry the entire full sized SUV with one towel, when using this amazing towel along with the Griot's Spray-On Wax.The fabric is soft and will not scratch your beautiful paint finish. It is also super absorbent. The waffle design of the fabric really soaks up and holds the water! But my favorite feature of these towels is the built-in (or should I say sewn-in) hand pockets. Each corner of the towel has a sewn pocket for your hands. It is amazing how much easier this makes the job.These towels will spoil you and you may never be able to use any other again!
summary: Best drying towel I have ever used!

reviewText: I got two of these for my birthday a few years back.  They are the best towels I've ever owned.  Griot's includes thoughtful innovations such as the little "pockets" that your hands fit into while maneuvering the towel.  These towels have remained soft with years of usage and are as absorbent today as the day I received them.  The price is ridiculous but I am still tempted to buy them as a gift for my motorcycle enthusiast dad.Based on my time with these, I believe this is something worth splurging on.
summary: the best towel I've ever owned

reviewText: I've several waffle weaves for drying cars after washing.  Some are ok, some are poor, this one is excellent.  The best that I've found in absorbing water and has a very soft finish to not scratch your show car finish.  Just never launder it with any of your micro-fiber cloths that you have used for spray detailers or removing waxes.  This will compromise its ability to absorb water.
summary: The best waffle weave for drying your car

reviewText: This is a really nice quality MF towel, but it's too big to be useful. The size makes it easy to drag on the ground or a tire and pick up dirt that will scratch your nice clean paint. It's also a total pain to wring out, I've tried all sorts of folding combinations but nothing seems to work well for me. If this were half the size I would probably give it four stars but as it stands it's just too big and cumbersome to work with.
A little on the expensive side for something made in China.  For this price, it should be made in the USA.  Good product otherwise.
summary: Nice product - should be made in the USA!

reviewText: The price was an issue, but I went ahead and got it. I'm glad I did. I have never had a drying towel or chamois dry this easy. The towel just keeps absorbing. I used it on my 2013 Highlander. The roof just holds water no matter how much I try to flood it. This towel doesn't push water around like a chamois it absorbs it. I dried the whole vehicle and I could barely squeeze any water from the towel. The pockets come in handy when going down the sides of the car.

These mini fuses are sometimes had to find, especially in the variety.  I haven't used them yet but I am sure the will come in handy.  Thet come in a case with each fuse clearly marked.  I would recommend these to anyone.
This fuse assortment is a much better deal than getting fuses at the auto parts store. I will certainly reorder when I run low on fuses again.
Great value vs. buying a few at a time. I know I will use them but it may take 20-30 years. I would recommend.
THIS WAS A GREAT PRICE  ! and the product works as described. Hubby threw it it the emergency bag in his trk and has already used it several times.

Good deal on a bulk package of mini fuses.  Great to have on the shelf when you need them and the case is great to keep them organized.  I think I now have a lifetime supply of mini fuses but hey, I can worry about other things now! :)
These seem to fit the bill for what I was looking for.  Have used a few and they seem to hold without a problem

I saw several sellers offering this kit of assorted car (as well as motorcycle) fuses.Even here on amazon.com you can buy this kit from more than one seller at a time.This guy sells the kit for the fairest price. I didn't count the fuses as others did it.So I can't say whether 120 were in the box. But for this price you can't say ssth.
Don't need all that many. Not the best quality but it works. Wish they drop the quantity and up the quality and keep the same price. What can I say; I now have enough fuses to last a few lifetimes.

The assortment of fuses is very nice because they are the ones that give the most trouble. The numbers are hard to see but they are color coded so if you are a car guy you know that a blue fue is a 15 amp and so on. You can't beat the price and the super fast delivery.

To look at the photo of this kit,..... it may cause you to think it is just more "off shore junk" but be certain that it is not.  I was pleased when I received the two of these kits I placed my order for.  Even the plastic box is good material, and the fuses look as good as any you would or could buy anywhere else..... especially for the price!  I bought 2, but if I needed more I would certainly buy them again.  Enjoy!Gary
summary: This may not look good in picture but is very good!

reviewText: This is a nice big assortment of mini fuses at a great price. The fuses look a little cheap as far as the rating number markings on top of the fuses go, but that really does not make a difference.
I bought these here on Amazon pretty cheap and they turned out to be a great deal! I've used a couple of them with no problems. I'll buy again when the need arises.
summary: Great assortment at a great price

reviewText: I separated these into several small sandwich baggies so I had an assortment in each of our cars. I put a couple of each color into each baggie and threw them into the trunk with our emergency kit.

It's always not fun when you pop a fuse and you have every kind of fuse except the one that you need.  Well this is a pretty good set so that you should be all set when that fuse blows...  And it's always good to have a couple of them for when it blows again and you have to figure out why :(
The title says it all. This kit is a great value and is an incredibly good value. Worthwhile in any car kit.
summary: Great kit for a great price

reviewText: For the price of what I would have paid for 8 fuses at a local Auto Parts store I got 120 fuses here on Amazon. They loose one star because the print (15, 20, 30, etc.) is very hard to read. However they are the correct color to amperage.
These are the same fuses selling at most automotiver parts stores for $5 for a pack of 5 fuses.  Worked well and no issues thus far
Never know when you, or a family member, will need a fuse. Nice to have these on hand when needed.

installed these on a 1985 BMW 325e. I had some difficulty installing them because the instructions were not clear. There is a little latch that you must open using a screwdriver or other object to pry it open. I ended up watching the installation video on Trico's website before I realized how they install. It still took me a minute or two to get the J-hook of my wiper arms to slide all the way in to the wiper blades so that I could close the latch and lock them in.They fit nicely and seem to work nicely, with no streaking, etc.The all plastic housing does not give me much confidence that they will last very long, but I guess that remains to be seen. Because of all-plastic mounting system and installation confusion, I only give these 3 stars.
summary: Work OK, quality remains to be seen.

reviewText: Easy to install...took maybe five minutes.  Works great too.  The blades push the rain away and leave no streaks at all.

These wipers are awesome. They glide across the glass and leave no streaks whatsoever. Definitely a worthwhile purchase. I installed them on a 2006 Chevy HHR and he match was exact. Easy clip design and no gaps on contact.

We will see about durability, the jury's still out. But on my truck, 2004 Silverado, they are not able to follow the curvature of the windshield so the blade does not contact the lower right hand portion of windshield. They do look good and where they contact they are OK. When these go bad I will switch back to old style because of this fault.ONE YEAR LATER: Well it turns out these don't last any longer than the usual blade. The first meaningful rain in a year and after one day they are chattering badly. The blade, when it reverses direction does not bend, instead it keeps the angle inward, so it chatters and grabs on the return stroke leaving streaks of rubber. The rubber in this blade deteriorates in sun just like any other cheapo. Damn made in China junk.

These are great blades!  They work as good as the Bosch but look better and cost less. I put one of each on each side to compare them and was quite surprised that these lasted as long. I will keep getting these..
Not great but ok  I thought they would would be better, plastic frames won't hold up in cold weather !
I purchased a set for my car and they're exactly the same as the OEM  units at HALF the price!
I ordered these blades because they are the same design and style as the factory OEM blades on my 2011 Sonata.  So far they are working well and I'm happy with them.
I have a big compressor that is not very mobile.  This tank meets my needs for topping off our RV tires and the truck tires
summary: Works good for airing up the tires

reviewText: This is a well above average air storage tank, nice hose and carrying handle, vey compact but effective good buy for the price along with AMAZON prime.

I purchase this for inflating tires on my ATVs and truck while out camping. I have a nice little heavy duty 12 volt tank-less air compressor and it can take awhile to fill tires. I now just fill the 5 gallon tank then top off my tires...much faster and no complaints from family like before waiting on the 12 volt compressor to pump up 35"s. No leaks as delivered at 100lbs tested. I have removed the tire inflation chuck and replaced it with standard 1/4"ntp air-tool quick release connector so I can use it with a air hose for using a blow gun and other air-tools when portability is needed. My only concern is the on-off fill valve not sure how long it will last but will replace it if ever needed.
summary: Works and Holds Air as Expected

reviewText: Hey, it does what it is suppose to do. Size, weight, air gauge is all good. Would do it over again.Larry

I really like this tank.  I choose this one over other ones listed on amazon because I like how it looks and I like the handle.  I have picked up other ones that are just the flat piece of metal and it's not comfortable at all.Tank doesn't leak at all and I was so happy with this I just ordered another one for my father!Only thing I did so far was put a quick disconnect on the unit so now I can use other attachments and I am going to be adding some little rubber feet for the bottom so when I put it down I don't keep scratching stuff... very minor thing but I think it would make it that much better.Only gripe is that it's 100psi tank and all others are higher rated.  The saftey valve is rated at 125psi and just like another reviewer wrote this tank is probably too conservative as far as rating.. I fill mine to about 115psi.  Held pressure all night with zero drops.The welds are nice and the blue is a nice looking color as well.  It's also light, so anyone should be able to pick this up.  Even the little gauge that comes on the unit (unlike what is pictured) is blue..lolEDIT:  I got a second tank because I was so impressed with the first one that when the second one arrived I was truely dissappointed.  It looked used and I think it probably was... wrench marks all over the valve, leaking from the hose..etc.  I sent it back.Another thing that I am not a fan of is the large price hike it just went to..  This tank was $37... now it's almost $45.. Still a decent value I guess but I'm not keen on how the prices here sometimes go up drastically with no explanation why..-Nigel

This is a well made, clean looking tank. It weighs 13 and 1/2 pounds. The tank part measures 18" long and is 9.5" in diameter. My measurements do not include the handle and valve. Five gallons of compressed air is a very limited source, but works great for topping off car tires. Easy to store and carry. In my opinion this is a great little portable tank.
It sure took me too long to find out that I can simply get one from Amazon and program it in less than 30 sec !!!!!Thank you very much.

Works Perfect, great range. Setup was quick and easy.. (With all doors closed and unlocked, quickly cycle ignition on and off 8 times ending on the on position, the doors will lock and unlock to signal the vehicle is in program mode. Press any key on the keyfob, turn off ignition. and done..) don't get ripped off at the dealer *sometimes up to $120* just to program your keyfob.. I definitely recommend this product
summary: Works Perfect. Batter range than my old one.

reviewText: Worked like a charm!

I was able to program the two remotes I got and went through the process several times. Some of the times the remotes didn't transmit. Once programmed, they take several tries right next to my truck to get them to work. They won't work from ten feet away like my factory remote does. Putting in a fresh battery didn't help.While they may work for others, they're useless for my 2009 F150. Buy at your own risk.

Great deal on a seemingly integral piece of equiptment for your vehicle. Well-made, high-quality OEM replacement. Super easy to program, often taking less than 15 seconds per vehicle (instructions included). Great price, super fast shipping. I've ordered 3 of these and have yet to have any problems...good stuff

I actually own the older yellow model.I understand the newer model has an upgraded grill and can measure the appropriate amount of car wash.That's fine and it certainly is an improvement over the model that I have but the two units still look the same and suffer from one big problem.That problem is that they are too big to be used effectively as wash buckets. They are light when they are empty but once you fill them with six gallons of water, they become quite cumbersome. Just picture a steep driveway and a runaway bucket with six gallons of water! Luckily my yellow model does not have the casters so I don't have to picture that scenario. But then again, I can't move the bucket around easily because it is heavy.I personally use a standard Rubbermaid bucket to wash my car and I use this Ultimate Car Wash Bucket to store my detailing brushes. I tried to wash my car with this bucket a few times but I just found using a standard old bucket to be more effective. In the end, car washing is not a science, you don't need grit guards and all this fancy stuff. I mean what is a grit guard going to do for you? Some debris will still make their way to the good water.As a storage bucket, it's great and it holds all my long-handled brushes and small brushes. I am happy with the product because it solves another problem for me in that it holds a lot of my detailing supplies.I'll give it three stars because it's an awkward wash bucket but a great storage bucket. Considering the price, I'm sure you could find a better alternative for either use.
summary: Very cumbersome to use as a wash bucket...I use it for storage.

reviewText: I had the previous model of the Griot's Garage wash bucket, which did not have wheels.  The grit guard in the old model floated as well, so it was absolutely worthless.  While this thing is very over-priced for a plastic wash bucket, I bought one just to have the wheels.  I've long looked for a better bucket, and even considered mop buckets which have wheels.  However, they are essentially the same price, and don't have a grit guard of any type.  The grit guard on this one stays put, at the bottom of the bucket, so it actually does serve a purpose.  This would be well worth the money at $25-$35, but at the current price, you have to be pretty enthusiastic about your car wash equipment for this to be worthwhile.
summary: Finally, a wash bucket with wheels and a grit guard that doesn't float!

reviewText: This is the perfect bucket in lieu of the standard round bucket with a grit guard. After you fill it with water, it will get heavy so the casters are a welcomed addition. The included grit guard has a small car wash measuring divot so you don't have to worry about using too much or too little solution. The shelf gives you a place to put your wash mitt while not in use so you don't need to leave it floating in the water or trying to find a clean place to leave it.Although as others have said you need to be on a fairly flat surface so it won't roll away.

I have been using this wash bucket for several years now. It is well made and well designed. It is a little on the expensive side, I think it could be $10 cheaper. Still, I paid full price for it a few years ago and have been using it almost every weekend (except winter) since.The bucket is large. It holds a lot of water, which is important. You go through a lot of soapy water when washing a car, and this minimizes having to refell the bucket as often and dillute the soap mix. The reservoir cup at the bottom of the bucket (actually, it's part of the lower grate that prevents grit and dirt from staying in the water) is a great measure for the soap. I fill that with the car wash soap, then fill the bucket. It also really helps in mixing the soap with the water.The bottom grate is good for keeping the grit out of the water as much as possible.The handle is good and I've never had any problems with it, whether lifting a full bucket - or just pulling it along the driveway.The wheels are sturdy and durable. Each wheel pivots 360 degrees, making the wash bucket very agile and mobile. Sometimes too much so... if you're on an incline it can sometimes be hard to stop it from rolling away. Being able to pull the full bucket along is certainly a back saver though! I sometimes with the handle were a bit higher so I didn't have to stoop so much while pulling it.The upper shelf in the bucket is genius! Also a plastic grate, it is perfect for holding brushes and wash mits, as well as other detailing tools. It allows the wet mits and brushes to drain into the bucket, while still being handy and accessible. I have had the shelf pop out of one of the supporting holes several times, but it is easy enough to pop the little tab back in. I keep wondering how long until that breaks off - but it is still going strong.Also very nice that this bucket has a lid. Once all my washing tools are fully dry, I store them in the bucket with the lid on to keep everything clean and ready for the next use. The lid is flat and strong, so you can put things on top of it to maximize your space.I love this bucket, and have had several years of use from it - and expect several more! So, why four stars and not five?? For the price, which I consider to be on the high end, it could have a couple of improvements, such as: At least one locking caster wheel to prevent it rolling down slanted driveways. A longer handle or some sort of pull option so you don't have to stoop over to pull it. A little better fastening of the upper shelf to keep it from coming apart. None of these complaints are major by any means - but some room for improvement, so four stars. But highly recommended!!
summary: Fantastic car wash bucket... a wee bit pricey though

reviewText: I've had this bucket for a few years and LOVE it.  The size is right for car washes and it has a handy grate along the bottom to keep your sponge/mitt above any grime that settles in the water.  Having wheels makes it easy to maneuver this around the car as you go from wheel to wheel, etc...  One flaw, and the reason I took a way a star, is that there is a second raised "grate" to hold your sponge above the water but the plastic on mine broke the first time I used this thing and I haven't been able to use that grate since.  I don't consider that a critical feature so it didn't bother me too much.  Also, this thing is WAY overpriced.  But good luck finding a cheaper one purpose built for car lovers.  Such is Griot's Garage.
summary: A great bucket, but not perfect

reviewText: This is a pro's wash bucket, has a grate on the bottom to trap grit & dirt, and another that hangs above for your various detailing brushes, etc so you don't have to seach if you left your brush in the massive 6 gallon cap bucket. Having it on wheels is a bonus as i like to wash in great detail.$40 bucks may seem like a lot for a wash bucket....but it's worth it.I did not buy this from amazon ....I bought it direct from Griot, they were offering free shipping and gaurantee their products, with my recent unsatisfactory customer service rec'd from Amazon over a measly $12 purchase, I decided to check out the vast number of online vendors out there.

This bucket is OUTSTANDING.  It has many designed in features.  Pour the liquid soap in the provided center cup.  Bottom grates separate out the dirt.  Top grate is useful to hold tools while washing the car.  Once done (and all the gear has been washed and dried) I can store inside the bucket.  As I said, Outstanding.
summary: Perfect Bucket for Washing and Waxing Car

reviewText: The moment I took these out of the package and felt how abrasive they were I suspected that they would scratch alloy/clear coated wheels. So, instead of first trying them on my $3K, presently installed Lexani's I tried them on one of my winter-wheel Beyerns. The wheel is clean alright, but Lo and behold, that wheel now has hundreds of micro-fine scratches all over it. The material is just way too abrasive for alloy/clear coated wheels, it literally feels like the scrub brush we use to clean the shower.Anyway, they're great for cleaning calipers so I'll use them for that.

Its great that amazon has a griot products (makes sense since both are in washington), my experience has mostly been positive with this company and these  continue that, seems sturdy and up to the dirty task of cleaning wheels.  I would give five star rating, but the only thing is that it does not get into all the nooks that i need to partly because the head is on the big side.  Other than that, works great .

My wheels have large openings between the spokes, so I guess I didn't think out my purchase properly when buying this.If you have smaller openings it may suit you, but for me it just doesn't cover enough "real estate" for the work I have to do when I use it.
summary: Doesn't work for me and my style of wheel

reviewText: Not much to say about these other than they work really well. For the price they are a good bargain, they'll last longer than you think but they will eventually wear out.Don't bother with the short handled version unless you are cleaning motorcycle wheels.Combine these with a quality wheel cleaner like Griot's, Meg's Gold Class, etc and you'll make short work of keeping your wheels their proper color instead of brake-dust-brown.Pros- price, effectiveness, quality.Cons- they won't clean your wheels for you.

I originally got these to clean up the wheels on my 12-year old car, which I'm trading in this month.  Looks like it cleans great!  However... My wheels are all beat up, and I can't tell what they do as far as scratching goes.Most alloy wheels have a clear coat on them, just like the painted parts of the car.  These brushes will surely scratch your wheels if you use it on nicen new wheels with the clear coat.  I tested this on one of the rear wheels where the clear coat was still pretty pristine, and using a 10x magnifying loupe before and after cleaning, this brush produced scratches.  I will NOT be using these on my new car.No one will notice the clear coat scratches on your wheels.  So take my advice with a grain of salt.  If you clean your wheels with this brush, spend about $20.00 on a good sealant, such as Klasse All-In-One, or better yet, Gtechniq 1.5 Silo Seal.  These are wipe on, wipe off liquids that will help protect your clear coats.  So scratch up the rims if you must, but at least put on some protection after.I'm becoming OCD when it comes to detailing my auto, so I'll stick to hand-scrubbing my wheels with a foam finger mitt.Recommended for people who just want to see clean stuff - this does the job! Not recommended for people who are anal about being careful with their car from top to bottom (like me) :)

These brushes work great for cleaning the tail pipe and wheel barrels on my car.  I do wish the brush was a little softer and slightly more flexible to make it easier to clean directly behind the wheel spokes, but that might effect longevity.  I have used them quite a few times and they seem like they will last longer than expected.

I took a chance on these and they are so-so.  I am worried they might "blow off" if the wind was strong as they just fit (15" wheels) so maybe after they are on a little they might fit better.  No way to insure they will stay on so will have to weight and see. $500 plus tires need to be protected from SUN.

These are great tire covers. Then again, I'm outside Phoenix, AZ too.  These covers are loose-woven cotton canvas with a wire tension backer for quick-on/off.  They are NOT vinyl or vinyl-backed. When it rains, it is going to get the tire wet. They are good for a little wind-blocking, and UV blocking...but aren't going to help you a bit when it comes to rain or dust.I got them because out here in the desert, if you don't UV block your RV tires, you will be buying tires every single year, even if you don't put a mile on them...the sun is brutal to tires! These are like sunblock for your tires...I've used them before (then again, I've used old T-shirts, too), and they work excellent...but if you are in Louisiana, or Tennessee, or South Carolina, or anywhere else you are going to get 50-70-inches of rain each year with lots of year-round humidity...they will rot in no-time, and doubtful do anything to help preserve your tires...in that case, you need VINYL COVERS. (Here...we are lucky if we get 10-inches of rain a year...during a two-week time period...rot is NOT a problem).Bottom line:  Be aware that tires dry rot because of two things - OZONE and UV in combination.  You can't keep Ozone or Oxygen off your tires...so you break the 'dry rot cycle' by blocking the sun.  If you are in a dry hot climate and need sun protection...BUY THEM. If you are in a rainy place...take a pass, and look for vinyl (also a good sun-block, but it won't rot like canvas does when wet).
summary: Perfect for desert or dry-climate, not for wet climate

Makes my wife feel much safer driving my 98 jeep (with no top) to have an overhead dome light come on before she gets in.It was pretty easy install and I am sure they sell something else for more money that will work, but this is easy with a few steps1) power converter wired to light socket under driver dash2) power converter output wire connected and run up through the roll bar3) wire from roll bar (yes I drilled a tiny hole to pull the wire through) attached to light positive and negative metal tabs inside battery compartment4) closed up battery cover, strapped in place, and done.the whole thing was less than $15 for a really nice, door controlled, overhead dome light

Installed on a Corolla and can easily say this is the best most noticeable and useable auto upgrade I've done on the car.  The difference in lighting is like night and day. Take a typical LED (not old bulb) flashlight and these emit just under 100 lumens.  So it's like having 16 LED flashlights pointed out on the road over what you originally had. No reason to not get these since they don't cost that much more than regular bulbs either. These are nice and bright, and take only about 5 minutes to install. Perfect fit for my 2004 Toyota Solara.
summary: Drop in replacement for 2004 Toyota Solara headlight

reviewText: Bought it for a spare bulb so when the other one burns out I have one.They work like factory part and would recommend to every one.
summary: Phillips 9006 Standard Halogen Headlight Bulb ,low beam

reviewText: You will need an adapter harness to use the bulbs on the new Accord. These lights have a second vertical guide bar in their base which blocks them from plugging into the factory low beam H11 harness.Impossible to file or cut off without damaging the two contact blades in the bulbs, and beyond brain surgery to attempt to cut the second slot into the factory plug,  you will need an H11 to H9 conversion harness. At least two vendors on Amazon sell these conversion pigtails.
summary: Not Plug & Play on 2014 Honda Accord

reviewText: Headlight bulbs can be expensive from $5 to $50 so when saw these bulbs on Amazon I grab them. For $11 this is a great deal and they come in the blister pack as shown.

PERFECT upgrade from my stock WRX H11 bulb.  I simply used a small drill bit to remove the small tab to allow proper fit for my modification. ( instructions and much more info on the net ). Do go easy with the drill bit as I did destroy one bulb... if the tip grabs when drilling it will go in and all the way through!  Just use the sides to round off that tab, go slow and you will be good to go.All I can say is WoW... I can see now! The quality and build of these bulbs are superb, Made in Germany ( you know the Germans make good stuff).  IMO the BEST Bulb on the market! Don't fall for the blue tint is better as the blue tint is a color filter as WILL cut your light output! The silver labeled bulbs say they give you brighter light but they overdrive the bulb with end results a very, very, very short life. Those cheep HID kits that are not made for a stock reflector / lens and  is simply going to make your fellow oncoming car drivers mad. if you simply want brighter light that will help you be safe on the road this will work great for you!Quality, Clear Quartz, German made, INCREDIBLE Low price,and  long life...these bulb and simple mod is the way to go if you want to see what is in front of your WRX!I did use an inexpensive ceramic wiring harness extender available on Amazon2 x H11 Ceramic Male Female Type Wiring Fog Light Foglight Socket for Carto help protect my factory wires from the possibility of any additional heat from upgrading to the larger wattage bulb. This was a very easy modification and only takes about 15 min to make driving at night much less stressful! Highly Recommended inexpensive upgrade as those H11 bulbs are for the birds!
summary: Used in my 2014 WRX  H11 to H9 modification. PERFECT!

reviewText: Works just like the original did, no issues just remember not to touch the glass with  with your hands, ok.

At 10 years, my right headlight went out but if I knocked on the bulb assembly, it would light up.  I would have to knock on it from time to time but 3 years later, it was still working, but I bought this bulb anyway just in case.  4 months ago, knocking didn't work and I replaced the original Toyota bulb.  It was easy to replace, just twist off, twist back in and don't touch the glass of the bulb, just the rubberized plastic mount.  No tools needed! Compared to the original one still working, it is as bright, and I can see no difference.  I tried replacing the other original bulb so they'd be replaced in pairs and be in sync, but I found that when the bulb works, the bulb assembly gets very hot, and its impossible to twist the bulb off until it cools down.  So, since its easier to remove once the bulb blows or I let the car park overnight, I just carry another bulb in my glove compartment to prepare for the day it eventually really does blow.
summary: As bright as the original on a Toyota Corolla

reviewText: I got this to replace one on my 2005 Chevrolet Impala. It's the same fit and color/brightness as what was in the car before. It's been installed for two months and no signs of dimming, blinking, or not working.

These bulbs really improved the light output on our Mustang. The car has aftermarket headlamp assemblies and the bulbs it came with were terrible.These appear to be made very well and really lit up the road so it feels safe to drive again at night!

So here's the scenario. I was driving my car at night and noticed that I couldn't see that well. At some point I actually got OUT of my car to check to see what was the matter and determined that my headlight was out!!!! OMGWTHBBW what am I going to do?Well I did some online searching and came across the Philips 9006 Standard Halogen Headlight Bulb (Low-Beam), Pack of 1 available on Amazon with free (Prime) 2 day shipping.It seems you don't need a mechanic to change these light bulbs. I received the blub and actually replaced it myself. I can only attribute this to the quality design of the Philips 9006 Standard Halogen Headlight Bulb (Low-Beam), Pack of 1. I have no idea if you can just willy nilly change bulbs made from a different manufacture so take that with a grain of salt.So since I know for a absolute fact these will work in my vehicle and I can change them myself, Heaven forbid if I'm ever faced with a headlight deficiency crisis again I will purchase the same Philips 9006 Standard Halogen Headlight Bulb (Low-Beam), Pack of 1 and pray that I don't have to drive in the dark with only one headlight.. like Jacob Dylan did in that song. Such a sad sad song...
summary: OMG the best Standard Halogen Headlight Bulb (Low-Beam) EVAR!

reviewText: These are standard bulbs. They work. They're cheap. Not much else to it. These give more light and clearer light (less glare) than the "blue" expensive bulbs that you see. Buy these instead.
Phillips, Thank you for removing g the needless greedy markup for a car headlight bulb, and providing us with a comparable to factory replacement at a bargain basement price!!!
summary: Easy to install and every day affordable!

reviewText: OE for BMW fog lamps. No complaints. Inexpensive, name brand quality, easy to replace, bright, not much else to say

These worked great as OE replacement bulbs in my Honda... the low beam on the passenger side had gone out, and when I came across these, I just decided to replace both bulbs since they were so inexpensive. They work great, Can't beat the price!
Cheap and light quality was similar to oem, at this price I can have a couple spares on hand. Will buy more as needed

Reasonable price.  Works like just the OEM.  Don't see any difference with the light output.You will have to press the middle lever of the white receptacle to release the hook, then pull it down.  After the wire has disengaged, rotate the base of the bulb and pull it out from the socket.  Reverse the process and your are done.  Very easy except my old wire socket was stiff that I needed to wiggle it a little bit to pull out.
These are perfect replacement bulbs.  You can't go wrong. And for the price you should get two... I understand it's recommeneded anyway.

this is the standard OEM 9006 bulb... it's a warm white, very warm... maybe like 2700k-3000k.... these, while not having a white hot look, last a very long time in comparison to other 9006 bulbs I've used.... even other Philips brand bulbs don't last as long as this one....it's cheap and gives you a OEM like lifespan instead of having to change aftermarket 9006's every year when they burn out....I'm fine with the OEM look and not having the hassle .... so two thumbs up for this product

I wouldn't go so far as to say these are twice as bright as factory 9006 bulbs, but these are definitely brighter than they were before.  You do have some slight modifications necessary for the 9012 to fit in the 9006 housing, but it took less than 2 minutes to modify each bulb and they both fit the first time.
summary: Used as a replacement to 9006 bulbs

reviewText: It does what a headlight is supposed to do and for the price you cant go wrong.  Cant comment yet on life.
Nice and bright like a high beam should be. I'm glad I found a pack of one because I broke one when taking apart light assembly
I was really hoping that these would put out some good light, but I found them to provide less light than the originals.

I used these in my 2013 Impreza for the HIR mod.  I cut along the line with nail clippers and the popped right in.  They are much brighter than the stock bulbs, just remember to disable your DTRL if you want to prolong the life of these.
summary: Used these for the HIR mod

reviewText: These are great bulbs for the price. I've been told the more expensive ones just have a coating of blue on them to make them seem whiter, but actually put out less light because of that.I'm using these modified in my cars H11 socket since they are brighter than H11 bulbs. I'm quite happy with the amount of light output and the price is quite good.
Perfect fit, why spend more money buying their so called super bright halogen bulbs that burn out fast and don't always have a brighter light.

Used to replace the original H7 low beam headlight in my Mercedes-Benz Sprinter.  It is very easy to install, and the beam is properly focused.  Cannot comment on life expectancy as it has just been installed.

Its good to buy a few of these for your car and keep in your glove box, never know when you will need a bulb, and a local parts store will sell them at 2 to 3 times the price of these.  Only thing is, the price of these bulbs fluctuate a lot on amazon, so add to your wish list and check back often how much the price has changed.  Otherwise good bulb!

Although i didn't buy my first set from Amazon. These bulbs are brighter than the stock bulbs that came with my 2002 Acura RSX. They lasted about 35,000 miles before one burned out. I believe this is more than your Osram/Sylvania average.  The bulbs are tinted blue which gives the headlamp similar to the color of HIDs but definitely not the same output/volume of light.  You simply can't get the same amount of output without converting from a halogen system to HIDs.  I recommend you try these if you want better light output then what originally (OEM) came with the vehicle.Note:  This is not 35,000 miles of night time driving.  Just racked up 35,000 miles after installation.Update 11/28/12My second set from Amazon, I had one bulb burn out after 15,000 miles. Installed in March of 2011 and died in November of 2012. Guess there are consistency issues here.
These are nice bright/white headlight bulbs and I would get them again but I switched to HID's which are way brighter and whiter.
You pay a little more but I think you see much better then the cheaper bulbs. I suggest keeping extra package around as they do not last as long as the cheaper bulbs.

I have these on my tundra and my wife's civic. They are great, we used to have more expensive lights we bought at autozone or someplace but they would last for 6 months and burn out. My wife has driven with both high and low beams in this model for over a year and no problems yet. I always use rubber gloves when installing lights to keep from forming hot-spots. These are a great price ($27).
summary: Bright lights, way better than stock

reviewText: Installing these after using the stock bulbs, there was a clear difference in brightness at night. good price too, compared to the auto store.

I installed this on my car, it definitely looks whiter and clearer than stock. For the sale price on Amazon, its worth the money versus other brands. I recommend this to folks who want a nicer look for their light and dont want to blind on comming traffic. I would buy this again.UPDATE 1/30/12: After 8 months of use, no troubles, the light is still white and still running strong. I just saw there's an extra $5 rebate for these, so what better time to get an extra set!For the people that have failed bulbs, maybe they touched the glass with their bare hands. I used latex gloves when installing the bulbs to prevent any contact with oils and have not had any problems.UPDATE 5/11/13: One of the light is dead, the other still working just fine. Only added about 22k on the car, it seems to be short lived, I will have to knock this down to 4 stars. I will buy again, hopefully the next one will last longer.

Contrary to many people's experiences and reviews, these are in fact not a pure white, but rather just a cute looking halogen bulb that projects a less yellow hue of light. Other than that, it is whatever...

Bulbs are fairly bright - though not significantly brighter than OEM. I thought they would be more whitish in color - but they are in reality very much like the OEM bulbs - much more yellow than white. Not a deal breaker - as they do work and do light the way.

I don't want to spend hundreds of dollars getting an LED light kit for my car, but these bulbs are the next best thing. I have every other type of bulb for the last couple years, with no luck. These bulbs are VERY bright and come VERY close to being LEDs. I will be getting these brand of bulbs from now on.

So I bought these for my dads 03 mercedes S430, one early morning he gave me a ride and I noticed how dull and weak his headlights were! I said for a mercedes this is pretty bad! He doesn't have the xenon or HID headlights, just the old fashioned yellowish bulbs. I replaced them myself, I tested them out on a wall at his work, not as blue as I had hoped, but definitely a cleaner light and a wider angle!! I can't tell you how they looked at night, but he texted me that night after he went out for dinner and said thank you their great!!! So I guess they are a success!  For sure it's a cleaner , brighter light and throws off a wider angle on the street, sounds worth it to me.....

I needed to replace the headlights on my 2003 Subaru Outback, and decided to give these bulbs a try seeing as they claimed to be white(r) than stock. Read ahead for a (in my mind) fair review.PROS- Coming from my car's stock, these are bright and very white- Relatively durable- DOT Compliant- Not blueCONS- Don't last long enough for money spentCOLORPersonally, I dislike the blue tinted HID headlights. When in the car, I find them very distracting and I just don't like the color tint. These CrystalVisions do not have a blue tint, and while they are definitely not HID, they aren't yellow either! When reading reviews where people say that they aren't different from their stock headlights, it is important to note that they might be comparing it to the stock bulbs, and some manufacturers have whiter stock bulbs than others. I know that my 2003 Subaru Outback had yellowish bulbs, and in comparison these are much whiter. It all depends on what came stock with your car!DURABILITYThis is my one complaint. These didn't last very long...maybe a few months at the most. I installed them properly, using new mechanic gloves to avoid getting oils on the bulb. Several months later, you guessed it, I was opening up the hood again to replace the first. I decided to go with a more expensive but reportedly longer lasting bulb, and so far no problems. If these had lasted 6 months, I probably would buy them again at the current price of just over $20...but at this point I am sticking with the other brand I found!OVERALLYou might get lucky, I have read reviews of these lasting upwards of 9-10 months, but I wonder how often these people drive at night. I'm not recommending these if you don't want to spend $120 on headlights a year!

Yes the light is white, if not whiter than the OEM bulbs. You can't tell if the light is white or yellow unless you spend more than 1 second starring at it. Considering the fact that you have to spend at least $100 to switch to Xenon bulb assembly, I say these bulbs are worth the money.
summary: It's white but you have to look very carefully

reviewText: Very good replacement lamp for the Honda Pilot which takes 2 sets of these. Easy DIY, just google for it and you will find easy to follow instructional videos. Great product from Philips.
summary: Excellent replacement lamp with higher brightness

reviewText: Bottom line first, RECOMMEND HIGHLY - I bought aftermarket Fog Light Kit to match the OEM Fog Light option for my VW Jetta Sportwagen TDI. I installed them; they fit and looked great and a lot cheaper than factory option, but the KIT came with cheap bulbs, one burned out in an hour of use. So....I bought the Philips H7 Crystal Vision bulbs and have had them coming up on TWO YEARS... Love them. I also took pictures of my Fog lights with the original bulb at night right after I installed them with the bulbs they came with, and then I took picture, same place at night, after I replace the bulbs with the Philips CrystalVision Ulta, no doubt brighter, whiter, more penetrating straight ahead and as good or better side illumination. Better all around plus long lasting, what more could you ask for.Although I have had them for almost two years I admit I hardly use them, may be a few hours of use. However I am glad to have them now. Although we have FOG today after a cold front that made national news, it is not typically foggy here, but I just moved into a neighborhood that has a labyrinth of turns that are not well lighted. I now use the fog lights to illuminate the corners and turns. Love it.NOW MY RECOMMENDATION:- Stick with NAME BRAND, Like Philips.- Stick with standard Watts, aka 55 watts for an H7.- Don't go for SUPER bright higher watt lights, they burn out faster and are illegal!!- You are NOT an off road vehicle and there are laws that limit how bright road vehicle lights can be.- Repeat higher watt lights or ones claiming to be way more powerful WILL BURN OUT VERY FAST!!- No matter how bright your FOG light are, YOU CAN'T SEE THROUGH FOG.- Fog lights are more for others to see you than you to drive like an idiot in limited visibility.- DON'T SPEND more than $10 to $12 or so per bulb; bulbs costing $20 or more are a waste of money.- LAST forget BLUE TINT, trying to look like FAKE High-intensity discharge lamps (HID lamps), that is silly.Bottom line recommend these, they have proven to be long lasting and useful. These are a good value and mail order saves a bunch over the Auto Part stores that charge way too much. My budget was to spend less the least amount while getting premium quality. I think these fit that bill.
summary: Best VALUE in H7 Bulbs - Long Lasting, Name Brand, Fair Price - Highly Recommend

reviewText: I do not own these, and never will for good reason.Any bulb with a blue tint to it will have significantly lower light output. It's best just to use regular, clear ones rather than these with a blue tint to the glass.

Ok, one of my headlight bulb gave up after about 6 years of use (from brand new car).I got this set hoping to get a more Xenon like light.It took me a little bit of fiddling to install it but it was due to my own clumsiness.Once the one replaced (I left the other one installed), I do not see much difference in color or power. One thing I am not sure about is if there was a way to install it that would prevent me from putting it wrongly. It seems ok but there is a kind of rainbow effect (on the upper edge of the beam) resulting from it.I did not get anyone flashing me as if my lights were bothering anyone so I guess that should be alright but I cannot help wondering if I did it right.
summary: Easy to install but did I do it well?

reviewText: The bulb colour is approximately the advertised 4000K. It's certainly not that bright HID white; you'll want to go to the Diamondvision 5000K bulbs for that. Still, if you want a nice, natural 4000K bulb, this is a good buy. The price is right, and they haven't failed in the 2 months I've had them. Hardly an indication of how long it'll last, but it ought to be better than the Sylvania's. I feel like the throw has increased when I drive at night, and can now clearly see where the left beam is shorter than the right beam (as it should be). For anybody wondering, the bulbs have a slight blue tint to them.
summary: Works good, little bit brighter and whiter than OEM

reviewText: UPDATE:  While I'm pleased with the light output of Philips H7 Crystalvision bulbs, after 11 months, both bulbs blew. I was vacationing in Maine at the time, so I picked up a pair of standard halogens ($15 each bulb with my "Massachusetts discount") and installed them, so I'd have something other than my fog and running lights for night driving, but the standard halogens appear dim to me.  I ordered a replacement pack of the Philips Crystalvisions and will install them as soon as they arrive in the mail.I cheaped out on the build of my Porsche Cayenne and didn't spring an additional $1850 for Bi-Xenon headlights, something I regret as I've had HID headlights installed on other vehicles and, although oncoming vehicles may not appreciate the blinding white light they throw, I feel more secure driving at night with them as roadway visibility is greatly improved.  After trying Sylvania Silverstar, which are roghly the same cost as the Philips Crystalvision, to find they didn't offer more illumination than the factory halogens, I considered an aftermarket HID conversion kit, but read that some conversion kits can cause damage to the wiring harness.  With that, I decided to skip the conversion kit and give the Philips CrystalVision Ultra bulbs a try.  Installation is the same as with any bulb with the fit being an exact duplicate of the OEM.  The light produced by the Philips Crystalvision bulbs is notably whiter (with a slight tint of blue) and brighter than the Sylvania Silverstar, which were an improvement over the factory halogen bulbs, closely resembling HID.  The cost of a pair of Crystalvision bulbs is less than even the cheapest HID conversion kit being sold on flea-Bay, but they are a direct replacement of the factory bulbs and won't cause damage to your wiring harness.  I've been riding around with these bulbs installed for about a month and I'm extremely pleased with their performance.  So much so that I'm planning to purchase a pair to replace the factory installed halogens in my high-beams, and eventually the factory installed H11 halogen bulbs in my vehicle's fog lamps.  Highly recommended.
summary: Notably brighter anf whiter than halogen

reviewText: I replaced the original lights on my 2010 toyota sequioa.  I like the look, bright white light, no glare, no blue tint,  good visibility to the sides, illuminates the road better than the oem bulbs
Great Match for my Morimoto Retro-kit!!!  These lights came in advertising 4100K.  My retro-kit is 4300K, they match VERY well.  Nice bulb at a great price.

And this is based on experience.I plugged a pair of Sylvania SilverStar Ultra headlights into my previous car, a 1996 Subaru Legacy.  Displeased with the results, I restored the headlight lenses with the 3M kit.  The lenses were crystal clear to the naked eye and the light thrown by the SilverStars appeared pure white from the driver's seat but head-on the headlights still revealed a trace of yellow.  In addition to oxidation, plastic headlight lenses yellow over time on the inside.  The only 100% solution: replace the lenses.That said, when I replaced the stock low-beams on my 2013 Subaru Impreza hatchback, the CrystalVision Ultra H11s delivered 99.99999% of the marketing claims.  The light output is pure white from both the driver's seat and to oncoming traffic but without the harsh glare of misaligned or aftermarket HIDs.  At certain angles, one can see a trace of the blue tips in the reflector but it's not the cheesy blue of non-steet-legal bulbs.  Longevity is unknown at this time, but I donated the Legacy to charity with the SilverStars installed after at least three years of nighttime-only operation (the Impreza uses the 9005 high-beams as daytime running lights).  We can only hope the CrystalVisions perform as well.
summary: If you're still seeing yellow, you might need new headlight lenses.

reviewText: This is the second pair I have purchased for my Jetta and these are by far the best bulbs I have used when compared to the other three I previously ran: Anzo, X-treme Bright and Silverstars. There is a white output which brightens the road at night, even highlighting pot holes on my daily route that the other bulbs did not show.  Definitely worth the $$$.

I bought the Crystal Vision's to compare to the Silverstar Ultra's I had in my 2010 Fusion. The Silverstars are rated at 4100K, and the Crystal's at 4000K. But what was strange, was the Crystal's were actually white with some blue to it, the Silverstars are still yellow. I think it's a marketing scam with Sylvania. Philips seems to hold true to what they put out. Philips all the way! Very pleased!
Needed to replace a low beam headlamp on my Z4. This did the trick just fine. Seems to match the original and fairly easy to install.
HUGE improvement over my stock bulbs and only cost $20.  These are a really cheap and easy upgrade and are about as bright as you can get without going HID.

I like these lights they are DOT compliant. Blue is illegal in My state. These really light up the night. I think they are whiter than Sylvania Silver Star. I have Silver Star on my Fog LIghts and they are rated at 4000 K and so are these H11 lights. The Philips are wihiter and do not match perfectly but close enough. There is no blue in the light. So dont think you are getting HID lights. HID runs at 6000K not 4000K. GO to your local hardware store that has LED home lights displayed and see what 4000K looks like its white.

In my book, only HID's look like HID's, so buying these to make your headlights look more expensive is probably an exercise in futility.However... if you like bright, pure white light, the H11 CrystalVision bulbs absolutely demolish SilverStar Ultras, Nighthawk Sport, and Nighthawk Platinum -- and until today, I've been a very big Nighthawk fan.The color difference between OEM bulbs less than a year old and the CrystalVision bulbs was absolutely obvious on a newer Subaru Forester. I was expecting a bit more blue, but these are dead-on white. The difference in driving was spectacular, too, as peripheral details really became more pronounced with these bulbs. And, while they're really bright, I didn't have any problems with oncoming traffic blinking at me.For the price, you really can't go wrong giving these a shot -- especially if you're due for replacement anyway.

I recently ordered this for an '07 Mazda3 s Sport.I was always frustrated by the poor light performance of the stock low beam bulbs with its short lighting distance, lackluster brightness, and off white/yellow color.  I had to get something different and after some research, I ended up getting these bulbs and boy, what a difference!The lights are more towards the whiter end with an VERY slight tinge of yellow and blue if you look at it from certain angles, but that's only if you look REALLY carefully.  The light output is considerably higher which is a HUGE plus and the lighting distance is about twice the distance of the OEM lightbulbs.Good range + good light output + 4000k color temp = Safer.  You'll be able to see obstacles in the distance & one wouldn't need to turn on high beams as often on dark roads.I'd very much would rather spend the money on mid-$20 headlight bulbs and prevent accidents from happening rather than paying $1000+ for damage repair.  Wouldn't you? ;)

First of all, there is a slight difference in light output, whiter than normal. But to get that whiter look your gonna have to go to the 5000K diamond vision range which turn out to be illegal here in Australia (best to check on your local laws) the beam output length is the same as OEM, and this becomes shorter as you go whiter in light. These lights are pretty much for looks, although whiter light has more clarity, you sacrifice beam length for whiter light intensity. HID however are the opposite.It is true what people have said about the life of these bulbs. THEY HAVE NONE! Think of your normal OEM bulb, then reduce the life of that bulb by 75%, that is pretty much all you can expect out of these. Don't be surprised if they blow after going over bumps in the road. I've been experimenting with a few bulbs out there, Although Phillips do make very good long life bulbs in the 3300k light offering 120% longer beam, these whiter bulbs (4000k - 6000K) just don't last and will end up costing you a fortune in replacements.Osram Bulbs are much more durable from what I have found. still on my first set of OSRAM Nightbreaker Unlimited, Have lasted me 8 months and they do have a 20% whiter light rating.Lets get serious. If you really crave that white light for your car, research HID xenon kits. I know the white light is cool, but be sensible and kind to your back pocket unless you have cash to burn.

3 of my motorcycles use H7 bulbs for the regular (low beam) headlight.  I replaced all three with the Philips H7 CrystalVision bulb and the results were impressive.  The light output seems to be noticeably  higher, but the most impressive part is the light is bright white - not yellow.  You can see my videos on Youtube under RedonKiLaus.

It is somewhat brighter (less yellow) than the stock.  My 2013 Elantra GT has projector headlight and compared to the stock i see a bit of improvement.  Its more white than blue, but def not close to the HID lights.My only concern is the longevity, and i'll keep you posted.
summary: The reviews are all about the same

reviewText: Just installed these and it was a breeze. I put one in and compared with stock and it was noticeably whiter and maybe even a tad brighter (then again that could be due to the whiter color).These are a good in-between from OEM halogen and those third-party HIDs. The third-party HIDs are no good as they blind oncoming traffic. So for the price, these are worth it to me.Now we'll see how long these last, but the first install and test looks good.
The color do not look whiter, no difference at all from my stock 4000k halogen bulbs.Do not expect this to shine whiter beams, but it is slightly brighter than my stock Osram bulbs though.
summary: No color difference from stock bulb

reviewText: Great quality but the lights are too yellow. Switch to HID so these are now being used as fog lights.
I prefer Philips brand when you are getting new headlight bulb if you want them more brighter, Silver Star burns out to fast compare to a Philip Brand.
summary: This is a better product than others.

reviewText: I was extremely careful with installing these bulbs, but upon testing out the bulbs I found out that one of bulb might have been damaged. Upon removing the bulb, I had found out that bulb was coated with weird material. I have installed and removed a large number of bulbs so I do not think it's related to installation issue.Now, I am stuck with one usable bulb out of two.
