One of the challenges of our new "Touchscreen Age" is the ability to remove fingerprints from all of our screens. While a couple of smudges and fingerprints are not that big of a deal - they may become a little distracting if you try to view photos or watch a movie. The Toddy Gear cloth are a fun way to clean your screens and still show a bit of style. Admittedly, not everyone is going to understand why you would need a "Designer Screen Cleaner" - but never fear... the product was not designed for them.Notes-- Is effective in cleaning touch and other smart screens. It will clean your screen without the need for water. One side is to clean your device and the other (silk) side is used to polish.- Large variety of designs to choose from- Has an antimicrobial coating- Machine washableFinal verdict - While it is bit more expensive than the typical screen cleaner the Toddy Gear Microfiber cloth is very effective and comes in a wide variety of designs. While it may not be for everyone the Toddy gear cloth is a fun way to clean your touch screens with a touch of style.4 StarsPlease Note - I received this product for reviewing purposes.

I've always been a fan of microfiber cloths for cleaning, but the Toddy takes it to a new level.  This is an ultra-microfiber that is soft, lint-free, and seemed to absorb those smudgy fingerprints on my iPad almost instantaneously.  The silk-like patterned side is rather slick so when I went to clean my iPad I simply folded it in thirds.  The pattern, which almost looks like a walkway, is set against a dark brown background.  The Toddy logo is in the upper left-hand corner.The Toddys are perfect to keep on hand to clean everything from your glasses to your computer screen.  I especially like to use this Toddy on my iPad and my glasses as those tend to need the most cleaning.  As far as cameras go, the blue mircro fiber can "camouflage" a bit of grit.  If you have an expensive camera, you may wish to haveKimwipeson hand instead.  I did however, find this Toddy especially useful for cleaning the camera itself and my numerous black battery packs which tend to be print magnets.I did wash my Toddy and dried it on low heat.  Anyone who uses a lot of microfiber cloths for cleaning will warn you not to use any fabric softeners, including dryer sheets.  The Toddy came out of the dryer as good as new and continues to clean just as nicely as it did when I removed it from its box.  It does have "antimicrobial protection to prevent the buildup of mold & mildew," but I don't think I'll have that issue because it's not necessary to use any other cleaning products such as Windex with it.  Great little accessory to have on hand and I love it.Sample provided for review.
summary: This Toddy premium microfiber cloth is ultra-useful for dust and print magnet surfaces ...

reviewText: There are two cellphones and two 7" tablets in our house, and we've been cleaning them with pre-moistened B&L; Sight Savers. They work very well, but they cost about a dime apiece, and you can only clean 2-3 screens before all the alcohol has evaporated. I tried one of the Toddy Gear microfiber cloths, and I was sold. The plush side of the cloth does a fine job of removing the greasy fingerprints and dust that accumulate on a touch screen. The manufacturer says the silk side of the cloth can be used to polish a screen, but I found that it usually wasn't needed, with the microfiber side doing such a thorough job.I ran the cloth through a cold-water wash, then put it in the dryer to tumble with no heat for a half-hour, and it was good to go again.The Toddy Gear cloth is small enough to carry around with mobile devices. At 5"x7", it can easily be folded and carried in any pocket. All-in-all, it's a very handy and effective accessory for any device with a touch screen.A product sample was provided by the manufacturer for review purposes.
summary: A very handy cleaner for touch screens

i used a few of these to add a quick connect to my atvs and lawn mower, the size of the terminal was perfect and works with my battery tender...
This should have posted the gauge for the wire which would help decide if it will work for you.  I would recommend doing more research before purchasing.
I have a number of battery maintainers and these harness work on them all.  It makes it easier to connect some of the batteries that I leave in the car or trucks that I leave outside in the winter.
Great product and does the job nicely... Well made and just right for your installations needs. I would recommend for sure...
summary: Perfect for and project with a battery involved

reviewText: Fits easily over the hook of my M12000 Warn winch and is nicer than the red Warn handle.
Works well, looks good, solid construction.  It has a nice solid rubber grab handle and is solidly made.  I've just left it on the winch full time and it's surviving that just fine.
summary: Works well, looks good, solid construction

reviewText: This grab hook helps get my cable out with no problem.  Easier to grab and hang on to than the red strap that comes with the winch, especially when having to make long cable connections in the woods in the dark and in rough terrain.

Fills a void in the market and isn't outrageously overpriced. I use this strap with synthetic rope and it works well. If you have a nice big hook on your winch then this product isn't really necessary.I'm also not sure I would use this product with wire line. The product doesn't seem heavy enough to support much force that would probably be needed with wire line.

Quality product that fits my needs.  I use these as stabilizing handles for folks riding in the back of my 4 passenger golf cart.  I hang them from the roof support and they give a great assist getting in and out as well as stabilizing the rider.
Best step I have seen and very versitle... Solid and very rugged... I figure its great on and can help protect your vehicle from rear collision...  Giddy-Up.
Feels solid and looks like it will last a long long time. Fits a little loose but not bad. Really happy with the purchase.

I had read all of the other reviews about this step prior to purchase and expected it to meet high expectations upon arrival and it did.  I am pleased with the overall durability of the design, the composition and the welds are highly professional.  I use this as my step to gain entrance into my slide-in truck camper and there is ample room to shift both feet towards one end to accommodate opening of my door.  Also use it in my front mounted receiver when working on my truck, very nice for this...no more standing on inverted five gallon buckets.The square tubular portion that inserts into the 2" hitch receiver is solid metal, not just some thin wall material.Would work well to attach a tow strap or rope to in order to extract a vehicle.  There are no sharp edges on any facet of this step so one would not have to worry about damaging tow straps.I am the type of person that complains and critiques all of the manufactured stuff on the market that cannot and will not live up to its claims.  Well, with this step I have no complaints.  I almost cannot believe that there is actually something that is made so well still available in the 21st century.Chris

Like others have mentioned it is very heavy and rugged.  It is not quiet so imposing on the back of my Jeep as others have mentioned since the rear tire still sticks out further.  If I open the tailgate it makes for a very convenient step and I am sure that it will be a great tie down spot for the things that I am always carrying on top of the jeep.  It is a little loose in the 2in receiver but everything that I put in it is also loose; something about every two inch receiver that I have had.  To keep it from moving around I attached three 1/2 in by 1 in small strips of self-sticking Velcro; one on each side except the bottom.  I adjusted the Velcro so that as the hitch is fully inserted the Velcro is just exposed so it is sort of being wedged into the receiver opening.The quality of the finish leaves some to be desired.  There was still some welding splatter on the bottom and the paint job was chipping.  But for the price that is not a distractor.  It just means that I will probably wrap it with some waterproof leather strips or something else just as cool looking.
summary: Makes a good foot step for the back of my Jeep Wrangler Unlimited sport 4 door

reviewText: Kind of dresses up my back bumper.  I like the "stinger" look, and it's a functional step AND a recovery point, in the center of my rig.  It also puts me at the perfect height to get items into and out of the roof rack.

This thing is heavy duty. Totally solid. I only wish it had a rougher paint job. During the winter this thing is slippery and my boots slide right off it. On the upside it sticks out a little bit more than my spare tire. Exactly what I needed.

it looks pretty heavy duty but damn when its in your hand it is heavy and super solid! kinda glossy finish but nothing a matt black coat wont fix!looks pretty sharp and be useful to access the the roof rack! wish it flipped up though! thats the only improvement i would make to it!

I bought this for my skid steer, to do some plowing in the winter.  It does not look real durable (it's just cheap plastic and the cord is a little stiff) but it works great and is very bright.  I've had other "strobe" styled lamps, motorized rotating lights, etc.  They seem like junk in comparison, now.  An excellent purchase for the price. Time will tell on the durability and longevity.
summary: A great value for the price, MUCH brighter than comparable strobe and motorized models.

reviewText: I purchased this a number of months ago, nearly a year ago in fact. It has gone through weekly use, hot summer and very cold winter. No problem whatsoever. The LED is the way to go versus the revolving motorized light shield of others I have had that froze or wore out. I believe you will be highly satisfied with this light.
I bought this as a gag gift for a bad golf cart driver. It actually works really well and is in regular use - not just as a gag.
Basic safety device light. Magnet is plenty strong to keep it in place. It has worked so far. They give you plenty of wire attached to it.
I just receive my order with this Blazer C48AW LED Emergency Strobe Beacon Light. I'm very pleased with this light, is working very good and have very,very strong magnet.
summary: Very good emergency strobe beacon light

reviewText: I've been detailing my own cars and my customer's cars for a total of 13 years; I'm a professional detailer. I'm also very obsessive compulsive when it comes to detailing, I detail with a flashlight that positions on your forehead; looks funny but helps a lot. I've been using Meguiar's professional products (Mirror Glaze) for a while and then figured I'd try this product out on my own vehicle, I always test new products on my own cars before adding to my arsenal. Black Light is a great alternative if you want to save some time by skipping the polishing process after removing all contaminants and only if your car's finish is free of defects. I rarely detail cars that are defect free, unless it's my own vehicle, so I'm still applying a compound and/or polish and after applying a sealant it leaves an extremely wet and slick appearance just like Black Light; except it takes longer. After using Black Light on my own car I didn't notice any deeper or wetter appearance, only that the surface felt really slick like I had polished and sealed my car again. I own three different brands of DA buffers, one rotary buffer, 15-20 microfiber rags from different manufacturers and shelves full of detailing products to include all different brands and types of pads and mostly Meguiar's products. Would I buy this again? Maybe for my cars to reduce the time on my vehicles since they are well maintained. My theory as to why black light is so slick is that maybe this product contains both a polish and sealant in one, remember, just a theory not a fact. You can find a link to my website on Facebook since Amazon likes to dot URLs out in reviews, search for E (and symbol) J's Detailing.
This really makes my black jeep shine. Just apply thin coat in lines not circles like wax. Wait 20 min and wipe off with a microfiber cloth. Easy on and easy off.
summary: great for black or dark cars.

reviewText: I have been doing auto detailing for over 10 years now and chemical guys has got me hooked! On quick details for dark cars I love using  black light. It truly brings that dark finish back out and leaves a mirror finish. Top it off with v07 and it is a great quick combo to keep a great maintained finish. This isn't intended for paint correction so I would highly recommend this if your paint  doesn't have any major scratches or swirls. If your paint needs some correcting and you want best results then you need to clay bar or use a clay mitt to remove all contaminants , compound, polish and then seal &/or wax.

I have been detailing cars for over 35 years, and have used just about ever product you can find on a store shelf. I read some reviews for this last week and decided to give it a try on my Black Cadillac. I did the entire car in less then an hour and the shine was excellent.The thing that really got my attention however was the next day it rained and my car was out in it all day at the airport. I came home and put it in the garage, the next morning it looked like someone cleaned the car, there was not a spot on it, it was actually so clean I asked my wife is she wiped it down, she laughed and asked me if I did the same to her car which is lighter in color, but I had also don't with the black light. All I can say is I am very impressed, and will continue to use this product on my cars.

I purchased this product and have used on my Porsche Cayenne Turbo (black) and my Corvette (red). Applied with high speed buffer with great results.  Really brings out the color.  Before I used a light scratch remover on my Porsche, I used the Black Light.  I was surprised that it actually filled in a lot of the swirl marks on its own.  I still applied the 2500 grit swirl removal and then went back over the entire vehicle with black light.  Does a great job.

I've had this stuff for over a year but yet to use it. After washing a vehicle, I get too lazy to finish it out with a good wax job.I finally used this the end of last year after a wash and I was really impressed at how much the car shined. Looked clean for much longer than I've ever experienced.
summary: Best my truck has ever looked

reviewText: Just starting out in the detailing biz, or if you're an experienced detailer, buy and use this product! You can shop here and find every store bought product that you can find on the shelf at your local parts store or family shopping center, but you can't find "Chemical Guys'" product there.Checial Guys was the best find I ever made in my automotive detailing career. I only buy mostly polishes, waxes, and detailers from them, and you should too.When you want a polish that will give your car or your customer's car that brilliant shine, buy Black Light. CG's Buetter Wet Wax and Carnauba Waxes are also excellent choices, and Black Light actually enhances both of those products too.Nothing you buy off the shelf will come close to the finish Black Light will give your vehicle. Give Chemical Guys' products a try if you're serious about maintaining your vehicle's finsh and keeping your factory shine on your vehicle.

I use this product exclusively on any dark colored vehicle that I have worked on (it is also GREAT on any other color as well).  It is extremely easy to apply and just as easy to remove and it looks AMAZING!  I typically apply Black Light to the entire car, let it cure for 15 minutes to 1 hour (sometimes more, sometimes less) while I shine the tires and finish up some other odds and ends, then remove the Black Light.  I then wipe the entire car with Chemical Guys Hybrid V7 spray sealant.  The Black Light + V7 combo is a well known process in the detailing world and is hard to beat!  You will love this stuff, and it smells great too!
summary: From a PROFESIONAL DETAILER - this is a must have for any detailer or car enthusiast!

reviewText: If you are looking at this oil, you likely own a Volksagen, Audi, Mercedes, or BMW.  German auto manufacturers are particular about their oils and Motul is certified by all of them.  Unlike American "Synthetic" oils, this is 100% synthetic and not a blend.  Which means better consistency and lubrication for your engine.  This was my first oil change in my recently acquired New Beetle 1.8 turbo and it has certainly brought a little extra to my bug over the previous conventional 10w-30.The price is worth it and it can safely extend your oil change intervals to 5000, and in some cases, 7500 miles.
summary: Nothing but the best for my VW turbo

reviewText: I ordered this instead of the Mobil 1 Euro 0W40 that I had been using for a few reasons:1. recommended by various porsche mechs for lower wear/ longer engine life2. VW/Audi and porsche approvals3. prices similar4. I want the five liter package to save on packaging; one of the few better oils available this wayNice package, includes a pour spout that pulls out.
summary: Great product for VW/Audi or Porsche

reviewText: I drive my wrx in the city and also do some auto x and track days. This stuff doesn't appear to burn off between oil changes and is great for use all year around. I heard rotella T6 is cheaper and works as well but I'm an oil snob.

I used this oil in my tuned Subaru STI, and it works great.  Very little oil consumption.  I also like the extendable neck which is an integral part of this bottle.  Definitely the best oil for the money for a turbodiesel or turbocharged 4-cylinder.
summary: Great for turbo cars (diesel or gas)

reviewText: I've been using this in my STi for over 4 years now... I used to use Mobile 1 and wondered why I would always pull out LESS oil than I put in... Found this on my forum and decided to try it...  Needless to say it's awesome.  Car no longer burns oil and the fact that it's a little heavier weight means when you autocross it, it's not going to be super thin and burn.  Overall I love it.I use motul in both my Daytona 675's and couldn't be happier with their products...If this is for a DD then I'd probably look at something cheaper, like the Rotella sold at costco for the same price but you get 12 quarts, actually I do believe it's 10 bucks cheaper... but for anything performance this is the way to go.-Nigel

I ran this in my Last AUDI and I just did a change in my 2003 Porsche Carrera S4. Consumption has gone down drastically and the car drives noticeably smoother. At the price you pay on Amazon, you have nothing to loose. It's worth it.

When I know I'll be off-roading on a rugged trail, I always air down my tires to give me better traction and to soften up the ride.  Well, with this little gem I no longer need to use a screwdriver and a separate tire gauge.  Just screw the business end of this ARB deflator onto your tire's valve.  Then, take the small secondary knurled knob on the back of it and push it forward while turning counter-clockwise.  That smaller knob actually unscrews your tire's internal valve stem and holds onto it, allowing for a much faster deflate.  Use the sliding collar on the deflator to periodically check your tire's pressure, and once achieved, keep the collar in the closed position and use that back knob again to re-install the valve stem.  Don't overtighten that little inner valve stem too hard, as they have tiny threads.  Remove the entire deflator and move on to the next tire.  I deflate my 33" KM2's from 35psi to 18psi in less than a minute per tire.Note:  the included pouch makes great storage space for extra valve stems just in case.
Love it. I makes airing down tires easy and accurate. Give you alot of control when airing down tires. The gauge helps so you dont have to let out the air and then check it with a separate gauge.

reviewerName: C. Beard "I have not gone where I intended to...
reviewText: Makes deflating tires on the trail very easy.  I like well made products that save time and this fits the bill, you can always count on ARB to make good stuff.

if you dont know what this little gizmo does ill explain.where you air up or air down your tire, there is a little bitty valve installed in that rubber valve stem.  when you have a bigger offroad mud terrain tire (i have two sets, 35'' and 37'') it takes FOREVER getting down to 15 pounds of pressure from the 30 to 35 pounds i normally run.  when i say forever i dont really mean forever, more like 3 minutes or so per tire.  that doesnt sound bad, but times that by four and you are at 12 minutes just airing down.  thats 12 minutes you could be trying to break something expensive on your offroad vehicle.this little gizmo removes that valve completely while housing it in its body.  there is a part of the body that slides back then wham-o, you are airing down with no valve in the valve stem.  you are now looking at around a minute or so per tire.4 minutes versus 12 may sound trivial, but when you are wanting to go play in your jeep, toyota, whatever and you are stuck with a tiny stick or rock you found on the ground poking at the top of the valve stem you will wish you had this guy.
summary: an absolute must for airing down big offroad tires

reviewText: I used to hate airing down my tires. Now I love airing down my tires because this makes it so fast and easy. Where have you been all my life?
summary: I now love to air down my tires

reviewText: This product is of high quality and a great value. The only flaw would be that you have to deflate one tire at a time. I like it and have used it many times with no issues.
I was always the last to get my tires aired down.  Now I'm fast as my friends who already have these deflators.  Easy to use and rugged.

Very fast. Air down from 35 to 18 on all four tires within 3-5 minutes, then help others who only brought a stick to the trail.-1 star because the Amazon packaging it arrived in was small and left a kink in the hose. Doesnt seem to effect performance, but still irritating on a $40 tool.Recommend Viair 85-90P as a convenient way to air back up.

A solid product from ARB that gets the job done fairly quick -- and the pouch is well-made too. To be honest, I have not tried the kind that you actually leave on the tires, so I can't compare. But this thing worked very well for my needs.
Works great! Wish i would have gotten this earlier, when i was letting air out with corner of screw driver,lol..
Love the quality here, this deflates our tires very quickly for trail use.  I'd buy this again for sure, comes with a nice bag too.

bought this to air down the tires on my Jeep. Practiced in the driveway before a trip we are taking in a couple of weeks.Easy to control the deflation. Read the instructions - makes it easier. Compact size fits easy in the Vaiair compressor bag.
This is the same as anther one on the market but I think just because it says ARB on it i'm pretty sure its made better and the other one that looks like it.
The pads for my 5" electric polisher fit perfectly. The are snug and don't slip.It takes some effort to install them, but it is worth it to get a smooth action of the polisher
Gotta admit,, this will come in handy... These are a Value type Bonnet Kit but I think they will do the job
The 6 in bonnet fits great on my turtle waxer. Make shining my Cadillac a breeze. Always nice to have a clean caddie.

Nothing special. They do the job and they last a reasonably long time.I always hate it when the shipping is more than the price of the product, but in this case it wasn't too bad at all.  For $.35 I got 4 bonnets and am still using them.  I find that they do a good job, I don't worry about scratching, and they are washable.

These are just too thin to hold much removed wax and if you're going to do the job properly, you'll find yourself changing pads a dozen times while doing the whole car.  Easier to just use some good micro-fiber towels and hand buff.

If you want bonnets with the texture of a used kitchen towel and like to add swirl/scratch to your car than this is the product for you. It is by far the worst quality I have seen, this isn't even microfiber or clear coat safe. I can find softer material to use on my car at a 99 cents store. The blue pads are seriously the same material the dentist uses as a bib for patients, it feels like a cheap plastic sheet of foam and the white buffing pads feel like a dried up used rag you would use for cleaning kitchen counters. Don't waste your money on this cheap representation, shame on you Turtlewax for allowing such garbage product to be under your name brand.

I only got to check it out a a couple seconds, when I touched it to the contacts in my truck's dome light, it was a bright clean light, definitely what I was looking for.  But when I was installing it, one of the contacts snapped off the circuit board.  The end contacts are only attached via solder connections, and it didn't take much for that to break.  Looks like I'll just get a regular incandescent bulb from an auto parts place.  Disappointed.
summary: Good and bright, but it broke when I was installing it.

reviewText: This bulb is brighter than others that use 9 LED's.It makes my car's interior look like daylight.Buy it if you want something bright as hell... Just don't look right into the damn thing.Oh, and the color is really good. Very nice, crisp white color. Not bluish like some other "white" LED's.

This works great as a replacement for above head dome light.  Just be aware that you may need to adjust the position if it doesn't light correctly and as it is a LED (non-incandescent) it will shorten the dimming if your car has auto dim features on the light.  The light is a cooler white and not as warm.  Great if you know what you need.

The old light would give off too much heat, causing the plastic navigation light lens to crack. So after buying a new lens, I decided to replace the bulb with LED which is about 3x as bright and barely puts off any heat, you can touch it with your finger without getting burned while it's on. VERY bright light. One note, the back of it does not light up. You get 180 degrees of illumination so if you have something that requires more than 180, get a different bulb. My nav light only needed 180 so this was perfect
summary: used on boat to replace old light

reviewText: Brighter than my OEM single bulb. Fit perfectly in a na miata dome light. Easy!The coaster is an odd little addon though. Got a few chuckles out of it.
Ihaven't used it yet.  I have been looking for something this size.  They don't all have these features.  I beleive it will serve my needs.
Nice little inverter. Would be great for a laptop or charging a phone. Read complaints about the loud fan but I didn't notice and I can't imagine it being that big of a deal.
Nothing exciting, but it does its job.  I think it even had a USB outlet on it.  This went in one of our service trucks.

I have had this product running in my car almost every day since March of 2012.  The fan isn't too loud.  It is the same today as it was when I bought it new.  I am in the car A LOT.  This thing is on ALL THE TIME.  I do like how I can flip the power switch and it will shut off the fan as well as the 110 outlet but will keep the USB powered.  I don't like how the USB works.  I charge my Galaxy phone and my Wilson cell phone signal booster at the same time with this inverter while I keep my laptop charging.  It does not matter what I do. I can have nothing plugged into my 110, I can have something plugged in, I can have ONLY my phone USB plugged in.  No matter what the combination I cannot charge my phone.  For example.  Last weekend I put the phone on the USB.  At the time my phone had a 100% charge. I had a 10 hour car drive.  By the time I got where I was going (the phone plugged in the entire time) I was down to 77%.  I have tried switching to the other USB and it is the same concept.  No matter what I try this is the end result.  If it wasn't for this little issue I would throw 5 stars at this thing all day!
summary: Great For Running  A Laptop, Not So Great For Running Dual USB's

reviewText: We used it on our first road trip to PA and it worked great. At one point we used both the 110volt and usb connections without any problems. It is built tough and quiet. Has a power switch on front and indicator light. It was well worth the investment.
This little inverter packs a punch! Has plenty of power yet is small enough to use & store. The multiple outlets (AC & USB) will become very useful!!
This item worked as described but I had to send it back. However, if you need a good plug for traveling, this does it well.

It works well, and it feels solid. When you run it there's a little fan that turns on inside to keep it cool. At first I'm like "aww man, now I gotta listen to that fan the whole time" but now I realize that the fan keeps you from accidentally turning off the vehicle and leaving this thing on to drain the car battery...
summary: It works well, well built, fan noise is actually a plus.

reviewText: I like this power inverter for the following reasons:- It is cheap- It has 300W of power so it should be enough to power at least two laptops in the same time.- It is quite silent- It has also USB ports integrated.In these days and ages when most people are using a Smartphone and want to be in touch all the time, having such a power inverter can be very useful if there is more than one or two people needing power at the same time. I know I need my Iphone to be plugged as often as possible if I want a simple chance to keep the battery for the whole day (which is a shame I have to say!).In my case, the Bestek dual 110V is a perfect solution.

I bought this unit as a replacement for my old direct plug in inverter.  This model is light, quiet and easily powered a couple iPhone chargers and 2 laptops while our family was taking a car trip.  Now I carry this unit on business trips to be sure I've got 110V AC or USB power when needed.  It's small, light and easy to tuck into my carry-on bag.  The cord is about 12" long, so it reaches the floor for a front or rear seat power outlet.  My son loves it too!
summary: BESTEK Dual 110V AC outlets and Dual USB 3.1A 300w power inverter car

reviewText: Helpful advice, do your research before you buy. I wanted this to be able to vacuum out the car with my little mobile vacuum and I wanted to plug in my 13'' TV with a blue-ray player for trips. This does not supply enough power to do either. It works for plugging in small devices like charging electronics but it can be easily overloaded with big devices. You will need to purchase a power inverter with a larger capacity to power those other devices. I gave it 5 stars because it powers what it is suppose to power just be ware of what you want to plug in to it.
summary: Works but... only for smaller electrical equipment

reviewText: Works great from the cigarette lighter outlet to power a cell phone recharger and a 90w laptop.  small and quiet.

I bought this mainly for charging my apple laptop and it didn't work.  I never tried it for anything else so I can't comment on whether it works for other applications.  I was disappointed because I thought for sure that this one would work after trying others with lower wattages.  I ended up sending it back.
summary: This item didn't work for my intended needs.

reviewText: I must say that I am very happy with this purchase.  This was the perfect size to stick in my car's center console.  Unfortunately, you really should not run the inverter in a closed environment, so I did not feel great about turning it on inside the console.  What I found, is that the two USB ports charge regardless of whether the inverter is switched on or not(as long as it is plugged in, obviously).  This is great for me.  This means I can charge my phone while the unit is "off" and still have the AC power ready when needed.  I did not expect this to be the case at all and I am thrilled that it is so.  I have not tried to plug in any more power demanding electronics into this device yet, but I will report back.  I plan on updating this review as I use this inverter...UPDATE(7/20/2012):Aside from continuing to use this inverter in my car to charge my phone, I was able to make use of the A/C plug during recent power outages on the east coast.  I had already purchased the "Roadpro 12V Battery Clip-On and Cigarette Lighter Adapter" which I hooked up to a 12V tractor battery.  I plugged in this inverter and was able to power my TV and computer simultaneously making use of a power strip.  This worked for about a half hour, but I realized that I was drawing too much power from my battery and had to unplug the TV.  There is an indicator light on the unit to show if you are overworking it and the color switched from green to red.  Running the TV and computer was just too much, but after unplugging the TV, I was able to keep my computer charged until the power came back on three hours later.  I had tethered my phones internet to my computer and had power and internet the whole time and was able to use my computer normally.  I recommend only running one thing at a time off the A/C power.

During long car trips, there is a frequent need to charge my camcorder, camera batteries, my laptop and many more. However stopping at a place and plugging them is not convenient and wastes your time. Before buying this, my only solution was to fully charge everything before leaving home and during my hotel stays or bring an extra camera battery. Yet again that is not the perfect solution either.When I ran out of my camcorder charge while on a very scenic trip, the frustration of not being able to record made me decide buying one of these. I first hesitated buying due to some reviewers saying it burnt, or they were almost catching fire etc. (these things actually happen in many electrical items but very rarely once used properly) so I went for that and bought it. So far I have not experienced anything close to that. It is a single piece item: no cords to get loose (permanent attachment of the charging cord to the actual charger) or get lost... I still keep it in its bubble wrap under the driver seat. It is not heavy but heavier than a laptop adapter and it charges small items easily without keeping you off from your way.Having two USB charging ports is a plus too so that you don't need to daisy-chain this to a 12V multiplier that has USB function, however if you have a GPS charger then you still need an 12v multiplierBESTEK usb adapter car cigarette lighter socket car splitter adapter 4 way plug socket usb outlet dc charger power adapter 12V socket 24V dc adapter car charger Ipad Dual USB charger 2.1A MRS152UVto stick both in. (I used this with and without the multiplier and so far it is fine both ways.)It has a fan that works continuously but the fan is not noisy (I don't hear it while the car is on the go) and the unit never got hot even during 1-2 hour long uses.My only concern is the design of the item. It feels like it is metal outside with some sharp edges that can scratch the plastic parts of your car during your trip if not placed well. Besides, I am also worried that it could pose a big risk in case of a crash... I don't want to imagine a brick size sturdy object flying in the car. Therefore it would be best to keep it under the car seat or somewhere safe, if not in use and secure it as much as possible while using on the go.
summary: a good travel companion so far...

reviewText: I got a lower wattage unit from this same brand/company to keep in my computer bag for travel.  My dad liked it.  So I got this higher wattage version for them to keep in their van.  Can't beat the price.The fan noise isn't that annoying considering it's in a car making noise and the radio is often on.  I wouldn't use this without the car running though so that the battery wouldn't run down.

Does a good job. It doesn't charge everything that I plug in to the USB ports but I have found that it isn't the fault of the inverter.  I have a couple of older phones that require a lower amperage. I plug the older phone(s) into the AC side of the inverter and didn't have a problem so no big deal.  It is a bit noisy but most with fans are.  I don't notice it much once I start driving as the road noise drowns out any noise it may be making. I plan to purchase again for other vehicles.
works very handily for the computer, cell phones, etc. while I the car, We have had all 4 ports in use at one time and the cigarette lighter fuse did not blow.

I added this to my RV so that I could tune in TV stations easily. Some Digital TV's do have a signal strength indicator, but not all.  In those instances, this meter comes in handy.There are two minor issues though, and the first one really is not the fault of Winegard, as I am not sure what the solution is.The issue is that prior to going digital, TV stations used their Analog channel number for their identity. For example, a local TV station in my area always calls themselves "Channel 8" in addition to their call letters, which was of course their broadcast channel.But when we went digital, they still use the Channel 8 moniker, but that is no longer accurate as they broadcast on channel 20.  There is the problem. The Winegard Sensar Pro displays the true digital number, so in the above example, I would have to set the display for channel 20 to tune in "Channel 8" to the max signal.Unfortunately, there is no standard cross reference between the old analog and new digital channels, so you have to go to a website such as [...] and enter the station's call letters to get the true digital channel.As I said, there is no real solution, so I don't fault Winegard for that. They display the true digital signal, which is really the only solution.If you are going RV'ing to a specific destination, the easiest thing to do is go to one of the channel identity websites and get the channel information before leaving.The only real improvement I could see is when the device is turned off. Even in the off position, a LED is on. OK, one LED does not take a lot of current - maybe 10mA, but over time, say a week boondocking, that 10mA will result in loss of 2AH of battery power.  And 2AH here and 2AH there, pretty soon it adds up to a significant load.I added a disconnect switch so I could completely disconnect the Sensar Pro so there would be no current drain whatsoever for boondocking purposes. The current drain - even in the off position is the primary reason for 4 stars rather than 5, since at least occasional boondocking is a real possibility for a RV.
Works great in the driveway (about. 25 miles from stations). Haven't been able to try on a trip yet, but no reason to believe it won't work well. Pretty easy install, too.

A good guide to helping find a signal.  Helps eliminate all the trial and error time it used to take to find a TV signal.  I installed it using a 'Y' for the 12 volt power to I would still have the cigarette power outlet to power the TV and also power the meter.  It took about hour to install.  You will have to cut a new hole in the wall for this unit in order to keep the signal booster and power outlet,  They don't tell you this in the instructions

Digital TV has given us beautiful HD images, but if you've repeatedly gone through the ordeal of guessing where to aim your RV antenna, scanning for channels, then readjusting the antenna and re-scanning to see what you missed, you know that is a nuisance.  This device offered to solve that problem, so I ordered one.My 2011 Itasca Sunova 33C motorhome came equipped with aWinegard RVW-395 Sensar IV White DTV/HD TV Antennaand built-in amplifier, so I anticipated that replacing the factory-installed antenna amplifier with this SensarPro would be a simple swap job.  How wrong I was!  The factory-installed Winegard amplifier was mounted on a steel panel in a cabinet above the front passenger seat.  Unfortunately, the opening provided by the RV manufacturer for that booster was dramatically smaller than the opening that is required for this SensarPro.  This was no simple swap job.  Fortunately, I had a nibbling tool in my shop, some good files and old metalworking skills, so I went to work enlarging the hole in that steel plate.Complicating the work, this SensarPro requires screw tabs projecting into the top and the bottom of the rectangular mounting hole.  They're like the tabs you often see on metal electric outlet boxes.  It was lengthy, tedious work nibbling and filing that steel plate, but I'm delighted to say that my work was rewarded.  The RV factory had installed a splitter behind the panel to feed two TV from the original Winegard amplifier.  This SensarPro has connections for two TVs, so I was able to get rid of the splitter, thereby boosting the signal.After mounting this device on the panel opening I made and established all of the connections including the required 12-volts DC, oriented my antenna for optimum signal strength shown on the SensarPro panel, set the amplifier's gain at maximum and ran a TV channel scan.  Having my motorhome parked about halfway between New York and Philadelphia, I was able to pick up 46 digital channels.  The SensarPro instructions suggest setting the gain at 10, but my best results came from the maximum setting 20.  Perhaps if I'm closer to TV stations, I'll need to reduce the gain.  Thus far, I have been pleased with my purchase..
summary: Greatly Simplifies Aiming my RV Antenna

reviewText: I bought this after being frustrated with my old system of "rotate antenna, do a channel scan, rotate again, do another scan, etc".After installing, we went to a campsite we were at a few months previously where we only picked up one channel using the manual method.  Using the new Winegard Sensar Pro, we were able to home in more precisly in the direction of the antennas for different stations and picked up 3 more channels, including a nice digital PBS station, that we didn't find previously.My only gripe is that it's not easy to install this somewhere where you can see it or work the controls near where the antenna crank/rotator is.  I thought about this ahead of time and installed it in a spot where I can (barely) see the display while rotating the antenna, but it's awkward.  Not all RV's will be as flexible in the location, I'm sure.  But you can turn up the volume on it so if you're unable to read the numbers while rotating, you can at least go by the beeps.  You'd be moving around a lot more to work the different functions of the unit (go from scan to channel for instance), but it can be done.  In my case, I was able to mount it inside a cabinet in the bedroom where the antenna crank is located, just on the other side of the wall where the TV itself sits.  The TV in our trailer rotates to be viewed from the living area or the bedroom, so once I'm tuned in, I can even rotate the antenna and see the results on the TV itself, which has a signal meter too.  But the Winegard meter is more convienent now.Setting the gain is helpful... where we camp in the boonies, it usually means setting the gain all the way up to 20, but I can see how if you're near a broadcast tower, you might need to lower that to avoid overload distortion.  The gain might be less useful on digital broadcasts than analog... yes, there are still stations broadcasting in analog (near Astoria, Oregon in our case).Installation was no problem, but then I'm handy.  Since I wasn't just replacing the stock Winegard amp that came with our antenna, it meant making an entirely new cutout in a very awkward to work in place, but even if I replaced the stock amp, I would have had to enlarge that cutout to make this one fit.  So be prepared for some work there, or just let a pro installer do it if you're uncomfortable making holes in your RV.

reviewText: I won't rehash all the glowing reviews about this sets' superior construction and content. I will say that both its handles survived multiple whacks with a drive hammer and survived. It is billed as a "4x4" repair kit for off road tires, but will also work quite well on passenger car tires.So here's my experience with a few pointers to make things easier.First after you gather all the tools, lube, cement (more on this later), pre-thread the rope plug through the needle, making sure you have 2 even length plug 'legs' bent upwards towards the handle. Locate the puncture, pre-lube the reamer and have at it per the instructions. You really will have to twist and drive the reamer past the tread belts. Although you can repair a tire on the car, you need so much leverage to drive the reamer, (and the plug needle) through the tread and tread belts, it will be difficult. I would estimate 50-75lbs of arm pressure is needed to push through. The tougher the tire (i.e. LT type tires with a lot of tread), the more you will have to push. Here's tip # 1; take advantage of the removable handle on the reamer (hex key supplied with kit), and attach just the tool shaft to your electric drill--instant ream job! Just don't overdo it!Now that you've rounded and trimmed off the puncture all the way through the tread, cord, and belts, use the reamer as a 'plug' to stop any additional air from escaping. Things go better with air pressure in the tire since it supports the tread around the 'target area', so don't let the whoosh of escaping air rattle you.Next, remove the reamer. Air will escape, but if you have about 20-25 PSI of air pressure left in the tire, you will have plenty of time to grab your loaded plug needle and put it in the hole. My first repair was rear tire on a sports car. Very limited working space=very little leverage. I could not drive home the plug. Tip #2. The solution was to coat the plug and needle with rubber cement(purchase separately as it is not supplied)(disclaimer: I think this was mentioned in a previous review-thanks). The cement acted as a lubricant, and while still difficult, I finally was able to drive the plug home. In my case, the kit-supplied lube was ineffective. It probably would have been different if I removed the tire however.Note: This is an "open eyelet" kit. The plug 'needle' has a open slot to facilitate its removal from the tire whilst leaving the plug in place. DO NOT rotate the needle when driving the plug into the puncture. You risk spreading/breaking the eyelet off the needle shank within the tire, or jamming up the eyelet with the twisted plug.Feel free to drive the plug all the way into the tire until the sliding cone stops your motion. NO fear of going too far. Put pressure on the sliding cone, holding it against the tire, while pulling the needle out. The plug is now perfectly seated in the puncture. Just trim the leftover exposed nub with a blade, leaving about 1/8" excess above the tread, so it can be further seated by the rolling tire.One final point, you really need to carry, or have access to, an air compressor or air pump to re-inflate your repaired tire. Otherwise driving on a severely under inflated tire is inviting a blow out.Like everything else, this kit has it's limitations. It probably won't work if you have impaled a railroad spike as you cannot 'double up' the plugs. Also, side wall repair is out-too much flexing. Same with angled punctures.  However, when done properly, the self vulcanizing plugs should last the remaining life of the tire. Happy plugging!

I tried an alternative but this kit appears well made.  I did purchase some liquid rubber and gizzed up the plug a little before I installed it.  Has not leaked at all since installation.  Not cheap but this is a good kit and I would recommend it!

reviewText: I received this tire repair kit as a gift for my birthday.  I do some off roading on occasion with my truck and punctures are unfortunately common.  I not only hate the inconvenience of having a flat, but hate worse the charge and wait part of taking it to a service station to get fixed.  In the past I have owned other repair kits, but admittedly they have been cheap ones.  Too often they have broken on me, gotten twisted, or just were difficult to use.  This ARB tire seal set is top quality all the way.  It may be more expensive than most, but this is certainly one of those times that you really do get what you pay for.  The tools are heavy and very rugged, and the accessories make a joke of what I have in the cheaper set I own. I punctured and old tire I had on a rim in a couple of places and used this set to patch it with excellent results.  It was easy, fast, and the tire has been holding air solidly since then.  Lets face it, when you have a flat its always a pain in the rump and a total inconvenience.  This set can repair a tire in no time and be permanent.  The tools are top quality and you can buy replacement seals right here on Amazon.  Absolutely the best, and highly recommended...: )

I have purchased those cheap kits for tire repair and they are just to flimsy and wanted something stout enough to last and I found it with this kit. Very pleased with the construction.

After getting a big nail in my tire of my truck, I tried using my tire plug kit that I had from our car..... fortunately when the handle broke it did not go through my hand.... so a coworker had a kit similar to this (same kit, but a red case) and for the act of having to plug a tire, it was a pleasure to use. As soon as I got home, I ordered this kit.Since then I have had to use it twice... once on my truck and once as a favor to a neighbor. The handles are great as they are big, beefy, and unlike the other local auto store kits, you will not injure yourself.The only problem that I have had with my truck is the composition of the tires... they are thick. With that, the reamer that is included works well, but what I use instead is a drill with a drillbit to ream out the hold. On a car tire, that is not necessary, but on a truck (I have a Toyota Tundra) it just makes the job easier.Besides that, it is a great kit and I take it everywhere I go. My dad also needed a kit and I sent one to him as a gift--- he has used it twice and he also believes it is one of the best kits he has ever owned.
