Spend the extra money on Stinger's roadkill product - has zero smell , is much thicker, and doesn't cost that much more.  Anyone who's done these installs knows the pain is getting your innards out to access the sheet metal.  Why go through that and install something substandard.  Only points would be to have this applied to somewhere ventilated, like outside of the interior of a car or industrial use.Edit:  This started falling off some panels during winter, with temps routinely in the 30s.  I have to lower the rating another notch.  Junky!

this product works well. it is almost identical to dynamat extreme, yet is less expensive. the only diffrence being the aluminum is slightly thinner, but is still great quality. after much research i cant find what the adhesive is, but it is almost certainly a high percent butyl. the odor from it is so so faint its negligable. so its a great alternative to the name brands. will purchase more. and in fact it lays and rolls down better than dynamat. only took away a star because 3 dollars a square foot is still high for what it is.
Great product--easy to install

I used dynomat on the doors but was looking for something different for the floors and for the money this stuff was hands down the best bet. Free shipping and nearly 20% less than the online autostores made this a no brainer. Very good stuff, you won't be dissapointed.
I bought this to replace a missing one in the back of my wife's car.  It seems to be more sturdy than most included jacks.  Happy.

This is just what I was looking for and a Great price, thank you.  Will be using for back up on my little RV.  That little more insurance having this item takes a bit of stress out of different unexpected situations.Received before promised date and packaged well.
Fits into spare tire space for 2003 Hyundai Elantra. Is beefier than the factory jack. Comes with the tool to raise and lower it.
summary: Fits into spare tire space for 2003 Hyundai Elantra

reviewText: My husband's 97 Cherokee came with no jack, so I saw this on Amazon for less than $20.  It comes with the crank handle, which isn't mentioned in the Amazon ad.  Both pieces fit under his back seat.  He tested it on the Jeep and it worked just fine.

This worked well to change out 2 tires on my 2013 veloster. As other reviews stated there arent those teeth that normally hold the car in place. But they dont seem t be needed the car did mive at all and i have no doubt this will worknwell with future needs
summary: Works good for my 2014 kia and 2013 hyundai veloster

reviewText: Although made in China this jack seems to be sturdy enough. I tried it and it seemed to work fine jacking the car up but was sticky when lowering the car. The saddle (square on top of the jack) is flat and does not have the teeth that most jacks I've used have which grips onto the bottom of the car better. It also comes with a short shaft to insert into the jack. I suggest greasing the threads so they move easier. For the price you can't beat it but if you own a shop where it would get a lot of use I suggest buying something else.
summary: Fine For Emergencies But Not For Everyday Use

reviewText: This is one the simple and inexpensive ways to upgrade your car, no matter how old or new. It is surprising how something simple like this can actually make a difference in the way your wheel looks, whether you have alloy wheels or steel wheels with hubcaps. I have these valve caps on both my Honda and my VW (VW valve caps on that one). They add a really nice custom touch and look a lot better than the black rubber valve caps, which seem to break or fall off. The bonus key chain is very cool too!
summary: Easy and quick upgrade! A MUST HAVE!

reviewText: I was really surprised by these valve caps. They are a high quality valve cap that looks nice with my alloy wheals.

Nice and good looking, beware of the small screws that are supposed to be 'theft' proofing these valve caps. After the initial 'delight' wears out then you realize the PITA you have to live with. Firstly, filling air is a pain as you need to meddle with a super tiny allen key to remove the anti-theft screws. Good luck if managed to keep them safely. 2 of mine already rolled off on the black tarmac. Secondly, servicing at dealership or other 3rd party places, they will rip these off and even cause damage to the valves. My dealer luckily did not do any air pressure check / refill and just politely asked me to remove these. 3rdly already showing signs of corrosion. I doubt if these would last through the winter in snow and salt. Again, a cool thing to start with, but it wears off quickly.
summary: Good ones, PITA if you need to refill, inflate tires

reviewText: Nice little caps. They really stand out and make wheels look finished even if they are oem wheels. The wrench that is include is nice so they can be torqued past the point that someone can remove them by hand. I had no problems with the install, however one of my valve stems seemed stripped when threading this on, but it turned out to just be a bit of residual plastic from the old caps. Overall its a great deal.

These caps are well made and they make my rims look better too by dressing up a plain black plastic cap with these chrome and black finished caps.Comes with a key ring too, priced  under 10.00 bucks for both, Thats hard to beat!

I must admit I haven't installed these yet. Ohio weather, too cold, old man, I'll wait for the warmth of Spring. With that out of the way these look and feel great. Clearly they're no light weight plastic. Although I haven't even opened the clear plastic baggie I'm basing this on sight and feel, but there's even a small Allen wrench, I assume to lock  the valve cover.

These are a lot larger/heavier than I expected--which is a plus. The three triangles and cyase weigh a total of approximately ten pounds. They set up easily and seem like they would hold up well on a highway. Definitely a good value and a good item to have in case of a vehicle break down.

Safer and easy to use compared to road flares and they are reusable too. The quality is what you'd expect from any auto parts/accessories store so if you cant find them where you are and are thinking of these for your car for that 'just in case' scenario, buy em.

First off, there's no getting around it, these things are LARGE and HEAVY. But, this is one of those cases in which that's an excellent thing.Still haven't used them in real life, though I did take them out and figure out how to assemble them. Easy enough.They have this odd wire-like piece that's clearly supposed to attach somewhere when the triangles are set up, but I can't figure it out. Luckily this doesn't seem to be critical to its stability.

These things don't seem too strong.  I snapped a couple together and they seem like they'll break without much force.  However, they're heavy and don't seem like they'd get blown over on the side of the road.I put them in a dark room and shined a flashlight on them, but they didn't seem to reflect much.  So I bought a roll of white reflective tape and added small strips to each one.  Once it gets warmer I plan on setting up a couple in the driveway and using car headlights to see how they look from 50 feet away.I will echo what others are saying about the storage box... it's complete junk.  I bought 2 sets of these and the clasps on one box was already broken.  However, I just put a bungee cord around each box and that should hold them well enough.Overall, great price on a sturdy set.
But it looks like it is made very well.  It keep it in a rear storage compartment of my RV.  I hope that I never have to use it.
summary: Haven't Had to Use This Device Yet...

reviewText: I need to start with, it work as it should be,  but if you have a big battery or more than just one ( for your SUV / truck )  you better have it placed in sunny spot coz it would take a lot of sun to get the job done.
I love these units I bought 2 of them and use them daily in order to maintain my battery and when I am in the field it works great, I can leave the doors open and play the stereo with no issues.

I purchased a Deltran Battery Tender JR 5 years ago as well as a motorcycle battery. Both the battery tender and the battery are still going strong 5 years later, this is not a typo! Yes, I said 5 years! Anyone who owns a motorcycle (especially a Harley) knows that you typically replace batteries every 2 years. Because of the performance of my battery tender Jr I decided to pick up this Deltran Solar Panel. I recently had to move my bike to a garage with no electricity and had to install the solar panel on the outside of the garage fully exposed to the elements. I've only had it about 2 months but I must say that this solar panel has performed above expectations. We have had some of the craziest weather on record in New Jersey. Warm days, cold days, heavy rains, 50 mph winds, 3 and 4 days at a time without sunlight. Yeah, Mother Nature has been sending us all kinds of craziness. So today I decided to go to my garage and see what kind of mess this solar panel was in. At the very least I expected to find the panel damaged by all the rain we've had. To my amazement it was working perfectly! It was 2 in the afternoon and cloudy due to all the rain and the solar panel LED was green indicating a fully charged battery. The panel has not been hit with any sunlight for 2 days yet it has been able to fully maintain my 5 year old battery. Another great product by Deltran.UPDATE 3/28/2013: Here we are over a year after purchasing this Solar Panel and it continues to work great.  It has been through some of the worst storms on record here in the East Coast without sustaining damage. My "very old" motorcycle battery continues to be maintained. The bike started easily even after 6 months of sitting in storage.

I wanted to use it for a vehicle that is stored in my garage, the light blinks that shows it is charging but when I put a meter to test it shows no voltage. It claims it needs good direct sunlight but you would think in Arizona that would be good but I guess not. I will be returning it back to the company and may try another one and hope it works.**UPDATE, after talking with a company rep it is now working perfect.There was a problem with the leads and this was resolved and works great. Even when the sun is going down it stills shows that it is charging in low sunlight.  The company has good customer support thanks again.

Very simple and easy to use. Put it on your dashboard and leave in the sun. Be sure to buy the car adapter accessory: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003CJ927I/ref=oh_details_o06_s01_i00 So that you can easily plug it in inside the car.My only complaint is that there is no carrying case for this, I don't like to "throw" it in the trunk and break the glass.
Got this to keep my truck battery topped off when at the airport.  Works with even clouds or a dreary day.

Got this to keep my lawn mower maintained.  I keep it outside most the year, and was surprised to read that this product is NOT intended for outdoor use.  Called the company and they explained this product is designed to be used inside a vehicle.  Kind of defeats the purpose of this product.
These are good for changing small appliances like a lawn mower or snow blower. Would recommend to others, the price is pretty good and there are rubber backings on the inside.
I needed various spark plug sockets for both my trimmer and lawn mower; set is high quality and the rubber insert stays tucked in after each removal and installation.

I like these alot.  I've only used a few times so far since I got them.  But they have been very good to me.I do suggest that you get yourself something like this one "Great Neck OEM 25292 27-Inch Magnetic Claw Pickup Tool"  just in case it does happen to slip off or something.  Last time I used them the little rubber grip stayed on the new plugs that I installed and there is almost no way to get them out with any regular tool or thin pliers.  So my Claw sprang in to action and it worked really good and got the rubber grip off the new plugs and kept working....LOL.  The rubber grip probably slipped off cause I was using a lot of dielectric grease when installing the new plugs.  So I'm not worried about that too much especially cause I had a way of getting them out.Set wise I think there is a six piece set out there but this 5 piece set should have you covered for most vehicle applications out there.  Even the 5 piece is hard to come by, most sets out there are 3 or 4  piece.  So just get this one and the Claws. hahaha

I bought this set mainly for the 18mm plug socket since it was only slightly more than a single 18mm from elsewhere and came with all the other sizes too. Unfortunately, the 18mm socket won't grip a spark plug at all. The rubber insert's hole is just too big. I can't speak for the other sizes since I haven't used them yet, but I was disappointed that the 18mm won't hold a plug. Might try to wedge something in there to try to take up space. The set overall does feel solid and I'm sure they'll all last a very long time.
Even had the tiny one for those little plugs not even napa stocks that come on some trimmers.  comes on a rail and as such does not migrate all over your tool drawer.

My first time changing spark plugs, and it took only minutes.  These spark plug sockets performed just as described.  No issues grabbing the spark plug, whatsoever.  Very happy to put these in my tool collection.

These sockets are excellent, but I give 4 out of 5 stars because the product packaging is horrible.Sockets usually come with a plastic plug in the base of them that holds them to the packaging. In most of my experience, this plug is made with fins, so to speak, that will pop out of the socket as you wiggle the socket (or the plug) off of the packaging.These sockets had solid plugs in the bottom. Wiggling the sockets usually ended up in breaking the packaging right at the point where the plug left the socket base, leaving a plastic plug in the bottom of the socket and nothing to grab it with. But, these are spark plug sockets, with a rubber protector on the inside that has a very small whole. So not many things can be used from inside the socket to punch out the plug. I ended up putting a long nail down the socket and punching out the packaging with a hammer.It turns out I did not need these, and would love to return them; but I can't because I tore the packaging to shreds, and threw it away... whoops.

I've used the 5/8" socket to change the spark plugs on my truck and twice on my wife's SUV. During the last spark plug change on her car, the rubber insert which grabs hold of the spark plug came out of the socket and stayed with the spark plug. I didn't notice until trying to reseat the plug boot and it wouldn't fully seat. All worked out fine in the end, but a slight hassle nonetheless.Anyway, I found another 5/8" spark plug socket in another socket kit I had.

Had to break down and get some new sparkplug sockets. mine were ragged out missing the sleeves, time to give away & start fresh again. saw this nice set & price was good. real nice sockets if your looking for replacements, covers the bases.
These guys go right to the point. they are strong for their job, they are reliable, and they handle sparkplugs delicately. enough said

I just put on the wipers, and after two weeks (and two rains) notice that they do wipe as effectively as my Rain-X.  Fit was good, easy installation, appears to be well made.Pros:-Sturdy-Little to no streakingCons:-None yet (two weeks of usage)

I am rating the product one star to draw attention to my review.  The blade itself is good.  The materials, construction, and water removal are all good.  I tried the C-19-UB on the passenger side of my GS350 and it worked as well as the 24" factory one on the driver side.  The Anco blade is molded with a spoiler, which makes it similar in appearance to the factory wiper of the GS350 which is the holder and the refill assembly.  If I were to rate the product, I'd rate it 3 stars for the high cost not justified by any additional benefit over the factory blade refill.There two points I wanted to make are:1. Attention must be paid to letters -OE or -UB at the end of the blade model.  I suggest using the Amazon fit guide at the top of the product page or visiting Anco website to find specific models that will fit your vehicle.  I ordered C-20-OE and C-26-OE from Amazon Vine (which did not have the benefit of the Amazon fit guide) for the 2009 Toyota Highlander, and they do not fit.  I ordered -OE blades thinking -OE stood for Original Equipment.  My family owns and previously owned Toyota/Lexus cars and I am only familiar with the "cane handle" type of a windshield wiper arm.  Anco -OE blades will not fit this type of connector.  Additionally, the Product Description says that the blade has an "OE-style spoiler", so it is even more confusing what OE in the model number refers to.  Anyway, Toyota and Lexus have a "cane handle" type wiper arm and only blade models ending in -UB will fit this connector.2. I think these replacement blades are just too expensive.  I usually buy wiper blade refills at the dealer for about ten dollars for two.  These blades cost two to three times that (depending on the availability of a rebate).  I tried a C-19-UB alongside with the factory 24" blade on my GS350 and I did not find Anco blade to clean the windshield any better than the factory blade does.  On one of my previous cars, I tried Valeo 900 Ultimate blades (similar to Anco Contour).  I had the same opinion that, although these replacement blades work well, they do not work better than factory refills, and their high cost makes them unappealing to me.  I do not find that at 2-3 times the cost of factory refills, these blades work 2-3 times better.
summary: Good blade, but expensive.  Beware of different connectors -OE vs. -UB

reviewText: It is easy to underestimate the importance of good wipers. Ineffective wipers are a hazard and an annoyance.  This is a solid wiper that installs with relative ease. It works well in both heavy rain and that annoying smudge your windshield lighter precipitation. The windshield was clean, smudge and smear free. It doesn't whistle or stick or lift. Only time will tell how durable it is but overall, I am satisfied with this product.

When it came time to install this wiper, my husband and I were ready to come outside and I stopped to put on a sweatshirt. In that minute-long gap, my husband had the old wiper blade off and the new one, so needless to say, install was a snap.These wipers provide a really smooth wiping action with light to moderate rainfall (I haven't hit a bucketfuls of rain scenario yet) and are quite effective at cleaning with the automatic windshield cleaner.The only issue -- and it is a minor one -- is that in the lower right hand corner of the passenger side of the car (where this was installed) the wiper leaves a small sliver of area that it doesn't cover which is peculiar given the smooth arc it creates on the rest of its path.All and all those, this wiper works well (I don't rely on the corner while driving) and the all-in-one profile is sleek!
summary: Easy, easy installation and clean wiping...minus

reviewText: Works great so far on my SUV. I have not yet had a chance to try it in the snowy sub-zero temperatures that are, for me, the true test of a good wiper blade.  However, in the rain it has offered a squeegee clean visibility.  It also removes some gruesome smashed bugs without the nasty smear...will update after some extended use.  But right out of the box, it works well!

I put this wiper blade on a small sports car with a decently curved windshield (Audi TT).  So far, the wiper has been on the car 1 week & has gone through 80+ degree weather, rain, sleet & snow.  It is exposed to the elements during the day, but is garaged at night.So far, so good, but I can't tell the "superiority" of this ANCO blade over and ACDelco blade that is on another car.  In fact, the brand new ANCO blade on my other car started streaking within 4 days under the same weather conditions. The only difference was that the other car is kept outside all of the time, so was exposed to freezing temperatures & more weather at night.On the Audi, the ANCO blade seems to grip the windshield and it clears well in rain & slushy snow (2 days of rain, 1 day of slushy snow).  However, given the quick failure of the ANCO wiper blade on my other car, I cannot recommend this wiper blade, especially if your car is an outside car.
summary: Don't See the Premium in this Wiper Blade.

reviewText: This all season wiper is supposed to be able to resist corrosion and freezing.  The main thing is that the blade makes perfect contact with the windshield.

May 5, 2013 Update: Well these wiper blades are a massive disappointment. Within two months they began chattering and skipping in the center of the blade on my windshield. This is unacceptable in a wiper blade. Sometimes chatter can happen because something gets on the windshield, oil or the like. Not the case this time - the center part of the blade has deformed. The wiper blade portion has developed a fold over, it lays over on an angle from pressing against the windshield. I've never seen a wiper blade go bad this fast or skipped in the center of the blade (chattering normally happens at the ends of the blade).This 28 inch blade was installed on a 2012 Ford Focus driver side, replacing a nearly 1 year old OEM blade. The passenger side blade was not replaced (a good test for side by side comparison - both blades are 28 inches on this car). The OEM blade is a frameless blade just like this Anco. When I returned the original blade to the car, there was no chatter or skipping. This Anco blade may work on other cars or in shorter lengths, but it flat is a bad blade in this length on this car.The original review posted in April, 2013:Anco Contour wiper blades are excellent bracket less wipers. The blade installed easily, and clears my windshield quietly and streak free.I like these blades a lot better than the comparable Bosch blades. For certain cars a frame style blade is a better choice, in that case I like Michelin Stealth and Valeo better.This 28 inch blade installed fairly easily on my 2012 Ford Focus. The package included four different clips for different applications. Choosing the correct clip was a minor pain. Anco's clips don't look much like the Ford clip I was replacing. These Contour wiper blades are a universal style blade - they have no attaching clip connected permanently to them. Instead there is a hole with a raised ring on both sides of the blade. The correct clip for your car is snapped over those two rings. Personally, I would rather have something attached to the blade. I understand it makes it easier to manufacture a universal connector.The tiny instruction sheet was not terribly useful. It was a series of photographs and drawings trying to illustrate the different kinds of clips. It took me a few minutes to decipher those pictures. When it comes time to change this blade, I will be confused. The original Ford clip has two very clearly marked buttons to release the blade. The Anco has a goofy looking arrow that has to be wrestled over a tab. Why couldn't Anco simply replicate the two squeeze buttons?This blade has a really large spoiler over the spine. The spoiler is designed to catch the wind while driving down the highway to keep the blade pressed against the windshield. The flap or spoiler is kind of ugly and a lot taller than the Ford OEM blade. That flap does contact the wiper arm without affecting performance of the wiper.Not great mounting instructions and universal clips aside, this blade performs really well. A 28 inch blade is huge and is prone to chatter and streaks. The Anco blade does an excellent job of clearing my windshield.For some cars, this bracket less or frameless wiper blade is not the best arrangement. These tend to be older cars with more vertical windshields. The frameless blades don't work at all on rear window wipers. For my 2002 Buick Rendezvous, I have found through way too much trial and error that classic wipers with a frame are the best way to go. Michelin makes an outstanding Stealth blade that has the frame enclosed with a plastic frame. For a rear window wiper, there is no better than Valeo blades. The extra force and slim aerodynamic profile makes these blades stick to the rear window (wind coming over the roof top will try to lift the blade from the window if there is a spoiler on the blade).Overall, Anco has an excellent windshield wiper blade at a good price.
summary: The Worst Ever - chattering after not even 2 months

reviewText: I was soooo....happy to see these here on Vine. I had a set on my conversion van and sold it and just had another brand of wipers on the car. I love these. The contour of them make them hug the windshield and keep it crystal clear with just one pass. I also noticed that when it was an icy windshield these didn't freeze to the window like most do. It was almost as if they had their own little antifreeze coating. I live in Iowa and even today we are getting another 8 inches of heavy wet snow and it's nice to know that these wipers will handle the load. I had them on the van for about 2 years and they still worked like the day I put them on. Can't wait to get them on the car...
summary: ANCO C-22-OE Contour Wiper Blade - 22", (Pack of 1)

reviewText: In my area we have a high degree of temperature change and seasonal weather. Heavy ice under snow is not uncommon in the winter and cold damp nights with high daytime temps during the summer months is the norm. Windshield wipers take a real beating to say the least. We have two trucks, an F-250 Ford diesel and an F-150 Ford. With hauling our horses and other farm related work, the dust, weather and miles are a test for any wiper blade... the ANCO Contour blades pass that test. I replaced one of the 22 inch blades on the F-250 and one of the 20 inch blades on the F-150. The "Kwik Connect" installation was easy. They form a tight fit against the windshield that doesn't faulter with highway speeds. On the other side of the vehicles I used a $30.00 premium wiper blade. The ANCO blade has proven itself to be superior in all areas. I highly recommend the ANCO Contour wiper blade and believe it to be one of the best blades on the market.
summary: A very nice replacement wiper blade.. best on the market.

reviewText: Amazon tells me that this product does not fit my 2004 Audi TT. Other sites tell me it does. Ultimately, there was no way of finding out whether I needed the OE or UB version of this wiper blade. I got one of each. The OE version is for those cars that use this style of wiper blade as original equipment and as it turns out, the OE version fits perfectly well once you figure out which of the several adaptors included is required and how to install it on the blade. The instructions are less than clear but after several attempts, I was able to install it. It fits well and operates properly. It rained today so I used it and found that it runs smoothly and without noise or skipped spots. The UB version has a different set of attachments and would not fit with any of the provided adaptors. Based upon the inaccurate information scattered about the web, some related to older iterations of Anco Contour blades, you might want to purchase this at a location where you can try it out and immediately return it if it proves not to fit. Once you know what definitely fits, you can come back to Amazon for future purchases.
summary: Fits, but instructions leave something to the imagination

reviewText: These are decent, middle-of-the-road wipers. The rubber is heavy and seems like it will be durable. My old blade (a Michelin...looks almost identical) had started chattering and leaving a huge streak. Replacing it with this blade fixed the problems, but I suspect most new wipers would have. I did notice streaks near the edges of the blade, though, so this wiper isn't leaving as wide of a clear path as it should.If you have a car with "opposing" wipers (rather than both going in the same direction, they move towards each other, both attached at the lower corners), you will have to remove and rotate the attaching bracket in order to keep the "spoiler" on the top edge (this is illustrated in the instructions) on your passenger side.  A bit of a hassle, but not a huge deal.The price seems a little steep, currently $13.53 here, with a MSRP of an astounding $28! I can tell you these are DEFINITELY not worth $28. As $14 wipers, I would give these about 3.5 stars.  For $28, I would expect something really special, which these are not.  They are just okay.  For $28 wipers, I'd only give them two stars.Note: When I ordered these, it appeared that they would fit my Chrysler, but they do not (I needed the UB, rather than the OE, version).  My wipers have a J-shaped hook, and none of the adapters included with this version will work with that.  I did get the UB version as well, which, aside from the connection point, are identical to these.

This Anco contour wiper blade installed easy with just a snap. My husband said it was a breeze. They really work well in heavy rain ( big drops white and hard to see through) to keep the window clear.  Also removes morning frost quickly and cleanly. Will have to wait unitl later to try in the snow, but expect excellent results.
summary: EASY TO INSTALL, WORKS GREAT TO CLEAN CONTOURED WINDSHIELD.

reviewText: The wiper installs easily, looks nice, perhaps has more rubber on the non-wiping part (not sure why, unless it's supposed to make you feel like you're touching an actual squeegee blade or something)...and it stutters going across the windshield.  Ugh.Installation:  very easy, snap in an adapter, slide it on the little hook on your wiper arm, and you're done.Usage:  on a DRY windshield, it looks like it'll work fine.  But once it gets wet, most every time (not all, but most) it goes back to resting position, it stutters across the windshield.  I'm not sure what to make of this:  in the past two months I've replaced the windshield itself, and applied RainX.  Neither of it helps the stuttering/jumping back, and neither of my previous blades did it.  (Oddly enough, one of my previous blades was also an ANCO...and it worked better.)I'm hoping that these need additional wear or break in time, but if they're not smooth wiping in a couple more weeks, I'm tossing them and putting the old ones back on.  Given my current experience with these, I wouldn't recommend or purchase them again.
summary: Average wiper - fits early 2000 VWs with an adapter

reviewText: Anco C-20-OE Contour Wiper Blade-20" are great. They do the job and keep the rain off the windshield.My visibility has improved and they are quiet! I love them, my old ones on my truck were very noisey,and made a horrible screeching sound. They work for me and they will work for you. Plus they are very easy to install.Just make sure you order two as there is one in each pkg. Thanks.

I used this as a replacement for  stock wiper blade.  It was easy to install and works well.  To be honest most wiper blades perform well when new so only time will tell if these hold up better than cheaper "stock" wiper blades.  So far no streaking or squeaking so they get 4stars (-1 star for the relatively higher price tag).
summary: Easy to Replace And Work Well

reviewText: I tried to install this on my '08 suburban and it doesn't have the right type of adapter included. The '08 and '09 suburbans have different wiper attachments and although the parts finder says this works, it does not.  I even had several other people look at it including a mechanic and we all came to the conclusion that either the adapter is missing or this is the wrong type for my vehicle. Living in rainy Florida I replace my blades frequently and Anco is the first product that has been not compatible.'
summary: Did not work on my '08 suburban

reviewText: The wiper blade was very easy to install - I had to choose the right adapter out of the three included, and snap it on, and then snap the whole thing to my car. It wipes well so far.

Anco has made wiper blades for a long time and quality is always there with them.Plain and simple,they work and work well.They are very easy to install and last at least a year.At least on my car wipers last long.Im in California and it doesn't rain much but when it does it does and you need good wipers.Anco wipers will do a good job for you.I recommend highly.

I have been using a jointless wiper blade ever since it became a popular replacement for the factory jointed type that is usually pre-installed when you buy a new vehicle. The ANCO C-20-OE Contour Wiper Blade - 20" fits the bill when you need to replace or just want to upgrade to a better performing wiper blade. Got this just in time to coincide with persistent rainy weather we've been having in my state. Snow on the other hand is a different story, no way for me to simulate that kind of weather event. It also worked well with frost accumulation on the windshield. It wiped away the frost smoothly, with no kind of hesitation or drag while in the wiping motion.My thoughts:Performance: the jointless type ANCO C-20-OE Contour Wiper Blade - 20" is contoured better to "hug" your windshield with minimal resistance and pressure points. This translates to better wiping ability thereby enabling you to see better in inclement weather. Since it is jointless, this type of wiper gives you uniform wiping pressure, eliminating the pressure points or the "streaks" that you see across your windshield as it moves across the windshield. The curvature of this wiper is aerodynamic, it will prevent a lift-off of the blade even in high winds.Installation: it took less than 10 minutes to install the ANCO C-20-OE Contour Wiper Blade - 20" without using any of the adapters for the wiper arm of my vehicle.Very satisfied with how the ANCO C-20-OE Contour Wiper Blade - 20" has performed. It is in the middle of the pack as far as price is concerned compared to other jointless name-brand wiper but gives you an awesome wiping performance. Highly recommended!
summary: Superior wipers compared to factory-installed jointed type

reviewText: The ones on the current vehicle were a bit more than a year old but in Florida the harsh sun and daily thunderstorms combined with love-bugs and all the rest put wiper blades through the paces. This arrives promptly, takes about 1 minute to install (literally). No squeeking, no streaking. This was my first experience with this brand but like it better tha PIAA...highly comparable to Bosch brand and better than the factory installed version by far.

Note: these blades only fit certain vehicles, which doesn't include the common hook-type attachment present on most vehicles. Make sure you need this "OEM" fit. If you're looking for a more generic fit (including the hook-type), the same blade is available asANCO C-28-UB Contour Wiper Blade.These blades installed without a hitch. I hadn't used single-beam wiper blades before, so this was something new for me. They work fine. But so has every other wiper blade I've ever used (at least when new), some of which only cost a third of what this product does. I don't know that these will last three times as long as other wiper blades I've used (including Anco's 31-series), and am guessing that the others represent a better value.The supposed benefits of this design? "Resists corrosion & freezing". Can't say that I've ever had an issue with either corrosion or freezing with any of the blades I've ever purchased, and I live in northern Utah, where we get a lot of cold and snow.Anyway, they work fine. If you feel a need for this blade design (and these fit your vehicle; double check!), go for it. But I'm pretty sure I'll be back to the cheaper blades next time, since they work just as well for me.
summary: A decent blade, but a bit pricey. Limited fit. Cheaper ones work just as well.

reviewText: This is a nice looking wiper blade, if you are the kind of person who notices things like that. It is all a matte black, one piece unit, without the 'traditional' metal looking flanges. It has a 'performance' look to it.I like that the blade comes with three different attachment clips, so you can pick and chose the right one for your car. That is a thoughtful touch - normally I have to futz too much with getting a wiper to fit, clipping things to 'make' them fit.They work well in the rain, clearing off a nice section to see out of, as all wipers do when they are new. They work smoothly and evenly over the glass.They don't work as well for dust, but that's really not what these are made for.Although these are touted as being superior for cold weather, the real test for me will be this summer, in the Arizona desert temperatures. Usually any wipers I install around spring end up warped by the heat a few months later. And the dust doesn't help, either. :)Recommended for wet rainy days, for ease of attachment, and for a stylish look.

These windshield wipers by ANCO as I stated in a previous review of other ANCO windshield wipers, are the best wiper blades I have ever owned. The thick rubber blade and solid housing makes these wiper blades very durable. As I stated in my previous review, every swipe of these wiper blades not only dries the windshield but it cleans it. There was a heavy rain storm about two days after I installed my new wiper blades and I was extremely pleased with the wipers performance. Very easy to install, installation takes about 30 seconds.

At the time I selected this blade, the product page gave me the green light with the claim that this will fit my 2005 Toyota Prius, which has flat, cane shaped wiper blade arm attachments; however, it does not. The page  fit results now correctly show as incompatible for my car.On the back of the package, it shows the three types that it does fit, all of which have a silhouette that somewhat resembles a needle cartridge for a turntable. I tried all three clips to see if any were multi-compatible, but none were.

The material/rubber is good, but not high quality soft rubber.The type of rubber in the blade is very important how well it swipes the water.Other factor includes the weight, the curve, etc.The mounting bracket on this is not universal and I think it fits only American cars like Chevy or dodge.It doesn't fit Honda.

The Anco wiper blade I ordered installed easily on my car's passenger side and works well.  It is streak free and there is no clattering or noise.  I don't know what the durability of this blade will be so I left off a star for now, I will update a few months from now.  The package came with several adaptors for various applications but before ordering, make sure the blade will fit your vehicle.  This is easy to do with Amazon's garage app that stores your vehicle to match it with parts that fit.

It was quick and easy to install. I like the unibody design over the old multi-arm style. The rubber is pliable and contours to my large curved windshield so I get a clean swipe every time. The Anco blade seems sturdy and rugged. You need that during the snow storms.

reviewerName: Lisa Shea "be the change you wish to see in t...
reviewText: We ordered this ANCO 21" contour blade for our 2004 Honda Odyssey. We thought that the various connectors meant that it would connect properly - but as it turns out it would not connect properly. So the review that follows is for the other contour blade we received, a different length, for our other car.We got a single ANCO 22" contour blade to review, and we reviewed it side by side against a new regular ANCO (non-countour) blade on the other side of the front windshield. I own a Subaru Forester. The Contour blade was slightly clearer and slightly quieter. Both were just as easy to put on and remove.I'm 44 and have been driving since I was 16. In those years I definitely learned early on the value of using a good quality windshield wiper. After all, it's a relatively cheap part which can help prevent a quite expensive (and harmful) accident. So definitely I would say if you're currently using a cheap windshield wiper blade that it's well worth upgrading to something good quality.Do you need to go from normal ANCO to the contour ANCO? Again, I would say it's worth having the best you can get. This is about seeing the road in front of you in an already slick situation. You've got enough else to worry about in a thunderstorm or snowstorm. You don't need to worry about being able to see the road on top of everything else.I'll update this when both wear out, to give notes on the durability of them, but I assume both will have the normal range of durability.

I seem to replace them a lot more often now than I ever have in the past. This is not bad. Like these ANCO's, they are easy to attach, are good performers, and they seem to be relatively inexpensive. These ANCO's are all of that.Feel confident that there are good wipers that work well, and that attach very easily. They just don't seem to be anything too significantly better or worse than any of the other wiper blades out there. That is its strength and its weakness. if you need new wipers, buy with confidence ...

The wiper comes with 3 different plastic clips to attach the wiper to the wiper arm.  It was relatively easy to figure the correct one to use and how to attach it, but with no help from the instructions.The whole operation took less than 5 minutes. The instructions included could be a bit better for those of us who have to use the little adaptor pieces. reviewText: This is a great Toyota coolant for the money. Works as described and easy to use. Highly recommend this to anyone looking flush their Toyota's coolant.

Newer Toyota and Lexus vehicles use non-traditional red or pink Antifreeze/Coolants.For clarification:Super Long Life Coolant (pink) 50/50 Pre-diluted - 1 Gallon.  Manufacturer Part Number: 00272-SLLC2Long Life Coolant (red) Undiluted - 1 Gallon.Requires dilution with distilled water. Manufacturer Part Number: 00272-1LLAC-01Toyota data for the Super Long Life Antifreeze/Coolant (pink):"Toyota Genuine coolant is the only guaranteed compatible antifreeze for your vehicle's cooling system and offers protection against corrosion of metallic parts and damage to rubber parts. The use of non-genuine coolants will corrode the parts and gradually block the cooling system, damaging the engine. The boiling point of the Genuine coolant is kept at the optimum level for operating temperatures in a Toyota vehicle. This ensures no evaporation of the coolant, thereby maintaining the level of the coolant for optimum operating temperatures.  Features include:*Quality'Designed, tested and approved by Toyota R&D.;'Ethylene Glycol based for extra long lasting aluminum protection.'No silicates.'Cannot gel.'No seal abrasion.'No borates.'No aluminum corrosion or pitting.'Formulated with de-ionized water'Pre-Diluted 50/50'No additional water needed for reducing concentration.'Pink coolant - for use in models which require the Super Long Life coolant."Amazon price was only $20.84 incl. free shipping (at time of review).Check your owner's manual to verify which type of coolant is required for your Toyota model or just use Amazon's Parts Finder.  My 2006 3.5L V6 came with the pink coolant from the factory so I'm going to continue using the same type; not taking any chances by mixing it with regular green coolant.  I've considered buying the undiluted red one and diluting it myself but the owner's manual and my dealer's parts department don't recommend it.
summary: Make sure to get the CORRECT type of Toyota Antifreeze / Coolant.

reviewText: I generally liked this product. I loved its being so much smaller and lighter than traditional battery chargers. However, there was a big issue and a variety of small annoyances.The big issue I encountered was that the charger never transitioned to Maintenance mode (trickle-charge). I had used the car in a way that didn't recharge the battery (series of very short trips on a cold night with a passenger that insisted on using the electric seat heater). I could hear the weaker rev'ing of the starter. When I got home, I connected up this charger, but 8 hours later, the status lights indicated normal charging mode, when I would have expected it to have long been in trickle charge. However, the battery seemed to have been fully recharged (from healthy sound from the starter motor).Related to this is the absence of a finer-grained charging status, for example a 3- or 4-element bar. On traditional battery chargers there is a gauge showing the voltage difference between the battery and what the charger is supplying. As the battery charges, the needle on this gauge drops. This lets you know when you are close to charged, or that the battery isn't taking a charge. And when you are initially connecting the clips, it helps confirm that you have a good connection. For example, I know from prior experience with these traditional chargers that there are several bolts on my engine block that would seem to be excellent grounding points, but aren't (insulated by thread-lock glue?). When I experimented by attempting to use these bolts, this charger gave me no indication of this problem -- the status lights were the same as when I connected to a good ground. Consequently you don't get an indication of one of the most common problems using a charger -- an inadequate connection of the clips.The hanging hook is a very useful feature. Unfortunately it seems to be made of a very brittle plastic. While it may be adequate for hanging the charger on a wall, it is grossly inadequate for the pictured use of hanging from the hood latch -- a situation when you are likely to be frazzled and may inadvertently stress the hook. When I encounter features that apparently compromise quality for trivial cost-savings, I always wonder if there are hidden ones critical to the functioning of the device.The product is better than what is pictured. Instead of a cord ending in battery clips, it has theBosch C35AC0 Quick Connect Cable Harness for C3 Battery Charger with Built-in Cable Fuseto which the battery clips are then connected. This harness provides the option -- which I didn't test -- of being left attached to a battery to provide a simpler and surer connection of the charger, and is especially useful for infrequently used batteries that are maintained on trickle charge (for example, boats, classic cars). Also, if the charger is to be used by someone who just can't understand the concept of where to connect the clips, this is an excellent accommodation. If you use the charger with multiple batteries, you might consider getting some/all of them their own harnesses. Additionally, my experience is that this is the part of a charger most likely to be damaged, and it is an advantage that it is easily replaceable.Although the manual is very short, it could be much better organized and laid out. Before you get to the two pages of operating instructions, it has four pages of warnings that should be obvious to almost anyone likely to be using this charger. I know that these are required to be there, but the way they are presented may well cause impatient or easily frustrated people to just stop reading. The big annoyance involves a very nice feature: The cover folds out so you can see a keyed picture of the charger while you are reading the instructions. Unfortunately, the legend for the keys (numbers) is not provided until after those names are being used (in the "Warnings"). And the basic instructions for operating the charger, including turning it to Standby before unplugging, is not in the "Operating Instructions" but part of a long individual "Warning" at the end of the "Warnings" section, and consequently easily to miss.DEFICIENCY: The manual for this product is available only as hardcopy. Because so many of my product manuals are available in electronic form, my "bookshelf" is on my computer and portable devices. This had the advantage of not only having manuals readily available and easily searchable, but it is easy for me to add annotations and bookmarks (I use the free FoxIt Reader as alternatives to Adobe Acrobat as well asNitro PDF Professional V6that is much cheaper than Acrobat, especially during its frequent sales and rebate offers).DEFICIENCY: No registration for this product. In the old days of mail-in registration cards, processing them was often an expense that wasn't worth it. But on-line registration is very inexpensive and something I would think well worth it for notifying customers in case a problem/defect is discovered in this product.What were they thinking?: The manual suggests using the packaging for storage, but that packaging is probably too fragile for anything but infrequent use where you are very careful taking it out and putting it back in: The cover is very thin plastic (reinforce-able or mend-able with normal packaging tape), and the base is a little more substantial. The packaging is closer to what you want to minimize the amount going into the waste stream.========================Advice for purchasers:The manual tells you to cycle the charger into standby mode (blue ring) before unplugging it (but doesn't say whether that is to protect the device or you). I found this to be non-obvious and thus hard to remember. I used my label maker to put this reminder on the charger (but Bosch, it would be nice if you had this on the next version).-- Douglas B. Moran
summary: Small size and weight big advantage, but charging status was not fine-grained enough

reviewText: Simplicity and performance are two of the numerous characteristics that define this charger. It is a leap forward in technology from the old square metal-cased charger that was the norm. It is simple to hook up and with just one push of a button it goes about its business efficiently and thoroughly. Easy to use and easy to store. Another winner from Bosch.

This isn't one of the giant wheeled battery chargers, heavy duty, meant for farm use.  This one is designed for a motorcycle (has a 6v mode as well), or a car (such as a sports/classic car that may sit a lot of the time).  Hooking it up is pretty straightforward, connect power, hook to the battery, and then select your mode on the charger.  For me there was only three options, motorcycle/car/AGM, I chose the AGM (as I have a non-gel Optima battery).  By morning the battery had been charged, and is on trickle charge.The hook on the device is very nice to attach to the hood, or some other object around the vehicle.  The only complaint I have is that a few of the cords are too short.  From the charger to the wall seems to be a bit short, had to use an extension car to get it in proper position by my car (although this may not be an issue for everyone, as my garage is quite large, and the car not by a wall).  The other short cord is the detachable one that goes on the battery (this is also very nice, and additional hookups can be ordered inexpensively) doesn't seem to be long enough to tuck someplace where i can hook it up without opening the hood, I guess it's not meant for that.Overall this charger has a lot of functionality showing you exactly what is going on (if you hooked it up backwards, what it's doing, etc), a method to easily hook up to multiple cars, and plus comes with the Bosch name.  Would recommend this.

reviewText: Upon unboxing the Bosch Model  C3 6.3/12.6 VDC Battery Charger, it is immediately evident that  this is a high quality product characteristic of the Bosch name.  The C3 is very compact compared to the old car battery chargers of the past.  The charger is constructed of a high impact plastic and therefore not susceptible to rusting as were the old metal box chargers.  All mode and status displays are on the front of the charger, as well as the single mode select button.  The C3 is equipped with a heavy duty 120 VAC power cord as well as a durable DC charging cable.  The DC charging cable is equipped with in inline disconnect, allowing the supplied insulated alligator clips to be left connected to the battery between charges.  The DC charging cable is also equipped with an inline 10A automotive type fuse to provide short circuit protection to the C3 charger.The Bosch C3 battery charger is microprocessor controlled and hence should be considered a "smart charger".  The C3 is designed to the sense the charge state of the battery, as well as determine the appropriate charge rate.  The C3 can provide a pulsed charging current of up to 3.5 A  for deeply discharged batteries, as well as provide a low current trickle or maintenance charge.  The C3 continuously monitors the battery charge state and automatically reverts from pulse to trickle charging when the battery is fully charged.The Bosch C3 battery charger was tested on a moderately discharged Delco S2000 115 AH deep cycle battery.  As expected, the C3 immediately switched to pulse charging, remaining in the pulse mode for approximately 7 hours before reverting to a trickle charge mode.The Bosch C3 battery charger performed flawlessly.The 36 page Bosch C3 instruction manual  is very well written and printed in 3 languages, English, French and Spanish.  Bosch strongly emphasizes operating safety.  The manual clearly addresses the potential for charging wet cell batteries to "off gas", thereby creating an explosive atmosphere.  Therefore, the charger should never be connected or disconnected from the battery while the battery is charging. Bosch also cautions the user from operating the charger in wet conditions.Bosch emphasizes that this charger is only designed to charge 6.3 or 12.6 VDC wet cell or gel cell rechargeable batteries.  It is not designed to charge dry cell batteries.The Bosch C3 Automatic Battery Charger is packaged with the C3 automatic charger, a battery charging cable equipped with a disconnect and an inline 10 A automotive fuse, red and black insulated heavy duty alligator clamps, a removable hanger and an operating manual.  Bosch provides a generous 2 year limited warranty on parts and workmanship.The Bosch C3 Automatic Battery Charger is a high quality product that should provide many years of reliable service when used in accordance with the supplied operating instructions.  Although the C3 isn't designed for high current vehicle starting applications, it proves to be very versatile for many battery charging applications.The only shortcoming found with the Bosch C3 charger is that the AC line fuse is internal and not field replaceable.  Bosch might consider making the AC line fuse user replaceable in later production runs of this product.
summary: Awesome multi-purpose trickle charger for gel cells, automotive and deep cycle batteries!!

reviewText: I'm very pleased with this Bosch C3 Battery Charger, it's not your basic car battery charger because it's a "Smart Charger" it's computer controlled meaning it adjusts to the needs of the battery that's being charged. You do need to select the type of battery being charged, car, motorcycle or AGM  but after that this charger takes control. If the charger senses a 12 volt battery is between 8 and 10.5 volts it automatically switches to pulse charging, this allows the battery to recover the best possible way enhancing the charging process for such a low condition. This is just one of the many computer controlled advantages of this type of battery charger.I added the optional Bosch C35AC0 Quick Connect Cable Harness for C3 Battery Charger, it's a direct connect harness you can connect to your car or whatever battery that's installed. You simply plug the charger into the end of the harness, I have one in my sports car that's stored Winters, it makes it very simple to just leave the charger connected, once the battery is fully charged the Bosch C3 charger switches over to a trickle, when I want to use the car I just unplug the harness and drive away.  I can't say enough about this great charger, buy one and you won't regret it!Update: I found that chargers made by NOCO use the same plug and make many options for connecting to different application at a lower price. I'm guessing NOCO makes chargers for Bosch and use the same quick plugs. For the same price as Bosch's C35ACO quick connect harness the NOCO harness includes a battery  monitorNOCO Genius GC015 12V Eyelet Battery Indicator
summary: The Bosch C3 Charger is a smart charger that works!

reviewText: A few of the reviews were spot on about the major flaws.  The biggest being you have to touch a button for it to do anything.  That is simply terrible.  I bought this thinking the Bosch name would mean something, but it does not mean good in this case.  Not sure why they even developed this product.  I used this for one of my classic cars and as others have said, if the power is interrupted, you are back to square one and HAVE TO PUSH A BUTTON! terrible design and thinking on their part.  I highly recommend the CTEK version instead, I've been using it for years and it's brought back batteries that my regular 2amp/15amp couldnt!  That's impressive.EDIT: The CTEK 3300 is a far superior device for the same money.  I've been trying to use the Bosch to get my camaro battery charged without success for the last two weeks.  I hooked up the CTEK yesterday and 4 hours later, the car started and was driveable.  The other advantage of the CTEK is the memory for knowing last state, so if there is power loss, it comes back to same place it was.  Also, once it's done charging, it goes into maintenance mode automatically.  Exactly how a product like this should work!CTEK Multi US 3300 12-Volt Smart Battery Charger
summary: Sounds like it's great...but it is in fact terrible

reviewText: Somehow it started in a wrong mode and then after turning it off and back on it picked up correct mode.I, generally,  have a high regard for Bosch products but this one falls short of top quality professional grade tool.

This battery charger is so easy to use, it does almost everything except hook up the clamps!  This is not your typical charger.  This thing is very sturdy and well built.  It's compact and small, but has plenty of cord to get the job done.  The small size also makes it easy to leave in your engine compartment and close your hood so no one steals it if you charge overnight.  You can't do that with those big square chargers.Simply hook it up and choose your mode by pressing a single button.  If your battery is near dead, it automatically detects that and begins pulse charging to get you up and running even sooner.  It also brings your battery up to full charge and then kicks over to trickle charge mode automatically.  Sweet!The hook attachment makes it easy to simply hang from the hood latch while working, so it's out of the way.  Put the clamps on, plug it in, choose your mode, and you're charging!They also have an inexpensive harness with quick disconnect you can add to multiple cars, motorcycles, or lawnmowers.  This speeds up changing the charger out even more.... and it was quick already!I highly recommend this charger.
summary: Easiest battery charger you'll ever use.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Summary: Ideal for storage, the automatic modes are good for less technical people, but do limit what you can do.  Definitely not a "High power" charger.As a "Smart" charger, you just hook it up to the battery, plug it into the wall and push a single button - the onboard logic figures out what you need and does the rest.  It will tell you if you've put the terminals on backwards, it will decide if it's a 6VV or 12V battery, and then starts to charge.  This makes it very simple, but won't let you try and resurrect 12V batteries which are below 8V.The charger itself is a nice size - fairly small and comes with a detachable plastic hook so you can hang it on your car or motorcycle when charging.  It comes with alligator clips or a direct hook up so you can use the speed connector.I wasn't able to find a current rating in the literature but looking at the back it's rated for 60 watts.  This suggests that it will charge your battery at perhaps 4-5 amps.  That's an overnight charge at best.  When I was a kid we used to have a 20 amp charger that could bring a dead battery back to enough charge to start your car within an hour or two.  Other chargers have a "start" mode where it can jump up to 50 or more amps.  If you need this capability, look atSchumacher XC103 SpeedCharge Battery Charger with Engine Startor perhapsSchumacher XC75 SpeedCharge Battery Charger with Engine StartAlthough it's listed as having four modes, I was only able to figure out 3:  1) Pulse charging (when the battery is very low, below 10.5 volts  2) Regular charging, then (3)trickle charging when it's full.Perhaps the other mode is the AGM mode - this only kicks in when it detects an AGM battery and it's very cold outside - Really kind of a limited situation.I'm using it on some 12V AGM cells right now,
summary: Perfect for long term storage, top up & overnight charging...but no fast charge option

reviewText: Seems counter intuitive to purchase fluids online, but once I started ordering Mobil 1 products on Amazon, I haven't looked back. I have 2 bikes and 2 cars and use Mobil 1 on all of them for everything - engine oil, diff fluids, tranny fluids etc.Amazon prices are great, 2 day shipping on prime makes it a no brainer as opposed to going to the shop.

2007 Honda CB900F 919 Hornet. I found this stuff in the local parts store by accident while looking for brake fluid. Came home and looked it up on the Mobile site and went back and got some. The price is about the same online as it is at the local outlet. (FYI. Here in Fort Lauderdale, for some reason, oil, brake fluid, car finish products, and wax, etcetera, are either the same or cheaper in the store, for the most part, than they can be had online. AutoZone has been matching the Amazon online prices if they are lower than store prices on many of these products if you take the printout to the store with you.) Drained the oil and replaced the filter with a K&N K&N KN-204C Powersports High Performance Oil Filter, that I did get cheaper online at Amazon.com. It took ALL of the four quarts and a smidge of a fifth to fill her back up to the top line in the sight glass. The manual says, "check with engine off," so that's what I did. Before the oil change, I did notice some jerkiness at low speed when I would just start down the driveway. This is gone. And, the shifting throughout the range is flawless, both up and down, at any speed. I'm convinced that this is truly MADE for motorcycles. By the way, just a note to anyone who has been away from bikes since before they invented oil JUST for motorcycles ... this is a requirement nowadays, as the automotive products seem to have additives that the bikes don't need, and may cause the clutch plates to slip, and other problems. Yeah, yeah, I know, that was a LONG time ago ... no comments from the peanut gallery!

reviewText: Having some experience with spray detailers, I had an idea what to expect. Basically some gloss, a slick surface, and short-term protection. There is some controversy regarding whether water beading is a sign of good protection, but I won't get into that. What water beading (or sheeting) does accomplish is it at least shows the presence of product.There's another way to show presence of a car wax/sealant that a car detailer showed me years ago, and that's the steam test. It doesn't measure protection, per se; it just shows the presence of a product so you can see how uniformly it covers an area, how easily it comes off, etc. Basically you coat some product onto a bathroom mirror and allow steam to build up in the room. Areas of the mirror coated in wax/sealant will have a uniform layer of steam that is different from untreated areas. It won't repel steam, the barrier causes tiny water droplets to build up uniformly, (appearing as if there is 'more' steam there). You can try it yourself and see what I mean.I bring this up because after noticing that the V7 just didn't seem to do as much as other similar sprays (the gloss was fair but not very good, and I didn't notice the extra water beading that other spray detailers provided at least short term), I wanted to see what it was leaving behind. I did the test, using the V7, along side a couple other spray detailers.The results surprised me. The areas treated with V7 left very little behind, with some streaks of presence. I also applied some Meguiars UQW and Turtle Wax Ice, both of which showed solid coverage (and the TW had remarkable durability to removal, incidentally).  When I applied two more coats of V7 over its area, it began to show more signs of coverage, confirming my results: This appears to be an extremely watered-down detailer, high in alcohol so that it "flashes" (evaporates) quickly. It came completely off with a bit of soapy water, whereas the other products actually were rather stubborn to remove.I give it two stars because as a quick detailer, it's fine. It will clean off fine dust and fingerprints, and leave a wee bit of shine. In the gallon size the value is fair, but $18 or so per bottle is silly, seeing as how it has just about zero sealant properties and even the shine it leaves is inferior to some $8 spray waxes.I've heard that CG is hit and miss with their products, but V7 is generally regarded as one of the hits. In my experience, it is not. Maybe they make some good stuff, but this isn't it. I don't want to judge the company by one product, so I'll give another one of their products a try, probably.  I gotta say, they do a really good job with graphic design on their packaging; especially the "vintage" line. I digress.

I've used Hybrid V7 twice now and I really like it. It smells great and is pretty much removed in an effortless manner. I don't intend on using it as a quick detailer for in between washing. My main use will be for... wait for it... DRYING my car. Once my car is fully washed and there's standing water left on the paint, I take a damp microfiber towel, mist the V7 in a sweeping motion to achieve better coverage on each panel, and then I dry the paint with the damp MF towel. Sounds kinda weird to dry water with a damp towel and using a liquid spray, but it works and the V7 adds a layer of lubrication between the paint and the drying towel, making a safer drying technique. The Hybrid V7 also adds a nice shine to paint that is well maintained or polished (in this case, my paint has been polished and well maintained) and also adds some slickness to the paint. My plan is to use it after every wash during the drying process and also add that fortifying protection for the paint sealant (Menzerna Power Lock, in this case), so I'm getting two jobs done during one process. My gallon of V7 is nowhere near done and I'm already itching to buy more, lol.EDIT: 05/07/2013I recently made a discovery about the V7, a negative one at that. I use Menzerna Power Lock paint sealant on my paint as the main protection, two coats of it to be exact. I noticed that every time I used the Hybrid V7 after the wash during the drying stage, it seemed as if the water was no longer beading and had a lot of surface tension going on as if there was no wax protection whatsoever. After talking with some fellow auto geeks on the Autogeek forums, I've discovered that the V7 must not "play well" with the Menzerna sealant. It's not necessarily a bad product, the V7, but it seemed to have an ill effect on the MPL, so I stopped using it altogether and I moved onto using a different synthetic spray wax. I'm sure the V7 works well with other Chemical Guys products, but certainly not with Power Lock. If any of you guys use Power Lock, I suggest you use something else to top off your main wax/sealant protection.

At first glance this stuff and its texture sorta reminds one of something out of that old movie, The Blob.  When I came across this strange looking goop at an auto show I decided to take a chance on it for two reasons.  One being that I had never seen anything like it, and second and most importantly, I am sure I am not alone in being one of those poor slobs that owns a car with a windshield that has one of those well known  hazes or films on it that are near impossible to get rid of.  Many of you know what I am talking about I am sure.  That haze that seems to forever be on the inside of some windshields that tenaciously resists anything one seems to throw at it.  And even when you do manage to get a ahead of it a little with a lot of scrubbing and swearing, it just tends to reappear sometime down the road.  This stuff actually did the trick in opening up a can of whoop a** on my horrible and aggravating haze. In the past I have scrubbed my windshield with ammonia, cleaners of all kinds, stiff brushes, pastes, you name it, only to see the haze return like a bad dream.  This cleaning clay was much easier to use that it appears it would be, and a little of it goes a long ways. But even if it was horrible to use or rinse it would have been worth it for me. I used it on the inside of both my car windshields and they have been crystal clear now for weeks. And all I can say is Hallelujah. Even if I never have another use for this stuff ever again it was worth the price just for that. I really can't attest to its effectiveness on water stains and such that other people have commented on since I presently don't have any glass around with that problem.  But with it being so delightfully effective on the windshield problem I had, I would not hesitate to try it on any real glass problem in the future.
