Griot's Garage started life as a web-based "petrol head" web site. The owner - a car collector himself - only sold products that his company either designed or discovered and came with Griot's personal stamp of approval. My friends in the Ferrari club are regular users of Griot's Garage goods and nobody cares more for their cars than the Tifosi! High praise indeed.My daily driver - an Audi A3 - has twin chrome tail pipes that are always turning black from the exhaust. I have tried several polishes but none gave me the cleanliness and shine I wanted. I crawled under the back of the Audi and started to polish away. I squeezed a small bit onto the tail pipe and then wrapped a soft cloth around it. It took only a few minutes to turn a dark and dirty tail pipe into the cleanest part of the car. Sweet! (Until I realized I now had to wash the whole car to make things even...)I next used the paste on a stainless steel knife blade. It had a few spots from the dishwasher (tiny circles of rust) and with a brisk rub, they disappeared quickly. Of course, I throughly washed the knife afterward because the warning on the tube says the paste is toxic!Finally, I gave our chrome kitchen faucet a quick polish. It did a great job on the dull finish but did not have much of an impact on some calcium deposits (not its fault...)Summary - This paste worked well on steel and chrome. It did not have an offensive odor (a lot of these products smell or ammonia) and it doesn't scratch the surface if used on a clean surface and with a soft cloth.Recommended.
summary: Does a great job on steel and chrome

reviewText: A small dab of this metal polish combined with a cotton towel brought chrome and brass back to life. I tried this on several heavy chrome components of a 1960s pinball machine  as well as the heavy brass 1910 designs of the Cutler Mail company (mail chutes). No use of the Dremel or other electric buffing components was necessary. Simple handwork did the job and I ended up being able to rescue a number of items that looked quite time-worn. 2.5 ounces doesn't sound like a lot, but you need so little for any one job that it's plenty (unless, of course, you're working on large components such as the chrome bumpers or wheels of a car).

I polish a lot of Aluminum and have tested several different brands and types of rubbing compounds and polishes. They all work to some degree, but this Griot's Garage polish is my new favorite. It seems to take less effort to get a decent shine from old aluminum, and with a little more elbow grease, you can get things to really shine! I was very impressed and will be recommending this to my friends as my go-to polish of choice for aluminum. I am certain it works just as well on steel, copper, etc. This is a high quality product without a lot of hype. The product speaks for itself and I am happy to help promote fine quality products like this one.

Had used my Gerbar Gator MacheteGerber 22-41576 Gator Machete with Sheathquite extensively this past week (clearing brush). After give a good manual cleaning of the gunk, tree sap etc; I then tried to bring back the luster with Griot's Metal Polish which did what I expected ... gave it a nice general cleaning and shine I then finished up my restoration with Meguiar's Metal Finishing PolishMeguiar's Ultra Finishing Polishwhich gave it the extra sparkle needed before my next Amazonian adventure.Griot's Metal Polish indeed cleans, polishes and protects!

I've been a die-hard fan of Eagle One Nevr-Dull and thought this would provide the perfect test environment to put Griot's against.  I used it on my Harley polished stainless and chrome, and it cleaned them up BRILLIANTLY!  Don't get me wrong, I love Nevr-Dull and it's hard to do 'one better.'  But I believe the Griot's polish did a little bit better job than the Nevr-Dull, and -- this is the big part -- it's nice not to have to polish an entire motorcycle pinching a cotton ball.The hard thing about any polish is that it totally depends on how dirty something is to begin with before you can rate the performance.  I keep my stuff clean and it still took a bit of elbow grease, but nothing unusual.  Likewise, it doesn't take a lot of polish to get the metal sparkling again.In the end, this is a bit more expensive than Nevr-Dull, but I feel it's worth the additional cost.  I barely put a dent in this bottle so I know it's going to last a bit before I need to replace it.  I also love having it in a tube.  If you have shiny objects that you want shinier, this is an outstanding metal polish!I received this from the manufacturer for testing and review and have shared my honest experience in this review.
summary: Great on Chrome and other shiny things!

reviewText: Some have noted that a lot of work is needed with this polish.  That is true but you need to know what results you desire.  The finer the polish, the more work will be required because less material is removed but you also have less risk of damage and the end result is more mirror like.  This polish is very fine so it will take some elbow grease if applying it by hand but the results are excellent.  If you have a lot of material to remove, start with a polish that has greater cutting properties then finish with this.  You will like the results.
summary: A very fine polish so some work is needed but outcome is very good.

reviewText: I owned an aluminum bodied roadster for several years . Before I gave up trying to keep it polished and got it painted, I tried many metal polishing products including "Blue Magic", "Simichrome", "Autosol","Everbrite", "Midas Touch", "Met-all", "Peek" and "Rolite". The Griot's works very well on silver and brass and a little goes a long way. I did not try it on aluminum. Does it work better than the others? I'd say not, so I would base my purchase on a cost analysis of the comparable products.I've never been a fan of Griot's. I've tried various products and have felt that they are over-priced. This works well but price justification is the issue.5/7/14: Just used it to clean up the stainless steel burner top in my motor home and it did a great job. Again, nothing to compare it against.
summary: As good as other similar products. Better...?

reviewText: This is one of the better metal polishes I've used. Now if only so much muscle power weren't needed to get the job done. Alas, that isn't a comment on the polish but rather on my advancing years.
I used this product to shine up the little figures I weld. It does the job with just as much rubbing as most other products. I didn't find it to be better or worse than other similar products.
summary: I didn't find it to be better or worse than other similar products

reviewText: Griot's Garage Metal Polish is a very good quality metal polishing cream with aluminum dioxide.  White compounds (such as this) which contain aluminum dioxide are used to finish off soft metals such as aluminum, brass, and copper.  They can also be used as an intermediate stage in polishing iron, steel, and nickel and chrome plating.CAUTION:  This white polish should *not* be used on gold or silver as recommended on the package as it is too abrasive.  Instead, use a good quality polish with jeweler's rouge such asWright's Silver Cream.  It will also remove the protective lacquer from brass.This cream is best applied with a soft cotton material;  an old jersey-knit tee shirt is ideal.  Don't be stingy with the polish—start off with a generous amount and let the product rather than your thumb do the work.  Double the cloth to provide sufficient cushioning and as the material blackens, switch to a clean area.  A soft cotton flannel is ideal for a final buffing, especially for bright plating.I tested the Griot's polish on a decades-old aluminum Bialetti moka pot and on a chrome-over-brass kettle.  In both instances, it effectively removed oxidation, small scratches, and mild pitting and it left a mirror finish on the aluminum.

My husband decided to use this product on his motorcycle instead of the truck wheels due to the high temps outside. The motorcycle's chrome parts were not hot due to it being in the garage, so he felt the polish would work better. It turns out he was right. He was thrilled to see the polish removed even some of the most stubborn marks on his motorcycle. Since he didn't think these marks would ever come off (he tried with some other products), he has decided that this is his new go-to product for polishing his motorcycle.He'll be trying it on his truck wheels once the weather is cooler. I'll update the review to cover how it works with chrome wheels at that time.

Purchased this polish for my chrome wheels on my F-150 pick-up. Over the Winter I had a build up of grime and oxidation that would not come off with soap and water. I had purchased a bottle of the Turtle Wax version of this cleaner and noticed that is took alot of elbow grease to clean the wheels. In some cases I had to apply it twice. When I used the Groit's metal polish it took me half the time. The paste goes on easy and is a little thicker than the Turtle Wax, so it stays in place. Buffing out was easy and did not leave any powder marks. The shine was life the wheesl were brand new. This is not the first Groit product that I have purchased. I am completely impressed with the product line and will continue to use the metal polish as well as other products.

I gave this Griot's Garage Metal Polish to my husband to use since he is a mechanic.  He used this to polish his motorcycle instead and it really worked well!  So well that he is anxious to try it out on other cars he is restoring or working on.  After seeing his motorcycle, before and after, I would say this polish is a good deal for the price.  The tube is good size and the polish works very well.

I have a lovely bronze sink in my guest bathroom. Unfortunately it tend to collect a lot of water spots. I'd been looking for a good polish when I found this.I applied the polish with a paper towel since I didn't have the recommended cloth. It was easy to squeeze just the right amount on the paper towel. Then I rubbed and rubbed and rubbed... Until the polish turned all black (it was so messy that I ended up putting on gloves), then I buffed that off with a clean paper towel. The sink was much shinier, but it took another rub and buff session before it was back to it's original shine.I was concerned that if I used the wrong polish it might damage the bronze, but Griots didn't hurt it a bit. I'm a little wore out from all the rubbing and buffing required but the sink is shiny again.This gets the job done but requires a lot of effort on your part. It would probably be awesome in an application with a buffer.

I used this to polish my polished Aluminum exhaust pipes and muffler on my Motorcycle.  It cleaned them right up, and they shine brightly.  It even cleaned up the haze that the last polish I tried just couldn't cut.  Very good product.  I highly recommend it.

Over the years, I've taken great pains to preserve the finish on my now nearly 20 year old, one owner M3.  But never before had I taken the plunge and tried "paint cleaning clay."  The idea - you rub play-doh all over your car to clean it? - struck me as somewhat ludicrous. A colleague and fellow BMW addict insisted that it works and that I try it.I've tried it and I'm sold. Cleaning with Griot's clay will be step one in my exterior car care routine from here on out.  Unlike another amazon reviewer, I had no problems with 'sticky clay' on the car or my hands - and no need to don the gloves that come with this kit.  Start with a good wash, of course - P21S "shampoo" or one of the Meguiars wash preparations are my usual choice.  Dry well.  Then generously spray the Spray Shine on an area about 12 inches square.  Pull off about half of the clay provided, spray it well and work it in your hands. Spray it again, then start to rub.  Wipe the car with one of the microfiber polishing towels provided.  Wow.  The surface of your paint will feel as smooth as silk. Those tiny bits of bug, sap, and grime will be gone. And the process itself is a very pleasant, tactile experience. The clay provided with this kit seems to be very mildly abrasive and the entire process is effective but very gentle on your paint.I follow with a fine polish - 3M Imperial Hand Glaze is my preference - and then wax - P21S carnauba or Zymol for me, although there are lots of other choices out there. With that regimen, my "Hellrot" '95 M3 looks pretty darned good.Overcome your skepticism and try it.

This clay bar kit is actually everything you need in a clay bar kit. You get a great amount of clay, Speed Shine and 3 super soft and plush microfiber towels. I really want to replace all my other microfibers with Griot's! I don't use the gloves, though. I'm weird about gloves, lol. The clay is a bit stickier than what I've used in the past, but it doesn't really stick to my hands or anything else. The Speed Shine is great, too, and it smells really good. I'm thinking of getting the gallon size of Speed Shine, which will basically fill up the standard 35 fl. oz. bottle around 3.5 times, making it a better value than getting a new bottle each time it runs out. I have to discipline myself, though. If I start looking at car care products, I feel like a kid in a candy store... I want it all!! Great kit, though. I'd definitely buy it all again.

I am a fan of Griot's, they have some good stuff and lots of videos that you can watch and they explain the best way to use their products. I do buy other brands of car products too.This clay bar thing was new to me, never used it before. I heard about it from when I had my car detailed the last time.Couple things to remember, it is easy, don't press hard, do small areas. I was working on 2'x2' or smaller areas of my car in my garage, use the speed shine to keep it lubricated and fold over the clay as it flattens out.I started with a just washed car and waxed the car after I finished with the clay bar and WOW!! Big difference in the shine.My car is white, the paint needed a little TLC and this was the trick.It is easy to see, or feel, where you need to work the clay on the paint. Surface should be very smooth when you have finished an area, if not just do it again. Took my time and it came out great. My neighbor thought I had my car repainted, did I mention, it is a 1998 model with original paint. It is not a garage queen and it has been parked outside a lot in the last 16 years.I cannot compare with other clay bar kits but this one sure exceeded my expectations.

Okay so this my first time using a clay system to clean the grime off the paint.  All I can say is wow, makes the paint super smooth and shiny just like it rolled off the showroom floor.  Just follow the directions and watch the instructional video on youtube by Griot's.  This is a complete system to restore your clear coat paint.  All you need after this is just some good carnauba was to protect from the elements.  The supplied quantity is good and I think it should treat a regular size SUV at least 15 times.  Highly recommended!

It accomplished exactly what I bought the product for. Even though I had enough Speed shine I bought the kit mainly for the clay but wanted the included micro fiber towels which are a soft great towel to use. You save a some of money buying these combo kits over buying them separate. If memory serves me correctly when buying this kit you basically get the towels free versus buying the items separately.

I thought I had to have this little brush to clean the lug nuts on my three cars. It does work and works well on the lug nuts however it is an extra brush that I probably could have done without. Its one of those things that is nice to have but not absolutely necessary. I found that with good wheel cleaner and most any rag I can do the same job. This brush will probably last a  very long time.
summary: Does What It Is Designed To Do---Somewhat

reviewText: It's a lug nut brush, it did a good job cleaning up months of grime, but it takes some elbow grease and time.  I don't mind putting in the time to get results, and I'd recommend this product to anyone else that wants a detailed finish to their wash.  Worked wonders on my WRX wheels.
The bristles on the brush are basically strands of stiff plastic and I have not found it to do any cleaning at all around the lug nuts. Save your money.
summary: Bristles too stiff to do any cleaning

reviewText: Griot's Garage makes quality products and I have occasionally purchased items from their catalog.  When I came across this lug nut clean brush, I saw an opportunity to use the right tool for the job.  It works as I expected.

Saving knuckles is important and this is the tool to have.  Saves so much time and energy getting in and around lug nuts.  This was a replacement for one that I already had, and had been using for 5 years.  One of my kids decided to use it to uncover dinosaur bones and ruined the brush.
This works well for lug nut cleaning but it could be a bit stiffer to work better.  You just need to use a lot more cleaner instead.
summary: Ok brush. Wish it was a bit stiffer.

reviewText: I am a bit of a fanatic when it comes to keeping my car clean, so this was another tool to add to my arsenal of brushes for getting in to difficult areas without damaging anything. Works fine and is stiff enough to get out the dirt.

I am on the fence with this product.  Being from Griot's I know they have a lot of depth of products for car care so I thought I would give this a shot.  The bristles are very stiff, almost too stiff.  They don't want to fit around the lug nuts and when they do, they end up bending the bristles.  And I know what you are thinking, it was my wheels, well I tried it on 2 totally different styles of wheels to see if it made any difference and not much.  If your lug nuts are exposed, its probably okay.  If they are recessed, I would look for another product.  And where is it made?  No clue, couldn't find any stampings or label on the packaging to note country of origin.

I haven't used this product yet but expect it will do a better job than the toothbrush I was using!  I use it with two other effective products available on Amazon, Sonax 230200-755 Wheel Cleaner and Mothers Wheel Brush.  If you have invested in chrome wheels, these products can really make those wheels sparkle.  Brake dust is hard to remove, but these products do the job.
summary: A Good Brush for cleaning those lug nuts and wells

reviewText: I was expecting something that I could push onto my lug nuts and twist and the lug nuts would come clean, but the bristles seemed to weak... maybe I got the wrong thing, but this isn't for me and it's just gonna sit in my shed...
summary: Didn't work for what I was expecting...

reviewText: I have washed these towels several times and I cannot get them to stop shedding like a dog. They are wonderfully soft, thick and plush but they just keep shedding fibers like mad.
Washed them first they are very good towels for buffing your car will buy more to dry car off when done washingI highly recommend this product
These microfiber towels are very thick and are great for buffing off wax residue, polishing, and general detailing. They are holding up very well after a few washes.

Good price and fast delivery.  I just had my car painted and these cloths are excellent for washing drying the car and also for applying and removing wax.  They are very soft and won't scratch the paint as will sponges and shammeys.

I was looking for a micro fiber towel for use with quick detail sprays and decided to try these. I am not that impressed with them. Even though they are thick and soft they seem to leave the fine micro fiber hairs on the car like lint. I now use them for washing the vehicle and seem to work fine for that.

I love thse towels, very soft, perfect size.I use then to wash my car and to remove polishes and waxes.Tip: wash them before use, they will not shed after you wash them, absolute no shedding.Also use them when I do a Rinseless wash, they are very plush so they trap the dirt deep down inside the fibers keeping the dirt away from your paint.I gave it five stars for so many reason.Great price too.
I really like these towels a lot.  They are soft and absorbent with a soft silk type edging.  If they were borderless I would give them 5-stars.
They are very soft and absorbent and so far are staying that way after washing them a few times. They are a decent size too.

Wanted extra outlets in my truck for an FM Transmitter for my iPod, charger for the iPhone/GPS, a heated seat and reverse sensor. Fits them all perfectly and the mount meant I was able to mount it and never worry about it getting smacked around or tossed about when not using.
Great useful unit. It easily enables me to power my cell phone, blue tooth ear piece, GPS device, and my passengers electronic devices all at the same time.

When you're in a car with two cell phones and two kids with DSi's and DVD players, you need more than the standard two outlets that most vehicles provide. This was a great investment and is perfect for traveling, especially with a family and a lot of electronics.It is kind of bulky but I don't know how you would get rid of that without having the four outlets.Some of the plugs are tight going in but stay put and come out with a good pull.
summary: A Great Investment for Electronics and Travel

reviewText: I have 1 DC socket in my car (Honda CRV). This thing is exactly what I was looking for! I have my GPS, portable DVD player, Phone Charger & DC/AC power inverter connected to all 4 sockets, plus an iPod cord in the USB port to charge my iPod. It has a great bracket so you can attach it somewhere in your car. I'm thinking of using velcro to attach it, rather than screws. 1 of the 4 sockets is spring loaded, so you can put your cigarette lighter in that one if you needed to. The rest of the 3 sockets are regular. But all 4 work great! The whole thing is just very convenient and I wouldn't change a thing about it.
summary: Exactly what I was looking for!

reviewText: The 4 12V outlets are very handy the cable seems to be heavy enough, the light on the unit is a bit bright for my application and the USB outlet is WAY handy!

Good 1 to 4 car DC power duplicator. The power light would not turn on until I turn the car key to accessory which is good. It will not unnecessarily drain the car battery. Construction materials seems solid. I can connect to my car power ports in the front and in the back. The attached electrical cord comes in handy when positioning the duplicator in the car. The USB port is a bonus. Price is good. I give this product 5 stars.

I actually installed this backward so the USB port and LED light were facing toward me, and put the cigarette lighter connecters in the back. makes it slightly less ugly if you use multiple devices that stay plugged in.  I plug in my phone, tablet, Satellite radio and GPS. The feel is substantial, the connector plugs are very snug after multiple weeks of use. I previously purchased a Bell multi-socket adapter and it didn't come close to this quality - the Bell one constantly popped out. This one say's put. highly recommended.
summary: very well made - except for the USB port on the back

reviewText: I ordered this based on other reviews that emphasized how well made and rugged it was- and those reviews were absolutely correct. The case is tough and flexible and not likely to crack. The mounting bracket is wide enough to provide good support with either the included screws or the included adhesive patch. I used the adhesive to mount it at the top of the shelf above the glove box in my 2003 Honda Element, where it stays solidly attached.
summary: Does what it should, and does it well

reviewText: This is very nice, we can plug into the cigarette lighter and have 4 ports for other electronics, just wish it had more than 1 USB port
summary: Auto Socket Duplicator Plus USB Port

reviewText: Great product. Am able to charge all of my toys along with using the USB Port. I have affixed it to the side and works very well.

I use this product on my van to charge phones, GPS, power converter. There are many pros and a minor con:Pros:1) It has its own fuse like car's. So it is cheap to replace the fuse.2) The cable is quite long (more than 2 feet) so kids in the back seats can use it too.3) One of four sockets is for cigarette, so it can be used to replace the taken socket.4) Extra USB port is quite useful. Since many wall USB cables to charge phones are detachable, I can use a cable and hook it up to the USB port to charge phones/tablet.Con:The front LED light is quite bright and can not be adjustable, I have to use tape to reduce it. I really should give it 4.5 stars but I could not.I've just have it a couple of weeks. Still works fine so far

I ordered this unit to run my emergency light, cell phones, and other electronics in my plow truck.Super high quality unit, and even comes with an adapter that has a built in fuse (standard push in fuse) that's easily replaced should you overload the unit in use.  I cut that end of, and hardwired it to my additional fuse panel that I run for all my electrical add-ons, so I didn't even use my trucks cigarette lighter.Great buy !

I bought this as a gift to my husband for our jeep wrangler. It came really fast, and I had every intention of installing it myself so that he would see it when he came home. Unfortunately there are a couple screws that are much easier to place into the bumper if you are using two people. The instruction manual definitely only shows one person doing this, but it was a lot more convenient to have the help of another person. Other than that the light bar fit perfect, its strudy and it looks good because it is not huge in comparison to other light bars. Once we installed two spot lights it looked even better and the spot light fit perfectly even tho they were a different brand. Good buy, recommend it.
summary: Great Investment - two people to install

reviewText: Put this on my 2012 Black JKU took me a second to figure out that I didn't NEED to cut or mod anything. The screws are a serious pain in the @$$ as far as installing but just neded some patience...maybe would of been easier to take off front bumper?!?! ....I have 3 of the KC 130 watt slim-lites on it...like it! Think it is pefect for those of us that want an easy light bar on the stock bumper.....Oh, only thing I did to the bar was drilled holes by where the lights mounsso i could run the wiring through the bar (fun times!) ...down to the mount where I drilled through the round mounting bracket to keep the clean look...after the wires were connected and everything tighted up then got some stuff (forget the name) that closed/filled in the gaps left by the holes I drilled for the wires on the bar...overall very happy..

I did contact the seller before it arrived to make sure it would fit my 2012 JK Unlimited. I was told that it would fit with no problems. Wrong, I had to modify the plastic tray between the bumper and grill. In fact, I made a new panel becuse I did want to cut up the factory one. It does look good after I did the mods, which I was informed that I would not have to do.
summary: It will fit a 2012 JK Unlimited with "DRILLING & MODIFICATION"

reviewText: First, the good...  So, I have a 2013 Jeep JK and you DO NOT need to cut anything to mount this bracket.  I almost did but kept playing with it until I FINALLY figured it out.  Do not give into temptation and cut the plastic piece between bumper and grill - trust me - it will work.  It's a pain to mount but it does work.Now, for the bad.  I bought this because it was a "Mopar" product.  It showed up in a box with a Mopar sticker over another sticker.  The directions clearly stated it came from Rugged Ridge (their version of the same product was $15 less expensive).  I haven't mounted the lights yet but it looks like it will work out pretty well.

I like this light bar hear are a couple reasons one it is consider a oem part and will bolt right on to you jk jeep plus for me I didn't want a light bar that was taller then my hood and I wanted a bar that behind the bumper so it work for me
Nice bar but doesn't fit my 2012 JKU w/mod. The holes in the lower bracket don't match the holes in the frame. You'll have to drill.

I bought this before I studied the Kelvin charts for color. Pretty bright, not as bright as 1156 and extremely unpleasant color for my RV interior. May be good for tail light or such, but the light reminds me of standing under a blueish street light.

I have purchased a few of these at a time, replacing the lights on our 2012 Heartland Torque fifth wheel.  The first light I changed over was the porch light, and I have had the light on for more than a year!  We live full time in the trailer so battery usage is critical. The LED bulbs reduce power consumption dramatically.  The UV testers did not do much for me but the bulbs are great and very cost effective.  I am not sure how long they will last, but some of the bulbs are reaching two years old and they are still burning bright!
summary: Great Source of Light, No Battery Draw!

reviewText: I bought these based on past reviews and I have to say these bulbs work awesome on the outside lights for a 2002 Forest River Sport toy hauler, nice and bright. We mainly camp off the grid and rely on battery so upgrading incandescent lights to LEDs is a big benefit consuming 1/10th the power.  These lights are blue/white and bright! They work very well for outdoor lighting and loading lights on the back of our toy hauler.
summary: These LEDs bulbs work Awesome for external RV lighting too

reviewText: Installed these replacement bulbs from Amazon for my RV without a hitch. These are brighter than the original, and use 9.5% of the power [.14 amps vs 1.49 amps] of the 1141 bulb. not inexpensive, but the circuit was maxed out and I had to do something to reduce the load.

Replaced almost all the overhead 1141's with these.  They are really much whiter of a light, and I love em.  Plenty of room for them as they are almost identicle size to the stock bulbs, but as you know, LED's draw much much less power.  Highly recommend these especially to RV owners.
summary: A great white LED bulb for the RV

reviewText: Low energy.  Good light. Easy to install.  Everything I wanted.  I am very glad I bought it.  Don't know what to do with the silly detector.

I bought several LEd lights for my RV to test them out, and this one was way too blue for my taste.  Bright for the lower number of LEDs it has, but the light doesn't match my other bulbs and looks un-natural to me.
summary: Not warm white.  Too blue for my taste.

reviewText: Only regret us not changing to these sooner. More light, I like the bluer light, less drain on the12V  system and they should never burn out.

I must have 20 1156 bulbs from various places.  (all chinese made I am sure)  This one is the only one that works without adding a ballist resistor. (YMMV)  With newer cars  this is a plus.  Now you will still get a warning that a bulb is out, but at least it works.  The other bulbs I have that do not work in the newer cars seem to work in the older cars. So as family comes over I slowly replace the bulbs on my families cars with the box I have sitting around that don't work on my MINI.
summary: This bulb seems to work where most do not.

reviewText: I bought these to replace the incandescent bulbs in our RV interior ceiling lights.  I was looking for similar brightness.  They sure are!  They are a bluish white light (6000K) but not glaring. Because I boondock (dry camp) with a solar charging system and need to conserve batteries I need these lamps.  The old bulbs drew 3.7 amps while these only draw 0.2 amps!  I will replace all the rest now!  I have only used them for one week so far so hard to tell if they will last.
summary: Bright LEDs work well in RV

reviewText: I bought 3 different high rated LED lamps to replace 1411 tungsten lamps and of the three this produced the best light, both in terms of brightness and in having a clean white light. This will be my LED of choice for the additional 1411 bulbs I will be replacing.
summary: Best white light and brightness at good price

reviewText: This is no better than scotch tape.  I thought it was going to be a flexible fabric type product.  Instead it is like a plastic tape that doesn't stay stuck. I do not recommend this product.  It's a waste of money.

It's works, waddya u want?  I like this because it is thicker then most tapes, it grabs more material thus making a stronger bond.  Double edge sword though because the repair is more visible then using thinner tape.  I say to hell with the looks, but if you a panzy who cares about looks, but the thin one.

This Tape is intended for awning repair, but it will do a lot more.  The distinctive advantage of this tape is that it will resist heat, and will not gum up like its distant cousin, Duct Tape.  Yes, it will repair an awning, or a boat/car/motorcycle cover.  I have seen it go through a washing machine cycle.  The adhesive is strong, and will not decay as regular duct tape will.
this product is great. repaired my daughters awning that had a fight with the wind. it had a few splits and puckers. this tape did a fantastick repair//
A fast and easy way to repair those small rips or tears that appear in your awning.I keep a round a roll for on the road.

I first washed the awning with soap and water and then used acetone to remove any unseen films.  After applying, the tape stuck for a few minutes and then peeled off.  Admittedly, this is strong but if only it would have stuck I would've been happy.  It may me that my awning was too porous since it was/is old.  If you have a newer awning, you might get lucky and it will adhere.

I had a rip in my RV awning approx 6 inches long and didn't want to buy a new awning so I purchased this tape to solve the problem.  I cleaned the awning surface with acetone and applied the tape.  It stuck very well to the awning and the rip is barely noticeable.
After 1.5 months in the sun it ROTTED out. Not made for outside awnings as advertized. DO NOT BUY THIS JUNK!

Got these to add a bit more LED lighting to my Yamaha Roadstar.  These lights went up under the saddlebags to throw blue light onto the chrome pipes and wheels, and they do a great job.  Bright as heck, well made, look to be totally waterproof, Easily installed, the 3M tape holds them securely in place on the saddlebag mount.  100% satisfied, and highly recommend!
summary: Good quality, fast shipping, great price!

reviewText: Not sure about the longevity of the leds. I put them on my motorcycle to add some accent lights. Very nice glow that isn't overpowering.
hooked these strips up to my amp for my subs and the beat with the music. these are great. sweet

I put two strips in the footwells and put the other two in the trunk because 3 of the leds from one of the strips didn't light up. The 3M tape in the back of the strip was ok and the wire was about a 24 gauge or maybe smaller so its a little hard to work with. I put up a pic of the two in the footwells. overall these are way better than another set i bought from another seller, these dont start to flicker after a few minutes of being on like the others. Ive had these on for more than an hour at times when driving and no flickering!

I put these in my car and ill say they are very bright!  I covered half of it with tape and that fixed the issue.  Th only problem with these is that the gauge is very high probably a 25 and is hard to work with when stripping the wires.  Other than that I am very satisfied.

This is my second order. My first I used as moon lighting in my 90 gallon cichlid tank. I simply attached the 4 pcs. to my strip light, wired to a transformer and bingo "moon" lighting. I love to keep our vehicles looking good,perhaps to a fault.I have used every major vinyl and rubber protectant  on the market, after trying this for the first time,I am hooked.The other reviews says a lot of great things about this product and I think they  are correct.303 puts a protective layer on interior and exterior surfaces.You can really see this film on the surface that is different then any other product.Its a satin finish that has a great look.Just apply and wipe off with a microfiber towel.I will do an update after applying to all the interior and exterior plastic and tires  on our 2013 Rav4.Everything else on the market seems to disappear after a few weeks(parking in the garage ) we will see.I bought the 128 oz. container(pour into a smaller spray bottle) and saved quite a bit over the smaller cotainer.Thats a lot of stuff,but I just did 2 other  vehicles and used 8 oz including tires rubber floor mats and  plastic pieces around the engine.

I purchased this product based off of other recommendations from boat and car enthusiast.  I was looking for something better than Armor All, or the other standard car products out there.  My initial use was for the black plastic trim on my F-150 pickup which had faded to a greyish color versus the dark grey almost black factory color.  It's awesome.  It's easy to put on, doesn't streak and lasts about 4-6 weeks.I spray the 303 on a rag and then apply to the areas I want protected, I then wipe the area dry.  I do this in small sections to make sure I get a nice even application.Since using this on the truck and being very satisfied I started using it on everything that takes any kind of sun abuse.  Basically anything plastic or vinyl that spends time in the sun, like the roof of our pop-up camper, our ATV's (3 of them), the dirt bike, the riding mower, the push mower, and the vinyl seats on everything from the mower to the boat.  It really works well protecting items exposed to the sun.I have a friend that has used this product on his boat seats for the past 8 years and they look as good as the day he bought the boat, and they feel new.  He swears by it and I can see why.  I've seen dashes and vinyl that's had Armor All on it and they look like crap after a few years, 303 does the job that other products simply fail to do...even though they claim to work.This product is worth every penny.  I know it's a little spendy, but it really is worth it.  If you're like me and try to buy quality items that you plan on keeping for 7-10 years, this is the product you need to keep them looking new.  I only wish I had known about this product sooner.

reviewText: I own a 2013 BMW Mini Cooper and I haven't taken it in for its first service appointment yet, but I sat down with the head mechanic and asked about keeping the engine clean with my regular routine of spraying Simple Green in the entire engine, scrubbing areas with various foam and bristle brushes, then using a nearby water hose with a light trickling of water to clean the engine off, then applying a spraying of 303 Aerospace over the whole bay and let dry for a few hours.  The mechanic said it would be much appreciated  during servicing, as a clean engine is easier to diagnose and work on, and the dressing helps keep the rubber hoses in the engine from deteriorating, which are usually the things to fail first and need replacing.I use 303 Aerospace solely as an engine dressing, and while the instructions say to spray on and wipe off after a few minutes, when it comes to engines, clean the engine, and while wet, soak the entire bay with 303 Aerospace.  If possible, leave the hood open and let it air dry for a few hours.  Close the hood after that and engine cleaning is done!I have Klasse VLR protectant for my usual treatment of exterior plastic/vinyl areas but when doing the engine, I often go over the car exterior with 303.  Can't hurt.Highly recommend this for engine dressing.Keep in mind, this will not 'restore' plastic/vinyl to look like new.  It'll keep the materials looking the way they do.  So if you have a brand new car, start using this and it'll keep the car looking new.  If you have faded or worn out areas, it'll keep those areas from getting worse, but won't make it look better.  This works as a protectant, but doesn't restore.For restoration, you'll need to research other products.I keep this in my auto detailing kit always.

I just bought my fourth gallon, yes, gallon of 303. And I've received tremendous value from the first three over a lot of years.I use 303 on just about everything in my car that is smooth and not paint (Zaino for the paint.) The door seals are six years old and look perfect. The plastic headlamp lenses are perfect. Tires. Wheels. Trim. Instrument cluster.My teak outdoor furniture looks great. (Get some big Scotch-Brite pads and 409. Spray the teak liberally with 409, go over with the Scotch-Brite, rinse with a hose, let dry, then treat with 303 Protectant -- you'll be stunned how well it works. Every month or so, a quick spray of 303, then wipe it dry, and you're done.)I keep 303 around because pretty much anything that has a hard surface (so that you can wipe it dry ... that's key) looks better and lasts longer. I have a carbon fiber frame on my bicycle. 303 keeps it looking perfect.Every time I work on something, or clean it up, I 303 (for me, it is a verb) it. Rubber soles on shoes. A vacuum cleaner. You name it.Truly, out of everything I get on Amazon, it is one of the only things I would clearly give six stars to if I could. It keeps my stuff looking good. It restores stuff that is looking worn. I can't recommend it more highly.
summary: Beyond useful; my go to product so many ways

reviewText: I use this on a million different things around the house, the motorhome, the vehicles, you name it! It really does leave a protecting layer on any surface, except maybe glass. I use it on the motorhome for conditioning the slide seals, air conditioner shrouds, spraying the front before a trip makes removing bugs a breeze, and many more things. On my cars I use it to keep running boards, rubber door seals and more black and supple. I even use it on the lawnmower! Did not see anything wrong or damaged on the unit when it delivered so I mounted the part that is when things became apparent that it might be an unanticipated problem.  The first thing I noticed after mounting it and closing the hood was that the design of the unit was going to exaggerate a problem with the hood on the highway or heavy headwinds.  The jeep hood already has a slight issue with catching wind and bouncing up and down, but, the design of this unit has the Deflector jutting straight out before curving upward.  This creates an even larger point to catch wind and creating drag forcing the hood to jump even worse and at lower speeds so you tend to be watching the hood movement even more than normal.  Second issue I had with the part was the quality of the forming, at least with my part.  Once inside the jeep I noticed that the right side looked lower so I checked the mounting and everything was exactly the same as the left side.  Checking closer it was apparent that the right side was slightly misformed, it had more bend than the right so that the top of the deflector was lower(closer) to the hood than the left.  Yes, it is quite noticeable from inside the vehicle but not a huge issue.  Overall I am considering just removing it and not have it on the Wrangler

I've installed HIDs three times total in my car, and out of all of the bulbs, these were the most difficult.Before I begin on that, let me start off with the brightness.I ordered the 5000k ("Diamond White"), for maximum brightness, for my 2012 Impreza. Originally had Xentec HIDs, which one ended up failing.The light output of this bulb is far superior to that of the Xentec, likely 3 times as bright. Though I don't have a projector housing, and the light isn't exactly concentrated as if I did have the correct housing, they look fantastic.As far as installing them, my headlight ended up coming damaged. The plastic clip which turns to lock into the headlight housing was somehow chipped (as if the package was opened before). I had to almost force-turn it into the housing for it to stay, but it's secure at the moment. The package did in fact look to be opened and carelessly re-closed, as if they were returned, but at the moment i'm not worried.Overall, for the money (which I didn't really know whether it would have been worth it before purchasing), these headlights are ten times as good as the Xentec pair I had bought twice before, and the stock halogen lights my Impreza had when bought.

Unlike most people who purchase these types of kits, I was not as concerned about the "look" of HID headlights on my 2011 RAM.  I was more interested in the brighter, more visible light and the low current draw associated with HID technology.  I ordered this kit hoping it would be of good components and well contructed, and it appears to be just that.  I've tested the current draw after the ballasts charge and the lights are stabilized and they are drawwing a steady 16.3 watts, which is primarily what I was after.  The bulbs throw a very bright, well-defined pattern that is cutoff on top by my stock reflector housings.  I have them aimed just a little lower than the stock setting as to not blind oncoming traffic and I have not been flashed once.  I did very quickly order 5000K bulbs to replace the 4300K bulbs that I originally ordered with the kit because I wanted slightly more white spectrum light, rather than the yellowish light that the originals threw.

reviewText: I have had these installed now for a few weeks. I absolutely love them! Took around 30 minutes to install, hardest part was getting my factory headlight bulbs out( 2012 Ford Escape). They are INCREDIBLY BRIGHT! Make sure your headlights are adjusted properly so you don't blind oncoming traffic. I ordered the 8k color bulbs( super white with blue tinge) They are exactly as described, a little more blue than I was expecting. But, overall, I am very satisfied with the color. I had to order LED fog light bulbs to match them.Night time driving is a blast now, highway signs POP.

The kit was extremely easy to install and had everything I needed. It works great and is so much brighter than the old halogens. I got the 6000K bulbs and they are exactly what I was looking for. I apologize for the delayed review.  I actually bought this kit for my dad who resides in Malaysia.  I recently made a trip back, so I thought it was a good idea to get him the HID kit so he can see better at night.  This kit was going into his Mercedes 200.  Okay, on to the review...The presentation of the box is very nice, but it is made of cheap material.  However, the product itself is packed nicely in the box, and the construction of the box is made well enough to protect the Bulb, ballast and wiring.  To save on luggage space, I discarded the box.  I bubble wrapped the parts and sandwiched them between my clothing.  They survived the journey half way around the world.  The instructions leaflet was actually very helpful...especially the graphic depictions.  The installation is straight-forward.  We managed to get the new kit working in under 30 minutes.  Tidying up the cables were a whole different story! :)The light are much much brighter than the OEM H4 bulbs.  HOWEVER, for some reason, one of the 6K bulb was a "tad" bit more yellowish than the other.  My dad did not really notice it.  He was more excited to see how much brighter his lights were.  The other complaint was the high beam.  I think the bulb for the high beam is not sufficient with this setup, but since he drives in town mostly, that's not a big issue.Overall, this Kensun kit looks like a quality product.  The cables are well constructed, and the ballast are well built.  They don't look like the cheap e-bay versions, and this HID does not flicker.  However, for those of you who need Hi-beam with your H4, you might want to look at their bi-xenon conversion kit...

reviewText: first the hook seems like it will get into places I can't use my current ones for.  However I am surprised that otc used such a cheap light hollow plastic handle on this. I never thought I needed one of these until I had to replace the power steering cooler on chevy Silverado. The clamps at the pump end are very inaccessible from the top. Then its very difficult to pull a hardened hose off the fitting because there is too little room to get a good grip on the hose.Do yourself a favor-- get a set of cable pliers with these for the clamps, and you will be prepared for just about anything.

The tool fits in my hand nicely and the angle makes it easy to remove a hose. The metal seems to be of good quality,just be careful if you need to reuse the hose again not to poke it because the tool is very sharp at the tip.

This hook is made really well.  The design and the quality that has gone into it is really nice.  I have only used it a few times so I don't have a lot to go on but I think it will be with me for a long time.If comes to a point where you have to use this hook to remove the hose it probably means that hose is getting replaced, so it can and it will tear the hose which is a good thing.I like that the whole tool is just the right size to fit into most places.

This is one of those tools, that is inexpensive, and so simple to use, that anyone who deals with hoses on barbed fittings should have one.  There's not much to it, just a handle, attatched to a steel hook.  The hook is sharp enough, to wiggle between the hose and the fitting, and break it loose, if it gets 'glued' to the fitting, and the bigger the hose, the better it works, it seems to be made for radiatior hoses, although so far, it has worked on any hose I have tried it on.One word of caution, the end is sharp, which it has to be, in order to get under a hose tight on a fitting, so pay attention to the angle of the hook as you are using it, so it does not pierce the hose if you intend to reuse it.  With any amount of caution, this shouldn't be a problem, but it does bear mentioning.  I might also add, the 'twist' of the hook, is suited for right handed people, if you have a hose you can only reach with your left hand, or if you were born left handed, it will require more caution to use.  I have found it will still work, but you need extra care to be sure the point stays between the hose and fitting.It seems to be built fairly sturdy, so far so good, the hook seems to be made of good quality steel.  About the only potential problem might be the hook pulling out of the handle, but so far, it has stayed tight.  Time will tell, if it ever works loose.  After using it to remove the radiator hoses on my truck, my first thought was 'why didn't I think of that'.  Instead of wrestling with the hoses, they popped right off.-edit-After using this tool more and more, I raised the rating to 5-star.  I was uncertain how strong this tool would be, or how it would hold up to hard use.  I was working on an agricultural sprayer, which has 2 inch hoses rated for 150 PSI, which makes a radiator hose seem flimsy.  Anyway, the hoses were rusted onto steel hose barbs, and without this tool I am positive I would have just cut the hose off just past the end of the hose barb, and removed the little piece off the barb any way I could, leaving me with a hose a couple inches too short.  With care not to poke the hose, I worked the hook between the hose and barb, squirted soapy water in between (WD-40 works well for that, also), moved a quarter turn from where I started, and did it again.  By the time I worked my way around the hose, it broke loose, and came right off.  I pulled about as hard as I could, didn't bend the hook part, and it stayed securely in the handle.  I have now sworn off my 'old' method of hose removal, which was using a small screwdriver to pry the hose loose, and can say that the more I use this tool, the more I figure out the exact angle to hold it, and the better it works.The handle can get a little slick if you get oil or anti-freeze on it, but cleans up much easier than if it were rubbery or deeply textured.  Fortunately, it is shaped so it doesn't slip easily.
I purchased this to fill up my tool chest.  I haven't used it yet but I plan on using it to replace some hoses on my boat and truck this year.

The rack wasn't anything I intended to use, though it seems sturdy enough; I'm cutting-to-fit a steel plate to place under the top so that I can mount a 38" dual-band amateur radio antenna, the steel should both reinforce the top and make the antenna work better, too. The radio box is being mounted inside on another steel plate fitted to the floor of the box, it's quick release so I can take it inside with me when I stop for the night. About the only other thing I intend to store in it is my Aerostitch rainsuit, so there should be more than adequate room for circulating air to cool the radio transmitter. reviewText: Being a wrench-head for over 45 years, I keep a few cars around to use at the appropriate seasons. I try and keep them charged up to avoid the costly $100 batteries. My brand new truck today sits with a built-in little B&D; BM3B colorful charger to avoid drainage. When you connect these chargers, do not expect them to charge your battery from Zero volts. Best performance is when a battery has medium charge in it so the 1-2 Amp current can be fed slowly. You will see the orange light for a day or two then here comes the green light which is great news.When you store an older car (60's-70's) for a long time, disconnect the battery (-ve and +ve_) both and hook up to charger, in newer cars (80's plus) you will lose the settings and the memory so it is best to connect the charger +ve lead to the battery and the -ve lead to a good ground like the alternator frame.This is a wonderful device and I have 3 of them running on my project cars and will get one for the yard tractor soon.

Had bad experienced with NOCO always stuck on Standby, try out B&D; and received 2 dead ones when plugged in power, no LED lit.  Returned to Amazon, got 2 new ones.  Let see how their quality control this time.Update: Got 2 new ones works fine, somewhat my fault and somewhat B&D; poor design.  LED will not turn on UNLESS battery cable is connected to car battery then connect to charger with power AC plugged in wall socket to complete the loop.  If only AC power plugged into wall socket, LED is OFF which is poor design that made me think device is defective.  It should have power/ready LED but this device only have CHARGING (Green) or FAULT (Red) LED.  The first 2 charger I returned probably works fine but I'm used to plug in a device in AC wall socket, LED power/standby should turned on first.  I got no LED light so thought it malfunction.So before you claim the product is defect due to NO LED LIGHT lit when plugged into wall AC, make sure connect the other end to your battery terminal to make complete loop in order for GREEN LED to flash (charging.) This is not a good friendly design but it works and fairly priced.

reviewText: This is great for keep batteries up to mark when is storage. The product is light but I would not say it feels that it can be easily broken. I believe it is how you handle your stuff. Used this on one battery so far with good results. Just follow the directions very closely to avoid potential issues.

The "Black & Decker" unit does a good job. There's some kind of circuit in there that can detect when you've got it connected wrong, when a correct charge is underway, and when the charge is complete. When status is "complete," the unit is not delivering current to the battery (I checked with an ammeter in series with a clip lead)This unit further can detect when it has become time to top off the charge, automatically switching back on again to restore a full charge.I use it on a trailer boat parked in the garage.  The outdrive has an electric circuit to prevent corrosion in salt water, and it will drain the battery in about a month unless I disconnect the battery or use this maintainer.  It works well.I've watched how the LED will turn solid green indicating a full charge, and, after a period of time, go back to flashing green to restore a charge as described above.The connection safeguard is pretty cool -- brushing the adapter across the carpet in the boat when it's slightly moist triggers the LEDs to indicate a bad connection. That's sensitive.I like that they include three ways of feeding the battery. Each method connects to the output cable of the charger.In particular, the 12V power connector (cigarette lighter plug) is an excellent way to backfeed a charge to the battery. For the boat, I don't have to lift the engine bay lid, un-do the plastic retention strap and plastic lid to the battery box to get to the terminals. For a car or truck, it saves having to put the clips on the battery terminals and perhaps leaving the hood slightly open.Just remember to make sure your accessory jack is always on, and not disconnected when you turn off the key to the vehicle.In the Olde Days the auto supply houses like Pep Boys sold little boxes called trickle chargers. They had a transformer and a set of diodes to take household current and convert it a voltage just a little bit higher than a fully charged battery.  This was a good match, because leaving it connected for a reasonable amount of time would typically not boil the battery and ruin it like a charger with higher current capacity would do. You also would check the level of battery acid every so often, and top it off with distilled water to compensate if the charger did cook off some electrolyte.With Digital Technology (insist on including the hype word in there, regardless of whether there's any digital circuit involved) the contemporary "charger/maintainer" can deliver more current than the old trickle type, but also can sense, electronically, when enough is enough and shut down. This means you can leave it on there for prolonged periods of time and not risk burning out a "maintenance free" battery whose cells are not easily checked for level anymore.

reviewText: Now the clunk is less audible, and sometimes not even happening.

Well. Just got my relay kit today and was looking at it and how it would fit the 2008 Saturn Vue. Its a good idea to use a relay kit to power up your HID's but it would be nice is the wires were long enough to reach the battery. This is a very easy plug and play setup, but no play if I cant wire it to the battery. Im going to have to splice more wire between the fuse and relay to make the wire long enough to reach the battery on the Saturn Vue. Not so much of a big deal, but the more cuts in a wire the higher the residence (ohms) you make. Working with high power car audio, you never make any unneeded cuts in your wiring. Voltage has to stop at each cut before it reaches the end and that's something good installers don't want. Like I said good relay kit, made very well just the wires could be longer. Even the wires to the HID's could be longer. Or GM before placing the battery should of thought ahead for something like this. I bought a set of HID's for a 1996 Mercury Grand Marquis and ordered the relay kit for that too. Big car, wonder how short the wires on the relay kit will be for that?3/24/14 Installed the relay kit. I had to add 5 inches to the main fused power wire, was a little short. All in all everything is working good and I put the fuse back in for my day time running lights and they even work good now. No more one light off and the other on. But I pulled the fuse out anyways. The HID's are on a timer with life. So having them on all the time lessens the life of the bulb.

This harness is of pretty good quality components and appears to be well constructed.  I was concerned that it might be too short after having read some of the other reviews, but I installed this to 2011 RAM and was able to route the wire to the remote ballast by running it in front of the radiator which gave me a straight shot to the ballast and actually had a few inches to spare.  I have monitored the temperature of the wiring and relay and have not witnessed any unusual heat buildup. However, if you plan on installing this, or any relay harness to a vehicle with a CANBUS electrical system, you will need to add a capacitor/diode setup to stop the relay from hyper triggering or "buzzing" under the hood when the vehicle is running.  Although the HID ballasts will fire the bulbs, this is caused by the CANBUS system sending very fast, pulsed current to the relay causing it to engage and disengage very quickly.  Without this modification, I doubt the relay would last very long and would probably fail prematurely due to excessive coil or contact wear.
summary: Well constructed and stays cool in operation.

reviewText: On my Jeep Wrangler I had several places that are plastic and seems like they always get scuffed. I have used several other products before using Meguiars and found  not one  be very effective. My problems is that it always seems to be temporary, since  after a few weeks I will notice the touch up begins to wear and the old scuff places reappear. I am so pleased with this product. I could write a book on its merits. try it you will be impressed. and it cost so little to.

I used this on my 1998 BMW F650. It had some fading on all the black plastics after 16 years, this made it look like it was fresh out of the factory. I am so impressed with this product, I will be using it on all my vehicles now. My favorite part is that this is a conditioner, not a dye, so no mess at all. It also does not stay slick (which would be very bad on a motorcycle).By the way, it works on other colors than black, really any porous unpainted plastic bits (like the trim/ body panels on all new vehicles) of any color will look rich after a quick dab with this stuff.

As a car owner who has to park his car outside every day, I know how plastics tend to fade over time in the sun. It's an inevitability, and do I wish that the factory just painted all the parts of the car instead of having plastics showing. However, there is a fix to fading black trim. This product, dubbed the Ultimate black restorer, does its job well.This will restore black trim back to black, and I couldn't be happier. Its nice making a car that is 17 years old look next to new again with this, along with a good wax (Meguiar's Ultimate Liquid Wax). The bottle is rather large and will last for quite a while even if you are generous with applications. Try to keep this off the paint or wipe it up right away though.

This is a product that has overstated its abilities.  This product will be more useful for protecting vinyl from fading than it is for restoring badly faded vinyl.  If the vinyl is really faded, it will probably be necessary to use a dye and probably 2-3 applications of that to get a uniform appearance on the surface.  Two examples: http://www.amazon.com/Forever-Car-Care-Products-FB813/dp/B001879CUS/ref=sr_1_10?ie=UTF8&qid;=1404566736&sr;=8-10&keywords;=vinyl+dye and http://www.amazon.com/Solution-Finish-Black-Plastic-Restorer/dp/B006NZRAFE/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid;=1404567046&sr;=8-1&keywords;=solution+finishAs for the running when it gets wet, this may be a function of using it too thickly and not buffing the surface to remove excess product.  This is just a WAG because I have not exposed the test surface to water yet.Faded exterior vinyl is one of the hardest problems to solve and it is 10X better never to let the vinyl fade in the first place.  The Meguiar's product should prevent this problem but it has a limited ability to restore vinyl.
summary: Useful but Meguair's overrates its capabilities.

I bought this for my Mazda CX-5 and it fits well. I like that I can flip the sides up and have small walls or lips to the mat. The mat is a bit thin but will protect my car well and I don't imagine it breaking or tearing.

I put this into my DC2 Integra.  I was able to cut this with a sharp utility knife.  It works well to protect items and it's a very hard rubber or plastic type of material.  Don't expect this to absorb much impact.  It's on the slippery side which is good for me so i can move htings around easily in the trunk.

reviewText: Ok this cargo mat  is great for protecting your trunk. I brought it for my Prius and I did not even end up cutting it... I just folded it up so it could also protect the back of the backseats. Overall it is nice... it has some dimples at the bottom that stop it from moving around and it also has a nice rough surface at the top so your items do not move around much in the trunk. Anyway very good buy but it really stinks... so you need to buy some Febreeze or whatever to make it smell better before you put it in your car...

I bought this because i am tired of my carpet in my trunk shifting around. I laid it out, put weight on it to flatten it out a while,then laid my carpet on top and trimmed with shears.  Installed perfect fit perfect. Easy as that! Anybody can install this if they have a pair of shears and an example piece that they can go by. Literally from flatten to installation was 5 minutes. I say flatten because it comes as a roll and will not lay flay right when unraveled. Put weight on it a while and its fine. Fits good amd was exactly what i was looking for.

Be sparing in the amount of colored repair paste you use. The clear filler shrinks upon drying, but the heat-activated colored paste seems to form a raised blob on the surface of the repair if too much is used. Better to repeat the application than end up with a raised blob. Also -- a small electric craft iron is a much better heat source than the supplied heat-transfer iron.
better understand now what you can do (repair) and what not... if you are trying to mend a tear or rip just simply forget it...

We must be realistic with these kits:  once the leatherette or vinyl is ripped or torn it well never look perfect and new again.There has been damage, and anything you use will build it up a bit and be impossible to look like new.Even so, if you do get a rip, this material will allow you to seal it up, close up the hole, and prevent it from getting snagged and made worse.The price is rasonable and the glue/adhesive is of course, being 3M, of excellent quality and suer does weork well.mixing for color is not too hard, and merely requires patience to persevere to get the color as close as possible to do.I used it on my boat and thought it was very much better than nothing, and better than a lot of money to have sections replaced.
summary: The is a very good kit for little money.

reviewText: I had a whole in the seat upholstery in my Jeep. The surface was cracked all around the hole, so it was sort of a spiderweb. I used the adhesive that comes with the kit to fill the hole and cracks, and it seems to work okay. It is white, but dries clear. Then you do the hard part. You get a number of small containers of the surface material (sort of like thick paint) which you have to combine and mix to get the right color.  That is harder than it seems.  If you have black upholstery you are in luck. In other cases you are going to be mixing.  You use a small tool that comes with the kit to mix and spread the surface material over the repaired area, matching the color (hopefully) and filling in any remaining imperfections. You then have to cover the repaired area with the 'paper' material in the kit, so the finish will match the grain. Then you have to apply heat to the surface (covered with the paper) to cure the surface material. You get a 'tool' to do this - a piece of wooden dowel rod with a dime size metal disk on the end.  You are told to heat it on an iron, and rub the paper.  I did this a few times, but it was taking forever for the heat to dry and cure the glue. Then I pulled out the old reliable travel iron (which we don't use), and heated it to the cotton level, and use the tip of the iron to rub the paper.  That worked much better that the little tool. The end result is a patch.  You can see it - probably because of the slight difference in color.  The patch is flexible which is perfect for a seat area. Best of all, the spiderweb is not expanding. So, all in all, it did what I wanted it to. If you can do a better match on the color you will be more satisfied. Do not expect that the gash on your dashboard will be filled and invisible - it will be better, maybe much better, but not perfect.
Put a small hole in my leather motorcycle seat and this product fixed it in just a few minutes.  Worked exactly as they advertised it and I appreciated being able to fix the hole.
really great suction or pump!!!  Just what I needed for my garage or tool.  It comes in handy!! great price too
The pump has worked perfectly to fill a couple of rear differentials.  Probably be in the garage using it again this weekend.

This pump works just fine, fluid doesn't leak out of the plunger mechanism. It is meant for a gallon bottle and screws right to the top but I used it for smaller bottles as well - just had to trim the opening a little. Cheap! And very handy to have around the shop

I bought this to change the VTM fluid on my Honda Pilot.  It worked like a charm.  The end of the hose has a barb fitting that locks into the fill hole at the top of the differential.  This is a great design feature for my use because the fill hole on the Pilot is recessed, making it difficult to hold a hose in place.  I was able to pump 3 quarts of VTM-4 fluid in about 20 pumps with no leaks or spills.  Great item for the price.

I did not know how big the tubes were untill I got it out of the box. I was thinking of using this to suck out fluids from my car like steering fluid and brake fluid but the tube was too big for it to fit in the over flow. I was able to Jimmy-Rig it to work. It takes a few pumps for it to start working but does a good job keeping it from going back in where it came from. I did have to flip it up-side-down in order for the remaining fluid to get pumped all the way through it. I was not sure how to clean it out so I pumped some degreaser through it to hopefully get some of the oil out. Feels fairly strong for the price.Don't let the picture fool you it is fairly big

I purchasedLucas 10013 Fuel Treatment - 1 Gallonand a few smaller bottles of fuel treatmentLucas 10020 Fuel Treatment - 5.25 oz.along with this pump. So now I save money by buying in bulk and have the small bottles to refill to make it easy to leave in the car and put in my gas tank. True to form this thing pumps about 1oz a pump so 5 pumps and my bottles are full. The pump head has a place to hang the filler tube to prevent leaking.
