reviewText: This works great. Screws on to the top of a one gal jug to pump fluids. Worked perfect to change the rear diff fluid on my Honda pilot. No need to try to pour and spill everywhere.
Used this to pump out power steering fluid.  Nice job pumping and will probably use it for other fluids.  I am batman.
I looked at all pumps and decided to try this one and I def made the right choice. This thing works great and it has quality parts on it.. DEF recommend it

I was tired of dealing with the typical low-powered, very slow 12-volt pumps that are commonly available, so I did a search for a higher-quality unit that led to this 88P model. So far I am not disappointed. It appears to be very quality-built, it runs quietly and it fills tires much quicker than the typical 12-volt pumps. Plus, this unit is rated to pump up to 120 psi. Be aware that this one is designed to clip to the battery terminals, not plug into a 12-volt car outlet. That is not a fault; it clips to the battery so that there is enough current for it. A typical 12-volt outlet would likely not have enough circuit capacity to run it, and would blow fuses. This unit has its own in-line fuse.  The instructions suggest that the vehicle engine be running when using the pump so you don't drain the vehicle battery, but I do use it for short periods of time without the engine running.  I have had it only a few days, so I will post an update if something goes wrong. But at this point I am extremely happy with the pump and believe it will prove to be very useful and durable, and it appears to be well worth the extra money beyond the typical cheaper units.

Long cord and air hose, chuck is good quality. First impression is that the unit is much quieter than I expected. More of a low drone than a loud clatter. Definitely worth keeping around for emergency use.

I purchased this compressor to replace a cheap compressor I purchased at the auto parts store. There is no comparison. This compressor inflates my tire as quickly as a gas station compressor and I don't need quarters! Having to attach it to the car's battery is a bit of a pain, but that is the price you pay for performance. This thing inflates so fast, despite having to connect to the battery, you still save time compared to the cheaper units that plug into the lighter socket. A must have. I try to check my tire pressure with every 10 degree temperature change. You should too. One more thing, the air pressure gauge is extremely accurate.
summary: Just as fast as a gas station air pump.

reviewText: This is the most impressive low-cost compressor I've ever seen.  I use it to air up my Jeep's 35x12.50-15 tires after going offroad.  It brings them up from 11 psi to 30 in about 20 minutes for all four of them.  Other offroaders are surprised at how well it works for this price, and a few have bought them also.Note that it gets very hot while doing this much work.  I splash a little bottled water over the compressor head every few minutes to cool it.

I needed a pump for large truck tires. Most of the others arent up to the task and overheat before filling up a single tire. While this wont go as long as Viair's top of the line, it doesnt cost two hundred plus dollars either.I have ran it non stop for five minutes. It gets hot but does not quit. The cable is nice and long. Does not come with a bag so I went to home depot and got a small husky soft side tool bag that works great.Guage is accurate on mine as I tested with two seperate tire gauges.Good value, good product.

I needed a portable compressor that could inflate my 33" tall tires on my truck. Well, the 88P will do just that is about 5 minutes, with the truck running (pulls a large draw of power). Just clip the alligator clips on the positive and negative, twist on the brass inflator chuck on the valve stem,  turn the compressor on, and off it goes! I combined this purchase with the Black Mechanics 9191 Tool Bag (11x7x6) because Viair doesn't include a carry bag (you just get the cardboard package to store it back into). Cardboard will NOT last, but a canvas bag will! I really like this compressor, get one for yourself...

I have used this to air up completely flat REAR FULL SIZED TRACTOR TIRES. It's the real deal. It would have been nice to get a carry bag with it, it's too nice a tool to have just rolling around in the trunk with no protection. If all you're trying to do is air up tires, toys or the like, this will do fine, no matter how big the tires are.
summary: As Premium as a Portable Air Compressor Can Be

reviewText: Although this is not a cheap compressor it should last. It inflated a couple of tires fairly quickly and seems to be well built.

We shopped around for an air compressor to place in our old pickup truck.  The Vlair seemed to best suit our needs in a price range that we could afford.  The truck is used strictly for utilitarian purposes and does not have the best tires.  So, the pump gets used often to reinflate them.  It has never failed to fill our needs and fills the tires rapidly and accurately.
summary: The Vlair seemed to best suit our needs in a price range that we ...

reviewText: To start with, you can't do much better than the fine review J. Schaeffer put up on this and comparable units. His info made this purchase a slam dunk for me. Long story short, I don't think there's a better value in inflators.Here's a few pros and cons than may not have come up elsewhere+ Solid and well made. The unit is heavy and everything on it is substantial, including the little storage ports for the inflation accessories.+ Easy use. Connect it, run it until you're ready to check pressure, switch it off to see if tire is fully inflated.+ Fills quickly. I'm ready the leave at the same time as the kids with on-board compressors.+ Long cord and hose - keep in mind I have a 2 door Wrangler; your longbed crewcab may be another story.+ Compact. Fits great in the storage well of my Jeep JK's back seat area, along with a tow strap and receiver hook.+ Threaded valve - positive connection that doesn't pop off like garage style clipsCons- Gauge seems vary  3-4 #- Gets hot. Of course the body of the pump gets hot, but even the hose near the unit gets uncomfortably hot. You'll find out when your fills are done and you go to coil it up. Gloves are a nice idea.One thing I might note: I let the Jeep idle while I fill and the unit sounds like it's cycling up or down, but I've concluded this is due to additional loads on the battery switching on and off while your vehicle runs. It's particularly noticeable if your air conditioning is on while you fill.I've used this unit 4 times since I got it, and have been impressed every time. This is a first-line purchase for any off-roader, and a great piece of kit for any light portable inflation needs. This is the one to get!

This is by far the best portable air compressor I have ever owned. It is very capable and fast. A light truck tire can be completely inflated (to 35 PSI) in less than 5 minutes. it is well made with cast aluminum instead of plastic like so many of the others. And the price is not so much where it is unaffordable. I like the schrader valve fitting at the end of the generously long hose. I made an adapter from a 1/4" NPT schrader valve to a clamp on tire valve so I can inflate my tires without unthreading the coupling and loosing air in the process.
summary: If you want a quality portable air compressor this is the one!!

reviewText: Tried this out today and was pleased. I did an oil change on my GF's BMW 325ci and checked the tire pressures. The rear tires were both about 4lbs light so I hooked this up and it took about 5 seconds to fill each tire up to the required pressure.  It is not to noisy and appears well built.I also bought the Rothco mechanics bag that is suggested with this and it fits perfectly, although a little tight when combined with the 6ft hose extension, tire repair tools & supplies.4 stars because it does not come with its own bag and for terminal clamps that could be a little larger, but other than that a really nice unit for backups/emergencies.

It did a great job of inflating tires. The gauge is accurate and the screw-on adaptor works very well. However, the clamp jaws are too small to clamp on the battery posts. I ended up have to use a jumper cable on the battery end and then clamp it on the other end of the cable to get a decent connection.

Bought this to air up my tires on my Jeep XJ when offroading.  I have used the unit several times and it has worked as advertised.  Great unit for the price.  I read where some have complained of the small clips for the battery and I do agree with them.  If you don't have a "military post" battery terminal, it may be difficult for you to attach to the battery terminal.  Since I have that kind of terminal, connection is easy.  Your milage may vary there, depending.The unit is quieter than I had expected it to be and is a workhorse.  I have used it on other tires (lawn mower, motorcycle, etc.) and it fills them up quickly.  The time for my 31" tires is quicker than I expected as well.  No regrets on purchasing the item.  This particular model did not come with a bag, but it is small and will fit in any small zipper bag.

Pretty powerful little guy.  Great for emergencies.  I was able to top off my 33 inch offroad tires with. No issues. I wish the cables were a little longer.  That would have pushed it to five stars.  Hard to reach the back opposite side on my full size truck.  Cars should be fine.

I bought this pump to replace a portable air compressor that I used for years on my Jeep and bought it based on previous reviews. After several uses, I will say this is a perfect compressor and much lighter, functional, and quieter than my previous pump of the same price. I will buy this again if needed. Great purchase.
This compressor is the real deal, not to be confused with plasticy imitation-tough compressors.  It pumps passenger tires very quickly.

I've burned out the cheaper inflators I have purchased at big box stores. And, they simply take forever. This unit is awesome--I use an old ATV battery to make it portable. The long air line is high quality and this machine is a beast. My high-pressure truck tires no longer take forever to fill. I'll watch the duty cycle carefully to make it last as long as possible. If there is some unforeseen issue with longevity, I will edit my post. Very happy with the product.

Love this Compressor! Should make a bag for it..stores in box..alittle cheesy..come on VIAIR.. airs up my 31" off road tires, effortlessly..also bought an ARB tire deflator & works well with that item..

I got this to maintain tires for our 3 family cars and to occasionally help some of my friends to do the same. I've used this for a few weeks and I'm already impressed by it - the physical build quality is great, no loose or rattling parts, the compressor is not overly loud and doesn't "jump" all around the pavement during the work. The hose and the screw-on chuck are also pretty sturdy and feel like they would last a very long time. The built-in pressure gauge is fairly accurate (just make sure to turn compressor off before looking at the gauge) but you should still get a separate dedicated tire pressure gauge (preferably not some cheap plastic crap with digital display). The only minor drawback is the lack of the storage bag but it's not an issue if you primarily store it at home and you can find plenty of aftermarket bags which can easily fit this in. Overall it's a great product and much, much better than various similar products by more "recognizable" brand names.One minor warning, though - make sure to measure the distance between your car's battery terminals and the rear tires on your vehicle BEFORE purchasing this model. The attached power cable and the hose are long enough for most cars and compact SUVs but you might need to order power cable extension or purchase a different model (Viair sells plenty of these) with longer cable/hose if you have a pickup truck with a long bed length or a large SUV.

Considering this is one of the more expensive models, it should come with that, which is way better than just storing the product box in your vehicle.I opted to purchase this bag to put the compressor in and it fits well, but I hate that I had to spend more money on something that should be included:G.I. It would take longer and not be as enjoyable to use however would have saved me some hard-earned money.Another negative is that the battery jumpers on this are really small; they don't even fit over my entire battery terminals. The tiny clamps should be much bigger.If you use a Viair model that has a lighter plug on it in conjunction with this adapterRoadpro 12V Battery Clip-On and Cigarette Lighter Adapter, you will find that the battery jumpers are bigger and can clamp on to the battery much better.

reviewText: After considering and rejecting many of its competitors, I chose this unit. It is fast and just plain works great! Be glad that is uses battery clips instead of a cigarette lighter power source -  you need the extra amps this option provides.I do wish it had a quick disconnect end so that other devices could be easily attached, but they can be easily spliced on if that is important to you.

The good is that it is well made and has sturdy construction and should last for years. The hose it comes with attaches to the tire valve by threading onto it which is great and works much better than the ones you need to keep pressed against the valve stem. In part this feature is also a necessary one as the hose needs to be threaded and left attached to the tire while you turn on the compressor.The one aspect of the design that I do not like is that it clips onto the battery posts instead of having a plug for a cigarette lighter socket. My battery for my truck is on the left front side and with my SUV on the right front corner of the engine compartment. the Battery cables to power the compressor are long enough to have the compressor sitting on the ground while it is operating but the air hose has to be able to reach all four tires. You really need to buy at least one of the Viair 6 foot extension hoses with the threaded fittings at both ends (male and female).I was barely able to reach the right rear tire of my short bed extended cab truck using the 88P's hose and the 6' extension hose. Not a concern with small sedans but if I had a long bed truck with a crew cab or an RV I would need two or more of the 6' extension hoses to reach all the tires.There is a pressure gauge but it is not accurate. This is to be expected as the air coming out of the compressor is very hot and so the reading cannot be accurate. I used the TPMS to know the actual amount of air in the tires as the compressor ran and then double checked with a hand air pressure gauge that I know is accurate (most are not). I put in 2-4 lbs. more than the spec for the tires and let them cool down for several hours and then rechecked and adjusted the pressure in each tire.I was adding air to truck tires that needed 80 PSI and this 100 PSI rated compressor did very well in adding 8-10 lbs. of air per tire. I had to let out a lot of air to reset the TPMS sensors on my truck after a tire dealer rotated the tires and failed to do the reset. They have never done the reset unless I catch them and then have them do it before I leave. For someone with load range G/H tires that need 100 or greater PSI I would go to the next compressor in the Viair line that is rated for 150 PSI.The compressor power cables include a fuse and holder which is a nice touch and protects the electrics and with a compressor is better than a thermal fuse that would be tripping all the time. The compressor package includes an adapter for sports equipment.I need to get a case for it as it ships with a box that is not going to hold together in the truck and it is too small to hold the needed 6 foot extension hose. This is not a negative comment only something to consider if you plan to leave this in your car or truck.
summary: Great compressor if you work within its limitations

reviewText: I've tried with my Toyota Hilux 013 double cab, and it's perfect to carry,it can be use to inflate several devices or vehicles, i've use with one Yamaha Serow tyres and it pump it up in few seconds, the one thing that other people and myself considers noot good is about there aren't carry bag and no information.Well about all, buy it, it's very powerfull, stable , strong , you'll have a little monster with high perfomance.

reviewText: Just what I need for my pickup.  Ties anything down securely and worry free.  No tangle when stored as its retractable.  Go for the wider belt (2"), dont go for the narrow 1" as it will twist and tangle up when you are retracting.  Also the 2" belts has better coverage and distribution of the pressure so it does not cut into things (boxes).
I purchased 8 of these straps ( 4 packs)....out of the 8, 2 didn't retract to the closed position. But they were fairly easy to work once you got the hang of them.
These are very nice, I use them to hold a jeep wrangler on a trailer and they work perfect for this.

It's worth understanding that unlike typical ratcheting straps, the handle has two "rest" positions.  One of the jobs of the red tab is to jump the handle from one position to the other.  In one position, the device works like a seat belt retractor, with the strap able to pay out or self-retract, just like seatbelts in a car.In the other position, the handle works like a typical ratcheting strap system.  HOWEVER, even in this position, realize that these straps are made of seatbelt material, which is kind of slick, so the wound up material will slip over itself on the spool quite a bit before you get maximum belt tension.When you ratchet the belt down, keep tightening until all this "slip" or "slack" is pulled out.  Then tighten it some more for good measure!  And most importantly, when you're done tensioning, DO NOT return the handle to the "seat belt retractor mode" position, or you can lose tension all together.  With normal ratchets, you're probably used to returning the handle all the way back down flat prior to hauling.  On this product, that's bad, because putting the handle all the way down flat is the "retractor mode" position!  You'll need to leave the handle slightly up for "locking-ratcheting mode".  It will look funny, but it is the position it needs to be in.I can see a situation, in some applications, where the hustle and bustle of freight handling can cause the lever to be unintentionally whacked down flat into the "retractor mode" position, which may cause the belt to go slack.  That is a risk.  For my application, these are wonderful, and greatly simplify tidying up your straps.
summary: A Small Learning Curve, But Great Once You Figure Them Out

reviewText: these straps are game changers.  i will never go back to the old style straps for anything but general utility.  these take 1/4 of the time the old straps do.  the only thing is the price.  they still wear out like other straps..  if the webbing is against something, it will still wear through, just like any other strap.  but if you make the mistake on these, you are throwing 20 bucks out of the window.  i only use these for tying down atv's or anything else where i can be completely certain that the only part of the strap touching anything but air is the hooks.

I spent about 1.5 hours applying it to my '02 Explorer's gray trim.  It looks great now.  I started out applying too little product because I was afraid the small bottle would run out before I finished the vehicle.  Once I started using an ample amount, the process worked much better.  My explorer has a lot of trim and even after I was done, there was still a little bit left in the bottle. ReNu Finish is the only one that works for any length of time.  I've use 4 or 5 others that keep the fenders black on my 2010 Jeep for one or two wash's or rain storms and then do it again. I lived in CO. this summer, where it rained every two days and had to recoat fenders only every two months with ReNu. With normal weather, which I'm getting now, ReNu would probably last at least 5 or 6 months. It takes a little work getting it on but its worth it. Make sure to wipe it dry when done. I'll update this when I give more time.

reviewText: Rotella is a fantastic oil and T6 is the icing on the cake!I have been in construction for over 40 years and I can tell ya that the preferred brand for our heavy equipment (dozers, loaders, excavators and such) has always been Rotella.  And now with T6 you just get more of a great thing.  Tried and true and may they never stop making great diesel engine oil.I get mine at Walmart for 21something a gallon.  Not 100% sure, but swear I get an extra 1mpg in my Duramax now that I switched over to the T6 from the regular Rotella T.  Best part is my cost only went up by about $8 a gallon - or $20 an oil change.  Knowing that most engine wear happens at start-up and that synthetic holds the edge with cold circulation abilities, I love being able to switch over to synthetic for so little money.*******************************************************************************************************************************************************Edit:  Wanted to add that I spoke with Shell Tech Support to confirm that T6 is fine to use in all ambient temps.  As some may have noticed, it is a 5W-40 and if it were a conventional oil you most likely would not want to use it in a hot climate like Vegas.  But being full SYNTHETIC, there is no issue whatsoever - IT IS GOOD FOR ALL CLIMATES.  Oh and he was able to confirm too that I can absolutely use it in my Honda Goldwing as well.  However, NOT in any engines that call for 0W-20.  Just an fyi for yas, the 0W-20 requirement of some engines is not to be played with as there are tight ports that could otherwise easily be clogged by any higher weight oils.  Deviate from that at your own risk.And finally, with the $5 rebate they keep running, my Duramax oil changes are now only about $8 more using Synthetic T6 over Regular Rotella Triple T.  And I "can" extend those oil change intervals if I wish.  Awesome!  Love this stuff.  Oh, and they claim a 4 year shelf life, but that has more to do with liability over future oil advancements than it does with oil "spoiling".  Mobil 1 claims 5 years.  Keep the lid closed tightly and store your oil between 32-100F and use it within 5 years and all should be good.One last note about SYNTHETIC OIL so as to be clear that I do not make a blanket statement that it should be used by all.  There are certain benefits that synthetic brings with it's higher price and if you feel these are something that you want then use it.  They are:* Better cold starts when MOST engine wear occurs.* Excellent cold weather pour-ability and lubricity.* Slightly better mileage.* Longer engine life (mainly because of the better cold starts), however, maybe ask yourself when's the last time you ran an engine to death.* You "can" go with longer engine oil change intervals simply because synthetic tends to take longer to break down than conventional.  This can offset the extra cost of synthetic; doing less oil changes.

I run 10 quarts of this in my Duramax, having replaced conventional oil. When I was searching for synthetics the price of most was prohibitive. Rotella, as they do with their standard oils, is a real value. Of course, oil ratings are subjective unless you do an analysis. So far the oil feels good off of the stick (you can't rate color on a diesel--they look black almost right away). I'll update this at 10,000 miles
summary: Great oil at a competitive price

reviewText: I like the Battery Minder line of products.  Whether you believe in the ability of desulfation to revive a battery, or just want to hang on to the concept that a charged battery wont sulfate enough to matter, this charger does what it does well.  It is only a 2A charger, and only charges with a temperature-compensated charge voltage and float voltage optimized for flooded lead-acid batteries.  There is a version for AGM if so inclined, that just has a slightly different charge voltage.  What I like about this charger is that it provides an indication of where it is in the charge process, and also if it is compensating up or down based upon temperature.  The charger always flashes the desulfation light, so it is claiming that it is always doing that, regardless of what charge stage the battery is in.The charger has a "load" light, which would indicate to you if you have a short in your car (or I suppose internal to the battery), so you can be forewarned.  I have not had to use that indicator, and hopefully it will not light up...The other interesting feature of this charger is that it provides a "rest" period on the battery every so often to see if it behaves abnormally.  If there is a short or the battery is starting to go bad, this test stage may be an indicator before you get a hard failure of the battery.For the most part, Id compare this unit to the far cheaper ($50ish) Battery Tender, made by a competing company.  I have both.  I like both.  I prefer the increased indication that is provided by the status lights on this one, and also like the fact that this one uses a multi-frequency desulfation process, which though I have not had to prove to work or not work, does in theory help reduce the formation and presence of sulfate crystals.  This unit can also run its temperature compensation to a remote location, which is good if the vehicle you are maintaining is outside of a garage.I do wish this product were around $30 cheaper to be competitive with the  battery tender which is also temperature-compensated.  This one is differentiated by its desulfation capability, but the much higher price causes it to be docked one star.
summary: Charger with a bit more information available

reviewText: I studied the specifications of many battery chargers and reviewed their customer feedback on amazon.com before I chose the BatteryMINDer 2012 charger.Positives :- Temperature compensated charging to prevent over- and undercharging by using a temperature sensor- Shows actual state of charging (soft start, constant current, constant voltage, float)- High frequency charging pulses (instead of regular current charging) to reduce battery sulphation- Can be connected to any AC power source between 110 and 240 V- Long charging cables to locate battery charger away from batteryThe BatteryMINDer 2012 has lights to indicate a weak battery or bad cell which are activated depending on the battery voltage at the end of a 10 min. battery test (battery at rest). This battery test is first done at the completion of the constant voltage charging stage, and then every 12 hours while in float stage.My experience is that this battery test will NOT detect a battery that has been charged and passed the battery test, but then fails to start the engine the next time, i.e. that fails to hold charge. I am guessing that a longer battery test(at least one hour) might catch batteries that charge up okay, but fail to hold charge. Other battery smart chargers (e.g. CTEK) also have very short test periods, so will probably not catch such batteries either.The other minor disadvantage is that the BatteryMINDer 2012 has a maximum current of only 2 amps, so charging a battery  that is significantly discharged will take some time.
summary: Excellent Battery Charger with Temperature Compensation

reviewText: This is the third BatteryMINDer I have purchased.  The first was the aviation version to keep my aircraft battery peaked due to less frequent flying.  The second has been used in a more utility capacity to service batteries for boats, jet ski's, garden tractors, and auto's.  It has performed well by recovering and maintaining batteries that would otherwise be lost or difficult to revive.  This latest version does not seem to have the size and heft of the previous chargers, but when I used it the result was the same.  I charged a battery in one of my cars that has been sitting for two to three months with no use.  It took 24 to 48 hours before it brought it up to normal levels, and I left it attached for several days.  I have to believe it conditioned the battery back to a very serviceable level.  It is not a fast recovery charger, but if the advertised capabilities of the charger are accurate it will lengthen the life of my batteries.

5-SMD white LEDs for 194/168 bulbsThese work just like any other 5-SMD (5-chip) LEDs designed for 12V applications. The 10-pack was a great price. The major caveat is that you need to be sure your housing has enough room for this LED because it is about 1/8" longer than an actual 194 or 168 bulb.Some people notice that the LED stays dimly lit when the car is off (or the lamp is turned off). This is largely dependent on the electrical system of your car. My late model Ford does this, but my older Ford and later model Chevrolet do not exhibit this condition. And even when it is dimly lit, it is drawing microamps of current and is not a whole lot to discharge your battery or generate heat.Don't use these as turn signals because there's not enough resistance to work with traditional flasher modules. You will need a LED-specific flasher module, but most 194/168 bulbs are used as sidemarkers, interior lights, trunk lights, and license plate lights.The color temperature is typical of a white LED, around 6000K or so. It does not look blue, and is more like a really crisp white that is on the verge of becoming blue. It certainly looks legal when used as a license plate light and improves the interior lighting of a car. Most modern cars actually already have LED interior and exterior lighting, and I'd imagine that in the next 5-10 years, most if not all cars will go this route for power savings and cost savings. It is far easier to manufacture/integrate a surface-mounted LED light versus an incandescent bulb and fixture, not to mention reductions in maintenance without the need to replace bulbs all around the car. Although, if those LEDs do fail, it be expensive to replace the entire lamp!Overall: 5/5 stars, very affordable and easy to upgrade your sidemarkers and other 194/168 bulbs. Just be aware it may not fit a tight lamp compartment because it is about 1/8" longer than a 194/168 bulb.

reviewText: This is german engineering at its finest.  The light is very bright!!!  It's perfect bright clean white look.  No hint of blue.  Very bright!!! Blinding!!

The lights took a long time to arrive but it was expected. Put the lights in 3 trucks.  2010 sequioa - inside lights; 2004 tacoma - parking lights; 97 4runner - parking lights.  I like the look in the interior of the sequioa. light is 180 out from the factory lights.  the factory lights really look yellow compared to the white light from these LED's.  Not every light worked the first time. You also need to try the bulb both ways before tossing it out as not working. Biggest problem here was getting the covers off and bulbs out in the Sequioa.

New Review after about 3/4 year.ALL of the lamps that were installed have developed flickers or have just gone out. The vendor readily replaced the first 2-3 that stared flickering within 2 weeks. By now the rest have started flickering and one or two are completely dark.They seem fine if they are not on full-time. ones in the parking/license lights are the first to fail, then the overhead dome lights. the best ones remaining are in the doors, only on when that door is open. The dome lights lasted until one day I had the doors open for an hour or so while cleaning, then a couple of those started flickering.I haven't contacted the vendor again. I don't remember what the warranty is. No sense in going through the trouble to get more of these, just to have them fail.I suspect they are not running an adequate resistor, if any internally; instead pushing for maximum output, which raises temps and lowers lifespan.oh well. May just go back to incandescent.1. light quality: typical slight-blue LED output. They are brighter than incandescent in a non-focused housing like a dome light, and acceptable for clear marker lights, license lights, etc.. very happy with these in interior and puddle lights and dome lights. They throw a lot of flooded light. In a focused lens they are about the same as a filament bulb, just not as much pinpoint focus.2. bulb quality: it's a solid bulb that is a little tight to install, but even in really tight sockets they did not break on me. they run a little warm in always-on use, so i'm not sure what to expect from them long-term. Of the 12 I have installed, 2 have had one element (each bulb has five) start to flicker. the flickering would stop if I pressed on it. The vendor has quickly replaced the bulbs and has said they'll provide 90 day warranty. This works for me.3. price. $10 for 10 LED bulbs is reasonable. Keep in mind, at this price, while some may have given me trouble, the cost is no more than incandescent.4. I'm giving 5 stars because the vendor and the low price makes up for the problems I've seen so far. It's a neat product and affordable to experiment with.EDIT - docking one star to 4. Afte a few months, half of these have lost several LED elements.
summary: they fail quickly but the vendor tries

reviewText: 3/5 Stars because you get what you pay for out of these... but highly recommended, understanding their downfalls.Pros:*Fitment of the bulbs into the automotive socket was a little tight, which I prefer.*Leads are wrapped fully around terminals, meaning you don't have to re-bend +/- terminals if your socket doesnt match.*Bulbs are just as bright (if not marginally brighter) then OE incandescents.*Instant response to voltage, unlike the delay experienced with OE bulbs.Cons:*terrible packaging (loose in small manila envelope shipped from china)*Quality Control is on par with china crap standards, several LED assemblies were not fully socketed to the base, (easy fix, just apply light pressure to snug them in)**Note: as with most LEDs, if the bulb doesnt light when first installed, try installing it the other way around, as LEDs require positive and negative leads to be correct in order for them to work.
summary: Worth The price for a Replacement bulb, but dont expect it to be revolutionary!

reviewText: Replaced all the interior lights on a 2014 Jeep Grand Cherokee.  This 10 pack allowed me to replace the two lamps in the rear lift gate, two lamps in rear above the grab bar, two lamps in the front overhead console, two lamps below the dash in the foot well, one lamp in the glove box, and one lamp to disassemble for the map lights.  Unfortunately, with this particular vehicle, the map lights are not bulbs that can be replaced.  They are already LED lights, but they are warm 2,700 kelvin lights and these are 6,000 or 7,000 kelvin (bright white).  You have to cut off the old map lights, and re-solder the individual LEDs from this kit back onto the ribbon cable for them to match.  This isn't a shortcoming of this product, but rather my particular vehicle.  These are 5 star all the way.
Use these everywhere. Any 194 will fit perfectly as a replacement. They are polarized so if it doesn't work flip it around.  I have them in my truck and my tractor. In the cold or heat they work fine

I replaced the license plate and running light bulbs in my F-350 with these, all the interior lights in my wifes Lincoln MKS, and several lights in my camper.  These are brighter (and obviously whiter), use less power, and run much cooler than the original 194 bulbs.  I highly recommend them.

reviewText: I used to crimp little ends on to wires and hook them to the relay and wrap them with electrical tape... VERY time consuming and almost always failed in one way or another. I've replace all that crap with these... idk why I never did this in the first place!

I just wish the various relays & connectors for relays used a consistent colour code layout. But that is not a negative comment on this specific component - it's fine.

I mean for $5 this thing is perfect to keep in the proverbial battery box. reviewText: Some devices seem to stop working but with the batteries having lots of charge left.  Kid's toys in particular.  So instead of having to test them in a flashlight and try to eyeball if the brightness means lots of power left, it is easier to use this.  I then save ok batteries for tv remotes, my computer mouse, clocks and other things that can last quite a while even with partially depleted batteries.  I put some "dead" batteries in my computer mouse and they lasted probably 3/4 of what a fresh set lasts.  Not bad considering they were going to be thrown away if I hadn't checked them.I've used in on AA, AAA, and button batteries and it has worked fine.
summary: Makes quick work of figuring out if a battery is really dead

reviewText: The feel is cheap but it helped me feed out batteries that I thought were on their last legs. Biggest grip so far is the metal strip on both ends of there the battery gets inserted should have been all metal rather two little strips. Some sort on indent where the battery goes would have been nice so the battery stayed put when taking a measurement. At first I expected more from Amprobe but then I remembered the last amp clamp from them and it was also quite cheap feeling. For 8 bucks it's fine.

I wanted an inexpensive way to check batteries and this fits the bill.  I have a multimeter, but it's necessary to check batteries under load.  I was concerned when this tester arrived, as it's obviously cheap.  But cheap is fine if it works, and this product works great.

I was sad my 3.7 volt batteries can't be tested with this and am wondering what I need to test my rechargeable batteries to see whether they are storing the max energy any longer  . Still learning how to do the button cells . However I did do a jar full of alkaline AAA and AA plus some C , D and 9 volt  and threw out some batteries and kept some others I was going to toss them all and start over . My charger basically does the same thing but is not as friendly. I really was hoping to find how much capacity my batteries had and whether that was full or they showing they no longer took  a full charge anymore . I do not believe there is anyways to do that with this device after looking through the confusing notes that came with it . I guess I need a little more education on this topic .  I took off one star because there is no way to measure full capacity and adjust the load test or see a actual voltage reading . It will come in handy to clean out 20 years of accumulated batteries that often were retired after a brief use for a rechargeable and then mixed in with expired ones in a jar . I used to recharge my alkalines when that was all you could do but it is so messy I just toss them appropriately now . That was the good thing about this I was able to go very rapidly through the accumulation of 20 years and then send the dead ones on their way to the proper waste disposal station in my County for batteries . They ask they no longer be put in trash because their so toxic . I do not believe their is a law but it is the right thing to do . Here they dispose of them along with medical waste like sharp's at our Counties yard by appointment to drop off . No charge .Ended up buying a $2 ohm meter from harbor freight and using it for the button cells and larger stuff but no load test unless I do it in the device when powered on . I guess that works ? I am not very handy with electrical , never have been .

We all know the drill.  Something stops working or doesn't seem to work right so we take the batteries out, put them back in in a different order, blow out the thing, and then go off to find "new" batteries.  We open the battery drawer, basket, or whatever.  There is a mix of batteries that came from different things.  Maybe we keep the batteries we just took out because maybe they'll work find in something else that doesn't need "as fresh of a battery".  Pretty soon you have a mess of batteries and you have to try multiple combinations to find some that work and we barely ever throw them out.Please tell me that does not all just happen to me and my family.  If it does, then enjoy your laugh.With this little gadget I take the guess work out of my battery drawer and the possibility that something needs a new battery.  This tests everything from the watch type batteries that my 3D glasses for the TV use to the 9V in the smoke detector, to the AA, AAA, C & Ds that go in to the Nerf guns or whatever else you happen to kill batteries with.I really like this cheap simple little thing and regret that I wasted so long to break down and buy it.  Now I'm off to the battery drawer to start the culling of the dead batteries, some have been with me for a long time, in and out of many devices but their time has come to leave the drawer and go off to the dump.
Good little battery tester for the money, comes in handy when your not sure if its the battery or the item that's not working.

I was going for the HK version product that you can find here at Amazon as well but this has Prime shipping.The item is very light so you get the "cheap" look when holding it but it does what it promises: Checking the battery status on a easy to read gauge. No more hitting the remote control or guessing wich battery is almost dead.Really worth the price for not having to buy batteries without needing to (imho they are expensive).
summary: Does what it promises with Fast Shipping

reviewText: I have a large collection of rechargable and non rechargable batteries that I use for different purposes. Sometimes it is not very easy to distinguish the flat ones from the full ones and this small handy item does a great job for this purpose. I had spared more than 15 old batteries for recycling assuming they were flat and half of them turned up to have good level of charge in them. I may use them for clocks or other less demanding stuff. This is a very good item that can be used to test all common battery types and would eventually save one good amount of money. I hope it lasts.UPDATE after 1 week: I have concerns on the accuracy of the reading for button batteries. I bought a brand new set of button batteries (CR1616) for my watch and just out of curiosity tested one with this tool. First it is very difficult to get it in the place and second after the indicator needle wandered up and down a little while it showed  the 'replace' area. Which I believe is totally wrong. Then I tested it with two other brand new button batteries from different types (LR44 and CR2032)The reading with LR44 was consistent and accurate but CR2032 behaved somewhat similar to CR1616 (the needle jumped up and down then decreased back to 'replace battery area') I think the circuit in some button batteries is not strong enough for this device. For that case, I think if you see the needle at least once going up then assume that the battery is ok, do not expect it to stabilize in the green zone.Despite this flaw about button batteries, I still rate this item 5 stars due to its value for price rate and accuracy in major battery types. If you are not a heavy button battery user, then you won't regret this purchase.
summary: very handy and useful item but has a flaw about button batteries

reviewText: I started with one unit to give it a try in our travel trailer. They came quickly from BestDealUSA. The light is the really "white" light but it is fine. I didn't bother looking at the color of the wires. If the light didn't come on I just reversed the connection. They mount easily on the metal heat shield in our fixtures. It isn't quite as bright as a single 921 bulb (I had removed one of the bulbs from the double fixtures to reduce electric needs when on battery) so I ordered 5 more to use in both sides of the double fixtures.  Then I ordered 4 more to use in more fixtures. One of these required some jiggling to get it to come on and 3 of the 36 LED's don't work. Have driven about 100 miles on bumpy roads with these in place and they are working fine. New Jersey state parks don't have any hookups for camping so we do a lot of "dry" camping - the battery life is certainly extended with these LED's rather than incandescent bulbs. At this time I recommend them - time will tell if they continue to work so well.  UPDATE: When I told BestDealUSA about the "bad" light they immediately sent me a replacement. You can't beat that.  UPDATE March 2014:  Looks like the units now being sold aren't the same one's I got.  Also note that the price has doubled. reviewText: What an improvement over the stock blade.  I used this on the passenger side of my Prius.  Took all of 20 seconds to install and the blade leaves no streaks or spots.  The cover over the attachment point is a nice touch. Who could ask for more.

So far I'm loving the Bosch ICON 18A. It fits my 2005 Toyota Prius great; it gives a little bit more coverage than the stock passenger claw that came with my vehicle.The ICON size letter suffix refers to the manufactured curvature of the blade, which provides for effective surface contact, so check Bosch for proper fit with your vehicle.I bought the previous generation 426A (because it was available) for my driver side, so I'll be able to see, and will report back over time, whether the upgraded model is anything more than just a packaging change. I tested my blades last night, and they gave me a wonderfully streak-free wipe from tip to tip. These things are very nice.I replaced my rear wiper rubber this year as well, so with it being new I look back at it and see the disadvantage of my old claw-style wiper, which has four pressure points at the tips that wipe more clear than along the rest of the blade. The Bosch blades are clearly superior.These cost more, but they are awesome, and they look good too. I've uploaded a photo, though I try not to let you see my cracked windshield in it.I will remember to come back next season to report how well they hold up. reviewText: This specific 18 inch wiper blade went on our 2003 Toyota Matrix, passenger side.This wiper does not come with any adapters. It is specifically for cars with "u" type hook connections. Though you might be able to fudge on size a little (I used the 22 inchBosch 22A ICON Wiper Bladeon my driver's side which recommended a 21 inch blade with no problems) but you cannot fudge on connectors. Please make sure that this specific wiper blade is certified for your vehicle.The most difficulty I had was removing my old wipers because I had no instructions for that. Once removed, this Bosch blade installed, literally, in seconds. It does come with rather simple directions for installation, and has a snap down protector where the hook is inserted into the arm connection.Anyway, not much to say about a wiper blade if it works and this works fine. It arrived in time to be used on a normal sleet and snowy winter day in the Midwest of the United States. The moisture was wiped away quickly with no streaking. Durability questions are always an issue with any product, and I typically revisit my reviews if there are any abnormal issues there. I expect at least 1 year out of my blades, and usually I get 2 or 3 years.An easy 5 stars for a nice looking piece of equipment that installs easily and (so far) wipes away sleet and snow with no streaking.Note: Since I also acquired theBosch 22A ICON Wiper Bladefor the driver's side of my 2003 Toyota Matrix (21 inches is the exact size recommended for the driver's side of my car) the review for that is pretty much identical to this one.

reviewText: I'm really impressed with the Bosch ICON Wiper Blades.  They work great and were very easy to install.  There is no streaking or squeaking with these blades. I have been using wipers from a well known French brand for years, so I decided to make a change. These work just as well, if not better.  Fitting them is very easy, a <5 minute task :-)

reviewText: First, I am not used to spending $16 for one windshield wiper, but more like $10 for a pair at Walmart.  Having said that, I can honestly say these Bosch wipers may be worth the money. They mount like any other wiper hooking into that "U" shaped end of the wiper arm, without any additional plastic adapters, as they are made specifically for the model car you own.I did get to try them out in the rain twice and they really do work well, leaving my window streak free (better than my Walmart ones). Prior to switching to these wipers I had been using theRain-X Latitude 8-In-1 Premium Graphite Coated Wiper Blades. The hardware and blades did not feel cheap, which made me hopeful that these would last a good while.Installation was easy; they snapped right in to place.  I just had to make sure that I placed the correct blade on the correct side, as Bosch gives two different parts depending on drivers or passengers side.Performance so far has been excellent.  We have had several downpours and the Bosch blades keep my windows clear with no streaking or sticking.My recommendation is that they are well worth the price, for the value received and when comparing them to the Rain-X blades they come out slightly ahead because of the quality.

I have used a variety of wiper blades but Bosch has always made some of the best wiper blades in my opinion. I have always found them to be reliable and provide a good clean wipe for at least a year of use. I was excited to try out these Bosch ICON blades after seeing the advertisements for them. I have had the chance to try them out for a couple of weeks and get a good idea of how well that they work. We have had a ton of rain in recent weeks and I can tell you that they work perfectly in the rain. They clean the window very nice without any squeaking or sticking to the window. We also had a couple days of snow and ice mixture. They seem to do an equally good job in the snow and ice. Since these wipers are totally covered the ice can't get inside the wiper frame and freeze solid. This is a big plus in my opinion and helps to keep the wipers from being frozen in place. They were very easy to install as well. It took me longer to take them out of the packaging then to put them on my truck. If your wiper arm has the hook on it then it just slides into place and there is a cover that closes. The cover is nice because it would keep the wiper from totally coming off your car in the event that it slides off of the wiper arm. I think most people would really like these wipers and this is the wiper that I will probably continue to use as long as the price is fair.

reviewText: November 21, 2012 Update - Well these blades are not worth the extra premium price. They lasted just barely 9 months on my car. Normal life is a year (these are on a 2002 Buick Rendezvous - I've gone through roughly 9 sets of wiper blades, all lasting over a year). As I said in the lower part of this review, yes it was complicated to remember how to pull these blades off. They are different from all other blades around and those two little squeeze spots were hard to figure out after all this time. I won't be repurchasing these blades.The replacement blades I purchased this time are Michelin - a hybrid wiper, classic frame with full blade coverage:Michelin 5022 Stealth Wiper Blade, 22" (Pack of 1)The original review:The Bosch Icon wiper blade is Bosch's top of the line frameless wiper. This is an outstanding blade that is surprisingly easy to install.The most important step with wiper blades, is finding the correct blade for your care. Gone are the days when I could go to a parts counter and ask for a 24 inch refill (refills don't exist anymore). There is a part finder on Amazon. I would also recommend using the blade finder at Bosch to simply double check the blades required. A lot of cars have two blades that are a different length. Oddly, my Buick Rendezvous did not have the third rear wiper listed, the part finders both places only listed two blades. There are also A and B versions of these blades, so be certain to pick the correct blade.The hardest part of installation is removing the old wiper blade. While visiting Bosch's blade finder, I stumbled on an excellent video that demonstrates how to replace wiper blades. Removing the old one is the longest part of the video. This particular blade is for the U shaped end of the metal wiper arm. There is usually a clip on the inside of that U on the pivot side of the wiper arm. It is also a good idea to lay a towel down on the windshield just in case the wiper arm jumps out of your hand - it's not unheard of to crack a windshield that way.The final step is to open the black plastic clip. Slide the U shaped end of the wiper arm through that clip and into the holder. Pull back and snap the clip down. The end of the wiper arm is now encased in lovely plastic. That's it, there's nothing more to do. Pretty simple.Replacing both wiper blades on my Buick Rendezvous at midnight, took me 20 minutes total, and that included washing my hands and recycling the packaging materials. I'll admit that I've changed a lot of wiper blades.The Icon blade is a direct competitor to the Goodyear Assurance wiper blade. It's pretty amazing to see these two blades side by side. The only real difference between the blades, the Bosch has an aerodynamic spoiler to help force the blade against the car window at speed. And the clip mechanism on the Goodyear is more universal, but leaves the clip exposed to the elements. Honestly, these two differences are nice looking, but I'm not sure they really make that much difference in the big picture.I installed the Goodyear Assurance blades about a year ago and couldn't exactly remember the clipping mechanism. So it took me a moment to remove the old blade. In a year or two when I replace these blades, I'm certain I will forget about how that plastic cover is clipped on, and will struggle just as much with the Bosch blades. In their marketing information Bosch talks about how the clip prevents snow and ice build up on the wiper blade. In all my years of driving in really bad snow storms, I've never seen a wiper blade have a problem with the cover to the attaching point.This is a good looking blade. Bosch and Goodyear both have eliminated that external frame with all the pivot points and metal or plastic holders - those really did get snow under them and create problems. They are now using a spring steel plate wrapped with plastic. There are no moving parts with this system. The rubber wiper blade is actually exactly the same as an external frame wiper - it sits inside a slot like all the rest. The end caps are attached tightly and should never fall off.Overall, this is an excellent wiper blade. Given that a wiper blade lasts for a good year or two, I think these are worth the extra cost over Bosch blades. I would shop based on price versus the Goodyear Assurance blades - they are virtually the same thing.Goodyear GY-WB765-22 Assurance Black 22'' Premium Rubber Graphite Coated Wiper Blade

We just had a really heavy snow and by that I mean 6 inches of very wet heavy snow. I don't like clearing the windshield of my van because it's a full size conversion van and I can't reach the middle of the windshield so the wiper blades have to move that heavy snow off and they did it without any hesitation. I thought sure they'd hit that heavy stuff and slow way down and move it slowly but they moved it with the first swipe and no slow moving like they were stuck. They just wiped it away as if it were just rain water. They did a complete cleaning of the window, tip to tip, with just the right amount of pressure, no streaking or smearing.

I've never thought much about windshield wiper blades. I buy new ones when they start to peel away from the wiper holder and usually have them installed when I get an oil change or at the auto parts store. I've never in my life even attempted to change the blades myself - until now.I began by looking up how to replace the windshield wiper blades for my car in the manufacturer's manual. I have a 2005 Chevrolet Impala and Chevy made it seem pretty easy in the manual. Unfortunately, when it came down to actually performing this task, the manual's instructions left a lot to be desired. It just wasn't clear to me which way to pull the blades to remove them. Chevy said to pull them towards the windshield, but that apparently means a different direction to them than it does to me. I finally figured it out after watching a video on YouTube after searching the internet for how to remove the blades.The instructions on the Bosch package were also a little ambiguous for me. It wasn't clear to me at first that there is a latch that has to pop up on the Bosch blade before you slide the shepherd's hook on the wiper through the blade. I will confess without shame that it took me nearly an hour to figure that out. In my defense, this was the first time and the old blades didn't have such a latch so it didn't even occur to me that the Bosch model would. Once I figured the latch out, the rest was easy.I actually really like the latch - the blades seem even more secure to me than the old ones I had. While I've never personally had a blade fly off the car while driving, I have heard of it happening and it never hurts to be a bit more secure. The last thing you'd want is to lose a wiper blade in a thunderstorm.When I got my oil changed in early December 2010, I had them change my wiper blades with some very inexpensive ones. They worked well enough. I replaced those cheap blades with these Bosch blades just two months later at the end of January 2011. Since the old blades were practically new, I was able to get a good feel of the difference between those and the Bosch 22A ICON Wiper Blade. I have to say, as someone who never paid any attention to wiper blades unless there was a problem, I do believe I can see the improvement. The old blades streaked just a bit - not enough to interfere with visibility, but it was there. The Bosch blades wipe the windshield very well, leaving a very clear view of the road without streaks.I ordered both the Bosch 22A ICON Wiper Blade, which I've reviewed here, and theBosch 22B ICON Wiper Blade, 22" (Pack of 1). I studied the product descriptions for both models carefully and also examined the two blades side by side when I received them and I honestly can't tell a difference in the 22A and 22B models. If there is one, it totally escapes me. They seem to be interchangeable and can be used on either the right or the left side of the car. Although some cars have use wipers of different lengths on each side, my Impala uses 22-inch blades on each side.The manufacturer claims that these blades will last approximately 40% longer than other blades, and while only time will prove whether this is true or not, having looked at the Bosch blades next to my old blades, I can believe it might be true.I would say that if you are looking for a better wiper blade, then the Bosch  22A ICONS Wiper Blade is a good choice.
summary: High-end blades deliver very clear visibility even in thunderstorms

reviewText: The function of this blade is great - it makes for a nice clean windshield.  I was waiting to test this in some snow, but it looks like we wont be getting any this year. reviewText: This specific wiper went on our 2003 Toyota Matrix, driver's side. For starters, my car requires a 21 inch wiper blade (e.g.,Bosch 21A ICON) and this is a 22 inch blade. This still fits fine with absolutely no problems. That's pretty much because at 22 inches there's just an extra 1/2 inch on each end which doesn't seem to make any difference on my car. I'm not recommending you do the same, but just adding that for me being off one size was no problem.Note: This wiper does not come with any adapters. It is specifically for cars with "u" type hook connections. Though you might be able to fudge on size a little (like I did) you cannot fudge on connectors. Please make sure that this specific wiper blade is certified for your vehicle.The most difficulty I had was removing my old wipers because I had no instructions for that. Once removed, this Bosch blade installed, literally, in seconds. It does come with rather simple directions for installation, and has a snap down protector where the hook is inserted into the arm connection.Anyway, not much to say about a wiper blade if it works and this works fine. It arrived in time to be used on a normal sleet and snowy winter day in the Midwest of the United States. The moisture was wiped away quickly with no streaking. Durability questions are always an issue with any product, and I typically revisit my reviews if there are any abnormal issues there. I expect at least 1 year out of my blades, and usually I get 2 or 3 years.An easy 5 stars for a nice looking piece of equipment that installs easily and (so far) wipes away sleet and snow with no streaking.Note: I also acquired aBosch 18A ICON Wiper Bladefor the passenger side of my 2003 Toyota Matrix (18 inches is the exact size recommended for the passenger side of my car) and the review for that is pretty much identical to this one.
summary: Esthetically pleasing, nothing wrong with them

reviewText: I've had this on my Saturn now for over a year. Its still going strong! Winter blades don't last long enough to justify the price but this does. It doesn't get clogged up nearly as easy as regular blades. It seems to be sticking to the window better and highway speeds too. They are a lot of money and I decided to go for it after only using the cheapest blades forever. It seems to have been a good choice so far.

I will never go back to the "old" style wipers.  This new design (well it's been out a couple years now) works so much better for me.  They don't collect ice like the old ones.  They wipe cleanly and follow the contour of the windshield.  They look better - simpler and more attractive.They're easy to install - and come with "adapters" for various types of wiper arms.  On my car they do not require the adapters (Crossfire).  I just snap off the previous ones and snap these on.When it's time to deal with winter, and your windshield is covered with snow and ice, I just lift the blade off the windshield, flex it a little bit, and all the ice and snow comes off leaving a nice clean wiper blade.  Very easy to clean.They last a long time for me, I probably leave them on longer than I should but they don't streak so to me that's a sign that they're still OK.If you have not tried these, you're missing out - I would never go back to the metal frames and rubber inserts - too many moving parts and problems!
Bosch wiper blade seems to be the best wiper blade I have purchased so far, no noise clean sweep the first time, works Great!

reviewText: Summary: Excellent premium wiper at a premium price, but convenience and "longer lasting rubber" means that cost should be comparable in the long run - one nice feature is that it's good for both winter and summer use.Here in Michigan, your wipers often freeze in the winter.  In certain conditions ice freezes the blade so it no longer flexes to conform to the windshield, which means it stops wiping.That means you end up rolling down your window at stoplights and flicking the blade as it comes by, or having to stop every so often and whacking the blade with your snow scraper.  Winter blades have a rubber jacket around the blade holder but this rubber sleeve typically falls apart in the summer.  It also creates a huge amount of blade lift since it's so big check it outAnco 30-18 Premium Winter Wiper Blade - 18"- the result is that you end up swapping back and forth much as you would winter tires.These blades have a very low profile and also do not freeze - result is that you can keep them on year round.  The design looks a little unusual -  the blade holder is a very flexible, thin and springy metal - it actually forms a "U" when off the car.It just so happens that when I ordered these from Amazon Vine, they only had the drivers side for one of our cars and the passenger side wiper size for our other - this actually gave us a true back to back comparison.  We had new wipers put on our Ford Flex just about a month ago and while they performed admirably in the snow storm we had today, the ICON blades definitely did better.If you have any questions or comments, or if you found this info helpful, please let me know!
summary: Installed easily, definitely better than OEM - plus it's perfect for winter

reviewText: Nothing really wrong with Rain-X but these are better in the sense that they never leave a streak.They're as noisy as most any other wiper but work especially well in the hardest rain I've seen.I live in South Florida so trust me, I've seen rain as hard as it gets and these wipers are up to thetask.  I'm a Bosch Icon adherent now and Rain-X is a 2nd-favorite.
summary: Outstanding; no streaks, better than Rain-X

reviewText: I have been impressed with frameless blade technology.  I find that blades featuring this design tend to do a much better job of maintaining contact with the windshield, clearing away rain much more effectively than the older wipers do.These Bosch blades are among the best I've used.  They are well designed and manufactured.  They installed on my old Lexus RX300 without any hassles at all.With these wipers combined with Rain-X treatment on the glass, rain doesn't stand a chance.  The frameless design ensures excellent blade contact.  The blade itself is engineered to be durable and highly effective.These Bosch wipers are much better than the Rain-X Latitude wipers they replaced.  In fact, although I properly installed the Rain-X wipers, the driver's side blade fell off of the car because of a manufacturing/design defect where the blade attaches to the wiper arm on the car -- the mounting bracket remained in the wiper arm, but the wiper blade flew off.  Not the sort of thing you want to have happening on the highway during a rainstorm.Our winter has been mild, so I haven't had the opportunity to see how these perform under winter conditions.  Given how well they deal with the rain, and given how well constructed they appear, I doubt they'll have issues with a bit of ice and snow.All in all, these are excellent blades and worth the premium in price over traditional blades.  In my experience, they also beat the competition in their class in terms of reliability.  Great blades.  Give them a try.

The Bosch Icon wiper blade is Bosch's top of the line frameless wiper. This is an outstanding blade that is surprisingly easy to install.November 21, 2012 Update - Well these blades are not worth the extra premium price. They lasted just barely 9 months on my car. Normal life is a year (these are on a 2002 Buick Rendezvous - I've gone through roughly 9 sets of wipers). As I said in the lower part of this review, yes it was complicated to remember how to pull these blades off. They are different from all other blades around and those two little squeeze spots were hard to figure out after all this time. I won't be repurchasing these blades.The most important step with wiper blades, is finding the correct blade for your care. Gone are the days when I could go to a parts counter and ask for a 24 inch refill (refills don't exist anymore). There is a part finder on Amazon. I would also recommend using the blade finder at Bosch to simply double check the blades required. A lot of cars have two blades that are a different length. Oddly, my Buick Rendezvous did not have the third rear wiper listed, the part finders both places only listed two blades. There are also A and B versions of these blades, so be certain to pick the correct blade.The hardest part of installation is removing the old wiper blade. While visiting Bosch's blade finder, I stumbled on an excellent video that demonstrates how to replace wiper blades. Removing the old one is the longest part of the video. This particular blade is for the U shaped end of the metal wiper arm. There is usually a clip on the inside of that U on the pivot side of the wiper arm. It is also a good idea to lay a towel down on the windshield just in case the wiper arm jumps out of your hand - it's not unheard of to crack a windshield that way.The final step is to open the black plastic clip. Slide the U shaped end of the wiper arm through that clip and into the holder. Pull back and snap the clip down. The end of the wiper arm is now encased in lovely plastic. That's it, there's nothing more to do. Pretty simple.Replacing both wiper blades on my Buick Rendezvous at midnight, took me 20 minutes total, and that included washing my hands and recycling the packaging materials. I'll admit that I've changed a lot of wiper blades.The Icon blade is a direct competitor to the Goodyear Assurance wiper blade. It's pretty amazing to see these two blades side by side. The only real difference between the blades, the Bosch has an aerodynamic spoiler to help force the blade against the car window at speed. And the clip mechanism on the Goodyear is more universal, but leaves the clip exposed to the elements. Honestly, these two differences are nice looking, but I'm not sure they really make that much difference in the big picture.I installed the Goodyear Assurance blades about a year ago and couldn't exactly remember the clipping mechanism. So it took me a moment to remove the old blade. In a year or two when I replace these blades, I'm certain I will forget about how that plastic cover is clipped on, and will struggle just as much with the Bosch blades. In their marketing information Bosch talks about how the clip prevents snow and ice build up on the wiper blade. In all my years of driving in really bad snow storms, I've never seen a wiper blade have a problem with the cover to the attaching point.This is a good looking blade. Bosch and Goodyear both have eliminated that external frame with all the pivot points and metal or plastic holders - those really did get snow under them and create problems. They are now using a spring steel plate wrapped with plastic. There are no moving parts with this system. The rubber wiper blade is actually exactly the same as an external frame wiper - it sits inside a slot like all the rest. The end caps are attached tightly and should never fall off.Overall, this is an excellent wiper blade. Given that a wiper blade lasts for a good year or two, I think these are worth the extra cost over Bosch blades. I would shop based on price versus the Goodyear Assurance blades - they are virtually the same thing.Goodyear GY-WB765-24 Assurance Black 24'' Premium Rubber Graphite Coated Wiper Blade

I was given one blade for free to test out.  I'm very pleased with this wiper blade, so I bought another one to match.  I think that's a decent testimonial.The performance in the rain is very good.  It's quiet and effective.  The last thing I want to think about in wet conditions is whether my wipers are going to do their job or not.The installation is pretty simple.  It's easy enough to remove the old blade and install the new one in under a minute.  The clip is slightly non-standard though.  I'm a little worried that it won't be quite as simple to remove it in the future when I replace it (unless I replace it with the exact same one and can read the instructions on the new package).  The cover that slides over the clip isn't completely intuitive, so I can imagine having a hard time remembering how it went on.Other than that, this blade performs very well and even looks really nice.Be careful when you select the blades for your vehicle, because your vehicle may require different blades for the driver's and passenger's side.  I drive a pickup truck, so life is a little simpler for me.Also, remember to be careful when you remove the old blades.  Never leave the wiper arm extended if it doesn't have a blade attached.  It's too easy for the arm to snap back down and shatter your windshield.  Gently put the arm back in place against the windshield while you're fumbling around with the packaging for the new blade.
I have been using wipers from a well known French brand for years, so I decided to make a change.  These work just as well, if not better.
