reviewText: The Bosch 24A ICON wiper blade, 24" fits my Fit, is durable, and was easy to install.  It has a powder black finish that matches my wiper arm.I do recommend it.  Good wiper blades are a must if you live where the sun don't shine much.  Four stars because I prefer OEM parts, but if they weren't available, I'd buy this.

This is the first wiper of this type that I have used (non-hinged frame type) and I have to say that I am impressed.  Usually at highway speeds, my regular wipers start to lift a bit or do not maintain full contact with the windshield, but these low profile wipers keep full contact along the full length, for a clear windshield.  There was no squeak or stutter at any time, even in light rain or when using washer fluid, and they were able to keep up with a full-on heavy rain, which some wipers do not seem to be able to do.  This 24a wiper fits the drivers side of a 2009 Sonata among others (use a 20a for the passenger side of the 2009 Sonata), and works as good or better than any other wiper I have tried so far.  Installation was a snap, just following the directions/diagrams on the back of the package.  I do not live in an area with snow or ice, so I cannot on this wiper in "winter" conditions.

Bosch Icon wipers are great all year long, in the Winter ice and snow doesn't build up like it can on framed wipers, they flex making even contact across the glass with out pressure points. I've been very pleased with performanceand life these wiper offer. They mount on standard wiper arms with a solid grip and stay on once locked down. I clean the edge with a soft cloth and sometimes use a rubber treatment after months of use, I find this keeps thewipers in tip top shape.
summary: Bosch Icon wipers are great all year long

reviewText: I've had these on my car for a little over a year and a half. (I know, because Amazon just reminded me of my prior order as I checked out the product page to order another set.) Only now are they starting to show signs of aging. Before these, I had wipers from Rain-X (two different kinds) and while they cost about 75% as much, they lasted 30% of the time. You do the math.In case you're not familiar with them, Bosch is the company that actually makes the OEM wiper blades for many high end cars (like BMW, for one). In fact, you'd probably be surprised by how much inside your car is made by Bosch. So, you're not buying from a company that is just marketing cheap parts made in China and selling it with a lot of marketing. You're getting OEM quality with these, if not better. So, when considered in that light, as well, these blades really aren't that expensive.So, the blades really do last, but will you be happy with them while they do? I think so. They hold the shape of the windshield well, and never flap or vibrate, no matter how fast you're going. The bracket is solid, and worked well on the J-hook in my car. Many other "universal" mounts didn't work so well, notably the ones from the aforementioned Rain-X wipers. The single piece design is also great for those living in cold climates, as it is less vulnerable to ice and snow build-up.They don't streak or chatter, and even after having them on my car for over a year, they are only streaking a small amount.Given that your eyes are the most important safety device on your car, you owe it to yourself to not skimp on wiper blades. But I'm pleased to report that despite the upfront cost, these are actually MORE cost effective than many other premium wiper blades, given that they are the only expensive wiper blades I've ever used that actually lasted longer than the cheap ones.Tip: the A or the B after the model number (e.g. 22A) refers to the spring force of the blade (i.e. how hard it is to pull it straight). The B applies more force, and would be useful if you have a highly curved windshield. The fact that Bosch offers not just a variety of lengths down the inch, but also two different spring forces, is another indicator of the fact that these are not your average wiper blades. I found that having an A on the driver side and a B on the passenger side works best on my car. If in doubt, just try A all around, and then if you find that the blade is missing spots on the ends of the blade, return the A and get a B.Last tip: Amazon's database is helpful, but by no means complete. If you think this will fit your car, but Amazon says it won't, ignore Amazon. They say neither blade I have on my car will work, and yet I'm extremely happy with them, as you can tell.
summary: A good value given their durability

reviewText: I bought this 24A ICON wiper for my Frontier and it was real easy to install them.  It took more time to take out my old Goodyear wipers that lasted me about 6months.  These Bosch wipers run very smooth and no streaks.  We will see how long they last me.

This is a very light wiper made mostly with composite materials instead of metal parts. Our MDX requires two different sizes, a 24A and a 21B - the letters correspond to driver's side(A) and passenger's side(B).Replacing wipers is pretty easy. You may need to look at the instruction as different manufacturers have different ways of releasing them from the hook, but basically takes only thirty seconds to remove the old and snap a new one. For the Bosch Icon wipers, just type in search "Bosch wiper blades -hook installation video II" for online video instructions.CAUTION:Be careful when you leave the wiper standing on your windshield after you remove the old one.  The wiper is spring loaded, without the wiper it is pure metal and it may snap back to your windshield glass.These wipers look a lot better compared to my old one.  It is designed for high speed and supposedly to last 40% longer than conventional types (for that, only time will tell).  The softer frame curves and conforms to the shape of the surface glass as opposed to conventional wipers that has two parts - the metal frame and the moving part that is the rubber.
Replaced Acura wipers with these. Much better. This is the second set of these I have purchased. First set lasted 4 years.

First month of really bad winter , this blade has worked the best Ive had. You really need to have for 6 months before I can tell you if its worth the money. Very expensive. My cheap blades usually only last about 6mo. easy to put on. squeeky clean. works on freeway speeds pretty well. update later.
summary: so far works great for winter, but steep price!

reviewText: I have a Kia Borrego SUV, and it is a challenge to get wiper blades that actually do a good job on the large windshield.  So far, I have been highly pleased with this set of Bosch ICON wiper blades.  They are quiet, and work without streaking.  I have used them twice during snow storms, and they have done very well.It was easy to find the correct sizes needed, using the parts finder tool at the top of the Amazon page.  My spouse installed these on my vehicle, and he said they were not any harder to install than a standard wiper blade.  I am very satisfied with these blades, and will likely purchase them the next time I need a replacement.

I am a big fan of "beam" type wiper blades, which don't have external hinged arms.  Not only do they keep a closer contact with the windshield, but they are much less prone to clogging with ice and snow. I've used earlier versions of the Bosch ICON on my wife's car for a few years and the new style looks to be even better.  The rubber is more supple and there's a subtle "wing" air deflector molded into the blade, to help keep it on the glass at high speeds.With a good beam blade installed, you can skip switching to "winter blades" if you're in the snow belt - the ICON will do just fine.  I also like that they seem to last longer than traditional blades - I usually get a full year out of these.One feature of the ICON I like, so far shared only with theValeo 900-ULTIMATEof blades I have tried, is the hinged cover over the mounting hardware.  Not only does this make the blade easy to install, it also makes it easy to remove, unlike those with the spring latch you have to somehow get to release.Do make sure that you get the right size and style for your car.
summary: A great blade made even better

reviewText: I typically buy Bosch brand wipers, but a few months ago Amazon had a sale on another brand of wipers (Valeo) so I gave them a try. Never again. They broke, had to return them, broke again, etc. So I gave up and went back to Bosch. These are awesome wipers. Very quiet, don't leave streaks, and are very durable and resistant to ice/snow in the winter. And they last a long time. I've gotten at least 2 years on my last pair of these. They are worth the price.

This wiper blade was much harder to install than my old one. It sort of flopped around, getting in the way with the 24" length until I could get the attachment secured. I have not noticed any difference in wind resistance from my old blades. They do not squeak or stutter or streak after several storms, however, pine needles seem to get stuck in the assembly much easier and have to be removed in order not to have the streaking.They work as well as the old wipers which really cost less, but they do look better.
I got a pair of wiper blades from Costco. They were made by Good Year so I figured they had to be good but for some reason on my prius they didn't work very well but these work great!

These wiper blades were very easy to install. It took less than a minute. They do their job well. Good contact with windshield along it's entire length so there are no missed spots. No streaks. They seem to be made out of good quality materials.Overall, I am very satisfied with these wipers. As far as longevity goes, time will tell and I will update this review if I notice the performance deteriorating over time.

These Bosch Icon Windshield Wiper Blades work great and were very easy to install on my Chrysler Town & County minivan. My car needed these 26A size on the driver side andBosch 20A ICON Wiper Blade - 20", Pack of 1on the passenger side, which I confirmed using the Amazon "Find Parts" tool that shows up at the top of most automotive accessory pages.These blades looked flimsy compared to the ones it replaced since they do not have the ridged support bracket, but my concerns were groundless as they fit and performed very well, leaving not streaks and not "squeaking". Having never replaced my own wiper blades before, I went to the Bosch site to watch the helpful installation video and was able to learn everything I needed to know (really very easy).These exceeded my exceptions in both functionality and ease of installation!Highly Recommended!CFH
summary: Very Good Wiper Blades - Highly Recommended!

reviewText: What an improvement over the stock blade.  I used this on the driver's side of my prius.  Took all of 30 seconds to install and the blade leaves no streaks or spots.  The cover over the attachment point is a nice touch. Who could ask for more.

I usedBosch 22B ICON Wiper Blade - 22", Pack of 1on the passenger side of my 2010 Honda Odyssey.  It worked so well, I bought the 26A size for the driver's side.  It fits perfectly.  Very quick and easy install.  Anyone can do it.  In the rain, the blades wipe cleanly without streaks.  I'm very happy with them.

I installed this wiper blade on my 2006 Lexus, which my husband is driving in the Seattle area while he is temporarily assigned there. Living in Texas, we don't get much precipitation of any kind so the kind of wipers you use aren't as critical as in areas that see more weather. The ICON line is Bosch's extreme weather blades. I purchased the Bosch Evolution blades for my 2004 Texas driven PT Cruiser, and upon comparing the two, the ICON blades are thicker and feature a different slope which would clearly handle snow and sleet easily.There are no instructions for removing your old blades on the Icon packaging and I had to Google some videos to figure out how to do it. Installing the new blades was easy and there are clear illustrations on the back of the package.Be sure to  plug your car's year, make and model number in the Amazon "Find Parts That Fit my Vehicle" tool to assure you buy the correct blades. My cars all require different sizes on the driver and passenger sides and windshields have different slopes so this is important.These Bosch blades are frameless, meaning that there is no metal frame holding the rubber wiper. The entire blade is thick rubber. I like this better because there are no metal tips that could potentially scratch your windshield should the rubber fail and the rubber is thicker so it makes better contact with your windshield.Of course, it's how well they work that matters and these perform beautifully. My husband drove through a recent snowstorm and some sleet and said these blades made a huge difference and helped him maintain excellent visibility. Get caught in a downpour or a snowstorm and you will be glad you have good wipers!Recommended.

Below is an answer from Bosch when I asked about the Marathons sold at Wally world. They are the same as Evolutions. They are not Bosch's higher end flagship Icons as some people suspected. If you like the Evo's you can save some cash by buying Marathons instead.I cannot personally testify about anything except the Icons witch are fantastic blades. Its the only line I have used. I think the only advertised difference is the longevity between the Icon/Evo lines but if wally worlds price for the Evo equivalent Marathons are low enough on my next trip around I'll try them. There does however seem to be better reviews on Amazon with Icons but I was just glad to find wipers that lasted yrs again instead of just months like other brands ended up doing for me. Hope I helped save a few bucks for someone here.BTW: When installing these beam blades make sure the higher ridge on the frame is up. You should be able to read Bosch. If Bosch is upside down then flip the blade around. While looking at the end or tip of the blade from a side view,it looks like a scoop and should appear like this ( and not backwards like this ). The higher ridge acts like a spoiler on the rear of a car and catches wind to force it downward onto the glass while driving. I read on some reviews were people discovered they mounted them backwards and the blade lifted instead. Some cant be installed wrong,but some can.===Question to Bosch===Are the Bosch Marathon wipers sold at Walmart stores the same blade as bosch Icons? If not what line are they from because they are not even listed on the bosch site?Thank you======Answer==Hello,The Marathon wiper blades are equivalent to the Evolution wiper blade.  They are not listed on our website because they are exclusive to Walmart.Thank you,Robert - Bosch Parts Specialist-----Original Message-----From: mailgenerator {at} de.bosh [mailto:mailgenerator}Sent: Tuesday, December 11, 2012 4:55 PMTo: Communications bosch (RBNA/COM)Subject: Request from Contact function

It rains a lot in New Orleans. Umbrellas are as much accessories as purses or wallets. Sometimes the sky opens up and rain falls in sheets, like driving through a car wash. Down here we need really good windshield wipers. But it's not always clean, we live in the mud and swamp and that splashes up on the car and the windshield, and then of course bugs commit caricide and birds crap and the windshield takes it all while we try to see out of it and not get killed by our fellow New Orleans drivers.The Bosch blades were easy to install. We drive a 2011 scion xb and needed the 22B and the 20B. Ordering is easy, Put Bosch icon wiper blades in the amazon search and just pick anyone, then a screen will come up on the page telling you to make sure this is the right size blade. The page has a menu and you click the make, model, and year of your car and it will tell you exactly what you need and you can go to the right page for the size of wipers for your vehicle.After Jim installed the wipers we had a huge rainstorm and they kept the windshield clear while he drove to work. We also had one of those on and off sprinkles where we had to use the intermittent wiper setting and the icons did a good job of not stuttering and skipping over the windshield. They also did a good job when we sprayed the wiper fluid up and used the wipers to get dirt and gunk off. They didn't get the dried bird poop off but we haven't a wiper yet that does completely.I will update about how long they lasted, we do not garage our cars and so the blades are exposed to rain, sun, humidity, and heat- the usual New Orleans climate.

These are simply awesome wipers.I have the set on a 2001 Chevy Blazer and I could not be more happy with them.They wipe evenly without streaking and never leave any of the mess any other blades I have used tend to do over time.Installation was a snap and should be for even the least mechanically inclined people out there.Both this 20B and the other 20A blade perform the same so there really isn't a difference in the two when it comes to the review.They have held up great for a long while now and I expect a lot more life out of them.I would say these are a great buy.I will update if I feel like they don't last as long as they should, but I really think these blades are quality and will outlast my last set.Thumbs up.
summary: I am buying these from now on.

reviewText: I've had Valeo ULTIMATE and these ICON aero-style wipers for maybe six years on two different cars.  They are not streak-free, as I reckon they are advertised to be.  The passenger-side blade almost always doesn't fully make contact on the windshield by the fender--many others complain of this.  In other words, they don't contour as well as advertised.I think wipers that use refills work better, and are more economical.  Only reasons I use these ICONs is because they look better than the blades that came on my car, which were the non-refillable type.Meh.

I've had these on my car for a little over a year and a half. (I know, because Amazon just reminded me of my prior order as I checked out the product page to order another set.) Only now are they starting to show signs of aging. Before these, I had wipers from Rain-X, and while they cost 75% as much, they last less than 50% of the time. You do the math.So, these last, but are they good while they last? Absolutely. They hold the shape of the windshield well, and never flap or chatter, no matter how fast you're going. Their bracket is solid, and worked well on the J-hook in my car. Many other "universal" mounts didn't work so well, notably the ones from the aforementioned Rain-X wipers.They don't streak, and even after having them on my car for over a year, they are only streaking a small amount.Given that your eyes are the most important safety device on your car, you owe it to yourself to not skimp on wiper blades. But I'm pleased to report that despite the upfront cost, these are actually MORE cost effective than many other premium wiper blades, given that they are the only expensive wiper blades I've ever used that actually lasted longer than the cheap ones.
summary: Actually a good value when you consider the durability

reviewText: I bought this for my 2006 F-150.  I've only used these blades for a couple months now but they work great.  The wiper is easy to install and is the best yet for removing water and what not from my windshield.  If you take care of your wipers, they will take care of you.
summary: Best wiper blade I've ever used.

reviewText: I discovered one thing for sure. When you're driving across the Peace Bridge into Canada during a lake effect snow storm and your windshield wiper motor fails, RainX could be your new best friend. .. but enough about my adventures.  Well, maybe not because it is sort of relevant.There wasn't a thing wrong with my old hinged wipers but the chance to replace them with this premium priced alternative was an offer I couldn't pass up, even if could only get one so I replaced the passenger side and left the driver side wiper in place. I understand there is an installation video, but really, it's putting on a windshield wiper, not installation of an intake manifold gasket. As I noted all of my exterior window surfaces are treated with Rain-x and I should be writing a review lauding that product because I have used it for years.Before my little mechanical setback, the Bosch wiper was working just fine; no streaking , squeaking or stutters but certainly not anything to write a review about or in any manner that was noticeably superior to its' less costly and much older companion. That's when the real test started as it was the driver side mechanism that failed. As I leaned towards the center of the car, I did have a smidgen of regret that the passenger side wiper wasn't the longer of the two. And it became abundantly evident while the wiper was effectively clearing a bit over half the window, the way Rain-x dissipated the snow flakes and road mist was more impressive.I suppose in the long view (sic), I'll probably replace the other blade with one these beam technology models since they are purported to have a longer life span but for the moment I'm not convinced the significantly higher cost is worth it to me.

reviewText: These Bosch wiper blades work great.Pros+ They leave the window completely clean, no streaks+ They look good, classier than your average blades+ Very simple to installCons- None

I just replaced these exact blades that I had on my S10 pickup for three years. reviewText: ThisBosch 22B ICON Wiper Bladewas installed on my 2006 Chevrolet Trailblazer.  Living in Washington, rain is just part of the package.  I'm not complaining as I've lived here all my life, but you do need to be prepared.  Prior to switching to these wipers I had been using theRain-X Latitude 8-In-1 Premium Graphite Coated Wiper Blades.  With only a few dollars difference, I figured the comparison would be worthwhile.Quality seems very good.  The hardware and blades did not feel cheap, which made me hopeful that these would last a good while.Installation was easy; they snapped right in to place.  I just had to make sure that I placed the correct blade on the correct side, as Bosch gives two different parts depending on drivers or passengers side.Performance so far has been excellent.  We have had several downpours and the Bosch blades keep my windows clear with no streaking or sticking.My recommendation is that they are well worth the price, for the value received and when comparing them to the Rain-X blades they come out slightly ahead because of the quality.

In the twenty-fixe years that I've been driving, I haven't given much thought at all to windshield wiper blades unless there was a problem with mine. Either they worked, or they didn't. When they started peeling away from the wiper I would have them replaced, usually during an oil change or I would have one of the helpful gentleman at the auto parts store install them for me. I never had to do this myself.When I was offered the Bosch 22B ICON Wiper Blade, 22" to review, I thought this was an opportunity to see what difference, if any, a better windshield wiper blade made in comparison to the cheap blades I used in the past. I also realized that this was an opportunity to see how easy it was to change the blades myself in order to rate the installation process for this review.I dug out the trusty manual for my 2005 Chevrolet Impala and saw what looked to be very simple instructions for replacing the blades, which bolstered my confidence. I also verified that my car used the same size blade on both sides of the windshield - apparently some cars use two different sizes. I ordered both the Bosch 22B ICON Wiper Blade, 22" and its counterpart, theBosch 22A ICON Wiper Blade, 22" (Pack of 1).When the Bosch blades arrived, I scrutinized them side by side. Although they have different part numbers, I honestly cannot tell a difference, so I'm not sure why they have two different part numbers. They seem to be interchangeable.I then began the task of removing the old blades from my car. Having never even watched this procedure being performed before, I was at a bit of a loss when actually attempting to do it. Although the instructions in the car manual seemed clear enough, they really didn't describe the procedure well. I finally managed to remove them after watching a video on the web showing how to remove them. As it turns out, Chevy's idea of the `down' direction and mine are slightly different.Once the old blades were gone, it was time to install the Bosch blades. The instructions on the Bosch package were mostly OK, but it wasn't quite clear enough that these blades had a latch that had to be popped open before I could attach them to my wipers. Once I figured that out, the installation was easy. My old blades don't have that little latch, and I have to say that it makes me feel like the blades are just a bit more securely attached than the old ones.Since I installed these blades a couple of months ago, we've had quite a lot of rain and several storms in our area. I even got caught in a thunderstorm complete with tornado warnings and golf-ball sized hail on the way home from work a few weeks ago and these Bosch wipers did an excellent job considering the weather. I do believe that they are much better than the old cheap blades they replaced. Those blades were only a month old, but they left a slight streak when they wiped. The Bosch blades wipe the surface completely clear, making for an unimpaired view of the road.When these need to be replaced, I will definitely look at a new pair of Bosch blades rather than the old cheap ones again.
summary: Not hard to install, windshield stays clear even during hail and thunderstorms

Anyone who does long trips and carries kids in the back of a car that doesn't come with its own AC power outlet should find this product useful. Amazon's Pocket(?) Power Inverter is one of those little gizmos you didn't know you were missing until you start using one and maybe not even then. It will provide up 120V AC and supply up to 130W if plugged into the cigarette lighter (cable included), up to 175W if attached directly to your car's battery with the provided battery clip cable.I only tested the cigarette lighter option because I can't imagine myself ever connecting anything to my car's battery for the purpose of drawing power. When plugged into the cigarette lighter, it powered a portable DVD player via the AC port while charging a Kindle through the USB port, thus proving its worth. While it won't shut down under non-optimal conditions, a blinking LED does alert you when the battery voltage drops below 10.5V, then the Inverter itself overheats or when the attached device attempts to draw more than 175W.My test drive (literally) revealed the following - I will prefix the positives with a '+' and the negatives with a '-'+ Small size - true, it would fit in a pocket without cables but I can't see why anyone would ever want to carry this in their pockets.+ Cables included, both the cigarette lighter and the battery clip cable and they are both long enough to be useful.+ Setup is quick and simple.+ Manual explains and illustrate the setup.+ Amazon's backing, including a 1 year warranty and Amazon's return policies and support are the best in the known Universe.- According to the manual (didn't happen while I was testing it) it does NOT shut itself down when overheated, when the battery output drops or when the attached device demands too much power.- Not exactly an elegant solution - our DVD player had its own AC/DC converter and we ended up with lots of wires and little gizmos on the back seats.- No carrying case or pouch makes it easy to misplace the cables. Does Amazon really believes that we are going to keep this in our pockets?I am going to rate Amazon's Inverter as a 4 stars (I like it but I don't love it). It's a good product but no little gadget that doesn't come with a case or a pouch to store 'it' and its accessories will ever deserve or get 5 stars.

I really love this inverter.  I've used other inverters that claim to provide 150 Watts or 175 Watts, but their claims are bogus (explained below).  And to find an inverter that offers this much payload at this low price is sweet!First of all, what's an inverter?The electrical system in your car, boat, or RV runs on a 12 volt DC system.  Your cigarette lighter outlet provides power at 12 volts DC.  This is fine for things like a phone charger that have a 12 volt DC plug, but what about items that you normally plug into the wall in your home or office?  Those devices run on 110 AC power.  The role of the inverter is to change (or "invert") the output from your car's electrical system from 12 volt DC to 110 volt AC.This AmazonBasics inverter provides a grounded 110 outlet for plugging in those household devices as well as a USB outlet for things like iPhones, iPads, etc. (which is a nice bonus).So what makes this inverter different?  First it's important to know that your vehicle's electric wiring isn't intended to run your toaster or hair dryer.  Even though an inverter might be designed to provide a high output for larger devices (like a TV or satellite receiver), your vehicle's poor little cigarette outlet can't handle the load.  I've used inverters that claim to support a higher load, and they either blow their own internal fuse, blow a fuse on the vehicle, or (worst case) don't blow any fuses and just burn out the wiring to that outlet.  That's bad.So the difference with this inverter is that it supports loads up to 130 watt through the cigarette lighter outlet.  For loads from 131 watts to 175 watts, there is a set of alligator style clips to connect directly to the vehicle's battery.There are plenty of other inverters out there that connect directly to the battery, but I've never seen one this compact and this inexpensive.Warning:  Only use the direct connection to the battery while your vehicle is parked.  Don't try to prop open your hood and drive down the road watching TV.Here's a little tip.  Before you purchase any inverter, look at your devices and see what their loads actually are.  Sometimes those specs are written in gobbledygook and are hard to decipher.  And some devices have two loads: the initial startup load and the actual running load. The startup load for this inverter cannot exceed 175 watts.  To be absolutely certain of the draw from your device or appliance, consider using something like thisKill A Watt Electricity Usage Monitor.  You plug the monitor into a wall outlet and then plug your device into the monitor.  The readout shows you the peak usage and the running usage.  If the peak draw is under 175 watts, then this inverter is OK for you.Bottom line, I'm very happy with this inverter.  It's the first one that I've ever had any success with at this wattage.  Just make sure not to overload the 12 volt DC outlet with more than 130 watts.  And don't use your toaster while you're driving down the road.

Amazon hit a homerun with this one.  We were debating purchasing a cigarette-lighter car-adapter power cord OR power inverter.  With a power inverter, it's a win/win.  You don't have to purchase special cigarette-lighter car-adapters (like for her Medela machine or my laptop), you just purchase 1 power inverter and plug in everything like you would in an electrical outlet in your house.  Otherwise, we would have had to purchase a cigarette lighter adapter separately for every device we wanted to use in a car.175watts is especially important!  That's a lot.  My new high-end work laptop only pulls 130watts.  The packaging mentions a TV/VCR, which seems exceptional, too.This comes with a cigarette lighter adapter as well as direct-battery connectors.  I don't think we'll ever need to pop the hood and directly connect this to the battery though, but it IS nice that they've supplied that.When it is on, you see a nice blue LED light and you can flip the device over if it's at night and you don't want to see the blue glow. reviewText: The Amazon basics 175W pocket power inverter is the lightest I've seen, weighing in at only 6.1 oz. with the cigarette lighter plug attached.  It is also quite small at 4" x 8" x 0.8", perfect for packing in your computer bag.  Besides powering your laptop, it also includes a USB port capable of supplying 2.1A, which plenty for charging a phone, iPad or just about any USB accessory.  I tested the little unit on my Dell laptop.  It powered it easily.  Next, I plugged in a 100W light bulb.  Again, no problem.  The unit has a fan that comes on as necessary to keep the unit cool.  With a 100W load (the light bulb) the fan ran continuously.  I found the fan to be rather loud and high pitched.  In a car, you may not care but the noise level is significant at 58dB at 1 foot (measured with my audio meter).  What I found odd is that the fan ran much faster when the load was reduced or removed.  For some reason, the voltage to the fan must drop significantly once a load is placed on the inverter.  While the inverter is rated at 130W continuous, you can't (or at least shouldn't) do that from a cigarette lighter socket.The manual is a little confusing.  It says you can run the inverter from the cigarette lighter for loads under 130W but also says for 120W-130W to use battery clamps (included) to hook it directly to the car's battery.  Personally, I wouldn't advise running it over 90W from a cigarette lighter socket.  At 90W output, the unit draws 10A from the socket.  That's okay, since most laptop power adapters require no more than 90W.  At 100W, it drew 11Amps, which is over the maximum continuous power most lighter sockets are rated (and fused).  I didn't test the unit it past 100W.If the unit was quieter, I would have given it 5 stars but for using in the car, you may be very happy and you will be hard pressed to find a more compact and light inverter.
summary: Very light weight but rather loud.

reviewText: An inverter is used to convert the power (12 volt DC) from your vehicle to 110 Volt AC which is what most electronic gizmos use to charge.  It supports up to 130 watts through the cigarette lighter (12v connector).  If you want to go higher voltage than 130 watts (175 watts is max with this device), alligator clips are included to attach directly to your car battery.  I haven't found that necessary in my life so have not tried it.I've used this inverter several times on long car trips to charge my Asus tablet & smart phone; worked great.  Yes, the cooling fan is a little obnoxious at first but I really don't notice it much anymore.It's compact so I keep it in the car all the time.  Good value for the money.

I used this to recharge an iphone and laptop and it worked very well.  The fan turns on under load and is noticable but not a big deal since the radio and road noise in my car drown it out.  The inverter is so small that a fan is a must to keep it cool.  Advantages to this unit are its small size which can fit in most compartments in a car, lightweight, relatively inexpensive and easy to connect and use. It also has a 2.1 Amp USB Port that is very handy to charge the phone or ipod. The negative is the noise of the fan and the unit must be unplugged from the power port in the car to turn it off.This is a very useful and easy to use inverter.  It can also be attached directly to the battery for heavier loads but I did not test that capability.UPDATE: 1/29/13: The power inverter's plug no longer works.  The electrical connectivity is intermitent.  If I move the wire it connects and then disconnects indicating a bad internal connection.  This inverter is just not durable enough for me to recommend it.  I have deducted 2 stars.

reviewText: In the limited time I have had the inverter my first impressions are favorable although the listed load capacity of 175w may be a bit misleading.My primary intended use is to provide on the go charge capability for a laptop that draws approximately 65w continuous power, well within the inverter's recommended range of not more than 120w when plugged a cigarette type 12v outlet. In instances where required power is more than 120w but not to exceed 130w continuous, the inverter should be clamped to vehicle battery terminals with the included clips. The upward range of 175w refers to the device's maximum supportable load for no more than 5 seconds in peak load situations.  Use for a device, or combination of devices, surpassing 130w is not recommended.This slim form device features one AC port and one USB port, a built-in cooling fan, 12v adapter cord and a battery clip cable but does not have a separate on/off switch. The fan is rather loud and seems to be engaged as soon as the device is attached to a power source.  At this point I cannot address long term reliability however I did notice the unit tends to heat up pretty quickly (the manual also indicates unit temperatures can reach 158 degrees Fahrenheit) although thus far neither the auto cutoff feature nor low voltage indicator lights have been activated during my use.It will support simultaneous power/charging of one USB and one AC device as long as the 130w maximum load continuous threshold is not exceeded. It is projected the inverter can be used for up to 2.5 hours before full depletion of a vehicle's battery charge is likely. Obviously, projected time will vary based on other factors like age, condition and existing charge of the battery itself.The manual further advises caution should be taken when using the inverter when cranking a vehicle's engine as the increase power required may negatively impact powering and charging.

I use this primarily to power a laptop (which draws only 75 Watts) as well as to charge my iPhone 4S. Here is why I like it:1. This is very lightweight and compact. I used to use an inverter made by Radio Shack that worked fine, but it was heavier and bulkier. It also had no cord and plugged directly into my cigarette lighter, which meant that I could not position where the AC outlet was. But since this unit has a cord that attaches from the unit to the cigarette lighter, I can easily position the AC outlet on this unit.2. This is easy to use. Just plug one end of the cord into the inverter, and the other end into the cigarette lighter (I actually plug a multi port charger into my cigarette lighter because that gives me multiple DC and USB outlets; I use one DC outlet for the inverter and the other for my GPS).3. Let me respond to some of the negative comments. reviewText: Tools needed:wirecutter, a screw driver, and electrical tape or cap.Total time: 20 minutesYou car has two types of voltage leads. One is constantly on (BAT), one is only on with the key (called "ACC"). The OBD2 readers get their power off the pin that is connected to the (BAT), so it's not shut off with the car, AND another pin that has power only when the car is on. BAT is ALWAYS pin #16, and ground is ALWAYS pin #5. The other pins are for sending and receiving data, and one is 12volts when the vehicle is on, but it varies by manufacturer.However, since you only need power when the vehicle is ON, just go ahead and follow Michi's diagram, but just extend the wire from the GREY harness to any 12v accessory wire (back of cig lighter is easy). Clip off the lead from the BLACK plug and cap off any wire that's left there. Now the unit will only have power when the car is on, and we don't even have to figure out which is pin is the ACC since it's already wired. Make sure you cap the wire off the BLACK plug on pin#16 tho, that way it doesn't spark when you turn it on.The only drawback here is that if you wanted to power a scanner up without the vehicle being started (which mechanics would want for sure), you can't. But for your purposes, you now have a BT adapter that only turns on with the car.tl;dr- cap black pin #16, run lead from grey harness inside the adapter to 12v ACC, done.
summary: ***Quick mod for automatic shutoff with key ***

reviewText: AmazonBasics Programmable Digital Tire GaugeThis tire gauge looks exactly like the newer Accu-Tire programmable gauge. The first thing you should understand is that the programmable aspect is just a reminder. Whether you actually program the gauge is not significant, I found that it doesn't really serve a purpose when I use the gauge on 4 different cars and a motorcycle which all have different tire pressures. For instance, one car has 32 psi front/rear while the motorcycle is supposed to be filled to 32.9 psi in the front and 36.9 psi in the rear. This Amazon tire gauge only reads tire pressure in increments of 0.5 psi, just like other digital tire gauges.The Amazon gauge is rather large, heavy, and bulky. There are rubberized coatings on some parts of the gauge to provide a better grip. It automatically reads the tire pressure when you hook it up to a Schrader valve on a tire. It quickly resets, but not so quickly that you don't have time to register the reading. The SET button allows you to manually reset it for the next reading.I compared the readings on this gauge with myCampbell Hausfeld AU110000AV 99 PSI Key Chain Digital Tire Gauge, and they matched exactly. I compared the readings to that of the on-board TPMS on one of my Chevy cars and it was within 1 psi.My biggest complaint with the Amazon gauge is the "release valve". I purchased this thinking there was an actual release button so I could release air and check the readings in real-time. Unfortunately, it is just a machined nub that pushes in the Schrader valve on your tires. The seal on the gauge isn't that great and requires careful alignment to ensure no leaks.That said, the release valve nub came in handy. I have a set of tires on a car that have Schrader valves with really short stems that don't seem to accept the ends of the caps or even my finger nails. The nub on this Amazon gauge was able to release the air without any problems.The Amazon gauge was also perfectly compatible with all of my vehicles, and the swivel top allows you to use it in odd/hard to reach locations. The backlit LCD display is also easy to read as long as you keep the display at a flat angle to your face. Apparently the polarization is very strong because if I tilted it a few degrees away from my face in any direction, the text disappears.The Amazon gauge comes with a semi-rigid zippered case that makes it handy to keep in your glove box or in a purse/bag, or a tool kit. The instruction manual states that it uses a pair of CR2032 lithium coin-cell batteries, which are more resilient against temperature extremes and have a decent storage life (3-5 years).Overall: 4/5 stars, rather pricey but seems to be very ruggedized. Swivel top makes it versatile enough to reach all odd-ball valve locations. I honestly could live with using my cheap Campbell-Hausfeld keychain gauge even though it isn't as fancy as this Amazon gauge. Also, it looks like this gauge is just a rebranded Accu-Tire gauge.
summary: Same as the Accu-Tire brand tire gauge, lots of useful features

reviewText: I love this little gadget.  It's heavy duty, well designed, feels solid in your hand.  The head swivels as needed, and there's even a built-in light. Nice bright led display with large numbers, easy to read.  Comes in a very nice padded case, so it will be safe to store in your trunk or glove box, or anywhere in your garage.  Very nice quality, I'm impressed!

This seems to be a quality item and when I can get it to seat/seal on the valve stem, I get accurate readings compared to my other gauges. It is easy to program, but it is difficult to properly seat on the stem.

I got tired of those "pencil" gauges that hardly ever are accurate.  And such a pain to use.  You can easily push this on and wait to not hear the hiss of escaping air and then the pressure is easy to read.Those complaining about not being able to figure out how to program it was not an issue for me.  I know what the tire pressure is supposed to be so I never intended to "program" it.I do have one observation however.  I have a TPMS on my 5th wheel and it's readouts on all four tires are 3 pounds less than this gauge.  I tried another gauge I had and it said about the same readout as this gauge.  Now, I'm concerned.  Could the usually reliable TPMS be off or is it this gauge.  At least the TPMS even if 3 pounds less would still let me know of any pressure/temperature issue.

I am a fanatic about maintaining the pressure in my tires. I also follow MY recommended pressures, not the manufacturer's (I run a few psi over spec). Add to that that I live in a temperate zone, as most all of us in North America do... and I get a lot of use from tire pressure gauges.I have used digital, graduated stick type, and high accuracy dial type over the years. Each has it's advantages (although a stick type's only advantage is that it fits in your pocket easily, as they are not very accurate). But I like the combination of accuracy and ease of use provided by a good digital gauge. Easier to read, and often easier to use.This gauge is the best I've ever had - at far below the price of some I've owned. It takes only seconds to register your pressure, which is displayed in large numbers with an illuminated back screen. It holds the reading for 10 seconds. The angle of the head and size of the unit are well designed, making it easier to make good contact with the valve stem than many others I've used (nothing I hate more than bleeding air while trying to get a good seal with a gauge). There is even a small LED flashlight feature that is useful if you are trying to work in the dark.You can pre-set the desired pressures for your front and rear tires into the gauge to serve as a reminder. These setting don't actually perform any function (such as telling you how much over/under you are), which would be a nice design upgrade... but it is useful for those who don't easily remember the prescribed pressures.The bleeder side of the head (used to let air out of the tires) is a little awkward to use, due to the angle. But it is still useful. The case for the gauge is actually very nice and zips closed. It has enough padding to protect the gauge, should it be dropped on the road or garage floor. The feel of the tool is good - very ergonomic. I rate this gauge five stars because it excels at everything I need in a tire pressure gauge, and the odd bleeder angle is not enough of a problem to take away a star. I love it!
Easy to read; light and portable; very nice durable case.  Can be set to remember the correct pressure. Highly recommended.

I saw this gauge and I had to jump all over it.  It was an identical clone to an old faithful Sears Craftsman design - down to the screen an LED lamp.  They stopped selling that one about 5 years ago and went to a new design, and I was forced to use inferior gauges.It's accurate, easy to use, with the swiveled head, and easy to carry on the motorcycle in a pouch.The carrying case is also helpful too to insulate it against temperature extremes (more the sun shining directly on it.

THE PRODUCT ARRIVED ON TIME AND IN PERFECT CONDITION. THE READOUT IS LARGE ENOUGH AND CLEAR AND THE SWIVEL HEAD PROVIDES EASY VIEWING FROM ANY POSITION OF THE VALVE STEM. MY 2 STAR RATING IS BECAUSE AFTER CHECKING MY FIRST TIRE, THE VALVE FITTING CAME OFF OF THE GAUGE. I DID NOT WANT TO GO THROUGH THE HASSLE OF EXCHANGING IT SO I SUPER GLUED IT ON AND IT HAS HELD, AND IT WORKS. FOR WHAT LOOKS TO BE A WELL MADE GAUGE, I WAS DISAPPOINTED.FOLLOW-UP 6/8/13  I CHANGED MY RATING FROM 2 STARS TO 5 STARS BECAUSE I WAS SENT A REPLACEMENT AND IT IS WORKING PERFECTLY AND HAS NOT FALLEN APART.

I'm quite picky about keeping tire pressures right where I want it. Naturally, I check PSI at least once a month, and whenever we have a sudden temperature drop. I've had plenty of vehicles with onboard PSI read-outs, but those are by no means 100% accurate. So having a good tire gauge is very important. My current "go to" gauge was theAccutire MS-4021B Standard Digital Tire Gauge. It was basic, as it only provided the PSI, no LED light, buttons, etc. But it worked. I never had issues with getting a seal. The one I wanted to be my favorite is theAccutire MS-4350B Programmable Digital Tire Gauge. That had all of the features I liked such as a light, back-lit display, memory for tire pressures, etc. But, it wouldn't always get a good seal with every tire. Some worked well, others, not so much.Then along comes the Amazon Digital Tire Gauge. It basically combines all of the features I want/need, and then some. You have a swivel head (no more awkward angles), air-bleed knob on the back, back-lit display, LED light, and memory that will let you store front/rear tire PSI so you don't have to dig around your owners manual or check a dirty door jamb.I was skeptical it could do everything it claims, and do so reliable. So I've been using this for about a month between various vehicles and every tire I could get my hands on to get a solid feel for it. After all, not all air stems are created equal. But I'm pleased to report that it's been working perfectly. It always gets a solid seal and I don't have to keep moving it around to prevent air leakage.Pros:* Rotating head* Back-lit LCD* Programmable PSI for front/rear* LED Light* Air bleed knob* Bonus: It comes with a case.Cons:* The case could be sturdier so the LED light switch doesn't accidentally get squeezed.It's rare when I don't post a real "con" for a review. I naturally assume there is always *something* that could be improved on or isn't working perfectly. In this instance, the only slight negative is the free cheap case. And that's not even really an issue for me. :) But it sounds like Amazon really did their homework on this one. I consider this highly recommended.

reviewText: Received these right on time, I put them on myself (I'm a 54 yr old woman) just used blue painters tape to line them up correctly, took about 30 min. They look great!
The quality is great and construction is well done giving a perfect fit to the window frame.  The adhesive is strong and has held up.
Easy to install, works great.  Only issue I had was that they came in a relatively easy box, placed inside of a coffin sized box.  Came off the truck, I had no idea what was gonna be in it lol.
I was unable to install these so I had my local Chrysler dealership install them. I noticed that each front one is cracked, but too late to claim it. I had easier installs with WeatherTech
These are awesome. They were a snap to install and build quality is as expected. Rugged Ridge is quickly becoming one of my go to vendors for Jeep stuff.

Got this to tow my 28' travel trailer. Well made. Easy to  put together. Only thing I had an issue with is the bolts for the ball mount need to be torqued to 260 lb's and as most of us don't have a torque wrench for this application we'll need to ensure that it's done to manufactures spec - given it is critical for towing safety. Your local RV service center can do this for you. Mine did it for free, but it might cost you another 50 bucks to have it properly torqued.I do love it and I am VERY happy with the purchase. By far, based upon my research, this offers the best value for the tow and hitch weight. My brother-in-law has a $600.00 setup that for all intents and purposes is really not nearly as nice as this one. He helped me put it all together at his place and really like it.Works great with my Nissan Armada LE 4x4

This thing is heavy duty! It does include a SOLID shank and high grade bolts. The box was damaged when I received it but this thing weighs well over 75lbs total so the cardboard didn't stand a chance. All of the hardware was in a bag that was zip tied to something so nothing was lost or damaged.It took me about 1 hour to install on my 26' travel trailer, but most of that time was spent looking for an 11/32 drill bit to install the sway control bracket to the trailer. Other than that bracket, everything else is bolt on. The weight distribution clamps that bolt onto the trailer do not seem very tight when you tighten the single bolt against the tongue, but the instruction state this up front and assure you that it will be tight once you lock in the chains. I can attest that once the chains are lock in properly, they aren't going to move a bit.I have experience with much more expensive setups and I know believe that they are a waste of money for most people. If you have serious sway issues or you a tow a billion miles a year, a setup with built-in sway control instead of friction (like this one) may better fit your needs but I have no issues pulling my 26' TT with my 2006 Yukon Denali XL and this setup. Even though the Denali's air shocks level out the trailer, the Camco keeps it from porpoising (bobbing up and down) due to the soft ride shocks.
summary: don't waste money on a more expensive one

reviewText: First time trailer owner and was given great advice.  The difference is amazing.  I would not tow without this set!

When I bought my 23' travel trailer I did not think I needed one of these hitches. I drive a diesel 2002 F350 with air bag helpers in the rear. I had owned a 34' fifth wheel that my truck pulled like a dream. I figured this little bumper pull would be no problem at all. Boy was I wrong. The front of my truck seemed to be gliding over pot holes and such like I was a giant ship in the water. Really uncomfortable at times. This hitch system really leveled things out. The whole setup seems smoothed out.

First of all... shank is included! This is incredible. What a fantastic buy. My rv dealer wanted $800 to install hitch, almost did.... This is a quality product... SUPER HEAVY! I could not recommend more. I have a 2007 Dodge 1/2 ton quad, and 27' Crossroad zinger. A crazy good buy.
summary: I was scared and skeptical, got a wonderful surprise.

reviewText: Pro's-Easy to install with the right tools (specifically a drill bit that will allow you to drill 6 holes through the trailer frame for the anti-sway bar-Easy to hook up after the first time (the first time takes a little bit extra because you have to find the right height for the trailer to sit level with your vehicle)Con's-The brackets that stay on the trailer and have the chain connect to them are not very secure. While driving you have the weight of the bars holding them in place. If the trailer is not connected the brackets can become loose. They basically just sit over the fram rail and have a bolt on the back to tighten them in place. The bolt can work itself out over time. It also leaves a lot of wear marks on the frame from the bolt moving around while driving.-The drop bar that came with the set is perfect for an SUV or small truck (we used it on our 99 Suburban). When I sold the Suburban and got a 2001 F-250 Turbo Diesel I had to purchase a bar with the lower drop to get the trailer to sit level. The bar was an additional $100. My truck is not lifted or anything, it just sits higher than an SUV. Keep this in mind depending on what you are putting it on. Make sure to measure your hitch drop to make sure you get the right stuff up front.

If you have a trailer, spend the money and get this.  Even if you think you're fine without one, get one.  It helps with gas mileage, keeps your front tires on the ground, keeps the trailer from swaying like crazy when passing large vehicles. It makes towing so much safer.

I bought this to replace my lost O2 sensor socket. These worked great on my OEM O2 sensor and my UEGO wideband sensor I installed. Those things are expensive to replace so using the right tool makes it so you don't have to worry about rounding off the weak socket or stripping it. They also allow you to connect to a torque wrench and get the sensor to the proper torque specs.

Okay, got this kit when I replaced the oxygen sensor in my neighbor's 2003 Chrysler Town & Country LXi FWD 3.8L V6 OHV 12V.If you search for Standard Motor Products Oxygen Sensor http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000C81R0C/ref=wms_ohs_product) on Amazon, you'll read a more detailed account of how I used this kit in this application.Basically, the socket with the large opening was a lifesaver to install over the sensor, that was out in the open but inaccessible with a standard wrench, with the sensor wire though the slot. Got it out and back in quickly and painlessly.My application required a looong extension to reach the sensor that was down in the engine compartment, with a ratchet from over the top of the engine.
summary: Would not have gotten the sensor in and out so easily without this kit!

reviewText: The wax went on easily and quite thinly (after warming it up per the instructions) and it buffed off very easily as well. Decided to give this wax a try as a friend had recommended it to me. I am now using on all 3 of my vehicles after a test period on one of my older vehicles. Still testing the duration of the wax for have only been using for about a month now but even if I had to reapply every 2 months I would be happy. The autos still bead water like I had just waxed them yesterday and I frequently was and clean my vehicles. It is a soft and very easy wax to apply and to take off making it a breeze to wax you vehicle. I have already placed an additional order for more wax.

Lasts about six months for me. Holds up pretty well in wintertime. Can be used as a one step product or part of a multi step process of your choosing. Pleasant smell and very easy to work with when brought up to the right temperature. It works really well when it is in a liquid or runny consistency. If the product is thick when you open the cap, put the bottle in the sun while you wash your ride. Will not take long to liquify this wax. You use less product and less time when you do it right.Shine is durable and beads up for several months. 4 mos is ideal but 6 months is acceptable for a time limit on this wax. Many friends now use this wax after watching me use this product. Money well spent.

Overview: Collinite No.845 has a reputation as a very durable wax, thought I would need another brand as a top coat for deep shine but I was wrong, looks great by itself.This is not a cleaner wax! You need to prep surface for good result(clay/chemical polish)Pros:* Exceptionally reflective <3* expected to last at least 3 months outdoors(will confirm later)* Fills in fine swirls and scratches* Easy application with soft foam applicator(Tips below)* Easy to buff off* Multiple coats are great* great on windows/mirrors and wheels!* Doesn't haze on plastic trim like some waxes.* Relatively in expensive* 1-2 ounces coats a small car using foam pad.Cons:* Smell isn't great,but not terrible either. At least compared to other waxes (Not all that important though)* Bottle has safety cap, and no nozzle to dispense(Fix below)* Has to be shaken vigorously to get a proper mixture of solvent to waxTips: USE GLOVES!!! Car care products have nasty chemicals and solvents you don't need in your blood stream.1. Wax is solid at 70*F and colder. Heat wax using warm water on the outside of the bottle to get it viscous. Shake well, Get a sauce dispenser (Photo available in gallery)and pour contents into the dispenser. this will make it easier to put onto applicator pad/MF towel.2. Prep surface before applying wax by washing, claying, then prewax polishing.(this applies to all non cleaner waxes)3. Waxing step: always warm the wax by putting the sauce bottle in a bowl of warm water (water at 90*F works well) and shake well before putting onto a pad. (Soft foam Pads work better than MF pads or towels IMO)4. Use up and down patterns with low pressure for waxing, do not do circles (Will prevent swirls). work the wax into the paintmaking  with the pad making sure complete coverage.5. Allow to haze (takes about 10-20 minutes)6. buff off the haze with a MF towel in the same up and down pattern using light pressure and fast short strokes7. For Best results do another coat 12 hrs later (If not possible you can wait an hr)8. Enjoy the ShineHave tried  turtle spray wax, eagle spray wax, mothers California gold glaze and carnauba wax, chemical guys butter wet wax (Looks spectacular but fragile). Wont be using those anymore.
summary: Great wax, Tips and tricks for application

reviewText: I installed this easily on my '13 Wrangler. Yes, it is easiest to remove the spare tire and yes, you will need to grind some of the powder coat off to get a good ground. To reduce the possibility of rusting while providing a good ground, I got a 99 package of the electrode lubricant at my local auto parts store. I put it on the area I ground down with my Dremel and am still getting good readings.

When I went to install this I just had a huge laugh at how insanely thick and solid this is.  It's not going anywhere and won't give you any bounce or flex.  It appears to be 1/4" steel.  Installs in three minutes.  You do need to scrape off some of the paint with sandpaper so your antenna mount can get a good ground connection.

My only complaint is that the bolts are silver in color, instead of black like all the other hardware on the Jeep.  Major oversight Rugged Ridge!  Heavy duty, nice wrinkle coat finish.  Mounts perfectly behind spare tire and the sliver bolts are not evident to the on-looker.  Nice clean, easy installation, positions the antennae perfectly to run the coax into the tailgate and through the hole provided by Jeep.  Very happy with the product.

reviewText: The unit is very rugged and looks as if it will be around longer than I will be.  As others have stated, when mounted on the Jeep Wrangler Unlimited Sport it is approx. 3 deg off of being completely horizontal.  But with the number of different models of jeep that are around it seems to be very close.  I was able to shim the antenna slightly and get it close to vertical.  As an engineer everything needs to at the correct orientation or it will bug me to no end.  But I am happy with the unit.  I would have been willing to spend slightly more money to get Rugged Ridge to have a unit that is adjustable and to have a grounding bolt as part of the unit.I know that the unit is also meant for flags, but I would think that since it is also sold as a CB antenna mount that the buyer would not have to sand off the powder coating to get a ground.

First off, let me start by saying that this is a very high quality product. I've purchased several items from Rugged Ridge for my 11' Jeep Wrangler Unlimited:Side stepsTrailer hitch mountTail light brush protectorsetc.This item is just as high quality as the rest of those. However there is one major functional issue that I think the manufacturer overlooked - You need a way to ground this mount to the vehicle so that you can lower the SWR of your CB setup without damaging your CB equipment. If you're using this for an off-road flag mount or to mount a 'no ground plane' antenna then its perfect. However if like most people you're going to mount a CB antenna which requires a good ground plane, then you're going to have to make some modifications to be able to ground this.Basically what I did was take a hammer and chisel and scrape off the powder coating down to the metal around the left hole. I then used that hole to mount another stud which connects to a grounding strap. Then on the underside of the right hold (where your coax cable ground shield will touch) I scraped the powder coating off of there down to the bare metal as well. Then I was able to run my ground strap from the left hole through my tailgate and onto the metal surface of my Jeep.I tried this setup the first time without doing that and my SWR was around 2.5 - 3.5 depending on the channel, I could not get it any better. After doing this my SWR is between a 1.0 (perfect) and 1.2 on all channels.My setup is:FireStik II antenna (tunable tip)FireStik mount studFireStik 18' coax cableFireStik SS-3H HD springMy stock spare tire (255 75R17) is also slightly contacting the antenna which may be an issue. I plan to purchase the FireStik quick disconnect which will raise the antenna a few inches and hopefully reduce the contact. The contact is not doing anything to impact my SWR, however it could potentially damage the antenna at some point. Also with it touching the tire, the spring isn't going to do much if you hit something over-head head-on, because the antenna can only flex back so much. I wish Rugged Ridge had done a little additional R&D; before they rolled this item out due to that and the issue with grounding.

Bolts on easy enough.  Like others have mentioned it isn't "level" and your antenna will tilt.  Furthermore, any antenna I would have used wouldn't have cleared the stock Jeep spare tire so I had to make a modification (another bracket) to mount to this one.  If I had to do it over again, I would have just made my own bracket in the beginning.
