Used in my 2010 Nissan Altima 4dr.These bulbs are BRIGHT, end of story! For the $$$ you just cannot go wrong.
summary: Now I need sunglasses to look in the mirror.

reviewText: Replaced the courtesy mirror incandescent bulbs in my 2013 Subaru Legacy with these LEDs.  They are an exact fit, and are VERY bright, with a very slight blue tint. I would describe them as about 6500K in color.  They are bright enough that if you are driving at night, you don't want to accidentally flip up the vanity mirror  because you will loose your night vision.  Otherwise, they are much better than the dim yellow light provided by the incandescent bulbs.
I like these, they are much brighter than stock.  They put a a slight white-bluish hue but it's still much better than stock.
This gauge is top notch very good quality feels good in hand should last a long time as long as you dont run it over.. HA

This works great and seems to be accurate compared to my other gauges. The only weird thing is that the pressure gauge itself runs off of a small button cell battery (included) but the light runs off AAA batteries (not included).
summary: Works great, needs two types of batteries

reviewText: Gauge is simple in construction and is simple to use. It is doing what I bought it to do.Quality of construction appear adequate.

The gauge is good quality and construction. I love the lighted tip and backlit display as it makes working in poorly lit areas a breeze. One minor complaint is that the unit turns off too quickly in my opinion. I know the feature is to save battery but it does get annoying to have to keep turning it back on after filling the tires with a compressor. All-in-all, this is a great product that I would buy again if I had the chance to do it over.

Works dang good, has light at end for seeing yourself to the tire stem. Has backlit screen showing tire pressues in lbs or other increments. Cuts off after a minute or so or you can hold down and turn off. So far has been better than most Accuair gauges.

This is one little unit that does exactly what it say it will do. Very easy to operate and as far as I can tell, is quite accurate.  Since I am pulling a 38' 5th wheel, knowing the air pressure in both the truck and trailer tires is really important. This device makes the process very quick and easy.
This has other measurements other than psi that get my way but it appears to work alright, have to toggle between BAR, PSI and etc. not dig'n that a lot but it's ok, do like the idea it lights up

In my garage my wife's SUV's left rear door hits the left front fender of my car with the very corner which is above the wheel, and I already have 4 dents to remember my wife by.  To avoid the 5th dent I decided to try this film.The film softens the hit, but, I think, there is still a very good possibility that the door's corner will make that dreaded fifth dent in my fender.  Basically, the film protects the door edge from chipping, but does very little to protect another vehicle's body in cases when your car's door hits another car.  I think that, unfortunately, no matter how much I dislike those short fat tube looking door edge guards, I will have to get one of them for my wife's SUV to protect my car.On the positive side, the film was easy to apply, just make sure to clean surfaces first.  However, it is quite expensive at ten bucks for two doors.As a note, both of our cars are black, so I do not think it is an issue for us, however, based on my experience with clear door guards and any "stick-ons" to the car, I am pretty sure the film will accumulate dirt around the edge and the outline will become visible on a light colored vehicle.  Also, if the film yellows from sun and weather (like headlight lenses for example), it will look terrible on a light colored car.Overall, albeit expensive, this is a good way to protect your car's door edge, if this is all you need.
summary: Expensive for what it is.  May become visible on light-color cars.

reviewText: Asked my electric guy to apply and he did it wrong thinking that it is not that wide, this one looks like as if it is 1/2".On a video they demonstrate much wider film. I had it applied properly on second door but not sure if it will stick there.

Applies very easily as long as you clean the surface real well and do the job in an enclosed environment (garage).  Wouldn't dare try outdoors since even a gentle breeze could tangle up the tape rendering it useless.  Those wondering how invisible it is - well, try sticking a piece of clear packing tape to your car and see how that compares as this is essentially what it is, just much thicker, stickier, and doesn't curl up so easily.  Beware that if you apply to rear doors, since most cars are very curvy today the standard length for passenger cars might not be long enough.  Front doors are okay though.  Overall, remains to be seen how effective some thick packing tape on the door edge will hold up over wear and tear with car washes, weather, and such.
summary: Install easily, anyone can do it

reviewText: I've had it on now for a few weeks. Hard to say if it works because I had no knicks along the door to begin with so all I can say is it still has none. Only a long time will tell if it keeps working but I can say that it sticks well, even after going through the automatic car wash with it's big brushes several times and is clear so you don't notice it is even on the car, my car is white and I never notice it at all. It was easy to put on by myself and I'm not that handy with these sort of things.

I own a fleet of vehicles and they sometimes get parked VERY CLOSE together. This film is easy to apply to clean door edges. I love that it helps to prevent chips as well, as I have a car with a few chips. For the price, you really can't go wrong, this is a must have for my vehicles!
Not bad - does the job would be nice to have a bit wider sizes…can be a little tight to put on.  But seem to work well - durably made. Will protect.  A little tough not to show on a black car.
These are easy to use. We applied them to my Vintage Lincoln sedan. It is black in color, and these work perfectly. They've already prevented at least one door from chipped paint along the edge.

The saying you get what you pay for fits. This is an expensive solution to protecting your door from chipping. How it works is you put a strip of semi-adhesive material along the edge of your door. It's not like packing tape but more rubbery. The problem with this is yes it will protect the edge of your door from paint flaking off if you ding it, however this won't protect your door from dents or larger dings like the thicker, rubber trim will that you can buy. So yes this will work to keep the paint in place and provide a bit of protection, but in my opinion this really isn't worth the money, it provides too little protection.I applied it to a Honda ridge-line truck, I have 4 doors and only got one set so 2 doors are protected, 2 are not. It's important you clean both the front, edge and back side of the door where the film sticks otherwise it will fall off.Once applied the film blends so you can hardly see it's on.Now I am not going to ding my door to test this, but from initial inspections it doesn't look like it does much good. It's like putting laminated piece of paper on your stomach and then getting hit. You are still going to feel it, its still going to damage but it will soften the blow....a little....It's a nice idea but for me this should be marketed as a "as seen on TV" item for those late night TV shoppers. It's a novelty item to give you the illusion of protection. If you want real protection you need something thicker and more substantial.
summary: You get what you pay for...  Seems more like a novelty item

reviewText: If you want max protection from major slams, this product is not for you. But if you want something that is nearly invisible and will protect your paint from chips due to careless door opening this fits the bill nicely. It's just a heavy strip of clear plastic with maximum stick adhesive. Installation, no prob, go slowly and peel as you go to a clean door edge and you are done. It stretches a little so you can turn slightly without wrinkles. I find doing the outside in it's entirety first, then folding it over the edge second, gives the best results.It's no intellectual dilemma, if you buy this don't expect it to protect your paint when you slam your door into a stucco wall. But if you only slightly bump into a lawn mower in your garage it it serves quite nicely.

Be clear on what this is.  It is - essentially - a tape that goes along the outside vertical edge of your door.  It does not protect you from dents or door dings from other cars.  If you park in a garage with cinderblock walls (like I do) then this will keep you from chipping the paint on the edge of your doors.  Application is fairly straight-forward - clean the paint first.  Once properly applied, you really can't see it too easily.  One word of caution; dont apply it in the cold - warm up the strip before applying it.
summary: Only protects the edge, not side, of your door

reviewText: My previous experience with door edge guards is with plastic U-channels that slide into position on the edge of a car door. Those work well, but are highly visible (ugly.)This product is more like a thick semi-sticky plastic tape. It isn't all that hard to apply properly, but does require SOME skill. My first mistake was in only cleaning the outside of the car door beforehand. Since the tape is intended to fold over and also stick on the inside edge of the door, that too must be well cleaned beforehand. Once that was done, my results were excellent, in a total time of under 10 minutes. If you look very carefully from a few feet away the tape is barely visible - further away, it's entirely unnoticeable to me. Good to know my car doors are now invisibly protected.Other pointers:1) don't install over a sharp bend in the door. The tape is forgiving of minor changes in direction, but has nowhere to go in a 90 degree bend. I solved that by starting below that bend, which is fine as the tape still covers anything that might hit another object as the door opens.2) If you need to shorten the tape (as I did), you may find it easiest to cut at a 45 degree diagonal from both directions, and then finish with a 90 cut between the diagonals - in other words, in the shape of 3 sides of a stop sign. That more easily approximates the rounded edge of the original tape.3) If you care about existing nicks in the door edge, fix those first. As my 2002 Prius is a decade old this month, I didn't bother.Finally, if your car has 4 doors, you'll need two of these kits.
summary: Works well. Takes a bit of skill to apply

reviewText: We chose 3M 08582 36" Door Edge Protection Film for our 10 year old Dodge Grand Caravan which is still in great shape. The product was easy enough to install after cleaning and drying the door edges, and it seems to stick nicely with a quality feel to it. The one thing I will say is that this does not look like it will protect against anything more than very minor dings and scrapes when opening your door. If you swing your door open and hit something full force, this will most likely not protect against damage from that. Still, if you're concerned with the possibility of minor scruffs, this may provide you some piece of mind.Is this necessary for most vehicles? Probably not, as long as you're careful opening your car doors. If you really want this type of protection, understand that this is a quality product but not a miracle worker and you should be satisfied with your purchase.

This 3M Door Edge Protection Film contains two strips of virtually invisible clear thin and strong Edge Paint Protection Films which has adhesive on one side and clear plastic on the other. The Adhesive helps to stick on the car's door edges and stay put if applied properly and thereby protecting the paint surface from accidental scratches or dings.From my observation using this product it was clear that the material is not thick enough to take serious abuse of the door against unwanted bumps into other objects. This was clearly intended as sort of "peace of mind" for people who love and care for their "new" car and are extremely conscious about slightest dings and scratches on their shiny newly purchased car.I know, I know I have gone thru' this before when I had bought my car years ago even a single scratch or even a bird droppings on the windshield would make me upset. This product is for people who would like to protect their investment from possible daily bumps and accidental scratches to their car's door edges.Applying the product does require high degree of dexterity. It can be complex if your car has multiple bends and curves. But with patience and a steady hand most users of the product can apply the clear tape with relative ease.Just make sure that the surface of the car is clean of grease and is dry before applying. It is intended to be a permanent solution. So after applying if you want to peel the Film be prepared for some surprises like glue sticking to your door etc;The product itself is "3 star" [It is OK] worth. But the price factor pulls one star out of the 4 star rating [I like it]. I think it is worth half the price that is being currently offered. If 3M included 4 strips for 10 dollars it would be a 4 star product.But hey! if you love your car and care about not getting scratched or paint chipped off your door, you will pay anything for it right? - May be.. May be not...! depending on what type of car you have and what is the current condition of the car.This Protection film might have other uses too.. basically any metallic shiny painted surface which needs protection can benefit from this industrial grade clear tape.
summary: If you love your car you will like it!

reviewText: When my wife bought a new Honda Fit earlier this year, we had asked the dealer to install door edge film. Afterward they said it looked awful, took it off and refunded our money. I still wanted protection, not only for her car but also mine, so I bought the 3M kit here. I just installed the film on both cars and am absolutely delighted. The film installed very easily and conformed to bends and even tight curves in the door edge. If you're more than a few inches away, you can't see it at all. The film is thick and resilient and should do well to protect the door edges against nicks and scrapes.

Looks ok, and stays on. I haven't banged by door yet so I can't comment on the quality of protection, but it sure gives me a piece of mind the next time someone decides to be careless with opening my door.
I like the look of it but it fits loose and I had to use zip ties so it wouldn't flap around when Im riding.

the material seems durable, if it breaks down ill repost...simple, and roomy.  Straps are what you would expect. simple straps.I think it could use an addtional strap to hold the bottom end in place...It should be said the size indicated is wrong.14x4x4" but in actuality it is 14.25x3.75x5.5, the first 2 measurements being within an reasonable amount of error is fine by me, but the last 5.5 tall when i thought 4, just didn't allow me to mount the bag where i thought i could.And being that i dont like bags hanging off my chopped down bobber as it is, i didnt like having to mount it in an more open space, that and it being any larger than i thought it was left me a bit disapointed...None the less, so cheap and decently made, its not going back...I dont want to detract from the bag just becuase the size is wrong, but i dont know if this deserves the 4 starts i gave it... it was good enough to keep, and at this point i cant identify a flaw... so

I bought this bag due to the high ratings.  I received the bag yesterday and not really amazed by it.  It says leather "Shell" but I doubt it.  It doesn't feel or looks like a real leather to me.  It looks a lot rougher than it shows in the picture.The original plan was to put it on the fork on my 04' VTX1300c but it doesn't work.  I don't blame the bag because it clearly states that it is for handle bars.  But the bag is pretty big to go on the handle bars.  I could easily put an Arizona Ice tea can in it with some extra space.  So I ended up putting it on the back of the sissy bar.Pros:- Big- Sturdy- Low PriceCons:- Very stiff (like plastic stiff)UPDATE (9/17/2013)After using it for about 15 miles on the sissy bar, it scratches the pain of my fender because of the hard material they call "Leather".  See the Pictures that I put up.
summary: Fuel Helmets SH-BARBAG Black Fuel Handlebar Bag

reviewText: I wanted this on my handlebars but would not fit, I mounted on the windshield above the headlight. It looks good and fits my wallet, phone, gum, lock, and sunglasses case and it is full. Hope it last, quality seems decent.

This made of a somewhat cheap material, but it seems good enough to keep using. I use it for a padlock, gloves, a couple bungees, and cigarettes, so it's not huge. Would also work to fit an emergency tool kit with just a few wrenches and a pair of pliers.

I liked this so much that I ordered a second one for my other bike. It's large enough to carry the tools I need. I found it is better to use zip ties instead of the leather straps that come with them when you attach them to the handle bars.

The straps that connect it to the handle bar are included. The bag itself is solid and well made, but the connecting straps are too thin compared to the solid construction of the bag. This bad is not made to go behind a windshield because of where the buckles are placed.

This is NOT a leather item.  It's pretty much 100% synthetic.  The photo in the add is clearly a leather pouch, but the one i got in the mail is definitely not.That being said, it's OK and it's a good value for the $12 I paid.  I'm going to mount it on my bike and just be happy with it.
Looks great ..easy to mount..I put it on my rack..very convenient...matches my saddle bags on my Yamaha Vstar 1100.
Not the thickess leather handlebar bag I've seen, but for the price if I get two or more years use out of it I'm way ahead

I bought for use on a Honda VTX1300c. It works well even though the attachment straps aren't quite at the right lcoation for my handlebar configuration. I do recommend it though. It has nice straps on the fron and appears to be well built. I've had it on my bike for about 200 miles thus far.
summary: Great size and very thick and rigid.

reviewText: Don't purchase this item the straps that hold it to your handlebars are so thin you find your tool bag flying away. Also don't place items in this bag you want there is no way to secure it from anybody from opening it unless you wrap it with a chain and lock. Go to your nearest Motorcycle Store and purchase your moneys worth and know you stuff is secure when you are away from your bike.
Great tool bag. How ever i found the leather to be a little bit hard. I didnt use it long before I removed it but maybe it will soften up after a few or many opeaning and closings.

This is a five star SH-BARBAG Black Fuel Handlebar Bag. Very nice and ridgid. Opens easily. Just an all round nice bag. I dont know if it is leather or not, but It looks like it is. Nice 5 stars to this vendor. Thanks AJL
summary: Five star bag all the way...

reviewText: Added this to my Honda CT90 Trail bike's handle bars.  Now everyone calls it my 'purse'.  Looks pretty gay and will go with a pink helmet....

The gauge is accurate and it speaks the truth! Kinda fun and it doesn't cost much more than the mute version. I compared this gauge to a theoretically much more accurate gauge and the results were identical (i.e., within 0.5 psi - the resolution of this gauge). Get one and amaze the wife and kids. Well, maybe not amaze but perhaps amuse; at least for a few seconds.

This item serves it's purpose.  You have to be careful to get a good fit over the tire valve, but then that is also necessary with traditional gauges.  The numbers are easy to read and I have no problem clearly hearing the voice telling the pressure even when not  wearing my hearing aid.  It is plastic and I think it could easily be broken if one is not careful, but that is workable.  A friend liked mine so much that they immediately ordered one for themself.  Highly recommend.
This is a good digital tire pressure gauge. Mostly plastic which makes it a kuttke ddifficult to get on the valve and it may not be all that accurate.
summary: Anytime Tools 100+1 Piece Tamper Proof/security Screwdriver Bits

reviewText: You get what you pay for.  The talking is probably unnecessary, but the price was right and it works fine.

Only 4 stars because:The language toggle button is right where you press with your thumb on the handle to press this gauge into the tire's valve.  Also, it doesn't curve enough to get quite in between the tire spokes of motorcycle wheels
If you get tired of trying to guess what your tire pressure is with the manual guages, this tool is for you. Works great.

I bought this on a whim because the new tire pressure monitors in newer model cars can put a scare in you,sometimes arbitrarily.(tire pressure drops in ratio to lower temperatures).I have a hard time reading the old gauges,& sometimes affixing them properly to the valve stem.Happy to say this little gem is easy to attach,reads PSI accurately & clearly. I calibrated it & It's fine out of the box.Batteries are cheap enough.Don't know the life expectancy,but most gauges do act up in time.I am going to buy a few for stocking stuffers,especially for my older friends and my "girls".Highly recommend

It is accurate to within .5 PSI.  It announces the tire pressure and is easy to attach. I checked all four tires and the spare. Now satisfied all tires have the same recommended pressure. It announced the pressure in either English or Spanish. Now I can throw away my old pencil gauges that were notoriously inaccurate.  I like it.
I do wish the reach brush was a little stiffer.  That being said I am extremely happy with the way the work.  My wheels, tires, and inner fender well come out clean with minimal effort
summary: Useing for a couple months and I am happy

reviewText: Nicely made with quality material and workmanship.Very good ergonomic with soft rubberized grip that is not slippery when wet.Stiff bristles with soft split ends produce no scratches and allows effiecient transmission of your elbow grease to the cleaning surfaces.All three different size and length should take care of all yourtire and wheel  cleaning needs.
If you are looking to buy these brushes it is CHEAPER to purchase them SEPARATELY then buy them in this kit.DO THE MATH AND SAVE SOME $$$$$

Great stuff, strong and durable, definitely a bargain when compared to what stores are selling them for individually.  The brissles are strong enough to remove everything, but soft enough they wont scratch stock wheels.  I would recommend using a microfiber mit to do any chrome or high dollar rims but for tires or running boards these are perfect.

These are matched well for tire and wheel cleaning. I also used the long brush with soft bristles to scrub the plastic splash guards on each end of the car and the wheel splash guards. Saves getting my wash mitt as dirty .  Bristles are long enough they worked very good on the rims, plus the short brush has stiff bristles for the sidewalls. Good buy.

It cleans tires very well. Kind of tough to get into all wheel wells, especially if it's a lowered vehicle with not enough of a gap. The rim brush doesn't scratch any of the rims that I have cleaned (chrome, aluminum, etc). I did have to purchase wheel woolies to get into the tighter places around some rims.
summary: Great for rims, tires, and wheel wells

reviewText: I like the fact that these have a threaded screw mechanism with a large paddle knob on the back in order to adjust the tightness in which you use them. This allows for a variety of materials to be used and accounted for. Other cover clips such as the ones that my brother has are made of a rubbery type of material, and consist of a circle with an inner circle that "snaps" in to hold the material. I italicized the snaps because the plastic is flexible enough to consider it being squished in instead. These Pro Grips are made of tough hard plastic. You could flatten a dime with these suckers. :-) Ok that is an exaggeration but you get the idea, they are made of tough hard plastic and should give you a lot of years of use.The other thing worth mentioning is the multilayer serrated teeth that make up the teeth. With about a whole one eighth of an inch opening or more this enables you to multi-fold the material that it is holding, or to be able to supplement the material with a secondary material designed to protect your tarp. The footprint is smaller however, but when you consider how small a grommet is which is the customary method for securing tarps these things are huge.With the closed ring on the back, something you can easily tie a cord onto, or use a rubber tie down with that makes these all the more desirable. The ones my brother has and is using over his classic Miata right now only have a half loop, with one side open. Considering how soft the material is that is a much weaker system than these Pro Grips have with as they put it "Prehistoric holding power".So that about sums it up. I find the convenience, holding power, and adjust ability to accommodate different types of material the shining stars on these tarp clips. The face or mouth could be even larger but the existing size will suffice for most jobs. Highly recommended.

I purposely tried to run these little guys through the ringer when testings. I hold true that if they can handle abuse that I'm bound to give in my pre-camping testing they should hold up pretty good for some time to come.I marked a couple of these and made sure that I abused the marked ones as much as possible over a couple days. Over tightening them, yanking on them, stepped on, used a sling shot to hurl them at a telephone pole, also clamped them onto a piece of canvas and then hung as many as 4 bricks from them for the day. You know the excessive abuse level, lol. Not only do they hold up a tarp or whatever you want to fit in their jaws well they also held up pretty well with all the abuse that I gave them. Before I go on camping trips I like to make sure that my gear isn't going to crumble just because it gets banged around or you fall off the side of a small cliff and still want to setup shelter. These are important periods in camping and it's nice to know you have something reliable to work with.So I like to punish test gear well before any trips.Granted I did have one of the test clips brake on me but that was after an excessive amount of abuse and well after I thought it should have broken. It happened when I  fired it out of the sling shot for the 5th time, with a pretty substantial pull back. I know my method of testing sounds odd or off to you but like I said, if it can handle extreme abuse it can handle simple applications. Also note that they will bend fairly easy and the "tail" is the weak point of the system. So be sure when storing them that nothing is putting pressure on them from the side or that nothing could.One thing I did notice is that over tightening them to the extreme will start to cause some damage to the tightening mechanism, if your's start to show a white line around the base of the screw inside the "jaw", then you can pretty much kiss that one goodbye. That's a weakening of the material and I experienced that with one of the text units but that was only after excessive tightening (used a pair of pliers to tighten them down).So far, these have passed my test and I would recommend them, they do have some flex to them but it seems to be just the right amount and the plastics used seem to be pretty sturdy. I gave the remaining shark clips to my father to use when he takes his RV out so he can easily extend his tarps over the side. He seems pleased and he enjoyed watching me test these out, he even contributed to some of these ideas.
summary: They hold tight and are strong.

reviewText: I keep finding ways use these and had to buy a second set.  Newest set is holding the top on my gazebo through the tropical weather we get in Florida.

We used these to hold down the cover on my car that was stored under the car port.  We attached these to the cover near the wheels and then ran a bungee cord under the car to the hook on the other side.  They're holding on really good and we don't have to worry about the cover blowing off anymore.For what they are these are really good and I can say they work.

At first blush I did not think much of these but was I ever wrong, big time.  These little ProGrips really know how to hold them.  Simply unscrew the "fin", place the folded tarp material (it helps if an edge is used with the sewn hem included in the fold for security purposes) in the jaws, tighten and repeat on another edge close to the corner.  Use a decent quality tie-down rope or strong rope material.I tested the Clips with my riding mower covered with good old blue tarp material.  The winds and rain beat the daylights out of the tarp and the ProGrips held as if they were a part of the mower.  The mower did not get wet and the Clips held without permitting water or wind to get in.  The metal corner holes in the tarp are useful and ProGrips add to the product in an even better way by allowing the tarp to be tighter on the covered object.
summary: Ya Gotta Know ProGrips Will Hold Them

reviewText: I have a large tarp that I use for various tasks.  It has gromets around the edge that give me lots of places to tie it down.  However, those gromets are never in precisely the right place.  These "shark cover clips" work perfectly.  You use a thumbscrew to form a pressure clamp on the tarp, and the end has a loop that you can use for a bungee or (thin) rope.  These work especially well if your tarp has a seam at the edge and you can get the clamp to fit inside the seam (so the seam provides a bump past which the tightened clamp cannot get over).I found the tightening mechanism to work well.  It has held up on one rain storm without ill effect.  My only concern is how well the plastic will hold up over time (sun, freezing temperatures, rain, etc.)

I frequently go camping with my kids (BSA).  One thing we always try to do is stay dry.  We usually succeed.  I like to use a fiberglass tarp over the tent to add that extra layer of "waterproof".  You can use the grommets to tie string to the tarp but sometimes you need a fastener where this is no grommet.  That's where these come in.There is a clamp on one end and a sturdy loop (for cord) on the other end.It is easy to use - just open the clamp, slip over the tarp and close the clamp.The clamp has "teeth" and a wider opening to accomodate the cord that is usually at the edge of most tarps.The clamp is very sturdy and will not come loose.Then you can use the loop to put cord or a bungee through and anchor to a tree or the ground.The material is very sturdy and to my eyes will not break.These will be very handy on most campouts, and could be useful at home if you have a car you want to cover or some other item to be covered by a tarp!

I really like these tarp cover clips. The jaws open wide enough to slip over the welting on the edge of some covers and you can double up the tarp for a stronger grip. They are easy to tighten and can be tightened very snugly. The only thing I don't like is the pointy end but I'm hoping these don't pop loose and cause any damage. Overall very good tarp clip for static holding of a tarp or cover. However, I would not recommend using them to hold a boat cover (or similar) while driving down the road, I don't think they will hold well enough against the wind.
summary: Excellent for holding tarps and boat covers!

reviewText: Great hard and thick plastic grips for holding down a tarp. They're stronger than a tarp so should hold up well. I had been using a type where you slide a lever to close the gap but this screw type should make a better grip and easier to get it tight.

I ordered this vest in XL it says XL but its sized so small. It actually is a medium. If your going to order this vest make sure the size you order is three times what you normally wear. ORDER LARGER. I ordered it so I can wear a hoodie under it and there is no way it would ever fit.

Vest was well made.  However, the XL size I ordered was more like a medium.  I normally wear size large, so I figured I would order an X-Lg and have some extra room for winter shirts.  This thing fits like a medium.  Can't even snap it.  Lucky I had a friend that wanted it.
Excellent vest for the price but sizes run VERY small. I normally wear an LG to XL shirt and ordered a 2X vest. It fit but just right...no spare room. Order a larger size and you will be very happy.
Very well made and priced right. This is REAL leather NOT patch leather. It is very good quality and soft enough to be comfortable. You will not find a better leather vest in this price range.

I love the quality and construction of this vest!  HOWEVER, the sizes are NOT true at all!!!  They don't just run small, they run ridiculously small!!!  I mean, a 4XL is too small for someone who wears XL...  My 4XL fits my daughter who wears a womens medium!  It really turned out to be a waste of time; especially, when I wanted the vest for this weekend.
I ordered a larger size as everyone said in their review to do, however this was so small I gave it to my son. If you wear a XL order a XXXL minimum, It may fit.
Been using many filters for many years, some never will be seen in my cars nor friends. I think you will never go wrong with K&N products!

This brand is very good and I highly recommend this filter for your next oil change. It spins on like it's supposed to and apparently does the job.
Made a side by side comparison with the oil filter previously on the car and this is definately a great quality item.  for the price its a must get.

I have no complaints that I can think of. I reserved 1 star because it wasn't anything particularly special about it. I liked that I got it free shipping 2 days and Amazon validated that it is the right one for my car.
Fits right on my miata and it's a k&n, had the nut off one before but this one is fine to get off. For a wash and waxer like my self it works great

reviewText: I use this filter on my Nissan and Honda.  Fits just like the factory filters I use.  No leaks, no issue.

I've been using K&N filters for years and this size fits all of my Honda cars. If your filter is mounted in a weird spot then you can go for the HP version that has a nut mounted on the end of the can.

I love K&N products and I am slowly switching all my cars over to their line up of oil filters for all my cars and also my 3 motorcycles . I may pursue to see if I can find one to fit my lawn tractor. Good quality.
Hard to tell how well it is working, but this was an easy install and fit two different kinds of Honda autos.  The product seems nice and solid.

The K&N; website wording characterizes both the PS and the HP series filters as premium, but the PS series is certainly NOT a premium filter at all.The metal in the housing is thinner, its diameter is smaller, the flow-holes around the central mounting hole are smaller, and the width of the sealing gasket is not as wide. There is a sloppy amount of glue between the base plate and the outside housing. The term "contractor grade" came to mind as being a cheaper, barely functional product designed for a jobber, not the end-user with an eye on quality.I've asked K&N; to consider changing the wording of their product description to more accurately reflect the inferior quality of this filter compared to the HP-series.Since I don't need the HP series "nut" on top of the filter, I thought I'd save a buck or two on a filter of equivalent quality otherwise.  Poor economy.-----------UPDATEI've received satisfactory responses from K&N; staff in their marketing and in their consumer affairs departments. I identified myself as a longtime customer and expressed disappointment that the "PS" series failed to live up to expectations.  Based on their subsequent communications with me I remain a loyal customer.
summary: Not as good as the HP series K&N

reviewText: Use these all the time.  Good filter product.  Look up the filter comparisons on You Tube to see the difference.
K&N makes excellent oil filters and is one of two or three quality brands like Wix and Bosch I generally buy for my vehicles. When deciding between them I shop for price.

This oil arrived and is consistent with the advertising on the webpage. I am very happy with the oil. I will be purchasing my motor oil from Amazon again in the future.

Poured it in, and I'm done.This is a good price for this specification oil, and you get 6 quarts when others for the same price only sell you 5 liters.I'll buy this again.

I started using this product about a year ago and I change my oil every three months which is over kill for this oil but I want to try and get every mile I can out of this car and the car is still running great and there is no reason that I can see at this point that I wont be going over 200K easy on the car. Great oil to drowned yourself in, multi purpose is a great thing and this weight of oil is perfect for so many things. So lube yourself up today.

Give it a try, you won't regret it.

reviewText: Don't get me wrong, this is a great oil if you need a VW 502 spec. However, a 5qt jug of Mobil 1 0w-40 (also 502 approved) can be had at Walmart for half the price.
I changed the oil on a Dodge Caravan. So far it's been driven 2000 miles and the motor is running smooth. The Van was running rough prior to this oil change. Thank you
Use it for my Lotus Elise.  No issues and seems like a high quality. Would buy it again.Price was good through amazon.

Pennzoil Ultra is the company's top of the line motor oil.  Shell, parent company of Pennzoil, engineered this 5w-40 European Full Synthetic product to meet the tough European Specifications.  Indeed, you would be hard pressed to find a common late model gasoline European vehicle that is not covered by this product (always double check though).Its approvals include Mercedes-Benz 229.5, BMW LL-01, Porsche A40, Ferrari, Maserati, Fiat, VW 505.00, and VW 502.00.These specifications all speak to the quality of the product. In particular, Mercedes-Benz 229.5 (used in the majority of gasoline engine Mercedes cars the past decade) is particularly tough to meet.In normal operating conditions, when you have a European vehicle, an approved oil allows you to comfortably run the full oil change interval recommended by your manufacturer.  Some of these European manufacturers have very long oil change intervals, which is why the correct oil with a strong additive package is so very important.Due to licensing, very few products meet current Ferrari specifications in North America.  This is about your only choice if you have a Ferrari in North America (you must be very happy if you have that Ferrari), and that specification sets this product apart from its rival European products from Mobil and Castrol which do not meet Ferrari spec.  The technical specs are all impressive.  This product has a very low NOACK volatility and proper viscosity for the majority of European vehicles in most climates.This is a highly recommended product. Depending on price and your personal preferences, Mobil 1 0w-40 is another terrific option that meets most of the same specifications besides Ferrari, Maserati, and Fiat.
summary: One of the Best Motor Oils for European Vehicles!

reviewText: This "Neoprene Red Thermal Fleece Face Mask" fits well on son's huge head and has made the seemingly never ending Winter somewhat more tolerable when he has to shovel the absurd amount of snow we were graced with this year. This did have a bit of a chemical smell, but it dissipated fairly quickly when left to air out on the front porch for a day or two.The mask fastens with Velcro and fits tightly around the chin and mouth but is a little loose above the nose, which can cause his glasses to fog up from his escaping breath. The mask does make a big difference in comfort and the bright red color is reassuring as it would be easy to see if should get accidentally trapped in one of the huge snow drifts that has accumulated in our yard.Recommended!CFH

Very light and folds up very small . At this price you can afford to by a few . I tuck them in glove boxes , in my bikes kit etc . You always seem to have a hood on your jacket or a knit hat but they are not always enough . If you put this on your good as gold in any weather . They do smell funky when new . That goes away but wash in cold water by hand and let air dry . Do not use bleach a little scented soap is great but rinse well and dry before storing . I saw where one person thought they didn't vent well and cut out a mouth hole . I have not had that problem yet with the nose hole and other vent it seems to be fine . However it would be easy to do . You would get fraying and allot less life span I imagine . Otherwise these should last for years . These cover the neck well and my cheeks up to my eyes . They even cover the ears . With a thick knit hat or ear band your set for very cold weather . Works perfect with a skull cap and bike helmet . I feel l am ready for anything with this and my Rando hat by Oregon research and it is such a light set up and comfortable .Very pleased came back and ordered another in a different color as a runny nose will keep one in the wash . A must have in Winter around here . I do not know how I lived without this all these years . It weighs about as much as a hankerchief but is very warm and it easily folds up to fit in a breast shirt or inner jacket pocket so you can carry it at all times during the winter  for when you need it . Great glove box stuffer for the winter emergency kit. At under $4 a deal and my first one came in about two weeks much better then the 8 weeks forcasted . Customs can sometimes hold things up but it is worth the wait . Because problems can happen it is good to split orders up over time just in case . This is a very neat product which I had never seen before . I am very pleased as Amazon opens up the world to me while saving gas and time .Note Jan 7th 2014 . The weather here is below zero now . This is very useful but I am now having fog in my glasses . Simple fix fold over and cut small mouth hold for breath or pull down from cheek bone away from glasses . Can be a little messy with a runny nose . However for $2 roughly it is definitely worth trying and keeping in pockets within ones Winter Coats and jackets as well as the car emergency kit or glove box .

My Fleece Mask keeps my face warm in cold days that I have to ride my motorcycle. I would recomend it to all my riding budies. I don't have a problem with the fogging of my wind shield on my helmit or shades. The mask is soft and made of good quality. This product is money well spent.

I do not wear a full face helmet, don't even like them.  They seem to take away from the ride,  like wearing a hat in a convertable car. So this works great keeping the wind off you face even at higher speeds.  Nose holes had to be enlarged for my big nose and you still get alittle wind at the corner of my eyes and made my eyes water alittle at 23 degrees. The red matches my bike.

I like this item but originally missed the reviews that noted that the shipping speed is really slow, at least from the vendors that seem to be higher up on the lists here.The item is as promised but standard shipping speed is really, really, really slow.  I didn't upgrade the shipping service, so I can't comment on whether or not doing so would result in more reasonably quick receipt of this item but anyone ordering it should be aware that it can take a very long time (relatively) to receive.Beyond the shipping speed issue and more directly related to the item be aware that this item has a distinct odor that will take some time to disappear.  That can be resolved by opening the package the item ships in and leaving the item out where it can air out.  Don't expect that process to be quick either as it may take several days (more likely weeks) for the smell to wear off.Once the item has aired out sufficiently it should work well for several years if it is treated reasonably well.
summary: Warning, shipping speed is best measured in months....

reviewText: -Used this in two of my car interiors, lexus and murano.-Nice cool white color, but there is a slight, nearly unnoticeable blue to it.-I have tried others ranging from ebay(its a gamble), superbright leds(great product but pricey), to vleds(medicore/good) and this ones is up to par and much cheaper, esp for a packet of 4.A couple bugs with led for car int..-Based on my experience, led's have different levels of pulsing (when the car engine is on) from diff brands, but this one has very minimal pulses and nearly unnoticeable. I am guessing that this is the norm for cars that are designed to light up the interior with halogens and I rather not invest too much finding the perfect bulb.-The fade in/out feature for interior lights, while locking/unlocking the vehicle, can get a bit choppy with certain cars that is not designed for leds. Example: the lexus light fade in/out in comparison where the murano lights dims for a sec then shuts off, making the led flaw in the lexus noticeable.I would recommend these, just wish someone would have recommended these to me earlier.

Bought these to replace the incandescent bulbs in my RV. These little bulb put out white light and use 1/10th the power of the stock bulbs. The are a softer light then the incandescent. I am off the grid most times when camping and the LED lights are a must have to conserve battery power. With several lights inside and out we have no problem going a week without a charge! before we would have to fire the generator up 2-3 days into the trip to charge batteries.

Bright white with just a hint of blue that makes them stand out from farther away than standard halogens. Have had them installed all winter and they still work great. For the money, I don't think you could ask for more than that.
Use them to replace the burned out lights in car. They are bright and do the job. Must say I would recommend them

Attracted to their low price, I tried substituting these LED bulbs for the filament bulbs in a couple of my motorhome's overhead fixtures hoping I'd eventually be able to replace all of my incandescent bulbs to save power.  To make the electrical connection, I had to pry the wires from the base slightly.  Once I did that, and ensured that the polarity was correct, all of the LEDs in the bulbs came on.  But even with all of them working the light output was nowhere near as much as I was getting from my filament bulbs.  Though these are advertised as being "white" the color of the light was a cool light blue, casting a not-at-all warm light.  The difference in light color and light intensity between these LED bulbs and my regular incandescent filament bulbs was dramatic.  As much as I would like to reduce my lighting power consumption which would, of course, greatly increase the time I could light my coach before having to charge my batteries, these won't do it for me.  Sadly, I must continue looking for warmer, brighter LED bulbs.
summary: Not Willing to Trade My Incandescent Bulbs for These

reviewText: These are built quite sturdy and feel as though they can hold up a pickup truck although I don't really have one to test it with. I used it to prop up my Nissan Juke and it worked perfectly. The job was to repaint the muffler so I had to back up onto these. very good A++++++++++++++ but be care full when you try doing it by yourself, you need someone stand right front of you help you.
summary: very good A++++++++++++++ but be care full when you try doing ...

reviewText: Light weight , handy and easy to haul around and use. Stackable, can also be hung on wall for storageIts all plastic, so wont rust, but make sure you dont lreave it in sun light for months at a time.
Fairly easy to drive up onto.  Wish they were an inch wider but it's not an issue as I think other ramps are the same width.
summary: stack for storage, solid but lightweight

reviewText: I change my own oil. I mostly enjoy changing oil. Using better oil and better filters than a quickie-lube place gives me great satisfaction for my vehicle ownership."Mostly" you say? I hate jacking up cars. Get the jack, position the jack, jack the car up, get a jackstand, position the jackstand, lower the car on to the jackstand, continue working. Then, raise the car, remove the jackstand, lower the car, remove the jack. Too much work.Instead, i've bought these ramps, and hands-down, they're the best item i've ever bought for vehicle maintenance. It's so much more convenient to put the ramps in front of the car, then just drive up.They seem to be well made and sturdy, and they give a nice elevation to the car that makes it easy to get under and work. Highly recommended.
I bought these beacause they were 'supposed to be low clearance...guess again. They seem to be of good construction, but now I will have to use them as 'stands' not 'ramps'...

For the last 30 years I have had a pair of steel ramps.  Heavy to move around and tend to rust.  The Rhino Gear ramps are tough, light weight, and certainly won't rust.  I like that they have the wheel stop to help prevent driving off the ramp and they are a little longer so they slide under the front of the car much better than my old ramps.  Time will tell if the plastic holds up with use but the way they are designed I don't expect any problems.

When trying to drive on these they often tend to move forward so your car is on the ground again. Sometimes they move right or left even when you drive on them absolutely in a straight line.To use them in a safe way you'd have to block them from suddenly shooting forward. a long stick of sturdy wood will do the trick if you can fix against a not moving object. If the piece of wood is wide enough it will also help the ramps from misaligning
summary: driving on them is a pain in the behind

reviewText: These ramps work well with our Camry or Prius. The rubber stoppers on the bottom of each ramp keep it from moving around when driving up on them. They also fit together for more compact storage when not in use.

These ramps are great. Like others have said though, buy them local. You will find them cheaper. I have seen them at most major auto parts chains as well as Wal-Mart has them for $50. They held my Land Rover Discovery just fine with no bending or other scary sights/sounds.My truck was up on them for about 5 hours and not a hitch. These are also nice because on the bottom there is a small rubber foot which did not let them slide at all going up or coming down. And like mentioned by others, if slipping is an issue, just get some cheap rubber floor mats and put them on those.Also, they are nestable which does really help for storage space.I would recommend this ramps.
summary: Work great - even on a pig like my Discovery

reviewText: I bought these because they were LIGHT weight to replace jack stands and a jack for oil changes and such maintenance jobs on my sportscar.  With a 3-4" clearance the car goes up these with no issue.  The tires are 245/45/18.. and fit fine.I would say these weigh about 10-15lbs at best.. if you've used steel ramps, or a decent jack and stands you'll greatly appreciate the weight difference immediately.. and frankly driving up two ramps is safer and easier/quicker for oil changes,.. and any other work that needs about 1-2 feet of clearance.Buy them if you do your own oil changes.
Works driving my pickup on them but still put jake stands just in case, so will update if anything goes wrong with them  They are better priced here than anywhere else I could find

Will say that I've only used these once.  Changed the oil today for the first time ever.  I will say that this gave me complete piece of mind being underneath the car.  As a novice, I probably would have been a bit nervous using my ratchet to unscrew the bolts if I were only using jackstands and/or a floor jack.  Tires sat perfectly on the ramps.  Obviously want tires centered on it but wasn't difficult since they're wide enough for a little bit of placement error.  Once the vehicle was on them, there was plenty off clearance underneath.  Remember, for safety reasons, needs to be on a flat surface.  I was able to use these inside my garage with no prob!
summary: Better peace of mind than jackstands.  Nice and sturdy!

reviewText: These seem pretty sturdy. They are made out of thick plastic. I used them to lift my 2010 infinit g37x.

I have a low SLK230 and these ramps worked perfectly to get it off the ground.  I've tried others from local stores and just scrapes along the bottom plastic molding and frame.  They stack nicely together and are easy / light enough to store in other places.  The only change I would make would be to add some type of rubber bottom.  I had to get a mat to prevent these from sliding a little while loading the car up on the ramps - still cheaper than local shops for the style I needed.

What is not to like about these ramps? I used them on my Dodge 3500 Diesel truck, this truck is heavy in the front. Didn't move or bow and my stock (265/70) tires fit nicely but a bigger tire will hang over the side. I am sure the car will be easy. I do like the nesting feature and they stand up nicely in the garage.
use them to raise my M3 so I can put a jack underneath ! very strong, would recommend, I also saw these at autozone

Easy to use, plant firmly, and crazy sturdy. I prefer them to jack stands but it was scary the first time I drove an auto onto them. My manual is so much easier to control, my wife's automatic lurches forward a bit unpredictably. I got the hang of it now so no big deal but the first time was a learning experience. Both cars are AWD so they didn't move around for me.
Works as intended, as you can see I'm not dead and writing this review, thanks RhinoGear ^_^

(2012 Accord LX with 16" rims and stock tires)(Reasons why -1 star):-My car is stock height, but these ramps come very close to scrapping the bumper (within an inch).  I don't see anyone being able to use these ramps with a low profile sports car.-There was a bit of excess plastic on the bottom that I had to cut off to get one of the ramps to lay flat and not see-saw wobble.  Quality control should have caught this.-There isn't a lot of room for error if you don't have your tires perfectly centered.  If you have a performance car with extra-wide tires then you'll probably have rubber hanging off the edges.-The stop-lip at the end of the ramp could be a bit taller.  If you idle into it, it will stop your car from moving.  But if you accidentally hit the gas too hard, it won't do much to stop you.  If you have large diameter tires, it would be very easy to roll to far without feeling it (until your car slams into the ground and you destroy your bumper).
summary: Could be a bit longer and wider.

reviewText: Very solid car ramps.  Worked great.  My only issue is I wish there was more surface area for the ramps to grab - they do move at times.  Still, great quality and heavy-duty design.

I have a 2011 camaro and these are very handy when i need to wash the bottom of my car or do a oil change. They are very well made and saves the hastle of putting the car on a jack. I use these a lot.

These are not my first ramps, they arrived in a huge box with a lot of packaging paper (so packaged well).  I put both on the floor next to each other in the living room, one of ramps had extra plastic material on the center part of it's bottom (who ever took the plastic out of the mold didn't do a good job cutting off the excess), so one ramp was swinging lift and right as my kids jumped on it, while the other ramp was perfect and not moving.  So I used a small handsaw to finish It myself.  A very simple thing for the factory to observe before shipping a none conforming part!FYI, I do have race ramps that I use for my lower sport sedan, and they have a 10 degree slope.Update 6-23-2013I was trying to go up the ramps slowly several times, I over did it and the right side ramp went under the tire and the ramp was bent (the walls from inside broke off with the center wall, twisted and some minor cracks appeared, so one mistake going up this 17 degree will cost you 55 bucks, burned faster than a match...I did drive again on top of these ramps, but not sure if they are safe for use.  I think a floor jack and couple of jack stands along with a very good knowledge of where to place and lift the vehicle is the best solution.used on a 2009 Chrysler Town and Country van. - curb weight 4750 lbs.Update 9-20-2013I forgot to mention, a day after the ramps were damaged, I called the manufacturer and they sent me new ones (which I'm selling as is) and sent back the damaged.
summary: Steep ramps, poor quality control, one mistake and they're gone

reviewText: Had too use them while out dry camping. My truck weighs about 9500 lbs and it held it up but the ends where starting to buckle my buddies truck weighs a bit more and they did not hold up to the 1600lb rating he sent his back.

reviewText: I've own both the original and the new style nesting Rhino ramps.Since they move on concrete, the originals were easily drive over, given the very low lip at the end of the ramps.  Yes, I drove over the originals and took a chunk out of the ends, as the ramps landed on the rocker panel "pinch weld."I sold the originals and bought the new style ones, hoping they would be better.THEY ARE NOT! reviewText: I have a 6000 pound FWD van. I had no issues of slipping while driving up the ramps. I don't know what other people are complaining about but I had mine on smooth concrete in my garage and they didn't budge. No issues of cracking or popping either. The large wheels sat very well in the ramps. These are quality ramps. Just kick them up under the front tires and drive up. They won't budge. reviewText: I really like my RhinoGear 11912 RhinoRamps MAX Vehicle Ramps (Pair, 16,000lb. GVW Capacity).Solid, sturdy, light weight compared to others competitors and good heigth.
Be care full as they may launch forward depending on the surface you are using them. If the floor is smooth try to wedge them from the front other wise put them on a rubber mat.

I basically had to get a running start on them, and then stop on a dime once on top.  Any time I attempted to creep up them slowly, they would just push across the ground.
The ramp keeps sliding on the pavement. So I put a towel under it. Did not work. It seems only way this ramp will work is to back it up with something to keep it from sliding. Returned

I wanted a pair of ramps that would work on my Jeeps and my smaller vehicles. It doesn't matter if I'm rolling a jeep with 35s or a mini cooper on these things. Plenty of clearance and they don't slide.

Using these ramps the job was a breeze.I have a front receiver on my pickup that limits clearance at the front, I had no problem getting under the front end using these ramps.These ramps are very light and easy to move around.
