My ramps did not budge an inch when driving up on them, and I have aggressive all terrain tires for use in my pastures.See my pictures of my Toyota Tundra on the ramps.

I have wanted a pair of these for awhile.  They are perfect for having around for the little auto work.  The photo and description make them seem tough - and they are.  These tire ramps are extremely heavy-duty with very thick walls.  The pads are extra-wide which is an added bonus. And it ships with a rubberized stop to prevent the ramps from sliding.  Overall, very good quality.  Would buy again, if needed.
great cutoff switch, works as described.  no instructions, but doesn't need any.  I go with putting on the ground side.  Works fine and easily.

This is a somewhat inelegant solution to a battery switch.  Contact is made or broken by screwing the knob down tight or loosening it so that its threads don't connect one terminal to another (the two parts are insulated one from the other by a plastic gasket).  The clamp fits a standard battery terminal okay, the cyllndrical terminal is too small for a standard battery clamp to fit securely ... I manufactured a copper shim to eliminate the mismatched size.  Make the terminal the right size and the switch a simple 1/4 to 1/2 turn twist and you've got a five-star product.

Good quality and shipping time. The product works fine but cannot be mounted on batteries with posts having parallel cylindrical design and made of brass. Previous battery posts on batteries I have bought were made of lead and some taper. There is no "give" to the brass, like lead. This device will not seat and slips off too easy on the brass non-tapering posts

So I wanted to add a battery disconnect to my RV batteries and ordered this.  But when It came time to actually put this on I was not impressed. Battery cable wire size was to big for the switch.  Would have been better to see prior to purchase.

I used this on my RV batteries to shut off the power drain and keep the corrosion at bay when the trailer isn't in use.  Although the trailer has a master shut off switch, there's still a little power drain that occurs.  This was aiding the corrosion building up at the postitive terminal.  Just loosen (not disconnect) the green knob and your disconnected.  Easy.  Only issue I can see is the galvanized bolt and nut will probably rust down the road.  And also the bolt doesn't exactly sit flat against the indentation or flange, so when tightening up the nut, you may turn the bolt right through the metal flange requiring another wrench to hold it.
summary: Does exactly what it's supposed too

reviewText: Another great product from Meg's and smells awesome too! They've put the gripper trigger on this item as well and it makes a world of difference. Really makes you appreciate the quality of Meg's

I received this product as part of a gift pack, and was eager to give it a try sinceJohnson Wax 32 Oz Blue Trigger Spray Original Windex  80127and other traditional glass cleaners weren't cutting the road grime the way I'd like them to on my windshield.First, I washed and dried my vehicle.  Second, I applied this product as directed.  Third, I was impressed by the results, even with some minor streaking issues.The slightly oily finish this cleaner leaves on the glass was a concern at first, and I did note some streaking, so I went back over those spots with a clean, dry, microfiber cloth to remove them.  Once that was removed, glass looked great.  Cleaning off the windshield at the gas station seemed to be easier with the glass cleaner having been used days before.  Rain seemed to run off easier too.  Usually I useRain-X 800002243 Glass Treatment- 7 oz., but I'm not sure that I'll need to do that using this cleaner withBosch 24-CA Clear Advantage Beam Wiper Blade - 24"(s) installed.
summary: Far better than traditional ammonia based window cleaners

reviewText: This glass cleaner is phenomenally fantastic, just spray and and wipe off! It leaves no streaks, sometimes if you're lazy, just spray on your windshield and let your wipers do the majority of the wipe. It will still be clear! However if you have some really bad tough water spots, then I'd suggest getting either glass cleaning clay or a detailing glass cleaning razor and get super clean windows. It'll be like they are just straight out of the factory. Don't get me wrong however, this is a fantastic window cleaner, I just bought a second bottle.

Being an automotive detailer I pretty much have tried them all.  I like to keep my work supplies separate from my personal use products.  I always have a bottle of this on hand.  Works on all window types and contains no ammonia.  Streak free finish when combined with a microfiber glass cleaning towel.  Not to mention, I was surprised to discover that a glass cleaner actually smells good too!
summary: Best OTC glass cleaner I've ever used, period.

reviewText: This Meguire's window cleaner is OK and it will clean a window but I would compare it to Windex or any other common window cleaner. If you want a really easy cleaner that is streak free that stays on the window I would suggestTrico 47112 Aquapel Aerosol Glass Windshield CleanerAquapel is much better and truly is streak free. Just remember to use a soft cloth or microfiber towel.
summary: This cleaner is OK, there are better products

reviewText: I've been using Meguires products for years and have been very satisfied with many of their products, but not this one.  I've tried many different types of glass cleaners from the age old Windex, to spray foam cleaners, paste cleaners, and finally this one.  This one is horrible.  While initially the cleaner seems to work, it leaves behind a thin oily residue on the glass.  In more than 30 years of detailing and taking care of cars I've never encountered a product that hazes/fogs faster than or more than this one does. To make sure I tested the product on all kinds of glass from auto glass to windows in the home, mirrors, aquariums, etc. and even tried using different drying tools from several types of paper towels, microfiber towels, synthetic chamois, and the results were always the same...it fogged/hazed on all the types of glass in a very short time.Do not waste your money on this cleaner.  I've found the very best results come from just plain distilled or R.O. water and a high quality microfiber towel.  It doesn't fog, won't harm interior window tintings, and costs practically $0.

I have used waterless wash products for years and this one is among the better ones I have used. Over time I have probably tried about a half-dozen different brands. I would have given this a "5" if it were not so expensive. I contacted the company and asked about larger refill sizes but they don't have them and at this time have no plans to make larger refill sizes. So, in spite of the fact that it works quite well I will be shopping around for something that is more economical.

I thought that I would pick this up to try it out. It is technically illegal to wash the car in my neighborhood and we do not have a gutter nearby so the soapy dirty water sits there in the neighbor's curb so I thought that I would be neighborly and also..because.. well... it hurts to wash the car. I drove the car through a cheapy car wash for $8.00; you know the type. I then drove the car home and used Meguiars Ultimate Wash and wax anywhere spray. It worked very well. It produced a shine and smoothness almost as smooth as a clay bar. I would highly recommend using this. You may want to follow up with a clay bar afterwards, and then Meguiars Tech wax; that is good stuff as well ! This is a great hobby ! Happy shine !
it works alright. it kind of smears, especially on glass, and doesn't wash that great. If its a must have then i guess it's worth it but i wouldn't recommend.
Just used it on my car and it cleans very well. Very easy to use and doesn't leave my residue. The paint surface becomes slicker after usage and shiny too. Highly recommended.

I use this to clean the inside faces of the doors, the car body's door frames, the gas filler door, and the like, where I don't want to shoot a big jet of water (soaking the interior of the car). A small spray is effective in loosening a fair amount of crud that may build up, and the waxed surface looks and feels smooth after buffing.
summary: and the like, where I don't want to shoot a big ...

reviewText: This is a new consumer product from Meguiars.  However, the concept of water-less washes has been around for some time now.  When this product came out I was skeptical, especially since it is not yet at this point widely available just anywhere, combined with the fact that a bottle of this stuff goes for as high as about $15.00.About me:  I am a mobile automotive detailer/car enthusiast.  I also have extensive knowledge in auto body and paint as well.  I have replaced rusted out panels on my own vehicle, have done my share of welding, and I have also repainted my own truck.  If you were to browse my profile and other reviews you would quickly learn that I am an avid Meguiars product loyalist and typically rate their products no less than 4 star ratings/reviews.My vehicle/weather conditions:  1994 Ford Bronco, BLACK, 95 degrees, semi shaded, cleaned, polished with a dual action buffer and waxed just one week prior to utilizing this product.  The vehicle was what should be expected when using a product like this, semi-dirty, but not gritty, grimy or considered filthy.Application:  Following the bottles instructions, I shook the contents of the product thoroughly, and grabbed a total of 4 microfiber towels, even though the product advised 2 for best results.  Why 4?  My vehicle is large, I am a detailer and I do not roll the dice on my newer paint job, or anyones, for that matter.  I began with the top of the vehicle, sprayed product, wiped product in one direction, and wiped again with the other clean/fresh towel.  I repeated this throughout the entire process until the vehicle was complete and switched to two new towels only half way through the job ONLY applying product to the painted surfaces and working my way from the upper most panels while saving the lowest panels for last.Results:  Once the job was complete I did a walk around of the entire vehicle.  First, I noticed a few spots where the product streaked and smudged to a haze.  This could have been my error, but I did follow the directions and thought that I was doing things right.  Overall, not a big deal, I just re-applied a little bit more and wiped off with another clean towel.  Next, I noticed some light surface scratching in a couple of spots, one, on the hood, and two on my passenger side door.  Remember, I just buffed this a week ago and gave it a thorough inspection post buffing and waxing and I did not have these on my vehicle.  THIS WAS MY PRIMARY CONCERN WITH THIS OR ANY WATER LESS WASH PRODUCT.  This was the main reason I didn't rush out to buy the product as soon as it was released.Overall:  If you are 100% on keeping your vehicle in PRISTINE condition I highly recommend on sticking to the conventional way of cleaning things and using water.  My business relies on my vehicle looking amazing, if my vehicle was always dirty, scratched and grimy I probably would not have much of a selling point.  However, this product may be great for enthusiasts who wish to wipe down their vehicle every other day or as soon as it starts collecting light dust or finger prints.  I have never been huge on wash and wax products combined, although, they are better than nothing.  I believe Meguiars is on the right path with this product.  However, if you have an extremely dark colored or black vehicle or an extremely expensive paint job I couldn't pull myself together to recommend a product like this to use on a regular basis.  It certainly isn't a regular basis substitute for doing things the old fashioned way.Notes:  It says it can be used on glass and other surfaces.  Yes, it can be.  But, why would you want to at the cost per bottle?  Save the windows for being cleaned with glass cleaner, don't start spraying down everything you own with this stuff.  One final note I'd like to say and it's a positive one at that.  The bottle says cleans 3-4 vehicles and that might hold true if you are figuring all of the surfaces top to bottom, glass included.  But, I cleaned all of the painted surfaces of my truck with this bottle and the painted surfaces alone and I could EASILY do at least 5 more washes with this stuff (if I really wanted to).  I will try it again in a couple of days, perhaps I just need more practice with their product.  But, I have tried other water-less washes and have had better results, such as Optimum no rinse.Closing:  Don't expect this product to take out water spots.  I had some spotting on my hood after it rained out and happened to dry on the vehicle and this product did fade/blend the spots down a little but did not remove the stubborn ones.I hope this somewhat critical review helped.  I love Meguiars about as much as anyone else but like to say things as I see them.  I wouldn't want every single person rushing out to get a bottle of this only to be somewhat disappointed.  I understand that not everyone is so picky about keeping a vehicle looking as perfect as possible and if you have a lighter colored car or silver than you might not mind this product so much.  Finally, this product smells like a strong fruity bubble gum type of smell.  It's nice at first but if you're around it long enough it gets overwhelming.  I'd recommend to wash your hands afterwords, no, not with this stuff, with soap and water!

I had been cleaning my car regularly with Quick detailer every couple of days just to keep my car shiny.  The reason I do this is because I live in a condo and don't have access to a water hose, otherwise i would clean it that way.I then read online that this can be bad as it can cause scratching.  I then learned of waterless wash.Well, I have to say this works a lot better than quick detailer as far as cleaning.  My car looked shinier compared to the quick detailer.I still like to use quick detailer in between washes as it provides some mild wax protection and is generally cheaper.The wash will get out mild to moderate dust, but I still think it can't replace good old water/soap washes.  Every once in a while, I will go to a car wash to get  a more thorough cleaning.
summary: Cleans well for those who can't use hose and bucket.

reviewText: I like this stuff.  Smells good, easy to use and I can clean my whole car in about 10 minutes.  I never used it on a really dirty car, but it allows me to clean in between regular washes and keep my car looking great.  Wish it was a little cheaper but I'll definitely keep this stuff on hand.  My car beads rain really well too so I have to think this stuff protects the paint a little.
summary: Easy to use for a quick wash.

reviewText: have to agree with other reviewer.  no standby, even though there is a standby light, it never comes on.  the 3300 seems to be a better unit.  and then there were sparks.  not in connecting to the battery but when i plugged it in.  weird.  i do like the series of lights, but thats not worth the extra $.  why no standby?on the 3300 you attach it to the battery and the standby light comes on.  then you plug it in.  on the 4.3 you attach it to the battery and nothing.  no lights.  anyway, once you plug it in you can set it for what you want.  just dont plug it in near the battery.i found the cables to be the same length as my 3300, plenty long for what i need.

I leave this hooked up through the cigarette plug (sold separately) on my vehicle I don't drive that often.  It has maintained that battery for a long time.  It's nice to know my battery won't die and freeze in the winter time as well.The LED's on the front of it are kind of cool if you look up what each of the stages really means.It gets a little hot when charging in a closed up car in the sun but that hasn't caused any problems yet.

At about 1/2 the previous price.of the 7000 series, you really don't lose much. The best feature is the recondition mode which has brought several of my batteries back from the dead. Bonus setting for AGM batteries such as the Odyssey, so it transmits enough voltage without burning them up.Did I mention that CTEK chargers go on forever-just don't get them wet.

this company makes chargers for many of the high end cars such as Porsche so when they came out with this new improved model, I took it at much better price than the older models that have the car's logo on them and received a better unit.  I have a few of the adapters that I have installed and will install more on my other vehicles.  The one comfort adapter with LEDs stopped showing the LEDs lit within 6 months and althought it still charged with it, I wouldn't recommend that one but the others are fine.

I was ready to buy another battery for my BMW but I bought this and it brought my battery back to life. This was after returning the Battery Tender which doesnt work well in frigid temps.The wires are on the thin side though so I docked it one star and if your engine is at all warm they get real limp like almost gonna melt,. The battery tender I originally had came with real thick sturdy wiring.

The CTEK 56-864 Battery Charger works great.  I have yet to have any issues.  The only thing I do not like about this charger is the LEDs of the charge steps.  To me, it is just too confusing, but still a good charger.

I hadn't been aware of CTEK Battery Chargers until I purchased a Moetefindt trailer from Germany.  The trailer is equipped with interior lights, a winch, and a security system, all of which are powered by a large 12 volt battery.  Incorporated with the battery is a CTEK Charger which is designed to keep the battery in top-rate condition when not connected to the tow vehicle electrical system.  The charger originally installed was designed to operate on 220 volts which is the standard for Europe.  I purchased this one to operate correctly in the USA.This charger provides an excellent method of analyzing a battery using LEDs.  These LEDs also show the progress of the charging operation.  The charger also incorporates a de-sulphating procedure which is designed to extend battery life, and also to recuperate an otherwise unusable battery.  Finally, through its analytic process, the charger also shows if a battery cannot be re-charged.Am planning to purchase another for regular use so I won't have to "borrow" from the trailer.
While other inflators have failed after a couple of months of weekly use, this inflator keeps going. Fills auto tires much faster then expected.  Hose and cord of enough length and not too long.
summary: Good Cord & Hose Lengths.  No Motor Burnout Yet

reviewText: This is very lightweight, the carrying bag is thin but sturdy enough, and it has a pocket inside to keep the directions if you fold them!  I wish the accessories were in a separate container or secured inside.  I put mine into a small zipper bag to keep them together.  When you put the inflator back into the bag it only fits one direction, because of the LED light.I agree that the light could have used a focusing lens but I do like the way it swivels to give you more options on positioning.  The instructions say the gauge is just a guide and not to believe it's the correct pressure.  I found the gauge to be about 4 lbs. lower than actual, so you do need an independent tire gauge to check to see if there was enough pressure.  I do like the way you can set the pressure you desire and it will turn off when it reaches it, a nice safety feature.It was easy to put on, the buttons are self-explanatory.  A good value, I think.
summary: A handy item to keep in your car

reviewText: I was in a parking lot when my car's "check tire pressure" light came on. One tire was looking just a little low, so I decided to stop right there and use this device for the first time.It was very simple to take it out and set it up-- the only design flaw is that the back "hatch" where the plug and extra nozzle heads are is a bit too small and really should have a separate compartment for the nozzle heads... they'll get lost so easily! But I digress...I set it up and got it onto my tire. You have to set it a little above the actual PSI you want because the lever prevents it from going quite that high. I set it and, bingo! In 30 seconds I had a full tire again.A woman stopped to ask me if I had a flat, then noticed what I was doing and said, "Oh, look at that. You even have the equipment you need."Gotta say, I felt very cool. "Yep, lady, I'm like a tire superhero."For good measure, I checked all the other tires and topped them off before putting the device back. It was super-handy, and it's so small that it easily stores under my back seat. Everyone with a car should have one of these.

A powerful inflator, with a great screw-on hose design, and a so-so gauge.What I like best is the screw-on hose.  No more trying to flip a clamp quickly enough to prevent losing air from the freshly-inflated tire (or deflating it further when you first attach the inflator)-- there's the briefest hiss of air when you screw the hose onto the valve.  This feature alone is to make me really like the BellAire 4000.Also, it fills the tires faster than my standby battery-poweredSlime COMP07 Inflator, and much faster than either of my old (since-retired) 12V inflators. I have not had any problems with it blowing out the 12V socket's fuse, although that is a risk with this kind of inflator.The unit is compact, not as loud as other inflators I've used. It comes with a nylon carry-bag (fitted to not add bulk) which will decrease the inevitable gunking-up of car accessories that live in the trunk, and has storage for both the hose and power cord (which also keeps them from being damaged as they ride around in your trunk).  The power cord seems long enough for most standard passenger vehicles. All of these are signs that the designers were actually thinking about how this inflator will be used and stored.The flashing hazard light is a nice touch also, in the unfortunate case of needing to do a roadside inflation. The onboard worklight has 3 small LEDs in a swivel head, which is handy, but would be more useful if brighter.The major flaw in the unit is, predictably, the pressure gauge, which is only vaguely accurate (analog) and has an outer dial to set the desired pressure.  The inflator is designed to stop when the pressure set on the gauge is reached, but since the gauge isn't accurate, I got results like setting the gauge to above 35, with 31 PSI in the tire, and having the unit refuse to fill until I set the dial to 40PSI.  This means you need a separate tire pressure gauge and may have to disconnect the hose a couple of times to check the actual pressure.  Effectively, the pressure setting becomes only a safety cut-off "ceiling".So what this inflator could really use is an onboard, accurate digital gauge.  Since I can buy a decent, accurate, handheld digital gauge for 10 bucks, it seems like integrating that function into an inflator should be easy.Other quibbles: The tight-fitting nylon bag is almost too small.  The cable storage compartment could be a little bigger. The carry-handle is a simple plastic ring that protrudes from the top of the inflator-- a proper padded handle (maybe a T-shaped one) could have fit in the same spot.  Without the handle, the unit is a bit awkward to carry one-handed (although it isn't heavy).The one big feature I would add to this unit would be an AC-power adapter, since when I use it in my enclosed garage, I have to open the garage door, start the car, back it out partway, and then use the unit.  An AC adapter would make it so I could just plug into the wall at home, but still be able to do emergency roadside work with the 12V adapterSo could this inflator be improved? Certainly, with a better handle, more accurate and digital gauge, a brighter LED, and support for AC power. But hands-down it's the best tire inflator I've used, so I still give it 5-stars.  Recommended.
summary: a really good inflator, with a poor pressure gauge

reviewText: They do a great job of packing several functions into a device without adding size/weight.  I have the Goodyear pump which I love but I bought this because of the programmable pressure gauge.  VERY, VERY handy if you need more than a couple of pounds.  The work light is at a good level and is bright enough to help change a tire at night.  I tested it in a completely dark garage.  The emergency flasher is bright enough to be seen at least 1/10 of a mile away.  (I walked to the end of the driveway.  It can probably be seen from farther away.)Pros:1) Programmable Pressure Gauge.  GREAT feature.  Easy to us2) Work light that's a little bit off the ground...higher than other pumps I've had.  Illuminates well.3) Storage compartment in the back for power cord and attachments. Forget about accessing it in the dark but it's still very handy.Cons:1)  VERY plastic.  You drop this device and you're going to be picking up pieces.  It may or may not still function but it won't look good any more2)  This is a personal thing...but I'd love a quick attachment adapter.  Sometimes I don't want to screw it into a tire.  I just want to add a pound quickly and move on.3)  Not a big con but the bag was a weak effort.  I'd rather save $.25.  The storage compartment makes it moot.4)  Again, not a big con...just wish the cord was a little longer.  Manufacturers of most of these pumps in general seem to forget most vehicles have the power source in the middle.  So I am already losing three feet plus by the time it reaches the ground outside the door.  When I am inflating lawn mower tires or something I have to get it very close to the rear of the vehicle or back the car out so I can get closer to the door.
summary: Slick Little Device.  I Definitely Recommend It

reviewText: Received the item and immediately put it to use on our daughter's bike.  It hadn't been touched for over a year and the tires were very low.  At first glance the tire inflator seems to have all that you will need.  It is shaped like a triangle with a reflector, comes in a cheap carrying case, has a 10 foot hose (which does not reach the rear tires on our larger SUV unless plugged into the second row port), has different adapters for charging different sized tires, an auto shut-off when desired PSI has been reached and of course the gauge.The BellAire tire inflator took about 1 minute to inflate our bike tire.  I did not test on our vehicles 22 inch tires as we had recently taken them to the shop for a patch.If the time comes to use on our vehicle then I will update my review to reflect that usage.  This product should be purchased by all to be kept in the trunk for those emergency moments.  I have found that the auto shut off and gauge are a bit off but then again most cheap devices aren't perfect in that respect.  The round carry handle is useless and painful.  I have also found it very difficult to open the back storage compartment.Highly recommend for all vehicle owners!
What can you say about bearing grease? The can was easy to open and it's big enough to squish truck bearings in. My wheels turn nicely now, thank you.

This is a quality product that is Made in the USA. It appears to be equal to or better that Lucas brand. My experience is short term and I will update after having the chance to drive my truck for a few thousand miles to see how the grease wears. I have always wanted to try the Timken brand because I swear by their bearings that have served me well. So far I am impressed enough to buy some more when needed as I am forced to frequently repack my bearings due to salt water spilling onto the roadway from the marsh that I drive through during high tides. Brackish water is brutal on bearings especially if you can't rinse it off. My tub of grease arrived in an old style cardboard can with a tin bottom & a pop off lid that is different from the advertised picture. The one in the picture appears to be a plastic tub with screw on lid that would be nice for storage and probably allot less prone to leak. This isn't a problem for me since I usually go through a whole tub on a bearing repack but I would prefer sellers use accurate photos when advertising products or at the very least state the fact that products may differ from the advertised picture in the product details. I was surprised at how well this product shipped. It arrived in pristine condition with absolutely no leakage. I never imagined that I would be buying grease through the mail but after the good experiences on my past two Amazon purchases I will probably continue since I can get the exact product I want, when I want it & at a good price.
Timken makes the highest quality bearings. They also require the highest standard grease. Use this for your wheel bearings, grease steering linkage.. High temp Red grease by Timken..the best.
Twenty words to comment on grease. It's packaged very good, the price is good, it's a nice color, it smells like grease, and no I'm not going to taste it.
Works great and cost less here than at the auto store, this is a very good bearing grease for any high temp/pressure appliation
Add me to the good reviews on this!  Typical Timken quality product!  Used this for all bearing (wheel) for my truck and wife's car.-Nigel

I admit that my assignment of 4 stars is more my fault than that of the product. I wanted a LED strip for my snake cage - but didn't notice this was a battery powered bit of gear. I shrugged my shoulders and put it in anyway. Really nicely made, for a change (from just about anything). Lights are bright enough but spaced a bit too far apart. I'm not 100% positive what the perfect use is for this. Might be good in a little used small shed or engine compartment in a boat or something. The real issue here is that it's just not bright enough for close work and too small for larger spaces where you might just need 'some' light. If the LED's were half the distance and there were twice as many, it would be a terrific product for small spaces - but of course that would mean even more batteries - and this uses quite a few to begin with.Not right for the snake cage but perhaps great for a large tool box or something similar. Worth the decent price, either way, should you find the right use.
summary: Nice product for the right use

reviewText: This is a stick-on strip with 3 tiny but bright LED lights on it. Be sure that the length is what you need; you can't cut it and there are only a few spots of adhesive on the strip.Speaking of the adhesive, it is not repositionable. If you decide the position is not right, you will need additional adhesive or some other method of putting it back in place. (Yes, I got it wrong the first time. I'm no expert at DIY tasks!)I found the package easy to pry open and the directions clear. The battery pack is heavy once you insert 8 AA batteries, but the adhesive for mounting it seems adequate. The instructions point out that you need to leave some slack in the wire to the battery pack. Even with that, it will probably be tricky changing the batteries. The case opens on both sides, with 4 batteries placed on each side. The side facing the wall is held with Velcro-type pieces backed with adhesive. If you install it in a tight place, separating the Velcro to change the batteries will be challenging.At this time the item is expensive for something so simple. I like battery-powered LEDs for some uses, and a search on Amazon for LED battery lights comes up with many options, some very reasonable.

This LED tape light definitely can be called an "multi-purpose" light.  I wanted this strip of lights because when the power goes off I want to be able to prepare the quickly prepare my residence for any indeterminate outage.  Flashlights are fine and my Coleman lantern helps, but the LED feature lights up a wider area quickly and easily.Yes, these can be installed in any number of areas, especially in a work situation.  One relative even wanted them to light up a display hutch.  They do take eight AA batteries, which makes the battery pack a bit heavy.  My only problem with this is that the fully loaded pack weighs approximately nine ounces.  The wire connecting to the strip is 5" leaving me fewer options for permanent installation unless I decide to place it flush on a workshop table or a place where the battery pack can be tucked away without dangling.Do I like this LED tape light?  Actually I love it, save that one picky, minor caveat.  Otherwise I'd give it five stars.  I plan on using it as a portable strip either for inside use or perhaps my occasional outside needs.  Included are instructions for permanent installation, cleaning instructions, and a brief cautionary note on the dangers of looking directly into the light.  I like this better than another strip I have that gets quite hot and would definitely recommend this alternative over the less expensive, but hazardous light strips.
summary: This is an excellent LED save one minor caveat ...

reviewText: I am going to mainly focus on price on this review. But first, about the product:1. It has 3 fairly bright LED lights2. It is battery operated. There is no easy way to connect it to AC power.3. It has 3M brand adhesive to stick this thing (and its large battery pack) wherever you want.4. It has a high build quality and will probably last a long time, even outdoors.5. The lights are all in a row and because of the way they are mounted, they aren't very adjustable once you install them somewhere.That said, I gave it a 3 star review. It money were not a consideration, I would probably give it 5 stars because it works well and the battery lasts a long time. However, the MSRP for this item is $100 and it is currently selling on Amazon for $50. This is absolutely too expensive for an item like this. The pricing makes no sense at all. There is no amazing feature of this device, the design isn't revolutionary or particularly ingenious. It is just plain expensive.I just don't get it. and neither should you, if you care about saving money. Especially with how inexpensive LED based lighting devices are these days. I can understand if you want a high quality under cabinet light for your garage, but you could just get inexpensive tap lights. The whole thing just doesn't make sense.

Just got this 3M (3) LED light tape and like it. It's unlike most products but useful for inside a car or trunk. It takes 8 AA batteries and does NOT offer input for any outside power supply limiting use. The lightis good for walkways or stairs in the dark, or anyplace needing battery powered lighting. Would be great if it had a timed photo cell option but no luck here, just ON-OFF switch on the battery box. The LED'scolor is good, not too blue but mine very slightly greenish. Each LED has mounting tape and being 3M no doubt should be strong. Price seems a little high for what you get but depening on your needs this lighttape might be well worth it.

We all seem to have a dark spot in a closet or basement that isn't used all the time but where it would cost a fortune to put in a light socket.This tape light can solve that problem. The three lights on the tape are bright enough to light up a good sized closet so you can easily find what you are after. The eight AA batteries make it self-contained, so you don't need to worry about wiring. And, the tape and the battery box come with adhesive patches to apply it permanently on a wall or shelf.My main problem is the battery pack: Eight AA batteries is kind of a lot. Even if you don't use it often, the instructions say that you can expect only about 12 hours of life out of them, so you will want to use rechargeables. Of course, if it is in a closet that isn't used all that much, they could last a really long time. Also, to replace the batteries, you will have to be able to remove the pack from the wall. It attaches to the wall with super-velcro, which will work in _most_ applications. If your wall is something like cinder block, the stick on super-velcro might not be enough to hold it.A lot of the other tape lights are designed by professionals and take some putzing around to get them to work. This short tape is self-contained: Put in the batteries and put it up. No need to worry about wire, transformers, etc. (Compare prices, though. The other light tapes seem to have taken a surprising dip in prices. They may be worth the trouble, depending on your needs.)
summary: For that dark spot in your life

reviewText: Got this to go under a kitchen cabinet where we don't have enough light at times. Very easy to install and I was pleasantly surprised by how much clean bright light it produces from just 3 LEDs. reviewText: I have always been searching for Crappie (aka as Calico) decals for our bass boat that is named Crappie Lander.  We figured this would be a perfect way to make our own custom images that would be unique and stand out since the boat is a glittery jet black.  After finding the perfect sized Crappie fish picture we wanted to use, we printed it on the included stencil paper.  Then I carefully cut out the image using anXacto Precision Knife.  I would say this was the most difficult part of the process since you have to be careful to cut the lines on the pattern.  If you have a complicated image with many turns and twists you may end up pulling your hair out.  The less complicated the image the better.After cutting the image out, you remove the cut out image and then apply the transfer film over the stencil (you end up with two sides with covered adhesives).  It is important the transfer film is larger than the stencil.  Remember that the image that you will be "etching" on is the open area on the stencil sheet, not the area you just cut out - that part you can just throw away.  Now we are ready to apply the image to our boat.  We peeled away the backing of the stencil liner and placed it on the boat.  Smoothed out the image to make sure there were no air bubbles and that the stencil was securely in place.  Remove the transfer film and use the included masking tape to protect the paint in case you go outside the stencil area.  We took the Trizact sanding disc and lightly went over the entire image.  I continuously checked our progress by using a moist detailing cloth to see how things were turning out.  If more sanding needed to do done, we just made sure the area was dry and sanded it some more.I clearly understand the concept of how 3M came up with this idea.  I reminds me of etched glass you see on fancy wine goblets.  I guess only about 10% of your clear coat is actually removed and if you decide you don't like how it looks the image can be easily removed with the3M Scratch Removal Systemand a buffer.  Was this "easy" and did I take less than 30 minutes...NO.  It was not difficult but if you want it to come out looking perfect, make sure to give yourself at least an hour and half.
summary: Not just for cars - custom designs for our bass boat

reviewText: I gave this 3 stars because it isn't fair of me to rate this because of the missing Stencil Film, because of Vine I'm required to post my review so here it is. With the main part of this kit missing I wasn't able to try it out but after reading other reviews and included directions would think long and hard before trying this it on my car. Sanding the paint down is a commitment you can NOT go back on, damage from sanding finished paint work isn't easy to reverse so be very careful  Maybe a bike like another reviewer but not my car. I don't think this is the best way to go to make a custom stencil, have the body shop do it if you must.

I was expecting something that I could just cut out and adhere to my car. There's too much of a process involved and the mere mention of how it can easily be removed with 3M scratch removal system makes me nervous.If you're into hand-crafted artistic endeavors, you can have a blast copying some complex image onto the surface and tracing it out with some type ofXacto knife set, and then apply it to your car. It could make for a fun project if that's you.This is a product for the brave, faith-filled adventurer, for someone willing to experiment on his or her paint job or for someone who has seen it applied to someone else's car first and is comfortable with the results. I am none of the above when it comes to my car's paint, so my apologies for thinking it sounded like a good idea at the time and then backing out. If I was driving my first used car with its dents and scratches I would have been a more willing participant. The "okay" rating will have to reflect the price of the product compared to the price of an equivalent handy craft and the quality of the instructions and materials.

I thought this product offered an EASY way to transfer any printed image onto my car; like printing something on special paper that was easily transferred over. The operative word there being 'easy' and there's nothing easy about this process; at least not for me. The directions show a rather complex star shape, which would be virtually impossible for the average person to replicate, given the steps require precisely cutting the design out with a razor blade. It would be painstakingly tedious work for anyone, including a highly talented artist, to cut all that intricate detail perfectly and come up with a usable design that didn't look like garbage.As if that wasn't complicated enough, then you have to tape the design onto your car perfectly, and hope the stencil doesn't move one iota while you buff the paint off your car with actual sandpaper -!!- all for an end result that looks mediocre at best. I guess if you have nothing better to do, this would be a great little project for a hobbyist. But I seriously have to wonder if there aren't better alternatives that would take less time, look 1000x better, and not require intentionally scratching your car in the process.Bottom Line -- Nice idea, but not for me.

This kit is impossible to use and is not worth the money. Regular vinyl stick decals are easier to apply. The fact that this kit comes with wet sand paper indicates that it is difficult to use and may cause damage to the paint surface.

First off I initially was going to give this product 2 stars but changed to 3  -- the two star rating had more to do with my annoyance at the product than actually how the product worked.I was expecting something much simpler.  As someone who can't cut a straight line to save my life (forget about curved lines) this is not a product for me.  Finally I decided on something simple (the Oregon "O").  -- after talking my husband into cutting it for me the next step was to apply it.  ---While it only takes off a little bit of the clear coat that was not a risk I wanted to take on my new car so I put in on my barbecue stand which has an dark high gloss finish on the doors.  It is a subtle effect.the concept of a make your own decal for a car is great.  however the execution of this product just has too many steps.  I can see this being great for a beater car as a way of personalizing it but not much more than that.Overall too complex and not something I would risk putting on my car.
summary: More complicated than I was expecting

reviewText: As advertised, There's no chemical residue because it requires scuffing the surface of your car. I was not comfortable sanding the my paint job, so we tried it out on our bikes. After printing our designs on the masking sheets, we went out and bought an x-acto (like the other reviewer, we didn't have one either), and cut out our designs. Getting the designs on the curved surfaces of the bikes was probably a little more difficult than doing it on a flat car surface. The sanding made me nervous, but I managed.The results were mixed, the design looked OK on the dark blue bike, but was invisible on the white and silver bikes. It's a cool idea if you are looking to customize your vehicle.

The first thing that anyone interested in this product should know is that this kit is intended to lightly scuff the surface of your car's paint to achieve the intended result. It is by design.  So if you are AGAINST any sort of shenanigans, this is not the product for you.This kit is NOT for the anal retentive car owner that easily stresses out from even the most minor wear on their car's paint.  If you have a $10,000 paint job on your Ferrari, you're probably not in the market for such a product anyway.  This is for the guy (or gal) who wants to personalization their import subcompact, and do it in a fun, cheap, and relatively safe way.With that out of the way, I am writing this review for how well the product performed as advertised.The way this kit works that you use the provided masking sheet in your laser or inkjet printer to print your design.  The masking sheet is a semi-adhesive masking film on a liner sheet.  After your design has been printed, you use a x-acto knife (which was, unfortunately not provided) to trace over the edges of your graphic, so it can be removed from the backing sheet.  Then, you apply a thicker white transfer film on top of the masking film to provide some structure to the film as you remove the liner.  The reverse image is applied directly to your car's paint, and then the transfer flim is removed, leaving the masking film on the car with your graphic in the exposed areas of the paint.  Then you follow a series of steps to lightly sand the exposed area of clear coat to achieve the intended effect.  Again, if you follow the instructs carefully, sanding your paint should remove only 1 to 2% of the top clearcoat.I used this kit to apply an engine rotor graphic my 2004 Mazda RX-8.  Unfortunately the paint color is Lightning Yellow, so the graphic was not terribly noticeable. I imagine on a black car it would be easily recognizable. Therefore I decided to remove it using my 3M headlight restoration kit which I had previously used to restore the car's headlights to a brilliant shine.  The matte image rubbed out very quickly, which was a testament to how light the impact to the paint really was.  It took way longer to remove nearby swirlmarks, which is the only downside of this product--if your car has lots of swirl marks and you decide to remove the graphic, you may have to do a larger area than the graphic to ensure 'even-ness' of the removal.  But other than that, the car looked exactly as it did before.  I was told the removal process takes an additional 3-4% of your car's clearcoat, so all told, it cost roughly 6% of the car's clearcoat, which I believe is an insignificant impact to the paint.  Most professional auto detailers will take off at least that much in a typical swirl-removal job.The only criticism I have against the kit is that it did not come with a x-acto knife, which is required.  I was expect to use it right away but had to defer it to another weekend because I had wasted time looking for a x-acto knife lying around and ended up having to go to the store to buy one with a new blade.Verdict:  Good product, but not recommended for light colored paint.  For best results, work slowly but diligently when trimming your graphic, and take your time with the sanding pads, using very light pressure.
summary: Great results, easy to do.  Very low tech.  Not for light colored paint.

reviewText: I tried a few of the cheap ELM327 OBD2 Bluetooth adapters. They were either DOA or quit working after a few weeks. I had an emissions check coming up on my truck and my latest ELM327 kicked the bucket. The cost of repairs after a failed emissions test can be quite a bit more than the $150 for the ScanTool OBDLink.Two things I noticed right off the bat:1. The ScanTool is made very well compared to the cheap plastic of the ELM327s.2. The ScanTool software works surprisingly well even compared to Torque Pro.Other big things:The ELM327s get hot and never turn off unless you unplug them. The ScanTool never got hot and it automatically turns off when the car is off for a while. It also has a button that you press to put the device in pairing mode. The ELM327s will pair with anyone who gets close enough to your car.
Kelly-K of Shiftn Steel Sport Riderz says it's the tool that will save you time and money by not going into a dealer to get that check engine light fixed! Tells you the codes that the pro's use!

I bought this for use with the Torque Android app and it's performing wonderfully in that setup. I have no complaints. Setup and pairing was a breeze and I have not had any issues reconnecting since I got it. Data transmits over nicely and I have no wire to deal with that I need to route to my device.

Works great with my Hyundai Veloster Turbo, and the Torque app on Android.  It does include its own application for Windows, and there's a proprietary Android app too, but Torque is the most convenient of them all.  Torque has full support for the adapter, including the enhanced data rate mode.Pro:-Turns itself off during inactivity-Turns itself back on when the attached vehicle's ECU does something, like when the doors are unlocked-Only streams data when an application is listening on the other end.  Otherwise it remains idle.-Near instantaneous response, even on AndroidCon:-Expensive.  Premium product at a premium price.-Somewhat large: I could not fit my OBD-II / Fuse panel cover while it is in place.  I tried working around this with an extension cable, but it was no use.  I'll have to cut the cover to make room.

reviewText: Works fine for what I'm using it for. The key fob things are pretty good. But the clip is poor quality. Has already broken after about one week.

First off I'd like to say this unit works excellent. The remote fobs are excellent and the range seems to be pretty darn good.I installed it into a 1996 F250 with an OEM non remote power lock setup. Power locks are nice but without a remote setup their usefulness is somewhat limited. I did a search here on Amazon and came up with this setup for far less than I expected. After reading many of the reviews I knew the instructions would be lacking but decided to give it a try anyway. I'm glad I did.This system isn't super advanced but does offer a couple of features other than just locking and unlocking the doors if you choose to use them. One feature is the notification system. The system shows a wire being hooked to the "direction light." This wire "flashes" once for lock and twice for unlock. The idea is to connect this to your outside directional lights to give you a visual indication that the system either locked or unlocked the doors. I didn't utilize this feature but if I did I think I would connect it to the horn instead of the lights. Just a way to confirm to myself that I did indeed lock the doors before walking away. There is also a wire for unlocking the trunk but with the exception of a label in the instructions there is no indication as to whether this is actually active in this system.A feature that would be nice is to allow the user the ability to "setup" some features. One feature that some may like is to allow the user the ability to change the output of the "flash" output. I would prefer one flash for unlock and two for lock but there is no way to change this. For the price of this unit though it would be hard to really fault this system for its "basicness."The last issue here to discuss is the instructions, or lack of them. The reality is that it would be very difficult to include very extensive instructions because each installation is going to depend on the model of vehicle you are installing this into. A better layout of the basic drawings would be nice though. It took me a little while to figure out exactly how the diagrams related to the included unit but I did figure it out. By far the more difficult part was coming up with the vehicle specific diagrams. the service manual I had included the wrong diagrams and therefore added a lot of work to this installation. That is not the fault of the maker of this unit though, that is a problem with my service manual.Overall I would highly recommend this unit to anyone who feels they can figure out the wiring. If wiring diagrams confuse you and vehicle wiring scares you, then I recommend you either buy something else or have this installed by a professional. Personally I think it works great and was well worth the effort to figure it out.
summary: Works great! Instructions could be better.

reviewText: I got these for my 2005 GMC Yukon to replace the dome and rear map lights. For the dome light, they work perfectly! The map light is a bit more complicated. It appears GMC puts resistors in the rear map lights to reduce the intensity of the map lights. This is really a good idea because if your rear passengers turn on the lights in the back, it will impair the drivers ability to see the road. The tings is, while this does dim the LED lights, they are not as forgiving to the dimming effect and are simply not putting out enough light. Because the lights is so directed from these SMD LED lamps, I don't think they would interfere with the driver. I plan on removing the resistor to get a bit more output from these. That is a project for a future day. Until then, they work GREAT in the dome area.NOTE: Unlike standard incandescent lights, LED lamps are polarity sensitive in DC systems. If you install these and they dont work, turn them around.

Deep Cycle batteries are perfect for prolonged parking, constant drain and longevity, in other words, just what a Prius needs. That 12 volt battery in the rear of the car IS, the heart of your car. When it dies, and it will, just look at your car because that is all you can do...nothing works, period. In case you think it cannot happen to you, wait 'till it does.  There is NO warning and for some reason that little black box of a battery IS the single weakest link in the most reliable vehice in the world. It dies for many reasons, two friends of mine had theirs die and l thought it was so funny to see how they carried on, then it happened to me...no fun at all! You cannot even open the trunk to even think of getting to your 12 volt battery. If an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure...for the Prius make that a ton of cure. All l did was to not quite close a door...the next day?....three thousand pounds of dead weight. Found out that locking the Prius every time shuts down all main parasitic electric draws...wish l had known...now with this Deep Cycle l am good for ten years, at least. Don't push using your factory 12volt much longer than four years...you will avoid the worst nightmare ever. And, oh, no matter what Naysayers tell you, replacement is an easy thirty minute job...watch the U Tube how to...
summary: Avoid THE worst nightmare ever on a Prius.

reviewText: First if you have 2010 or newer Prius, changing this battery is trivial. Earlier models had a strange strap holding it down, but on the 2010, it is the same as any car, except its in the trunk just like a BMW and many other cars these days.My Prius would not start; push the button the dash lights up but car not "ready" can't get to turn off either. Intermittent and Very strange. Actual mileage was great but indicated miles to empty was way way too short. Other odd ball things. Finally got to the point where I got the "can not enter P" message while turning it off. Googled that and saw I needed a 12v battery. Once I looked into that I found out how to get to the display of battery voltage (hold the "info" button on display and turn head lights on and off 3 times. Go  to diagnostics...) and sure enough battery was only at 9 V rather than 12+Changed that stock battery out and it's like a new car. Only odd thing was that the miles to empty was still off by 100+ miles until I bought gas. Now it's all perfect again.

Even the crappiest battery is great at first, but from research this one should well outlast the others and provide superior service, assuming ok treatment.  Check back in 7 to 9 years and I'll let you know if I was satisfied.  In general, discharge and lack of proper charging kills batteries prematurely, with temperature a small factor as well.  This battery arrived with 12.57V (resting volts) indicating 90-100% charge.  It has a "12/13" sticker, which I presume to mean December 2013 manufacture date.  I ordered it January 6th, 2014, so this is ideal.  Thanks to "Everything-Aftermarket" it came quickly and well packaged, though foam padding on the top would be a good idea instead of just packing paper.  The plastic handle is super-easy to remove and reattach, and the lead terminals are the pencil-style used by Toyota Prius.Prius in general tends to kill batteries prematurely due to lots of electronics which have functions while the vehicle is off, such as re-pressurizing the breaks before entry, venting the fuel system, always listening for the key fob, and sometimes powering the dome light or headlights, etc.

reviewText: We didn't get a lot of snow and ice this year but this did the job anyway.  The scraper is solid and I like the fact that you can easily orient the brush two different ways depending on where you are brushing the snow from your vehicle

This brush arrived just in time for yet another Nor'easter here in New England.  It wasn't a huge storm, so it was perfect for trying out this brush.  I personally like the OXO grip products.  I own a couple of other brushes by them, as well as a santoku knife.  Although this brush handle is hollow, it feels thick enough and quality built to me.  The brush on it is thick without being too stiff, and can be rotated with the push of a button for either sweeping, or pushing the snow. And, it has a nice thick scraper on it that doesn't get in the way when you're just sweeping. Although the whole brush does indeed feel solid, I do have to agree with the other reviewer here that mentioned that the rubber grip on the bottom that makes it easy to hang onto should go the full length of the shaft.  Or at least for half of it.  The smooth plastic above the grip gets pretty slippery once its wet, and it's sometimes just more convenient to hold the brush a little higher up.  Not a big miss in my opinion, but something worth mentioning...The only thing I can say someone may object too as to this brush is its length.  I have a small medium size truck, and at 22" it seemed that I was reaching  a bit here and there.  For someone with a big SUV or truck, this would be aggravatingly short in my opinion.  I suggest that if you have a bigger vehicle you move up to the OXO extendable brush that at the time of this writing is only 5 dollars more.  It's basically the same brush with a twist type extendable handle.  As for this brush, I still give it 5 stars.  It's a good quality brush with that great OXO rubber grip that I feel will last, and is reasonably priced... : )OXO Good Grips Extendable Twister Snowbrush

reviewText: I general I love OXO products. I have several of them around the house. I am thrilled that a company focuses on making products that are easy to use and hold. That's doubly true when it comes to products that need to be used in the ice and snow.The OXO Good Grips Twister Snow Brush is about two feet long. The brush on the end of its head rotates 90 degrees and "locks" into position. So you can use it lengthwise or cross-wise depending on what you are trying to brush. The bristles are gentle, which is good. They won't scratch the car's finish.At two feet, it's just the right length to go just past the midway point on my Subaru Forester windshield. If someone had a massive hood it might not quite reach.We like it best in the cross-wise position. You can push and pull the snow fairly easily. One minor down side is that the bristles, as mentioned, are soft. So the times that you have to "wham the brush into the snow" to create a starting position, the bristles don't do that very well. Also they tend to "collect" the snow, not shed it. So the brush ends up looking fluffy and white fairly quickly. You then have to whack out the snow to do another pass.I'm in my 40s and live in New England, so I've gone through many, many snow brushes over the years. This is definitely far better than most of the ones I've tried. I do think I'll still need the stiffer brushed brush in the car for the times I need to break through a thicker layer of snow to get things started, but that's OK. In general I appreciate this brush immensely.I was provided a review copy of this brush from the Amazon vine system.

I live in NH where it snows quite a bit, so I was excited to try this snow brush. I have tried every brush I have been able to find through the years, but this one is much more well made.  I only gave it 4 stars because you cannot extend the handle, it is pretty short. I have long arms but this snow brush still falls short of reaching over the roof and across the windshield to clean off snow.  I like the turning brush head, that is a cool feature but be careful of snow getting caught in the turning mechanism, though you can be a little forceful to get it back into place. I love the handle of this brush, better than any other snow brush handle. Sturdy, thick, no molded plastic, very comfortable and well made. I just wish it had a longer handle or could extend a little. Overall I really like this brush and will buy some for my kids.

A welcome replacement to my old hardware-store bargain-bin scraper+brush combo, the thick handle is easy to grip while wearing gloves (without the resulting ache from having to hold tight to a too-narrow handle).The brush is long enough for a decent reach on my cars but might be short for a taller vehicle.  The longer handle provides better leverage for scraping stubborn ice.The locking button means the brush won't change position suddenly.  I like the adjustable brush, since I use a different motion for sweeping off loose snow vs gathering the icy debris I've loosened with the scraper.The only problem is the minimal snow we've been getting in central Maryland the last couple of years, which is giving me few opportunities to use my new brush!  Recommended.
summary: sturdy and ergonomic-- now I just need more snow

reviewText: I received this brush just in time for a wet snow in our area. I also just acquired an SUV. Since this brush extends, it worked very well removing the wet snow from the roof of the SUV. The brush is stiff enough to push the snow very easily. That the head turns also allowed me to change from pushing the snow to sweeping the snow. This is a well-thought-out product that makes sense. The fact that it also extends means that it is compact when I need it to be and has a longer reach when I need help stretching to reach across the car. A great product from an innovative company! I have purchased OXO products over the years and I think that I should buy stock in this company; if OXO continues like this, it is a worthwhile investment. I trust their products because they work.

So many snow brushes I come across have a wimpy brush - with just a couple of rows of weak bristles that can do little more than dust off a little powder snow. The OXO Twister's brush is much more rugged than most I have used, usefully so. It managed fine with a couple of inches of wet, heavy snow. I like the twist feature, though the brush width is rather small for use perpendicular to the handle.The ice scraper blade is very rugged and works well - I wouldn't mind if it were a bit wider, but that's a tradeoff against scraping force.  The handle is solid and comfortable and usefully long.
summary: Unusually dense brush, swivel feature works well

The color I chose was "Warm White" because I didn't want the bulbs to be too harshly colored. (I don't like the blue-white color some LED's put out. It's too "cold" looking.)Anyhow, I installed these bulbs in my trailer, and they are practically indiscernible from the incandescent bulbs both in light output and color. They don't get nearly as hot as the incandescent bulbs do (they just get warm), and the power consumption is very much reduced. With the incandescent bulbs, I would have half of the lights on, and my trailer's power converter's fan would turn on. Now I can have all of them on, and the fan doesn't turn on. These are way brighter and I can see all the indicators clearly during the day and they are NOT blinding me at night.A few extras for people who are interested:The bulb is a single lens SMD5050 that operates at ~3V and draws ~30mA. In order to allow it to work with 12-14V car installations, there are two resistors in the bulb housing, 180 Ohm each. So the total power draw is 420mW at 14V, out of which 90mW ends up in the LED to give you the light.So far I have not noticed them turning blue over time or anything like that. Not only does this oil fully meet VW 502.00 specs, but I noticed an IMMEDIATE reduction in engine noise, that is only getting better with time. Very impressive.The price on Amazon is about what I paid at my local Autozone for 6 quarts. I'll buy from here next time. Use this oil with confidence.

reviewText: Castrol EDGE 0w-30 SPT Synthetic Motor Oil has been loved and raved about by European car owners for a decade now.  It is one of Castrol's premier products in that it meets so many tough European specifications including Mercedes-Benz 229.5, BMW LL-01, VW 505.00, and VW 502.00.These specifications all speak to the quality of the product. In particular, Mercedes-Benz 229.5 (used in the majority of gasoline engine Mercedes cars the past decade) is particularly tough to meet.The product has often been referred to as German Castrol because for many years it was produced in Germany.  Now, you may still find it made in Germany, but some cases are showing up from Belgium.  Rest assured, it is still the high quality product meeting the tough European specifications no matter where it is produced.The low pour point of this product, approximately -50 Degree Centigrade suggests it has a significant percentage of Group IV Synthetic base stock in its formulation. Group III base stock is also high quality today, but the fact remains that Castrol is putting very high quality ingredients into this premier product. Of course, the oil companies today never tell us the exact formulation, so we can only take best guesses. Nevertheless, it is clear that it is a high quality product no matter what base stock is used because it does officially meet the tough European specifications listed on the bottle.When you have a European vehicle and you use a motor oil that meets the manufacturer specifications, you can feel comfortable going to the full maintenance interval recommended by your manufacturer under normal conditions.This is a highly recommended product. Depending on price and your personal preferences, Mobil 1 0w-40 is another terrific option that meets the same specifications as well as a few additional ones.Note - This product seems similar to Castrol's new 0w-40 product.  One difference though is that Porsche requires a 40 weight, so the 0w-40 product meets Porsche specification while this 0w-30 product does not.

Many of the light fixtures in my trailer are a dual lamp design, so I can leave the standard bulb in one side and put the LED in the other, and use either or both as the situation requires. It's a cool setup that allows me to really dial down my battery use when necessary, but still have plenty of light available . reviewText: I bought this locally because I had a coupon and it was cheap. I had been wanting to try a spray wax, and to be honest I planned on getting one of the more expensive ones, but for $4 after coupon it was too hard to pass up. I didn't expect much, and certainly not what it achieved.Application is about as simple as it gets, you spritz a few times over an area then wipe it into the surface with a microfiber cloth (immediately after a wash, of course). You don't need to drench the entire surface with spray; it spreads rather well, and three or four sprays onto a door panel was enough to spread across the area. As the cloth got wet with the solution, it began to streak a little bit, but the streaks disappear in a few seconds.Outcome: I noticed a nice, satiny shine, almost soft. It gives a nice silkiness to the finish. A nice shine I expected, as well as some water beading, after all it's a spray wax; what I didn't expect was the effect it would have repelling dust. Normally I use an auto-duster every morning, and sometimes in the evening. When I went out to my car the morning after application of the spray, I noticed it just didn't seem dusty. I knew it claimed to repel dust with its static properties, but I didn't put too much stock in it. So I skipped my morning dusting for the first time in a while. After three days I still hadn't used my duster, every time exiting my car saying aloud "how is it not dusty?" Seven days later when I washed the car again, the washing almost seemed unnecessary. A bit of dust began to settle, but not nearly as much as seven days without dusting normally would have produced. Update: I've noticed that during drier days, dust will settle a bit faster.Now, I park on a dirt/gravel driveway, under a car port (a roof, but open on sides). That's usually a guaranteed coat of dust daily. Five days after coating the car with Ice Spray I received a new CA Duster (my old one was shot). I actually put it in my trunk without using it. I'll probably try other spray waxes for fun, but I will be surprised to find anything that works so much better that it justifies the $10-$20 prices that some of them go for. This stuff works so well that the low price makes me feel like I found some secret. FYI the $6-$7 price is typical even at brick and mortar stores.So far as protection goes, I don't expect this to replace conventional wax/sealant, of course (update: actually, if you applied this regularly enough, it might do just that). All I can vouch for is the dust repellent effect and the shine, which I witnessed last almost seven days (note: I mean it reduces it significantly, not eliminates it). My guess is it also provides short-term UV/environmental protection, being that it contains polymers similar to the stuff found in conventional new waxes (I use the term "wax" loosely).Update: I tried applying a second coat for the first time today, with surprising results. I applied it one day, then the next day gave the car a light washing and applied the Ice Spray again. Wow. There actually IS a difference with two coats. The satin-y sheen is even deeper and more pronounced, and more slippery. This stuff is definitely not like some quick detailer. It produces a deep shine, it beads water very well, and if you wanted to, I bet you could apply this stuff once per week and it would be as good as standard waxing. I'm gonna test it out during rainy weather to see if it holds up.

I bought this Turtle Wax ICE spray wax for the specific reason that it says on the bottle "Synthetic Formula Prevents Water Spots". I have used this Turtle Wax ICE spray wax twice on my jetski and it is still water spotted every time I take it out of the water.Before I took my jetski to the lake this time, I used 3M's Marine Cleaner/Wax first to remove any old water spots. Then I liberally applied the Turtle Wax ICE spray wax and wiped it off. I did this twice just to make sure I had applied enough. Got back from the lake and the jetski is water spotted everywhere. Obviously the jetski gets wet but not much different than a car in rain or splashing through puddles of water.I would be satisfied if the water spots came off easily but they don't. I am going to have to use the 3M Marine Cleaner/Wax to get the water spots off again. But next time I will use Eagle One's NanoWax spray wax instead. That is what I use on my two other boats (20' and 16' both fiberglass) and the water spots come right off with another application of Eagle One's NanoWax spray wax.The bottle of Turtle Wax ICE spray wax calls it the most advanced wax yet and that it has a "Synthetic Formula that Prevents Water Spots". Maybe I just got a bottle of water or they forgot to put in the ingredient that prevents water spots. I'll just use it on my lawn tractor as it rarely gets used in the rain.Overall a very disappointing spray wax product that is way over-hyped.
summary: Absolutely does NOT prevent Water Spots.

This fits a 2004 Ranger step side well but is a little narrow and almost allows you to remove the tailgate by sliding the lock to the side. I didn't like that there was so much slop so I made a spacer out of a 1in (inside diameter) washer 1/8 thick, I had to grind a flat on the outside of the washer for clearance but it did take care of the excess slop that some reviewers are getting.I also had some flat rubber left over from a previous project and cut it to fit the washer and glued it to both sides of it using silicone adhesive. I know it's a pain in the *ss but sometimes you have to improvise.As per some of the other reviewers here to offer protection from the elements, and to protect the paint, I cut an old bicycle tube twice as long as the lock and used it as a protective sleeve around the lock folding the excess length over the top after squirting some WD40 into the key hole.After reading all the reviews it seems that there was a change in the construction material used, the lock I received was all metal except for the plastic around the radius, I presume it is to help to keep it from scratching the hinge. Otherwise it does seem to be a secure deterrent, enough to make a thief move on.The diameter of my hinge is 1 & 3/4.
summary: Works well with some minor adjustments.

Why would anyone spend $15 to lock their tailgate on their truck?  After all the truck came with a tailgate lock from the factory.  The OEM factory locks will keep honest people from taking a tailgate, but if the bad guy wants it all it takes is a hit from a screw driver and punch the lock out.  Then simple walk away with your tailgate.This master lock is all metal construction, well built, fits perfect, provides the needed security at a bargain price.  If you want to remove your tailgate simply use the key to unlock the Master lock and proceed to remove your tailgate.With replacement tailgates costing up to and over $3,200 to replace, the price of this lock is darn out right cheap.  Will this $15 investment have saved me from having to pay my deductible?  I won't ever know now that I have it.  On the other hand I no longer have concerns about parking my truck and coming back to a missing tailgate.Make the investment and think of it as a one time insurance payment for your tailgate.

I am a retired auto mechanic who still performs a lot of my own work. Easiest maintenance any owner can perform is an oil change. I use synthetic oil and premium filters and have always replaced the "crush" drain plug washer. I have used several different styles of washers: a stainless steel washer that is similar to spark plug washers, nylon washers, fiber washers and aluminum washers. These washers appear to be the aluminum style with a coating on each side that helps seal the drain plug and oil pan surfaces. I feel these are inexpensive insurance against drain plug leaks and replace the washer on every oil change.

I try to always use only Genuine Toyota parts on my 1997 Toyota 4Runner (see my videos on Youtube under RedonKiLaus).  On my last oil change, the dealer was out of gaskets - but now I have enough for 10 oil changes.  That's probably about 5 years for me since this truck isn't driven every day.

Need to purchase these separately to do an oil change. In my opinion a part like this costing pennies to manufacture should be included with the oem filter cartridge kit. Thus the one star deduction.

Bought this product because it just makes sense,  a truck tail  gate is just plain dead weight.  the install was good and straight forward.  When you first close the gate and then reopen the gate ( hold on as usual) it falls down except for the last may be 8 inches then it coasts down. reviewText: The decal is as illustrated, no profanities as the title may suggest.These are really easy to apply if you follow the instructions.Starting with a CLEAN surface.First rub the sticker with a plastic card (credit card will do) to ensure the image is pressed firmly on to the application paper.Next, peel back the backing paper to reveal the decal stuck to the application paper in reverse. Pull the backing paper off slowly, you'll have the backing paper doubling back on itself as you pull it backwards. Be careful if it is windy, you don't want the decal to fold and stick to itself.Position the decal on the window at one side (the bottom works best so you can ensure it is straight). Then use the credit card to smooth out the decal.Any minor bubbles can be smoothed out, and any that are left will disappear the next time it gets hots from the sun.These look really good.

I love this decal. I have one on each of my two cars. My wife tells me she constantly gets dirty looks on the road by others with a back windshield filled with a stick figure family. She sometimes passes cars that have them just to see if they react in the rear view mirror and to her amusement they do. Even people without the stick figure family get a good laugh out of this decal. While driving home one day a cop pulled along side me and asked me to roll down my window and to my amazement, asked me where I purchased the decal as he wanted to put one on his personal vehicle because he stated his wife had gotten carried away with putting stick figures on her car. Installation was breeze as the instructions were detailed and on point. Take your time and it will come out great. I would also like to mention, the decal has lasted numerous car washes and bad weather.

reviewText: These turned out to have more of a blue tint to them than I was looking for, the problem I have found in the Festoon LED's is that it is hard to match the color of the 194 bulbs.

Installed these in my 05 tahoe as previous other led bulbs started to flicker out. This bulb is bright, after replacing all my interior lights with leds these replaced interior dome light and back cargo area light. These are great and they have heat sinks on back which are a plus also.

The Bosch blade was easy to install and it did a great job while driving in heavy rain and wind gusts condition. They are as good and effective after 10 days of use as they were on day one.Each blade comes with clear installation instructions right on the packaging and I believe that I had it all done in less than one minute which is something given that I'm a little rusty when it comes to replacing wiper blades.
