This meant the cables had to reach over their engine to attach and they sure did. Saved by the length!  Totally recommend these over the short ones.  You never know and since the long ones will work when all you need is a short length but the short ones won't work when you need a long length just buy these!

I HAVE NOT REMOVED THE CABLES FROM THE NEAT PACKAGE AND WITH LUCK NEVER WILLThere are only three things I look at when I buy cables.NO TANGLE IS ESSENTIAL. NO MATTER WHAT.Nobody today makes a inexpensive cable set with high quality clamps and these are the one place some are much better than othersThe wire size and material must reflect the length of the cable.  Aluminum is a deal breaker for me most of the time.  If the advertising does not specify copper you might get a clue from the weight.Normally current ratings involve voltage drop of 10% which is acceptable most of the time.Normally jumpers are used to jump charge a battery that is low or dead. rather than actually start the other engine.Any battery that has been drained to 70% normal terminal voltage is damaged and will never fully recover.  Only high end charger / maintenance instruction books will tell you this.I expect this set to perform as jump charge assets for my lifetime as long as they stay clean and dry.

I hope that I don't have to use them anytime soon in an emergency. I have used them once and let me tell you; they work. They work excellent. I didn't jump off my own car thankfully but I helped someone else. They a good tool to have. I would recommend having these always.
summary: Hope that I don't have to use them anytime soon

reviewText: Great thick cables to get the job done without fear of getting the cords too hot jump after jumps.  A great item to carry in any car or just to have around the house.

With an order of wire and relays, I saw this package of five fuse holders for less than three bucks. Could not pass this up. They hold blade type fuses and have 16 gauge wire, five times. What a deal this was. Thanks to Amazon for that.
These fuse holders are of very good quality. I buy them  a lot. Will continue to purchase them. You can't go wrong with this product
This was a add on item and you get five holders for less than the price of one at my local auto parts store.
I used these to put a fuse on my LED fogs. It worked great and came with 5. What more could you ask for?

Did't work the plugs were off set and the fuses will not plug into them.  Thanks to Amazon for refunding me my purchase price because all they did was take up room in my garbage can.  DO NOT BUY THESE unless you plan on throwing your money away.

These are great fuse holders and the wires are good. No complaints so far except, I'll have to use pliers to get the fuse out as they are IN THERE! No big deal, I guess that's how they should be but jeez, they are really in there.  =)

I have one visor organizer to hold CDs and I wanted another for some other items on the other visor.  This Hopkins VSR Visor Organizer meets my need and cost $4.74 delivered free with my Prime membership.  Not the pinnacle of quality, but with the low price, I give it 4 Stars.

Hi,This product saved my headache, I have a lot of cards, Civil id, family card, medical insurance and so on, I don't want to carry them with my in  the pocket anymore and I wanted something that keeps them organize and readily available in the car. That is what this Visor does!!!Great quality and space is not too bad,  I hooked it up to my 2012 expedition, it is so neat and organized.

I was really looking for 'straps for sun visor'.  Found them.  Two cost more than this organizer with straps...and shipping cost more than the straps!  Found this and am very pleased.  Now instead of just straps, I have an organizer with straps. It's lightweight, mesh pockets so you can see what's in them.  Can't beat the price.
summary: Thought I only wanted straps...til found this

reviewText: I drive a jeep wrangler, and I needed somewhere to store my gate access card for work. This was the answer. It has just enough space for everything I need, and it keeps everything in place, even when the top is down.

I really like having this organizer and having everything secure and at my finder tips.  My job requires me to be in a vehicle about 85% of my time and little things like this really help keep me organized.
Great fit, well made and very light weight and reasonably priced visor organizer.  Doesn't add any bulk to the visor and is very convenient.

This ice scraper mitt is a great concept and certainly keeps your hand warm when you need to scrape frost or ice off your windshield and windows, especially on those cold winter mornings.  If you're looking for something for snow, this is not it.  It's specifically made for ice.  The only hangup I have on the mitt design is that the scraper itself has an elongated point extended toward the left to get the hard to reach places such as around window trims or under the windshield wiper and the direction that it's facing is made for left handed individuals.  I'm right handed so it's a little awkward using it to getunder the windshield wiper.  If the point were going in the opposite direction, I'm sure it would feel more natural to me.  I think if it were expanded on both ends, it may have made it more neutral but alas, it doesn't.
summary: Great for frost and ice, but made for lefty's

reviewText: It seems to be an unwritten law that whenever I am running late, the ice on my windshield will not melt. I have to hop out of the car with a flimsy Dollar Store ice scraper that is only marginally effective, leaving me later, wetter and grumpier than usual.  These mitts may just be the answer.  Essentially, a thumbless potholder with a ice scraper embedded, they promise to keep your hand warm and dry while removing that annoying ice.  The scraper blace itself is far more substantial than most. It is made of thick plasic, about four and a half inches wide. The side has a serrated edge.  The colors are strong an vivid. The red is gorgeous and the black is rich. They are water resistant and have an elasticized wristwith a cuff that is about four inches. The cozy,grey fleece lining is sure to keep hands warm and toasty.They are one size fits all and are ambidextorous.  Lefties and righties, large and small hands will all be able to use these. Although I have not yet had to uutlize them, they seem to be an ideal solution to one of winter's woes and a thoughtful gift for those who have to brave inclement weather.UPDATE 11/28/12-Used this mitt to to clear an ice and snow laden windshield.  It was excellent, cleaning the ice off efficiently and effectively.  The mitt is waterproof and my hand was warm and dry.

My husband and I both have these ice scrapers in our cars.  They are fantasic!  You have to pull off your gloves if the ones you are wearing are thick, but the mitt keeps our hands warm and protected so that it is easy to slip on our gloves again after using and our hands stay warm.The scraper itself has a wonderful edge which takes the ice off nicely.  For tough ice spots the serrated looking edge cuts through wonderfully and allows us to remove the ice pretty well.  We both love the mitt idea.  It makes it so that our hands are not wet or cold, and the ice scraper works quite well and is easy to use and hold on to.
summary: Works Great On Ice In Any Weather

reviewText: I am tired of scraping ice and having it go up my sleeve. This ice scraper mitt will prevent that from happening. We may not get more than a few days of ice in Las Vegas but I do travel and this will be in the truck!

These are really soft and warm inside. Very, very large. I'm 5'3" & wear a size 7 ring on ring finger (wedding ring finger)and these almost came up to my elbows. I was worried that the handle inside the glove would be short but it's really quite long, about 6 inches so you can easily get a strong grip on it. The scraper itself is somewhat small but it did a great job and fast without hardly any pressure needed to remove a thick layer of ice that covered the entire windshield & my hand was warm while doing it. I realized it is somewhat difficult to get the glove up over my sleeve of my winter coat. You definitely need your other hand to help stretch it over so no way could I put both gloves on at once. I'm putting one in my car and the other in my van. Thanks vine....great gift....

X-Gear Solid Ice Scraper Mitts (2-Pack, Black and Red)This is a slightly different take on the classic ice scraper by enclosing a scraper within a plush "glove" that is also waterproof. The plush material feels like the stuff used in many winter gloves and Mechanix Wind Resistant gloves. It is a warm and comfortable polyester material. The outer covering of the X-Gear is a more water resistant cover.The scraper itself is a big drawback to the overall design. It is nothing more than a standard scraper design (flat tapered handle) tucked inside the "glove" and secured with a plastic tie. I confused this tie with the same type of tie used for labels on new clothes, the ones that fit through with a "T" and are supposed to be cut off. Well, after I cut the tie on my X-gear scraper, I noticed the scraper can now be removed from the "glove"!After using the X-Gear for a few minutes on my windshield, the lack of ergonomics becomes very apparent. The ice scraper that I had been using had a much longer molded handle designed for comfort and reach. When using the X-Gear, it is essentially like using the small compact scraper but with a big glove wrapped around it.The material enclosing the scraper handle makes it hard to grip securely. The external mitt can be tight if a thick jacket is worn. I could feel the cold air seeping in through the mit. I felt that if I could wear my regular gloves, it'd be a lot warmer although the gloves could get wet in slushy conditions. The scraper mitt could at least dry out separately while I wear my gloves to conduct other business.The scraper blade itself is very good. It's very sharp and consistent, and made short work of the ice on the windshield.Overall: 4/5 stars. It does keep your hand rather warm and dry, but the scraper itself isn't that ergonomic. The ice chisel design is very innovative though, and comes in handy with surfaces like side view mirrors or the ice that builds up on windshields. I'd give it 5 stars if the scraper handle were designed better.
summary: Scraper handle could be better, still feels colder than using gloves

reviewText: This is a nice product.  I am I big guy and when I have this on it comes up to my mid forearm.  In single digit temps it kept my hand warm while scraping off the snow and ice.  I bought two of them for my car and my daughters.  I would absolutly buy another one if I was in the market, but I can't see needing one anytime soon.Oh, another nice feature is the scrapper pops out of the glove so you can wash the glove!This thing is just all around win!
summary: Scrapes Snow and keeps my hand warm

reviewText: I really like these covered scrapers because I am often wearing a business suit and don't have gloves with me.  The X-Gear design is fairly large (not very good for fitting in a glove compartment) and that can be a negative if you have difficulty with it conflicting with whatever sleeves you are wearing.  It extends 3 1/2" inches beyond your wrist.  This can be a real positive in keeping ice and snow from slipping inside.One very nice touch is that the scraper inside the mitt is covered in a soft cloth to make it a bit warmer to the touch.  Of course this has the downside that you won't be able to grip the scraper handle quite at well.So both major features of these scrapers have advantages and disadvantages to them.  Satisfaction will definitely be a matter of personal preference.

These are awesome.  I put one in my car and one in my wife's.  They are perfect for those times you dont have a glove and you need to brush off a light snowfall.  The handle for the scraper goes inside the glove so you can hold it when scraping.  The inside of the glove is a very thick fleece.  The outside is waterproof and very thick.  These are perfect for those quick parking lot wipe downs that are a necessary part of life.  (Also, pretty funny that these arrived last night and we have snow this morning!)

These scrapers were a lot nicer than I anticipated.  They are thick with a warm plush interior, and a tight fit around the wrist that keeps snow out and holds them on nicely.  The scrapers themselves are thick with a good blade that works well and is firmly attached to the glove. I kept one and gave one to my daughter and we are both pleased with these. They appeared made to last a long time, so I thought they were a bargain.
Fit perfect on our jeep wrangler 2010. Extremely easy to install.Great replacement to original. Nice black finish not too shinny.

Professional quality and appearance.  I couldn't be happier with the look in replacing the chrome JEEP logo, giving more of a blackout look to the vehicle.  Nice way to stand apart from the crowd a bit, even more so when paired with other blackout accessories.
This badge was super easy to install and is a great cheap mod.  Looks great for the people looking for a little different, bolder look
summary: Another great, cheap mod to make your Jeep unique

reviewText: My 2012 MW3 (black) should have come with all black accessories but it didn't.I saw this when "shopping" and had to have it. The hardest thing was removing the chrome "Jeep".This emblem came sandwiched between two pieces of clear palstic which made it an absolute breeze to install!It looks 10x better than the chrome one.Now I need to figure out what to do with the antenna and door key locks.
Getting rid of the chrome emblem changed the whole look of my Jeep. Especially when the entire Jeep is Black and White. The old Chrome emblem was an eyesore. Extremely easy to install and looks great
Very simple, cheap cool way to improve your JK over the chrome logo especially if you have all black accessories on your rig.

I installed the black emblem along with the black bezels for the lights. This gave my jeep a new look. Easy install.  Anyone can do it.  Use a hair dryer to remove the old emblem. Then some acetone to remove the old adhesive. Once it is all cleaned up, stick the new logo in place, and you are done!
The color is perfect. Just shiny enough and so deep black.  I blacked out my Amp'd JK with this and the rugged ridge grill inserts, the Euro light guard kit, and now the front looks awesome.
I have all black components on my orange crush JK.  The black "JEEP" on the grill was the finishing touch I was looking for.
This is nice small touch to jeep, my jeep is all black and this was nice change from Crome to simply black, very easy installation
Originally I had taken my chrome one off, but a Jeep ain't a Jeep without the badge on the grille. Looks much better black.

I'm replacing the chrome accents on my 2011 Sahara Tan JKU with black ones. This was a very easy upgrade. I sat my Jeep in the sun for a couple of hours, went out and the old logo just pulled right off after cutting behind them with some fishing line. Then you're left with some sticky residue which comes off very easily with liquid glue remover and elbow grease. I actually marked just above the tops of the old letters with black perm. marker before removing them. Then you just pull the backing paper off of the new logo and apply - moving the logo up 1/8 inch to just cover your marker marks. There is also a film attached to the front of the letters so they all go on at once, you don't have to apply each letter individually. This took about 30 minutes total to remove the old logo and apply the new one. It's been a month and it still looks awesome - no fading so far.
Went on easy, lined up just fine, and is a good fit for my blacked out JK.  No issues at all after being on for about a year so far.

It is such a subtle change to the Jeep, but it makes a really big difference to me.I am sure the average person will never notice that my emblem is Black and not chrome, but it really is a striking change when you know it is there - especially on a Silver Wrangler.Will have to see how the adhesive holds over time...
summary: You may be the only one who knows...

reviewText: Really looks Great. Did headlight trim, turn signal trim, grille inserts, and didn't like the chrome Jeep up front. Installed the black Jeep in seconds, and it finished the front.

I bought this nameplate to replace the shiny chrome one that comes on the 2013 Rubi (and most Jeeps, really). The letters are separate just like your existing nameplate probably is now, but remember: you install it as one piece by leaving the front backing in place and sticking the whole thing on. To line things up, I just used some blue painter's tape to underline the old plate before removing it. Good stuff. Get one :)
summary: Great for Those That Want to "Black Out"

reviewText: High quality logo that directly replaced my chrome one on my black ops wrangler. Could not be happier. Removal of the old logo was a breeze (just use paint thinner to get rid of the residue and then prep the surface with rubbing alcohol. The logo comes perfectly spaced out sandwiched between two sheets of sticky plastic. Just peel, place, and press. I recommend marking exactly where your old logo was so you can get a perfect stock match. Definitely get this logo if you are looking to get that "black-out" look

got the logo to swap out that old chrome one. Looks way better on the silver 2011 jeep with the black trim the hardest thing with this was getting off the old logo. It is actually a mopar part and is already spaced apart to fit like the stock logo. to install you just pull off the backing and place on the jeep and pull off the plastic on the front and your done.

I own a 2012 Wrangler (white) and I've removed all chrome and the hood logo was the last piece to go.  I replaced it with this black emblem, and it looks awesome.  Getting the old emblem off was really easy using a hair dryer and pliers (just to grab it since it was so freakin HOT).  It was a little work to get the adhesive off, but a little WD40 worked great for that.  Then I cleaned off the film from the WD40 with 409, and finally used an alcohol swab to prep the surface of the hood.The new emblem looks great.  I ordered two more, and plan to remove the Wrangler decal on the side of my jeep and replace them with these bad boys.

When looking for snow clearing devices, remember one thing:  Many states are now requiring that you clear ALL of the snow off of your car, including the roof.I have been looking for a better scraper for the winter, and I think I have found it in the Snow Broom.  It appears to be well made, and the length is perfect to clear the roof and hood/trunk.I'm just waiting for the first snow to run actual tests with it.
summary: Good so far, awaiting test conditions...

reviewText: The good:  Easy to assemble/disassemble.  It's super light weight and it won't scratch.  It locks and has a great read for getting the snow off of your roof.  Ice scrapers are always handy to have, especially one on a long shaft to help with the windshield.The bad: seems very cheap and I can't see it handling heavy snow accumulation.But I do like the concept and it is safer for your car's finish than a houshold broom.
summary: Excellent idea, a little on the cheapo side

reviewText: It is nearly Christmas and we haven't had a huge snow yet.  Tomorrow...ugh.  Anyway, I like that this has both the snow broom and scraper together.  It feels very sturdy and the ice scraper works really well.  When it snows tomorrow, I will update whether or not the broom part works as well as I believe it will, judging from the sturdy construction.I do NOT look forward to using this.Stay warm!**update. It works wonderfully well at pushing snow off of my FJ without me feeling like I am using some abrasive broom on the truck I love.The blade seems to have fallen off of the ice scraper end, which is a bummer.  Maybe the ice was too thick the last time.

Having lived in Chicago, Philly, and soon to be Minneapolis I have seen and used my fair share of window scrapers and various window-scraping conditions. I would put this at a 3 of 5 stars because there really isn't anything special about it and it is almost too specialized.Pro's: Telescoping handle for reaching further is steady and not wobbly; big push pad for heavy snow; decent sized-sturdy scraping unit.Con's: Telescoping handle (I was really excited about this part, but found that the leverage just isn't there to make the scraper work at a greater distance. I'm 5'5" so maybe this is a great feature for taller people who can get the leverage); the push pad is huge and gets in the way if you don't take it off; there isn't a brush to brush off the scraped ice/frost and the pad won't do the job on that stuff.I think this product is great if you are in an area that gets a lot of wet, heavy snow that doesn't freeze to your windshield. But if you live in the real winter areas where that lovely layer of ice builds up on your windshield you will wish you had a standard brush and scraper tool that fits easily in your trunk or on the back floor of your car. This puppy needs the trunk.
summary: On the whole it's OK, but not the greatest

reviewText: We has a 10.5" snowfall last week so I had a perfect opportunity to try this out on my CRV that sits outside.The good is it does do a much more efficient job than a brush and is much kinder to the paint. I like that the foam head unscrews and snaps onto the handle for compact storage in the car and there is a hole in the scraper so it can hang on a nail or hook. When using the scraper end it is best not to have the foam head attached.The bad/inconvienent is the foam head screws on and when using it the head can start to turn if you put counterclockwise pressure on it. The telescoping handle takes a bit of fiddling to get it into the lock position.Aside from those issues it is so much easier to clear snow off my car especially the high roof on my compact SUV I will continue to use it and would recommend with reservations.
summary: I like it but it could use some improvement

reviewText: This is not a bad snow pusher and ice scraper as far as they go.  My only real problem with it is the sheer bulk of the item which makes it a little inconvenient to just store in in the back seat of my smaller car.

I waited for actual snow before writing this review, it's snowed about 3 inches so I unpackaged this unit donned my gloves and hat and set forth to clear my car. There are two clips on the unit where the handle is stored, unclipped the handle and adjusted for size. ( I have a small SUV) First setback was the units handle locking and unlocking system is tight and secure, really really tight and secure! After some grunting and twisting I got the thing set up. When tight, unlike the photo the scraper is at a 90 degree angle to the snow pusher ( more on this later). The foam snow pusher actually did a good job and cleared snow cleanly with no marring, it seemed to hold up to the usual edges and bumps from wipers, antennas, etc. and the length made the job quick.After snow removal I used the scraper end to get the light coat of ice off the windows. Because the foam pusher end is at 90 degrees to the scraper you end up trying to manage scraping with a wet 18 inch or so pusher end oriented up and down dripping icy water on you while trying to scrape horizontally. Trying to unlock the handle for storage with wet cold gloves was an exercise in frustration I managed it by sitting in my car for some leverage. Now I'm no weakling but I can't imagine a slightly built person or a lessor grip actually adjusting this thing on a cold dark wet icy morning with cold wet fingers. I was soaked by the time I was done.Overall, a good idea, but poor execution.

Living in the Midwest, I have lots of experience with snow and the need to remove snow from a vehicle.  This was the first time I had used a snow broom type product.  The best part of the product is that the head is very large and allows fast clearance of snow by pushing and pulling motion.  It also did not damage the paint on my vehicle.  The telescoping pole feature works fine and does not collapse back onto itself when using.  The head does come loose from the pole occasionally, but that may be technique related.  The head unscrews and clips onto the pole for storage.  The ice scraper part is just typical, nothing special.  What I don't like is the overall size/bulkiness of the product.  It takes up a huge amount of space in my trunk, vs. a typical snow brush.  Thus, I have gone back to using my trusty snowbrush and separate ice scraper.  I do think the Snow Joe would be great for someone with a large truck.

The foam isn't tight on the housing and I had a hard time getting the pole to slide on the shaft. I do like that I can store it and it takes up little space in my vehicle but I'm on the fence if I am going to keep it.

Haven't had the opportunity  to use this yet since we've had no snow. But I can say it is made entirely of plastic and styrofoam, so I'm not sure how well it will hold up. It does come apart and store flat, which is a nice feature. The materials seem a little flimsy, but I think if you're very careful with it, it should do fine with light snow.

I've never owned a snow broom before. I excitedly tried this one out on my SUV tonight, and had mixed feelings:THE GOOD:It works very well to push large amounts of snow off cleanly-- even did a better job than my usual brush, with much less effort.THE BAD:The locking mechanism and connection to the "broom." My hands were very cold, which made it hard to screw on the foam "broom" to the handle, but I got it. Then I tried to pull out the telescoping handle, and couldn't. I had to step on the foam and pull up on the handle. That worked. However, it wouldn't stay locked in the "out" position. While I was pushing the snow around, the handle kept retracting. That would be pain enough, but here's what was worse:The handle ALSO kept unscrewing from the foam. The foam was actually spinning around in the wind. I couldn't get it to stay securely on, even though I tightened it as far as it would go. The slightest movement made it loosen and start unscrewing again.So, in short, I'll still keep it handy because even with the annoyances, it got the job done faster than with a brush and scraper and with less worry about scratching my car, but if I were looking for a snow broom, I'd try a different model first.

I lived on Lake Ontario for 8 years. Lake effect snow was a daily topic of news from November to May. So I moved further south to get away but the snow followed me. Luckily not as much.But when snow does cover my minivan, which is parked outside at all times, it is a pain to quickly remove snow before going on my way. The Snow Joe is a good way to reach far, clear without scraping and scratching and get the snow off of the roof.The Snow Joe collapses down and detaches from the head. The handle snaps onto the head for storage.The only issue I had with it was that the handle didn't always stay tightly screwed onto the head and the handle was sometimes hard to lock into the telescoped position.Overall, the foam is nice and gives me confidence that I won't get scratches and the telescoping handle reaches the top of the van and middle of the windshield. The ice scraper on the other end is okay, pretty standard.
summary: Nice Product! Wish I Never Had to Use it

reviewText: This has to be the largest snow pusher/scraper I have ever seen!  The pole/handle is adjustable so you can vary the length of it which is nice for those hard to reach spots.  The snow pusher part...well, it's just BIG, it's made with a foam spongy type material, I'm not sure how long it will hold up, to me the entire thing felt a little clunky due to it's size, but my son thought it worked well.  Nothing spectacular.  I'd have to say that the best feature is the adjustable handle.

When home and the car is out and gets snowed on, I usually use a broom to clear it, though I think that might not be great for the paint. (When away, I use a brush/scraper combo thing.) So I was pleased to try this out. It makes light work of pushing the snow off the car, and I love it for that. Additionally, for scraping, the long handle makes scraping go a bit easier in places. I think I am going to be very happy to have this this winter. Four stars because it's just not excellent... the foam end will wear out and as another reviewer said, the scraper end ends up at an odd angle, relative to the foam end. But I like it.Pros:1. Long length and large foam rectangle means you can push snow off quickly.2. Long handle was also helpful for scrapingCons:1. Blue foam end is probably just the right thing, but it doesn't seem durable2. The two ends should be at the same angle, but are at 90 degree angles.Overall, I found it to be a helpful tool, and I'm happy to have it this winter.

I normally hate snow, but after getting this, it was pure torture waiting for the snow to come.  Thankfully, it finally did.This is everything the manufacturer says it is.  I have grip problems because of disc issues in my neck, yet I was able to easily able to unscrew the handle to its full length.  Because I'm short, I needed the full length of the handle to get the roof of my Hyundai Sonata.  This Snow Joe made it very easy to clear the entire width of the car's roof from one side, without having to walk around to the other side of the car.  The ice scraper worked very well on my windows, and I was able to clear both sides of the windshield (again, from one side of the car, without having to walk around to the other side of the car).So, if I like this Snow Joe so much, why did I mark it down a star?  Because the handle gets COLD -- FAST!  It wasn't horribly cold for these parts (around 30 F), and I normally wouldn't bother with gloves if I'm just clearing snow from the car without having to go anywhere.  While it took less time than it usually does to clear the snow from my car (probably less two minutes to scrape the windows AND clear the snow from the rest of the car), by time I was done, my hands were painfully cold -- even though I had been storing the Snow Joe in my warm house.  Be sure and wear gloves when you use this, even if you normally "don't need no stinkin' gloves!"
summary: Let it snow!  Let it snow!  Let it snow!

reviewText: Driving with snow on your car or truck is not only dangerous it's just dang rude.  Eventually that snow will fly off, or worse, ice over and fly off creating unsafe conditions.  Shoot, in many states it's illegal to leave snow piled on your car/truck so, use this to push or pull it off.The blue blade is foam, no sharp edges, no way to scratch up your vehicle.  It's light weight and when disassembled is rather compact.  I say disassembled because to remove the blade, you have to unscrew it. I expected that it would fold, but the unscrew thing isn't a problem.
summary: Snow Broom, soft and safe for your car

reviewText: The Snow Joes easily pushes heavy, wet snow off the roof, hood, and trunk of your car and works better than brooms. It's made with a durable reinforced molded polyethylene foam head and prevents scratching. The telescoping handle extends up to 49-inch providing maximum reach with no strain on the operator. The snow joe snow  features an ice scraper as well to assist with ice buildup on your windshield. This product breaks down to a convenient size when not using and offers a two year full warranty. To extend the snow broom for the first time, screw the pole to the foam head. Twist the bottom portion of the pole to the left and pull hard. You will only need to pull hard the first time you use the snow broom. To lock the lower pole in place, simply twist the pole to the right.
I have a 3/4 ton truck and like these snow removers.  This one would have gotten 5 stars if the handle was longer

I was looking forward to getting this Snow Joe, and when it arrived we quickly saw both pros and cons.The long adjustable handle is both a pro (great for staying dry while brushing off your car in the snow), but also a con - (the handle is nearly impossible to open and once you finally open it -- impossible to close) - I could barely fit it in my trunk with the handle stuck in the "extend position".The wide broom portion is a definite plus for cleaning off a car in a hurry; it's nice and lightweight as well. I'm not sure how durable the broom portion will be because it seems to be made of some sort of styrofoam?The ice scraper is another con - it's a very small scraper (just over 3") which was surprising for having such a large broom on the other end.  However, at $20.00, the price is a pro.  Good gift item for a coworker too.
summary: Good but it has some cons too

reviewText: This Snow Broom is an improved "snow pusher" for 32 cents more than I paid for my smaller version (Sno Brum Snow Removal Brush) several years ago. Thanks to Amazon Prime's free shipping, the new, larger "broom" actually cost me $8.63 less than the old one. And, it has an attached ice scraper. This is absolutely the best automobile snow removal tool ever invented. You get a clean car with no scratches. You should order one right now so you are ready for next year's snow.
summary: Upgrade to My Old Snow Broom

reviewText: Wish I would have gotten one of these years ago.  We've received more snow then usual here in NEPA this past season and this has helped clean the cars off much faster (with excessive snowfall) then a scraper or regular broom.  Telescoping handle is very nice and the scraper on the other end is great as well.Def worth the investment.

I live in an apartment, so if it snows, my car is getting covered. This "snow broom" is sturdy enough to pull even heavy, dense snow off my car without scratching it. It even retracts and folds up neatly so that it doesn't dominate the floor of my backseat area. It's a little awkward for heavy scraping, but it does work. If you have to park your car outside when it snows, this is a good way to get an overnight's worth of accumulation off of your car.

Due to lack of current garage space one of our vehicles is staying outside in the winter for the first time and here in the North East we're going through a particularly bad cold, blustery spell. It was with great relief that I received the combo ice-scraper and snow 'broom' as, up until now, we haven't needed one and so we were without.The telescopic stem comes clipped to the foam broom for storage and easily screws into the base for use. On one side is a firm plastic scraper and the other has the hardy blue foam rake. Our car was covered in snow about three inches deep and it was quickly dispatched by using the sturdy but soft broom part. It was so cold that the wipers were frozen to the screen and after using the scraper to get off the ice I used it to pop up the wipers so they would work.There's no chance of damage from using the scraper or the broom and really it's a simple fact that without it I would not have been able to drive my car. So for that, and the super low price, this is a five star product.The fact that it can be folded back up for storage is just the icing (hah!) on the snowy cake.
summary: A new car owner in the snow

reviewText: Having started from scratch in my parent's garage I built a body shop that became the largest shop in the Western County. I had 11 full time employees, some of the best in the industry, and spent more time polishing old world lacquer, and then finally urethane finishes (after they took the lead out of the lacquer and it wasn't the same anymore). It was a twenty year run and did high end collision work serving the local Benz and BMW dealerships. Using Lamb's wool sheepskin shearing bonnets and ultra fine compounds after fine sanding, finally finishing with swirl remover and machine glaze, and hand glaze would produce a finish so incredible that you had to tone it down in order to match the factory finishes look. This is one subject that I could write a book about. I literally spent thousands and thousands of hours behind a polisher like this Bosch. Thank you for giving me the opportunity to establish my qualifications. Now onto the review.I am comparing this Bosch GP712VS polisher/grinder to the Makita 9227C and are priced competitively. In no particular order I am going to review features. The Makita has a 3 prong outlet and the Bosch has a 2 prong outlet. I noticed right away that the Bosch did not insert into the power strip plug in very convincingly. I plugged and unplugged several times and realized that the problem of becoming unplugged on extended polishing was a certainty. After comparing it to the Makita that the third prong in addition to the secondary grounding it also established a much stronger connection to the outlet.The Makita makes quite a thing to do about having easy access brushes for more frequent inspections but having to remove a couple of screws attaching the outer housing isn't much of a hindrance so this isn't especially important. For example if you are using it with heavy use it is recommended to check every 6 months.RPM's start at 750 on the Bosch and goes up to 3,000. The Makita starts at what seems like 0 and also goes to 3,000. The Bosch starts with an instant full on safety switch, but the Makita is a soft start. That is a plus in the safety feature department because although the tool should be unplugged before changing bonnets etc, but in reality that doesn't always happen. The soft start on the Makita would give you a forewarning if you accidentally squeezed the trigger when it wasn't intended to, but the Bosch lockout in the default position absolutely the safest way for disc changes. Both have a single wrench change disc button in the head. So you can lock the head with an easy access button while using a single wrench to unlock the disc. By the way these polishers come with the snap hook pad type, but standard grinder backing pads are available in the 7" that would install on this as well. You will need the attaching nut for that style of backing pad as well. I also like the side handle configuration as seen on the Makita 9227CY which could be due in part to my growing accustomed to that handle. On the other hand I find that with the wrap around handle which both the Makita and Bosh have are fine for flat surface polishing, but when the bonnet gets snagged on something like a side door rear view mirror, door handle, or antennae base etc it tends to grab it. I find the wrap around handle to have less control in those types of situations because you are in a weaker control position due to not having any leverage. With a side handle the polisher runs less of a risk of ever flopping sideways in the crunch moment.The trigger switch is a bit tricky on the Bosch with 3 different slide forward positions. First one/default you can't squeeze it. (That is good for changing pads). You have to slide it forward and hold it there for starts. It is spring loaded to slide all the way back to the safety position so keeping it in that middle position is a bit of a challenge. This is an important factor because when you are initiating a new polishing spot, the procedure is you smear the bonnet on the surface usually about a foot square while feathering the trigger. This soft start approach by using the feathering trigger technique keeps the material on the car instead of flying away at full speed. Only when you have it "smeared" over the area do you speed it up to the 2400 speed which is the recommended speed of dedicated polishers in order to obtain the most gloss. The soft start on the Makita makes this procedure easier to do. So feathering the Bosh full on switch on and off while having to resist the spring trying to slide it back, and staying off of the third and foremost position of the switch keeping it full on is a bit of gymnastics. The Makita has the good old fashioned on/off switch with a keep on button on the side.The Bosch is a 12 amp polisher, and the Makita is a 10 amp polisher. So the Makita is a gentle giant but the Bosch is stronger workhorse with 2 more amps. Both have sufficient power for polishing and most all grinding tasks. (Commercial grade grinders spin at 6,000 RPM's and built heavier which are designed strictly for grinding purposes) The lighter weight of these polish sanders are just what the doctor ordered for a tool that you will often be using for extended periods of time. The Makita is listed at 6.6 pounds and I could not find any published weight for the Bosch but doing a side by side lift they both appeared to weigh the same.In conclusion the Makita with the ease of use of the on-off switch which is ideal for polishing wins as a polisher. The brute force and quick starts which is good for grinding, and not so for polishing wins in those regards. So if you are planning on doing mostly grinding and polishing occasionally, the Bosch wins. Both are fine tools. You can't go wrong either way.
summary: Five Stars for a Five Star Product

reviewText: I wanted to love this buffer.  The manual says it is intended for polishing and brushing metal and polishing stone.  The assembly instructions refer to several pieces that were not included.  However it does not say they are options and doesn't give any part numbers or info so you may order them.  All that is in the package is the buffer with D-Handle and mounting bolts, a velcro backed polishing plate and the manual.  So you can't use this buffer without at least buying a foam pad.  For almost $200, they could at least include one pad.  The gold standard Porter Cable polisher includes a foam pad and sanding disk for $60 less.My sample unit was leaking oil from the gearbox.  Also, I'm not crazy about the trigger assembly.  It is awkward to use in my opinion.  I'd prefer the standard trigger with button lock but the "Tri-Control" paddle locks even when you don't want it to and it's easy to bump it off when you are using it and want it locked on.  Not a great design...These quirks aside, I found this to be a very powerful and capable buffer.  Other than the aforementioned trigger, it is very comfortable in my hands and you can put a lot of pressure on it without it straining.  The electronic feedback keeps the speed constant regardless of the amount of pressure you apply.  The operating position is very comfortable and the polisher has 6 speeds from 750-3000 RPM.  I'd advise anyone who has not used a standard polisher to be careful and start at slow RPM.  You can easily burn through the paint or leave swirl marks if you use too much pressure or high RPM.  A random orbit polisher is a better choice and more forgiving for anyone not experienced in using this type of tool but if heavy cutting or sanding is required, this machine is very capable.
summary: Decent tool with some quirks but pricey for what you get

reviewText: This is the real deal. I own an old airplane and it needed some work. I used this to buff the old plexiglass windscreen and to bring back the sparkle to the old paint. The adjustability is perfect and so is the weight. I'm super happy with this polisher and look forward to using for many years. I'll probably have to designate who get this in my will otherwise my kids are going to fight over it.

This Bosch GP712VS Large Angle Polisher is a car finish tool called a rotary polisher.  These polishers are used by professional body shops, detailers, etc. Combined with pads, such as cutting, polishing, and finishing pads, and chemical products to do a variety of processes to a paint finish.  With the correct combination they can remove minor defects and swirls from a car's paint, apply polishing oils, and apply wax.  It is important to note that no pads are included with the polisher.  Pads would have to be purchased separately and attached via the supplied backing plate.However, much of these processes are truly left to a professional.  This machine is powerful enough that if the technique is not correct with the proper pad and liquid product, you can "burn" the paint finish.As simply a pro-consumer, I choose to use a DA polisher instead as it's much safer on the paint as I do not have any professional training or experience.  Nevertheless, I did strap a non-aggressive finishing pad on this product, set it at a low speed, and applied some wax.  It worked great.  The quality of this Bosch product is apparent.  It has good weight to it, and a motor that sounds oh so professional and strong.One look at this product and you will see and feel, it is truly professional quality.  If you are a professional, you likely know with this polisher, you are buying one of the best!  Recommended for professionals.  Consumers should stick with a DA polisher or work by hand.

The Bosch large angle polisher is well balanced and seems to function well at various speeds. I like Bosch tools and have a few and have always found them to be good quality. Here's the problem... I acquired the polisher to polish, which it seems to do well, but I also wanted to use it for sanding. It would work well particularly for taking off paint or rough sanding or some limited grinding. There are few if any sanding discs available. The Bosch site itself only sells hook and loop up to 6". This is a 7" machine. I shopped Home Depot, Farm and Fleet and Menards and found nothing in hook and loop in the 7" size.I did find some on line, but they are very expensive and must be bought in large quantities. Amazon sells only one disc type in the 240 grit for about $16. for three. If you just want this machine for polishing, wool, hook and loop buffs are available for about $12.-$15. I have little doubt judging by the solid feel of the machine and its seeming power and variable speeds that it will work well if you want it only for polishing. If you want it as a more versatile machine, look elsewhere.

I just put on the wipers, and after two weeks (and two rains) notice that they just don't wipe as effectively as my Rain-X.  I will try to clean them to see if that makes any improvement.Otherwise the fit was good, easy installation, and they lasted more than a day (unlike the Anco's I bought when I had no other choice).  Like the idea of the wear indicator as well, but not sure how accurate it is.
summary: Better than Anco, Not as Good as Rain-X

reviewText: These wipers come with four different types of adapters which should make them compatible with most car makes.My car uses the most common type of adapter, the J-hook.  I have always gotten blades that have an obvious hook on them and have snapped them on without even having to think about it.These required several minutes of me having to think about which adapter to use, although the pictures showing each type of adapter on the inside of the cover was pretty straightforward.It took me several minutes of struggle to get the adapter for the hook type mechanism to fit securely onto the blade.  At first I had simply put the adapter into the connecting place on the blade, but it clearly wasn't secured and would simply lift right off.  After a few minutes of puzzling over the installation picture, then trying different things on the adapter, I finally was able to get it to snap securely onto the blade.The adapter seems a bit big and bulky.  It's a minor point but still, it is definitely bigger than other wipers have.Right after I installed these on my car we had a nice downpour here, our first in many months.  These performed flawlessly.I did not remove the little sticker that covers up the yellow wear indicator.I can tell when a wiper blade needs replacing easily enough and don't want a yellow reminder to look at.  Here we get so much sun glare year round that I replace wiper blades about once a year, and tires every two or three years, even though they still have plenty of tread, due to rubber rot.These seem about as good as the Bosch wiper blades they replaced, although not quite as simple to install due to having to attach an extra piece.

I was very surprised at how easy these are to put onto the car and especially appreciate the video here on the product page. Even more, it is nice to have wipers that work well both in rain and snow.My Saturn requires two sizes (one for driver and a different for passenger), so be sure to check sizes before buying.

The ACDelco 26" Clear Vision Wiper blade fits the driver's side and the 21" the passenger's side of my 2004 Dodge Durango 4X4. The wipers themselves perform great! They "hug" the windshield, leaving a streak-free clear field of vision. What worries me is the flimsy hardware. The clip/bracket is only held together with a small piece of cheap plastic that can easily come off. With the harsh winters we have here in Western New York, I worry these wipers will easily break off when frozen to my windshield.It will be interesting to see how the wear indicator works out since it is suppose to take out the guess work of when to change your wipers. I was always going by the the numbers of streaks left behind to let me know it was time for new wipers.UPDATE 01/22/2013It happen...we have about 4 feet of snow fall and the temperatures fall down to 10 degrees Fahrenheit. I went to lift the wipers off the windshield and I saw one of the black plastic brackets fly up in the air and was left with the wiper on my hand. Luckily I was able to fins the bracket to attach the wiper back on till I could get back home to change them to a winter wiper.I believe these are probably a great Spring or Summer wiper but not made to tackle a harsh winter.
summary: Shreak free and hugs windshield but...

reviewText: I received two of these wipers (20" and 22") for my 2003 Toyota 4-Runner.  I had been using theBosch 20-CA Clear Advantage Beam Wiper Blade - 20"- a pair of them - prior to switching out for these.Both products offer excellent windshield wiping 'clear vision' without squeaks or streaking, which makes both products winners in my book.  However the Bosch is my choice over these ACDelco ones.Why?Well, the ACDelco 20ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blades sit up higher (have a higher profile) than the Bosch ones.  That means that when the wipers are on, I see them in my peripheral vision more than I'd like.  It didn't seem like a big deal at first, and I thought I'd get past it, but the more I used them, the more distracting it became.The blades come with 4 adapters and 'not great' instructions, but they're easy to install and work well. For the price I wanted to like them as well as the previous (Bosch) brand, and I didn't.The wear indicator is a nice feature if it works, but like the 'maintenance' light on my car that goes off automatically when it thinks I'm due for an oil change - it's a suggestion.In the case of wiper blades, if it's still working - I'll still use it! We all use things differently and in the case with wipers, in different environments.  For example a car that has these wipers and is driven on the coast where the air is salty and wet, should have a much faster wear on the blades than someone in a non-salty environment.  Just like a car left in the hot sun for months out of the year versus being garaged, would have a different wear on their wipers.Overall, these are top notch blades with a slightly elevated list price.  They are easy to install, but may be taller than you'd like when compared to other brands.  If they were the same price as another brand I like I still wouldn't get them because the fit on my car isn't what I like.However, the product is a good one in terms of function, and you truly won't know if they are right for your car until you try them.  Unless your car is a 2003 Toyota 4Runner and in that case - skip it.
summary: Quality wiper, slightily more expensive than comparible and may be too tall for your liking

reviewText: By and large this is a very good replacement blade.Not the cheapest but certainly there are more expensive replacements out there.Double check your vehicle's specifications before ordering.Easily installed.As with most new items, time will tell how well and long the wiper blade will maintain a clear windshield.
summary: Fine for now...time will tell longevity...

reviewText: Down here in the swamp life is hard on a wiper blade. We don't park in the garage, though I hear some people do, but I put that down as yankees pulling our chain. Everyone knows garages are for storage and possibly gramp's still, not that I anything about no moonshine, no sirree.What I do know is that a wiper blade will get hit by humidity so thick we can swim through the air, the sun beating on it mercilessly, rain pouring onto that wiper blade like a car wash! It will be hit with hail, road debris flying through the air, and chunks of rocks off the back of illegal dump trucks and legal ones alike.And through it all we expect it to clean our windshields! and the ACDelco does just that. Easy to install, which various size clip included to get it perfect for our car, a great large cleaning arch and a blade that clings to to the windshield tighter than that 'gator did Uncle Beaudreux's leg that time they were mudbug fishing down in the bayou.We have had these going on several months now and they continue do to the job of wiping our windows from the muck and rain and clear us a nice spot to see all the crazy drivers down here when it's raining. You'd think we'd be the best drivers in rain anywhere, being used to it and all, you'd be wrong. But with the ACDelco clear vision we can see 'em slamming on their brakes, makings sudden crazy lane changes, in pouring rain.Recommended highly if you live in a swamp, or any where else!
Wiper came loose and allow arm to scratch wind shield. I even check several times to made sure wipers are attached securely. Lousy design.

I've been using beam blades for some time now, but just for kicks I bought a really cheap traditional blade to see if the performance was really any different.  Initially, all blades seem great - they wipe well and all perform about the same.  Beams are definitely nice in the winter time and that was reinforced by my recent test with the traditional style.  On highways, the beam stick to the windshield better and chatter less.I've tried many different types of beams from Bosch, Valeo and others.  The ACDelco's rate right up there with them, and honestly even among the "premium" vs. standard beam blades, I have never seen much difference in performance even when the price is substantially different.This blade in particular is very easy to install on my 98 Camry.  Over time it's just like others where it'll leave small streaks, but generally won't miss a large swath.  Also like all beam blades I've tried, their aerodynamics cause a bit of a low pressure zone right behind the blade, causing some water to follow the blade from the edge of the windshield back into your view.  This is the most annoying aspect of them to me, and these blades have that effect just like all the others I've tried.In summary, I think this blade performs as well as any other brand of beam blade, so in the future, price would be the deciding factor for me.
summary: Great initially, but average as time goes on

reviewText: 4/10/13 UPDATE: since these wipers are a Gold Box deal today, I thought some would want to know that these wipers are still performing well after approx. 3 months.  They have been through snow, ice & rain, and the wipers still grip the windshield well & do a nice job of clearing without streaking.  At the current GB price, I would purchase the wiper despite the high profile snap.ORIGINAL REVIEW:As with most wipers that I have tried, these ACDelco wipers work quite well out of the box.  They grip well in rain & snow events and do a great job clearing the windshield.  However, time will tell.  My car is an outside car & is exposed to beating down sun, below zero cold, ice and snow.  I will update this review in a few months to let you know how the wipers are doing.Installation is easy, but you need to make sure they are snapped in.  My installer (spouse) did not & after a couple of uses, one of my wipers fell off when I was trying to clean my windshield. With a quick snap back on, the wiper has stayed in place since.The only mild annoyance about these wipers is that they seem to have a high profile snap mechanism (they stick up pretty high).  I've kind of gotten use to them, but I still notice.So, overall, as with most new wipers, the ACDelco wipers are performing well.  I will update with a report on the yellow dot sensor & the longevity of the wipers when exposed continuously to outdoor elements.
summary: Work Well But High Profile Snap Mechanism

reviewText: There are quite a few reviews I read where they had assembly problems - glad it wasn't just me!The instructions are very small and non intuitive. I ended up needing my car owner's manual to see how to remove the old wiper - but that's more of my car problem (Honda), not this wiper.My car is a 2007 Honda Civic. The style of my wiper (and for Honda wipers in general I believe) is the 'hook' style. See the pictures they have on the product page. For the 'hook' style notice the adapter you have to use. BTW, this package comes with all kinds of adapters depending on which one you need for your car, so that's good. Kind of wasteful too I guess, but you should be covered for your car.When I finally got my old wiper off, this was easy to install. BUT, I cannot put the original Honda cap over the wiper - it won't fit. So the new wiper changes the looks.But I don't really care much about that - the wiping action is really good. At least for now (I've only used this for a few weeks). Doesn't leave any smears, cleans very well.Not sure how to recommend this product - it works well in it's cleaning/wiping action. But it might be difficult to install (more because of the old wiper for me), and it may change the look of your wipers (so you can't mix and match for sure, unless you don't care about looks!). You might want to look at some instructional pictures/videos for more information on the installation..But if wiping/cleaning action is really important to you (and I'm sure it is to some degree), this one works really well in that regard.Hope that helps.

I really appreciate that the product page for this item contains an installation video. Watching that before installing my wipers made installation a breeze. I had them installed in just a few minutes. These wipers appear to be sturdy and well constructed. They do a good job of wiping with no streaks. Overall, great product.

These are generally OK blades in that they do what they are supposed to do - clear the windshield. However, I found them to be a clear notch below the Bosch ICON in terms of both performance and build quality.On the plus side, the ACDelco's come with a wide variety of attachment accessories. I can't imagine there is a wiper arm that these won't fit on using one of the supplied connection adapters.The overall heft of the blade, however, is definitely lower than that of the ICON. The ACDelco's are lighter weight and just don't feel as "solid" as the Bosch.That translates to performance. I put the ACDelco on the passenger side, and kept the ICON (about 1 month old) on the drivers side. The Bosch cleaned very well - no streaks or misses. The ACDelco left some water in streaks on the upstroke, but got them on the downstroke. The Bosch were almost silent; the ACDelco made some noise - not what I'd call loud, but certainly louder in operation than the Bosch.The unique feature of the AC Delco is that it has a "wear strip" that turns color when (supposedly) it's time to change the blade. I don't see much value in that. I change wiper blades when one (or both) of the following occur:1. It makes more noise than I can live with2. It does not clean the windshield to my satisfaction.I really don't need a color change to help me make that decision.While the Bosch cost more, for me they are worth it. The AC Delco are less expensive but less effective. If you're not fussy about wiper blades these are worth a shot; if not go for the ICONs.
summary: Works OK; not as effective as the Bosch ICON

reviewText: Living in the Pacific NW, we get our fair share of rain, sleet, hail and a little snow.  I decided to test this wiper out against theRain-X 5079279 Latitude 8-In-1 Premium Graphite Coated Wiper Bladethat we had just installed on our 2000 Chevrolet Impala.  Both install very easily (We put one on either side) and the price point on each is similar and something we are comfortable paying for a good wiper. Where they differed was on performance; the ACDelco was the clear winner when it came to wiping the windshield and coming into contact with all the areas it should have. I'll assume that it's in part due to its claim of having "1,500 pressure points".  All I can say is that the Rain-X one missed two very small areas on our windshield because it wasn't connecting with the glass just right.  Overall I'm pleased with this wiper and will come back (hopefully) to update it when the wear indicator appears.
summary: I can see clearly now, the rain is gone!

reviewText: I installed these Wipers on my truck and it only took me a few minutes. My truck uses a hook lock to hold the wiper blades in place so it was just a matter of snapping the correct adapter into place, pulling off the old wiper blades and installing the new blades. While replacing my wipers I was comparing these new blades to my previously used Bosch Clear Advantage blades. In many ways they are very similar but overall these blades look slightly cheaper and the hook adapter is noticeably larger and stands out more. The size of the adapter isn't a huge deal to me but if I was deciding on which blades to purchase and they were both similar in price then I would probably go with my old blade because they look better. These have worked well so far and give me a clean and streak free window when it comes to rain. They aren't the best when it comes to ice but most wipers aren't. They remove snow effectively as well. They also have a indicator on them that turns yellow when it's time to replace the blade. Sounds like a cool idea but really shouldn't it be obvious if you need new blades because they will start to streak or break apart. These wipers perform well I just wish they would minimize the size of the adapter to give them a sleeker look.
summary: Gives a clean and streak free window. Good in the rain and snow.

reviewText: I am a big fan of these single beam wiper blades, and this blade works well. The blade contours well to the windshield, no missed spots, no chatter.The wear indicator seems to be a small colored dot that changes color over time, not really a "wear" indicator, but an indicator for the lengths of time the wiper is exposed to the elements. Perhaps this blade lasts so long they want to remind you to buy another set?The downside of this particular blade is the adapter. It is big, bulky, and overly complex. I am glad they post the video online because the instructions may not be clear.The install of the proper clip is fairly easy, but there are too many parts in the box, no indication as to what needs to be used together, and it is difficult to identify the proper orientation for the clip to be installed.I use what I thought was the most popular u curve slide in clip. The adapter for that type on this blade is very large. Most wipers I have used have a very low profile for this type, the u curve slides easily into the main connector. But on this blade you have to add a bulky tower connector and the u curve attaches there.If you have a blade that slides down into a hidden area, I wonder if there might be some clearance issues. My car doesn't have that so I stare at that big black box right in front of me all the time.

These are fantastic wiper blades made by ACDelco.  They went on easily and have been working great to keep my windshield streak free.  I have great vision driving in the rain when using these and they do their job perfectly.  They do a great job of hugging the windshield. They have a built in wear indicator that lets you know when to replace them, and I am curious to know how long these are "suppose" to last.  I highly recommend these for your car.

This ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade replaced the worn out OEM passenger side wiper on my G35.  The newer beam style design works much better than the old spring-loaded metal framed wipers.Likes:>Easy to install.  Includes several wiper adapters.  Motorists who have replaced wipers before shouldn't have any problems.>The beam design utilizes a flexible plastic frame for increasing the contact points on the windshield, and exerting more down force on the wiper for large, consistent, clean sweeps.>"Advanced rubber technology" claimed by ACDelco does work better; provides less streaking and squealing of the wipers for smoother operation.>So far I've only used this wiper during two rain showers.  Noticeably smoother when clearing light rain/mist and had no problem clearing the windshield during heavier downpours.>Comparable to theBosch 22-CA Clear Advantage Beam Wiper BladeI'm currently using on the driver's side.Dislikes:>Costs about double the price of conventional wipers and more than the Bosch CA Beam wipers.>Questionable effectiveness of the wear indicator on the side of the blade.  I usually replace blades when they start to crack, tear, streak, or squeal.Overall:This wiper does its job very well but costs more.  Long term durability and resistance to the elements (most wipers degrade just sitting under the sun) remains to be seen.
summary: Newer beam style windshield wiper works well.

reviewText: One thing that is a must for me is a good set of wiper blades given the variety of inclement weather in our area.  Mind you, I'm putting these blades on a car that is what I call my fair weather car.  I'm not on the road with this particular car unless the weather promises to be reasonably good.  If you are in a particularly snowy area, you may wish to bypass this type of blade and head directly to winter blades.  These are touted as all weather, but simply trying to clear the existing snow on my windshield didn't appear to be as effective as snow blades on our truck.Installation is fairly simple and if you are unfamiliar with the blade setup on your vehicle, simply insert the information into the Amazon "Find Parts that fit your vehicle" and you'll be sure to get the proper fit.  Also, make sure you order from the same type of blade.  For example this one is ACDelco Clear Vision, but they offer other styles.  They may fit, but two different styles of blades could be problematic.  Some vehicles take two wipers of the same length, while other take two different ones.  The directions are inside the package and are in the form of one to eight step-by-step visuals.  The vehicle I purchased for takes two different lengths, one 19" and the other 21".WHAT'S IN THE PACKAGE:~  Wiper BladeAdapters:~  Top Lock Pinch Tab~  Top Lock Push Button~  Hook Lock~  Pin SideThere are a couple of points that I especially like about these blades, but the best one is the wear indicator.  Simply remove the tab before or after installation.  Blades should be replaced every six months, but unlike some things like oil, they can be easily forgotten.  My last set of blades was, should I say, quite sick looking because the previous owner of the car didn't take car of simple maintenance.  The other thing I liked was the tight mesh to my windshield from the more than "1500 pressure points."  I purchased one wiper blade and received the other one from the Vine program.  How well they perform in the long run and how well the wear indicator works remains to be seen.
summary: ACDelco has a good solid wiper with a wear indicator, a feature I like ...

reviewText: These blades are nice and snug against the windshield. They have a curve that goes right up against it. I got these for my son's S10 Chevy pick up truck, and they work great. My only concern was installing them. I didn't do it right the first time, and the wiper flew right off the wiper arm. My son installed it again, and I guess he did it right, because it has stayed on ever since. He said he really likes these blades, because they have a indicator that shows you when they need to be replaced.

I put a set of these blades on my truck 2 months ago. according to the package it's hot selling point is the "wear indicator" where the black dot will change to yellow to let you know when you should change the blade.Well, admittedly I am no where near the yellow dot, in fact my dot is still very much black. HOWEVER I have hit another snag with these wiper blades and that is that the blades provide multiple hinge attachments so that the blade can be used with any wiper arms. Here is the problem The top lock pinch tab that is separate and needs to be attached to the blade and then you choose the adaptor needed to convert the blade to your vehicle ie.side lock, hook lock, pin side, etc. It is a classic engineering quandary, theory vs. practice: What looks great on paper doesn't quite make it in the real world.I live in Wyoming. It is cold and dry and sometimes wet & frozen, we have temperature fluctuations. Twice since I've snapped all the components together I've had to re-attach them because the cold warps the plastic and causes them to pop apart. I have actually been able to overcome this problem with trusty duct tape. And with the tape making sure everything holds together these are pretty good blades. But I don't think a person should have to pay 17-plus-bucks for something that will require duct tape to secure success.
summary: Needs duct tape to hold it together.

reviewText: I removed the driver's side wiper blade from my pick-up. I was unable to install the ACDelco with any of the adapters that were furnished. I went to the Amazon web site and entered the information for my vehicle and the response was that this wiper blade was a match for my vehicle. So, it must be just me that can't get it installed and I need to try a different approach.I took my Frontier back to the Nissan dealer where I purchased the vehicle. I asked the dealer to install the wiper blade and while there go ahead and change the oil and rotate the tires. The dealer did the oil and tire thing as usual but was unable to get the ACDelco blade to work. I asked him to put my original blade back on, which he did, and I recycled the ACDelco.Against the advice I did look this gift horse in the mouth and it had no teeth.

I put this wiper on my 2003 Chevy Astro van and it works fine! It come with many different attaching pieces, so be sure to watch the video -- the little tiny diagrams are hard to see in the package. I don't know if the package would be any different in a retail store, but the one I got was easy to open -- it just kind of pops open without needing a knife or nuclear weapons.This kind of vehicle the wipers come off easy -- the hardest part was trying to figure out which piece to use.The only drawback to me is the price -- it seems a bit high.

These are the best. They say they have lots of pressure points, and it must be true, as my winshield has never been so clean and clear. I will not go back to the cheap generic wippers again. I also love the idea that they come with Wear-indication system, that alerts the driver when it's time to replace the blade as the indicator turns from black to green to yellow. Now I will know when it it time to buy new and not have to wait for it to suddenly stop performing in a rainstorm.
summary: ACDelco is  the best windshield wiper blade on the market. perform great, and come with wear indicator.

reviewText: I've used several brands of wiper blades over the years, and these are among the best I've used. No streaks, easy to install, and high build quality. Not much more you can ask for. I have only been using these for a couple weeks now so I'll provide an update in the summer to see how well they hold up. But as it stands right now, I'd definitely recommend these wiper blades.

AC Delco Clear Vision 24 Inch Wiper BladesThese blades are similar to the Bosch, Rain-X, Michelin, and Pylon single-piece frameless blades that are sold in retail stores. They are approximately 3-4 times the cost of a traditional framed wiper blade. I've used the Michelin, Rain-X, Pylon, and Bosch Clear Advantage single-piece frameless blades in the past, and have found that the rubber blade generally lasts 1-3 years before they start to deteriorate. By deteriorate, I mean the rubber starts to set into a shape and no longer clears the glass as well as I'd like, which can result in streaking that can't be fixed by cleaning the blade using alcohol or other cleaners. The single-piece blades cost more and don't deliver any significant benefits to justify the added cost, but they look cool and all the foreign luxury cars come with them from the factory as of 4-6 years ago.The AC Delco Clear Vision blades come with a multitude of adapters, unlike the blades that are generally sold in most retail stores like Meijer, Target, or Wal-Mart (those are generally designed for the J-Hook style of arms which is common). However, many late model GM cars use a different attachment which requires an adapter that happens to be included in the AC Delco Clear Vision package.The AC Delco blades use adapters that are easy to clip into the body of the blade. I chose to use the J-hook adapters because my car uses those type of wiper arms. Installation was literally a snap. I immediately noticed that the blades were clearing my windshield without any streaks compared to my 3 year old Rain-X frameless blades.The spring that is used to provide the pressure for the blade to press against the windshield appears to be very strong, but this isn't much different from any other new wiper blade. These AC Delco blades have a "wear indicator" strip that is covered by tape to be removed after installation. I did an Internet search on these indicators, and it appears Valeo uses them on their VW branded blades, and is nothing more than a strip that changes color with exposure to UV radiation. This makes sense, since UV radiation contributes significantly to rubber deterioration. However, time will tell on when this indicator recommends replacing the blade. Even when I park my car outside year-round in Michigan, I can easily get 3 years out of a set of wiper blades: framed or frame less and regardless of brand. And even then, I could get by with using ratty old wiper blades. There's nothing that suggest the blades will fall apart and be unsafe to use within a year, especially when frameless blades cost so much these days.In conclusion, are these AC Delco Clear Vision blades worth every penny? I have yet to be convinced that frameless blades are superior to framed blades. Sure, there are less joints and moving pieces, but at a price point that is 3-4 times that of the least expensive Pylon/Trico framed blades? I can't say these or any other frameless blades are mandatory especially when they last just as long as the cheap framed blades before streaking. To be safe, replace your wiper blades each year but my experience shows they can last 2-3 years easily as long as nothing physically breaks.Overall: 4/5 stars, great frameless construction, comes with a multitude of adapters that clip into the body, strong spring to provide coverage on windshield. Still doesn't fully conform to my curved windshield at the edges, and these still don't convince me they will outlast an inexpensive framed blade.I will keep this review updated as I continue to use these wiper blades.UPDATE: 14 JAN 2013I've been able to use these blades in a variety of conditions, and this morning was the first time I had the opportunity to use this in freezing precipitation (ice and melting ice). The blades started to take a "set" in shape instead of trying to hug the glass, probably because of ice on the blade material. They began chattering and streaking and I noticed the driver side was skipping over a spot on the glass, but the interesting part is that the wiper arm connects to the blade right at this spot so there is definitely enough pressure. So all in all, these blades performed on-par or worse than the 3-year old Michelin Radius blades that these replaced.
summary: Good design, nothing extraordinary or special though

reviewText: I've always liked ACDelco parts, and have never really had an issue with any of them.  I'd usually bought and used whatever wiper blades were at the auto parts store (typically ANCO.  I've never been impressed with ANCO.  They seem to be cheap plastic junk that break at the pivot.)These ACDelco seem to be just as good as the other standard quality blades I've used.  They wipe nicely, fit the windshield good.  They aren't like some where the outer 2" doesn't even touch.So far, so Good.
summary: Decent wiper, average construction comparable to many others.

reviewText: This is the second brand of this type ("frameless") of wiper that I have used and I have to say that I am impressed with these ones as well.  Usually at highway speeds, standard framed wipers (or worse yet -jacketed winter wipers) start to lift a bit or do not maintain full contact with my windshield, but these low profile wipers keep full contact along the full length for a clear windshield.  There was no squeak or stutter at any time, even in light rain or when using washer fluid, and they were able to keep up with a full-on heavy rain, which some wipers do not seem to be able to do.  The drivers side wiper on my car covers more than 50% of the wipered area and the windshield is at relatively low angle which causes many wipers to lift or lose contact at highway speeds. This wiper works as good or better than any standard type wiper I have used.  Installation was a snap, just following the directions/diagrams on the back of the package.  I do not live in an area with snow or ice, so I cannot on this wiper in "winter" conditions. The wear indicator is a nice feature, and I am curious to see if it will accurately indicate that a change is necessary when the time comes.
summary: ACDelco 22ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator - 22" (Pack of 1)

reviewText: I have been using a jointless wiper blade ever since it became a popular replacement for the factory jointed type that is usually pre-installed when you buy a new vehicle. The ACDelco 24ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator fits the bill when you need to replace or just want to upgrade to a better performing wiper blade. There was no rain yet in my little corner of the country when I got this wiper so to be able to give a comprehensive review, I have to "simulate" rain-like conditions by turning a hose with a shower nozzle on the windshield in the driveway of my garage. Snow on the other hand is a different story, no way for me to simulate that kind of weather event. It also worked well with frost accumulation on the windshield. It wiped away the frost smoothly, with no kind of hesitation or drag while in the wiping motion.My thoughts:Performance: the jointless type ACDelco 24ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator is contoured better to "hug" your windshield with minimal resistance and pressure points. This translates to better wiping ability thereby enabling you to see better in inclement weather.
