Since it is jointless, this type of wiper gives you uniform wiping pressure, eliminating the pressure points or the "streaks" that you see across your windshield as it moves across the windshield. The curvature of this wiper is aerodynamic, it will prevent a lift-off of the blade even in high winds.Installation: it took less than 10 minutes to install the ACDelco 24ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator without using any of the adapters for the wiper arm of my vehicle.Very satisfied with how the ACDelco 24ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator has performed. It is a bit on the pricey side compared to other jointless name-brand wiper but gives you an awesome wiping performance. Highly recommended!
summary: A great upgrade from a jointed-type wiper

reviewText: I got the 21" and 19" ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade for the front windshield of my 2002 Subaru Forester. The printed instructions showed how to remove and replace the wiper blades for five different attachment types. My car had the "Hook Lock" type of attachment to the wiper arms. If you're not real familiar with your wiper blade attachment details, I highly recommend watching the installation videos on the ACDelco website or on this page. If you're outside with your car, you can take your smartphone and scan a QR code in the instructions with an app like QR Droid. There are several attachment adapters included for the different types of attachments. For the Hook Lock type used on my car, there was an adapter to slip on before attaching the blades, but the video makes it clear how to proceed.As best I can remember, these are the first frameless wiper blades that I've had, so I'll be watching closely to see how they perform. Snow and ice aren't much of a factor here, but we get about 50 inches of rain a year, and the summer heat is fierce, with a lot of UV from the sun. The acid test for any windshield wiper blades is how well they're performing six months or a year down the road. Regarding the indicator that changes color to alert you to change the wiper blades, I'm a bit skeptical about that. I change wipers when they stop performing satisfactorily, and I'll have to see if that coincides with the indicator.My initial impression of the ACDelco blades is very favorable, but I plan to update my review in a few months after seeing how well the wiper blades are performing then.Note: On the new wiper blade is an adhesive tab that says "REMOVE." It wasn't obvious why, but I think that it was covering a piece that will change color when exposed to a certain amount of UV radiation, thus signaling that it's time to change the wiper.
summary: My first impression of the blades is good, but only time will tell

reviewText: The wiper comes with several adapters, and you have to choose the one that's right for your car. Unfortunately for me, the one that's right for my car is HUGE... and very distracting.I noticed it right away, as soon as I sat in the driver's seat. It actually impinged on my vision just a little on the bottom of the windshield-- it had a higher profile than my other wiper (which I left on the passenger side for comparison purposes), and it was just distracting because of its bulbous shape. When I turned on the wipers, I actually felt like it was dangerous, because it was such a focal point that my eyes kept going to the adapter while I was driving in the rain... every time the wiper went by, I couldn't help but notice it again. Like a giant black bug or something-- you just can't NOT notice it. I hoped it would get more invisible to me as I got used to it and continued driving (it was a long drive home), but that didn't happen.It makes very good contact with the windshield and worked well, with no missed spots on the windshield. I'm guessing that if you needed any other adapter than the one I needed, you'd probably be fine-- but the one I needed just made it too much of an eyesore.I had already thrown out the old wiper, so I'm out of luck and need to buy another one now.
summary: Works well, but adapter is very distracting

reviewText: These wiper blades work fine. That said, so do all other new wiper blades I've ever purchased. They don't feel like they're built of adamantium, or made of magical unicorn rubber, so I don't see why they're so expensive. The adapters they come with work fine, but they do stick out in a rather bulky way, as has been pointed out in other reviews. I'm sure that's dropped my gas mileage a non-noticeable amount. They do come with a magical color-changing "time to replace" indicator, but it's usually not hard to figure out when wiper blades need replacing: they stop working well.Anyway, they're fine, but for the money, I'd just stick with the ANCO cheapies. All blades work great when new, but need to be replaced regularly. I haven't yet seen a pair that are worth three times the cost of the generics.
summary: Works fine, but nothing special. Costs too much, I think.

reviewText: The wiper blades work well so far (of course, they always do when they're new) and make good contact with the glass along the whole length of the blade, although  I think the "1,500 pressure points" is just marketing hyperbole.  I like the versatility of working with different styles of wipers but installation wasn't entirely simple.  I have the hook style wipers and the diagrams inside were tiny and not very clear.  You have to snap on a different adapter depending on the style and it makes for a rather large knob at the connection point - bigger even than theBoschblades (although the blades themselves are thinner).  Even then it popped off easily when I bumped it while scraping frost from the windows - never had that happen with other blades.  And frankly, they're just kinda ugly and look big and clumsy.  I'm also not too keen on the "wear indicator" as it seems "gimicky" and I have no idea how it works.  It seems I ought to be able to see when the performance deteriorates but this way it'll probably just have a big yellow dot in front of me whether I want to replace them or not (we don't get a lot of rain here in SoCal).

The ACDelco wiper blade was easy enough to snap into the wiper holder of my car, clinging nicely to the glass without warping or riding up on the ends. In other words, it clings tightly.I usually use Rain-Ex on my windshield, since I live in the southwestern United States, and it doesn't rain frequently. That said, when it does rain, we can get a deluge. I found the blade held its own in a recent torrent. It also worked while driving through snow in the high country, although I think the blade works more seamlessly in rainy situations.The color changing feature on the rubber blade itself is a smart idea. I usually find myself using a wiper blade until the rubber is completely worn off, not thinking about changing it until the metal itself starts scraping down my windshield. This should help remind me to stay on top of my car maintenance duties every time I clean off the windshield.Recommended as a nice, precision wiper blade with a helpful reminder feature.

reviewerName: Joel Avrunin "Electrical Engineer who loves S...
reviewText: I installed these blades on the front of my 2002 Toyota Sienna.  The blades that I owned previously were the traditional skeleton-frame blades with a 6-point contact system on the windshield.  These traditional blades work fine, but they do tend to get clogged with snow and ice, and the single points of pressure don't always apply pressure evenly on the windshield.  The ACDelco Clear Vision are a flexible blade that applies even pressure along the windshield with no skeleton behind them.  My first experience with this type of blade was the Rain-X Latitude which worked quite well, but fell apart rather quickly.Enter the ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade which is very similar to the Rain-X Latitude.  I received the 24" and 18" blades to fit my car.  The first thing I noticed is that the blades ship in hard plastic cases that open very easily.  No scissors or razor blade required - the box just pops open.  Inside the box is a huge array of attachment mechanics for various wiper blade styles.  There are Top Lock Pinch Tab, Top Lock Push Button, Side Lock, Hook Lock, and Pin Side.  For the Toyota Sienna, the hook lock set was the right one.  You just "snap" the hook lock adapter into the blade and then snap the hook into the adapter.  The instructional photos are rather small - it would be nice if the adapters were more clearly labeled (or the instructional pictures bigger), but I figured it out.Another innovation is a circle that changes color when exposed to UV that acts as a "timer" for when to change the blades.  You remove a protective cover of tape and the black circle will eventually turn yellow.  I haven't had them long enough to evaluate this feature, but it's a great idea.  I didn't realize how poor my old wipers were performing until I put on new ones, and frankly, I can't remember when I changed them last.  A physical indicator is a nice feature, both for helping ACDelco to sell more blades and for me to know when I should be looking to replace the blades.The blades clean off regular rain just fine - no streaking and very clean.  The flexible design means snow and ice won't build up on them.  My last experience with frameless blades (Rain-X latitude) showed them to be less durable than the traditional type, so I'm hoping the ACDelco Clear Vision hold up better.  Time will tell - I'll likely update this review in 6 months with my experience.  For now, I'm quite happy with the replacement and can recommend them.
summary: Easy to install and performance is excellent - recommended replacement wiper blade

reviewText: TheACDelco 26ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator - 26" (Pack of 1)was not difficult to install because I am familiar with blade installation.  If you need instructions, this is not best wiper blade.  Arriving with several adaptors, none were needed, but were stored until this blade is replaced later this year.  As for the wear indicator, I cannot comment because it's a new blade and from what I understand, a new product to ACDelco.  It does clear the windshield as required, but isn't the most sleek in style.  It's price point is higher than many and I suspect that's because of the wear indicator.  Since I change blades a maximum of annually, this is wasted on the car which wears the wiper.  Should you need a reminder, assuming that this really does give a visual clue, perhaps this is a great blade for your car.  For the price, it's not a bad blade, just not an outstanding blade.

The ACDelco Blade arrived just a few days ago and it was put to the tests in a few hours after installing it.  Installing it was not difficult but prepared to spend a few minutes if this is the first install.  Luckily, I did and all went better than expected.  The hardest job as usual for me at least was removing the old wiper.  Did it; put the new one on and enjoyed driving in the rain.  The ACDelco works like a charm.  Full, clean swipes with no rattling and no skips.  From one side of town to the other in the rain and not an issue whatsoever.  The real test came a few days ago.  The weatherman said we would get 4" of snow in the next several hours and sure enough we got about 6" and it was heavy.  So what!  I have an ACDelco on my side and am not concerned.  I hit the road with a full blast of wet, heavy snow falling and not a concern again.  That blade did so much better than the other non-ACDelco blade and made my side clean while the other side had a few artifacts leftover.  I did not think a new blade could be so effective; however, this one was and I expect it to continue for quite a while.  If not, I'll be back for a re-review.
summary: Fantastic Wiper Blade that WORKS under Worst Conditions

reviewText: This was easily installed on my Honda Pilot.  I have had these one piece wipers before and they do a very good job of clearing the windshield without leaving streaks.  They lack the aerodynamic foil that keeps them from flapping around at very high speeds, but these are on my Honda Pilot, so I'm not going 120 MPH anyway.  There were many installation options, but once I figured out the correct piece to use for my car, they clicked on easily.The wear indicator is an interesting feature, that I assume will become ugly and probably have nothing to do with how the rubber is holding up.  I tend to replace my wipers when they stop doing a good job.  I guess the "wear indicator" just reacts to the accumulation of UV light and/or water.
summary: Install was really easy on my Honda Pilot (2010)

reviewText: These are very easy to install.  They've been through rain, snow & sleet so far & have performed perfectly.  The "wear indicator" is a gimmick, in my opinion because I think it's pretty easy to tell when your wipers need changing; I don't need a yellow dot to know that I have streaks in my vision zone.
summary: Very Easy Install & No Streaks - Fits my 2010 Mazda 3

reviewText: I have been using this 22" ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade for several weeks on the driver's side of my 2007 Hyundai Accent GS. I have to say I'm not really impressed.Fit and mounting are okay though the so-called instructions printed on the back of the label insert are almost impossibly to see and are somewhat vague. The J-Mount connector that my car requires sits rather high on the wiper arm. MUCH higher than the Bosch 22" Clear Advantage wiper blade I had been using. It's mildly distracting and somewhat unattractive.The important part - Function. In mild to moderate rain the Clear Vision wiper blade does a good job of clearing the windshield. It seemed to struggle a little during a brief heavy downpour. But the worst part is how these work in light mist and fog. The wiper blade leaves what can only be described as a film on the windshield. It's not highly visible all the time but catch the sunlight at the right angle and it becomes rather difficult to see out the windshield. I've tried cleaning the blade twice with isopropyl alcohol and a microfiber cloth but it still films/streaks the entire windshield in mist and fog. Heavy use of washer fluid will clear the streaking/filming but that's just wasting washer fluid.I'll probably leave these on the car for now since it's the dry season but once it starts raining every day when summer gets here I'm going back to the Bosch blade.I really can't recommend these wiper blades.
summary: Mediocre- Middle of the Road Wiper Blade

reviewText: Upon first opening the AC Delco wiper blade I was a bit daunted.  There was a wiper blade along with 4 plastic fittings and no paper instructions.  There were printed pictures on the package wrapper but they were too small and too dark to be of use.  Fortunately, I was familiar with the style of the wiper arms on my truck (Ford F150) and it was not too difficult to pick out the snap on piece needed to connect the blade.  A little more close inspection and I was able to see how the piece slipped in and snapped to the blade.Because I really don't see the use of a wear indicator (just replace the wiper when it doesn't work well any more - not when a dot changes color) and the instructions are non-existent in the packaging, I think this is a 4 star product.  Yes, I know Amazon has a video on how to use the blade - but it is pretty inconvenient to stop and watch a video on installation.  Otherwise, the blade works well and makes good contact with the window.  It is replacing a similar style blade I bought at the local big box store for a little cheaper.

I like the way ACDelco has provided all the various connectors for attaching the wiper. This makes the blades virtually generic. Great idea. Also the color coding to tell you when to replace is a nice touch. I particularly like the 16" wiper as it fits my rear window. For some reason the rear window blades don't last as long as the front ones on my vehicle.

I received one 22"ACDelco 22ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear Indicator - 22" (Pack of 1)and installed this on the driver-side of the windshield of my 1998 Ford Expedition Eddie Bauer SUV.  This was one of my very first attempts to install a replacement blade and I found it rather easy to do.One of the challenges living near the ocean is dirt and grime from salt and sand. The wiper has done a great job so far in cleaning the mess without leaving streaks.We've had quite a bit of nasty weather this month and the wiper covers the entire area without any skips, streaks or squeaking.I will order another for the passenger side as well.  I also appreciate the wear indicator as a gentle reminder to replace these, occasionally.
summary: Easy to Install Even for this Novice

reviewText: I got this for use on my husband's F-150.  He says it works as well as any other blade he's had on his truck.  Where this really shines? It has a Wear Indicator that tells us when it needs to be replaced.I'll come back in a few months to say if it's lasting as long (or longer) than other wiper blades.

The ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade with Wear indicator comes with five adaptors and is fairly easy to install. It does a good job in the rain and with light snow without too much streaking or squeaking.I'm not sure how useful the wear indicator will actually be--it's usually very obvious when the wiper blades need replacing. I have had toothbrushes with a similar feature where a stripe of colored bristles had the color fade away and found that they signaled for replacement prematurely, when the bristles were still in excellent condition.

This ACDelco blade has proven itself in some pretty tough mountain and high plains driving where we frequently encounter rain, then snow, and then sleet and ice all within the span of an hour as elevation changes.  This blade kept up with every element with no problem.  I use a deicing windshield wiper fluid; so that along with this blade kept our windshield more clear than our OEM Toyota blades.  Very easy to install.  Highly recommended.

reviewerName: Mary Jo Sminkey "15 years of Amazon Reviews!"
reviewText: These wipers require replacing the entire wiper component, not just the plastic part. So the first difficulty I ran into was figuring out how to get the original ones off, as this isn't even in my car manual. Had to google it to find out how to do it. Then to put the blades on, you have to figure out which adapter to use and how to snap it into place. The directions for this are ridiculously small and impossible to decipher, so it's pretty much a trial and error thing. Once I got it snapped on, I was able to put the blade on, and it seemed to work reasonably well enough for a couple weeks. That was, until I was driving in a slight drizzle, turned on my wipers, and I guess the window had some dry spots that caused the blade to stick a little bit and the connector just snapped off, sending the entire blade flying through the air. Thankfully it didn't hit anyone, or another car, or I could have had some real damages to pay. Luckily I saved the original wipers which went back on the car ASAP. These went into the garbage. I will note that my wipers use the J-style connector, and another reviewer mentioned a similar issue with their car and the same style connector, so it may be a particular issue with this one. However, I am just not sure I would trust these wipers and these connectors that aren't permanently attached to the wiper and prone to just snapping apart.
summary: Total Fail, Came off While Driving

reviewText: Until I started to take advantage of the opportunity to test different wiper blades, my general tendency had been to replace the blades when the metal frames began to etch the windshield. Since this set is designed without metal brackets that won't work so I suppose I will have to remove the little yellow tab and wait to see how long it takes the indicator to change colors from black to yellow.  I have customarily lived in areas with a considerable amount of all forms of precipitation but I also have never believed the wiper was a substitute for an ice scraper or the defroster so I don't place inordinate demands on the rubber filaments either.With the exception of the wear indicator, The Delco blades don't appear substantially different than the Bosch Icon blades they are replacing or the Rainx Latitude blades the Bosch blades replaced last year, all of which are on a shelf in the garage since they weren't worn out and I can't seem to force myself to throw out anything with some life left in it, so the inexpensive but utilitarian ANCO bracketed blades that started this process are there as well.All of replacement bracketless blades have left the same minor streaking on the driver's side ever since my wiper motor died and I believe I may have bent the arm out of position when the blade got tangled with the passenger side blade.The wiper blade comes with four adapters to accommodate most wiper attachment configurations. Since all of my current cars employ the hook lock system, installation of the blade is basically error proof as long as the correct adapter is selected and not inserted upside down which is pretty easy to determine considering there Is a yellow tab on the topside side.  For those who still feel uncomfortable, ACDelco has videos on their site as well as here that can lead the timid through the process step by step.
summary: I wonder if Delco plans to market an obstructed Vision Wiper Blade?

reviewText: I put a set of these - this and a 24"er on a Corolla S.  I had begun to think there was something wrong with the windshield or the arm of that car since I've had three different sets of blades (including OEM) on that car, and none of them have worked right, even brand new.  These have laid that theory to rest, and I'll be going right to these next time I need blades for that car.I had noticed before I put them on that they are built very similarly to the new Bosch blades I recently put on my other car, but these have four extra pieces for different mounting methods - an all-in-one solution.  They also have a "wear indicator" that I find kind of goofy.  I suppose after a while I'll have an annoying white spot on the blades before I'm ready to change them (and I really don't like to have everything pushing me to buy more stuff unnecessarily).  Anyway, I'll forgive them for that little trend that hopefully won't last.
summary: First to work for Corolla S

reviewText: The last time I had my wiper blades replaced they were changed at the dealer (big mistake). I'm not sure of the brand but they were problematic after just weeks it seemed.The Delco blades were super easy to install myself (I'm not good at things like this either).  The end result is streak-free windows and noise free wiper blades. I'm not sure how long these wipers will last, but based on initial impressions I am very pleased.[ the packaging was super easy to undo without ripping up your hands with the tough plastic casings found in many products like these - that alone was a treat.]Highly Recommended.

These ACDelco wiper blades ship with multiple adapters so they will fit a variety of vehicles. The installation directions cryptic and virtually useless.  I wish I'd noticed the videos provided on the product page before I did my install.The adapters are bulky in size and are noticeably distracting in your field of vision when you're driving.  Furthermore, both the adapters and the blades are made of plastic similar to what you'd expect from a Chinese made dollar store toy.  The blades feel super flimsy and do not even have the strength to hold the wiper against the curve of the windshield from end to end.  The actual rubber wiper does a decent job, where it touches the glass.These blades come equipped with a wear indicator that is supposed to let you know when it is time to replace the blade.  I do not have any expectation that the blade will actually last long enough for that indicator to be needed.*This review applies to both of the two different lengths of blades I tested*

At first I thought it would be a struggle to open the package like some other bubble packs, but if you look on top on the upper right, it says "abrir, open, ouvrir". Pry it there and it will open easily.There are three attachments, so whatever kind you have on your wiper it most likely that will fit with one of them. Mine is a Honda Accord 2001 and it is just a hook. Anyway, you should make sure this wiper is the one for your car. There is an online guide that is very easy to navigate to find your car making sure this wiper blade will fit.I have been using this for weeks and it works great. No streaks and seems to work effortlessly. It is not that sleek looking, but other than that, there is nothing to complain. Priced very reasonably.

These ACDelco Clear Vision blades are certainly premium quality, and they work great on our 2000 Dodge Caravan. I was able to install them with no problems in less than a minute, and so far they are holding up nicely to our harsh winter. The wipe is smooth and flawless with no streaking or stuttering. We've had them installed for a couple of weeks now and we love them, hopefully they'll stand the test of time and continue with the top notch performance. So far so good, and I'd definitely consider them in the future.

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: What can one say about a windshield wiper blade? It's easy to attach and includes a plethora of connection types, so unless you have a Model T, this should attach to your arms (well, your car's wiper arms) correctly. The wear indicator seems more of a gimmick. Who actually replaces blades when they wear? It's when they get damaged, or leave behind an annoying streak at eye-level that won't go away.  Or when the window is getting scratched by the metal arm.... So when installed, new, they do what all other blades I have ever used do - they leave the window streak free and dry. Time will tell if they last better, handle snow (we have a skiers nightmare of snow in the midwest right now - AKA - none) or ice. But right now I'm happy.  I give it 4 instead of 5 stars due to the high price and gimmicky wear indicator.
summary: It's a wiper blade - works as it should

reviewText: AC Delco 24ACD Clear Vision Wiper Blades do everything you'd expect them to. They wipe away the water from a windshield smoothly without stuttering and jumping. There is no streaking, squeaking, or chattering. The newfangled I-Beam type of spring helps give the wiper blade an even pressure across the entire surface of the windshield. The design also seems to help prevent lift-off at highway speeds, keeping them working great matter what vehicle speed. Overall a very good design that seems to hold up the AC Delco name.

I got one of these for my wife's Taurus, which has a pretty rounded back window that causes some 'missed' spots at the ends of the blades of standard flat wiper blades. These wiper blades are naturally rounded and contact the glass along the entire edge. I was able to use one size larger, increasing visibility while still making full contact with the glass.The one thing I really don't like is the connection when the the wiper blade is mounted to the wiper arm on the car. The package includes a whole range of options to choose from, covering nearly any make or model car, but the connection point is WAY too big. Normally, the arm of the wiper fits inside of the wiper blade frame, providing a thin profile. These blades have plastic clips that attach to the wiper arm, and then attach to a base on the wiper blade itself. This makes the connection point for a wiper arm to the blade twice as thick as my old wiper blade (1" compared to 1/2"). Along the entire length of the blade, the profile is kept very simple and thin, but once you get to the wiper arm connection, it's much taller then the rest of the blade. Despite the fact that the AC Delco blade is only a little bit taller then my old blade, the design makes it look a LOT taller. After replacing the rear wiper on my wife's car (without her knowledge), she walked by and the wiper blade 'knuckle' immediately caught her attention and she questioned me about it. She was surprised to find that it wasn't too much taller then her last blade as she too was fooled by the odd profile of the wiper blade.I ended up buying a different brand of blades for my wife's front wipers (Trico). These were much slimmer and shorter, and seemed easier to install, but they didn't include nearly as many connector pieces, so likely wouldn't be as universal as these blades. If they made these connectors so large in order to accommodate a larger variety of vehicles, I'd simply say that it wasn't worth it.Overall, I like the fact that the wiper blade does a good job contacting the glass, and the blade works well and is streak-free, however the size of the connecting piece is, in my opinion, unnecessarily large. If you have a vehicle that you normally have trouble finding a wiper blade to fit, I'd recommend giving these a shot. Otherwise, I'd have to give these blades a few months to determine if the longevity makes it all worth it because I personally just don't like the appearance.
summary: Functions great, but I don't like the design very much

reviewText: These wiper blades are the flexible, non-metal frame style which I prefer. They have a wear indicator on each blade which is unique. It's a small spot on the blade which changes from black to yellow when it's time for new blades. (Be certain to remove the protective sticker from the wear indicator when you install the blade.)Each blade comes packaged with several adapters for use with different style wiper arms. The videos on this product page are EXCELLENT! Watch the one for your style wiper arm and you'll have no problem installing this blade.Note: Because many cars require two different size blades for the windshield, the blades are sold individually. Use the Amazon Parts Finder tool at the top of the product page to make sure you order the right size blades for your particular car.I used a water hose to test the blades when I initially installed them and they worked perfectly - no areas where the blades failed to make contact with the windshield. Luckily, last weekend we had some heavy rain and I was able to put them to the test. Again, they performed beautifully.Windshield wipers aren't especially exciting or interesting until they fail in a rain or snow storm. If you can't remember when you changed your blades last, it's probably time to do it. These blades would be a good choice.

These wiper blades were super easy to install.  It took only a couple minutes if that.They works pretty well too.  They seem to be a pretty nice quality.  I've been using them for a few weeks now and haven't had any problems with streaking or anything else.I think it's really neat that there's a built in indicator that will turn yellow and let you know when your blades need replaced.  I haven't seen this feature in any other blades out there.  Hopefully it's accurate.I think these wiper blades are pretty good and I would recommend them.
summary: Works well and tells you when to replace...

reviewText: The best thing about the ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade is the way it works, no spots, no streaks, just a perfectly clear windshield. I got one to replace a wiper, and it works so well I'm getting one for the other side. Another great feature of this wiper is it comes with adaptors to fit all wiper arms. I don't know if the wiper arms on my car are hook lock, side lock, pin lock or whatever. But with the ACDelco Clear Vision Wiper Blade I don't need to know, because whatever it is the adaptor to fit my car comes with it. Simple. Also these blades come with a wear indicator to let me know when they need to be replaced, and since I never change my wiper blades until it's long over due, I'm anxious to see how that works. All and all a great wiper.

This blade was easy to install. Although the number of adapters and having to choose and connect them seemed an extra step that I've never had to do with other wipers. These ride higher when at rest than other wipers I have used and that is an irritation. There are no skips or streaks when I have used them in rain, sleet and frost covered windscreens. They do work quietly.They have a built in indicator that tells you when the wiper needs replacing. It will be interesting, because in most products that have this type of device- it seems to tell you to replace it much sooner than you normally would. However, you could use it as an indicator to buy new blades and have them on hand.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Summary - nice blades with adapters for all types of attachments.  Indicator sticker changes color to remind you to change your blades.  Design is good for winter - won't freeze.I recently replaced the wipers for my mothers car and got the wrong kind of attachment - kind of annoying since it was a case of someone opening the package and putting the wrong one back in.Anyways, that can't happen with these - they include 4 adapters so all major attachment types are covered. This does mean  you have to do a minor bit of final assembly, but if you were going to replace your wipers to begin with, this shouldn't be a problem.There's a "Wear Indicator" which is in fact nothing more than a sticker which will eventually change color as it ages.  You peel the cover and I assume it changes color over time as it is exposed to the air.  One issue is that this type of chemical change is very temperature dependent.  You could be in a mild climate and not use your wipers and have them change sooner than someone who uses them all the time, but lives in a colder climate.Anyways, enough nitpicking about the sticker.  This is a similar design to the Bosch Icon.  -rather than having a thin spring with lots of articulating little arms, this wiper blade is basically 2 honkin big spring bands connected to the bracket.  This means that you can't get ice buildup between the arms and have the blade freeze up.  If you don't know what I'm talking about, you're lucky enough to live in one of the warm states.TIP - when your blade starts to streak, you can typically get another few months of good performance by cleaning the blade with a rag and some rubbing alcohol.Overall, very good blade, I'd pretty much disregard the "wear indicator" though

While this does a fine job of clearing your windshield, sometimes it'll lift a tad bit and keep streaks on your windshield. Save yourself the frustration and just get the one with the brace on the back instead.
summary: Get the one with the brace instead

reviewText: I replaced the reverse bulbs I had in there previously with these and out simply these are 10 times bighter. I thought the ones i had were bright but you can bare even look at these without even seeing spots in your eyes. If people cant see me backing up they are blind or just dumb. Cree bulbs Ive used in the past in other applications and they simply just last. Cree bulbs don't flicker. Excellent buy.

Holycow Bright and I'm very Happy with my Purchase. They arrived faster then I thought. I read somewhere that the bulbs are heavy which they are and tend to fall out of socket, well I didnt have any issues like that. I'm guessing that person had a weak socket that shouldve been replace. I'm excited How Bright they are and wish this company had 1156 too. I recently bought 15W Reverse kit which is Garbage and good thing I bought 2 kits cause something keeps blowing out 1 or the other sides, Anyway the bulbs are BRIGHT. My Con is the price at 21.99 and 6.99 to ship. ok I can understand 15 with Free shipping  but not what I payed. I just purchased a pair of the same type LEDs in 1156 and are super Bright too and I payed 15 free ship so This place could do the same.
summary: Where were these when I was looking for reverse lights??

reviewText: Well, they do plug right in (mind the polarity of course).  Whether they're brighter than the stock bulbs, I'm still undecided.  In a dimly lit area, backing up still seemed like it was dim back there, but it's hard to tell when it's still somewhat bright from other lights.I haven't yet reversed in a totally dark area which is where I do run into issues with my stock bulbs.When installing, I checked it out with one new and one old... these new ones do *seem* brighter but my initial test just didn't convince me one way or another.  I'll update my rating from 3 stars when I have a bit more to go by... I'd like to get more and replace the cargo lights on my truck because on occasion I turn those on too for extra reverse lights, but I'll have to know before I order more.Incidentally, mine shipped all the way direct from China.  They arrived okay, but know it'll take a while for them to arrive and you won't have tracking via China Post.  They just showed up one day, but it was probably only 2 weeks total.
summary: Easy to install... brighter than stock though?

reviewText: I've tried a variety of these (12 v LED lights) and so far, for my purposes (RV use), these are far and away the most effective I've found (so far?...).  They're certainly not the least expensive, but they work the best.  I think they're brighter than the incandescent lights I replaced and use substantially less power, which is most helpful when camping without a power connection, which I do regularly.

PRO:-Modules are /extremely/ bright.  I always test LEDs using a 12VDC source before installation, and these ones quite literally stunned me for a moment.  It was brighter than the brightest camera flash I've ever seen (I admit I was only a foot away or so, but still).-Heat sink looks solid.-Mounts perfectly in place of incandescent 921 bulbs.  Brighter than them by a considerable margin.-Works with (my) stock reflectors.  Results may vary depending on your car's reflector design.-Extremely easy to install.  Just pull out the old ones and toss in the new ones.  If they don't light up, flip them around the other way and try again.  Basically idiot-proof.  No documentation required.CON-Pricey.  Other similar modules cost $20, but may not be as superbly bright as these are.-Heavy.  They weigh considerably more than the incandescent 921 bulbs, so if your car is subject to a lot of vibration (Rallycross, track days, really terrible potholes), they might flop around a bit in the socket.  Let's hope not.These LED modules are fantastic and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend them to any Veloster owner.  I'm sure they'll work great for many other vehicles as well.
summary: Excellent modules for my Hyundai Veloster Turbo

reviewText: I installed this panel under the cover of my vehicles dome light. Though this item is obviously made in China, it is still working several months after purchase and is very bright.
I ordered this for my buddy for his Silverado extended cab truck.  It really lights up the inside of his truck.  It is very bright.  I will be ordering one for myself.

This panel is very bright. The white is not as easy on the eyes as the incadesent bulbs but if you take into consideration the brightness, electrical resistance savings and the fact thant you will be able to start your vehicle in the cold morning even if you left your door slightly adjar then it is worth it.
this is the brightest panel I bought yet. Bright white w/ very little blue. Very happy w/ this and will buy another
These things are bright. I bought three of em and they light up the night in my truck cab. The sticky side doesn't work on all materials but thats an easy fix
Nice replacement for the trunk light. Provides more light but uses less energy. The double sided tape makes installation a breeze.

I used these to replace the 1156 bulbs in my RV. They don't come with 1156 adapters but they probably should. If they had them I wouldn't have used them because the adapter wire would obstruct the light. I cut off the connector wire from the supplied adapters and attached it using T tap connectors behind light reflector. It took some time but worked out nice. The flat LED projects light a lot better than a round bulb that is sending light in the wrong direction.The color of the light is perfect. It made the previous LEDs look dingy.A few of the LED boards had the positive and negative wire colors backwards. So I had to connect red to black and black to red. I verified that the wiring in my RV was correct using a volt meter.The adhesive gave out on one of the lights within a day. I believe it was because I didn't have it pressed down onto the slightly curved surface well enough. When I was putting it back in place I did it with the light on, bad idea. The ground from the 1156 socket made contact with the metal on the circuit board next to the LEDs and it burnt out each one that it touched.These use .3 amps at 12.5 volts which is about 4 watts.It would be nice if they made a plastic reflector(like a flashlight) that would fit onto the board and focus the light from the LEDs into a smaller spot.These are shipped from China and take about 2 weeks to receive.
summary: Perfect for my RV dome lights

reviewText: Replacing my OEM dome light bulb with this 48 LED festoon was a snap. In and out in less than 30 seconds. Now I have brilliant white light in my cab, and plenty of it. The process could not be easier. Awesomeness.

I use these in my RV Trailer and these things are bright. They do ship from China so be prepared to wait for a little bit (1-2 weeks) But for the price I could not complain too much. Smaller ones than these run $18-$25 at auto zone for ONE! Color temp is definitely in the 6000k-7000k range so they do have a blueish tint to them so be aware of that. Overall still a great deal.

These are very very bright. I mounted these under my hood and they illuminate the entire engine compartment as well as the surrounding area... Makes working on my truck at night very easy and they don't drain the batter at all.

After having poor experiences with various other LED lights which were too blue and/or too dim to adequately replace the filament bulbs in my motorhome's overhead fixtures, I ordered just one of these light panels to evaluate.  Much to my surprise and delight this assembly of LEDs was as bright, as measured by my Gossen Luna-Pro light meter, as the 12V flat-based filament bulb that it replaced.  The color of the light from these LEDs is very close to daylight white but not blue like other LEDs that I've tested nor orange like the light from the factory-installed filament bulbs.Each of my Itasca motorhome's overhead ceiling light fixtures contains two flat-based bulb sockets.  There is adequate space within the fixture to install two of these panels with adapter, behind the fixture's diffuser.  The LED panel consumes considerably less power than the filament bulb it replaced and emits less heat, but it still gets warm.  I've ordered additional light panels from another Amazon vendor that sells them for less, and I plan to use them to replace most of the filament bulbs in my fixtures.Short term, my experience with this light panel has been very positive.  If my long-term experience after installing them in multiple fixtures is any different, I'll come back and revise this review.
summary: Much Brighter with Better Color Than Previous LED Lights I've Tested

reviewText: This is a very nice kit, but unfortunately i bought the wrong one. Looking forward to doing a full swap

The led dome light works great and really lights up my vehicle, I have a Chevy Malibu 2001.  It is also nice knowing that it is not using as much power as a regular bulb, so there is a less chance of it draining your battery if it was accidentally left on. It does auto dim when the lights are turning off like my regular bulbs did, which I like.  I would definitely recommend these to anyone wanting a white/blue color lighting and not the regular yellowish color dome lights.

These little pads are bright white and give off a great amount of light. I have one light in my travel trailer that uses 3 of these and they are very nice and give off a real nice amount of light at a very favorable hue.

I am pretty disappointed in these panels. The light output isn't as high as some of the other panels I have used including those with fewer individual LED's. Because of this I have not put these into service. I will probably find a use for them some day... Beyond the low output there aren't any build defects, they seem to be sturdily built and the adapters are on par with other LED products I have purchased.

I have replaced every interior light on my RV trailer.  These are most efficient at saving power, so I replaced every interior area light bulb on my trailer with them.  Additionally, these things last nearly forever, so when you replace that burned out bulb, that will be the last time you'll have to do it.
summary: Great improvement and better lighting with lower power consumption

reviewText: 10 cubic feet is a nice size.  It is about half the volume of the average refrigerator.  Much bigger and it becomes cumbersome to manhandle.  Canvass is good; it breathes while being water resistant. You may even take it to your dry cleaners after a few years, not just for cleaning but to renew the waterproofing the same way you do on the more expensive cloth rain coats. Canvass is strong and durable; the build quality here is careful.8 buckle straps means two important things.  You have enough flexibility to adapt to most vehicles.  You have sufficient redundancy against one or two strap failures.  Unlikely that any will fail, but I like failsafe features.  I know there are fancier fasteners, but buckles are strong and they actually work.It is always best practice to balance your vehicle's load, whether on the roof or in the trunk.  This bag balances easily.  Just face the zipper to the back, out of the wind.  Zippers seldom pry open from wind, but sometimes we, or one of us, can be less than careful.  Soft bags are flexible for many shapes.  It is just over a foot high, laying flat, but you can fit bigger things which might be excluded by a hard case.You can leave the interior of your vehicle alone.  No rummaging at the motel, only to repack the next morning when you are anxious to get going.  This bag cleans easily, spilled either on or in.  Throw away the shipping box because it has a handy storage bag for your closet.  Always store it clean and dry.  Hi-Ho Heinenger -- away!

In terms of a "soft" cargo carrier for the roof of your vehicle, this Advantage SportsRack cargo bag is likely the best you will get in this price range (I haven't tried all cargo bags so I'll leave some wiggle room).Unlike similar bags with securing straps that seem minimally attached to the bag, this carrier has reinforcement strips crosshatched across the top of the bag with the tie-down straps securing from the edge of the bag. I have seen other bags with the tie-downs on the edge with the actual support extending only a few inches before ending. I like the way these strips extend for the length of the bag. These strips are also double stitched except where they cross a fellow reinforcement strip and a single stitch is used (only a small area).The ad for this bag clearly states that the bag is water-resistant which should not be confused with waterproof. A generous (approximately 1-1/2") flap is sewn around the bag to enclose the entire zipper area in an attempt to prevent leakage if you are driving through a downpour, but the bag makes a point to advertise that water may leak in at this area and at the seams in certain situations.The actual tie-down straps have a tension-locking buckle (visible in the picture) for securing. I can't say that this is my favorite type of tie-down, so for extended highway driving, I will likely add an additional securing straps across the top.Final notes: The product title lists this bag as black, and it is. I reiterate this only to keep those who look more at the picture than the title from being surprised when a black bag arrives. Also, if you have a small car with a trunk rack and fill this bag up, you will have absolutely no visibility out your back glass or your rearview mirror (which should be obvious to others experienced with this product type but possibly something not realized by all).All and all, this bag is worth its purchase price, but if you have the money to spend a hard box would be better for safety and save you some gas money if you are driving very far.

I was hoping that the outside of this bag would have been of a smoother plastic/pvc like material that would allow for wiping of bugs off at least the front of the bag after a long trip. That is not the case at all with this bag. Instead you have to get out a soft brush and sit there and work with some cleaners and rinse it gently to make sure the water proofing is maintained.Overall it's a nice roof top cargo bag but the lack of ability to easily clean off bugs is rather annoying and disgusting at the same time. I live in a state that has a high insect population during the summer and if you mess up and drive at dawn or dusk with this on top of the car or van you end up with a massive amount of bugs coating it. I was able to use a friends luggage wind deflector to reduce the amount of bugs on the bag but better construction of the bag would have not needed this.Also the underside of the bag is like the rest of the bag, rough fabric that I didn't want laying against the paint on the roof of my car. I had a sheet of tacky rubber that I put against the top of the car that I just peeled off after my weekend trip with everyone, that worked great to protect my paint.Overall, I'm disappointed in some of the aspects of this product but I do realize that most people aren't as particular about certain things like I am so I adjusted my review score accordingly.
summary: The outside of this cargo bag likes to collect bugs and they are hard to clean off.

reviewText: This is a great choice if you have a smaller vehicle, tight budget, and lack of space for a hardshell box.  The bag is very well made and the installation is easy.But you have to keep in mind that this is water resistant, not waterproof.  Amazon carries a one not that much more expensive than this one and it is supposedly a lot better in wet weather.In reality, the best option for your roof is a box from Thule, Yakima, or Sears.  I would pony up for one, but my issue is storing it when not in use.So, I will use this bag, but anything that I don't want wet will have to go in a dry bag before gong in this bag.

This isn't built for daily use for long periods.  I can see getting twenty or so good uses out of it.  For someone like me, that is more than enough.This is a relatively well constructed bag that you could practically fit a body in...not that I recommend that.  It is very roomy and worked perfectly on my FJ Cruiser luggage rack.  I also can see using it in the back of the truck just to carry things.  It is large, but no so ginormous that I can't handle it.The fasteners worked well and the bag held up great to an eight hour road trip.

I was very pleased with this roof top cargo bag. The nylon canvas is nicely heavy and durable; I need that kind of quality because I tend to abuse my camping gear.Eight tie straps make the bag versatile for use with my roof rack (Jeep Cherokee). The buckles are strong enough when tightened down evenly on all sides. The key is to strap and weight the buckles as evenly as possible to prevent any side of the bag from straining in transit, and to close the zipper at the back/leeward end of the vehicle.I might have preferred the kind of buckles that clip in to each other, like a Fastex buckle, but from experience I know those break really quickly (usually after being stepped on). So I see these simple buckles as a decent choice for getting long life from the cargo bag.The straps are wide and well stitched to the outside of the cargo bag. The zipper is sturdy and wide enough to operate with cold, wet hands. Thoughtfully, there are two zipper pulls, so I can close the bag anywhere along the zipper seam (and not just from one end to the other). I added a small padlock between the two zippers for extra security.There is a zipper flap to help rain bead off the bag, instead of dripping instantly into the zipper backing fabric. I still use dry bags inside the cargo bag for anything that has to stay dry, however. I'll be adding Seam Sealer to the seams soon, but I tend to add that to everything I use for camping eventually.There are four possible attachment points to the top of the cargo bag, where the reinforcement straps loop over each other - these are good for adding additional tie-down straps, webbing, or cord to the roof rack.The cargo bag shape is squarish and roomy enough for a simple weekend camping trip, or for adding extra gear to a week-long traveling excursion.My particular plan is to use the bag on my roof rack for paddling trips, so I can keep all wet/sandy/muddy water gear completely outside of the Jeep's interior. The bag also nicely fits into my canoe, so I could pack it up at home, and then move the bag right into the boat, without having to repack anything at the staging area.An unexpected bonus was the water-resistant stuff sack that arrived with the cargo bag. It's nice to have something to keep the bag inside of when not in use for storage and ultraviolet light protection; I can also use the stuff sack as a container inside the cargo bag when it is set up for travel.Altogether, I'm pretty pleased with this addition to my outdoor gear ensemble.NOTE: The cargo bag arrived black, not blue as pictured in the Amazon blurb. I like the black better anyway. :)

This rooftop carrier is made from the same weight material as most luggage, it zips closed with a sturdy zipper and has a covering over the zipper to protect the contents from the weather. The carrier has two heavy adjustable straps per side, my small SUV only has front to back side rails and the carrier straps held two suitcases down well, although side to side bars would ensure an even better hold. Because you have to mount the straps over the carrier rather than under the carrier it isn't going to be as easy to open and close as a hard shell in the middle of your trip but because the straps compress the load it offers  a lower profile than a shell.

If you are in a pinch and need to take a few more items on your trip than your car can carry, this is not a bad choice. It's very sturdy and I never worried about my things falling out, but it's not aerodynamic - there was a noticeable decrease in our MPGs. THe straps were very versatile, so the bag could be used with any vehicle, but if you don't get them really tight the noise is loud and awful, if you do get them tight, the noise is still unpleasant albeit tolerable. It is water resistant and it did keep our stuff dry in a sprinkle - mostly, a little water had leaked in but not yet got to anything that mattered. It is nice that it folds up very small and is soft enough to be squished in a corner if needed.THis is a nice emergency bag, but I would prefer not to have to use it for long trips.
summary: Roomy Bag, Best for Short Trips

reviewText: I'm sure they'd be fine for automotive lights. Fairly dim for an RV overhead lights though but not nearly as dim as the last set I tired. Off to try again.
It fit perfectly in my 03' Eclipse with the rear view mirror map lights! People always ask me how'd you get those lights to be so bright.

These bulbs are great. I'm using them in my 06' Ford F150 as map lights and they light up everything. They do have a blueish tint to them, so I would probably rate the color at about 6-6500K. But they are really bright.
These are about 10x brighter than my original parking lights (2006 subaru impreza). LOTS of light that needs little energy!
I have installed these on the backup light for my 2004 Honda (Acura) TL. Bright but do not cast light as well as the conventional incandescent bulbs; the biggest weakness of LEDs.

Have used these for about 4 months.  Bought two.  One of them has blown one strip of the LEDs on one side. Lights had about 150 hours on "on time".  The bulb with bad LED strip is still usable but I expected it to last longer. I guess it is nice to know that each side of LEDs operate independent of the others, so you can loose some and the others will keep on working.
summary: Some of the LEDs on one bulb stopped working after 4 months intermittent use.

reviewText: This is a very mild cleaner, with a great scent. If you have a heavily soiled interior you may need something with more cleaning power that has added protection, reach for Mother's VLR. Granted VLR doesn't have a nice scent to it, it does work extremely well and with "condition" your leather, vinyl, and rubber parts. This is a perfect product if you don't need the added conditioning.
This is a good one clean and protect and also smell good. You will not get the wet look if that is what you are looking for.
I use this to clean the inside of my Jeep and it smells great too! Works very well on the spills in the cup holders, surpised me what is could clean!

Ordered this a a comparison to Meg's interior cleaner/dressing.Wins over that in a few ways, in my opinion.-Leaves a completely satin finish-Does a good job at not attracting dust.-Little goes a long way. Usually apply few sprays to applicator pad and is enough to do the doors and 1 quarter of car. Like to split interiors into sections.-Smells good. Goes away fairly quickly, but that's okay, Dont like scents to linger too longHowever, I would be remiss if I did not post a few negatives:-Not as long-lasting-Spray nozzle has seized up and will not spray. Resolved by moving to  one of their pro bottles with a chemical resistant nozzle.Never had this issue with meg's bottle.

reviewerName: Jay "My opinion doesn't have to be yours..."
reviewText: Does an excellent job on my interiors without leaving a slippery/greasy feel on surfaces like the steering wheel...The faint pineapple like scent is pretty good as well...Highly pleased with this product.
summary: Does an excellent job on my interiors without leaving a slippery/greasy feel ...

reviewText: The summary about covers it.  This is really good stuff, and suitable for almost any interior surface of your car.  Smells great, and works well to remove residue left from hands/fingers.  (on screens, steering wheel,arm rests, etc.)  Leaves behind a nice clean surface.  Great product.
summary: Great interior cleaner.  Smells great, cleans, repels dust, OK for electronics.  Use microfiber cloth.

reviewText: Unlike most interior detailers that just try to shine up dirt this actually cleans, leaves no oils and has a factory sheen to it.
cant really go wrong with Chemical Guys products. has a nice clean smell and does not streak or smear on dash,or hard plastic panels.

This stuff works great, it will remove black shoe marks off of beige interior kick panels and fingerprints off of wood trim in one swipe and it also does a great job dusting and cleaning all interior areas
I am impressed so far with this interior detailer spray. The only thing that I am not impressed with so far is the scent and how long it lasts. I'm not a fan of pina colada.

I'm not a fan of off the shelf interior cleaners that leave a glossy slick uneven coat on my interior.This product cleans and make the interior panels looking like new.  You can apply gels and gloss after, but I like my cars looking factory fresh. Works for me

I like this product, but I find myself comparing interior detailers to Meg's Quick Interior Detailer. I have used that for many years and thought maybe I would try something different. This products smells good and definitely leaves a matte finish. I found that it leaves behind a haze and needs to be buffed off (may well be because it was cold outside, but who knows), which is one extra step that I didn't want to have to take. Overall I think this is a good product, but for the price, there are much better alternatives, which might keep me from purchasing this again. I will stick to my Megs and keep my quick swipe of the interior in my detail routine, but give this 4 stars because it really isn't a bad product. Unfortunately just not the right price.

Dexron VI is the recommended transmission fluid for many late model GM transmissions and is value priced. Of course, check with the owners manual, service manual or dealer for your specific requirement and capacity prior to purchase.
summary: Dexron VI is recommended for many late model GM transmissions

reviewText: Did a flush for my BMW 328i auto, 100k miles tune up.  Shifts butter smooth and feeling good knowing that my tranny is well protected.

I have a 2005 GMC Envoy XL whose automatic transmission was having issues. After much research online, I decided flushing it (I had about 50K miles since previous flush) would be the easiest potential solution.After getting two cases and flushing the AT, the issue was gone. Fixed. Done. I will be doing this every 40-50K miles from now on.
The Dexron in my '05 Northstar Cadillac STS looked like motor oil coming out, even though it's "lifetime" fluid.This should last longer, and I'll likely drain/fill every 30K miles.
Have used this product on older Dexron II GM cars and all responded very well to it; great for often neglected trans service.

I was personally quite disappointed with this oil.  After getting my new bike and filling it with the other Castrol 4T Mineral based 4-stroke motorcycle oil, it ran smooth and shifted with little effort.But this synthetic stuff is just terrible in comparison.  Hard shifts, missed shifts.Just not for my 1 cylinder push rod 4 stroke 250cc wet clutch.
summary: Not for 1 cylinder push rod 4 stroke 250cc wet clutches

reviewText: Conventional motorcycle oil is suitable for normal use but for extended service intervals synthetic oil is a better choice. However, unless you are racing full synthetic isn't really necessary. Castrol Actevo Xtra part synthetic fits this application perfect at around 60% the cost of full synthetic. If you have anything with a wet-clutch and integral transmission, use an oil that's formulated specifically for the application. Using an automotive oil 10w40 and above (non energy conserving) won't damage the clutch, but it doesn't have friction modifiers for the clutch (extending the life) or anti-foaming additives for high rpm engines.  Do your bike a favor and use the right oil.
After 3 oil changes, things are looks MUCH cleaner with this oil. I am sticking with it for a good while over more spendy ones.

I use this oil in my 2006 Kawasaki Ninja 500R and 2006 Ducati Monster S2R1000. They both run great. I was gonna buy the Mobil 1 or the Motul oil, but this seems to be fine. I maintain the bikes well and change the oil regularly, so this oil suits me just fine.
summary: Good quality oil at a great price point.

reviewText: Use this oil For my Brute Force 750 and it seems to love it better than Mobil 1.  I like Mobil1, don't get me wrong.  But this oil is better in a Kawasaki.  More guys and gals will tell ya, this stuff is just best in a Kaw.  Even in -3 the motor purred liked a kitten and ran like a top.  I swear by this oil and always have.  Put it in my 1500 classic too.  Never once had motor or clutch problems over the years.
summary: Best oil for my Brute force 750

reviewText: I change the oil on my 2008 Kingpin myself, so I am always interested in seeing what else is out there. The price on this 6-pack was pretty cost-effective and cheaper than what I could find the 'official' Pure Victory kit. The shifting and overall feel of the bike after the oil change appears to be identical to the victory oil that was in there before - if not a little smoother. At the very least, it doesn't feel different in a bad way. So, I saved some money and the bike is, for me, riding the same. Win - win. :)
summary: Cheaper than Victory oil and just as good

reviewText: Castrol makes very good oil for all cars bikes trucks. You cant get better oil for the money way better then Mobile 1.Def recommend this oil brand
Used this oil on my Victory Vegas and So far I love it, three months later and still running smoother than whatever oil the dealership put on the previous oil change.

MUCH BETTER BUY THAN THE LOCAL MC DEALER!! I would like to give my local MC dealer some business, but the price is is 1/2 to 1/3 less for the same product. MC-specific oil is expensive due to it not having the slippery stuff in it due to a MC having a wet clutch.

I purchased this for my Victory Vision motorcycle and I'm very happy! I've always used victory brand oil since new. I wanted to try something else and was recommended this. I noticed my bike ran smoother and seemed to run a little cooler as well. I highly recommend!
Use in a 1300 VStar Motorcycle. No problems, no fuss.  Seems to keep the oil cooler but who knows for sure. It's good oil thats a given.

Paid about 45 bucks for the six-pack: that works out to $7.50 a quart -- hard to beat for 100% synthetic oil. I had some reservations about using this racing oil for my Suzuki m50 street cruiser but she's been running smooth and happy since I poured the Castrol in. The API "SL" rating might not be hi-tech enough for the very newest bikes, but it far exceeds the specs for my 2005 model. Get this stuff while its still around.
its great! my bike runs better then i thought it would. more smooth then ever before. i will buy again!

Castrol was always my #1 choice for oil in auto or bike, and since synthetic came along it's the only oil I use in either vehicle and have never had any issues or failures of my motors, even when 'beat' a bit.  Castrol's been around since long before my time, and I'm a senior citizen now, and it's kept cars on roads and in races, and planes in the sky for that long.
I used it on my 2000 Honda Shadow (it's a cruiser). No problems what so ever, I even felt an improvement on shifting from first try.

This is a great high quality motorcycle oil available at an excellent price from Amazon.  My bikes take 4 quarts each, and I have 3, so two cases is enough for oil changes for all of my bikes.  I find the price to be cheaper from Amazon than it is available by the quart from the large box store starting with a "W"  :-)

This is great product!  Just performed my first oil change after the 600 mile "break-in" period on my 2011 Hayabusa.  From the start, I noticed that my transmission shifts much more smoothly and seems to run cooler.I combined this oil with a K&N; oil and air filter change as well.

The price offered by Amazon is about 30% lower than I can find anywhere else.  I think this oil is every bit as good as Mobil 1 and is priced better.  My FJR seems to run and shift the same on either brand.

Natures Lube for everything.... and I mean everything ;)In this case for my Yamaha R6. Seems to work well. I mean I rode my bike today and it didn't die.Motor oil is motor oil. Just change it regularly and don't fret over which one is better.

extremely useful, especially if you have a travel trailer where the only means to clean the gray tank out is through the toilet.With this setup nothing gets dirty and all one needs to do is keep an eye on the water levels.
I used this to clean out my black water tank. Worked as described to fill the tank for flushing. I used this in conjunction with the sewer solution to flush the contents uphill to my sewer clean out.

I just went on our first trip in our new KZ Spree 195. I figured I'd do it right from the beginning and purchased this and a few other tools to properly handle the waste tanks. I filled the tanks a bit so they weren't used "dry" and we really only used the toilet a few times. I drained the tank once each evening and then refilled to about 1/3 full to keep fluid in the tank.When it was time to go, I drained the black tank, and watched the waste pass by in the clear elbow thinking that it looked about right, but I figured I'd try a back flush anyway. I was surprised to see that I got as much or more out after the first flush then simply draining it alone. Then again, I figured surely there couldn't be a need to flush a new tank twice, but I tried it anyway, and again was surprised to see more waste flush by. Then of course, I just had to see if a third time would net the same results, and I again saw more stuff fly by. My fourth flush on a new tank that was lightly used for two days finally came clear.I'm convinced and wouldn't think of owning a camper without this tool.

I have a Lance trailer.  As much as I love the trailer, the dump tube for both waste tanks is almost a level tube and needs some way to evacuate the tanks.  This flush valve appears to be the answer!  I haven't used it yet, but plan to use it this week when I prepare the trailer for the weekend.  Even though the black tank has a flusher, this will really ensure that the tank is empty.  It is NOT to be left on the dump tube - it should only be used and then removed to storage while traveling!

This thing works nicely. When that nice clear water runs from your tank through the clear plastic tube it's very nice to see that everything's nice and clean. This thing fit a little too closely to allow full movement of my blade valve handles so I combined with a Camco 39572 5" Clear Sewer Hose Adapter which I just leave attached to the trailer dump outlet with a cover. If you don't have a sensor that you can see from the hydrant I also recommend using the RAINWAVE WATER TIMER .. SAVE WATER - FLOW METER in addition to measure the gallonage you are using on the backflush. Caution - don't lose the little rubber backflow preventer under the water valve.

Valterra is known for quality RV products and this is no exception. Flushes tank quickly, with high water flow and clear pipe shows when tank is clean. No more hoses through the window or cutting holes in in your tank for nozzles to flush your black water tank.

bought this after watching some videos online on black water tank cleanouts.  This fluch valve works exactly as expected and makes black water tank cleanup super easy.  Just shut in the dump vlave and fill and flush with fresh water.  Couldn't get any easier than that, and there is no mess of spraying water or anything of that nature.  I highly recomend this product.

I could never get my Camco performing as well as I'd hoped. Camco's weak point is the complicated and flow-restricting fresh water valve. This has a very simple water inlet that allows full flow from the hose to flush my tanks. And the Valterra valve is smooth as silk. I bought this from my favorite local RV shop for more than currently it costs at Amazon. Had Amazon had this current price way back when, I would opted for the Flush King over the Camco version.
I use it to tight all the suspension system of my Jeep Wrangler. I'm very satisfied with this impact wrench.
summary: The best you can get for this price

reviewText: I am really impressed with this unit. Now it does not have brush cap/ access holes so when the brushes wear out I'll have to take it apart but WOW! For some reason I feel like rotating my tires. I can't wait to see how it does busting hub nuts and the nuts on harmonic balancers.The case is kind of cheapy but it does come with 4 impact sockets.I definitely recommend this affordable tool to any DIYer.

I wanted an ac powered impact wrench for small projects, however this one was bigger than I had expected. It comes with 4 or 5 impact nuts (hardened steel), for tightening and loosening bolts like bicycle wheel axis, scooter variator nuts, and larger car bolts (like wheels, engine mounts, etc). for the rest I can do little with it, as the tool is too big for the job I need it for, and I should have gone with a battery powered version instead.It rotates pretty fast, hammers the bolts pretty hard too!I would not do any bolt/nuts under an M16, or 11/16, because the device will overtighten them, and probably cause thread wear.But for big jobs, it's good enough.
summary: So far so good! Excellent for car!

reviewText: This thing is so Bulky and Heavy and unbalanced.. I took it out of the box and put it back. This would be good for nothing more than taking off lug nuts once a year for a rotation. There are smaller, more powerful electric impact guns on the market that you can fit inside a wheel well let alone an engine compartment.
summary: Too Big, and Bulky to be Practical.

reviewText: Im very disappointed in this wrench. The 12 volt wrench like this is better...go figure! I just performed a strut job on my toyota and it had troubles breaking the bolts off and the 12 volt could break em. Im glad i decided to purchase the 12 volt version of this as well. The clicking of the 12 volt drives me nuts but at least i know them bolts or nuts are coming off. I guess this wrench needs more power or sum thin. Im not sure it just doesn't work well. Ik already i will be using the cheaper impact as its more handy because of its compact size compared to this and it just works better. I guess i will just keep it for backup. Good luck on who else decides to purchase this. Maybe you will have better luck!

At least read the one about how to turn off the alarm. I turned it on and it SHRIEEEEKED, which was GREAT but the landlady lives right across the hall from me and to keep her from running out her door having conniptions, I had to find a BIIIG pillow to put the BodyGard under until I could read the directions and turn off The Shriek. How loud is The Shriek? Well, if someone bothers you on the subway or in a bus or stairwell, the noise will echo from all four corners of the vehicle and if it does not stun the person it will at least draw ALOT of attention to you both. The button for The Shriek is flush with the BodyGard's body but I recommend hanging it from a zipper instead of putting it in a pocket, where a finger inadvertantly gripping it may cause a minor panic.The ring to hang this with is a decent size -- I would have wanted something larger but all I have to do is go into a hardware store and get one cheap.The knife to cut a seatbelt is a single(?)-edge razor in a setup similar to those free envelope openers they sometimes give out at the stationery store. It looks sharp enough - I hope it works. The user has to pull the red plastic cover away in order to expose the cutting edge, and that is simple enough to do especially since all you have to do is put a finger in the keyring and pull. In a real emergency situation I think that red cover will get lost in the process, and if so, I hope it can be replaced. Well, maybe it won;t get lost if your keys are hanging on it -- but ayway.. it's a thought.Flashlight beam is O..K.. a nice blue white light but not as intense as I think it should be. A second touch of the flashlight button produces a flashing red light which is GREAT.I would have like to have tested the glass cutter. It seems to be spring loaded and I hope it works. I could not find any glass (other than my balcony door or my apartment windows) on which to try it, and of course, with or without the landlady in such close proximity, THAT is a no-no.All in all, the Swiss+Tech ST81005 BodyGard ESC 5-in-1 Automobile Emergency Tool is a great, small tool that could easily save your life in many ways.
summary: If you don't like to read the instructions....

reviewText: This device provides a significant bit of added safety in your car. In the very unlikely event where you have an accident that disables the doors and power windows, you can use this tool to break a side window. The built in spring hammer will break tempered glass. The windshield is laminated glass and the tool can not break that. If you can't escape because your seat belt is jammed, the built-in cutter will let you cut the belt so you can get out. These functions could save your life. I was unable to test either function since I don't want to break any of my car's windows or slice a seat belt.There is also a little LED flashlight and LED red blinker. The manufacturer claims these could be helpful in an emergency. The flashlight is not very bright, but could help you find your keys if you drop them. The flasher is also rather dim and I can't think of any situation where I would want it. There is also an audible alarm. This alarm is pretty loud and could scare off a potential assailant.You can get a visor clip for the tool that will put it in easy reach in an emergency. That is what I plan to do. All in all, this is a very helpful lifesaver for a reasonable price. I gave it four stars instead of five because it really is too big for me to use on my key chain.
summary: Handy Lifesaver. A little too heavy for my keychain

reviewText: The size is nice if you want it as a keychain.  Supposedly you can buy a visor clip, which I think would be more ideal if you have more than one driver per car.The seatbelt cutter looks strong and I didn't want to test the glass breaker, but it should work based on past experiences with said tool.I like the lights a lot.  The sound is loud, but probably not loud enough to really scare off a potential attacker or to alert others to your location.The batteries are easy to replace.All it all, it's priced right and hopefully you never need it.

The tool is light and not particularly impressive. The plastic seems flimsy.  There are seven features in this emergency tool.  The price seems high for the quality.Features:1) flashlight - very weak and I really don't know how effective it would be. If you could not get your key in the ignition, I suppose it would help in that instance.2) flasher - press the flashlight button twice and you get a red flasher. Again, very weak and I have no faith that it would be visible at any distance.3) sonic alarm -very loud and the button is NOT recessed so it would be easy to accidentally turn it on.  This might be handy but it is also easily squelched by covering the speaker hold in the back of this unit. You would have to have this tool on your person rather than stored in the car to use  this feature. If this is carried in a pocket, I can see you pocket screaming unintentionally at one point or another.4) seat belt cutter - I can't test it, but the cutter is nicely covered but it comes with a key fob and the fob attaches to the blade cover. I think it would pull out, it is not very secure. I did test it on paper and the cur was reluctant.5) glass breaker - can't test this one out but I have to say I am not impressed by the small button. I would prefer something more substantialI would like to give the product a fair review but I really cannot test the cutter or the glass breaker. Another reviewer felt it would break glass.  The batteries are button batteries which are a hassle, and expensive, and a AA would be so much easier.If  I was in the market for an emergency tool for my car, I would continue to look elsewhere.

I was a little disappointed to realize this device is made out of all plastic and feels a little less than sturdy.  It's also rather bulky and no way would I use it as a keychain.  The LED lights (white and red flashing) are bright enough to help out in a pinch.  The sonic alarm isn't extremely loud and would probably get somebody's attention.  The seatbelt cutter should work and although I hope to never have to use the punch glass tool, it is nice to have.  I just wish it felt a little more sturdy and was a bit more compact to really be used as a keychain.

This is one of those, "You just never know" type devices that gives your or your loved ones a little bit of peace of mind.
