I rate it up there with smoke detectors and fire extinguishers.The main reason I give only 4 stars is because the LED flashlight is a poor design in that it is too easy to press and turn on by accident, in your pocket or perhaps a purse.Also, the size of this thing is really large that you wouldn't want to put your keys plus a 3" x 2" device in your pocket!  Better yet, take off the fuzzy dice and attach this thing to your rear view mirror!  Just yank on it to use it in an emergency!  (It's designed to slide out easily)This is 5-in-1 which includes a personal alarm, but that too, is a bit too easy to trigger, nor do I think effective versus yelling, which your basic instinct will make you do anyways.Overall, this is a good buy for peace of mind to hang on your rear view mirror for easy use when you may need it.
summary: Large for a key ring, but great for the glove box

reviewText: Swiss+Tech makes a lot of interesting products. I have quiet a few (kind of a gadget geek.) I just gave my wife their 7-in-1 tool - very similar to this one except it has a tire pressure gauge and the tread depth gauge. I actually like this one more and will keep it in my car because it has a smaller size but still has the basic emergency tools that seem like smart things to have at hand.In particular, I like having the glass smasher and seatbelt cutting tools. At race tracks, most SCCA corner workers carry a pocket knife and glass smashing tool in case they have to extract a driver stuck in a burning car. As a 25 year member of the SCCA, I have drunk the Kool-Aid and see the value of these two potentially valuable tools. I donate items to a corner worker awards fund and think I'll get a few of these to donate at the annual worker holiday party.The light, alarm and flasher are probably more useful in common real world situations (I can't tell you how many times a week I use a flashlight...) so these get high marks too.If I was still managing a small team of technical folks, this under $10 stocking stuffer would be their holiday gift from me.Recommended
summary: Compact size, useful tools, great price

reviewText: great stuff!! ive had these before!! i cant promise anything but i use them also as caution flags for things sticking out of my truck!! they are larger then the 1' x 1' required by fl law

So, these are shop towels, not sure what else to say....they are the same red towels you can buy at any auto parts store.  They are meant for use in the shop (appropriate name right).  If you are not familiar with the use of a "shop towel" and intent these to be as soft as micro fiber or as thick as a beach towel, you will probably be disappointed.  They are throw-away shop towels at a cheaper price than you would find in an auto parts store.....level set expectations and you won't be disappointed.
Meets all my criteria for shop rags. Lots of them, and can wipe things up. Makes it a good deal in my opinion.
These are nice towels, not as heavy as I had hopped, but still nice and sturdy, I expect each one to last for a long time.

These are good disposable rags to use around the house, for your car, etc.They are quite thin so I would not plan on washing them to use multiple times. You could try using them and then washing them once or twice and re-using themn but be ware that the blue dye will get all over on other things you wash so I would recommend you wash them separately. You've been warned! I tried washing a few of them with some white rags and the white rags turned sky blue.I use these to wipe down my car motor, clean my wheels, things like that. It's nice to not have to mess up my nice microfiber towels that I uses for waxing my car.But when these get dirty, I just throw them away since it's more of a hassle to try to wash them than it's worth.

I don't really work on cars beyond the most basic, but find that an OBDII scanner is good when seeing that dreaded "Check Engine Light" (CEL) or, most important, buying a used car and want to find out what's going on with the engine.Last summer I almost pulled the trigger on a Mercedes SL500, beautiful car, but the CEL went on during the test drive.  "Must be the gas cap", said the seller.  I pulled out my cheap $20 OBDII and found lots of codes popping up, and after looking them up noticed wonderful issues like cylinder misfiring, ERG problems, O2 sensor problems, and more.  Good news was that apparently the gas cap was fine!The Innova 3130c is a lot more than $20, and finds a lot more.  I found it easy to use, and to have an extensive code database.Is it worth the money?  It depends.  Certainly if you are doing work on a car yourself, yes.  If you are buying a car, it is good to weed out the lemons (and costs less than a prepurchase inspection).  It's a good choice for the money, build quality is high, and Innova is solid in the OBDII reader field.
very good A++++++++++++++ the best one for Diagnose to your car

This is an easy to use device that comes in an attractive black carrying case.  It is simple to set up. Insert the included batteries and cable, affix to the car's DLC and you are good to go. While I did have to manually input the data on a 98 ford it did  the other vehicles automatically. I found the screen readable.  It correctly identified a coolant issue. I do wiSh the full manual was included but other than that this is a worthy, cost-saving scanner.

This OBD2 scan tool can be used on all 1996 and newer vehicles.  My 2003 Infiniti's "Service Engine Soon" or MIL (malfunction indicator lamp) lit up after it was parked for six months with the battery disconnected  (traveling/driving my other vehicles) and a family member inadvertently disconnected the trickle charger.  No problem, I thought, and recharged the battery, then drove the car the next day.  However, after about 1 mile, the car's MIL lit up and went into "limp"mode (doesn't shift into higher gears, rpms higher during driving, and engines idles high, etc.) I immediately put this Innova 3130c Scan Tool to good use.How the Innova Scan Tool 3130c worked so far:>Easy to use: insert 3 AA batteries (included), plug in the OBD2 cable with the ignition switch "off", turn ignition switch to "on" (without starting the engine) and the Scan Tool automatically turns on. Press the power/link button.>Scan tool did not automatically i.d. the vehicle so year, make, and model had to be manually entered.>Pressed the DTC (Diagnostic Trouble Codes)/FF (Freeze Frame) button and code displayed was for "Throttle Body Sensor".>I went to the Innova website and downloaded the necessary software for advanced diagnostic info which is free for one month which advised cleaning or replacing the throttle body.>Because I've experienced the same problem two years before, I learned from online forums and google searches that the onboard computer had reset completely with the battery disconnected for so long and it was necessary first clear the code, which this scan tool does with a push of the red Erase button, then reset the throttle body position sensor and idle speeds using exact sequences of key on/off, accelerator pedal fully depressed/released, etc.>Can be connected to the PC via USB cable for downloading relevant software, recording vehicle data, or using more advanced features.>The Enhanced DTCs and ABS DTCs functions did not work with my 2003 Infiniti.>Haven't tried this Scan Tool with my newer vehicles because they're running fine with no MIL or other problems.>Comes with a sturdy, nylon carrying case for the scan tool, OBD2 cable, and USB cable,etc.Overall:Good, informative vehicle trouble code reader with more advanced features such as Live Data (recording and playback) mode, Special Tests, Enhanced DTCs, ABS DTCs, etc.  My local auto parts store won't even let me borrow their code reader and wanted to sell me a basic reader for $60, local repair shops wanted $100 just to read the code, and a local dealer wanted $150 just to diagnose the problem.  This Scan Tool provides motorists with trouble codes and repair options so they may choose wisely where to spend their money (or save even more money by DIY) for vehicle repairs.  Please note that more inexpensive scan tools  such as theAutel MaxiScan MS300 CAN Diagnostic Scan Tool for OBDII Vehicleswill provide the basic codes but don't have the more advanced features that some motorists may require.
summary: Useful vehicle trouble code reader but subscription required for more detailed online info.

reviewText: My primary beef with this product is lack of Mac support, plugging the device into my Mac's USB port results in nothing but a complaint about the disk being of unknown format. I have a Windows 7 virtual machine available, and I was able to mount the device there, download and install Innova's software and get a report for my car. The Windows software was clunky and required installing database DLLs I'd have rather not installed, but it seems to work OK. While I didn't have any error codes to look at for my 2003 Civic, the report the application generated helpfully pointed out I'm likely to need a new catalytic converter soon (based on my car's age and mileage).I'm not happy with the industry trend of having me provide my personal information in order to use a device. Certainly, Innova doesn't really need my phone number or address to activate their device. I am not looking forward to future mass mailing hitting my mailbox/recycle bin. I guess it could be worse, they could have Facebook integration...The hardware is adequate, and a good step up from my last code scanner, an Actron Pocketscan, who's small screen and cryptic onscreen display would lead me astray with my Civic. At least this Innova knows the idiosyncrasies of my particular make and model of car. I'm almost looking forward to my next check engine light. Almost.

As many other reviewers have reported this scanner is good for personal use. However there are cheaper less feature packed models that will accomplish the same goal such as theINNOVA 3040Setup was a bit of a pain. No Mac support at all (not surprised) so I had to use my shop PC instead.Installation and setup of the software was clunky but got through it just fine.The overall hardware is solid, no complaints. Very easy to read screen/menu even in fairly direct sunlight.One of the best features I thought was the live data review which you can record and playback.Since I don't have an entire fleet of vehicles to test/use this on, I'm sure this will more than serve its purpose for many check engine lights to come!

This is a great scanner.  It has a nice long cord and the screen is backlit.  It works quickly and has pretty easy to use interface.  It worked with basic functions on my 2004 BMW, but had much more expansive functions on my 2010 Honda.  The scanner produces codes with plain english explanations.  There is an online component through innova repair solutions.  You get a trial membership, but then it costs money to use that.  It works pretty well with live data response.There are more basic scanners out there that will eventually do most of the same things, but this is a very nice product for someone who will use it fairly frequently.By the way, mine came with a MicroSD card installed in the battery compartment.  It is very small - the size of a pinky nail.  I see from some other reviews, that some may have shipped without it.  Mine came with it.
summary: Tool is great, but online component is extra

reviewText: I am not a sophisticated mechanic, but I am handy at fixing some things.  And one thing I have learned is to never take my car for service before first checking it with a scanner.  I have saved many hundreds of dollars getting fixit tips from the internet based on what my scanner told me.  And, by taking good care of my car and truck, I get lots of mileage from them - they are all at least 15 years old.My previous scanner was very basic and gave basic codes on two short lines of a very small display.  So this Innova scanner is a real treat to use.  And for all it does, it is really simple to use.  I have no DTC codes to read at the moment but connecting, scanning and navigating the menus was very simple.  I really like the system status indicator for emissions testing readiness.  The live data reading and capture is also easy to use.  I just hope it is a while before I need to use the fix assist feature.There are some things I didn't like about the scanner including the lengthy installation (complete with a reboot) on my Windows 7 laptop.  Also, the instructions that come with the scanner also do not mention how to install the software - there is no included disc.  One line directing to plug the scanner into the PC and letting the PC detect it would have been helpful.  I also had to enter my 1996 Ford and my 1998 Chrysler info manually (perhaps they were too old to auto detect?).  Finally, this model does not come with the ABS and airbag coverage for either of the autos I tested.  For the price, I think they should have included that option.
summary: Works well but may not have all of the feathres you want

reviewText: First of all, for a mechanic that has a small shop or someone that does repair on the weekend for money, this is a nice tool. However, for the average "joe" or "jane" that tinkers with their car, there are better options out there.The thing with these dedicated devices is more related to their competition with laptop based tools and either a usb or bluetooth enabled OBDII reader.many OBDII readers can be purchased on eBay or even amazon to use with a laptop. There are also bluetooth enabled OBDII devices that can link with your cell phone (android based) and can complete a large amount of diagnostic work. The best app that I have seen is TORQUE, see the google play store, Some examples Soliport ELM 327 Bluetooth OBDII OBD2 Diagnostic Scanner orSuper Mini ELM327 V1.5 OBD2 OBD-II Bluetooth CAN-BUS Auto Diagnostic Tool for Windows XP, Vista, Win7, OSX and Android,PLX Devices Kiwi Bluetooth Wireless Trip Computer and OBDII ScannerSo as an everyday alternative that is very robust, not quite as much as this one, but very good for most tasks, a combo android cell phone or laptop and a good obdii scanner can get you the same place with a little less $$.Finally, the device is pretty easy to use, but not very intuitive. You will need to read the manual.You also have additional add ons that you can purchase to enhance the ability of the scanner and the amount of information that can accessed based on vehicle manufacturer ....Overall this is a great tool for a power user or a mechanic. They also have cheaper alternatives that you can use if your level of expertise is not as high or needs are not as significant ...INNOVA 3100 CAN/OBDII Code Reader
summary: Good for high tech mechs, if you need one for around the house, better alternatives are around .** Company response in comments

reviewText: This is a very handy scanner to have, especially for the home mechanic.  Not only can it scan trouble codes, it can also read MAP, O2 sensors etc and help you to see if one or might soon fail.  This is vary useful, as well as the misfire analysis that can tell you what the conditions were when a misfire occurred and help you troubleshoot it, I wish I'd had this last year when my 02 Durango was throwing a persistent misfire that we couldn't track down the source of, because I'm pretty sure this would have been able to pinpoint the problem.  When we plugged it into both our cars, it recognized both cars and could pull the VIN#, make, model, etc.Also, I love the fact that you can upload data to their website and have it generate reports showing you what is wrong and what was going on under the hood at the time, and even what might fail in the future and how much it would cost - very handy.  The basic report is free, but the premium membership report is $19 for one month or 1yr for $59.  This is really pretty reasonable, considering what all they offer - the premium membership has videos to even show you how to do some repairs.  None of my cars have a check engine light on right now, so I can't test how well it diagnoses the problem yet - I update as soon as I am able to do that.  It is definitely nice that it can tell you whether or not you will pass an emissions test.What I don't like, is that the ABS data for Honda and Toyota, costs extra - $99 extra.  Also, the unit I received had the tiny micro usb card just laying loose in the box and I almost didn't see it because the card is pretty tiny.  Which was another minor complaint, their instructions didn't say where you put the card in and it took me a while of hunting around to find the slot where it goes under the battery cover near the usb plug.Overall, at this price, this scanner does considerably more than other scanners that can only read and reset the DTC's, and right now while it is on sale I would say it's an incredible value and you can't go wrong purchasing it.
summary: lots of great features, but some cost extra to use

reviewText: I can only review this item as a regular scanner as the advanced portions of its programming are not available to my Subaru.  But for what I have used it for it works great.  It found my oxygen sensor was bad and told me so.  Or at least confirmed my suspicions as the most likely reason among several.  It's been replaced and the ten year old car (with 34,000 miles...not bad huh) is back to running beautifully.  I connected on the steering column and turnd the key on and it scanned immediately and found what it needed and was ready to proceed.  In the memory it found the sensors info I guess and pretty soon indicated it should probably be replaced.  I went to the advanced mode and it indicated that it did not function for Subarus which is the only model I can actually report that on I scanned the list and they are primarily american manufacturers if you want advanced services.  Since it did what it did so quickly and efficiently I had no need to use the pc software.  If and when I do I'll come back and report but based on my initial experience I'd say it's a pretty sophisticated piece of equipment that will read II but is not backwards compatible with I.  (my son said I should point out that it does work on Ford Trucks tho why they should take precedence here I haven't a clue)  I'd recommend it.

The Innova 3130c is claimed to be a full-featured diagnostic scanner with advanced information about error codes and hints as to how to fix problems. It comes in a nice zippered case with a removable ODBII cable and a USB cable, plus three AA batteries. The included Quick Reference Guide makes no mention of the USB cable, and while the box says that software is included, there is no CD or any indication of where to get the software. Visiting Innova's site doesn't clarify the mystery - if you go to the "Downloads" page for the 3130c, you are offered only the full user manual (which only says that software is optional) and a link to Adobe Reader. The Innova web site currently shows only the 3130b model, and the product picture shows a CD. Hmm...Remembering that I've had some products that essentially contained their own software, I connected the USB cable to my PC. Aha! Windows mounted a pretend CD that had an Innova Downloader. I ran that and it downloaded the software. Some hint about this in the packaging (say, a mention in the Quick Reference or a slip of paper) would have been very welcome. I can imagine some purchasers might complain that they had an incomplete product.Sometime later I then decided to go to the 3130b page and its download link - the software is shown there. Sigh....I see other reviewers had an issue with a SD card missing. The 3130c I received included the card.I first tried the 3130c on my 2013 Audi. The tool itself identified the car as a Volkswagen and had no information on model, etc. It could pull up raw data about the engine, but did not offer support for "enhanced" codes I then tried on my wife's 2013 Honda. Again, it did not identify the model, engine type, etc., but did claim to support enhanced codes. But when I asked the tools to retrieve those codes, it said "a link could not be established".A nice feature of the 3130c that my other scanners don't have is the ability to record live data for later analysis. You can have the tool either record the data when an "event" occurs (such as would trigger the check engine light), or manually, and you can ask it to record the next 100 seconds, previous 100 seconds, or 50 seconds before and after. You can review some of this data on the tool itself, but much more information is provided if you use the PC link.The software that gets installed is not self-contained - it links to the Innova web site where you must register an account. A "Basic" subscription is free and gets you limited access to data and assistance, whereas a "Premium" subscription gets you more. The first time you connect it says you get one month of premium access.Although neither of my cars was showing any codes, the tool lit the yellow "caution" light for the Honda and flashed a symbol for the evaporative system. But it said no codes were pending. It wasn't until I connected the tool to the web site that it then told me that the car hadn't yet completed its built-in tests - while it has a few thousand miles on it, it did just return from a dealer visit for a recall - one not shown in Innova's database - so maybe the dealer reset something.The menus and controls on the 3130c are confusingly labeled and at times I could not figure out how to get to menus such as Live Data. I just kept pressing buttons until I got there. The downloadable user manual has a lot of tutorial information on ODBII diagnostic capabilities and is worth a thorough read.The 3130c's improvement over the 3130b is that it claims to support getting information about ABS systems. It didn't work for me on either of my cars. I note that there is an update for the 3130b that adds this support.Since neither of my cars is "throwing a code", I couldn't test the "Fix Assist" technology, though note that you have to connect to their service from a Windows computer to get this. The extended code support is limited to a few manufacturers, and at least for the Honda, which is claimed to be supported, I'm not convinced it really knows anything. For my Audi I have a "VAG-COM" cable from Ross-Tech that connects to a laptop and provides far more detailed information and modification ability than the Innova. Of course, this cable is more expensive that the 3130c and is specific to Volkswagen-Audi vehicles, but I imagine that there are similar products for other manufacturers. You may want to investigate these before buying the Innova. Otherwise, you might be satisfied with one of the less expensive scanners such as some of the Actrons. I have a $30 Actron I bought from Amazon a while ago and it is basic but retrieves codes just as well.Edit: June 1, 2013A coworker had a car that had an intermittent Check Engine light, so I brought out the Innova to see what it said. It readily displayed the code, which was for the oxygen sensor, and the tool displayed some simple advice on checking wires. I then connected the tool to the PC and it brought up the Innova web site. The site report displayed the code, said it would cost about $600 to fix it, and that their technicians had a "verified fix", and wouldn't I like to upgrade to Premium to see it? What? I thought I had a one month free premium membership!I contacted Innova support who told me that the free membership was only for the first car I got a report on, a tidbit NOT mentioned in the page promising the free month. However, I now see fine print on another page that says "For each subscription, users will be allowed to register and make UNLIMITED Diagnostic Reports for 1 unique vehicle." A month is $19.99, a year is $59.99. So if you have two cars, you need two memberships.
summary: Confusing menus, poor instructions, Windows and subscription required for advanced features

reviewText: This device could easily pay for itself after a few uses.  Apparently, cars can have error codes that don't rise to the degree of lighting up the check engine light.  That was the case when I hooked up this to my vehicle.  It showed a transmission problem code, but no dash light lit up.  I took it to a local shop and was able to get a sensor replaced before additional damage was done.This device can be for the novice or the pro by showing you the codes, offering fixes via the Fix Assist, as well as doing live snapshots of data which are helpful to the pros.  It will also remember your vehicles so you don't have to enter it each time.  I guess it needs your vehicle type to determine what fixes you'll need.It comes with a nice, durable case and it appears well built.  It should last a long, long time.I wish I had gotten this a long time ago.  Who knows how much it would have saved me.
summary: Can read codes even when engine light doesn't show.  Saved me $$$

reviewText: I got this scanner to replace another Actron scanner I had which was damaged. The Actron scanner was 50% more expensive then this Innova scanner.I find this scanner quite a bit better visually... first, the screen is MUCH easier to see. I remember using the Actron in any sort of sunlight required twisting, turning and shielding the unit from the light in order to view the screen. The Innova screen has a backlight and is easily viewable at all times... I had absolutely no trouble viewing the screen at any time. Second, the Actron displayed information only about what option was selected, which normally required a lot of key presses to cycle through the data and find out what's going on. The Innova has icons across the top letting you know basic information at all times, such as engine monitor problems, MIL status, and the number of DTCs present. It also displays DTC information in a much more expanded and understandable format, while the Actron used a sort of shorthand to display the information as condensed as possible. If you're use to reading DTCs, this probably won't matter much, but for those who are less fluent, this would be a big improvement.The Innova is a bit more responsive and I find I can move through menus a bit faster then the Actron. I also LOVE the fact that the Innova would actually remember my vehicle, while the Actron would require me to enter the information each time... this is probably the biggest benefit the Innova has over the Actron, in my opinion.While testing the scanner, I disconnected various sensors and waited for the MIL to light up... upon doing so, I connected the scanner and it told me clearly what the problem was each time.I have three complains about the Innova though...First, the included 'software'. The unit comes with a USB cable which connects it to your computer. Upon connecting it, my virus protection came up with a generic malware warning and refused to allow it to run. I rarely have problems like this, so to be safe I installed it on another computer I no longer use. The scanner uploaded the software onto the computer, and installed itself, along with three other required programs. When finally finished, any attempt to use it simply sent me to a website asking me to sign up for an account. Anyone who's not comfortable with providing websites with personal information would be stuck here, as the sign up process included full name, address, phone number, email, VIN, etc. Getting through that, I was finally at their website, which showed me detailed information about when the scanner was hooked up to my vehicle. This would have been extremely useful had it been a program that actually ran on my computer, and not a link to a website... if I ever needed to scan a friend's car at their house, it would be nice to bring everything up on my laptop, but having to find a WiFi connection before doing so ruins what could be a great feature.As mentioned in the product's description, there are additional resources available at the website location, such as available recalls and technical service bulletins for my vehicle, as well as videos and detailed information on DTCs... access to this part of the website requires a premium membership at $20 per month or $60 a year. If you're like me and wants a scanner for the rare DTCs that pop up, you'll find the premium membership to be an unnecessary expense, and a bit of an annoyance as your constantly reminded of what your missing out on and why you should upgrade. It seems the growing trend these days with gadgets... buy the tool, connect it to your computer, but to make full use of it, you need a paid subscription.Second complaint, a minor one, the control buttons. My Actron's buttons were simple and you knew what they were for... up, down, left, right, back, 'enter', and 'help'. Navigating the Acton right out of the box was pretty straight forward. The Innova has three obvious buttons... up, down, and enter, but also has four other buttons... a red labeled 'brick' (turns out it's an eraser and will delete DTCs), a green labelled 'on' button with two arrows, 'DTC/FF', and 'LD/M'. I'm familiar with scan tools, but I was a bit lost when I first tried using it out of the box. Read the instructions first, and get acquainted.The final complaint would be another minor complaint, but worth noting: the construction. As nice as the unit is, the construction is one place where the unit doesn't compare to the Actron. The Actron I owned felt sturdy and could probably be dropped off an 8' ladder without damage. The Innova is made of a very hard plastic and would probably be cracked by a drop from the hood of your car. If your a professional that deals with a lot of tools being bounced around and dropped, I'm not sure how long this unit would last.Overall, despite its cheaper price tag, I'm a bit happier with the Innova rather then my Actron. The screen visibility and layout is much better and unit is more responsive and user-friendly when navigating, while providing the same features. I would only ask for a stand-alone program for viewing data on a computer, rather then having to sign up for and use a website account.

I've used OBDII code readers for a number of years now and find them indispensable for figuring out why your car's check engine light is on.The INNOVA Electronics Fix-Assist 3130c takes performs that task perfectly, as well as offering suggestions for car repair based on the codes it reads from your car engine. It is a complete mechanics tool, offering scan and report for everything your car computer can report, including a LIVE mode - an engine running monitor that graphs out performance of the engine while you put it through the paces.The unit requires 3 AA batteries and has a backlit, white display. It also comes with a USB cable so that you can connect it to your computer and get further information about repairs.You can record trouble codes from a cleared state, triggered on the DTC code getting set or a manual trigger which can really help if you are trying to figure out any engine code issues. The scan with ignition on and engine off gets any set error codes or conditions, but the real excitement is using the tool to examine the engine load parameters, or resetting those bad codes and watching the engine while they pop back up. The unit also has special tests for the O2 Sensor, EVAP leak, and power train systems that are not continuous monitor.This unit will allow you to understand a bit more about any issues they are having with a modern OBD2 equipped car before they visit their mechanic to discuss any repairs. You can also be certain you don't have emissions problems before you go to the inspection station. In fact, many states they use similar OBDII code readers to 'Pass' your car for emissions testing.The unit worked perfectly for me - correctly identifying both cars I connected it to.My biggest problem with this code reader is that to get the full functionality of this fine machine, you must pay almost $60/yr fee per car. That is not advertised on the packaging and I don't care for those kinds of hidden fees in a product that is already somewhat expensive. For a two car family, that's $120/yr and unless your cars are older and you will be doing your own repairs, it might be more cost effective to buy a regular scanner (without Fix-Assist) for around $30. However, if you often do your own repairs, this is an extremely valuable tool and definitely worth the money.I also think that for the price, a full printed users manual should have been included. Instead, it is available for download on the INNOVA website.This is a great automotive accessory you can get for any car (built in 1996 or newer) to help you understand your machine and survive modern auto repair with your wallet intact. It is an easy plug and play system, even for people with no automotive background, and I give it 4 stars.

This is an excellent scanner for personal use and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.  The unit comes in a nice, padded case, unlike myActron CP9580A Enhanced AutoScanner Plus with Code Connect, Trilingual, OBD II, CAN and Expanded ABS Coverage.  I do prefer the Actron over the Innova, but that is due to the software in the unit and my familiarity with the Actron.  The Innova is a solidly-built unit that works very well and looks like it should last for a long time.The unit immediately identified my vehicle and provided me with a readout of the particulars of the engine, transmission, etc.  No codes were found when I connected the unit, so I went through the menus and found that there are good number of tests and a ton of data at your fingertips with this unit.  I did O2 sensor tests, ABS tests, live data review, evap tests, etc.  The live data includes pretty much everything a user would ever need or want to know about the operating state of his/her vehicle.I really like the live graphing feature in this unit and I have been impressed with the other features as well.  I like the fact that the cable is not secured to unit permanently as with many scanners.  With my Actron, you will have to replace the unit if your cable is damaged, but the Innova will allow you to replace just the cord.  This may not seem like a big thing, but it would be a lot better to spend $20 for a new cable instead of $200 for a new scanner.The unit can be upgraded via the internet, so it should be fairly future proof for use with newer cars.I do feel that the menu is better on the Actron, but I am simply accustomed to that unit.  I can't fault the Innova at all, so my preference is not indicative of any fault with the Innova.

Microfibers are one of the nicest inventions of the last decade.  But they are not all alike, quality aside.  These are the ones you want for coarser applications, like washing cars and other big surfaces.  One of the most useful properties of microfibers of all sorts is that they do not depend on liquids (let alone surfactants) to be effective cleaning cloths.  This is the grade you want for dusting around the home.  Above the doors and windows.  Behind the TV.  The refrigerator top.  All those places that you would rather not go with some bucket of cleaner, even if it does not need a rinse after.  These do a great job dry, and better than spraying that "dust magnet" on a cloth.These are good for polishing glass either after washing (you get a bunch), or else out of the dishwasher for a final polish.  I am making my crystal radiant.  And my paintings love them, a light touch works well.  Those under glass, get their glass dusted in a second or even scrubbed if the glass is dirty.  These cloths are thin enough to be flexible around the house as well as good in the garage. The 10-pack price is fair for this quality.No, they are not really made to clean your eyeglasses dry or for your computer screen.  There are really fine grade microfibers for those applications.  But in a pinch these will work.  It is the micro that gets you down to the physical level where dry fibers can wick away oils on your lenses and such.  Think of it this way:  these are the modern equivalent of those lovely old French Terry cloths.  I hope they make a bath robe from this, perhaps in a better color.  Socks, now there's an idea...
summary: These are not fine grade microfiber but they are fine quality

reviewText: I've been using microfiber cloths for years, for everything from cleaning glasses to cleaning and drying cars.  This pack from Heininger contains relatively thick cloths that are well finished along the edges--there's no need to worry about fraying here.  They work well for dusting and cleaning.  If you're looking for microfiber cloths, these are a decent choice.

Living with three grown men and a dog in the swamp, my house gets dusty. I can clean and dust and the next day can write my name in the furniture. The Heininger microfiber towel calls itself a "garagemate" but works great in the house. Dust just jumped off the furniture and clung to the towels. The instructions call for it being washed with like colors, so I expect some fading, and you aren't supposed to use dryer sheets or fabric softener.These towels are excellent for picking up dust and dirt.
summary: Dust collector, in a good way

reviewText: I've been using microfiber towels for years. They are absolutely the best way to wash and wax your car. Before discovering the Heininger towels, I used the "standard" yellow ones. They do a good job and aren't very expensive. When I got the Heininger towels, I expected them to be very similar to the pile of microfiber wipes that I own. I couldn't be more wrong. These towels are actually different!I figured that microfiber is a commodity and that one brand is pretty much the same as another. This one isn't. The towels are noticeably thicker, softer, and more absorbent. One of these towels lasts as long as two of the others when I am drying the car. They wash clean on the permanent press washer cycle and dry on the "warm" setting on my electric dryer. At about $1.75 each, they are reasonably priced. Personally, I prefer the light colored towels that show any dirt picked up more easily. The dark ones tend to hide the dirt. A dirty towel can scratch your car's finish. Try these. They are absolutely great.NEW INFORMATION 5/16/2013Now that I have had these a while, some serious problems have emerged:1. These towels are not very absorbent. I have a couple of dozen of the basic "yellow" microfiber cloths. They soak up the water! I tried these and they didn't drink very much. I washed them and they still don't begin to compare with their competition. It took a while to learn this due to the very rainy weather here.2. They shrunk! The cloths started off being a nice size and very thick. After one wash they are now smaller than my old cloths.As a result of these issued, I have removed some stars.

These are good quality 12x16" microfiber towels that come in an assortment of colors (Black, Green, Red).  They are of good quality (80% polyester, 20% polyamide) and the stated dimensions are accurate.  These microfiber towels are a bit rougher in texture than some with a slightly different composition (e.g 80% poly, 20% nylon) which is actually a plus for heavy duty cleaning which is the intended use for these towels.  They are great for cleaning windows and windshields, your car, bathrooms, household furniture, dishes, tools and equipment, and so on.  Microfiber cloths are great for cleaning as they are lint-free, very durable, hold a lot of water, and yet wring dry very easily and air dry very quickly.  Very good for "touch up" cleaning of cars and boats.  Good for upholstery as well.  (These are different from the softer micro-fiber cloths used for cleaning camera lenses and eye-glasses.)These deliver everything promised.  If you have never tried micro-fiber cloths for cleaning, you will be in for a pleasant surprise, they're great.  These are as good as any I've seen, and better than many others as they came clean with no strong odors or stray fibers from the manufacturing process as some cheaper towels so.  Kudos for that!Note never use bleach or fabric softener on micro-fiber towels as it will ruin them.  They come clean easily, usually, so often you can just rinse by hand and twist out excess water and hang up to dry.  If needed, you can wash in cold water with soap.These are better than average micro-fiber towels and a good value.(Note: They're even cheaper if you use subscribe & save.)

reviewText: I'm incredibly particular about what I use when detailing my cars, and I'm happy to say that the Heininger towels made it onto my personal list of "approved" products.First, I like the size of these towels - at 12x16, they're somewhat larger than the other brands I use. I find myself usually folding these sorts of towels into small squares, and the extra size gives me more working time with a single towel...definitely a plus. They are also very soft and absorbent, but still seem able to hold up to hard use.About the only gripe is that they tend to shed a bit when brand new out of the box. I used one to clean my windshield, and I could see a series of fine threads afterwards left on my window. Wash a few times and this is gone - but other brands seem a bit better out of the box. Still, the size, thickness and softness make up for it, and at the price, these are definitely worth checking out.

Let me say that I love microfiber towels. I use them for everything. In housework, they are good for windows, drying dishes, and dusting. I keep them in our vehicles to dust the dash and use during washing and drying and of course, the windows. They are the best thing you can use for windows, no lint comes off on your windows like paper towels do. Dust and particles stick to the microfiber towels so you're not just spreading loose dust around.Something I've came across is that in the clothes dryer, everything sticks to microfiber towels so if you stick one in the dryer, lint and hair will stick to it instead of all your other clothes. I've started using one for that purpose in my dryer.Now for these particular towels: I was disappointed in them. It gives the dimensions so that part is my fault but I pictured them bigger. They are not anywhere as big as the ones that I was already using. They aren't as thick either. These are smaller and thinner.They are nicer, thicker and bigger than ones that I got at the dollar store though so I would rate these about mid-quality.I do like the dark colors, keeps them from looking yucky and discolored from dust, grease and grime.They are mostly polyester so the color doesn't bleed in the wash but it's best to wash them alone so lint from other items doesn't stick to them. Never use fabric softener on them, hurts their ability for stuff to stick to them, the amount of water they'll soak up and will start streaking your windows.

I would put these on-par with Z-wipes and notch or two above the bulk variety you can find at your local Costco.  They did shed significantly less than the Costco variety upon initial use and after using all of the above, I would say that they do pick up dust and cat-fur better than the Z-wipes, and significantly better than the Costco version.If I had to choose between these and the Zwipes, I'd go with the Zwipes variety pack as they have some purpose built microfibers that work exceptionally well on glass, drying, etc.  For general purpose cleanup and/or dusting around the house, these are superior.

These towels seem well-made and have been really useful the few times I've used them.  I expect to use them again with some Meguiar's products to buff up my Hyundai Equus.  Not usre if that is the best use of these towels but I'll edit this review if I find out anything useful in that regard.
summary: Handy product that I keep ready for action in my garage

reviewText: These towels do an amazing job when it comes to cleaning a car.I would recommend these towels.The more plush microfiber towels seem easier to clean with and absorb more dirt,water, and so forth.I also prefer the black towels.Good deal for the money.5-Pack Of Microfiber Towels-Two Black 16" by 16" All Purpose Micro fiber Cleaning Towels - Two - 16" by 16"White All Purpose Microfiber Cloths - One 16' By 18" Microfiber Glass Cleaning Towel

Wonderful towels.  They seem to be very well made, decent thickness and a great size.Endlessly useful for everything under the roof.  I've never understood why so many microfiber towels are primarily pastel colors.I'm glad to find some that are a decent, useful size and available in darker colors.

From cleaning stove tops, car glass, windows, wiping dust off just sanded woodwork, etc. I currently have two other brands in house, both purchased in 36 packs so I welcomed the chance to test this product head to head in all the usual daily uses mentioned. Physically these are the same size, same make-up (80%-20%) and subjectively nearly the same knapp or feel to hand as the other products. They performed exactly the same both wet and dry, rinsed the same and dried in the same amount of time. Other than color, I could detect no difference. So why only 2 stars? These are nearly 4 times the price of the other brands tested per cloth.Make no mistake, these are top quality microfiber clothes, fluffy and not thin, do everything well and rinse easily. But so do the other brands and they do it much much less expensively.

reviewText: I regularly use microfiber towels, generally for cleaning tasks anywhere (household, outdoor, garage, automotive, etc). That was better for car work (Polishing, Waxing), but the Heininger GarageMates did much better for polishing metal, cleaning glass, and interior work like plastics and leather.There's virtually no fuzz on these, which makes them great for things like glass and mirrors which I've had a heck of a time doing with anything but newspaper. Plus if you have a coffee accident, the towel is right there to bail you out.So good quality microfiber towels in a ten pack, at a low Amazon price- recommended.

reviewText: I've been detailing my own vehicles for the past 15 years and have become rather particular about what makes contact with the paint. Use the wrong type of towel and you can end up with swirl marks or worse, scratches on the paint. Things you may not notice until the wax starts to wear off.First it's important to note that these aren't meant to be used with soap and water or to dry off a soaking wet vehicle. They aren't large enough and really aren't the best material. For that, you'd want a good wash mitt and 100% cotton towel. But if you're looking to do some waxing, dusting, or touch-up with a detailing spray, these are perfect.I've already used them for my regular detailing on my black GMC Sierra Denali and they worked exactly as I expected them to. Yes, it's a fun color to keep clean! I dusted with my duster, applied the detailing spray, wiped it off with the microfiber towel, and then followed up with another unused towel to make sure I didn't miss anything.That second pass with a dry towel is important. That's how you make sure you don't end up with smear marks. Then dusted the interior, also using the microfiber towel, with the GM detailing spray which takes care of all of the leather and plastics. Finish up by wiping down the chrome wheels and I've got a shiny truck.So they passed the initial test and worked great. Only time will tell after multiple uses and washes if they hold up. I'll post a follow up review once I've gotten some more use out of them. For now, I consider them recommended.
summary: What more could you ask for?

reviewText: This little thing is great for cars with OBD II female connector under the steering wheel where the thigh goes under. It's low profile so it won't hit my leg, like other "taller" adapters or wired adapters.The bluetooth is an older protocol (hard code pin code) which is actually good for me. I have Android 2.2 double din radio/navigation installed in a BMW X5 (E53). Android 2.2's bluetooth does not support dynamic pin number that some bluetooth device requires (e.g., newer bluetooth keyboard).As for communication, connecting to bluetooth and establish OBD II connection both takes about 2-5 seconds simultaneously from Android app. It sends info to my app on both Android 2.2 and Android 4.2 devices just fine (using Torque).However, Torque is reporting some communication errors over bluetooth, but it's like 1% of times. That is acceptable to me, especially for an wireless mini adapter at this price range. It's almost a no-lose situation to take a risk.

There are some things that you may not like but which I cheerfully overlook. First of all it's not a custom fit. For a custom fit seat cover, look to paying up to $250. For the savings, I always went with generic covers from Costco. The Costco covers were pure fabric. There was no water resistance other than the thickness of the cover. If you spilled something, you just had to be fast enough to pull the cover away from the actual seat. With a good dollop of a spill you won't make it. But a little oops was not a big problem. This cover truly is water resistant. It has what appears to be a rubberized lining under the tough fabric material. Dickies does not advertise it as waterproof, so I assume that liquid will seep through very slowly. Even with a larger than normal spill, you should be able to recover before anything seeps through.It allows for side air bags. Both sides have zippers. You don't zipper the side that contains the side air bags. The Costco covers didn't have that feature, so I just hoped I didn't get hit from the side. I would get these just for that feature.I drive a 2009 Toyota Rav4. This cover doesn't fit perfectly. it's actually just a teeny bit larger than it need be. But that's better than the Costco cover, which was a teeny bit smaller than it should have been. Being smaller, the Costco cover would often come off when I got up. This cover does no such thing. It stays put. There is occasional drift because of one of the sides not being zipped, but it's minimal and a quick tug fixes it.Living in Hawaii, I often get in the car with damp clothing from the beach or "jungle" hikes. The fact that this covers the seat, doesn't come off easily, and is made of tough water-resistant material sells me on it.
This is a fantastic cover for those truck seats. Durable,  and functionally attractive, this seat cover will protect and stand up against the working person challenges.

This seat cover is slightly large for the Dodge Ram 1500 Crew Cab drivers seat, but it is well made & fits adequately enough that we find its usefulness far outweighs the fit.The cover is a black canvas with a polyester coated backing (I assume that is why 100% polyester is in the product description while Canvas is in the title).  There are side zippers to help fit the cover over the back & holes positioned for a arm rest & safety belts.  The backrest is made as shown in the picture - the cover is not designed for a moveable headrest, so you either have to raise your headrest & put the cover over the headrest or modify the seat cover & get more slack in your cover.This cover is on our construction truck.  We have always used universal covers on this truck rather than custom covers because the construction truck covers get a lot of wear & dirt & spills.  The previous cover was polyester & lasted about 1-1/2 years.  This cover is heavier & seems to be more durable.  Time will tell, but I am pleased with the materials & construction quality.

Dickies Heavy Duty Black Rear Bench Seat Cover was what I expected.  It is made of heavy polyester material that should wear very well.  It is made to be water resistant and can be removed to machine wash.  There are two reinforced seat belt slots with elastic banded top and bottom side holders.  Having used seat covers in the past, I was very much aware of how difficult they are to install and get to stay in place and this one is no exception.  After making some alteration, I was finally able to get this to look and function ok.  I had to slit the seat belt slots to make them fit the ones in my old truck but this was a simple alteration.  Then the one addition was to add a small bungie cord to keep the tension on the back of the seat and two other bungie cords to keep the tension on the bottom sides.  These were easy to do and now my old vinyl seat is warmer and should last longer.  The cover is priced right and looks good.  It should last for some time and if your in need of a seat cover it is well worth looking into.

This Dickies bench seat cover is made to be durable and water resistant, and is designed to cover bench seats that don't include seatbelts (which isn't mentioned in the online description at Amazon even though a large percentage of rear bench seats do have seatbelts). It's not hard to install over the seat. The surface is thick, like a canvas, not soft. When new it has an unpleasant chemical odor since it's 100% polyester. I would prefer a natural fabric like hemp that doesn't outgas a synthetic smell. This cover is good for protecting the seat but it doesn't have a smooth feel and can't be kept covering seats where people will sit and use seat belts. Thus, it has limitations that make it less versatile than I'd expected. It's OK for some people but I'd prefer something else.
summary: Heavy duty seat cover, not for seats with seatbelts

reviewText: This is a very nice light-weight but sturdy rear seat cover. It's advertised as 'universal' and if you are not fussy about the snugness of the fit then universal is accurate. It's held in place by straps on either side of the seat. While that makes it easy to install, it does not offer any protection to the outer sides.I tried the cover in my Dodge Caravan and it is a little too big and rumples up. It fits nicely on the larger seat in my husband's Chevy Avalanche, and that is where it will stay, protecting the seat from tools and other stray items he tosses in the back.The cover has two openings for seat belts but I would not rely on them to match up with the belts already built into the seat or to be able to use the shoulder belt. Our vehicles back seats are used mostly for stowing and hauling things around rather than passengers so that was not an issue for me. If one is often transporting passengers I would recommend a cover made specifically for the vehicle.
summary: Good protection from stowing and hauling cargo

reviewText: Just received this LED yesterday.  It is not quite as bright as 1141 and a slight bit more yellow. Not near as bright as 1156 and is quite yellow side by side. I paid $5.95 Monday and I wanted to buy a matching lamp for the fixture in our RV but today, Friday the price has gone up $4.00 to $9.95. In my opinion, it is not worth ten bucks. Disappointed. I would have given this item 4 stars (like it) but I can only give 3 stars (it's okay) because the vendor nearly doubled the price of the item which has greatly reduced the value of the item.

I bought 10 of a similar type that were a bit harsh.  I still liked those but some people complained about them.I decided to try two of these, and they light is warmer, not as bright, and installed these as reading lights in my RV.I will be buying a few more and installing them over my dinette so I can alter the mood by changing the color slightly.I still like the bright white ones for the outstanding brightest, but these definitely have a place.
summary: Nice Warm Color. I will buy more

reviewText: We purchased these to replace the cool white version of them we had purchased from BrightChoice earlier in the year. We weren't very fond of the cool white color once we had them in our RV, so when the warm white version became available on Amazon I jumped on them.These are just as high quality as the cool white ones, only with a warmer tone that more closely resembles that of incandescent bulbs. I moved all the cool white ones to the outside luggage compartment and inside our closets where we need the cooler lighting, and put these warm ones inside on all the rest of the fixtures.Our total 12v usage now is about 80% less than it was with incandescent bulbs, and these are a whole lot cooler operating and should last for many years. If you're looking for warm LED replacements for single pole (1141, 1156, etc.) incandescent bulbs, then these are the ones to buy. Great quality, energy efficient and warm white.

We RV a lot. The coach had pocket halogen spot lights. These were hot, both to touch or to sit under. I wondered about changing them out with LEDs, and gave these a try.I wanted the warm white LEDs. Why these cost double the price of the bright white LEDs is not clear. That is the only annoying thing about this transaction.The lights are bright. They put off more light than the 20 watt halogen they replaced.There is very little heat. The fixture base is warm to touch, not flaming halogen hot.The lights installed easily. If they are typical for LEDs they should last a long time.
Definitely a significant drop on the load to the 12 battery on my travel trailer and I can certainly see that it will help with keeping the heat down during the summer months.
summary: definately drops the load on my Battery for my Travel trailer

reviewText: Works great in my Forest River R-Pod Model: R-177.  I have one installed as my porch light.  I can keep it on all night without concern of draining my battery.

This is my very favorite LED bulb for use in our '71 Airstream trailer. I've now replaced all the inside bulbs with these, and am very much appreciating how much longer the house battery lasts, and how much less heat the bulbs generate. Things are also a lot brighter inside than with the original incandescant bulbs.Highly recommended!
summary: My favorite LED bulb for use in an Airstream trailer

reviewText: I bought several different LED 1141 replacement lights to test out for our recently acquired travel trailer.  After reading about how much less energy the LED's use than the incandescent 1141's I was convinced the switch would be worth it, despite the relatively high cost.  We do a lot of dry camping (no shore power) and I don't want to have to think too much about always turning lights on and off to conserve battery power.  Plus I think (hope!) that the LED bulbs will last a lot longer than the incandescents, two of which burned out in the first two weeks of owning the trailer.Anyways, first I tried these:  http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B002BN5ZT0/ref=oh_details_o01_s00_i00Despite saying "warm white" these are actually a very bright white, probably 1.5x as bright as the incandescent 1141's they replaced and a very clean white light.  If super-bright and clean light is what you want these will do it.  For me, though, they robbed some of the "cozy" feeling I like when having dinner or playing cards in the trailer at night, so I installed them in the main overhead light, which I usually only turn on when I'm looking for something.Next I tried these:  http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003TKI4VU/ref=oh_details_o02_s00_i00These were a warmer white but they were probably only 50% of the brightness of the incandescents they replaced.  They didn't give off enough light that we could comfortably play cards by these alone at the dinette, so I knew these weren't going to be good for my needs.  Because they're such low-light I'll probably just use them as replacements for the exterior lights on the trailer or something.These new lights (the ones this review is for) are pretty much perfect.  They're slightly brighter than the 1141's and not quite as "warm" but they're definitely close enough on both accounts that you'd only really notice the difference if you saw them side-by-side in a fixture or you're especially sensitive to lights in some way.  So if you're looking for a "good as it gets" replacement for your old 1141's in an RV benefit from my testing and get these, because they're more or less dead on.
summary: Excellent replacement for the 1141's in our travel trailer.

reviewText: I am finishing the process of increasing our RV boondocking battery time by changing over all of our light bulbs to LEDs. Hopefully this will result in a dramatic decrease in draw on the batteries and reduce amount of generator usage thus saving fuel.Almost all of our RV lighting is the very standard Gustafson Lighting pancake lights, some in a single and some in dual dome configurations. I needed a total of 23 bulbs to complete the changeover of these lights. Both my wife and I really like the "warm feel" and look of tungsten bulbs so we wanted warm white lighting that would be very close to what was existing, something that feels like home and not a hospital or garage. To achieve a bright LED with something close to 3000K seems to be rare to find and generally much more expensive than something in white or cool white color temperatures(3500K-6000K).Jump to the results: This light is fantastic! It is very bright without being harsh, it is a nice warm white color temperature and is a perfect replacement for tungsten bulbs. It fits the pancake lights without any problem so there is no worry about length or diameter. In order to achieve a combination of good lighting and energy savings we did a mix of these bulbs and the Brightech 66 LED bulbs ([...]) based on location. In our kitchen area we used the 66 LED lights for all fixtures. For the living room area, bedroom and bathrooms we installed mostly these 36 LED bulbs however on a few of the dual dome configurations we used the 36 LED on one side and 66 LED on the other so we have the option of more light if needed but we can just run the lower wattage bulbs for general usage.The difference in wattage / amp draw is very dramatic. To calculate your savings over a standard 1141 tungsten bulb here are some figures. A tungsten 1141 uses 18.4 watts and puts out 259 lumens. The 66 LED bulbs from Brightech use 5 watts with 300 lumens, the 36 LED bulbs from Brightech use 1.8 watts with 200 lumens. This means I can use 10 Brightech 36 LED bulbs or 4 66 LED bulbs for the same power draw as one tungsten.These are an excellent value that have a nice look and just as important will save me gas. I highly recommend.

Great lights, arrived quickly.  I am using these in my travel trailer.  They are bright and give off a nice warm light.  Nice product at a very reasonable price considering the free shipping if you purchase over $25 worth of products.  I had tried one and hoped to purchase more once I looked at it, but they were unavailable.  Hopefully they will last a long time.

I recently replaced all of the incandescent bulbs inside our camper with these LED's.  The light level is comparable to the old bulbs.  The light is a warm white, not quite as yellow as the old ones.  We use a lot less energy / battery life by creating light without all the heat.  The light fixtures now remain cool to the touch, even after extended use.
summary: Great Replacement for the Incandescent Bulbs in our Camper

reviewText: well i hooked it up in our cabin/rv hoping for a lot of light, and i was kinda disapointed.  id say it is equally bright as the 1156 bulb it replaced.  it drew .3 amps instead of 1.3.  so the draw decrease was nice, but it wasnt any brighter than an 1156.  slightly cooler temp color if youre into the florescent light look.

I just installed a number of these in my RV to replace 1156 incandescent bulbs in the overhead pancake light fixtures. They are working really well and provide just as much light as what they replaced. I feel a lot more comfortable using all the lights when dry camping now, as they use a fraction of the energy. I also tried LEDWholesalers 18 x 5050 SMD LED 3.6w Warm White bulbs, but found them to not be quite as bright.I definitely recommend the Warm White over the regular White (or Cool White, depending on the manufacturer.)
Not the best smelling freshener on the market.  I use a different product to help the car smell better but this did fit the bill and made the odor go away.

I really like this product but I do like the spray better. This, however, does its job keeping odors away. I keep one in each bathroom and although it is slower acting than the spray, it still does a great job.

I'm not sure if it just covers up smoke smell or eliminates it. I put this in my car that I smoke in, and it does seem to eliminate the odor, but not permanently.It kind of smells like fresh laundry or febreeze. It's a fresh, clean scent. I like it, and I would probably buy this product again.

My wife has the pickiest nose on the planet.  She likes it.  That is high praise.  She ates everything else that smells fake,  they last about 2-3 weeks.  Depends on airflow.  I use one in the car and one near the dog.

reviewText: I love this stuff, no matter what I have left in my van it kills the smell. I haul gas cans and other things in the summer and also it just has a funk to it sometimes. It's a 98 w/198k on it so it's my old work van that I use to haul and even though I don't smoke I'm sure one of the other occupants did but this makes it all go away.This is the same as the spray just a longer lasting and constant odor blocker. the material looks nice and the packing is good too. only matter that I haven't have time to install of it. once I install it I shall post the latest result of the HID light. let share the idea of this HID kit. Thanks

reviewText: BRIGHT! I like the color of these. Everything came in the box, and it was well packaged. The only problem was there was very vague instructions. You could figure it out on your own, but it would be nicer with instructions. It was a tight fit in my pontiac grand am. Great product overall!

Simple install and a great upgrade to any vehicle, this is my 3rd set and I will continue to buy as they have not let me down. I love the 8k color, not too much blue but not too white... Great product

Heads-up:  For a Ford F350 install, this requires the removal of your grill in order to get at the bolts to remove your headlight assemblies.  It took about an hour and a half. The translation to english is a joke.  Many instructions simply don't make sense.  The pictures are conflicting in their attempt to cover several different types of HID Xenon conversion bulbs for several different makes/model of cars.
