This is a great budget HID KIT.  Being an HID supplier, sometimes I get low and need to order more kits right away.  Being an amazon prime member I love the two day shipping.  These are 6,000K and true to the color, a diamond white.  These are NOT pure white but are a slight Xenon HID Look.  These are PERFECT if you want something bright and legal.Box is Nice, Comes with instructions and brackets, Quality of bulbs good. I have not had a bad ballast especially after buying 5+ Kits thus far!I would totally recommend these to anyone.  Also If you change the bulb size other then the 9006 6000k the HID kit will be priced more.
summary: Quailty Cheap HID Kit... NO problems. Great Price

reviewText: After reading many reviews, I had originally decided upon the Innova 3160B. That is until I saw that the Actron is exactly the same as the OTC brand which appears to also be related to Bosch brand, so I changed my mind at the last minute and bought the Actron CP9580A. After reading so many negative reviews, I will admit I was reluctant and worried I might be buying a problem.I took delivery on my Actron yesterday, spent that evening reading the manual and connecting to the internet to try and update my programing. I read where the OTC website is the place to update, so that is where I started. I want to say that my office PC is running Win7 Pro and it would not change the programing into Actron and load on my Scanner. So I tried my laptop, which is also running Win7 Pro (both are 64 bit) and although it would load on my laptop, it still would not recognize my scanner. So I did what only other choice I had, go to Actron's website and see if it would work for me. On my office PC the program (OTC Scanning Suit 4.0 or Actron Scanning Suite 4.0) would load, but not setup or be recognized. Once I downloaded the Actron version onto my laptop, it fired up immediately, setup and recognized my scanner immediately also. The updated software was downloaded in 8 minutes (I also have the fastest download capability my ISP offers at 50mbps). Once I attached the Data Link USB to the scanner and laptop, it recognized the scanner immediately and asked if I wanted to check for updates. I said "Yes" and within a the 8 minutes, it was updating my scanner. Once finished, I disconnected my scanner and turned it back on to see what program was now loaded and it read "SW ID: 6A4D) the newest and most current software is now loaded onto my scanner.I took the scanner out and tried it on my 2000 Mitsubishi, my 2008 Ford and my F250 Diesel. It appeared to work flawlessly. I am completely happy so far. After I've had it for a month or so and no problems arise, I will change my rating to 5-stars, or possibly down grade it is things start acting up in a negative manner. I do not know what or how the people that gave this scanner bad reviews did, but the setup and update process through Actron worked perfectly with no hassles or delays what so ever.I bought the scanner without the plastic hard case, only because I didn't see $40 bucks for a plastic case. However, I am very careful of my stuff, especially electronic gadgets. I don't drop, throw or misuse or abuse them. I keep them in a drawer with my other electronic automotive tools and if I won't need it for a while, I remove the batteries. To me, common sense prevails on the longevity of anything type of tool. I did download the .pdf manual and loaded it on my laptop and my office PC, so I can learn more about it either in the garage or in my office. I bought it for my Diesel, because my check engine light keeps coming on and I really don't want to pay the $800+ to have some clown replace the ICP (Injection Control Pressure) Sensor when I can do it myself for under a hundred dollars, including the part. So my scanner has already paid for itself.It may be a little early to offer a really good review, but after everything working out so smoothly so far, I wanted to share my first impressions. As of Day-2 of ownership, I am a happy camper! To Be Continued!

So far I used it on my own car, to see what the check engine light came on for and was able to clear it with no problems. I also used it three times on friends car . Very useful equipment for today's computer controlled cars . Easy to use just follow the instructions on the screen. Already paid for itself.

The price goes up and down and I waited until it was the lowest I've seen to buy. This device does it all and was showing me codes I have never seen from my truck. It's very detailed and easy to use for the most part. Amazon has the best price usually, but again, monitor the price for awhile and get it when the price is low.

I would've given it had it been made in the USA (took off x1 star for being made in China).The CP9850A works well on my '04 TL.  It can access ECUs for engine, tranny (mine is stick shift so it doesn't matter but for those w/automatic it would be of a great help), ABS & VSA.  Accessing SRS, Memory system, Instrument, Climate control & such requires Honda's HDS; a hefty $2,000 at Snap-on tool program.The display is automatically back-lit when you connect the unit to the vehicle, and you can adjust the brightness (contrast; "+" darkens the screen & "-" brightens, which seems backwards to me).  Domestic models seem to recognize with auto identification but I had to enter the TL manually.For DIYer, this scanner would suffice and is woth the money as a shop/dealer charges $100+ per visit just to reset codes, CEL, ABS, etc.... I bought CP9580AL for protection as it is a precision instrument.

An excellent all around scanner, capable of reading ABS and wheel speed sensors on some later model cars in addition to OBD II trouble codes, internet updatable, and loaded with features.  Great tool for the advanced DIY'er or a pro.
summary: Excellent balance of features and price

reviewText: Reads ABS, engine and 4 wheel drive codes for my 2001 Silverado. Glad to see that it can read 4 wheel drive codes as many scanners do not. Reads code and offers the most likely cause for the code in the order of the most likely first. Shows live data. Good to keep in your car. Does not run tests like the much more expensive units that the car dealers have.

I still haven't used the one I bought, but I've used the exact reader at Advance Auto, and it has never let me down.I read some people were having problems updating the software. I did not run into any problems, just follow the instructions on Actron's website.

I got this adapter so I can monitor my car's voltage while my very high powered sound system is playing. It is good to keep an eye on it to make sure your alternator and capacitor are keeping up with the music also good to make sure all of your electrical items are getting correct voltage and for trouble shooting. Very neet little things to have.
summary: Great for a heavy sound system

reviewText: It's definitely not super accurate, but I wanted to keep the interior of the car stock looking so this plugs into the outlet and gives me a general idea of where the electrical system is at. You will need another meter like I have connected directly to the battery bank also in order to have a true reading. It's easy to read and in a neat package. Also if you need the outlet back you can take it out.
summary: Will give a general idea but not super accurate

reviewText: Quick and easy to use to check voltage of your car/boat/truck or whatever. Just plug it in and watch the voltage and see what your alternator is actually putting out. Very easy to read and see.I use this in our boat and car and more to check charging systems off and on to make sure they are working well and hopefully prevent breakdowns. If voltage is high or low I can use this to see it and fix it  before I am stranded on the lake or at the store.

I am impressed by the build quality of this simple volt meter.  There is a fuse built in and the plastic is very solid.  The side spring connectors have good tension to keep this plugged in tight.  Despite the blue tint to the lens, the LEDs are RED colored.  You get readings with .1 decimal increments.  The readings in my car update about every second as the alternator voltage varies.  I measured this against a Fluke meter and it tracked almost exactly.  Will probably order more  for stocking stuffers.  These would be great to keep in the glove box just like a tire pressure gauge!
summary: Extremely well made.  RED led readout

reviewText: Received sooner than expected. Well packed and are better quality than others I have seen in the past. Will purchase again when I need more. Nice bright display.
This thing only works in one of three cigarette lighters in my RV.  The display does appear to be LED so don't leave it plugged in for long.  More cheap Chinese stuff.

they work very well, I got 2 of them they are made well and are almost accurate , only off by 0.2 volts. can not beat the price. I use them on my motorcycles to make sure my charge system is working good and to make sure I have good battery voltage. they work great I leave them plugged in all the time. I would buy more for sure

I have a Wrangler JK and have added many mods so I wanted a quick way to monitor the voltage of my battery.  This allowed me to do just that.  Functions as expected, easy to read and is accurate.  No complaints here.
summary: Cant beat it for the price

reviewerName: Alf "Let the cat out of the bag!"
reviewText: This made in China thingy is cheap and works great.  I am totally happy with it.  Let's see if it lasts!
This inflator has an easy to read gauge.  The hose clamps on to the valve stem of the tire securely.
I guess you can make it work for you but be gentle with it. The base is not very heavy duty and mine cracked, making it useless.
summary: okay but not a very solid construction

reviewText: I bought this inflator for my car because of the head that comes with it.  I have another inflator with a right-angle clip on attachment that leaks no matter how I try.  This inflator's head sealed properly so it's a keeper.  Only time will tell if the years will have any impact on it..  Right out of the box, this inflator worked properly.  There was nothing to tighten and that's a plus in my book.  The gauge gave reading that seemed very close to those of the other gauges I have including a Topeak D2 SmartGauge and an Amazon Basics.I only gave this inflator 4 stars because a key issue is reliability over the long term.  Since I've only had the gauge for a few days, I can't comment on that.
This gauge/filler is high quality and works like a professional one.  Flexible hose makes filling bikes, lawnmower, cars, etc tires easy!

This gauge is terrible.  It does not inflate well, the trigger pull is tiny, your hands will cramp up before something is inflated, even a soccer ball took minutes to inflate.  Trust me, view what other customers viewed after this item and try those. Pass on this, don't get suckered in by the low price.

There are some confusing reviews for this product that made me curious enough to buy it. To clear up the confusion: this tire inflator does not readily work with Presta valves and it does not ship with an adapter, so you will have to get your own adapter. I am primarily using it for my bike tires that are rated 110 to 140psi - my compressor produces about 110 psi, maybe a bit more. Even though this inflator is only rated up to 100psi, I with the 200psi gauge this allows me to check and correct the tire pressure quickly.I tried the inflator with a car tire and noticed that the mechanism that clips it to the valve is a bit unusual (and flimsy/cheap). Air will escape unless the hose is held totally straight and there is no lateral force to the connection. This is a bit difficult to achieve. This is no different when I use it with the Presta adapter. I am not sure I would order this product again.

I recently purchased several cell phone mounts that work in my car's cd player but was thinking that the visor idea was not bad so gave this a try.  It's probably the best option for anyone out there that actually uses their cd player or in a car that may not have one, but in general, the phone is set on the backend of the visor so makes it awkward to try to actually touch any of the buttons.  This shouldn't be a problem if you're using a blue tooth headset, but if you're one that likes to interact with it for GPS or anything else, it's an awkward reach.  The good news is that it fits just about any size phone be it small or large including Smartphones such as the Samsung Galazy, Iphone, ad Blackberry.  It would also accomodate old tiny phones such as the motorola razor.  The grip is firm and adjusting it is extremely easy.The final comparison is that if you have this plugged into the car charger, the cord is now hanging from your visor which is not ideal.  I would still recommend a dash mount or cd mount device over this one where it functions more like a built in and is much closer to you and the dc power outlet.
summary: Great idea, but I prefer the cd mount

reviewText: Is your dashboard too packed with other stuff? This is the solution for you... You can use your Sun visors to clamp this on. The clamp is very long so the attachment is very sturdy.One drawback is that you cannot use the visor while the mount is on it... obviously.

This visor mount is very well made and thought out.  It has a large clip that holds the body of it tightly, and there is a nice snug swivel on it that allows one to adjust it to any direction for viewing or storing as you drive.  Both the sides of it and the back has that nice non slip rubber that works very well in keeping the phone from slipping or falling out if upright.  The side panels, or claws can be squeezed in with a ratchet sound that holds even a small cell phone tightly, and you can release the grip by a push of the button on the side.  All in all its a pretty nifty little gadget if you own either some kind of smart phone with a touch screen, or a GPS unit.  You can answer a call with just a touch of the phone and talk via the speaker with it raised to face level and just across from you.  (Just make sure to mount it far enough away from your line of sight as the directions state).The only down side to this model is that it is not really designed for flip style cell phones.  Even the directions included suggest it is best used with touch screen phones and GPS devices.  It will adjust and snugly hold a flip phone efficiently enough, but since a flip phone has to be opened to answer a call it would require one to pull it all the way out while on the road.  Not convenient at all.  Trying to get it to hold a flip phone while open didn't work very well either.  It slipped and just isn't designed for it.  If you still own and are happy with your flip phone as I am, this thing really isn't much good for anything but acting as a holder between calls.In conclusion, this is a very well made gadget that can come in very handy for handling calls or for holding a GPS device while on the road.  Especially if you like talking on the speaker while driving that is of course the safest way.  However just keep in mind as noted that it is neither recommended nor works well with flip phones...  : )
summary: Well Made....But Not Recommended For Flip Phones

reviewText: I wasn't sure about this.  I have a BLU 5.3 inch phone...similar size to the Galaxy Note.  Surprisingly, the easy slide gripper on this grasped the huge phone securely.  The visor clip worked easily and fit well on my sun visor in my FJ Cruiser (SUV).  The rotator won't  allow me to move the phone into any position I wanted, but it did have a fairly good range of motion. So I was able to adjust the phone into a good position eventually.I would definitely recommend this product.  And if you have one of the larger cell phones, like a Galaxy 3 or the Note or other big smartphones, you can rest assured that this will work for you.

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I already have a suction mounted phone holder mounted to my  windshield, but the problem has always been where to mount that second phone! Not only that, I transcribe things via audio on my second phone and have in the past held it to get the right position for a clear audio transcription. Now I have the second phone mounted to my visor and it puts it in the perfect spot to record my voice and keep the phone in a good place so it doesn't get lost. my only complaint is that when I need to use the visor I have to remove the phone and try to remount it. It really works best with the visor up in my car. The swivel doesn't lend itself to good visibility when the visor is in use. Overall though I LOVE this mount and wouldn't want to be without it.
summary: Visor mount, perfect for someone who needs to mount a second phone.

reviewText: Why does it say +sticker first of all? There is no sticker that came with them. Second they are way too touch you tap them and they will flicker or not work. Dont think the circuit these lights are wired in is very stable.

I've got a GO Power Solar cell and I wanted to reduce the power requirements of my trailer.  I bought and installed a set of these on my exterior lights.  They  are easy to install and produce as much or more light than the bulbs that were replaced.  Just check the number on the bulb in your fitting and order an LED that will fit the light.

Replacing the standard light bulbs with the 68 SMD LED lights from EZ Motoring is working out great. I have done this  in 8 main locations  in our cougar trailer.  Over the bed area I went to a  36 SMD as I did not want the brightness that the 69 SMD puts out.

Very Bright and Very White. Not much Blue hue at all. I'm using them in the footwells of my Eclipse and they light up EVERYTHING! Light is dispersed evenly all the way around. I'll update as far as longevity goes. I've had them for almost 2 months now and they are still goign strong.
Not only was this cheaper than the national RV supply store but this product uses far less energy in our motorhome. They are a bit brighter than the old school bulbs too.
BRIGHT!! I can see so well at night! I definitely recommend these LEDS. They are constructed well. Very good output.
FINALLY a bright enough LED that is useful in our RV!  This appears to me to be equal to a small 40-60 watt incan bulb, VERY bright!

I purchased a couple of these bulbs for my 2014 Jayco Fifth wheel to replace the 921 "hot lights" in an attempt to save power during dry camping. So far the bulbs have performed well with no failures, they are about 80-85% of the brightness of the hot lights but draw a small fraction of the power. The two bulbs I purchased matched in color unlike some of the other LED's sold on amazon. They are fairly blue in color.

I installed these little guys in the dome light of my '97 Expedition and, although they are not significantly brighter, they make it easier to read a map as the light is seems to improve the contrast.

very bright, works fine, light is bright and fine. works very well, love it. thanks again for such a great bulb.

reviewText: I had no assortment of mini fuses, and when I was adding some fused taps for misc electrical mods I had to pick some up. These were by far cheaper then anything I could find at a local auto store or ebay. And so far I've had no issues with them. I've used 4 for adding tap-a-fuse and inline fuses, and replaced 2 in my car's interior fuse box. Haven't had an issue with any of these that I've put in so far. The only thing I wish these had was a case. I dropped the box these came in and they flew everywhere out of the bags. I would've gladly paid an extra buck or two to have a cheap plastic divider case come with this. I'll just have to keep my eye out at Harbor Freight for something that'll work.
Not much to expect.  I do wish i got the kit that had dividers.  This just comes in a cheap small box with the fuses in zip-lock bags.  Cant beat it for the price.

I replaced two fuses on my truck because of an upgrade with my highbeam lights (HID from halogen)...the spike from the start of my kit I bought was over 10 amps (13.2) so I replaced it with a 15amp fuse and it works so far....happy with my purchase

Not much to say other than they came on time and were a good deal for alot of mini fuses.Around here a small amount of fuses cost big bucks but getting them on-line is a better deal so that's what I did.

This is a great little kit to have on hand. Fuses are colored and labeled. Keep it in your toolbox because you will need them. I would recommend to anyone looking to have a little storage a automobile fuses.

My daughter needed a fuse for her Escape, so I went to the local NAPA store to pick one up. It was 50 cents. No big deal. So when I saw this on Amazon for 120 pcs for 8 bucks, that's only 6 cents each.  I figure we will have enough fuses to last a lifetime!!Would have given it 5 stars, but for the fact that the fuses are color coded and not marked with the size.

These small mini blade fuses are the size used in many late model autos such as the Hyundai line.  The assortment covers all the most used fuses and is way less money than the local auto parts store.  I purchased these when the local auto parts store charged me $4.00 for 5 fuses of one size.  I don't see any difference between the 5 for 4 fuses at the local parts store and this box of fuses.  This is a much better value.

These are great, nice quality, If you look at the fuses it shows the type of fuse engraved on the top.The filament gets bigger with the bigger fuse ( they are not all the same like the cheap ones)A+ box.A+ in general.Look at my submitted customer pictures for EXACTLY what you get.

It's an item you hope you'll never need, but feel good about having. After looking at the choices for mini-fuse assortments, this seemed to fit my needs the best. The cost is only around 7 cents per fuse. It comes in a small, rather sturdy cardboard box with closure tabs, barely larger than a cigarette pack. Keep it in your car, stow it in your glovebox, door pocket or anyplace it will stay dry. Fuses of the same rating are individually contained in tiny separate zip-lock bags. Originally I thought of buying a compartmented plastic box, but decided to keep them in the compact original package to minimize rattling. For as often as you might need a fuse, it's no trouble to find its little baggie. Most other assortments come in a blister pack that, once it's opened, becomes almost useless for storage.The fuse colors reasonably match the color guide on the box.  ON THE ONES I RECEIVED, ATOP EACH FUSE IS MOLDED THE AMP RATING, not marked with color ink or paint, but still visible. There is no fuse-removal tool in the kit, but most fuse panels contain a tool, possibly stored in the lid of the fuse box. If not, a long-nose pliers works well. Before ordering, be sure your fuse panel actually uses mini fuses. Both of our cars, a 2006 Lincoln Town Car and a 2006 Mercury Grand Marquis have only mini fuses in the panel located beneath the left side of the dashboard. I have not yet checked on the overall height of the fuse to be sure the fuse box lid will fit over it. One of the reviews mentions this possibility.The assortment contains the following quantity/amp rating of the seven different amp values:30/15 amp, 25/10 amp, 25/20 amp, 10/5 amp, 10/7.5 amp, 10/25 amp, 10/30 amp.I gave it 4 stars only because I haven't had to replace any fuses yet. Happy about that.

I picked up 2 of these to replace the PIAA fog lights I have installed in my aftermarket plate steel off-roading bumper.  I really needed a 3" light housing, but the mount tabs in my bumper allowed me to make some adjustments and get these 4" lights to fit perfectly behind the fog light holes.  I used my existing wiring because these lights have such a low current draw.  Factory lighting is sufficient to power these.I must say, these are actually too bright to use as everyday running fogs.  They have a very wide flood pattern which I tried to aim down but the spread is just too wide.  But, off road at night these things are AMAZING.  Street signs light up blindingly bright at over 100 yards away.  Shadows are filled in, and I can confidently go on tricky trails at night.  They light up wide to the sides, too, so I can see around corners much better than before on the trails.They put off a very white light.  Not blue, not yellow.  But WHITE.  The housing on these lights is some of the most solid I have ever seen in fog lights, too.  Strong stainless steel hardware/bolts/brackets seem to be built to last through lots of trail abuse.  They mount in tight and don't shake at all.If you need a running light on an off roader, these are amazing for the price.  I plan to put 2 more of the square ones on the bed rack of my truck to have as utility lights, too.  Easy to install, and they put off far more light than I was expecting.  And I'm a light-loving freak who is easily disappointed.  These made lots of my 4x4 friends very jealous.

Microfiber is made from strands/threads that can be 100th the diameter of a human hair. They have a positive charge that actually attracts dust and dirt particles. The fine threads are ultra absorbent and hold 7 times their own weight in fluids. Despite their amazing softness, the tiny, thin fibers shred dirt off surfaces so effectively that they often eliminate the need for any toxic cleaning chemicals.  Around the house they're great for cleaning glass without ammonia, granite countertops without chemicals, or messy sprays to clean wood surfaces.  I have been using these for several years in cleaning, waxing, polishing and detailing my car without the worry of micro scratches and swirls on the paint.  In fact, I don't allow any other type of cloth to touch my car. After washing the car using these, then drying the car using these, then applying wax with these and removing the excess residue, a clean one can be used last to polish the car to a brilliant shine.  Much more effective than terry cloth or conventional rags.  Besides their amazing abilities to do so many things well, it's comforting to know that microfiber is produced from left over waste products of refining petroleum that would normally have found their way into landfills. These sold by Amazon, come in 3 different coolers, so they can be reserved for designated tasks based on their color; the blue ones only to apply products on your car, reserving the whites to remove residue and also polish the surface, and the yellow ones, say for household cleaning applications.  I have bought several orders of this product from Amazon over time, who as usual seem to offer the most value and cannot recommend them highly enough. I'd give 6 stars if I could.
summary: Soft, absorbent, eco-friendly cloths are the ultimate in cleaning.

These are decent basic cloths made of a blend of 90% polyester and 10% polyamide.  While they feel fine for most every day cleaning tasks, when compared to a more premium quality cloth like the Quickie Dusting and Polishing cloth (which is 85% polyester and 15% nylon), the difference in both thickness and softness is pretty noticeable.  The Quickie is both thicker and softer. On the other hand, it also costs four time as much, so that bump in quality comes at a price.  I recommend a cloth like the premium Quickie for interior dusting and cleaning of delicate surfaces and video screens.  These Amazon cloths (as well as other cheaper quality cloths, including Quickie's own branded 24-pack) are better suited for glass, non-delicate surface dusting, car washing, and other cleaning chores.  They're roughly the size of a hand towel but very absorbent, so they can also be used for drying vehicles or other large surfaces. I purchased these to wash my car.  I had at some point purchased some super cheap micro fiber towels from I think Big Lots and they were fantastic.  They don't sell them anymore and so I got these to replenish my supply, and I just don't think the quality is as good.  But they do the job and I'm happy with them.

There are so many products that tell you to clean with a "lint-free cloth." These fit the bill, and you can't beat the value. They come in three colors: blue, white, and yellow. They're about 12" x 12" square.
I always seem to need a microfiber cloth these days for electronics and automobiles amongst other things. This was a great deal and they are good cloths. I would buy again if I needed them!

I found these right when I was in the middle of unpacking and setting up a kitchen - FANTASTIC for drying dishes and cleaning up spills. Also, even without cleaning products, these did a great job taking care of dust and grime in the kitchen. These are higher quality than some other similar priced microfiber cloths I found at a dollar store... and this kind of quantity is helpful. You'll never run out.
Come on, buy them. They are CHEAP and they are nice quality! Buy a 24 pack and use some in the garage, some in the kitchen, some for cleaning, some for ANYTHING. Really nice cloths.
highly recommend and well made. Stay soft even after multiple washes. Try washing with atsko sport wash it leaves no residue behind and rinses clean the first time.

The best reason for getting this value pack of 24 micro fiber cleaning cloths is that you have something handy that you can use but then throw away if needed. We all know those jobs that husbands are children do like detailing a car, or cleaning up some nasty mess and the mother tells you to just throw the hand towel away, it is too stained or nasty to put in the wash or reuse. These towels are durable enough to use daily when needed but to also use for that job that will result in the imminent death of the towel.

So many people have been talking up microfiber, I figured I would give it a try.  I love these microfiber clothes.  They seem to be good quality.  I am not an expert on microfiber clothes, so my opinion and experience is limited. I have also purchased some Meguiar's clothes as well.  The quality seems about the same. However, I can tell you I used these clothes all the time now and cannot believe its taken me this long.  Highly recommend.

You can never have too many cleaning cloths. Typically I use rags made from old sheets and t-shirts, but when I had the opportunity to try these microfiber cloths I jumped at it. Let me tell you, they are great. They pick up and hold much more dust and dirt than any rag, and they are gentle on all surfaces. So I big fat resounding 5 stars to this product!

they're basic microfiber clothes, with tags on them... which is bad.  They're a BIT too small, but it's what i paid for, and a lot of them.  I was aiming to dry my car off with these and they do get a lot of water up but only so much, kinda, a little.. actually.  They're good for other quick small drying needs.  they kinda feel cheaply made.

Very good for value. Be sure to follow the initial cleaning instructions! If you are using them for around the house or automotive purposes make you do not use detergents this will degrade the softness!

I'm a bit of a car fanatic and very careful about what products I use on my cars.  I took a box of these bug splatter sponges with me to a Ferrari club rally to put them to the test.  After a full day of rallying on the back roads of northern New Hampshire and Vermont, the front of my car was covered with bugs -- as was the fate of my fellow club members.  Upon our return to the hotel, most of us were out in the parking lot cleaning our cars.  Most were using detailing spray and paper towels to remove the bugs... at least until they saw me using the Meguiar's Bug Splatter Sponge.  It wasn't quite "one wipe and they're all gone", but pretty darn close.  I didn't have to work hard at all and 95% of the bugs were gone in just a minute or two.  I then went over the front of the car with detailing spray and buffed it to a just like new rosso corsa shine .  I ended up giving away the other sponges in the box to other club members... but only after they came begging.  This is a good product that really works and I'll be buying more.  You can achieve the same result without it, but not without a lot more work.  Me?  I'd rather be driving or sitting in the hotel bar talking about driving.

It isn't bug season around here so I used this on a car that had bird poop, mud spatter and sap on it as that is what similar products say that they can address.I've used Meguiar's auto products for years and have always found them to do a good job across their range, however, other brands are occasionally superior for individual specialties. (See: "Guru Reports" for rankings, if you can find it. It was a publication by a person who did comparisons in actual long term use, ten years ago.)This product is five little sponges sealed in foil pouches. One side is rough, the other smooth. This worked as well as "Purple Power Bug Wash and Wax" and "Turtle Wax Bug and Tar Remover" and the rough sponge did make it easier to attack the various dirt. However, none of them did a decent job of removing the sap and the rough sponge was not an advantage with the sap. I surmise that the sponge will be an advantage in removing dried on bugs.The Meguiar's needs to be washed off after application, the others only need to be polished after they've dried.
summary: As good as other similar products. Better...?

reviewText: How is this disposable sponge better than a regular one?  It isn't.  That's the problem.I suppose I could see leaving one of these in your glove box, just in case the OCD kicks in, and ya just GOTTA get that bird poop off NOW!!!  But it leaves a foamy residue that needs to be rinsed off.  And at that point, I may as well just use kleenex and a dab from my water bottle.It's small, very sudsy and does a mediocre job of washing off bird poop.  And if the bird poop happens to be large, then this tiny little thing ain't gonna be what I grab for; not unless I want poop on my fingers.  Eeeew!  I'll stick with a wad of paper towel, or a couple fast-food napkins; thanks much.It works ok, but certainly not well enough to justify an ongoing expense of 10 bucks a box.  Meh, don't bother. Just another overpriced gimmick.
summary: Nothing Special - It's an Acne Face Pad for Your Car

reviewText: These disposable pads work well at getting the bugs off, and they are simple to use. Just remove from the package and start cleaning. One negative is the fact that they dry out very quickly in the heat. To combat this issue, my husband rewet the pads which allowed them to be used longer. 1 pad worked for the front of a GMC Sierra that was covered in bugs. It took 2 pads to complete the entire truck. After using the pad, the truck then needed to be sprayed off to remove the cleaner. One thing to note is that this is a messy process as the cleaner in the pad gets all over your hands during the cleaning process. The good thing is that it did not irritate my husband's hands. His hands just needed to be washed after using the pad.

It's spring... and spring means I can't see out my windshield. Jumped at the chance to review these sponges by Meguiar's, because I've used some of their other car cleaning products and found them to be great, if pricey.First off - while the sponges are quite saturated, one wasn't enough to thoroughly clean the windshield on my mom's SUV.Secondly - I had to apply SO MUCH elbow grease to effectively get rid of the bugs, I felt I might have been better off with something like a Mr. Clean sponge. This "specialty two-sided sponge" wasn't much more than a microfiber disc with a little padding in the middle.Thirdly - what's in the sponges? I'd like to know. Didn't smell like much more than windex. In which case I could do this myself.

I am slowly getting away from Meg's products as there are much better alternatives out there.  I have some favorites I consistently use, but this will not be one of them.For the results I got from using a pad on a moderately bug splattered front bumper, it managed to accomplish the job but with much effort (I have found a lot of Meg's products require a LOT of effort).  It accomplished the job, but barely.  There are other alternatives.  Pass this one by, as there is no magic in removing bug splatter.  A bit overpriced, but you are paying for convenience of a single use sponge and cleaner pre-packed and ready to use.  Perhaps best used in situations where you are traveling. Not worth the money spent.
summary: Like most Meguiar's products, a lot of marketing hype and satisfactory results, nothing spectacular.

reviewText: The water in my neighborhood is really hard.  It leaves spots on my car that can't be removed by other car polishes.  It still takes a bit of elbow grease (effort) and some patience.  But this Meguiar's Water Spot Remover eventually restores the shine to my car - when other products and paste waxes fail.This stuff also works great for whitening, polishing and removing scratches from my yellowed headlight lenses.  (My car is ten years old.)  Nothing makes a car look older than yellowed and foggy headlight lenses.  This doesn't make them totally white again.  But they are definitely lighter and clearer than they've been in a while.  It makes my car look years younger.  (New headlight lenses are really expensive, I checked.)  This is a product I highly recommend.For removing lighter water spots, I use Meguiar's Ultimate Quik Wax spray instead.  Just spray and wipe.  Enjoy.Meguiar's Ultimate Quik Wax 15.2oz Liquid Spray Bottle.
summary: Works Better Than Anything Else.  Also Great for Cleaning, Polishing Yellowed Headlights

reviewText: I have baked on water spots on my vehicles, but I generally don't worry too much about that. However, this made it easy to remove them and increase the shine on my vehicles making them look brand new. For light recent water spots I would say this is overkill... just get a spray and wipe, but for baked on, this is the way to go to save you time and get great results.
summary: Very good for baked on water spots

reviewText: I wasn't able to get a gasoline stain off my corvette, but I was able to get some hard water stains off my SUV left from the winter rain/snow/pavement salt concoction.  Works well overall.

I was hoping for something that would easily and quickly remove water spots. While it will remove water spots that are very light, you can get the same or better results using a paste/liquid wax that has some built-in cleaning/polishing agents. The Meguiar's Water Spot Remover did not work on some water spots in one of our sinks and the water spots were fresh. I used a polishing/cleaner wax and was able to remove the water spots. I think Meguiar needs to spend more time at the company and less time out with his show. Lately I am finding that about 1/2 the Meguiar's products I buy are a waste of money and I can find a better product from a competitor. A few of Meguiar's products are really good, this is not one of them.

The Meguiar's car products have always been satisfactory for me, so I looked forward to trying their Water Spot Remover.  I tested it on a Legacy the same color as the product container and for fun on a white washing machine that somehow has plenty of water spots.Applying product by hand as I did is a little bit of work, like applying a rubbing compound. User is advised to not let the product dry, advise I followed to the letter.  After applying  the water spot remover, I removed it with several wipings with a microfiber towel.Most water spots came off with the first application. Some areas required a second rubbing with the water spot remover. The treated surfaces were shiny and smooth. Meguiar's suggests protecting the treated surfaces with their ultimate wax. I used another brand of wax with good results.Bottom line - It's a little extra work, but the results of using this water spot remover will be worth the effort for most users. Even our old washing machine now has a smooth, shiny finish.

We recently purchased a white Jaguar XJ8. It's a few years old, but still has a nice shine. We used this product on it the other day, and honestly, the car practically glows! It went on easily, and with two of us waxing the car in the garage, out of the sun, we had it done in about 45 minutes. A little elbow grease was involved, but that's all part of it. Our next project is our 2006 Jeep Commander, which is also white. I'm anxious to see how it works on that as well, because although it has a good shine, it is not in as good a shape as the Jaguar. Very pleased.

Meguiar's  has now got my attention. I have bought some other product from them. Out of five,  four of them worked for me. Love the color of this. Didn't think this wax would improve the look. I was looking for something that was white wax. Glad I got this one. I have a shiny white vehicle. Not a dull one. The price was great as well.
summary: I now have a great Looking Vehicle

reviewText: What else can I say. This product is really top of the line. Even though it is called White Wax, it does a wonderful job on my light grey Camry. Rubbed out several spots that, fortunately, were not dented from parking lot jerks. Great product and I always use Mugular's products.

I couldn't wait to try this wax on my white Nissan; the idea behind the wax is really great. Unfortunately, after using the wax, I really didn't notice anything different than if I used a good synthetic wax. Nice idea, but nothing special.

with the correct pads, you'll be able to remove mild oxidation and cleans. The product advertisement can be slightly misleading, I find the white wax is rich in polishing oil too, not as much as the black wax can carry but there. Longevity is not quite what i expected, didn't last long. Expect it to last around 4-6weeks depending on the weather too
summary: Great consumer line wax. cleans and protect.

reviewText: best wax I have ever used...I have a silver explorer....and after using this wax..it looked brand new ...looked like it was repainted.....wax went on and came off with ease..............

Meguiar's new White Wax is a terrific product and don't let the name fool you, it can be used on any color, not just white.Why is it called white wax?  Simple, it helps address a problem most visible on white and lighter colored vehicles.  On light vehicles, you can see contaminants on/in the paint more easily.  That spec of brown/black that doesn't want to come up, overall dullness, etc.  These issues are extremely visible on white and light colored cars.White wax helps address it because it is a cleaner wax with a heavy dose of cleaning properties, to help remove those contaminants that ruin the look of the paint.  Furthermore, it has enough cleaning ability that it could potentially remove very light scratches as well!What makes it even more powerful is that it includes a terrific applicator.  One side is very soft, like you would use to apply any wax, but the other side is soft with just a bit more texture, this gives the product even more "bite," to remove contaminants or light defects.  The applicator is great.  I have even used the applicator with a more aggressive product to remove scratches.Truly, I have used white wax on a silver and black vehicle.  Meguiar's also makes a new black wax.  The black wax can also be used on any color.  The black product is called Black Wax because on a black car the contaminants in paint are less visible, so it cuts back on the cleaning/cut, and instead adds more polishing oils.  On a black car, polishing oils always add depth to the paint that makes it oh so deep looking, and it can also hide minor imperfections.Overall, these new White Wax & Black Wax products are great and not for only the colors the name suggests.  If you want more cleaning in your All in One Wax, White Wax is a great choice and comes with that great aggressive on one side, applicator.  However, if you want more polishing oils in your all in one product to add depth to the paint and hide some minor imperfections, try black wax.  Some fanatics are applying white wax, followed by black wax.  I will say that the longevity of White Wax does not seem as long as some of Meguiar's sealant only products, such as NXT Wax.  However, at the same time, since White Wax does remove some contaminants, it helps prep a cleaner/smooth surface to apply the wax, which could help a heavily contaminated car stay protected slightly longer.White wax targets the main issue of lighter colored vehicles.  Nevertheless, it can be useful for any vehicle.  The longevity of the wax protection in the product could be longer, but waxing is so easy with this "liquid paste," that you won't mind waxing more often.  The only downsides: the toothpaste tube packaging gets wrinkled up, the liquid paste psychologically encourages you to use more product than you need, and therefore you will use this product quicker than you would a traditional liquid wax or paste wax.
summary: Nice Product, Awesome Applicator, Not Just for White!

reviewText: I would have believed a "white wax" was advertising hype and "BS".  Anyway I fell for it.Used the wax on both our cars, one a white 7 year old BMW,  the other a 14 year old British Racing Green old roadster.  Both cars are daily drivers, original paint, garage-kept. The wax absolutely made a visible difference.  It's easy on-easy off.  Doesn't require a large amount of wax.  In fact application of too much wax creates a removal problem so a light layer of wax works best.To achieve the results I washed, clayed, glazed and waxed the car. Didn't take long and I couldn't be more pleased with the end result.I'm sold and could not be more pleased.Your mileage may vary.

I have medium grade leather in my car, and it gets a lot of sun and heat during the day.  The leather is about 8 months old and is still in near mint condition.  Application of the conditioner took a hour for a 4 door sedan.  Time will tell if it helps extend the life, but it does feelt better to the touch.

As someone who loves leather upholstery in vehicles because of the comfort factor and has saddles,bridles and coats of this wonderful material, I have done a lot of leather care. Many products advertise as an all in one, time saving product. This can be fine for an item that got dunked in mud and must be immediately cleaned because time does not allow an intensive job but you must follow up with the good stuff to protect the leather. That is my experience. A horse falls or gets bogged when out working cattle in muddy conditions. You have to speed clean and take care of yourself and the horse but a day or so later you do the proper cleaning and conditioning of the saddle and chaps and boots. These are big investments and so you take care of them, and they take care of you, your life can depend on them. I have used many products that claim to be for leather upholstery and found most of them inadequate. The Meguiar's name is familiar to me as we have always had old cars from a Model To to a designer series Lincoln and Meguiar's is a sponsor of many classes in car shows. I was familiar with their metal and paint cleaner and polishes but a leather product was new to me. I recently purchased a used leather couch and love seat in excellent shape but wanted to clean and protect it  from spills and wear. I stored it for a while before I brought it home so I vacuumed and cleaned it with a leather cleaner and put a light coat of leather treatment on it to moisturize it. I keep a cover on it when I am not around to discourage dogs and cats from sleeping on it. I noticed that someone had dropped a piece of chocolate bar on it when I removed the cover so it was mooshed into the leather and i thought, "Well I will clean and seal it with the Meguiar's". I followed the steps and cleaned it and it dried quickly. The sealer conditioner takes longer to dry. A day to dry completely but it was dry to the touch in less than half an hour. You have the option of two finishes, you buff with a cloth for the matte finish and just let it dry for the gloss. I think that since I opted for the gloss, I have a slicker finish so coffee or CHOCOLATE will not get into the leather itself to stain. I was amazed that the cleaner did pull out some dirt. I always remember that leather is a skin and needs moisture but we also must protect it so I think that the Meguiar's has succeeded in that nothing stays on the surface to scratch the leather, it is very slick and I like that.

I just applied the leather treatment to my Equus ultimate - which has plenty of leather.  The instructions were clear and the application and sealing were very straightforward.  i reckon i have enough product left to do the car again on another day.

Great product to clean and condition leather, whether it's new leather or older leather.My husband has tried it on both.  Helps restore older leather and protect leather that's still in good condition to extend its life.  Quality product.

I used this Gold Class Leather Sealer Treatment on the leather seats in my truck and it worked great.  First, I tested a small area to see how it would turn out.  It looked really good, so I did the entire seats.  There are only two easy steps,  First, prep the leather and that means cleaning it with the Leather Prep.  I used the cloth that came in the kit to do the prepping. Second, I applied the Leather Sealer with the sponge that also was included. I then took a clean, soft cloth and buffed the seats a little,  The seats look great!  There wasn't any lingering odor either.  My truck seats look sharp!  I will continue to use the Gold Class Leather Sealer Treatment because I like my truck to look great!  When you have an investment in a vehicle you must keep the maintenance done and this treatment is the best maintenance for my truck's interior.

The leather seats on our car are getting a little old and stained, so it was time to clean them up a bit. This leather treatment seemed just the thing. It includes a cleaner and a sealant. The instructions say to use the product on an inconspicuous spot first to test for color fastness. Since our seats are a rather light gray color, I was a little concerned. But the spot I tested looked all right, and I did the whole car.The cleaner did help, but there were some stains that stayed on the leather. When I applied the sealant, the stains became even more noticeable. So while the cleaning and sealing did make most of the seats look a lot better, the stains still stand out, even more than before. That's unavoidable, I guess.The two bottles are small, and I used more than half of the product already. So I'll need to buy more to do the car again.
summary: Turned out better than I thought, but not as good as advertised

reviewText: Whether you are detailing your car yourself, or do detailing for a living, this is an above average quality product which provides good results.The application process is pretty straightforward.  As long as you follow the directions you can see the quality look, as well as smell the product offers.  If you are seeking a better option for your auto leather, or simply want to try a newer product, you will be pleased with the results.  I used in three of my cars, all Audi's and the leather looks outstanding.

Leather seats are so durable and look great even as they age, that it's easy to overlook their proper care. If leather isn't cleaned but even more importantly kept supple, it will dull, dry and eventually crack.  The traditional  solution to leather care, whether a jacket, a sofa or the seats in a car has been the two step routine of cleaning with saddle soap and conditioning with mink oil.  It's a labor intensive process but the results are immediate and substantial. A quality alternative product that's easier to use would be welcome. Many are offered on the market, but how does Meguars new offering measure up and compare? Their product comes with two bottles of material, a cleaner for the first step and a sealer for the second step. There is also a spray top pump included for the cleaner, a foam pad to be used to apply the sealer and one small microfiber towel. Application is straight forward. Unscrew the cleaner cap, remove the container seal, attach  the spray cap. Spray the cleaning liquid directly on the leather. Spread and massage in with the included cloth to remove dirt and liquid.  Allow it to dry and then apply the sealer with the foam pad. Before it can dry remove it with a clean cloth and buff.  My seats were long overdue to be cleaned and the areas you might expect to be most dirty did show dirt was removed as evidenced on the microfiber cloth. The sealer was applied as directed. The results were good, with the leather appearing more glossy and having that clean squeak when I sat on the seat.For the sake of comparison, I repeated the process on my passenger seat but used saddle soap and then mink oil. It's a trickier application since it requires wetting the saddle soap and working into  a light foam. The foam is applied to the leather with a damp cloth and worked in. It must be removed with a different damp clean microfiber cloth so no drying soap remains.  The advantage is that in ringing the rag you can see how much dirt was removed.  My impression is that the saddle soap removed more dirt and left the seat cleaner without whatever chemicals are in a cleaning spray  and possible fumes that might emanate while driving, small as they might be. Saddle soap is a mild,soap but it includes lanolin and glycerin which soften the leather unlike unknown chemicals in a bottle. Mink oil is exactly that; oil that's from minks and is very similar to human sebum, the oil that lubricates our skin.  Leather is, of course, animal hide or skin, unpleasant as that is to dwell on, so it seems much more logical to keep any leather conditioned with oils that would be there naturally. What was the comparative results? As a car enthusiast of many years, the latter process to me is far superior. Why? Saddle soap is gentle and used properly, softens the leather. Mink oil "feeds" leather by putting back oils that belong there. The leather in car seats is usually coated with sealers from the factory to make it more waterproof and durable in weather so oils may not penetrate easily. But it seems logical that especially perforated leather does allow acceptance of the oil. Due to its thick consistency, when it is applied it coats even the seams and the stitching, imparting greater protection and more complete conditioning and waterproofing qualities. Running my fingers over both seats allowed a tactile verification that the mink oil side felt much more lush, "plump" and leather- like. The Meguar's side looked glossy, but the leather felt unaffected, like the sealer just sat on  top of it, as I imagine it did. If you want a product that's easy to use and leaves a great look to your leather, I can recommend this Meguar's product with three and a half stars being a more exact score. If you want far superior results, in my humble personal experience at least, there is no substitute to the more effective, natural and even logical solution of using the time tested and proven method of a good saddle soap and mink oil which easily deserve 5 plus stars. Amazon sells 12 oz of Fiebling Saddle soap for $8.99. Meltonian Mink Oil Paste is  presently $6.74 on Amazon which includes shipping but for this one time it would be wiser to buy it at a local store for under $3.00. That amount will last many uses and can be used to wisely condition your leather jackets and even outdoor boots.  One other premium alternative product is Leather Honey Leather Conditioner, which is one of the best leather products available. So, yes, recommended. But there is a much better, logical, and cost effective  alternative.
summary: Meguirar's vs old school saddle soap and mink oil

reviewText: did two cars with this and still had some left over. easy to use and comes with a microfiber towel and applicator pad. very simple and easy to you and leaves the seats looking nice and new. I used it on light gray and dark black seats and very pleased.

reviewText: This package contains a sprayer head, which fits on the cleaner (step 1) bottle, a rather generous microfiber towel, an applicator sponge, and two small bottles of solution.First, screw on the sprayer onto the cleaner bottle. If you can't squeeze it, that is because it has a lock on it. Twist the base of it, just above the screw top, and you'll be good to go.The cleaner works well. It is (as far as I can tell) a watered-down soap solution, which isn't far away from the 10% woolite/water solution that Rolls Royce recommends for its leather.  So, not bad at all!The sealer goes on next, after the cleaner has completely dried. It is supposed to resist stains, and smells of chemicals. I'm guessing it has silicone in it.  Not bad or good, just what I think.The sealer is supposed to dry in an hour, and cure in 24, so leave plenty of time after treatment for full effect.Overall? My dealer sells something similar for $500. Of course, that also comes with a warranty, which is worth a hunk of that change. On the other hand, I bet anything this works just as well.So, I'm recommending this. Just keep in mind that it comes in fairly small bottles, so don't count on doing more than a car and a half (or two small cars) with it.Sean P. Logue, 2013

This headlight lens correction kit contains three dual-sided sandpaper pads, a very soft microfiber hand towel a bottle of PLASTX and a packet of headlight protectant.Before you start working on your headlights they suggest that you run a strip of masking tape along the edge of your lights so you don't accidently scratch your paint with the sandpaper. I skipped this step because I didn't have any masking tape on hand and decided just to be careful. I didn't scratch my paint job during the process so all was good. You will also need a small cup of water and something to mist or spray water with. A spray bottle would be perfect but I suppose you could also use and hose with a misting or light spray nozzle if need be. They include three different grit sandpapers in the package. You will need to put all three in a small cup of water and let them soak for a minute. Then take the course sandpaper labeled #1 and sand the front of each headlight lens in a up and down motion. There is no certain amount of time that you will need to sand. You will really need to judge for yourself depending on how much oxidation is built up on your headlights lens. You will need to keep spraying or misting while you are sanding because you need to keep it from drying while you are working on it. It also helps rinse away powder that comes off so you can judge how much more sanding to do. When you are happy with the results you do the same thing with the #2 sandpaper but switch to a side to side motion. Then you do the same with the #3 pad which is a super fine grit that gives a nice finish. When you are finished you should take some water and rinse off your headlights and dry them with a towel. They you will open the bottle of PLASTX which is a clear plastic cleaner and polish and apply a generous amount to the microfiber towel that is included and polish each headlight lens in a manner similar to waxing a car. Once complete you will take a clean towel and wipe of the remaining polish. They give you a decent size bottle of this cleaner / polish so you should have plenty to use again some other time. Next you will open the packet of headlight protectant and apply in the same way as the cleaner / polish. My truck is now about 10 years old and the headlights were very oxidized and foggy looking. I had took a before and after picture of them for comparison and I am very pleased with the results. They were badly in need of a cleaning before this process and now they look very decent. No they don't look brand new but I would say about 75% better than before. For the cost of this kit I am happy with the results. Purchasing a new set of headlights could easily cost be 20 times the cost of this kit so I feel like it is a very good investment and a smart way to improve the look of my truck.
summary: My headlights look about 75% better, good value, works well

reviewText: I have tried different ways of cleaning the dull plastic headlight covers from light sandpaper to rubbing compound and nothing has worked very well.  This is the first time trying a lens cleaning kit and I'm impressed.  Megular's Headlight Lens Correction Kit comes with three small light rubbing pads.  These are numbered with pads 3 and 4 on the same pad reverse side.  Starting with pad 1 wet and rub up and down.  Then side to side with pad 2 and continue the same process through pad 4.  Clean surface and use the micro cloth to apply the rubbing compound and then finish with the Megular protection compound.  All of this is included in the kit.  These are simple steps and do get results with a much clearer headlight cover.  The one caveat is that it does require some work.  You don't just put it on and wipe it off.  It requires some good old elbow grease but the results are good.  The real test will be to see how long this will last before reapplying.  Well worth getting to make those plastic headlight covers clearer again.Addendum: It has now been about a month with this on the one headlight and it still looks good.  It won't return the headlight to crystal clear new condition but it has kept it a whole lot less cloudy. (May-29-13)

Well this was a waste of time. I tried it twice and didn't get any better. And on the package it says " Guaranteed to remove your oxidation or your money back. How can I get my money back? I don't know if I should try another brand.
summary: Got worse than the other Headligght Lens

reviewText: I used Meguiar's G3700 Headlight Lens Correction kit according to the included instructions, and it did indeed improve the clarity of my 2003 Passat's headlights. It's not a cheap fix however, especially considering that one can use regular wax or even toothpaste to get the same effect. Meguiar's with it's various pads seemed to overcomplicated and extend the process. It took longer than that wax/toothpaste method too. After a treatment, the headlight covers were clearer, but not back to factory clear. All in all, I don't find this to be a necessary product where there are less expensive and quicker methods to mostly restore your headlights.~ Kort

I have always found Meguiar's products to be among the best so I was happy to test this new product.  I used this on a 1997 Accord that had oxidized headlights. Results were good but the kit should include one more sandpaper sheet.  The kit includes a protectant to apply to the newly cleaned headlights.  I used a 3m kit in the past (on a different car) which did not include a protectant and the headlights discolored again in about 6 months.  Time will tell if Meguiar's protectant keeps the headlights from oxidizing again.  Overall, this kit is fairly easy to use but I preferred using a drill with a cleaning solution (as the 3m kit had) to using sandpaper and sanding by hand. That's just my personal preference but some will prefer the convenience of this kit.
summary: Works well but takes some elbow grease

reviewText: I used the Meguiar's Headlight Lens Correction kit on my 1993 mini-van. The headlights were very foggy and the lights appeared dim. The kit did not restore it to 'new' but there is a significant improvement, about 75% better. On a 20 year-old vehicle, I am pleased with this result.The cleaning process took about 45 minutes. It doesn't require any special tools, everything is included in the box. There are four types of sanding pads, a polisher and a protectant, just need to add a little water to wet the pads. Be prepared to use some muscle while scrubbing.The only improvement I can recommend is that the kit should come with extra sandpaper or larger pieces so that it can be used on more than one car. There is ample polish left over and a very nice reusable cleaning cloth included with the kit.Overall, compared to the cost of a new headlight, this is a good deal.
summary: Improves the clarity of car headlights

reviewText: I personally prefer using this type of product with a drill attachment, as I think it does a better job of removing the final swirls, but I have to admit I thought this one works well without.It is typical of these products: start with relatively rough sandpaper (on a pad), and work up until you are done with the fine. Don't worry, it really works and won't hurt the plastic. Just make sure you keep the pads clean when you use them so you don't grind dirt or sand into your lens. After the final sanding, use the polish to polish out the sanding marks. The polish in this kit did a nice job in this regard and was hardly any more work than the drill attachment versions.This kit also includes a preservative final coating, which not all such products include. I would have preferred that it came in a resealable bottle rather than a open-once pack, but at least it comes with it ... this SHOULD make the lens look better longer.Will it make the lens look brand new? No. if your lens is too far gone (those just beginning to show sun damage might do better). But it will make it look good, and for my truck that is now 14 years old, it is just fine.

The lens on my headlights were definitely in need of some cleaning/polishing, so I opted to try this product. I found the directions a little confusing. They identify four pads that you use to basically sand down the lens. But the box contained three pads, two of which are the exact same number. So right from jump street I was lost. Anyway, I did the best I could to follow the directions as close as possible with what was available. After sanding back and forth, up and down, I dried the lenses and applied the PlastX special sauce. I buffed the lenses as best I could with the included polishing cloth. After completing these tedious tasks, I applied the "bonus" polish that is included in a squeeze packet.After all of this, I stood back and convinced myself that my headlights looked newer. But in all honesty, I don't really think they looked much better, and they certainly didn't reflect all of the effort I applied to do this.While this product is not very expensive, I recommend that you look for other alternatives that claim the same thing, but that take much less effort and elbow grease.
summary: Confusing directions; some effort required; missing pieces

reviewText: I used this on my mother's car who's head light lenses were completely cloudy. After using this, they look a lot clearer!This product was easy to use and the results were quite good. There is still a lot of the product left over however the sandpaper pieces that came with it are used so I wish they included more of those.

I like the thicker consistency and it keeps my car shinier than other brands.  Almost all car waxes are carnuba wax based, and this is no expeption.  However, the extra ingredients really help it outperform on my black car surface.
summary: Really better than the normal stuff

reviewText: First time using wax in a tube--different to work with.  Not difficult, but different.  Covers minor scratches very well. Hard to buff off, so do small sections at a time. I didn't use a buffer with this first application but will probably do so next time. Doesn't clean up water spots, which most waxes have been able to do for me in the past. Not sure how many washings it will endure before needing to re-wax.I have used the pricier Zymol for black cars.  Zymol works much better.  If price is a big factor, then Meguiar's is a good choice.  I balked at first when seeing the price tag for Zymol but you truly do get what you pay for in this particular instance.So, overall, this wax did a good job.  I will update my review once I see how many washings I can get out of waxing.

Ehhhh, what can I say, it's black paste.  There isn't a "wow" factor here and the instructions kind of scare me about getting it on anything but black paint.  So far not impressed.  It comes in a paste tube which cracks easy and allowed oil from the wax to leak out.  Appication is easy as usual and it gives a good decent darker shine.  Not what I would call a "wet shine".  I think the idea here is that this will cover scratches or swirls on black paint; not what happens in reality.  Not feeling this one folks.

I've used and liked a variety of Meguiar's products over the years and have rarely been disappointed. This wax is turning into one of my all-time favorites.It applies very easily provided the car is in the shade (black cars plus sunlight = a surface that's way too hot for any wax). I'm especially pleased with the packaging - it comes in a tube much the same as toothpaste. The wax itself is gray colored and thick, and the tube makes it very easy to dispense without any mess or wastage. Very well done!It can be applied with a buffer, but I just applied it by hand using the included applicator (a round piece of foam). Very easy to apply.It buffs off easily after letting ir dry to a haze. I used a couple of microfiber cloths, turning them frequently and starting a new cloth when the old one got loaded with wax. I then did a final buff with a fresh micro fiber cloth. (While Mcguiar also makes the cloths, I get mine from Sam's Club - very inexpensive, and decent quality).The shine was tremendous - this is why I got a black car! It looked so good I didn't want to take it out of the garage to keep it clean.I can't speak to the longevity of the shine or the protection as of yet, but other Meguiar waxes have provided me with a very long-lasting shine. I'll update the review should this not prove to be durable.If you have a black car, get this. The shine will not disappoint, and you don't have to work very hard to get the job done. Highly recommend!
summary: Brilliant shine; easy to apply; great packaging

reviewText: Way happy with this stuff. Really easy to apply with a DA and leaves a wonderful mirror like coat. I'd imagine the chemical guys setup for black cars is better but this stuff is like 1/4 the price and 1/2 the effort being that it is only a wax not a glaze and wax. Works better than turtle wax or any synthetic I've used.

I was hoping that this wax would have enough pigment in it to cover up some tiny scratches in my shiny black Equus, seeing as how it is intended for shiny black cars.  Well, that won't work as the product is just gray and the white of the scratches just shines right through.  Now, back to its intended purpose of waxing shiny black cars.It does a good job, is easy to apply and the instructions are clear.
summary: Solid product but not much pigment

reviewText: The Best for Black PERIOD. I have some swirls, I am going to order the swirl remover and see how it works also...A must for all Black Car Owners!

I'm a long time user of Meguiar's products since about 2008 when I got my black full size extended cab pickup. I've taken care of my vehicle with their stuff ever since getting the truck but it is my daily driver so there are long stretches of neglect because I don't have time to work on it or the weather is uncooperative. Anyway, I already am a fan of most of their products because my truck still looks fantastic when I do a full detail on it.The Black Wax does a beautiful job. It goes on easily and smoothly, dries quickly and comes off easily. Since this wax has mild cleaning ability I used it after washing and drying the truck. I think the results look better than Ultimate Liquid Wax but really the ULW does such an awesome job it is hard to say without the lights some guys use to show off their work in pics. I like the fact that this wax has a lot of polish in it to make black (or dark) paint really pop. It actually looks gray but there are no dyes or colorants in it unlike (apparently) all other colored waxes on the market.The container is a little surprising to me. I guess they want to highlight the fact that this is different from their other waxes and sealants but I don't really care much for the metal toothpaste tube they are using. Maybe the composition of the wax needs the extra protection of a non-plastic container? Whatever. I can see this being my primary wax withMeguiar's Ultimate Quick Detailer,Meguiar's Ultimate Quik WaxandMeguiar's Ultimate Wash and Wax Anywhere Spray- three other Meguiar's products that are outstanding - for in between full details.If you need some high quality MF towels I love these -3 Pack Cobra Miracle Towels, 16 x 24 inches. I bought the same MF towels in a 6 pack (that Amazon or the mfg doesn't seem to carry anymore) in August of 2008. They are still going strong with no fraying. Heck they still look practically new. I'm careful with them and only use them for applying and removing UQD, UQW and wax/sealant.Do you own a Ford? Are you incensed every time you have to clean your wheels because of the awful brake dust that crappy Ford brake pads produce? GetTurtle Wax Ice 3-in-1 All Wheel & Tire Cleaner. Turtle really made an outstanding wheel cleaner. It is the easiest one I've personally used with the least amount of effort and best results. It leaves a protective film that looks good. Give it a try I think you'll like it too. I also like theTurtle Wax T484B ICE Total Interior Care Sprayfor the inside of the truck. The smell isn't wonderful but after a few hours it imparts a freshness to the cab. And it shines up the plastic on the radio and instrument panel.

I am not a specialist by far about polish. I usually get my car cleaned by professionals because I do not have the time to do it myself.This time, my car was fairly dirty after the recent pollen outbreak and I got the chance to review the Meguiar G6207 Black Wax.It came in the box like in the picture with a tube of polish and a foam applicator. A very few basic instructions. I would have liked to be told how long to wait before passing the cloth after the polish dries up but I did not see anything related.It took me a total of three and a half hours to do my car completely, including windows, interior wash and vacuum. Out of that time, I would say it must have taken me about one hour and forty five minutes to wax the car and then finish it up. I did it alone and my car is large. I will try to post some pictures but I don't see any link at the time of the review.The final result is very satisfactory. Cleaned and dried, the car looked good I must say but up close, many imperfections were visible, many related to residues of incrustrated tree sap I am afraid.After waxing the car, the defects may still be there but they are hidden by a strong glossy finish that makes the black car paint like a mirror. It is a very pleasant finish. It is worth noticing that the tube was not completely used up in the operation so it should be enough for a large SUV.I still have to add that while I was passing the few remaining passes with the cloth for a perfect shine, I felt the hair on my forearm react to static electricity. As well, the car got covered with what may look like dandruff coming out of the dried wax itself and maybe bits of the microfiber cloth I was using. They all flew away as I drove to refill my tank.I will not have to wash my car and wax it soon again hopefully but I am happy that I did not waste my time.I would defintiely recommend Meguiar's G6207 Black Wax.
summary: A very glossy finish in less than two hours

reviewText: I have a black Lexus and the shine is great. I only use Meguiar product on my cars and never have been disappointed  Another great Meguiar product.

I am reading some reviews that claim that its not that great since it did not remove the scratches.  Well I detail cars for a living and products like this "enhance" not fix.  If you want to fix your scratches you would need to spend a lot more and pick the right compounds and polishes, not to mention you would need a good DA polisher and pads.  Meguiars have the M105 and M205 to fix scratches.  Megs black brings out the true luster of dark cars after paint has been corrected giving it that wet car show shine.
works great and easy to use. removed lots of swirl and haze from our black TSK...leaves no residue, easy on and easy off...very pleased with this product..

I've been using paste wax for the past 30+ years and I appreciate how it provides a beautiful finish.  This is the first time I've used a "black wax" and it does do a nice job.I used Meguiar's Black Wax on my 1996 black Honda Civic.  The hood is quite scratched up by now so I thought this might be a good test to see what effect it had on a scratched up surface.  I wish I could attach the photos I took.  I put Meguiar's on the right (driver's side) and Turtle Wax on the left (passenger side).  Both look great, but I'd give the Meguiar's black wax just a shade more credit for a slightly nicer, darker mirror finish.I really like the tube, it is easier than dipping the applicator into a tin.  I also really like that it doesn't leave behind "white dust".This is a very nice product!(I will try to upload some photos to the main product page.)

I have an 09 Range Rover and wash it every week....wax 1x's a month.  Changed to t his wax and it was a very very noticeable difference.  I am very happy... looks showroom new now...very shiny and deep black.
summary: Great to make your black car look brand new

reviewText: I have been waxing cars for the better part of 35 years. Maybe it was just the car I used this on, but I was not impressed at all with this.The tech wax and number 7 glaze for sure worked better on my Mini. I found this hard to remove and it had a lot of smudges to it. I tried it by hand and also with a machine, still had poor results and will re do the car today. I am going to give it a try on another dark car  I have and see if it is any better, but for now this does not work for me, and I use almost all of Meguars products with no issues.
Meguar's black wax is actually grey.  It leaves a grey/white residue.  It is easy to apply, seems to leave a good shine.  Prefer Turtle Wax Black wax for my black truck.

I was using Turtle Wax "black box", which is also great... but this single application product from meguiar's is really fantastic.  As with all liquid(ish) wax, let it dry... let it dry a long time.... and you're going to get great results.
summary: Good stuff for a black car

reviewText: While the title says 'black wax' it can also be use on lighter colored cars. Of course, you need the paint surface to be prepped and cleaned otherwise your effort of waxing will be in vein. it has slight/small cleaning property, using the correct pad and speed, it will remove light swirls. gloss?probably on par or slightly lower than the meg's mirror glaze #7, but the advantage of this is it has sealant property. If you have a new car and it is dark colored, you won't be dissappointed! Longevity?last about 4-6 weeks roughly~

This wax is more like gray and you still can't get it on any vinyl parts, because it will still turn white.  I am guessing the wax is of similar wax to Meguire's regular wax with regard to durability.

I purchased this and used it once, it worked so good I bought another tube the same day.  Works great with DA polisher, I bought the Harbor Freight DA with a finishing pad and left a deep black glossy shine.  So much easier than hand buffing. A little goes a long way.

I am very happy that this product produced the results it promises.  The swirl marks on my black Kia Sorrento are completely gone and the car looks showroom new.
