I have recommended this to all my friends with black cars. I used the included foam applicator and some cheap microfiber towels from Wal-mart for polishing. I can't imagine better results are possible any other way. It took some elbow grease to get the job done, but the results are well worth it. I am anxious to see how long it lasts.  So far, we've driven through a couple horrendous downpours and the dried dust and dirt wipes off easily. I'm lucky to have a garage, so I'm hoping I'll get through the summer and fall with a pretty great shine.This is the product to use on your black car.

1995 Eldorado with original deep candy apple red paint, essentially always garaged and the paint looks great although it has picked up some light micro-scratches after years of hand washing.  I had to choose between Meguiar's offering of a white wax for light colored cars, or this black wax . . . I went with the black.The product comes in the old-fashioned metal (not plastic tube).  Has about the consistency of toothpaste and goes on and buffs off easily enough.  And with this "black wax", I was not making endless circuits around the car cleaning up those wax residue white spots that seem to mysteriously emerge for hours in cracks and crevices.  This stuff is more work (obviously) than a spray wax but not difficult to buff off like some of those old paste waxes.  Results?? . . .Looks super.  Nice deep shine, slick as oiled glass, and even on this red (not black) car, the micro paint scratches and swirls seem to have disappeared.  Has only been on about 10 days, with the car garaged.  One 100 mile drive in the rain and a machine touchless car wash and, as one would expect, rinse water was beading and running off superbly.Nice product.  If it deteriorates quickly, I'll come back and edit my review to reflect that.
summary: Nice results on candy apple red

reviewText: This is nice metal polish.  It's your typical high polish product. Take a cotton rag and you can use to polish all kinds of things around the house to brand new state.  Works on watches nicely.

I have a sports car that tends to put out lots of soot in the exhaust...after a few days driving, my highly polished stainless steel exhaust tips start to look downright black. Simple washing removes the soot, but leaves a stain that's proven very difficult to completely remove.Enter Meguiar's Fine Cut Metal Polish. A small dab polished into the exhaust tips completely polishes away the residue. It just takes a moment, and leaves my exhaust tips looking like new. The product is now a staple in my detailing kit, and I'm glad I found it.Definitely recommended!

Keep this in your garage for those chrome touch ups or a must have around the fire station. Whether getting ready for show or parade this product will take a dull water marked metal and turn it to shine! Like most quality products it will take a little elbow to do the work but it is not complicated or messy. It will not run or drip. This product is something anyone who takes pride in how their vehicle looks will want to have!
summary: Great for the antique car buff!

reviewText: This polish has a car wax like consistency and an initially cream-like color. I tried it on both brass and aluminum and was very pleased with the results. This is quite fine and will not remove surface scratches from metal; it is more for the final buffing to give your metal a high-quality shine. Works precisely as described.
summary: Polish goes on like car wax

reviewText: I have used many different types of metal polishes over the years. This one is good. It does a great job polishing with less effort than some traditional polishes, although I must say I did have slightly better results with less effort using the Griot's polish. Still, this is a good brand with a decent reputation and this polish is certainly better than other ones I've used. If you haven't used a polish like this on old metal such as silverware, copper, and especially aluminum, you will be impressed by how much better your old stuff looks after a few minutes spent polishing it with this stuff.
This is an effective metal polish.  It seems to be pretty versatile, working well on jewelry and even chrome on your car.  No complaints.

After much use of my Ontario MacheteOntario 6145 Military Machete (Black)out in the wild safari (okay, my neighbors unkempt backyard) it needed a good cleaning and polishing after the hunt (weed hunting).I first usedGriot's Garage 11238 Metal Polish - 2.5 oz.which is a rougher paste, but cuts through any grime unseen by the naked eye. The final step was Meguiar's Fine Cut Polish ... worked very well, and when buffed clean I was a happy adventurer.Meguiar's Fine Cut Polish gives a high lustre to automotive metals and also edged weapons and tools.

My motorcycle has a lot of metal on it, aluminum, steel & chrome.  This cleaner works on all of it and does it well.  It removes oxidation, reduces small swirls and brightens all it touches.  I like it better than Noxon as it seems to clean & add a bit of renewed luster & shine at the same time.Good buy.

I have always enjoyed using Meguiar's products. This is no exception. The first job I had for this was my barbeque grill that had been sitting out all winter. By the time I was finished it was shining like a new unit. The wife actually though I had purchased a new one. Before she got too upset with me I showed her the polish can.

There is not too much one can say about a metal polish; it either works or it doesn't. I used this one on a non-automotive part (a brass doorknob and lock plate. It worked fine, but it took a little more effort than I thought it would. So it appears this is a very fine product that won't damage the metal ... just be warned that being fine it will also take more effort to do the job.

The only thing I've used this on is to polish the spinner on my airplane. It was dull and in need of some shining up. I used a big buffer and it did the trick. It made a big difference. I'd buy it again the next time I need to shine the spinner.

Firstly - the product I received was packaged exactly as shown, except . . . instead of "Fine-Cut", the little box on the label contained the word "Finishing". I'm guessing it's the same product and that Meguiar's has modified the name to something that sounds more friendly.I've been using this Meguiar's Finishing Metal Polish predominantly on motorcycle aluminum applications - also a little chrome or stainless steel where I want to touch up problem areas.  I've just been using it as a maintenance polish and applying by hand.  It takes a little elbow grease (but not as much as many other polishes out there).  Nothing tricky here.  Applies like most of the rest - dab on, rub in vigorously, wipe off.Results? . . . an absolutely dazzling mirror finish.

Meguiar's Fine Cut Metal Polish works well, but does require a bit of effort if you opt not to use an electric polisher.  Product is a paste, off-white in color and feels like sand and water, not cream.  It took about 5 applications and no more than 5 minutes to get a nice shine.  I used it on my car's trunk chrome insert, it always seems to get dull over time.
summary: Works well but requires a bit of elbow grease

reviewText: Works wonders in my foam cannon on in my buckets alike. Creates very good lubrication, in essence, does exactly what it is meant to. Also smells WONDERFUL!

not as foamy as they say, tho i do have electric washer i did test it out against chemical guys mr pink. honey dew felt more foamy but mr pink sprayed out more foamy. and mr pink is cheaper :)here is a link to my testyoutube.com/watch?v=ECo3cWRCOZQ
summary: not as foamy as they say

reviewText: I use this product in a foam gun and not a pressure washer lance.  The product smells great and also suds really well.  I've used this product and the Mr. Pink product and they are both equally great.  I noticed that Mr. Pink is a little more thicker than this product.  You can't go wrong with either product.
i love it it works great smells awesome and does what its  just what they claim it to be nothing more

This was the first product I have ever bought from Chemical Guys. I have always been a fan of car detailing but have limited my purchases for supplies to the local car parts stores. I had read great reviews on Chemical Guys and figured it would be worth a shot trying a car wash/snow foam from them to use with my foam gun. This stuff blows away any basic cleaner you would buy off the shelf. It generates a thick foam that coats the car and loosens up any built up debris before you begin washing with a mitt. Not to mention that the smell of the soap is awesome! I have added many other Chemical Guys products to my aresenal since this purchase and am looking forward to using them all once Spring is in full swing here in Ohio!
I use this soap with a foam cannon to get the best suds I have ever seen. Can also be used with traditional sponge and bucket combo. Another 5 star product from Chemical Guys
Not bad. I use it with a foam gun  . It does good on the suds and has a good smell .  Next on the list is maxi suds II then mr pink.
Puts out a great spread from a foam gun or cannon with just 2 oz per wash; doesn't strip away any sealant or wax so far.
This stuff does a great job at loosening up dirt/mud off of a car, let sit for 1.5-2 minutes on the car and the dirt comes off without any effort some stubborn spots require a wash mitt but not much.
Foams up great with my MTM hydro foam lance. Suds up and removes a lot of dirt prior to rinsing!

As the description says it's very concentrated and foams up big time. A gallon of this cleaner will last a long time. I originally bought it just to use with a foam nozzle attachment for my pressure washer but I've got so much of it now that I'm using it as normal car shampoo and it's working well.Using a good clean sponge and the two bucket method I'm not getting any swirling in my paint so I think this cleaner is effective at lifting up the dirt like it says.

I hated to stop every time I wanted to wet my throat on a long ride. An occasional sip of water or something refreshing is great.This was so reasonably priced I had to give it a shot. I was surprised. Much nicer than the price shows. Very nice quality. Easy to install. Nicely adjustable and it will hold a water bottle, soda, or after market flip top beverage container.Awesome.
not real happy, this does not really work well to hold a bottle of water, unless it's half empty or full however you look at it. I have already taken it off my Harley.

I really like this cup holder.  It has a foam liner that you can remove for a larger cup/bottle if you like and you can adjust this to hang just about anywhere.  I did have to use an additional strip of rubber along with the one that came with it as my handlebars are 7/8" and the included strip just wasn't enough for a tight fit.  The chrome is shiny, it looks good, and it does exactly what it's made to do.
summary: It holds my drink and looks great

reviewText: Would like to have more infomation about the best way to mount it but great quality for the price. Everything is metal except for the cup holder.  Still it goes well with my Chrome bike.
What a deal, It is about ten dollars cheeper than the bike store. It is the idenical cup holder that they sell.
I had this Cup Holder for about 2 weeks before the bolt that held the up came loose and my cup fell off. I was so mad. When you get it make sure every bolt is tight or you will loose it.
summary: Make sure you fasten your bults first before you take it for a ride.

reviewText: Lowlife  husband of mine wouldn't put the darn thing on, its still sitting in the closet, so i have to hold the drinks with my hands.T.hey get sick of holding, so i put in his lap for him to hold it
summary: Diamond Plate Chrome Motorcycle Cup Holder

reviewText: I worked my way through college detailing cars at a dealership in Phoenix. We used the BIG heavy professional grade "buffers" with the 10 inch wool pads which would cut to fresh paint in a hurry.  These buffers were unwieldy, noisy, and heavy.  When I received this Griot's Garage RO I was pleasantly surprised at the compactness and the the build quality of the unit.  I like the adjustable handle and the adjustable speed on the unit.  Due to weather conditions here (HOT) I am going to wait until my garage is under 90 degrees to actually use the RO, but I am confident it will do the job just fine.  BTW, if you are considering purchasing one of these units, opt for the 25' cord.  From experience, I can tell you that a 10' cord WILL unplug from your extension cord at the most inappropriate time, lol.  The extra few bucks for the 25' vs 10' cord will pay for itself in convenience.  I will update this in a few months.

I purchased this with a coupon from Advanced Auto Parts, To me It does the Job with a few  subtleties.1) First 3 pads cost anywhere  between $28-33 dollars this is  expensive especially when you need to get orange and red pads .2) I notice that as I break down each section of the car to Polish the Unit Heats up when used more than 5 mins. What is this about a poor design do I need to get a pair of Landscape  gloves  to used it.I guess for 100+  it is worth it I probably should saved up to buy a Flex.

This thing is a powerhouse. Works very well and has tons of power. The design is great too except the speed control is agitating to change while trying to keep contact. The power switch could be better designed also but overall it works great.

The Lifetime Warranty gives you that peace of mine.  This is really a nice polisher. Has more power then the Meguiar's  Dual Action Polisher, but a little bit heavier.  I'm not a professional detailer so can't comment on the $400.00 dollar polisherYou don't have to use the Griot 6.5 inch pads, you can used other manufacturers pads as well.  I like to use the Lake Country pads 5.5 inch pads.  Just make sure you use the 5 inch backing plate otherwise the 6 inch backing plate will damage the 5.5 pads.  The reason I'm giving it 3 stars was because the speed control dial no longer works. Speed setting 1 and 6 are the only speed settings that work.  Switching out under 30 day replacement.  Hopefully this will be good.

Finally  broke down and bought a DA polisher. Settled on the Griot's after much on line research. So far I have not been disappointed. Have used it to do over have the 5th wheel trailer with good results. Also have used on the 13  year old truck with good results. Works as advertised. No complaints so far.
I hate waxing a car. This makes the job so much easier. If fact, it was so easy doing the car, I also did the truck and then the RV. Bring 'em on.

I Was a little skeptical because of other polishers I've used. But this thing is great. I received it today with a Groits polishing and waxing pad, and I used them all today, just to test it out. Absolutely impressed. I am right now, looking into other Groits products to use with this polisher. I've been a big fan of Meguirs but it looks like things are going to change. Love this thing.

Plenty of power, adjustable front handle, good price. I like this a lot better than others models like the porter cable, and while it doesn't have the throw of a Rupes or the power of a Flex it's also a heck of a lot cheaper.

Ive been detailing cars for many years, I've tried almost every polisher on the market and want to tell everyone this is the best polisher you can buy.I've been using my Porter Cable XP for over a year now, this past Saturday I received my GG DA and here is what I noticed right away.So much power , I polished my truck in half the time compared to the PC, much more powerful.It's much more easier to use than the PC, feels great in your hands.Unlike the PC it won't bog down, no matter how much pressure you put on it the pad continues to spin, that's where the faster correction comes into play.Love the handle in hard to reach areas, like large hoods.IMO its the best polisher I've ever used, it comes real close to the Flex, I mean very close but for a fraction of the cost, I used the Flex too, it's a fine machine but doesn't do more than the GG DA.Do yourself a favor and buy this DA if your looking for one.
White with a hint of blue. Lights up the Fit interior nicely. Didn't really need 4, but it was a fair price.
Purchased these for my dome/map lights in my car.  They are bright and give off a pure white light.  Satisfied with the purchase.

The lights that worked, work great.  I'm happy with them, and am keepign them in the car.  White light with just a hint of blue.  (not the more amber colored leds)My only problem was several did not work completely, and had some of the LEDs out.  Wasn't worth the hassle of returning, and I had extras, so it worked out.  But I would suggest not ordering the exact number you need.Hope that is helpful!
summary: They are bright, they fit in the socket they are designed for.  Some of mine had bad LEDs.  Order extra if you buy.

reviewText: They are the identical product as listed "31mm Festoon 12 LEDs SMD LED Bulb White for 3022 DE3022 3175 DE3175" with the only difference that this package has four bulbs. I could use one only for my Camry as my map light require longer festoon bulb.However the white light looks good in the interior and my kids like them.
summary: Cutequeen White 31mm(1.25") 12-SMD 12V Festoon Dome Light LED Bulbs DE3175

reviewText: My cars current interior door lights were, well a little dull at best. These were a great solution for that. All four worked correctly and were simple to install. Makes a huge difference in my 1995 honda accord ex. Great deal for the money, theres no way you will be disappointed.

I just finished Washing my car with a two bucket system with CarKem ruby red wash and wax. Pro wax 1 Polish. Spray and Shine.to top it off Wolgang 3.0.  I have to say this stuff is $$ have used many different synthetic sealants from Simoniz Synthetic Sealer to Hi Temp products.This is good a product with a nice mirror like finish. wife walked in and noticed a spot on her dress from the reflection the car shined. cool (:
summary: I have tried  them all this one is good

reviewText: I have always been a dedicated Mirror Glaze person until I discovered that there are products that far surpass what even they offer. This went on super easy using the straight line method illustrated on autogeek.com and it wiped off to a super glossy shine after 45 minutes. Amazing stuff that is supposed to last 4-6 months (almost twice as long as regular wax).

This is the BEST sealant I have ever used. Goes on easy, comes off easy. Leaves a deep shine you will love. Only needs 12 hours to cure. I have see other sealants that need 24 hours. Best bang for your buck!
I have a civic, silver, 11/11 and used it for first time. Very use to apply and remove. I let 10 minutes under the under the paint and rub carefully with a microfiber towel.

I've been detailing cars for 30 years, I tried many sealants/waxes and here to say it's the best I ever used.I applied it to a truck that I did a full correction on, it was so easy to apply but that's not what makes it the best.It's when I wiped it off which was easy, then I noticed this incredible super high gloss like no other.It truly blew me away, not only did it shine but it was so slick, as I wiped my micro towel over the paint I felt no drag, no friction and that's what you want, what will help to avoid swirls down the road, the towel just glided over the finish.From this day on its all I'll use for my paint sealant step.

while this looks really cool in my jeep noone mentioned that you have to cut these knotches out with a razor knife and its pretty thick plastic and the squares are so close together that its easy to cut into the next block or out side the lines.. i proble would have oredered a dif one but if you have time and are fairly nifty you can def make this look cool just take your time

The switch pod fits well as a replacement for the factory item.  You can not tell the difference between the color of this pillar and the surrounding factory plastic.  I installed switches in all 4 locations because it seemed that it would be better to do that than to take it off later to add switches. I purchased the switches from a different manufacturer because I liked the styling of them better.  For whatever switches you purchase you have to cut out the switch openings.  I think the mfg should punch out the plastic at the factory and then placed a plastic cover over the openings.If you are good with an Exacto knife it will be easy to cut the openings for the switches; the plastic is soft.  The included instructions are well written and clear with good pictures.  For the price they should include some hardware with it (the reason for 4 stars) For one metal clip they have you take the plastic wire track cover off of the rear tailgate and use the one in the middle.  There is also a plastic clip that holds in the existing pillar.  This clip tends to break when you remove the old pillar.  They could have included this hardware and received 1 more star.When I installed my switches I used #12 gauge wire and so the pillar was a little difficult to try to mount.  What did help was to run the wires through one of the u-shaped supports on the back of the pillar.  Once installed the pillar looks good.  I had installed long wires for the switches that were long enough to run under the dash.  There is plenty of room under the dash and that is where I will connect to the various devices using butt splices.I would buy this again and recommend it to others for the 2012 JK.
summary: Fits well and looks great on Jeep Unlimited 4 door JK - black interior and exterior

reviewText: Almost a perfect match to the factor interier. Also came with 4 rocker switches. Did know it came with them so it was better than expected.
This works well on a variety levels.  It's fairly easy to install, it allows easy access to run the wires and it looks good with the surrounding trim.

This is a great product.  The color is spot on with the existing pillar.  It is a little difficult to install but well worth it.  The installation is hard due to jeep not rugged ridge.  The placement of the pillar by Chrysler is extremely tight so you do have to wiggle it in.  The best way i found out how to do it was to remove the snap in panel on the side of the dash and pop the twitter loose from below.  This also allows you to run a wire down.  I would strongly suggest to install a terminal strip below the steering column panel.  The bottom panel closest to the peddle simply pops out and there is a bar there to mount a terminal stirp with can be picked up over amazon or radioshack.  I used 4 daystar rocker switches and used a 8-wire cable from the switches to the terminal strip, this makes the installation a one time deal and not have to take it down every time you add or change a switch.
Fit my 2014 JKUR perfectly.  Great switch panel.

Put this in my 2014 Rubicon unlimited. It is close enough for government work, but isn't a perfect match. Was easy to install and holds switches well. i put in 3 Daystars and a DPDT on the bottom. Would suggest being really careful when cutting. You could easily cut out too much. I put lots of masking tape on the areas around where cutting - you have to apply lots of pressure and i always end up slipping or getting impatient. Got it done without ruining it
summary: Very good - not a perfect match for a 2014 Wrangler

reviewText: Fit nicely in my 2012 JK.  Cutting out the holes for the rocker switches was a bit of a pain but if you take your time you shouldn't have any problems.  Plastic was sturdy and it was a close enough match to the OEM plastic that no one would ever notice.

To help quiet engine sound on the RV, installing it under the "door" to the engine, helped a little.  It wasn't large enough to cover the whole "door".  It does do as it's described, it reduces sound. It does not eliminate it.
summary: It did help but it was a little on the small side

reviewText: I followed the instructions and was able to 'tame' one of our car's door speakers. It worked but keep in mind that the 'easy to install' claim applies to the mat itself. Getting to the point where you can actually install it, that's a separate story.If you are good with your hands, get this by all means. It does what it claims it does but if you are afraid to take your car apart to get to the place where the mat needs to be placed well... there are people who do this for a living. It will cost you more but you will worry a lot less.Oh, also keep in mind that, depending on how big your project it, you may need more than one mat to complete it.
summary: Surprisingly effective. Easy to install? ... it depends

reviewText: This is a small piece of extremely heavy vinyl.  It is very sticky feeling, with a tacky surface, and the stickiness is transfered to your fingers as you handle it.  It is thin but feels like lead.  I suppose this is what it takes to deaden sound.  It looks like it might melt into a mess in very high heat although I didn't test it for that.  It is described on the box as a "self adhesive, comformable mat that reduces road noise and vibration.The instructions say to:1. Prepare area by removing any carpteing, lining and/or panels to expose metal substrate.2. Clean the surface with rubbing alcohol and let dry.  Ensure surface is free of oil, dust and debris.3. Using standard household scissors cut the 3M Sound Reduction Mat to fit the size of the desired area.4. Peel and discard the yellow liner off the back of the mat.5. Using even pressure, carefully conform and firmly apply to the surface.  If additional conformaity is needed, use a heat gun or blow dryer to heat the mat to 95 degrees to 115 degrees.The box suggests use in the trunk, door panel, or for speaker installations.  My first thought would be the engine compartment but as I said this is something that appears to me it would melt in high heat, and the directions to use a blow dryer to help this conform to curved surfaces supports that viewpoint.  With that in mind, I would be hesitant to use this here in our sub tropic weather where in the summer the interior of a car can climb to well over 120 degrees.  I would be afraid of this melting into a mass of sticky goo.I've seen other sound reduction technologies in cars.  They look more like a thick blanket, rather than heat sensitive vinyl.In addtion, the added weight of several of these in a car is worth considering.  This is like lead as far as weight.In a cold climate this might be ok, but I am going to not use this in our sweltering weather due to the melting propensity of it.If your climate doesn't get extremely hot, this would be OK to place under a speaker or subwoofer installation, as it would help to deaden any vibrations.  If you plan to soundproof your entire car or even just the engine compartment, you would need a lot of these.  This is a pretty small piece when you see it in person.
summary: Not a bargain, becomes soft in high heat

reviewText: While this sound reduction mat comes in a single box and it measures 2 1/2 square feet, it actually is created in two separate pads.After you open and unfold the pads, you cut them to size and place them inside a door, trunk or hood. As you can guess, you will likely need a larger size for larger products. What I liked about this was that it was easy to cut and it is peel and stick.I joked with my husband about installing it across his nose to stop his snoring ... but I'm afraid it would also prevent him from breathing ... so we had to use it on the car.

Installing sound reduction mats in your car is a great way to reduce road noise and vibrations.  The matting absorbs the sounds and adds weight to a panel, reducing it's tendency to vibrate.  Matting can be placed inside trucks, engine walls, inside doors - pretty much anywhere there is metal it can stick to.We have a 1984 Mustang that is a street legal drag car.  It has a loud exhaust, it is so loud that it sets off car alarms when driving by parked vehicles.  Everything in that car vibrates including my teeth.  The most annoying vibrations came from the trunk. We cut long strips of the 3M Sound Reduction Mat and adhered it to the parts of the hatchback where they touched metal-to-metal. The vibrations halted.  Now time to go to the next section of the Stang.  However, We are going to have to purchase more rolls since this roll is was only big enough to do a small job.I am pleased with the performance of this product, but it made me aware that there are many other brands that offer larger mats at better prices.  Besides mats, there are also sprays, foams, and insulation available from different manufacturers.

I thought this would be a quick and easy solution to muffling the rattles emanating from a 1998 ford.  I was wrong. The product is a fairly hard black vinyl with an adhesive back.  Designed to be used on metal surfaces, it must be applied when temperatures are higher than 40 degrees farenheit. The surface must be thoroughly cleaned. The mat may be sized by cutting with scissors or in my case an exacto knife.The backer is removed and the mat is positioned.  Then ideally, the mat will fit securely and the offending noises muffled. If necessary you may use a blow dryer or heat gun.Sounds great. But it isn't quite so easy. First, it being winter in NY, I had to wait until the temperatures rose. I had planned to use this in a door. But the material is inflexible, cuttable, but still inflexible. Worse, I couldn't get it to stick in position. So I wound up taking it off. My brother then took the remainder for the back floor of his suv. He had better luck getting it to stick using a heat gun. He is satisfied with its noise muting capabilities.This product was not for me. Unless you are adept at accessing the offending parts and fairly handy, this requires significantly more work than the package suggests. When properly applied, it does seem to work. I wonder if the adhesion is effected by heat as well as cold. Obviously, the material becomes more brittle in the cold and does not adhere. Conversely, in high summer heat, does it melt or become gooey? I dodn't know. I think the product can perform adequately but unless you are experienced with this type of installation, I would pass.
summary: More of a Project than I Anticipated

reviewText: This 3M sound reduction mat's appearance is best likened to gasket material according to my husband who has a great deal of experience with such things...just in case you wanted to have a better handle on what it looks like.The main limitation of this mat is its size. It is ideal for speaker use, but any larger application will require multiple sheets. If we wanted to use this in our door panel, we would  probably prefer to buy a larger sheet or product and place it there in order to maximize the sound reduction through consistency and lack of gaps as well as to reduce the weight that several of these mats would ad. We park along a curb or sidewalk nightly and already have to finagle opening our passenger door to get out of the car. If it were just a bit more weighty with this material, it would be more difficult to keep it from scraping the concrete. Anyone using this mat for a large surface area would need to consider such issues.However, for a speaker or speakers, this would be fine if you can find the temperature sweet spot that allows for an easier application. It took a bit of doing for us to make this work, and if were doing a vertical stick, it probably would not have staid put at this point in time (early spring).
summary: The size of this product limits its application

reviewText: What's in the box?* One sound-deadening sheet approximately 5/32" thick.  You can use it as one mat, 19 11/16" by 19 11/16", or as two smaller mats (it has a perforation down the middle).* Instructions.In general, I find 3M products to be of superior quality.  I do like this product, but have some reservations.  In regard to performance, it DOES work!  I used it for an application other than an automobile, which is also other than its intended purpose.I have a small work/storage room in my basement.  It has slab floor, drywall, and is narrow, less than 5' wide.  I have a backup sump pump in the room, which has a control module which manages the backup pump's battery, etc.  The module has always produced an electrical buzz/hum, which can be quite annoying when in the room.  The module is in the corner of the workroom on a small cabinet, so it is about 5" from a wall on two sides of it.  The walls both have pegboard, and in the past I tried fixing some Styrofoam to board by the module.  This served only to slightly amplify the buzz.So I decided to try this product.  For my application, I mounted some 1/8" thick wood that I had from a packing crate on the pegboard.  I did this, so I would not damage the pegboard with the 3M mats.  The mat gripped well, but like anything else of an adhesive nature, you want to measure right and work slowly, as adjusting it afterward is not really an option.  Once you have peeled the paper and applied it, it is on fairly well.  You could get it off, but would likely wreck it in the process. As far as sizing it, cutting this is like cutting other dense, adhesive type materials.  A sharp blade with firm, steady strokes is best.  The blade will get a little gummy so plan on changing it out or cleaning it afterward.  TIP: If you rub a little WD-40 on sides of the blade, it helps it glide through a little more easily.For my purpose, I separated the mat into two halves at the perforation.  I needed to trim them slightly to fit my application.  I applied them so that the module had a mat behind it and on one side.  I didn't think I'd have great results, especially with two sides still not dampened.  However, the sound of the buzz was dramatically reduced.So, this stuff works, and it adheres well, etc.  Now the issue: there is not a lot of it to a box, and at over $15 a box, it can be pricy per square foot.  If you are using this to deaden sound in a whole car, or even a large area of a car, four doors, trunk, etc., I could see it get expensive very fast.It does work as advertised.  I think there needs to be a little more per box to warrant using it, unless you have a very specific application in a contained area (one door, one speaker area, etc.).
summary: Works As Advertised, But Can Be Costly

reviewText: This sound reduction mat is made of a flexible rubber-like material that is about 1/8 inch thick. It is adhesive and comes rolled up with a paper liner. The adhesive used is super sticky and adheres well. The mat can be cut with regular scissors to get a perfect custom fit. The mat is very flexible but I found using a blow dryer to heat the mat really helped mold it to the surface. The mat is 19  by 19  inches, but you should know that it is perforated down the center. I'm not sure if the mat was very effective in reducing the sound. Maybe we just didn't apply enough to make a significant difference. I think it does help though.

This 3M Sound Reduction Mat is designed for use in cars, but I used to on our shop workbench to reduce the noise and shaking from a vibrating cleaner. This mat did a great job at absorbing the vibration and the size was perfect for the bench top.I am not sure that a mat this small would do much in my truck to reduce road noise, but there are other uses for this product.Recommended!CFH
summary: Good Sound and Shake Reduction - Recommended

reviewText: I applied this in the trunk all at once, using the entire mat.  It would have taken a lot more material to do the doors not to mention time.  So for the sake of time and effort I did the trunk.  It did deaden some sound - that's how I know it works.The job of cutting the right sizes and applying to a lot of contours is more than I think most people are prepared to do plus will require more units.  But if you spend a lot of time in your car, it seems practical to me.
summary: Fast and easy to apply in the trunk

reviewText: I installed this sound reduction mat in the trunk of my Mitsubishi Lancer Rally Edition. It' not the quietest of cars so I figured it could use a little soundproofing. Even though this roll looks somewhat big it was used up quite quickly. I didn't have enough to cover the entire truck but was able to do most of it. Installation was a breeze on My Lancer because all I had to do was reach under the truck liner and apply the adhesive mat. It stick's fine to a nice and clean surface. Just be sure to clean any area that is dirty or dusty prior to attempting to install the mat. I don't notice any sound difference when driving really but notice a little difference when riding in the back seat of the car. I think this product works a little but might not be for the average person because it would take so many rolls and so much work installing it. Especially if you are doing the inside of your door panels it's a lot of work with only a small payoff. However if you have a loud sound system or just an extremely loud car then it may be worth the work.
summary: A lot of work for only a small difference, you will need many rolls to do a entire vehicle

reviewText: This sound-deadening material is super-easy to install, just peel and stick.  Quieted down the noise from my engine bay into the cabin significantly.  The only downside I can find is that this stuff is super-heavy.  If you are a firm believer in the Lotus motto of "adding lightness" this might not be for you.

Being that this only comes in one size that's a big downside. I hope to see 3M make other sizes available for bigger applications like most people  are doing. I installed this in the trunk of my vehicle and did not notice a big difference in road noise reduction. I think there are better alternatives. I've seen big mats and bigger rolls through other vendors online. Overall, unless this is just for around speakers I don't think this will fit many applications unless you want to buy a lot, but if you are buying a lot there are some other semi and custom products to fit your exact need.

While comparing this to Dynamat Xtreme, so far I prefer Dynamat, except for the price.Dynamat has a foil backing which gives it a nice feel to contour the mat to wrap around complex objects.So far I can't tell the difference in sound reduction between the two.I would use this one when I need to cover large areas at low cost.I'll use Dynamat when I want it to look nice with the shiny foil.
summary: Similar to Dynamat, but without the foil backing

reviewText: So, we have a vehicle with a center console that squeeks and makes an inordinate amount of noise if we actually put anything inside the console. Nothing major but just enough to irritate the ever living daylights out of everyone in the car when driving for more than 2 minutes. We know what the problem is and have resorted to "stuffing" things around the opening or leaning on the center console etc to make it stop. It's annoying but not covered under warranty. When this came up for review, I thought it would be a good idea to try out.First, this isn't a very big mat but was more than ample for our needs. It's about 20 inches which would be too big for the entire bottom but not large encough to "wrap" the entire console area. The console is about 14 inches so this required trimming. Then, due to the sizing, I was afraid it may not allow the console insert to fit back in but it does. This is flexible, takes a bit of time to cut to size and then installation is sticky but not a huge mess. The console 'box' fits back in place over this, squeek is stopped and no more rattling sound thanks to the insulative properties.All in all, it's not the easiest thing to work with but certainly well within the DIY realm and gets the job done.
summary: Bit of a pain to work with but does the job

reviewText: Seems to work as well as the D brand.  Most of these products are similar.  They are self-adhesive flexible tar paper.  They stop vibration by adding weight to the vibrating panel.  So be aware that you will add significant weight to your vehicle if you go too crazy.  If you are just looking to make the vehicle quieter (e.g. reduce road noise) a foam or fiber type insulation will work better and be much lighter.  But this works as designed.
summary: Works as well as the D brand.

reviewText: I think that for a sound deadening material like this to work, you would need to install a lot of it if the goal is to make a noticeable difference in noise levels inside a car. Just adding it to exposed trunk panels which I thought might be the source of excessive road noise didn't seem to make any difference at all. Perhaps the real point is that reducing annoying sound levels requires expertise far beyond mine. I suppose that isn't the fault of the product, but it is a matter of expectations not being met. A professional who knows what they are doing would probably need a whole lot of this material installed in the right places to make a difference.
summary: Doesn't seem to make a huge difference

reviewText: For years auto sound reduction has been ruled by Dynamat and various similar products.  Now that this 3M product has been released it appears that sound reduction might go more mainstream.  The amount of product that I received from Amazon Vine was not large enough that I could do a definitive test, but it seems to absorb sound as well as other similar products.  Because of the size of the 3M distribution network, this product could be just the thing to make consumer-installed sound reduction widely available not just to car enthusiasts, but also to the general public.
summary: Might Make Sound Reduction More Mainstream

reviewText: I was going to put this in front of the shifting lever in the '88 Trooper to try to suppress road noise, but I decided the speakers would benefit most. I still have a mess-load of mat left for when I get around to pulling up the carpet.I sliced out eight squares of mat, each barely an inch in size, took off the speakers, cleaned the mating metal surfaces as directed and let it dry, then stuck each square on between the speaker mounting points and installed the speakers on top of it, with excellent results; I can crank the stereo up and not get any rattle.The mat is like a heavy sheet of tar. I have a similar two-inch wide roll of this same material on my boat, not sure where it came from, as it was already there, but it is the same thing only more narrow and there is an entire roll of it, so stuff is out there, perhaps it is also a 3M product. Unlike my tar strip roll, this mat does have a crosshatch pattern on the surface, which may help to dissipate noise when applied to a large surface.I am not keen of permanently added weight on my vehicle - not that it is excessive, but every pound makes a difference. It feels heavy, so entire sheets of this stuff in the car may not be what I would consider an asset, but I may do the floor eventually and report on its effects in the future, but it did work magnificently for the speakers.

This stuff would probably be best suited for a speaker that vibrates, or a subwoofer that rattles anything that isn't bolted down in your car.  It's very site specific, and there can be some tinkering involved if you have trouble locating the exact cause and source of the noise you're trying to eliminate.  The price ain't bad, provided you only need a small amount, but this could quickly add up and be quite expensive, depending on your need.The good thing, is it does NOT have a funky industrial smell.  In fact, it doesn't smell like much of anything, which is a huge bonus, since materials like this can downright stink to toxic proportions.I had a creak in the passenger side of our car, under the seat, and this helped dampen that a tad. Prolly it could have been applied better, but it's good enough for me.  I placed the excess under my Bi-pap in the bedroom, and it really helped cut down on the whirring noise, which reverberated on the shelf it's sitting on.  So for that purpose, it worked pretty well.The sticky backside has plenty of adhesive, however, the material itself is quite thick and stiff, so the adhesive often doesn't stand a chance of holding it down on uneven surfaces.  It sticks, just not always well, or exactly how you'd want.The black rubbery kinda mat does seem to rub off a bit and leave black marks or scuffs -- or at least that's the impression I was left with, given the black marks it left inside the product packaging.  Seems like this is the type of stuff that could melt  and decompose a bit in heat; or at least get a little soft and gooey, like tar.It's pretty stiff, but is somewhat pliable too.  It can be hard to cut to specific shapes. There's a perforation down the center, so clearly they intend this to be used as 2 pieces.  But again, you could cut it to size with a really tough pair of scissors, or a box cutter.Overall, this stuff is pretty good for specific applications.  Just be prepared to work with it to achieve your perfect result.  A tad costly if you need a good amount.  But it works well enough.
summary: It Helps, But Can Be Hard To Work With

reviewText: This product did block noise in the spot it was placed but the entire piece of material is 20x19.5 inches so will only be useful if your noisy spot is smaller that this. One side has glue on it.
summary: Works fine but is too small for most applications

reviewText: This is a good idea for a product because most of us have car noises and vibrations we'd like to eliminate. However, I have a couple issues with this product.For one thing, the instructions are intimidating. After reading them (and re-reading them), I decided this would be best installed by someone who's done this kind of thing before. I could do it, but I'd likely end up messing up and the frustration level seems high. The examples illustrated on the package are not impressive, and I'm sure I would do much worse.Secondly, to do a thorough job it appears that you need more than one box of this mat. For example, to apply the mat to the trunk area requires 2 boxes (the estimated time is 30 minutes--I assume this is for a professional), and 1 box is required for each door (the estimated time is 15 minutes per door.)I might consider trying to use the mat for speaker installation because that requires less than one box. However, in looking at the illustration I'm again intimidated.This might be a great product if you've had experience with something like it before, but I'm going to leave this one to the professionals.
summary: Sometimes It's Best To Use A Professional

reviewText: I used this in the wheel well of my suv to try to deaden some road noise.  The mat was brittle and some of it broke into small pieces that I discarded. The mat itself is small and it would take quite a few of them to make much difference in the amount of road noise infiltrating a car.  It would also be a tremendous amount of work and time to install on floor boards. doors and wheel wells.  The investment in time and money wouldn't be worth a little less noise.
summary: Not enough to do much with

reviewText: This sound reduction matting material from 3M is a thick, pliable, self-adhesive sheet.  The dense material dampens sound waves and vibrations.  It comes rolled and the sheet is perforated down the middle.  It is very malleable and will adapt to fit around stereo components and fill cracks or holes.This product is really intended only for people with experience installing audio equipment in vehicles and is not ideal to be used under a fan or blender where it will be visible.  It does still function but it is slightly tarry and hard to keep clean.

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I love my loud corvette and the rumble it makes when I start it up. It really gives me a thrill, however I also like to take phone calls (on Bluetooth) while driving and the rumble can be too much. I had bought a similar product to be installed in one of my cars when I put new carpeting in a few years ago and it worked extremely well with sound reduction. I installed several pieces in my corvette and am very happy with sound reduction although I will need to add more pieces when I upgrade the speakers.
summary: I have a corvette with very loud, aftermarket pipes and upgraded engine...

reviewText: Well, you can see the size of this mat listed in the title for yourself.  Although it might be nice to have a huge sheet if you're doing the engine compartment of your car, multiple sheets fitted together is probably more convenient in most cases.  Car audio applications are the obvious choice (heard of Dynamat?) - you know, getting that license plate to stop rattling with the bass.  But start thinking of any appliance you have vibrating in your basement or utility room in your house: chances are you can make that less annoying fairly easily with one or two of these.  Be careful, though - a real disadvantage is that stopping vibration from being annoying is so easy that it might dissuade you from getting to the root of the problem.Use a heat gun to apply, bend, and remove if necessary.

This product is easy to install (have to pull up mats to get to metal surface so it adheres well.Need to watch the temperature in that if it is too cold or hot will not stick.For real effectiveness several of these would be needed.I kept trying to think of other uses for this product.  It is so heavy and rugged but not extremely thick (maybe about a 1/4 inch).There must be some way to use this to deaden common household noises.I put it under my coffee grinder but that did nothingI just think this is such an innovative product that there must be great unintended uses for it.

I installed this in the door panel of my truck and I'm noticing a slight reduction in sound and rattles.  I only had the one mat to try out so I didn't expect to feel like I was in a sound-proof booth with just one installed, but it did cut down on the rattle.Simple to install with no special tools required, very strong adhesive.

I placed this under my Infinity Basslink.  I placed a false bottom in my Crossfire to hold my Pioneer AVG-VDP1 - Real-time Vehicle Dynamics Processor and AVD-W6210 Touch Screen Display.  This Sound Reduction Mat worked perfectly to support the Basslink and make it right.  No more road noise and vibration.  It was easy to adhere to the false bottom of the support for the Infinity Basslink.  It just stuck on.Do not stuck on if your tempertures below 40 degrees or in won't stick.You can scan the bar code on your phone to see a video.

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: This is one of those "common sense" products that people forget common sense when using. The ideal use is when installing speakers in your doors or deck. More powerful speakers bring out every vibration in your vehicle and can sound tinny. Applying a sound deadening material when installing speakers is pretty much a requirement. This box has enough for two larger oval, or three smaller round speakers. It will help reduce vibration and slightly "flatten" the sound. If you have a noisy trunk - especially in the wheel wells, this will also help deaden the sound - but you'll probably need two boxes.This is a SMALL quantity of material. 1.76 x 1.76 feet. Cut a piece of paper that size - it's not that much.  If you need to deaden sound in a small problem area, it will work.  Consider it a "small project" size.  Anyone expecting to make a $15,000 car sound like a $60,000 car by adding sound deadening is dreaming.  You'd have to strip the car of almost all the interior, door panels, dash, etc. to apply the stuff - hardly a practical solution, or anything 99.999% of the population could do!Application: The instructions show using scissors - I prefer a utility knife with a piece of scrap wood as a cutting surface. This stuff looks and feels like a mixture of tar and rubber, and leaves a gummy residue on the scissors. You can clean this off with solvent, or as most guys do, with gas (I don't smoke.)  I'd rather just throw away a 10 cent blade.1) For oddball shapes or curved areas, make a paper template and cut that to shape. Put that on top of the mat as a template and cut.2) Clean the application area with rubbing alcohol and let dry3) Use a blow dryer on the mat to soften it up - this is by feel, but you want to flexible.4) peel and apply.Scrap pieces can be used to fill in small areas or cover seams, holes, etc.If you have a rust-bucket (I've had a few) and have water coming in the floor boards or trunk, this stuff is a nice patch material.  If you can find the hole, say in the floorboard, sand the metal to remove the rust and paint - ideally inside and out. Apply a piece of this inside, overlapping the hole by about 1" on all sides. If you can, do the same thing on the outside. Where the patches meet they will bind together. This forms a seal/plug and keeps the water out. You'll need to cover the patch in something - carpeting, etc. in areas where you'll step on them.(floorboards, for example.) If you have a swiss-cheese rusty piece of metal, clean as best you can - you need clean, bare metal - not rust - in order for this to stick. Heat the metal (if it can be done safely, use a torch) then apply the mat. It will melt into the holes!  Otherwise, heat the metal with a blow dryer, apply the mat, then heat up as hot as possible with the same blow dryer. Apply pressure. The idea is to press the now soft mat into the holes.  Instant large area patch!
summary: For SMALL projects or areas, easy to apply - also patches holes!

reviewText: I found this product very easy to install -- easy to cut, easy to apply, and easy to trim after application. Sticks nicely as well (otherwise it would not do much sound deadening!)Be warned ... you'll probably need more than you think. I used it on my 1999 Silverado, to help dampen the sound resonation. I did not cover the holes in the inner door panel because (1) I wanted to see how well it worked solely as a dampener and not a blocker, and (2) I wanted to leave the access holes as they are, for now, due to some upcoming body work to be done. In this way, one box covered nicely the back door and most of the passenger front door. I would have needed at least one more box to cover the holes in the inner skin on these two doors, maybe two.Does it work? Yes. Even with the limited use, it dampened the sound. It also makes the back door sound more solid when closing.Will I buy more? Yes. Once the body work is done, I will do a full inner skin cover. It will be easy, as the way it sticks I don't have to remove the pieces already installed. I'll just leave them and cut more to fill the holes.I have never used competing products so I cannot comment on them, but this seems to be a nice alternative to the well-known DynaMat. It is a good thickness and it is very easy to use. Won't add much weight to your car either.

I was hoping to use this to muffle noise in my trunk over my spare tire which has been used a couple of times. The description talks about it being used in a trunk. To do so would have required at least two of these mats and possibly three.  I did lay it over the area and it cut down the noise somewhat.  If I took the time to fully cover the trunk area I think it would work even better but I have not done it yet because this is supposed to be used on bare metal.The instructions say you can only do this if it is above 40 degrees and you are to use this only on a metal surface. You are to clean the surface with rubbing alcohol. You then peel the yellow liner of the matt and apply to the surface. A heat gun or blow dryer can be used if "additional conformity is needed."I did not use this on a metal surface but used it on the material that covers the part of my trunk that holds the mini spare tire. I actually used Duct Tape to hold it in place.  It did muffle some of the sound coming from my spare tire area even though I did not use this as per the instructions.I did not use this as per the instructions so my review has to be viewed based on that.  This is only supposed to be used on metal surfaces. While this says it is for use in a trunk the picture shows it being used on the metal surfaces on a trunk which varies from trunk to trunk or in a door panel or around speaker installations. This will take some expertise and an ability to cut this to fit corners and curves.My limited and technically incorrect use muffled some sound so I think this works, I wish this could just be laid over the entire back of a trunk or on the floor of a car or truck without having to go to bare metal to do so. It would be easier and I think it would work.
summary: This Seems To Work But It Can Only Be Used Under Certain Circumstances

reviewText: I was intrigued with this product, but didn't realize until it arrived how much work was involved in utilizing it. I have not yet tried using this on the door panels yet, but I have installed this in the trunk, under the lining and I'm amazed at what just this one small install has done to cut down road noise. Because of the reduction in noise - noise I didn't even realize was there until it was gone - I'm now more tempted to get this in my door panels as well. One should note that this is not a job for the faint of heart. I needed help from my stepsons with the trunk install - and the liner in the trunk is fairly easy to remove. The door panels are going to be weekend jobs.
summary: amazingly cuts down on road noise like you'd never think it would

reviewText: We have a water pump that makes a lot of noise when it is running despite being enclosed in a small wooden box.  Two rolls of this was able to line the entire interior of the box, and has significantly reduced the amount of noise that escapes the pump when it is running.I don't know how well it would work in a car, because there are so many places that sound can get through, but maybe for small problem areas it would be useful.  It worked great for our application, even sticking very permanently to the unfinished wood box.//-Update-//A few weeks after using this on the water pump I was driving to work and was getting annoyed by rattling in my center console.  I stopped off at an auto supply store and bought another roll of this mat.  I lined my cup holder (where my stainless steel coffee cup was rattling), and my glove box.  It is thin enough that it doesn't take up any space, but does the job of silencing vibrating keys, flashlights, coffee cups, and similar items very well.
summary: Too small for much of a car, but worked great on my water pump's box.

reviewText: For me the time and effort to install this product is not worth the benefits, if any. A trunk installation requires two mats, but I tried it with the one I had. If you don't mind sizing and installing contact paper, then you may not mind installing this sound deadening mat. There seems to be some reduction in sound from the trunk, and most likely a second mat would have produced better results.The 3M mats would probably work best for smaller applications, like around speakers, and for those who like little projects and don't mind expending some time and effort to install the mat.

This mat is small, dense and self-adhesive. It's is designed for installing in your car to reduce road noise and around speakers for better sound quality. The package contains one mat that is a little over 2.5 sq. ft. The mat is perforated in half for smaller applications, but can be installed in one piece. It cuts easily with household scissors, but it does get adhesive on them so don't use your best pair for this project.Prepare the surface you are applying the mat to by cleaning well with alcohol and allowing to dry. Any hint of grease will affect adhesion. Also, the mat is stiff at lower temperatures. Heating it with a blow dryer makes it easier to apply and to cut with scissors.The real issue comes about when you must remove door panels, carpeting or the dash to install the mats. Even though the package estimates installation of one mat to be 15 minutes per door, 30 minutes per speaker and 30 minutes for the trunk, I think this is extremely unrealistic for the average car owner. Plus, you will need many more mats to apply it to all these locations for maximum sound reduction.After taking a look at my car doors closely and realizing I had no idea how to remove the inner panel, I decided that I had another completely different application for this mat that would be perfect and more within my skill set. I own a couple of serger sewing machines. These machines run at speeds of up to 1500 stitches per minute and are really loud. They also vibrate like crazy. I applied this mat on the table I serge on and the difference is very gratifying. Much quieter and very little vibration! Plus the surface of the mat keeps the machine from "dancing" around the table when sewing at high speeds.I can imagine many more uses for these mats and plan to get a few more for under my bench power tools, under my large food processor and under my stand mixer.
summary: Many, many uses for this product

reviewText: These sound proofing mats are extremely stiff. I wanted to use them in my vehicle's tailgate. I took the precaution of taking a hair dryer out to warm them up so they would fit securely since the flooring has some very wide grooves. Even with that these would not conform to the flooring, they lay on top.It would take several more purchases in order to cover the whole area; there are numerous other products out there that seem more reasonable in cost. With this partial coverage there is no difference in the sound level and I have no confidence that these will stay on with the constant loading and unloading of items, since they refuse to stick to the whole flooring, but just the tops of the wide  grooved surface - wish they would state that surface must be completely flat. It does show the mat bending to the curve and bumps of a door in their directions - sure didn't work for me.
These are nice and bright and stand out even in daylight. The only thing That I found is, in cold weather during winter time, one of the lights would flicker.

Before I start this, there are cheaper alternatives on amazon with more bulb quantity, but dont give into temptation like I have in the past. Those are cheap, too "blue" and half of them dont work. ORDER THESE INSTEAD YOU WILL BE MUCH HAPPIER!I bought these to replace side marker lights in an S2000 and they worked perfect. They are very bright and are almost a pure white. Id say theyre in the 5000K range which is white with a hint of blue, but no where near the blue range. All of them lit up perfect and also looked great when I replaced the bulbs in the gauge cluster of '98 Camry.These are also almost the same size as OE bulbs so you shouldnt have any problems with these being too long. I will definitely order from this seller again.
summary: ALMOST A PERFECT WHITE, BUILT WELL, AND EXTREMELY BRIGHT

reviewText: Exactly what I needed. I've been replacing all my bulbs with LEDs where I can. They work and have great color.

One thing with these white LED bulbs - they do give a sort of "pinkish" color to a red parking light (rear) on my 2005 TSX. But that is not the fault of the bulb - red lens and you're supposed to use red LED. But for my front door lights, they are excellent - very bright. So bright that I have to remind myself not to stare at these bulbs when opening the door - especially at night.

Just installed these yesterday and they are nice and white, but not as bright as I'd hoped.  I'm also curious to see how long they will last.  The price is decent and will probably buy again if need be.  Overall I'm satisfied with this purchase.
summary: Satisfied, but not as bright as I'd hoped

reviewText: They do warn before you buy to see if the light would fit. I measured and thought I had enough room. I managed to fit it in for my license plate lights. I had to bend it slightly but it works. The light is bright and makes my wrx look a bit more modern. I don't like the older yellow lights

Good light, super white and bright. The only downside is that they seem to have a small quality control issue. I've bought about a dozen of these, and only LED on one bulb has burnt out in about 5 months. Used these in my reverse lights, tag light, and trunk light. Even with the one (barely noticeable) LED burnt out, still very pleased with this product.
I have these on my '05 impala and '04 Regal, both with the 3.8L engine.  Works great to replace the plastic elbows that always seem to leak and break.

I bought these elbows to replace my plastic oem one that crack. It is an excat fit and slides right into place. Very solid metal. No leaks from elbow either. And it cost just about the same as the plastic ones that break and crack over time from heat exhaustion. Would recommend product.

These were perfect. I replaced the coolant elbow on my 97 Lesabre with 3800 V6, and it worked perfectly. Time will tell if they last, but even if they don't, they shouldn't destroy themselves like the plastic ones; meaning I can just install a new O-ring and be good to go.

I ordered these to replace the plastic coolant elbows on my wife's 2001 Pontiac Grand Prix 3.8L. The plastic ones finally got too old to withstand the temperature and began cracking and leaking. If you've got a 3.8L GM motor and are loosing coolant but don't know where - it's most likely these little bad boys. These elbows go between the intake manifold and the belt tensioner (top), and between the belt tensioner and the block or the water pump (bottom - depending on model). There a couple of video's on YouTube that tell you how to replace these on various GM models, but the process is the same regardless of model or year, with few exceptions.Takes about an hour the first time you have to do it ;)These elbows are made out of quality aluminum and will most likely outlast the vehicle at this point. They are machined perfectly - I used a little liquid wrench on the o-rings so they would go in smoothly without tearing or sliding off their seat. Popped right in and the fit and finish is perfect.
summary: Great replacement for all plastic 3.8L GM coolant elbows

reviewText: If you own a Buick 3.8 engine you will need these elbows sooner or later to replace that cheap plastic junk that was originally equipped with 3.8 engines. They are not that difficult to install if you have some mechanical skill but should be combined with other service such as a water pump replacement. Best to plan now before next winter if you reside in cold weather states. If your running DexCool antifreeze it can be found at most WalMart stores at good prices. Good Luck.

This was my first steam cleaning machine and I wish I didn't wait so long to find out how useful they are. You can clean and sanitize so many surfaces without using any cleaning products so it is great for the pocketbook and the environment. Floors are a breeze and because it leaves them barely wet they dry in no time.Overall the HomeRight Steam Machine is well designed, easy to use and has attachments for a large variety of chores. I like that there is a compartment on the machine to store all of the smaller attachment and adapters. If you fill it with 40oz. of water it will produce steam for 45 minutes but also included in the manual is the information that 26oz. will run for 30 min and 13oz. for 15 minutes. That is handy when you just want to do a small job. It takes only about 8 minutes for it to heat up.I had one particular chore in mind when I ordered this steamer. My 2005 Weber Performer grill had years of baked on grime inside the kettle and I had just been cleaning the grate with a wire brush so it needed some attention too.  It did a great job and there is no better way to clean your grill grate than steam and the included brass brush.  You can order replacement brushes and attachments directly through the HomeRight web site.There is one flaw in the design though, the handle has a ribbed hard plastic grip that is uncomfortable and it is best if you wear a work or rubber glove if using for an extended period. That is the only reason I gave it 4 instead of 5 stars. The manufacturer really needs to redesign that.
summary: Compact, easy to use and versatile

reviewText: Let's go over some of the basics of this machine.It provides steam.  Steam can be very helpful in the cleaning/removal of a lot of things.  It comes with a lot of attachments, and some general attachments as well.  We found the floor attachment to basically just heat/dampen a microfiber cloth, not really that great.  However the wallpaper removal one has had good success, as well as a few of the more general tips/extensions.It does take a few minutes to heat up, and then needs to be emptied after use.  It should also be noted that distilled water is recommended to be used, although the manual says that other water can be used (in our case we have a reverse osmosis filter, so we used that).My biggest complaint is storage of all the accessories.  Some fit in the machine, which is great, but a lot don't, and combined with the hose, etc it means you kind of have a mess wherever it is sitting.It's a good cheap way to get steam power for cleaning, and if you have tile/stuck wallpaper/annoying stains, it might help you out.
summary: Small, lots of accessories, provides Steam

reviewText: I was wary about the ability of the HomeRight C800880 SteamMachine On-Demand Power Steamer and Wallpaper Remover when I got this considering my previous experience with a brand-named steam cleaner (my reviews for a McCulloch MC1246 Portable Steam Cleaner) which was disappointing. And was I wrong! The HomeRight C800880 was right on the money when you need an efficient, high-performance steam cleaner. For those shunning away from chemical cleaners, steam is the ONLY alternative to give you an all-around cleaning initiative. The HomeRight C800880 gives you the results you need from a powerful steam cleaner that holds and maintains the high temperature and superheated status of the steam.My impressions:Power: the 1500-watts boiler of the HomeRight C800880 gives you the steam power you need to tackle a variety of cleaning jobs. Soap scums and hard water stains in the bathroom and kitchen, "baked-in" grime on your stovetop and oven, goes away like it wasn't there. What's amazing is that the HomeRight C800880 was able to maintain the superheated status of the steam thereby save you time in your cleaning chores because the boiler is powerful enough to give you very hot steam in an extended period of time. The waiting in-between for the machine to build up pressure to create very hot steam is minimized.Portability: the HomeRight C800880 is light and small enough to be carried or pulled around your home where you need it to tackle your cleaning chore. The wheels and the handles gives you the mobility you need to move around with the steamer to tackle your cleaning jobs with minimal difficulty.Attachments: the HomeRight C800880 has a complement of attachments to address a variety of cleaning chores: a nylon brush, a brass brush, wallpaper steam plate, floor steam mop with cleaning cloth, a squeegee and a jet nozzle. The 8-feet hose and the 8-feet power cord is long enough to give you that reach to accomplish your task with minimal movement of the main steam unit. You are pretty much covered regardless of where you want to clean and sanitize in your home.For its size and weight, the HomeRight C800880 packs a cleaning power packs power comparable to other similar, larger units. Although the manual stated that the waiting time for this unit to build up steam is 8 minutes, I found that 10-12 minutes of waiting time builds more pressure and the steam more super heated to give you a much more powerful cleaning objective. Very pleased at this little steamer. It has exceeded my expectations in every way.
summary: On demand cleaning power right at your finger tips!

reviewerName: Mr. Deeds "Opportunity is limited only by ima...
reviewText: The manufacturer got it right with the HomeRight SteamMachine - and ours gets a workout throughout the year.It's very simple to setup - just add water and plug it in. There is an attachment for practically every chore I need it for:* Cleaning the tile floors (we have two wild dogs)* Cleaning my BBQ grill* Cleaning the glass of the pellet stove in winter* Cleaning the stove (inside and out)* Cleaning the bathrooms - bathtubs, showers, sinks, floorsThe unit is compact and light, so it's easy to move about the house. But it delivers high-pressure power that cleans every surface put to task. A very well-made, well-designed little steamer.
summary: Big cleaning power in a small package

reviewText: This is one cool machine, definitely one of my favorite cleaning tools. I have not used it for wallpaper yet, only for cleaning but I am so pleased with it.  I have cleaned sinks, toilets, doors, showers, floors.  It came with a very detailed, illustrated manual so it was easy to get it ready for use.  It has lots of attachments to use and they are both illustrated and described in the manual so you know what they are for.  Strong pressure and I was surprised how long you can use it before having to refill the tank. I haven't even had to refill it on the projects I've used it for because they've all been under 30 minutes and I still had water to go when finished that I ended up draining before storing it.  My spouse started using it willy nilly without reading the manual on what not to use it on and ended up stripping the paint off a door that didn't have a finish on it...so pay attention to what surfaces to avoid using it on (the manual details this).I would highly recommend this steam machine.
summary: Fantastic cleaning machine, great value for all you get with it

reviewText: Excellent Product:Tackles all of our cleaning challenges with great results.Pros:  Great to clean kitchen stains, rug stains, bathroom stains and even hard water stains.  Great set of attachments.Cons: Not many to speak of...if you follow the directions it works 100% perfectly.  Product does make you wonder how long it will last...but time will tell that.Our story is quite simple...we live in a home with 8 people and a small dog.  Things can get messy.  On top of that we have well water which is hard and destroys most of our faucets and shower heads.  Third, we cook a lot Indian food which can stain kitchen cabinets and tile caulk pretty easily.We first wanted to attack our kitchen...since we spend a lot of time in there.  Again, we cook a lot of Indian food and it can get quite messy and does stain almost everything it touches due to turmeric.  Our kitchen cabinets, unfortunately, are white.  We basically attached the included scrubbing brush and went to town on our cabinets.  While the stains did not disappear 100%, I can safely say that 90% of them were removed without scratching the surfaces.  EXCELLENT.Second - we decided that we would try this on the hard water build up around our shower heads (cheaper then replacing them)...much to our surprise this thing pulverized the calcium build-up and our shower heads were almost new again.  It also aided in removing the hard water spots that occur on faucets and shower doors... EXCELLENT.Third - rugs - dog - accidents - kids - accidents - stains :) - Yep...we hit all of our major spots on our carpets and I can say we had about 80% success there without using any chemicals.  Very Good.  I cannot blame the steamer because some of those stains are quite old and probably permanent at this point.Overall - with the quality of this machine, the included accessories, and the fact that the pressure is right and the thing cleans..I give it 5 stars.  Excellent.

I've received this as a 'for review' unit but the seller did not ask or even imply that a 'positive' review was expected in exchange.It worked well for most of our cars. Once connected it will:- display diagnostic codes- erase ALL codes- retrieve I/M readiness status- display the VIN number on 2002 or newer vehicles- rescanThe MS300 supports the OBD II or OBD2 (On-Board-Diagnostics II) system and it understands all OBD2 protocols that a car may use: PWM, VPW, KWP2000, ISO9041, EKWP2000 or CAN. Once the proper protocol is detected, the MS300 is ready to display whatever Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) the car computer's memory may be holding.It should be noted that:# it only retrieves codes already stored in the computer# it does NOT provide any 'real-time' monitoring# it is completely stand-alone and no Web-updates are possible# it does not have printing capabilities# it is powered through the car's own DLC (Data Link Connector)In my case, I was able to diagnose within minutes the source for the 'Service Engine Soon' warning on my dashboard:P0442 - EVAP Emission Control System Leak (Small)I erased the codes and, if the warning reappears, I will know EXACTLY what to tell the technicians._________________________________________Note:It did NOT work on our Honda Insight 2010, a hybrid. No matter how many times I try, all I get is a 'LINK ERROR'.
summary: Excellent tool, manual needs some editing

reviewText: I have always wanted one of these but always thought they cost hundreds of dollars.  As a woman I know that I am a target for any dishonest repair shop, and not knowing I am familiar with car mechanics they sometimes lie to me about what my car needs.So for that reason alone, I was delighted to get this small but powerful tool.  Now before I take my car in for maintenance I can scan its codes quickly and be prepared for the inevitable news that I need a lot more repairs on my car.  I can smile and drive off and leave them looking confused and puzzled when I don't take the bait.  Not to slam all repair shops but I have run into some heavy duty attempts at conning me into paying for repairs my car doesn't need.I carry this with me in my car, especially on car trips, for those scary times when I'm on the road and the check-engine light comes on.  I also keep the manual in my car so I can diagnose the code by the side of the road and decide if it's safe to keep driving.This just plugs in, and you push the button and read the codes, or lack of them.  It's simple and fast to use.  When I used to buy and sell used cars I could have used this.  The repair manual is complete with hundreds of codes and descriptions for whatever readout you get.  You will need to write down your code when you get it, and compare it with the manual to see what it is indicating.I love how this will also check the emissions control system, and the air conditioning system.On my 2012 Accura the plug is right there under and to the left of the steering wheel. It's not even in the dash or in a compartment, so it's simple to find it and plug this in.  You plug this in while the key is turned so the dash lights come on but the car is not running, to activate the cars electrical system.  This requires no batteries.To test how accurate this is, I dislodged the gas cap and tested my car with this.  Sure enough it gave me the code for a problem with the gas line.  I can promise you this works and is accurate based on my test of it.How they can sell this small computer at this price I have no idea, and the 40 page manual that comes with it is amazing, giving you hundreds of codes and which parts need replacing. I am thinking the price must be wrong here.I have taken back control and empowered myself when I go to a car repair shop with this.
