It's my new secret weapon and I love it.I was supplied with a free sample which did not affect my review.  This is a great product at an amazing price.
summary: Keep this in your Car Emergency Kit:  Read Your Own Check Engine Light Codes

reviewText: Our car computers hold SO much information but the message we, as consumers, receive is a little yellow engine light that frankly incites so much fear that, when I see it, I want to pull over and dial 911 before my car bursts into flames. Sure, I've been told that sometimes it is nothing more than reaching a magic number on the odometer or any number of tiny other things, but that engine light is still so vague and yet so terrifying...and that's what the dealership wants. Terror. I called the dealership about my engine light and a "diagnostic reading" was $150 then they could tell me what needed to be done. So that engine light, that may have popped on for nothing more than me crossing some imaginary mile, could cost me $150 for nothing more than to have them to turn it off. And God forbid you just leave it on...try selling a car with the engine light on. Tell your buyer "it is just the mileage indicator".This plugs right into your car under the dash on the drivers side. A meaningless fault code will appear on the little screen. And even if you don't have the fault code guide book right with you, you can type that exact code into Google. Well, any time i have ever done it anyway, it gave me the meaning and diagnosis of the engine light. This also gives you the option of turning the d--- thing off. So if it is a "just wanted to let you know you've driven 50k miles" light, you don't have to drop a couple of bills getting the dealer to explain that.I've used one of these for years when I've had less-than-new cars. This one was sent to me for test and review. Currently I don't have any check engine lights or problems. I plugged it in anyway and it appears to work fine. I am at 41000 miles, so if I get that idiot light at 50k and this product doesn't work, I will update. But DEFINITELY invest in one of these if you have a car that isn't under a full bumper to bumper warranty in your family. It will save you far more than it costs.

I'm a big fan. Quite by coincidence, the manufacturer of this device offered me a sample about a week after my CEL came on. The following is my honest opinion.So many of us have been there - you're driving along quite happily and suddenly your dashboard gets a little brighter. As you notice exactly WHICH light came on, it suddenly becomes a burning stare of gloom, an automotive Medusa. Okay, I'm being dramatic, but it seriously makes for a crappy day. A week later, this little guy came in the mail, and following the relatively well-written and simple instructions, I plugged it in and started reading.Turns out my code isn't the end of the world - something to do with one of my fuel system gaskets that is either going to be an $80 or $120 part. But still, unless you have your code read (I know autozone does this for free but I don't have one near me) by a mechanic, you're driving blind, so to speak. Another nifty feature is the code reset. Just for kicks, I reset my codes and hey presto - off goes the CEL. Of course about 50 miles later it was tripped again (if only resetting codes would magically fix the problem) but it's nice to know it works. You can also read your VIN number which is handy, especially if you're buying a used car and want to make sure everything matches up!Overall, this is definitely worth the modest price. It works very well, has a small profile (I keep it in the glove box) and the cable is long enough to be used while sitting in the driver's seat. Definitely recommended without reservation.

With my former car, I got complacent with the dealer repairs and paid dearly.  The fee for diagnostics at a dealer is high - up to $200, which of course can be negotiated down but what a hassle.  Worse, much worse is that the role of diagnostics and that of repair if vested in the same party can lead to abuse.Put another way, those that deal with customer service and don't even see which mechanic works on the car are gamblers in a losing game.  You can get away with it sometimes but it will catch up with you.  For that reason, people need their own diagnostic tool that can read error codes.  The book that comes with this diagnostic tool tells what the error codes mean.This device is great.  No battery needed - it uses the car's electrical system (without the motor running).  It plugged into my car with no problem.  Sample was provided.

This diagnostic fault code scanner tool has proven to be a very valuable tool so far. This scanner connects to the 16 pin connector that is in most newer vehicles. To tell if your vehicle is OBD II compliant and able to be read with this scanner tool then you will either need to locate the 16 pin data link connector if you are familiar with what it looks like or you can check the car or trucks emission control information label. Most of the time the data link connector can easily be found under the dash and it very simple to access. I had no problem locating the connector on my 2002 Mitsubishi Lancer OZ Rally Edition.Our check engine light has been on for years and the dealer has told us that it's nothing to worry about and that it's just something to do with the catalytic converter. They have turned it off several times but it always comes back on. I always wanted one of these scanner tools so I can read the error codes on my own but they were always more money than I was prepared to spend for one. At it's current price this scanner is extremely affordable and I am pretty sure it cost less than any others I have seen so far.This tool seems well made and very durable. The scanner is in a hard plastic case that can take a lot of abuse. The cable is thick and strong as well and about 3 feet long so it's plenty long enough to connect and sit in the car with it in your hands while you use it. The 16 pin connector on the end fits perfectly into the data link connector in my car. It doesn't have any batteries to replace and the LCD screen is back-lit and powered by your car or truck. The screen is bright green and very clear and easy to read.The manual is lengthy but it's very clear and easy to read as well. It contains all of of the definitions that you will need to interpret your fault codes. I did a quick scan of the manual but I could have figured it out without the manual because it's so simple to operate. Simply plug it in and turn your ignition switch to on but don't actually start your car. It will take a minute or two to initialize and read your car's computer. Once it's complete you can go into option 1 and get a list of every fault code that has been recorded. Once you have your codes you can look them up in the manual and find out what the problem is. This function works perfectly.If you go into option 2 then you can delete all of the fault codes that are recorded in your car's computer. I love option because I always had to disconnect the battery for a few minutes in order to clear the computer. You really can't do no harm by deleting the codes because if there is still a problem then they will be recorded again and your service engine soon light will illuminate after several trips in your car. This option works perfectly as well.Option 3 will perform a systems diagnostic and test the operations of the emissions control system. This might be important if you are trying to get your car to pass a emissions test.Option 4 will provide the VIN number if your car or truck is compatible with this function. My car isn't compatible with this option so I am unable to test it.Overall I think this tool is awesome and anyone who works on cars or trucks will appreciate it. It was a welcome addition to my toolbox and one of the most useful tools in my garage.Sample provided for review.
summary: One of the most important tools in my garage. Affordable, well made and works perfect

reviewText: The DB Power Autel OBD-2 code reader is a small solid basic code reader. The device can read codes, save a snapshot of the codes, and reset the codes - all pretty standard features of a code reader. The control package is rugged, the buttons and LCD have a membrane cover. This is for the backyard mechanic that will do occasional reads, it is not a commercial reader, one that an auto mechanic would use every day. All that said, this is still a solid device with heavy insulation on the wire and good strain relief. For the price, this is extremely well built.The cable is just over two feet long - exactly the right length to plug in the analyzer and sit in the driver's seat. The LCD is backlit with reasonably sized characters. The two buttons have a solid distinct sound when they are pressed.The instruction manual is excellent. There is a long preface about OBD, the abbreviations used, and the caveats for which era of cars will work with the analyzer (the simple answer, if your car is newer than 1988, you can probably read the codes.Using this device couldn't be easier - turn off the car, plug in the connector, turn on the ignition (without starting the car - the battery light will be lit up on the dashboard), press enter on the scanner. There is nothing more to do. When finished, turn off the ignition and unplug the scanner. There's no reason to overcomplicate using this.The OBD connector is easy to find in most newer cars - the Federal government requires the plug be within a short distance of the steering column. Unlike most things in a car, these connectors are in a similar location. You might want a flashlight to find the plug. Sometimes the sockets are covered by a flip down panel.This tool only reads stored codes. It does not do real time reading. It does not read additional data like some of the USB / wireless readers.I tried this on a variety of cars and managed to reset a code on one car. Bottom line - the thing flat out works. I fully expected it to work easily on a 2002 Buick Rendezvous and a 2012 Ford Focus (I was able to read the VIN on both of these cars). I expected the Mercedes to not work at all - I have read that there are odd things about Mercedes that doesn't fit standard. Well in fact it worked perfectly on a 1999 Mercedes E320. Vin number for Mercedes is not supported. There are numerous cautions in the manual about certain compatibility issues with Japanese and European cars - that is for very old cars. Current production cars will have no problems with this analyzer. If your car does not scan - more than likely you had the ignition on before plugging in the meter, or you have the engine running. I did not expect the analyzer to work on a Ford Focus Electric (this is a full battery electric, NOT a hybrid) - it in fact did not work, there is nothing to read on that car, it is zero emissions. The operative thing, with the electric, the tool went through every protocol and then showed an input error and stopped scanning. Exactly as I expected.Resetting codes was super easy. There is a menu setting to erase codes, after pressing enter, there is a Yes / No display. If you press Enter again, all codes are reset. If you press Scroll, the codes are not erased. I like the "are you sure" moment on the display. Yes / No is a weird thing to display - there is no button to press for No. After codes are reset, it will look like nothing happened. I rescanned, and the code remained. In order to see the actual reset or clear in of the code, you need to turn off the car and turn the ignition back on.The manual has a huge list of error codes. I was surprised to find the exact code from a Mercedes. I didn't expect to find that code in the book.This is a reasonably priced reader. For a backyard mechanic that knows which end of a wrench to use, this is a great tool. For the average person, this is probably a needless purchase - unless you understand cars pretty well it is difficult to do anything about those codes. For example - what would you do about a P0938 - Hydraulic Oil Temp Sensor CKT Range/Performance - code? Most of the codes are that cryptic to the average person. The only way the average person saves money with this is if they try to bypass set codes to pass an emission test (if your state requires OBD scan emission tests). If you are really going to repair a Check Engine light, a mechanic already has more sophisticated tools to read the computer, and that will be part of the cost of the repair (he isn't going to reduce the cost of the repair because you tell him the code is P0938, and he might want to check the hydraulic oil system).

Following the directions in the accompanying manual, I was able to use this device to scan the codes in my car's computer and read my vehicle's VIN. Although the nearby Pep Boys shop will run a FREE scan for me, having a scanner of my own is much more convenient and I can see the results myself without having them "interpreted" by the mechanic.The dealer where I bought my car new won't hook up a scanner for less than $100. This little gadget will certainly save me some bucks because I can identify the problem myself and have a good idea of what kind of repairs may be necessary before I take my car to the shop. If you have detected a problem and have fixed it yourself, you can reset the code that causes your engine light to come on. Not only does it scan the codes on my car, it also scans the codes on my Winnebago Itasca Sunova Model 33C motorhome. This scanner will be accompanying me during my travels in my coach to help us sniff out any troubles that come up.For anybody who wants to know what is going on with his or her car or other compatible vehicle, this scan tool is a reasonably-priced way to become informed.I was provided a free sample of this device in exchange for an honest review, which you have just read.
summary: Does What It Claims to Do

reviewText: Anyone who has driven a car for years has had that panicked feeling when the "check engine" light came on.  Is the car going to burst into flames?  Am I permanently damaging the engine by continuing to drive?  Should I pull over and call AAA or just limp home?I've been in that position several times, and then I had to blindly trust the repair guy at the shop when he brought me me the estimate with dollar signs in his eyes.  They charge me $80 for using a diagnostic machine like this one, plus parts and labor for whatever they say is causing the problem.  Even with a shop I mostly trust, I always feel like they push for repairs I don't really need.  I don't like feeling taken advantage of, or having to trust that I really need a new widget for $800.  This fault code reader will save me lots of money by letting ME decide whether the repair needs to be done now or later.This meter works on cars built after 1996, most of which are OBD-II compliant (they use the same type of plug for the meters, and the coding system for errors).  It plugs into an outlet that's found under the dash on the driver's side in most vehicles.  Mine was hanging right there in plain view when I looked under the dash.  You plug the meter in, then turn the ignition to "on" but don't start it.  The meter will do the diagnostic and then give you whatever codes it finds.  You can look in the meter's user's manual or online to see what the codes mean.  It's really that simple.On the meter's package, I read something I wouldn't have thought of myself.  If you're thinking of buying a used car, you can use this meter to check the soundness of the engine.  It will show you any hidden engine issues via the stored codes in the car's computer.  Brilliant!I don't have an error code to diagnose right now, but I did plug the meter in on my car so I'd be able to write a knowledgeable review.  I will love going to the repair shop next time and being able to tell THEM what the error code is.  If I know the code has nothing to do with an $800 widget, I won't be taken advantage of.I received a complimentary DB Power Engine Diagnostic Fault Code Reader for testing and review purposes.
summary: Figure out what that "check engine" light means before you take your car in for service

reviewText: First off I want to say that theDB POWER Car Engine Diagnostic Fault Code Reader Scan Scanner Tool OBD2 OBD II MS300worked perfectly in our 2009 Malibu.  It  works on OBD-II compliant cars built after 1996 (most of them are OBD-II compliant)  & will retrieve the VIN (Vehicle Identification No) on 2002 and newer vehicles that support Mode 9. When we try it in our 2004 Toyota Sienna & 2006 Civic, I will update my review with the results.One great idea on the packaging suggests you use this to identify any problems with a used car before you buy it.My husband & I were surprised how easy to use this Code Scanner is. The hardest part was getting under the dash to look for the data link connector (DLC). Trying to save my hubby a sore back, I suggested he  do an Internet search to find the DLC location for our Malibu. He decided to look for it first & found it quickly under the dash & centered under the steering wheel. Following the easy-to-understand manual, he hooked it up & continued to follow the step by step instructions. We didn't expect to find anything wrong with our Malibu...and when the scanner's LCD screen didn't show any diagnostic trouble codes (DTC) we knew we were correct. To make sure the scanner was actually working, I decided to check for the VIN number. The VIN number showed up on the screen, so I'd say this code scanner works as promised.I've been told that some car part shops will hook up a scanner for free, but it's nice to have your own. If you're on the road & your car breaks down, this scanner could save you from being ripped off. Also, if you plan on buying a used car, hook this code scanner up to it to check the car for any problems before you buy it.I'll update my review & let you know if it works on  our 2004 Toyota Sienna & our 2006 Honda Civic.No batteries needed.Limited One Year WarrantyUPDATE: 2004 Toyota Sienna...the DLC (it's white)  is located under the dash, slightly to the left of  the steering wheel.  This code scanner worked for our Sienna (no problems were found); however the VIN is not supported.review sample provided

reviewText: The Autel MaxiScan OBDII scan tool requires no batteries and is easy to use. First - read the user manual as it is very good. After that, refer to your car's manual to find the location of your car's OBDII port (if you do not know where it is), plug the scanner in, then follow the user manual to use the scanner. This is a good scanner for cars built from 1996 on as cars since then have been required to have an OBDII port.If you lose your manual, one is available for download from various websites (just search for 'Autel MS300 manual') though the link on Autel's website seems to be broken at the moment. Still, a complete pdf copy of the manual was available in several other places.Before I plug the scanner into my car's port, I turn the car on to make sure that all accessories are turned off (radio, a/c, heater, fan, GPS, etc...) and then I turn the car back off. This ensures that there is no unexpected power variance from accessory use while the scanner does its thing. Then, with the engine OFF but your key in the ignition switch:* Plug in the scanner's OBDII cable into your car's OBDII port* Turn the ignition key only to engage the electrical system; do not turn to engage the car's starter* Press the Enter button (blue button on the left) and the unit will begin its scan* Once scanned, press the Scroll button (blue button on right) to see if the scan found any issues* If codes exist, the manual has a very detailed list of scan codes and description for you to reference* Turn the ignition key back to the off position, remove your key and remove the scanner's cable from your car's OBDII portThis scanner does not require any batteries to operate as it works from the power supplied by your car's battery via the OBDII port connection. It communicates with your car's central processing hub which collects information from the electronic control units of the major systems within your car (that is what the 'CAN Protocol' reference is about). However, to use it and to read results from it, the unit needs to be plugged into the OBDII port in your car... so you should keep some paper and pencil handy when using it.Our local dealership charges $80 just to plug their scanner into our car's OBDII and perform this diagnostic, so this Autel MaxiScan will save me that much each time that I need to use it. Additionally, I found the readout's black lettering to be easy to read against the backlit background,The last page of the users manual notes that this Autel MaxiScan device has a one year limited warranty, and that all warranty issues are handled directly with Autel through their website. If an issue arises before that period expires I will return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. We did receive this product gratis from the seller and have put it through the paces to objectively find out how well it performed. My statements here reflect that testing.If you are looking for an OBDII scanner of this style and size, for use as I have described above, then I recommend this one highly based on its ease-of-use and excellent user manual.Go for it.
summary: Autel MaxiScan MS300 OBDII Car Engine Diagnostic Scan Tool - CAN Protocol - Easy to use - No batteries required

reviewText: I love that this scanner requires no batteries - it works off your car's power. It's cheap and a good thing to have on hand should your check engine light come on. I know AutoZone will test your car at no charge, but the check engine light has to be "on" for them to do so. Some mechanics will charge you $79 on up to check your codes.This is easy to use once you find your car's diagnostic port (usually under or near the steering wheel under the dashboard). I think the manual that comes with this leaves a little to be desired, I found more info on how to use this by watching the Autel YouTube videos.It doesn't work on all cars - and I don't know why it doesn't. It appears to me that cars built in Japan have less success with this. I tried more than once and got a LINK ERROR for my 2010 Toyota Yaris. I never got it to work with my car--I've had no CEL warnings though. I also tried it on a friend's 1996 Chevy Lumina that has had several CEL warnings recently, it gave me the code numbers to look up, cleared the codes, and a few days later the CEL came on again...so it clears the codes, but not permanently. ~~~~ sample received for evaluation ~~~~

reviewText: This is the best funnel I have found to service the cooling system on my truck. You can fill the cooling systems with this funnel locked down, so you can keep coolant in the funnel while the engine is running, and as the coolant goes down you can add more coolant. Once the air is out of the system, you can put the plunger into the funnel to stop it up, remove the funnel and put the extra coolant back in the jug. Just set the funnel into the jug and pull the plunger up, all the extra coolant will empty into the jug. I wish I had purchased one of these years ago. It also comes with all the adapters needed to service all makes of cars and trucks.

I drained and flushed my cooling system this Saturday and after I was done I noticed my engine was running a tad bit warmer than it was prior to the coolant flush and refill.  After diagnosing the issue I was sure I had a large air bubble some where in the system.This funnel is exactly what I needed.  Today I got home and waited for the car to cool back down.Took the radiator cap of and put on the appropriate adapter (each cap adapter has a corresponding plastic insert that goes into the radiator opening, look for the matching letter on both the adapter and insert.  Put the adapter over the insert and lock it on.  Now put the funnel into the adapter and now it's ready to use.I put the plastic plug rod I to the funnel to stop the flow and filled it half way with coolant.  I started the car and put the heat up tot he highest temp and turn the blowers to the lowest setting.  I took out the plug rod and some of the coolant got sucked into the radiator.  There was still a fair amount  in the funnel.The engine reached it's temp, I let it idle a 2500 rpm and burp!  Air started to be released into the funnel and more coolant was drawn in.  When I was done I put the plug rod back into the funnel and carefully removed it and placed the funnel into the coolant bottle and released the plug.  It was the cleanest "Spill Free" coolant task I've ever done thanks to this funnel!
summary: Received it today and already love it!

reviewText: i bought this in the hope it would work with the Bluetooth torque app and it works flawlessly as a car lover i would like to see what my cars doing(boost,temp,torque,engine load,) and this works perfect simple to set up for anyone thinking about doing gauges this is way simpler and customizable.

Thanks to all the other reviews, I've put one of these through it paces with Torque Pro.  It talks to my Droid 2 phone without a hitch tested over 10 hours _each_ driving a Toyota Corolla 2003 and MX-5 2011. Some data sent to Torque were available from my car dashboard such as rpm, speed, engine temperature, gas level, and trip odometer reading; they were identical to Torque so I presume all the other data provided was true: engine load, MPG, 02 sensor voltage and many more. I do not have an MPG computer on my cars, and this provides one, at the least.  I had to calibrate it but its now spot on, less than 1 MPG off when compared to manual calculation of filling a tank to full against miles driven from last full fill.  The engine load values and instantaneous MPG reading help me further 'tune' my driving style to maximize gas mileage.I don't know how long this dongle will last, but for $12 it does everything Torque asks of it, and Torque warns that many clones of the original product [ of which this is one] malfunction or transmit wrong values over time.Two minor annoyance are it has no off-on switch so the device is on all the time once installed, even with the key out of the car.  The LED face the wrong direction when mounted on my cars, its either flat against a wall or dashboard so you can't see it.Note, Torque free does not work as cleanly as Torque Pro.  Bluetooth pairing did not work reliably [ I had to manual find the device sometimes], if it did work it took a long time to complete and some dials didn't work as smoothly or quickly and may give the wrong impression of how well Torque Pro really works.  With Pro, I just pop the Vgate dongle into the OBDII and turn the app on, and it locks on quickly and reliably, on both my cars.
summary: Does what it supposed to do

reviewText: This is a do-it-yourself kit designed for anyone who'd like to add these color lighting effects to the interior of their vehicle. There are 2 panels of LED lights which you connect to the controller and power via a connection to a DC/cigarette lighter adapter or the vehicle battery. It's got a modular connection design, so you can connect additional LED panels and extension cables if you wish. There is tape and velcro for you to secure the cables, though the cables are hard to keep hidden and the controller remote requires direct line of sight for the signal to work. The installation instructions seemed a bit incomplete but overall were adequate for me to get everything hooked up. The cable connections have arrows for you to align and it is recommended to use electrical tape to secure the connection between the controller and the DC adapter [that connection is loose unless you do something to secure it]. For novices, using the DC plugin power adapter is preferrable to trying to hook the wires directly to a battery. Oddly, the kit recommends professional installation even though it seems to be marketed for do-it-yourself installation.The main problem I encountered during installation was that it wouldn't power on until I opened up the remote control battery compartment and discovered that the battery had come installed upside down. Once I flipped it into the correct position everything worked fine and I got to enjoy the colored lights. This is a simple way to add colored lighting in your vehicle, while a true do-it-yourself veteran could probably obtain needed components to install something similar at a lower cost. This kit might contain either more than you need or less than you require for the amount of lighting that you intend to install, so it may not be the best option for everyone.
summary: a kit to add LED color lighting inside your vehicle

reviewText: The lights are amazingly bright!  These are the "water proof" lights so they can go outside as opposed to the others.The kit came neatly packaged and included everything required to install in a car, truck, boat, RV, etc.  However, the directions are just adequate because they look like a photo copy of a photo copy, so the graphics are fuzzy.  You have to use pliers to crimp the power wires to the cigarette lighter adapter that is included with the kit.  When I first hooked it up, it wouldn't work but it did after I took the watch battery out of the remote and re-installed it.  Then everything worked great!  The remote allows you to change from bright white to many different shades of colors and brightness.  Since the remote is infrared, you have to mount the receiver sensor somewhere in line-of-sight for the remote to see it.Installation in a car is pretty simple with the two 1-foot light strips that are included.  Since the controller can handle up to 36 feet of light strips, I'm considering buying some extension light strips to mount under the awning of our RV.  You can get a 5-foot light strip for about $60 or a 10-foot light strip for about $100.  You can also get two 1-foot light strips with a 1-foot extension cable for about $23.  5-foot extension cables run about $11.
summary: Water resistant lights-very bright eye catcher

reviewText: I received a starter kit and installed them on my motorcycle.  They look nice, and it was a breeze to install.  They do not appear to be weather proof at all.  So you'll be taking a big chance with these on your motorcycle if you ride in the rain or store the bike outside.  And to be clear, these lights are not sold as weather proof.  I managed to get all the connectors tucked up out of the way of any rain or splashes.  Time will tell on that.

What you get . . . .2 LED light strips, each strip being about a foot long with 9 LED light emmitters attached equidistant along the strip.  Extension cables (a one foot, and a two foot) to string the two strips together in series as desired.  A Y-connector if you want to split the 2 strips in parallel to go 2 different directions.  The controller module/cable that the light strips plug into.  And the fused cable that the controller module plugs into.  This fused cable is then connected to any DC power source . . . boat, car, truck, motorcycle, garden tractor, combine, monster truck, and so on.  A cigarette lighter adapter is included for less permanent installations.  And of course the remote control unit to provide nearly countless combinations of color/fading/flashing styles.I installed mine up under the fuel tank on a motorcycle, attached to the underside of the frame rail, to illuminate the engine area when parked at night and I want to show off a little bit(electrical current draw on a single strip is super low, just a watt or two).This all goes together very easy, plug-in style, and hooks up to your 12VDC power source - hardwire it or use the cigarette lighter adapter.  By the way, this controller unit has the capacity to add many additional strips, totalling up to 36 feet.  LED lifespan is advertised to be 8-10 years @ 6-8 hours of use per day. Nuff said.The big challenge:  Operation is easy using the remote.  The only real challenge involves getting a clean installation look without exposed or dangling wires.  Not too hard to do with some pre-planning, especially since this is meant to be an indirect lighting source and the strips should be hidden (i.e. people should see the light but not the light strips . . . or the wiring).  Also note that the controller module needs to be installed more or less "line-of-sight" in order to receive signals from the hand-held infra-red remote control unit.Cool light kit, all self-contained. Not complicated and can be a lot of fun to plan and install.
summary: Good self-contained and versatile starter LED light kit

reviewText: Works with my iPhone 4s. Download app and connect.  I think it is much better than a standard scanner.  I am able to view variety of car information using this.

This small unit works well charging our iPads and Kindles, phones and iPods.I've had similar, smaller devices in the past that heat up quickly...one even started smoking and had to be tossed out of a moving vehicle. (The statute of limitations has passed on that littering charge, I hope). This charged my phones and iPad without getting too warm, so I feel better about it. My phone would charge in my car without this device, no problem. But my iPad wouldn't. So now I have that covered.Really wish I had gotten a larger unit so I could use it for camping or other useful devices. I may end up purchasing a larger one of these once I feel comfortable with the longevity of this one. So far, pretty good!

At just under 2 pounds, this 500 watt inverter works well for low/med draw items like charging laptops, phones, tablets etc. while it will run a few more power hungry devices, it's best to go up a version or two so you don't always use at max output.  Maximum AC output listed is 4.17 ampsNice modern design case vs many power inverters that have more industrial look about them.  Comes with both power socket plug and battery terminal clips with wire set for each.You must determine the draw of what you will be plugging into any power inverter, this is just right for your electronic charging needs (note some exclusions/cautions in owners manual) and even has two USB outlets (max available shared 2.1 amps but note not full 2.1A from both at same time) PowerBright customer service says you can get full 2.1 amps when only using one USB outlet at a time however...so for the most part you don't need to use your AC adapters if you don't want.Update on the USB outlets;Seems they are 2.1 amps but only charge at the slower DC rate like hooked to a computer and not the fast AC rate like a wall adapter.  Of course using your AC wall charger in the EN500 outlet will get you fast charge as normal.I need to experiment with different USB cables to see if I can get the EN500 USB outlet to fast charge rate...  a slight chance since there are two versions of USB cable out there, one for power only and one for power and data communitcations.  Chance that power only cable will work better with the EN500 but not tested yet.  Have tested this with OTHER power sources/devices and it changes between AC/DC.Keep in mind if you are going to power a higher draw device, you really need to use the supplied wires with clips for direct battery attachment as the interior power outlet is not rated for heavy loads for longer periods or higher peak startups .Calculate what your devices use before you attempt to use them with the inverter.  Most devices will state amperage draw  on their labels.If what you need to use on regular basis draws more toward the max output, I recommend you go to at least the next size up or whatever output works at less than maximum ratingBuilt in cooling fan turns on at 158 F internal case temperatureEN500 has auto shut down under these conditions;Low battery voltage (10.5v)OverloadInput voltage too highOverheatedOutput short circuitThere is also a built in fuse to protect the inverterEN500 is not waterproof and needs to stay dryBe sure to read your owners manual for all cautions and warnings before use.  User manual also available to read in .PDF form at the Energizerpower web siteSold under the Energizer brand but manufactured and warranted by the PowerBright company, See the PowerBright web site for warranty claims or phone number in owners manual.Used within it's limits it will do a good job for you, used outside of it's limits you are asking for problems.
summary: 500 watts of power in a user friendly case... buy the model that best fits your power requirements

reviewText: I never paid much attention to these kinds of products.  A while back I received a power adapter for the car that was very small.  I think it was Amazon Basics.That product made me realize how invaluable things like that can be.  However, when charging my phone on that particular device it would barley make a dent in it.  For instance, I could be driving for ten minutes and if I unplugged it, it would still beep low battery at me.I have not had that problem with this product.  Its pretty much like plugging in my phone at home and I like that very much.I have never hooked it up to a battery so I can't really comment on that.Its pretty sizable so its not something your probably going to want to leave plugged in inside your car at all times, depending on how much neat freak you are or where you live I guess.  I don't consider this a con as I believe to get the power the size probably directly relates.I can recommend this product.

There are a variety of ways to recharge iPhones and iPads from lighter sockets in one's car, but it's a little tougher to recharge a laptop computer on the go. This is a great solution. Plug this Inverter into the car lighter socket, then plug in my MacBook Pro to recharge while I drive. In the meantime, I can also connect the iPhone and iPad via the USB sockets and have them recharging at the same time. The only downside is that there is no lighter socket passthrough so I can't plug in my bluetooth phone speaker at the same time. That would be the only addition that I'd suggest.The overall unit works nicely and I haven't noticed it getting warm when running my computer gear (none of which admittedly draws nearly the amperage that this could provide). The lighter plug provided is a little tight for a standard socket, and getting it plugged in was tough at first. Wires are also provided so that the unit could be attached directly to a 12v battery should that be your desired setup.

This is a decent power inverter to power many AC devices, including charging a laptop and also accessories the require USB power. it is fairly compact, but at least the unit I received had some defects in the casing at least and I wish to point out that it not made by the Energizer Bunny people, but under license. This or may not lead to quality issues that may be typified by the flaws I observed in the case. I will post photos when I can. However, that being said, I believe that this unit has good quality and will probably serve you well.this unit has battery clips and also a cigarette lighter plug -- but you have to change them by unscrewing the posts on  the back.If the fuse blows on the unit for some reason, it is inside the cigarette lighter plug.

Let's get right to my biggest complaints:1.  Opening the packaging is not fun.  Companies should realize this and do something to make life easier for the people buying their stuff.2.  This thing smells INCREDIBLY foul for several days after opening it.  Imaging going to a auto parts store - and a tire store - extracting their odors.  That's what Energizer did here, and then they dumped said extract all over this gadget.  I left it out in my shed for several days before even using it.3.  The blue light on the front is WAY too bright.  It's obnoxious - you can't even look at it without a burning, searing pain in your retina.Once it was self defumigated, and I could use it...well, it works very well.  It's quiet, and it does exactly what it's intended to do.  Depending on if you have any kind of AC cords with special plugs/transformers built in, be sure to notice that the AC plugs are slanted in and down - directly over the USB ports if the cord has a "brick" at the end.I had no problems with any of the outlets - the operation was silent, the blue light was blinding, and power was supplied to everything I tried.  One other note:  I used a couple of low-power devices via the AC adapter that had LCD panels - and the LCD panel on the device wasn't steady as when plugged into a standard AC outlet.  For lower powered devices, you may need a line conditioner - my assumption was that this power inverter wasn't supplying the power steadily and evenly, but I didn't get the voltmeter to be completely sure.Overall, it's a good inverter with a couple of weird problems that would make me shop around a bit for something of equal quality to see if the competition had "solved" the problems.  It's a good inverter, about on par with others I've used in the past.
summary: Open it and leave it outdoors for a couple days

reviewText: This item works just as described! I like it for the uses it offers and I'm grateful I bought it.

If you are on the  go and rely on electronics you will need this product to make sure their is power.  The item may appear a bit bulky, but depending on the layout of your vehicle, it can easily be mounted (is not part of the packaging).  However, since it obtains power from your cigarette lighter if offers a very portable solution.  In addition to USB plugs, it also offers power plugs for that laptop or other device which has a traditional power plug.  While the item is very good, the one drawback is a cigarette plug option.  This is due to the main plug using the lighter and most users already use the lighter for various connections.  The lack of the lighter plug is more of a plus and may be offered in upcoming products.It promptly fires up and once turned on, you will notice a bright blue indicator.  Finally, in addition to your lighter it can also be connected directly to your battery.  A good alternative for those seeking to have sufficient power, especially while travelling.

Energizer 500W InverterThe most interesting aspect of this inverter is that it has a pair of USB ports. After reading more about it, it appears to be 2.1A shared between the 2 ports and is advertised as being iPad compatible. I know that my BlackBerry 9900 is a finicky smartphone that can only be charged using the included BlackBerry charger, Samsung S3 charger, PowerGen, or Motorola Droid2 chargers from my experience. The BB 9900 will not take a charge from any Belkin charger even if it is rated at 1A, 2A, etc... So I always include the BB 9900 in my charger tests.This Energizer inverter will not charge the BlackBerry using the USB port, although if you plug a charger into the A/C socket it could probably do it. The inverter's USB ports also charge my Samsung Galaxy S3 in USB mode, which means it isn't wired properly to charge in AC mode. My PowerGen and Belkin car chargers all charge the S3 in AC mode, so Energizer should have fixed that in their inverter from the get-go. The USB charging mode is limited in current output, while the AC charging mode is the full 1A current output that most adapters provide.The inverter only operates in 100W mode when plugged in via the cigarette lighter, mainly because most lighters are fused/rated for 10A-12A operation which at 13.2 VDC, ranges from 132-160W maximum and it is a safer idea to de-rate that down to approximately 100W. In order to get the full 500W capability, the Energizer inverter has to be clamped directly to the car's battery terminals. Energizer includes brackets and screws that could be used to permanently install the inverter somewhere in your vehicle. For example, a RV or camper with an auxiliary battery where you could tap into the inverter at your convenience.This inverter is also SIGNIFICANTLY larger than other typical inverters. It's about 2-3 times as thick which makes it bulky to pack.Overall: 4/5 stars, it would be 5 stars if Energizer fixed the USB ports so they would charge smartphones in AC mode as well as charge up some of the picky smartphones like the BB 9900.
summary: USB ports are listed as 2.1A shared, but isn't wired properly:won't charge BlackBerry and only charge in USB mode for my Android

reviewText: This unit is great for road trips - your devices will never be without power!  The USB ports are especially useful for keeping the entire family's cell phones charged while on the go.  It's a little large, but conveniently fits out of the way under the front dash area in my Lexus RX330.  The customer support is good too if you ever need it - Energizer stands behind this product.
took it camping and was real handy in recharging my iPad and phone. Haven't used anything bigger on it but small electronics worked fine.

This Inverter comes with both power socket plug and battery terminal clips with wire set for each. The LCD display on the unit tells me how much is being charged. The built-in cooling fan turns on at 158 F internal case temperature. In my usage, the fan never gets turned on. So, the whole unit runs silently. This is good as the fan itself will consume the battery power also.For people that mainly connects this inverter through cigarette lighter, I don't see good reasons to pick up this inverter, as the cigarette lighter connection limits the output powder to around 130W only. But then, on the end, it seems pretty awkward to connect the inverter to car battery under the hood while driving.This inverter along with a portable 12V deep cycle battery (the marine battery, not the typical car battery) is the main power source during my camping trips. It is connected to the 12V battery's terminal directly. So, I can get the 500W power if needed. I use this setup to run an air pump to inflate air beds. I use them to run the light bulbs for camping site lighting and inside-tent lighting. Also to use them to power stereo speakers for dancing party on the camp site. Of course, they are used to charge cell phones, tablets.This inverter has good safety features and it shuts down itself under following conditions: (1)input voltage is too low, (2)input voltage is too high, (3)output is overloading, (4)output is short circled, (4) or the inverter itself is overheating.In summary, this inverter works great for my application and I like its silent operation and safety features. I am not sure this 500W inverter is the best choice (from cost point of view) if the need is just for charging cell phone, laptop, camera, tablets. For that, I might go with a 150W inverter, which is cheaper, smaller and more portable.
summary: Silent operation with good safety features.

reviewText: Sturdy. Functions correctly to charge your device but be certain you buy a unit large enough to meet your expectations.  I have the smallest unit at 500W.  I can charge my phone and iPad but did not do my due diligence to ascertain what this unit is capable of since Watts are not necessarily the unit of power many are accustomed to using.  My simple desire was to be able to use a standard vacuum cleaner in cleaning the car without dragging out the 50 foot extension cord.  When I met with failure I  did the research and found that I need at least the 1500W unit.  Be aware that some devices have an initial power surge, so may require an even larger unit to handle that allowance.  The description might also allow you to think that all the units have an LED readout screen that gives you needed information. This lower power model does not.  It is somewhat larger than I anticipated for just being able to charge small devices. Also puzzling was that it comes with wires that allow you to connect it directly to your battery under the hood. I see the usefulness of this if you have a unit to power, say, a small TV for tailgating, but why would you hook it up to your battery to charge a small device like a cellphone or tablet? A useful and sturdy product, but crunch the numbers to understand what you really need.
summary: Useful but choose the size you need

reviewText: The Energizer 500W DC power inverter comes with 2 AC and 2 USB plugin ports and can be connected to your vehicle's battery power via a cigarette lighter plugin or battery clamps. You can charge or power multiple devices within the confines of what this inverter is rated for. If you have something that will need more than 500W continuous power or more than 1000W peak you should buy a different model inverter that has more power throughput capability. This one will show you its status as you are using it, and it seems to function fine when used properly. The only drawbacks I think could be addressed are the packaging (plastic that you have to cut and dispose of) and lack of a carrying handle or carrying case. This isn't too heavy but it could have been made easier to carry and included a protective storage case with a handle and recyclable packaging. Overall this is a good option if you have small appliances you'd want to use with your vehicle's power and also be able to power or charge USB devices, phones & tablets, etc.

Overall, this is a great power inverter.  I have the lowest model (500W), but that's plenty for the types of devices that I want to run from the car like a laptop, game console, and/or TV.  I also really like that this inverter not only offers your regular 'plugs,' but well-powered USB ports to free up the plugs for more standard things.While I haven't done it, I also really like that you can hardwire this thing straight to your battery and mount it inside the cabin.  For those looking for a more permanent replacement, this thing has even more advantages.  Its high build quality makes me believe it will last and make it worth the extra effort.In all, it's a great inverter.  My only recommendation -- and it's nothing against the product -- is to take a look at the types of things you want to run off of your inverter and make sure you buy the correct power.  500W is sufficient for light users, but tailgaters running blenders and such are going to need the bigger one.I received this from the manufacturer for testing and review and have shared my honest experience in this review.

reviewText: The Energizer power inverter is working flawlessly for us to recharge my laptop on the go.  For a KINDLE, or a TABLET or a CELL PHONE, do NOT waste the energy to convert from a DC source to AC through an inverter to just go back to DC again in the wall adapter charger - that's just a great way to waste energy needlessly.  Simply charge those types of devices directly via DC as long as the cables are available.Since I only have an AC charger for my laptop, it makes perfect sense to use this inverter to recharge my laptop battery - the price of the inverter is much less than the DC power cord and has additional functionality.  When we go on short trips now we're able to power up small fans on our dog crate, other possible uses would to be powera small portable stereo or small HDTV at the park (we have a LONGRoadPro RP-203EC 12V 12' Extension Cord with Cigarette Lighter Plugwhich is perfect in this case!)Be careful not to use this motors to power any device with larger motors, heating elements or to draw too much wattage by overloading the device.
summary: Excellent inverter at a good value in a range of wattages - beware higher wattages will drain a typical 12v auto battery QUICKLY

reviewText: This unit is relatively large (size of a can of ham) and lets you plug a standard 3 prong cord in so you can charge a laptop. There is also the option to use USB.The USB ports are shared, outputting a total of 2.1 amps, so if two units are plugged in, it will slow down any charging by half.There are two AC outlets. 500W continuous/1000W peak power output. This isn't a lot of wattage, so for example, you couldn't really run a standard hair dryer off it (they run around 1200 watts.)A thermal fan cools the unit as it charges.If you travel with a laptop or other unit requiring a standard AC outlet, this is useful as you don't have to have a 12v to DC cord for each unit and can use the standard power cord.
summary: Can charge a laptop wo USB or 12V lighter interface

reviewText: I had some plans for this that included a Vanguard GAEMS portable gaming system (suitcase with a 19" monitor in there that also mounts an Xbox or such inside for portable gaming).  The Xbox itself uses 175W, the monitor a fraction of that.  Yet this would power neither of them.  Not concurrently, nor individually.  Nada.I pulled my Harmony remote charging base in the car, tried that, and that would power, so I knew the inverter at least works, and isn't defective.USB charging worked for my tablets and my phone, although it's far more convenient for me to use my dual USB cigarette adapter for things like that, rather than the large box here.The other major complaint I had is the short cable for the cigarette lighter.  Give me something long enough to reach the back of my SUV where I'm more likely to have things set up that need AC power. The provided cable wasn't even long enough to reach from the center mounted dash cigarette jack to the armrest between the seats - a short straight shot.  I had just enough to reach to put the unit on one of the front seats, that was it.  And since not all vehicles have a rear mounted cigarette plug (something I think all auto makers should do) I have no else I can plug it in.Had it worked, I probably would've given it 4 stars, taking one off for the shot cord.  But since this 500W unit couldn't even power something at about 30W, let alone something that's only using 175W, it's completely useless.

Love this inverter.  It serves many purposes at once since you can charge something with a regular cord as well as USB cords at the same time.This is perfect for road trips, when the long drive drains your kindle, laptop, ipod, etc batteries.The USB port charges quickly, noiselessly and the unit is not overly large so it doesn't create a space problem in your vehicle.This is a product that I would definitely purchase again, extremely useful, well-made and would even make a great guy gift.

This 500 watt modified sine wave power inverter works either from the cigarette lighter adapter in your car or directly off a 12V battery.It converts 12 volt direct current battery power to 120 volt alternating current power so you can operate/charge low power devices such as lights, eReaders, iPods, cell phones, fans, laptops, etc.  It has 2 normal 120V outlets like you would find in your house, plus 2 USB power outlets.Items that worked successfully:A 60W incandescent light bulb, a 13W compact fluorescent light bulb, a Kindle Fire, an air filter / fan for the house, a camcorder battery charger, iPod charger, netbook laptop, 32" LCD TV, etc.  I confirmed that it does cut off power when the 12V battery drains down below 10.5V to protect the battery.I found that the inverter is too small to power a coffee maker.Pros:~Comes with both cigarette lighter adapter and alligator clip power cords, plus hardware to hard-mount it if you want to.~It's fairly light (2 lbs) and compact for use in the car.Owner manual is good.**The best thing about the unit is that it is completely SILENT almost all the time!(unlike my old one)**~The internal cooling fan did come on when operating at higher output levels, but is silent when charging batteries.Cons:~Couldn't power my 18V electric drill battery charger, but the instructions did warn that some battery chargers will not work with the modified sine wave format of this inverter.  A true sine wave would be needed.~No LCD screen on this model (EN500).This is a great product at a good price that works for most low power devices.  5 stars!

I was not expecting it to be as large or bulky as it is, but it is solidly built and works wellfor charging the small electronic devices that I need it for. Perfect size for charging cell phone, camera battery, laptop, tablet etc.I would recommend this product.

This is unbelievable, I thought I was buying from a reputable brand. This is my 2nd energizer (Or I guess Power Bright is their manufacturer) inverter. I got the 1st one earlier this week. It was returned the day it was received because one of the 120V wires coming off the main board hasn't attached, it had come off (It was holding on by 1 strand). The replacement came in today, first thing I checked was that wire through the grill slots, it was attached. Plugged it in to my car battery (via the attached clips), powered up just find. Attached a 50w LED work light (50 watts load at the plug, not 50 watts light output), worked just fine. Fan didn't power up. Attached a 175-200 watt load (my Dremel Rotary Tool, it pulls 1.5A (I've tested this with a DMM)) with the LED light. There was a sizable arc inside the unit. It continued to arc, followed quickly by a FIRE and a lot of smoke until I removed the positive terminal of the battery from it. Looked like a fool trying to blow through the fan opening to put it out, then quickly snapped a pic with my phone..unbelievable. This is suppose to have the usual safety circuitry built in , NONE of it worked as designed, it continued to short internally with my battery connected. This is a DANGER to anybody who uses it with high loads. I seriously question the engineering design and manufacturing if I had 1 dead on arrival and the 2nd caught on fire due to some internal fault (I'm not going to take it apart to see which component failed). Its totally unacceptable.Oh and if anybody says that dremel was too much for it. I've measured it pulling 1.55A at 110V (modified AC sin wave) from my Cobra 500watt power inverter I have permanently mounted in my car, you know the $25 dollar one on amazon right now. I use it on that thing frequently with no issues. I stepped up to energizer thinking it would be a good product, but the dirt cheap one that I've had a year or 2 works better.
summary: First unit had faulty internal wiring, 2nd unit CAUGHT ON FIRE with 250 watt load (Look at customer images).

reviewText: This thing works just like you'd expect and has all the connection options you need.  I mainly wanted it to use as a backup power supply, paired with a 12V deep cycle battery, in case of a power outage.  I hook it to the battery with the alligator clips (included), turn it on and it works no problem.  It recharges my Android phone (via USB) and I tested it with a 200W personal heater (via 2 prong plug) and that worked just fine with the 12V battery.The cigarette lighter is a nice option too, basically giving you a generic way to power devices without having to get the "car adapter" for that particular device.  Note, though, the warning that cigarette lighters are for 100W.  If you want 500W you need a battery to connect to with the alligator clips.Basically if you have this, a 12V battery and a battery tender/charger, you've got a nice, generic home backup power supply which, while not remotely as robust as a generator, is a cheap and convenient way to power your gadgets in a power outage.

This review is for the 500W version of the product.The lowest capacity version offered on this product page was tested for a week and I am pleased to inform that it performed amicably well in all areas. The inverter had enough capacity to run most electronics like a laptop, couple of CFL bulbs even inductive loads such as a small box fan without any problems. Do not expect this to run anything bigger like your refrigerator or vacuum pump. The rated capacity is 500W for this model and you must always use loads considerably 'lower' than the rated capacity.PROS[+] It includes all the cables for operation with 12v DC battery & Cigarette lighter port in car[+] The two USB ports work without powering on the inverter - Great power efficiency[+] Near silent operation (The FAN is thermally controlled) and rarely comes ON[+] Good thermal heatsink even for the entry level model[+] Very competitive price especially for entry level modelCONS[-] No physical ON/OFF switch[-] Clam-shell packaging is difficult to openAdditional notes:------------------For using the inverter with 'full load' please use the provided direct to battery cables as the total current drawn can exceed 10-15 Amps. The included cigarette lighter port cable has a limitation of 10 Amps of current draw and might blow if you put large load (Especially inductive loads) on the AC outputs. The cigarette lighter port cable does have a user replaceable fuse.The 'idle' current drawn when the inverter is running (Blue light is ON) is about 350mA with no load. When the inverter is OFF (Blue Light is OFF) the inverter does not draw any significant current. But for certain solar installations it could pose problems as the two USB port's DC-to-DC converter does draw some negligible current under no load condition. While I personally like the fact that USB charging ports function without having to powering ON the inverter I think for certain solar installations adding a ON/OFF switch on the battery side might be needed to avoid 'phantom' current drawn when the unit is not used.Overall this inverter worked great for me. I am giving 5 stars!Cheers!

My grandmother once noted 'Rick, if there's a lemon in the bunch you'll get it!' and unfortunately she's been proven right more than once in my life.  So it went with this inverter...the first one that came had defective wiring inside and eventually after blowing several fuses burned completely up and I wrote a scathing review before tossing it in the trash.  But I am nothing if not fair minded and have long ago learned that most often the second time's the charm for me so after being contacted by the manufacturer and offered another one to try I said, 'why not'.It arrived this last Friday as we were preparing to go for a camping trip and I thought that would be a perfect testing ground.  After gingerly plugging it into the cigarette lighter that it's predecessor has so disliked I was surprised to see the blue light come on that indicated it was powered and ready to go.  My cell was pretty near dead so I charged it on the way up to the mountains and over the course of the weekend we used it to charge a laptop (and there are three pronged outlets on it (2) that make it convenient to use a laptop charger along with usb plugs for the cell phones.  The real test was Sunday when we took it and attached the battery cable hookups directly to the truck battery to run a drill to drill two nail holes in a board to put up a feeder and it worked like a champ.I can vouch that it has excellent safety circuits since the first one kept blowing fuses instead of burning up my cigarette lighter circuit and only finally shorted out when I attached it directly to the battery.  So I am actually very happy to recommend this product because the first unit I got proved it won't hurt your vehicle if it overloads or does have a manufacturing problem and I can personally attest to the fact that the manufacturer stands behind it big time.I'm changing my rating to 5 Stars because it did everything we needed of it on the camping trip and is well built.But note that the fuse in the lighter plug in is 10amp and should be replaced with a 10 amp should you ever need to.  Which seems unlikely after it worked all weekend with no issues. The book refers to a 35amp fuse but that's inside the unit itself and is not the one in the cigarette plug.  And make sure you read the book thoroughly so you know how to set it up for direct connection to a battery before you do so.  Hard to find a 500amp inverter so I'm glad to get a chance to praise it after all.  I recommend this excellent product with no reservations.
summary: First One Defective - Second One Worked Like A Champ!

reviewText: It works good just as most of the reviewers have said, but the one I got stunk very badly when I took it out of the box. The smell is similar to the smell that I have found on shoes, tools and other products that came from China (appears to be something in the plastic/glue they use). I'm a smoker so my smeller is not too good, but I can smell this thing from across the room. I'm surprised, because I read a lot of the reviews before I bought this thing and I don't remember anything about it smelling, so maybe I got a bad one. I've had this thing out of the box for several days now, but the smell is just as powerful as the day I opened the box for the 1st time. I'll be keeping it because it will be used mostly outdoors were it don't smell as badly, but I won't be buying another or recommending this thing!

I'm very pleased with the Energizer 500-Watt power inverter. It offers a lot of convenience in a portable package. It can also be permanently mounted in the vehicle if so desired. There is plenty of power on tap to charge a laptop battery, run a small appliance, or even use some smaller power tools. There is a 1000-watt start-up surge rating, which seems to be enough for most things a person would normally want to run off a power inverter.

I've had several inverters, from super cheap ones to the higher end true sine waves.  For what this inverter provides, it is well worth the money.  It is powerful enough for most needs and they provide both battery clamps and standard wires.The item is well built and cords plug into it and remove easily.  It has bright indicator lights so there is no question about what's going on.The fact it has 2.1A USB ports is great.  However, be aware that that is shared between both USB ports.  So you cannot charge two higher amperage devices, such as iPads, simultaneously.  You could, however, use the USB port for one and the AC charger for the other and that would solve it.  I don't really charge two at the same time, so it's never an issue.The included  mounting hardware make it a snap to put in.  I would recommend one for every car.  They can be life savers!
summary: For the price, you can't beat this inverter!

reviewText: If you plan to connect this straight to a 12 volt battery, it is great.  It provides 500 watts of power in a compact, quiet, and well made package.  If you plan to connect it to a cigarette plug, this is a terrible choice.  When plugged into a car's cigarette plug, it only supports 100 watts of power because it operates so inefficiently at lower wattage.  There are models out there that can give you 300 watts from a car's cigarette plug, without tripping the fuse in the car.  If you go over 100 watts with this one, you'll trip the fuse.  The delta is basically used up in heat and powering the fan.This is a great inverter for heavy duty use, connected straight to a battery.  It is not efficient enough to be a good choice for cigarette lighter applications.
summary: If you plan to connect this straight to a battery it is great.  Don't get this if you plan to use it with the cigarette plug.

reviewText: This Energizer Power Inverter works as it should.  It seems well built and looks good too.  Devices like this are very useful for road trips and surveillance jobs.  I highly recommend this little unit.  It is powerful enough to drive a full size blender... don't ask.
summary: Great device that works as it should

reviewText: This inverter is non-sinusoidal.  Basically, this makes it unfit for your expensive electronics like laptops.  I plugged my MacBook Pro AC adaptor/charger into this thing and it flashed my screen like a Christmas light.  I hope it's not damaged.It comes in one of those cursed welded plastic display hangers that you have to destroy to open.  That's ok though because I feel sorry for anyone that would buy this P.O.S. junk from China.  Live and learn.

This is a well-built, if bulky unit that has performed admirably. I had a USB input in my Honda Fit, but it's not always powerful enough to charge things like iPods, iPhones, and iPads (and most things with an i in front...). It powers the devices while connected, but cannot add to their battery life. Fortunately, the Energizer works really well. It's functional and seems to run without getting too hot. However, it's pretty big and doesn't tuck away easily in some remote part of the car when not in use. It's not really substantively larger than other power inverters with similar output capacities, but it's still big. There are also a few cables that attach to it, so I recommend getting some sort of bag to store everything in together. I use one of those reusable shopping bags, and when the unit isn't in use, I just throw it in the truck.Overall, the build quality is very good and it works well.

The storm season is upon us and this is the time to get ready for it. With so many gadgets as part of our everyday life, candles and flashlights aren't enough during a power outage. So, having at least one power inverter is essential to recharge our small electronics and having some lights in the darkness. The Energizer EN500 is designed to be used mainly in a motor vehicle, but it can also be used at home with a rechargeable Sealed Lead Acid Battery that would not ooze fumes or spill acid.I tested the Energizer EN500 with two different AGM batteries, both 12 volts, one 7Ah and the other 35Ah. Using the USB ports, I recharged a few gadgets, like Smartphones, MP3 players, a weather radio, and a netbook. And later left a regular lamp connected to the AC outlet for a few hours. It performs well, so I think the Energizer EN500 is a great option for a budget power inverter.
summary: Essential and affordable modified wave power inverter

reviewText: A few years back, having suffered through an extended power outage and hearing alarmist reports of storms that coulda/woulda/shoulda been bearing down upon my area that were likely/possibly to negatively impact power availability at my home I went out and picked up a small power inverter to use in times of emergency.  Since that time (knocks on my own head a few times for luck) the power outages have been fairly few and I've not had to rely upon that little inverter for much of anything other than the ability to charge up some small electrical items (most frequently phones, iPods, iPads and the like).  That particular inverter offers at least one USB port, pass-thru of the 12 volt cigarette lighter port, and one standard (U.S.) 120 volt AC port.Seeing the availability of this 500W inverter, I somewhat jumped at the chance to grab another inverter figuring that I could just move the original inverter over to wife 2.0's vehicle.  That is easily possible, though I would note that in thinking of putting this Energizer 500W Power Inverter into service I have concerns about just how big this inverter is by comparison.  Relatively speaking, the inverter that I had been previously using was only slightly larger than a pack of cigarettes, or perhaps 2 or 3 standard sized Kitkat candy bars stacked directly on top of each other.  This beast easily dwarfs that one in comparison.  It's heavier, bulkier, larger and more demanding of space in my vehicle.  Certainly I can make the room in case of emergency, but if I am not going to use this regularly, finding it a home in the vehicle where I can still get to it quickly enough if needed is a concern.I wish that this inverter offered the pass-thru for the cigarette lighter port, though would note this is more obviously intended to be cabled directly into the electrical system in a more permanent fashion.Potential purchases should be aware that this device is not intended to power large devices, or devices with high power demands. For example, a blow dryer, microwave oven, or other device that pulls a higher level of power would overwhelm this device and wind up popping the device's fuse or fuses in the vehicle that it was connected in.  If you are looking to power more demanding electronics then please check through the entire line of offerings and choose one of these inverters that is rated for and intended for use for higher power draw levels.  For most typical usage (small electronics, laptops, iPods, iPhones, iPads, Android tablets, Kindle Fires, Android smartphones, etc.) this device would work fine and could/should provide plenty of on-demand power in case of an emergency or during road trips with this device in use.
summary: Bit of a behemoth, missing pass-thru cigarette lighter port

reviewText: I love that this inverter comes with traditional outlets and USB ports.You can run this off your car cigarette lighter or run it off the included battery cables on a full sized battery.  This is a huge plus if you will be camping or if you are worried about a prolonged power outage. No it won't power your refrigerator, but you will have days (weeks) of cell phone and flashlight power.

Energizer Power InverterThis looked like a good product.  My first dismay was the astounding difficulty to get into the product.  The plastic clam shell was nearly impervious to my special packaging cutting tool.  Then the liberal application of tape on the pieces that were already carefully sealed in their molded plastic pockets compounded my frustration.  Once I got it open, I read the brief overview and took it to the garage to test.  I attached the leads with the power port (formerly known as a cigarette lighter receptacle)  adapter and then plugged it into the power port in my SUV.  BTW I am a bit concerned about the exposed connections on the back.  I'm not an electrician but they look like it would be entirely too easy to cross those with something conductive and poof!Anyway the blue light on the on off switch came on when I turned it on.  It looked like it worked.  I put my Dirt Devil on it to test as I use it to vacuum the SUV.  It didn't care for the inverter and sounded pathetically weak.  I turned it off, started the car and tried again.  The vac wheezed without actually turning over.  The inverter then went belly up.  It did not recover after one hour.  I tried multiple power ports in two different vehicles with no success. The literature states that it can accept up to a 1000 watt draw on starting.  I can't find a site that give me the draw on the Dirt Devil but since the lights don't dim when I plug it in, I suspect it isn't drawing 1000 watts.  I liked the idea of an inverter.  This one didn't respond to any resuscitation so I'm not impressed.  Luckily it was provided at no charge for review purposes.UPDATE:The day after I posted this review there was a response from Energizer customer support.  I made contact and had explained to me that my test device ie. Shark Vacuum, exceeded the rating of the inverter and had blown a fuse.  That had occurred to me but I was unable to locate a fuse. The rep, explained where the fuse was and how to change it.  Even more, he said that they were adding instructions to the product on the location of the fuse and how to change it.  But Wait!,in addition they are adding two spare fuses to avoid future issues like I had.  The rep asked me to test the inverter with the alligator clips that go directly on the vehicle battery.  I did test it and it worked fine.  I am waiting to receive the fuses that the rep has sent.  When they arrive I will re-test the inverter with the cigarette lighter adapter.  I will be back to add further updates.  As a note, I review a lot of products and seldom have I seen such superior customer service,up to and including adding directions to the product based on my review.  I commend Power Bright Technologies, the manufacturer of the product for their proactive support.Final Update:  I received the fuses and tested the unit again.  This time all went fine.  I commend the vendor for good customer support and since my original test was beyond the parameters of the tested unit, I have revised my score based on the corrected test and the superb customer support.

reviewText: Summary - great inverter delives plenty of juice for power tools, but one of my chargers didn't like it :(I used aP3 International P4400 Kill A Watt Electricity Usage Monitorto measure power consumption of the devices I used.Bosch 20V Litheon Charger - 49 wattsDremel 10.8V Lithium charger - 9 wattsGreenworks 40V Lithium Charger - 98 watts (wall outlet)Black and Decker jigsaw 135 watts (no load)  / 220 watts (Cutting 1/2" plywoodPorter Cable Quicksand 106 watts (no load) / 174 watts (sanding w/ 80 grit)To cut to the chase, I was able to get both the jigsaw and the sander working at the same time and the Bosch and Dremel chargers never missed a beat.  That's a good ~470 watts of power tools and charger.On the other hand, for some reason the Greenworks 40V charger would start up then shut down.  I played around with the kill-a-watt and think it might be the line frequency.  The line frequency of a wall outlet is 60 hz, but for some reason the kill-a-watt sees this as 11 hz.  I don't think Energizer is really using 11 hz, but the kill-a-watt thinks it is.  This must be the same issue that causes the Greenworks charger to shut off.I did trip the internal breaker when I tried to run a heat gun.  The heat gun on low pulls 656 watts then quickly ramps to 874 - still below the surge, but the gun neve started up, tripped the breaker right away.Although this inverter has a cooling fan, it never seemed to kick in - either that or it's *really* quiet.  The inverter comes with two sets of connectors - cigarette type connector for lower power applications (Most cars use a 10 or 15 amp fuse, which means you can't run more than 120 or 180 watts before you blow the car fuse - DAMHIKT)  and an alligator type for hooking directly off the battery.  I did all my tests with the engine off - if you are planning to do some major work off this inverter, I suggest you leave your vehicle in idle so you don't end up walking.Mounting brackets just in case you want to mount directly to your vehicle - they do raise the inverter away for a cooling gap.
summary: Solid 500W for power tools, but your charger might not like it!
