We, like most families these days, have lots of portable electronic equipment including smartphones, laptops, Bluetooth speakers, Bluetooth keyboards, and such. When we go on a trip with 4 people in the car it isn't unusual to have as many as five of these devices being used, sometimes at the same time. There never seems to be enough charging outlets available. This little device fills the bill for us.We have been using a 140 Watt inverter for a few years already. It has two AC outlets but no USB ports so isn't nearly as handy as this new one. The old one has an internal fan, and a bit of a noisy fan it is. We are all relieved when we turn it off and get rid of that raspy sound. Also that old inverter is about 2" x 7" x 5" so quite large in comparison to this Energizer 120W unit.I tried plugging in my 14" laptop, and two Samsung Galaxy S3 smartphones and it worked just fine. With no internal fan it is completely quiet.As a few others have said taking up a cup holder isn't very practical unless you have one of those cars with a zillion cup holders. Our two cars only have two cup holders in the front seat, and we use both of them most of the time. So we put this Energizer in the arm rest closed compartment. One concern I have, and I'll have to monitor it, is will this Energizer overheat when placed in the arm rest compartment and put to heavy use.My only complaint is when I actually did have it in a cup holder, and it was night time, the blue light is bright and I could see it's reflection off the two side windows in the front seat so it was a bit distracting. Since we'll be keeping it in the arm rest box it won't be an issue. In other cases when bright LED lights bothered me I put a piece of black electrical tape over the light and just poke a small hole in the tape so I can see the light, which works fine. I've done this with several pieces of equipment.It's a nicely designed, and seemingly sturdy little device.

I've had a number of these style inverters and each one had I hated. The reason was some were built very cheaply, there would be a fan running that was loud in the device itself and even with a car radio on you could hear this hum coming from your cup holder. Others were just built so cheap and they cracked in the heat of being in the car when parked. This however is very solid, it's quiet and it has more than enough plugs for even me. It has 1 AC outlet which I used to run my laptop off of when traveling. It also features 4 usb plugs which for me allows me to plug my GS4, nexus tablet and GPS (if I bring my standalone) in with one plug to spare.I use a fitbit so it's handy being able to charge that while on the road driving.If you are looking for a power inverter this is a great one. It does come with 2 plugs, a cigarette lighter as well as clamps so you could hook it directly to a battery if you needed to.
summary: Exactly what a techy on the road needs.

reviewText: ENERGIZER 120W Cup Inverter is perfect for most needs as long as you are aware of the power output limitations. Remember even-though it has one 120V AC socket does not mean that you can plug anything you want and expect it to run. In my tests I found out that hardware engineers at ENERGIZER has given considerable amount of thoughts with 'safety & protection' in mind when designing this product. In most cases 'over-estimating' the load momentarily causing  the DC & AC outputs to cut-off while in operation. Having said, It does work perfectly when you keep the load on the device well below the limits of 120 watts.Also, as there are no physical ON/OFF switch for this CUP inverter, embedded smart electronics in the device constantly monitors the load & will change the bi-color status LED from Blue to RED indicating overload. I found that the USB ports current draw & the 120 watt inverter share the same 'overload' logic. This can be a problem in some situations wherein the 120v A/C load may draw little bit above the rated limit thereby momentarily shutting off the USB ports. Once the overloading device is removed the unit will automatically start working. While this design keeps the user & device safe during operation it can add some inconvenience inadvertently when the user without knowledge adds a device which overloads the device.PROS[+] Silent Operation[+] Good safety protection[+] Small design with 4 USB ports[+] Includes Battery Clips[+] Smart power draw (Draws power only when load is detected)CONS[-] Bright Blue Light is a distraction while driving.[-] The shape & design of the cup inverter can be problem in some cars as it tends to fall out.[-] The overload circuit is common for both USB and 120v inverter cutting off USB output at times.[-] If you plug-in all four USB ports for charging it would take long time to charge the devices as they are shared.Side-note:Not having a Physical ON/OFF switch is not a deal breaker for me. But worth mentioning as it can be a problem in some cars wherein the cigarette lighter port does not power off when key is removed as it might drain the car battery if left unattended with a large load. Without any load however the device draws negligible current <20mA and can be left connected to the car's cigarette lighter port.I really like this product apart from the limited power of 120 watts. Perfect for most needs and the price is just right.Thanks for reading my review. Happy Shopping!

This cup inverter it’s a great idea, and it can also be used at home matched with a sealed acid battery, it comes with the alligator clamps for it. There are two things to keep in mind though, if being used on a car or inside the house, the inverter has little ventilation slits around its case, if one places it on a cup for a long time it will get hot, this will shorten its lifespan because circuits don’t like heat and it can even be dangerous. So, I recommend getting one of those cup holders that only are made of a plastic ring that held the cup by the top part. In this way the inverter would still have air for ventilation. If an open cup holder it’s not available, then the best is to give the inverter time to cool off after each gadget recharging.It comes with an AC outlet and four USB ports, but one must remember that it has a limit of 120 Watts, so it will only be able to charge up to that wattage regardless of the amount of devices plug into it.
summary: Tiny but efficient inverter, it can be used at home too

reviewText: This Energizer 180W 12v DC to 120v AC Inverter exceeds my expectations in performance and practicality. I love having this in my older truck that lacks the convenient built in inverter and USB charging ports found in our newer van (which my wife primarily drives). Here are my observations:Pros -+ Form Factor; designed to fit into a car's cup holder+ AC Power; capable of charging my laptop and also tried it successfully to run a small inkjet printer+ USB Charging; has 4 USP charging ports, which is handy, but see "Cons" belowCons -- USB Ports are shared so charging time is slowed down when multiple devices are plugged in at the same timeThis is a very handy and good quality inverter that is perfect for owners of older vehicles.Highly Recommended!CFH
Quiet, small, and gives you a 110 outlet.  Just don't push the amps.

I am very pleased with the size of this Energizer car charger.  It is short enough that when it is in our dash-mounted cup-holders, it doesn't block the storage cubby just above them.  This is quite an improvement overanother cup-holder chargerwe got a couple of years ago.  That one was much taller, had a noisy fan, and some of the ports ultimately quit working.At first, the only drawback I saw to this Energizer charger was that the blue power light is very bright and annoying at night.  But then I actually tried using it, and I found its performance lacking.  I plugged in my Motorola Droid Razr at 50% charge, then I launched Pandora and listened to music (with earbuds) as we drove on the highway for about 35 minutes.  At the same time, my husband plugged in his HTC Thunderbolt to charge (without actively using any programs).  When we got to our destination, I was shocked to find that my charge level had dropped to 40%.  Using my usual car charger (plugged directly into the lighter socket), my phone would have made a significant gain in its charge during that time.  Certainly it wouldn't have LOST any charge.  Even using very power-hungry apps (GPS navigation, for example), my phone charges while plugged in.I tried this charger again during another trip when my husband did not have his phone plugged in and I was not using any apps.  Over a period of about 30 minutes, I did gain 10%, which is smaller than I'd expect, but at least it was sort of charging.Then I read some of the reviews of this charger here on Amazon.  In the comments of Ryan Winkleman's 3-star review, Energizer admits that this charger is not compatible with his Galaxy Nexus LTE, and may not be compatible with other phones, as well, saying, "Certain phones are not compatible with IPad 2.1a chargers. IPad charging has a unique pin configuration and most other usb devices are compatible, unfortunately some phones will not charge with that configuration."I don't really understand the whole pin and amps thing, and I don't think I should have to.  It's not like I have an ancient dinosaur of a phone.  If this product is known to not be compatible with certain mainstream products, shouldn't Energizer disclose this on the product page?  Or shouldn't it at least be described as a charger DESIGNED for Apple products, rather than just saying that it's "compatible"?  It just feels a little deceptive to me.
summary: May not work well with Android phones

reviewText: Occasionally I like to use my laptop in the car, mostly connected to a wifi hotspot and try to get some work done while my wife drives.  Unfortunately my laptop is a few years old and can only do a few hours on battery, which means I need to plug it in.  Previously I had used 400+ watt inverters, which worked fine, but took up a lot of space, and were quite loud.  This inverter is a lot smaller in terms of capacity, but it offers enough for most laptops out there, it's also near silent.I questioned it being able to fit into a cup holder, not sure that I wanted the power cords all going up to the center of the car instead of a mess of cables on the floor.  Turns out it provides two nice things, one because there is usually a 12V receptacle near the cup holders, this means it has a nice and short cord.  The other is that it fits into the cup holder which means it's not rolling around, it stays nice and secure.  It didn't fit perfectly into our 2004 Pontiac Grand Prix cup holder, not being able to go all the way to the bottom, but still is secure enough.Having 4 USB ports seems a bit overkill, but seeing as how almost everything charges or runs off of usb, it's probably a great thing.  It provides the hard to find 2.1amps (which means you can charge your full size iPads while still powering them), however it is shared across all 4 USB ports.  What this means is that if you have two power hungry retina 10" iPads you won't be able to charge them both at full speed.  Probably not a concern for most people, and having 2.1amps is great since it is much much faster instead of just staving off an empty battery.The only minor gripe is that with the MacBook Air's wall art (without the extension), it covers up a few of the usb ports.  I would assume this is true of the larger MacBook Pro (and retina) power adapters as well.  It's not a huge deal, if you have a thin usb cable head it might still work, and the ones on the side should still work.  Otherwise just make sure to test fit it and bring the extension if necessary.Overall this is a very compact unit, it's almost dead silent, it provides USB (and 2.1!) charging.  The new generation of laptops are providing enough battery life for a days work and then some, but for everyone else, this is a great way to give yourself a boost on the go.

This is a thoughtfully designed nice piece of equipment which delivers what it promises, but there are limitations. An iPad charger is unlike most other USB chargers in that it delivers 2.1 Amps (or 10.5Watts) in order to properly and promptly charge the device; obviously with this 2.1A charger, an iPad will use up all the available current by itself, making it sort of pointless to plug in other devices simultaneously. I tried this out by plugging an iPad 3, iPad Mini and an iPhone into this unit and watching video on the iPad. While when it started, the devices claimed to be charging, but they quickly figured out they were not and lost the lightning bolt battery icon, or got the "Not Charging" label where the battery typically would be. So, just because you have 4 USB ports, doesn't mean you can charge 4 devices. Far from it. You should be able to charge 4 low power devices simultaneously as standard USB devices draw at most 0.5A apiece.Installation was quick. It popped right into my Civic's cup holder, and while the power plug was a bit stiff getting into the cigarette lighter port, it did go in with a bit of firmness. Fine for charging a couple of cell phones on road trips.

This device works as advertised. So far we've only used it for the USB ports, but we're  pleased with the result. The cup fits nicely in the cup holder, and kind of blends in with our dark center console in our Jeep  Commander, so its very unobtrusive  in appearance. The ports are very handy to reach. Worth the purchase, especially for someone who has several devices and travels a lot.

Best road trip idea ever.  I have some buds who live in their cars during the work week and they are going to love this thing.  It has too many USB charging ports (OK, four, but that's enough to make power cable spaghetti on the passenger seat) and an appropriately powered 110/120V outlet for a laptop or other non-USB powered toy.  I say "appropriately powered" because I've seen inverters sold with cigarette lighter adapters that are rated at way too many watts; enough to fry in-dash electronics and other car components if carelessly used (like, say, trying to run a hair dryer off of a cigarette-lighter-powered inverter and yes, there are people that, er, uh, careless out there).The little pamphlet that passes for a user manual looks like something you'd normally toss but if you haven't spent any time exploring inverter and battery basics it is worth a read.  You do *not* want to routinely run down your car battery charging stuff with this item while the engine is off...car batteries aren't designed for repeated discharge.  Use this thing while you're driving, not while you're parked with the engine off to avoid discharging your car battery.  Some items shouldn't be charged with this device and they're listed explicitly in the manual - take the suggestions seriously or you may toast such items.That said, most of the warnings are along the lines of "don't stick your tongue in an electric socket while standing barefoot in a puddle" and unless you really try, you'll have a hard time screwing up your car or your electronics with this gizmo.  The only downside is you have to give up a cup holder but since my car has about 70 of them it's not a huge deal for me.  Really nicely done!
summary: Slick idea!  Pay attention to the manual.

reviewText: Fantastic! This little inverter fits right in the cup holders of my Jeep Cherokee and actually gives me 180 watts in a modified sinewave form. It comes with a cigarette outlet socket, and also battery clamps for direct battery attachment.There is one AC output plug, and four USB plugs. I haven't needed to attach five devices at once, but so far it's had no problem with three (my iPhone, laptop and ASUS tablet). As long as all electronics fall within 180 watts of power draw, it works very smoothly.I spend a lot of time living in my Jeep, car camping out on the road, and already use this inverter more than my array of other ones. It's more convenient, is quieter, and stays put in the cup holder.Energizer has been branching out lately with all kinds of new gear for cars, camping and survival. I like this trend. Highly recommended little inverter that packs a wallop.
summary: Excellent 180 watt inverter for any car with a cup holder

reviewText: I have 2 of these and really like them.  Nice compact size that fits perfectly into my cup holders.  It's about the same proportion of a regular soft drink cup, but with the top half cut off.  Very solidly built. No cheap rattling noises when I shake it.  4 USB ports for handy gizmo charging.  And a 3 prong outlet for anything else you wanna plug in. Just be aware to not plug in a heavy drain device without the car running, otherwise you'll run your car battery dry.  The cord isn't too long, so you gotta use a cup holder near a cigarette lighter/accessory port.  I've got one up front, and the other in the back of the car. Like the versatility of the 2 locations.  Works flawlessly for me.  Love it!

On longer trips, we've got a minimum of two phones and an iPad to charge, sometimes more, and I wanted something more elegant than 12V splitters.Unfortunately, the Energizer inverter's packaging bodly advertises 2.1A for iPad use, but the fine print (and actual usage) tells a somewhat different story. Fortunately, Amazon puts "shared" in the title -- because in a retail store, I think most people would think this puts out 2.1A x 4 ports at first glance.In any case, it will happily charge an iPad, and you can get creative with the AC plug and a USB hub if you want. Not the elegance I was looking for, but it's pretty flexible.The inverter itself fit wonderfully in my wife's Forester -- in fact, the distance of the cord and the fit both made me wonder if this was built using the Forester's center console as a stand-in. In more shallow cup holders, the fit is acceptable. The build quality is decent, and I was pretty impressed with how quiet it runs for an inverter.For people who need inverters but are put off by the size and overall look of a typical inverter, or if you're simply looking to have everyone in the family able to charge their phones on a road trip, this is a great product.

In Feb. while vacationing our car was broken into and our heavy, old, dinosaur of a converter was stolen.  I am happy to say that now I'm glad because this new Energizer Cup Inverter is perfect, and much better than my old model.Love, love that it has 4 USB ports as well as a laptop outlet, finally...we call charge all of our gadgets at once.  Even while keeping our GPS plugged into the car charger!  Another plus is that the Inverter fits into my cup holder.This is one product that will be getting a lot of use, it is worth every penny you'll spend on it, and I also see the product as great gift potential.I have not run into any issues, have not had it for long, but really, there's not a whole lot that can go wrong here, it does as it's supposed to, and has a little light that comes on and lets you know if it's working or not.

I was wishing for just this sort of thing for long car trips, and was totally psyched to discover that it exists. Our family travels with a variety of devices as well as computers, and the AC power is such a win!Pros:1. Yes, the AC power, which we use for laptops2. Cupholder design gives it a solid place to sit, instead of kicking around the carCons:1. As others have noted, the four USB ports share the 2.1A, so it will be slow charging if you use all four USBs. (However, if you just want to keep devices charged, it's fine.)Win. This is a huge help.

reviewerName: Mary Jo Sminkey "15 years of Amazon Reviews!"
reviewText: This is an inexpensive in-car inverter with a convenient shape design that allows the device to fit into a cup holder in your car. The four USB outlets let you simultatiously charge up to four portable devices such as iPad, iPhone, laptop computer, GPS, etc. (each output providing about .525 amps. Charging a single device would provide the full 2.1 amps for a faster charge.)The AC plug output can be used for a heating pad, baby bottle warmer, etc.In the past, I have had car problems by blowing fuses on the cigarette lighter connections.  I needed such an inverter to provide multiple charging outputs. On a recent trip the device performed perfectly for charging an iPad and iPhone with no fuse problems. I have no complaints.
summary: Excellent, compact charger for your car

reviewText: When we travel, we have many gadgets that need to be charges in our family.  This multi function plug is great!  We can plug in phones, laptops, iPads, even our electric ice chest.If you're in need of an adapter. I highly recommend this one.

It has USB plugs (4) and has a connector to the 12V connector.  It has an household plug that can recharge a computer.  It has a switch that turns on/off.  This charges iPod, iTunes, charges USB devices.  It is ultimately useful!

This charger is the greatest thing since sliced bread.  With 4 usb ports, you can charge all those different gadgets at one time.  And for the oddball item without a USB port, you can plug in into the AC port.  It works very well, it doesn't get hot, and they say there is a fan in it, but I don't hear it.  Worth every penny for the connivence.

I usually have a lot of apps running in the background on my phone and I use Waze for GPS as I drive. Like most GPS apps I've used, including TomTom, it is intensive on battery use. If I have less than 80% of the battery when I plug it into the conventional car charger, I actually lose a percentage point each 20 minutes I drive when using Waze (yes, plugged in). Not so with this Energizer inverter! Running the same apps, including running Waze on my commute, the iPhone went from a 60% charge to 69% charge in 15 minutes on one test run. In another test run, while NOT using Waze, it went from 71% charge to 79% in 8 minutes. I never get this fast of a charge with a conventional 'fast' car charger. I'm using an iPhone 4S and my husband's 3GS was also plugged in on the second test run and he got the same results. The package states that it has a 'whisper quiet' fan - and they're not kidding. Holding it up to my ear, I can hear nothing. I have another older inverter that is a big, heavy rectangle. I was surprised how well this works and how light weight it was - no visible (or heavy) spikey heat sinks. The unit also comes with alligator clips for plugging straight to a car battery sans cigarette lighter port. The shape fits great in a cup holder and has cut-away areas so it can still cool with its fan when in the cup. The unit has built-in protections for your car battery.  If it detects a fall in power, it will turn itself off and the Red or Blue LED light detectors make it easy to spot what mode it's in. I am very impressed with this inverter.
summary: Whisper quiet and a FAST charger for iPhones

reviewText: This inverter is amazing. I have been able to charge a laptop, my phone and an old MP3 player all from the same device while driving. At 180W output, even if the laptop was up and running, I would only put a small dent in the total output power.There are 2 caveats.First, you must be willing to give up one of your cup holders. Sure, there are other ways to mount this, put it on the floor, etc, but none of them are the way it was meant to be used. If you have a bigger family and frequent fast food or convenience stores, this can definitely be an issue. That being said, my family isn't big, so giving up a cup holder in the back of the car (with my USB 2 cables snaking between the seats) was a non-issue.The other issue is that blue light. During the day the blue power indicator is easily spotted and not distracting. Turn down the daylight, and enter the night and guess what? Holy COW that blue light is positively BLINDING. The first thing I recommend you do when you take this out of the box is to put a small piece of black electrical tape over the light. When I had this in the front of the car it made for a heck of a distraction during night driving. Of course, if all your travels are during the day, no problem.Overall- without the blue light covered, this gets a 3 star rating. With the blue light covered, it's 5, but that's because I am able to look past the lost cup holder. If you can't lose a cup holder, then this is definitely not a device for you and likely would merit 1 star, even though it works amazingly well.

This charging station fits well in my center console cup holder. The connection to the cigarette lighter outlet was strong.I love having the ability to charge multiple USB devices as well as have the option of charging standard outlets. This unit will pay for itself since I won't have to keep buying car adaptors for each new device my kids get.

I've been using this around town to keep my iPad charged...nothing too strenuous.  I've run a number of 120W (+-) items off the AC plug without any problems. One day soon, I'll plug in a power strip, add some lights and see how it works fully loaded.The only reason I took one star away is the blue LED is too way bright and distracting at night.  I stuck a piece of tape over it, but that sort of defeats it's purpose...there really should be an ambient light sensor that turns it down when necessary.  Other than that, I don't have any complaints.

the wax smelled GREAT!! I doubt they put any fragrance in it -- it just smelled so (faintly) flowery, perhaps like the tree it came from. Anyway, after getting thru that olfactory experience, I reveled in the sight of that beautiful flat plane of Carnauba wax and then got to work.I took a square of cheesecloth, folded it into eighths, rubbed a decent shmear of wax onto it and then using flat strokes, I waxed an area about 14 inches by 3, immediately buffing it with another folded square of cheesecloth to bring out the gloss and keep it from drying and turning white on my dark finish. I also added a fine mist from a spray bottle to further enhance the shine.THIS takes time and patience, and must be done (IMHO) in the shade for best results,  but the reward is great -- I can't wait to see how this finish looks in the rain! UPDATE- it rained and the water beaded up in little round beads of varying impressive shapes -- I realized however that each bead in the sunlight is like a magnifying glass which will intensify the sun's rays on my finish, so a wipe with a dry and thirsty beach towel helped remove most of the water beads (have no chamois right now). That would actually apply to any kind of wax job, and Griot's is no exception.Now my paint job is not the best, thanks to the local Auto Paint shop. But while using Griot's Garage 11029 Premium Carnauba Paste Wax I could actually SEE the metalflake in the paint come back to life.So I did the car, segments at a time, unfolding and using the same eight-fold square of cheesecloth about 4 times before discarding it. I took me a long time to wax the whole car, but it IS worth it. The chrome (the parts that were not rusted) gleamed. I need to get some steel wool and take care of the surface rust on the bumpers before waxing them any further -- however, the wheel trim (chrome) rings sparkled.I would think one can would be sufficent for about 3 applications, maybe less on a larger car. I store the can (which BTW opens and closes easily) in a cool spot close to room temperature.The price? WELL worth it.
summary: WONDERFUL !!! When I first opened up the tin,

reviewText: A lot of old adages ring true for the most part. The one that goes, "You get what you pay for," probably applies here. The first thing I noticed was the price! Almost four times more than popular brands. Truthfully, I have never come across Griot's Garage wax - probably because it is very high end. Now I know where to get it.It's heavy. I noticed right away that it felt heavy for its volume. I hope that it's like electronic goods where heavy suggests higher quality. The can attaches in a way that keeps the lid on securely - somewhat like the way a camera's rear lens cap attaches.Finally we get to the product. Griot's claims to have the highest grade of carnauba wax. Looking at it, I would guess that it's more than just a claim. It is not as creamy or pasty as most canned waxes. It looks like soft wax, which is what it is. The consistency is somewhat like a harder paste wax, which means it can break off in chunks more easily. This has nothing to do with the performance or behavior of the product. It's just something I would want to know if I read a review.I'm so used to reading that one should let the wax dry, often to a slight haze before wiping it off. I was surprised reading that with Griot's, one should buff it before it dries. Not forgetting that a little goes a long way, I used less than I normally would if I were using a popular mass-market brand. I put a thin layer on the hood and then immediately began to buff it. I noticed that it went on easily and buffed just as easily. For products that require drying to a haze, it's a chore to get it off. You have to rub a lot harder. I was very pleased that finishing off with Griot's takes so much less elbow grease. I was on the verge of buying a random orbital buffer, but with Griot's I don't think it's necessary.There are two more things to consider - beading and longevity. Not too long after I waxed, it began to rain. After the rain, I noticed that beading was tighter than I had ever seen it with other waxes. Tighter means smaller beads. The beads were also clearly more circular. Tight circular beading tends to indicate a higher degree of hydrophobic properties. In other words, it acts as a better barrier or shield against water.It went on and off easily and the beading is great. The last thing to consider is the longevity. I want to finish this review so I will have to wait and see. If it doesn't last a long time, I will do an update. However, I would be shocked if it were not to last long. Carnauba isn't a famous car wax ingredient for nothing.

My experience with this wax is limited to one of my cars and about a week of exposure, so I can't give an opinion on how well this wax job will stand up over an extended time.  And, that's an important consideration, so maybe I'll come back in 6 months or so and add something.  But, for now, I can only say that this is really impressive wax.  It goes on easily.  It wipes off easily.  It leaves the car's finish looking great.  It smells nice.  I am very happy to have it and look forward to using it again.Couple of things - one is that the manufacturer is recommending you use some of their other products with this wax.  I didn't and I don't really see why they're needed, even if they're nice.  Second, this is expensive wax.  It's very nice, but I imagine that a lot of buyers won't care to pay what it costs.  I'll just say that this seems to be better than less costly products I've used on my cars before, so I definitely think it's worth some premium in price.  Whether it's worth its full price or not, I'm not sure.  If you really love your car and don't mind paying up to treat it well, you'll probably be happy with this wax.
summary: Premium wax is the right name

reviewText: This wax's feature of *not* smearing a semi-permanent, white chalky film when touching black trim is noteworthy. And the canister seals well and appears very robust - a weak spot with so many auto products these days.This wax is even more solid than the old "Classic" brand standard of decades ago, and its smell is much more pleasing. Reiterating from other reviews: find a shady spot, ideally outside in the shade of a tall tree that is not hanging over the car to drop sap and misty pollen on your project.Work quickly over a small area and make your way around the car. It's worth the effort. Another reviewer mentioned P21S. While I've never used it, I know many car-club concours enthusiasts love it. If a user of that product feels this may be better, it is good indeed.Including one hand applicator pad wouldn't kill them, though.
summary: When You Need to Have the Best

reviewText: Ah, springtime.  Time to restore the steed after a long winter of rain, wind and grime.  Out where I live, it is also time for green sticky pollen to start blowing around and collecting on my beautiful old M3 - and thus time to get a smooth layer of wax on the car to protect it and make it easier to keep clean.To take full advantage of a high quality, high carnauba content wax like this, start with a good wash and hand dry.  Then you may want to give the car a rubdown with paint cleaning clay, to remove sap, bugs and any other contaminants that remain.  Whether you skip the clay step or not, you absolutely should use a lightly abrasive polish - 3M Imperial Hand Glaze is my choice.  And then, once all that prep work is done, a good carnauba "paste" wax for post-polish protection.I usually use P21S carnauba wax, but along comes this Griot's Garage "Premium Carnauba Paste Wax" from Amazon Vine.  So, is it up to snuff?Yes, absolutely.  To be honest, it seems to me a lot like rebranded P21S.  To call it a "paste" is a bit of a stretch.  Like most waxes with high carnauba content, it is more like a solid block.  You can use it with one of those machine polishers, or so they say.  Me, I apply by hand using a foam applicator pad.  You rub and rub the surface of the "paste" and get just a bit of the wax on the pad.  The friction and heat from your hand begins to melt the wax down, and it applies in a light, smooth coat.  Remember this, especially if you are applying and buffing by hand -- don't wait around for it to dry completely, or it will be a bear to buff off.  Thus, apply it one small section at a time, give it a minute or two at most to begin to "set," then buff, and move on to the next section. Unlike those 'one-step' polish/waxes, this wax won't leave a chalky mess behind and it will not clog your buffing cloth, whether you use microfiber or soft cotton.Like most natural waxes, it isn't going to last and last, like some of those hard shell, plastic polymer sealer waxes.  But it is going to make your car gleam, assuming you have properly prepared the paint before you apply the wax.  Water beads up and runs right off the wax surface.Some folks here have suggested comparing this wax with products like Turtle Wax "ICE."  That's apples and oranges. ICE is a silicone wax. It's inexpensive. But all is not sweetness and light. Granted, cheap silicone waxes can create a 'hard shell' coat on your paint. Alas, they also will eventually make the paint on many fine cars - esp. German marques like BMW, MB and Porsche - become cloudy and will be a bear to remove. Don't even think of it if you care about your car.Three times a year, that's my usual drill with comparable carnauba paste waxes, and I expect that will be about right with this Griot's Garage wax as well. However, having just received and applied this wax, I'll have to report later on its staying power.  But for now, it is easy to use, looks great, and seems to be a dead ringer for my accustomed P21S.  I'd call it a toss-up between the Griot's Garage carnauba and P21S carnauba, and will use either one with pleasure. This is good stuff.
summary: Right up there with the best

reviewText: .I'm no car waxing expert, but this seemed easier to work with then Nu Finish, my previous car polish.PROs:* It doesn't whiten black plastic or rubber trim (see Note 1).- It didn't dry too quickly (in full shade. See Note 2.)- No white gunk or powder messing up crevicesOKs:- Durability vs other waxes & polishes is unknown.- Water beading is impressiveCONs:* ExpensiveI waxed a brand new white car. I applied a thin coat as instructed and it came out fine. I waxed both plastic and rubber black trim...No problem. You save a lot of time and hassle when you don't have to worry about staining your trim or gunking up crevices. The chrome lettering and logos, for example were no hassle to wax.Looks like I used over 10% of the can to wax a brand new compact car (Hyundai Elantra GT). So maybe I'll get 8+ waxings instead of the 14 claimed.- - - Alternatives - - -I've orderedTurtle Wax T-465 ICE Paste Polish - 8 oz.(orT-465R) to try next. About 20-40% less expensive per ounce, and highly rated by Consumer Reports for durability.- - - Notes - - -Note 1: Rubber shows some evidence of wax but looks fine.Note 2: I used it in the garage. Terry cloth applicator. I buffed it out after 3 to 6 minutes. It seemed like I had plenty of time and there was no danger of the wax getting too dry. Maybe on a low-humidity day it would be more of a problem.~~~ Comments & questions welcome ~~~

Griot's products are always high quality - just not inexpensive. However, they are often good value and this product falls into that category. You can find less expensive waxes but these products usually have a polish / cleaner component. If your car needs polishing, this isn't the stand-alone product for you. This is the wax for your prize BMW, Porsche, Mercedes Benz or Ferrari - a car that you will be showing off at a car show or concours d'elegance. If the finish isn't clean and polished, this wax won't make it beautiful. On my old BMW, I had to wash and then clay bar the surface before the paint was ready for this wax. Once I did that, it really shined beautifully. I tried to take a shortcut with the Toyota and I was disappointed with the results.Have a nice car? Care that it shines like new? Do your own washing and waxing? This is the wax for you. Else, find a wax and polish all in one product because this won't work well for you.Recommended with reservations as stated above.
summary: Great finish, easy to apply, beautiful shine

reviewText: My primary consideration in the choice of Carnauba Wax over other common types of car waxes was its performance over longer periods. My understanding is that the particular formulation of the Carnauba product has little or no effect on this aspect. I received this product in exchange for an honest, timely review and as the deadline approaches, this aspect has met my expectations. If this changes later on, I will update this review.The primary advertised differentiator between this product and other Carnauba car waxes is ease of application. I found the description to be accurate. I don't mean this to be "faint praise" but rather that there has been a multi-year gap in my use of paste waxes (shoulder injury) that makes me unable to make a more specific comparative statement. But I am pleased.Another advertised differentiator of this product is that a smaller amount goes further. Again, this seems to be an accurate characterization. However, advertising being what it is, I suspect the claim that this quantity is enough for 14 cars is probably relative to compacts (or sub-compacts?) and optimal technique. Unfortunately, I didn't do a before-and-after weighing of the container (on a kitchen scale) to get an accurate measurement of how much I used on my mid-sized car.-- Douglas B. Moran

This paste wax is labeled a premium product and priced as one. It lives up to its billing. Unlike a lot of cheaper waxes, it goes on easily and cleanly, not showing up as white on black trim areas of the car. I just applied and buffed it off manually, and it was easy to do. The wax really adds a shine to the car, and protects the paint well from water.I needed more wax than the 1 ounce suggested to cover a Honda Civic, so I won't get as many waxes as advertised. Given the price of this product, that makes it even more premium. But if it lasts a year or so, as claimed, the wax seems worth the price.

The Griots Garage Carnuba Paste Wax is a great carnuba wax that is easy to apply and remove. The end result was a very good shine that is better than most comparable waxes including carnuba and synthetic.  I normally use Mother's carnuba wax and the difference in shine was indeed noticeable.  The downside to this product is that it costs significantly more almost any other wax out there. Moreover it does not even include an applicator pad like some of the other wax products out there do.  If you are willing to pay the exorbitant price this is a premium carnuba wax that will give you wonderful results.  If you are on a budget you can get a very similar shine for about 1/3 to  the price.
summary: Excellent Results But The Price is Exorbitant

reviewText: I tried this product on my Audi Cabriolet.  It was very easy to apply and the finish was as described on the product description.  Griot's has entered into the professional detail arena so this product can be used for the novice or the person whose business is auto detailing.  The wax is soft and adheres to the cloth, so any scratches you might expect are minimal.  The finish was what I expected.  Very smooth and a very nice sheen.

This is the best carnauba wax I've used so far. I have used Meguiar's and Mother's brand waxes before, and while they are good, this is much better. This is also the first time I've used a paste wax and I think I've been converted to this type. Application of this product is easy, and the best part is it doesn't need to dry to a haze before being buffed off. Makes things go faster and buffing it off is easier when not dry. It also doesn't smell like petroleum distillates which is great. The shine left behind is great, and I did test it's water beading by pouring some water on the hood of my car. This wax passed my little "test".I don't drive a car that costs well into the six figures so I won't be using car care products that cost $100+ for a small bottle or container. This wax is certainly much more expensive than the other brands I had been using, but it's also about the limit of what I'd personally spend. It looks like this tin will last a good while so that's a plus. Also, I used this wax on my table saw's top and it performed beautifully for that role as well. I am slowly being swayed to the Griot's Garage brand products as every one of them I've used so far has been great, and performed very well.Edit:I REALLY like this wax. I washed, clay bared, and waxed my car a few months ago. I washed it once after waxing, and washed again recently, thinking I'd need to reapply the wax. I clay bared the car after washing and was amazed how clean the clay was. Crud wasn't really sticking to the car either as I'd gone through through the washing. I applied a spray wax instead of this wax since it was faster and easier. Wow, with all the other waxes I've used they never last this long or perform this well after a couple months in the sun, with two washes, and lots of dirt. Superb.

I love my cars, but I hate waxing them.  This Griot's Carnauba paste wax doesn't make it any easier, but at least the outcome is spectacular.  Paste wax is not for the uncommitted.  It's not a product you can apply in 15 minutes and walk away feeling it was a job well done.  Properly waxing a car with carnauba paste wax is a more zen like experience.  OK, I exaggerate a little; but not too much.  If you're seeking a wax that is easy on and easy off, this isn't it.  You have to take your time to prepare the car carefully; wash it, clay it and then wax and buff it.  It you take your time and do it right, Griot's Carnauba Paste Wax delivers an impressive, protective shine.  I use it on my Ferrari and other classic cars.  At less than $3/ounce it's a bargain.  I really can't tell the difference between this wax and waxes cost several times this much per ounce.  Highly recommended.

Carnauba Wax comes from the fronds of a variety of Palm tree that only grows in Brazil. The wax is very durable and one reference said it is harder than concrete. It protects the palm leaves from the constant intense rays of the sun in the tropics. So it is ideal for protecting your car's paint. There are other products that last longer, but nothing matches the rich and deep warm  gloss that can be achieved using Carnuba wax. It should be applied, ideally, to paint that is not only washed, but depending on the condition of the paint, polished and or clayed to assure it will cover paint that is not  opaque due to oxidation. Only then can it achieve it's complete potential. Apply it with a sponge applicator in a circular motion using it sparingly to one section at a time, allow it to dry to a light haze and remove it with a quality microfiber cloth. Then buff it by hand or orbital buffer. Carnauba wax varies in price by manufacturer and can be very expensive. Previously, my favorite product for the most bang for the buck is called P21s Concours Carnuba Wax. The results if used patiently are spectacular and it costs about five dollars an ounce. My ultimate choice is Pinnacle Sovereign Paste Carnuba, but it is a staggering twelve dollars an ounce or almost $100 for an 8 oz. tin.  This Griot's product costs about $3 an ounce which makes it a screaming bargain by comparison. I found it easy to apply and the gloss is very good. My only question is how long the application lasts. No wax lasts forever and if the results last 5 or 6 months as the two products I mentioned will, that is outstanding. I read some comments of people who said this product did not have that longevity, though I will need to update this later to see what results I observe. Considering how much work and how time consuming it is to detail your car, I think paying double or more for a product that lasts longer is actually cost effective. My results so far are encouraging with this product; easy to use, good shine achieved, very reasonable price comparatively. If it has longevity, this will prove to be a real bargain.
summary: A good value for Carnuba Wax.

reviewText: This can be used with a hand pad or dual action machine pad.  I've used both.  This wax goes a very long way.  Every time I use it it seems that I could have used less.  It provides a nice shell (that I can tell), and isn't too difficult to remove.  I've left it on overnight and it's easily removed with a little detailing spray.  It does, however, leave some yellow/white marks on black rubber and trim, but that's your own fault if you're not careful applying it.  It always comes off with a little scrubbing.

This wax delivers what it promises. I just finished waxing a silver truck and a red compact car. In both instances, the shine is outstanding. Both vehicles truly have that "wet" type shine that is hard to get. Here's what I found to be the pros and cons.Pros:1. Easy to apply with a buff pad. The wax is the texture of butter you just got out of the fridge so it's stiff enough not to glob on your pad but soft enough to smear.2. The was goes on evenly and smoothly. I did the vehicles by hand to ensure good coverage.3. The wax dried to a soft white haze very quickly and buffed off pretty easily using microfiber towels. It leaves very little residue after the first pass but you will need to buff out an area at least twice to get all the wax off.4. After doing both vehicles I've used about 1/4" of the wax so this can is going to last a long time.5. It smells really good. Waxing a vehicle takes some time to complete so not having to put up with an unpleasant chemical smell is a plus.Cons:1. Takes work. Think Karate Kid "...wax on, wax off...". This wax requires elbow grease to get the best results.2. I normally use an orbital polisher to apply the wax and buff it out by hand. I can't think of a way to use that tool with paste wax (I normally use liquid wax). If you normally use an orbital I'd think twice about using this.3. Staying power. I live in the Southwest where the sun really takes a toll on vehicles. I don't enjoy waxing my vehicles but having to do it only once or twice a year helps. I don't know how long this will last and there are no indications on the can. If it hangs tough, I'll come back and update this review accordingly.In summary, if you don't mind taking the time to hand detail your vehicle, you can't go wrong with this wax. It ultimately boils down to the appearance of the shine and this wax excels in that area.

Okay, so I'm a bit of a freak about keeping my Jeep's paint in good shape. I may get teased by others (many Wrangler owners wear their mud and scratches as a badge of honor) but I want that mud to wash off easily! More importantly, I want those tree branches to slide frictionlessly (is that a word?) along the freshly-waxed surfaces without being able to dig in hard enough to leave a scratch!  I also love the deep shine I can get on that dark green paint and the fact that when I wax it really well, people often initially think it's black instead of green; it's so glossy and reflective, you can't see the color as easily behind the colors of everything it's reflecting.Most often until now, I've been using the liquidMegiuar's Tech Wax 2.0, but I also have cans of both theTurtle Wax ICE Paste PolishandMeguiar's Cleaner Wax Paste. The Griot's Garage paste wax, at the time of this review, costs more than double the next most expensive item in that list.In terms of application and removal, I found it to be as easy to apply as the liquid Tech Wax and a little bit easier than the two pastes. The removal, if done at the recommended time just before it's completely dry, is actually the easiest of the four.  It may not be as significant of a difference as it sounds, but the difference is there.  If you allow it to dry completely it's about the same level of effort as all of the others.  Now, I've seen some reviews saying something along the lines of "there's no way it will last the advertised 14 waxes on even my subcompact car", and I really have to disagree.  To date I've done two coats on the Jeep, and if you look at the can you can hardly tell it's been used at all.  You don't need to spread it like frosting on a cake, just rub the applicator pad on the surface of the paste, even if you can't see it on the pad, as long as you're getting a solid haze on the paint you're using enough.I'm also happy to see that I don't seem to be getting marks on the black plastic components.  I already have plenty of them from using the other products (except the ICE) so a few more wouldn't have mattered, but luckily I don't have to worry about it.The price is high though. I almost don't want to recommend it because of that, and if saving money is a high priority for you then I can safely say buy something else.  Seriously, the Tech Wax is an excellent product that is just as effective at protection and gloss as this stuff is.  It's less than half the price, and it's available in a paste as well if that's your preference.  However, maybe you're the type that will think about the fact that you'll probably have this can for at least a couple of years, and spread over that amount of time, the price difference is pretty negligible. In that case, maybe try it out and see how you feel. Maybe the slightly easier application and removal will make it worth the extra money... just don't go into it expecting the wax to somehow give you a better shine than the others.  I can't tell the difference, and I doubt anyone else could either.
summary: Works Great! Price Seems High Though.

reviewText: First off - this is not a cleaner, it is a wax.  It is almost pure carnuba paste wax and it behaves that way.  Sure it cost $40 but if you use this right you can wax 2-3 dozen cars with it.Start with a really clean car (use clay for best results) and go at it with this wax.  Go very light on the amount, more is not better here, and work in small areas.  You have to buff this off, meaning it does not dry to a powder that you wipe off.  It is a wax and needs to be rubbed in to get it off. It is more work than most everything else but the results are worth it.Nice, deep wax shine.  Nice!
summary: Pretty much perfect for a wax

reviewText: I'm pretty cheap and wouldn't normally spend $40 on car wax, but I think this might be worth it.  Previously I've used cheaper products like Turtle Wax or Nu Finish but the humidity is pretty low here and it always dried quickly and was a lot of work to remove - not to mention the messy dust left behind that required another wash to get rid of it.  But the Griot's Carnauba wax went on easily (and it smells *really* good) and was easy to wipe off.  In fact, it was so much easier that I not only waxed my new Civic but also my wife's Odyssey (and a minivan is a LOT more work than a small car).  And it's especially nice that you don't have to worry so much about getting the wax on the plastic or rubber trim since it doesn't leave a mark like other waxes.As for the finish, there was a small but noticeable difference on my brand new car, but there was a huge difference on my wife's van which she takes to a local car wash on a regular basis.  The water truly "beads up" more on the sections with the carnauba wax compared to whatever was previously used.  I don't think I can go back to using anything else now, but fortunately it looks like this tin will last a while.  (Also, one of the pictures shows a cloth and applicator pad but my order came with just the tin of wax and nothing else.)UPDATE 7/24/13: There is perhaps one drawback to the "superior beading action" with this wax - it leaves spots.  We don't get a lot of rain here in SoCal but a rainstorm the other night left a beautiful coating of beaded water all over my car in the morning.  Since I hadn't washed it in a week there was a light coating of dirt which soon gave my car a leopard-spotted appearance, even after a short drive on the freeway.  I'd noticed this a couple times earlier when the sprinklers had left water on one side of the car.  The water beads up so effectively that it doesn't "sheet" off very well.  I guess it's not a problem as long as I can keep it washed, but it's not as perfect in a real-world setting as I previously imagined.

This isn't bad for paste wax.  It goes on fairly well with their special red waxing pad of high density foam, which won't crumble under the relentless job. It's fairly smooth and easy to get onto the pad and it goes on smoothly. I just had to remember, small sections and wipe off as it dries because it gets too hard after a while to easily remove.No, you can't do it in the sun, yes, you need to do it in small sections and thoroughly remove the wax, and if your finish is older, there are products such as paint cleaning clay to remove haze and minor scratches (there's another major pain)  before you apply this. If you do not have muscles like Schwarzenegger, you can use a random orbital polisher to make the job go easier. But--anyway you slice it, it's a job. However, it works well and will protect your finish far more than the Deluxe Super Wash at your local car automat. Before you start, it's well to acquire the supplementary products, either Griot or Mother's or someone's, to really do a good job as you are going to be investing "sweat equity."This wax isn't cheap. That is partly because carnauba comes from exactly one place in the world, a small crescent of shore in Northern Brazil, where the Copernica pruneifera palm grows. Due to the special climate, the carnauba palm closes up its leaves during the dry season and protects them with this natural botanical wax. The wax is filtered and graded, and the best grade wax is mixed with additives that improve spreadability and the finish. Even with polyurethane sealers and other chemical developments, the rare and natural carnauba palm wax is still unsurpassed for polish and protection.

This is an easy to apply wax, which leaves a magnificent shine. Griot's Garage Premium Carnauba Paste Wax results in a smooth, protective finish that feels significantly better than the greenish cream wax that I had been using. I can already see how the carnauba paste will last much longer than the lower-end options available; this wax is firm, yet workable and the finish is absolutely astonishing.The value of the results obtained from the amount that gets used is enough to persuade me to continue using this product in the future. It is worth the extra cost, and I am sure the longevity of the finish will duly reinforce my observations so far. I highly recommend Griot's Garage Premium Carnauba Paste Wax to those who not only desire an impressive shine, but also those who demand reliable protection from the elements - this stuff is great!

Over the years, I have used a number of waxes, sealants, and protectants on my vehicles. I have used other Griot's Garage products for several years - including the Paint Sealant and Best Of Show wax (a carnauba wax in liquid form). I also continue to use other brands (Meguire's, Turtle Wax) because each product has a special nich.  I have been wanting to give the Premium Carnauba Paste Wax a try for some time, I finally did just that. I love it!!This is a solid paste wax, not a thick liquid. It is best applied with (and I recommend) a foam wax pad. You could get by with a terry wax pad, but it wouldn't be my choice.  The paste is solid, but also very managable when getting it onto the pad. Basically, the same way you'd work with a solid shoe polish... oh wait, NO ONE is going to get that reference! Just a simple light press and twisting motion with your pad onto the paste will do just fine. You don't need a lot - just a very thin coating.Apply as you would most waxes, with gentle circular motions - frequently overlapping the applied areas, and continuing to move the product around until the coating is very light and thin. This wax works wonderfully with an orbital machine, but can be done just as easily by hand. I've done it both ways, with no trouble. Carnauba wax is one of the hardest waxes there is, and will create a great protective barrier between your car's fine finish and the harsh elements it is subjected to every day.The protection is fantastic, and the shine is deep and brilliant. Water beading is outstanding. I cannot yet attest to the lifespan, but I will try to update this review later with that opinion. Griot's Garage is well known for making and selling products for "car nuts", of which I can be accused of being. If you care enough about your car's finish to take a big portion of your weekend on occasion to detail it - then you will likely fall in love with this wax. I did a full sized SUV without making much of a dent in the amount of product, so I assume that I should be able to get 10 full uses, or close to it.And no review of this product would be complete without commenting on the aroma. This stuff smells so good, my wife wants them to make candles out of it. Truly - this stuff smells amazing, and provides some geat aroma therapy for you while you get the car waxed!
summary: Ultra-hard protective shell for your car's finish

reviewText: I grew up using this type of wax to protect the family cars, and I still find it to be the most effective. It loses a star due to the difficulty of applying and removing the wax, but it is worth it for the protective shine that results. Griots is a great wax that you only really need to apply once a year as opposed to other "easier application" waxes that need to be refreshed 4 or more times a year.  It's current nearly $40 price tag makes it a premium product in my book, but it does perform like one. Being a paste wax, it is a little easier to apply and remove, and the final finish is spectacular.If you have the time and want the best for your vehicle's finish, I find Griot's Carnauba Paste to be an exemplary product, even with it's premium price tag. It deserves it.~ Kort

I normally use Adams products, so I welcomed the opportunity to give this product a try. Since this was a vine product, I don't have the entire Griots lineup. I washed the car with Adams car wash mix. I didn't have the time to clay this car, or do any corrections.The wax applied very, very easily. It was a bit slow to haze over. To the point I applied the entire car. I then used the porter cable with a finishing pad and easily removed the wax. All said and done this was probably a 10 minute job.It rained today and the beading of the water was really not that impressive. I didn't do the doors as I was out of time and the difference is minimal between the waxed and unwaxed surfaces.
summary: Easy to apply, easy to remove..

reviewText: The first thing I noticed when opening this container of Griot's Garage 11029 Premium Carnauba Paste Wax, was the fragrance. It had a pleasant, fresh, almost floral scent rather than a heavy chemical one like some car waxes.  It also has a very nice consistency, creamy and smooth and easy to spread on the car's finish. The instructions say to not let the wax dry completely before polishing, so doing a small area at a time and then polishing that area seemed like a good way to use this product. It comes with a densely textured application sponge or you could use an orbital motorized polisher.  I did it by hand. A little of this wax goes a long way. I was surprised at how little I had to use. At this price that's a good thing because these 14 ounces will polish a lot of cars!  After applying it to the surface of the car I allowed it to cure for 3-5 minutes and then used a soft microfiber cloth to polish it.  It took a fair amount of work (good exercise!) but the car looked really, really shiny when I finished. It doesn't dry to a powder which is nice because you don't have any white gunk in the crevices or around door handles or trim. In fact, you can use it on plastic or rubber trim according to the instructions.  I did the polishing in the sun but it wasn't too hot that day. I think if it were a typical hot summer day, it might dry too fast so in that case it would be better to find some shade.  This wax gave it a deep glow, the type you can only get from polishing a car with real paste wax rather than just using some pour-on polish.After doing the whole car I wanted to test to see how water would react on the surface, so I got out the hose and gave it a quick spray. The water beaded up very nicely, actually better than I've seen with any other wax or finish. It takes a little bit of time and patience to wax a car with this wax, but the results are so worth it.

Carnauba has always been the best wax to use for cars.  This Griot's Garage Premium Carnauba Paste Wax is no exception.  Just apply a thin coat of wax in small areas and then rub it with a soft rag to polish.  It will protect your car's paint finish, make your car shine, and make water bead up and run right off.  Just don't try to work large areas at a time or it will be harder to rub to a polish.  This Griot's product was obviously intended to be used with one of their random orbital polishers (which I don't own) so it does not come with an applicator.  But any foam applicator available at your local Wal-Mart or auto parts store will work fine.  It takes some elbow grease to work any wax into a shine by hand, but it is not as difficult with this wax as it would be with other brands of paste wax.  A little goes a long way with this stuff.  The instructions tell you not to wait until the wax turns white to wipe it into a shine, and this makes waxing your car a faster job.  The remaining shine is very good -- my car had a showroom look to it after I was done, and I waxed by hand.The main downside to this product is it is incredibly expensive compared with other brands of carnauba wax that are readily available.  It costs probably 4-5 times as much as other brands of carnauba car wax.  It does polish a lot easier than other brands of carnauba wax, which may be worth its higher cost if you wax by hand, but if you own an electric polisher you really don't need to spend this much to get a great shine and protect your car's finish.  If you want the best carnauba wax out there, though, this probably ranks right up there.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: I've been using Blue Coral paste carnauba wax for years.  They use a lot of Meguairs at work.  The difference between these paste waxes and the chalky looking Turtle wax liquid that most people use is that this contains no abrasives.  Abrasives polish the haze away from oxidized paint. If you wax once a year and leave your car out, that's fine.  Otherwise, if you really want to pamper your car, use the paste wax.Carnauba is a naturally occuring wax  - you can buy hard bars of it for woodworking and other purposes.  This has additives that help you apply and buff out the wax.  The big difference between various brands of paste carnauba wax is therefore in these ingredients and how they are processed.I found this wax texture to have a smoother texture and a firmer feel in the can - for example the Blue Coral paste wax is softer so that you end up with more on your applicator.  At the same time, it doesn't rub off as easily - it seems to streak more, requiring you to go back and rub out again.In addition to using it on my cars and motorcycles, I also use it on my bicycles and countertops.  It restores the shine to the high traffic areas and seals the surface from stains.
summary: Good for more than just cars...

reviewText: I've used some of those other glass products and never noticed a difference but this is the real deal. Takes a bit of work and time to do it right - just like waxing your car. Well worth the effort. Of course, the rain stopped right after I applied this, but it seems to have made cleaning up bugs and such easier. I'll update this review if I get the chance to test it in the rain.

This is a little bit labor-intensive to apply, but well worth it.  I was skeptical at first, but a couple days after I gave my Jeep the ol' Griot's Glass Sealant treatment, it rained, and the rain just danced off my windshield.  My wipers didn't have to work as hard.  And it's true.  The "bug jerky"- Ha! pops off a lot easier after having the windshield treated with this.  I'm going to be treating all our cars with this glass sealant!

I've used this stuff, intermittently, for years. It definitely has a place in the automotive detailing pantheon. If you are the type that keeps your car sparkling clean, and waxes it religiously, a "slick" coating of petroleum-based magic (Rain-X is the same thing) over your glass, to help keep it water-stain free and dirt repellant, truly is the icing on the cake. But it definitely takes some time and commitment to get the coating right, with repeated applications. You can actually eliminate the need for using wipers by applying it on your windshield, but, realize that if you decide to start using your wipers, you will get a hazy mess for quite a few strokes. Classic car owners that don't drive in the rain all that often, and have flaky/ineffectual wiper mechanisms, love this stuff.It's also very important to PROPERLY clean all the glass (not just if it's a windscreen you're dealing with) before applying this. Note that polishing your windshield on occasion is a good idea anyway, and is a huge factor in allowing your wipers to work their best. A reasonably cheap electric glass cooktop polish (like Wieman brand) works nicely.When considering this product, you need to ask yourself if it's worth the effort. If you regularly encounter clinging dirt/mud or ice in your travels, it probably is. Because clean up will go much easier. Also, if your car is parked on a highly traffic'd urban street, rinsing the windows with plain water will get them perfectly translucent again, even if it's been parked for a few days.Having clean glass is a safety concern, and so should be a priority. The multiple treatments and overall time it takes to get it right, though, means I subtract one star.
summary: Worth It - If You Have the Time

reviewText: This window treatment works okay, but is difficult to apply and leaves an alcohol smell on one's hands after use.  The instructions direct one to apply two complete coats of liquid, letting each coat cloud up first.  Those steps worked just fine.  What was difficult was wiping off the windows to where there was no longer a film.  That takes more elbow grease than indicated and I think too much considering some of the other competitive products out there.  Now I'll wait for rain to see if it repels water and saves my wiper blades as advertised...In the meantime, I may use it again, but I won't reach for it first.

In my mind, there are three leading auto glass 'sealant' treatments out there - Rain-X, Aquapel, and this product, Griot's Glass Sealant.  Aquapel is the most expensive of the three, and as far as i can tell, it is the clear leader in terms of function and longevity.  But for about as much as this 8 oz bottle costs, you get one or possibly two Aquapel applicators, each of which contains just enough solution to treat one windshield or rear window.  But there is no question that Aquapel is pretty miraculous stuff - properly applied, it makes rain skitter across your windshield and fly off into the ozone, and it remains effective for months, even with frequent trips to the local car wash.Griot's Glass Sealant and Rain-X appear to me to be more or less equivalent and second tier.  Both will go on relatively easy.  Both will give your auto glass a clear coating that has moderate water-shedding properties.  Both seem to last a few weeks at most before requiring a new coat.But if you do not mind applying Glass Sealant every few weeks - and it really is not a chore - and if you do not demand the somewhat amazing rain shedding properties of Aquapel, then this reasonably priced 8 ounce bottle of the stuff represents good value for money.  Me, I'm willing to spend the extra coin for the Aquapel treatment.  Here in the Pacific Northwest, it's really nice to be able to cruise along at 30 or 40 mph and watch the rain literally fly off your windshield, driven away by the force of the wind on the glass - you barely need to use your wipers.  Glass Sealant doesn't quite amaze, but it does make your wipers work far more effectively than they do on untreated glass.

Sometimes your windshield wipers can't keep up with a downpour, or perhaps they are starting to wear and you forgot to replace them. A glass sealant like this can help by speeding up the movement of rain off the windshield.This product has a strong alcohol odor. It's not difficult to apply as long as you can easily reach your entire windshield. (I cannot unless I stand on a stool.)Cleaning your window carefully before applying this. We have a surplus of minerals in our water and I was not able to get all the calcium spots off the windshield, even though I cleaned it with a spray glass cleaner followed by wiping with a microfiber cloth. I applied the sealant to the driver's side windshield only, in order to see what difference it made. It broke up the hard water spots so now they are tinier spots but more of them. Still, the overall clarity is improved.When rain hits the windshield, it rolls off faster than it would without the sealant. I've observed this before with a different (but similar) product and I think it can be very helpful.

I like this product, but, it's not a WOW type of product. It does it's job and nothing more, but, nothing less. Not sure I'll buy it again as I have other products that do just as well or better for less money. I'd give this product a 6/10 where as I prefer 8/10 or better when I buy some of these boutique type car products.

I thought that this product would be a pain to use. The instructions are to apply, dry to a haze, buff and repeat the steps.It is easy to apply and buff out so it wasn't bad after all. I did 6 windows on a Honda CRV and by the time I worked my way around the car it was ready to buff.  Then I just worked my way around again. The whole process only took about 20 minutes and I used about 1/5 of the bottle. The windows looked great and I anxiously awaited rain to see how it performed.While I was waiting for the first rain one morning the car had condensation on it and drops had dribbled down the windshield and back window.  I turned on the wipers to clear the window and was shocked to see that the path of the dribbles had etched into the sealant surface and the marks would not go away. I tried using washer fluid and it wouldn't clear it either. Driving into the sun that first day was not pleasant. The marks have faded to the point they are not noticeable anymore, two weeks later they were faint but still there.When the coat of sealant is fresh, about the first week, rain will just slide off the windshield. In a misting rain even the intermittent wipers would not be needed.  When the wipers are used they sweep the rain off cleanly without leaving streaks.  Three weeks after the first application the wipers still clean the windows with no streaks. After 4 weeks the windows need another application.I was ready to write a scathing review after the condensation etching issue but the fact it allows my wipers to do a much better job so long after application has endeared the product to me because no matter how new my wipers were they streak the windshield and of course the streak is always right in front of the driver.My only previous experience with a product like this was with RainX. I hated applying RainX because it was so difficult to buff out and as the coating wears off it caused a terrible chattering from the wiper blades so I quit using it.
summary: Easy application and streak free windows for weeks.

reviewText: OK, I'm a Griot's Garage product fan. I have been using their products for years and have yet to find one that wasn't as good or , in most cases, better than similar products on the market. The same holds true with this glass sealer.Briefly, the idea behind this product is that it seals the glass on your car's windows with a wax-like coating so that rain drops slide easily off as you drive. The first time I used a product like this (Rain-X), I was fascinated by the rain dance the droplets did as they scooted off all of the windows (NOTE: it's not just for the front windscreen!) However, I have noticed that recently, Rain-X has stopped being as effective as it had been (formula change?) so this new offering tempted me.Quick report - it's better than my old faithful Rain-X. But my report is only partially complete because products like this also make getting frost and squished bugs off the glass a lot easier. in NJ, we are in-between frost and bug season so a more "complete" report is not possible. However, it does a darn fine job in rain so I suspect that it will work fine on frost, snow, and bugs.Note - if you have an older car with a rock "peppered" windshield, this and any other similar product the effect won't be as magical. These chemicals seem to like new, smooth glass best. But they will work well on the side and back glass - really something special if you've never tried it.Finally, your windows have to be CLEAN. Really clean. Griot's makes a glass polish that I used in preparation for this test and it makes the glass as clean as you can get it.Drive in rain or snow? Have morning frost or summer bug splatter to clean off? Try this product. It worked for me.
summary: Works well - very similar to "old" Rain-X

reviewText: The primary test of this product is how well it lasts and performs when much of the water on the windshield is sprayed up from the road surface and thus is contaminated with dirt and oil and being rubbed across the windshield by the wipers. I live in a locale where winter is the rainy season and unfortunately this review sample arrived two days after what was likely the last non-trivial rain for many months so I have been unable to do this primary test before this review was due.I use this type of product outside the rainy season because it makes cleaning the windows faster and better. Since I try to park under trees for shade, bird droppings are not just inevitable, but almost immediate. And then there is dust from unending construction in the area. So far, this has been doing an excellent job. For comparative testing I left some window areas untreated -- a strip on the far side of the windshield and on the rear window, and I treated only one of my station wagon's back panel windows. Substantial positive difference.Application was easy. From the instructions, I expected a significant haze to form -- and be buffed out -- but there was a barely perceptible one (not complaining -- it means that there is little product being wasted).The cap on the bottle has two minor problems:First, it pours sloppily. This is not a problem when treating a windshield because you don't need to be precise in wetting the cloth. However, if you want to do a small job, such as the outside mirrors,...Second, that the cap is to be pulled up to open the center hole is not obvious to some -- it takes more force than people expect and the label on the cap is difficult to spot and almost impossible to read (small print, minimal elevation produces negligible contrast in many lighting conditions). Consequently, some may treat it as a cap to be unscrewed.--- Douglas B. Moran
summary: Excellent performance for keeping windows clean (but used outside rainy season here)

reviewText: First of all, you need to make sure your windshield is REALLY clean before you apply this.  Not just squeegeed-at-the-gas-station clean, but really soap-and-water-and-towels-and-rinsed-and-buffed-dry clean.  Then you can apply it.  There are several different opinions on what is best to use for applying, and I'm not qualified to make that call, so you'll have to ask someone else that.  But at the very least, plan on having a bag of lint-free towels.You have to apply the product in a "cross-hatch" pattern, let it dry to a haze, apply it again, let it dry to haze again, then buff it thoroughly till it's crystal clear all over.  If you wax your car regularly, this might seem like no big deal (and you're going to love this stuff, and you probably already use something like this, so I'm wasting your time here).  But if you're not much of one for detailing your car, this is going to seem like a lot of work.However, one you get it on properly, it really does work well.  It will repel not only water, but dust and grime, too.  It makes it easier to remove frost and ice from your windows.  Baked-on bugs are easier to remove.  Your wipers will be more quiet.  It's a great product, but just know what you're getting yourself in for as far as application.
summary: Big hassle to apply, but it does work

reviewText: As usual, Griot's products are top-notch. What I won't do, is lie to you and tell you that this is completely different than Rain-X. What I will do is tell you that this is a great product, which works at least as well as Rain-X, and comes from a brand I trust for products to use on my car.Is there anything wrong with just using the inexpensive Rain-X? No, not at all. This stuff feels the same, smells the same, etc. Actually, Rain-X is probably even a bit easier to apply, considering it comes in a spray bottle.So, the product works great, but it's likely more expensive than a competing product, and I don't doubt that the competing product performs just as well.

Yes, it's from Griot's Garage and they're known for excellent but expensive auto items. This glass sealer is no exception. It works as advertised but at almost $9 per bottle it's expensive. This Griot's sealer works just as good as Rain-X. I see no reason to pay the extra money unless impressing your friends is paramount.3 stars for a decent glass sealer.-2 stars due to pricing

I used this on my wife's car, which probably just needs new wiper blades.  But this helped significantly to get the water to bead up and out of the way (instead of the wet 'smears' we got before).  It's a bit of work to spread it on and wipe off - kind of like waxing the car - but the results were good.
