This is a well made and effective 5W battery maintainer. It came quite well packaged, a box, within a box, within a box plus additional packing paper, bit of overkill actually. Even so the unit arrived without the indicated stainless screws but substituted my own without issue.Like many I have the typical outdoor shed storing a lawn tractor all winter and like many, every spring it's dead as a door nail. Although a bit early I went out, checked the mower (it was dead, just a few clicks). Set the panel in one of the shed windows, attached the clamps properly and tried again after a week of semi-sunny March weather. (the window only gets morning direct sun). Engine turned over and started right up so apparently as advertised it will charge a small battery.One thing of note, unlike the car cigarette charger attachment the battery clamps have no indicator light. You have no way of seeing if power is flowing or connection is made with out a multimeter or tester. A glaring omission for many a home owner as most would like some indication that the unit is actually "on".For remote battery maintaining and even charging of small batteries this will do the job.

The first thing I noticed about this charger is the sturdy construction and engineering.  It has separte plugs for clipping on to a battery or plugging it into your cigarette lighter plug.  It's simple to use either of these plug adaptions due to the unique lead adapter plug that comes off the 6 foot lead from the solar cell.  All you have to do is select the plug end you wish to use and plug that lead into the solar cell lead.  I had kept my RV plugged into the home electrical source to keep the battery charged.  I didn't know if this system would be able to keep my RV charged as I have a electronic mouse deterrant and a couple of alarm units that run off the battery.  They are small electrical draws but do tend to drain the battery quickly.  This solar battery charger has kept the RV battery fully charged.  I will recommend this solar charger to my friends and family.
summary: Well built and easy to use.

reviewText: As other reviewers said, this isn't for charging a vehicle with a dead battery, but mostly for trickle charging vehicles that aren't used much.  It would be ideal for a boat or ATV.  I use it for a truck I rarely drive.  Of course, it works far better in sunny days.  I don't really know how to evaluate how well it works because I can't see it happen!  But the parts are good quality.  I love that you can put it on either your battery or you can use the 12 volt plug into your cigarette charger.  That is a nice feature for ease of use.

This is the kind of device that you can use to keep the battery charged up on an occasionally used piece of equipment like a riding mower or a motorcycle that can be near some sunlight.Or, if you are parking somewhere for a while in the sun and you want to help make sure that your vehicle will start when you get back, this device can be useful.I have used it with my lawn mower and it keeps the battery in tip-top charge, ready to start right up!It's pretty large, a bit bigger than 1 foot by 1 foot, and has clamp-type connectors (that seem pretty sturdy) and a cigar / accessory plug, and screws for mounting to something which could help to keep it properly pointed at the sun.It can be helpful if all you need is a trickle charge and not a boost!

NOCO BLSOLAR2 Battery Life + Black 2.5W Solar Battery Charger and maintainer is an excellent product. It is very easy to setup and use.I hooked it up to my lawnmower battery to maintain the charge and so far so good. I would recommend it because it works well. I am not a very technical person  and I could hook it up.

NOCO BLSolar2 2W and 5W panels:First things first with solar panels. Even the very best solar cells are generally 15%-20% efficient. I've been hearing about how solar panels will become the dominant alternative energy source in "the next 5 years" for the past 20+ years. I started using the NOCO 2W charger knowing that based on my calculations, it probably won't be powerful enough to maintain a car battery, and that a 10W is a more appropriate size for a maintainer. After using this NOCO 2W charger for over a week, and taking down some data along the way, my conclusion is that the 2W isn't enough unless you are living closer to the equator with the panel directly under the sun with longer periods of daylight. The 5W is more useful as it can provide enough current to overcome a vehicle's standby current draw AND maintain the battery's charge.I'm in Michigan and tested this panel in the sun (as much as we can get in February/March) but we mainly had cloudy days and the amount of daylight is fairly restricted during this time. I started off on a E-series van that has minimal amount of electronics and standby current draw/parasitic draw. The initial voltage as 12.05 VDC. After using the solar charger for 2 days, the voltage actually dropped to 12.03 VDC. At first I thought it was the LED on the cigarette lighter adapter, but further experimentation showed that there is about 10-20 mA of current draw when the panel is not being hit with sunlight. I did a second trial run for a period of 4 days. The starting voltage was 11.93 VDC at 32F, but 4 days later the voltage dropped down to 11.88 VDC at 25F.The typical parasitic draw for a car is about 30-60 mA, so a battery maintainer has to overcome that current draw and provide enough capacity to actually charge the battery. I normally use 800mA Battery Tenders, which are "smart" chargers that can provide a meager amount of charging power but are more intelligent when it comes to maintaining. The NOCO 2W provides up to 21 VDC, but I'm skeptical about the charging current.So I grabbed an older car battery and left it right under the sun. I used a clamp DC ammeter and observed that the panel would provide a maximum of 30mA when there was direct sunlight. If a cloud went overhead, or I turned the panel over, it would draw up to 20mA of current.I took the 5W panel and ran it through the same tests. It provides 120mA of current in direct sunlight which is roughly 25% of the maximum advertised charging current. When the panel was flipped over, I only saw a peak of 10mA current draw from the panel itself.Doing some math, a 10W panel would be more appropriate for all conditions as the larger panel would work better in conditions like Michigan, at least being able to overcome parasitic draw during the day. I'd recommend disconnecting it at night or when it is cloudy though.Overall: 4/5, great build quality but the 2W is just too small of charging capacity for a car battery. If you live near the equator and have plenty of bright sunlight during the day, this may work for a smaller capacity battery. The 5W is more reasonable, but a 10W is what I'd recommend. You still need to park your car in a way the panel can directly face the sun and when you expect lots of daylight. It is a green way of maintaining your car battery or charging a separate battery.UPDATE 13 APR 2013:I have been using the 5W on the E-250 van. When we had sunny days, the 5W panel would actually charge up the battery. I saw it go from 11.98 VDC to 12.01 VDC over the span of just a few hours.Once we started to get non-stop cloudy and rainy days (it has been raining and cloudy for over 8 days straight), the 5W panel cannot provide sufficient current to the battery. The open terminal voltage at the solar panel is 20-21 VDC, but the current is too small to maintain the battery. As a result, the battery voltage is steadily dropping by 0.02-0.03 VDC per day with the panel hooked up. I removed the LED on the cigarette light plug, and that slowed down the discharge to 0.01 VDC a day. The bottom line is that IT NEEDS DIRECT SUNLIGHT during the day, or else it isn't providing a sufficient charge. The 2W, even in direct sunlight, is providing a mediocre amount of current that is insufficient to overcome parasitic draw and self-discharge of the battery. Get at least the 5W, but a 10W will work a lot better.
summary: You need at least the 5W to charge a car battery, 2W is too small, avoid cloudy days. Needs direct sunlight.

reviewText: I've been using the 5 watt version for several months now.  It's mounted outside in New England and exposed to full sun and all the weather that can be thrown at it.  Despite some very hot days (full southern exposure) and soaking rains, nothing seems to bother it.  I use it to keep the battery in my John Deere tractor charged.  It's advertised as a charger and maintainer, but I'm not sure it's a "smart" maintainer.  By smart, I mean I have other maintainers that vary the charge rate and whether they are charging at all based on battery status.  Although I'm not certain, I believe this device maintains a constant low level charge.  In any event, my JD battery seems no worse for wear and now it always cranks strongly, even if I haven't used the tractor for a couple of weeks.  Very pleased.
summary: Well Built -- Not Sure It's a "Smart" Maintainer

reviewText: I am very happy with this charger; I used it to recharge my dead mower battery after I left it unused in the mower all winter. I did not keep track of how many days it took to recharge it but it worked. Now I have the mower parked in the garage next to the south wall, charger cord runs outside through a port and maintains my battery. I did not use the suction cups, although it comes with both the suction cups and four screws to mount it.
summary: Easy to hook up and charged my dead battery

reviewText: My husband groaned when I ordered this..."one more piece of junk" were his exact words. You see, we have tried two or three of these in the past and each has failed to live up to expectations. One was roughly the same price and two were substantially more costly, so when this inexpensive little device came up for review, he was less than enthusiastic. I thought "hey, what do we have to lose" and went for it anyway.Glad I did because this one - despite the low price - delivers! In fact, by the next morning the spouse came to breakfast with this thing in his hands to show me all the reasons it was such a nice little device. We have a travel trailer and like many people, have to constantly mess with the battery..or worse, we forget about it. Yes, we have a battery tender and usually just end up taking the battery out of the travel trailer, hooking it up in the garage and leaving it there for ages OR forgetting and letting the battery run down more than it really should (the fate of our last battery). Of course, the price of batteries makes this less than desirable especially when having to shell out a couple hundred dollars each.Our current battery is an AGM so this was tested on that. It was down about 15% at the time this was tested. The day was sunny but had some clouds. We are in Florida so even during winter have a fairly long day of sunshine. We were both rather surprised how fast this managed to charge the battery...no, it's not as fast as hooking it up to electricity but def had close to full charge by that evening. We didn't really keep a close eye on it but the next morning when went to take a look it was already fully charged.It should be understood that this is a trickle charger NOT something you will use to jump-start a car. If the battery is really low (not suggested especially for AGM batteries) then it could certainly take much longer to restore. We are using this to maintain a charge in AGM batteries for a travel trailer and as such, it is just about perfect!The suction cups on each corner make this easy to attach to a window in the travel trailer for maximum sunshine then simply run the cables and viola'...done! Love the fact that it is then all but maintenance free. To be on the safe side, we went ahead and connected our usual battery tender to assure no overcharging. No more forgetting, no more hauling a battery in/out, no more nothing. Simple but effective.
summary: Affordable Travel Trailer Solution! Better than expected

reviewText: The NOCO BLSOLAR2 Battery Life+ solar battery charger is a kit that comes with a solar panel that connects to either battery clamps or a DC cigarette lighter plugin cable. The kit also has suction cups for attaching the panel to a window where it could receive sunlight. This is a 2.5W kit, which offers a modest amount of current that is OK for keeping a battery charged or slowly recharging a drained battery - it certainly won't get a fully dead battery charged up right away, so it's for maintenance, not emergencies. Where I am in Florida this works pretty well, as you can position the panel to get sunlight and it will steadily bring charge to your battery. This is ideal for 12v batteries as the package suggests, so if you have a lawnmower, ATV, scooter, and other devices with small batteries, this will work quite well. For automobiles this can help keep the charge for when you go for long periods without driving the vehicle. This is a useful item, though some users may wish to use a more powerful solar panel to speed up charging time. Since the cables used to attach the panel to a battery are detachable you could use them with a different solar panel if you wished to. The one thing that I find lacking with this kit is a portable protective case to store the panel and cables in when they aren't in use, as a small panel such as this could be kept in a handy case. Since there's no case, you may wish to store this in a generic storage tote to protect it.* Update: I've now gotten the 5W kit, which provides a larger solar panel that gives more power for faster recharging. It works just like the 2.5 watt kit except it will charge batteries faster. I would recommend the 5W kit to charge larger batteries. Amazon's Vine program applied my original review to both the 2.5W and 5W versions.
summary: Pretty good solar battery charger for maintaining charge

reviewText: I like this unit.  It is very well made and solid.  The wiring and connectors are all top quality unlike others I have tried in the past (some of the others had corroded terminals right out of the box).  The output voltage is right on the money (full sunlight).  It will come in handy keeping my tractor charged during those long winter months and I will use it when I park my car at the airport for longer trips.

Fuzzbean noted that Amazon is mixing reviews for the 5 watt version (which this review is about) and a less powerful version (2.5 watts) so pay attention to mentions of suction cups - they are apparently included with the 2.5W as there are no suction cups included with the 5W edition.  Not that I have anything against suction cups, you understand.I'm tardy in posting this Vine review because I found this difficult to seriously test in my environment.  I have no rarely-used vehicles.  The battery I need to maintain is really two batteries connected together in parallel to supply an inverter for emergency use during a power outage.  Each of the two is a 12V 110Ah AGM battery (relatively robust batteries).  I didn't expect to be able to tell that this device was doing a lot for them as they take a while to drain appreciably under load and my guess is that a low-volt/low-amp trickle charge would take days to recharge them if it ever did.So I just hooked up a borrowed multimeter and started taking measurements.  Even with a pretty good coating of pine pollen (it's that time of year in NC) and full cloud cover I was consistently seeing 6+ volts  When I wiped the panel clean and the sky cleared, I tried again and consistently saw readings of 7 - 8 volts even though the panel was not in direct sun.  Due to my own ignorance I was unable to get a reliable milliamp reading but I'm hoping that since the voltage output exceeds promises, the milliamps at least meet them.  This 5W version promises 410 milliamps vs. the 2.5W version's 180 milliamps.One thing that bothered me a little was a "helpful tip" in the accompanying instructions: "For extra waterproofing and to extend the life of the panel, cone bead around the edges of the inside frame."  I guess I should be handier, but "cone bead" implies to me that I need to go buy some kind of caulk (last time I was at Wally World there were a zillion kinds of caulk and you can count on me to always choose the wrong one) and seal the thing up.  If this is a good thing to do, why not just do it before it leaves the factory?  Anything I put caulk on ends up looking like a pastry item decorated by the Three Stooges so maybe I'm just overly sensitive.  And don't get me started on "cone bead" as a compound verb.I should confess that I own a NOCO Genius G7200 charger/maintainer that I'm very happy with, so I may have a bias toward their products (for the suspicious, the G7200 was not a Vine thing; I bought it with my own real money).  I was tempted to ding this solar panel a star for the "cone bead" thing but gave that star back because these people seem to offer good stuff at reasonable prices and this feels like a solid, well made item.  If you have use for this kind of thing, the current Amazon price of $35 seems very reasonable.
summary: Solid item from a firm I've had good experience with

reviewText: I have the 5 watt and 2.5 watt versions of this solar panel, and I have to give them full marks for being easy to use, well-made, and put together nicely as a kit.The NOCO solar panels are sold as "Battery Maintainers" and that is their most obvious use, but they don't have to be just for keeping engine batteries topped up. I have half dozen batteries I use with my various solar panels (old car batteries, deep-cycle batteries). I charge them up, then bring them in to my RV to attach to my inverters, and run appliances and electronics from them that way.These panels come with battery clamp connectors, so I just attach them to my batteries outside in the sun. I have a multimeter to tell me when a battery is fully charged and ready to go. Since I don't need to run anything directly from the solar panel, and I use electricity sparingly, I don't need bigger panels. I just give them the time they need to do their thing. It's more crucial that I have a large enough wattage on my power inverter, actually.With these being as low-watt as they are, you don't need to buy/hook up an additional charge controller. That makes these basically plug and go panels, which is nice if you are new to using solar power and don't want to drop a lot of money experimenting with it. You still need an have an inverter for AC power uses, however.PERSONAL SOLAR NOTESAltogether, I have a 15-watt solar panel, two five watt panels, the 2.5 watt panel and a 1 watt mini-panel (from different companies). I also have an assortment of stand-alone solar gadgets. I have four deep cycle batteries I am always charging up with a panel attached, and rotate things around. I have several inverters to hook different things up to.If you live in a sort of camping/RV/low income situation, like I do most of the time, this really is enough to get by with. I can use my entertainment devices, lights, low watt cooking appliances, fans for air and a small personal space heater, and that's all my needs right there.RECOMMENDATIONObviously, for the typical person living in a home with all the luxuries, this isn't going to be enough of a solar system to run a household. We are only talking 2.5 or 5 watts in either panel. However, for people living an extreme frugal lifestyle, or living out of their car or an RV, these panels are nice to have around.More to the point for most people, these little panels could be lifesaving if an emergency situation hits your area. You could pull out your car/boat/lawn mower battery and charge it up if you had to, and - using an inverter or a DC appliance - get power. You could charge your phone and make a call out, or connect to the internet. You could charge your Kindle and the kids could have days of reading time available. You could hook up a lamp and have light.And they do keep a car battery topped up nicely with the included cigarette lighter (12-volt plug) connector.  :)
summary: Nice chargers for getting your feet wet with solar

reviewText: The instructions indicate that it is designed to work well in "low-light, cloudy and overcast conditions" and I have to agree.  They indicate that it will output 15 to 22 volts in "full sun".  I tested on an overcast but "bright" day (no direct sunlight, 100% cloud cover) and it output 21.3 volts inside, right next to a window.  In my living room "near" a window but not with anything you could construe as direct light, it output just over 14 volts.One caveat (not a fault of the charger) to be aware of is that the 12 volt plug which you'd plug into a "cigarette lighter" (politically correctly named these days "power adapter") in your car won't work in many modern cars because there is no connection when the ignition switch is off.  So for many cars you'd need to make the connections under the hood and that certainly is not convenient.  The adapter does have a light on it which makes it easy for you to test your vehicle.However if you were taking a trip somewhere (camping?) and using your car for music or some other such purpose then this charger might help offset the power drain.Keep in mind that at full power it will only generate 5 watts and that's not much!It is definitely a nice (small) solar panel, but it has limited usage roles.

There is nothing like a brand new idea for a vexing ongoing problem that solves that problem.  NOCO solved that problem with ease and effectiveness.  Before I used the NOCO I attempted to start my mower only to find that the winter drained the 2-year-old battery to the point that it would not start but it did turn over.  So, I attached the Solar Battery Charger to my grass assassin so that in a few weeks I would be ready for the annual hunt and chop routine.  Frankly, I did not expect great results; however, I was delightfully surprised when I returned two days later to find a fully charged battery but a mower that begged to be run and used.  I suggested to it that we would have to wait for something of value to cut and it frowned and returned to its previous resting state with one exception:  it was ready to go and I only had to use the NOCO to "get it done."

When I ordered this thing, I was expecting something no bigger than my iPad, but it's actually larger than your average car sunroof.It stores easily, and provides plenty of power for those outages that last for days--like the 2003 blackout, the 2005 blackout, the blackouts after Irene and Sandy here in NYC alone.  To not have some way of charging your devices, even if not especially in a big city, where you might be out of power for days or weeks, is frankly stupid.Even for total non-emergencies, it's a good idea.  Say you're on a road trip, and your cell phone or tablet battery is dead.  Are you really going to run the engine and burn gas just to charge your precious device?Unless you're rich enough to have yourself airlifted to some resort where they have power during a major blackout, get yourself a camp stove, a Petzl headlamp, and this solar batter charger at the very least.
summary: Because the Sun will never run out of power during your lifetime.

reviewText: I've been using this to keep the battery on our infrequently used tractor up to snuff and it seems to do the trick. It will not readily recharge a discharged battery due to the very modest power output, but as a way to fight off the normal slow degradation of an unused battery it does just great.

Batteries gradually lose charge over time, even if you're not using them. Hooking this product up to your car battery (or one of similar size) will slow down, if not stop, this process. However, the NOCO only puts out 5 watts, and when you realize that your tiny nightlight draws the same amount of power, you begin to understand why calling this thing a "charger" is a bit of a misnomer.Used solely as a maintainer, this product seems to work well when hooked up to a riding lawnmower that sees use every few weeks (the real test will be over winter).The NOCO comes with two options for hooking it up to the battery: directly via small alligator clamps, or indirectly via a cigarette-lighter DC outlet.I do have a gripe with the product though. It's clearly meant to be permanently mounted, judging by the included screws and the mounting holes in the corner. In that case, the included cable isn't very long, since you would presumably have to mount this somewhere that gets sun and then run the cable to your battery, which is more than likely indoors. If you're hooking it up via the DC outlet, then you have no included way to mount this without running a cable from the outside of your vehicle to the inside.*EDIT 3/29/14: So I had a spare mostly-charged power chair battery lying around at the end of the season, and as a test I hooked the NOCO up to it (had to use an extra wire between the battery and the panel since the included cord is somewhat short), made sure the panel was in good sunlight, and left the battery in the tool shed all winter (roughly September to March in New Jersey). The battery was working in late October but was dead when I tested it last week. I'm not particularly surprised, and it was nothing a few minutes on a powered charger couldn't fix, but I wanted to make sure that info got out there in case that was anyone's anticipated use (though, to be fair, NJ isn't exactly the sunniest state; in the Southwest you might have better luck).
summary: Once you realize what you have, a good product

reviewText: The build quality is good. The included cables are of nice gauge and quality. The clamps are nice and strong. But 2.5w just doesn't offer much of anything. Go with the higher rated model for sure. It's nice and compact and easy to mount with screws or the included suction cups. Seems durable, but it's still got glass on it, so it's not indestructible. It seems like it should survive any accidental drops, but if it hits just right, for sure the glass will crack. Overall, it's just ok, given the wattage. But for what it is, 4 stars seems fair. Certainly doesn't cost much, but then, it doesn't offer much either.

This solid unit is easy to use. The wires are a little flimsy, and could use an upgrade, but the unit itself it very nice. This charger is definitely for maintenance purposes only, and not for emergencies, but it's great to keep in the trunk of your car, or outside the house. I plan on mounting mine outside for the summer to keep the small power tools and lawn mower charged. Definitely worth the money.

Like many, our tractor and other lawn products sit all winter without being started. Not every season but often enough we have had to take the battery out to be charged at Sears or somewhere else. Or they are sluggish when starting up in the spring. This solar charger is a good solution to priming the battery before start-up.While I wouldn't keep it out all winter I did use it to juice up our tractor this spring. It was very easy to attach (like any set of clips for a battery) and I placed the solar panel in the sun and let it sit for a few days.When I went to start the tractor, it almost didn't turn over (uncommon, without using the charger) so for a second, I was afraid I had actually drained the battery instead of charging it.But then it roared to life. Yeah!I had some concerns though. This is a glass solar panel (I'm not sure it could be anything else) so I was concerned that it would fall over or get knocked over and break. I'm not sure there is any way around this but it is difficult considering that it sits outside. I know it can be mounted somewhere for a more permanent placement which could keep it safer but finding somewhere that gets enough sun and is the right angle can prove difficult.Additionally, the cables are short. So you have to have your motorized vehicle close which usually means having it sit outside (hence not wanting to leave the unit and tractor outside all winter).A nice unit with some limitations.
summary: Easy to Use, Glass Front, Slow Charge

reviewText: I've been using this to trickle power to my marine batteries and it seems to work quite well. I did a lot of research on this topic a while ago and found out that as long as you have 5W or less (this one is 2.5W) then you do not need a charge controller to maintain the battery.BatteryMINDer Charger-Desulfator - 12 Volt, AGM Batteries, Model# 2012-AGM, which I use when my batteries are mostly run down. I use the solar charger and the BatteryMINDer with the 12V GEL Marine batteries that I use for my RV (I used to also have a boat and trolling motor). Anyways, one cool feature about the solar charger is that if I run the battery all the way down, the BatteryMINDer does not recharge it. It reports an error condition. However, if I put the solar panel trickle charger on that same battery for a day, then I can use the BatteryMINDer to fully recharge the battery. I imagine that the solar panel would eventually fully recharge the battery too, but I haven't actually tested that. Still, the solar charger is a good way to keep your batteries in good shape and topped off.

The solar panel came neatly packed and included a decent instruction manual.  The connectors have rubber skins on them to prevent accidental short circuiting.  I tried it out on my car battery and on a hobby 12V 7Ah battery.  Both worked great. The charger is rated at 2.5W max, 180mA, 15-22V in full sun.  I measured 22V as advertised.  The charger is really just a battery maintainer because it puts out so little amps, but that is what I need it for.It has a nice compact size and is lightweight (9.2"x9.2", 1.8lbs).  The suction cups are cool for mounting on the inside of a window.  One of my cars has power at the 12V outlet with the key off and the other doesn't.  No power equals no solar charge as well.  The manual says "If your 12V plug connector does not operate while your vehicle is off, you can charge and maintain your vehicle through the OBDII connector.  You can purchase this accessory online at batterylife.com".  I checked the website, but no mention of the OBDII connector.  I sent an email to the company and 2 weeks later, no response.The manual says "For extra waterproofing and to extend the life of the panel, use a silicone bead around the edges of the inside frame."  I decided to do this and used some masking tape to get a clean look.  It would have been nice to come that way from the factory.

This solar panel is designed to maintain an already charged small battery.  Right now we are using this on the motorcycle and its working great.  We plan to take this on our next trip to maintain power for the battery backup and I'm looking to use this to power the cell phones & ipad.  Nice unit, works well, and is well made.

We have a small truck that rarely gets used anymore, but when we need it, it sure is nice to have it.  I've gone to multiple times to start it only find that it barely cranks or it doesn't start at all.  I've set this battery charger so that it is facing outside the windshield and will collect a great deal of sunlight from a southerly direction.  I plan on leaving it there except for when I need to use the truck.  It plugs into the cigarette lighter and will slowly charge the battery.It appears to be well constructed and I really like that 4 plastic suction cups were included.  It makes it easy to adhere it to the windshield so I don't need to find something to support it.  And we also have a 12 volt battery to an old riding lawnmower so I may actually have to buy another one for it.Great idea using free energy (solar) to charge a battery.  I have several different types of solar chargers and this is among my favorites.  The charger is about the size of a square, single layer cake pan.
summary: NOCO BLSOLAR2 Battery 2.5W Charger and Maintainer

reviewText: It's hard to tell how this is going to work out in the long run but I checked the output with a voltmeter and it was as stated. It comes with holes for permanent mounting but I think I'm going to mount it on a piece of marine plywood so I don't have to puncture the roof on my trailer. I used the pigtail connector to my trailer battery but you could also leave it on the dashboard of a car and use the cigarette lighter jack supplied. I will update as soon as camping season gets underway.

First impressions:The unit appeared to be solid, and it was easy to use. One thing it was missing was some sort of indicator light that showed that it was charging. The instructions stated to just use a voltmeter, but it would be easier to have this built into the unit.After first use:We set up the solar panel in direct sunlight and connected it to my husband's dirtbike battery that needed charging. The process was easy, but we found that the charging process was slow. That being said, it worked well and fully charged the battery with some time.Final Thoughts:It would be nice if the wires were a bit longer in case you wanted/needed to mount the panel in a higher location. We feel this would be a great unit for when you're out camping/riding and want to make sure your battery is charged during your down time.Obviously, there is no storage for the solar panel, so you can only charge when there is good sun.Overall, my husband was very happy with this unit.
summary: Works well and is easy to use

reviewText: With only a little under half an amp of current available under direct sun, this panel won't bring a dead battery up to full charge, but it's just the thing for maintaining a car that isn't driven regularly- if you leave the car outdoors. I typically only buy a new car every 8-10 years, and keep the old car as a spare. A panel like this is a lot more convenient than periodically starting the engine, or running a cord from the house or garage to a charger tucked in under the hood.  The instructions say that the panel should be capable of doing a full charge on batteries up to 20 amp-hours in capacity, and to test that I've currently got mine on the battery of my scooter, which has been sitting in the garage all winter without a charger. I'm thinking this might also be useful for charging batteries on mobile electronics, like cell phones and iPods.Overall construction looks reasonably solid, and four wood screws are included in the package, suggesting the user might screw it to an outside wall or the roof of a shed. I'm thinking it would be a good way to keep the rechargeable battery in a game camera in the woods topped off, too. Amateur radio licensees might consider it for powering a low-power remote repeater. At the asking price, it's inexpensive enough to buy one just to experiment with.
Older Airstream trailer, this keeps the battery topped off just fine. Trailer jack, lights, radio and panel all have full power.
summary: Great for keeping trailer batteries fresh!

reviewText: But I will review it as is.  The rain should be gone for the weekend so I can see how much it will charge.  With the rain we have been having, it's only a partial charge and not a fair review but I have to leave a review.  Lovely days ahead in S. La, so I'm hoping for a full charge this weekend to update my review.
summary: Too  much rain to give a full review but not bad so far!

reviewerName: Mr. Deeds "Opportunity is limited only by ima...
reviewText: I picked up the NOCO BLSOLAR5 Solar Battery Charger for the 2 12-volt batteries we use for our portable electric fence. The fence is out in our pasture for our sheep and there is no electricity out there. So I had to walk out with the fresh battery from the house, exchange it with the dead battery out in the pasture, and then lug the dead battery back to the house and plug it into the charger.This solar charger made that process a whole lot easier. I attached the solar panel to a wooden post and use it to charge one battery while the other is in use. I usually get 3 days on each charge, so by the time one battery is dead or running low, the other is fully charged and ready to go.The NOCO BLSOLAR5 saves me time and I love it. Great product - built well, too, so I am sure it will last for years.
summary: Recharges the 12-volt batteries we use for our electric fence

reviewText: First, let me start off by stating that this is an un-bias review, I purchased this product from amazon, unlike many of the Amazon Vine product reviewers.Being an automotive technician with an engineering background, I can not for the life of me recommend this product to the general consumer. Make no mistake, as others have claimed, the build quality of this Item is great, but aside from the rest of the reviews, there is one aspect I haven't seen covered that MUST be addressed:The output voltage is way too high for any automotive installation application. after installing the solar array, I decided to take some readings to see what kind of output I was receiving, before finishing the install.First sunny day of April, 74degrees, and located in TN:Voltage: 24.2v in direct sunlightAmpere: 0.3Most 12v systems recharge at a voltage range between 13.2-14.7v via the alternator, or battery charger, Hooking this device in with a 24v output (even at low amps) can cause the battery to over-charge, the ecu to throw an over-voltage check engine code, or even worse, fry the ECU.devices such as lawn mowers, trolling motors, four wheelers, tractors, etc, that may not use or monitor battery voltage may be better suited for use with this, although I would not recommend charging even those batteries at such a high voltage.
summary: Be Sure To Read This Review!!!

reviewText: I feel like I should dock them a star for using the word "charger" in the title but what do I know?  I suppose a maintenance charge is still a "charge".  Just realize that the purpose of this device is to maintain your battery -- to keep it from losing charge naturally from sitting idle.  The smaller one, which I have, doesn't even output .2 amps and even the larger one is under half an amp so it's literally just a trickle of energy.  The idea is you keep your emergency power battery (or scooter battery or whatnot) charged up over long periods of disuse, by mounting this solar panel somewhere and leaving the battery hooked to it.It's waterproof so you can leave it outdoors.  It's very simple to hook up and comes with what you need to mount it and connect your battery.  You'll have to wait a year (or a few months anyway) before I can really tell you how well it kept the battery charged but for now I can say the quality looks good!

reviewerName: Raquel S. "Avid Amazon Fan and Kindle User"
reviewText: For the price, the NOCO BLSolar2 Battery Charger/Maintainer would be worth trying if you have vehicles that sit for a long time between use. For me, I have a riding lawn mower that sits a long time between use and every single time my husband has to charge the battery to get it going. This was the main reason I picked up this device. Living in sunny Florida, I'm hoping this will work to my advantage too.The setup is quite easy and NOCO give you the option between battery connectors or a 12V lighter plug connector your car. You also get suction cups and mounting screws, if so needed. The connectors have caps to protect it when not in use.It took me a few scant minutes to connect the solar panel to the lawn mower. I then covered the mower and moved the solar panel to a sunny spot. Time will tell how well this device works and I will come back to update with the information.Right now, for the price, it's build quality, and ease of use I give the NOCA Battery Charger/Maintainer 5 stars. However, since I don't know how well it works yet, I'm pulling it back to 4 stars until further notice.
summary: Interesting concept. Time will tell how well it works.

reviewText: As most of the Amazon Vine reviewers has pointed out this product's Build quality is very good and I fully agree with them. The product also works as advertised. I tried it using on a old Ford Focus 2001 car that I seldom use and sits in the garage most of the time and connected this 5W Solar Battery charger and Maintainer via the cigarette port for several days.  The battery did seem to charge adequately. I did monitor the battery voltage from time to time using both aFluke 87-V Digital Multimeterwhich I own and also used aScanGauge II Automotive Computerand it maintained 13.8v which is considered nominal for that battery in the focus.This obviously is not designed to fully charge a dead battery but merely trickle charge the battery when you do not use your vehicle for couple of weeks and it perfectly works for those situations.Having said, One of the user reported on Amazon concerning about the panel's high voltage output in direct sunlight and the possibility of overcharging small batteries. I must admit it is quite possible if this 5W panel is left alone with a small size battery for extended period of time and I fully agree with that reviewers concerns.That approximately 24 vDC - 25.1 vDC output from the panel indicates the Open Circuit Voltage (Voc) most panels of this type do always output similar voltage characteristics and as long as they are installed properly do not pose any sorts of risk damaging a huge car battery for example as it will take considerable amount of Amps to ruin a standard car battery which this panel can never provide as it max out at about 400 ma under full sunlight and cannot overcharge it.If you are paranoid about the Open Circuit Voltage (Voc) you can always install aZENER DIODE 1 WATT 14V 5% DO-41diode which falls in that range of voltage which you feel safe for the battery (Cheap option) along with aSchottky Blocking Diodesor better install aCharge Controllerbetween the panel and your car battery just to be safe.Hope this proves useful to others.Happy Shopping here on Amazon.

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: 2.5 Watt charger:I put my Fluke meter on this to check the actual output:17.5 VDC - constant.35 to .9 watts - varies with lightI'm in the Midwest - Chicago, and it's winter. We're marginal when it comes to solar power use - not enough sun.  For a trickle charge this is fine - it's better than nothing. But if you need more than a couple of watts and are not in a sunny location, then you'll need a more powerful charger. The 5 watt version may give you 2 watts in bright Midwest sun. This one only provided a max of .9 watts.As for attaching to your car - almost all auto power plugs/outlets/lighters power down when the auto us not running. So plugging this into your "lighter" will do no good. It does include small battery clamps, but if you use the clamps, how in the world will you get the other end inside the car where the solar panel is? This would be a major project for most vehicles. You obviously don't want to stick this on the hood of your car - it will be stolen pretty quickly.If your "lighter" is always on (plug in your GPS, charger, etc and see if it stays on), this is ideal.  If you're in a secure lot, this is also good. This lower power unit would be good for smaller batteries - motorcycle, electric trolling motor, boat, etc.  For an auto, you'll need the larger unit.It includes four suction cups that hold VERY well, and four screws for a more permanent attachment.  The screws and suction cups use the same holes.  Looking at the quality, I would think this would sell for $50.  I'm going to see how it works on my solar landscaping lights this summer.Currently it sits on the roof of our house and keeps a motorcycle battery charged. I use this battery to power a motion controlled light on the deck. Plenty of battery life and the panel keeps it topped off.
summary: Excellent quality, typical solar low power output

reviewText: Put this on a skid steer out back ( Bobcat) and placed a piece of plexiglass on the suction tubes to water proof it a bit since it is out side

Only had this unit in operation for a couple of weeks maintaining my RV batteries but it's keeping them charged at what my meter tells me is a "full-Level".  I installed the unit on the roof using the supplied stainless steel screws so it gets full sun.  Installation was relatively quick and easy.  Of course running the charging wires to the battery was a chore as it's a distance from the roof to the battery but that's expected since the charge wires also had to be extended to get from the panel to the battery.  The true test will be in a few months after the unit has been in the summer sun for a while.Four stars only because the unit needs further testing before a full evaluation can be given.I'll update ths review in the fall or if there's a change.Update 9/6/2013:  The unit spent the summer keeping my RV batteries charged.  It's still working just fine.

This is an excellent solar battery charger for those situations where power is not readily available or inconvenient. It is well made and high quality. It is also the latest solar cell technology where it does not require clear sunlight but can charge even on cloudy days. It can also handle bright sunlight and hot Summer days along with rain. It is weatherproof and rust resistant. Overall one of the better solar battery chargers. There are some things to consider when using this solar battery charger. It only outputs 5 watts which is about 410ma or 1/2 amp DC and that is a on a sunny day. So don't expect this solar charger to restore a run down or drained battery, it does not provide enough power. It will be good for those vehicles/boats/atvs that have on-board computers (like engine computers) or other electronics that draw a current from the battery even when shutoff. Our boat draws about 50-100ma even when shutoff and if you don't use it or charge it for a week or two then the battery will get low. This solar charger is a great way to handle that discharge and then you don't have to worry about a leaving your boat/etc for a long period unattended. With small batteries (like with ATVs, motorcycles and similar) you might have to worry about overcharging although not likely since this solar charger only works during the daytime. Overall an excellent and quality solar battery charger that can be very useful.

I haven't had this long enough to know if it's going to add life to my ride on mowers' battery life or not.  However, since I've hooked it up, the mower seems to be turning over better then it used to when it had sat for a few weeks.  So it seems the trickle charge is keeping the battery topped up.  This unit is weather resistant, but not weather proof.  I mounted it flat on the side of my shed, under an eave.  It gets great Sun all day, and is out of the rain, unless it's raining sideways (which happens here.)

This is my first experience with a solar panel which may be a good unit to start out with. Documentation states that it is specifically for charging all types and amps of led acid batteries but 12 volt: There are a few FAQs on their website but not much else.It is glass so if you drop it it will probably shatter. But once mounted it shouldn't be a problem unless someone throws a rock at it.Even though it is supposed to be weather proof, the instructions say to caulk around the edges to help prevent water from getting in.It has two types of connectors: alligator type clips and accessory/cigarette lighter adapter. It also comes with mounting screws and 8 feet of wire.There is no way of telling how the charge is going. My AC trickle charger at least has a red and green light to indicate the process. Hooking a voltmeter up is fun to watch it change as you tilt the panel so I know it is working.The FAQs state while low it is possible to overcharge and there is no protection against that.It was easy to hookup to my car battery but I plan to get a small battery and use it for a light in our garden shed which is a long extension cord from the house. From there the possibilities are endless.
This is a great item and is well worth the low price.  In an emergency this is great thing to have.  It works great for keeping English cars happy too.
summary: Great Idea and it works too.

reviewText: The NOCO Solar Battery Charger works well to keep charged 12V batteries maintained. The 180 mA charge is not sufficient to charge a battery, but is sufficient to keep it from discharging.The solar panel is well built, not too large at 10" x 10", and provides multiple mount options - suction cups or you can screw it in permanently.I had a perfect opportunity to try it on a friend's boat which was just out of the boat motel for the spring. We suction cupped the NOCO to the windshield and connected it, on an overcast day, to an uncharged battery and got about a 1.5 Amp rise in the battery. We then charged the battery and left the NOCO connected for the next 2 weeks. The NOCO did an excellent job maintaining the battery at full charge. The NOCO is an excellent product for an infrequently used vehicle. Over the summer, we plan to go fishing about twice a month and we can be assured that we will have a fully charged battery.The cigarette power adapter charger seems like a great idea, but I do not have a "live" outlet in the car to test it out.I am excited about the product and once the summer is over will try to see if I can re-purpose the solar panel for other projects.
summary: Product "maintains" a battery charge - It does not charge a battery!

reviewText: After all the storms we experienced in my state, I think that having an alternative power source is essential, everyone should have at least one solar panel, a rechargeable battery and a power inverter. Why? Because in extreme emergencies the usual energy sources aren't available, while the sun comes back to shine nearly everyday.I experienced this first hand after we endured the Sandy superstorm. All of my neighbors were using gas generators during the power outage that followed, but in a matter of three days they simply ran out of gas. Not having gas in their cars either, or phone land lines, they were facing a total lack of communication. In top of all, we were not allowed to live our area either, because according to the Governor office, it was not safe.I was the only one in my block that has solar panels, even though small ones, they were enough to charge the devices my family needed charged, and to keep my batteries recharging. Ironically, I chose solar panels instead of gas generators because of the cost, contrary to what people believe, having an emergency solar charger isn't that expensive. So, I helped my neighbors to keep their cellphones charged.  We all learned to rely on solar energy, which we had plenty.I added the NOCO BLSOLAR5 5W Solar Battery Charger to my solar emergency system, which right now includes a few solar panels, batteries and inverters. This is an affordable way to have an emergency charger. This charger has many uses, but like I said before, in my experience this is the best one.This solar charger is low-priced, but it's great quality. I also like that the fuse included in the water-resistant fuse holder, can be replaced. The other two elements needed to complete an emergency solar charger kit are a rechargeable battery similar to this one12V 8.5AH Sealed Lead Acid (SLA) Battery for CSB GP 1272and a power inverter like this oneCobra CPI 480 400-Watt 12-Volt DC to 120-Volt AC Power Inverter with 5-Volt USB Output- I recommend both products because I own a couple of each, and they were a lifesaver.That's it, simply use the NOCO BLSOLAR5 5W Solar Battery Charger to keep a sealed AGM battery charged, and every couple of weeks half discharging it using the inverter as a way to maintaining it, and when another storm hits, you will be able, at least, to charge your cellphone.
summary: An excellent addition to a solar energy emergency kit

reviewText: Like another reviewer here, I got this with specific intent in mind - keeping what I expect is going to be a lightly used motorcycle's battery charged while it sits semi-neglected waiting for me to have some more free time and cooperative weather to take it out for a relaxing ride.  Since I've become a fair weather rider and am more cautious about taking a motorcycle out on overly crowded roadways, the motorcycle that I own is going to be left sitting for longer periods that I'd like, leaving the battery to slowly drain, which leaves me a few options to keep the battery ready when I am finally ready to use the m/c.I could pull out my old plug-in charger and let it sit like the vampire that it is while it provides a trickle charge, or I can make use of this device to use the free sunshine to get the same results.  Not that I expect a trickle charger to pull that much electricity, but given that I've got a house full of electronic items and with each monthly electric bill I see a reminder that my home is pulling more than twice what my neighbors do (which neighbors they are actually comparing to is something I wonder, but that's a different story for another day) and I feel like I'm paying more than I otherwise might need to (uh, gee, would that electrical usage also have something to do with two young ladies in the household, my wife's daughter and my own daughter, and their usage of hot water in the showers to wash their hair, followed by the use of the blow dryers to dry their hair, etc.) I figure that I should probably do what I can to avoid using utility company provided power when possible.Heck, I wish that solar power would come down in cost even more and that I could power things like the water heater and the blow dryer with solar, but the panels are still costly and the number of panels needed is still higher than I'd like so I'm back to using devices like this one which work fine for the types of purposes they are designed for.If you don't ask too much from it (or expect too much from it) it is a very useful device.  Don't expect it to power your home or even power a single device, but do expect it to be useful for keeping a battery charged.
summary: For what it is, it's nice

reviewText: This is a well-made quality item in that the cables and fitments seem of high quality as is the unit itself.This is not really a charger for your car battery, it's more of a maintainer. If you will not be driving your vehicle for a while, and it's parked outside, or you park near a window, you can use this to keep the battery from not draining down. Most modern day cars have some drain just by nature of all of the electronic devices that are powered all the time, not to mention alarms. If you don't drive for a few weeks, the battery may be drained. Using this device can solve that issue.It's nice that this comes with both the lighter port plug as well as direct battery terminal plugs includes. Some other ones do not come with both.

This solar powered tender and charger is considerably bigger than the picture suggests. At around 18" around it may look at place on top of a shed or in the yard. Do take into account the size.But it's very well made and it was showing a charge even in doors. Unfortunately this brings up my biggest complaint. It comes with a cigarette adapter and clips but... No stock tender connector. This means in all likelihood you will have to expose the battery on a motorcycle and hook up directly. Perhaps theres a peripheral connector available but I haven't checked.So the unit works, it's priced right and does what it says on the box. Just shame they missed out the most important connector for bikers.  One star off for that but otherwise great!

The unit is slightly larger than I envisioned (about 10" x 10") and seems to be of decent build quality. Despite the claim, I'm not sure how well it will stand up to years in the sun. The accessories (cables) are of better quality than I expected.It can be easily mounted with screws, the included suction cups (such as to a car window), or just propped up against something. It has an 8 foot cord to allow placement of the cell away from your battery. It comes with a set of clamp-on connectors (like jumper cables) and a connector for charging through a cigarette-lighter-style 12V port.On a clear and sunny February afternoon, I hooked up a voltmeter to the output and it is generating the peak rated 22V at 150 milliamps.If you are unfamiliar with these devices, they are not meant to power your devices directly, you use this to charge the battery that feeds your devices. I use it to charge a 12V tractor-mower size battery that I use to power camping gear (lanterns, DVD players).4 stars for build quality and utility, with a bonus star for its bargain price. 5 stars.UPDATE: taking it down a star since the build quality wasn't quite as high as I had hoped. After a very short life, it was knocked this off the workbench in my garage by my cat and the glass shattered into a thousand pieces.
summary: I get a charge out of this product!

reviewText: Easy to put up. WWorks well. Needs at least 9 hours sunlight to do its job. Be careful because there is glass.Best for smaller conventional lead acid batteries. An AGM battery probably does not need it.5 stars from me.

I had little or no expectations about this product as to what kind of power it can provide for a 12v battery in a 1 sq ft footprint.I have not used it for my car, but I am using it as a  battery backup for my NFS, DSL Model to ensure 100% uptime.  The way I have wired it is to use a car battery, a 110v inverter and this solar charger and I have let the solar charger let hang over the window with both the wires coming through the window and charging the battery.  The battery is wired to a inverter and then to the power supply which powers my internet accessories.It has been a month and so far, I have not had any issues with this.Overall, at the current prices - it is a great deal and it works pretty well.
summary: Very decent performance for its price

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: I have a wireless webcam which I was hoping to use in the yard.  With a 12 volt gel cell and a voltage converter to step down to USB (5V)  (I used something like thisMotorola Vehicle Power Adapter micro-USB Rapid Rate Charger) and a water resistant tub, I was able to set the camera out in the yard.Having measured the current draw at 220 mAh, (12v) I'm probably good on the gel cell - currently using 7.2AH like this: (UPG UB1272 - AGM Battery - Sealed Lead Acid - 12 Volt - 7.2 Ah Capacity - F1 ...On a decent day it will provide 200 mA but with clouds it drops to 120-130 mANote that the solar panel can deliver 410 mA but I've yet to get an accurate reading since the voltage is a lot higher (~15-18) and the load I'm applying affects the draw.  Can't tell the actual charge level of the battery but it hasn't died so far in a week's testing....
summary: Can provide remote power for wireless devices - if added to a gel cel....

reviewText: These make the clunky, wind-up "blind" style obsolete.Don't be discouraged if, initially, when popped out of their bag, they are reluctant to stick well on the glass. It takes a little time for them to relax, stretch out and flatten. Once in place, they are easily peeled off and repositioned.The absolute best feature is how, when accidentally lowering the rear window, they "snap" away from the glass as the window starts to make its way down, alerting you to your mistake. Then when winding the window back up, they reattach themselves in place - brilliant.
summary: Virtually Defies the Laws of Physics

reviewText: A couple of decades ago when I was a kid, I remember my parents' green-plaid luggage.  It was heavy.  Since I was the only son, my dad and I were the ones that had to carry all of the luggage by the handles - this is before the genius idea to put wheels on luggage!  I actually don't think they put wheels on the actual luggage until the 90's, why didn't they think of that 20 years earlier??  It would have made those family trips a lot easier that's for sure.These Brica pop-open static cling window shades are great.  They've been installed for a few weeks now and have not fallen down.  Before that, we had these bulky suction cup shades that were a bit temperamental.  The suction cup ones also don't like when you roll down the window when you forget to take the shade off.I've accidentally rolled down the window (a  little) a couple of times with the Brica static-cling shades and they are very adaptable, they will bend, yet still stay "static-clinged".  This gives us the flexibility to crack the windows as needed, and not have to keep putting it back up like with the suction cup types.Static-cling has been around forever, almost as long as "wheels" - why didn't someone think of this earlier for our first-born?  Genius (and relatively recent) ideas like wheels on luggage and static-cling baby shades is why I still keep the faith and that maybe one day I become a billionaire with some great new idea no one else has thought of.
summary: Genius! Far better than the suction cup types!

reviewText: These window shades are the easiest to use and they work great.  They block out the glaring sun, but the kids could still see the scenery as we drove along.  They are very lightweight and cling to the windows without slipping or falling off.  When we arrived back home I just pulled them off the windows and put them back in the bag where they will be ready for next time.  These shades left no marks or smudges on the windows either. I love the Brica 2 Count Pop Open Cling Window Shades.

Approx $8 at Amazon PRIME the Brica 2 Count Pop Open Cling Window Shades are flimsy, yet get the job done. You cannot open or close the back windows while using, or they will fall off. Overall and helpful product at a reasonable price.

I have a VW Vanagon Camper.These are working out well.Just press them to the window and you have shade for the area of glass.I can partially close the curtains and still see out but still have privacy.I need to get a few more.
summary: Stays put and Shades Car Window Nicely

reviewText: Solid feel and good sprayer. Easy to fill up and use right away. A good partner with any gallon sized car products.

Very nice bottles for mixing chemicals at home. It is much better to buy concentrated liquids and mix your own based on the ratio you prefer.These bottles have quality nozzles and are built from quality plastic. The bottles feel sturdy and are not cheaply made. To top it all off, the bottles have dilution ratios on the side for quick mixing.The only thing I wish was that these were a tad cheaper.

I gave it 4 stars because the only minus I see in the bottles is that they drip from where you attach the sprayer to the bottle when you tilt the bottle. Even when you tight the sprayer to the bottle is still drips which is not a big deal for me because its only a few drops.

So much better than the more expensive "Garden Treasures" spray bottles found at the local hardware store!  The GT bottles leak from the nozzle when you shake them and implode the body of the spray bottle as you spray unless you leave the neck loose to allow air in.  The Chemical Guys sprayer has neither of those problems, shoots a straight spray 3 times as far, and makes a much larger mist spray.There's a nice "blank form" on the side of the bottle with spaces to write in the product name, ingredients, flammability, and many other characteristics.  Labels are in English and Spanish.  There's also dilution ration marks from 1:1 to 5:1 but oddly no fluid volume marks.  All of the markings on the bottle are under a clear plastic sticker so are much less likely to get rubbed off like is happening to the markings on the GT sprayer after only a few months of light use.As other reviewers warn, the nozzle inside the CG spray bottle doesn't reach all the way to the bottom.  Some consider this a flaw, but it's made that way to avoid picking up gunk that settles to the bottom that will clog the sprayer.
summary: Much better than spray bottles at the local store

reviewText: These are by far the best sprayers we've ever used.  We use them daily in the brewery.  Had them for about a month now and they're still going strong.  Ordering backups soon just in case.

These bottles are sturdy and well made.  I use them to hold diluted products that I pour from a gallon jug.  I've only used them for a few washes so far, but they look like they will hold up well.  I'm sure cheaper bottles work just as well, but I don't regret paying a little extra for these.  If you're debating between the 16 oz and 32 oz, I recommend these over the 16 oz, which you'll end up refilling too often.  These are obviously bigger but still comfortable to use.

These are some of the best spray bottles I've tried.  They prime easily, and the ergonomics are good.  It seems like most sprayers eventually lose their prime or end up with a sticking valve, but that is not the case with these sprayers.
summary: These are some of the best spray bottles I've tried.

reviewText: The bottles on chemicalguys.com are $6.99 a piece which is crazy. For $12.96 a pack of 3 is a good deal. The bottles are high quality and have the dilution ratios on the side. These are a must for detailers and enthusiasts.

I got fed up with spray bottles from another vendor who says their sprayers are the "finest". They would last a few months and quit working, leaking fluids all over my hand in the process. For much less money, these seem to be better quality. I'll let you know in a few months if they last.
I need another set.  I used these for bulk purchases of care care products.  Much cheaper in the long run and these work well.
Very durable spray bottles. Sharpie friendly and uv protectant.

These are solid spray bottles!I have been mixing my products for cleaning my car improperly and these are perfect. They have a sticker with the proper dilution to pour product. These are pricey but honestly they will last as they are chemical resistant and should not melt of go back with degrease products.

I chose these sprayers for their chemical resistance. I used this acid wheel cleaner in it, which works very well for cleaning wheels. Since it's slightly acidic, I wanted a robust sprayer. This sprayer worked the first time, but when I tried to use it a week later, it was completely clogged. What a piece of crap for this price point.
summary: Not worth the price and no better than the $1 sprayers from Target or Wal-Mart

reviewText: These are the greatest thing since sliced bread if you want your car to dry spotless.  I live in a coastal area with very hard water.  It is essential that water not be allowed to just air dry on your car.  Before, I was using oversized bath towels to wipe down my car and was having to constantly wring the water out.  With this, all you need is a small towel to finish the job and I don't ever have to wring it out.  The squeegee gets 95% of the water without marking up your paint.If there is any negative to this, it's that it doesn't do well on rounded body parts.  It does its best work on the broad panels of sheet metal and glass.  But that's OK.  That's why I use a small towel to finish the job off.
summary: I should have gotten one of these years ago.

reviewText: This is the first one I've used, so I can't compare it to other brands, but I love it!  It's big and clears the water off the car very quickly.  It doesn't work as well for curved panels or tight spaces, but for big, flat panels, it's perfect.
summary: Makes drying the car much quicker!

reviewText: Nice size to keep in my truck with a microfiber towel for whenever I happen to visit a car wash. Does not scratch and removes water with ease

I had a really old squeegee that worked better.  It bit the dust and thought this would be better.  It leaves too much water behind.  Going to try a Ettore all-purpose 12"Update: I am now using the Ettore 17012 All-Purpose Squeegee, 12-Inch.  It works great and is cheaper.
Works perfectly! Only reason I did not give it a 5 star rating was of the feel, this water blade feels a bit cheap. So far, it has not fallen apart.
While I have not yet used, it is part of my traveling repair kit as friends recommend it.
summary: Excellent price for these compared to local stores

reviewText: I see now that there would not be any plug or adapter for my sewer connections that this would not work on.No more had to leave the adapter at a campsite because I could not get it out.

I purchased this for a cleanout plug at our local restaurant.  It was a simple PVC plug with a recessed fitting.  I thought this tool would be great since we couldn't get it open... I was wrong.  First, due to the fact that it was literally in the floor the tool needed to be manipulated and reshaped.  I did this by bending the plastic after heating it up first with a heat gun.  I allowed the plastic to cool for about 15 minutes assuring it wouldn't be soft.  Now that it had the right shape I inserted the end into the recessed fitting in the plug only to find that neither side was a great fit.  One end was way too large, the next was about right but due to rounded corners made the product slide out and essentially warp/strip the fitting.I believe at least one, if not both of the other reviews as of April 24th are BS reviews... I tried this on simple PVC, I couldn't imagine this thing opening a brass plug that has any tightness and perhaps even seizure to it.  I finally wound up getting it open since it was PVC by taking my 20.00 heat gun to it, softening the plug at the threads and prying it out with a flathead.  Which was so quick and easy I wish I did this in the first place!
works great especially for me in my rv going from campground to campground. I have had plenty of trouble trying to open the sewer cap
I have not tried this out , but can see it helping out on older plumbing .Should beat using pipe wrenches. Lets all get one
We filter our water twice coming into our RV, first with these at the tap and then on-board the RV. buying them 4 at a time is very economical.

I have used this filters for years, they seem to last one year of good camping.  The are always at a cost of around $17 dollars plus or minis.  If you buy these at $ 37.41 for a four pack that comes out to $9.35 each.  That's not to shabby, I have seen them at the camp ground stores going as high as $25.  Each

I like the idea of having a four-pack as I had purchased a single for half the price of what four cost me. As I do a lot of camping, having a water filter is a must as you never know how good the water is - these filters takes the guess work out of the equation.A single filter comes with a flexible hose which I would recommend and if your hose inlet is flush with the side of the camper/trailer etc. a right angle elbow connection is a good idea too.
I have been using these filters every time I fill the main tanks and it never tastes like plastic or ever tastes bad. will continue to use for years. However don't let filter freeze or it ruins it.

I have using these for a nub of years now and they do work well, this is the best price I have found. I have been buying 1 at a time for almost twice as much. they came very fast and will be used on my next trip.

I use these with Klasse all in one to remove light scratches and other paint marks that happen in the door sills of my cars from shoe marks etc. Washed after use and it's still like new, this 12 pack will last a lifetime for the casual car care hobbyist!

Great budget-friendly item to add to the garage arsenal. Microfiber wrapped around medium foam. Works great for sealants and wax application. I used them with liquid wax, and I love that they don't absorb 50% of what you're trying to apply to a surface - like standard foam pads do. You want a bit on the applicator, but enough to prime it so it spreads easier.If you use liquid products with these, be sure to give them a good pre-soak in hot water and microfiber detergent to break down the wax/sealant. I also like to wash these separately from microfiber towels - especially the ones you dry or clean windows with. These will hold a lot of product which can and most likely will, spread to the rest of everything in the wash.I use a little bit more microfiber detergent in a small (hot water) load, let it wash half way through the cycle, then stop it so it can soak for 10-15 minutes, and then let it finish on it's own. If you use a dryer, make sure you do it on low heat.AND ABSOLUTELY NO FABRIC SOFTENERS, that includes dryer sheets. Stay awayyy!

reviewText: If you're low on pads, this is a great value when you need a little bit of everything.Keep in mind a single pad is going to be hard pressed to do a large job all on it's own, but this will let you try out all the Hex-Logic pads at once to see how well they perform, so you can decide which individual pads you will want in the future.The pad cleaner that it comes with is CONCENTRATED, meaning you'll want to dilute this with water or use it in a small bucket as a pre-soak. If you let your pads sit long enough for all the compound to cure inside the pad, a pre-soak is necessary and this cleaner does a good job. FWIW, you shouldn't let your pads get to that point anyways.As I said this gives you one of everything.Yellow - Heavy Cut & Levelling pad, for use with heavy cut compounds for severely damaged surfaces.Orange - Medium Cut & Heavy Polishing pad, for use with medium compounds & one-step products on damaged surfaces.White - Light Cut and general purpose polishing pad. This is probably the most versatile and well-used on good/decent paint.Blue - Pure polishing pad for use with All-in-One cleaners and glazes, will remove light imperfections and is a really good glazing pad.Black - Extra Fine finishing pad, use this with glazes and all-in-one cleaners on black/dark paint, or paint that's in extremely good shape and/or new. I personally like using this with glazes on new paint that have a sealant built in, or for use with pure sealants and cleaner-waxes.Red - This is the finest of them all, used for the very final application of wax and/or sealants. You can use it for glazes, too - but those will be more effective using the blue or black pads.And finally, the green pad - a cross between white and orange. This pad is extremely versitile and is a great all-around pad for less-than-perfect finishes. I wouldn't use this for final polishing out a black car, but it has the ability to polish out oxidation without cutting, like the orange pad. It was actually designed around ceramic and extra-hard paints that a white pad can't quite correct, and an orange pad can diminish.If only they offered this kit with the ability to choose each of the 7 pads...

reviewText: You'd think that microfiber towels couldn't vary that much, but these are far superior to even the best ones that they sell at auto stores.  These are much thicker and absorbent.  Well worth the money.

You would expect towels this good to cost significantly more than bargain basement towels at a department store or auto parts shop, but they don't.  There is no excuse to spend your money on cheap towels when you can get these at such an affordable price.These are great for any exterior work you need to do, but I use them primarily for the application of detailing spray and wax buffing.  They are plenty absorbent if you choose to use them for drying, but I would recommend purchasing an actual drying towel.Remember to wash them before you use them to get rid of any green funk that might transfer onto your vehicle.

I have been using these towels for a couple of weeks and they do an excellent job.  Contrary to the picture, the towels are an almost florescent yellow that will show up dirt very quickly.  This is as it should be because if you're serious enough about your car's finish to buy theses towels, you don't want to be using a dirty towel on it.The towells have different sides.  One side has a medium high loft and the other side's loft is about half that.  Both side pick up wax pretty well but obviously the side with the higher loft will pick up more wax.The edges of the towels seem very well done as well.I expect that with reasonable care, these towels should be several years of good service.
summary: Really nice towels for the money.

reviewText: Super soft, they are the perfect size for a quick detailer spray or cleaning windows and glass. I don't feel like I'm marring my paint with them.

I recently used these microfiber towels when I waxed my car and they were excellent. Worked great for removing the wax and buffing afterward. They are a nice size and very thick, one towel was capable of doing the entire car. I would buy them again.

Like other Chemical Guys products, you get a quality product at a reasonable price. These need to get a quick wash first to remove loose bits(not lint). They spread/absorb quick detail sprays exceptionally well. They are dual sided, one short nap and the other long for versatility. I've washed mine at least a dozen times with no fraying or loss of shape/fluff. These towels do not leave any traces of lint, even on glass which is the main reason I like these so much.

These things are SO PLUSH on one side and tight but SOFT nap on the other side. Best microfiber you can buy and the lime green helps you see the dirt.I own some supreme 530 ones and these are every bit as soft but not as thick. These gordos weigh 2.3 oz each in case anyone was curious.

These are quite possibly the best microfiber towels I have ever owned. Plush, and dense - which is important. It has a really good thickness, which is great for polishing away sealant and wax. I wouldn't use these for drying a car off, but I will use the heck out of them for quick-detail sprays, spray waxes, and removing wax & sealant. They are super good on glass, as well. One side has a long nap, slightly looser side - and the other side is dense, and short napped for removing product.Take care of these, even if they are at a really good price point - you won't be sorry. Use a good detergent such as Chemical Guys (CWS_201_16) 'Microfiber Rejuvenator' Cleaning Detergent.The ONLY thing that I have a complaint about, is the lack of color choices.If you could buy these microfibers in Black, Blue, Red, Yellow, Orange, and white? I'd probably buy at least a dozen of each color. One can NEVER have too many microfibers - and it's nice to separate their usage by color (glass - blue, interior - white, etc). Makes it nice to separate your was load of towels & applicators based on their usage... I can't imagine a half load of used soiled wax removal towels with your best glass cleaning towels. Make sense?I will definitely keep a good supply of these on hand.
